meta.note: Official-source-first dataset. Visa-free reach is derived by inverting each country's own official visa-policy pages; gaps remain where governments don't publish enumerated lists.

countries.name: Afghanistan
gaps: No official nationality-specific visa-free or visa-on-arrival country list is published on mfa.gov.af or any official Afghan government domain.

Tourist e-Visa launched ~March 2026 (confirmed by mumbai.mfa.gov.af official listing) but no comprehensive nationality eligibility/exclusion list published on mfa.gov.af. Travel aggregators and Wikipedia report exclusions for Iran, Israel, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and residents (not necessarily citizens) of Azerbaijan, China, India, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Malaysia, Oman, Qatar, Russia, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, UAE - but these are NOT confirmed by an official mfa.gov.af publication and cannot be reflected in e_visa[] per official-source-first rules.
E-visa portal (eafghans.com/e-visa) returned HTTP 403 during this verification pass; cannot confirm if it is a fully official government domain vs. a government-contracted service.
econsulate.mfa.gov.af timed out during this verification pass (June 2026); status of legacy online application portal uncertain.

Israel entry ban: Multiple non-official sources report Israeli passport holders are refused entry to Afghanistan. No explicit statement found on any mfa.gov.af page. Cannot be formally recorded per official-source-first rules, only noted in gaps.

Bilateral diplomatic/service passport visa exemption agreements: Wikipedia (citing IATA data) lists China, Cuba, India, Iran, Tajikistan, Vietnam as having 30-day visa-free arrangements for non-ordinary passport holders; Turkey suspended its 2008 agreement effective June 2024. No official mfa.gov.af or embassy page publishes this list - all sourcing is from aggregators. Excluded per official-source-first rules.

UN Laissez-Passer / Interpol Travel Document holders reportedly receive visa on arrival at Kabul International Airport only (Wikipedia). No confirmation found on any official mfa.gov.af page; excluded per hard rules.
Investor residency permit program (1–10 year permits for foreign investors) reported in news sources but no official program page found on moci.gov.af, mfa.gov.af, or moi.gov.af; omitted.
No official CBI, golden visa, digital nomad, startup, or fast-track talent program found on any official Afghan government source.
Afghanistan is under Taliban (Islamic Emirate) governance since August 2021; many official digital services are limited or inconsistently maintained. Completeness is accordingly low.
E-permit visa listed on MFA types-of-visa page but no dedicated page found (404); exact purpose, fee, and eligibility undetermined.
Exit visa listed on MFA types-of-visa page but no dedicated page with fee/duration details found.
Processing times not published for any standard visa type on mfa.gov.af.
Entry allowances (single/multiple) not specified for most visa types on official pages.
Tourist e-Visa entry points: only Kabul International Airport confirmed as of June 2026; other airports and land borders not officially confirmed.

countries.name: Albania
agreements: EU Candidate Country (accession negotiations ongoing)
Stabilisation and Association Agreement with EU (in force since April 2009)
Visa Liberalisation with Schengen Area (since December 2010 - Albanian citizens travel visa-free to Schengen for short stays)
SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area, joined November 2024)
gaps: The official MFA visa regime table at punetejashtme.gov.al is rendered as an interactive JavaScript dropdown; the full per-country list with exact max_stay_days could not be programmatically extracted. Country names in the visa_free list are cross-referenced from the Wikipedia article on Visa policy of Albania, which cites Law No. 79/2021 and Council of Ministers Decision No. 858/2021 as its basis.

Seychelles visa-free status sourced only from Wikipedia (citing Law No. 79/2021), not independently confirmed from the official MFA dynamic dropdown table. Source_official set to false for this entry.

The exact minimum investment amount for the Investor Unique Permit (Article 69) is set by joint ministerial instruction (Ministers of Finance and Interior) rather than in the primary law text. One secondary source referenced a possible Law 43/2025 that may have substantially revised thresholds (e.g., EUR 300,000 for real estate, EUR 100,000 for business), but this law could not be confirmed from any official Albanian government publication as of June 2026.
Albania's CBI program was announced but suspended in March 2023; no official government page exists to confirm current status. Absence of a program is inferred from lack of any active official page.
Minimum income requirement for the Digital Nomad Unique Permit (cited as EUR 450/month) was found only in secondary sources, not on the official e-albania.al page.

The UAE 10-year residence permit (Golden Visa) as a conditional access basis was confirmed in prior record based on the official MFA page, but could not be re-extracted from the live MFA page in this validation cycle due to dynamic rendering. Retained on prior-cycle authority.

Exact list of countries eligible for diplomatic passport visa exemptions cannot be independently confirmed from the official dynamic MFA table. The list is sourced from Wikipedia (Visa policy of Albania), which cites the official Albanian MFA page.
No OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card exemption was found for Albania in any official source.
The diplomatic/service passport waiver list does not include specific bilateral agreement dates or names for most countries.

Status of Bahrain and Oman 2026 exemptions: the official MFA page confirms only Saudi Arabia and Qatar for 2026. Bahrain ordinary-passport exemption observed in 2023–2024 and Oman ordinary-passport exemption observed in 2023–2025 have lapsed for 2026. Their diplomatic passport status (if any) was not independently confirmed - they do not appear in the current record's conditional_access diplomatic list and that omission is retained.
No confirmation found that Thailand ordinary-passport exemption extended into 2026 - the official MFA page names only Saudi Arabia and Qatar for 2026.
Visa fees for Type C and D visas are set on a reciprocity basis and are not published in a fixed fee table on the official MFA website; exact USD amounts could not be confirmed.
Transit visa category not documented on official Albanian MFA website; Albania does not appear to have a separate airport transit visa regime per available official sources.

Albania-Morocco ordinary-passport visa-waiver agreement reportedly signed March 2025 but not yet confirmed in force as of June 2026 from any official Albanian government source. Morocco currently appears in conditional_access (diplomatic passports only) - not promoted to visa_free until entry-into-force is confirmed officially.

Albania-Dominican Republic agreement signed September 2025 covers diplomatic/official/special passports only and was not yet ratified as of June 2026. Dominican ordinary passport holders require an e-visa for Albania (confirmed via evisalbania.com and indirect official confirmation). Dominican Republic does not appear in visa_free or conditional_access (ordinary passport) lists — this is correct. If the agreement is ratified and extended to ordinary passports in the future, Dominican Republic would be added to visa_free.

countries.name: Algeria

The Dublin embassy omits Argentina and Poland from the diplomatic-only list; Oslo includes them. Minor inter-post discrepancy; Oslo used as source.

Max stay days for diplomatic/official passport exempt categories not explicitly stated on official source; the general 90-day-per-entry rule applies to regular visas but is not confirmed for diplomatic/official passport holders.
No official Algerian government source confirms an e-visa or ETA system.
RBI and fast-track programs: no official English-language source found; may exist in domestic legislation or Arabic-language publications.
Algeria is a member of the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU), which calls for eventual free movement, but the AMU has been largely inactive. No operationally active free-movement agreement is in force.
Dual citizenship policy for Algeria not found on official English-language MFA pages.
The Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic is a disputed territory; its inclusion in the visa-free list reflects the official Algerian government listing.
The Budapest press release for Hungary/Slovenia does not specify the date the measure took effect.

Claims that holders of valid US, Canada, UK, or Schengen visas/residence permits (beyond Hungary and Slovenia) can enter Algeria visa-free or obtain a VoA appear only in aggregator sources - NOT confirmed on any official mfa.gov.dz page verified during this research. Not recorded pending official confirmation.
OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholder exemption for Algeria not found on any official Algerian government source.

The MFA main 'Work and Residence in Algeria' page (mfa.gov.dz/services-for-foreigners/work-and-residence-in-algeria) returned no content - formal residence permit and long-term residence details could not be verified from official source.

2026-06-27: All *.mfa.gov.dz subdomains (cglondon, emboslo, embdublin, embbudapest, embwashington, embabudhabi, embcanberra) returned SSL certificate errors - could not re-confirm diplomatic/service passport conditional_access entries or southern-Algeria VoA press release this run. Entries preserved per safety rule. Re-check mfa.gov.dz SSL status on next validation run.

countries.name: Andorra
agreements: Bilateral Convention with France and Spain on entry, movement, sojourn and establishment (signed 4 December 2000) - Andorran, French and Spanish nationals benefit from coordinated movement and certain equal treatment provisions
Bilateral Convention with Portugal on residency and movement (signed 23 July 2007, in force 1 September 2008)
Coordinated visa policy with Schengen Area (2003 tripartite agreement between France, Spain and Andorra - Andorra follows Schengen visa requirements for third-country nationals)

Agreement on Exemption from Visa Requirement for Holders of Diplomatic and Official Passports between India and the Principality of Andorra (signed 15 March 2024 at Andorra la Vella, in force 15 June 2024)
gaps: Visa policy: Andorra's official sources (govern.ad, portaljuridicandorra.ad) do not publish a specific country-by-country visa-free list; the law categorises entry by document type (EU/EEA ID card, passport for others, Schengen visa for those requiring it).
No official e-visa or ETA system exists for Andorra.
Visa-on-arrival: No official sources mention a visa-on-arrival system for Andorra.
Fee amounts for most authorization categories are not published in the statutory text; fees are set by regulation and adjusted periodically.
Processing times for most authorization categories are not specified in official sources.
Path to permanent residency (years) is not specified in the official sources reviewed; renewal schedule is 2-2-3-10 years but no explicit 'permanent residency' designation found.

Conditional access - other bilateral diplomatic/official passport agreements: The govern.ad international agreements page references an Excel file (ACORDS_BILATERALS_en vigor.xlsx) listing all of Andorra's bilateral treaties, but the file could not be accessed programmatically.
Transit visa: Andorra has no airport, seaport, or independent border; transit through Andorra is not a separately defined visa category in official sources.
Working holiday: The young persons with work option (Art. 26 bis) is the closest equivalent to a working-holiday visa but its exact age limits and quotas were not specified in the sources retrieved.

countries.name: Angola
gaps: The SME portal pages for individual visa categories (e-visa, residence title, work visa) are behind a login wall and detailed eligibility criteria could not be confirmed from the public-facing official pages.

Minimum investment amounts for the Investor Visa are not stated verbatim on the official source; the 2021 Private Investment Law (Law No. 10/21) states any investment amount is eligible, but no specific threshold appears in official sources.

Path-to-permanent-residency years not explicitly stated on official pages (after 3 years uninterrupted investor stay: mentioned in the official Angola Consulate Dubai guide, but 'temporary residence permit' rather than permanent residence is specified).
No official source confirms a digital nomad, startup, or highly-skilled worker fast-track visa program for Angola.

No official source confirms any freedom-of-movement agreement membership for Angola (SADC Protocol on Facilitation of Movement of Persons has not been ratified by Angola per available sources); agreements array left empty per strict official-source rule.

Niue is listed in the Presidential Decree as one of the 14 Oceania countries; it is a New Zealand-associated territory with no sovereign ISO-3 code under ISO 3166-1 (NU is its two-letter code but not alpha-3); retained as iso3=null.

No official Angolan source found granting conditional entry (visa-free/VoA/e-visa) based on holding a third-country visa (US, Schengen, UK, Canada, etc.), residence permit, or permanent residence card. Angola's entry rules are nationality-based, not credential-based.
No official source found for OCI or equivalent diaspora special-status entry rules for Angola.

The MIREX bilateral agreements document (angola.or.jp, dated 12 February 2019) may not reflect post-2019 agreements. Wikipedia notes pending (not-yet-in-force) agreements with Benin, Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Ghana, Morocco and Timor-Leste for diplomatic passports - these were not confirmed on any official Angolan government source and are excluded per strict official-source rule.
Exact agreement dates for Cuba, Ecuador, and Zambia diplomatic/service passport waivers are not stated in the official MIREX document.

Angola–Congo Republic (Republic of the Congo, COG) diplomatic/service passport agreement details were found on angolex.com (non-official aggregator), not on an official .gov.ao domain; excluded from conditional_access per official-source rule - noted here as a gap.

UNRESOLVED (2026-06-27): Philippines (PHL) - Council of Ministers reportedly approved adding the Philippines to the visa-free tourism list at its 8th Ordinary Session (O País, 27 Aug 2025; Philippine Inquirer citing Angola Embassy Manila DFA notification). Wikipedia's Angola visa policy article (updated June 2026) records an October 17, 2025 effective date. However, the official Angolan SME FAQ page (sme.gov.ao/ao/perguntas-frequentes/evisa-english-version/) does NOT list the Philippines as of 2026-06-27 re-fetch. Per strict safety rule, Philippines has NOT been added to visa_free. Monitor the SME page and governo.gov.ao for publication of the amending Presidential Decree.

UNRESOLVED (2026-06-27): Kenya (KEN) - Angola and Kenya agreed on mutual visa exemption for ordinary passport holders on 21 October 2023. Kenya has broadened eTA exemptions to include Angolans (Legal Notice No. 93, May 2025). The reciprocal Angolan side (Kenyans entering Angola visa-free) is not confirmed on any official Angolan government page (SME, governo.gov.ao, MIREX). Kenya NOT added to visa_free pending official Angolan source confirmation.

UNRESOLVED (2026-06-27): The African Union Laissez-passer agreement signed in Addis Ababa (reported by africadosul.mirex.gov.ao) covers AU officials, dependents, and work specialists - it is NOT an ordinary-passport nationality-based exemption and does not affect the visa_free list. Correctly excluded.

Turkey (Türkiye): From January 1, 2026, Armenian and Turkish diplomatic, special, and service passport holders may obtain an e-visa free of charge (fee waived, not unconditionally visa-free). The 90-day claim from aggregators contradicts the confirmed 180-day unilateral exemption; no official mfa.am source confirms such a new agreement. Not separately recorded; needs official confirmation.

Main mfa.am domain has been blocked by Radware DDoS protection on every validation pass since June 2026. The visa_free unilateral list (mfa.am/en/visafreelist) and bilateral list (mfa.am/en/whoneedvisa) cannot be directly re-verified until the domain becomes accessible again.

countries.name: Australia
agreements: Trans-Tasman Travel Arrangement (Australia–New Zealand)
gaps: The subclass 188 investor stream minimum investment amount shown on the live official page is AUD 2.5 million, but the stream is closed to new applications so this figure is historical. The corrected amount is recorded for documentation accuracy.

National Innovation Visa (858) salary threshold is tied to the Fair Work High Income Threshold (FWIT), indexed annually on 1 July. The figure AUD 190,100 applies from 1 July 2026. The 1 July 2026 amount was confirmed from Addisons law firm and Hartman Immigration (citing Fair Work Commission), not directly from fairwork.gov.au (which returned timeout on 2026-06-29). Re-verify against fairwork.gov.au/tools-and-resources/library/K600486_High-income-threshold-amounts to confirm the official figure once the page is accessible.
The complete path-to-PR timelines for subclass 188 investment streams and subclass 888 depend on individual state/territory nomination conditions; no fixed durations are stated on official pages.
No visa-on-arrival policy exists for Australia - confirmed from official sources.

No credential-based conditional entry rules found on any official Australian government source: Australia does not grant visa-free, VoA, e-visa, or ETA access to travellers based solely on holding a valid US, UK, Schengen, Canadian, or other third-country visa or residence permit. Every traveller must independently meet Australian visa requirements.
No OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholder conditional entry rule found for Australia.

No bilateral diplomatic/official passport visa suppression treaties found. DFAT Protocol Guidelines confirm diplomatic staff posted to Australia require a formal subclass 995 diplomatic visa - diplomatic passport alone does not confer right of entry for non-transit purposes.

Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR, and Taiwan (ROC) passport holders - CONFIRMED visa-exempt (2026-07): the official BiH Embassy (Oslo) consular page explicitly lists them among visa-exempt categories ('Passport holders in special administrative regions of the People's Republic of China: 1. countries.name: Botswana

SACU (Southern African Customs Union) - member; facilitates trade but does not establish freedom of movement for ordinary citizens
Botswana-Namibia bilateral identity card agreement (February 2023) - Namibian nationals may enter Botswana using national identity cards in lieu of passports
gaps: The 90-day max_stay for visa-free nationals is based on a general gov.bw statement and the Embassy page rather than a per-country table - individual bilateral agreements may set different limits. Russia Wikipedia source suggests '30 days per visit' limit not reflected on Embassy page.
The official Botswana Embassy Washington DC page lists 'Yugoslavia' as visa-free; Yugoslavia is a defunct state and was excluded from structured data.
No official government source (*.gov.bw) confirms a minimum investment amount for a dedicated investor residence permit or golden visa.
CBI $75,000 minimum investment figure comes from Arton Capital's BotswanaCitizenship.com portal, not from a government gazette; official regulations have not been published on gov.bw as of June 2026.
Citizenship by Investment (Citizenship Amendment Bill 2025) was passed by Parliament in December 2025 but status of presidential assent and formal enactment is unconfirmed on gov.bw as of June 2026.
Work Permit Point-Based System details referenced in official Botswana Government communications but no stable official web page was accessible during research.
The SADC Protocol on Facilitation of Movement of Persons has been ratified by Botswana but has not entered into force regionally.

Multiple gov.bw sub-pages (/residency-and-work/work-permit-application, /residency-and-work/permanent-residence-application, /visa-applications/visa-application-tourism-visa, /taxonomy/term/114) returned HTTP 500 errors during June 2026 re-validation and could not be scraped.

No official Botswana government source (*.gov.bw) found confirming credential-based conditional entry (i.e., entry for holders of US, UK, Schengen, Canadian, or other third-country visas or residence permits).
Turkey visa-free status confirmed from Embassy page, but no specific bilateral agreement date or treaty text found on gov.bw.

The evisa.gov.bw portal's JavaScript-rendered content was not accessible via WebFetch during June 2026 re-validation (page only returned navigation markup); the country list in e_visa[] is preserved from prior research based on the original evisa.gov.bw/#/needvisa scrape.

Holy See / Vatican City (iso3: VAT) - UNRESOLVED OFFICIAL-SOURCE SELF-CONTRADICTION: The official Botswana Embassy Washington DC page simultaneously lists 'Holy Sea' (typo for Holy See) in the visa-FREE section and 'Vatican City' in the visa-REQUIRED section. These are the same sovereign entity. Per safety rules, Holy See/Vatican City is excluded from visa_free pending resolution of this contradiction. If the 'Holy Sea' entry is the operative one, Holy See holders would be visa-free; if 'Vatican City' is operative, a visa is required. Botswana immigration authorities should be contacted directly to resolve this.

'Sumatra' appears in the visa-required list on the official Embassy page - Sumatra is an Indonesian island, not a country. This is an apparent data-entry error on the Embassy page; Indonesian passport holders are confirmed to require a visa (Indonesia is listed separately as visa-required). No structured entry was created for 'Sumatra'.

Mexico visa status (RESOLVED 2026-06-29): Mexico REMAINS visa-free for entry to Brazil as of June 2026. The 2026-06-27 run incorrectly classified Mexico as e-visa based on speculative articles about future plans. The e-visa narrative was about Mexico requiring e-visa for Brazilians (reverse direction, from Feb 5 2026), not Brazil requiring e-visa for Mexicans. Current classification: visa_free, 90 days. Monitor for any future Brazilian reciprocal measure against Mexican passports.

Argentina visa status (RESOLVED 2026-06-29): Argentina REMAINS visa-free for entry to Brazil as of June 2026. The 2026-06-27 run incorrectly classified Argentina as e-visa based on speculative VisaHQ Dec 2025 articles. Multiple June 2026 sources confirm Argentina remains visa-free under Mercosur arrangements. Current classification: visa_free, 90 days, national ID accepted.

Full list of nationalities required to obtain e-visa under the January 2026 permanent e-visa regime: confirmed only for USA, Canada, Australia (all effective April 10 2025 / permanent Jan 1 2026). France was briefly on e-visa then restored to visa-free Feb 24 2026. Gov.br pages remain CAPTCHA-blocked for definitive extraction of the full 30+ country list.

Open Doors 2026 pilot evaluation scheduled for Q4 2026 - the visa-free status of the eight new countries (Denmark, France, Hungary, Ireland, Jamaica, Bahamas, Saint Lucia) may revert to e-visa if the pilot is not extended.

China visa-free status: The record now reflects both the Open Doors 2026 framework (30 days, extendable) effective Feb 24, 2026, and the separate MRE/MTur bilateral press release (May 11 - Dec 31, 2026, 30 days for tourism/business). The interaction between these two instruments is not fully clear from available sources.

VIPER minimum investment amount: R$700,000 (North/Northeast) and R$1,000,000 (other regions) confirmed from multiple official MRE consulate pages citing RN 36/2018, but the specific portaldeimigracao.mj.gov.br PDF pages confirming updated 2026 amounts were not extractable.

Digital Nomad visa income requirement (USD 1,500/month or USD 18,000 savings): confirmed from multiple official MRE consulate pages but slight discrepancy (USD 1,500 vs USD 1,800) noted in some sources. The USD 1,500 figure is used here per majority of official consulate pages.
Kosovo status: Code 12 in QGRV - Brazil does not maintain diplomatic relations; visa may be granted for up to 90 days but not recorded as standard visa-free entry.
RASD (Western Sahara/Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic): Code 13 - Brazil does not maintain diplomatic relations; visa granted on laissez-passer. Not included in standard visa categories.

Conditional access Type A (credential-based entry based on holding a third-country visa such as US/Schengen/EU/UK/Canada visa, residence permit, Green Card/PR): No official Brazilian government source found for any such rule. Brazil's entry policy is nationality-based.
Conditional access Type B (OCI card or other diaspora/special status): No official Brazilian source found for any OCI cardholder or similar special status granting entry.

countries.name: Bulgaria
agreements: EU/EEA freedom of movement
Schengen Area
gaps: The official MFA website (mfa.bg) does not enumerate individual Annex I (visa-required) countries - the site only references Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 without listing them explicitly. Bulgaria does not operate a standalone e-visa portal (no official evisa.bg or equivalent found). All visa applications are paper-based through diplomatic missions or VFS Global.

ETIAS is not yet operational as of June 2026; expected to launch in Q4 2026. The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) became fully operational at Schengen external borders on 10 April 2026. When ETIAS becomes operative, all Annex II nationals will require an ETIAS travel authorisation for short stays. The exact date ETIAS will become mandatory is not yet confirmed.

The investbulgaria.com official website requires authentication or may be blocked by bot protection; program details cited from law-firm and investment migration secondary sources referencing the Foreigners Act.
The exact processing time for the digital nomad permit and RBI golden visa are not officially published on a government page accessible during this research.

A potentially updated diplomatic/service passport PDF may exist on the MFA website after January 2025 but was not located during this validation; the Georgia suspension (March 2026) may not yet be reflected in any updated MFA PDF.
Dual citizenship policy for naturalized citizens not confirmed from an accessible official source during this research.

Minimum income threshold for the digital nomad permit (EUR 31,000) was based on the minimum wage at time of launch (January 2025); the current minimum wage figure post-euro adoption and potential adjustments were not re-verified from an official source.
The diplomatic/service passport table (mfa.bg PDF, last updated 14 January 2025) does not list agreement dates for individual bilateral visa waiver arrangements.

The Visa Facilitation Agreements page (mfa.bg/en/services-travel/consular-services/travel-bulgaria/visa-facilitation-agreements) may not be accessible publicly; any additional facilitation agreements listed there may not be fully captured.

DJRV (Declaracion Jurada Regional de Viajero): mandatory electronic customs/immigration declaration form for all air travelers entering or exiting Guatemala, administered by SAT (Superintendencia de Administracion Tributaria, the tax/customs authority, NOT IGM). Confirmed mandatory as of at least 2023 per official SAT communications; US State Dept advisory (updated 2026-06-11) explicitly mentions this requirement. Not recorded in visa_policy or eta fields as it is not an entry authorization mechanism.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
agreements: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) Free Movement Protocol (entered into force 30 April 1980) - visa-free for ECOWAS member nationals with ordinary passports. NOTE: Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso withdrew from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025 (AES/Alliance of Sahel States); ECOWAS instructed remaining members to maintain visa-free movement for AES nationals until further notice. As of June 2026, all 14 original members are still treated as visa-free per Wikipedia (April 2026) and no Guinea-Bissau official cancellation found.

CPLP (Community of Portuguese Language Countries) Acordo sobre Supressão de Vistos em Passaportes Diplomáticos, Especiais e de Serviço - visa-free for diplomatic/service passport holders of Angola, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Mozambique, Portugal, São Tomé and Príncipe, Vietnam
CPLP Mobility Agreement (signed Luanda 2021) - facilitates residency procedures among CPLP member states; does NOT extend ordinary-passport visa-free entry to Guinea-Bissau
Belarus–Guinea-Bissau visa exemption agreement for diplomatic/official/service passport holders (signed 7 May 2025, pending entry into force)
Serbia–Guinea-Bissau visa exemption agreement for diplomatic/official/special passport holders (signed April 2023, pending entry into force)
gaps: Guinea-Bissau's official government website (gov.gw) does not resolve - no official immigration portal accessible on a .gw domain.
No official list of visa-exempt or visa-on-arrival nationalities published on a Guinea-Bissau government domain was found.
rgb-visa.com appears to operate Guinea-Bissau's electronic visa system but is a private .com domain - data from it cannot be marked source_official.

São Tomé and Príncipe ordinary passport status: Africa Visa Openness 2025 report claims Guinea-Bissau switched São Tomé from visa-on-arrival to visa-free in 2025, but this cannot be confirmed from an official Guinea-Bissau government source and is contradicted by commercial aggregators. Listed here as unverified; ordinary São Tomé passport holders should verify current requirements with a Guinea-Bissau embassy.

CPLP Mobility Agreement (Luanda 2021): Guinea-Bissau ratification status for ordinary-passport travel facilitation not confirmed from an official Guinea-Bissau source. The Luanda Agreement primarily addresses residency, not visa-free tourism entry.
CPLP diplomatic/service passport visa suppression agreement: Guinea-Bissau's specific ratification date not confirmed from an official .gw domain source.
Serbia visa waiver agreement (April 2023): source is Wikipedia only; entry-into-force date unknown.
Belarus visa waiver agreement (7 May 2025): signed per official Belarus MFA (mfa.gov.by); ratification by Guinea-Bissau not confirmed; entry-into-force status as of June 2026 unknown.

Max stay for ECOWAS nationals: Wikipedia states 'indefinite period of stay' per the 1980 ECOWAS agreement, but the ECOWAS Phase I protocol standard right is 90 days. No Guinea-Bissau official source specifies the exact duration.

No conditional entry rule found granting visa-free or visa-on-arrival access based on the traveller holding a valid US, Schengen, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, UAE or other third-country visa or residence permit.
No OCI or analogous special diaspora/heritage status conferring special entry rights to Guinea-Bissau was found.
No official RBI, golden visa, or investor residence program found.
No official fast-track, digital-nomad, or startup visa scheme found.

Timor-Leste and Equatorial Guinea (CPLP members): their diplomatic/service passport status in Guinea-Bissau was not confirmed - Wikipedia lists only 7 CPLP members (excluding Timor-Leste and Equatorial Guinea) as covered by the diplomatic/service passport suppression agreement.

Visa on arrival max stay discrepancy: rgb-visa.com/Fees.html lists the Short Stay single-entry visa as valid for 30 days (EUR 61.45); Wikipedia states VoA is valid for 'a maximum stay of 90 days'. The 30-day figure is retained as the standard single-entry VoA duration per the operational e-visa fee schedule; the 90-day figure may refer to the maximum duration achievable when a multiple-entry VoA is issued at the border, which is an exceptional case. No Guinea-Bissau official source clarifies this discrepancy.

Mauritania/Morocco visa-free claim (2026-06-27): Some non-official aggregators (e.g. thingstodoinguineabissau.com) claim Mauritania and Morocco are visa-free for Guinea-Bissau. This is not supported by Wikipedia, rgb-visa.com, or any official government source. Mauritania is an associate/suspended ECOWAS member (not a full member); Morocco is not ECOWAS. These two countries remain visa-required per the best available evidence.

Mali (MLI), Niger (NER), Burkina Faso (BFA) - ECOWAS withdrawal impact (2026-06-29): These three countries formally exited ECOWAS on January 29, 2025. ECOWAS instructed remaining members to continue granting visa-free movement to AES nationals until further notice; as of June 2026, no Guinea-Bissau-specific cancellation has been confirmed from any official source. These three are retained as visa-free in this record based on ECOWAS's 'until further notice' instruction and absence of a contrary Guinea-Bissau official announcement. Travellers holding Malian, Nigerien, or Burkinabe passports should verify current status with the Guinea-Bissau embassy before travel. If Guinea-Bissau implements visa requirements for these nationals, this entry must be updated.

Iraq diplomatic passport MoU (8 Feb 2025) sourced from Iraqi MFA (mofa.gov.iq); no corresponding announcement confirmed on Moroccan diplomatie.ma - recorded with source_official=true as mofa.gov.iq is an official government domain.
No official digital nomad, startup, talent, or fast-track visa program found on official Moroccan government sources.

Morocco is not a member of any formal freedom-of-movement bloc; the agreements array is empty because no official source confirms membership in ECOWAS, GCC, EU/EEA, Arab League free movement, or similar multilateral arrangements.
The diplomatic/official passport agreement table on consulat.ma does not specify agreement dates or maximum stay durations for most bilateral agreements.

Azerbaijan official Moroccan MFA announcement URL could not be confirmed from diplomatie.ma directly (SSL error); AZERTAC (official Azerbaijani state news agency) used as source - bilateral facts cross-checked via multiple secondary sources (MoroccoWorldNews, APA News, hespress).

countries.name: Mozambique
agreements: SADC (Southern African Development Community) member state
CPLP (Community of Portuguese Language Countries) member state - multilateral diplomatic/service/special passport visa suppression agreement among CPLP members
gaps: The eVisa portal's eVisa-eligible section lists a comprehensive global country list but does not individually enumerate stay durations per country - only that they are eligible for eVisa (specific approved duration varies by visa type applied for).

Restricted countries (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal, Somalia) are noted as requiring embassy-based visa applications; no further details (fees, processing times) found on official sources.

No official government page found confirming a formal citizenship-by-investment or golden visa/residency-by-investment program. Media sources (November 2025) mention a proposed tiered investor residency (USD 500,000 for 5 years, USD 5,000,000 for 10 years) but no official government page confirms this program is live.
No official digital nomad, skilled worker fast-track, or startup visa program found on official Mozambican government domains.

ETA fee as of February 2026 portal: approximately USD 48 per VisasNews and Wikipedia - not yet confirmed directly from evisa.gov.mz (returned HTTP 403 in two consecutive validation passes, June 2026). fee_usd set to 48 in ETA visa_type entry based on non-official corroboration; treat as provisional until evisa.gov.mz is directly accessible.

SADC Protocol on Facilitation of Movement of Persons: Mozambique is a SADC member but it is unclear from official sources whether Mozambique has fully ratified the free movement protocol; practical bilateral visa-free arrangements are captured in the visa_free list.

TYPE A (held third-country credential): No official Mozambican government source found granting visa-free, VoA, ETA, or expedited eVisa entry based on holding a valid US, Schengen, UK, UAE, GCC, Australian, Canadian, or any other foreign visa or residence permit.
TYPE B (special status): No official Mozambican source mentions India OCI card, or any equivalent diaspora/heritage status, as conferring conditional entry.

Bilateral diplomatic/service passport agreement texts for Egypt, Turkey, Thailand, Venezuela, Vietnam bilateral waivers were not found on official Mozambican government domains; their presence on evisa.gov.mz waiver table is taken as authoritative confirmation.

visitos.senami.gov.mz (SENAMI eVisa portal) returned ECONNREFUSED in 2026-06-27 validation pass; could not confirm whether it contains additional immigration details beyond the evisa.gov.mz platform. Previously noted as the redirect target for senami.gov.mz.

Wikipedia (Visa policy of Mozambique) and the Embassy of Mozambique in Japan mention a visa-on-arrival option at border posts for nationalities without Mozambican embassy representation (~USD 50, 30 days). The Japan Embassy qualifies this as applicable for 'travelers from nations lacking Mozambican diplomatic representation.' No official SENAMI or evisa.gov.mz page was found confirming a universal visa-on-arrival service - this is NOT added to visa_on_arrival without official confirmation. Preserve as gap.

Wikipedia cites Eritrea and Sri Lanka as nationalities requiring prior SENAMI written approval before entry (similar restriction to the known 6 restricted countries). This was not confirmed on any live official Mozambican government domain in this validation pass - the restricted list (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal, Somalia) is preserved unchanged pending official confirmation.

countries.name: Myanmar

gaps: The evisa.moip.gov.mm portal pages rendered blank (likely JavaScript-heavy SPA) — e-visa country list was sourced from official Myanmar Consulate Hong Kong (myanmarconsulatehk.org) which mirrors the official evisa.moip.gov.mm notice.
The exact current e-visa tourist and business eligible countries may have changed since the consulate page data was last updated — the official portal evisa.moip.gov.mm could not be read directly.

No official page was found for RBI (residency by investment) or fast-track/skilled worker/digital nomad visa scheme — absence is consistent with Myanmar's current political and regulatory environment.

Japan/Korea/Macau VOA: The second pilot is confirmed as starting 21 October 2025 via tourism.gov.mm/en/information-pages/visa-on-arrival; end date of 20 October 2026 is inferred as one-year from start — a dedicated renewal announcement page was not found.

Hong Kong VOA pilot expired 10 March 2026. No renewal announcement found as of June 2026 via Myanmar Consulate HK website or web search. Entry retained in visa_on_arrival with expiry flag per preservation rule. Must be re-checked when official renewal is announced.

Serbia conditional_access entry retained from prior record (mofa.gov.mm October 2025 PDF) but not found in Embassy of Myanmar Riyadh bilateral table on June 2026 re-fetch (table lists 23 countries without Serbia). Serbia may have been omitted from the Riyadh table, or the bilateral agreement may have lapsed; kept pending direct MFA confirmation.

No official Myanmar government source was found establishing conditional entry rules based on holding a third-country visa, residence permit, or permanent residence — Myanmar's entry system is based solely on nationality and passport type.
Taiwan/Chinese Taipei is listed as eligible for Business/Workshop/Transit VOA; its status as a separate non-state entity means it has no bilateral treaty but is treated administratively.
Colombia and Sri Lanka bilateral exemption effective dates not available; only stay durations sourced from Embassy of Myanmar Riyadh bilateral table.
Myanmar does not offer digital nomad, retirement, investment, working holiday, or medical visa categories — these are absent from all official sources reviewed.

Malaysia ordinary passport visa-free pilot: exact end date not confirmed from official Myanmar source (Myanmar Consulate HK announcement references start from October 2025 as one-year pilot; approximate end approximately September/October 2026).

Russia ordinary passport: Riyadh embassy table (June 2026) lists Russia bilateral agreement with 90 days for both passport types, but no ordinary passport column value was explicitly confirmed. Russia listed in Riyadh table; kept at diplomatic/service only per prior record until direct confirmation of ordinary passport terms is available.

countries.name: Namibia
agreements: SADC (Southern African Development Community) - member state; no formal SADC Protocol on Free Movement of Persons in force as of data collection
gaps: The official MHAISS pages at mha.gov.na (countries-exempted, immigration-control, visas-immigration-control-act-act-no-7) were not accessible; data cross-verified from Embassy USA, Embassy Berlin, Swiss Mission, Embassy Sweden, Visit Namibia, and The Namibian newspaper.
The Namibia Visa Fact Sheet PDF (Version 4, May 2025) from mha.gov.na is image-based and contains no extractable text - unreadable by automated tools.
The eservices.mhaiss.gov.na portal returned SSL certificate errors in this validation session; complete current VOA country list from the e-services portal not directly verified.

The September 2025 expansion (36 countries/territories per official MHAISS September 23, 2025 announcement) is sourced from secondary reporting of the MHAISS announcement (eiglaw.com/Erickson Immigration Group) and The Namibian newspaper, not from mha.gov.na directly. The official MHAISS announcement date was September 23, 2025; the effective implementation date has not been confirmed directly from the government portal.
No official digital nomad or skilled worker fast-track extension or renewal pathway was found; the Digital Nomad Visa is explicitly non-renewable (must wait 12 months).
Dual citizenship policy under Namibian Citizenship Act not explicitly confirmed for naturalized citizens from official source - not recorded.

The RBI investment amount (N$3,950,000) is cited by private developers referencing the Foreign Investments Act; the official mha.gov.na immigration-control page did not load to confirm the amount directly.

CONDITIONAL ACCESS (type A - held third-country credential): No official Namibian government source found granting visa-free, VOA, e-visa, or eTA entry on the basis of holding a valid US visa, Schengen visa, UK visa, residence permit, Green Card, or any other third-country credential. All entry rules reviewed are purely nationality/passport-type based.

CONDITIONAL ACCESS (type B - special status / OCI): No official Namibian government source found granting entry waiver for OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholders or any equivalent diaspora/heritage status.

Some pre-April-2025 VOA countries sourced only from namibia-botschaft.de (Embassy Berlin) - e.g., Cambodia, Chile, Czech Republic, Hungary, Mexico, Nicaragua, Romania, Slovakia, South Korea, Thailand, UAE, Vietnam - have not been directly re-verified against the eservices portal due to access issues; embassy source treated as authoritative.

Haiti fee exemption confirmed by secondary sources only (VisasNews, search result summary referencing Embassy USA October 2025 PDF); the October 2025 Embassy USA PDF (namibiaembassyusa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Namibia-Visa-On-Arrival.pdf) was not extractable as it is image-based.

Schedule 3 (Visitor's Visa Fee Exempt Countries) and Schedule 4 (Simplified Visitor's Visa Application Countries) from the 2014 Regulations may have been amended by subsequent Gazette notices not found during research.

RONLAW consolidated Immigration Regulations 2014 (with all amendments) could not be fully extracted due to JavaScript PDF viewer rendering / binary PDF format.

South Ossetia mutual visa-free agreement (90 days, signed 3 February 2018) noted in Wikipedia as 'yet to be ratified' - no official Nauru gazette confirmation found.

The ECRCP standard rate prior to the Iruwa Initiative restructuring (previously listed as USD 115,000) could not be independently confirmed as a now-deprecated figure from an official archived source; the current official page shows USD 90,000 as standard.
Exact fee amounts for Business Visa subtypes (diplomatic, education, religious, research, employment subtypes vs. general AUD 6,000 rate) not officially published in detail online.
Full details of Public Service Employment Visa (Gazette No. 256, 2025) could not be extracted from binary PDF.
Processing times for all visa categories are not officially published online.

No student, digital nomad, retirement, investment, working holiday, or medical visa categories found in official sources.

countries.name: Nepal

OCI (Overseas Citizenship of India) cardholders have NO visa exemption for Nepal - OCI is an Indian government document with no legal validity for Nepal entry; OCI holders must obtain a standard tourist visa.

Complete enumeration of all individual nationalities eligible for visa on arrival (as opposed to just the restricted list) was not available on any official page; the policy is 'all nationalities except the restricted list'.
Nepal's digital nomad visa was announced in May 2025 but has no official launch page as of June 2026; not recorded as an active fast-track program.
Residential visa path to permanent residence or citizenship is unclear from official sources - no official statement found on whether long-term residential visa holders can naturalize.
The maximum per-entry continuous stay for NRN visa holders is not explicitly stated in official sources beyond the 30-day on-arrival grant; extension up to 1 year per DOI is confirmed.

Business, student, and work visa fees and maximum durations are not published on available official embassy pages - these are directed to the Department of Immigration (immigration.gov.np) which has persistent SSL errors blocking access.
Transit visa fee and maximum stay not published on available official embassy pages.

moha.gov.np restricted-country list (as of 2026-06-29, re-checked) still shows only 12 countries (no Iran), confirming the page has not been updated since the March 13, 2026 decision; Iran's addition is confirmed via ntb.gov.np official tourist visa page (fetched 2026-06-29) and corroborated by Xinhua (english.news.cn), Kathmandu Post, and multiple official-cited news sources.

fr.nepalembassy.gov.np (Paris embassy) shows all 14 bilateral-agreement countries with '90 days' for diplomatic/official/service passports - this may be a generalized statement. China/Pacific Islands NZeTA trial scheme (launched 3 Nov 2025): Whether the 12-month trial will be extended or made permanent beyond ~2 November 2026 has not been confirmed on any official page as of 27 June 2026.

countries.name: Nigeria
agreements: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) free movement of persons protocol
gaps: The specific named countries covered by Nigeria's bilateral visa abolition/waiver agreements (non-ECOWAS) for ordinary passport holders are not published in a consolidated official online list on immigration.gov.ng or interior.gov.ng.

Minimum investment thresholds for Investor Visas N3C (Large Scale Corporations), N3D (Ultra Large Scale Corporations), and N3E (Oil/Gas/Power Sector) are not stated as specific dollar amounts on the official info-center pages.
Minimum financial requirements for the Retirement Visa (N5B) are not specified as exact amounts on the official page.

Post-withdrawal visa-free status of Burkina Faso (BFA), Mali (MLI), and Niger (NER): These three countries formally withdrew from ECOWAS on January 29, 2025. ECOWAS maintained visa-free movement for their nationals during a six-month transition period (ends July 29, 2025) and has continued it 'until further notice' post-transition. Nigeria's official NIS website (immigration.gov.ng) does not address their current status - the F5A exemption page references only 'ECOWAS member States', which BFA/MLI/NER are no longer. Whether Nigeria individually extends visa-free access to these three nationalities (by bilateral agreement or extended ECOWAS-derived right) is not published on any official Nigerian government domain as of June 2026. Classified as unknown/unconfirmed; these nationalities are NOT listed in visa_free to avoid false visa-free error.
Path-to-citizenship timelines for investor or highly-skilled residence visa holders are not specified on official immigration.gov.ng pages.
No official digital nomad or startup visa program found on official Nigerian immigration sources.

Diplomatic/service passport waiver agreements with Brazil, China, Namibia, Singapore, South Africa, and Turkey are referenced in Wikipedia/TIMATIC but no standalone official Nigerian government (MFA/NIS) page was found to verify these; not recorded per official-source-first rules.

The Nigeria-Vietnam diplomatic/official passport waiver (signed Oct 2019, 90-day max stay) is confirmed by credible news sources but no standalone official foreignaffairs.gov.ng press-release page was found; recorded with source_official=false.

The Nigeria-Ethiopia diplomatic/official passport waiver (MOU signed Feb 2020, ratified by Ethiopia 2025) is confirmed by credible news sources but no standalone official foreignaffairs.gov.ng press-release page was found; recorded with source_official=false.

The foreignaffairs.gov.ng page for the Nigeria-Angola agreement had an expired SSL certificate at time of June 2026 re-validation; the agreement is accepted as official based on the .gov.ng domain appearing in official search results and VON corroboration.

No credential-based conditional entry rules found: Nigeria does not grant visa-free or e-visa access to foreign nationals solely on the basis of holding a valid US, UK, Schengen, Canadian, or other country's visa/residence permit.
No special-status conditional entry rules found: No OCI or similar diaspora/heritage status recognized by Nigeria for entry purposes.

Saint Kitts and Nevis visa-free agreement: specific passport types eligible (ordinary vs official/diplomatic) not delineated in the official SKNIS announcement texts. 90-day duration confirmed by NIS spokesperson Akinsola Akinlabi per TheCable.

Rwanda visa-free agreement (effective ~May 15, 2026): specific passport types eligible (ordinary vs official/diplomatic) not delineated in the official NIS spokesman statement. Recorded with source_official=false as no dedicated immigration.gov.ng page was found at time of June 2026 verification. The NIS F5A exemption page has not yet been updated to reflect Rwanda. Max stay of 30 days confirmed by NIS spokesman.

Nigeria-UK 2026 agreements: the Statements of Intent on Business Visa Expansion may lead to a future fast-track business visa arrangement for UK companies; current scope is not ordinary-passport visa-free. Monitor for further developments.

countries.name: Palestine
gaps: Palestine does not operate an independent border control or visa issuance system. Entry to the West Bank is governed by Israeli immigration policy (cogat.mod.gov.il, eta.gov.il); entry to Gaza is controlled by Hamas and subject to severe restrictions. Rafah crossing (Egypt-Gaza) closes regularly with no warning and for long periods. Erez crossing (Gaza-Israel) has been damaged and closed since October 7 2023. No stable regular entry system is operational for Gaza as of June 29 2026.

The Palestinian MFA General Department of Protocol page (mofa.pna.ps/en-us/theministry/generaldepartmentofprotocol) contains only a reference to 'Countries Palestinian Passport Holders Can Enter With/Without Visa' — outbound travel data, not inbound visa policy. No inbound conditional access rules are published there. The domain returns SSL certificate errors preventing direct WebFetch.

Diplomatic passport bilateral agreements: The Palestinian Authority issues diplomatic passports. Aggregators list countries granting visa-free access to Palestinian diplomatic passports, but no official Palestinian MFA source documenting specific bilateral visa suppression or waiver agreements with named dates was found. Not recorded per the hard rule requiring an official source.

Schengen/US/UK/GCC visa holder conditional entry rules: Palestine does not publish such rules because it does not operate an independent entry system. No aggregator or official source documents such rules for Palestine specifically.

Gaza entry: Rafah crossing (Egypt-Gaza) closes regularly with no warning and for long periods as of June 2026; Erez crossing (Gaza-Israel) closed since October 7 2023. No regular foreign-national entry system operational.
OCI / diaspora status entry rules: No evidence in any source that Palestine grants special entry status to OCI cardholders or diaspora holders. Not recorded.

UK FCDO notes British-Palestinians on the Palestinian Population Register or holding Palestinian IDs must use a Palestinian travel document to exit Gaza or the West Bank, and may only exit through Allenby (Jordan) or Rafah (Egypt) crossings. This is an exit rule for PA-registered individuals, not an inbound entry rule for ordinary foreign nationals.

agreements.notes: Seychelles and Lebanon signed a visa waiver agreement on November 12, 2024 covering all passport holders from both countries. Lebanese ordinary passport holders already entered Seychelles visa-free under the general policy; this agreement formalises mutual visa-free travel.

Seychelles and Egypt signed a Visa Waiver Agreement on April 5–6, 2025 covering ONLY diplomatic and official passport holders. Ordinary passport extension was discussed but NOT agreed at the time of signing. Egyptian ordinary passport holders continue to enter Seychelles under the general visa-free policy (not under this agreement).

Seychelles and the Kyrgyz Republic signed a Visa Waiver Agreement on May 4, 2026 during Minister Barry Faure's official visit. Passport types covered and effective date are not specified in the press release. Kyrgyz ordinary passport holders already entered Seychelles visa-free under the general policy.

Seychelles and the Maldives signed and implemented a mutual visa waiver agreement effective May 15, 2026, during Minister Barry Faure's official visit to the Maldives. Citizens of both countries can visit each other visa-free for up to 30 days. A short-stay visa waiver agreement was originally concluded in June 2023 that laid the foundation for the current implementation. Maldivian ordinary passport holders already entered Seychelles under the general universal visa-free policy; this agreement formalises mutual reciprocal access. Passport types not specified in available sources (likely all ordinary passports).

Seychelles and Angola signed an Agreement on Mutual Visa Exemption on August 18, 2025 at the Ivato Conference Center in Antananarivo, Madagascar. Covers ONLY diplomatic, official, and service passports - NOT ordinary passports. Signed by Angola's Minister of Foreign Affairs Téte António and Seychelles Prime Minister and Minister of Fisheries and Economy Jean-François Ferrari. Angolan ordinary passport holders continue to enter Seychelles under the general universal visa-free policy (not under this agreement). No official Seychelles MFA press release confirmed; source is Africa-Press reporting.

Kyrgyz Republic visa waiver (May 2026): passport types covered not specified in press release; full agreement text not available on official domain.

The UK's ETA full country list was confirmed as exactly 83 nationality entries from the Appendix ETA National List (Immigration Rules): Phase 1 (1) + Phase 2 (5) + Phase 3 (43) + Phase 4 (34) = 83. This count was re-verified against the live Appendix ETA National List on 2026-06-29.

Indian nationals (including OCI holders) on ordinary passports are on the Visa National List and require a UK visitor visa.

TWOV rules apply to transit only (arrival and departure by air, max stay 23:59 next day, no public funds/work/study). They are NOT general entry rules. Electronic/printed e-visa copies are explicitly excluded - physical visas/PR cards only.
Syria-US visa exclusion: Syrian nationals holding a B1 or B2 category US visa are specifically excluded from TWOV 3(a) and (b) per TWOV 4.

Diplomatic passport waivers in conditional_access reflect footnotes in the April 2026 UK Visa Requirements for Carriers document. Exact bilateral agreement dates are not published in UK immigration rules for these specific exemptions.

countries.name: United States
agreements: Compact of Free Association (with Federated States of Micronesia, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and Republic of Palau - visa-free travel, work, and study rights with unlimited stay)
gaps: EB-5 processing time in months/years: USCIS updates processing times monthly at egov.uscis.gov/processing-times; no static figure available from official sources as times vary by country of birth and visa availability. Not recorded to avoid inventing data.

E-2 Treaty Investor minimum investment amount: US law does not specify a fixed dollar minimum; the requirement is a 'substantial amount of capital' proportional to the enterprise cost. No official fixed amount to record.
Complete list of E-2 treaty countries: Available at travel.state.gov but not confirmed live in this session.
Exact ESTA application fee: Fee information is on esta.cbp.dhs.gov but the page was not fully readable in this session.
US does not have a formal 'digital nomad visa' program as of June 2026. No official program to record.

Bermuda ISO3: The British Overseas Territory of Bermuda does not have its own ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code separate from GBR in standard lists (BMU is the two-letter UN/IOC code). Set to null pending schema clarification.

Conditional access - credential-based (third-country visa/permit): Confirmed absent from US law. The US does NOT grant visa-free, visa-on-arrival, e-visa, or ETA entry based on holding a valid visa or residence permit from any third country. No such rule exists in official US immigration law.

Conditional access - special status (OCI/diaspora): No official US government source confirms any entry benefit for Indian OCI cardholders or similar diaspora/heritage-status holders entering the United States.

Conditional access - other diplomatic/service passport waivers: 22 CFR 41.2 contains only one nationality-specific diplomatic/official passport waiver (Mexico). No other bilateral 'visa suppression' agreements for diplomatic/service/official passports were found for any other country in official US sources.

22 CFR 41.2(g): Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (TTPI) - historical exemption for TTPI natives. The TTPI dissolved in 1994 when Palau gained independence, and the three successor states (FSM, RMI, Palau) are now covered by Compacts of Free Association. This CFR section may be a historical artifact; not recorded as active policy.

22 CFR 41.2(c)/(d)/(e): Bahamas, Cayman Islands, Turks and Caicos, British Virgin Islands nationals have limited visa waivers under specific conditions (direct travel restrictions, criminal record certificates, etc.). These are niche rules with complex conditions not fully verified in this session; not recorded to avoid partial data errors.

Ordinary passport holders; unilateral visa exemption valid until December 31, 2026

Visa-free entry for tourism with mandatory Tourist Card (US$10, included in airfare for air travelers since April 2018). Officially listed among countries authorized to enter with a Tourist Card (no prior visa) for tourism by the DR Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MIREX) under Ley 875 sobre Visados. Stay up to 30 days. (verified 2026-07)

Falls under FSM's general visa-free regime: nationals of all countries may enter with a valid passport, sufficient funds, and proof of onward travel for stays up to 30 days (extendable via entry permit). Confirmed by the FSM Embassy 'For Guests & Visitors' page: 'Valid passport, sufficient funds and proof of onward travel are sufficient to grant entry for 30 days.' Cross-checked against Wikipedia 'Visa policy of Micronesia'. (verified 2026-07)
Citizens may enter and stay in Georgia without visa for one full year.

Category A (Exento de visa): nationals of Kuwait enter Guatemala visa-free on a valid passport for up to 90 days (extendable once to a maximum of 180 days). Listed on the official Instituto Guatemalteco de Migracion (IGM) Categoria A list published at igm.gob.gt/clasificacion-de-paises/ (Categoria-a-actualizada-2023.jpg). (verified 2026-07)

Haiti applies a default visa-free policy: every nationality enters for up to 90 days except the nine countries in the visa_required list (Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam, Yemen). A tourist fee of USD 10 is collected on arrival; passports must remain current for at least six months. The build expands this negation entry against visa_required.nationalities_iso3, so it excludes only Haiti and those nine. Source: https://www.haiti.org/tourist-visa/ (verified 2026-07)
Visa waiver effective 4 February 2024. Tourism only, non-extendable, once every 6 months. Ordinary passport holders.
GCC member. Visa-free for 3 months within any 6-month period per bilateral agreement.
Visa-free for ordinary passport holders; up to 30 days

Unilateral visa-free regime by Kyrgyz Republic. Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 855 (31 Dec 2025): GCC nationals receive 180 days within any 360-day period (upgraded from prior 60/90-day rules). Diplomatic/service passports have separate bilateral arrangement.
Listed on the St. Kitts & Nevis High Commission London visa-free list.
GCC nationals: 6-month entry stamp at airport/border, extendable to 1 year at no cost.
No visa required
On exemption list. Not in any extended stay category; general 30-day rule applies.
No stay duration specified on official list
No visa required

Visa-free for social/tourist visits up to 90 days. GCC national; not on Malaysia's official visa-required list (imi.gov.my operates a negative list - absent nationalities are visa-exempt for social visits). Corroborated by Timatic. (verified 2026-07)
Visa-free under Disposición N° 002-2026, effective February 16, 2026.
GCC citizens enjoy freedom of movement and right of residence in Oman without a visa, including movement by national ID card.

All Kuwaiti nationals (ordinary passport holders) may enter Pakistan without a visa for up to 90 days for business and tourism purposes, with multiple exit/re-entry permitted. Policy announced by Prime Minister of Pakistan in late July 2024, effective 23 August 2024. Confirmed by Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs press release (Embassy of Pakistan in Kuwait) and EY Tax Alert (29 August 2024). No prior visa application required - air ticket sufficient.
Visa-free up to 3 months under Resolution 22706.
Visa-free under Executive Order No. 408. Initial 30-day stay; extendable.
GCC member - visa-free entry with passport or national ID. No stay limit published for GCC citizens.

Citizens of all GCC member states enjoy visa-free entry to Saudi Arabia using their passports under GCC freedom-of-movement agreements. Saudi Arabia is in the process of permitting movement by national ID card.
Indefinite stay permitted

Singapore's ICA publishes a list of countries/territories whose nationals REQUIRE a visa; all other passport holders are visa-exempt. The ICA page states that holders of passports/travel documents NOT from visa-required countries do not need a visa. Stay duration (14, 30, or 90 days) is determined by the Visit Pass issued at the checkpoint. Visa-required countries as of June 2026: Afghanistan, Algeria, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Egypt, Georgia, India, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Yemen. Additionally, holders of refugee travel documents, alien's passports, Palestinian Authority passports, UAE temporary passports, Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permits, and PRC Travel Documents require visas.

Visitors with a valid passport (6 months validity), return/onward ticket, and sufficient funds receive a visitor's permit on arrival for up to 3 months in any 12-month period (Immigration Act). The specific Tourist Visa product on the immigration.gov.sb/visitor-visa-tourist/ page describes an initial 30-day on-arrival grant with extension to 150 days available. Countries requiring PRIOR APPROVAL from the Director of Immigration before arrival are listed in visa_policy.notes.

Category A (exento de visa) for ordinary passport holders per El Salvador's official DGME classification 'Clasificacion para Fines de Exencion y Obligatoriedad de Visas de El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras y Nicaragua' (listed '(A) EXENTO DE VISA'); visa-exempt for up to 180 days (corroborated by the Wikipedia visa-policy table). Source: https://www.migracion.gob.sv/servicios/listado-visa/ (verified 2026-07).
Up to 15 days visa-free; extension possible up to 90 days subject to immigration requirements.
No visa required.

Seychelles grants visa-free entry to all ordinary passport holders except Kosovo. A Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival for up to 3 months (90 days), free of charge; extendable in 3-month increments up to 12 months total (SCR 5,000 per additional 3-month period). Visitors must demonstrate minimum funds of US$150 or equivalent per day, hold a valid return/onward ticket, and have confirmed accommodation. IMPORTANT: Although no visa is required, ALL travellers must obtain a paid Electronic Travel Authorisation (TA/ETA) prior to departure via seychelles.govtas.com or the Seychelles e-Border app. Standard processing (24 hours): EUR 10; Premium processing (6 hours): EUR 30. Failure to obtain the TA before travel may result in a penalty fee on arrival. Kosovo passport holders are explicitly refused entry as Seychelles does not recognise the State of Kosovo.
Visa exemption for tourism and short-term business, effective 15 July 2024. Upcoming change: Will reduce to 30 days once Royal Gazette publishes Cabinet decision of 19 May 2026.
Ordinary passport.
90 days within 180-day period, ordinary passport
Visa-free entry for tourism, private and business purposes up to 90 days, established by Presidential Decree No. 289/2020 dated 21 July 2020, effective 1 August 2020.

Reverted to 10-day visa-free per official MFA visa page, which lists Kuwait under 'Up to 10 days' (entry 88) and states: 'Citizens of Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and China are granted a visa-free regime for a period of 10 days, provided they have a flight ticket to their home country or a third country.' The 30-day claim was sourced only to the kursiv.media aggregator and is contradicted by the official source; reverted on 2026-06-27 re-verification.

Vatican City has no border controls with Italy per the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. The five entrances into Vatican City State are manned by the Pontifical Swiss Guard and Gendarmerie Corps but entry formalities for foreign visitors are governed by Italy/Schengen rules, not a separate Vatican visa. The governing legislation per the official informazione_generale page is Law N. III of 7 June 1929 on citizenship and residence and Regulation N. XXXVI of 27 September 1932. Vatican authorities have not published a nationality-specific visa-free list. In practice, no separate Vatican visa is required; visitors who can lawfully enter Italy under Schengen rules can enter Vatican City. Note: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is expected in late 2026; nationals of approximately 59 currently visa-exempt countries (including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea) will require ETIAS authorisation before entering Italy/Schengen and by extension Vatican City. Vatican City citizens and European microstate nationals (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino) are explicitly ETIAS-exempt. ETIAS is a travel authorisation, not a visa, and does not change Vatican City's underlying policy of having no separate national visa system.
Visa-exempt; Middle East nation.
90 days within 6-month period
Free entry

Visa on arrival (Visa d’entrée aéroport) is confirmed available at Bujumbura Melchior Ndadaye International Airport via the official migration.gov.bi portal (step1/8). Fee: $70 USD single entry, valid 1 month. The Burundi Embassy Washington DC (official) also confirms visa on arrival at the airport ($90 multiple entry up to 30 days, $70 single entry, $40 transit). Applicants must complete an online pre-registration form via migration.gov.bi prior to boarding. Note: The Paris Embassy website only describes advance applications; the migration portal and US Embassy both confirm VOA is operational.
Visa on Arrival available for tourism, business, investment, or government job purposes. Fee: USD 50 paid in cash. Single entry. Issuance at discretion of immigration officer.

Comoros law (Loi n°88-025, Art. 2) requires all foreign nationals to hold a valid passport and a Comorian visa. Visas are available on arrival at the airport or port. Tourist visa: up to 45 days; short-stay visa: up to 3 months; transit visa: up to 5 days. Fee discrepancy: UN Mission page (official) lists 60 EUR for 45 days; IATA Timatic/Wikipedia states 30 EUR; US State Department (travel.state.gov) notes 'between 30–50 Euros'. The 30–50 EUR range is more consistent with aggregator sources; 60 EUR is retained from the UN Mission page as the official Comoros government citation pending clarification.

Visitors of any nationality may obtain a tourist visa on arrival at Djibouti (Ambouli International Airport and other border crossings). Fee is USD 23, paid in cash. The US State Department country information page confirms visa on arrival is available at a $23 fee. The French MFA (diplomatie.gouv.fr, updated June 2026) confirms VOA is possible for one month ('pour un mois'). The UK FCDO (June 2026) also confirms tourists can purchase a visa on arrival in cash USD. No official Djiboutian government source publishes a nationality exclusion list. Max stay: French MFA states 1 month for VOA; exact figure not confirmed on official Djiboutian government domain but the French MFA's June 2026 update provides the most recent official-government confirmation of 30 days.
Tourist Visa on Arrival.

GID entry requirements page states: 'Visa can be acquired from all Gambian Embassies and some Consulates abroad as well as Visa upon arrival at the border.' gambia.gov.gm states: 'Where there is no Gambian diplomatic representative, participants shall have the privilege to obtain entry visa at the Banjul International Airport upon arrival.' Short visit visa valid up to 90 days. Note: countries that require both visa AND clearance must also have pre-approved entry clearance valid for 30 days before arrival.

All non-exempt nationals may obtain a single-entry short-stay visa on arrival at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport. Requires a letter of authorisation from the Migration Office of Guinea-Bissau obtained in advance. Short-stay single-entry visa: 30 days (fee EUR 61.45 + EUR 2.50 processing per rgb-visa.com/Fees.html). Longer-duration and multiple-entry visas (3 months, 6 months, 1 year) are also available through the e-visa/pre-enrollment system (rgb-visa.com) or at a Guinea-Bissau embassy. US State Dept confirms: 'A visa is required. You can get it on arrival.'
Visa on Arrival (VoA). Cost IDR 500,000.

Visa on arrival available at international airports/ports for all nationalities except Burundian and Palestinian citizens, for stays up to 90 days. The February 2026 fee increase (15-day tier tripled from €10 to €30) was confirmed to apply exclusively to the eVisa system; VoA fees at airports/embassies/consulates were not confirmed to have changed as of June 2026. Pre-increase VoA fee tiers per the eVisa portal (may still apply on arrival): 1–15 days = €10/US$10; 16–30 days = €35/US$41; 31–60 days = €40/US$47; 61–90 days = €50/US$59. Diplomats and employees of certain international organizations are exempt from visa fees. Visa can be extended to a maximum total stay of 90 days while in Madagascar.

Tourist visa granted on arrival free of charge to all nationalities. No pre-approval required. Effective 15 April 2025, entry is not granted on Israeli passports (Third Amendment to Immigration Act 1/2007, ratified by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu on 15 April 2025). Entry requirements: passport with MRZ and minimum 1 month validity, confirmed return ticket within 30 days of arrival, prepaid accommodation at a registered facility or proof of sufficient funds (minimum USD 100 plus USD 50/day), completed IMUGA Traveller Declaration (within 96 hours before arrival). Yellow Fever vaccination certificate required if coming from endemic countries (children under 1 year exempt). Entry at port of entry subject to admissibility determination by Immigration officers (Immigration Act ss. 7 & 8). Max stay of 30 days confirmed by Maldives High Commission London official page (re-verified 2026-06-29). Extendable up to 60 additional days (total 90 days) in-country by applying to Maldives Immigration before expiry. Extension process was streamlined by Maldives Immigration effective April 23, 2026 under the Maldives 2.0 Initiative.
90 days from date of arrival. Fee waived. Diplomatic Relations/Pacific Island Forum Members category.

Citizens of most countries are eligible for visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (Kathmandu), Pokhara International Airport, and Gautam Buddha International Airport (Bhairahawa/Lumbini), as well as other designated land border entry points. Options: 15 days (US$30), 30 days (US$50), 90 days (US$125). Multiple-entry. Maximum stay per calendar year is 150 days. Nationals of the following countries are NOT eligible for visa on arrival and must obtain a visa from a Nepalese diplomatic mission in advance: Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe, Eswatini (Swaziland), Cameroon, Somalia, Liberia, Ethiopia, Iraq, Palestine, Afghanistan, Syria, and Iran (added March 13, 2026 per Ministry of Home Affairs decision). Refugees holding travel documents are also excluded. Official/diplomatic passport holders of restricted-country nationals retain access.

Tourist or Business Visa on arrival available for nationalities not otherwise exempt or excluded. Valid 30 days, extendable for two additional 30-day periods at $50 USD each. Processing completed at port of entry. Exceptions: (1) Bangladesh and Myanmar nationals must obtain an advance visa before travel - they are NOT eligible for visa-on-arrival. (2) Nationals of the 12 pre-clearance countries (Bangladesh, Cambodia, Cameroon, Ghana, Haiti, Iran, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Sri Lanka, Vanuatu) must obtain written pre-clearance at least 5 days before travel per Executive Order No. 499 (issued 11 February 2026, effective 30 March 2026). All visitors must hold a valid passport (min. 6 months validity), return ticket, proof of sufficient funds, and sign the Palau Pledge. $100 USD Palau Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee (PPEF) applies to all visitors (effective 1 January 2018); exempt: Palauan citizens, diplomats on duty, crew on duty, transit passengers.

From 1 January 2018, nationals of all countries can obtain a visa on arrival at Kigali International Airport and all land borders without prior application. Fee: USD 50 for single entry (30 days). Multiple entry: USD 70 (90 days). Applicants also have the option to apply online via irembo.gov.rw before departure.
Category B - visa on arrival at Dakar Blaise Diagne International Airport only; free of charge

All GCC nationals receive landing visa per NTB official policy effective 5 September 2019. Fee: Le800,000 single / Le1,200,000 multiple (non-AU, per SLID March 2023). Duration: 30 days; extendable once in-country.

GCC member state nationals are eligible for visa on arrival. syriascopetravel.com (2026) lists UAE at $100 fee per 15-day entry, confirming GCC is not fee-exempt. Wikipedia also lists GCC as VOA. Duration not specified beyond the 15-day sample. Fees for individual GCC members other than UAE not confirmed.

Visa on arrival available at Dili International Airport and Dili Sea Port only. Fee: USD $30 cash (single entry). Transit visa: USD $20 for stays under 3 days. Extendable in-country: USD $35 for up to 30 additional days or USD $75 for 30-60 additional days (per customs.gov.tl; migracao.gov.tl states $40 for extension - discrepancy between official pages). Maximum cumulative stay 90 days. Travelers must show: sufficient funds (USD $100 per entry + USD $50 per day of stay), valid passport 6+ months with at least one blank page, return/onward ticket, accommodation proof. Land border arrivals (except Indonesians, Portuguese, and US nationals) must obtain advance Visa Application Authorization.

Citizens of countries not listed in Schedule 1 receive a visitor permit on arrival upon payment of a fee of $100 (AUD), unless waived by the Minister. Permit is valid for up to 30 days, extendable for a further 30 days. Per Regulation 2(1)(b) of the Immigration Regulations 2014 (2022 Revised Edition). Ireland falls in this category as it is explicitly excluded from the EU-Tuvalu visa waiver agreement.

Visa obtainable on arrival at official entry points or in advance via e-visa at visa.immigration.go.tz. VoA confirmed available as of June 2026 per Tanzania Immigration Department guidelines (visa.immigration.go.tz/guidelines) and US State Dept (updated Oct 2025).

All foreign passport holders (except US Nationals of American Samoa) are issued a gratis 90-day Visitor's Permit upon arrival in Samoa. Requirements: passport valid for at least 6 months after intended departure date, return or onward ticket, valid visa/permit for onward destination, documented accommodation, evidence of sufficient funds, no deportation history, no health problems posing a risk to Samoa, no criminal convictions with sentences of 1 year or more, and not appearing on any alert/warning list. Extensions beyond 90 days must be applied for at the Immigration Office in Apia before the permit expires. Note: The MFAT Entry Requirements PDF (binary-unreadable, last updated July 2021) references '60 days' as a 'no permit required' threshold; the operative permit-on-arrival duration of 90 days is confirmed by the MPMC immigration authority (mpmc.gov.ws) and the Samoa High Commission (samoa.org.nz/visa-passport/).
Category B - visa obtainable at port of entry (visa on arrival); can also apply via e-visa portal online. Single-entry 30-day visa costs USD 30 at port of entry.
ETA required (£20). Allows visit up to 6 months.

ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) will be mandatory for all visa-exempt third-country nationals entering Schengen area including Hungary. Confirmed for Q4 2026 launch, with a 6-month transitional period (travellers meeting all other entry conditions will not be refused entry solely for lacking ETIAS during transition, extending into approximately April 2027). ETIAS is valid for 3 years or until passport expires. Fee applies. As of June 2026, ETIAS is not yet operational.

ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) will be required for visa-exempt third-country nationals once operational.
