Thailand e-Visa system (thaievisa.go.th) launched globally on 1 January 2025 across 94 Royal Thai Embassies and Consulates-General. Applies to nationalities not entitled to visa exemption. Specific visa types and stay durations depend on visa category applied for.

Trinidad and Tobago operates a fully electronic visa system. All entry visas are electronic (no physical endorsement in passport). Approved visas are sent via email. Multiple-entry e-Visa fee is 800 TTD. Nationalities not on the visa-exempt list may apply for e-visa through the official portal at nationalsecurity.gov.tt. Possession of an e-Visa does not guarantee entry.

As of April 2026, Venezuela operates a mandatory electronic visa (e-visa) system for all nationalities that require a visa to enter Venezuela. Applications submitted online at cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve. Visas delivered electronically by email. Tourist (TR-V) and Business (TR-N) visa categories available. Processing time approximately 15 days (reduced from approximately 6 weeks). Visa validity 1 year, multiple entry. Fee amount unconfirmed from official Venezuelan sources; aggregators report USD 180. MPPRE published a user manual in February 2026 confirming the system is operational for North America tourist visa applications.

As of August 2023, Vietnam e-visa is open to all countries and territories. Single-entry USD 25, multiple-entry USD 50 (fees confirmed unchanged as of Circular 28/2026/TT-BTC effective April 1, 2026). Valid 90 days from grant date, single or multiple entry. Processing 3 working days. Valid at 13 international airports, 16 land borders, 13 sea ports. Apply at evisa.gov.vn (main portal as of Nov 2024) or evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn.
Category C - must apply and obtain a visa before travelling to Zimbabwe. E-visa available online at evisa.gov.zw.

COD.notes: Citizens of East African Community (EAC) Partner States receive a free EAC access visa valid 1 to 6 months under Article 7(1) of the EAC Common Market Protocol. The MAE (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) free-visa page confirms: documents required are passport/travel document photocopy, access stamp photocopy, and passport photo; price is free; validity is 1 to 6 months. EAC also offers a free EAC study visa for students (1 year). Burundi is itself an EAC member. Somalia joined the EAC on March 4, 2024 and is now a full EAC Partner State; as of the EAC official page, all Partner States implement Article 7(1) visa-free entry.
Visa waiver agreement established on July 28, 2022 on all categories of passports

Haiti applies a default visa-free policy: every nationality enters for up to 90 days except the nine countries in the visa_required list (Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam, Yemen). A tourist fee of USD 10 is collected on arrival; passports must remain current for at least six months. The build expands this negation entry against visa_required.nationalities_iso3, so it excludes only Haiti and those nine. Source: https://www.haiti.org/tourist-visa/ (verified 2026-07)
EAC Partner State; exempt from eTA per Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025
No visa required
Visa-free under Executive Order No. 408. Initial 30-day stay; extendable.

Citizens of EAC Partner States are issued a Visitor's Pass (VP-1) free of charge upon arrival, valid for up to six months. Citizens of Uganda and Kenya may enter using their national ID card. No permit fees apply for EAC citizens. This is a genuine entry pass - not a visa on arrival - consistent with EAC free-movement obligations.

Singapore's ICA publishes a list of countries/territories whose nationals REQUIRE a visa; all other passport holders are visa-exempt. The ICA page states that holders of passports/travel documents NOT from visa-required countries do not need a visa. Stay duration (14, 30, or 90 days) is determined by the Visit Pass issued at the checkpoint. Visa-required countries as of June 2026: Afghanistan, Algeria, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Egypt, Georgia, India, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Yemen. Additionally, holders of refugee travel documents, alien's passports, Palestinian Authority passports, UAE temporary passports, Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permits, and PRC Travel Documents require visas.

Seychelles grants visa-free entry to all ordinary passport holders except Kosovo. A Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival for up to 3 months (90 days), free of charge; extendable in 3-month increments up to 12 months total (SCR 5,000 per additional 3-month period). Visitors must demonstrate minimum funds of US$150 or equivalent per day, hold a valid return/onward ticket, and have confirmed accommodation. IMPORTANT: Although no visa is required, ALL travellers must obtain a paid Electronic Travel Authorisation (TA/ETA) prior to departure via seychelles.govtas.com or the Seychelles e-Border app. Standard processing (24 hours): EUR 10; Premium processing (6 hours): EUR 30. Failure to obtain the TA before travel may result in a penalty fee on arrival. Kosovo passport holders are explicitly refused entry as Seychelles does not recognise the State of Kosovo.

Visa-free for up to 30 days for nationals of African Union member states under Togo's visa-exemption decree adopted by the Council of Ministers on 26 May 2026 (effective 18 May 2026), which exempts nationals of all African states from an entry visa for stays of up to 30 days. An online travel declaration at voyage.gouv.tg must be completed at least 24 hours before arrival and the resulting travel slip presented at border checkpoints; ECOWAS members instead retain their 90-day visa-free privilege. Confirmed by the official Togolese Embassy (Bern, Switzerland) notice and the 26 May 2026 Council of Ministers communiqué. (verified 2026-07)
Citizens of EAC member states are not required to apply for a visa to enter Tanzania. EAC members listed on official immigration site.
Visa abolition agreement. No visa required. Max stay 90 days per March 2026 Ministry of Internal Affairs announcement.

Vatican City has no border controls with Italy per the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. The five entrances into Vatican City State are manned by the Pontifical Swiss Guard and Gendarmerie Corps but entry formalities for foreign visitors are governed by Italy/Schengen rules, not a separate Vatican visa. The governing legislation per the official informazione_generale page is Law N. III of 7 June 1929 on citizenship and residence and Regulation N. XXXVI of 27 September 1932. Vatican authorities have not published a nationality-specific visa-free list. In practice, no separate Vatican visa is required; visitors who can lawfully enter Italy under Schengen rules can enter Vatican City. Note: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is expected in late 2026; nationals of approximately 59 currently visa-exempt countries (including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea) will require ETIAS authorisation before entering Italy/Schengen and by extension Vatican City. Vatican City citizens and European microstate nationals (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino) are explicitly ETIAS-exempt. ETIAS is a travel authorisation, not a visa, and does not change Vatican City's underlying policy of having no separate national visa system.
Category A - no visa required. Listed on official Zimbabwe eVisa portal FAQ page under 'Entry without Visa'.
Visa on arrival eligible. Conditions apply.

Comoros law (Loi n°88-025, Art. 2) requires all foreign nationals to hold a valid passport and a Comorian visa. Visas are available on arrival at the airport or port. Tourist visa: up to 45 days; short-stay visa: up to 3 months; transit visa: up to 5 days. Fee discrepancy: UN Mission page (official) lists 60 EUR for 45 days; IATA Timatic/Wikipedia states 30 EUR; US State Department (travel.state.gov) notes 'between 30–50 Euros'. The 30–50 EUR range is more consistent with aggregator sources; 60 EUR is retained from the UN Mission page as the official Comoros government citation pending clarification.

Visitors of any nationality may obtain a tourist visa on arrival at Djibouti (Ambouli International Airport and other border crossings). Fee is USD 23, paid in cash. The US State Department country information page confirms visa on arrival is available at a $23 fee. The French MFA (diplomatie.gouv.fr, updated June 2026) confirms VOA is possible for one month ('pour un mois'). The UK FCDO (June 2026) also confirms tourists can purchase a visa on arrival in cash USD. No official Djiboutian government source publishes a nationality exclusion list. Max stay: French MFA states 1 month for VOA; exact figure not confirmed on official Djiboutian government domain but the French MFA's June 2026 update provides the most recent official-government confirmation of 30 days.
Tourist Visa on Arrival.

GID entry requirements page states: 'Visa can be acquired from all Gambian Embassies and some Consulates abroad as well as Visa upon arrival at the border.' gambia.gov.gm states: 'Where there is no Gambian diplomatic representative, participants shall have the privilege to obtain entry visa at the Banjul International Airport upon arrival.' Short visit visa valid up to 90 days. Note: countries that require both visa AND clearance must also have pre-approved entry clearance valid for 30 days before arrival.

All non-exempt nationals may obtain a single-entry short-stay visa on arrival at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport. Requires a letter of authorisation from the Migration Office of Guinea-Bissau obtained in advance. Short-stay single-entry visa: 30 days (fee EUR 61.45 + EUR 2.50 processing per rgb-visa.com/Fees.html). Longer-duration and multiple-entry visas (3 months, 6 months, 1 year) are also available through the e-visa/pre-enrollment system (rgb-visa.com) or at a Guinea-Bissau embassy. US State Dept confirms: 'A visa is required. You can get it on arrival.'

Nationals not on the 88-country visa-free exemption list (and not from Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Vietnam) may apply for an 'Entry Permit' (Authorization to Enter and Stay, aka visa-upon-arrival) at any border checkpoint Visa Room upon arrival. Fee: MOP200 single / MOP300 multiple for individuals; MOP400/MOP600 for family passports; MOP100/MOP150 for children under 12; MOP100/MOP150 for groups of 10+ with collective travel document. Officials of diplomatic missions of Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Vietnam holding diplomatic/consular identification may also apply for visa-upon-arrival.

Visa on arrival available at international airports/ports for all nationalities except Burundian and Palestinian citizens, for stays up to 90 days. The February 2026 fee increase (15-day tier tripled from €10 to €30) was confirmed to apply exclusively to the eVisa system; VoA fees at airports/embassies/consulates were not confirmed to have changed as of June 2026. Pre-increase VoA fee tiers per the eVisa portal (may still apply on arrival): 1–15 days = €10/US$10; 16–30 days = €35/US$41; 31–60 days = €40/US$47; 61–90 days = €50/US$59. Diplomats and employees of certain international organizations are exempt from visa fees. Visa can be extended to a maximum total stay of 90 days while in Madagascar.

Tourist visa granted on arrival free of charge to all nationalities. No pre-approval required. Effective 15 April 2025, entry is not granted on Israeli passports (Third Amendment to Immigration Act 1/2007, ratified by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu on 15 April 2025). Entry requirements: passport with MRZ and minimum 1 month validity, confirmed return ticket within 30 days of arrival, prepaid accommodation at a registered facility or proof of sufficient funds (minimum USD 100 plus USD 50/day), completed IMUGA Traveller Declaration (within 96 hours before arrival). Yellow Fever vaccination certificate required if coming from endemic countries (children under 1 year exempt). Entry at port of entry subject to admissibility determination by Immigration officers (Immigration Act ss. 7 & 8). Max stay of 30 days confirmed by Maldives High Commission London official page (re-verified 2026-06-29). Extendable up to 60 additional days (total 90 days) in-country by applying to Maldives Immigration before expiry. Extension process was streamlined by Maldives Immigration effective April 23, 2026 under the Maldives 2.0 Initiative.

Citizens of most countries are eligible for visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (Kathmandu), Pokhara International Airport, and Gautam Buddha International Airport (Bhairahawa/Lumbini), as well as other designated land border entry points. Options: 15 days (US$30), 30 days (US$50), 90 days (US$125). Multiple-entry. Maximum stay per calendar year is 150 days. Nationals of the following countries are NOT eligible for visa on arrival and must obtain a visa from a Nepalese diplomatic mission in advance: Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe, Eswatini (Swaziland), Cameroon, Somalia, Liberia, Ethiopia, Iraq, Palestine, Afghanistan, Syria, and Iran (added March 13, 2026 per Ministry of Home Affairs decision). Refugees holding travel documents are also excluded. Official/diplomatic passport holders of restricted-country nationals retain access.

Tourist or Business Visa on arrival available for nationalities not otherwise exempt or excluded. Valid 30 days, extendable for two additional 30-day periods at $50 USD each. Processing completed at port of entry. Exceptions: (1) Bangladesh and Myanmar nationals must obtain an advance visa before travel - they are NOT eligible for visa-on-arrival. (2) Nationals of the 12 pre-clearance countries (Bangladesh, Cambodia, Cameroon, Ghana, Haiti, Iran, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Sri Lanka, Vanuatu) must obtain written pre-clearance at least 5 days before travel per Executive Order No. 499 (issued 11 February 2026, effective 30 March 2026). All visitors must hold a valid passport (min. 6 months validity), return ticket, proof of sufficient funds, and sign the Palau Pledge. $100 USD Palau Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee (PPEF) applies to all visitors (effective 1 January 2018); exempt: Palauan citizens, diplomats on duty, crew on duty, transit passengers.
Category B - ordinary passport; visa on arrival at Dakar Blaise Diagne International Airport only; free of charge. Embassy page also lists DRC in Category A, likely for diplomatic passports.

2026-07: EXCLUDED the documented 'restricted nationalities' (including Pakistan) from this visa-on-arrival catch-all. These nationalities do NOT get a genuine visa on arrival: at airports all travelers need prior visa approval before boarding, and at land borders these restricted nationalities specifically require advance approval (3 days to 1 month processing) - i.e. an advance-approval / pre-arranged visa, not a true VOA. Pakistani (PAK) ordinary passport holders are therefore not eligible for unconditional Syria VOA and have been removed from the on-arrival expansion. (verified 2026-07). From January 2025, the Syrian transitional government allows essentially all nationalities (except Iran and Israel, and subject to pre-approval requirements for many nationalities) to obtain a visa on arrival at Damascus and Aleppo airports and at land borders with Lebanon and Jordan. Fees vary by nationality. At AIRPORTS: all travelers require prior visa approval before boarding regardless of nationality. At LAND BORDERS: most nationalities can obtain VOA directly; restricted nationalities require advance approval (3 days to 1 month processing). Restricted nationalities (not exhaustive): India, China, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Nepal, Egypt, Sudan, Libya, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Russia, Yemen, Iraq, Belarus, South Africa, South Korea, and others. Sample fees (single-entry, per syriascopetravel.com 2026): EU/Schengen ~$75; UK $150; Canada $100; Australia/NZ $150; USA $200; Russia ~$50; Turkey ~$50. Visa issued as stamp on separate sheet rather than in passport. Israeli nationals and those with Israeli passport stamps are denied entry. Iranian nationals require an advance visa from a Syrian embassy and are not eligible for VOA. Fee of $300 for North Korea and Democratic Republic of Congo noted in syriascopetravel.com but unverified from official source.

Visa on arrival available at Dili International Airport and Dili Sea Port only. Fee: USD $30 cash (single entry). Transit visa: USD $20 for stays under 3 days. Extendable in-country: USD $35 for up to 30 additional days or USD $75 for 30-60 additional days (per customs.gov.tl; migracao.gov.tl states $40 for extension - discrepancy between official pages). Maximum cumulative stay 90 days. Travelers must show: sufficient funds (USD $100 per entry + USD $50 per day of stay), valid passport 6+ months with at least one blank page, return/onward ticket, accommodation proof. Land border arrivals (except Indonesians, Portuguese, and US nationals) must obtain advance Visa Application Authorization.

Citizens of countries not listed in Schedule 1 receive a visitor permit on arrival upon payment of a fee of $100 (AUD), unless waived by the Minister. Permit is valid for up to 30 days, extendable for a further 30 days. Per Regulation 2(1)(b) of the Immigration Regulations 2014 (2022 Revised Edition). Ireland falls in this category as it is explicitly excluded from the EU-Tuvalu visa waiver agreement.

All foreign passport holders (except US Nationals of American Samoa) are issued a gratis 90-day Visitor's Permit upon arrival in Samoa. Requirements: passport valid for at least 6 months after intended departure date, return or onward ticket, valid visa/permit for onward destination, documented accommodation, evidence of sufficient funds, no deportation history, no health problems posing a risk to Samoa, no criminal convictions with sentences of 1 year or more, and not appearing on any alert/warning list. Extensions beyond 90 days must be applied for at the Immigration Office in Apia before the permit expires. Note: The MFAT Entry Requirements PDF (binary-unreadable, last updated July 2021) references '60 days' as a 'no permit required' threshold; the operative permit-on-arrival duration of 90 days is confirmed by the MPMC immigration authority (mpmc.gov.ws) and the Samoa High Commission (samoa.org.nz/visa-passport/).
Visa on arrival at any port of entry or from selected Zambian Missions Abroad; can also apply via eServices portal

ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) will be mandatory for all visa-exempt third-country nationals entering Schengen area including Hungary. Confirmed for Q4 2026 launch, with a 6-month transitional period (travellers meeting all other entry conditions will not be refused entry solely for lacking ETIAS during transition, extending into approximately April 2027). ETIAS is valid for 3 years or until passport expires. Fee applies. As of June 2026, ETIAS is not yet operational.

ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) will be required for visa-exempt third-country nationals once operational. The Entry/Exit System (EES) became fully operational on 10 April 2026 across all Schengen countries, after a progressive rollout beginning 12 October 2025. ETIAS is scheduled to start operations in Q4 2026; no precise date confirmed as of June 2026. Applies to all Annex II nationals entering the Schengen area including Italy. The application fee is EUR 20 (updated from the originally proposed EUR 7, adjusted for inflation and additional operational costs); authorization covers multiple short stays within 3 years.

All foreign nationals not in the 40-country free ETA list must obtain paid ETA. Tourist ETA fee: USD 20 (South Asian/SAARC countries, applied/at mission) or USD 25 (SAARC, on arrival); USD 50 (all others, applied/at mission) or USD 60 (all others, on arrival). Business ETA: USD 30 (SAARC) or USD 55 (all others); no on-arrival business ETA. Transit visa is free for 48-hour stays. Children under 12 receive free tourist ETA up to 30 days from any nationality.

Latvia introduced an Electronic Travel Declaration system from 1 September 2025 (amendment to Article 4.4 of the Immigration Law). Third-country nationals who are not citizens of an EU member state, NATO member state, OECD member state, EEA country, Swiss Confederation or Brazil, AND who do not have a valid Latvian visa or residence permit, must submit the declaration at least 48 hours before arrival via eta.gov.lv. Note: ETA exemption is based on EU/NATO/OECD/EEA/Swiss/Brazil bloc membership, NOT identity with the ordinary-passport visa-free list. Turkey (NATO member) is ETA-exempt even though Turkish ordinary passport holders are NOT on the ordinary visa-free list. Exempt nationals include all visa-free countries plus Turkey. This is NOT a travel authorization/permission to enter - it is a pre-arrival security declaration. Page last updated May 19, 2026.

All visa applications processed online via the official eVisa portal at https://evisa.immigration.gov.ag/agEvisa-app/. The system allows applicants to apply online; an approval or denial letter is sent once processed. Processing time approximately 5 working days. A soft or hard copy of the eVisa should be carried. Immigration officers at ports of entry reserve the right to deny entry even to eVisa holders.

E-visa available online via evisa.bj before arrival - visa on arrival is NOT available. Options: 30-day single entry (50 EUR self-apply / 60 EUR via embassy), 30-day multiple entry (75 EUR / 85 EUR), 90-day multiple entry (100 EUR / 110 EUR). Processing approx. 24 hours.

Burkina Faso operates an official e-visa system via applicant.visaburkina.bf (Ministry of Security / Direction Générale de la Police Nationale). The eVisa authorises entry and stay for a maximum of 90 days for tourism or family purposes. On 11 September 2025, the Council of Ministers (presided over by Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ) adopted a measure waiving visa FEES (not visa requirement) for all nationals of African AU member states (all 54 African Union member states; excludes non-sovereign territories). African nationals still must apply online via the e-visa portal - this is a fee waiver only, not a visa exemption; confirmed by the Council of Ministers statement. Short-stay visa costs (for non-African applicants): Tourist visa 33,000 FCFA single / 55,000 FCFA multiple; Business visa 77,000 FCFA single / 93,500 FCFA multiple; Conference/Studies/Training/Visit visa 55,000 FCFA single / 71,500 FCFA multiple; Express visa 104,500 FCFA. IMPORTANT: US citizens are subject to a total entry and visa ban as of 1 January 2026. On 30 December 2025, Burkina Faso's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced the adoption of equivalent/reciprocal visa restrictions against US citizens, in response to the US proclamation of 16 December 2025 placing Burkina Faso under a full entry ban. US citizens are currently unable to obtain a Burkina Faso visa or enter the country.

All foreign nationals not falling under visa-free or visa-on-arrival categories must obtain an e-visa/e-permit prior to entry into Bhutan. Applications are processed through the tourist online visa/permit system at immi.gov.bt. Processing time is a maximum of two working days. Passport must have minimum 6 months validity from intended date of departure from Bhutan. Valid travel insurance is mandatory. All tourists must book through a licensed Bhutanese tour operator and pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF).

All ordinary passport holders not covered by bilateral exemption agreements must apply online through the official evisacam.cm portal (operated by MINREX). Short-stay visa up to 6 months (180 days) - normal processing 72 hours, fee XAF 100,000 / approx. EUR 152; express processing 24 hours, fee XAF 150,000 / approx. EUR 229. Long-stay visa up to 12 months (360 days) - fee XAF 150,000 normal / XAF 200,000 express per diplocam.cm. Transit visa up to 5 days (free) per diplocam.cm. NOTE: Cameroon High Commission UK (cameroonhighcommission.co.uk) cites a paid transit visa at EUR 153 for 4-30 days - this may represent a separate paid transit category; the free 5-day transit is sourced from diplocam.cm (MINREX official). Visa sticker affixed at embassy/high commission or at border entry point. Launched April 30, 2023 per Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023 implementing Law No. 97/012 of 10 January 1997.

Cabo Verde operates an online pre-arrival visa application system via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv. Tourist visa allows up to 90 days stay (extendable once for additional 90 days). All travelers (including visa-free) must also pre-register via ease.gov.cv and pay the Airport Security Fee (TSA, approximately EUR 30.83 / CVE 3,400 for international flights) prior to arrival.

E-visa available via evisa.dgdi.ga and edgdi.dgdi.ga. Single-entry 1–3 months costs 70 EUR (or 45,000 XAF) + 15 EUR processing fee. Six-month multiple-entry costs 185 EUR (or 120,000 XAF) + 15 EUR processing fee. Processing time 72 hours. Valid only for air entry via Léon Mba International Airport, Libreville. Governed by Law N°5/86 of 18 June 1986. As of December 2025, e-visa system digitised to cover all short-term categories: tourism, business, family visits. NOTE: US citizens face a reciprocal visa suspension effective January 1, 2026, announced December 18, 2025 by Gabonese Council of Ministers.
Standard e-visa category. Note: as of April 2025 amendments, if applying via visa/permit of qualifying country, requires multiple-entry visa or permit valid for at least 1 year.

The PAF portal designates all countries not in the visa-free (code 2) category as requiring an e-visa. This includes USA, Canada, and UAE - previously recorded under visa_on_arrival with PAF 'code 1' designation, but re-classified to e_visa after 2026-06-27 re-verification: (a) US State Dept confirms US citizens must 'apply online' for a visa before travel - no VOA option; (b) official paf.gov.gn states UAE nationals require an e-visa; (c) secondary sources describing US/Canada 'code 1' as an extended-validity e-visa (up to 5 years) rather than a true visa on arrival. Visa types: Tourist Visa (USD 80, max 90 days), Transit Visa (USD 50, max 3 days), Transborderment Visa (USD 150, 5-year validity), Long Term Visa/VLS (USD 150, 1 year), Diplomatic/Service/Courtesy (VDSC, fee per approval letter). Process: apply online at paf.gov.gn/visa, receive Entry Visa Letter, collect visa at border arrival counter. Processing time: ~72 hours.

E-visa launched 1 July 2023 via equatorialguinea-evisa.com (VFS Global as official technical partner of the Government of Equatorial Guinea). Confirmed operational by official Government Press of Equatorial Guinea (guineaecuatorialpress.com). Available for Tourist, Business, Emergency Humanitarian, and Congresses/Meetings/Seminars categories under Decree No. 49/2019 of December 2, 2019. Fee: EUR 105 for stays under 90 days (Spanish MFA June 2026 re-confirmation). Processing: 72 hours after payment (UK FCDO June 2026 re-confirmation). E-visa approval letter must be printed and presented on arrival. Entry via Malabo International Airport. The Embassy of Equatorial Guinea in Washington DC separately lists an embassy-based visa at USD 200 standard / USD 300 for 90–180 day stays; cash no longer accepted as of 7 February 2025 (online or money order only). The embassy notes the EG Visa Online system is completely separate and independent from embassy services.

Since 2017, citizens of ALL countries and territories may apply for a Kyrgyzstan e-visa online via the official e-visa portal (evisa.e-gov.kg). Visa types include: Tourist (TS, up to 30 days), Business (B, up to 90 days), Investment (I, 5–10 years), Digital Nomad (DN, up to 1 year), Student (S, up to 90 days), Transit (TR, 3 days), Relatives (RL, up to 90 days), Driver (T, up to 6 months), Special Work SW1/SW2 (up to 60 days extendable to 1 year), Sapar (J, up to 1 year), Ethnic Kyrgyz 'Meken' (M, up to 1 year), and others. Fee depends on category; applications typically processed within 5 working days.

Visitors requiring a visa may apply online through the official e-visa portal. Fee: US$100 for visitor visa; US$150 for student visa. Processing time approximately two weeks. Visa is emailed upon approval. Dominican Republic nationals explicitly require a visa. Stays under 24 hours from countries normally requiring visas do not require a visa. Official e-visa portal: evisa.stkittsnevisonline.com (note: evisa.gov.kn redirects to this address). The Embassy DC FAQ also references www.evisa.gov.kn as the entry point.
E-visa available online via evisa.gov.ly (can_apply_online: true, exemption_type: NONE). Tourist e-visa: 30-day stay, 90-day validity, single entry, fee USD 63.

Visa applications and payments are processed fully online via the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs website. An entry permit is issued electronically once approved. There is no need to send documents to a Malian Embassy. Confirmed by the UK FCDO travel advice page (updated June 2026) which references the portal at diplomatiemmc.gouv.ml/vitrine/. The Mali Embassy in Washington DC also links to this portal for all visa applications. The MFA portal (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml/vitrine/) was re-checked in June 2026 - it presents an interactive nationality checker ('Ai-je besoin d'un visa pour voyager au Mali?') with ordinary, diplomatic, special, refugee, and UN laissez-passer passport types. Note: the portal URL appearing in official sources varies slightly between 'diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml' and 'diplomatiemmc.gouv.ml'.
E-visa eligible; K2 (30 days), K4 (30 days), K6 (transit, 10 days)

From 5 January 2025, Mauritania replaced visa-on-arrival with an e-visa system. All visa-required nationalities must apply online before travel at anrpts.gov.mr. Available durations: 30, 90, 360, or 720 days. Fees for 30-day visa: Arab and African nationals - approx. €41; Rest of World - €55/$60. Fees are paid on arrival in cash (exact change required; payment is NOT made online). The visa approval carries a QR code and must be printed. Biometric data is collected at the entry point. As of June 2025, Mauritanian embassies no longer issue sticker visas - e-visa is the only route.

Malawi operates a full e-visa system at evisa.gov.mw for all nationalities requiring a visa. Fees (per immigration.gov.mw/visa/visa-fees/): Transit USD 50, Single Entry USD 50, Multiple Entry 6-month USD 150, Multiple Entry 12-month USD 250. The single-entry fee was reduced from USD 75 to USD 50 under the 2026 regulations. Category 2 nationals are encouraged to apply online in advance despite being eligible for visa on arrival.

Effective 15 November 2021, the MyVISA (eVISA) system is available to all nationalities that require a visa to enter Malaysia. Applications must be submitted from outside Malaysia, Singapore, Israel, and North Korea. The eVISA applies for social visit, employment-related, and other pass types. Official portal: malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my

E-visa available online via eservices.mhaiss.gov.na for all VOA-eligible nationalities; strongly recommended to apply in advance as it avoids additional NAD 400 manual service fee charged for visa applications submitted on arrival. Holiday visa (up to 3 months) available online.
Tourist Visa available via official Niger e-visa portal.

Nigeria offers an e-Visa for short visits via evisa.immigration.gov.ng. The NIS visa classes page states 'Short Visit Visas allow travelers to visit Nigeria for a period not exceeding three months (90 days)'. Individual sub-categories have specific durations: Tourism Visa (F5A) – single entry, 30-day stay, valid 90 days from issuance, not extendable; Business Single Entry (F4A) – 30 days; Business Multiple Entry (F4B) – up to 30 days per visit; Visiting Single Entry (F6A) – 30 days; Transit Visa (F3B) – 1 to 7 days; Sports (F7E), Creative Arts (F7F), Study Tour (F7G), Academic Exchange Programme (F7H), International Cultural Exchange (F7I), Emergency/Relief Work (F7K), and others. The maximum ceiling across all short-stay e-visa categories is 90 days; most specific tourism/business categories are capped at 30 days per visit. All short-stay e-Visa categories are non-extendable. Nigeria phased out Visa-on-Arrival effective 1 May 2025; all short-stay applications must now be submitted via the e-Visa portal or Nigerian embassy/consulate.

Nationalities not qualifying for visa-free entry may apply for an e-visa through the official Royal Oman Police e-visa portal evisa.rop.gov.om. The portal lists visa categories including Tourist Visit (Unsponsored and Sponsored), Resident Sponsored, and Visit Sponsored. Specific eligible nationalities are determined via the interactive eligibility wizard on the portal.

Nationals not covered by ECOWAS free movement or the September 2019 VoA/landing visa policy must obtain a visa in advance. The official eVisa portal (evisa.sl) is operated by the Government of Sierra Leone. SLID officially directs all advance visa applications to evisa.sl. Applications can also be submitted at Sierra Leone embassies or consulates abroad.

All visitors not listed under visa-free or visa-on-arrival categories must apply for eTAS (Electronic Travel Authorisation for Somalia) online before departure via etas.gov.so. The eTAS is a single-entry permit valid from the stated arrival date; entry must occur within 180 days of the arrival date. Effective September 1, 2025. NOTE: Taiwan (TWN) nationals are included in this eTAS category — a temporary entry ban on Taiwanese nationals was imposed in April 2025 and lifted in June 2025; they now require eTAS like all other non-exempt nationalities (confirmed via Wikipedia citing official Somalia immigration sources).
Listed as 'Congo {Democratic Rep}'. Reduced fee: Single entry USD 50, 3-month multiple entry USD 125, 6-month multiple entry USD 250.

An e-Visa (Autorização de Entrada) can be applied for online via the official SMF e-Visa portal (smf.st/evisa). Processing time is up to 7 working days. Payment is made at the border upon arrival. Requires: scanned passport (PDF), reservation details, return ticket, and proof of means of subsistence (100 EUR/day). Applies under Decreto Lei 11/2009 and Lei 5/2008. Nationalities that already qualify for visa-free entry or visa on arrival may still use the e-Visa as an alternative route.

Tourist and business eVisa available via official portal evisa.gov.sz (Ministry of Home Affairs). Valid for single entry within 90 days of issuance; allows stay of up to 30 days. Processing time 2-5 business days (some sources cite 5-15 business days). eVisa must be obtained before travel. Visa on arrival has been suspended following the eVisa system launch. The Ministry of Home Affairs also offers Student and Transit eVisa categories. No official list of eligible countries or fee schedule was found on the evisa.gov.sz portal as of June 2026.

Thailand e-Visa system (thaievisa.go.th) launched globally on 1 January 2025 across 94 Royal Thai Embassies and Consulates-General. Applies to nationalities not entitled to visa exemption. Specific visa types and stay durations depend on visa category applied for.

Trinidad and Tobago operates a fully electronic visa system. All entry visas are electronic (no physical endorsement in passport). Approved visas are sent via email. Multiple-entry e-Visa fee is 800 TTD. Nationalities not on the visa-exempt list may apply for e-visa through the official portal at nationalsecurity.gov.tt. Possession of an e-Visa does not guarantee entry.

As of April 2026, Venezuela operates a mandatory electronic visa (e-visa) system for all nationalities that require a visa to enter Venezuela. Applications submitted online at cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve. Visas delivered electronically by email. Tourist (TR-V) and Business (TR-N) visa categories available. Processing time approximately 15 days (reduced from approximately 6 weeks). Visa validity 1 year, multiple entry. Fee amount unconfirmed from official Venezuelan sources; aggregators report USD 180. MPPRE published a user manual in February 2026 confirming the system is operational for North America tourist visa applications.

As of August 2023, Vietnam e-visa is open to all countries and territories. Single-entry USD 25, multiple-entry USD 50 (fees confirmed unchanged as of Circular 28/2026/TT-BTC effective April 1, 2026). Valid 90 days from grant date, single or multiple entry. Processing 3 working days. Valid at 13 international airports, 16 land borders, 13 sea ports. Apply at evisa.gov.vn (main portal as of Nov 2024) or evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn.

CIV.notes: All nationals of ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) member states are exempt from visa requirement under Protocol A/SP.1/5/79 of Dakar dated 25 May 1979 on the free movement of persons, the right of residence and establishment. DEI services page explicitly states e-visa is issued to nationals of 'foreign countries outside ECOWAS or without a visa exemption agreement with Benin'. ECOWAS members: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Cote d'Ivoire, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Togo.

Burkina Faso formally withdrew from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025 (together with Mali and Niger, forming the Alliance des États du Sahel / AES). The official visaburkina.bf portal (Ministry of Security) states that ECOWAS nationals are exempt from the residence permit and only need a valid consular identity card for stays. On 14 December 2024, the AES joint declaration adopted in Bamako explicitly stated 'The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) is a visa-free zone for all nationals of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS),' granting ECOWAS nationals the right to 'enter, circulate, reside, settle and leave the territory of AES member states in compliance with national laws in force.' The 12 current ECOWAS member states are: Benin, Cabo Verde, Côte d'Ivoire, The Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo. Note: Burkina Faso itself is an AES country, not an ECOWAS member. Max stay of 90 days is based on the ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol standard; AES declaration does not specify a numeric cap but references compliance with national laws.
Visa waiver agreement established on July 28, 2022 on all categories of passports
Visa-free entry up to 90 days
Visa-free entry; 90-day limit (ECOWAS member). Listed as 'Costa do Marfim' on the Portuguese version of the official page.
ECOWAS member state; visa not required for all passport types
ECOWAS member. Visa exempt per PAF e-visa portal country selector (code 2). 90-day max stay confirmed by APIP official page.
ECOWAS member state - free entry with valid travel document.
ECOWAS member state. Same basis as Benin entry above.

Haiti applies a default visa-free policy: every nationality enters for up to 90 days except the nine countries in the visa_required list (Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam, Yemen). A tourist fee of USD 10 is collected on arrival; passports must remain current for at least six months. The build expands this negation entry against visa_required.nationalities_iso3, so it excludes only Haiti and those nine. Source: https://www.haiti.org/tourist-visa/ (verified 2026-07)
African country exempt from eTA for up to 60 days per Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025 (Legal Notice No. 93, Seventeenth Schedule)

All ECOWAS citizens can enter Liberia visa-free under ECOWAS Protocol A/P 1/5/79 on Free Movement of Persons, the Right of Residence and Establishment. Must hold a valid ECOWAS Biometric Passport with at least 6 months validity. Confirmed by the official Consulate General of Liberia in New York (liberiaconsulate-ny.com): 'all ECOWAS citizens can enter Liberia visa-free using ECOWAS passports that are valid at least six (6) months.' Also confirmed by LIS (lis.gov.lr) which states it 'adheres to the ECOWAS, MRU Protocols on the free movement of people, goods and services.' The Liberian Embassy in the US (liberianembassyus.org) also states 'ECOWAS Passports do not require visa.' Citizens of ECOWAS member states are explicitly excluded from the e-VoA requirement per the March 2025 LIS announcement. No maximum stay duration specified on official sources. 16 member states including Liberia itself; 15 other nationalities exempt.

ECOWAS free movement protocol (effective April 30, 1980) exempts nationals of Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo from entry visas to Mali. Mali formally withdrew from ECOWAS on January 29, 2025, but a joint AES-ECOWAS declaration of December 14, 2024 confirmed that AES countries remain a visa-free zone for all ECOWAS nationals, and ECOWAS reciprocally extended the same rights to AES nationals until further notice. As of June 2026 no formal revocation has been announced. Re-confirmed by maliembassy.us in June 2026 validation run.

Full mutual visa abolition under bilateral agreement - applies to all passport types including ordinary passports. Listed on official MFA page without qualifier. Max stay 90 days per Wikipedia. Re-confirmed on official MFA page 2026-06-29.
ECOWAS free movement protocol; formal ECOWAS grace period ended July 29, 2025, but visa-free still applies until further notice per Fragomen July 2025 alert.

Citizens of ECOWAS member states are exempt from the standard visa requirement. The NIS Tourism Visa (F5A) page explicitly states it applies to 'Citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements'. As of June 2026 there are 12 active ECOWAS members (15 minus Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger). Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger formally withdrew from ECOWAS on January 29, 2025, after the one-year statutory notice period elapsed. ECOWAS granted a six-month transition period (January 29 – July 29, 2025) during which visa-free movement for their nationals was explicitly maintained. After the transition period ended July 29, 2025, ECOWAS has not announced formal termination of visa-free movement; it continues 'until further notice' per ECOWAS Commission statements. The official NIS Tourism Visa (F5A) page and immigration.gov.ng do not specify whether Burkina Faso, Mali, or Niger nationals retain visa-free access to Nigeria following the formal ECOWAS withdrawal. Their visa-free status is recorded in data_quality.gaps. Max stay under the free movement protocol is governed by the ECOWAS Protocol and is not stated verbatim on the NIS website.
Visa-free under Executive Order No. 408. Initial 30-day stay; extendable.
Category A - visa exempt; ECOWAS free movement

Singapore's ICA publishes a list of countries/territories whose nationals REQUIRE a visa; all other passport holders are visa-exempt. The ICA page states that holders of passports/travel documents NOT from visa-required countries do not need a visa. Stay duration (14, 30, or 90 days) is determined by the Visit Pass issued at the checkpoint. Visa-required countries as of June 2026: Afghanistan, Algeria, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Egypt, Georgia, India, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Yemen. Additionally, holders of refugee travel documents, alien's passports, Palestinian Authority passports, UAE temporary passports, Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permits, and PRC Travel Documents require visas.

Under ECOWAS Protocol A/P.1/5/79 dated 29 May 1979, citizens of ECOWAS member states may enter without a visa and reside for up to 90 days. Free landing visa issued at ports of entry per SLID (March 2023). Current ECOWAS membership is 15 states (Mauritania withdrew). Right to reside is granted but does not confer right to employment. Sierra Leone itself is excluded from this list as the destination country. Both the NTB official page (September 2019) and SLID landing-visa page (March 2023) confirm ECOWAS nationals as visa-free.

Seychelles grants visa-free entry to all ordinary passport holders except Kosovo. A Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival for up to 3 months (90 days), free of charge; extendable in 3-month increments up to 12 months total (SCR 5,000 per additional 3-month period). Visitors must demonstrate minimum funds of US$150 or equivalent per day, hold a valid return/onward ticket, and have confirmed accommodation. IMPORTANT: Although no visa is required, ALL travellers must obtain a paid Electronic Travel Authorisation (TA/ETA) prior to departure via seychelles.govtas.com or the Seychelles e-Border app. Standard processing (24 hours): EUR 10; Premium processing (6 hours): EUR 30. Failure to obtain the TA before travel may result in a penalty fee on arrival. Kosovo passport holders are explicitly refused entry as Seychelles does not recognise the State of Kosovo.
Listed as exempt on the official evisa.td portal under 'Pays exemptés'. Duration not specified on official portal.

Citizens of the 15 ECOWAS member states enjoy visa-free entry for up to 90 days under the ECOWAS free movement protocol (since April 30, 1980). Countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Togo. An online travel declaration at voyage.gouv.tg must be completed at least 24 hours before arrival. ISO3: BEN, BFA, CPV, GMB, GHA, GIN, GNB, CIV, LBR, MLI, NER, NGA, SEN, SLE, TGO.

Vatican City has no border controls with Italy per the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. The five entrances into Vatican City State are manned by the Pontifical Swiss Guard and Gendarmerie Corps but entry formalities for foreign visitors are governed by Italy/Schengen rules, not a separate Vatican visa. The governing legislation per the official informazione_generale page is Law N. III of 7 June 1929 on citizenship and residence and Regulation N. XXXVI of 27 September 1932. Vatican authorities have not published a nationality-specific visa-free list. In practice, no separate Vatican visa is required; visitors who can lawfully enter Italy under Schengen rules can enter Vatican City. Note: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is expected in late 2026; nationals of approximately 59 currently visa-exempt countries (including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea) will require ETIAS authorisation before entering Italy/Schengen and by extension Vatican City. Vatican City citizens and European microstate nationals (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino) are explicitly ETIAS-exempt. ETIAS is a travel authorisation, not a visa, and does not change Vatican City's underlying policy of having no separate national visa system.

Visa on arrival (Visa d’entrée aéroport) is confirmed available at Bujumbura Melchior Ndadaye International Airport via the official migration.gov.bi portal (step1/8). Fee: $70 USD single entry, valid 1 month. The Burundi Embassy Washington DC (official) also confirms visa on arrival at the airport ($90 multiple entry up to 30 days, $70 single entry, $40 transit). Applicants must complete an online pre-registration form via migration.gov.bi prior to boarding. Note: The Paris Embassy website only describes advance applications; the migration portal and US Embassy both confirm VOA is operational.
Visa on arrival eligible. Conditions apply.

Confirmed visa-on-arrival at Maya-Maya International Airport Brazzaville per aeroport-brazzaville.com. API-Congo (.cg official domain) uses the term 'exempt' but the airport source clarifies this is a VOA arrangement. Max stay not specified. Reclassified from visa_free to visa_on_arrival in June 2026 re-validation.

Comoros law (Loi n°88-025, Art. 2) requires all foreign nationals to hold a valid passport and a Comorian visa. Visas are available on arrival at the airport or port. Tourist visa: up to 45 days; short-stay visa: up to 3 months; transit visa: up to 5 days. Fee discrepancy: UN Mission page (official) lists 60 EUR for 45 days; IATA Timatic/Wikipedia states 30 EUR; US State Department (travel.state.gov) notes 'between 30–50 Euros'. The 30–50 EUR range is more consistent with aggregator sources; 60 EUR is retained from the UN Mission page as the official Comoros government citation pending clarification.

Visitors of any nationality may obtain a tourist visa on arrival at Djibouti (Ambouli International Airport and other border crossings). Fee is USD 23, paid in cash. The US State Department country information page confirms visa on arrival is available at a $23 fee. The French MFA (diplomatie.gouv.fr, updated June 2026) confirms VOA is possible for one month ('pour un mois'). The UK FCDO (June 2026) also confirms tourists can purchase a visa on arrival in cash USD. No official Djiboutian government source publishes a nationality exclusion list. Max stay: French MFA states 1 month for VOA; exact figure not confirmed on official Djiboutian government domain but the French MFA's June 2026 update provides the most recent official-government confirmation of 30 days.
Tourist Visa on Arrival.

Visa on arrival at port of entry. Official Saint Lucia Department of External Affairs visa-requirements list marks this nationality YES(poe) = visa issued at the port of entry (generally up to 6 weeks). https://stluciaconsulate.ca/wp-content/uploads/forms/Saint-Lucia-Visa-Requirements-by-Country-of-Citizenship.pdf (verified 2026-07)

Nationals not on the 88-country visa-free exemption list (and not from Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Vietnam) may apply for an 'Entry Permit' (Authorization to Enter and Stay, aka visa-upon-arrival) at any border checkpoint Visa Room upon arrival. Fee: MOP200 single / MOP300 multiple for individuals; MOP400/MOP600 for family passports; MOP100/MOP150 for children under 12; MOP100/MOP150 for groups of 10+ with collective travel document. Officials of diplomatic missions of Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Vietnam holding diplomatic/consular identification may also apply for visa-upon-arrival.

Visa on arrival available at international airports/ports for all nationalities except Burundian and Palestinian citizens, for stays up to 90 days. The February 2026 fee increase (15-day tier tripled from €10 to €30) was confirmed to apply exclusively to the eVisa system; VoA fees at airports/embassies/consulates were not confirmed to have changed as of June 2026. Pre-increase VoA fee tiers per the eVisa portal (may still apply on arrival): 1–15 days = €10/US$10; 16–30 days = €35/US$41; 31–60 days = €40/US$47; 61–90 days = €50/US$59. Diplomats and employees of certain international organizations are exempt from visa fees. Visa can be extended to a maximum total stay of 90 days while in Madagascar.

Tourist visa granted on arrival free of charge to all nationalities. No pre-approval required. Effective 15 April 2025, entry is not granted on Israeli passports (Third Amendment to Immigration Act 1/2007, ratified by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu on 15 April 2025). Entry requirements: passport with MRZ and minimum 1 month validity, confirmed return ticket within 30 days of arrival, prepaid accommodation at a registered facility or proof of sufficient funds (minimum USD 100 plus USD 50/day), completed IMUGA Traveller Declaration (within 96 hours before arrival). Yellow Fever vaccination certificate required if coming from endemic countries (children under 1 year exempt). Entry at port of entry subject to admissibility determination by Immigration officers (Immigration Act ss. 7 & 8). Max stay of 30 days confirmed by Maldives High Commission London official page (re-verified 2026-06-29). Extendable up to 60 additional days (total 90 days) in-country by applying to Maldives Immigration before expiry. Extension process was streamlined by Maldives Immigration effective April 23, 2026 under the Maldives 2.0 Initiative.
Visa for sixty days on arrival

Visa on arrival for ordinary passport holders under Namibia's African Union nationals policy effective April 1 2025; AU rate NAD 1200; diplomatic/official/service passport holders visa-exempt (see conditional_access); confirmed on official Namibia Tourism Board visa-on-arrival list (verified 2026-07)

Citizens of most countries are eligible for visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (Kathmandu), Pokhara International Airport, and Gautam Buddha International Airport (Bhairahawa/Lumbini), as well as other designated land border entry points. Options: 15 days (US$30), 30 days (US$50), 90 days (US$125). Multiple-entry. Maximum stay per calendar year is 150 days. Nationals of the following countries are NOT eligible for visa on arrival and must obtain a visa from a Nepalese diplomatic mission in advance: Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe, Eswatini (Swaziland), Cameroon, Somalia, Liberia, Ethiopia, Iraq, Palestine, Afghanistan, Syria, and Iran (added March 13, 2026 per Ministry of Home Affairs decision). Refugees holding travel documents are also excluded. Official/diplomatic passport holders of restricted-country nationals retain access.

Tourist or Business Visa on arrival available for nationalities not otherwise exempt or excluded. Valid 30 days, extendable for two additional 30-day periods at $50 USD each. Processing completed at port of entry. Exceptions: (1) Bangladesh and Myanmar nationals must obtain an advance visa before travel - they are NOT eligible for visa-on-arrival. (2) Nationals of the 12 pre-clearance countries (Bangladesh, Cambodia, Cameroon, Ghana, Haiti, Iran, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Sri Lanka, Vanuatu) must obtain written pre-clearance at least 5 days before travel per Executive Order No. 499 (issued 11 February 2026, effective 30 March 2026). All visitors must hold a valid passport (min. 6 months validity), return ticket, proof of sufficient funds, and sign the Palau Pledge. $100 USD Palau Pristine Paradise Environmental Fee (PPEF) applies to all visitors (effective 1 January 2018); exempt: Palauan citizens, diplomats on duty, crew on duty, transit passengers.
Free visa on arrival for 90 days per official visa-on-arrival page.

2026-07: EXCLUDED the documented 'restricted nationalities' (including Pakistan) from this visa-on-arrival catch-all. These nationalities do NOT get a genuine visa on arrival: at airports all travelers need prior visa approval before boarding, and at land borders these restricted nationalities specifically require advance approval (3 days to 1 month processing) - i.e. an advance-approval / pre-arranged visa, not a true VOA. Pakistani (PAK) ordinary passport holders are therefore not eligible for unconditional Syria VOA and have been removed from the on-arrival expansion. (verified 2026-07). From January 2025, the Syrian transitional government allows essentially all nationalities (except Iran and Israel, and subject to pre-approval requirements for many nationalities) to obtain a visa on arrival at Damascus and Aleppo airports and at land borders with Lebanon and Jordan. Fees vary by nationality. At AIRPORTS: all travelers require prior visa approval before boarding regardless of nationality. At LAND BORDERS: most nationalities can obtain VOA directly; restricted nationalities require advance approval (3 days to 1 month processing). Restricted nationalities (not exhaustive): India, China, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Nepal, Egypt, Sudan, Libya, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Russia, Yemen, Iraq, Belarus, South Africa, South Korea, and others. Sample fees (single-entry, per syriascopetravel.com 2026): EU/Schengen ~$75; UK $150; Canada $100; Australia/NZ $150; USA $200; Russia ~$50; Turkey ~$50. Visa issued as stamp on separate sheet rather than in passport. Israeli nationals and those with Israeli passport stamps are denied entry. Iranian nationals require an advance visa from a Syrian embassy and are not eligible for VOA. Fee of $300 for North Korea and Democratic Republic of Congo noted in syriascopetravel.com but unverified from official source.

Visa on arrival available at Dili International Airport and Dili Sea Port only. Fee: USD $30 cash (single entry). Transit visa: USD $20 for stays under 3 days. Extendable in-country: USD $35 for up to 30 additional days or USD $75 for 30-60 additional days (per customs.gov.tl; migracao.gov.tl states $40 for extension - discrepancy between official pages). Maximum cumulative stay 90 days. Travelers must show: sufficient funds (USD $100 per entry + USD $50 per day of stay), valid passport 6+ months with at least one blank page, return/onward ticket, accommodation proof. Land border arrivals (except Indonesians, Portuguese, and US nationals) must obtain advance Visa Application Authorization.

Citizens of countries not listed in Schedule 1 receive a visitor permit on arrival upon payment of a fee of $100 (AUD), unless waived by the Minister. Permit is valid for up to 30 days, extendable for a further 30 days. Per Regulation 2(1)(b) of the Immigration Regulations 2014 (2022 Revised Edition). Ireland falls in this category as it is explicitly excluded from the EU-Tuvalu visa waiver agreement.

Visa obtainable on arrival at official entry points or in advance via e-visa at visa.immigration.go.tz. VoA confirmed available as of June 2026 per Tanzania Immigration Department guidelines (visa.immigration.go.tz/guidelines) and US State Dept (updated Oct 2025).

All foreign passport holders (except US Nationals of American Samoa) are issued a gratis 90-day Visitor's Permit upon arrival in Samoa. Requirements: passport valid for at least 6 months after intended departure date, return or onward ticket, valid visa/permit for onward destination, documented accommodation, evidence of sufficient funds, no deportation history, no health problems posing a risk to Samoa, no criminal convictions with sentences of 1 year or more, and not appearing on any alert/warning list. Extensions beyond 90 days must be applied for at the Immigration Office in Apia before the permit expires. Note: The MFAT Entry Requirements PDF (binary-unreadable, last updated July 2021) references '60 days' as a 'no permit required' threshold; the operative permit-on-arrival duration of 90 days is confirmed by the MPMC immigration authority (mpmc.gov.ws) and the Samoa High Commission (samoa.org.nz/visa-passport/).

ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) will be mandatory for all visa-exempt third-country nationals entering Schengen area including Hungary. Confirmed for Q4 2026 launch, with a 6-month transitional period (travellers meeting all other entry conditions will not be refused entry solely for lacking ETIAS during transition, extending into approximately April 2027). ETIAS is valid for 3 years or until passport expires. Fee applies. As of June 2026, ETIAS is not yet operational.

ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) will be required for visa-exempt third-country nationals once operational. The Entry/Exit System (EES) became fully operational on 10 April 2026 across all Schengen countries, after a progressive rollout beginning 12 October 2025. ETIAS is scheduled to start operations in Q4 2026; no precise date confirmed as of June 2026. Applies to all Annex II nationals entering the Schengen area including Italy. The application fee is EUR 20 (updated from the originally proposed EUR 7, adjusted for inflation and additional operational costs); authorization covers multiple short stays within 3 years.

All foreign nationals not in the 40-country free ETA list must obtain paid ETA. Tourist ETA fee: USD 20 (South Asian/SAARC countries, applied/at mission) or USD 25 (SAARC, on arrival); USD 50 (all others, applied/at mission) or USD 60 (all others, on arrival). Business ETA: USD 30 (SAARC) or USD 55 (all others); no on-arrival business ETA. Transit visa is free for 48-hour stays. Children under 12 receive free tourist ETA up to 30 days from any nationality.

Latvia introduced an Electronic Travel Declaration system from 1 September 2025 (amendment to Article 4.4 of the Immigration Law). Third-country nationals who are not citizens of an EU member state, NATO member state, OECD member state, EEA country, Swiss Confederation or Brazil, AND who do not have a valid Latvian visa or residence permit, must submit the declaration at least 48 hours before arrival via eta.gov.lv. Note: ETA exemption is based on EU/NATO/OECD/EEA/Swiss/Brazil bloc membership, NOT identity with the ordinary-passport visa-free list. Turkey (NATO member) is ETA-exempt even though Turkish ordinary passport holders are NOT on the ordinary visa-free list. Exempt nationals include all visa-free countries plus Turkey. This is NOT a travel authorization/permission to enter - it is a pre-arrival security declaration. Page last updated May 19, 2026.
All types of passport. Tourist/Business.

All visa applications processed online via the official eVisa portal at https://evisa.immigration.gov.ag/agEvisa-app/. The system allows applicants to apply online; an approval or denial letter is sent once processed. Processing time approximately 5 working days. A soft or hard copy of the eVisa should be carried. Immigration officers at ports of entry reserve the right to deny entry even to eVisa holders.

Visa-required nationality; ordinary-passport holders obtain a Bahamas visa online as an Electronic Entry Visa (EEV) via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs eVisa portal (evisa.mofa.gov.bs), which covers 100+ visa-required countries: apply and pay online, EEV presented to Border Management on arrival (single-entry valid 3 months). Listed on the MOFA needs-visas page. Source: https://mofa.gov.bs/evisa-online-services/ (verified 2026-07)

All foreign nationals not falling under visa-free or visa-on-arrival categories must obtain an e-visa/e-permit prior to entry into Bhutan. Applications are processed through the tourist online visa/permit system at immi.gov.bt. Processing time is a maximum of two working days. Passport must have minimum 6 months validity from intended date of departure from Bhutan. Valid travel insurance is mandatory. All tourists must book through a licensed Bhutanese tour operator and pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF).

All ordinary passport holders not covered by bilateral exemption agreements must apply online through the official evisacam.cm portal (operated by MINREX). Short-stay visa up to 6 months (180 days) - normal processing 72 hours, fee XAF 100,000 / approx. EUR 152; express processing 24 hours, fee XAF 150,000 / approx. EUR 229. Long-stay visa up to 12 months (360 days) - fee XAF 150,000 normal / XAF 200,000 express per diplocam.cm. Transit visa up to 5 days (free) per diplocam.cm. NOTE: Cameroon High Commission UK (cameroonhighcommission.co.uk) cites a paid transit visa at EUR 153 for 4-30 days - this may represent a separate paid transit category; the free 5-day transit is sourced from diplocam.cm (MINREX official). Visa sticker affixed at embassy/high commission or at border entry point. Launched April 30, 2023 per Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023 implementing Law No. 97/012 of 10 January 1997.

E-visa available via evisa.dgdi.ga and edgdi.dgdi.ga. Single-entry 1–3 months costs 70 EUR (or 45,000 XAF) + 15 EUR processing fee. Six-month multiple-entry costs 185 EUR (or 120,000 XAF) + 15 EUR processing fee. Processing time 72 hours. Valid only for air entry via Léon Mba International Airport, Libreville. Governed by Law N°5/86 of 18 June 1986. As of December 2025, e-visa system digitised to cover all short-term categories: tourism, business, family visits. NOTE: US citizens face a reciprocal visa suspension effective January 1, 2026, announced December 18, 2025 by Gabonese Council of Ministers.
Standard e-visa category. Note: as of April 2025 amendments, if applying via visa/permit of qualifying country, requires multiple-entry visa or permit valid for at least 1 year.

E-visa launched 1 July 2023 via equatorialguinea-evisa.com (VFS Global as official technical partner of the Government of Equatorial Guinea). Confirmed operational by official Government Press of Equatorial Guinea (guineaecuatorialpress.com). Available for Tourist, Business, Emergency Humanitarian, and Congresses/Meetings/Seminars categories under Decree No. 49/2019 of December 2, 2019. Fee: EUR 105 for stays under 90 days (Spanish MFA June 2026 re-confirmation). Processing: 72 hours after payment (UK FCDO June 2026 re-confirmation). E-visa approval letter must be printed and presented on arrival. Entry via Malabo International Airport. The Embassy of Equatorial Guinea in Washington DC separately lists an embassy-based visa at USD 200 standard / USD 300 for 90–180 day stays; cash no longer accepted as of 7 February 2025 (online or money order only). The embassy notes the EG Visa Online system is completely separate and independent from embassy services.
Eligible for India e-Visa.
Eligible for tourist e-visa

Since 2017, citizens of ALL countries and territories may apply for a Kyrgyzstan e-visa online via the official e-visa portal (evisa.e-gov.kg). Visa types include: Tourist (TS, up to 30 days), Business (B, up to 90 days), Investment (I, 5–10 years), Digital Nomad (DN, up to 1 year), Student (S, up to 90 days), Transit (TR, 3 days), Relatives (RL, up to 90 days), Driver (T, up to 6 months), Special Work SW1/SW2 (up to 60 days extendable to 1 year), Sapar (J, up to 1 year), Ethnic Kyrgyz 'Meken' (M, up to 1 year), and others. Fee depends on category; applications typically processed within 5 working days.

Visitors requiring a visa may apply online through the official e-visa portal. Fee: US$100 for visitor visa; US$150 for student visa. Processing time approximately two weeks. Visa is emailed upon approval. Dominican Republic nationals explicitly require a visa. Stays under 24 hours from countries normally requiring visas do not require a visa. Official e-visa portal: evisa.stkittsnevisonline.com (note: evisa.gov.kn redirects to this address). The Embassy DC FAQ also references www.evisa.gov.kn as the entry point.
E-visa available online via evisa.gov.ly (can_apply_online: true, exemption_type: NONE). Tourist e-visa: 30-day stay, 90-day validity, single entry, fee USD 63.
E-visa eligible; K2 (30 days), K4 (30 days), K6 (transit, 10 days)

Malawi operates a full e-visa system at evisa.gov.mw for all nationalities requiring a visa. Fees (per immigration.gov.mw/visa/visa-fees/): Transit USD 50, Single Entry USD 50, Multiple Entry 6-month USD 150, Multiple Entry 12-month USD 250. The single-entry fee was reduced from USD 75 to USD 50 under the 2026 regulations. Category 2 nationals are encouraged to apply online in advance despite being eligible for visa on arrival.

Effective 15 November 2021, the MyVISA (eVISA) system is available to all nationalities that require a visa to enter Malaysia. Applications must be submitted from outside Malaysia, Singapore, Israel, and North Korea. The eVISA applies for social visit, employment-related, and other pass types. Official portal: malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my

Nationalities not qualifying for visa-free entry may apply for an e-visa through the official Royal Oman Police e-visa portal evisa.rop.gov.om. The portal lists visa categories including Tourist Visit (Unsponsored and Sponsored), Resident Sponsored, and Visit Sponsored. Specific eligible nationalities are determined via the interactive eligibility wizard on the portal.

All visitors not listed under visa-free or visa-on-arrival categories must apply for eTAS (Electronic Travel Authorisation for Somalia) online before departure via etas.gov.so. The eTAS is a single-entry permit valid from the stated arrival date; entry must occur within 180 days of the arrival date. Effective September 1, 2025. NOTE: Taiwan (TWN) nationals are included in this eTAS category — a temporary entry ban on Taiwanese nationals was imposed in April 2025 and lifted in June 2025; they now require eTAS like all other non-exempt nationalities (confirmed via Wikipedia citing official Somalia immigration sources).
E-visa required. Single entry USD 100, 3-month multiple entry USD 200, 6-month multiple entry USD 350.

An e-Visa (Autorização de Entrada) can be applied for online via the official SMF e-Visa portal (smf.st/evisa). Processing time is up to 7 working days. Payment is made at the border upon arrival. Requires: scanned passport (PDF), reservation details, return ticket, and proof of means of subsistence (100 EUR/day). Applies under Decreto Lei 11/2009 and Lei 5/2008. Nationalities that already qualify for visa-free entry or visa on arrival may still use the e-Visa as an alternative route.

Tourist and business eVisa available via official portal evisa.gov.sz (Ministry of Home Affairs). Valid for single entry within 90 days of issuance; allows stay of up to 30 days. Processing time 2-5 business days (some sources cite 5-15 business days). eVisa must be obtained before travel. Visa on arrival has been suspended following the eVisa system launch. The Ministry of Home Affairs also offers Student and Transit eVisa categories. No official list of eligible countries or fee schedule was found on the evisa.gov.sz portal as of June 2026.

Thailand e-Visa system (thaievisa.go.th) launched globally on 1 January 2025 across 94 Royal Thai Embassies and Consulates-General. Applies to nationalities not entitled to visa exemption. Specific visa types and stay durations depend on visa category applied for.

Trinidad and Tobago operates a fully electronic visa system. All entry visas are electronic (no physical endorsement in passport). Approved visas are sent via email. Multiple-entry e-Visa fee is 800 TTD. Nationalities not on the visa-exempt list may apply for e-visa through the official portal at nationalsecurity.gov.tt. Possession of an e-Visa does not guarantee entry.

E-visa via e-visa.gov.uz (single entry, up to 30 days, USD 20); listed on official Uzbekistan e-visa eligible-country list (Embassy of Uzbekistan, uzembassy.uk/page/319). Distinct from outbound record (Uzbeks are visa-free to Côte d'Ivoire). (verified 2026-07)

As of April 2026, Venezuela operates a mandatory electronic visa (e-visa) system for all nationalities that require a visa to enter Venezuela. Applications submitted online at cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve. Visas delivered electronically by email. Tourist (TR-V) and Business (TR-N) visa categories available. Processing time approximately 15 days (reduced from approximately 6 weeks). Visa validity 1 year, multiple entry. Fee amount unconfirmed from official Venezuelan sources; aggregators report USD 180. MPPRE published a user manual in February 2026 confirming the system is operational for North America tourist visa applications.

As of August 2023, Vietnam e-visa is open to all countries and territories. Single-entry USD 25, multiple-entry USD 50 (fees confirmed unchanged as of Circular 28/2026/TT-BTC effective April 1, 2026). Valid 90 days from grant date, single or multiple entry. Processing 3 working days. Valid at 13 international airports, 16 land borders, 13 sea ports. Apply at evisa.gov.vn (main portal as of Nov 2024) or evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn.

All persons who ordinarily require visas to come to Zambia are eligible to apply for e-visas via eservices.zambiaimmigration.gov.zm. This includes both VOA-eligible nationalities (who may choose to apply in advance) and the 51 nationalities requiring visa prior to travel (who must apply online before arrival and cannot get VOA). Single entry USD 25, Double entry USD 40, Multiple entry USD 75. Visa valid 90 days from date of first issuance. Persons below age 16 cannot apply for an e-Visa independently and must be included in the travelling adult's application.
Category C - must apply and obtain a visa before travelling to Zimbabwe. E-visa available online at evisa.gov.zw.

DJI.notes: On October 31, 2024, at the 23rd COMESA Summit in Bujumbura, Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye announced: 'As part of its commitment to accelerate integration and meet the challenges linked to the free movement of goods and services, from today Burundi will exempt all COMESA member countries from short-stay visa requirements.' Verbatim quote from official MFADC Magazine Nr 18 (November 1, 2024), published by Burundi's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Development Cooperation. COMESA has 21 members; Burundi itself is one. The 20 other member states whose nationals are exempted are listed in the nationality field above. Max stay days for 'short-stay' not specified in the official announcement.
Visa waiver agreement established on July 28, 2022 on all categories of passports
Citizens of Djibouti with a valid passport can enter Ethiopia without a visa (Visa Exemptions section on official VoA page). Max stay days not specified on the official page.

Haiti applies a default visa-free policy: every nationality enters for up to 90 days except the nine countries in the visa_required list (Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam, Yemen). A tourist fee of USD 10 is collected on arrival; passports must remain current for at least six months. The build expands this negation entry against visa_required.nationalities_iso3, so it excludes only Haiti and those nine. Source: https://www.haiti.org/tourist-visa/ (verified 2026-07)
African country exempt from eTA for up to 60 days per Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025 (Legal Notice No. 93, Seventeenth Schedule)
Visa-free under Executive Order No. 408. Initial 30-day stay; extendable.
Category A - visa exempt; bilateral agreement

Singapore's ICA publishes a list of countries/territories whose nationals REQUIRE a visa; all other passport holders are visa-exempt. The ICA page states that holders of passports/travel documents NOT from visa-required countries do not need a visa. Stay duration (14, 30, or 90 days) is determined by the Visit Pass issued at the checkpoint. Visa-required countries as of June 2026: Afghanistan, Algeria, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Egypt, Georgia, India, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Yemen. Additionally, holders of refugee travel documents, alien's passports, Palestinian Authority passports, UAE temporary passports, Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permits, and PRC Travel Documents require visas.

Seychelles grants visa-free entry to all ordinary passport holders except Kosovo. A Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival for up to 3 months (90 days), free of charge; extendable in 3-month increments up to 12 months total (SCR 5,000 per additional 3-month period). Visitors must demonstrate minimum funds of US$150 or equivalent per day, hold a valid return/onward ticket, and have confirmed accommodation. IMPORTANT: Although no visa is required, ALL travellers must obtain a paid Electronic Travel Authorisation (TA/ETA) prior to departure via seychelles.govtas.com or the Seychelles e-Border app. Standard processing (24 hours): EUR 10; Premium processing (6 hours): EUR 30. Failure to obtain the TA before travel may result in a penalty fee on arrival. Kosovo passport holders are explicitly refused entry as Seychelles does not recognise the State of Kosovo.

Visa-free for up to 30 days for nationals of African Union member states under Togo's visa-exemption decree adopted by the Council of Ministers on 26 May 2026 (effective 18 May 2026), which exempts nationals of all African states from an entry visa for stays of up to 30 days. An online travel declaration at voyage.gouv.tg must be completed at least 24 hours before arrival and the resulting travel slip presented at border checkpoints; ECOWAS members instead retain their 90-day visa-free privilege. Confirmed by the official Togolese Embassy (Bern, Switzerland) notice and the 26 May 2026 Council of Ministers communiqué. (verified 2026-07)

Vatican City has no border controls with Italy per the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. The five entrances into Vatican City State are manned by the Pontifical Swiss Guard and Gendarmerie Corps but entry formalities for foreign visitors are governed by Italy/Schengen rules, not a separate Vatican visa. The governing legislation per the official informazione_generale page is Law N. III of 7 June 1929 on citizenship and residence and Regulation N. XXXVI of 27 September 1932. Vatican authorities have not published a nationality-specific visa-free list. In practice, no separate Vatican visa is required; visitors who can lawfully enter Italy under Schengen rules can enter Vatican City. Note: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) is expected in late 2026; nationals of approximately 59 currently visa-exempt countries (including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea) will require ETIAS authorisation before entering Italy/Schengen and by extension Vatican City. Vatican City citizens and European microstate nationals (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino) are explicitly ETIAS-exempt. ETIAS is a travel authorisation, not a visa, and does not change Vatican City's underlying policy of having no separate national visa system.
Visa on arrival eligible. Conditions apply.

Comoros law (Loi n°88-025, Art. 2) requires all foreign nationals to hold a valid passport and a Comorian visa. Visas are available on arrival at the airport or port. Tourist visa: up to 45 days; short-stay visa: up to 3 months; transit visa: up to 5 days. Fee discrepancy: UN Mission page (official) lists 60 EUR for 45 days; IATA Timatic/Wikipedia states 30 EUR; US State Department (travel.state.gov) notes 'between 30–50 Euros'. The 30–50 EUR range is more consistent with aggregator sources; 60 EUR is retained from the UN Mission page as the official Comoros government citation pending clarification.

GID entry requirements page states: 'Visa can be acquired from all Gambian Embassies and some Consulates abroad as well as Visa upon arrival at the border.' gambia.gov.gm states: 'Where there is no Gambian diplomatic representative, participants shall have the privilege to obtain entry visa at the Banjul International Airport upon arrival.' Short visit visa valid up to 90 days. Note: countries that require both visa AND clearance must also have pre-approved entry clearance valid for 30 days before arrival.

All non-exempt nationals may obtain a single-entry short-stay visa on arrival at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport. Requires a letter of authorisation from the Migration Office of Guinea-Bissau obtained in advance. Short-stay single-entry visa: 30 days (fee EUR 61.45 + EUR 2.50 processing per rgb-visa.com/Fees.html). Longer-duration and multiple-entry visas (3 months, 6 months, 1 year) are also available through the e-visa/pre-enrollment system (rgb-visa.com) or at a Guinea-Bissau embassy. US State Dept confirms: 'A visa is required. You can get it on arrival.'
