US_VISA.notes: US: any valid visa - TWOV (Transit Without Visa) scheme - landside transit only. Applicant must: (a) arrive and depart by air; (b) be genuinely in transit to another country on a reasonable transit route; (c) not access public funds/medical treatment/work/study in the UK; (d) intend and be able to leave the UK before 23:59 on the day after arrival; (e) have a confirmed onward flight departing before 23:59 the next day; (f) be assured entry to their destination. Must be travelling to or from (or on part of a reasonable journey to or from) the USA. Physical visa only - electronic visas (including printed versions) not accepted. Note: Syrian nationals holding a B1 or B2 US visa are EXCLUDED from this rule (TWOV 4). Source: Annex A, Home Office Transit Guidance v9, 25 March 2026.

Applies to ordinary passport holders of Category B countries only. Category C nationals must still obtain a Guatemalan visa regardless of US/Schengen/Canada visa held.

US_VISA.notes: US: multiple-entry visa (not an ESTA) for the United States - Nationals of Bolivia, China, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, India, and Venezuela holding a valid multiple-entry US visa may enter all Caribbean parts of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba) without a separate Dutch visa for up to 90 days. Jamaica nationals with a valid multiple-entry US visa may enter all Caribbean parts EXCEPT Curaçao (they are already visa-free for Curaçao by nationality). Guyana nationals with a US multiple-entry visa may enter Sint Maarten (they otherwise require a visa only for Sint Maarten). NOTE: This rule applies ONLY to the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom - NOT to European Netherlands (which is Schengen). Source: NetherlandsWorldwide official government website.

Requires valid residency permit or valid visa from USA, UK, Canada, Schengen area, Australia, or Japan. Traveller must be a national of a Group 2 country AND hold a valid US visa. Official text: 'citizens of the second list countries are required to be either residents or have a valid entry visa for one of the following countries (the United States of America, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Schengen Agreement countries, Japan), or to be residents of one of the countries The Gulf Cooperation Council'.

US_VISA.notes: US: any valid visa - Traveller must hold a valid visa issued by the United States. As of Executive Decree 196 of October 28, 2024 (Gaceta Oficial No. 30149-D, modifying Article 2 of Executive Decree 521 of August 6, 2018), the prior requirements of multiple-entry, prior use in the issuing country, and minimum 6-month validity are all removed; any valid visa is sufficient. Passport must have minimum 3 months validity. Proof of economic solvency of at least USD 500 required. Round-trip ticket required.

Land border crossing restricted to 6 designated routes: Yukhovichi-Dolostsy, Jezerishche-Nevel, Liozno-Kruglovka, Redki-Krasnaya Gorka, Zvenchatka-Dubovichka, Selishche-Novozybkov. E-visas excluded pending settlement of technical aspects. Agreement in force since January 11, 2025.

Passport valid ≥6 months required.

US_VISA.notes: US: valid US nonimmigrant visa (must be valid on day of eTA application; not required to be valid on day of travel to Canada) - Citizens of the 17 eligible visa-required countries may apply for a Canadian eTA (instead of a visitor visa) if they currently hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa. The US nonimmigrant visa must be valid on the day of applying for the eTA, but does not need to be valid on the day of travel to Canada. Travel must be by air only (flying to or transiting through a Canadian airport). By land, bus, train or boat, a visitor visa is still required. Temporary stay only (normally up to 6 months). Traveller should bring old passport containing the US visa when flying. Effective May 26, 2026: Indonesia (IDN) and Malaysia (MYS) added to the eligible country list.

Payment receipt does not guarantee entry - approval email required before travel. One 90-day extension available in-country.

A single-entry Schengen visa does not suffice if the traveller intends to re-enter the Schengen area on return. Andorra itself imposes no visa; the credential requirement is a de facto consequence of Andorra's geographic position. Confirmed by govern.ad tourist visas page and visitandorra.com.

Does not grant entry into Austria beyond the transit zone; only exempts from the Category A transit visa requirement.

Five identity parameters must match 100% between travel document and visa: name, first name, sex, date of birth, nationality. For stays exceeding 90 days in Belgium specifically, a Belgian residence permit or Belgian D visa is always required.

The Schengen visa must be valid and not exhausted. Applies regardless of whether entry is by air, land, or sea. SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Third-country nationals holding both a valid Type D (national long-stay) visa issued by a Schengen member state AND a recognized valid travel document are exempt from Swiss visa requirements. Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period. Exception: holders of a valid Type D visa issued for the purpose of transit to the issuing Schengen state are excluded. Also exempts holder from work-visa obligation for certain gainful activities (long-term permit or Type D visa holders under footnotes V1, V12, V13, V14, V16, V17, V18).

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa (valid for more than 6 months from arrival date) - Nationals of Cambodia, India, Nicaragua, Myanmar, People's Republic of China, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam who prove at the time of arrival in Colombia that they hold a visa valid for more than six months issued by any country belonging to the Schengen Area are exempt from the Visitor (V) visa for stays up to 90 days.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Nationals of Cambodia, India, Nicaragua, Myanmar, People's Republic of China, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam who prove at the time of arrival in Colombia that they hold a visa valid for more than six months issued by any country belonging to the Schengen Area are exempt from the Visitor (V) visa for stays up to 90 days.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type C (short-stay), multiple-entry only - Groups 3 and 4 nationals holding a valid Schengen Category C (short-stay) visa with multiple-entry authorisation exclusively may enter Costa Rica without a consular visa. Visa must be multiple-entry; minimum validity 1 natural day from the intended entry date; visa must not have an effective start date after the intended entry date. Maximum stay: 30 calendar days (extendable; stay cannot exceed remaining visa validity). Source: DGME Alcance N° 148 (migracion.go.cr/visas/).
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Groups 3 and 4 nationals holding a valid Schengen Category C (short-stay) visa with multiple-entry authorisation exclusively may enter Costa Rica without a consular visa. Visa must be multiple-entry; minimum validity 1 natural day from the intended entry date; visa must not have an effective start date after the intended entry date. Maximum stay: 30 calendar days (extendable; stay cannot exceed remaining visa validity). Source: DGME Alcance N° 148 (migracion.go.cr/visas/).

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: double or multiple-entry Schengen visa - Third-country nationals holding a valid double or multiple-entry Schengen visa may enter Cyprus for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. This exemption does NOT apply to nationals of Turkey and Azerbaijan.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid double or multiple-entry Schengen visa may enter Cyprus for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. This exemption does NOT apply to nationals of Turkey and Azerbaijan.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type C (short-stay) or Type D (national/long-stay) Schengen visa valid for Schengen states - Holders of a valid Schengen visa (text on the visa reads 'valid for Schengen states') can travel to Germany for up to 90 days in any period of 180 days. This is counted within the Schengen 90/180-day allowance and applies during the visa's validity period.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of a valid Schengen visa (text on the visa reads 'valid for Schengen states') can travel to Germany for up to 90 days in any period of 180 days. This is counted within the Schengen 90/180-day allowance and applies during the visa's validity period.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type D (long-stay visa / national visa, valid more than 90 days) - Aliens with a visa valid for more than 90 days for a specific Schengen country (long-term visa / D visa) are exempt under Article 21 of the Schengen Convention from the requirement of a visa for Denmark for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Aliens with a visa valid for more than 90 days for a specific Schengen country (long-term visa / D visa) are exempt under Article 21 of the Schengen Convention from the requirement of a visa for Denmark for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: multiple-entry visa (visado de entradas múltiples) - Decree No. 691-07, 18 December 2007: holders of a valid Schengen multiple-entry visa may enter with valid passport and Tourist Card for tourism purposes. Stay up to 30 days. The decree specifies 'Unión Europea (Schengen)' as the issuing zone. Note: Cyprus and Ireland are NOT Schengen members; a Cyprus or Ireland national-only visa may not qualify under this decree. Schengen-area visa only.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Decree No. 691-07, 18 December 2007: holders of a valid Schengen multiple-entry visa may enter with valid passport and Tourist Card for tourism purposes. Stay up to 30 days. The decree specifies 'Unión Europea (Schengen)' as the issuing zone. Note: Cyprus and Ireland are NOT Schengen members; a Cyprus or Ireland national-only visa may not qualify under this decree. Schengen-area visa only.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: valid long-stay visa (Type D national visa) issued by a Schengen State - Holder of a valid long-stay visa (Type D) issued by any Schengen State may move freely within other Schengen States (including Spain) for up to 90 days in any 180-day period without requiring a separate Schengen visa. Applies to nationals who would otherwise require a visa. Confirmed on Spain's official consular entry conditions page: 'This visa will not be necessary if the interested party has a valid residence permit or a valid long-term visa issued by a Schengen State.'
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holder of a valid long-stay visa (Type D) issued by any Schengen State may move freely within other Schengen States (including Spain) for up to 90 days in any 180-day period without requiring a separate Schengen visa. Applies to nationals who would otherwise require a visa. Confirmed on Spain's official consular entry conditions page: 'This visa will not be necessary if the interested party has a valid residence permit or a valid long-term visa issued by a Schengen State.'

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type D long-stay (national) visa issued by any Schengen member state - A third-country national holding a valid long-stay (Type D / national) visa issued by any Schengen member state satisfies the visa entry condition for Finland under Schengen Borders Code Article 6(1)(b) (Regulation EU 2016/399): no additional Finnish or Schengen short-stay visa required. Stay subject to the 90/180-day rule. Periods under a long-stay visa are not counted toward the 90-day limit. Holders of a long-stay visa issued by an ETIAS country are also exempt from ETIAS (ETIAS Regulation EU 2018/1240, Article 2(2)).
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: A third-country national holding a valid long-stay (Type D / national) visa issued by any Schengen member state satisfies the visa entry condition for Finland under Schengen Borders Code Article 6(1)(b) (Regulation EU 2016/399): no additional Finnish or Schengen short-stay visa required. Stay subject to the 90/180-day rule. Periods under a long-stay visa are not counted toward the 90-day limit. Holders of a long-stay visa issued by an ETIAS country are also exempt from ETIAS (ETIAS Regulation EU 2018/1240, Article 2(2)).

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: EEA: valid uniform format category D visa (EEA state or Switzerland) - TWOV scheme - landside transit only. Must hold a valid uniform format Category D (national/long-stay) visa for entry to an EEA state or Switzerland. All TWOV 2 base requirements apply. Physical documents only - electronic versions not accepted. Source: TWOV 3(i), Home Office Transit Guidance v9, 25 March 2026.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: TWOV scheme - landside transit only. Must hold a valid uniform format Category D (national/long-stay) visa for entry to an EEA state or Switzerland. All TWOV 2 base requirements apply. Physical documents only - electronic versions not accepted. Source: TWOV 3(i), Home Office Transit Guidance v9, 25 March 2026.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type D (national long-stay visa) - Third-country nationals holding a valid long-stay (Type D) national visa issued by any Schengen member state may travel to other Schengen member states, including Greece, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, provided they meet entry conditions (valid travel document, sufficient means, no security threat, not in national alert system). Governed by Article 21 of the Schengen Convention as amended by Regulation (EC) 265/2010.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid long-stay (Type D) national visa issued by any Schengen member state may travel to other Schengen member states, including Greece, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, provided they meet entry conditions (valid travel document, sufficient means, no security threat, not in national alert system). Governed by Article 21 of the Schengen Convention as amended by Regulation (EC) 265/2010.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa (Type C or Type D) - Nationals of Category B countries holding a valid Schengen area visa (issued by any Schengen member state; both Type C short-stay and Type D national/long-stay accepted) are exempt from obtaining a Guatemalan visa for up to 90 days. Confirmed by the IGM official FAQ page (igm.gob.gt): 'visa Americana, Canadiense o de Schengen vigente, no es necesario tramitar visa guatemalteca.' Also confirmed by Guatemala Embassy in India advisory. Category C nationals are excluded.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Nationals of Category B countries holding a valid Schengen area visa (issued by any Schengen member state; both Type C short-stay and Type D national/long-stay accepted) are exempt from obtaining a Guatemalan visa for up to 90 days. Confirmed by the IGM official FAQ page (igm.gob.gt): 'visa Americana, Canadiense o de Schengen vigente, no es necesario tramitar visa guatemalteca.' Also confirmed by Guatemala Embassy in India advisory. Category C nationals are excluded.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Guatemalan nationals holding a valid Schengen visa may enter Guyana visa-free for up to 90 days. MFA verbatim: 'Guatemala for 90 days for holders of Diplomatic/Official Passports and holders of an US Permanent Resident Card or a valid US/Canadian/Schengen Visa'.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Guatemalan nationals holding a valid Schengen visa may enter Guyana visa-free for up to 90 days. MFA verbatim: 'Guatemala for 90 days for holders of Diplomatic/Official Passports and holders of an US Permanent Resident Card or a valid US/Canadian/Schengen Visa'.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Honduran nationals holding a valid Schengen visa may enter Guyana visa-free for up to 90 days. Source: Embassy of Guyana Belgium and ISS eligible-countries page. NOT independently confirmed on minfor.gov.gy.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Honduran nationals holding a valid Schengen visa may enter Guyana visa-free for up to 90 days. Source: Embassy of Guyana Belgium and ISS eligible-countries page. NOT independently confirmed on minfor.gov.gy.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Mexican ordinary passport holders with a valid Schengen visa may enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Source: Embassy of Guyana Belgium and ISS eligible-countries page. NOT confirmed on minfor.gov.gy.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Mexican ordinary passport holders with a valid Schengen visa may enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Source: Embassy of Guyana Belgium and ISS eligible-countries page. NOT confirmed on minfor.gov.gy.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type C uniform visa (two or multiple entries) - Uniform Schengen Type C visa must be for two or multiple entries, valid for all Schengen Area Member States. Single-entry C visas (C01) do NOT qualify. A C02 visa is not considered valid if both entries into the Schengen Area are used before entering Croatia. Visa and passport must be valid at moment of entry, during stay, and at departure. Passport valid for at least 3 months after planned departure from Croatia. Stay not to exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Uniform Schengen Type C visa must be for two or multiple entries, valid for all Schengen Area Member States. Single-entry C visas (C01) do NOT qualify. A C02 visa is not considered valid if both entries into the Schengen Area are used before entering Croatia. Visa and passport must be valid at moment of entry, during stay, and at departure. Passport valid for at least 3 months after planned departure from Croatia. Stay not to exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type D (national long-stay visa) - Per EU Regulation No 265/2010 of 25 March 2010: a third-country national holding a valid long-stay visa (Type D) issued by any Schengen Member State may travel to Hungary and other Schengen states for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, under the same conditions as a residence permit holder. Must hold a valid travel document and meet other entry conditions.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Per EU Regulation No 265/2010 of 25 March 2010: a third-country national holding a valid long-stay visa (Type D) issued by any Schengen Member State may travel to Hungary and other Schengen states for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, under the same conditions as a residence permit holder. Must hold a valid travel document and meet other entry conditions.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Ireland: Irish short-stay visa endorsed 'BIVS' (visit family/friend, visit tourist, conference/event, business) - British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS) - Irish visa variant. Visa must be endorsed with the letters 'BIVS'. Must first travel to Ireland (issuing country) before visiting UK. Allows travel within the Common Travel Area (Ireland and UK, excluding Isle of Man and Channel Islands). Duration in UK decided by UK immigration officer. Up to 90 days total. No UK transit visa required if transiting UK to reach Ireland provided travel into Ireland by 23:59 on the day after UK arrival.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS) - Irish visa variant. Visa must be endorsed with the letters 'BIVS'. Must first travel to Ireland (issuing country) before visiting UK. Allows travel within the Common Travel Area (Ireland and UK, excluding Isle of Man and Channel Islands). Duration in UK decided by UK immigration officer. Up to 90 days total. No UK transit visa required if transiting UK to reach Ireland provided travel into Ireland by 23:59 on the day after UK arrival.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa (uniform visa or national long-stay visa) - Holders of a valid Schengen visa (uniform short-stay visa or national long-stay visa) issued by any Schengen member state do not need to apply for a separate Iceland visa. Stay subject to the 90/180-day Schengen rule. Visa must be valid.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of a valid Schengen visa (uniform short-stay visa or national long-stay visa) issued by any Schengen member state do not need to apply for a separate Iceland visa. Stay subject to the 90/180-day Schengen rule. Visa must be valid.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type D (national long-stay visa) - Pursuant to EU Regulation 265/2010, a valid long-stay visa (Type D/national visa) issued by any Schengen member state confers the same free-movement right as a residence permit: the holder may move freely within the territories of other Schengen states for up to 90 days in any 180-day period during the visa's validity. Must fulfil standard Schengen entry conditions and must not be on alert lists. Does not confer automatic right of entry; border authorities may verify entry conditions.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Pursuant to EU Regulation 265/2010, a valid long-stay visa (Type D/national visa) issued by any Schengen member state confers the same free-movement right as a residence permit: the holder may move freely within the territories of other Schengen states for up to 90 days in any 180-day period during the visa's validity. Must fulfil standard Schengen entry conditions and must not be on alert lists. Does not confer automatic right of entry; border authorities may verify entry conditions.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid visa - Honduras nationals who hold a valid US, UK, Canadian or Schengen visa may enter Jamaica without a visa for up to 30 days.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Honduras nationals who hold a valid US, UK, Canadian or Schengen visa may enter Jamaica without a visa for up to 30 days.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid visa - Nationals of these 15 countries may enter Jamaica visa-free for 30 days ONLY IF in possession of a valid US, UK, Canadian or Schengen visa AND proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio. Source footnote verbatim: '*Applicable only if in possession of a valid US, UK, Canadian or Schengen visa AND proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio'.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Nationals of these 15 countries may enter Jamaica visa-free for 30 days ONLY IF in possession of a valid US, UK, Canadian or Schengen visa AND proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio. Source footnote verbatim: '*Applicable only if in possession of a valid US, UK, Canadian or Schengen visa AND proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio'.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: European Union: European Union Laissez-Passer - Holders of European Union Laissez-Passers whilst on official European Union business.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of European Union Laissez-Passers whilst on official European Union business.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid long-term visa (for more than 3 years) - Visa-free entry for up to 7 days with the right to re-enter visa-free after 21 days from the date of departure from the Kyrgyz Republic, in the presence of long-term visas (for more than 3 years) of the United States of America, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, or Schengen zone. Applies to citizens of Republic of India and People's Republic of China.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Visa-free entry for up to 7 days with the right to re-enter visa-free after 21 days from the date of departure from the Kyrgyz Republic, in the presence of long-term visas (for more than 3 years) of the United States of America, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, or Schengen zone. Applies to citizens of Republic of India and People's Republic of China.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type C (short-stay) - Any third-country national holding a valid short-stay visa (Type C) issued by any other Schengen State can enter Latvia without a separate Latvian visa. Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Any third-country national holding a valid short-stay visa (Type C) issued by any other Schengen State can enter Latvia without a separate Latvian visa. Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa (Type C or Type D), excluding transit visas - Holders of a valid Schengen-area visa (Type C short-stay or Type D national/long-stay), excluding transit visas, issued by any Schengen Agreement state may travel to Moldova during the visa's validity. Applies to nationals listed under Footnote [2] of the official MFA visa regime page.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of a valid Schengen-area visa (Type C short-stay or Type D national/long-stay), excluding transit visas, issued by any Schengen Agreement state may travel to Moldova during the visa's validity. Applies to nationals listed under Footnote [2] of the official MFA visa regime page.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type C (short-stay / Schengen C-visit visa) - Visa must be valid, multiple-entry, and stamped in passport. Applies to non-lucrative visits (tourism, business, transit, studies, medical treatment). Type D (long-stay national visa) is not listed and is NOT included.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Visa must be valid, multiple-entry, and stamped in passport. Applies to non-lucrative visits (tourism, business, transit, studies, medical treatment). Type D (long-stay national visa) is not listed and is NOT included.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type C (short-stay) multiple-entry - Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen Type C visa, valid for at least 5 days beyond the intended stay, may enter North Macedonia visa-free for up to 15 days per entry; total stay not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen Type C visa, valid for at least 5 days beyond the intended stay, may enter North Macedonia visa-free for up to 15 days per entry; total stay not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Holders of valid foreign travel documents with a valid Schengen visa may enter, transit through, and stay in Montenegro for up to 30 days, and no longer than until the expiry of the visa if the validity period is shorter than 30 days. As of 2024/2025, Bulgaria and Romania are full Schengen members; their visas are now covered by this entry.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of valid foreign travel documents with a valid Schengen visa may enter, transit through, and stay in Montenegro for up to 30 days, and no longer than until the expiry of the visa if the validity period is shorter than 30 days. As of 2024/2025, Bulgaria and Romania are full Schengen members; their visas are now covered by this entry.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: EU: European Blue Card held in another participating EU/EEA country for at least 12 months - Holders of a valid European Blue Card issued by another EU/EEA country (held for at least 12 months) who are applying for a Blue Card in the Netherlands are exempt from the MVV requirement. Spouse/partner and minor children are also exempt. This is an MVV-waiver for long-stay entry. Source: IND MVV Exemptions page.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holders of a valid European Blue Card issued by another EU/EEA country (held for at least 12 months) who are applying for a Blue Card in the Netherlands are exempt from the MVV requirement. Spouse/partner and minor children are also exempt. This is an MVV-waiver for long-stay entry. Source: IND MVV Exemptions page.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Group 2 – conditional visa-free entry for 14 days, non-extendable. Traveller must be a national of a Group 2 country AND hold a valid Schengen area visa.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Group 2 – conditional visa-free entry for 14 days, non-extendable. Traveller must be a national of a Group 2 country AND hold a valid Schengen area visa.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa (any EU member state) - Traveller must hold a valid visa issued by any of the states that make up the European Union. As of Executive Decree 196 of October 28, 2024 (modifying Executive Decree 521 of August 6, 2018), prior-use, multiple-entry, and 6-month validity requirements are removed; any valid visa is sufficient. Passport must have minimum 3 months validity. Proof of economic solvency of at least USD 500 required. Round-trip ticket required.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Traveller must hold a valid visa issued by any of the states that make up the European Union. As of Executive Decree 196 of October 28, 2024 (modifying Executive Decree 521 of August 6, 2018), prior-use, multiple-entry, and 6-month validity requirements are removed; any valid visa is sufficient. Passport must have minimum 3 months validity. Proof of economic solvency of at least USD 500 required. Round-trip ticket required.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Chinese nationals holding a valid Schengen Area visa with minimum 6 months remaining validity from date of arrival in Peru are exempt from tourist/business visa requirement. Single or multiple entries within a 6-month period. Based on Decreto Supremo N° 069-2016-RE (published 01/09/2016).
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Chinese nationals holding a valid Schengen Area visa with minimum 6 months remaining validity from date of arrival in Peru are exempt from tourist/business visa requirement. Single or multiple entries within a 6-month period. Based on Decreto Supremo N° 069-2016-RE (published 01/09/2016).

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Indian nationals holding a valid Schengen Area visa with minimum 6 months remaining validity from date of arrival in Peru are exempt from tourist/business visa requirement. Single or multiple entries within a 6-month period. Based on Decreto Supremo N° 006-2017-RE (published 06/03/2017).
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Indian nationals holding a valid Schengen Area visa with minimum 6 months remaining validity from date of arrival in Peru are exempt from tourist/business visa requirement. Single or multiple entries within a 6-month period. Based on Decreto Supremo N° 006-2017-RE (published 06/03/2017).

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Mainland Chinese nationals traveling as tourists holding a valid or unexpired Schengen visa may enter visa-free for an initial stay not exceeding 7 days (FSC No. 112-11). The 7-day stay may be extended by an additional 14 days to complete a maximum of 21 days. Passport must be valid; return/onward ticket required. No derogatory BI records.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Mainland Chinese nationals traveling as tourists holding a valid or unexpired Schengen visa may enter visa-free for an initial stay not exceeding 7 days (FSC No. 112-11). The 7-day stay may be extended by an additional 14 days to complete a maximum of 21 days. Passport must be valid; return/onward ticket required. No derogatory BI records.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid tourist, business or resident Schengen visa - Indian nationals traveling as tourists and holding a valid and current Schengen tourist, business or resident visa or residence permit may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible period of 30 days (AJACSSUK provision, effective June 8, 2025). Valid passport and return/onward ticket required. Admitted from any port of entry.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Indian nationals traveling as tourists and holding a valid and current Schengen tourist, business or resident visa or residence permit may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible period of 30 days (AJACSSUK provision, effective June 8, 2025). Valid passport and return/onward ticket required. Admitted from any port of entry.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: Type D (national/long-stay visa) issued by another Schengen Member State - Foreign nationals holding a valid long-stay (D-type) visa issued by another Schengen Member State are entitled to stay in Schengen Member States other than the one which issued the visa (including Poland) during the validity of that visa for a period not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period. Traveller must carry the D-type visa and a valid travel document.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Foreign nationals holding a valid long-stay (D-type) visa issued by another Schengen Member State are entitled to stay in Schengen Member States other than the one which issued the visa (including Poland) during the validity of that visa for a period not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period. Traveller must carry the D-type visa and a valid travel document.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: uniform Schengen visa (Type C or Type D) - Third-country nationals holding a valid uniform Schengen visa (short-stay Type C) or long-stay national visa (Type D) or residence permit issued by any Schengen Member State are exempt from the airport transit visa (ATV) requirement when transiting through the international transit areas of Portuguese airports. This is an airport transit exemption only under Article 3(5)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Schengen Visa Code) - it does not grant a separate right of short-stay entry beyond the existing visa/permit.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid uniform Schengen visa (short-stay Type C) or long-stay national visa (Type D) or residence permit issued by any Schengen Member State are exempt from the airport transit visa (ATV) requirement when transiting through the international transit areas of Portuguese airports. This is an airport transit exemption only under Article 3(5)(a) of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Schengen Visa Code) - it does not grant a separate right of short-stay entry beyond the existing visa/permit.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: uniform visa (two or multiple entries) - Holder of a uniform visa valid for two or multiple entries issued by a Schengen state. Visa must be within its validity period and the number of entries and duration of authorised stay must not be exhausted. Stay in Romania must not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. Traveller must still meet general entry conditions (valid travel document, proof of purpose and financial means, no SIS/national alerts).
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holder of a uniform visa valid for two or multiple entries issued by a Schengen state. Visa must be within its validity period and the number of entries and duration of authorised stay must not be exhausted. Stay in Romania must not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. Traveller must still meet general entry conditions (valid travel document, proof of purpose and financial means, no SIS/national alerts).

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Holder must possess a valid (unexpired) Schengen area visa. Nationals from the excluded list remain subject to Category C (consulted visa requiring prior DGME authorization) regardless of holding a Schengen visa. The official RREE visa checker (rree.gob.sv/visas/) explicitly asks whether the traveller holds a valid US, Canada, or Schengen visa as a determining condition for entry category.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Holder must possess a valid (unexpired) Schengen area visa. Nationals from the excluded list remain subject to Category C (consulted visa requiring prior DGME authorization) regardless of holding a Schengen visa. The official RREE visa checker (rree.gob.sv/visas/) explicitly asks whether the traveller holds a valid US, Canada, or Schengen visa as a determining condition for entry category.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa - Foreign nationals holding all types of national passports with a valid Schengen visa may enter, transit and stay in the Republic of Serbia up to 90 days during a six-month period, and within validity of said visas. Two-passport rule applies: may present expired national passport with valid visa sticker together with a valid national passport without visa. Residence permit in card form must be accompanied by valid passport.
SCHENGEN_VISA.conditions: Foreign nationals holding all types of national passports with a valid Schengen visa may enter, transit and stay in the Republic of Serbia up to 90 days during a six-month period, and within validity of said visas. Two-passport rule applies: may present expired national passport with valid visa sticker together with a valid national passport without visa. Residence permit in card form must be accompanied by valid passport.

SCHENGEN_VISA.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen visa or resident permit - Passport must be valid for more than 3 months. Visa or resident permit must be valid. Official SMF text (Portuguese): 'Um passaporte com validade superior a três meses; Um visto Schengen válido ou um visto válido dos Estados Unidos.' Wikipedia also confirms resident permits (not just visas) from the US or Schengen area qualify.

UK_VISA.notes: UK: UK short-stay ('C') visitor visa (all standard visitor categories except visitor in transit and visitor for marriage or civil partnership) - Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme (SSVWP). Must hold a valid UK short-stay ('C') visa (not an ETA, not a long-stay 'D' visa, not a BRP card). Traveller must have already landed and gained lawful entry into the UK on foot of the current UK visa before travelling to Ireland. Each distinct period of leave to remain in the UK (up to max 180 days) requires a prior legal entry into the UK. Maximum stay in Ireland is 90 days or the remaining time on UK permission, whichever is less. Note: for Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Peru nationals, a UK ETA cannot be used - only a pre-1 February 2024 short-stay UK visa qualifies. Ukraine nationals are covered but are also now unconditionally visa-free as of 25 February 2022. Belarus and Russia were removed from the SSVWP. Ecuador was never confirmed on the current official SSVWP list. Programme not reciprocal. SSVWP page last updated 9 May 2025.

UK_VISA.notes: UK: UK standard visitor visa endorsed 'BIVS' (all standard visitor categories max 6 months except visitor in transit and visitor for marriage/civil partnership; also Permitted Paid Engagement visas) - British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS). Visa must be endorsed with the letters 'BIVS' by UK visa officer (discretionary; no appeal against non-endorsement). Applicants must be resident in China (including HK/Macau) or India at time of application. Must first travel to the country that issued the visa (i.e., if UK-issued BIVS visa, must enter UK first). Single entry BIVS = single entry to Common Travel Area (CTA). Multiple entry: must re-enter issuing country first on each new entry to CTA. Duration up to 90 days or remaining UK permission, whichever shorter, as decided by Irish immigration officer on arrival. Ireland must be primary destination if applying for Irish BIVS visa. Note: HK/Macau passport holders are already visa-free for Ireland and do not need BIVS.

E-visa valid 30 days, extendable up to 6 months with multiple entries. Processing 24-72 hours. Apply via www.acces-maroc.ma
UK_VISA.conditions: Foreigners subject to visa formality holding a valid ordinary passport and a non-electronic multiple-entry visa of the UK, valid for a minimum of 90 days from the date of application. E-visa valid 30 days, extendable up to 6 months with multiple entries. Processing 24-72 hours. Apply via www.acces-maroc.ma

UK_VISA.notes: UK: any valid UK visa - Holder of a valid UK visa (previously used or unused single-entry visas accepted; e-visas of other countries not accepted; must be valid by date of entry into Türkiye). Egypt: ages 15–45 only. Iraq: ages 15–50 only. Libya: ages 16–45 only. Single entry, 1 month.
UK_VISA.conditions: Holder of a valid UK visa (previously used or unused single-entry visas accepted; e-visas of other countries not accepted; must be valid by date of entry into Türkiye). Egypt: ages 15–45 only. Iraq: ages 15–50 only. Libya: ages 16–45 only. Single entry, 1 month.

UK_VISA.notes: UK: any valid visa - Nationals of Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, and Vietnam holding a valid entry visa issued by the United Kingdom may apply for Taiwan Travel Authorization Certificate (TAC) - multiple-entry, valid 90 days, up to 30 days per stay. Passport must have at least 6 months remaining validity. Must possess onward/return air or ferry ticket. Must never have been employed as a blue-collar worker in Taiwan.
UK_VISA.conditions: Nationals of Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, and Vietnam holding a valid entry visa issued by the United Kingdom may apply for Taiwan Travel Authorization Certificate (TAC) - multiple-entry, valid 90 days, up to 30 days per stay. Passport must have at least 6 months remaining validity. Must possess onward/return air or ferry ticket. Must never have been employed as a blue-collar worker in Taiwan.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: valid permit of stay in one of the Schengen states - Permit must be valid. Traveller must leave Albania no later than 3 days from the date of expiry of the permit.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Permit must be valid. Traveller must leave Albania no later than 3 days from the date of expiry of the permit.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit - Holder of a valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) issued by any Schengen member state is exempt from the airport transit visa (Category A) requirement. Applies to nationals of countries that otherwise require a transit visa. Does not grant entry into Austria beyond the transit zone; only exempts from the Category A transit visa requirement.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Holder of a valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) issued by any Schengen member state is exempt from the airport transit visa (Category A) requirement. Applies to nationals of countries that otherwise require a transit visa. Does not grant entry into Austria beyond the transit zone; only exempts from the Category A transit visa requirement.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid residence permit - Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen Member State may travel visa-free to Belgium for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Five identity parameters must match 100% between travel document and permit: name, first name, sex, date of birth, nationality. Certain French temporary receipts (récépissé) and German Aufenthaltstitel without specific endorsements lack visa-free value. Cyprus and Ireland residence permits in principle have no Schengen visa-free value except those explicitly issued to family members of EU citizens under Directive 2004/38. UK residence cards and visas carry no Schengen visa-free value.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen Member State may travel visa-free to Belgium for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Five identity parameters must match 100% between travel document and permit: name, first name, sex, date of birth, nationality. Certain French temporary receipts (récépissé) and German Aufenthaltstitel without specific endorsements lack visa-free value. Cyprus and Ireland residence permits in principle have no Schengen visa-free value except those explicitly issued to family members of EU citizens under Directive 2004/38. UK residence cards and visas carry no Schengen visa-free value.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: permanent resident - Indian Nationals who are permanent residents of a Schengen country do not require a Bahamas visa. Must present proof of Permanent Residency status together with valid passport to Immigration at time of entry.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Indian Nationals who are permanent residents of a Schengen country do not require a Bahamas visa. Must present proof of Permanent Residency status together with valid passport to Immigration at time of entry.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid residence permit - Nationals of countries with whom Bosnia and Herzegovina has a visa regime may enter without a BiH visa for up to 30 days if they hold a valid residence permit issued by a Schengen Agreement signatory state. The permit must be valid for at least 30 days beyond the date of entry. One continuous stay cannot exceed 30 days.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Nationals of countries with whom Bosnia and Herzegovina has a visa regime may enter without a BiH visa for up to 30 days if they hold a valid residence permit issued by a Schengen Agreement signatory state. The permit must be valid for at least 30 days beyond the date of entry. One continuous stay cannot exceed 30 days.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: permanent resident - Haitian nationals holding an ordinary passport who are permanent residents of a Schengen Area country do not require a Barbados entry visa. Source text verbatim (official MFA PDF): 'No Visa required holders, permanent residents of UK, USA, Canada Schengen countries & Green card holders.'
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Haitian nationals holding an ordinary passport who are permanent residents of a Schengen Area country do not require a Barbados entry visa. Source text verbatim (official MFA PDF): 'No Visa required holders, permanent residents of UK, USA, Canada Schengen countries & Green card holders.'

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen member state residence permit - Third-country nationals holding both a valid residence permit issued by a Schengen member state AND a recognized valid travel document are exempt from Swiss visa requirements. Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period. Exception: holders of a valid residence permit issued for the purpose of transit to the issuing Schengen state are excluded. The recognized Schengen residence permits are listed in the SEM's official compilation (PDF updated 08.05.2026).
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Third-country nationals holding both a valid residence permit issued by a Schengen member state AND a recognized valid travel document are exempt from Swiss visa requirements. Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period. Exception: holders of a valid residence permit issued for the purpose of transit to the issuing Schengen state are excluded. The recognized Schengen residence permits are listed in the SEM's official compilation (PDF updated 08.05.2026).

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: any valid residence authorization - Nationals of countries on the prior-visa-required list (91 countries per corrected Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026, published 23 Jan 2026, correcting the original 96-country Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2025 of Nov 2025) are exempt from the prior visa requirement if they hold a valid residence authorization (autorização de residência válida) issued by an EU Member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, San Marino, Switzerland, or Vatican. Verbatim: 'titulares de autorizações de residência válidas emitidas por Estados-Membros da União Europeia, Islândia, Liechtenstein, Reino Unido, San Marino, Suíça e Vaticano'. No max stay stated in the exemption clause; traveller enters without needing a prior visa.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Nationals of countries on the prior-visa-required list (91 countries per corrected Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026, published 23 Jan 2026, correcting the original 96-country Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2025 of Nov 2025) are exempt from the prior visa requirement if they hold a valid residence authorization (autorização de residência válida) issued by an EU Member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, San Marino, Switzerland, or Vatican. Verbatim: 'titulares de autorizações de residência válidas emitidas por Estados-Membros da União Europeia, Islândia, Liechtenstein, Reino Unido, San Marino, Suíça e Vaticano'. No max stay stated in the exemption clause; traveller enters without needing a prior visa.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: residence permit allowing multiple entries or with minimum 90 natural days validity (excluding refugee/asylum) - Groups 3 and 4 nationals holding a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state - that allows multiple entries OR has a minimum validity of 90 natural days from the intended entry date - may enter Costa Rica without a consular visa. Refugee and asylum categories are excluded. Document must be officially issued. Maximum stay: 30 calendar days (extendable). EU states listed on DGME page: Germany, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Croatia, Denmark, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Groups 3 and 4 nationals holding a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state - that allows multiple entries OR has a minimum validity of 90 natural days from the intended entry date - may enter Costa Rica without a consular visa. Refugee and asylum categories are excluded. Document must be officially issued. Maximum stay: 30 calendar days (extendable). EU states listed on DGME page: Germany, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Croatia, Denmark, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: residence permit issued by Schengen Member State - Residence permit must be valid; stay may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period; does NOT apply to nationals of Turkey and Azerbaijan. Legal basis: Decision No. 565/2014/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Residence permit must be valid; stay may not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period; does NOT apply to nationals of Turkey and Azerbaijan. Legal basis: Decision No. 565/2014/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: any valid residence permit issued by an EU Member State (excluding Ireland and Denmark) - Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit in another EU Member State, or EU citizens' family members holding a residence card or permanent residence card in another EU Member State, may stay in the Czech Republic without a visa for up to 90 days within any 180-day period (non-profit purposes). Residence permits issued by Ireland and Denmark are excluded. Family members of EU citizens whose short-term visa has expired may also stay up to 3 months if they qualify as spouse, parent, or dependent offspring of an EU citizen.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit in another EU Member State, or EU citizens' family members holding a residence card or permanent residence card in another EU Member State, may stay in the Czech Republic without a visa for up to 90 days within any 180-day period (non-profit purposes). Residence permits issued by Ireland and Denmark are excluded. Family members of EU citizens whose short-term visa has expired may also stay up to 3 months if they qualify as spouse, parent, or dependent offspring of an EU citizen.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid residence permit of a Schengen member state - Non-EU citizens holding a valid residence permit issued by any of the fully-applying Schengen states (Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland) do not need a visa for visits to Germany of up to 90 days in any period of 180 days when not taking up work.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Non-EU citizens holding a valid residence permit issued by any of the fully-applying Schengen states (Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland) do not need a visa for visits to Germany of up to 90 days in any period of 180 days when not taking up work.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit - Aliens with a valid residence permit for another Schengen State are exempt under Article 21 of the Schengen Convention from the requirement of a visa for Denmark for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Time spent on a residence permit in Denmark or another Schengen country is not counted toward the 90-day limit. Residence permits valid only for the Faroe Islands or Greenland are not valid for other Schengen entries.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Aliens with a valid residence permit for another Schengen State are exempt under Article 21 of the Schengen Convention from the requirement of a visa for Denmark for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Time spent on a residence permit in Denmark or another Schengen country is not counted toward the 90-day limit. Residence permits valid only for the Faroe Islands or Greenland are not valid for other Schengen entries.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: permanent residence (residencia permanente) in EU/Schengen member state - Decree No. 691-07, 18 December 2007: holders of permanent residence in an EU (Schengen) member state may enter with valid passport and Tourist Card for tourism purposes. Stay up to 30 days.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Decree No. 691-07, 18 December 2007: holders of permanent residence in an EU (Schengen) member state may enter with valid passport and Tourist Card for tourism purposes. Stay up to 30 days.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid residence permit issued by a Schengen State - Holder of a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen State may move freely within other Schengen States (including Spain) for up to 90 days in any 180-day period without requiring a separate Schengen visa, provided they hold a valid travel document. Applies to nationals who would otherwise require a visa. Residence permit stay periods are not counted against the 90-day visa-free allowance. Authority: Article 21 of the Convention Implementing the Schengen Agreement; confirmed on Spain's official consular entry conditions page.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Holder of a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen State may move freely within other Schengen States (including Spain) for up to 90 days in any 180-day period without requiring a separate Schengen visa, provided they hold a valid travel document. Applies to nationals who would otherwise require a visa. Residence permit stay periods are not counted against the 90-day visa-free allowance. Authority: Article 21 of the Convention Implementing the Schengen Agreement; confirmed on Spain's official consular entry conditions page.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen State residence permit - Any third-country national holding a residence permit of a Schengen State does not need a visa to enter Estonia. Source page last updated 18.12.2024.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Any third-country national holding a residence permit of a Schengen State does not need a visa to enter Estonia. Source page last updated 18.12.2024.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit (issued by any Schengen member state) - A third-country national holding a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen member state satisfies the visa entry condition for Finland under Schengen Borders Code Article 6(1)(b) (Regulation EU 2016/399): they do not need an additional Finnish or Schengen short-stay visa. Stay subject to the 90/180-day rule. Periods of stay under a residence permit are not counted toward the 90-day limit. Transit through other Schengen states to reach the issuing state also permitted under Article 6(5)(a). Additionally, holders of a residence permit issued by an ETIAS country are exempt from the ETIAS travel authorisation requirement (ETIAS Regulation EU 2018/1240, Article 2(2); confirmed by Finnish Border Guard FAQ at raja.fi).
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: A third-country national holding a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen member state satisfies the visa entry condition for Finland under Schengen Borders Code Article 6(1)(b) (Regulation EU 2016/399): they do not need an additional Finnish or Schengen short-stay visa. Stay subject to the 90/180-day rule. Periods of stay under a residence permit are not counted toward the 90-day limit. Transit through other Schengen states to reach the issuing state also permitted under Article 6(5)(a). Additionally, holders of a residence permit issued by an ETIAS country are exempt from the ETIAS travel authorisation requirement (ETIAS Regulation EU 2018/1240, Article 2(2); confirmed by Finnish Border Guard FAQ at raja.fi).

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: carte de résident de longue durée-UE (EU long-term residence permit) - Holder of a valid EU long-term residence card (carte de résident de longue durée-UE) issued by another EU member state (Directive 2003/109/CE), plus eligible family members as defined in Article 2(2) of Directive 2004/38. Exempts holder from requiring a long-stay visa to cross into France. The holder must satisfy general entry conditions (valid travel document, sufficient resources, no SIS alert). Subject to Articles L.313-4-1 and L.313-11-1 of the French Code on Entry and Stay of Foreigners.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Holder of a valid EU long-term residence card (carte de résident de longue durée-UE) issued by another EU member state (Directive 2003/109/CE), plus eligible family members as defined in Article 2(2) of Directive 2004/38. Exempts holder from requiring a long-stay visa to cross into France. The holder must satisfy general entry conditions (valid travel document, sufficient resources, no SIS alert). Subject to Articles L.313-4-1 and L.313-11-1 of the French Code on Entry and Stay of Foreigners.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Under the Agreement between the Federated States of Micronesia and the European Union on the short-stay visa waiver, signed and entered into provisional application 20 September 2016, citizens of EU member states - excluding Ireland, which opted out per protocols annexed to the EU treaties - may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period. UK citizens are also excluded following Brexit. Applies to holders of valid ordinary, diplomatic, service/official, or special passports issued by EU member states. Excludes travel for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity. Formalised by Council Decision (EU) 2016/1879 and Council Decision (EU) 2017/234. The UK opted out pre-Brexit and remains excluded post-Brexit. Confirmed by EEAS press announcement and EUR-Lex CELEX:22016A1025(01). Agreement remains in effect as of 2026.

EEA: valid common format residence permit (EEA state or Switzerland, pursuant to Council Regulation (EC) No. 1030/2002) - TWOV scheme - landside transit only. Must hold a valid common format residence permit issued by an EEA state or Switzerland pursuant to Council Regulation (EC) No. 1030/2002. All TWOV 2 base requirements apply. Physical documents only - electronic versions not accepted. Source: TWOV 3(h), Home Office Transit Guidance v9, 25 March 2026.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: TWOV scheme - landside transit only. Must hold a valid common format residence permit issued by an EEA state or Switzerland pursuant to Council Regulation (EC) No. 1030/2002. All TWOV 2 base requirements apply. Physical documents only - electronic versions not accepted. Source: TWOV 3(h), Home Office Transit Guidance v9, 25 March 2026.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit - Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen member state may travel to other Schengen member states, including Greece, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, provided they meet entry conditions. Governed by Article 21 of the Schengen Convention as amended.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit issued by any Schengen member state may travel to other Schengen member states, including Greece, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, provided they meet entry conditions. Governed by Article 21 of the Schengen Convention as amended.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: any valid EU member state residence permit - Nationals of Category B countries holding a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state are treated as Category A and may enter Guatemala without a Guatemalan visa for up to 90 days. Sourced from Acuerdo IGM-015-2025 (image-based PDF, Article 10 not extractable as text). Category C nationals are excluded.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Nationals of Category B countries holding a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state are treated as Category A and may enter Guatemala without a Guatemalan visa for up to 90 days. Sourced from Acuerdo IGM-015-2025 (image-based PDF, Article 10 not extractable as text). Category C nationals are excluded.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit - Residence permit issued by one of the Schengen Area Member States. Permit and passport must be valid at moment of entry, during stay, and at departure. Passport valid for at least 3 months after planned departure from Croatia. Stay not to exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Residence permit issued by one of the Schengen Area Member States. Permit and passport must be valid at moment of entry, during stay, and at departure. Passport valid for at least 3 months after planned departure from Croatia. Stay not to exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: valid EU permanent residence card (as defined in EC Regulations 2006 / Directive 2004/38/EC) - Holders of a valid EU permanent residence card (issued under Directive 2004/38/EC) are exempt from Irish visa requirement under Article 3(b)(ii) of S.I. No. 473/2014 (as amended). Applies regardless of nationality.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Holders of a valid EU permanent residence card (issued under Directive 2004/38/EC) are exempt from Irish visa requirement under Article 3(b)(ii) of S.I. No. 473/2014 (as amended). Applies regardless of nationality.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EEA/EFTA: any valid residence permit issued by an EEA/EFTA country - Non-EEA/EFTA nationals who hold a valid residence permit issued by another EEA/EFTA country may enter Iceland without a separate Iceland visa, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Non-EEA/EFTA nationals who hold a valid residence permit issued by another EEA/EFTA country may enter Iceland without a separate Iceland visa, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit - Lo straniero già residente in uno Stato Schengen e titolare di permesso di soggiorno, è esente da visto per soggiorni non superiori a 90 giorni su un periodo di 180 giorni. [Official Italian MFA: A foreigner already resident in a Schengen State and holder of a residence permit is exempt from visa requirement for stays not exceeding 90 days in a 180-day period.] Must present valid residence permit and valid travel document. Must not be on the Schengen Information System alert list. Must fulfil standard Schengen entry conditions (Article 5(1)(a),(c),(e) of the Schengen Borders Code).
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Lo straniero già residente in uno Stato Schengen e titolare di permesso di soggiorno, è esente da visto per soggiorni non superiori a 90 giorni su un periodo di 180 giorni. [Official Italian MFA: A foreigner already resident in a Schengen State and holder of a residence permit is exempt from visa requirement for stays not exceeding 90 days in a 180-day period.] Must present valid residence permit and valid travel document. Must not be on the Schengen Information System alert list. Must fulfil standard Schengen entry conditions (Article 5(1)(a),(c),(e) of the Schengen Borders Code).

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: any valid EU residence permit - Citizens of Syria and Yemen holding a residence permit issued by any EU country are visa-free for Jordan for 1 month per 6-month period. Residence permit must be valid for at least 6 months. Non-refundable return or circle trip ticket required. Note: e-visa is NOT available for Syria; Syria must apply via embassy if not holding qualifying credential. Source: Wikipedia citing Timatic/IATA.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Citizens of Syria and Yemen holding a residence permit issued by any EU country are visa-free for Jordan for 1 month per 6-month period. Residence permit must be valid for at least 6 months. Non-refundable return or circle trip ticket required. Note: e-visa is NOT available for Syria; Syria must apply via embassy if not holding qualifying credential. Source: Wikipedia citing Timatic/IATA.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid visa (including permanent residency) of any of 32 European countries: Greece, Netherlands, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Latvia, Romania, Luxembourg, Lithuania, Liechtenstein, Malta, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, Slovakia, Slovenia, Iceland, Ireland, Estonia, United Kingdom, Austria, Italy, Czech Republic, Croatia, Portugal, Poland, France, Finland, Hungary - B-2 Tourist in Transit status. Applies to nationals of countries that require a visa to enter Korea. Traveller must be transiting through Korea en route to or from one of the 32 European countries, or has departed from one of those countries and transits through Korea bound for country of origin or a third country. Must hold confirmed onward flight departing within 30 days. Visa must be affixed as a sticker on the passport. Must not have been denied entry to Korea within past 3 years; must not have received fine of KRW 5 million+ or deportation order; must have stayed no more than 3 days in any prior transit country. Resumed April 30, 2023. The 32 qualifying European countries are: Greece, Netherlands, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Latvia, Romania, Luxembourg, Lithuania, Liechtenstein, Malta, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, Slovakia, Slovenia, Iceland, Ireland, Estonia, United Kingdom, Austria, Italy, Czech Republic, Croatia, Portugal, Poland, France, Finland, Hungary.

Must hold confirmed onward flight departing within 30 days. Visa must be affixed as a sticker on the passport. EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid residence permit issued by a Schengen area Member State - If the non-EU national has a valid residence permit issued by another Schengen area Member State, no visa is required. Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period. Verbatim from guichet.public.lu/sejour: 'If the non-EU national has a valid residence permit for family members of an EU citizen or a valid residence permit issued by another Schengen area Member State, no visa is required.'
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: If the non-EU national has a valid residence permit issued by another Schengen area Member State, no visa is required. Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period. Verbatim from guichet.public.lu/sejour: 'If the non-EU national has a valid residence permit for family members of an EU citizen or a valid residence permit issued by another Schengen area Member State, no visa is required.'

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid residence permit - Any third-country national holding a valid residence permit issued by any other Schengen State can enter Latvia without a separate Latvian visa. Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period in Schengen states other than the issuing state.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Any third-country national holding a valid residence permit issued by any other Schengen State can enter Latvia without a separate Latvian visa. Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period in Schengen states other than the issuing state.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU: any valid residence permit (excluding transit visa), issued by an EU Member State or Schengen Agreement state - Holders of a valid residence permit or valid visa (excluding transit visas) issued by one of the Member States of the European Union or one of the States Parties to the Schengen Agreement, by the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the United States of America, or Canada may travel to the Republic of Moldova during the validity of that document. Applies to nationals listed under Footnote [2] of the official MFA visa regime page.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Holders of a valid residence permit or valid visa (excluding transit visas) issued by one of the Member States of the European Union or one of the States Parties to the Schengen Agreement, by the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the United States of America, or Canada may travel to the Republic of Moldova during the validity of that document. Applies to nationals listed under Footnote [2] of the official MFA visa regime page.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: permanent residence permit (any Schengen Area member state) - Permanent residents of any Schengen Area country of any nationality do not require a Mexican visa for tourism, business, or transit.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Permanent residents of any Schengen Area country of any nationality do not require a Mexican visa for tourism, business, or transit.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: EU or Schengen: temporary or permanent residence permit - Third-country nationals holding a valid temporary or permanent residence permit issued by an EU Member State or Schengen Agreement signatory country may enter visa-free for no longer than 15 days upon every entry, with total stay not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid temporary or permanent residence permit issued by an EU Member State or Schengen Agreement signatory country may enter visa-free for no longer than 15 days upon every entry, with total stay not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

EU_RESIDENCE.notes: Schengen: any valid Schengen residence permit (Type C short-stay or Type D long-stay visa / national long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state) - Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit or long-stay visa (Type D national visa) issued by any Schengen Member State are authorised to enter Malta (and other Schengen states) for transit or short stays without an additional Schengen visa, provided the total stay does not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period and all other entry conditions of Article 6(1) of the Schengen Borders Code are met (valid travel document, sufficient means, no security threat). Entry is for transit to reach the issuing Schengen state or for short-stay visits. Other conditions of Art.6(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/399 still apply.
EU_RESIDENCE.conditions: Third-country nationals holding a valid residence permit or long-stay visa (Type D national visa) issued by any Schengen Member State are authorised to enter Malta (and other Schengen states) for transit or short stays without an additional Schengen visa, provided the total stay does not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period and all other entry conditions of Article 6(1) of the Schengen Borders Code are met (valid travel document, sufficient means, no security threat). This is an MVV-waiver for long-stay entry, not a Schengen short-stay provision. Source: IND MVV Exemptions page.

Acceptable status documents include: valid Form I-551, foreign passport with valid temporary I-551 stamp (ADIT), foreign passport with temporary I-551 printed notation on immigrant visa with CBP admission stamp, expired Form I-551 with Form I-797 for pending I-751/I-829/I-90, valid re-entry permit (Form I-327), Form I-94 with unexpired ADIT stamp and passport-style photo.

OCI.notes: India: OCI card / e-OCI - OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card grants a lifelong multiple-entry visa for entry into India for any purpose. No stay limit. Exempt from FRRO/FRO registration for any length of stay. As of the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (effective May 1, 2026, Gazette of India), the OCI credential is now issued digitally as an 'e-OCI' (QR-coded certificate); physical cards remain available on request but are no longer required for travel or immigration clearance. OCI cardholders must obtain a Digital e-Arrival Card before boarding flights to India. OCI card (or e-OCI) must be carried along with the foreign passport. Eligible to persons who were citizens of India at any time after 26 January 1950, or who were eligible to become citizens of India as on 26 January 1950, or who belonged to a territory that became part of India after 15 August 1947, and their children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and spouses of Indian citizens or OCI cardholders (marriage subsisting for at least two years). Not available to citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh. Special/restricted area permits still required for certain zones (e.g. parts of Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh).
