Holders of diplomatic or service passports issued by Brazil, China, and Russia do not require a visa to enter Republic of the Congo.
Chinese nationals holding passports endorsed 'For Public Affairs' (公务护照, a special Chinese passport category below diplomatic/service but above ordinary) do not require a visa.

Bilateral Agreement on Exemption Visitor Visa signed in 1987. Only holders of Diplomatic passports of China (PRC) may enter Colombia without a visitor visa for up to 30 days. Official and Service passport holders are NOT covered by this agreement.

Holders of valid diplomatic passports, service passports, and passports for public affairs of China may enter Comoros without a visa for a stay of less than 30 days. Mutual visa exemption agreement between the People's Republic of China and the Union of Comoros; entered into force 26 February 2016.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports of these thirteen countries are exempt from visa requirement. Ordinary passport holders of Georgia, Moldova, Serbia, Ukraine have ordinary biometric passport visa-free access. Armenia, China, Iran, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Russia ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Only holders of diplomatic passports from China (People's Republic of China) are exempt from the visa requirement, irrespective of whether they enter Denmark to perform official duties. Note: holders of Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passports are visa-free under ordinary passport rules (listed separately in visa_policy).

Holders of diplomatic passports, service passports, and passports for public affairs issued by China are visa-exempt for up to 30 days per entry. Based on the bilateral mutual visa exemption agreement between the People's Republic of China and Eritrea, entered into force 2015-04-15. Individuals intending to stay beyond 30 days must complete residence formalities with local authorities.

Holders of diplomatic, service/official and special passports issued by the People's Republic of China are exempt from Schengen visa requirements for Spain. Bilateral agreement recorded in EU OJ 2023/C 340/09 (27 September 2023).
Holders of diplomatic passports of the People's Republic of China. 90 days in any 180-day period.

Holders of valid Chinese diplomatic passports are exempt from the short-stay visa requirement for Finland and the entire Schengen Area under the EU-China Agreement on short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports. Agreement provisionally applied from 12 February 2016; in force 1 January 2017 (Council Decisions 2016/431 and 2016/2044). Covers diplomatic passports only; service, official, and ordinary passport holders are not covered by this agreement. Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period.
Dispense de visa s'appliquant seulement aux titulaires d'un passeport diplomatique. Max stay 3 months. Source: Arrêté du 10 mai 2010 (as amended), Annexe B §1, in force from 19 June 2025.

Airside transit only without a visa. Applies to People's Republic of China nationals holding a Diplomatic or Service passport. Footnote 1 in UK Visa Requirements for International Carriers (April 2026). Landside transit and standard visitor entry still requires a visa.

Holders of valid diplomatic passports, service passports, and passports for public affairs (official passports) issued by the People's Republic of China (including Hong Kong and Macao SAR) may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for 30 days. Based on bilateral visa exemption agreement between Georgia and China in force since 3 February 1994 (as referenced in China NIA mutual visa exemption records). Ordinary passport holders from China are separately covered by the 11 September 2023 ordinance and the 28 May 2024 bilateral agreement (30 days, tourism only) and are listed in visa_free.
Holders of Diplomatic and Service passports issued by the People's Republic of China are exempt from visa requirements for stays not exceeding 90 days.

Holders of Chinese diplomatic passports, service passports, and passports for public affairs (official) do not require a visa for Guinea for a maximum stay of 30 days. Agreement on mutual visa exemption effective 16 September 2017. Nationals holding ordinary Chinese passports endorsed 'for public affairs' are also covered for 30-day visa-free stay.
Holders of diplomatic passports from China are visa-free; service and ordinary passport holders require a visa. Per bilateral agreement referenced in the Hellenic Republic MFA country visa table.
Chinese diplomatic and service passport holders enter visa-free. MFA verbatim: 'China (People's Republic of) for holders of Diplomatic/Service Passports'.

Chinese nationals holding valid Diplomatic Passports, Service Passports, or Public Affairs Passports (Pasaportes de Asuntos Públicos) are exempt from visa requirements for entry, exit, transit, or stay in Honduras for up to 30 days from date of entry. Those wishing to stay beyond 30 days or for purposes other than tourism/transit must obtain a visa in advance. Holders assigned as members of a diplomatic/consular mission must still obtain the appropriate Diplomatic or Consular visa. Agreement signed Beijing, 12 June 2023 (Acuerdo Ejecutivo No. 09-DGAJTC-2023). NOTE: Chinese ordinary passport holders require a consular visa to enter Honduras. El Heraldo fact-check (citing INM) confirms that the bilateral exemption does NOT extend to ordinary passports; only diplomatic/service/public affairs passport holders are covered. An 'Authorization for Entry Without Visa' from the INM can be issued for specific cases (official missions, humanitarian grounds, work) but this is not a standard visa-free entry right for ordinary passport holders.

Bilateral visa waiver agreement: holders of Chinese diplomatic passports may enter Hungary visa-free for up to 90 days. Chinese service passport holders receive only 30 days (separate entry). NOTE: Visa-free travel for diplomatic, service and official passports is temporarily suspended until 6 March 2027 per official Hungarian consular information.

Bilateral visa waiver agreement: holders of Chinese service passports may enter Hungary visa-free for up to 30 days. Chinese diplomatic passport holders receive 90 days (separate entry). NOTE: Visa-free travel for diplomatic, service and official passports is temporarily suspended until 6 March 2027 per official Hungarian consular information.

Holders of diplomatic, service, and special passports of China are exempt from entry visa per bilateral agreement signed June 6, 2022. Stay duration not stated in the official mofa.gov.iq announcement.
Holders of diplomatic passports issued by China are exempt from the visa requirement for Iceland. Service and ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Nationals of these countries require a visa on ordinary passports but are exempt on diplomatic or service (official) passports. Sourced from the official Israeli MFA Tourist Visa Table (2022_Foreign_Visa_to_Israel.pdf). China note: 'Diplomatic/Service Passports exempted for 90 days'. BIH (Bosnia Herzegovina) removed from this list: the 2022 tourist visa table shows BIH national as 'req.' and official as 'exe.' - Bosnia should be in this list; added in corrections. Turkey: 2022 table shows national as 'req.' and official as 'exe.' - confirmed.

Holders of diplomatic passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. Exemption applies only to national territory of Italy; does not extend automatically to other Schengen states unless covered by a separate bilateral agreement with those states. NOTE: Georgian diplomatic passport holders are subject to an EU-wide suspension of their visa-free access from 6 March 2026 to 6 March 2027 (Georgia was not in this diplomatic list but the EU suspension for Georgian diplomatic passports is noted separately).

Holders of diplomatic, official or service passports of GCC countries, ASEAN countries, Azerbaijan, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil (30 days), Bulgaria, China, Chile (30 days), Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Djibouti, Egypt, Georgia, Hungary, Kazakhstan (30 days), Lebanon, Peru, Russia, Slovakia, Tunisia, Turkey, and United Kingdom may enter Jordan without a visa for up to 3 months within any 6-month period (unless otherwise stated). Based on bilateral visa suppression/waiver agreements. Source: Wikipedia (Timatic/IATA).

Holders of special passports of China, Egypt, Peru, Russia, Singapore, and United Kingdom may enter Jordan without a visa for 3 months within any 6-month period. Based on bilateral agreements. Source: Wikipedia (Timatic/IATA).
Holders of Diplomatic, Official or Service Passports from the People's Republic of China for a period not exceeding thirty (30) days. Ordinary passport holders from China require eTA.

Bilateral visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic and service passports. Duration varies by country (30–90 days). Countries: Hungary, India, Indonesia, Iran, Republic of Korea, Kuwait, Pakistan, Romania, Serbia, Turkmenistan, Morocco, China, Chile, Brazil, Singapore, Laos, Lebanon, UAE, Bahrain, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Japan. Exact per-country durations not individually published on the MFA page.

Bilateral visa exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and service/official passports only. Ordinary PRC passport holders may additionally benefit from the temporary June–October 2026 pilot program (see conditional_access: temporary_visa_free_pilot). Agreement date listed in Osaka embassy PDF.

Bilateral visa exemption agreement effective 06.11.1989 for diplomatic, service, and official (public affairs) passports. Ordinary Chinese passport holders are NOT visa-free - they must obtain a VOA or e-visa to enter Laos. The 1989 agreement also covers Lao ordinary passports with valid official visas for public affairs travel (not relevant to Chinese ordinary passport holders seeking tourist/general entry). The temporary 15-day visa-free entry for Chinese tourists under Visit Laos Year 2024 ended December 31, 2024.

Holders of Chinese Diplomatic Passports may enter Liberia visa-free under a mutual visa exemption agreement. Effective date: February 10, 2016, per China MFA official list of mutual visa exemption agreements (cs.mfa.gov.cn). Also referenced in Liberia MOFA cooperation agreements list (mofa.gov.lr, listed September 5, 2016). Covers diplomatic passports only; ordinary, service, and official passports are NOT covered. Note: China is also among the 23 countries whose citizens must apply at the Liberian embassy for an ordinary visa rather than use the e-VoA, consistent with a functional Liberian embassy existing in China.
Diplomatic passport only. Bilateral visa exemption agreement signed 11 December 2015, entered into force 29 January 2016. Non-working stays of a maximum of 90 days within any 180-day period.
Diplomatic, Official, Service and Public Affairs endorsement passport holders from China; 30 days; visit for official purposes; gratis (no fee)

Citizens of China holding diplomatic or service passports may enter Lesotho without a visa for up to 30 days, under the Agreement on Mutual Visa Exemption between the People's Republic of China and the Kingdom of Lesotho (entered into force 24 August 2016). Stays exceeding 30 days require residence formalities with local authorities. Ordinary Chinese passport holders still require a visa. The reciprocal arrangement covers diplomatic and official passports of Lesotho for entry to China.
Chinese holders of diplomatic passports may enter Latvia without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under bilateral visa waiver agreement. Ordinary Chinese passports require a visa.

Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, special, and/or official passports (specific passport types vary by country) per bilateral visa abolition agreements signed between Morocco and each listed country. Full per-country breakdown of covered passport types available at the official source URL. The specific passport type covered for each country is documented in the official table (diplomatic / service / special / official columns).

Diplomatic and service passport holders of China, Iran and Turkmenistan are exempt from Moldova visa requirements for up to 30 days, based on bilateral agreements. Ordinary passport holders of these countries require a visa (China is Footnote [2] - credential-based conditional access; Iran/Turkmenistan are Footnote [1] - must obtain a visa unless diplomatic/service/special passport).

Holders of diplomatic, service, and public affairs (gong wu) passports of China are visa-free for stays of less than 30 days pursuant to a bilateral mutual visa exemption agreement in force from 4 November 2023. Madagascar passports covered: diplomatic and service passports. The Chinese MFA list describes Chinese coverage as 'diplomatic, service passports, passports for public affairs of China.'
Diplomatic and Service passport holders only. Bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Nationals of Belarus, China, Georgia (all passports), India (diplomatic only), Iran, Indonesia, and Mongolia holding diplomatic, official, or service passports may enter North Macedonia visa-free under bilateral waiver agreements. India: diplomatic passport only (not service/official). Specific stay durations not confirmed from official North Macedonian government pages; bilateral agreement texts not directly scrapeable.

Holders of diplomatic and service category passports of Brazil, China, Cuba, Russia, and Rwanda do not require a visa for a maximum period of 90 days. Chinese nationals with public affairs passports also receive 90 days.

Citizens of the People's Republic of China holding valid diplomatic or service passports (excluding Chinese 'public affairs' service passports per Article X of the agreement) may enter, exit or transit Malta visa-free for up to 30 days. Members of diplomatic/consular missions during their term of posting are also covered. Stays beyond 30 days require application through diplomatic channels. Officials at vice-ministerial level or above / major-general rank or above must notify Malta 5 working days before travel for official purposes. Agreement signed in Valletta on 18 December 2007; entry into force per notification procedure under Article X.
Diplomatic and Official/Service passport holders only; 30 days each. Ordinary passport holders use Tourist Visa on Arrival (pilot program active through 29 Aug 2026).
Diplomatic and official passport, Up to 30 days / 1989.03.30. Ordinary passport holders are NOT exempt; they require an e-visa.
Visa abolition limited to diplomatic and service passport holders only.
Holders of diplomatic passports (and service passports for public affairs) of China are exempt from visa requirements for stays up to 30 days. Agreement entered into force on December 15, 2018.

Holders of Chinese diplomatic passports are visa-free for short stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen Area (including European Netherlands). Based on EU-China Agreement on short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports, Council Decision (EU) 2016/431, in force 1 January 2017. Applies to all Schengen member states. Ordinary Chinese passports still require a Schengen visa.
Chinese diplomatic passport - applies to diplomats who are not going to work at the embassy in Norway.

Holders of diplomatic and official passports of the People's Republic of China are exempt from visa requirement to enter, stay up to 30 days, exit, and transit through Nepal. Based on bilateral agreement. Note: Chinese ordinary passport holders receive a gratis (free) visa on arrival - not visa-free.
Holders of Hong Kong (China) diplomatic and official passports may enter Pakistan without a visa for up to one month. Entry 19 in dgip.gov.pk visa abolition table (as of 21-02-2024).

Visa-free entry for holders of Chinese diplomatic, official (公务), or official ordinary (因公普通) passports. Stay not exceeding 30 days. Requires an official invitation and a designated hosting/receiving unit in North Korea. Those intending to stay longer than 30 days, or to work, study, establish permanent residence, or conduct journalism, must apply for a visa before entry. Holders of private ordinary passports (因私普通护照) must obtain a visa outside North Korea before arrival. Agreement originally effective 1956-10-01 (diplomatic and official passports) and 1965-01-01 (official ordinary passports); updated/re-notified effective 2024-07-26. Re-confirmed June 2026 via kp.china-embassy.gov.cn.

Holders of diplomatic and service/official passports of the listed 29 countries are granted visa-free entry for 90 days under bilateral visa suppression agreements. China also includes Public Affairs passport holders. These exemptions apply only to diplomatic/service/official passport holders; ordinary passport holders of these countries are subject to standard visa-on-arrival or free-visa-on-arrival rules by nationality.

Holders of Chinese diplomatic, service, and official (passports for public affairs) passports are Category A (visa-exempt); ordinary passport holders require visa on arrival (Category B). Agreement entered into force 2014-05-03.

Holders of diplomatic, public affairs and service passports issued by the PRC are exempted from visa requirements for a stay of up to 30 days in Singapore under long-standing bilateral arrangements, subsequently affirmed through an exchange of diplomatic notes following the 19th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation on 7 December 2023.

Mutual Visa Exemption Agreement between People's Republic of China and Solomon Islands, in force 24 November 2022. Covers holders of valid diplomatic passports, service passports, and passports for public affairs (gongwu/official) of the PRC. Stay not to exceed 30 days from date of entry. Work prohibited. A separate ordinary passport agreement entered into force 28 December 2024 (see visa_policy.visa_free).

Agreement Between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Sierra Leone on Mutual Visa Exemption for Holders of Diplomatic and Service Passports, entered into force 24 December 2018. Covers holders of valid diplomatic or service passports (including passports for public affairs) of the PRC. Stay must not exceed 30 days; stays exceeding 30 days require registration with competent authorities. Diplomatic/consular mission members and families holding qualifying passports are exempt for the duration of accreditation. Ordinary passport holders are NOT exempt - they qualify for landing visa under BRICS/non-AU category.

Holders of Chinese diplomatic passports, service passports, and passports for public affairs. Agreement entered into force 2018-02-03 per China MFA official list. STP domestic implementing instrument: Decree n. 09/2017 of 25 April 2017. The Chinese MFA official source specifies 30 days and covers 'passports for public affairs' in addition to diplomatic and service passports.

Holders of a valid Chinese diplomatic passport are visa-free for short stays in Slovenia (and all Schengen area states) under the EU-China short-stay visa waiver agreement for holders of diplomatic passports. Maximum 90 days in any 180-day period. Agreement entered into force 1 January 2017.

Holder of a Diplomatic Passport does not require a visa (service passport holders do require a visa). Footnote **) on the Swedish Government's official list of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when entering Sweden (last updated 01 September 2023). Applies to mainland China excluding Hong Kong and Macao.
Service/diplomatic/official passport holders only. Ordinary Chinese passport holders qualify only under the 55+ age-based exemption for 14 days.
Visa-free entry for up to 30 days. Ordinary passport holders require a visa. Bilateral agreement referenced on Turkmenistan MFA consular page.
Bearers of valid Diplomatic, Official or Service passports do not require visas. Per agreement dated 25th October 2006 (SI 25/98).

Holders of diplomatic or service passports of China may enter Tunisia visa-free for up to 30 days per bilateral agreement effective 29 September 2006. Reciprocal: diplomatic and special passports of Tunisia entering China also exempt. Does not extend to ordinary passports (which now have a separate tourism visa-free arrangement since October 2023). Longer stays require residence formalities with local authorities.
Holders of diplomatic and service passports of the People's Republic of China may enter Tanzania without a visa for up to 30 days. Bilateral mutual visa exemption agreement, effective 11 July 2005.

China (República Popular China): ordinary passport holders require a prior consular visa (with conditional exception for holders of valid US/Canada/UK/EU visa - see credential entries). Diplomatic passport holders only are visa-free for up to 30 days. Bilateral diplomatic passport agreement. Service/official passports not confirmed in this exemption.
Visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic passports of China (up to 30 days). Accredited diplomatic mission employees and family members may stay for the entire period of work without a visa.

Bilateral visa exemption agreements between Vietnam and each listed country for diplomatic and/or official passport holders. Stay duration varies by bilateral agreement and not individually specified in the official source reviewed. Cuba also includes Seaman's passports and ordinary passports for official missions. Brazil agreement dated 12 February 2005 covers diplomatic passports only. Source: Vietnam Government Portal official visa exemption page.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports issued by the Russian Federation, People's Republic of China, Arab Republic of Egypt, Republic of Indonesia, and Ukraine may enter, transit or stay up to 15 days in Kosovo. Note: ordinary passport holders from Russia and China require a visa.
Diplomatic, Official and Service passport holders only

Holders of Chinese diplomatic or service passports may enter Zimbabwe visa-free for up to 60 days under the Mutual Visa Exemption MOU between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Republic of Zimbabwe for holders of Diplomatic and Service Passports, effective 12 November 2014. Stays beyond 60 days require registration with competent authorities.

Chinese nationals holding Diplomatic, Official, Service, or Public passports are eligible for VOA. The 2025 ICA handbook states: 'Citizens of China who are Diplomatic, Official, Service and Public passports holders can get Visa on Arrival (VoA) in Papua New Guinea.' The live ICA VOA page specifies 'China (Diplomatic, Official and Service Passport only)' - the 2025 handbook additionally adds 'Public' passport class. Ordinary Chinese passport holders under tour groups are covered separately. Duration not stated on ICA page.

Ordinary-passport holders of China are not eTA-exempt and must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) before travel; only Diplomatic, Official or Service passport holders (max 30 days) are exempt (see conditional_access). Per evisa.go.ke/general-information (verified 2026-07)

Ordinary Chinese passport holders are eligible for the Lao e-Visa; China is explicitly listed on the official 'Who Can Apply' page (laoevisa.gov.la, Consular Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs LAO PDR). e-Visa valid 60 days from issuance; maximum stay 30 days, single-entry; fee USD 50. Ordinary Chinese passport holders are NOT visa-free (the 1989 bilateral agreement covers only diplomatic/service/official passports); the Visit Laos Year 2024 temporary 15-day exemption ended 31 December 2024. Chinese travellers use e-Visa or visa on arrival. (verified 2026-07)

VNM.notes: Acordo sobre Isenção de Vistos em Passaportes Diplomáticos e de Serviço, signed 03.04.2008. Ordinary Vietnamese passport holders are NOT on the visa-free list and require a visa to enter Angola.
Diplomatic, service and official passport holders of Vietnam may enter Albania visa-free under a bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.
Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Vietnam do not require a visa to enter Bulgaria. Ordinary passport holders require a visa. Source: official MFA table, last updated 14 January 2025.

Holders of Vietnamese diplomatic and official passports can enter Brazil without visas for a stay of up to 90 days (or up to the period of their mission, in case of Vietnamese officials accredited by the Brazilian government). For all other purposes or cases, a visa is required prior to entering Brazil.
Bilateral visa exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic passports. Non-working stays up to 90 days in 180-day period. Agreement entered into force 16 August 2009.

Holders of diplomatic or service category passports issued to nationals of Austria, Brazil, China, Gabon, Israel, South Africa, Turkey, Uganda, Venezuela and Vietnam do not require a visa for Côte d'Ivoire. Source: Côte d'Ivoire Ministry of Foreign Affairs official document dated 15 March 2013 (Conseil aux voyageurs / Annexe.pdf). Note: The CEPICI PDF (2018) lists these same countries with 'passeport ordinaire' notation for some (e.g., South Africa, Gabon, Israel, Uganda, Brazil) in the 'visa required but no prior DST consultation' list - this indicates their ORDINARY passports require a visa, while diplomatic/service passports are exempt as per the 2013 MFA Annexe document. No stay duration specified in source.
Bilateral visa exemption agreement in force for diplomatic passports only (not service passports); 30 days. Exact agreement date not published on checked official sources.

Bilateral Agreement on Exemption Visitor Visa signed in 2012. Holders of Diplomatic and Official passports of Vietnam may enter Colombia without a visitor visa for up to 90 days. Service passport holders are NOT covered.

Holders of diplomatic or official passports of Vietnam, South Korea, Pakistan, and Bahrain are exempt from visa requirement. South Korea ordinary passport holders also have ordinary passport visa-free access. Vietnam, Pakistan, Bahrain ordinary passport holders require a visa.
Diplomatic or official/service passport holders only are visa-free. Confirmed at Embassy of Algeria in Oslo and Dublin.
Holders of diplomatic passports of Vietnam. 90 days in any 180-day period.
Dispense de visa s'appliquant seulement aux titulaires d'un passeport diplomatique. Max stay 3 months. Source: Arrêté du 10 mai 2010 (as amended), Annexe B §1, in force from 19 June 2025.

Airside transit only without a visa. Applies to Vietnamese nationals holding a Diplomatic or Official passport. Footnote 5 in UK Visa Requirements for International Carriers (April 2026). Landside transit and standard visitor entry still requires a visa.

Holders of diplomatic or service passports issued by CPLP (Community of Portuguese Language Countries) member states do not require a visa for an indefinite period of stay. Based on the multilateral CPLP 'Acordo sobre Supressão de Vistos em Passaportes Diplomáticos, Especiais e de Serviço'. Ordinary passport holders from these countries are NOT covered by this rule (subject to normal visa requirements unless separately exempt as ECOWAS members). Note: an Africa Visa Openness 2025 report (visaopenness.org) claims Guinea-Bissau switched São Tomé and Príncipe from visa-on-arrival to visa-free status for ordinary passports in 2025, but this could not be confirmed from an official Guinea-Bissau government source and commercial sources (Savory & Partners) continue to show visa required - treated as unverified and listed in gaps.

Holders of diplomatic passports from Vietnam are visa-free for up to 90 days in a 180-day period; service and ordinary passport holders require a visa. Per bilateral agreement referenced in the Hellenic Republic MFA country visa table.

Holders of Diplomatic and Official passports of Vietnam may visit the HKSAR visa-free for a stay not exceeding 14 days. Ordinary passport holders are required to hold a valid visa. Note: from October 2024 IMMD extended multiple-entry visa validity to 3 years for ordinary Vietnamese nationals, but ordinary passport holders still require a visa.

Holders of Vietnamese diplomatic and official passports may enter Croatia without a visa under a bilateral Agreement on Visa Cancellation for Holders of Diplomatic and Official Passports signed in Hanoi on 29 October 2009. Exact stay duration limit not confirmed from official source; check full agreement text.

Bilateral visa waiver agreement: holders of Vietnamese diplomatic or service passports may enter Hungary visa-free for up to 90 days. NOTE: Visa-free travel for diplomatic, service and official passports is temporarily suspended until 6 March 2027 per official Hungarian consular information.

Nationals of Kenya, Rwanda, and Vietnam require a visa on ordinary and service passports, but are exempt on diplomatic passports only. Kenya remark: 'Exe only for diplomatic Passport'. Rwanda remark: 'Only for diplomatic passport'. Vietnam remark: 'Only for Diplomatic passports'. Sourced from the official Israeli MFA Tourist Visa Table (2022_Foreign_Visa_to_Israel.pdf).

Holders of diplomatic passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. Exemption applies only to national territory of Italy; does not extend automatically to other Schengen states unless covered by a separate bilateral agreement with those states. NOTE: Georgian diplomatic passport holders are subject to an EU-wide suspension of their visa-free access from 6 March 2026 to 6 March 2027 (Georgia was not in this diplomatic list but the EU suspension for Georgian diplomatic passports is noted separately).

Holders of diplomatic, official or service passports of GCC countries, ASEAN countries, Azerbaijan, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil (30 days), Bulgaria, China, Chile (30 days), Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Djibouti, Egypt, Georgia, Hungary, Kazakhstan (30 days), Lebanon, Peru, Russia, Slovakia, Tunisia, Turkey, and United Kingdom may enter Jordan without a visa for up to 3 months within any 6-month period (unless otherwise stated). Based on bilateral visa suppression/waiver agreements. Source: Wikipedia (Timatic/IATA).
Bilateral visa exemption agreement effective 17.07.1977 for diplomatic and service passports (30 days). Ordinary passport holders also visa-free (30 days, agreement effective 05.03.2004).
Diplomatic passport only. Bilateral visa exemption agreement signed 22 May 2009, entered into force 16 August 2009. Non-working stays of a maximum of 90 days within any 180-day period.

Diplomatic and Official passport holders from Vietnam; 90 days; visit for official purposes; gratis (no fee). CORRECTED: 'service' passport type removed - live official page lists Diplomatic or Official for Vietnam.

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Lithuania and the Government of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on the Exemption of Visa Requirement for Holders of Diplomatic Passports. Signed Hanoi 23/01/2019; entered into force 17/11/2019. Covers diplomatic passports only (not service or official passports). Vietnamese ordinary passport holders require a Schengen visa.

Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, special, and/or official passports (specific passport types vary by country) per bilateral visa abolition agreements signed between Morocco and each listed country. Full per-country breakdown of covered passport types available at the official source URL. The specific passport type covered for each country is documented in the official table (diplomatic / service / special / official columns).

Footnote [1] on the official MFA page: ordinary passport holders of these countries appear in the visa-REQUIRED section and need a visa or e-visa to enter Moldova. Only holders of diplomatic, service and special passports retain a treaty-based visa exemption under international agreements in force at the time the relevant Moldovan law was adopted. Max stay not specified on official source.

Diplomatic and service passport holders of these countries are exempt from Moldova visa requirements for up to 90 days within any 6-month period, based on bilateral visa waiver agreements. Ordinary passport holders of these countries are separately covered by unconditional visa-free access.
Diplomatic and Official passport holders. Bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.
Diplomatic and Official passport, Up to 90 days / 2024.03.07. Separate from the ordinary-passport 30-day waiver.
Diplomatic and Service passport holders of Vietnam only: visa-free entry up to 90 days, Tourist & Business. Ordinary Vietnamese passport holders require eVisa.

Agreement on waiver of visa requirements for holders of valid Diplomatic and Official Passports signed 30 October 2019 at Presidential Villa, Abuja (witnessed by Vice President Yemi Osinbajo and Vietnamese Deputy PM Vuong Dinh Hue). Effective 29 November 2019. Holders may enter, exit, and transit Nigeria without a visa for a maximum of 90 days from date of entry. No standalone official Nigerian MFA/NIS press-release page was accessible at time of research; source is Channels Television (state-accredited Nigerian broadcaster reporting the signing ceremony at the Presidential Villa).
Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of Vietnam are exempt from visa requirement to enter, stay up to 90 days, exit, and transit through Nepal. Based on bilateral agreement.
Holders of Vietnamese diplomatic and official passports may enter Pakistan without a visa for up to three months. Entry 48 in dgip.gov.pk visa abolition table (as of 21-02-2024).

Ordinary passport requires a visa (Resolución 210/15/03/23), obtainable as a visa on arrival at Silvio Pettirossi airport per the official MRE 'Visas de Arribo' page (ordinary Vietnam is now classified visa_on_arrival). Diplomatic, official, and service passports are additionally fully exempt per MRE visas-new page.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter El Salvador. Ordinary passport holders from these countries may face different requirements (Category B or C). The table on rree.gob.sv/visas-para-extranjeros/ only partially rendered during validation (rows A through Azerbaijan visible); this list was cross-referenced from the Wikipedia article on El Salvador visa policy which aggregates the RREE data.
Holders of diplomatic and official passports of Vietnam do not require a visa to travel to Uganda under the bilateral visa abolition agreement.

Vietnam: ordinary passport holders require a prior consular visa (Nota 5). Diplomatic and service/official passport holders are visa-free. Bilateral exemption documented in the Régimen de Visas de Admisión.

Visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic passports of Vietnam (up to 60 days). Ordinary passport holders of Vietnam require a visa. Accredited diplomatic mission employees and family members may stay for the entire period of work without a visa.
Diplomatic, Official and Service passport holders only

Ordinary Vietnamese passport holders are not visa-exempt (only diplomatic/official passports are visa-free under a bilateral agreement) and must obtain Uganda's mandatory pre-travel e-visa online at visas.immigration.go.ug; no visa on arrival. Single-entry tourist visa USD 50, up to 90 days (verified 2026-07).

IDN.notes: Acordo sobre Isenção Mútua de Vistos para titulares de Passaportes Diplomáticos e de Serviço, signed Jakarta 11.04.2017. Ordinary Indonesian passport holders also visa-free under Presidential Decree No. 189/23.

Diplomatic, service and official passport holders of Indonesia may enter Albania visa-free under a bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa. Note: Indonesia ordinary passport holders had a temporary exemption in 2025 that was NOT extended into 2026.
Bilateral agreement; diplomatic and service passports only
Bilateral visa suppression agreement. Indonesian holders of diplomatic and service passports may enter Austria visa-free for up to 90 days. BGBl. Nr. 146/2008.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Indonesia do not require a visa. Agreement on Visa Exemption for Diplomatic and Service Passport Holders between Indonesia and Burundi - ratified as of July 2023 MAE press conference.
Bilateral visa waiver agreement. Applies to holders of diplomatic, service/official, and special passports. Belgium (BNL) applies this in harmonisation with Benelux partners.
Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Indonesia do not require a visa to enter Bulgaria. Ordinary passport holders require a visa. Source: official MFA table, last updated 14 January 2025.
Holders of Indonesian diplomatic and official/service passports are exempt from visa requirements for Bosnia and Herzegovina. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.
Bilateral visa exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and service passports. Non-working stays up to 90 days in 180-day period. Agreement entered into force 22 April 2011.
Only holders of biometric diplomatic and biometric service passports from Indonesia are exempt from the visa requirement, irrespective of whether they enter Denmark to perform official duties.

Holders of diplomatic, service/official and special passports issued by Indonesia are exempt from Schengen visa requirements for Spain. Bilateral agreement recorded in EU OJ 2023/C 340/09 (27 September 2023).

Dispense de visa s'appliquant seulement aux titulaires d'un passeport diplomatique ou de service/officiel. Max stay 3 months. Source: Arrêté du 10 mai 2010 (as amended), Annexe B §1, in force from 19 June 2025.

Citizens of India, Nepal, Peru, Indonesia, Egypt, Guyana, and Sri Lanka holding valid diplomatic or official/service passports issued by their country may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for a specified period under bilateral visa suppression/waiver agreements. Exact stay duration per bilateral agreement not specified on the source page. Confirmed via official Georgian tourism authority source (georgia.travel).

Holders of diplomatic or service passports from Indonesia are visa-free for stays up to 30 days; ordinary passport holders require a visa. Per bilateral agreement referenced in the Hellenic Republic MFA country visa table.

Indonesian diplomatic and service passport holders enter visa-free for up to 30 days. MFA verbatim: 'Indonesia for 30 days for holders of Diplomatic/Service Passports'. Note: ISS eligible-countries page lists Indonesia at 30 days without a passport-type restriction - MFA (primary) restricts to diplomatic/service passports only.

Bilateral visa waiver agreement: holders of Indonesian diplomatic or service passports may enter Hungary visa-free for up to 90 days. NOTE: Visa-free travel for diplomatic, service and official passports is temporarily suspended until 6 March 2027 per official Hungarian consular information.

Holders of a diplomatic passport issued by Indonesia are exempt from Irish visa requirement under Schedule 2 of S.I. No. 473/2014 as substituted by S.I. No. 17/2026 (in force 16 February 2026). Up to 90 days.

Holders of official, service, or special passports issued by the listed states (Schedule 2, S.I. No. 473/2014 as substituted by S.I. No. 17/2026) are exempt from Irish visa requirement ONLY when arriving in the State in the company of a Minister of the Government of that state where that Minister is on an official visit to Ireland (Article 3(f) of S.I. 473/2014 as amended by S.I. 58/2024). Does NOT apply to general official/service passport holders travelling independently. Note: Georgia has been removed from Schedule 2 by S.I. 242/2026 (effective 15 June 2026) and is no longer in this list.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Indonesia exempt from entry visa. Agreement signed September 23, 2024 by Iraqi Deputy PM/FM Fuad Hussein and Indonesian FM Retno Marsudi on the principle of reciprocity. The mofa.gov.iq announcement confirms signing only; entry-into-force date not specified. Wikipedia notes this may not yet be in force.

Holders of diplomatic passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. Exemption applies only to national territory of Italy; does not extend automatically to other Schengen states unless covered by a separate bilateral agreement with those states. NOTE: Georgian diplomatic passport holders are subject to an EU-wide suspension of their visa-free access from 6 March 2026 to 6 March 2027 (Georgia was not in this diplomatic list but the EU suspension for Georgian diplomatic passports is noted separately).

Holders of service/official passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. Exemption applies only to national territory of Italy; does not extend automatically to other Schengen states unless covered by a separate bilateral agreement with those states.

Holders of diplomatic, official or service passports of GCC countries, ASEAN countries, Azerbaijan, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil (30 days), Bulgaria, China, Chile (30 days), Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Djibouti, Egypt, Georgia, Hungary, Kazakhstan (30 days), Lebanon, Peru, Russia, Slovakia, Tunisia, Turkey, and United Kingdom may enter Jordan without a visa for up to 3 months within any 6-month period (unless otherwise stated). Based on bilateral visa suppression/waiver agreements. Source: Wikipedia (Timatic/IATA).

Diplomatic and official passport holders, maximum 30 days. Reciprocal arrangement came into effect July 20, 2016. Ordinary Indonesian passport holders have separate visa exemption arrangement (15-day ePassport registration system).

Bilateral visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic and service passports. Duration varies by country (30–90 days). Countries: Hungary, India, Indonesia, Iran, Republic of Korea, Kuwait, Pakistan, Romania, Serbia, Turkmenistan, Morocco, China, Chile, Brazil, Singapore, Laos, Lebanon, UAE, Bahrain, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Japan. Exact per-country durations not individually published on the MFA page.
Bilateral visa exemption agreement effective 16.07.2001 for diplomatic and service passports (14 days). Ordinary passport holders also visa-free (30 days, agreement effective 23.09.2011).
Diplomatic and service passports. Bilateral visa exemption agreement signed 7 July 2010, entered into force 22 April 2011. Non-working stays of a maximum of 90 days within any 180-day period.
Diplomatic, Official and Service passport holders from Indonesia; 30 days; visit for official purposes; gratis (no fee)

Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, special, and/or official passports (specific passport types vary by country) per bilateral visa abolition agreements signed between Morocco and each listed country. Full per-country breakdown of covered passport types available at the official source URL. The specific passport type covered for each country is documented in the official table (diplomatic / service / special / official columns).

Footnote [1] on the official MFA page: ordinary passport holders of these countries appear in the visa-REQUIRED section and need a visa or e-visa to enter Moldova. Only holders of diplomatic, service and special passports retain a treaty-based visa exemption under international agreements in force at the time the relevant Moldovan law was adopted. Max stay not specified on official source.
Diplomatic, Official, and Service passport holders. Bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Nationals of Belarus, China, Georgia (all passports), India (diplomatic only), Iran, Indonesia, and Mongolia holding diplomatic, official, or service passports may enter North Macedonia visa-free under bilateral waiver agreements. India: diplomatic passport only (not service/official). Specific stay durations not confirmed from official North Macedonian government pages; bilateral agreement texts not directly scrapeable.

Indonesian nationals holding valid diplomatic or service/official passports are exempt from the Schengen visa requirement for Malta under a national derogation communicated to the European Commission. Listed in EU Official Journal notice on national derogations from the visa requirement (2023).
Diplomatic and Official passport, Up to 30 days / 2011.11.15

Diplomatic and Service passport holders of Indonesia: visa-free entry up to 30 days, Tourist & Business. All Indonesian passport types also eligible for ETA (30 days). Ordinary Indonesian passports use the ETA pathway, not the Visa Exempt pathway.
Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Indonesia are exempt from visa requirements for Niger. Ordinary passport holders from Indonesia require a visa.
Indonesian diplomatic and service passports - applies to diplomats who are not going to work at the embassy in Norway.
Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of Indonesia are exempt from visa requirement to enter, stay up to 30 days, exit, and transit through Nepal. Based on bilateral agreement.
Holders of Indonesian diplomatic, official and service passports may enter Pakistan without a visa for up to one month. Entry 17 in dgip.gov.pk visa abolition table (as of 21-02-2024).
Diplomatic passport holders of Indonesia do not require a visa to enter Panama. Ordinary passport holders of Indonesia require an authorized visa.

Bilateral agreement between Peru and Indonesia on visa exemption for holders of diplomatic, special, or service passports. Agreement signed in Lima on 14 November 2024; ratified by Peru via Decreto Supremo N° 006-2025-RE (published 05/02/2025). Exact stay duration to be confirmed from the published agreement text in Diario Oficial El Peruano per Article 2 of the decree.
Ordinary passport requires visa per Ley N°3.569/28/08/2008. Diplomatic, official, and service passports exempt per MRE visas-new page.

Holders of diplomatic and service/official passports of the listed 29 countries are granted visa-free entry for 90 days under bilateral visa suppression agreements. China also includes Public Affairs passport holders. These exemptions apply only to diplomatic/service/official passport holders; ordinary passport holders of these countries are subject to standard visa-on-arrival or free-visa-on-arrival rules by nationality.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter El Salvador. Ordinary passport holders from these countries may face different requirements (Category B or C). The table on rree.gob.sv/visas-para-extranjeros/ only partially rendered during validation (rows A through Azerbaijan visible); this list was cross-referenced from the Wikipedia article on El Salvador visa policy which aggregates the RREE data.

Holder of a Diplomatic Passport or a Service Passport does not require a visa. Footnote *) on the Swedish Government's official list of third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when entering Sweden (last updated 01 September 2023).

Agreement between the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine and the Government of the Republic of Indonesia on Visa Exemption for the Nationals Holding Diplomatic and Service Passports, signed 17 February 2019. Applies to Indonesian nationals holding diplomatic or service passports. Ordinary passport holders use e-visa (separate ordinary-passport waiver agreement signed 29 June 2022 but not confirmed ratified as of research date).

Indonesia: ordinary passport holders require a prior consular visa (Nota 5). Diplomatic and service/official passport holders are visa-free. Bilateral exemption documented in the Régimen de Visas de Admisión.

Bilateral visa waiver agreements between Vietnam and each listed country for diplomatic, official and service passport holders. 30-day stay. Source: Vietnam Government Portal official visa exemption page (vietnam.gov.vn).

Holders of diplomatic and service passports issued by the Russian Federation, People's Republic of China, Arab Republic of Egypt, Republic of Indonesia, and Ukraine may enter, transit or stay up to 15 days in Kosovo. Note: ordinary passport holders from Russia and China require a visa.
Diplomatic, Official and Service passport holders only

Mutual Reciprocal Visa arrangement between Indonesia and Solomon Islands, extended to ordinary passports under subsequent arrangement per immigration.gov.sb. Covers diplomat, official, and ordinary passport holders. Maximum 90 days, single entry, fee exempted, work prohibited. Applicants must apply before arrival via eVisa portal and present grant letter on entry. Indonesian nationals otherwise require prior approval from Director of Immigration. Corrected 2026-07-03 from visa_free to e_visa: only fee/online fee are exempted, not entry. Per immigration.gov.sb/mutual-visa-indonesia/, holders must apply outside Solomon Islands via the online eVisa portal ('Apply for a Visa'), await an approved grant letter, and present it on entry - a full visa applied for and granted online, matching the e_visa definition, not visa_free.

DZA.notes: Diplomatic, service and official passport holders of Algeria may enter Albania visa-free under a bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Algeria do not require a visa. Cooperation agreement on abolition of visas signed March 17, 2022 during working visit by Burundi Minister of Foreign Affairs Albert Shingiro.
Bilateral visa waiver agreement. Applies to holders of diplomatic and service/official passports. Belgium (BNL) applies this in harmonisation with Benelux partners per Convention of 11 April 1960.
Diplomatic and service passports only. Visa suppression 28 May 1980.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports of Algeria do not require a visa to enter Bulgaria. Ordinary passport holders require a visa. Source: official MFA table of countries whose citizens (holders of diplomatic and service passports) require/do not require visas, last updated 14 January 2025.
Holders of Algerian diplomatic passports are exempt from visa requirements for Bosnia and Herzegovina. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Holders of Algerian diplomatic and official passports can enter Brazil without visas for a stay of up to 90 days (or up to the period of their mission, in case of Algerian officials accredited by the Brazilian government). For all other types of passport, a visa is required prior to entering Brazil.
Bilateral visa exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic, service and official passports. Non-working stays up to 90 days in 180-day period. Agreement entered into force 28 May 1991.
Bilateral visa exemption agreement for diplomatic and service passport holders. Ratified by President Biya on January 29, 2026 per Decree No. 2026/034, confirmed via prc.cm.
Bilateral Agreement on Exemption Visitor Visa signed in 2013. Holders of Diplomatic, Official and Service passports of Algeria may enter Colombia without a visitor visa for up to 90 days.

Holders of diplomatic and service/official passports issued by Algeria are exempt from Schengen visa requirements for Spain. Bilateral agreement recorded in EU OJ 2023/C 340/09 (27 September 2023) - Information on national derogations from the visa requirement under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806.

Dispense s'appliquant seulement aux titulaires d'un passeport diplomatique ou de service/officiel. Max stay 3 months. Source: Arrêté du 10 mai 2010 (as amended), Annexe B §1, in force from 19 June 2025.
Holders of diplomatic or service passports from Algeria are visa-free; ordinary passport holders require a visa. Per bilateral agreement referenced in the Hellenic Republic MFA country visa table.

Bilateral visa waiver agreement: holders of Algerian diplomatic passports may enter Hungary visa-free for up to 30 days. NOTE: Visa-free travel for diplomatic, service and official passports is temporarily suspended until 6 March 2027 per official Hungarian consular information.

Holders of diplomatic passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. NOTE: Georgian diplomatic passport holders are subject to an EU-wide suspension of their visa-free access from 6 March 2026 to 6 March 2027 (Georgia was not in this diplomatic list but the EU suspension for Georgian diplomatic passports is noted separately).

Holders of service/official passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. Exemption applies only to national territory of Italy; does not extend automatically to other Schengen states unless covered by a separate bilateral agreement with those states.

Official passports only. Bilateral visa exemption agreement signed 15 January / 28 May 1991, entered into force 28 May 1991. Non-working stays of a maximum of 90 days within any 180-day period. SEM source lists only 'Official' passport type for Algeria - diplomatic not covered.
Diplomatic and Service (Official) passport holders only. Bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Algerian nationals holding valid diplomatic passports are exempt from the Schengen visa requirement for Malta under a national derogation communicated to the European Commission. Exempted for diplomatic, official and service passport holders only
Holders of Algerian diplomatic and service passports are Category A (visa-exempt); ordinary passport holders require visa on arrival (Category B).
Holders of diplomatic and official passports of Algeria do not require a visa to travel to Uganda under the bilateral visa abolition agreement.

Bilateral visa exemption agreements between Vietnam and each listed country for diplomatic and/or official passport holders. Stay duration varies by bilateral agreement and not individually specified in the official source reviewed. Cuba also includes Seaman's passports and ordinary passports for official missions. Brazil agreement dated 12 February 2005 covers diplomatic passports only. Source: Vietnam Government Portal official visa exemption page.
Diplomatic, Official and Service passport holders only

Ordinary Algerian passport holders are not visa-exempt (only diplomatic/official passports are visa-free under a bilateral agreement) and must obtain Uganda's mandatory pre-travel e-visa online at visas.immigration.go.ug; no visa on arrival. Single-entry tourist visa USD 50, up to 90 days (verified 2026-07).

EGY.notes: Diplomatic, service and official passport holders of Egypt may enter Albania visa-free under a bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Bilateral visa suppression agreement (Visumbefreiungsabkommen). Egyptian holders of diplomatic, service, or special passports may enter Austria visa-free for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. BGBl. Nr. 19/2014.

Holders of diplomatic, special (official), and service passports of Egypt do not require a visa. Agreement already in force after ratification procedures completed in both countries. Signed March 2021 during Burundi-Egypt cooperation summit.
Bilateral visa waiver agreement. Applies to holders of diplomatic, service/official, and special passports. Belgium (BNL) applies this in harmonisation with Benelux partners.

Holders of Egyptian diplomatic and official passports can enter Brazil without visas for a stay of up to 90 days. However, in case of Egyptian officials accredited by the Brazilian government, a visa is required. For all other purposes or cases, a visa is required prior to entering Brazil.
Category D2 – no visa required for diplomatic/official/service passports only, up to 30 days. Ordinary passport holders require a visa (Category A).

Egypt - bilateral visa exemption agreement in force for diplomatic and service passport holders. Ratification date reported as December 29, 2023 by non-official sources; official decree text on prc.cm not directly verified.

Bilateral Agreement on Exemption Visitor Visa signed in 2015. Holders of Diplomatic, Official and Service passports of Egypt may enter Colombia without a visitor visa for up to 90 days within a 6-month term.

Holders of diplomatic, service, and special passports of these seven countries are exempt from visa requirement. Ordinary UAE passport holders also have ordinary passport visa-free access; Egypt, Kuwait, Lebanon, Morocco, Oman, Syria ordinary passport holders require a visa.
Citizens of Egypt with diplomatic and service passports are exempt from the visa requirement, irrespective of whether they enter Denmark to perform official duties.

Holders of diplomatic, service/official and special passports issued by Egypt are exempt from Schengen visa requirements for Spain. Bilateral agreement recorded in EU OJ 2023/C 340/09 (27 September 2023).
Holders of diplomatic passports of Egypt. 90 days in any 180-day period.

Citizens of India, Nepal, Peru, Indonesia, Egypt, Guyana, and Sri Lanka holding valid diplomatic or official/service passports issued by their country may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for a specified period under bilateral visa suppression/waiver agreements. Holders of diplomatic or service passports from Egypt are visa-free; ordinary passport holders require a visa. Per bilateral agreement referenced in the Hellenic Republic MFA country visa table.

Bilateral visa waiver agreement: holders of Egyptian diplomatic passports may enter Hungary visa-free for up to 90 days. NOTE: Visa-free travel for diplomatic, service and official passports is temporarily suspended until 6 March 2027 per official Hungarian consular information.

Holders of special passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter Italy for tourism. Stay duration limits and specific agreement dates are not published on the official page. Exemption applies only to national territory of Italy.

Holders of diplomatic, official or service passports of GCC countries, ASEAN countries, Azerbaijan, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil (30 days), Bulgaria, China, Chile (30 days), Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Djibouti, Egypt, Georgia, Hungary, Kazakhstan (30 days), Lebanon, Peru, Russia, Slovakia, Tunisia, Turkey, and United Kingdom may enter Jordan without a visa for up to 3 months within any 6-month period (unless otherwise stated). Egyptian holders of diplomatic passports may enter Latvia without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period under bilateral visa waiver agreement. Ordinary Egyptian passports require a visa.

Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, special, and/or official passports (specific passport types vary by country) per bilateral visa abolition agreements signed between Morocco and each listed country. Holders of Egyptian diplomatic passports may enter Pakistan without a visa for up to one month. Entry 13 in dgip.gov.pk visa abolition table (as of 21-02-2024).
Ordinary passport requires visa per Ley N°3393/30/11/2007. Diplomatic, official, and service passports exempt per MRE visas-new page.

Agreement between the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Government of the Arab Republic of Egypt on mutual exemption from short-stay visa requirements for holders of diplomatic, special, and service passports. Signed March 19, 2026 in Riyadh by Prince Faisal bin Farhan (Saudi FM) and Badr Abdelatty (Egyptian FM). Entry into force date not confirmed; not applicable to ordinary passport holders.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from the listed countries do not require a visa to enter El Salvador. Mutual visa waiver agreement signed 23 January 2025 in Cairo by Somalia's Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ahmed Moallim Fiqi Ahmed and Egypt's Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Dr. Badr Abdelatty. Allows diplomatic passport holders to enter, exit, transit, and reside without restrictions for up to 90 days. Approved by Somali Cabinet (chaired by PM Hamza Abdi Barre). Note: Egyptian ordinary passport holders are already eligible for visa on arrival under the separate eTAS framework.

Holders of diplomatic passports issued to nationals of these 20 countries can visit Chad without a visa for up to 90 days. Source: Circulaire 002/MSPI/SG/2017, dated 8 August 2017, issued by Chad's Ministry of Security and Public Immigration (MSPI). Note: the Chad Embassy in Paris document (2019) confirms diplomatic AND service passport holders pay no visa fee ('Le visa est gratuit pour les détenteurs de Passeports Diplomatiques ou de Services'), but that document describes a fee waiver for a required visa, not a visa-free waiver - it is therefore NOT a separate service-passport visa-free rule. The visa-free waiver in Circulaire 002 names only diplomatic passports. The 20-country list is confirmed by the Wikipedia Visa policy of Chad article citing the same circular.
Holders of diplomatic and official passports of Egypt do not require a visa to travel to Uganda under the bilateral visa abolition agreement.

Egypt: ordinary passport holders require a prior consular visa (Nota 5). Diplomatic and service/official passport holders are visa-free. Bilateral exemption documented in the Régimen de Visas de Admisión.

Visa-free regime for holders of diplomatic passports of Egypt (up to 90 days). Ordinary passport holders of Egypt require a visa. Accredited diplomatic mission employees and family members may stay for the entire period of work without a visa.

Holders of diplomatic and service passports issued by the Russian Federation, People's Republic of China, Arab Republic of Egypt, Republic of Indonesia, and Ukraine may enter, transit or stay up to 15 days in Kosovo. Note: ordinary passport holders from Russia and China require a visa.

IND.notes: Diplomatic, service and official passport holders of India may enter Albania visa-free under a bilateral agreement. Ordinary passport holders require an e-visa. No OCI card exemption identified.

Holders of Indian diplomatic and official passports may enter, exit, and transit Andorra without a visa for a maximum stay of 90 days in any 180-day period. Agreement on Exemption from Visa Requirement for Holders of Diplomatic and Official Passports between India and the Principality of Andorra, signed 15 March 2024 at Andorra la Vella, entered into force 15 June 2024.
Bilateral agreement; diplomatic passports only. Ordinary Indian passport holders require a visa (e-visa available per india.mfa.am); no unconditional visa-free access for ordinary passports.

Transit without visa (TWOV) only - Indian official passport holders (passports issued by the authorities of the Republic of India to officials of the Government of India) may transit Australia without a visa. Must arrive by aircraft, depart to a third country by aircraft within 8 hours of arrival, and must not clear immigration or leave the airport transit lounge.
Bilateral visa suppression agreement. Indian holders of diplomatic passports only (not service passports) may enter Austria visa-free for up to 90 days. BGBl. Nr. 126/2023.
Bilateral visa waiver agreement. Applies to holders of diplomatic and service/official passports. Belgium (BNL) applies this in harmonisation with Benelux partners.
Diplomatic and service passports only. Visa suppression agreement 29 July 2019.
Holders of diplomatic and service passports of India do not require a visa to enter Bulgaria. Ordinary passport holders require a visa. Source: official MFA table, last updated 14 January 2025.

Holders of Indian diplomatic or official/special passports are exempt from visa for stays up to 90 days, per bilateral visa exemption agreement between Bahrain and India signed 15 July 2018, entered into force 19 December 2018.

Indian nationals who hold diplomatic or official passports do not require a visa to enter The Bahamas. Bilateral Visa Waiver Agreement signed 29 November 2018 between the Commonwealth of The Bahamas and the Republic of India for holders of diplomatic and official passports.

Holders of Indian diplomatic and official passports are exempt from visas for stays of up to 90 days. However, in case of Indian officials accredited by the Brazilian government, a visa is required. For all other purposes or cases, a visa is required prior to entering Brazil.
Category D3 – no visa required for diplomatic/official passports only, up to 14 days. Ordinary passport holders require a visa (Category B).

Diplomatic passports of India only. Ordinary and official/service passport holders from India still require a visa. Bilateral visa exemption agreement signed 01 November 2018, entered into force 31 January 2019.

Bilateral visa exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic passports only. Non-working stays up to 90 days in 180-day period. Agreement entered into force 7 December 2016. Note: India OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card does NOT grant entry to Switzerland; OCI is an Indian domestic benefit for entry to India.

Bilateral Agreement on Exemption Visitor Visa signed in 2001. Holders of Diplomatic and Official passports of India may enter Colombia without a visitor visa for up to 90 days, which may be extended at the request of the Mission or Consulate to which the holder is attached. Service passport holders are NOT covered.

Holders of valid diplomatic, official, or service passports of India may enter, stay, and transit Comoros without a visa for up to 90 days. Agreement between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the Union of Comoros on the exemption of visa for holders of diplomatic, official/service passports. Signed 11 October 2019; entered into force 1 March 2021.

Holders of diplomatic, official, and service passports of these nineteen countries are exempt from visa requirement. UAE is listed in both this category and the diplomatic/service/special category above. Ordinary passport holders of Colombia, Mexico, Panama, Marshall Islands, Kiribati, Peru, Tonga, Palau, St. Lucia, Dominica, Grenada, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, Trinidad and Tobago also have ordinary passport visa-free access. Cuba, India, Tuvalu, Vanuatu ordinary passport holders require a visa.
Citizens of India with diplomatic passports, service passports, and official passports are exempt from the visa requirement, irrespective of whether they enter Denmark to perform official duties.

Bilateral visa exemption agreement between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the Republic of Ecuador for holders of Diplomatic and Official passports. Agreement signed 22 June 2007; entered into force 18 August 2008. Covers diplomatic and official passports only; service passports are NOT included in this specific agreement. Note: ordinary Indian passport holders require a visa to enter Ecuador.

Holders of Indian diplomatic passports do not need a visa for short-term stays in Spain (less than 90 days). Special passports also exempt per EU OJ 2023/C 340/09. List includes Albania, Algeria, Andorra, Angola, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Austria, Barbados, Belarus, Belize, Belgium, Bolivia, Botswana, Brazil, Bulgaria, Chile, People's Republic of China (up to 30 days), Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cuba, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Egypt, El Salvador, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Holy See, Honduras, Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Iceland, Israel, Italy, Jamaica, Japan, Kazakhstan, Korea, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Malta, S.M.O. of Malta, Macedonia, Mexico, Monaco, Montenegro, Morocco, Mozambique, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Nicaragua, Norway, Pakistan, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, The Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russian Federation, Saint Lucia, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, San Marino, Serbia, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, Suriname, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, Uruguay, Vatican, Venezuela, and Vietnam. China limited to 30 days. UN Laissez-Passer holders require a visa regardless of nationality.
Bilateral agreement; diplomatic and official passports only

Transit without visa (TWOV) only - airside transit, must arrive by aircraft, depart to a third country by aircraft within 8 hours of arrival, must not clear immigration or leave the airport transit lounge. TWOV for diplomatic passports does NOT apply to holders of diplomatic passports from: Arab Non-National Passports, Afghanistan, Algeria, Angola, Bahrain, Comoros, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Madagascar, Mauritania, Morocco, Pakistan, Russian Federation, Saudi Arabia, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, Yemen and Zimbabwe - these holders must obtain an appropriate Australian visa.

Citizens of the relevant foreign country holding diplomatic or service (or official/special) passport are visa-free under bilateral intergovernmental agreements (Group I). 79 countries listed in the official PDF dated 29 April 2026. Permitted stay varies by country (30 or 90 days). Libya temporarily suspended. See PDF for full per-country details.
Diplomatic passport only. No specific agreement date on official page.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of any country may enter Bolivia without a visa. Specific bilateral agreements confirmed: Equatorial Guinea (signed 23 November 2017, cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2017/11/23/8345), Switzerland (signed 7 December 2018, cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2018/12/07/7883; stay duration linked to period of functions/assignment), Honduras (March 2024, covering diplomatic and official passports), Chile (effective March 9, 2026, cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2026/03/09/24588/, covers diplomatic and official passports for official travel). The blanket 90-day rule for all diplomatic/official/service passports is widely reported by Timatic but has not been confirmed verbatim on a directly-accessed official Bolivian government page beyond these specific bilateral agreements.

Holders of Congolese diplomatic and official passports can enter Brazil without visas for a stay of up to 90 days (or up to the period of their mission, in case of Congolese officials accredited by the Brazilian government). For all other purposes or cases, a visa is required prior to entering Brazil.

Chile has approximately 73 bilateral visa exemption agreements for holders of diplomatic, official, and/or service passports. Under these agreements, nationals of the partner country holding the specified passport type may enter Chile visa-free for up to 90 days (tourism, no paid employment). Officials posted to a diplomatic mission or consular office may remain for the duration of their assignment. Confirmed individual agreements include: Switzerland (diplomatic/official/service passports, signed 19 Jan 2024, ratified by Chilean Senate 7 Mar 2025); Oman (diplomatic/special/service/official passports, signed 22 Mar 2022); Morocco (diplomatic/official/special/service passports, signed 20 Sep 2016); South Africa (diplomatic/official passports, signed 1 Sep 2016); Azerbaijan (diplomatic/service/official passports, signed 13 Sep 2018); Bolivia (diplomatic/official passports, signed 25 Apr 2025, in force Mar 2026). Full authoritative list in MINREL VIDO Manual (May 2025 edition) - image-based PDF, not machine-readable.

China has bilateral mutual visa exemption agreements with 158 countries/entities covering diplomatic and/or service/official passport holders. Max stay is typically 30 days per entry; some agreements allow 90 days (e.g. Vietnam, Mexico, Mali, Rwanda, Bahrain, Burkina Faso, El Salvador, Madagascar, Lebanon); unlimited stays for specific passport types under agreements with Bolivia, Mongolia, Turkey, Laos, Bangladesh. A small number of agreements also cover ordinary passports (e.g. Mauritius, Seychelles, Fiji, Georgia, Solomon Islands, Antigua and Barbuda, San Marino, UK, Mexico, Vietnam). Exact passport types and stay limits vary by bilateral agreement - full list at cs.mfa.gov.cn.

France–Côte d'Ivoire Agreement on reciprocal short-stay visa exemption for diplomatic passport holders, signed in Paris on 20 January 2025, in force from 1 June 2025 (Décret n° 2025-357 du 18 avril 2025, published on legifrance.gouv.fr). Diplomatic passport must retain at least 3 months validity beyond intended departure date. Must be accompanied by official diplomatic note or mission order. No employment (including self-employment) permitted. Multiple stays not exceeding 90 days within any 180-day period. Covers France (metropolitan departments, overseas regions/departments, overseas collectivities, New Caledonia) and Côte d'Ivoire territory. Diplomatic passports only - service and official passports are NOT covered by this specific agreement.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of any country are exempt from the prior visa requirement and may receive diplomatic, official, or courtesy visas. Despacho 244/GMAI/2025 states: holders of diplomatic or service passports, as well as citizens traveling by invitation of Cabo Verde authorities, receive differentiated treatment (diplomatic, official, or courtesy visas). Pre-existing bilateral agreements: Cuba - Decreto n.º 79/82, de 28 de agosto (diplomatic/service/official passports, duration of mission); Russia - Decreto n.º 8/95, de 28 de agosto (diplomatic and service passports, 90 days, though Russia ordinary passport holders are now also visa-free per the gov.cv exempt list).

All flight crew members holding a Flight Crew Member's License or Crew Member Certificate issued under the Chicago Convention are exempt from visa requirement. Also covers flight crew and attendants on emergency or rescue flights, and civilian crew of ships.

Holders of diplomatic, service, official or special passports from countries that have concluded bilateral visa waiver agreements with the Czech Republic are exempt from the visa requirement for short stays. The specific countries and maximum stay periods are governed by individual bilateral treaties. The visa regime for holders of diplomatic, service and special passports may differ from ordinary passport holders - holders are advised to contact the respective Czech consulate to confirm. The 'Countries with Visa Waiver Regime' page (mzv.gov.cz) lists these bilateral agreements but the full per-country list could not be rendered due to JavaScript gating. Note: Georgian diplomatic, service and official passports are currently excluded from the Schengen visa-free regime by European Commission decision (suspended March 6, 2026 – March 6, 2027); Georgian ordinary passport holders with biometric passports are unaffected and remain visa-free.

Holders of diplomatic and official/service passports of India may enter Djibouti visa-free for up to 90 days under the Agreement on Mutual Exemption from Visa Requirements for Holders of Diplomatic and Official/Service Passports between India and Djibouti. Agreement signed 22 September 2022, entered into force 01 February 2023.

The Dominican Republic has concluded bilateral visa suppression/waiver agreements for holders of diplomatic, official, and/or service passports with numerous countries. The MIREX services portal lists these categories (DM = Diplomatic, OS/OM = Official/Service, CS/CM = Courtesy) and states that a Diplomatic Note from the relevant mission specifying diplomatic rank or position is required. Sources confirm holders of diplomatic, official or service passports of at least the following countries enter without visa: Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, France, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Israel, Japan, Malaysia, Morocco, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Russia, Serbia, Singapore, South Korea, Switzerland, Tajikistan, Taiwan, Trinidad and Tobago, Ukraine, Uruguay, Vietnam. Exact per-country durations and bilateral agreement dates not published on MIREX portal.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports are exempt from the criminal background certificate requirement at land border crossings with Colombia and Peru, 'de conformidad con los tratados internacionales de los que Ecuador es parte' (in accordance with international treaties to which Ecuador is a party). This exemption is stated under Art. e of Lineamientos applying Acuerdo Ministerial Nro. 0007 of 11 January 2024 (Ministerio del Interior). The underlying entry right itself (visa waiver) depends on the specific bilateral treaty with the passport-holder's country.
Visa not required for official/service passport holders of AU member states, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), UN and its specialised agencies.

Diplomats and Consular Corps are explicitly listed among visa-exempt categories in the Feb 2026 'New Visa Policy' document (Section I: 'DIPLOMATS AND CONSULAR CORPS'). Section IV states: 'Nationals of the 27 EU member states including Great Britain and Switzerland, Tourists on Chartered Flights and Tour Operators holding diplomatic, official/service or ordinary passports can travel to The Gambia visa free and are not required to be in possession of clearance.' Entry conditions: must possess valid travel document, enter through a recognised entry point, have visible means of sustenance, must not be a prohibited immigrant.

Diplomatic and service/official passport holders from 101 PBVDD partner countries are visa-exempt for visits up to 30 days under bilateral Perjanjian Bebas Visa Diplomatik dan Dinas (PBVDD) agreements. The list as of 12 August 2024 covers: Albania, Angola, Antigua & Barbuda, Argentina, Armenia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Bangladesh, Belarus, Belgium, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Brazil, Brunei Darussalam, Bulgaria, Burundi, Cambodia, Chile, China (PRC), Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cuba, Czechia, Denmark (e-passport only), Ecuador, Egypt, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Fiji, Hungary, India, Iran, Italy, Japan, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Mexico, Moldova, Mongolia, Montenegro, Morocco, Mozambique, Myanmar, Namibia, Netherlands, Nicaragua, Niger, North Korea, North Macedonia, Norway, Pakistan, Panama, Papua New Guinea, Paraguay, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russia, Rwanda, Saint Kitts & Nevis, Senegal, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Solomon Islands, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Suriname, Switzerland, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, Vietnam, Greece. NOTE: Ireland - diplomatic passport only. United Kingdom - diplomatic passport only. Denmark - e-passport only. Sweden - e-passport only. Holders must carry a Diplomatic Note of assignment or visit notification from their Foreign Ministry.

India has operational bilateral visa exemption agreements with 107+ countries for holders of diplomatic and/or official/service passports. Most agreements grant 90 days visa-free; some grant shorter stays by agreement. Stay periods and covered passport categories (diplomatic only vs. diplomatic+official vs. diplomatic+official+service) vary by agreement. Ordinary passport holders are NOT covered by these agreements. Full list at mea.gov.in/bvwa-passport and mea.gov.in/bvwa-passport-only.htm.
