Holders of a diplomatic passport issued by the People's Republic of China are exempt from Irish visa requirement under Schedule 2 of S.I. No. 473/2014 (as originally enacted, confirmed in S.I. 17/2026). Up to 90 days.

Holders of a service passport or public affairs passport issued by the People's Republic of China are exempt from Irish visa requirement under Article 3(f) of S.I. No. 473/2014 (as amended) ONLY when arriving in the company of a Minister of the Government of the PRC where that Minister is on an official visit to Ireland. The PRC 'service passport' and 'public affairs passport' are specifically defined in Article 2 of S.I. 473/2014.

Diplomatic, service, and official passport holders from most countries benefit from additional visa suppression agreements beyond what ordinary passport holders receive. Specific duration depends on bilateral agreement.

Holders of diplomatic, service, and official passports of all countries are exempt from ETA-IL per the official PIBA ETA-IL page. The official Tourist Visa Table confirms that most countries' official passport holders are either already exempt or additionally exempted even when national passport holders require a visa. However, note that some countries' official passports still require a visa (per individual entries in the tourist visa table).

Holders of diplomatic passports of any country (except Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Japan, Nigeria, Mexico, Republic of Congo, Serbia, Syria and Yemen) may enter Jordan without a visa for up to 3 months within any 6-month period. Based on multilateral diplomatic convention and bilateral diplomatic agreements. Source: Wikipedia (Timatic/IATA).
Bilateral visa exemption agreement effective 27.03.1989 for diplomatic and service passports; stay duration not specified in official table. Ordinary DPRK passport holders require a visa.

Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from all countries are exempt from Saint Lucia visa requirements and visa fees, regardless of nationality. The official visa fee table lists 'Exempt' for both 'Diplomatic Passports' and 'Official/Service Passports' at all places of issue (UK, USA, Canada, Rest of World, Saint Lucia). The DEA Visa Requirements by Country PDF confirms this with per-country entries such as 'YES(pta) NO(DIPLOMATIC/OFFICIAL)' for Armenia, Azerbaijan, Haiti, Macedonia, Moldova, Ukraine - countries whose ordinary passport holders require a visa.

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Lithuania and the Government of the State of Israel on the waiver of the visa requirement for the holders of diplomatic or service passports. Signed Jerusalem 01/03/1995; entered into force 27/11/1995. Note: as of 2001 Israeli ordinary passport holders are also visa-free under Annex II, so this agreement is practically applicable only to diplomatic/service passport holders; the treaty remains in force and expressly covers diplomatic and service passports.

Holders of a diplomatic passport (any nationality except US), 'Laissez Passer' issued by the United Nations, or 'diplomatic or consular identity card' issued by the Macao Special Administrative Region are granted unlimited stay upon entry. US diplomatic passport holders are explicitly excluded and must obtain advance visa through a PRC diplomatic mission.
Diplomatic Passport holders of any state travelling to the RMI on a diplomatic mission. No period restrictions, fee waived. Listed under 'ALL OTHERS – VISA WAIVERS' section.
Laissez-Passer (LP) holders travelling to the RMI on official missions. No period restrictions, fee waived. Listed under 'ALL OTHERS – VISA WAIVERS' section.
Holders of UN travel documents do not require a visa to enter North Macedonia.

Any national holding a diplomatic or service passport receives up to one month visa-free access per Wikipedia (Visa policy of Mali). Note: This is unconfirmed by directly-read official Malian pages (maliembassy.us, diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml). The Mali Embassy Canada page shows diplomatic passport holders must still present a 'note verbale', potentially contradicting a blanket exemption.
Diplomatic and Official/Service passport holders only; 90 days each. Ordinary passport holders use Tourist Visa on Arrival (pilot program active through 20 Oct 2026).

Diplomatic and Service passport holders of Sao Tome & Principe: visa-free entry up to 90 days, Tourist & Business. Ordinary passport holders: visa-free up to 30 days (see visa_free). Covered under CPLP multilateral agreement.

Holders of diplomatic and official/service passports are exempt from visa requirements for stays up to 90 days. Exemption does NOT apply to passport holders from: Afghanistan, Iraq, Kosovo, Libya, Palestine State, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Yemen.

All diplomatic and service/official passport holders are issued a gratis (free) visa per the immigration regulations. Subject to reciprocity: exempt 'except where reciprocal visa requirements apply to Malawian diplomatic or service passport holders'.
Exempted for diplomatic, official and service passport holders only

Disposición N° 002-2026 (Article 2, effective 16 February 2026) maintains visa exemption for holders of diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs (asuntos públicos) and special passports of any nationality with which Nicaragua has migration-facilitation agreements ('con los cuales el gobierno de la República de Nicaragua ha afirmado acuerdos'). Specific confirmed bilateral agreements on file at legislacion.asamblea.gob.ni include: Nicaragua–Peru (signed Lima, 4 June 2004; ratified Decree A.N. 4965, 12 December 2006, published La Gaceta No. 13, 18 January 2007 - covers diplomatic, special, official and service passports); Nicaragua–Taiwan/ROC (diplomatic, official and service passports); Nicaragua–Sweden (visa suppression convention); UK (La Gaceta No. 54, 5 March 1969 - all passport types, superseded for UK nationals by general visa-free grant under Disposición 002-2026). No maximum stay duration is specified in Disposición 002-2026 for this category; conditions revert to individual bilateral agreement terms.

Applicable only to holders of diplomatic passports, service passports, or passports for public affairs of the People's Republic of China. Added to Schedule 5 of the Immigration Regulations 2014 as item 4 per Immigration (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (Gazette No. 124, 25 March 2025, GN No. 344/2025). China's MFA mutual visa exemption list also confirms this agreement as entry #99, in force 1 April 2025, max stay 30 days.

Applicable only to holders of diplomatic passports or official passports. Added to Schedule 5 of the Immigration Regulations 2014 as item 5 per Immigration (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (Gazette No. 124, 25 March 2025, GN No. 344/2025). Maximum stay days not specified in the gazette text.
Diplomatic passport holders of the Republic of China (Taiwan) do not require a visa to enter Panama. Ordinary passport holders of Taiwan are visa-free under Resolution 22706.

Holders of diplomatic, special, official, or service passports from countries that have concluded a visa suppression agreement (convenio de supresión de visas) with Peru are exempt from visa requirements. As of the official May 2015 RREE list, agreement partners include: Algeria, Argentina, Austria, Azerbaijan, Barbados, Belize, Belgium/Netherlands/Luxembourg (Benelux), Belarus, Bolivia, Brazil, Brunei, Bulgaria, Cambodia, Chile, China (diplomatic/special/service only - ordinary passport still requires visa), Colombia, South Korea, Costa Rica, Denmark, Ecuador, Egypt, El Salvador, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Russia, Philippines, Finland, France, Georgia, Greece, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Israel, Italy, Jamaica, Jordan, Kuwait, Laos, Latvia, Macedonia, Malaysia, Malta, Morocco, Mexico, Moldova, Montenegro, Mongolia, Nicaragua, Palestine, Panama, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, Czech Republic, Dominican Republic, Romania, Serbia, Singapore, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, Uruguay, Venezuela, Vietnam, and others with more recent additions. This list may not be exhaustive - the official updated January 2024 PDF (cdn.www.gob.pe) returned HTTP 403 during research.

Holders of diplomatic passports of any nationality are exempt from the airport transit visa (ATV) requirement when transiting through the international transit areas of Portuguese airports, under Article 3(5)(e) of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Schengen Visa Code). This is an airport transit exemption. Note: this is distinct from bilateral diplomatic passport visa waiver agreements for short-stay entry, which are governed separately.

Nationals of countries listed in Romania's Annex 3 (bilateral visa waiver/suppression agreements) who hold diplomatic, service, official passports, or seamen's books are exempt from the Romanian visa requirement. The specific countries covered are listed in Annex 3 of Romanian visa regulations (referenced at mae.ro). Note: The European Commission adopted an EU-wide implementing regulation on 6 March 2026 temporarily suspending visa-free travel for Georgian holders of diplomatic, service, and official passports (effective 6 March 2026 to 6 March 2027), incorporating and superseding earlier national-level actions by Romania and other member states. Georgian ordinary passport holders remain visa-free under Annex II (biometric passports). The Annex 3 full country list was not accessible from official sources during research (mae.ro returning HTTP 503).

Holders of diplomatic, official, service, and/or special passports of numerous countries (100+) may enter Russia without a visa under bilateral agreements. Stay is typically 90 days per 180-day period (or 3 months per period). Specific countries and permitted passport types (D=diplomatic, O=official, S=service, Sp=special) vary by bilateral treaty. Notable exceptions: visa-free exemption for diplomatic/official passport holders of EU member states, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland has been suspended. Israel diplomatic and service passport holders require a visa. Belarus and South Ossetia have freedom of movement. Precise per-country conditions are governed by individual bilateral agreements listed on the Russian MFA portal.

Holders of diplomatic or official/service/special passports issued to nationals of the listed countries do not require a visa. Russia: diplomatic passport only. Source: IATA Timatic via Wikipedia (not confirmed from official Sudan government domain).

The official RREE visa checker (rree.gob.sv/visas/) lists OEA (Organization of American States), Naciones Unidas (United Nations), and Comisión Europea (European Commission) as recognized passport-issuing entities alongside sovereign states, indicating holders of travel documents issued by these international organizations are subject to the visa-exemption framework. Specific conditions for each organization's travel documents were not enumerated on any static official page found.

Holders of Diplomatic, Service, Special and Official passports issued by any country are exempt from the Entry Fee requirement and may enter Suriname without paying the entry fee. No specific stay limit stated beyond general 90-day tourist rule.

Bilateral and multilateral agreements grant visa exemption for a determined duration to holders of diplomatic or service passports from countries that are in general subject to visa requirements. Official list confirmed on voyage.gouv.tg (section on bilateral agreements): Brazil, Tunisia, Central African Republic, Turkey, China, Iran, Comoros, Kenya, Cuba, Libya, Djibouti, Mauritania, Egypt, Morocco, Eritrea, Qatar, Gabon, Russia, Indonesia, São Tomé and Príncipe, Suriname, Somalia. Verbatim (French): 'Il existe des accords bilatéraux, multilatéraux qui accordent une exemption de visa pour une durée déterminée aux titulaires d'un passeport diplomatique ou de services d'un pays qui en règle générale est soumis au visa.' Exact stay durations per country are not published in machine-readable form on the official portal. Note: several of these countries (Tunisia, Central African Republic, Comoros, Kenya, Libya, Djibouti, Mauritania, Egypt, Morocco, Eritrea, Gabon, São Tomé and Príncipe, Somalia) are now also covered by the all-AU visa-free policy for ordinary passport holders as of May 2026.
Diplomatic passport holders exempt for 90 days within 180 days. Service/ordinary require visa.

Diplomatic Visa is given to non-citizens who hold diplomatic passports and are on diplomatic mission for a foreign government in Vanuatu with their family members. Duration is at Director's discretion. Multiple entry. Fee-exempt.
Diplomatic passport type only
All countries' diplomats, UN personnel, and DCAF workers granted multiple-entry free visa of 6 months at airport/border.

Holder of a diplomatic passport (MRZ-compliant, minimum 6 months validity). Free visa on arrival for 30 days. Official visits must be pre-notified to Maldives Immigration via the relevant authority in Maldives. Note: the immigration.gov.mv/diplomatic/ page has returned HTTP 404 on multiple research occasions; the diplomatic VoA policy is referenced in search cache but not directly verifiable from the live page.

Holders of diplomatic or special passports of the listed countries may obtain a visa on arrival valid for a maximum of 2 months. Source: IATA Timatic via Wikipedia (not confirmed from official Sudan government domain).

Holders of diplomatic, official, service and special passports issued to nationals of any country can obtain a visa on arrival. Foreign officials or diplomats must present an official Note Verbale from the appropriate authorities. Visas to diplomats are gratis (no visa fee assessed). Multiple-entry visas are only granted to diplomatic and official passports.

A Gratis Visa (free of charge) is issued at Zambia Missions Abroad or at ports of entry to members of the Diplomatic Community on presentation of letters of accreditation and/or Diplomatic Passports. Also issued to diplomats not accredited to Zambia but visiting on official business on presentation of letters of invitation. Applies to diplomatic passport holders of any nationality. No fee charged.

cbi.name: Antigua and Barbuda
cbi.program_name: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Programme

options.notes: Non-refundable contribution to the National Development Fund (NDF). Minimum US$230,000 per application. Processing fees: US$10,000 (single applicant), US$20,000 (family up to 4), US$20,000 + US$10,000 per additional dependent from 5th onwards. Due diligence fee: US$8,500 (principal), US$5,000 (spouse), free (child 0-11), US$2,000 (child 12-17), US$4,000 (dependent adult 18+ or parent 55+). Passport fee: US$300 per person.

Purchase of approved real estate project with minimum value US$300,000. Property cannot be re-sold until 5 years after purchase unless an alternative approved real estate is purchased. Processing fees same structure as NDF option. Same due diligence and passport fee structure.

Investment in an approved business. Single applicant minimum: US$1,500,000. Joint investment (minimum 2 persons): total US$5,000,000 with each person contributing at least US$400,000. Businesses must receive prior approval from the CIU. min_amount reflects per-person minimum for joint investment.

Contribution to the University of the West Indies (UWI) Fund. Minimum US$260,000 for a family of six or more (processing fees included per official page). One family member receives a one-year tuition-only scholarship at UWI. Families of 7 or more incur an additional US$10,000 per additional dependent. Families of fewer than 6 are not eligible for this option.

cbi.processing_time: Not stated verbatim on cip.gov.ag fetched pages
cbi.notes: Program established 2013. August 2024 price increase raised NDF minimum from US$100,000 to US$230,000. ECCIRA framework (signed September 2025): all five Eastern Caribbean CBI states (Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and Saint Lucia) have now ratified the ECCIRA agreement. Saint Lucia completed ratification after its December 1, 2025 general election reconstituted the National Assembly; implementation was formally postponed to June 2026 pending this ratification. As of June 2026, all five jurisdictions have ratified; the 30-day aggregate physical residency requirement within the first 5 years, mandatory interview protocols for all applicants and dependents aged 12+, enhanced due diligence, and biometric data collection are entering into force in June 2026. Applications submitted before June 30, 2026 bypass the new 30-day physical residency requirement. Post-June 2026 applicants are subject to the 30-day minimum aggregate physical presence within first 5 years (with a minimum of 5 days in the first year) plus mandatory participation in an integration or orientation programme. Restricted Countries List (Afghanistan, Iran, North Korea, Somalia, Yemen, Sudan) confirmed on cip.gov.ag/faq/ - nationals may apply only if they migrated before age of majority OR maintained permanent residence outside those countries for at least 10 years. Applicants must take an oath of allegiance either in Antigua and Barbuda or at a diplomatic mission abroad. All fees subject to change per official schedule page.

cbi.name: Argentina
cbi.program_name: Citizenship by Investment (Ciudadanía por Inversión) - Decreto 524/2025

options.notes: Investment must be classified as 'relevant' by the Ministry of Economy. Minimum investment threshold and eligible sectors not specified in the decree text - the Ministry of Economy is tasked with defining qualifying investments via separate regulation. The decree was signed July 30, 2025 and published in the Official Gazette July 31, 2025 (Boletín Oficial). Applications are submitted to the Agency for Citizenship by Investment Programs (Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión) under the Ministry of Economy. Security clearance required from multiple agencies (Ministry of Security, UIF, SIDE) prior to approval.

cbi.processing_time: 30 business days (from receipt of Agency report by the National Directorate of Migration)
cbi.notes: Established by Decreto 524/2025, signed by President Javier Milei on July 30, 2025. Amends Citizenship Law No. 346, adding Article 2° bis. No prior residency required - applicants qualify 'regardless of length of residence'. Investment amounts not specified in the decree; deferred to Ministry of Economy regulation. ARCA (tax authority) tasked with enabling processing of tax identification numbers for approved applicants. Official Gazette source: https://www.boletinoficial.gob.ar/detalleAviso/primera/329061/20250731

cbi.name: Austria
cbi.program_name: Austrian Citizenship for Exceptional Services (Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz §10 Abs. 6)

options.notes: No fixed investment threshold is set in the law. The provision requires 'extraordinary services' (außerordentliche Leistungen) in the special interest of the Republic, which may include economic, scientific, cultural or athletic contributions. The Federal Government (Council of Ministers) confirms each case individually. There is no published minimum investment figure on the official source; non-official sources report figures of €3 million–€10 million but these are NOT confirmed on official government pages and are not recorded here.

cbi.processing_time: Not specified on official source. Council of Ministers meets twice yearly to decide applications.
cbi.notes: Section 10(6) of the Austrian Citizenship Act (Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz) allows the Federal Government to grant citizenship without satisfying the standard requirements (10 years residency, secured livelihood, renunciation of foreign citizenship) when the grant is in the special interest of the Republic based on extraordinary services already rendered and expected to continue. This is a discretionary merit-based program, not a conventional CBI program with a published investment schedule. Applications are filed at one of Austria's 9 provincial governments. Dual citizenship is permitted under this provision. Official source text (German): 'Die Voraussetzungen des Abs. 1 Z 1 und 7 sowie des Abs. 3 entfallen, wenn die Bundesregierung bestätigt, daß die Verleihung der Staatsbürgerschaft wegen der vom Fremden bereits erbrachten und von ihm noch zu erwartenden außerordentlichen Leistungen im besonderen Interesse der Republik liegt.'

cbi.name: Botswana
cbi.program_name: Citizenship by Investment Programme (Citizenship Amendment Act 2025 / Impact Investment Program)

options.notes: The $75,000 minimum contribution figure is reported by Arton Capital (the MoU partner appointed in September 2025) via BotswanaCitizenship.com and widely cited in investment migration media. This figure has NOT been published in an official gov.bw gazette, regulation, or statutory instrument; it is noted here as the working figure pending official proclamation. The upper range cited is $90,000 under a limited quota system.

cbi.notes: The Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2025 was passed by Parliament on December 17, 2025 (second reading), then sent to committee stage for clause-by-clause scrutiny. As of June 2026, no official gov.bw source confirms the bill has been signed into law or that regulations setting the investment threshold have been formally gazetted. President Duma Boko signed an MoU with Arton Capital on 26 September 2025 during the UN General Assembly, branding the program 'Impact Investment Program.' The $75,000–$90,000 minimum contribution figure originates from Arton Capital's registration portal (BotswanaCitizenship.com), not from a government gazette. Sectors targeted: manufacturing, mining and energy, agriculture, infrastructure, financial services, tourism, technology and digitalisation, sport and creatives, health, green energy and renewable energy. Investors granted citizenship are restricted from: voting, holding public office, accessing free government education, applying for government funding, being allocated state/tribal land, or serving in disciplined forces.

cbi.name: Cambodia
cbi.program_name: Citizenship by Investment / Naturalization by Investment (Sub-Decree No. 225)

options.notes: Personal investment of at least KHR 4 billion (approx. USD 1 million) in an approved priority-sector project with a valid investment permit. Priority sectors include agriculture, food processing, manufacturing, waste management, tourism, digital/tech industries, innovation, SMEs, industrial parks, and affordable housing.
Personal cash donation of at least KHR 12 billion (approx. USD 3 million) to the national budget or humanitarian sector, paid through the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

cbi.processing_time: Not specified officially; applications require approval from Ministry of Interior and final grant by Royal Decree.
cbi.notes: Cambodia's citizenship by investment framework was formalized effective December 1, 2025 under Sub-Decree No. 225 implementing the amended Law on Nationality (Articles 21 and 22). The program is a discretionary sovereign naturalization framework - not a standardized CBI program. Final citizenship is granted by Royal Decree after Ministry of Interior vetting. Dual citizenship is explicitly permitted under the new law. Sub-Decree No. 225 has been reported by multiple law firms (Andersen Cambodia, Angkor Law Firm) citing the official Royal Gazette.

cbi.name: Dominica
cbi.program_name: Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment Programme

options.notes: Economic Diversification Fund (EDF) donation. Single applicant: US$200,000. Main applicant + up to 3 dependants: US$250,000. Each additional dependant under 18: US$25,000. Each additional dependant 18+: US$40,000. Additional fees: processing US$1,000; due diligence US$7,500 (main applicant), US$4,000 (dependants 16+); Certificate of Naturalisation US$500 per person; mandatory interview US$1,000 per person (16+).

Minimum real estate investment of US$200,000 in an approved government project. Government fees: main applicant alone US$75,000; main applicant + up to 3 dependants US$100,000; each additional dependant under 18 US$25,000; each additional dependant 18+ US$40,000. Additional fees: processing US$1,000; due diligence US$7,500 (main); mandatory interview US$1,000 per person (16+). Property must be held for 3 years from citizenship grant date (5 years if the future purchaser is also a CBI applicant).

cbi.processing_time: 3 to 4 months from application submission to approval in principle
cbi.notes: Program established by Citizenship By Investment Regulations 2013 (SRO 43 of 2013), amended in 2020 and 2024. All applicants aged 16+ must attend a mandatory interview. Applications must be submitted through authorised CBI agents. Payments accepted in USD, EUR, or GBP (EUR/GBP amounts must be equivalent to or greater than the USD minimum). Governed by the Citizenship By Investment Unit (CBIU), 1st Floor, Financial Centre, Kennedy Avenue, Roseau.

cbi.name: Egypt
cbi.program_name: Unit for Granting Egyptian Citizenship in Exchange for Investment

options.notes: Direct revenue (grant) of USD 250,000 deposited by bank transfer from abroad to Public Treasury Authority. Non-refundable. Source: official GAFI PDF at investinegypt.gov.eg.

Purchase of real estate owned by the State or public legal persons, minimum USD 500,000 transferred from abroad. If disposed of before 5 years from purchase date, USD 250,000 must be deposited as direct revenue to Public Treasury Authority. Non-refundable. Source: official GAFI PDF at investinegypt.gov.eg.

Setting up or participating in an investment project with at least USD 400,000 transferred from abroad and at least 40% participation of project capital. Per Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. If liquidated/suspended/disposed before 5 years of operation, USD 250,000 must be deposited as direct revenue. Source: official GAFI PDF at investinegypt.gov.eg.

Cash deposit of USD 1,000,000 at the Central Bank of Egypt by bank transfer from abroad. Refundable after 3 years in Egyptian pounds at CBE exchange rate on refund date (not exceeding exchange rate on deposit date), without interest. Source: official GAFI PDF at investinegypt.gov.eg.

Cash deposit of USD 750,000 at the Central Bank of Egypt by bank transfer from abroad. Refundable after 5 years in Egyptian pounds at CBE exchange rate on refund date (not exceeding exchange rate on deposit date), without interest. Source: official GAFI PDF at investinegypt.gov.eg.

cbi.notes: No residency period required prior to citizenship grant. Administrative fee of USD 10,000 transferred from abroad to the Central Bank of Egypt. Upon security authority approval, investor is granted temporary residence for 6 months to execute the chosen investment program. Citizenship granted to investor and minor children up to age 21, by decision of the Prime Minister. Unit is affiliated with the Prime Minister's Office and located at GAFI headquarters. Security clearance required.

cbi.name: El Salvador
cbi.program_name: Adopting El Salvador – Freedom Passport (Pasaporte de la Libertad)

options.notes: Total investment of USD 1,000,000 payable in Bitcoin (BTC) or Tether (USDt). Payment is split: a non-refundable application fee of USD 999 in BTC or USDt to commence evaluation, then USD 999,001 upon approval. Additional administrative fee of USD 999 per family member for family applications. Annual quota of 1,000 investors per year. Investment directed toward El Salvador's economic development, cultural enrichment, and social programs. Grants Salvadoran citizenship including right to vote. Reported processing time ~6 weeks. Spouse and dependent children under 18 may be included in one application.

cbi.processing_time: Approximately 6 weeks (as stated on official world.adoptingelsalvador.gob.sv)
cbi.notes: The program is branded 'Adopting El Salvador' and operated via the government domain world.adoptingelsalvador.gob.sv and adoptingelsalvador.gob.sv. The program is confirmed active as of mid-2026. Bitcoin lost mandatory legal-tender status in January 2025 but remains legal to use; the program now also accepts Tether (USDt) in addition to BTC. The Legislative Assembly separately approved reforms in May 2025 (57 votes) to Art. 152 of the Special Law on Migration and Foreigners, allowing foreigners who invest or donate in government-promoted programs to obtain definitive residence directly (skipping temporary residence), with a fee of USD 690. This reform covers residency rather than citizenship. Separately, 5,000 free passports for highly qualified scientists, engineers, doctors, artists, and philosophers were announced, but official details on that sub-program with specific eligibility criteria are not publicly documented.

cbi.name: Georgia
cbi.program_name: Georgian Citizenship by Exception / Special Contribution Citizenship Program

options.notes: Investment in a Georgian business employing at least 10 local citizens. Based on Article 17(2)(b) of the Organic Law of Georgia on Georgian Citizenship (investment contributing substantially to state economy development).
Refundable contribution to a government-approved fund, held for at least 5 years then fully refunded. Announced February 2025 as part of the Special Contribution Citizenship Program.

Non-refundable contribution to a special state fund. A discounted early-applicant rate of EUR 250,000 was offered at program launch (February 2025). Based on President's authority under Article 17(1) for exceptional merit/contribution.

cbi.notes: Georgia does not have a standalone CBI program in the traditional sense. Citizenship by exception is granted by the President under Article 17 of the Organic Law on Georgian Citizenship. The 'Special Contribution Citizenship Program' was announced February 24, 2025 by Deputy Foreign Minister Khvtisiashvili. Dual citizenship is permitted for those granted citizenship under Article 17 and Article 21-1 of the law. No language test or residency required for citizenship by exception. Regular naturalization requires 10 years of continuous lawful residence. The specific investment amounts (EUR 3M business / EUR 2M refundable fund / EUR 300K donation) were announced for the program but the official government implementing regulation details were not directly verifiable on matsne.gov.ge at time of research - figures sourced from government official announcements reported in February 2025.

cbi.name: Grenada
cbi.program_name: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Programme

options.notes: Non-refundable contribution to the National Transformation Fund (NTF). USD 235,000 is the updated minimum effective July 1, 2024 (per SR&O amendments and Caribbean MOA price standardisation). NOTE: The cbi.gov.gd homepage still displayed USD 150,000 as of June 2026 - this appears to be a website update lag; the SR&O-amended figure of USD 235,000 is confirmed by multiple licensed agent sources citing the official SR&O. The NTF finances projects in tourism, agriculture, and alternative energy sectors. Applications must be submitted through an Authorised Local or International Marketing Agent.

Investment in government-approved real estate projects. Minimum USD 270,000 effective July 1, 2024 (per SR&O 15 of 2024 / Caribbean MOA price standardisation). Applicant must hold the real estate for at least 5 years following the grant of citizenship. Projects include approved luxury hotels, resorts, and villas. Applications must be submitted through an Authorised Agent. Some approved projects may have different minimums (e.g. USD 220,000 for shared/fractional units vs USD 350,000 for sole-ownership units) - the USD 270,000 is the general programme minimum.

cbi.notes: Programme established under the Citizenship by Investment Act, 2013 (Act No. 15 of 2013). No requirement to reside in Grenada before or after citizenship is granted. Citizenship can be extended to spouse, dependent children under 18, dependent parents, and dependent grandchildren. Applicant must be at least 18 years old, have no criminal record, and be in good health. All applications must be submitted through Authorised Agents to the Citizenship by Investment Committee (CBIC). Key benefit: Grenada citizenship grants E-2 Treaty Investor Visa eligibility for the United States. Official cbi.gov.gd website confirmed processing time as 'Three - four months'.

cbi.name: Jordan
cbi.program_name: Jordanian Citizenship by Investment Program

options.notes: Medical sector (pharmaceutical warehouses, production/distribution of medical/surgical/healthcare equipment) OR food and logistics sector (food logistics services and large-scale storage facilities): minimum JOD 3,000,000 per partner; project must be operational meeting Jordanian employment requirements for 36 continuous months; must create 20 jobs in Amman or 10 jobs outside Amman. Grants Jordanian citizenship directly.

Existing investment within Amman: investor's average share of eligible fixed/tangible non-current assets >= JOD 700,000 over 3 years per audited financial statements; at least 90% Jordanian workforce with minimum 20 Jordanian employees average over 3-year period. Grants citizenship directly.
Existing investment outside Amman: investor's average share of eligible fixed/tangible non-current assets >= JOD 350,000 over 3 years per audited financial statements. Grants citizenship directly.

Stock market investment: purchase new shares >= JOD 1,000,000 distributed among at least 5 companies with max 20% in any single company; purchase completed within 4 months from Ministry of Investment letter to Jordan Securities Commission; trading permitted but profits/proceeds must be reinvested within 30 days. Grants citizenship directly.

Employment-based: employ at least 150 Jordanians in Amman or 100 outside Amman; all registered with Social Security Corporation for >= 1 year; same workforce maintained 2 consecutive years with written commitment to continue. No minimum capital floor. Grants citizenship directly.

New project in Amman (temporary passport pathway): >= JOD 700,000 investment + 20 Jordanian jobs. Investor receives temporary Jordanian passport valid 3 years; citizenship may be recommended upon verified full compliance.

New project outside Amman (temporary passport pathway): >= JOD 500,000 investment + 10 Jordanian jobs. Investor receives temporary Jordanian passport valid 3 years; citizenship may be recommended upon verified full compliance.

Purchase of shares in existing project (temporary passport pathway): >= JOD 1,000,000 with 50% allocated to fixed assets; must create 20% new Jordanian jobs; shares locked 3 years. Investor receives temporary Jordanian passport valid 3 years; citizenship recommended upon full compliance.

cbi.notes: Program comprehensively overhauled 2 July 2025. All passive investment options (bank deposits, treasury bonds, direct real estate for citizenship) eliminated. Eight active investment pathways now required, all requiring job creation. Annual cap of 500 investors. Two tiers: (1) direct citizenship grants; (2) temporary passport (3-year) pathway leading to citizenship. Real estate no longer grants citizenship - only a 5-year renewable residency permit. Applications via Ministry of Investment E-Services Portal at https://portal.moin.gov.jo/Investment/LoginPage. Program administered by the Ministry of Investment in coordination with Ministry of Interior per Council of Ministers criteria. Reforms reviewed every 6 months per July 2025 decree. Re-validation 2026-06-27: invest.jo returned HTTP 403; CBI structure confirmed unchanged via third-party aggregator cross-checks (amounts and structure match July 2025 cabinet decision).

cbi.name: Laos
cbi.program_name: Honorary Citizenship by Investment (Decree No. 14 of 2022)

options.notes: Minimum USD 500,000 donation toward socio-economic development of Laos (required in addition to the investment component)
Minimum USD 1,000,000 foreign investment into Laos (required in addition to the donation component). Total minimum commitment: USD 1,500,000.

cbi.processing_time: Ministry of Justice reviews within 5 business days of receipt, then evaluates for 30 days before forwarding to government for further review. Applications submitted to Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Lao consulate/embassy abroad.
cbi.notes: Decree No. 14 issued September 2022, announced October 2022. This is HONORARY citizenship, not full citizenship - it does not confer all rights of ordinary Lao citizens. Honorary citizens receive: visa-free entry/exit of Laos, right to reside permanently, right to purchase state-owned land for specified period, right to lease state and privately-owned land. Cannot own land outright. Applicants must be 18+, have no criminal record for intentional crimes, good health, no illegal drug use/conviction. Professional qualifications at doctorate/professor level preferred. Program has drawn skepticism due to honorary (not full) nature and Lao passport's low global mobility. Operational status as a functioning program in 2026 is uncertain - the program was gazetted but implementation details and whether applications are actively processed remains unclear from official sources only.

cbi.name: Mauritius
cbi.program_name: Naturalization for Investors (Section 9(3) Mauritius Citizenship Act)

options.notes: Under section 9(3) of the Mauritius Citizenship Act, an investor may be naturalized as a citizen if: (i) he has invested a sum of not less than USD 500,000 in Mauritius; and (ii) he has resided in Mauritius for a continuous period of not less than 2 years preceding the date of application. This is naturalization-by-investment (investor route), not a standalone CBI program with a direct donation option. Application submitted to the Secretary for Home Affairs; declaration made before a Supreme Court Judge or Magistrate; applicants must place advertisements in two daily newspapers.

cbi.notes: Mauritius does not have a dedicated citizenship-by-investment program (no donation-only CBI). The only investment pathway to citizenship is via naturalization under Section 9(3) of the Mauritius Citizenship Act, which requires both a minimum investment of USD 500,000 AND 2 years of continuous residency. Dual citizenship policy not explicitly stated on the official DHA citizenship page. Contact: pmo.citizenship@govmu.org.

cbi.name: Nauru
cbi.program_name: Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program (ECRCP)

options.notes: Contribution to the Nauru Treasury Fund. Standard rate USD 90,000 for a principal applicant (effective as of the Iruwa Initiative restructuring in early 2026). A limited-time promotional rate of USD 65,000 applies for the Iruwa Initiative (USD 25,000 discount from 3 February 2026): the ecrcp.gov.nr/contribution page body states deadline is 31 December 2026, while the ecrcp.gov.nr homepage and footer quote 30 June 2026 — the official page contains conflicting dates (both re-fetched 2026-06-29); the later date (31 December 2026) is recorded as the operative deadline in the contribution page body. Additional dependant contribution: USD 2,000 per dependent aged 16+; USD 15,000 per sibling of principal applicant or spouse (USD 17,000 if sibling is aged 16+). Application fee: USD 5,000 (principal applicant), USD 2,000 per dependent. Due diligence fee: USD 6,000 (principal applicant), USD 3,000 per dependent aged 16+, USD 3,000 per benefactor. Bank due diligence/transaction charges: USD 1,200 (applicant alone), USD 1,700 (applicant + up to 3 dependents), USD 2,200 (applicant + 4+ dependents), USD 1,000 per benefactor. Passport fee: USD 500 per passport. Source: ecrcp.gov.nr/contribution (official Nauru Program Office website).

cbi.processing_time: Three to four months from date of application submission
cbi.notes: Program allows unrestricted dual citizenship with no minimum stay or visit requirements. January 2026 Iruwa Initiative restructuring introduced: removal of age caps for children and parents, elimination of financial dependency requirements, abolition of marital status restrictions for dependent qualification. Family members eligible: spouse, dependent children, parents, siblings. Principal applicant must be at least 18 years old. Dependents aged 16+ may be required to attend interviews. No travel to Nauru required; Oath of Allegiance may be taken via audio-visual link or before a notary. Applications must be submitted through a licensed Agent. Source: ecrcp.gov.nr (official Nauru Program Office website).

cbi.name: North Macedonia
cbi.program_name: North Macedonia Citizenship by Investment Program

options.notes: Investment in a private investment fund established under North Macedonia law for at least 2 years. The fund must have minimum EUR 5,000,000 initial capital, invest in support of the economy/innovation (not real estate), and have no more than 500 foreign investor-applicants.
Direct investment in new business facilities (excluding hospitality/restaurants/shopping) that create at least 10 new job positions maintained for at least 1 year. Per adult applicant.

cbi.processing_time: 5–10 months (officially stated as ~5 months; industry sources estimate 8–10 months)
cbi.notes: Program was legislated in 2019 and has an annual quota of 1,000 applicants. Application fees: EUR 20,000 for main applicant, EUR 20,000 for spouse, EUR 10,000 per child under 18. As of 2026, Henley & Partners describes the program as 'under development - the government is currently in the process of setting up the program.' No passports have been confirmed as issued under this program since it was introduced. The official site mkcitizenship.gov.mk remains registered but was unreachable (ECONNREFUSED) during this research session. Program should be treated as legislatively active but operationally non-functional pending full government setup.

cbi.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
cbi.program_name: St. Kitts and Nevis Citizenship by Investment Programme

options.notes: Sustainable Island State Contribution (SISC) - minimum US$250,000 for main applicant or family up to 4 persons. Contributions support national development priorities including renewable energy, healthcare and education. Source: https://ciu.gov.kn/cbi-options/

Public Benefit Option (PBO) - minimum US$250,000 per unit contribution to Approved Public Benefit Projects that foster economic growth and job creation (infrastructure including schools, housing, arts centers, resorts, airport expansion). Source: https://ciu.gov.kn/press-st-kitts-and-nevis-citizenship-by-investment-faqs/
Developer's Real Estate Investment - minimum US$325,000 in an Approved Development (condo/unit in approved development). Resaleable after 7 years. Source: https://ciu.gov.kn/cbi-options/
Private Real Estate Sale (Single-Family Home) - purchase an exclusive private single-family home for at least US$600,000. Source: https://ciu.gov.kn/cbi-options/

cbi.processing_time: 160-180 days from submission to approval in principle
cbi.notes: World's first and oldest Citizenship by Investment Programme, established in 1984, administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CIU). Dual citizenship explicitly allowed. No mandatory residency requirement to maintain citizenship once granted. Official CIU FAQs state processing takes 160-180 days from submission to approval-in-principle; actual investment made after approval-in-principle is issued. Applications must be submitted through Authorised Agents only; cannot apply directly to CIU. Due diligence fees: US$10,000 (main applicant), US$7,500 per dependent aged 16+. Post-approval fees: US$10,000-US$25,000 depending on dependents. Banned nationalities: Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Russia. Citizenship can be passed to future generations. No personal income tax, wealth tax, or inheritance tax. CIU website updated December 2025 (Chairman's Update reference noted) but no changes to minimum investment amounts confirmed. Sources: https://ciu.gov.kn/cbi-options/, https://ciu.gov.kn/application-process/, https://ciu.gov.kn/eligibility-criteria/, https://ciu.gov.kn/press-st-kitts-and-nevis-citizenship-by-investment-faqs/

cbi.name: Saint Lucia
cbi.program_name: Saint Lucia Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP)

options.notes: National Economic Fund (NEF) donation: US$240,000 for single applicant with up to 3 dependents (raised from US$100,000 by the Citizenship by Investment Amendment Act, July 2024, to meet the Caribbean regional MOU threshold). Additional dependents under 18: US$10,000 each; over 18: US$20,000 each; spouse: US$35,000; newborn (<=12 months): US$5,000. Non-refundable.
National Action Bond (NAB): US$300,000 non-interest bearing bond with 5-year hold period. Non-refundable admin fee of US$50,000 additional.

Investment in approved real estate projects (high-end branded hotels, resorts, boutique properties): minimum US$300,000 plus administrative fees (US$30,000 single / US$45,000 with spouse). Current approved projects include A'ILA Resorts Villas & Residences; Canelles Resort (fully subscribed as of 2026).

Enterprise Project: Option 1 (solo): US$3,500,000 + US$50,000 admin fee; Option 2 (joint venture min US$1M per person): US$6,000,000 total + US$50,000 admin fee; Option 3 (with up to 3 dependents): US$250,000 + admin fees US$15,000-US$30,000. Eligible sectors: infrastructure, restaurants, marinas, agro-processing, universities, housing, social development. Application fee US$2,000 (main applicant) + US$1,000 per dependent. Due diligence fee US$8,000 (main) + US$5,000 per dependent (16+).

cbi.processing_time: Approximately 90 days from acceptance of application for processing
cbi.notes: Established under the Citizenship by Investment Act No. 14 of 2015. Administered by the Citizenship by Investment Board (statutory body). Amended July 2024 to raise NEF minimum to US$240,000 (Citizenship by Investment Amendment Act 2024). Dual citizenship: Saint Lucia generally permits dual citizenship. No residency requirement - entire process can be completed remotely. Official program URL is cipsaintlucia.com (government-operated Citizenship by Investment Unit website).

cbi.name: Samoa
cbi.program_name: Citizenship Investment Program (Citizenship Investment Act 2015)

options.notes: Investment in qualifying sectors: leasing and developing government lands; processing or manufacturing of agricultural or fishery products; tourism hotel resort development; information and communication technology; renewable electricity generation (solar, biofuel); or other services not restricted under the Foreign Investment Act 2000. Minimum net worth requirement of WST 2.5 million also cited in secondary sources. The Samoa Chamber of Commerce and Industry proposed in October 2025 to reduce the threshold to WST 2 million, but this reduction had not been enacted as of June 2026.

Investment in a government development fund for national development purposes. This option was proposed following Cabinet approval of recommendations in May 2024. Minimum amount not independently confirmed from an accessible official document as of June 2026.

cbi.processing_time: Minimum 3-year timeline: begins with temporary resident permit, progresses to permanent resident permit (with minimum 15 days per year physical presence requirement), then citizenship eligibility after 3 years.
cbi.notes: The program was established under the Citizenship Investment Act 2015 and officially launched on 31 January 2017. It is administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). As of 2025 reporting, no investor has successfully completed the process - the only application filed was subsequently withdrawn. In May 2024, Cabinet approved recommendations to amend the Act, including adding government bonds and national development fund as qualifying investment options. A stakeholder validation workshop was held on 26 September 2025 at Tanoa Hotel to develop a revised policy framework. The prior CBI-specific page at mcil.gov.ws/?page_id=2879 (old WordPress URL) no longer resolves to a CBI page - MCIL has migrated to a new Drupal site. CBI brochure PDFs from mcil.gov.ws returned 404 at time of research (June 2026). Investment amounts are drawn from secondary sources referencing the Citizenship Investment Act 2015 and Regulations 2016; they could not be independently confirmed from a directly accessible official PDF.

cbi.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
cbi.program_name: São Tomé and Príncipe Citizenship by Investment Program

options.notes: Non-refundable contribution to the National Transformation Fund. Single applicant: USD 90,000. Family of 2–4: USD 95,000. Each additional dependent: USD 5,000. Citizenship documents per dependent: USD 750. Submission fee: USD 5,000 per application. Post-approval addition fees: spouse USD 10,000; qualifying dependent USD 5,000; newborn (up to 1 year) USD 500. Program governed by Nationality Law No. 07/2022 and Decree-Law No. 07/2025. No real estate investment option currently available.

cbi.processing_time: 1.5–3 months to decision (official CIP site states 'approvals in as little as two months'); post-approval passport issuance approximately 3 months
cbi.notes: The program was officially launched on August 1, 2025, with practical acceptance of applications starting September 2025. 220+ applications received since launch as of late 2025. Administered by the Citizenship Investment Unit (CIU) under a public-private partnership, headquartered in Dubai, UAE. Applications must be submitted via a licensed Marketing Agent. Citizenship is granted for life and can be passed to future generations. Dual citizenship explicitly allowed. Physical visit to São Tomé and Príncipe is not required. Legal basis: Nationality Law No. 07/2022 and Decree-Law No. 07/2025. Official government portal: cip.gov.st (.gov.st domain). Blockchain-enabled citizenship system launched September 2025.

cbi.name: Sierra Leone
cbi.program_name: Naturalization of Qualifying Foreign National Investors (GO-FOR-GOLD pathway)
cbi.notes: The Sierra Leone Immigration Department (SLID) issued an official press release on 2 January 2025 announcing 'groundbreaking measures aimed at facilitating the naturalization of qualifying high-net-worth foreign national investors.' The release references the GO-FOR-GOLD residency program launched December 2024, which includes an upgrade pathway to citizenship. A CBI programme therefore exists officially. However, the specific investment minimums, fees, and detailed program structure are NOT stated on any *.gov.sl page; those details appear only on the private commercial operator website goforgold.center (TG 2050 LTD). Therefore no financial options are recorded per hard rules. The SLID website as of June 2026 does not feature active articles on this programme, creating uncertainty about current status.

cbi.name: Turkey
cbi.program_name: Turkish Citizenship by Investment (Exceptional Naturalisation)

options.notes: Acquiring property worth minimum USD 400,000 (or equivalent foreign currency) with title deed restriction on resale for at least three years; attested by Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change
Fixed capital investment of minimum USD 500,000 or equivalent foreign currency; verified by Ministry of Industry and Technology
Creating employment for at least 50 people; confirmed by Ministry of Labor and Social Security
Bank deposit of minimum USD 500,000 in Turkish banks with three-year non-withdrawal condition; attested by Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency
Purchase of minimum USD 500,000 in government bonds with three-year holding requirement; attested by Ministry of Treasury and Finance
Acquiring minimum USD 500,000 in real estate investment fund or venture capital fund shares; three-year non-sale condition; attested by Capital Markets Board
Contributing minimum USD 500,000 to private pension funds approved by Insurance and Private Pension Regulation and Supervision Agency; three-year minimum holding

cbi.processing_time: Not specified on official page; decision rests with the President of the Republic of Turkey
cbi.notes: Officially called 'exceptional naturalisation' under Turkish Citizenship Law. Residency permit not required as a precondition; property buyers receive renewable short-term residence permits automatically. All investment routes require attestation by relevant ministry. Dual citizenship is permitted under Turkish law (Law No. 5901). Source: invest.gov.tr (Republic of Turkey Investment Office, official government body). Real estate threshold confirmed still at USD 400,000 as of June 2026 (unchanged from September 2018 regulations).

cbi.name: Vanuatu
cbi.program_name: Vanuatu Citizenship by Investment (Programs: DSP/VCP, CIIP/Form D, REO)

options.notes: Development Support Program (DSP) / Vanuatu Contribution Program (VCP): Non-refundable contribution to the Vanuatu National Development Fund. Government-mandated fees: Single applicant USD 130,000; Married couple USD 150,000; Married couple + 1 child USD 165,000; Married couple + 2 children USD 180,000; Additional dependent USD 10,000 each. FIU Diligence Fee USD 5,000. Application fee 5,000 VUV (paid upon lodging). Citizenship fee paid only after Commission approval. Source: vancitizenship.gov.vu/index.php/citizenship/fees-and-charges

Real Estate Option Program (REO): Investment in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project (VGA Project). Commenced July 23, 2021. Four currently approved projects: Pacific Springs (Efate), Narpow Point Coral Bay (Efate), FPF Rainbow City Project (Efate), Milai (Espiritu Santo). Citizenship fees per family size structure apply on top of property investment. Minimum property investment amount not stated verbatim on official page. Source: vancitizenship.gov.vu/index.php/news-and-updates/101-real-estate-option-program-reo

Capital Investment Immigration Plan (CIIP) / Form D: Application fee USD 250. Citizenship fee USD 260,000 covers applicant, spouse, and 1 child under 18. Additional child under 18: USD 19,250 per person. Dependent aged 18–21: USD 44,250 per person. FIU Diligence Fee USD 5,000. Source: vancitizenship.gov.vu/index.php/citizenship/fees-and-charges

cbi.processing_time: Not specified on official pages; 3 months allowed to complete oath and pay fees after Commission approval (with possible 2-month extension upon written request).
cbi.notes: The Vanuatu Citizenship Office (vancitizenship.gov.vu) operates under the Office of the Prime Minister. Programs confirmed active: DSP/VCP, CIIP (Form D), REO. Dual citizenship policy is not stated explicitly on any official page found. Residency is NOT required for CBI programs. The EU removed Vanuatu from its visa-exemption list in December 2024 partly due to concerns about the CBI program. CBI fees confirmed directly from official fees-and-charges page (June 2026). Applicants should confirm current fees directly with the Citizenship Office as fees may be updated.

rbi.name: Albania
rbi.program_name: Unique Permit for Investors (Leje Unike per Investitorin)
rbi.notes: Based on Article 69 of Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners'. Minimum investment of 10,000,000 ALL (approximately EUR 85,000-90,000) - figure set by joint instruction of the Ministers of Finance and Interior; not independently verifiable from the official law text. One secondary legal source (imidaily.com, 2026) references a possible Law 43/2025 that may have updated investment thresholds significantly (e.g., EUR 300,000 for real estate, EUR 100,000 for business), but this could not be confirmed from any official Albanian government publication. Requires employment of 5 Albanian citizens per foreign investor. Initial permit valid 2 years, renewable for 3 years. After 5 years of legal residence, eligible for permanent residency. Standard naturalization requires 7 years of continuous residence.

rbi.name: Albania
rbi.program_name: Residence Permit via Real Estate Ownership
rbi.notes: Based on Article 84 of Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners'. A residence permit can be obtained through registered real estate ownership in Albania (applicant must own at least 50%). No statutory minimum investment amount is defined in the law. After 5 years of continuous legal residence, eligible for permanent residency permit. Standard naturalization requires 7 years of continuous residence.

rbi.name: Albania
rbi.program_name: Unique Permit for Digital Mobile Workers (Nomad/Remote Work)
rbi.notes: Introduced under Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners', for remote workers employed by or freelancing for companies/clients outside Albania. Available via e-Albania portal (service code 15146). Structure: 1 year initial + 1 year renewal + up to 5-year permit from year 3. Minimum income threshold referenced in secondary sources (approx. EUR 450/month); not independently verified from official law text. After 5 years of continuous legal residence, eligible for permanent residency.

rbi.name: Andorra
rbi.notes: Requires a minimum investment of €1,000,000 (one million euros) permanently and effectively in Andorran assets (real estate, corporate shareholdings, debt instruments, collective investment funds, public debt, life insurance products, or non-remunerated AFA deposits). Special provision: investment reduced to €400,000 if directed to the Andorran Housing Fund. Additionally, a non-refundable payment of €50,000 to the Andorran Financial Authority (AFA) is required for the main applicant, plus €12,000 per dependent. Under the prior regime the AFA deposit was refundable; Llei 2/2026 made it non-refundable. Investment threshold raised from €600,000 to €1,000,000 by Llei 2/2026 of 22 January 2026 (BOPA No. 15, 12 February 2026; in force 13 February 2026). Minimum stay: 90 days per calendar year. Work/business activity not permitted under this permit. First authorization valid 2 years; first renewal 2 years; second renewal 3 years; subsequent renewals 10 years. Official regulation: portaljuridicandorra.ad/L2026002 (Art. 96) and portaljuridicandorra.ad/R20251112A.

rbi.name: Andorra
rbi.program_name: Residència i treball per a professionals amb projecció internacional (Residency for Professionals with International Projection)
rbi.notes: For professionals and entrepreneurs who carry out activity with at least 85% of income/work generated outside Andorra. Requires establishing or acquiring an Andorran company (minimum 34% shareholding). Non-refundable payment of €50,000 to AFA (made non-refundable by Llei 2/2026) plus €12,000 per dependent, and investment of €1,000,000 in Andorran assets (post-Llei 2/2026). Minimum stay: 90 days per year. Governed by the Qualified Immigration Law as amended by Llei 2/2026.

rbi.name: Andorra
rbi.program_name: Residència i treball per compte propi (Self-Employed/Active Residency)
rbi.notes: For self-employed individuals establishing a business in Andorra. Requires constituting or acquiring an Andorran company (at least 34% shareholding) and obtaining a Foreign Investment Authorization. Non-refundable AFA payment of €50,000 (non-refundable under Llei 2/2026; Art. 38 ter) plus €12,000 per dependent. Must reside in Andorra for at least 183 days per year. Governed by Qualified Immigration Law as amended by Llei 2/2026 (portaljuridicandorra.ad/L2026002).

rbi.name: Angola
rbi.notes: The investor visa is granted by the Migration Authority (SME) to foreign investors or representatives of investing companies under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May (Legal System of Foreign Citizens, DP 13/19). It allows multiple entries and is valid for up to 2 years. After 3 years of uninterrupted stay, the holder may apply for a temporary residence permit. No minimum investment amount is stated on official source pages for the visa itself - any amount is eligible under the 2021 Private Investment Law (Law No. 10/21 of 22 April 2021). Application requires: criminal record certificate, medical certificate, passport copy (6 months validity), proof of investment registration (CRIP from AIPEX), two photographs, and proof of fee payment. Investor visas are obtained through Angolan consular missions. Source: Official Angola Consulate Dubai Investors & Tourism Guide (angolaconsulate.ae, official consulate domain).

rbi.name: Angola
rbi.notes: The SME portal lists a 'Titulo de Residencia Prorrogacao' (Residence Title Extension) as an available service. A special CPLP-track residence title extension ('Titulo de Residencia Prorrogacao CPLP') is also available for nationals of Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries (CPLP) member states. Specific eligibility criteria and minimum stay requirements are behind the login portal and could not be retrieved from public-facing official pages.

rbi.name: Antigua and Barbuda
rbi.program_name: Antigua and Barbuda Permanent Residence Scheme
rbi.notes: Introduced in 1995. Targets high-net-worth individuals. Requirements: demonstrated minimum annual income of USD $100,000; payment of flat annual tax of USD $20,000; minimum physical presence of 30 days per year in Antigua and Barbuda. PDF could not be directly fetched; document is referenced from immigration.gov.ag/general-services/residency/.

rbi.name: Antigua and Barbuda
rbi.notes: Available to any person who has been legally and ordinarily resident in Antigua and Barbuda for at least 4 years, or married to an Antiguan citizen for at least 1 year. Standard immigration residency route, not an investment program.

rbi.name: Argentina
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence as Investor (Non-MERCOSUR) - Residencia Temporaria como Inversionista
rbi.notes: For non-MERCOSUR nationals. Minimum investment of ARS 1,500,000 in a productive, commercial, or service activity. Temporary residence granted for 1 year, renewable for up to 3 years. After 2 years of residence and maintaining the investment, holders become eligible for citizenship; at year 3 eligible for permanent residency. No sector restriction. Requires title of property, securities, or partnership participation proving the effective capital investment. CAUTION: ARS 1,500,000 is subject to erosion from inflation and may not reflect current real-terms threshold - official page returned 403 on re-check and amount could not be independently re-verified as of June 2026.

rbi.name: Argentina
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence as Investor (MERCOSUR) - Residencia Temporaria como Inversionista Mercosur
rbi.notes: For MERCOSUR member and associate state nationals (Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname). Same investment requirements as non-MERCOSUR investor category. Temporary residence for 1 year, renewable up to 3 years. ARS amount subject to same inflation caveat as non-MERCOSUR program.

rbi.name: Argentina
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence as Rentista (Passive Income) - Residencia Temporaria como Rentista
rbi.notes: For foreign nationals with regular passive income from abroad (pensions, annuities, dividends, rents, etc.). Specific minimum income amount not confirmed from official source. Temporary residence for up to 2 years, renewable.

rbi.name: Argentina
rbi.program_name: Special Transitional Residency for Business/Investment Studies - Residencia Transitoria Especial para Negocios e Inversiones
rbi.notes: Short-term (2 months, extendable) transitional residence for conducting business negotiations, investments, commercial representation, or market studies. Does not lead to permanent residence directly.

rbi.name: Armenia
rbi.notes: Issued for up to 1 year, renewable annually. Eligible if: studying in Armenia; holding work permit in Armenia; spouse/parent/child of a Temporary Resident Card holder; relative of Armenian citizen or Special Passport holder; running business activity in Armenia; Armenian national; or other cases prescribed by law. Fee: 105,000 AMD (US citizens: 85,000 AMD). Processing time: up to 30 days. 3 years of lawful permanent residence enables citizenship application.

rbi.name: Armenia
rbi.notes: Issued for 5 years, extendable by 5 years. Eligible if: running business activity in Armenia; relative of Armenian citizen or Special Passport holder who has legally resided in Armenia for 3 years and has adequate accommodation/property; Armenian national. Fee: 140,000 AMD (US citizens: 90,000 AMD). Processing time: up to 30 days. No specific minimum investment amount stated on official page.

rbi.name: Armenia
rbi.notes: Granted by the Prime Minister for 10 years. Available to foreign citizens of Armenian ancestry and distinguished individuals who have provided significant services to the Armenian state and nation or are engaged in economic/cultural activities in Armenia. Holders receive a Special Armenian Passport, no visa required for Armenia, and enjoy rights/obligations of Armenian citizens except voting, running for office, and military service. State duty: 150,000 AMD. Processing time: approximately 3-4 months. Not an investment-specific program - no minimum investment stated. Genocide survivors receive this through a facilitated fee-waived procedure.

rbi.name: Australia
rbi.program_name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa - Investor Stream (subclass 188) [CLOSED]
rbi.notes: CLOSED to new applications as of 31 July 2024. Existing applications lodged before 31 July 2024 continue to be processed. The live official page confirms minimum investment of AUD 2.5 million (updated from the previously recorded AUD 1.5 million - the official page now states 'at least AUD2.5 million'). Leads to permanent residence via subclass 888. Must be nominated by a state/territory government. Points test required.

rbi.name: Australia
rbi.program_name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa - Significant Investor Stream (subclass 188) [CLOSED]
rbi.notes: CLOSED to new applications as of 31 July 2024. Existing applications lodged before 31 July 2024 continue to be processed. Required investment of at least AUD 5 million in complying significant investments under the Complying Investment Framework (CIF). Leads to permanent residence via subclass 888. No points test.

rbi.name: Australia
rbi.program_name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa - Premium Investor Stream (subclass 188) [CLOSED]
rbi.notes: CLOSED to new applications as of 31 July 2024. Required investment of AUD 15 million. Only available by nomination by Austrade on behalf of the Australian government. Leads to permanent residency via subclass 888.

rbi.name: Australia
rbi.program_name: Business Innovation and Investment (Provisional) visa - Business Innovation Stream (subclass 188) [CLOSED]
rbi.notes: CLOSED to new applications as of 31 July 2024. For people with business skills who wanted to establish, develop and manage a new or existing business in Australia. Points test required (minimum 65 points). Must be nominated by a state/territory government or Austrade. Leads to permanent residency via subclass 888.

rbi.name: Australia
rbi.notes: Permanent residence visa for holders of subclass 188 (provisional) granted before program closure. Multiple streams: Business Innovation, Investor, Significant Investor, Entrepreneur, Premium Investor. Applicants must have held the provisional visa and continued to meet requirements. Still being processed for existing subclass 188 holders.

rbi.name: Austria
rbi.program_name: Red-White-Red Card – Very Highly Qualified Workers
rbi.notes: Points-based system; minimum 70 points required. Key criteria: tertiary education (up to 40 pts), work experience (up to 20 pts), language skills (up to 10 pts), age under 35–45 (up to 20 pts), Austrian studies (up to 10 pts). Card valid 24 months, employer-tied. After 24 months with min. 21 months employment, eligible for Red-White-Red Card Plus (unrestricted labor market access). Standard citizenship requires 10 years legal residence (5 with residence permit).

rbi.name: Austria
rbi.program_name: Red-White-Red Card – Skilled Workers in Shortage Occupations
rbi.notes: For skilled workers in occupations on the Austrian shortage occupation list. Points-based assessment. Card valid 24 months, employer-tied. Eligible for Red-White-Red Card Plus after 24 months.

rbi.name: Austria
rbi.notes: Self-employed must demonstrate macroeconomic benefit through at least one of: minimum €100,000 capital transfer to Austria, job creation/preservation, knowledge/technology transfer, or regional economic significance. No points system applies. Processing of macroeconomic benefit assessment by Public Employment Service (AMS) within 3 weeks. Card valid 24 months. Minimum amount verified against official source.

rbi.name: Austria
rbi.notes: Requires founding a company developing innovative products/services/technologies, a coherent business plan, controlling influence (min. 50% equity), and minimum €30,000 capital. Minimum 50 points required. Points system: Qualification max 30 pts (vocational 20, tertiary 20, Austrian degree 30), Work Experience max 10 pts (1 pt per half-year), Language max 15 pts (German A2=5, B1-B2=10, C1-C2=15; English B2=10), Bonus max 30 pts (€50k+ extra capital=10, incubator=10, age ≤35=10). AMS reviews within 3 weeks. Card valid up to 24 months. Points system updated: maximum is 85 pts total (not previously specified).

rbi.name: Austria
rbi.notes: For third-country nationals with university degree (min. 3 years) and job offer for min. 6 months. Salary must equal at least the average gross annual salary for full-time employees. Card issued for 24 months. After 21 of 24 months in employment, eligible for Red-White-Red Card Plus.

rbi.name: Austria
rbi.notes: Grants unrestricted labor market access and fixed-term settlement. Available to: holders of RWR Card after successful first period, EU Blue Card holders after 21 months employment, family members of RWR Card holders. Leads eventually to long-term EU settlement permit and standard naturalization after 10 years legal residence.

rbi.name: Azerbaijan
rbi.notes: Foreigners can obtain a temporary residence permit by: (1) possessing real estate worth at least AZN 100,000 in Azerbaijan; (2) holding a fixed-term bank deposit of at least AZN 100,000 in Azerbaijani banks; (3) owning government securities or state-majority (51%+) company investment securities with nominal value of at least AZN 100,000; or (4) making a general economic investment of at least AZN 500,000. Initial permit issued for period requested (up to 1 year); extendable each time for up to 2 years.

rbi.name: Azerbaijan
rbi.notes: Foreigners can obtain a permanent residence permit after 2 years of continuous temporary residence by: (1) possessing real estate worth at least AZN 200,000; (2) holding a fixed-term bank deposit of at least AZN 200,000; (3) owning securities with nominal value of at least AZN 200,000; or (4) maintaining general economic investment of at least AZN 500,000. Permanent permits issued for 5 years, extendable for further 5-year periods.

rbi.name: Azerbaijan
rbi.program_name: Highly Qualified Specialist Temporary Residence Permit
rbi.notes: Highly qualified specialists in spheres of economy, industry, military, science, culture, sports, etc. may obtain a temporary residence permit for up to 1 year (extendable up to 2 years). Requires a justified application from the inviting authority, enterprise, or organization. After 2 years of continuous temporary residence, transition to permanent residence is possible.

rbi.name: Bahamas
rbi.notes: Minimum investment of USD $1.0 million either through real estate or purchase of Zero Coupon Bonds from the Central Bank of The Bahamas. Both investment types must be held for a minimum of 10 years. The current immigration.gov.bs page does not specify an expedited/speedy consideration threshold for BSD $1.5 million real estate - this detail could not be re-confirmed on the live page and has been moved to gaps. Processing fee: $200 non-refundable. Requires medical certificate (within 30 days), police certificate (within 6 months, covering 5 years of residence), passport photographs, birth certificate, two character references. Path to citizenship requires 10 years as permanent resident (including 12 months immediately before application) plus 6 years prior residency.

rbi.name: Bahrain
rbi.notes: Bahrain Golden Residency program offering permanent residency. Multiple eligibility tracks: (1) Property investors: minimum BHD 130,000 (USD 345,000) personal share value, may combine multiple properties; (2) Professionals: 5+ years continuous employment in Bahrain with average monthly basic salary exceeding BHD 2,000; (3) Resident retirees: 15+ years Bahrain employment, pension BHD 2,000+/month; (4) Non-resident retirees: pension BHD 4,000+/month; (5) Talented individuals: entrepreneurs, researchers, scientists, artists, innovators, athletes, other exceptional talent - subject to specialized committee review. Processing time: 5 working days (standard categories); up to 10 working days (talent category). Application fee: BHD 5; issuance fee BHD 300. No minimum stay requirement. Dependants (spouse, parents, children - no age limit) may be included. Golden Residency holders must obtain a separate work permit from LMRA to work. The real estate threshold was reduced from BHD 200,000 to BHD 130,000 in November 2025. Source: https://goldenresidency.gov.bh/eligibility and https://goldenresidency.gov.bh/faqs/

rbi.name: Bahrain
rbi.notes: The bahrain.bh national portal lists residency for foreign investors for periods of 2, 5, and 10 years, with investment share not less than BHD 100,000. This appears to be a separate investor residence permit distinct from the Golden Residency program. Additional details not fully available from official page text extracted.

rbi.name: Bangladesh
rbi.notes: Foreign private investors in industrial and commercial enterprises can obtain a 'P1' (PI) visa on BIDA recommendation. Investors must remit a minimum of USD 50,000 as initial establishment cost (encashment certificate required) to register a branch, liaison, representative, or 100% foreign-owned company in Bangladesh. BIDA provides visa recommendations online through BIDA OSS (bidaquickserv.org) within 24 hours if documentation is complete. The P1 visa allows the investor to reside in Bangladesh while conducting business. Note: bida.gov.bd now permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to investbangladesh.gov.bd. Long-term residence / permanent residency thresholds for investors are referenced in other contexts but no official BIDA PR-specific threshold page was accessible. Work permits for expatriates cost BDT 5,000 per individual per year.

rbi.name: Barbados
rbi.program_name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) - Category 1
rbi.notes: Requires investment of at least USD $2 million from funds sourced outside Barbados, plus proof of net worth exceeding USD $5 million. Category 1 holders are entitled to a work permit. The official immigration.gov.bb page states an application fee of BDS $300; secondary sources cite USD $3,500 (applicants under 60) and USD $5,000 (applicants over 60) - the higher figures could not be confirmed from the official government page directly.

rbi.name: Barbados
rbi.program_name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) - Category 2
rbi.notes: Requires ownership of property in Barbados valued at minimum USD $300,000. Renewable 5-year permit. Category 2 holders are not eligible for work permits. Official immigration.gov.bb page shows application fee of BDS $300.

rbi.name: Barbados
rbi.program_name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) - Category 3
rbi.notes: For persons who possess special skills deemed critical to the growth and development of Barbados. No investment threshold.

rbi.name: Barbados
rbi.program_name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) - Category 4
rbi.notes: For parents or grandparents of a citizen of Barbados who are over the age of 60 years. No investment threshold.

rbi.name: Belarus
rbi.notes: Foreigners who make investments in Belarus of at least 15,000 basic units (approx. USD 202,000 based on industry estimates; the official page does not state USD equivalent) may obtain a permanent residence permit directly. Eligible investment methods: creating a commercial organization, acquiring/constructing real estate (excluding personal residential use), obtaining intellectual property rights, purchasing shares in commercial organizations, concession-based investments, or public-private partnerships. Applications submitted to the territorial Office of Citizenship and Migration. The official page does not specify a path-to-citizenship timeline from investment-based residency.

rbi.name: Belarus
rbi.program_name: Hi-Tech Park (HTP) Simplified Residence for Foreign Workers and Founders
rbi.notes: Foreign workers and founders of HTP-resident companies enjoy visa-free entry to Belarus with extended temporary stay of up to 180 days. Temporary residence permit process is streamlined. No special work permits required for HTP residents when hiring foreign nationals. Requires establishing a legal entity in Belarus engaged in software development, IT services, or high-tech R&D.

rbi.name: Belgium
rbi.notes: Third-country nationals wishing to conduct self-employed activities in Belgium for more than 90 days must obtain a Professional Card from the competent regional authority (Flanders, Wallonia, Brussels-Capital, or German-speaking Community). There is no official fixed minimum investment amount. After 5 years of lawful residence, applicants may apply for long-term resident status. Application for the D visa is made at the Belgian embassy/consulate, supported by the regional Professional Card decision.

rbi.name: Belgium
rbi.notes: Combined work and residence permit for non-EU nationals employed more than 90 days in Belgium (since 3 January 2019). Employer applies on behalf of the worker to the relevant regional authority. Region makes work authorization decision; Immigration Office decides on residence. Standard decision period: 4 months from admissibility (extendable). After 5 years of lawful and uninterrupted residence, applicants may obtain long-term resident status (L card). EU Blue Card holders benefit from combined EU residency calculation for long-term resident purposes.

rbi.name: Belgium
rbi.program_name: Long-Term Resident Status (EC Long-Term Residence Permit)
rbi.notes: Requires 5 years of legal and uninterrupted residence in Belgium. Financial condition: stable, regular and sufficient means of subsistence (minimum EUR 1,038/month for single person, plus EUR 346 per dependent). Medical insurance required. Must not pose danger to public order. Study and vocational training periods count at 50%. EU Blue Card holders may combine EU-wide residency (minimum 2 years immediately before application in Belgium). Grants L card (EU long-term residence permit). Processing: Immigration Office has 5 months to decide.

rbi.name: Belize
rbi.notes: Available to persons who have made or are making a substantial commercial investment in Belize. Requires evidence of investments valued at not less than BZ$500,000. Supporting documents include real estate title, bank statements, company registration, trade license. Duration and fees not specified on official page. Renewable annually. No explicit path to permanent residence or citizenship stated on official page.

rbi.name: Belize
rbi.notes: Administered by the Belize Tourism Board. For persons aged 40+ with minimum annual income of USD $24,000 (USD $2,000/month) from sources outside Belize. Eligible income: pensions, annuities, Social Security, investments, inheritance, savings, retirement plans. Approved currencies: USD, GBP, EUR, CAD. Minimum 30 consecutive days annually in Belize.
