rbi.notes: EEA nationals only (Swiss nationals excluded). Annual quota of 56 permits for gainful employment, allocated 50% by lottery (twice yearly, spring and autumn) and 50% by government decision. B permit is issued for more than 12 months and is renewable. After 5 years of lawful residence, permanent residence (C permit) may be obtained. Citizenship requires 30 years continuous residence (or ordinary naturalization after 10 years subject to municipal ballot). No monetary investment requirement - residence is earned through employment. Non-EEA/non-Swiss nationals may not participate in the draw; they must apply for direct-issue permits in exceptional cases of national interest only.

rbi.name: Liechtenstein
rbi.program_name: Residence Permit (B) Draw for EEA Nationals - Without Gainful Employment
rbi.notes: EEA nationals only (Swiss and UK nationals excluded as of Brexit). Annual quota of 16 permits for non-gainful residence, allocated by lottery (twice yearly). Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial means to sustain themselves without recourse to social assistance. B permit annual and renewable. After 5 years, permanent residence (C permit) may be obtained. Citizenship requires 30 years continuous residence. No minimum monetary investment amount specified in official sources.

rbi.name: Lithuania
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit - Investor (Special Investment Agreement)
rbi.notes: Investment agreement under Article 13(1)(3) and (4) of the Law on Investments. Minimum private investment of EUR 1,448,100 in a project with job creation obligations. Annual revenue of the investor group must be at least EUR 2,500,000 in at least one of the last three years. Permit issued for up to 3 years. After 5 continuous years of temporary residence, may apply for permanent residence (EU long-term resident status). Path to citizenship: 10 years of permanent residence + naturalization = approximately 15 years total from first temporary permit.

rbi.name: Lithuania
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit - Investor (Business / Company Participation)
rbi.notes: Lower-threshold investment: investor or participant owning at least 1/10 of authorized capital of a Lithuanian company with personal investment of at least EUR 14,000 in the enterprise. Permit issued for up to 3 years. Path to permanent residence after 5 continuous years of temporary residence.

rbi.name: Lithuania
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit - Major Project Investor
rbi.notes: Major project investment agreement under Article 15(7)(6) of the Law on Investments. Requires at least EUR 20 million in private capital investment (EUR 30 million for Vilnius) AND creation of at least 150 new jobs (200 for Vilnius). Permit issued for up to 3 years.

rbi.name: Lithuania
rbi.notes: Available after 5 continuous years of legal residence in Lithuania on a temporary residence permit. Absence rules: periods outside Lithuania must not exceed 6 consecutive months and not exceed 10 months total within the 5-year period. Path to citizenship: naturalization after 10 years of permanent residence.

rbi.name: Luxembourg
rbi.notes: Minimum EUR 500,000 invested in an existing company with its registered office in Luxembourg. Investor must commit to maintaining the investment and employment levels for 5 years. Permit valid for up to 3 years, renewable. Ministerial opinion from the Ministry of Economy required before application. Long-term residence (permanent residence) available after 5 years of lawful uninterrupted stay. Citizenship by naturalization available after 5 years of legal residence with language and civics requirements.

rbi.name: Luxembourg
rbi.program_name: Investor Residence Permit - New Business Creation
rbi.notes: Minimum EUR 500,000 in a new business to be created with its registered office in Luxembourg. Must establish minimum 5 work positions within 3 years, coordinated with the National Employment Agency (ADEM). Ministerial opinion from the Ministry of Economy required. Permit valid for up to 3 years, renewable.

rbi.name: Luxembourg
rbi.program_name: Investor Residence Permit - Management and Investment Structure
rbi.notes: Minimum EUR 3,000,000 in an existing or new management and investment structure with registered office and required substance in Luxembourg. Ministerial opinion from the Ministry of Finance required before application. Permit valid for up to 3 years, renewable.

rbi.name: Luxembourg
rbi.notes: Minimum EUR 20,000,000 deposited with a financial institution established in Luxembourg, with a commitment to hold the deposit for at least 5 years. Ministerial opinion from the Ministry of Finance required before application. Permit valid for up to 3 years, renewable. Real estate investments do not qualify for any investor residence pathway.

rbi.name: Madagascar
rbi.notes: A 1-month 'Transformable' and 'Extendable' visa issued for investors, business creators, or those transferring businesses to Madagascar. Once in Madagascar, the holder applies for a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior (Department of Immigration) within one month. This visa type can only be issued by a consulate (not on arrival). No minimum investment amount is specified on accessible official pages. Managed by the Ministry of Interior/EDBM (Economic Development Board of Madagascar). Source URL updated to the verified EDBM official PDF (edbm.mg domain).

rbi.name: Madagascar
rbi.notes: A long-stay transformable visa for retirees or those making a definitive move to Madagascar, with vocation to obtain the permanent residence permit. Categories listed by Madagascar Embassy Paris include retirees (rentiers), family reunification, students, NGO members, missionaries, and journalists. Issued only by consulates, not at ports of entry. Once in Madagascar, the holder applies for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior within one month. Source URL updated to official Madagascar Embassy Paris page (ambamad-paris.diplomatie.gov.mg).

rbi.name: Malawi
rbi.notes: Authorises a person to reside in Malawi for the purpose of carrying on, practising or engaging in business, profession or occupation for gain, profit or reward as self-employed person, partner or proprietor. Minimum investment amount not stated on the official portal. Apply online via epermit.gov.mw.

rbi.name: Malawi
rbi.notes: Permit authorising permanent residence in Malawi. Eligibility criteria and investment thresholds not published in detail on the official portal page. Apply online via epermit.gov.mw.

rbi.name: Malawi
rbi.notes: Issued to a visitor with a valid Visitor's/Business Visit permit who has resided in Malawi for the maximum of 90 days but has legitimate and justifiable reasons for continued residence. Apply via epermit.gov.mw.

rbi.name: Malaysia
rbi.program_name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Silver Category
rbi.notes: One of three MM2H tiers (Platinum, Gold, Silver) plus a SEZ/SFZ category. Programme run by Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC). Financial requirements not directly extractable from official government pages (mm2h.gov.my returns HTTP 403 on category pages). Non-official aggregators indicate FD requirements around MYR 675,000 (Silver) but this cannot be confirmed from an official page. Programme does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship.

rbi.name: Malaysia
rbi.program_name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Gold Category
rbi.notes: Second-tier MM2H category. Financial requirements not directly extractable from official pages (403 errors). Programme managed by MOTAC. Does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship.

rbi.name: Malaysia
rbi.program_name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Platinum Category
rbi.notes: Highest MM2H tier. Financial requirements not directly extractable from official pages (403 errors). Programme under MOTAC. Does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship.

rbi.name: Malaysia
rbi.program_name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - SEZ/SFZ Category
rbi.notes: Category for investors in Special Economic Zones / Special Financial Zones. Specific requirements not extractable from official pages (403 errors). Programme under MOTAC.

rbi.name: Malaysia
rbi.notes: Requires MYR 1,000,000 fixed deposit in a Malaysian licensed bank (max 50% withdrawal after 1 year for approved purposes). Government participation fee: MYR 200,000 for main applicant; MYR 100,000 per dependent. Minimum offshore income of MYR 40,000/month. Visa valid for 20 years, renewable every 5 years. Pass holders may work and study in Malaysia. Processing time: 30 working days. Managed by Immigration Department (imi.gov.my). Does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship.

rbi.name: Maldives
rbi.program_name: Maldives Pearl Residence (Residence by Investment Program)
rbi.notes: Partnership Agreement between the Government of Maldives and Henley & Partners signed 1 July 2025 to develop and implement the program. Formally introduced by Minister of Economic Development at the 19th Global Citizenship Conference in London (5 November 2025). Program is specifically linked to real estate acquisition in designated development zones (Gaafaru, Fushidhiggaru, and Ras Mala in Kaafu Atoll). As of June 2026, the detailed investment minimums, residency duration, and full eligibility criteria remain unfinalized and not published on official government pages - program is still in development. No path to citizenship offered (Maldives Constitution restricts citizenship to Muslims). Contact: Invest Maldives (investmaldives.gov.mv).

rbi.name: Maldives
rbi.notes: Launched by Maldives Immigration. Aims to provide foreign investors in the Maldives with privileged and fast-track immigration services. Card holders receive permanent residency and priority (no-queue) processing at immigration. Investment thresholds and detailed eligibility not found on the official immigration.gov.mv page. The original announcement URL (immigration.gov.mv/corporate-resident-maldives-launched/) returned HTTP 404 again on re-verification 2026-06-29.

rbi.name: Maldives
rbi.notes: For foreign nationals married to Maldivian citizens. Apply for Marriage Visa within 30 days of arrival. Initial validity 1 year; renewable (extensions issued for 5 years per renewal). Applications submitted via IMUGA. MVR 50 card fee. Not an investment-based residency - included for completeness. Confirmed on MFA official page (foreign.gov.mv).

rbi.name: Malta
rbi.notes: Available to non-EU, non-EEA, non-Swiss nationals. Grants permanent residency (not citizenship). UPDATED via Legal Notice 146 of 2025 (published 22 July 2025, effective for applications from 1 January 2025). Key financial requirements: (1) Administration fee: €60,000 (€15,000 non-refundable upfront within 1 month of submission + €45,000 within 2 months after Letter of Approval in Principle). (2) Government contribution: €37,000 (unified, regardless of whether applicant purchases or leases property; replaces previous dual structure of €28,000 purchase / €58,000 rental). Spouse and minor children no longer attract a separate contribution fee. (3) Property: Purchase qualifying property at minimum €375,000, OR lease at minimum €14,000/year; property must be held/maintained for at least 5 years. (4) NGO donation: €2,000 to a local registered NGO approved by Residency Malta Agency. (5) Proof of capital: Option A - €500,000 total assets (of which minimum €150,000 must be financial assets such as stocks, bonds, bank deposits); Option B - €650,000 total assets (of which minimum €75,000 must be in financial assets). Assets monitored annually for first 5 years. (6) Adult dependant fee: €7,500 each (excluding spouse and minor children). Ineligible: Afghanistan, North Korea, Iran, DRC, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Yemen, Venezuela, Russia, Belarus. Processing: decisions within a 'reasonable timeframe'. Regulated by S.L. 217.26. Residence certificate does not expire as long as obligations are maintained.

rbi.name: Malta
rbi.notes: Separate from the MPRP; grants Schengen travel rights with Maltese residency. Full investment amounts not extractable from public-facing official pages - see S.L. 217.18 and MRVP FAQs (PDF). Eligible for four generations of family members. Investment must be held for minimum 5 years.

rbi.name: Malta
rbi.notes: Tax-residency programme for non-EU, non-EEA, non-Swiss nationals not already long-term residents. Provides flat 15% tax rate on foreign-sourced income remitted to Malta (35% on locally-sourced income). Administrative fee: €5,500 if qualifying property is in South Malta; €6,000 otherwise. Applicants must purchase or lease a qualifying property in Malta. Regulated by Malta Tax & Customs Administration (MTCA, formerly CFR).

rbi.name: Malta
rbi.notes: Available to non-EU/EEA/Swiss third-country nationals who work remotely. Minimum gross annual income: €42,000 (for applications from 1 April 2024 onwards; previous threshold was €32,400). Applicants must work for a foreign-registered employer under contract, or be a partner/shareholder of a foreign-registered company, or provide freelance/consulting services to foreign-based clients. Initial permit: 1 year; renewable up to 3 times (maximum 4 years total). Requires valid travel document, health insurance covering EU risks, property rental/purchase agreement, police certificate.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: Minimum investment of USD 50,000. Occupation Permit valid for 10 years, renewable. Eligible for 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after at least 5 years as Investor OP holder with cumulative turnover of MUR 20 million over 5 years (MUR 1.5 million in year 1). Year 6+ renewal requires MUR 5 million annual turnover. Application fee USD 1,000 upon approval; USD 50 non-refundable application fee. Updated August 2025.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: Minimum investment of USD 100,000. Occupation Permit valid for 10 years, renewable. Eligible for 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after at least 5 years with cumulative turnover of MUR 15 million over 5 years (MUR 1 million in year 1). Year 6+ renewal requires MUR 5 million annual turnover. Higher investment threshold with lower turnover target compared to Option 1. Updated August 2025.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.program_name: Permanent Residence Permit (PRP) – Real Estate Investment
rbi.notes: An investor who invests at least USD 375,000 in a qualifying business activity is eligible to apply for the 20-year Permanent Residence Permit. Foreign nationals may also acquire residential property under IRS, RES, PDS or Smart City Scheme (SCS) to obtain residency. 20-year PRP is renewable. Exact minimum purchase prices for IRS/RES/PDS/SCS schemes require verification on EDB/official property scheme pages.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: Available to foreign nationals above 50 years of age. Occupation Permit (Retired) issued for up to 5 years (changed from 10 years effective August 2025). Requires transfer of at least USD 2,000 per month (USD 24,000 per year) to a Mauritian bank account and minimum 180 days per year residency in Mauritius. Eligible for 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after holding the Residence Permit for at least 5 years with total transfer of at least USD 200,000 over the 5-year period. Application fee USD 50 (non-refundable). CORRECTION: Prior record stated 10-year permit duration and USD 54,000 over 3 years; updated to reflect August 2025 rule changes.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: Allows foreign professionals employed by a company in Mauritius to work and reside. Minimum salary: MUR 30,000/month. Valid for up to 3 years or duration of employment contract. Eligible for 20-year PRP after at least 5 years with a basic monthly salary of at least MUR 400,000 for 5 consecutive years. Expert Pass tier available at MUR 250,000/month. CORRECTION: Prior record stated MUR 150,000/month for PRP and 3-year path to PR; updated per August 2025 rule changes.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: New category introduced effective August 2025 for highly skilled professionals earning at least MUR 250,000/month. Administered through NELS (National Electronic Licensing System). Full eligibility criteria and PRP pathway not yet confirmed on official Passport Immigration Office page.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: Effective August 2025: minimum investment of USD 50,000 in services sector only. Must provide letters of intent from at least three clients (two local). Annual income targets: MUR 750,000 in year 1, scaling to MUR 6 million cumulative over 5 years. Occupation Permit issued for up to 10 years. Eligible for 20-year PRP after at least 5 years with annual business income of at least MUR 3 million for 5 consecutive years. Application online via NELS. CORRECTION: Prior record did not specify services-sector restriction or updated turnover targets.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: For foreign students who have completed at least an undergraduate degree at a Mauritius institution recognized by the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC). Application must be submitted not later than 6 months after publication of results. Business activity must fall within: Artificial Intelligence, Biotechnology, Fintech, Robotics, Financial Services, Information Technology. Effective August 2025: valid for maximum 2 years (reduced from 3 years), minimum salary MUR 25,000/month. After 2 years, must transition to standard Occupation Permit. Established under Section 13 of the Economic Development Board Act 2017 and Section 9A of the Immigration Act 1970. CORRECTION: Prior record stated 3 years; updated per August 2025 rule changes.

rbi.name: Mauritius
rbi.notes: Established under section 14 of the Immigration Act 2022 and section 13(1)(b) of the Economic Development Board Act 2017. Allows an applicant, spouse, dependent child, parent, other dependent, or person working exclusively for the family unit to become a resident for 10 years.

rbi.name: Mexico
rbi.notes: Investment must exceed 45,850 days of UMA. As of February 1, 2026 the daily UMA value is MXN $117.31 (confirmed by INEGI), giving a threshold of approximately MXN $5,378,663. Investment can be demonstrated through: (1) equity interest/shares in a Mexican company; (2) movable or fixed assets for business purposes; or (3) evidence of Mexican economic activity employing at least 3 workers. Visa grants stay of more than 180 days and up to 4 years. Must apply for Temporary Resident Card at INM within 30 days of arrival.

rbi.name: Mexico
rbi.notes: For retirees or those with passive income. Financial requirements include: average monthly income equivalent to 400 days of UMA (~MXN $46,924/month as of February 2026, based on UMA $117.31/day) for 6 months, OR average monthly bank balance of 20,000 days of UMA (~MXN $2,346,200/month) for 12 months, OR real estate ownership exceeding 40,000 UMA days (~MXN $4,692,400) in assessed value. Grants temporary residency for up to 4 years.

rbi.name: Mexico
rbi.notes: Permanent Residence Visa by Economic Solvency requires investment receipts or bank statements showing an average monthly overall balance of over $292,859 USD per month (12 months of statements required). Grants indefinite right to reside in Mexico.

rbi.name: Moldova
rbi.notes: Based on Law no. 200/2010 on the Regime of Foreigners and Law No 81/2004 on investments. Investment tiers tied to multiples of average monthly salary (AMS): 30–200 AMS or 1+ job = 2-year permit; 200–600 AMS or 8+ jobs = 3-year permit; 600–2000 AMS or 15+ jobs = 4-year permit; 2000–4000 AMS or 25+ jobs = 5-year permit; 4000+ AMS or 50+ jobs = 8-year permit. Application fee: 3,600 MDL. Permanent residence requires 5 years of temporary residence (other categories). No specific EUR/USD floor stated - amounts are in multiples of the national average salary, recalculated annually.

rbi.name: Monaco
rbi.notes: Any person aged 16 or over wishing to stay in Monaco for more than 3 months must obtain a residence permit. The official page specifies no fixed minimum financial amount - it requires demonstration of sufficient funds via salary, professional income, or savings (amount varies by bank). The widely cited €500,000 figure appears only in law-firm/aggregator sources, not on gouv.mc. Non-EEA nationals must first obtain a long-stay Type D visa from French authorities (or transfer from French residency of over one year). The first permit fee is €80. A personal interview is mandatory. The 'Ordinary Resident' permit (10 years residency) is the precondition for naturalisation eligibility. A valid Monegasque residence permit allows non-Schengen nationals to travel within the Schengen Area without a short-stay visa. Required documents include: valid passport with long-stay visa, proof of accommodation, financial references from a Monaco banking establishment, criminal records extract (less than 3 months old), and birth certificate.

rbi.name: Mongolia
rbi.program_name: Investor Residence Permit (T Visa / Investment Visa)
rbi.notes: Foreigners must invest at least USD 100,000 to establish a business entity with foreign investment, comprising at least 25% of business equity. Residency permit is issued for up to 1 year and renewable for up to 3 years. After 5 consecutive years of qualifying lawful residence (minimum 6 months per year), applicant may seek permanent residency. Permanent residency requires legal income of at least 10x minimum wage, Mongolian language ability, knowledge of traditions/customs and Constitution. Processing: ~10 business days via eimmigration.mn portal.

rbi.name: Montenegro
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Based on Property Ownership
rbi.notes: Third-country nationals may obtain temporary residence in Montenegro based on ownership of real estate with a taxable value of at least EUR 150,000 (as determined by the Tax Authority's transfer tax assessment). This threshold was introduced by legislation adopted December 2025 in force from January 17, 2026. Owners must prove both ownership and actual use of the property, and all property tax obligations must be settled. Permits are valid for up to 1 year and are renewable. Grandfathering clause: foreigners who obtained property-based residence before the law took effect may renew without meeting the new valuation requirement. Path to permanent residence: 5 consecutive years of lawful temporary residence (note: time spent on property-disposal residence does NOT count toward the 5-year requirement for permanent residence). Path to citizenship: 10 years total lawful continuous residence as a general naturalization rule.

rbi.name: Morocco
rbi.program_name: Moroccan Residence Permit - Investor Category (Certificat d'Immatriculation)
rbi.notes: An investor visa category exists within the ordinary visa framework as documented on the official Moroccan consular portal. Applicants require a recommendation from the Management of External Investments, a professional federation, a proper authority for supervision, Regional Centers of Investment (C.R.I.), or a Moroccan partner/foreign investor branch in Morocco. No minimum investment threshold amount is stated on the official source. After entry, foreigners staying more than 90 days must apply for a Certificat d'Immatriculation (residence permit) from the Bureau des Etrangers. This is a conventional residence framework, not a formal golden visa program with published financial thresholds.

rbi.name: Mozambique
rbi.notes: Available via official eVisa portal. Applicable for travel to invest in a project totalling a value equal or greater than USD 500,000. Duration options: 90, 180, 365 or 730 days (multiple-entry). Governed by Law No. 23/2022 of December 29. Processing time: 3 to 5 business days. This is an entry/investment visa, not a formal long-term residency-by-investment or golden visa program; it is a precursor to undertaking investment in Mozambique. No path to PR or citizenship specified on the official portal.

rbi.name: Namibia
rbi.program_name: Investment Permit (Employment Permit for Foreign Investors)
rbi.notes: Under the Foreign Investments Act 27 of 1990, a foreign national must invest foreign assets of more than N$3,950,000 into a Namibian business activity (or acquire >10% of shares in a Namibian company). This qualifies the investor for a 5-year renewable Employment/Investment Permit. After 7 continuous years with the investment retained, the investor may qualify for Permanent Residence Permit. Applications processed by the Immigration Selection Board (ISB) and Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security. Processing time approximately 8 weeks. Note: N$3,950,000 investment threshold is cited by private developers referencing the Foreign Investments Act; the mha.gov.na page does not state the amount directly.

rbi.name: Nepal
rbi.notes: Foreigners who have invested a minimum of USD 100,000 (or equivalent in convertible foreign currency) at once in an industrial enterprise in Nepal may obtain a residential visa. Requires a recommendation letter from the Department of Industry. Annual fee: Nepalese currency equivalent to USD 700 per year. Renewal fee: Nepalese currency equivalent to USD 1,200. Does not provide a direct path to permanent residence or citizenship. For non-investors who wish to reside in Nepal without conducting business, certified proof of income of at least USD 20,000 per year is required.

rbi.name: Netherlands
rbi.notes: For foreign nationals who wish to work in the Netherlands as self-employed or entrepreneur. Applicant's work must be of 'essential interest to the Dutch economy.' Assessed by Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) using a points system (minimum 30 points per category: personal experience, business plan, added value). No minimum investment amount specified for the general route. Alternative routes exist under the Dutch-American Friendship Treaty or Dutch-Japanese Trade Treaty (requiring 'substantial capital' - typically at least €4,500). Permit valid up to 2 years; renewable. Path to permanent residence after 5 years.

rbi.name: Netherlands
rbi.program_name: Residence Permit for Essential Start-Up Personnel
rbi.notes: Pilot program running from 1 June 2021 to 1 June 2028. For foreign employees essential to an innovative, scalable start-up in the Netherlands. The start-up must have max 15 employees and can sponsor up to 5 foreign employees. Employee must be an expert in a specialized field, and must receive mandatory participation: at least 1% equity stake OR financial value of €65,000+ through shares/options. RVO provides advisory assessment. Permit valid up to 3 years. Path to permanent residence after 5 years.

rbi.name: New Zealand
rbi.program_name: Active Investor Plus Visa - Growth Category
rbi.notes: Minimum NZD $5 million invested in higher-risk assets (managed funds, direct business investments, philanthropy max 20%) for 3 years. Applicant must spend minimum 21 days in New Zealand during the 36-month investment period. After meeting all conditions, can apply for permanent residence. New Zealand citizenship available after 5 years of residence. Application fee NZD $27,470. Processing time: 80% within 10.5 weeks for approval in principle. Accepts: direct investments, managed funds, philanthropy (max 20%). No changes to investment minimums confirmed as of page date March 2, 2026.

rbi.name: New Zealand
rbi.program_name: Active Investor Plus Visa - Balanced Category
rbi.notes: Minimum NZD $10 million invested in mixed assets for 5 years. Acceptable assets include direct investments, managed funds, listed equities, philanthropy, bonds, or property developments. Applicant must spend minimum 105 days in New Zealand during the 60-month investment period (reducible by 14 days per extra NZD $1 million invested, max 42-day reduction). Application fee NZD $27,470. Processing time: 80% within 10.5 weeks for approval in principle. No changes to investment minimums confirmed as of page date March 2, 2026.

rbi.name: New Zealand
rbi.notes: Invest at least NZD $1 million in an acceptable New Zealand business actively operated by the applicant. Work visa valid up to 4 years. Requires maintaining employment levels and proving active management. Eligible for Business Investor Resident Visa after 3 years of operating the business. Even after residence approval, business must be actively run for at least 3 years in total. Application fee applies.

rbi.name: New Zealand
rbi.notes: Invest at least NZD $2 million in an acceptable New Zealand business. Fast-track pathway to Business Investor Resident Visa eligible after 12 months of operating the business (not 3 years). However, business must still be actively run for at least 3 years in total even under the fast-track pathway. Permanent resident status available after holding resident visa for 2+ years and meeting all conditions. Launched 24 November 2025.

rbi.name: Nicaragua
rbi.program_name: Inmigrante con Capital o Inversionista (Investor Permanent Residency)
rbi.notes: Under Nicaragua's General Migration Law No. 761 and its Regulation (Decree 31-2012), foreigners who invest capital in any lawful economic activity may qualify for permanent residency as 'Inmigrante con Capital o Inversionista'. The official DGME page (migob.gob.ni) lists requirements including a MIFIC Certificate of Investment Registration (RUIE), company registration, municipal trading licence, tax clearance (DGI), and notarised declaration of income sources - but does NOT specify a minimum investment amount in cordobas or USD. The commonly cited $30,000 USD minimum appears in third-party and PRONicaragua materials; it is NOT confirmed on the currently accessible official pages and should not be relied upon. After 2 years of legal residency (reportedly requiring at least 180 days per year in-country), permanent residents may apply for naturalization. Dual citizenship is permitted under Nicaraguan law. Cost of permanent residency card: C$18,312.15 (approx. $500 USD) for 5 years; reduced rate of C$9,156.07 for subcategories under numerals 1 and 4 of Art. 30, Law 761.

rbi.name: Nigeria
rbi.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV) for small-scale enterprise investors. Requires evidence of US$250,000 – US$500,000 imported and retained as investor's capital, prior holding of F4B or F4C visa, security clearance from place of residence, proof of investment in a small enterprise, and business plan. Stay duration: 3 years, multiple entry (residence permit). Not applicable for extension, but residency can be renewed subject to continued compliance.

rbi.name: Nigeria
rbi.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV) for medium-scale enterprise investors. Requires evidence of US$500,000 – US$1,000,000 imported and retained as investor's capital, prior F4B or F4C visa holding, security clearance. Stay duration: 4 years, multiple entry (residence permit).

rbi.name: Nigeria
rbi.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV) for large-scale corporation investors. Minimum capital threshold is not stated as a verbatim dollar amount on the accessible official page. Requires significant capital/asset requirements verified by corporate registration and audited financial statements. Residency granted to key executives.

rbi.name: Nigeria
rbi.program_name: Investor Visa – Ultra Large Scale Corporations (N3D)
rbi.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV) for investors leading major multinational or ultra-large corporations. Must meet the highest thresholds of capital, assets, or turnover (specific amounts not stated verbatim on official page). Multi-year residency for strategic oversight.

rbi.name: Nigeria
rbi.program_name: Investor Visa – Oil, Gas & Power Sector (N3E)
rbi.notes: Specialized Permanent Residence Visa (PRV) for significant ventures in Nigeria's oil, gas, or power sectors. Requires technical expertise, substantial capital, and relevant industry licenses or partnerships. Minimum capital not stated verbatim on official page.

rbi.name: Nigeria
rbi.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV) for foreign retirees wishing to relocate to Nigeria from overseas. Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources (pensions, annuities, savings) and secure local accommodation. Health insurance strongly recommended. Employment not permitted. Specific minimum income/savings threshold not stated verbatim on official page.

rbi.name: North Macedonia
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit for Property Owners (EU/OECD nationals)
rbi.notes: Under the Law on Foreigners, EU/OECD citizens who acquire ownership of an apartment, residential building, or house in North Macedonia valued at a minimum of EUR 40,000 are eligible to apply for a long-stay (D) visa leading to temporary residence. Temporary residence is issued for up to 1 year and can be extended annually. Eligibility is restricted to EU/OECD nationals. Path to permanent residence and citizenship timelines not specified on official sources reviewed.

rbi.name: Norway
rbi.program_name: Residence Permit for Self-Employed / Sole Proprietor (Non-EU/EEA)
rbi.notes: Non-EU/EEA nationals with completed higher education or vocational training may apply for a residence permit as a self-employed sole proprietor in Norway. The business must be a sole proprietorship (not a limited company), must generate profit of at least NOK 341,373 per year pre-tax (confirmed on official page as of 2026). Applicant must actively participate in the business. Permanent residence is available after 3 years of eligible residence. This is not a passive investment program - active business participation is required. Citizenship timeline not stated on RBI page; citizenship general requirements vary by profile.

rbi.name: Oman
rbi.type: real_estate / business / bonds / fund / deposit / employment
rbi.notes: Renewable 10-year residency for international investors, entrepreneurs, and high-net-worth individuals. Seven qualifying investment routes: (1) Real estate in Integrated Tourism Complexes; (2) Company formation in Oman; (3) Government Development Bonds; (4) Muscat Stock Exchange shares; (5) Fixed-term bank deposit (minimum 5 years); (6) Owning a company employing 50+ Omani nationals; (7) Nomination under Foreign Capital Investment Law. Minimum capital threshold: OMR 200,000 (approx. USD 520,000) per investoman.om. Benefits include full foreign ownership, up to 3 domestic workers, sponsorship of spouse and children, fast-track immigration lanes. No direct path to citizenship through this program.

rbi.name: Pakistan
rbi.notes: Established under the Foreigners (Long Term Residency) Order, 2025. Grants foreign investors and their families residency in Pakistan for 5, 7, or 10 years, renewable. Minimum investment of USD 50,000 must be materialized within one year of approval through authorized banking channels. Each additional dependent (up to 7 - spouse, children under 25, parents) requires an additional USD 50,000. Annual renewal requires USD 50,000. LTR provides residency rights only - does not grant nationality or citizenship. Priority sectors: IT/technology, renewable energy, export-led manufacturing, agriculture, industrial development including SEZs. LTR Card issued by NADRA as proof of residency. LTR Digital Portal to go live; apply via invest.gov.pk. Confirmed from invest.gov.pk search result summary - direct page scrape timed out.

rbi.name: Pakistan
rbi.notes: Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) investor visa. Short-term: up to 3 years; long-term: up to 5 years (extendable by 2 additional years). No publicly disclosed investment threshold. SIFC recommendation letter required for visas over 1 year. For non-SIFC investor visas under the Business-Investor category: investment in SECP-registered companies of not less than USD 50,000 or real estate investment exceeding USD 100,000. Processing: 1-14 business days. Long-term categories allow legal residence. After 5 years legal residence and mastering an official language, foreigners can apply for citizenship (per visa.nadra.gov.pk).

rbi.name: Palau
rbi.notes: 10-year multiple-entry visa, renewable. Requires purchase or lease of dwelling for at least $250,000 USD (cash payments only) from a Palauan citizen, clan, family, non-governmental entity, or corporation. Applicant must have major medical health insurance. No felony convictions. Initial fee $20,000; renewal fee $10,000. Does NOT automatically confer permanent residency or citizenship.

rbi.name: Palau
rbi.notes: Up to 5-year investor visa; $50 fee. Specific minimum investment amount not stated on official page. Requires application in advance.

rbi.name: Palau
rbi.notes: Up to 2-year resident visa; $200 fee. Advance application required. General long-term residency visa.

rbi.name: Palau
rbi.notes: Web3/blockchain-based digital identity program administered by the Digital Residency Office (palaugov.pw/dro/). Does NOT grant physical residency rights in Palau or any pathway to citizenship or a Palauan passport. Purely a digital identity program. Exact fee amounts not confirmed from official palaugov.pw DRO page (page has regulatory PDFs but no readable fee schedule on main page). Aggregator sources cite $248/1yr, $1,039/5yr, $2,039/10yr - not verified from official source.

rbi.name: Panama
rbi.program_name: Qualified Investor Visa (Visa de Inversionista Calificado)
rbi.notes: Established by Decreto Ejecutivo 722 (and subsequent amendments including Decreto 109 and Decreto 193 of 2024). Grants immediate permanent residency upon approval. Three investment modalities: (1) Real estate: USD 300,000 minimum (valid until October 15, 2026, then increases to USD 500,000); (2) Securities/stocks on Panama Stock Exchange: USD 500,000 minimum for at least 5 years; (3) Fixed-term bank deposit: USD 750,000 minimum for at least 5 years. Investment must originate from abroad and be maintained for at least 5 years. Processing: approximately 30 business days. After 5 years of permanent residency, eligible to apply for Panamanian naturalization/citizenship with minimal physical presence requirement (one visit to Panama every two years suffices). Administered by SNM (National Migration Service) and MICI (Ministry of Commerce and Industries).

rbi.name: Panama
rbi.program_name: Friendly Nations Visa (Visa de Paises Especificos / Naciones Amigas)
rbi.notes: Established by Executive Decree 226 of July 20, 2021. Open to nationals of approximately 50 'friendly' nations (naciones amigas). Requires proof of economic ties to Panama (employment with a Panamanian company, own a Panamanian business, or real estate purchase) and a bank balance of at least USD 5,000 in a Panamanian bank. Grants permanent residency. After 5 years continuous permanent residency, eligible for naturalization. Eligible nationalities include: Germany, Andorra, Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Cyprus, South Korea, Costa Rica, Croatia, Denmark, Slovakia, Spain, United States, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Ireland, Israel, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, San Marino, Mexico, Monaco, Montenegro, Norway, New Zealand, Netherlands, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, United Kingdom, Czech Republic, Serbia, Singapore, South Africa, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Uruguay (approximately 50 nations total per Decree 226 of 2021). Note: The official PDF at migracion.gob.pa could not be fully parsed at time of research.

rbi.name: Panama
rbi.program_name: Economic Solvency Residence (Residencia por Solvencia Economica)
rbi.notes: Requires investment of at least USD 300,000 in real estate and/or a Panamanian bank fixed-term deposit (or mixed investment). Grants 2-year temporary residency first, then permanent residency after 2 years. Three sub-options: fixed-term deposit, real estate investment, or mixed investment. Available to all nationalities. Citizenship pathway after 5 years of permanent residency.

rbi.name: Panama
rbi.notes: Grants immediate permanent residency. Requires proof of lifetime monthly income of at least USD 1,000 from a government pension, social security, military pension, or private pension plan. The income threshold reduces to USD 750/month if the applicant purchases real estate in Panama worth at least USD 100,000. Available to anyone 18 years or older. Widely considered one of Panama's most popular residency programs.

rbi.name: Panama
rbi.notes: Permanent or temporary residency category for investors in agriculture or forestry sectors. Specific minimum investment amounts not found on official source pages at time of research.

rbi.name: Papua New Guinea
rbi.notes: Applicant must be the majority owner of a business investment in a registered resident business for at least 5 years with net assets and turnover exceeding K2 million; OR any property investment with a net investment in PNG of at least K10 million. CEO class: Chief Executive Officers of large companies (250+ employees, K10M+ annual turnover, operating 5+ years). Minimum residency of 5 years required before PR application. After 8 years continuous lawful residence, investor may apply for citizenship by naturalization. Confirmed via 2025 ICA handbook general provisions; specific PR fee schedule not re-verified in this session.

rbi.name: Paraguay
rbi.type: real_estate / financial instruments / tourism / productive investment
rbi.notes: Launched April 17, 2026 via MIC Resolution No. 0283/2026. Four investment modalities: (1) Productive investments (industry/commerce/services) from USD 70,000 with obligation to generate at least 5 formal jobs; (2) Financial instruments (stock market) from USD 200,000, no employment requirement; (3) Real estate from USD 200,000 (for economic activity, not personal/family use); (4) Tourism sector projects from USD 150,000. Grants permanent residency directly without prior temporary residency. Process mostly electronic; physical presence required only for national ID card issuance. Dividend tax rate reduced from 15% to 8% for residents. Path to citizenship via naturalization after 3 years of permanent residency. Official page ECONNREFUSED on June 2026 re-verification - program details preserved from prior verified fetch; not changed.

rbi.name: Paraguay
rbi.notes: Permanent residency available by demonstrating economic solvency: minimum USD 5,000 in bank/cooperative account, OR university-level degree with employment contract, OR property ownership (minimum 10 hectares), OR company incorporation with minimum USD 5,000 capital. After 3 years of permanent residency, naturalization citizenship is possible per Constitution Article 148.

rbi.name: Paraguay
rbi.notes: Special permanent residence process under Migration Law No. 6984/2022 for foreign investors using the Unified System for Business Opening and Closure (SUACE). Grants direct permanent residency without prior temporary residency requirement. Minimum investment amount not specified in available official content.

rbi.name: Peru
rbi.notes: Minimum investment of PEN 500,000 in a new or existing Peruvian company, made by international transfer through a Peruvian SBS-supervised financial institution. Applicant must commit to create at least 5 jobs for Peruvians within 1 year. Residency is granted for 365 days, renewable annually. After 2 years of residency, permanent residency may be applied for. Application fee: S/ 57.60 (code 07567 at Banco de la Nación). Processing time: 30 business days. Administered by Superintendencia Nacional de Migraciones.

rbi.name: Peru
rbi.program_name: Calidad Migratoria de Rentista (Independent Means / Passive Income Resident Visa)
rbi.notes: Requires proof of permanent monthly income of at least USD 1,000 from qualifying sources (pension, lifetime annuity, royalties, or dividends guaranteed for life). Income must be received through a Peruvian financial institution. An additional USD 500/month per dependent is required. Qualifying income does NOT include remote/freelance work, rental income, capital gains or interest. This visa grants permanent residency (indefinite validity). Governed by Decreto Supremo 002-2021-IN.

rbi.name: Peru
rbi.notes: Available to nationals of Bolivia, Colombia, and Ecuador under Andean Community Decision 878 (Andean Migration Statute, in force August 2021). Two-year temporary residence visa. After 2 years, permanent residence may be applied for. Applicant must have clean criminal record and demonstrate means of support. Implemented in Peru by decree effective October 23, 2023.

rbi.name: Peru
rbi.notes: Available to nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Uruguay). Peru ratified the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement effective January 1, 2024. Application can be made at a Peruvian consulate abroad or in-country. Two-year temporary residence, path to permanent residence after 2 years.

rbi.name: Philippines
rbi.notes: Requires remittance of at least USD 75,000 into a Peso Time Deposit at Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) or Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP). Funds must remain on deposit for minimum 30 days, maximum 180 days. Investment must be made within 180 days of probationary visa issuance. Eligible investments: shares of stocks in corporations in BOI Investment Priorities Plan (IPP) areas or manufacturing/services sectors. Probationary SIRV valid 6 months; Indefinite SIRV valid indefinitely while investment maintained. Issued by Bureau of Immigration upon endorsement by Board of Investments. No path to citizenship documented. Minimum age: 21 years. One-Stop SIRV Center at 2nd Floor, BOI, #385 Senator Gil J. Puyat Avenue, Makati City. Source: BOI official FAQ (boi.gov.ph) and DFA consular pages (dfa.gov.ph).

rbi.name: Philippines
rbi.notes: Issued by Bureau of Immigration under the Philippine Retirement Authority (PRA). Multiple options: SRRV Classic (age 50+, pensioner: USD 15,000; non-pensioner: USD 30,000; age 40-49, pensioner: USD 25,000; non-pensioner: USD 50,000) and SRRV Courtesy for foreign nationals (age 50+, pensioner: USD 1,500; non-pensioner: USD 3,000; age 40-49 non-pensioner: USD 6,000) and for former Filipinos (age 50+: USD 1,500; age 40-49: USD 3,000). Multiple entry, indefinite stay. Holders may retain their original citizenship. No documented path to Philippine citizenship through SRRV. Minimum age: 40 years.

rbi.name: Philippines
rbi.program_name: Treaty Trader or Treaty Investor Visa (9D)
rbi.notes: Available only to nationals of USA, Japan, and Germany under existing treaties of commerce and navigation. Applicant must enter to carry on trade/commerce or to develop/direct operations of an enterprise. No minimum investment amount specified on official page. Renewable visa; 1-year or 2-year validity. No documented path to PR or citizenship.

rbi.name: Poland
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit for Conducting Business Activity
rbi.notes: Available to non-EU nationals operating a sole proprietorship in the CEIDG register, holding shares/management board membership in a Polish limited liability or joint-stock company, or acting as a general partner in a limited partnership. The business must generate income not lower than twelve times the average monthly remuneration for the prior tax year. Minimum personal income requirement: PLN 1,010 net/month for a single applicant (2026 figures). No statutory minimum investment amount; program requires genuine business activity. Permit issued for up to 3 years. Permanent residence after 5 years of uninterrupted temporary residence; citizenship eligibility after further period. Applications submitted via the MOS portal (mos.cudzoziemcy.gov.pl) from April 2026.

rbi.name: Poland
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit for Conducting Business Activity (Company Director / Partner)
rbi.notes: Specifically for management board members of a sp. z o.o. that the applicant appointed or of which they are a partner, or general/limited partners in partnerships. Same income conditions as general business activity permit. Issued for up to 3 years.

rbi.name: Portugal
rbi.program_name: Autorização de Residência para Investimento (ARI) - Golden Visa
rbi.notes: Regulated under Article 90-A of the Aliens Act (Law 23/2007), as amended by Law 56/2023 ('Mais Habitação', in force from 7 October 2023). The 2023 reform eliminated the real estate purchase routes (EUR 500,000 and EUR 350,000 renovation) and the plain capital transfer route (EUR 1,000,000/EUR 1,500,000) that were available before October 2023. Current qualifying investment routes: (1) Capital transfer of at least EUR 500,000 for acquisition of units in non-real estate collective investment undertakings established under Portuguese law, with minimum 5-year maturity and at least 60% invested in companies based in Portugal; (2) Capital transfer of at least EUR 500,000 to establish a commercial company headquartered in Portugal combined with creation of 5 permanent jobs, or to reinforce existing Portuguese company capital with maintenance of at least 10 jobs (minimum 5 permanent) for a minimum of 3 years; (3) Capital transfer of at least EUR 500,000 for scientific research activities in public or private institutions within the national S&T system; (4) Capital transfer of at least EUR 250,000 for investment in artistic production or support of national cultural heritage; (5) Creation of at least 10 job positions. Note: some official consular pages (vistos.mne.gov.pt/en/ari-residency-permit-for-investors and Embassy Ankara page) still display legacy routes including real estate - those routes are no longer available for new applications under Law 56/2023. Minimum physical presence: 7 days in the first year, 14 days in each subsequent 2-year renewal period. Holders and family members may apply for permanent residence under Article 80 after 5 years. Applications managed by AIMA (formerly SEF).

rbi.name: Portugal
rbi.program_name: D7 Passive Income / Retirement Residency Visa
rbi.notes: For retirees and persons living from passive income (property, intellectual or financial assets). Applicant must demonstrate sufficient income. No statutory minimum amount specified on official page - documentary evidence of income/assets required. Leads to 2-year renewable residence permit; permanent residency after 5 years of legal residence.

rbi.name: Republic of the Congo
rbi.program_name: Republic of Congo Residence Permit (Carte de Séjour / Carte de Résident Privilégié)
rbi.notes: Residence permits available for 1 year (106,000 FCFA / ~€161.60), 3 years (206,000 FCFA / ~€314.04), or 5 years (106,000 FCFA / ~€161.60), issued by the Direction Départementale de la Surveillance du Territoire. Privileged resident card (carte de résident privilégié) requires uninterrupted residence of at least 10 years. Residence permits are issued automatically to: foreign nationals married for at least 2 years to a Congolese national; economic investors; and leaders of recognised religious denominations. No minimum investment amount stated for the 'economic investor' category on official sources. Source: API-Congo (Investment Promotion Agency) official .cg government domain.

rbi.name: Romania
rbi.program_name: Long-Stay Visa / Residence Permit for Company Administrator or Business Investment
rbi.notes: Foreign investors who establish and administer a Romanian company can obtain a long-stay visa (Category D, EUR 300 fee) and subsequently a residence permit for 'other purposes' (company administrator category). No statutory minimum investment amount for the visa itself is specified on the IGI website. Residence permit extensions are granted for successive periods of up to 1 year. After 5 years of continuous legal residence, long-term residence status may be obtained (per IGI long-term residence page). Naturalization (citizenship) requires 8 years of legal residence in Romania (or 5 years if married to a Romanian citizen), per Law on Romanian Citizenship 21/1991. No dedicated 'golden visa' or investment-based residency-by-investment programme exists as of June 2026.

rbi.name: Russia
rbi.notes: Established by Government Decree No. 2573 (Dec 31, 2022), effective Jan 11, 2023. Grants direct permanent residence (not temporary residence first). Investment options: (1) RUB 15 million in socially significant regional projects within 3 years; (2) RUB 30 million in a Russian company operating 3+ years and paying RUB 6 million/year in taxes; (3) Registration of a Russian commercial entity with RUB 4 million/year taxes paid, operating 2+ years; (4) Real estate investment with cadastral value: RUB 50 million (Moscow), RUB 20 million (Far East), RUB 25 million (elsewhere) - new build under 2 years old, held 1+ year before applying. Total annual quotas: 3,802 for 2026. Requirement to stay 6 months/year in Russia was removed in late 2025/early 2026.

rbi.name: Russia
rbi.notes: Presidential Decree No. 702 (Aug 19, 2024). Grants temporary residence permit (TRP) without quota for foreigners who align with traditional Russian values. Available to citizens of 47 countries (including US, UK, Canada, most EU states - list approved Sep 17, 2024 by PM Mishustin). No Russian language test or history exam required. Path to PR and citizenship follows standard TRP route.

rbi.name: Rwanda
rbi.program_name: Business Investor Resident Permits (Temporary) – multiple sector categories
rbi.notes: Multiple investor permit categories for foreign investors certified by Rwanda Development Board (RDB), covering: mining (A1/A3-1), agriculture/animal husbandry (B1/B3-1), manufacturing (F1/F3-1), hospitality (O1/O3-1), IT (W1/W3-1), transport/logistics (X1/X3-1), other sectors (Z1/Z3-1). New permit fee: 150,000 RWF (up to 2 years). Recurring permit fee: 250,000 RWF (up to 5 years). No minimum investment threshold published on official pages. Citizenship by residence requires 15 consecutive years.

rbi.name: Rwanda
rbi.program_name: Person with Assured Income Permit (K Permit)
rbi.notes: Issued to persons with assured income including retired persons who do not intend to be employed in Rwanda. Minimum age: 55 years. Minimum income: USD 5,000 per month required.

rbi.name: Rwanda
rbi.program_name: Itinerant Business Visa (V9) – Long-term Investor Visa
rbi.notes: Issued to a foreign investor, board member or representative of a multinational company who does not reside in Rwanda but has significant business activities in the country and needs to regularly visit. Fee: USD 200. Valid for 2 to 10 years (renewable). Multiple entries. This is a long-stay visa category rather than a full residence permit.

rbi.name: Samoa
rbi.notes: The Citizenship Investment Act 2015 establishes a three-stage pathway: (1) Temporary Resident Permit, (2) Permanent Resident Permit (requiring minimum 15 days physical presence per year), (3) citizenship eligibility after 3 years. This is the only known official investment-based residency pathway in Samoa.

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.notes: Under Law 94/2017, Article 19, foreign nationals may obtain elective residence via one of three options: (a) purchase of a completed residential building or portion for a price of not less than €500,000; (b) purchase of a raw/unfinished building for not less than €350,000, with additional completion/renovation costs not exceeding €150,000 (total cap effectively €500,000); or (c) a non-interest-bearing restricted 10-year deposit of not less than €600,000 in State of San Marino bonds or a specially created State fund. Application fee €1,000; one-time tax of €10,000 (deposit option). Private health insurance required. No public sector employment; no state benefits. Family extension available at €20,000 per additional dependent. After 10 years converts to registered residence (per official esteri.sm; one secondary source cites 5 years - esteri.sm is authoritative). Path to citizenship: 30 years total continuous registered residence. Investment amounts confirmed via startup.sm (official agency) referencing Law 94/2017.

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.program_name: Atypical Residence – Facilitated Tax Regime (Residenza Atipica)
rbi.notes: For foreign citizens generating income abroad who have not previously resided in San Marino for tax purposes. Subject to a substitute facilitated tax rate of 7% on foreign-source income, with a minimum of €10,000 and maximum of €100,000 annually. Private health insurance required. Cannot work in public sector or receive state benefits. After 10 years converts to registered residence. Source confirmed via esteri.sm and secondary sources referencing the same program parameters.

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.notes: Limited to citizens from EU countries, Switzerland, and countries specified by a specific Congress of State Regulation. Eligibility: minimum annual pension/passive income of €50,000 OR movable assets of at least €300,000. Facilitated taxation at 6% on pension income. Private health insurance required. No public sector employment; no state benefits. After 10 years converts to registered residence. Source: esteri.sm official page (types listed) and castellidisanmarino.com (amounts). The exact list of non-EU/Swiss eligible nations is set by Congress of State Regulation and not published on the English esteri.sm page.

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.notes: Under Delegated Decree 63/2014: entrepreneurs may obtain automatic residence if the business employs at least 5 full-time permanent staff on the startup job list (if >5, at least 50% must be San Marino residents). Property investment of €300,000 minimum (purchase or equivalent guarantee) required within 90 days of project approval; the property must serve as business headquarters or residence and carries a lien as wage guarantee. Priority sectors include technology, green economy, hospitality/tourism, entertainment, retail, arts/culture, healthcare/pharmaceuticals. Annual cap applies.

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.notes: Requires minimum commercial space of 200 m² and either property purchase OR a multi-year rental with a €150,000 surety deposit. Minimum 2 employees from job placement lists. Maintenance period 10 years. Sourced from toccacelibronzetti.sm (a San Marino-registered accounting/fiscal firm) citing applicable legislation; not yet confirmed on a .gov or esteri.sm official domain URL.

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.program_name: Residence for Company Founders (Startup Incentive / Residenza per Ragioni Economiche)
rbi.notes: Under Delegated Decree 63/2014 and Law 115/2017: requires ≥51% ownership of a startup. Employment thresholds: 1 permanent employee from incentivized sectors OR 3 permanent employees from other sectors (or applicant is under 40 years old). Bank deposit guarantee required: €75,000 initially, increasing to €150,000 within 2 years; alternatively, property purchase with minimum value €150,000. Maximum outstanding debt: €20,000 (unless on deferred payment plan). Annual cap: 50 approvals per year (adjustable by decree).

rbi.name: San Marino
rbi.program_name: Business Purpose Residence (Residenza per Motivi di Business)
rbi.notes: For shareholders holding ≥25% of company capital, sole administrators, or board chairmen. Eligible sectors: technology, green economy, arts/culture, development services, marketing, research, training, low emissions, health/pharmaceuticals. Requires private health insurance with minimum €30,000 annual coverage per person. Adequate housing documentation required. Duration: 12 months initial, renewable up to 5 years. No specific minimum investment amount stated; residency is linked to active company role rather than passive investment.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: Annual fee of SAR 100,000 per year, renewable for up to 5 years. Does not automatically lead to permanent residency or citizenship. Administered by the Saudi Premium Residency Center.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: One-time fee of SAR 800,000 for permanent residency. No path to citizenship confirmed officially. Holders do not require a local sponsor. Benefits include family sponsorship, ability to conduct business, own real estate, and exemption from expatriate fees.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: Requires a minimum investment of SAR 7 million in Saudi Arabia, a valid investment license, and creation of at least 10 jobs within 2 years. Grants conditional permanent residency. Administered by Premium Residency Center.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: Two tracks: (1) Investment of SAR 400,000 with at least 20% ownership stake; (2) Investment of SAR 15 million with at least 10% ownership stake and creation of 20 jobs within 2 years. Benefits include nominating 2 staff members for Special Talent Residency and exemption from Nitaqat workforce localization for 3 years.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: Requires ownership of Saudi real estate worth a minimum of SAR 4 million. Residency duration is tied to property ownership. New laws effective January 2026 bolstered this category.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: Targets exceptional professionals in scientific, healthcare, research, and executive fields. Salary thresholds range from SAR 14,000 to SAR 80,000 per month depending on designation. Application fee SAR 4,000. Points-based eligibility system.

rbi.name: Saudi Arabia
rbi.notes: For exceptional talents in sports, culture, and arts. Requires national or international recognition, prestigious award, or official recognition with endorsement from relevant Saudi ministry. Application fee SAR 4,000. Granted for 5 years, renewable once for another 5 years (minimum 30 months residence required for renewal).

rbi.name: Serbia
rbi.notes: Requires certificate or proof of funds of at least EUR 50,000 in a Serbian-registered bank account and proof of invested tangible and intangible assets in a registered company in the Republic of Serbia (confirmed on official welcometoserbia.gov.rs page). For permit extension, proof of paid cash capital contribution of at least EUR 5,000 into share capital of a registered Serbian company is required. Permit issued for up to 3 years, renewable. Path to permanent residence requires 3 years of continuous temporary residence; citizenship eligibility after 3 further years of permanent residence (total ~6 years). Based on Law on Foreigners (amended 2023, in force February 2024).

rbi.name: Serbia
rbi.notes: Available to startup founders with innovative business activities confirmed by a Serbian science and technology park. Permit issued for up to 3 years under the Law on Foreigners (2023 amendments). Specific eligibility criteria and financial thresholds not publicly detailed on official portal pages accessed.

rbi.name: Serbia
rbi.notes: Available to holders of tertiary education qualifications that are professionally recognized (nostrified diploma required). Permit issued for up to 3 years under the Law on Foreigners (2023 amendments). Specific financial thresholds not detailed on official portal pages accessed.

rbi.name: Serbia
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence for Real Estate Owners
rbi.notes: Residence permit available on the basis of real estate ownership in Serbia. No government-mandated minimum investment threshold stated on official sources. Permit issued for up to 3 years. Path to permanent residence requires 3 years continuous temporary residence.

rbi.name: Seychelles
rbi.notes: Available to investors who: (1) have made a USD 1 million or more direct investment in a Seychelles business; (2) have at least 5 years of business association from that investment; (3) have resided in Seychelles for not less than 5 years on a Dependent Permit or Gainful Occupation Permit (GOP); (4) have not been continuously absent for 1+ year without ministerial consent; (5) have not been sentenced to imprisonment exceeding 1 year. Processing fee: SCR 1,000 (non-refundable, paid upfront in cash); Permit fee if approved: SCR 350,000. Key benefits: exempt from GOP fees; may purchase residential land from government at 50% sanction fee reduction. Applications submitted in person or via prcitsection@immigration.gov.sc. Official site managed by Seychelles Investment Board (SIB) at investinseychelles@sib.gov.sc.

rbi.name: Seychelles
rbi.notes: Granted to persons who: (a) have a family or domestic connection with Seychelles, or (b) have made or will make a special contribution to the economic, social or cultural life of Seychelles. Does not permit gainful occupation (a separate GOP is required). Permit holder must reside in Seychelles for at least 5 days per 12-month period. Bank guarantee of SCR 20,000 required. Fee: SCR 1,000 processing fee + SCR 150,000 permit fee (5-year term, main applicant) + SCR 75,000 for spouse (if applied simultaneously) + SCR 25,000 per child endorsement. Holder is not entitled to free medical service or social security benefits.

rbi.name: Sierra Leone
rbi.notes: Officially announced by SLID in January 2025 press release. Program grants immediate Permanent Residency through investment in Sierra Leonean gold bullion deposited in government vaults for 5 years. No in-country residency requirement to acquire or retain PR. Upgrade pathway to citizenship exists. Specific investment amounts appear only on private operator website goforgold.center - therefore min_amount is omitted per hard rules.

rbi.name: Sierra Leone
rbi.notes: Foreign nationals residing, studying, or working in Sierra Leone for more than 90 days require a Residence Permit issued by SLID. Categories: Business Immigration Quota (BIQ), Company Quota (CQ), Employment, Student, and Dependant. Applications fully online via unifiedpermit.gov.sl. Non-ECOWAS fees (from SLIEPA FAQ): Employee 3,000,000 Leones; Self Employed 3,600,000 Leones; renewal 855,000 Leones. ECOWAS citizens: Employee/Self Employed 1,500,000 Leones.

rbi.name: Singapore
rbi.program_name: Global Investor Programme (GIP) – Option A: Direct Business Investment
rbi.notes: Grants Singapore Permanent Residency. Invest SGD 10 million in a new or existing Singapore business entity. Must hire minimum 30 employees with at least 50% Singapore Citizens. Minimum 10 new employees required for Re-entry Permit renewal eligibility after initial 5-year period. Application fee S$20,000 (revised 5 May 2025) plus S$100 ICA immigration processing fee. Processing approximately 12 months. After 2 years as PR, applicants aged 21+ may apply for Singapore citizenship (not guaranteed). Changes effective March 15, 2023.

rbi.name: Singapore
rbi.program_name: Global Investor Programme (GIP) – Option B: GIP-Select Fund Investment
rbi.notes: Grants Singapore Permanent Residency. Invest SGD 25 million in a GIP-select fund as shortlisted by EDB. Investment must be demonstrated within 6-month period of Approval-in-Principle (AIP) PR status, made from personal bank account in sole name at a Singapore-registered bank. Application fee S$20,000 (revised 5 May 2025). Processing approximately 12 months. After 2 years as PR, applicants aged 21+ may apply for Singapore citizenship (not guaranteed). Changes effective March 15, 2023.

rbi.name: Singapore
rbi.program_name: Global Investor Programme (GIP) – Option C: Single-Family Office
rbi.notes: Grants Singapore Permanent Residency. Requires minimum SGD 200 million Assets-Under-Management in a Single-Family Office, with a minimum deployment of SGD 50 million in EDB-specified investments (SGX-listed companies, qualifying debt securities, Singapore-licensed managed funds, or private equity in non-listed Singapore businesses) to be deployed no later than 12 months from Final Approval of PR. Application fee S$20,000 (revised 5 May 2025). Processing approximately 12 months. After 2 years as PR, applicants aged 21+ may apply for Singapore citizenship (not guaranteed). Changes effective March 15, 2023.

rbi.name: Slovakia
rbi.notes: Foreigners may obtain temporary residence by establishing a business in Slovakia (sole trader/trade license or LLC/s.r.o.). No minimum statutory investment amount is set by law, but applicants must demonstrate economic benefit via a Business Plan (job creation or activity in labor-shortage sectors). As of 1 July 2025, applications must be submitted at Slovak diplomatic missions abroad. Ministry of Economy issues an opinion within 60 days; Foreign Police decision within 90 days. Permit valid for up to 3 years, renewable. After 5 years of continuous legal residence, applicant may apply for permanent residence. Citizenship available after 8 years of continuous legal residence (including permanent residence). Governed by Act No. 404/2011 on Residence of Foreigners.

rbi.name: Slovakia
rbi.program_name: Residence for Significant/Major Investor (Certificate of Significant Investment)
rbi.notes: Investors holding a Certificate of Significant Investment from the Ministry of Economy may qualify for expedited residence permit processing. Specific minimum investment thresholds (previously cited as EUR 100 million / 300 jobs) could not be confirmed from official published sources during June 2026 validation; applicants should contact cudzinec@mhsr.sk or the Ministry of Economy directly. Permanent residence may also be granted directly in the interest of Slovakia for qualifying major investors. Citizenship may be possible under discretionary 'interest of the Slovak Republic' provisions.

rbi.name: Slovakia
rbi.notes: EU Blue Card for highly qualified third-country nationals. Requirements: university degree or equivalent higher professional qualifications, work contract or binding job offer of at least 6 months, salary of at least 1.2x the average monthly wage in Slovakia (the 2023 average was EUR 1,430/month, giving a ~EUR 1,716/month threshold for 2024 applications; threshold is updated annually by the Statistical Office). Valid for up to 5 years (or contract duration + 90 days if shorter). Fee: EUR 250 initial, EUR 140 renewal. Processing: 30 days from complete application. No labour market test required as of 15 July 2024. Blue Card holders can apply for long-term/permanent residence after 5 consecutive years of legal residence in Slovakia.

rbi.name: Slovenia
rbi.program_name: Temporary Residence Permit for Business Investors / Company Director
rbi.notes: Non-EU nationals may obtain a work permit (and thus residence) by establishing or investing in a Slovenian limited liability company (d.o.o.). For companies not yet registered for 6 months, proof of investment of at least EUR 30,000 for company start-up is required to obtain a work permit for a foreign representative. The permit is issued for up to 2 years and is renewable. After 5 years of continuous legal residence, permanent residency is available; citizenship via naturalisation after 10 years total. There is no dedicated 'golden visa' or standalone investor visa program - residence flows from business activity, not passive investment.

rbi.name: South Africa
rbi.notes: Section 27(c) of the Immigration Act 2002: Permanent residence for foreigners who intend to establish or have a business in South Africa. Specific minimum investment amounts are not stated on the official DHA page scraped; applicants must meet criteria per Regulation 24(4). No golden visa or standalone investor residence program with a specific minimum investment threshold was found on official sources.

rbi.name: South Africa
rbi.notes: Section 27(f) of the Immigration Act 2002: Permanent residence for foreigners who are financially independent. Specific minimum net worth/income thresholds not stated on the official DHA page scraped.

rbi.name: South Africa
rbi.notes: Section 27(b) of the Immigration Act 2002: Permanent residence for foreigners with exceptional/critical skills and qualifications. Applicants must be on the current Critical Skills List. Work visa holders may apply for direct permanent residence after 5 years.

rbi.name: South Korea
rbi.program_name: Immigrant Investor Scheme for Real Estate (IISRE) - F-2-8 Visa
rbi.notes: Investment in government-designated tourism and leisure facilities in areas such as Jeju Island, Incheon Free Economic Zone (Songdo, Yeongjong, Cheongna), Alpensia resort (Pyeongchang), Haeundae (Busan), and other designated zones. Minimum KRW 1 billion (increased from KRW 500 million in May 2023). Grants F-2 residence visa to investor, spouse, and unmarried children. After 5 years of maintaining investment, eligible to apply for F-5 permanent residency. CAUTION: Program was valid through April 30, 2026 per IFEZ official page; no official confirmation of extension found as of June 2026. Travelers should confirm current status with Korea Immigration Service before applying.

rbi.name: South Korea
rbi.program_name: Immigrant Investor Scheme for Public Business (IISPB) - F-2-12 Visa
rbi.notes: Investment in public interest funds designated by the Minister of Justice. Minimum KRW 1.5 billion (threefold increase from prior threshold). Managed through Korea Development Bank. Grants F-2 residence to investor, spouse, and unmarried children. After 5 years of maintaining investment, eligible for F-5 permanent residency. Preliminary investment screening requires personal visit to Korea at least once.

rbi.name: South Korea
rbi.notes: Non-investment points-based residency for highly skilled professionals. Requires 80+ points out of 135 based on age, education, income, Korean language ability, and residence history. Minimum 1 year of qualifying employment/residence to apply. F-5-16 permanent residency available after 3 years on F-2-7. Not an investment visa but a key highly-skilled residency pathway.

rbi.name: Spain
rbi.notes: ABOLISHED on April 3, 2025 by Organic Law 1/2025 (published BOE January 3, 2025), which eliminated articles 63-67 of Law 14/2013. Investment options were: real estate ≥€500,000 (unencumbered); shares/stocks in Spanish companies ≥€1,000,000; Spanish public debt ≥€2,000,000; business projects of general interest. Applications submitted before April 3, 2025 may still be processed under prior rules. Min_amount reflects the former real estate option (lowest threshold). Citizenship path is via standard naturalization (10 years residence generally).

rbi.name: Spain
rbi.notes: For non-EU nationals who wish to reside in Spain without engaging in work activities. Requires proof of sufficient economic means (400% of monthly IPREM for the applicant, plus 100% per dependent). Initial visa valid 1 year; can be renewed. After 5 years continuous legal residence may apply for long-term residence permit (permanent residence). Path to citizenship is 10 years (2 years for certain nationalities). No minimum investment amount required - based on income/savings proof.

rbi.name: Sri Lanka
rbi.notes: Minimum deposit of USD 200,000 in a Golden Paradise Foreign Currency Account (GPFCA) at a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka. Up to 50% of the minimum investment may be withdrawn after the first year from visa issuance. Visa validity: 10 years. Visa fee: USD 2,000 for 10 years. Permitted investments: condominium property, land and building leases, Sri Lanka Development Bonds, other government-approved investments. Includes spouse and dependents. No official pathway to permanent residence or citizenship stated.

rbi.name: Sri Lanka
rbi.notes: Minimum investment: USD 100,000 for 5-year visa or USD 200,000 for 10-year visa (amounts from search snippets attributed to immigration.gov.lk; full details in official PDF). Investment sectors include information technology, tourism, and other approved sectors. No official pathway to permanent residence or citizenship stated.

rbi.name: Sri Lanka
rbi.notes: Fixed deposit requirement: USD 15,000 or equivalent in approved foreign currency at an approved Sri Lankan bank. Monthly remittance requirement: USD 1,500 per principal applicant; USD 750 per spouse and each dependent child. Visa validity: 2 years, renewable. Fee: USD 200 per year per person (applicants and dependents over 16). Currently open for extensions only (existing visa holders); not open to new applicants. No employment permitted. No pathway to permanent residence or citizenship stated.

rbi.name: Sri Lanka
rbi.notes: Extension-only program for existing RGS visa holders; not open to new applicants. Investor category: minimum USD 250,000 in a Foreign Currency Account; dependent: USD 35,000 minimum. Professional category: monthly income of USD 2,000 (applicant) and USD 1,000 per dependent. Visa validity: 5 years from issuance date. Fee: USD 200 per person per year. No employment permitted. No pathway to permanent residence or citizenship stated.

rbi.name: Sudan
rbi.notes: Section 21(1) of Sudan's Investment (Encouragement) Act, 2021 provides that non-Sudanese investors shall be granted residence throughout the duration of their investment project. This is project-tied residency, not a standalone RBI/golden visa program. The law does not set a minimum amount for residence per se; the closest verifiable foreign-investor threshold is the earnest-money deposit in Section 22(2): the foreign investor shall deposit, before being granted a license, an amount that 'shall not be less than two hundred and fifty thousand Dollars or what equivalent thereof in foreign currencies acceptable by the Central Bank, through external transfer' (USD 250,000), recorded here as min_amount. Section 22(1) leaves the general minimum invested capital to be specified by regulations (not published on any accessible official source). The UNCTAD page mirrors the law text verbatim but is not itself a Sudan government domain - marked source_official=false.

rbi.name: Sweden
rbi.notes: Residence permit for non-EU/EEA nationals to run their own business in Sweden. Must own and actively manage at least 51% of the business. Financial self-sufficiency requirement: SEK 200,000 for applicant, SEK 100,000 per accompanying spouse, SEK 50,000 per accompanying child. Must demonstrate good industry experience, language skills (Swedish/English), and a credible business plan with established customer contacts. Permit duration: up to 2 years, renewable. After 4 years of work permit in Sweden can apply for permanent residence. Citizenship requires 8 years of habitual residence as of June 2026. Application fee: SEK 2,000.

rbi.name: Sweden
rbi.program_name: EU Blue Card for Highly Qualified Workers
rbi.notes: EU Blue Card for highly qualified employment. Requires higher education (minimum 180 credits) or at least 5 years relevant professional experience. Minimum salary: SEK 52,000/month (as of 9 July 2025, set at 1.25 times average Swedish salary). Employment contract for minimum 6 months required. Comprehensive health insurance required. Permit duration: 9 months to 4 years. Processing: 75% of complete applications decided within 1 month. Application fee: SEK 2,000. Path to permanent residence after 4 years of work. Citizenship after 8 years of habitual residence (as of June 6, 2026).

rbi.name: Switzerland
rbi.notes: Foreign nationals who establish Swiss domicile for the first time (or after 10+ years abroad) and do not engage in gainful employment in Switzerland may apply for expenditure-based taxation (forfait fiscal). Tax is calculated on total annual cost of living in Switzerland and abroad. The cantonal tax ruling underpins a B-permit (residence permit) issued by cantonal authorities. Available in 21 of 26 cantons (not available in Zurich, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Schaffhausen, and Appenzell Ausserrhoden). No specific minimum investment is prescribed by federal law; minimum tax base is CHF 434,700 as of 2025 under federal law with cantonal minimums varying. This is not an 'investment' program per se - no minimum investment threshold is legislated federally. The residence permit type is standard B permit. Right to lump-sum taxation ends upon acquiring Swiss citizenship or gainful employment in Switzerland. Official source: Swiss Federal Department of Finance (EFD).

rbi.name: Switzerland
