Must have monthly funds of at least twice the average monthly net salary in Slovenia (approximately EUR 3,200/month as of early 2026). Must hold valid health insurance (min EUR 30,000 coverage) and have a clean criminal record.
fastTrack.notes: Launched 21 November 2025. Permit issued for up to one year; cannot be extended. Reapplication possible 6 months after expiry. Alternative path: holders may switch to other residence permit categories at any time during permit validity. Family members may join immediately without duration restrictions. Applications submitted at Slovenian diplomatic missions abroad or at any administrative unit in Slovenia.

fastTrack.name: Slovenia
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU nationals with a valid work contract or binding job offer for highly qualified employment (at least 6 months under 2025 amendments) paying at least 1.5x the average annual gross salary in Slovenia. Requires higher professional qualifications (university level) or, for IT professionals, proven competence via certificates or expert opinion.
fastTrack.processing_time: 30 days (up to 60 days for complex cases)
fastTrack.notes: Issued for the duration of the employment contract plus 3 months, maximum 2 years; renewable for up to 3 years. Labour market test applies. Initial application fee EUR 70-102; residence permit card EUR 15.47. 2025 amendments loosened requirements: contract minimum reduced from 1 year to 6 months, and IT professionals may qualify without academic degrees.

fastTrack.name: Slovenia
fastTrack.program_name: Single Permit (Combined Residence and Work Permit)
fastTrack.eligibility: Third-country nationals seeking employment in Slovenia. Employer must demonstrate no suitable EU/Slovenian worker was available (labour market test).
fastTrack.notes: Combines residence and work permit into a single administrative procedure. Available for various employment categories including seasonal workers and intra-corporate transferees.

fastTrack.name: Slovenia
fastTrack.program_name: Work Permit for Foreign Company Representative / Director
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU nationals who are directors or procurators of a Slovenian company (d.o.o. or other entity). Companies with 10 or fewer workers may obtain no more than one such permit.
fastTrack.notes: For companies registered less than 6 months: minimum investment of EUR 30,000 for company start-up required. Valid for up to 2 years; renewable. Application fee approximately EUR 90.

fastTrack.name: South Africa
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals whose occupation appears on the South African Critical Skills List; must provide confirmation from a relevant professional body/council/board recognised by SAQA; valid employment offer required; visa issued for up to 5 years
fastTrack.notes: Governed by Section 19(4) of the Immigration Act. Critical Skills List is updated periodically and published in the Government Gazette. Effective requirements version: 9 October 2024.

fastTrack.name: South Africa
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals employed by a foreign-based employer; must hold a valid employment contract signed by both applicant and employer; minimum gross salary of R650,796.00 per annum; must be resident in a country with a valid long-term residence status (e.g., Green Card, work visa); B1/B2 US visa holders not eligible (must apply in country of origin)
fastTrack.notes: Port of Entry Visa (Remote Work Visa) exceeding 90 days. Official requirements document published by the South African Embassy (Washington DC). Minimum salary threshold: R650,796.00 per annum. Added to Immigration Regulations effective 28 March 2024. Application fee: USD $36.00 (from the US). Requires FBI criminal background check, medical report, proof of accommodation, and South African Revenue Service registration if present for more than 183 aggregate days.

fastTrack.name: South Korea
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals who are self-employed or employed by an overseas company, working remotely, with at least 1 year of work experience in the same industry, aged 18+. Minimum income approximately KRW 88.1 million/year (double South Korea's GNI per capita). Must hold valid private health insurance (minimum KRW 100 million coverage).
fastTrack.notes: Launched January 2024, made permanent program in 2025. Authorized stay up to 1 year, renewable once (maximum 2 years total). Dependents (spouse and minor children) eligible. Local employment in Korea prohibited. As of 2026, in-country status change from B-1/B-2 (tourist) to F-1-D permitted without leaving Korea if all eligibility requirements met.

fastTrack.name: South Korea
fastTrack.eligibility: World-leading talent in core future industries: semiconductors, AI, robotics, biotechnology, aerospace, defense, secondary batteries, displays. Expanded March 2026 to include STEM professors and researchers. Requires annual salary of at least 3x GNI per capita (approx. KRW 130-149 million). Must hold master's/doctorate from world top-100 university with 8+ years experience including 3+ at a global top-500 company, or equivalent research credentials.
fastTrack.processing_time: Priority processing at dedicated centers at Seoul Immigration Office; experts in national strategic technologies processed at twice standard speed
fastTrack.notes: Part of South Korea's 2026 Immigration Policy Strategy released March 5, 2026. Grants F-2 long-term residency with free work activities. Path to F-5 permanent residency after 3 years. Benefits include 50% income tax reduction up to 10 years, special school admission for children, and expanded housing loans.

fastTrack.name: South Korea
fastTrack.program_name: K-STAR Visa (F-2-7S) - Korea-Science and Technology Advanced Human-Resources
fastTrack.eligibility: Outstanding foreign master's and doctoral degree holders in science and technology, recommended as 'excellent talent' by their Korean university. Enables F-2 residency application without prior employment offer.
fastTrack.notes: Launched as part of 2026 immigration reforms. Cuts period-of-stay requirement for permanent residency (F-5) from 6 years to 3 years. Nationwide implementation in 2026 after pilot in 2023. Information session held at Seoul National University on April 27, 2026.

fastTrack.name: South Korea
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign entrepreneurs intending to establish a technology-based startup in South Korea. Must score at least 60-80 points under Korea's Startup Immigration Points System. Must hold bachelor's degree or higher. Physical office address required (virtual offices not accepted). Minimum capital KRW 10 million.
fastTrack.notes: Startup Korea Special Visa (D-8-4S) launched November 2024; expanded August 2025 to allow recommendation letters from local governments and accredited accelerators in addition to the Ministry. Typical pathway: OASIS certificate (startup evaluation) -> D-10-2 startup preparation visa -> D-8-4 startup visa. Jointly administered by Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS) and Ministry of Justice (MOJ).

fastTrack.name: South Korea
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign graduates of South Korean technical/vocational colleges in manufacturing fields, employed in designated population-decline regions.
fastTrack.notes: Introduced as part of South Korea's 2026 Immigration Policy Strategy. Allows F-2 visa application after just 3 years of continuous service in a designated population-decline region, bypassing the standard longer timeline.

fastTrack.name: Spain
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU nationals working remotely for companies located outside Spain. Must hold a university degree from a prestigious institution or have 3+ years of professional experience. Employees must work exclusively for non-Spanish companies; self-employed may work up to 20% for Spanish entities.
fastTrack.notes: Established under Law 28/2022 (Startup Law) amending Law 14/2013. Visa valid up to 1 year; can be converted to residence authorization (up to 3 years) via UGE-CE. Income threshold: 200% of monthly SMI (€2,442/month as of 2026). Processed by UGE-CE (Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos).

fastTrack.name: Spain
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU nationals planning to launch an innovative business project of particular economic interest for Spain. Requires a favourable report from the Economic and Commercial Office evaluating job creation, qualifications, and economic value.
fastTrack.notes: Established under Law 14/2013 as amended by Startup Law 28/2022. Financial requirement: 100% of IPREM plus 50% per dependent. Visa valid 1 year. After arrival, can obtain entrepreneur residence authorization through UGE-CE. Covered by Spain's 'Entrepreneurs Law'.

fastTrack.name: Spain
fastTrack.program_name: Highly Qualified Worker Visa / EU Blue Card
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU nationals with a valid employment contract for highly qualified work. Must hold a university/college degree (3+ years) or 5+ years of professional experience. Minimum gross annual salary €38,844 (2024); reduced threshold €31,075 for shortage occupations or recent graduates.
fastTrack.notes: Two routes: Spain's national Highly Qualified Worker visa (Law 14/2013) and the EU Blue Card. EU Blue Card valid 3 years, renewable for 2 years. EU Blue Card fee: €73.26 initial application, €16.08 card issuance. Processed through UGE-CE at inclusion.gob.es. Visa initially valid 1 year pending residence authorization.

fastTrack.name: Spain
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU nationals transferring within the same company or group of companies to Spain as senior management, specialists, or trainees.
fastTrack.processing_time: 10 days from submission (visa); 20 working days for residence authorization
fastTrack.notes: Established under Law 14/2013. Visa valid 1 year or duration of residence permit if shorter. Requires Initial Residence Authorization from Spain's Dirección General de Migraciones. Family members may apply concurrently.

fastTrack.name: Sri Lanka
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals who earn income remotely from clients or employers outside Sri Lanka; must have international health insurance covering Sri Lanka; requires recommendation from Ministry of Digital Economy
fastTrack.notes: Applicants must prove minimum monthly remittance (exact amount in official PDF: immigration.gov.lk/content/files/visa/digital_nomad/Digital%20Nomad%20Visa%20Category.pdf - PDF not machine-readable from web). Digital nomad holders cannot engage in local employment; all income must be earned remotely. Application submitted to Residence Visa Division of the Department of Immigration and Emigration.

fastTrack.name: Suriname
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals requiring Short-Stay Visa (MKV), Work Permit, and Residence Permit simultaneously
fastTrack.processing_time: Approximately 3-4 weeks (versus 6+ months sequentially) assuming complete documentation
fastTrack.notes: Launched by Suriname's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Business, and International Cooperation; announced October 2024, became operational mid-2025. Additional government fee of USD 1,500 beyond standard fees. All three applications (Short-Stay Visa, Work Permit, Residence Permit) reviewed concurrently. Source is Fragomen immigration alert citing the Suriname MFA; no direct official government URL confirmed.

fastTrack.name: Sweden
fastTrack.program_name: EU Blue Card – Fast Track Processing
fastTrack.eligibility: Highly qualified workers with higher education (min. 180 credits) or 5+ years relevant experience, employed in Sweden at salary of at least SEK 52,000/month (1.25x average Swedish salary, effective 9 July 2025).
fastTrack.processing_time: 75% of complete applications decided within 1 month
fastTrack.notes: The EU Blue Card has notably fast processing for complete applications (75% within 1 month). From 1 June 2026, new rules for work permits apply in Sweden.

fastTrack.name: Sweden
fastTrack.program_name: Residence Permit to Look for Work or Start a Business
fastTrack.eligibility: Highly educated individuals (second-cycle qualification: 60+ credit Master's, professional degree, or PhD) residing outside Sweden. Must demonstrate financial self-sufficiency of SEK 13,000 per month and hold comprehensive health insurance.
fastTrack.processing_time: 75% of complete applications decided within 7 months
fastTrack.notes: Allows highly-educated non-EU/EEA nationals to enter Sweden for up to 9 months to look for work or explore business opportunities without a prior job offer. Fee: SEK 2,200. If employment or business is established during the permit period, the holder may apply for a work/self-employment residence permit from within Sweden.

fastTrack.name: Sweden
fastTrack.program_name: Work Permit – General Fast Track Model
fastTrack.eligibility: Non-EU/EEA nationals with a job offer from a Swedish employer meeting salary and conditions standards. From 1 June 2026, new rules apply to work permit applications.
fastTrack.processing_time: Average 18 days for fast-tracked applications (from 100+ days prior to model change)
fastTrack.notes: The Swedish Migration Agency developed a new fast-track model for skilled labour migrant work permits, reducing average processing to 18 days for complete applications. From 1 June 2026, new rules for work permits apply. Application fee: SEK 2,000.

fastTrack.name: Switzerland
fastTrack.eligibility: Managers, specialists and other qualified workers from non-EU/EFTA states. Must hold university or higher education degree with several years of professional experience. Employer must demonstrate no suitable candidate available from Switzerland or EU/EFTA (precedence principle). Annual quotas apply (set by Federal Council via ASEO ordinance).
fastTrack.notes: Switzerland restricts non-EU/EFTA work admissions to highly qualified individuals. The employer applies for a B permit. Specific fast-track or talent visa for tech/startup not established on official SEM pages as of June 2026. Exemptions exist for multinational intra-company transfers, doctoral/post-doctoral researchers, and graduates of Swiss higher education institutions. Source: SEM.

fastTrack.name: Taiwan
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals with demonstrated professional expertise in one of 12 designated fields: Architecture, Biotechnology, Culture and Arts, Digital, Economy, Education, Environment, Finance, Law, National Defense, Science & Technology, Sports. Applicants must meet field-specific salary thresholds or hold recognized qualifications.
fastTrack.processing_time: Joint review by National Immigration Agency, Ministry of Labor, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and specialized authorities
fastTrack.notes: Combined open work permit, resident visa, Alien Resident Certificate, and re-entry permit valid up to 3 years. Open work authorization (work for any employer). Special tax incentives for high earners. Apply via Foreign Professionals Online Application Platform at https://coa.immigration.gov.tw/coa-frontend/four-in-one/entry/golden-card. Official site also at foreigntalentact.ndc.gov.tw.

fastTrack.name: Taiwan
fastTrack.eligibility: Nationals of Taiwan visa-exempt countries only. Age 30+: annual salary at least USD 40,000 (within last 2 years); Age 20-29: annual salary at least USD 20,000. Alternative: hold a digital nomad visa from another country. Bank statements must show average at least USD 10,000/month over 6 months. Must hold proof of international health insurance.
fastTrack.processing_time: Applications submitted to ROC overseas mission, forwarded to National Development Council for review; or domestic applications at BOCA/MOFA offices at least 10 working days before stay expires
fastTrack.notes: Program launched per Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals. Maximum stay duration and renewal period not specified verbatim on BOCA's official page. Also available via: https://foreigntalentact.ndc.gov.tw and https://digitalnomad.ndc.gov.tw/. Program information also at https://talent.nat.gov.tw/visa/digital-nomad

fastTrack.name: Thailand
fastTrack.eligibility: Five categories: SMART-T (Talent/highly-skilled experts in targeted industries, min income THB 100,000/month); SMART-E (Senior Executives, min income THB 200,000/month, 10+ years experience, bachelor's degree, senior management role); SMART-I (Investors in targeted industries); SMART-S (Startup entrepreneurs, THB 600,000 min deposit held 3+ months, company director or 25%+ equity in Thai firm); SMART-O (Dependents of SMART visa holders). All must work in 18 targeted S-Curve industries. Digital nomads/remote workers without Thai employment contracts ineligible.
fastTrack.notes: Maximum 4-year renewable permission to stay (2 years for SMART-S startup employees). No work permit required for endorsed employers. Spouse and dependents receive equal stay permission; spouse may work without separate permit. 1-year reporting cycle. No re-entry permit needed. Fast-track airport services available.

fastTrack.name: Thailand
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals working remotely for overseas employers, freelancers, digital content creators. Requirements: passport valid 6+ months, bank statements (3 months) with min ending balance THB 500,000, proof of income/salary slips (6 months), foreign employment contract or certificate authenticated by embassy.
fastTrack.processing_time: 2 working days from complete document submission
fastTrack.notes: 5-year multiple-entry visa. Each entry permits stay up to 180 days, extendable once for additional 180 days (total 180 days per entry). After maximum stay reached, must depart and re-enter using same DTV. Issued by Thai embassies/consulates abroad. MFA official program.

fastTrack.name: Trinidad and Tobago
fastTrack.eligibility: CARICOM nationals in 12 approved categories: University Graduates, Artistes, Musicians, Media Workers, Sportspersons, Nurses, Teachers, Artisans, Associate Degree Holders, Domestic Workers, Agricultural Workers, Private Security Officers
fastTrack.notes: Under Article 46 of the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas, eligible CARICOM nationals holding a Certificate of Recognition of CARICOM Skills Qualification can live and work in Trinidad and Tobago (and other CSME member states) with no restriction on freedom of movement and indefinite stay subject to immigration requirements.

fastTrack.name: Trinidad and Tobago
fastTrack.eligibility: Any non-national of Trinidad and Tobago seeking employment. Persons working for no more than 30 days in any 12 consecutive months are exempt from requiring a work permit.
fastTrack.notes: Work permits are processed online only. Fee is TT$450 per month for the approved period. Duration fee must be paid before the Work Permit is processed.

fastTrack.name: Turkey
fastTrack.program_name: Digital Nomad Identification Certificate / Digital Nomad Visa
fastTrack.eligibility: Ages 21-55; university degree; documented digital/remote work; minimum income of USD 3,000/month (USD 36,000/year); passport valid 6+ months; available to citizens of 34 specified countries (primarily European nations plus USA, Canada, selected former Soviet states)
fastTrack.notes: goturkiye.com is operated by the Turkish Tourism Promotion and Development Agency (TGA), an official government body. Applicants first obtain a Digital Nomad Identification Certificate online, then apply for the visa at a Turkish consulate. Launched April 2024. Holders may subsequently apply for a short-term residence permit via e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr.

fastTrack.name: Uganda
fastTrack.program_name: Entry Permit – Class G3 (Rare Skilled Expatriates)
fastTrack.eligibility: Expatriates with rare skills employed in agro-processing, manufacturing, and mining of selected minerals
fastTrack.notes: Class G3 is a special category for rare-skilled foreign nationals. No fast-track fee waiver or accelerated timeline stated on official page beyond standard work permit processing.

fastTrack.name: Uganda
fastTrack.program_name: East African Community Work Permit Fee Waiver (Kenya & Rwanda nationals)
fastTrack.eligibility: Nationals of Kenya and Rwanda under EAC Common Market Protocol
fastTrack.notes: Nationals from Kenya and Rwanda are exempted from payment of immigration fees; however, they must still apply and obtain a work permit. Tanzanian nationals pay reduced fee of USD 1,550 per year.

fastTrack.name: United Arab Emirates
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals employed remotely outside UAE with minimum monthly salary of USD 3,500 or equivalent in foreign currency
fastTrack.notes: Allows remote workers to legally reside in UAE. Requires proof of remote employment outside UAE, salary certificate. Total fees: AED 300. Overstay fine: AED 50/day.

fastTrack.name: United Arab Emirates
fastTrack.eligibility: Exceptional talents in Arts & Culture, Innovation & Invention, Athletics, Digital Technology, or other fields recognized by federal/local government authorities. Digital technology talents require approval from UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence.
fastTrack.notes: 10-year Golden Residency for exceptional talents. Requires government recommendation/approval per category. Total fees: AED 300. Covers arts, innovation, sports, digital technology, and other exceptional fields.

fastTrack.name: United Arab Emirates
fastTrack.eligibility: Artificial intelligence specialists sponsored by a technology-focused establishment in UAE
fastTrack.notes: New visa category for AI specialists. Single or multiple entry within a specified period. Sponsoring entity must be a technology-focused establishment.

fastTrack.name: United Arab Emirates
fastTrack.eligibility: High school graduates with cumulative GPA of at least 95% (or equivalent); OR university graduates with GPA of at least 3.8 within 2 years of graduation from UAE universities
fastTrack.notes: 5-year residency for high school graduates (95%+), 10-year residency for top UAE university graduates. Live ICP Golden Residency page (June 2026) states university GPA threshold of ≥3.8. A prior correction (March 2026) introduced a tiered Classification A (3.5+) / B (3.8+) system that is not reflected on the current live ICP page — reverted to the single ≥3.8 threshold. See data_quality.gaps for unresolved classification uncertainty.

fastTrack.name: United Kingdom
fastTrack.eligibility: Leaders or potential leaders in academia/research, arts and culture, or digital technology. Must be endorsed by an approved UK body or have won an eligible prestigious prize. Minimum age 18.
fastTrack.processing_time: 3 weeks (outside UK); 8 weeks (inside UK). Fast-track endorsement 2 weeks for eligible academic/research roles.
fastTrack.notes: Allows work in the UK for up to 5 years at a time, renewable. Path to Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) after 3-5 years depending on field and track. Application fee: £766 (or £561 + £205 endorsement route). Healthcare surcharge approx. £1,035/year. No need for employer sponsorship. Three fast-track endorsement processes available via British Academy, Royal Society, Royal Academy of Engineering, and UKRI.

fastTrack.name: United Kingdom
fastTrack.eligibility: Individuals wanting to set up a new, innovative, viable and scalable business in the UK. Must obtain endorsement from an approved body. English language proficiency required. Business idea must be original.
fastTrack.notes: No minimum investment amount specified by government. Visa lasts up to 3 years, renewable. Path to ILR (settlement) after 3 years. Application fee: £1,357 (outside UK) or £1,693 (extension/switch). Endorsement assessment fee: £1,000. Minimum 2 endorsing body meetings at £500 each.

fastTrack.name: United Kingdom
fastTrack.eligibility: Must have a confirmed job offer from a UK Home Office-approved employer, certificate of sponsorship, eligible occupation, meet minimum salary requirements, English language proficiency.
fastTrack.notes: Visa lasts up to 5 years, renewable. Path to ILR after 5 years. Faster decisions available for additional fee. Most common route for skilled workers.

fastTrack.name: United States
fastTrack.program_name: O-1 Visa: Individuals with Extraordinary Ability or Achievement
fastTrack.eligibility: Individuals who possess extraordinary ability in the sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics (O-1A), or who have demonstrated record of extraordinary achievement in the motion picture or television industry (O-1B). Requires evidence of sustained national or international acclaim. Must be coming temporarily to the US to continue work in the area of extraordinary ability.
fastTrack.processing_time: Regular or premium processing (15 business days with premium). Initial period up to 3 years, extendable in 1-year increments.
fastTrack.notes: Nonimmigrant visa. Can serve as a stepping stone to EB-1A (Alien of Extraordinary Ability) permanent residency. No annual cap. Petitioner (employer/agent) files Form I-129.

fastTrack.name: United States
fastTrack.program_name: EB-1A: Employment-Based First Preference - Extraordinary Ability
fastTrack.eligibility: Aliens with extraordinary ability in the sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics that has been demonstrated by sustained national or international acclaim. Can self-petition (no employer required). Must continue to work in the field of expertise.
fastTrack.processing_time: Regular or premium processing (45 business days with premium for I-140). No per-country annual cap for EB-1.
fastTrack.notes: Immigrant visa (permanent residency / green card pathway). Files Form I-140. No labor certification required. Can self-petition. Three sub-categories: EB-1A (extraordinary ability), EB-1B (outstanding professor/researcher), EB-1C (multinational executive/manager).

fastTrack.name: United States
fastTrack.eligibility: Professionals with advanced degrees or individuals with exceptional ability in the sciences, arts, or business who can demonstrate their work is of substantial merit and national importance to the US. Can self-petition - no employer sponsorship or labor certification required.
fastTrack.processing_time: Regular or premium processing. Processing times vary; check egov.uscis.gov/processing-times.
fastTrack.notes: Immigrant visa (permanent residency / green card pathway). Files Form I-140. Waives the job offer and labor certification requirement in the national interest. Subject to per-country annual limits which may result in wait times for nationals of high-demand countries (India, China).

fastTrack.name: United States
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign workers in specialty occupations requiring at least a bachelor's degree or equivalent in a specific specialty. Must be sponsored by a US employer. Subject to annual numerical cap (65,000 regular cap + 20,000 advanced degree exemption). Selection via electronic registration lottery.
fastTrack.processing_time: Regular or premium processing (15 business days with premium). Initial period up to 3 years, extendable to 6 years total.
fastTrack.notes: Nonimmigrant visa. Most common pathway for skilled foreign workers. Employer-sponsored only. Can transition to permanent residency (green card) through employer sponsorship (EB-2 or EB-3).

fastTrack.name: United States
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign entrepreneurs who have a central and active role in a startup entity formed in the US within the past 5 years, and can demonstrate the startup has significant potential for rapid growth and job creation. Startup must have received at least $311,071 in qualified investment from qualified investors (as of Oct. 1, 2024) or at least $124,429 in government grants/awards. Applicant must own at least 10% of the startup.
fastTrack.processing_time: Varies; filed on Form I-941 (Application for Entrepreneur Parole). Initial parole period up to 30 months, with one 30-month renewal possible.
fastTrack.notes: Parole (authorized stay), not a visa category. Does not lead directly to permanent residency; entrepreneurs must pursue a separate immigrant visa pathway. Spouses and minor children also eligible for parole. Investment and revenue thresholds updated triennially per CPI-U (last updated Oct. 1, 2024: investment threshold raised to $311,071; grant threshold raised to $124,429).

fastTrack.name: Uruguay
fastTrack.eligibility: Investors, operators, technicians, managers, and middle management linked to exporting companies. Any foreigner hired by local or international exporting companies, whether currently in Uruguay or abroad.
fastTrack.processing_time: Shortened timeframe vs standard; temporary residency duration: more than 6 months to less than 2 years.
fastTrack.notes: Uruguay XXI facilitates expedited access to temporary residencies to attract talent. Employer must submit application to Uruguay XXI first, then individual initiates online residency process and pays fees, then appointment is scheduled at National Immigration Directorate. Two tracks: MERCOSUR countries (Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Venezuela, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, Suriname) and non-MERCOSUR countries. Provisional identity card can be obtained in 20 business days, with same working rights as nationals. Contact: fast-track@uruguayxxi.gub.uy.

fastTrack.name: Uzbekistan
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign investors who have made an investment of USD 3 million or more in Uzbekistan
fastTrack.notes: 3-year investor visa for foreign investors. Confirmed on Embassy of Uzbekistan in the United States official site.

fastTrack.name: Vietnam
fastTrack.program_name: Special Visa Exemption Card (SVEC) for Highly Skilled Professionals
fastTrack.eligibility: Top-tier foreign talent including: scholars, scientists, university professors, digital technology experts with prestigious international awards; corporate executives from world's top 100 companies by market capitalization; cultural/artistic/sports figures with recognized global influence; elite athletes ranked global top 100; investors and honorary consuls. Must be nominated/invited by a Vietnamese government body or approved institution. Individual self-applications are not accepted.
fastTrack.notes: Established under Decree 221/2025/ND-CP issued August 8, 2025. Card valid up to 5 years, multiple-entry, each stay up to 90 days. Available in physical and digital formats. Not open to freelancers or typical digital nomads.

fastTrack.name: Zambia
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals employed in Zambia by government, private sector, NGOs, or religious organizations for a period exceeding 6 months. Requires employer (or practicing lawyer/immigration consultant) to apply on behalf of the expatriate. Applicant must remain outside Zambia until permit is approved.
fastTrack.notes: Valid up to 10 years (extendable). Holder must observe conditions on permitted area and nature of employment. Holder of an Employment Permit cannot buy land. After 10 consecutive years, holder may apply for Residence Permit (permanent). Requires local newspaper advertisements in two leading newspapers and a succession/training plan for knowledge transfer.

fastTrack.name: Zambia
fastTrack.eligibility: Business visitors intending to remain in Zambia for more than 30 days. Validity shall not exceed 6 months within any 12-month period.
fastTrack.notes: Requires covering letter from the institution doing business with applicant and completed application form (Form 25).

fastTrack.name: Zimbabwe
fastTrack.eligibility: Foreign nationals offered employment by a Zimbabwean employer who cannot find a suitable local candidate for the role
fastTrack.notes: The Temporary Employment Permit allows skilled foreign nationals to work in Zimbabwe. Application fee: USD 500 (non-refundable); USD 300 per dependent. Requires 15 documents including a completed I.F.5 form, contract of employment, notarized academic and professional certificates, police clearance, medical certificate, company incorporation documents, and proof of local advertisement for the role. Processing time not specified on the official page. Renewals require an application letter to the Chief Director of Immigration.

AFG.name: Tourist Visa
AFG.purpose: Issued for leisure travel and tourism purposes to Afghanistan. Requires valid passport and hotel booking confirmation.
AFG.notes: Issued based on applicant's travel purpose and supporting documents including valid passport and hotel booking confirmation. Applied for at Afghan embassies/consulates abroad.

AFG.name: Tourist e-Visa
AFG.purpose: Online single-entry tourist visa for eligible foreign nationals. Launched March 2026 via eafghans.com/e-visa portal. Confirmed by official Afghan Consulate General in Mumbai (mumbai.mfa.gov.af).
AFG.notes: Application fee ~USD 8 plus visa fee ~USD 120 (total ~USD 128). 30-day stay, 90-day validity from issue. Currently confirmed for entry at Kabul International Airport only. Explicitly unavailable for Indian citizens/residents per official Mumbai consulate listing. Full nationality eligibility list has not been published on mfa.gov.af as of June 2026. Express same-day processing reported available at additional cost.

AFG.name: Business Visa
AFG.purpose: Issued for commercial and business activities in Afghanistan. Supports validity from one month to three years.
AFG.notes: Fee range USD 40–300. Validity period from one month to three years. Requires valid business license, copy of passport, and supporting bank statements. Investors use this category: a single-entry business visa (extendable/convertible to multiple-entry in Kabul) or an on-arrival business visa via the 'Investment Desk' at Kabul International Airport (investinafghanistan.af). There is no separate investor/golden visa.

AFG.name: Work Visa (Entry Visa - Work)
AFG.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Afghanistan for employment with a registered company or organization (specialists, consultants, technicians, engineers, project managers, contract employees).
AFG.notes: Listed as 'Entry Visa Work' on official Afghan embassy fee schedules (Doha, Almaty): USD 100 for a single-entry 30-day stay (USD 150 urgent/express). Extendable or convertible to multiple-entry via the Consulate Directorate of the MFA in Kabul. Applicants must provide employer documentation and an MFA authorization reference number. A separate work permit from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (limited validity, renewed annually) is mandatory to legally work; details at investinafghanistan.af/page/coming-to-afghanistan.

AFG.name: Service Visa
AFG.purpose: Issued to holders of service passports who require diplomatic or consular access to Afghanistan. Free of charge.
AFG.notes: Exempt from fees. Validity from one month to one year. Requires official note from host country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Processed through Afghan political and consular missions abroad with MFA approval.

AFG.name: Entry Visa
AFG.purpose: Standard entry visa for foreign nationals invited by licensed companies or institutions operating in Afghanistan, or for Afghans with foreign passports married to foreign nationals who have not renounced Afghan citizenship.
AFG.notes: USD 100 fee. Three-month validity with one-month stay. Also covers Afghans with foreign passports married to foreign nationals who have not relinquished Afghan citizenship.

AFG.name: Residence Visa
AFG.purpose: For foreign nationals who need to extend their stay in Afghanistan beyond their initial visa's expiration date. Enables prolonged residency.
AFG.notes: Fee is USD 50 per month of stay. Duration from one month to one year. Available to those who originally entered on service, business, entry, student, or crew visa classifications.

AFG.name: Student Visa
AFG.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals for educational pursuits at recognized universities in Afghanistan. Based on agreements with recognized Afghan universities.
AFG.notes: Fee range USD 40–100. Three-month validity. Requires valid educational documents and enrollment at a recognized university in Afghanistan.

AFG.name: Visit Visa
AFG.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Afghanistan for specific purposes including sports competitions, exhibitions, or visiting family and acquaintances.
AFG.notes: Fee range USD 80–240. Validity three months with one to three months stay. Applied for at Afghan embassies and consulates abroad.

AFG.name: Arrival Visa
AFG.purpose: Visa on arrival issued at Kabul International Airport for foreign nationals with official organizational invitations. Requires MFA approval prior to arrival.
AFG.notes: Requires official letter from a domestic organization or official invitation from an international organization operating in Afghanistan. Issued only at Kabul International Airport with prior Ministry of Foreign Affairs approval. USD 200 fee.

AFG.name: Crew Visa
AFG.purpose: Issued to foreign aviation personnel including pilots, engineers, cabin crew, and aviation technicians traveling to Afghanistan for work within an aircraft.
AFG.notes: USD 600 fee. Six-month validity with six-month stay. Processed through Afghan political and consular missions abroad.

AFG.name: Transit Visa
AFG.purpose: For travelers passing through Afghanistan en route to their final destination. Requires valid documentation for the final destination country.
AFG.notes: Fee range USD 80–150. One-month validity with three to six days stay. Processed at Afghan political and consular missions abroad. Applicant must hold valid documentation for final destination.

AFG.name: Diplomatic Visa
AFG.purpose: Issued to diplomatic passport holders and representatives of foreign governments for official diplomatic purposes in Afghanistan.
AFG.notes: Typically exempt from fees. Processed through the Deputy of Foreigners Visas at MFA which handles issuance/extension of visas to Diplomatic and International Organizations. Distinct from Service Visa which covers service passport holders.

AGO.name: Tourism Visa (Visto de Turismo)
AGO.purpose: Recreational, sports, or cultural visits to Angola. Holders may not establish residence or engage in any paid activity.
AGO.notes: Fee is 36,600 KZ (Angolan kwanza) paid in cash at the border - no USD equivalent stated officially. Visa must be used within 60 days of issuance. Stay of up to 30 days, extendable once for an equal period. Requires valid passport (6+ months), photograph, vaccination certificate, and round-trip air ticket booking. Nationals of 98+ countries are exempt from this visa under Presidential Decree No. 189/23 of 29 September 2023. The e-visa portal (sme.gov.ao) allows online pre-authorization.

AGO.name: Short-Duration Visa (Visto de Curta Duração)
AGO.purpose: Urgent or short-term entry needs including business contacts, market research, and similar brief activities. No residence or paid employment permitted.
AGO.notes: Must be used within 72 hours of issuance. Maximum stay of 7 days, renewable once for another 7 days. Issued for urgent entry needs. No residence establishment or paid employment allowed.

AGO.name: Business/Temporary Stay Visa – Brazil Protocol (Visto Protocolo Brasil)
AGO.purpose: Market research, business meetings, investment negotiations, and board representation under the Angola-Brazil bilateral protocol. No paid activity permitted.
AGO.notes: Valid for 24 months (730 days). Maximum stay of 90 days per 12-month period; non-renewable within the same period. Processing time: 10 days. Applies to Brazilian nationals only under the Angola-Brazil bilateral protocol. Covers market researchers, business people, investors, and board members.

AGO.name: Work Visa – Long-Stay / Cape Verde Protocol (Visto de Trabalho Longa Duração – Protocolo Cabo Verde)
AGO.purpose: Long-term employment for Cape Verdean nationals under the Angola-Cape Verde bilateral agreement, covering periods of 3 to 36 months.
AGO.notes: Valid for 36 months (1080 days). Continuous stays of 3 to 36 months, extendable. Processing time: 15 working days. Applies to Cape Verdean nationals only under bilateral agreement. Short-stay variant (under 3 months): 36-month validity, multiple entries, processing 8 working days.

AGO.name: Work Visa – Long-Stay / France Protocol (Visto de Trabalho Longa Duração – Protocolo França)
AGO.purpose: Long-term employment (over 3 months) for French nationals or those working with French companies under the Angola-France bilateral agreement, including company leadership and internship roles.
AGO.notes: Valid for 36 months (1080 days). Stays of 12–36 months, extendable. Processing time: 30 business days. Requires employment contract and minimum salary of 1.5x Angola minimum wage, or 3+ years higher education qualification. Interns (VIE program or higher education students): maximum 12 months, renewable. Short-stay professionals (under 3 months): 36-month validity, multiple entries, 90 days per 180-day period, processing 8 business days. French nationals only under bilateral agreement.

AGO.name: Work Visa – Long-Stay / Portugal Protocol (Visto de Trabalho Longa Duração – Protocolo Portugal)
AGO.purpose: Long-term employment for Portuguese nationals under the Angola-Portugal bilateral protocol, covering stays of 12 to 36 months.
AGO.notes: Valid for 36 months. Stays of 12–36 months, extendable. Processing time: 30 working days; renewals: 5 working days. Portuguese nationals only under bilateral protocol. Short-term variant: 36-month validity, multiple entries, 90 days per semester, processing 8 working days. Academic, medical, sports, cultural, and scientific categories also available under same protocol with 8-working-day processing.

AGO.name: Study Visa (Visto de Estudo)
AGO.purpose: Academic studies or professional training at public or private institutions in Angola. Holders may not establish residence or engage in paid work except internship-related activities.
AGO.notes: Must be used within 60 days of issuance. Maximum stay of 1 year (365 days), renewable for equal periods until studies conclude. Multiple entries permitted. Study visa extensions can be processed at the SME portal (sme.gov.ao/ao/catalogo/actos/). No paid employment permitted except internship activities directly related to the course.

AGO.name: Medical Treatment Visa (Visto de Tratamento Médico)
AGO.purpose: Hospital or clinical treatment at public or private medical facilities in Angola. Holders may not engage in employment or establish residence.
AGO.notes: Must be used within 60 days of issuance. Maximum stay of 180 days, extendable upon justified completion of medical treatment. Multiple entries. No employment or residence establishment permitted. Medical visa extensions available via SME portal.

AGO.name: Privileged (Investor) Visa (Visto Privilegiado)
AGO.purpose: Granted to foreign investor citizens, their representatives or attorneys of investing companies, to enter and stay in Angola to implement and manage investment projects registered under Angola's Private Investment Law (Law No. 10/21 of 22 April 2021).
AGO.notes: The 'investor visa' is legally the Visto Privilegiado under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May (Legal System of Foreign Citizens). Must be used within 60 days of issuance; multiple entries; stay of up to 2 years (730 days), renewable for equal periods (extension processed in 5 working days). Processing up to 30 business days. Requires: passport (original + copy), two 4x5cm photos, proof from the National Private Investment Agency (AIPEX) on project implementation, and the Certificate of Private Investment Registration (CRIP). No minimum investment amount stated on official sources. Application via Angolan consular missions. Fee available on consultation with the consulate.

AGO.name: Diplomatic / Official / Courtesy Visa (Visto Diplomático / Oficial / de Cortesia)
AGO.purpose: For holders of diplomatic, service, special, or ordinary passports on official diplomatic visits, official government business, or courtesy calls to Angola.
AGO.notes: Must be used within 60 days of issuance. Maximum stay of 30 days, extendable to 90 days in justified cases. One or two entries standard; multiple entries possible in special circumstances. Separate from the bilateral diplomatic/service passport waiver agreements - this visa category applies where a bilateral exemption does not exist. Many nationalities holding diplomatic or service passports benefit from visa-free entry under bilateral agreements with Angola.

AGO.name: Temporary Stay Visa (Visto de Permanência Temporária)
AGO.purpose: For humanitarian reasons, religious missions, scientific research, family accompaniment of student/medical/privileged/work-visa holders, family reunification with residence-permit holders, and spouses of Angolan citizens.
AGO.notes: Legal category under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May. Must be used within 60 days of issuance; multiple entries; stay of up to 365 days, successively renewable. Processing up to 30 business days. Covers spouses of Angolan citizens and family members accompanying holders of study, medical, privileged, work or residence visas/permits. Fee available on consultation with the consulate. A CPLP-track variant exists for nationals of Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries (CPLP) member states.

AGO.name: Transit Visa (Visto de Trânsito)
AGO.purpose: For foreign citizens who must make a stopover in Angola to reach their final destination country. Does not permit residence or paid activity.
AGO.notes: Legal category under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May. Must be used within 60 days of issuance; valid for one or two entries; not renewable; maximum stay of 5 days. Minimum processing period 8 business days. Fee available on consultation with the consulate.

AGO.name: Ordinary Visa (Visto Ordinário)
AGO.purpose: For entry to handle particular/private affairs, family reasons, or business prospecting. Does not permit establishment of residence or paid employment in Angola.
AGO.notes: Legal category under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May. Must be used within 60 days of issuance; maximum stay of 30 days, extendable twice for equal periods (up to 90 days total). Under the Angola-Portugal bilateral protocol (Presidential Decree No. 240/21) it is issued single-entry with 8 business-day processing for family reasons and business prospecting. Does not permit residence or paid work. Fee depends on requested duration; available on consultation with the consulate.

AGO.name: Work Visa (Visto de Trabalho)
AGO.purpose: General work visa allowing the holder to temporarily exercise a paid professional activity in Angola in the interest of the State or on behalf of an employer. Does not permit establishment of residence.
AGO.notes: General work visa under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May, for nationalities not covered by a specific bilateral protocol (see the Cape Verde, France and Portugal protocol variants). Must be used within 60 days of issuance; multiple entries; valid until the employment contract ends. Lisbon consulate fee: EUR 235.80 standard (30 business days) or EUR 471.60 expedited (15 business days); approx. USD 255 standard. Requires an employment contract. Does not permit residence.

AGO.name: Residence Fixation Visa (Visto para Fixação de Residência)
AGO.purpose: For foreign citizens who intend to establish residence in Angola; serves as the entry visa pending the residence-authorization decision. Authorizes the holder to engage in paid professional activity.
AGO.notes: Legal category under Law No. 13/19 of 23 May. Must be used within 60 days of issuance; permits a stay of 120 days, renewable for equal periods until the final residence-authorization decision. Permits paid professional activity. Lisbon consulate fee: EUR 190.80 standard (30 business days) or EUR 238.00 expedited (15 business days); approx. USD 206 standard.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Tourism
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for holiday and leisure travel to Albania. Permits tourism activities for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
ALB.notes: Available as single, double, or multiple-entry. Maximum validity up to 5 years for multiple-entry C visas. Processing typically up to 15 working days; in exceptional circumstances up to 30 working days. Requires round-trip ticket, hotel booking, and proof of sufficient funds. Can be applied for via e-visa portal at e-visa.al. Fee based on reciprocity principles; waived for children under 6 and diplomatic passport holders.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Organised Group Tourism
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals travelling to Albania as part of an organised group invited by an Albanian tourism agency.
ALB.notes: Requires valid passports for all group members and a notarized license of the organising Albanian tourism agency. Processing up to 15 working days; exceptionally up to 30 working days.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Professional/Commercial/Business
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals conducting business meetings, commercial activities, or professional engagements in Albania for up to 90 days within a 180-day period.
ALB.notes: Requires invitation from Albanian host company, professional documentation, and business registration of the host entity. Available as single, double, or multiple-entry. Maximum validity up to 5 years for multiple-entry C visas.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Scientific/Cultural/Sports/Humanitarian
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals attending scientific, cultural, sporting, or humanitarian events in Albania.
ALB.notes: Requires invitation from Albanian host institution, accommodation proof, and proof of sufficient funds. Processing up to 15 working days; exceptionally up to 30 working days.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Official Visit
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign officials conducting official visits to Albania on behalf of their government or institution.
ALB.notes: Requires invitation from the Albanian host institution and a verbal note from the applicant's employer. Fee typically waived for diplomatic and official passport holders.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Medical Reasons
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals travelling to Albania to receive medical treatment.
ALB.notes: Requires medical diagnosis documentation, declaration from the receiving Albanian hospital or medical facility, and proof of financial means to cover treatment and stay.

ALB.name: Type A Visa - Airport Transit
ALB.purpose: Airport transit visa allowing foreign nationals to enter and remain in the international transit zone of an Albanian airport while awaiting an onward flight to a third country, without entering Albanian territory.
ALB.notes: Defined in Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners', Article 19. Grants the right to stay only in the international transit area of the airport until the onward flight departs; does not permit entry into Albania. Usually single-entry with duration matching the booked flights; may be issued multiple-entry for up to 6 months for travellers who prove a need for continuous, regular transit. Exempt from this visa: nationals already visa-free for Albania, diplomatic passport holders, aircraft crew under the Chicago Convention, and holders of a valid Albanian visa or residence permit. The countries required to obtain it are specified by Council of Ministers Decision. Fee based on reciprocity (CoM Decision 569/2018); waived for children under 6 and diplomatic passport holders.

ALB.name: Type C Visa - Transit
ALB.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals transiting through the territory of Albania en route to another country.
ALB.notes: Provided for in Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners', Article 20(4): a Type C visa issued to transit through Albanian territory, where the time of stay and validity correspond to the time required to complete the transit(s) and may not exceed 5 days. May be issued as single, double, or multiple entry. Applied for online via the official e-visa system. Processing up to 15 working days; in exceptional cases up to 30 working days.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Employment Activities (D/APU)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals who have obtained an Albanian work permit and intend to take up employment in Albania beyond 90 days.
ALB.notes: Requires a valid work permit, good character certificate, and employer invitation. Type D visas are issued for up to 1 year with a 90-day initial stay allowance, after which holders must apply for a residence permit (Unique Permit). Available as single, double, or multiple-entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Seasonal Employment (D/SP)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals undertaking seasonal employment in Albania under a fixed-term employment contract.
ALB.notes: Requires a seasonal employment contract and valid work permit. Typically issued for the duration of the seasonal contract.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Economic Activities (D/AE)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals undertaking economic activities (self-employment, entrepreneurship) in Albania.
ALB.notes: Requires work permit, good character certificate, and documentation of the planned economic activity. Holder must apply for a residence/unique permit after entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Professional Activities (D/AP)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals undertaking regulated professional activities (e.g., liberal professions) in Albania.
ALB.notes: Requires work permit, professional credentials, good character certificate, and invitation. Holder must apply for a residence/unique permit after entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Commercial Activity (D/AT)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals engaging in commercial trade activities in Albania beyond 90 days.
ALB.notes: Requires work permit, good character certificate, and commercial activity documentation. Holder must apply for a residence/unique permit after entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Study Purposes (D/ST)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals admitted to or enrolled in an educational institution in Albania for a period exceeding 90 days.
ALB.notes: Requires a document certifying registration or admission to an Albanian educational institution. Holder must apply for a student residence permit after entry. Available as single, double, or multiple-entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Family Reunion (D/BF)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals joining a family member legally residing in Albania.
ALB.notes: Requires proof of family relationship, housing documentation, and employment verification of the Albanian resident sponsor. Holder must apply for a family reunification residence permit after entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Humanitarian/Religious Activities (D/VHF)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign nationals undertaking humanitarian or religious activities in Albania under an authorised organisation.
ALB.notes: Requires organisation license, employer certificate, and motivation letter. Fee typically waived for humanitarian purposes. Holder must apply for a residence permit after entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Humanitarian Reasons (D/H)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa issued on humanitarian grounds to foreign nationals who cannot return to their country of origin due to circumstances beyond their control.
ALB.notes: Requires invitation and humanitarian motivation documentation. Fee typically waived. Holder must apply for a residence permit after entry.

ALB.name: Type D Visa - Diplomatic/Service Visa (D/DS)
ALB.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign diplomats, service passport holders, and accredited officials assigned to diplomatic missions, consular posts, or international organisations in Albania.
ALB.notes: Requires a verbal note from the sending state's foreign ministry and an invitation from the receiving Albanian institution. Fee waived. Many nationalities with bilateral diplomatic waiver agreements do not require this visa at all.

ALB.name: Unique Permit for Digital Mobile Workers (Leje Unike per Punonjesin Dixhital)
ALB.purpose: Residence permit for remote workers employed by or freelancing for companies and clients established outside Albania, allowing them to live and work remotely from Albania.
ALB.notes: Introduced under Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners'. Applicants must have a valid employment or service contract with a foreign entity and sufficient income (approximately EUR 450/month per secondary sources; not confirmed in official law text). Initial permit valid 1 year, renewable for 1 year, then extendable up to 5 years. Application submitted entirely online via e-Albania portal (service code 15146). Processing time up to 12 weeks maximum. Combines residence and work authorisation in a single biometric card. After 5 years continuous residence, eligible for permanent residency.

ALB.name: Unique Permit for Investors (Leje Unike per Investitorin)
ALB.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals making a qualifying investment in Albania, including establishing or acquiring a business with a minimum capital threshold.
ALB.notes: Based on Article 69 of Law No. 79/2021 'On Foreigners'. Minimum investment approximately 10,000,000 ALL (approx. EUR 85,000–90,000); threshold set by joint ministerial instruction and may have been updated by Law 43/2025 (unconfirmed). Requires employment of at least 5 Albanian citizens. Initial permit valid 2 years, renewable for 3 years. After 5 years continuous legal residence, eligible for permanent residency. Standard naturalisation requires 7 years.

AND.name: Règim turístic (Tourist Regime)
AND.purpose: Short-stay tourism and leisure visits to Andorra without engaging in any lucrative activity.
AND.notes: Andorra does not issue its own tourist visa. EU/EEA nationals enter with national ID card or passport, no visa needed. Third-country nationals who require a Schengen visa must hold a double/multiple-entry Schengen visa; Andorra itself imposes no additional tourist visa. Maximum stay is 90 days within any 365-day period (Art. 15, Qualified Immigration Law). Work is strictly prohibited during tourist stay.

AND.name: Autorització de treball temporal de fronterer (Temporary/Seasonal Cross-border Worker Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals residing outside Andorra to work in Andorra temporarily (seasonal) on a cross-border commuting basis, sleeping habitually outside Andorran territory.
AND.notes: Procedure G.2. Applicant must maintain legal residence outside Andorra and sleep habitually outside Andorran territory. Duration adjusted to a predetermined season of the year (e.g. winter ski/hospitality season). Requires a fixed-term contract with a company legally constituted in Andorra. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96. The permanent (non-seasonal) cross-border worker is a separate authorization (procedure C.1). Art. 24-25 of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització d'immigració temporal (Temporary Immigration Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside and work in Andorra temporarily in a designated economic sector.
AND.notes: Procedure G.1. Duration up to 12 months; non-renewable (mandatory waiting period before a subsequent temporary authorization). Specific labor activity in a designated sector required. Requires an employment contract with an Andorran employer compliant with labor law and minimum wage. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96. Art. 26 of the Qualified Immigration Law as amended.

AND.name: Autorització d'immigració temporal per a joves amb opció de treball (Young Persons with Work Option)
AND.purpose: Temporary authorization for young foreign nationals to gain professional experience and training while working in Andorra.
AND.notes: Procedure G.3. Targets young workers under a specified age limit. Government issuance fee EUR 22.61. This is the immigration work-permit route for young workers; a separate bilateral Work & Holiday mobility programme (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) also exists for nationals of partner countries. Art. 26 bis of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització d'immigració temporal per a treballadors d'empreses estrangeres (Foreign Company Workers Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows employees of foreign companies (EU, EFTA, or G7 registered) to provide services in Andorra temporarily.
AND.notes: Procedure H.2 (assignments over 30 days). Eligible companies must be registered in EU, EFTA, or G7 countries. Duration up to 12 months; exceptions for public interest projects may exceed this. Valid health/accident insurance coverage required. For assignments up to 30 days per year use the short-duration work notification (procedure H.1). Government issuance fee EUR 190.96. Art. 27 of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència i treball (Residence and Work Authorization)
AND.purpose: Full residence and work authorization for foreign nationals with permanent and effective employment in Andorra.
AND.notes: Procedure A.1 (initial); A.2 (renewal). Subject to the annual immigration quota. First authorization valid 1 year, then renewable. Requires permanent and effective employment in Andorra with an Andorran employer. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96 (initial), EUR 22.61 (renewal). Art. 28 of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de treball sense residència (Work Without Residence Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to work for a company legally constituted in Andorra while residing abroad, without establishing residence in Andorra.
AND.notes: Procedure I.1 (initial); I.2 (renewal). Authorizes working from abroad for a company legally constituted in Andorra, residing abroad throughout the period. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96 (initial), EUR 22.61 (renewal). Added by modified immigration law 16/2013 (Art. 28 bis of the Qualified Immigration Law).

AND.name: Autorització de residència i treball per compte propi (Self-Employment Residence and Work Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to establish a self-employed business or professional activity in Andorra.
AND.notes: Procedure J.1 (initial); J.2 (renewal); a prior reservation of the authorization (procedure J) is required. Foreign investment authorization required. Minimum capital participation of 34% in the Andorran entity. Non-refundable AFA contribution of EUR 50,000 (plus EUR 12,000 per dependent). Must reside at least 183 days per year. Professional authorization and professional association registration mandatory for regulated professions. Reservation period of 6 months. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96, separate from the AFA contribution. Art. 28 ter of the Qualified Immigration Law as amended by Llei 2/2026.

AND.name: Autorització de contractació en origen (Origin Country Recruitment Authorization)
AND.purpose: Facilitates collective recruitment of workers in their home countries for employment in Andorra.
AND.notes: Collective contract processing in workers' home countries. Internal transfers allowed within a company group if all entities are identified. Fee: €190.96. Specific procedures established by government regulation.

AND.name: Autorització de residència i treball del personal dels centres d'ensenyament (Educational Institution Personnel Authorization)
AND.purpose: Residence and work authorization for teachers and administrative staff at recognized educational institutions in Andorra.
AND.notes: Procedure E.1 (initial); E.2 (renewal). Renewable authorization. Requires employment contract at a recognized educational center. Covers both teachers and administrators (Art. 29 of the Qualified Immigration Law).

AND.name: Autorització d'immigració per a estudis, pràctiques formatives, entrenaments esportius d'alt nivell o recerca (Study, Internship, Sports Training or Research Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Andorra for studies, internships, high-level sports training, or research activities.
AND.notes: Procedure F (initial); F.1 (renewal). Duration corresponds to the academic year with possibility of extension. Requires enrollment proof, sufficient economic means, and accommodation documentation. Limited part-time work permitted within specified hours. Covers studies, internships, high-level sports training, and research activities (Art. 30 of the Qualified Immigration Law).

AND.name: Autorització de residència per ingrés en centres geriàtrics o establiments de cures mèdiques o terapèutiques privats (Geriatric/Medical Care Center Residency Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Andorra while enrolled in a private geriatric center or medical/therapeutic facility.
AND.notes: Renewable authorization. Requires proof of enrollment in a recognized private care facility and documentation of payment for facility fees. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96 (initial), EUR 22.61 (renewal). Added by modified immigration law 16/2013 (Art. 30 bis of the Qualified Immigration Law).

AND.name: Autorització de residència per raons de reagrupament familiar (Family Reunification Authorization)
AND.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to join family members who are legally resident in Andorra.
AND.notes: Procedure B.1 (initial); B.2 (renewal). Eligible sponsors: Andorran nationals and foreign residents with a residence and work authorization. Eligible family members: spouse, children, and dependent parents. Spouse and children of working residents gain work authorization; other family members on a case-by-case basis. Government issuance fee EUR 22.61. Renewable; duration linked to the sponsor's authorization (Art. 31 and 107-111 of the Qualified Immigration Law).

AND.name: Autorització de residència sense activitat lucrativa (Residence Without Lucrative Activity)
AND.purpose: Passive residency for financially self-sufficient foreign nationals who wish to reside in Andorra without engaging in any economic activity.
AND.notes: Procedure D.1 (initial); D.2 (renewal). Minimum investment of EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets (real estate, corporate shares, debt instruments, collective investment funds, public debt, life insurance, or non-remunerated AFA deposits). Reduced to EUR 400,000 if directed to the Andorran Housing Fund. Non-refundable AFA contribution of EUR 50,000 for the principal applicant plus EUR 12,000 per dependent (made non-refundable by Llei 2/2026). Separate government issuance fee EUR 3,000 (initial) and EUR 500 (renewal). Investment must be completed within 6 months (extendable by 6 months). Minimum stay: 90 days per calendar year. Work/business activity not permitted. Initial authorization valid 2 years; first renewal 2 years; second renewal 3 years; subsequent renewals 10 years. Requires health screening by Immigration Medical Service and private health/disability insurance covering 100% of expenses in Andorra. Art. 32 and 95-97 of the Qualified Immigration Law as amended by Llei 2/2026 and Regulation R20251112A.

AND.name: Autorització de residència per a professionals amb projecció internacional (Residency for Professionals with International Projection)
AND.purpose: Residency authorization for recognized professionals, executives, and entrepreneurs whose activity generates at least 85% of income or work outside Andorra.
AND.notes: For professionals and entrepreneurs with an international client base; at least 85% of income/work must come from outside Andorra. Requires establishing or acquiring an Andorran company (minimum 34% shareholding). Non-refundable AFA contribution of €50,000 plus €12,000 per dependent. Investment of €1,000,000 in Andorran assets required (post-Llei 2/2026). Minimum stay: 90 days per year. Duration: 2-year initial; renewals at 2, 3, then 10 years. Art. 33 and 98-99 of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència per a persones d'interès científic, cultural i esportiu (Scientific, Cultural, and Sports Interest Authorization)
AND.purpose: Residency authorization for internationally recognized researchers, artists, and professional athletes whose presence is of special interest to Andorra.
AND.notes: Requires demonstrable international prestige in the respective scientific, cultural, or sports field. Renewable. Art. 33 and 100-101 of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència per a nòmada digital (Digital Nomad Residency Authorization)
AND.purpose: Residency authorization for remote workers employed by foreign companies or self-employed serving exclusively non-Andorran clients, working via telecommunications from Andorra.
AND.notes: Introduced by Llei 42/2022 del 1 de desembre (Digital Economy, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Law). Annual quota: 50 permits for digital nomads, with a combined ceiling of 100 shared with the entrepreneurship program. Eligible for employees of foreign employers or self-employed workers serving non-Andorran clients only. No local Andorran clients or employers permitted. No requirement to incorporate an Andorran entity. Exempt from the €50,000 AFA non-refundable contribution. Private health and disability insurance required. Minimum stay: 90 days per calendar year. Initial authorization 2 years; first renewal 2 years; second renewal 3 years; subsequent renewals 10 years. Art. 33 bis and 101 quater-quinquies of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència per a participants en el programa d'emprenedoria (Entrepreneur Program Residency Authorization)
AND.purpose: Residency authorization for entrepreneurs participating in the government's official entrepreneurship and innovation program.
AND.notes: Governed by Llei 42/2022. Requires prior authorization from the Ministry in charge of the economy. Annual quota of 50 permits; combined ceiling of 100 shared with the digital nomad category. Exempt from the €50,000 AFA contribution if the business project is validated by a government-recognized entity under digital economy/innovation/technological entrepreneurship criteria. Art. 33 ter and 101 sexies-septies of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència i treball per a víctimes de tràfic d'éssers humans (Post-Trafficking Residence and Work Authorization)
AND.purpose: Temporary residence and work authorization for victims of human trafficking during and after their recovery period.
AND.notes: Humanitarian protection category. Added by anti-trafficking law 9/2017. Available to human trafficking victims after their protection/reflection period. Duration follows the recovery period. Art. 28 quater of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència i treball per a protecció temporal (Temporary Protection Residence and Work Authorization)
AND.purpose: Temporary residence and work authorization for beneficiaries of humanitarian protection in Andorra.
AND.notes: Added by humanitarian protection law 4/2018. For persons granted temporary protection status. Duration is transitional and temporary. Art. 28 quinquies of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Autorització de residència per a persones dependents (Dependent Persons Residency Authorization)
AND.purpose: Residency authorization for economically dependent family members of principal authorization holders in Andorra.
AND.notes: Duration linked to the sponsor/principal authorization holder's permit. Requires documentation of economic dependency and family relationship. Additional financial requirements apply: principal must demonstrate 300% of annual minimum salary plus 100% per dependent. Government issuance fee EUR 1,000 for the dependent (resident a càrrec). Art. 91 of the Qualified Immigration Law and Regulation R20251112A.

AND.name: Treball de fronterer (Cross-border/Frontier Worker Authorization)
AND.purpose: Permanent cross-border work: allows foreign nationals to work in Andorra on an ongoing basis while residing and sleeping habitually outside Andorran territory.
AND.notes: Procedure C.1 (initial); C.2 (renewal). Authorizes permanent work in Andorra during the authorization period, but the holder must sleep habitually outside Andorran territory (typically commuters from Spain or France). Requires an employment contract with a company legally constituted in Andorra. First authorization 1 year, renewable. Government issuance fee EUR 190.96 (initial), EUR 22.61 (renewal). Distinct from the seasonal/temporary cross-border worker (procedure G.2). Art. 24-25 of the Qualified Immigration Law.

AND.name: Programa de mobilitat per a joves Work & Holiday (Work and Holiday Mobility Programme)
AND.purpose: Bilateral youth mobility programme letting young nationals of partner countries live, work and travel in Andorra for a cultural and professional experience.
AND.notes: Administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (not the Immigration Service). Open to nationals aged 18-30 of partner countries listed on the official page: Canada, Ireland, Germany, United Kingdom, Republic of Korea and Iceland (the application form additionally lists Norway and Malta). Applications accepted year-round via an online form; selection is first-come, first-served. Contact: consulars@govern.ad, +376 875 704. This is the traveller-facing Work & Holiday route; the related immigration work-permit for young workers is procedure G.3.

ARE.name: Tourist Visa - 30 Days Single Entry
ARE.notes: Applied online via ICP portal or through UAE airlines/hotels. Valid 60 days from issue; 30-day stay from entry. Extendable once for 30 days (fee applies). Some nationalities receive visa on arrival free of charge.

ARE.name: Tourist Visa - 60 Days Single Entry
ARE.notes: Applied via ICP portal, airlines, or authorized travel agents. Valid 60 days from issue; 60-day maximum stay. Extendable.

ARE.name: 5-Year Multiple Entry Tourist Visa
ARE.purpose: Repeated tourism and short visits over 5 years
ARE.notes: Maximum 90 days per visit. 5-year validity from date of issue. Available to eligible nationalities. Applied via ICP portal.

ARE.name: Employment Visa / Work Permit
ARE.notes: Employer-sponsored. Requires job offer from UAE-registered employer. MOHRE work permit + ICP residence visa. Initial 2-year validity, renewable. Fee varies by emirate and employer type.

ARE.name: Remote Work / Digital Nomad Visa
ARE.purpose: Working remotely for overseas employer while residing in UAE
ARE.notes: 1-year renewable visa for employees of foreign companies earning min USD 3,500/month net. Must show employment contract, 3-month bank statements, health insurance. Applied via remotework.ae. Covers freelancers and company employees. Dubai-specific program.

ARE.name: Golden Visa (Long-term Residence)
ARE.purpose: Long-term residence for investors, entrepreneurs, skilled professionals, students
ARE.notes: 10-year renewable residence visa. Categories: investors (AED 2M+ real estate or AED 2M+ company capital), entrepreneurs (startup founders with approved project), specialized talents (doctors, scientists, athletes, artists, inventors), outstanding students (GPA 3.8+). No UAE sponsor required. Self-sponsored. Issued by ICP via online portal.

ARE.name: Retirement Visa - 5 Years
ARE.notes: For retirees aged 55+. Requirements: monthly income of AED 20,000+, or savings of AED 1M+, or UAE property worth AED 2M+. Renewable 5-year visa. Issued through ICP portal. No sponsor required.

ARE.name: Visit Visa to Explore Investment Opportunities
ARE.purpose: Investors and entrepreneurs entering to explore business/investment opportunities without a UAE sponsor or host
ARE.notes: Single-entry visit visa available in 60, 90 or 120-day validity options; no sponsor/host required. Applicant must be financially solvent, talented or highly qualified and a professional in their field, and meet prescribed financial guarantees. Applied via ICP (federal) or GDRFA-Dubai portals.

ARE.name: Jobseeker Visit Visa
ARE.purpose: Foreigners entering to search for employment without needing a host or sponsor
ARE.notes: Single-entry visit visa for one trip, in 60, 90 or 120-day validity options; no sponsor required. Eligibility: hold a bachelor's degree and be classified in MOHRE skill levels 1-3, or be a graduate of a top-500 world university within the last 2 years, plus meet prescribed financial guarantees.

ARE.name: Student Residence Visa
ARE.purpose: Foreign students enrolled at a UAE-accredited university or college
ARE.notes: Issued for one year at a time, renewable on proof of continued study. Sponsored either by a UAE-resident parent or by the accredited university/college. Outstanding students may instead qualify for a long-term Golden visa. Requires a study-duration certificate from the institution and a medical fitness test.

ARE.name: Family (Dependent) Residence Visa
ARE.purpose: Residents and citizens sponsoring spouse, children and parents to reside in the UAE
ARE.notes: Expatriate residents may sponsor spouse, unmarried daughters, sons under 25 and children with special needs, subject to a minimum salary of AED 4,000 (or AED 3,000 plus accommodation). Green visa holders may sponsor first-degree relatives. UAE citizens may sponsor spouse, parents and children (5-year visa). Dependent visas are tied to the sponsor's residence permit; sponsored members aged 18+ must pass a medical fitness test.

ARE.name: Medical Treatment Entry Permit (Patient and Companion)
ARE.purpose: Foreign patients entering for medical treatment under a licensed UAE hospital's sponsorship, plus an accompanying companion
ARE.notes: Sponsored by a hospital licensed and registered in the UAE; a financial-security deposit is required. Available as single or multiple entry for 90 or 180 days (Dubai/GDRFA); single-entry permit requires entry within 60 days of issue and allows a 90-day stay, extendable once with a certified medical report. A companion may obtain a matching permit and must enter with the patient. ICP covers Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah.

ARE.name: Transit Visa (48 / 96 hours)
ARE.purpose: Travellers passing through the UAE who wish to leave the airport during a layover
ARE.notes: Issued for either 48 or 96 hours; single entry and non-extendable. Sponsored by a UAE-based airline (e.g. Emirates or Etihad) and must be processed and approved before entering the UAE. The 48-hour transit visa is free of charge while the 96-hour transit visa carries a nominal fee.

ARE.name: Green Visa (5-Year Self-Sponsored Residence)
ARE.purpose: Skilled workers, freelancers/self-employed professionals and investors residing without an employer sponsor
ARE.notes: 5-year renewable self-sponsored residence permit; holder needs no in-country sponsor and may sponsor spouse and children. Categories: skilled workers (valid contract, bachelor's degree, MOHRE skill levels 1-3, salary AED 15,000+/month); freelancers/self-employed (freelance permit, bachelor's degree or specialised diploma, annual income at least AED 360,000 over the past two years); and investors/partners (proof of investment or partnership and required licences). Applied via ICP Smart Services or GDRFA-Dubai.

ARE.name: Blue Visa (10-Year Residence for Environmental Contributors)
ARE.purpose: Individuals who have made an exceptional contribution to environmental protection and sustainability
ARE.notes: 10-year renewable residence visa with no in-country sponsor required, for supporters of environmental action inside or outside the UAE - members of international organisations and companies, associations and NGOs, global award winners, and distinguished environmental activists and researchers. Launched at the World Governments Summit 2025; applications open to eligible applicants directly with ICP or via nomination by competent UAE authorities.

ARG.name: Tourist Visa (Visa de Turista)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals whose nationality requires a visa to enter Argentina as tourists. Permits leisure travel, family visits, and short-stay tourism.
ARG.notes: Required only for nationalities not covered by Argentina's visa exemption list. Many nationalities (Canada, USA, EU, Australia, etc.) enter visa-free for up to 90 days.
