Fee approximately USD 50 per the national consular transitory-visa fee schedule; exact amount may vary by nationality and reciprocity. Application submitted to Argentine consulate or embassy in country of residence.

ARG.name: Transitory Business Visa (Visa de Negocios Transitoria)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting short-term business activities in Argentina, such as commercial negotiations, market studies, meetings, and business representation.
ARG.notes: Permits business activities but not paid employment in Argentina. Separate from the temporary work visa categories. Applicable to nationals requiring a visa. Fee approximately USD 100 per the national consular transitory-visa fee schedule.

ARG.name: Transitory Visa for Technicians, Professionals and Artists
ARG.purpose: For foreign technicians, professionals, and artists performing short-term skilled work or artistic activities in Argentina for up to 30 days.
ARG.notes: Short-term work authorization for technicians, professionals, and performing artists (up to 1 month). Fee approximately USD 100 per the national consular transitory-visa fee schedule (USD 50 where the activity is religious). For longer-term work, the Temporary Work Visa (23E or 23A) applies.

ARG.name: Temporary Work Visa – Intra-Company Transfer (Category 23E / Personal de Traslado)
ARG.purpose: For foreign employees transferred intra-company to work in Argentina under a multinational corporate arrangement.
ARG.notes: Category 23E under Argentine immigration law. Fee is USD 250 (USD 150 base + USD 100 supplemental). Requires PIM (Entry Permit / Permiso de Ingreso) from DNM, valid RENURE, apostilled police clearance with Spanish translation, company incorporation certificate, work authorization document. Stay duration as per Entry Permit. Multiple entry. 60-day travel insurance required.

ARG.name: Temporary Work Visa – Migrant Worker (Category 23A / Trabajador Migrante)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals who have obtained a work contract in Argentina and wish to reside and work there on a temporary basis.
ARG.notes: Category 23A under Argentine immigration law. Fee is USD 250 (USD 150 base + USD 100 supplemental). Requires original notarized and legalized work contract (Contrato de Trabajo), PIM from DNM, apostilled police clearance with Spanish translation, and travel insurance. Stay duration as per Entry Permit. Multiple entry.

ARG.name: Transitory Student Visa (Visa de Estudiante Transitoria)
ARG.purpose: For foreign students enrolled in academic programs, exchange programs, internships, scholarships, or cultural exchange activities in Argentina for up to 12 months.
ARG.notes: Covers full-time students, international mobility students, cultural exchange volunteers, exchange program participants, interns, and scholarship holders per Directive 2802/2023. Valid up to 12 months (2 years for official education system). Requires PRECARGA / RENURE registration from Argentine educational institution, apostilled police clearance (for stays over 6 months if applicant is over 16), university acceptance letter, and proof of financial means. Application recommended at least 45 days before travel. Consular interview required after documentation approval.

ARG.name: Temporary Student Visa (Category 23J)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals pursuing long-term academic studies at Argentine universities or tertiary institutions requiring a full temporary residence classification.
ARG.notes: Category 23J under Argentine immigration law. Fee is USD 250 (USD 150 base + USD 100 supplemental). Requires university acceptance letter with syllabus, academic certificates, PRECARGA from university, 6 months bank statements, sponsor details with income tax returns (3 years), and travel insurance covering full stay. Stay duration as per Entry Permit. Multiple entry.

ARG.name: Digital Nomad Transitional Residence (Residencia Transitoria como Nómada Digital)
ARG.purpose: For foreign remote workers who provide services via digital or telecommunications means to clients or companies domiciled abroad, allowing extended stays in Argentina.
ARG.notes: Established by DNM Disposition No. 758/2022. Available to nationals of countries that do not require a tourist visa to enter Argentina. Duration: 180 days, renewable once for an additional 180 days (total up to 12 months). Requires signed application, CV, proof of remote work activity (contracts, company endorsement, income receipts), and at least one professional reference. In-person application only; not available via the RADEX online system. Includes perks such as discounts on transportation, hotels, coworking spaces, and cultural activities. Standard migration fee applies.

ARG.name: Seaman Visa (Visa de Marinero)
ARG.purpose: For maritime seafarers visiting Argentine ports as part of their employment aboard a vessel.
ARG.notes: Free of charge. Maximum stay is 10 days. Stamp validity up to 3 months. Two pathways: (1) E-Visa processed entirely by Argentina's Immigration Authority without consulate involvement; (2) Sticker Visa processed at the consulate. Sticker visa requires 14 documents including Spanish invitation letter from Argentine shipping company, Permiso de Ingreso from Immigration, original employment contract, and Seaman's book (CDC). For crew members on active maritime duties only.

ARG.name: Transitory Religious Visa (Visa Religiosa Transitoria)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals invited by a religious congregation in Argentina to participate in religious activities or missions.
ARG.notes: Requires invitation letter from Argentine congregation certified by Argentina's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Maximum stay up to 30 days, multiple entry. Stamp validity up to 3 months. Fee: USD 200. Requires cover letter on congregation's letterhead, Spanish translation, round-trip flight tickets (dummy acceptable), hotel reservation (dummy acceptable), and travel insurance covering entire stay.

ARG.name: Temporary Religious Visa (Category 23G)
ARG.purpose: For foreign religious workers assigned to serve with a religious congregation in Argentina on a longer-term basis.
ARG.notes: Category 23G under Argentine immigration law. Fee is USD 150. Requires apostilled police clearance with Spanish translation, congregation letterhead letter, flight reservations, and 60-day travel insurance. Stay up to 1 year, multiple entry.

ARG.name: AVE – Electronic Travel Authorization (Autorización de Viaje Electrónica)
ARG.purpose: An electronic travel authorization (e-visa equivalent) that allows foreign nationals who hold a valid US visa or ESTA to enter Argentina without applying for a full consular visa.
ARG.notes: Available to any nationality that would otherwise require an Argentine consular visa, provided they hold a valid US visa (B2, J, B1, O, P (P1-P2-P3), E, or H-1B) with at least 110 days remaining validity, or a current ESTA, or have had at least one US entry within the past 2 years. Cost: USD 400. Processed in 20 business days by National Directorate of Migrations. For tourism purposes only. Payment receipt does not guarantee entry - approval email required before travel. One 90-day extension available in-country. Indian, Chinese (PRC), and Dominican Republic nationals with qualifying US credentials may be exempt from the AVE fee entirely under 2025 resolutions.

ARG.name: Temporary Residence as Investor (Residencia Temporaria como Inversionista)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals making a qualifying productive, commercial, or service investment in Argentina, granting temporary residence leading to permanent residence.
ARG.notes: Minimum investment of ARS 1,500,000 in a productive, commercial, or service activity (amount subject to inflation erosion; verify current threshold with official source). Temporary residence granted for 1 year, renewable up to 3 years. After 2 years of residence and maintaining investment, holders become eligible for citizenship; at year 3 eligible for permanent residency. Separate tracks for MERCOSUR and non-MERCOSUR nationals. No sector restriction.

ARG.name: Temporary Residence as Rentista / Pensionado (Passive Income Residence)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals with regular passive income from abroad (pensions, annuities, dividends, rents) who wish to reside in Argentina.
ARG.notes: For foreign nationals with regular passive income from abroad such as pensions, annuities, dividends, or rental income. Temporary residence for up to 2 years, renewable. Specific minimum income amount not publicly confirmed on official page. Path to permanent residency after 3 years, citizenship after 2 years of residence.

ARG.name: Citizenship by Investment (Ciudadanía por Inversión - Decreto 524/2025)
ARG.purpose: Direct citizenship grant for foreign nationals making a 'relevant' investment in Argentina, as defined by the Ministry of Economy, with no prior residency requirement.
ARG.notes: Established by Decreto 524/2025, signed by President Javier Milei on July 30, 2025. Amends Citizenship Law No. 346 by adding Article 2° bis. No prior residency required. Minimum investment threshold and eligible sectors deferred to Ministry of Economy regulation - not yet published as of research date. Processing: 30 business days from receipt of Agency report by the National Directorate of Migration. Security clearance required from Ministry of Security, UIF (financial intelligence unit), and SIDE (intelligence agency). Applications submitted to the Agency for Citizenship by Investment Programs under the Ministry of Economy.

ARG.name: Diplomatic / Official / Service Passport Visa Exemption
ARG.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from eligible countries on official missions to Argentina.
ARG.notes: Holders of diplomatic, official, and service passports from a broad list of countries are exempt from visa requirements for official missions. Exempt countries include Albania, Algeria, Andorra, Angola, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Austria, Barbados, Belarus, Belize, Belgium, Bolivia, Botswana, Brazil, Bulgaria, Chile, China (up to 30 days), Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cuba, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Egypt, El Salvador, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Holy See, Honduras, Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Iceland, Israel, Italy, Jamaica, Japan, Kazakhstan, Korea, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Malta, S.M.O. of Malta, Macedonia, Mexico, Monaco, Montenegro, Morocco, Mozambique, Netherlands, New Zealand, Nicaragua, Norway, Pakistan, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russia, Saint Lucia, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, San Marino, Serbia, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, Suriname, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, UAE, United Kingdom, Uruguay, Vatican, Venezuela, and Vietnam. China limited to 30 days. UN Laissez-Passer holders require a visa regardless of nationality.

ARG.name: MERCOSUR Nationality Visa (Visa por Nacionalidad MERCOSUR)
ARG.purpose: Facilitates temporary establishment in Argentina for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associate states under the MERCOSUR Residency Agreement framework.
ARG.notes: Available to nationals of MERCOSUR member or associate states: Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Peru, and Suriname. Provides temporary establishment for up to 2 years. Requires valid passport (6+ months validity, 2 blank pages), photographs, application form, proof of address, certificate of good conduct (age 16+), and consular fee (USD/EUR 200 equivalent). Consular interview required.

ARG.name: Transit Visa (Visa de Tránsito / Pasajero en Tránsito)
ARG.purpose: For visa-required foreign nationals passing through Argentine territory with the sole purpose of continuing their journey to another country.
ARG.notes: Transitory visa for passengers travelling through Argentina en route to another State. Maximum stay up to 10 days; the National Directorate of Migration may grant one extension of up to 10 additional days. Fee approximately USD 20 per the national consular transitory-visa fee schedule. No visa is required if the traveller departs within 12 hours of arrival, holds an onward ticket, is declared a transit passenger by the carrier, and remains airside.

ARG.name: Transitory Seasonal Worker Visa (Trabajador Migrante Estacional)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Argentina to perform work that by its nature depends on seasonal conditions and is carried out only during part of the year (e.g. harvests).
ARG.notes: Transitory work category for seasonal activities. Duration up to 3 months. Requires an original labour agreement signed with an Argentine employer, notarized and legalized, stating the employer's valid RENURE registration number with the National Directorate of Migration. Fee approximately USD 50 per the national consular transitory-visa fee schedule.

ARG.name: Temporary Residence by Family Reunification (Residencia Temporaria por Reunificación Familiar)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals who are the spouse, parent, or child of an Argentine citizen or of a person holding permanent or temporary residence in Argentina.
ARG.notes: Granted for up to 3 years (matching the sponsor's authorized period if the sponsor holds temporary residence), with multiple entries and exits. Applicant must be within Argentine territory and apply online through the National Directorate of Migration's RaDEX system. Requires a legalized or apostilled birth/marriage certificate proving the family bond plus the sponsoring relative's identity documents. Leads toward permanent residence.

ARG.name: Temporary Residence as a Patient Under Medical Treatment (Residencia por Tratamiento Médico)
ARG.purpose: For foreign nationals who must remain in Argentina to undergo medical treatment at a public or private health facility, and for an accompanying relative or guardian where required.
ARG.notes: Granted for 1 year, renewable for the duration of the treatment. Requires a clinical history documenting the pathology and treatment plan, signed by the public hospital director or, for a private institution, with the treating professional's signature certified by the Ministry of Health. For minors, disabled, or seriously ill patients, an accompanying immediate family member, legal representative, or guardian may also be authorized. Applied online via the RaDEX system.

ARG.name: Work and Holiday Visa (Programa Work and Holiday)
ARG.purpose: For young citizens of partner countries to holiday in Argentina for up to about a year, with employment being incidental to the trip and short study permitted.
ARG.notes: Bilateral Work & Holiday agreements are in force with Australia, Denmark, France, Germany, Ireland, Netherlands, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, and Sweden; annual quotas vary by country and several (Denmark, Germany, Sweden) are uncapped. Generally for applicants aged 18-30 (extended to 35 for Ireland). Multiple entries permitted. Exact terms vary by agreement (e.g. Ireland: up to 9 months' stay, work up to 6 months renewable a further 3 months, study up to 3 months). Applied in person at the Argentine consulate with a compulsory interview; one-time participation only. Not available through the online RADEX system.

ARM.name: Visitor Visa (up to 21 days, single entry)
ARM.purpose: Short-term visit to Armenia for tourism, personal, or business purposes. Covers stays not exceeding 21 days.
ARM.notes: AMD 3,000 / USD 8 / EUR 7. Available via e-visa system (evisa.mfa.am, 3 working days processing) or in-person at Armenian diplomatic missions (10 working days). Fee is non-refundable. Armenia does not issue visas on arrival at border checkpoints.

ARM.name: Visitor Visa (up to 120 days, single entry)
ARM.purpose: Extended short-term visit to Armenia for tourism, personal, or business purposes. Covers stays up to 120 days.
ARM.notes: AMD 15,000 / USD 39 / EUR 34. Available via e-visa system (evisa.mfa.am, 3 working days processing) or in-person at Armenian diplomatic missions (10 working days). Fee is non-refundable. Visa may be extended by up to 60 days inside Armenia.

ARM.name: Multiple Entry Visitor Visa (60 days stay / 6-month validity)
ARM.purpose: Multiple-entry visitor visa for frequent travelers to Armenia for tourism or business. Allows cumulative stays of up to 60 days within a 6-month validity window.
ARM.notes: AMD 20,000 / USD 52 / EUR 46. Available via e-visa system (evisa.mfa.am) or diplomatic missions. Fee is non-refundable. Armenia uses a unified 'visitor visa' category for both tourism and business purposes.

ARM.name: Multiple Entry Visitor Visa (120 days stay / 1-year validity)
ARM.purpose: Long-term multiple-entry visitor visa for frequent travelers to Armenia for tourism or business. Allows cumulative stays of up to 120 days within a 1-year validity window.
ARM.notes: AMD 40,000 / USD 103 / EUR 91. Available via e-visa system (evisa.mfa.am) or diplomatic missions. Fee is non-refundable. Armenia uses a unified 'visitor visa' category for both tourism and business purposes. No separate work, student, or digital nomad visa categories exist in the official fee schedule.

ARM.name: Single Entry Transit Visa
ARM.purpose: Allows a single transit through Armenian territory en route to a third country.
ARM.notes: AMD 10,000 / USD 26 / EUR 23. Available via e-visa system (evisa.mfa.am) or diplomatic missions. Fee is non-refundable.

ARM.name: Multiple Entry Transit Visa (1-year validity)
ARM.purpose: Allows multiple transits through Armenian territory over a 1-year period, for frequent travelers passing through Armenia.
ARM.notes: AMD 18,000 / USD 47 / EUR 41. Available via e-visa system (evisa.mfa.am) or diplomatic missions. Fee is non-refundable.

ARM.name: Official Visa
ARM.purpose: Issued free of charge to holders of official/service passports traveling on official government business.
ARM.notes: Free of charge. Issued at Armenian diplomatic missions. Many countries have bilateral agreements for visa-free access for official/service passport holders - see conditional_access.

ARM.name: Diplomatic Visa
ARM.purpose: Issued free of charge to holders of diplomatic passports traveling on diplomatic mission.
ARM.notes: Free of charge. Issued at Armenian diplomatic missions. Many countries have bilateral agreements for visa-free access for diplomatic passport holders - see conditional_access.

ATG.name: Visa Exemption (Visa-Free Entry)
ATG.purpose: Short-stay tourism or visit for nationals of exempt countries without requiring a prior visa. Covers leisure, visiting family/friends, and short business visits.
ATG.notes: Nationals of EU countries, Commonwealth countries, and other listed countries (100+ total) are exempt from visa requirements. Standard max stay is 180 days (6 months). OECS nationals (Dominica, Grenada, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines) enjoy indefinite stay rights. China and Cuba are limited to 30 days per official footnote. A valid passport, return/onward ticket, accommodation confirmation, and proof of sufficient funds are required.

ATG.name: Visa on Arrival (VoA)
ATG.purpose: Single-entry tourist visa granted at port of entry for holders of valid US, Canadian, UK, or Schengen visas or residence permits who would otherwise require a visa.
ATG.notes: Available to any ordinary passport holder who holds a valid US visa, US Permanent Resident Card (Green Card), Canadian visa, Canadian Permanent Resident Card, UK visa or Resident Card, or Schengen visa or Resident Card. Fee is US$100 per passenger including children, or equivalent Eastern Caribbean Currency. Non-extendable and non-convertible except in medical emergencies. Not applicable to diplomatic or official passport holders.

ATG.name: eVisa (Electronic Visa)
ATG.purpose: Pre-travel visa for nationals not exempt from visa requirements, applied for online before travel for tourism, business visits, or other short-stay purposes.
ATG.notes: All visa applications are processed online via the official eVisa portal at https://evisa.immigration.gov.ag/agEvisa-app/. Processing time is approximately 5 working days (non-guaranteed). An approval or denial letter is sent once processed. A soft or hard copy of the eVisa should be carried when travelling. Immigration officers at ports of entry reserve the right to deny entry even to eVisa holders.

ATG.name: Business Visa (eVisa)
ATG.purpose: Allows foreign nationals not exempt from visa requirements to enter Antigua and Barbuda for business meetings, conferences, and short-term commercial activities.
ATG.notes: Applied for through the eVisa portal. Nationals from exempt countries do not need a visa for business visits up to 180 days. Specific fee for business category not publicly listed on official pages fetched.

ATG.name: Citizenship by Investment - National Development Fund (NDF)
ATG.purpose: Grants full Antigua and Barbuda citizenship to qualifying investors who make a non-refundable contribution to the National Development Fund.
ATG.notes: Minimum contribution US$230,000 (non-refundable) to the NDF. Additional fees: processing US$10,000 (single) or US$20,000 (family up to 4); due diligence US$8,500 (principal), US$5,000 (spouse), free (child 0-11), US$2,000 (child 12-17), US$4,000 (adult dependent 18+); passport US$300/person. Physical residency requirement: 30 days within the first 5 years. Mandatory interview required. Restricted nationalities from Afghanistan, Iran, North Korea, Somalia, Yemen, Sudan face additional scrutiny. Applications via licensed agents only.

ATG.name: Citizenship by Investment - Real Estate
ATG.purpose: Grants full Antigua and Barbuda citizenship to qualifying investors who purchase approved real estate at a minimum value.
ATG.notes: Minimum real estate purchase of US$300,000 in an approved project. Property cannot be re-sold until 5 years after purchase unless an alternative approved real estate is purchased. Same processing, due diligence, and passport fee structure as NDF option. Physical residency: 30 days within first 5 years. Mandatory interview required.

ATG.name: Citizenship by Investment - Business Investment
ATG.purpose: Grants full Antigua and Barbuda citizenship to qualifying investors who invest in an approved business.
ATG.notes: Single applicant: minimum US$1,500,000 in an approved business. Joint investment (minimum 2 persons): total US$5,000,000 with each person contributing at least US$400,000. Business must receive prior CIU approval. fee_usd reflects single applicant minimum. Same processing, due diligence, and passport fee structure. Physical residency: 30 days within first 5 years. Mandatory interview required.

ATG.name: Citizenship by Investment - UWI Fund
ATG.purpose: Grants full Antigua and Barbuda citizenship to qualifying investors who contribute to the University of the West Indies Fund, including a scholarship benefit.
ATG.notes: Minimum US$260,000 contribution (processing fees included) for a family of 6 or more. One family member receives a one-year tuition-only scholarship at UWI. Families of 7+ incur an additional US$10,000 per additional dependent. Available only to families of 6 or more. Physical residency: 30 days within first 5 years. Mandatory interview required.

ATG.name: Permanent Residence Scheme (Tax Residency)
ATG.purpose: Allows high-net-worth individuals to obtain permanent residency in Antigua and Barbuda in exchange for a flat annual tax payment, targeting retirees and wealthy individuals seeking tax residency.
ATG.notes: Introduced 1995. Requirements: minimum annual income of US$100,000 demonstrated; flat annual tax payment of US$20,000; minimum physical presence of 30 days per year in Antigua and Barbuda. fee_usd reflects the annual flat tax. Not a citizenship program. Details sourced from reference to the scheme on immigration.gov.ag/general-services/residency/; PDF could not be fetched directly.

ATG.name: Standard Resident Permit (Class A)
ATG.purpose: Grants residence to a foreign national who has been lawfully and continuously resident in Antigua and Barbuda for at least 4 years, typically after holding successive uninterrupted work permits.
ATG.notes: Class A resident permit for persons lawfully and continuously resident in Antigua and Barbuda for at least 4 years (the official Resident Permit category table lists Class A as the route for work-permit holders after 4 years). If applying via work permits, there must have been at least four consecutive uninterrupted work permits, and a valid work permit at the time of application. Marriage to a citizen is instead the separate Class B route (1 year). Resident permits are granted for 1 to 3 years at a time and the holder must reside in-country at least half of the validity period. Eligible to apply for citizenship after 7 years of lawful residence. Standard immigration residency route; not an investment program.

ATG.name: Nomad Digital Residence (NDR) Programme
ATG.purpose: Formerly allowed remote workers and digital nomads to legally reside in Antigua and Barbuda for up to 2 years while working for employers or clients outside the country.
ATG.notes: DISCONTINUED effective November 15, 2025. No new applications accepted. Previously required: remote work capability, demonstrated minimum annual income of US$50,000 for each year of the 2-year stay, valid medical insurance, police clearance. Fees were US$1,500 (single), US$2,000 (couple), US$3,000 (family of 3+). Granted special-resident authorisation for up to 2 years with income tax exemption on foreign-sourced income. fee_usd reflects the historical single-applicant fee.

ATG.name: Work Permit
ATG.purpose: Authorises a foreign national to be employed by a specific named employer in Antigua and Barbuda. Required for virtually all non-citizens who wish to work lawfully.
ATG.notes: Granted by the Labour Department under Section F (Work Permit Division, s.F5) of the Antigua and Barbuda Labour Code; the Immigration Department then endorses the permit in the passport. Employer-driven: the prospective employer must complete the Second Schedule of the application, evidence that the post was advertised locally, and show that no qualified citizen is available. A work-permit holder remains a 'bona fide visitor' with no right of abode and cannot automatically bring dependants. As of a February 2026 Cabinet policy, approvals are centralised with a mandatory 14-day local advertising period and a stated 21-day target processing time. Fee is not published on the official application form. CARICOM Skills Certificate holders and OECS Protocol State nationals may be exempt from the work-permit requirement.

ATG.name: Student Residence Permit (Class C)
ATG.purpose: Allows a foreign national to reside in Antigua and Barbuda while enrolled at a tertiary or other educational institution.
ATG.notes: Class C resident permit. Granted for one (1) year at a time (or the remaining known duration of studies) and is always temporary. Requirements: school acceptance letter, school report (after one year of attendance), proof of accommodation, a notarised sponsorship letter, a letter of financial support, passport, police certificate of character, health certificate and proof of insurance. Students are NOT permitted to work while holding this status. It cannot be converted to a Class A permanent residence permit while the purpose of stay remains study; after 4 continuous years, or on marriage to a citizen, other residence grounds may apply.

ATG.name: Residence Permit - Spouse of a Citizen (Class B)
ATG.purpose: Grants residence to the foreign spouse of a citizen of Antigua and Barbuda.
ATG.notes: Class B resident permit, available after one (1) year of marriage to a citizen of Antigua and Barbuda. Requirements: marriage certificate, applicant accompanied by spouse, proof of spouse's citizenship, passport, police certificate of character, health certificate and proof of insurance. Resident permits are granted for 1 to 3 years at a time. A spouse present as a bona fide visitor still requires an extension of stay until residence is granted. Eligible to apply for citizenship after 7 years of lawful residence.

ATG.name: Residence Permit - Home Owner / Retired Resident (Class E)
ATG.purpose: Residence route for retirees and property owners who wish to settle in Antigua and Barbuda outside the investment-migration and flat-tax schemes.
ATG.notes: Class E resident permit for home owners and retired residents, with a 2-year qualifying residency requirement per the official Resident Permit category table. Distinct from the Permanent Residence Scheme flat-tax programme (which requires US$100,000 minimum income and a US$20,000 annual tax) and from Citizenship by Investment. Resident permits are granted for 1 to 3 years at a time and the holder must reside in-country at least half of the validity period. Eligible to apply for citizenship after 7 years of lawful residence.

ATG.name: Visitor Entry Permit Extension (Extension of Stay)
ATG.purpose: Allows a bona fide visitor already admitted at a port of entry to extend their permitted stay beyond the period stamped on arrival.
ATG.notes: Granted by the Immigration Department's Extensions Unit under the Immigration and Passport Act 2014. Application must be made in person (children included) at least one week before the current permit expires. Under the Act the maximum single extension is 90 days; the general Entry Requirements page separately describes further extensions 'not exceeding six months' at the Chief Immigration Officer's discretion. Requirements: passport valid 6+ months, completed extension form (available online), a sponsorship form, a valid return/onward ticket, and proof of medical insurance. There is no unqualified right to an extension, and a visitor cannot work on an entry permit or extension - a separate work permit is required.

AUS.name: Visitor Visa (subclass 600)
AUS.purpose: Tourism, visiting family, or business visitor activities
AUS.notes: Applied for online via ImmiAccount. Tourist Stream, Business Visitor Stream, Sponsored Family Stream and Frequent Traveller Stream. Stay is typically up to 3 months per visit; some grants allow 6 or 12 months. Base charge for the Tourist stream applied outside Australia is AUD 250 from 1 July 2026 (onshore Tourist stream is around AUD 630).

AUS.name: eVisitor (subclass 651)
AUS.purpose: Short tourism or business visitor trips for eligible European passport holders
AUS.notes: Free online visa for eligible European passport holders (EU member states plus Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, UK British Citizens, Vatican). No visa application charge. Multiple entries within 12-month validity, up to 3 months per visit. Cannot work but may do business visitor activities.

AUS.name: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601)
AUS.purpose: Short tourism or business visitor trips for eligible non-European passport holders
AUS.notes: For eligible passport holders (e.g. USA, Canada, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Malaysia, Hong Kong SAR, Brunei, Taiwan ordinary passports, UK BNO). No visa application charge but an AUD 20 service fee applies when applying via the official Australian ETA app. Multiple entries within 12-month validity, up to 3 months per visit.

AUS.name: Visitor Visa (subclass 600) - Business Visitor Stream
AUS.purpose: Short business visits: meetings, conferences, negotiations, exploratory business
AUS.notes: Business Visitor stream of the subclass 600 Visitor visa. For short business visits such as attending conferences, negotiations or exploratory visits - not for working or being employed in Australia. Stay usually up to 3 months. Base charge AUD 250 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Student Visa (subclass 500)
AUS.purpose: Full-time study in a registered (CRICOS) course
AUS.notes: Requires a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) from a CRICOS-registered institution. Can work up to 48 hours per fortnight while course is in session. Base visa application charge is AUD 2,500 from 1 July 2026 (was AUD 2,000 from 1 July 2025, AUD 1,600 from 1 July 2024).

AUS.name: Temporary Graduate Visa (subclass 485)
AUS.purpose: Post-study work in Australia after graduating from an eligible course
AUS.notes: For recent international graduates. Post-Vocational Education Work stream and Post-Higher Education Work stream (plus a Second Post-Higher Education Work stream). Stay length varies by qualification (roughly 18 months to several years). Base charge AUD 5,750 from 1 July 2026 (up from AUD 4,600).

AUS.name: Skills in Demand Visa (subclass 482)
AUS.purpose: Working in a nominated occupation for an approved sponsor
AUS.notes: Replaced the Temporary Skill Shortage (TSS) visa on 7 December 2024, keeping the 482 subclass number. Requires an approved Australian sponsor. Three streams: Specialist Skills, Core Skills and Labour Agreement. Granted for up to 4 years. Base charge for the Core Skills stream is around AUD 4,015 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Employer Nomination Scheme Visa (subclass 186)
AUS.purpose: Permanent residence for skilled workers nominated by an Australian employer
AUS.notes: Permanent employer-sponsored visa. Direct Entry stream, Temporary Residence Transition stream and Labour Agreement stream. Requires nomination by an approved Australian employer. Base visa application charge around AUD 6,140 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Skilled Nominated Visa (subclass 190)
AUS.purpose: Permanent residence for skilled workers nominated by a state or territory
AUS.notes: Points-tested permanent visa. Requires an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list, a positive skills assessment, nomination by an Australian state or territory government, and an invitation via SkillSelect. Base charge around AUD 6,140 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) Visa (subclass 491)
AUS.purpose: Provisional 5-year visa to live and work in regional Australia, with a PR pathway
AUS.notes: Points-tested provisional visa valid for 5 years. Requires nomination by a state/territory government or sponsorship by an eligible relative living in a designated regional area. Holder must live, work and study in regional Australia. Pathway to the Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191). Base charge around AUD 6,140 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Training Visa (subclass 407)
AUS.purpose: Workplace-based occupational training or professional development
AUS.notes: For occupational training to improve skills for a job, area of study or field of expertise, or a professional development program. Requires an approved sponsor. Stay of up to 2 years. Base charge around AUD 535 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Temporary Activity Visa (subclass 408)
AUS.purpose: Short-term specific work or activities (events, entertainment, sport, research, religious)
AUS.notes: For specific short-term work or activities: invited by an organisation, entertainment industry, sporting activities, religious work, research, staff exchange, high-quality/superyacht crew, etc. Requires a sponsor or invitation. Stay length depends on the activity. Base charge around AUD 535 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Working Holiday Visa (subclass 417 / 462)
AUS.purpose: Holiday and short-term work for young people (age 18-30, or 18-35 for select nationalities)
AUS.notes: Subclass 417 (Working Holiday) is for passport holders of countries such as Ireland, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and South Korea. Subclass 462 (Work and Holiday) covers the USA, China, Thailand and others. Can be extended to a second and third year by completing specified regional work. Base charge AUD 840 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Partner Visa (apply in Australia) (subclass 820/801)
AUS.purpose: Spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible NZ citizen (onshore)
AUS.notes: Two-stage onshore partner visa: temporary (subclass 820) then permanent (subclass 801), applied for together. Applicant must be in Australia. A single base application charge (around AUD 11,710 from 1 July 2026) covers both stages; a reduced charge applies to former Prospective Marriage (subclass 300) visa holders.

AUS.name: Partner Visa (apply overseas) (subclass 309/100)
AUS.purpose: Spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible NZ citizen (offshore)
AUS.notes: Two-stage offshore partner visa: provisional (subclass 309) then permanent (subclass 100), applied for together. Applicant must be outside Australia when the provisional visa is granted. Single base application charge around AUD 11,710 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Prospective Marriage Visa (subclass 300)
AUS.purpose: Fiance(e) of an Australian citizen or permanent resident, to enter Australia and marry
AUS.notes: Temporary visa allowing the holder to enter Australia to marry their prospective spouse; the marriage must take place while the visa is valid (within 9 months of grant), after which the holder can apply for a Partner visa. Base application charge around AUD 11,710 from 1 July 2026.

AUS.name: Medical Treatment Visa (subclass 602)
AUS.purpose: Temporary stay for medical treatment or to support someone receiving treatment
AUS.notes: For people needing medical treatment or consultations in Australia, an organ donor, or a carer supporting a patient. Stay length is tied to the treatment. No visa application charge when applying from outside Australia; onshore applications attract a charge (around AUD 325).

AUS.name: Transit Visa (subclass 771)
AUS.purpose: Transiting through Australia by air to a third country
AUS.notes: Free visa allowing stay of up to 72 hours to transit Australia. Requires a confirmed onward booking to a third country within 72 hours and valid entry documents for the onward destination. No visa application charge.

AUS.name: Investor Retirement Visa (subclass 405) - Note: closed to new applicants
AUS.purpose: Retired investors (no longer available for new applicants since 2018)
AUS.notes: Closed to new applications. Existing visa holders may remain. Australia currently has no open dedicated retirement visa and no digital nomad / remote work visa.

AUT.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Visa C)
AUT.purpose: Tourism, visiting family/friends, or short business trips without employment. Permits travel throughout the Schengen Area.
AUT.notes: Fee is €90 (~USD 99); €45 for ages 6–12. Maximum 90 days within any 180-day period. Requires valid passport, travel insurance (min. €30,000), proof of financial means, and return commitment. Apply at Austrian embassy/consulate in country of residence. Processing typically 15 calendar days; up to 45 days if additional checks needed.

AUT.name: Airport Transit Visa (Visa A)
AUT.purpose: Permits passage through the international transit zone of Austrian airports without entering the Schengen Area.
AUT.notes: Required only for nationals of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, DRC, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Sri Lanka, and Syria. Exempt if holder has valid Schengen/Irish/US/Canadian/Japanese visa or qualifying residence permit. Standard Schengen visa fee (€90) applies.

AUT.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Visa C) – Business
AUT.purpose: Attending business meetings, conferences, or negotiations in Austria without taking up employment.
AUT.notes: Same Visa C category as tourist visa but with business purpose stated in application. Fee €90. No separate category for business short-stay; purpose is declared on application form.

AUT.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Visa D)
AUT.purpose: Permits extended stays in Austria from 91 days up to 6 months, typically as a precursor to obtaining a residence permit.
AUT.notes: Fee is €195 (~USD 215); €97 for children under 6. Cannot be extended in Austria. Stays beyond 6 months require a residence permit. Issued for one or multiple entries; exceptionally valid up to 12 months. Used as entry permit to then collect residence permit in Austria.

AUT.name: Job Seeker Visa (Jobsuchvisum)
AUT.purpose: Allows highly qualified third-country nationals to enter Austria for up to 6 months to seek employment, without the right to work during this period.
AUT.notes: Six-month Visa D category. Employment is strictly prohibited during the validity period. Intended for highly qualified workers who then apply for a Red-White-Red Card once they secure a job offer.

AUT.name: Red-White-Red Card (Rot-Weiß-Rot-Karte)
AUT.purpose: Points-based settlement permit granting the right to live and work in Austria for qualified third-country nationals including very highly qualified workers, skilled workers in shortage occupations, self-employed key workers, and start-up founders.
AUT.notes: Valid for 24 months, employer-tied for most categories. AMS (Public Employment Service) reviews macroeconomic benefit within 3 weeks. After 24 months (min. 21 months in employment), eligible for Red-White-Red Card Plus (unrestricted labor market access). Sub-categories: Very Highly Qualified Workers (min. 70 pts), Shortage Occupation Workers, Self-Employed Key Workers (min. €100,000 capital transfer or equivalent benefit), Start-up Founders (min. €30,000 capital, min. 50 pts). No specific USD fee published on official source.

AUT.name: EU Blue Card Austria (EU-Blaue Karte)
AUT.purpose: Residence and work permit for third-country nationals with a university degree and qualifying job offer, implementing the EU Blue Card Directive in Austria.
AUT.notes: Fee is €218 (~USD 240). Requires university degree (minimum 3-year program) or, for ICT professionals/service managers, 3 years comparable experience in the last 7 years; a binding job offer for at least 6 months; and salary at least equal to the average gross annual income for full-time employees (in 2026: at least €55,678 gross annual incl. special payments). Card issued for 24 months. After 21 months of employment, eligible for Red-White-Red Card Plus. Labor market test applies.

AUT.name: Intra-Corporate Transfer Permit (ICT)
AUT.purpose: Temporary residence and work permit for third-country nationals transferred within a multinational company to an Austrian entity as managers, specialists, or trainee employees.
AUT.notes: Implements EU ICT Directive. Covers managers, specialists, and trainees. Mobile ICT variant available for movement within multiple EU member states. Must demonstrate active employment relationship with the sending entity and temporary assignment to Austrian host entity.

AUT.name: Student Residence Permit (Aufenthaltsbewilligung Studierender)
AUT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Austria for the duration of their studies at accredited universities, polytechnics, or private institutions.
AUT.notes: Requires proof of enrollment at an accredited Austrian institution, adequate financial means (approx. €1,308/month), and health insurance. Students may work up to 20 hours per week without a separate labor market test. After graduation, permit can be extended for 12 months to seek employment or start a business.

AUT.name: Pupil Residence Permit (Aufenthaltsbewilligung Schüler)
AUT.purpose: Allows third-country national minors to reside in Austria to attend primary or secondary school.
AUT.notes: For pupils enrolled in Austrian primary or secondary schools. Requires proof of enrollment, health insurance, and proof of adequate means of subsistence.

AUT.name: Researcher Mobility Permit
AUT.purpose: Temporary residence permit for third-country national researchers to carry out research activities at an approved Austrian research organisation.
AUT.notes: Implements EU Researcher Directive. Requires hosting agreement with an approved Austrian research organisation. Family members may accompany. Mobile researcher provisions allow activity across EU member states.

AUT.name: Family Reunification Visa / Permit
AUT.purpose: Allows eligible family members (spouses, minor children) of third-country nationals with valid Austrian residence permits to join them in Austria.
AUT.notes: Fee is €260 (~USD 286); €130 for children under 6. For family members of asylum-status holders, different rules apply. Sponsors must demonstrate adequate financial means and appropriate housing. EU/EEA family members are governed by EU Freedom of Movement rules, not this permit.

AUT.name: Working Holiday Visa / Permit
AUT.purpose: Allows young nationals of partner countries to holiday in Austria and supplement their travel costs through incidental work or vocational training.
AUT.notes: Available to nationals of 12 bilateral partner countries: Argentina, Australia, Canada, Chile, Hong Kong, India, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Taiwan, and United States. Age requirement: 18–30 years. Primary purpose must be holiday; work is secondary and incidental. Apply at the Austrian embassy/consulate of partner country. Exact duration, quota, and fees vary by bilateral agreement.

AUT.name: Social Service Employee / Volunteer Permit
AUT.purpose: Temporary residence permit for third-country nationals performing social service or voluntary work (including European Voluntary Service) in Austria.
AUT.notes: Maximum 1 year, non-renewable. Must be placed with an approved social service organisation or European Voluntary Service programme.

AUT.name: Au Pair Residence Permit
AUT.purpose: Allows young third-country nationals to live with an Austrian host family and assist with childcare and household tasks while improving language and cultural skills.
AUT.notes: Categorised under special cases of dependent employment. Requires a formal au pair placement agreement with an approved host family. Specific age limits, duration, and pocket money requirements governed by Austrian law.

AUT.name: Red-White-Red Card Plus (Rot-Weiß-Rot-Karte plus)
AUT.purpose: Settlement permit granting unlimited (non-employer-tied) access to the Austrian labour market for holders transitioning from a Red-White-Red Card or EU Blue Card, family members of settled foreigners, and certain other settled third-country nationals.
AUT.notes: Fee is €218 (~USD 240). Distinct card from the Red-White-Red Card: grants unlimited labour-market access (employed or self-employed, not tied to one employer). Typically issued after 21 of the last 24 months in qualifying employment on a Red-White-Red Card or EU Blue Card, or to family members. Valid for 12 months; those lawfully settled 2+ years who meet Integration Agreement Module requirements may receive a card valid for 3 years.

AUT.name: Settlement Permit – Gainful Employment Excepted (Niederlassungsbewilligung ausgenommen Erwerbstätigkeit)
AUT.purpose: Settlement permit for pensioners and financially self-sufficient third-country nationals who wish to reside in Austria without taking up any gainful employment.
AUT.notes: Fee is €218 (~USD 240). Subject to an annual quota (Niederlassungsverordnung) and often heavily oversubscribed. No employment of any kind is permitted. Requires proof of secure fixed income; 2026 minimum monthly means: €2,616.78 (single), €4,128.24 (married couple), plus €403.76 per child. Also requires adequate accommodation, comprehensive health insurance, and German language pre-integration (A1).

AUT.name: Settlement Permit – Artist (Niederlassungsbewilligung Künstler)
AUT.purpose: Settlement permit for third-country nationals pursuing self-employed or dependently employed artistic activity in Austria (e.g. musicians, performers, visual artists).
AUT.notes: For persons whose income comes predominantly from artistic activity. For dependent employment an employer declaration is required; for self-employed activity a contract and proof of artistic education/training are required. Grants settlement with labour-market access limited to the artistic activity.

AUT.name: Long-Term Resident – EU (Daueraufenthalt – EU)
AUT.purpose: EU long-term residence status for third-country nationals who have lawfully and continuously resided in Austria for at least five years, granting near-permanent settlement with full labour-market access.
AUT.notes: Fee is €275 (~USD 303). Requires five years of continuous lawful residence, completion of Integration Agreement Module 2 (B1 German), secure fixed income, accommodation, and health insurance. Grants unrestricted access to the labour market. The residence-permit document is valid for five years and is renewable; the underlying long-term-resident status itself is of unlimited duration.

AZE.name: ASAN e-Visa (Tourism)
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for tourism and leisure purposes. Issued electronically via the ASAN Visa system.
AZE.notes: State fee $20 USD (confirmed by US State Dept travel.state.gov as of June 2026; azerbaican.az lists $20 + $3 service fee). Standard processing: 3 working days; urgent processing: 3 hours (available 24/7 including holidays). Available to nationals of approximately 90+ countries as listed at evisa.gov.az/countries. Single entry, 30 days stay. Registration required within 15 days for stays exceeding 15 days.

AZE.name: ASAN e-Visa (Business)
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for business purposes including meetings, conferences, and commercial activities. Issued electronically via the ASAN Visa system.
AZE.notes: Standard processing: 3 working days; urgent processing: 3 hours. Fee $20 USD. Same ASAN Visa system as tourist e-visa; purpose is selected during application. Available to nationals eligible for Azerbaijan e-visa.

AZE.name: Transit Visa
AZE.purpose: Issued to foreigners and stateless persons to allow transit passage through the territory of Azerbaijan to a third country. Available as single or double transit visa.
AZE.notes: Validity: 30 days from date of issue; maximum stay: 5 days. Issued based on transport route (air, water, rail, road, etc.). Both single and two-entry (double) transit visas are available. Applied for at Azerbaijani diplomatic missions abroad.

AZE.name: Labor (Work) Entry Visa
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for the purpose of taking up employment. Must be combined with a work permit issued by the State Migration Service.
AZE.notes: Entry visa is issued for the 'labor' purpose. A separate work permit must be obtained from the State Migration Service. Work permit is valid for 1 year (or the duration of the employment contract if shorter); extendable for up to 1 year per extension (up to 2 years in liberated territories). Employer must demonstrate no available qualified Azerbaijani citizens. Some categories are exempt from the work permit requirement (diplomatic staff, international organization staff, highly skilled migrants, athletes, etc.).

AZE.name: Science and Education Entry Visa
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for educational or scientific purposes, including enrollment at Azerbaijani educational institutions.
AZE.notes: Issued for the 'science and education' purpose category under ordinary entry visas. Students enrolled full-time at Azerbaijani institutions are also eligible for a Temporary Residence Permit. Multi-entry variants valid up to 2 years may be available for long-term study.

AZE.name: Medical Treatment Entry Visa
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for the purpose of receiving medical treatment at Azerbaijani medical facilities.
AZE.notes: Issued under the 'treatment' purpose category of ordinary entry visas. Applicants must provide documentation from an Azerbaijani medical institution confirming the treatment.

AZE.name: Personal/Family Entry Visa
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for personal and family visits, including visiting close relatives who are Azerbaijani citizens or residents.
AZE.notes: Issued under the 'personal travel' purpose category of ordinary entry visas. Family members of Azerbaijani citizens or temporary/permanent residents may also qualify for Temporary Residence Permit. Close family relationship with an Azerbaijani citizen is one of the grounds for TRP.

AZE.name: Humanitarian/Culture/Sport Entry Visa
AZE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Azerbaijan for humanitarian, cultural, or sporting activities and events.
AZE.notes: Issued under 'humanitarian' or 'culture and sport' purpose categories of ordinary entry visas. Athletes and coaches performing in Azerbaijan may be exempt from work permit requirements.

AZE.name: Diplomatic / Service Entry Visa
AZE.purpose: Issued to foreign officials holding diplomatic or service (official/special) passports traveling to Azerbaijan for official purposes. Citizens of 79 countries with bilateral agreements may enter visa-free on these passport types.
AZE.notes: Diplomatic and service visas form a separate category from ordinary visas. Holders of diplomatic/service passports from 79 countries (Group I per MFA PDF, April 29 2026) enter visa-free for 30 or 90 days depending on the bilateral agreement. Libya temporarily suspended. For non-exempt countries, diplomatic/service visa must be obtained in advance from Azerbaijani diplomatic missions.

AZE.name: Investment-Based Temporary Residence Permit
AZE.purpose: Grants temporary residence in Azerbaijan to foreign nationals who make qualifying investments in real estate, bank deposits, government securities, or the general economy.
AZE.notes: Minimum investment thresholds (in AZN): real estate >= AZN 100,000; fixed-term bank deposit >= AZN 100,000; government or state-majority-company securities >= AZN 100,000 nominal value; or general economic investment >= AZN 500,000. Initial permit issued for up to 1 year (3 years for highly skilled migrants); extendable by up to 2 years each time. After 2 years of temporary residence, eligible to apply for permanent residence permit.

AZE.name: Highly Qualified Specialist Temporary Residence Permit
AZE.purpose: Grants temporary residence in Azerbaijan to foreign nationals who are recognized as highly qualified specialists in fields of economy, industry, military, science, culture, or sports.
AZE.notes: Initial permit for up to 3 years; extendable for up to 3 years per extension. Requires a justified application from the inviting Azerbaijani authority, enterprise, or organization. Exempt from work permit requirement. After 2 years of continuous temporary residence, eligible to apply for permanent residence.

AZE.name: Visa on Arrival - Airport Visa
AZE.purpose: Allows nationals of eligible countries to obtain a 30-day single-entry visa upon arrival at international airports of Azerbaijan without pre-applying.
AZE.notes: Available at international airports for nationals of: Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Japan (fee reportedly waived), Indonesia, Iran, China, South Korea, Malaysia, Israel, UAE, Singapore. UAE nationals with residence permits can use the conditional UAE-resident-visa VOA channel. Japanese fee reportedly waived. Several of these nationalities (Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait) are also currently visa-free under Group IV (Feb 15 2026–Feb 15 2027). US citizens on New York-Baku flights can also obtain an airport visa.

AZE.name: Visa on Arrival - UAE Resident Visa Holders
AZE.purpose: Allows holders of a valid UAE residence permit to obtain a visa at international airports of Azerbaijan without pre-applying.
AZE.notes: Conditional on holding a UAE residence permit (resident visa) with at least 6 months remaining validity. Traveler must hold a valid passport (not a travel document) valid for at least 4 months. Excludes nationals of Syria, Iraq, and Afghanistan. Issued at international airports only.

AZE.name: Multiple-Entry Ordinary Visa
AZE.purpose: Long-validity ordinary entry visa allowing several entries into Azerbaijan for business, labor, study, family or other approved purposes; issued by Azerbaijani diplomatic missions abroad rather than through the single-entry e-visa system.
AZE.notes: Per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Azerbaijan issues ordinary entry visas as either single-entry (validity up to 90 days, one entry-exit) or multiple-entry (validity up to 2 years, several entries during the period). The single-entry ASAN e-visa covers short tourist/business trips; the multiple-entry ordinary visa (validity up to 2 years) is obtained from Azerbaijani diplomatic missions and suits long-term or repeat travel. A visa has three categories: diplomatic, service, and ordinary.

AZE.name: Work Permit (Permission for Paid Labor Activity)
AZE.purpose: Authorization issued by the State Migration Service allowing a foreign national to engage in paid employment in Azerbaijan. Required in addition to the labor entry visa and applied for by the employer on the employee's behalf.
AZE.notes: Every able-bodied foreigner over 18 wishing to work for pay must hold a work permit, applied for by the employer. Valid for 1 year (or the labor contract duration if shorter); extendable for up to 1 year each time (up to 2 years in liberated territories). Employer must request extension at least 30 days before expiry. Exempt categories include permanent residents, highly skilled migrants, entrepreneurs, diplomatic and international-organization staff, and professional religious workers. Distinct from the labor (work) entry visa, which authorizes entry; the work permit authorizes employment.

AZE.name: Family-Based Temporary Residence Permit
AZE.purpose: Grants temporary residence to foreign nationals who have a close family relationship with (or are married to) an Azerbaijani citizen, or who are a family member of a foreigner lawfully residing in Azerbaijan.
AZE.notes: A statutory ground for the temporary residence permit ('Permission card for temporary residence on the territory of the Republic of Azerbaijan') is a close family relationship with an Azerbaijani citizen (including spouse) or being a family member of a foreigner already holding a residence permit. Initial permit up to 1 year; extendable up to 2 years each time. After 2 years of continuous temporary residence, eligible to apply for permanent residence.

AZE.name: Permanent Residence Permit (Immigration Permit)
AZE.purpose: Grants permanent residence status to foreign nationals who have lawfully held a temporary residence permit for at least 2 continuous years and meet a qualifying ground (family, investment, employment, entrepreneurship, etc.).
AZE.notes: Official name: 'Permission card for permanent residence on the territory of the Republic of Azerbaijan'. Requires at least 2 years of continuous temporary residence under a qualifying ground. Issued for 5 years; renewable for further 5-year periods. Grounds include close family relationship with an Azerbaijani citizen, qualifying investment, highly qualified specialist status, foreign-company branch executive positions, and entrepreneurship meeting turnover requirements.

AZE.name: Investment-Based Permanent Residence Permit
AZE.purpose: Grants permanent residence to foreign nationals who maintain a qualifying investment in Azerbaijan (real estate, bank deposit, government securities, or the general economy) and have completed at least 2 years of temporary residence.
AZE.notes: Minimum thresholds (in AZN): real estate >= AZN 200,000; fixed-term bank deposit >= AZN 200,000; government or state-majority-company securities >= AZN 200,000 nominal value; or general economic investment >= AZN 500,000. Requires at least 2 years of continuous temporary residence. Permanent permit issued for 5 years, renewable for further 5-year periods. Distinct from the investment-based temporary residence permit, which uses lower AZN 100,000 thresholds.

BDI.name: Visa de Transit (Transit Visa)
BDI.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Burundi en route to another destination. Available at all entry points.
BDI.notes: Available at all entry points including airport. Crew members of aircraft, trains, and boats are exempt from the transit visa requirement. Fee is $40 USD or equivalent in Euros.

BDI.name: Visa d'Entrée Simple (Single Entry Visa)
BDI.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Burundi for tourism, short visits, or business. Single-entry permit valid for one month.
BDI.notes: Issued online, at the international airport, and at embassies. $90 USD or equivalent. The Burundi Embassy Paris charges approximately €65 for advance applications.

BDI.name: Visa d'Entrée Multiple (Multiple Entry Visa)
BDI.purpose: For foreign nationals requiring multiple entries into Burundi. Allows re-entry up to a maximum cumulative stay of 90 days. Renewable up to two times.
BDI.notes: Base fee $90 USD for 1 month; $180 for 2 months; $270 for 3 months. Renewable maximum 2 times. Issued at CGM (Commissariat Général des Migrations), international airport, and embassies.

BDI.name: Visa de Séjour (Extended Stay Visa)
BDI.purpose: For foreign nationals who need to extend their stay beyond the expiry of their initial entry visa. Issued by CGM only.
BDI.notes: Fee: $10 for every 5 days (up to 25 days); $70 per month thereafter. Validity from 5 days up to 1 month, renewable. Available at CGM only, not at border points.

BDI.name: Visa EAC (East African Community Access Visa)
BDI.purpose: Free access visa for citizens of EAC Partner States (Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, DRC, Somalia) under the EAC Common Market Protocol Article 7(1).
BDI.notes: Valid 1 to 6 months. Free of charge. Documents required: passport/travel document photocopy, access stamp photocopy, and passport photo. Issued at CGM or entry points. Somalia joined EAC on March 4, 2024.

BDI.name: Visa CEPGL (Great Lakes Countries Access Visa)
BDI.purpose: Free access visa for citizens of CEPGL (Economic Community of the Great Lakes Countries) member states - DRC and Rwanda.
BDI.notes: Valid 1 to 3 months. Free of charge. Documents required: passport/travel document photocopy, access stamp photocopy, and passport photo. Issued at CGM or entry points.

BDI.name: Visa d'Étude EAC (EAC Study Visa)
BDI.purpose: For students from EAC member countries studying in Burundi. Free of charge under EAC Common Market Protocol.
BDI.notes: 12 months validity. Free for EAC member country students. Issued at CGM. DRC students (also CEPGL members) pay $25 USD and visa expires December 31st of the year.

BDI.name: Visa d'Établissement (Establishment Visa / Long-Stay Residence Permit)
BDI.purpose: For foreign nationals and their dependents who wish to reside and establish themselves in Burundi for an extended period of up to 2 years. This is the residence pathway used by employed foreigners after their initial entry visa.
BDI.notes: Fee: $500 USD. Valid 2 years. Issued at CGM only. Requires at least 6 months of prior residence in Burundi, a request letter approved by the Commissioner General of Migrations, passport copy, current visa copy, and passport photo. For employed foreigners (the work-residence pathway) additional documents are required per the official MAE page: a work contract (contrat de travail), service certificate (attestation de service) and engagement deed (acte d'engagement) for company employees, plus a tax identification number (NIF) and business registration (registre du commerce) for any profit-generating activity. A separate free courtesy establishment visa (2 years) and diplomatic establishment visa (3 years) also exist - see their dedicated entries.

BDI.name: Visa de Résident Permanent (Permanent Residence Visa)
BDI.purpose: For foreign nationals who qualify for indefinite residence in Burundi. Grants a 99-year permanent resident status.
BDI.notes: Fee: $1,200 USD. Valid 99 years. Issued at CGM only. Requires ministerial authorization from Ministry of Interior, letter of application, passport copy, property title, and previous establishment visas received. A free variant exists for transfer to a new passport for existing permanent residents. The MAE also describes a free 'Visa de Résident Permanent' for diplomatic/courtesy holders under the free-visa page.

BDI.name: Visa d'Établissement Diplomatique (Diplomatic Establishment Visa)
BDI.purpose: For holders of diplomatic passports seeking to establish residence in Burundi as part of an official diplomatic mission.
BDI.notes: Free of charge. Valid 3 years. Requires: note verbale from organization, letter from Ministry of Home Affairs, diplomatic passport copy, and current visa photocopy. Issued by MAE.

BDI.name: Visa Sauf-Conduit (Safe Conduct Visa)
BDI.purpose: Emergency travel document for lost passport holders and Burundian citizens who require a short-term travel document.
BDI.notes: Free of charge. Valid 1 week. Issued at CGM or entry points. Intended for lost passport holders and Burundian citizens in exceptional circumstances.

BDI.name: Permis de Travail (Work Permit)
BDI.purpose: Work authorization for foreign nationals taking up employment with a registered employer in Burundi.
BDI.notes: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs maintains a dedicated official 'Work Permit' page, confirming a distinct labour-authorization category for foreign workers separate from the residence (establishment) visa. Employment-linked foreigners also obtain a Visa d'etablissement (residence, $500, 2 years) which for employees requires a work contract, service certificate, engagement deed, tax ID (NIF) and business registration. Fee, exact validity, and number of entries are not published on the official page and are left null rather than guessed.

BDI.name: Visa Etudiant RDC (DRC Student Visa)
BDI.purpose: For students from the Democratic Republic of Congo enrolled at schools or institutions in Burundi.
BDI.notes: Listed as a distinct category on the official CGM application portal: $25 USD, annual, multiple entry. DRC is a CEPGL (Great Lakes) member; unlike the free EAC study visa, DRC students pay $25 and the visa expires on December 31st of the year of issue.

BDI.name: Visa d'Etablissement de Courtoisie (Courtesy Establishment Visa)
BDI.purpose: For staff of organizations (e.g. international organizations / NGOs) granted courtesy status to reside in Burundi, and their minor children.
BDI.notes: Free of charge, valid 2 years, per the official MAE free-visa page. Requires a note verbale from the organization addressed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, a letter from the Ministry of Interior/Home Affairs, passport copy, current visa copy, and passport photo. The MAE free-visa page also lists free transfer and certified-copy (for minor children) variants of this visa. Distinct from the Diplomatic Establishment Visa, which is reserved for diplomatic passport holders (3 years).

BEL.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourism
BEL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Belgium and other Schengen states for tourism, recreation, or visiting friends and family for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
BEL.notes: Standard Schengen C visa. Fee is EUR 90 for adults (12+), EUR 45 for children 6–12, free for children under 6. Single, double, or multiple-entry options available. Multiple-entry visas issued for 1, 2, or 5 years based on prior visa history. Valid across all 29 Schengen states. Medical travel insurance (minimum EUR 30,000 coverage) required. Must apply to country of primary destination.

BEL.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
BEL.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to enter Belgium and the Schengen area for business meetings, conferences, trade fairs, or other professional activities not amounting to employment, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
BEL.notes: Same Type C Schengen visa framework as tourism. Fee EUR 90 (adults 12+). Paid work during the stay is not permitted under this category. Declaration of arrival required within 3 working days.

BEL.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Medical Treatment
BEL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to travel to Belgium to undergo planned medical treatment at a Belgian health-care institution for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
BEL.notes: Medical treatment is an officially listed purpose/category of the Schengen Type C short-stay visa on the Belgian FPS Foreign Affairs visa pages (diplomatie.belgium.be, 'Visa C - Short stays'). Fee EUR 90 for adults (12+), EUR 45 for children 6-12, free under 6 - same as other Type C visas. Requires a medical certificate issued by the treating doctor/institution, written confirmation of the appointment at the Belgian health facility, proof that the treatment costs can be covered or have been pre-paid, and medical travel insurance with minimum EUR 30,000 coverage. Belgian embassies publish a dedicated 'Short Stay Visa - C Medical treatment' document checklist (e.g. jordan.diplomatie.belgium.be/.../visa_c_-_medical_treatment.pdf). For medical stays exceeding 90 days, or for seriously ill persons who cannot be treated in their country of origin, a separate authorisation to stay for medical reasons (Article 9ter) applies instead.

BEL.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
BEL.purpose: Allows nationals of specified countries to transit through the international transit area of a Belgian airport without entering Schengen territory.
BEL.notes: Required for nationals of approximately 25 countries including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, and others. Fee EUR 90 (adults 12+), EUR 45 (children 6–12), free for children under 6, students, researchers, and certain young non-profit representatives. Holders of valid residence permits from UK, Canada, Japan, and USA are exempt. Diplomatic and service/official passport holders from many countries are also exempt.

BEL.name: Single Permit (Combined Work and Residence Authorization)
BEL.purpose: Combined work and residence permit for third-country nationals intending to work in Belgium for more than 90 days under an employment contract.
BEL.notes: Mandatory for all non-EU workers employed more than 90 days in Belgium since 3 January 2019. Application submitted by employer through regional one-stop counter portal. Region confirms receipt within 15 days; joint decision within 4 months (extendable). If no unfavorable decision within timeframe, authorization is automatically granted. Residence validity up to 5 years; renewal required at least 2 months before A card expiry. Holder also receives a national long-stay D visa from Belgian embassy to enter Belgium.

BEL.name: EU Blue Card (Highly Qualified Worker - Single Permit B29)
BEL.purpose: Combined work and residence permit for highly qualified third-country nationals employed by a Belgian employer under a salary above a specified threshold.
BEL.notes: Identified with code B29 on visa/permit. Applied via Single Permit procedure by employer. EU Blue Card holders benefit from family reunification without proof of sufficient means and can combine EU-wide residency across Schengen states for long-term resident status (minimum 2 years in Belgium immediately before application).

BEL.name: Intra-Corporate Transfer (ICT) Permit
BEL.purpose: Permits managers, specialists, or trainee employees being transferred within a multinational enterprise to a Belgian entity for more than 90 days.
BEL.notes: Separate procedure from the standard Single Permit. Employer must apply through regional authority. Holder also requires Belgian national long-stay D visa.

BEL.name: Seasonal Worker Permit
BEL.purpose: Authorizes third-country nationals to perform seasonal work in Belgium for a limited period exceeding 90 days.
BEL.notes: Listed as a separate work authorization category by the Belgian Immigration Office. Regional authority determines eligibility and conditions. Holder also requires Belgian D visa.

BEL.name: Au Pair / Youth Work Authorization
BEL.purpose: Allows young third-country nationals to live with a host family in Belgium, participate in family life, and perform light household tasks while learning the local language and culture.
BEL.notes: Listed as 'Au pair/Youth' work category by Belgian Immigration Office. Regional authority has jurisdiction. Holder also requires Belgian D visa for stays over 90 days.

BEL.name: Trainee Work Authorization
BEL.purpose: Permits third-country national trainees to perform on-the-job training in Belgium for more than 90 days within the framework of a training agreement.
BEL.notes: Listed as 'Trainees' category by Belgian Immigration Office. Separate from the Single Permit standard procedure. Regional authority has jurisdiction.

BEL.name: Volunteer Work Authorization
BEL.purpose: Authorizes third-country nationals to carry out recognized volunteer work in Belgium for more than 90 days.
BEL.notes: Listed as 'Volunteers' category by Belgian Immigration Office. Regional authority has jurisdiction. Holder requires Belgian D visa for stays exceeding 90 days.

BEL.name: Professional Card (Self-Employed / Entrepreneur)
BEL.purpose: Authorizes third-country nationals to conduct self-employed professional or commercial activities in Belgium for more than 90 days.
BEL.notes: No fixed minimum investment amount set by federal law. Issued by the competent regional authority (Flanders, Wallonia, Brussels-Capital, or German-speaking Community). Applicant must then obtain a Belgian national long-stay D visa from the embassy/consulate. After 5 years of lawful residence, path to long-term resident status and potentially citizenship.

BEL.name: Researcher Permit (Hosting Agreement - B13)
BEL.purpose: Grants third-country national researchers the right to reside and conduct scientific research in Belgium for more than 90 days under a hosting agreement with a recognized Belgian research institution.
BEL.notes: Designated B13 on visa/permit. Requires valid hosting agreement with recognized research organization. Regional employment authority declares admissibility first; decision issued within 60 days of complete file submission. Provisional 'Annex 49' document valid 45 days (renewable) issued while awaiting A card. Long-term mobility option available for researchers already authorized in another EU member state. Holder requires Belgian national long-stay D visa.

BEL.name: Student Visa (Higher Education)
BEL.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Belgium for more than 90 days to pursue degree-level studies at a recognized Belgian higher education institution.
BEL.notes: Applies to studies leading to a degree recognized in Belgium. Holder must obtain Belgian national long-stay D visa from competent embassy/consulate before travel. Upon arrival, residence permit application made at municipal administration. Official fees not published on the IBZ page consulted.

BEL.name: Student Visa (Secondary Education)
BEL.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to reside in Belgium for more than 90 days to attend secondary school education.
BEL.notes: Separate category from higher education. Holder requires Belgian D visa for stays over 90 days. Exact fee and processing times not published on official IBZ page.

BEL.name: Orientation Year After Higher Studies
BEL.purpose: Grants a one-year extension of residence to third-country national graduates of Belgian higher education institutions to seek employment or start a business.
BEL.notes: Maximum 1 year, non-renewable as orientation year. At the end, applicant must convert to a work or entrepreneurship permit. Only available to graduates of recognized Belgian institutions.

BEL.name: Working Holiday Programme Visa
BEL.purpose: Allows young nationals of partner countries to holiday in Belgium for up to 12 months while supplementing their funds through incidental work.
BEL.notes: Eligible countries: Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Taiwan, South Korea. Age limit: 18–30 at time of application. Financial requirement: minimum EUR 2,500 plus return ticket or funds therefor. Authorization valid 12 months and cannot be renewed. Leisure must be primary purpose; work is supplementary only. Requires Belgian national long-stay D visa before travel. Travel/health insurance required. Fee amount not specified on official page.

BEL.name: Family Reunification Visa (with Belgian National)
BEL.purpose: Permits eligible family members of Belgian nationals to reside in Belgium for more than 90 days for the purpose of family reunification.
BEL.notes: Sponsor is a Belgian national. Processing time depends on nationality of the sponsoring Belgian resident. Applicant receives a national long-stay D visa and/or residence permit upon approval. Specific requirements and timelines available on IBZ sub-pages.

BEL.name: Family Reunification Visa (with EU/EEA National)
BEL.purpose: Permits eligible family members of EU or EEA nationals residing in Belgium to join them for the purpose of family reunification.
BEL.notes: Sponsor is an EU/EEA/associated country national. Governed by EU Directive 2004/38 on freedom of movement for EU citizens. Specific requirements and timelines available on IBZ sub-pages.

BEL.name: Family Reunification Visa (with Third-Country National)
BEL.purpose: Permits eligible family members of legally resident third-country nationals to join them in Belgium for the purpose of family reunification.
BEL.notes: Sponsor is a legally resident non-EU national. Stricter conditions apply including proof of stable resources and accommodation. Processing time depends on sponsor's nationality. Specific requirements on IBZ sub-pages.

BEL.name: Family Reunification Visa (with International Protection Beneficiary)
BEL.purpose: Permits family members of recognized refugees or subsidiary protection beneficiaries residing in Belgium to join them for family reunification.
BEL.notes: Sponsor holds refugee status or subsidiary protection in Belgium. Specific conditions and timelines differ from standard family reunification. Applicant receives national long-stay D visa and/or residence permit upon approval.

BEL.name: Diplomatic / Official Passport Visa Exemption
BEL.purpose: Exempts holders of diplomatic, service/official, or special passports from certain countries from the Schengen visa requirement for short stays.
BEL.notes: Applies to holders of diplomatic, service/official, and/or special passports from countries with bilateral visa waiver agreements with Belgium (or the Benelux), including Algeria, Bolivia, Cambodia, Cape Verde, China, Congo DRC, Cote d'Ivoire, Cuba, Ecuador, Egypt, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, India, Indonesia, Iran, Jamaica, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mongolia, Morocco, Oman, Pakistan, Philippines, Qatar, Senegal, South Africa, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, and others. Scope (diplomatic only vs. diplomatic+service vs. diplomatic+service+special) varies by country per EUR-Lex 52023XC0927(01) BNL column.

BEL.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D)
BEL.purpose: Belgian national visa authorizing third-country nationals to enter Belgium and take up long-term residence (more than 90 days) for purposes such as work, study, family reunification, or self-employment.
BEL.notes: All long-stay categories (work, study, family, research, self-employment, etc.) require a Type D national long-stay visa obtained from the Belgian embassy/consulate in the applicant's country of residence before travel. Upon arrival applicants register at the municipal administration and apply for a residence permit (A card or equivalent). All nationalities are subject to the D visa requirement for long stays regardless of short-stay exemption status.

BEN.name: Visa Touristique / E-Visa (Short Stay - 1 month, single entry)
BEN.purpose: Short-stay e-visa for tourism, family, business/professional or medical visits by foreign nationals not covered by a visa waiver agreement.
BEN.notes: Fee is €50 self-applied online (≈$54 USD). Also available via embassy at €60. Must be obtained before arrival - no visa on arrival.
