Available to nationals of countries outside ECOWAS and without a bilateral visa exemption agreement with Benin. Per the official DEI text the 'visa touristique ou de visite' covers family, professional, health/medical (sanitaire) and tourism purposes and is renewable for the same duration - Benin issues no separate medical or family-visit visa. Issued via the evisa.bj online portal.

BEN.name: Visa Touristique / E-Visa (Short Stay - 1 month, multiple entry)
BEN.purpose: Tourism or short visits to Benin with the flexibility of multiple entries within the 1-month validity period.
BEN.notes: Fee is €75 self-applied online (≈$81 USD). Also available via embassy at €85. Must be obtained before arrival via evisa.bj. Same 'visa touristique ou de visite' category, which officially covers family, professional, medical (sanitaire) and tourism purposes and is renewable for the same duration.

BEN.name: Visa Touristique / E-Visa (Short Stay - 3 months, multiple entry)
BEN.purpose: Extended tourism or personal visits to Benin for up to 90 days with multiple entries.
BEN.notes: Fee is €100 self-applied online (≈$108 USD). Also available via embassy at €110. Must be obtained before arrival via evisa.bj. Longest tourist/visit e-visa tier; a stay may be renewed for the same duration, and CIPE registration is required for continuous stays beyond 90 days.

BEN.name: Visa d'Affaires (Business Visa)
BEN.purpose: Visa for economic, commercial, or industrial activities in Benin.
BEN.notes: Up to 90 days of stay per entry within a 2-year validity period; renewable. Fees in EUR: 1 month (€70 / 45,916 FCFA), 3 months (€90 / 59,036 FCFA), 6 months (€120 / 78,715 FCFA), 1 year (€180 / 118,072 FCFA); bi-national rates 3 months €20, 6 months €45, 1 year €75. DEI-issued visa (service PS00407 'Visa résident'); apply and pay online at service-public.bj, then complete enrolment in person at DEI Cotonou. Estimated processing 3-7 days. Legal basis: Loi N° 2025-15 of 2 July 2025 and Décret N° 2026-049 of 4 March 2026.

BEN.name: Visa Professionnel (Professional/Work Visa)
BEN.purpose: Visa for foreigners seeking to engage in professional or employment activities in Benin.
BEN.notes: For professional activity; stay up to 12 months, renewable for the same duration. Fees in EUR: 1 month (€70 / 45,916 FCFA), 3 months (€90 / 59,036 FCFA), 6 months (€120 / 78,715 FCFA), 1 year (€180 / 118,072 FCFA); bi-national rates 3 months €20, 6 months €45, 1 year €75. DEI-issued long-stay visa (service PS00407 'Visa résident long séjour'); a written request to the DEI director is required first, then apply and pay online at service-public.bj and complete enrolment in person at DEI Cotonou. Estimated processing 3-7 days. Legal basis: Loi N° 2025-15 of 2 July 2025 and Décret N° 2026-049 of 4 March 2026.

BEN.name: Visa d'Étude (Student/Study Visa)
BEN.purpose: Visa for foreigners intending to pursue studies or training programs in Benin.
BEN.notes: For study or training; stay up to 12 months, renewable for the same duration. Fees in EUR: 1 month (€70 / 45,916 FCFA), 3 months (€90 / 59,036 FCFA), 6 months (€120 / 78,715 FCFA), 1 year (€180 / 118,072 FCFA); bi-national rates 3 months €20, 6 months €45, 1 year €75. DEI-issued long-stay visa (service PS00407 'Visa résident long séjour'); a written request to the DEI director is required first, then apply and pay online at service-public.bj and complete enrolment in person at DEI Cotonou. Estimated processing 3-7 days. Legal basis: Loi N° 2025-15 of 2 July 2025 and Décret N° 2026-049 of 4 March 2026.

BEN.name: Visa de Transit (Transit Visa)
BEN.purpose: Short-stay visa for travelers passing through Benin on the way to another destination.
BEN.notes: Maximum stay of 8 days. Applied for at DEI offices. Specific fee not listed on official DEI services page.

BEN.name: Titre de Voyage pour Réfugiés (Travel Document for Refugees)
BEN.purpose: Travel document issued to persons holding refugee status in Benin, allowing international travel except to the country of origin.
BEN.notes: Issued by DEI to recognized refugees. Valid for travel to all countries except country of origin. This is a travel document, not a standard visa type, but listed as a formal DEI service for foreign nationals.

BEN.name: Sauf-Conduit (Safe Conduct Pass)
BEN.purpose: Emergency travel document issued to foreigners in Benin who lack diplomatic representation or have lost their passport, allowing return to their country of origin.
BEN.notes: Issued by DEI to foreigners without representation or who have lost travel documents. Valid only for travel to the holder's country of origin. This is an emergency document, not a standard immigration visa.

BFA.name: Tourist Short-Stay Visa (Single Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term tourism visits to Burkina Faso. Does not permit employment without prior authorization from the minister in charge of labor.
BFA.notes: Fee is 33,000 FCFA. Hotel reservation required. Available online via applicant.visaburkina.bf, at embassies, or at the border. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver (must still apply). US citizens are banned effective 2026-01-01.

BFA.name: Tourist Short-Stay Visa (Multiple Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term tourism visits to Burkina Faso with multiple entries. Does not permit employment without prior authorization.
BFA.notes: Fee is 55,000 FCFA. Hotel reservation required. Multiple entries allowed but total stay must not exceed 90 days within validity period. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Business Short-Stay Visa (Single Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term visits to Burkina Faso for business purposes. Does not permit employment without prior authorization from the minister in charge of labor.
BFA.notes: Fee is 77,000 FCFA. Available online via applicant.visaburkina.bf, at embassies, or at the border. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver. US citizens are banned effective 2026-01-01.

BFA.name: Business Short-Stay Visa (Multiple Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term business visits to Burkina Faso with multiple entries. Does not permit employment without prior authorization.
BFA.notes: Fee is 93,500 FCFA. Multiple entries allowed but total stay must not exceed 90 days within validity period. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Conference/Studies/Training/Visit Short-Stay Visa (Single Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term visits to Burkina Faso for conferences, studies, training, or family/official visits. Does not permit employment without prior authorization.
BFA.notes: Fee is 55,000 FCFA. Covers conferences, studies (short-term), training programs, and family/official visits under the short-stay framework. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Conference/Studies/Training/Visit Short-Stay Visa (Multiple Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term visits to Burkina Faso for conferences, studies, training, or family/official visits with multiple entries.
BFA.notes: Fee is 71,500 FCFA. Multiple entries allowed but total stay must not exceed 90 days within validity period. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Cooperation Visa (Single Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term visa for cooperation-related activities in Burkina Faso, typically for NGO workers, development cooperation, and official bilateral cooperation visits.
BFA.notes: Fee is 44,000 FCFA. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Cooperation Visa (Multiple Entry)
BFA.purpose: Short-term visa with multiple entries for cooperation-related activities in Burkina Faso.
BFA.notes: Fee is 79,500 FCFA. Multiple entries allowed but total stay must not exceed 90 days within validity period. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Express Short-Stay Visa
BFA.purpose: Emergency or expedited short-stay visa for urgent travel to Burkina Faso when standard processing timelines are not feasible.
BFA.notes: Fee is 104,500 FCFA. For emergency/urgent travel situations. Entry type (single/multiple) not specified on official page. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Transit Visa
BFA.purpose: For foreigners transiting through Burkina Faso, including stops caused by transport breakdown, awaiting a connecting flight, or other force majeure circumstances.
BFA.notes: Fee is 22,000 FCFA. Single entry; validity cannot exceed five (5) days. Granted to travelers transiting through Burkina Faso (e.g. transport breakdown, awaiting a connecting flight, or force majeure at the authorities' discretion). Requires passport, application form, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, proof of reason for stay, medical certificate (no contagious disease), health insurance, and stamp-duty receipt. Available online via applicant.visaburkina.bf, at embassies, or at border immigration services. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Long-Stay Business Visa
BFA.purpose: Long-stay (more than 90 days) visa for business purposes in Burkina Faso. Does not grant the right to work without prior authorization from the minister in charge of labor.
BFA.notes: Fee is 187,000 FCFA. One of three long-stay (visa de long sejour) tiers published on visaburkina.bf. A long-stay visa is valid for more than 90 days; when issued for multiple entries the total duration of stays cannot exceed 90 days per semester. Requires passport, application form, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, proof of reason for long stay, medical certificate (no contagious disease), certificate of support in Burkina Faso or proof of sufficient income, health insurance, and stamp-duty receipt; a residence permit is required for stays beyond 90 days. Apply via applicant.visaburkina.bf or an embassy. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Long-Stay Conference/Studies/Training/Visit Visa
BFA.purpose: Long-stay (more than 90 days) visa for conferences, extended studies, training, or extended family/official visits in Burkina Faso. This is the category used by long-term students.
BFA.notes: Fee is 110,000 FCFA. One of three long-stay (visa de long sejour) tiers published on visaburkina.bf; covers extended studies, training, and academic/official visits. Valid for more than 90 days; multiple-entry total stays cannot exceed 90 days per semester. Requires passport, application form, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, proof of reason for stay, medical certificate, certificate of support or proof of sufficient income, health insurance, and stamp-duty receipt; a residence permit is required for stays beyond 90 days. Apply via applicant.visaburkina.bf or an embassy. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BFA.name: Long-Stay Cooperation Visa
BFA.purpose: Long-stay (more than 90 days) visa for cooperation-related activities in Burkina Faso, typically NGO/development-cooperation staff and official bilateral cooperation personnel.
BFA.notes: Fee is 77,000 FCFA. One of three long-stay (visa de long sejour) tiers published on visaburkina.bf; for development/cooperation personnel. Valid for more than 90 days; multiple-entry total stays cannot exceed 90 days per semester. Requires passport, application form, two 3.5x4.5 cm photos, proof of reason for stay, medical certificate, certificate of support or proof of sufficient income, health insurance, and stamp-duty receipt; a residence permit is required for stays beyond 90 days. Apply via applicant.visaburkina.bf or an embassy. As of September 2025, African AU member-state nationals receive a fee waiver.

BGD.name: Tourist Visa
BGD.purpose: For visitors travelling to Bangladesh for tourism, casual visits to friends/relatives, seminars, conferences, workshops, study tours, or religious purposes. No commercial activities permitted.
BGD.notes: Standard issuance is single entry for up to 3 months. Double and multiple-entry options available for certain nationalities at different rates. Fees vary by nationality based on reciprocity (e.g. UK £105 single, USA £146). Validity begins from date of issue, not travel date. Extension up to 1 additional month possible through Department of Immigration and Passport (DIP) in Bangladesh. Application form must be completed online, printed, and submitted physically to a Bangladesh mission.

BGD.name: Business Visa
BGD.purpose: For businesspersons visiting Bangladesh for the purpose of trade, commerce, and investment. Requires invitation from a recognised Bangladeshi business organisation.
BGD.notes: Maximum validity 1 year; maximum stay 60 days per visit. Single, double, or multiple entry options available. Extension up to 3 years (max 6-month stays per visit) obtainable from DIP. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single/double, USA £146). Online application form must be printed and submitted physically to a Bangladesh mission.

BGD.name: Work Permit / Employment Visa
BGD.purpose: For experts, advisers, and employees working in government, semi-government, autonomous bodies, or industrial/commercial organisations in Bangladesh, or conducting unpaid work with registered NGOs.
BGD.notes: Initial visa valid for maximum 3 months / 90 days. Single, double, or multiple entry options available. Extensions up to 3 years obtainable through DIP. Requires employer letter, appointment letter, contract with salary details, and Ministry/BOI/BEPZA recommendation. Work permit (separate from visa) must be applied for within 15 days of arrival through BIDA OSS; cost BDT 5,000 per year. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single, USA £146).

BGD.name: Student Visa
BGD.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled at a recognised educational institution in Bangladesh.
BGD.notes: Issued for maximum 1 year with multiple entries. Max stay per visit depends on educational institution requirements. Extension up to course tenure obtainable from DIP. Requires invitation/declaration letter from Bangladeshi educational institution and bank guarantee documents. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single, USA £146).

BGD.name: Investor Visa (P1 Visa)
BGD.purpose: For foreign investors in private sector industrial or commercial entities seeking to establish or manage businesses in Bangladesh through joint ventures or 100% foreign ownership.
BGD.notes: Also referred to as 'P1 Visa' in BIDA documentation. Issued for maximum 1 year; single, double, or multiple entries. Extensions up to 5 years obtainable from DIP. Requires BOI/BEPZA/BIDA recommendation letter. Minimum investment of USD 50,000 required for branch/liaison/representative office registration. BIDA OSS processes visa recommendations within 24 hours with complete documentation. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single, USA £146).

BGD.name: E Visa (Employee Visa via BIDA)
BGD.purpose: For employees of private or public organisations (foreign and local companies) working in Bangladesh, processed through BIDA One Stop Service.
BGD.notes: Corresponds to the official Bangladesh Employment visa category code 'E' (3 months validity, multiple entry, 90 days stay per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa-category schedule at www.bdembjp.mofa.gov.bd/public/storage/pdf/Visa-Procedure.pdf). Applied for through BIDA OSS (bidaquickserv.org) for BIDA-registered companies. Work permit must be obtained within 15 days of arrival. Fee varies by nationality; contact BIDA for company-specific requirements.

BGD.name: E1 Visa (Machinery/Software Installation Visa via BIDA)
BGD.purpose: For persons engaged with machinery and software installation, project inspection, or related technical services in Bangladesh.
BGD.notes: Corresponds to the official Bangladesh Employment visa category code 'E1' (6 months validity, multiple entry, 30 days stay per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa-category schedule at www.bdembjp.mofa.gov.bd/public/storage/pdf/Visa-Procedure.pdf) for project inspection/supervision/maintenance/setup/software supply and equipment. Processed through BIDA One Stop Service (OSS); applicants may contact BIDA at +880-2-44826795-99 or info@bida.gov.bd.

BGD.name: NGO Visa
BGD.purpose: For individuals appointed to work in NGOs registered in Bangladesh, whether paid or unpaid roles with Bureau of NGO Affairs-registered organisations.
BGD.notes: Maximum 3 months per issuance; extensions up to 3 years from DIP. Single, double, or multiple entries available. Requires NGO Affairs Bureau recommendation letter and appointment letter with full terms and salary details. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single, USA £146).

BGD.name: Research Visa
BGD.purpose: For individuals participating in research, training, or internship programs at government-approved agencies or institutions in Bangladesh.
BGD.notes: Maximum 3 months validity; extensions up to 3 years from DIP. Requires letters from both host and home institutions, and consent letter from relevant Bangladesh Ministry. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single, USA £146).

BGD.name: Journalist Visa
BGD.purpose: For foreign journalists of newspapers, magazines, TV or radio networks, or news agencies seeking to collect information or fulfill official reporting duties in Bangladesh.
BGD.notes: Maximum 1 month per issuance; extensions up to 3 years from DIP. May require additional approval from Bangladesh authority beyond standard 7 working days. Requires press card, FF-I and FF-II forms, equipment list, invitation letter, and employer letter. Fees vary by nationality (UK £105 single, USA £146).

BGD.name: Intern Visa
BGD.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking internship programs at organisations in Bangladesh.
BGD.notes: Listed as a distinct category by Bangladesh High Commission London. Specific validity, max stay, fees, and entry details not published on the official page. Contact relevant Bangladesh mission for details.

BGD.name: Family / Accompanying Family Members Visa (Visa Types: FA2, FA3, FE, FJ, FN, FP, FPI, FR, FS)
BGD.purpose: For spouses, children and dependent family members accompanying a foreign national who holds a Bangladesh Official (A2/A3), Employment (E), Journalist (J), NGO (N), Sport (P), Investor (PI), Research (R) or Student (S) visa.
BGD.notes: Dependent-family visa whose code mirrors the principal visa holder's category (FA2/FA3 for Official A2/A3, FE for Employment, FJ for Journalist, FN for NGO, FP for Sport, FPI for Investor, FR for Research, FS for Student). Requires copies of all of the spouse's/parents' documents and an original family certificate proving the relationship. Validity and duration generally track the principal visa holder's visa. Distinct from the No Visa Required (NVR) endorsement, which covers spouses/children of persons of Bangladeshi origin. Documented on the official Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs mission visa-category schedule; application filed online via visa.gov.bd and submitted to a Bangladesh mission.

BGD.name: Sport Visa (Visa Type: P)
BGD.purpose: For sports organisers, players, coaches and similar personnel travelling to Bangladesh for professional sporting duty or service.
BGD.notes: Official Bangladesh visa category code 'P'. Issued to sports organisers/players/coaches for professional duty or service, based on a recommendation letter from the concerned sports agency/organisation. Validity and duration are set on the basis of the recommendation letter. Documented on the official Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs mission visa-category schedule; application filed online via visa.gov.bd and submitted to a Bangladesh mission.

BGD.name: Tablig-Jamaat Visa
BGD.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Bangladesh to participate in Tablighi Jamaat religious congregation and activities.
BGD.notes: Single entry; maximum stay up to 130 days, with extension up to 150 days obtainable from the Department of Immigration and Passport (DIP) in Bangladesh. Validity begins from date of issue, not travel date. Requires a letter from the Central Tablig Markus in the applicant's country and a letter from the Tablig Markus of Dhaka, Bangladesh. Processing at least 7 working days (21 working days for postal applications). Fees vary by nationality (e.g. UK £105 single entry, USA £146).

BGD.name: Transit Visa
BGD.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Bangladesh en route to a third country.
BGD.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category by Bangladesh High Commission London. Specific validity period, max transit stay, fees, and entry details not accessible on the official portal pages during research. Contact relevant Bangladesh mission for details.

BGD.name: Visa on Arrival
BGD.purpose: For tourism, business, investment, or government job purposes; issued at designated ports of entry in Bangladesh to eligible nationality holders.
BGD.notes: Fee of USD 50 paid in cash at Sonali Bank PLC counter at port of entry. Eligible nationalities: US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Russia, China, Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain, Egypt, Turkey, Brunei, and all European countries. Also available to: citizens of countries with no Bangladesh embassy, foreign embassy officials and UN staff based in Bangladesh, persons of Bangladeshi origin (non-SAARC), and investors with BIDA/BEPZA investment certificate. Issuance is at the sole discretion of the immigration officer and is not guaranteed. Extension beyond 30 days possible through DIP but described as difficult.

BGD.name: Government Delegates / Diplomatic / Official Visa
BGD.purpose: For government delegates, diplomatic personnel, other embassy officials, and staff of UN or international organisations travelling to Bangladesh on official duties.
BGD.notes: Listed as distinct categories by Bangladesh High Commission London: 'Government Delegates Visa', 'Diplomatic/other Embassy officials Visa', and 'UN and other International Organizations visa'. Holders of diplomatic/official passports from approximately 32 countries may be exempt from visa requirements under bilateral agreements. Full list of bilateral visa-exemption countries is not published on a currently accessible official Bangladesh government domain.

BGR.name: Visa A – Airport Transit Visa
BGR.purpose: Permits transit through the international transit areas of Bulgarian airports without entering the Schengen territory. Required for certain nationalities transiting through Sofia Airport.
BGR.notes: Fee is EUR 90 (approx. USD 97) following the Schengen visa fee increase effective 11 June 2024 (raised from EUR 80); see European Commission notice (home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/news/schengen-visa-fee-increased-11-june-2024-2024-06-13). Only required for nationals of countries listed in Annex IV of the Schengen Visa Code (Regulation (EC) 810/2009 as amended). Must be applied for at a Bulgarian embassy or consulate in person. Processing standard is 15 calendar days; may extend to 30 days in individual cases.

BGR.name: Visa C – Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Tourist/Visit)
BGR.purpose: Permits short-term stays in Bulgaria and the Schengen Area for tourism, family visits, business meetings, cultural events, or transit. Valid for up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen member states.
BGR.notes: As of 31 March 2024, Bulgaria issues uniform Schengen visas valid throughout the entire Schengen Area. Fee is EUR 90 (approx. USD 97) following the Schengen visa fee increase effective 11 June 2024 (raised from EUR 80, per European Commission notice); reduced to EUR 45 for children aged 6–12; free for children under 6. Maximum validity is 5 years for multi-entry visas with demonstrated travel history; single and double entry options also available. Applications must be submitted in person at Bulgarian diplomatic missions or authorized Visa Application Centers (VFS Global). Applications accepted no earlier than 6 months before intended travel. Standard processing is 15 calendar days; may extend to 30 days or exceptionally 60 days. The 90-day stay limit is calculated across all Schengen states.

BGR.name: Visa C – Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Business)
BGR.purpose: Permits short-term entry for business purposes including negotiations, contract signings, conferences, and commercial visits. Issued as a Type C uniform Schengen visa.
BGR.notes: Same legal basis and fee as the tourist Type C visa: EUR 90 (approx. USD 97) since the 11 June 2024 Schengen visa fee increase (Schengen Visa Code, Regulation (EC) 810/2009 as amended). Applicant must provide an invitation letter from a Bulgarian company or proof of business purpose. Issued as a uniform Schengen visa valid for all Schengen states.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Employment
BGR.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to enter Bulgaria for the purpose of taking up employment with a Bulgarian employer. A prior work permit (issued by the Employment Agency) must be obtained before the visa is issued.
BGR.notes: Governed by the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act (Article 15). The visa is issued for up to 6 months (180 days) and allows the holder to enter Bulgaria and subsequently apply for a residence permit at the Migration Directorate (MVR). A personal interview is obligatory. The employer must first obtain a work permit from the Bulgarian National Employment Agency. EU Blue Card holders follow a slightly different procedure. After obtaining a Type D visa and entering Bulgaria, the applicant must apply for a temporary residence permit within the first month. No e-visa option exists; applications must be submitted in person.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Study
BGR.purpose: Permits foreign nationals admitted to an accredited Bulgarian educational institution to enter Bulgaria to pursue studies. Includes university degree programs, language courses, and vocational training.
BGR.notes: Issued under the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires an acceptance letter from an accredited Bulgarian institution, proof of sufficient funds, and health insurance. A personal interview is obligatory. After entering Bulgaria on a Type D study visa, students must register with the Migration Directorate (MVR) to obtain a residence permit valid for the duration of their studies. Students may work limited hours under Bulgarian labor law.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Family Reunification
BGR.purpose: Permits family members of Bulgarian citizens, EU/EEA nationals, or third-country nationals legally residing in Bulgaria to enter and reside in Bulgaria for the purpose of family reunification.
BGR.notes: Governed by the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act and implementing the EU Family Reunification Directive (2003/86/EC) for third-country national sponsors. Eligible family members include spouse, minor children, and dependent parents. A personal interview is obligatory. After entry, family members must apply for a residence permit at the Migration Directorate (MVR). Spouses of Bulgarian nationals may follow an expedited path to permanent residency.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Investment (Golden Visa path)
BGR.purpose: Permits non-EU nationals who have made qualifying investments in Bulgaria (such as EUR 512,000 in approved investment funds) to enter Bulgaria. Leads directly to permanent residency without requiring a temporary permit.
BGR.notes: Governed by Article 25, paragraph 1, point 6 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires a minimum investment of EUR 512,000 in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) or ETFs listed on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange, maintained for at least 5 years. The Invest Bulgaria Agency (investbulgaria.com) must pre-approve the investment. After approval, a Type D visa is issued to allow entry, following which permanent residency is granted directly. After 5 years of permanent residency, the investor may apply for Bulgarian citizenship by naturalization. Bulgaria's Citizenship-by-Investment (golden passport) program was abolished on 5 April 2022; this path leads to residency only, not direct citizenship.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Scientific Research / Highly Qualified Employment (EU Blue Card)
BGR.purpose: Permits third-country nationals employed in highly qualified occupations (requiring at least a bachelor's degree and a gross annual salary at least 1.5x the average Bulgarian salary) to enter Bulgaria under the EU Blue Card scheme.
BGR.notes: Implements Directive 2009/50/EC (EU Blue Card Directive) and its successor Directive (EU) 2021/1883 as transposed into Bulgarian law. The employer must apply for an EU Blue Card (combined work and residence permit) from the Migration Directorate on behalf of the foreign national. A Type D entry visa is issued to allow initial entry. Blue Card holders have enhanced mobility rights within the EU/Schengen Area after 18 months.

BGR.name: Digital Nomad Residence Permit (Type D visa + residence permit)
BGR.purpose: Permits third-country nationals who work remotely for employers or businesses registered outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland to reside in Bulgaria for up to 2 years without taking up local employment.
BGR.notes: Introduced by amendments to the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act, approved by the Bulgarian Parliament in June 2025. Implementing regulations adopted by the Council of Ministers on 10 December 2025; applications accepted from 20 December 2025. Three eligible categories: (1) employees of companies registered outside EU/EEA/Switzerland; (2) entrepreneurs/managers owning 25%+ of a company registered abroad; (3) self-employed remote workers with at least 1 year of prior remote operation. Minimum average annual income of EUR 31,000 for the prior calendar year. The initial permit is valid for 1 year, extendable once for a further year (maximum 2 years total). Holders may not work for Bulgarian companies or Bulgarian clients. Administered by the Ministry of Interior (MVR). Entry is via a Type D long-stay visa; the permit is then issued inside Bulgaria. Processing time is not officially published.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Medical Treatment
BGR.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to enter Bulgaria to undergo medical therapy or treatment at a Bulgarian medical facility, based on an approved treatment and recovery plan.
BGR.notes: Issued on the ground under Article 24, paragraph 1, point 8 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires a certificate from the treating medical facility specifying the treatment and recovery plan, proof that all transport, medical and living costs are covered, health insurance (minimum EUR 30,000 coverage), evidence of accommodation in Bulgaria and a police clearance certificate. The Type D visa (valid up to 180 days) allows entry, after which a continued-treatment residence permit is issued by the Migration Directorate (MVR). Applications are submitted in person at a Bulgarian diplomatic mission; no e-visa exists.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Pensioners (Retirement)
BGR.purpose: Permits retired foreign nationals in receipt of a state or private pension, with sufficient means to support themselves, to settle in Bulgaria.
BGR.notes: Issued on the ground under Article 24, paragraph 1, point 10 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires a document from the competent authorities of the applicant's country certifying the pension, plus a Bulgarian bank account into which the pension will be transferred. Applicant must show sufficient financial means (pension income), accommodation in Bulgaria and health insurance (minimum EUR 30,000). The Type D visa (valid up to 180 days) allows entry, after which a renewable long-term (1-year) residence permit is issued by the Migration Directorate (MVR). Submitted in person; no e-visa.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Freelance / Self-Employed Activity
BGR.purpose: Permits third-country nationals authorised to carry out freelance (self-employed) professional activity in Bulgaria to enter and reside for that purpose.
BGR.notes: Issued on the ground under Article 24, paragraph 1, point 15 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires a certified copy of a permit to carry out freelance activity issued by the authorities of the Ministry of Labour and Social Policy, which must be obtained before the visa. The Type D visa (valid up to 180 days) allows entry, after which a residence permit is issued by the Migration Directorate (MVR). Submitted in person; no e-visa.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Representatives of a Foreign Commercial Company
BGR.purpose: Permits representatives of a foreign commercial company that has registered a commercial representation with the Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI) to reside in Bulgaria.
BGR.notes: Issued on the ground under Article 24, paragraph 1, point 6 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires a certificate of current registration of the commercial representation with the Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCI), issued no earlier than one month before submission, plus a document on the current state of the represented foreign company. The Type D visa (valid up to 180 days) allows entry, after which a renewable 1-year residence permit is issued by the Migration Directorate (MVR). This route does not itself grant the right to take up employment. Submitted in person; no e-visa.

BGR.name: Visa D – Long-Stay Visa for Real-Estate / Company Investment Residence
BGR.purpose: Permits non-EU nationals who have invested at least BGN 600,000 in Bulgarian real estate, or who own more than 50% of the capital of a Bulgarian commercial company, to obtain a temporary residence permit.
BGR.notes: Issued on the ground under Article 24, paragraph 1, point 19 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act. Requires proof from a licensed Bulgarian credit institution of an investment of at least BGN 600,000 (approx. EUR 306,775 at the fixed conversion rate EUR 1 = BGN 1.95583; Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026) in real estate, or ownership of more than 50% of a Bulgarian commercial company, together with related ownership and expense-justification documents. The Type D visa (valid up to 180 days) allows entry, after which a temporary (long-term) residence permit is issued by the Migration Directorate (MVR). Distinct from the permanent-residence investment-fund route (minimum EUR 512,000 under Article 25(1)(6)) tracked separately in this file's RBI and investment entries. Submitted in person; no e-visa.

BGR.name: Seasonal Worker Visa / Permit (Type C or Type D)
BGR.purpose: Permits non-EU nationals to perform seasonal work in Bulgaria in the tourism/hospitality (HORECA) and agriculture sectors, tied to the seasonal cycle.
BGR.notes: Bulgaria's implementation of the EU Seasonal Workers Directive 2014/36/EU. Two pathways: (1) seasonal work up to 90 days uses a short-stay Type C visa registered for seasonal work, with no separate work permit; (2) seasonal work from 90 days up to 9 months requires a work permit issued by the Bulgarian Employment Agency plus a Type D visa and a subsequent residence permit. Limited to HORECA (tourism) and agriculture sectors. The employer must obtain Employment Agency approval before the worker's arrival and provide adequate accommodation. Workers may change employer with Employment Agency permission without leaving Bulgaria. Maximum stay is 9 months in any 12-month period.

BGR.name: Intra-Corporate Transferee (ICT) Permit (Type D visa + ICT permit)
BGR.purpose: Permits managers, specialists, or trainee employees of a multinational group to be transferred from a company branch outside the EU to a host entity in Bulgaria.
BGR.notes: Bulgaria's implementation of the EU Intra-Corporate Transfer Directive 2014/66/EU. For managers, specialists and trainees transferred within the same group of undertakings from a non-EU branch to a Bulgarian host entity. Requires prior employment with the group of at least 12 months (managers and specialists) or 6 months (trainees). Entry is via a Type D long-stay visa; the ICT permit is then issued. The holder may work only for the specified receiving enterprise(s) in the manager/specialist/trainee role. Maximum transfer duration is up to 3 years for managers and specialists and up to 1 year for trainees; intra-EU mobility to other member states is possible under conditions. Administered together with the Bulgarian Employment Agency and the Migration Directorate (MVR).

BGR.name: Diplomatic / Official / Service Visa
BGR.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of countries that have bilateral agreements with Bulgaria requiring visas for such passport holders. For diplomatic passport holders of many countries, no visa is required (see conditional_access).
BGR.notes: Diplomatic and service passport holders of many countries are exempt from visa requirements per bilateral agreements (see conditional_access entries in this file). Where a visa is required for diplomatic/service passports, it is typically issued free of charge and through diplomatic channels with expedited processing. The official MFA table (last updated 14 January 2025) lists which nationalities require or do not require visas when holding diplomatic/service passports.

BHR.name: eVisa – 2-Week Single Entry Visit Visa
BHR.purpose: Short-term tourism or personal visit to Bahrain. Allows a single entry stay of up to two weeks.
BHR.notes: Available to nationals of 211 countries listed on evisa.gov.bh. Can also be issued on arrival at the airport for eligible nationalities. Employment strictly prohibited on this visa. Visa can be renewed through NPRA.

BHR.name: eVisa – 1-Month Multiple Entry Visit Visa
BHR.purpose: Allows multiple entries into Bahrain for tourism or personal visits over a one-month validity period.
BHR.notes: Available via the official Bahrain e-visa portal. Applicants must have a valid reason for multiple visits and meet eligibility criteria.

BHR.name: eVisa – 3-Month Multiple Entry Visit Visa (GCC Resident)
BHR.purpose: Allows GCC-resident foreign nationals to visit Bahrain multiple times over a 3-month period.
BHR.notes: Requires a valid GCC residence permit with at least 3 months remaining validity. Not available to all nationalities - specifically designed for non-GCC-citizen residents of GCC countries.

BHR.name: Visa on Arrival
BHR.purpose: Grants entry to eligible foreign nationals at Bahrain International Airport without prior visa application.
BHR.notes: Available to nationals of 204 countries as listed on the official evisa.gov.bh on-arrival page. Default duration is 2 weeks per UK government travel advice; up to 6-month visit visa also available. Approval is at immigration officer's discretion. Employment strictly prohibited.

BHR.name: 10-Year Multiple Entry Tourist Visa (Embassy)
BHR.purpose: Long-validity multiple entry visa for tourism purposes, available through Bahrain embassies abroad.
BHR.notes: Referenced in US State Department travel advisory. Available through the Bahrain embassy. Individual entry stay duration not specified in available sources.

BHR.name: Business eVisa
BHR.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to visit Bahrain for business meetings, conferences, or commercial activities without taking up employment.
BHR.notes: Available through the official e-visa portal. Applicants must demonstrate a business purpose. Cannot be used to take up employment.

BHR.name: Work Visa / Employment Visa
BHR.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to reside and work in Bahrain under a specific employer's sponsorship.
BHR.notes: Issued by the Labour Market Regulatory Authority (LMRA). Requires employer sponsorship. Applicants must enter on a visit visa first in many cases, then convert to a residence permit and work permit. Golden Residency holders must still obtain a separate work permit from LMRA to legally work.

BHR.name: Journalism Visa
BHR.purpose: Required for accredited journalists visiting Bahrain to cover news or media events.
BHR.notes: Advance application/accreditation is mandatory before travel. Per the official evisa.gov.bh NPRA FAQ, journalists must apply through Bahrain's media authority (the former Information Affairs Authority, now the Ministry of Information, mia.gov.bh) via its correspondent-accreditation form, not the standard eVisa portal.

BHR.name: Golden Residency – Property Owner Track
BHR.purpose: Long-term residency for foreign nationals who invest in Bahraini real estate meeting the minimum property value threshold.
BHR.notes: Requires personal share value of BHD 130,000 (approx USD 345,000) or more at time of purchase. Multiple properties can be combined to meet threshold. Application fee BHD 5 (approx USD 13); issuance fee BHD 300 (approx USD 795). Same fees apply per dependent. No minimum stay requirement to maintain residency. Dependents (spouse, parents, children of any age) can be sponsored. Work permit from LMRA required separately to work. Processing 5 working days.

BHR.name: Golden Residency – Professional/Employee Track
BHR.purpose: Long-term residency for skilled foreign professionals with a sustained employment history in Bahrain.
BHR.notes: Requires 5+ years of continuous employment in Bahrain with average monthly basic salary over BHD 2,000 (approx USD 5,300). Must maintain continuous Social Insurance Organization (SIO) coverage. Bonuses and allowances excluded from salary calculation. Application fee BHD 5; issuance fee BHD 300. Processing 5 working days.

BHR.name: Golden Residency – Retiree Track (Resident)
BHR.purpose: Long-term residency for foreign nationals who have retired after a long career in Bahrain.
BHR.notes: For retirees resident in Bahrain: requires 15+ years of work in Bahrain with average pension of BHD 2,000/month or more. Application fee BHD 5; issuance fee BHD 300. Processing 5 working days. No minimum stay requirement to maintain status.

BHR.name: Golden Residency – Retiree Track (Non-Resident)
BHR.purpose: Long-term residency for foreign retirees based outside Bahrain who receive a qualifying pension.
BHR.notes: For non-resident retirees: requires average pension of BHD 4,000/month or more. Application fee BHD 5; issuance fee BHD 300. Processing 5 working days.

BHR.name: Golden Residency – Talented Individual Track
BHR.purpose: Long-term residency for entrepreneurs, scientists, researchers, artists, athletes, and other exceptional individuals recognised for their achievements.
BHR.notes: Subject to committee review and approval. Eligible categories include entrepreneurs with demonstrated business success, researchers and scientists, artists and creatives with recognised work, technology/business innovators, athletes with notable achievements, and other exceptional talent. Application fee BHD 5; issuance fee BHD 300. Processing up to 10 working days.

BHR.name: Diplomatic / Official Passport Visa Exemption
BHR.purpose: Allows holders of diplomatic or official passports from countries with bilateral agreements to enter Bahrain without a visa.
BHR.notes: Bahrain has bilateral visa exemption agreements with select countries for diplomatic and official passport holders. Confirmed for India (signed 15 July 2018, in force 19 December 2018). GCC nationals enter using national ID cards regardless of passport type. Other bilateral agreements exist but Bahrain's MOFA website (mofa.gov.bh) was inaccessible for comprehensive list.

BHR.name: Family Visit eVisa
BHR.purpose: Short-term visit visa allowing an expatriate resident or Bahraini national to bring immediate family members (spouse, children, parents) to visit Bahrain.
BHR.notes: Issued by NPRA. A resident or citizen sponsor applies on the family member's behalf; kinship documents and proof of income/bank statement (guidance 300-500 BHD/month) required. Fee BHD 39 (approx USD 103). Processing 3-5 working days. A separate 'visa for the relatives of a Bahraini' (father, mother, spouse, children) is also available at BHD 30 issuance + BHD 5 endorsement + BHD 4 application.

BHR.name: Educational Residence Permit (Student)
BHR.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals enrolled as students at a Bahraini university or institute.
BHR.notes: Issued by NPRA (Ministry of Interior) to students enrolled at a Bahraini university or institute. Fee BHD 64 (approx USD 170). Processing 1 working day. Applicant must hold a valid entry visa and maintain valid health insurance. Applied for via the bahrain.bh eServices residence-permit form.

BHR.name: Self-Sponsorship Residence Permit & Re-entry Visa (Investor)
BHR.purpose: Renewable self-sponsored residence permit for foreign investors holding a qualifying share in a Bahraini commercial registration.
BHR.notes: Issued by NPRA for investors with a commercial-registration share (commonly cited minimum around BHD 100,000). Requires Commercial Registration pre-approval from the Ministry of Industry & Commerce before applying (confirmed in the official evisa.gov.bh FAQ). Issued for 2, 5 or 10 years: BHD 200 / 400 / 600 issuance respectively, plus BHD 5 application and BHD 250 transfer fee. fee_usd reflects the 2-year BHD 200 tier (approx USD 530). Processing up to 40 working days. Distinct from, and lower-threshold than, the 10-year Golden Residency. A parallel property-owner track exists for foreigners owning Bahraini property valued BHD 50,000+.

BHS.name: Visitor Visa
BHS.purpose: Allows foreign nationals not exempt from visa requirements to enter the Bahamas for tourism, leisure, or visiting family. Nationals of approximately 80+ countries must obtain this visa in advance through a Bahamas embassy, consulate, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
BHS.notes: Now issued via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs eVISA portal (evisa.mofa.gov.bs) or through Bahamas embassies/consulates. Official eVISA fees: single-entry visitor visa USD $160; multiple-entry visa USD $250 (valid for 3, 6, or 12 months); 3-year multiple-entry visa USD $500 (not available online). A sponsored visitor visa adds a USD $20 facilitation fee. Standard eVISA processing 7-10 business days. Applicants from visa-required countries include Afghanistan, Algeria, Cuba, Egypt, Haiti, India (without qualifying credentials), Iran, Nigeria, Pakistan, Philippines, Russia, Syria, Ukraine, Vietnam and others. Visitors must hold a valid return/onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. Standard max stay up to 8 months subject to immigration officer discretion. Work is strictly prohibited on a visitor visa.

BHS.name: Business Visitor Visa / BH-1B Visa
BHS.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter the Bahamas for short-term business activities such as meetings, negotiations, audits, or inspections without engaging in gainful employment.
BHS.notes: The BH-1B visa fee is BSD $3,000 per the official Immigration Fee Scale. Business visitors are not permitted to engage in any form of gainful employment or work. Short-term business activities such as board meetings and corporate inspections may qualify. Separate from the Short Term Work Permit which authorizes actual work.

BHS.name: Work Permit (Work Visa)
BHS.purpose: Authorizes non-Bahamian nationals to engage in gainful employment with a specific employer in the Bahamas. Issued annually in nine fee scales based on occupation level.
BHS.notes: Annual work permits are issued on a fee scale of 1-9 based on occupation: Scale 1 (executives/directors) BSD $16,275; Scale 2 (professionals/managers) BSD $13,125; Scale 3 (technical/healthcare) BSD $9,450; Scale 4 (skilled trades/supervisors) BSD $7,500; Scale 4A (consultants/physicians) BSD $6,250; Scale 5 (trades/hospitality) BSD $6,000; Scale 6 (instructors/artists) BSD $5,000; Scale 7 (clerical/entry-level) BSD $4,000; Scale 8 (general workers) BSD $2,000; Scale 9 (farm laborers) BSD $500. Religious/charitable organizations and passenger ship workers: Nil. Expedited processing available for Scales 7-9 (14 business days) at BSD $400; Scales 1-6 at 10% surcharge. Applications via online portal at epermits.immigration.gov.bs. Permit is employer-specific. Renewal available.

BHS.name: Short Term Work Permit
BHS.purpose: Authorizes non-Bahamian nationals to perform work in the Bahamas for a period of 1 to 90 days, typically for emergency or one-time professional assignments.
BHS.notes: For 1-30 days: BSD $200 non-refundable processing fee. For 31-90 days: additional documentation required including police certificate and medical certificate. Designated for emergency situations and intended as a one-time application. Examples include aircraft mechanics, corporate auditors, board meeting attendees, and disaster preparedness personnel. Certain professions (medical, legal, accounting, entertainment, veterinary) require authorization letters from relevant professional councils. Applicants should not be in the Bahamas during processing. Online application via epermits.immigration.gov.bs.

BHS.name: Government Contract Worker Permit
BHS.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals employed under government contracts to reside and work in the Bahamas for the duration of their contract.
BHS.notes: Specific fee, duration, and requirements are not published on the immigration website. Applications via online portal at epermits.immigration.gov.bs. Contact: (242) 225-5337 or (242) 322-7530-5.

BHS.name: Permit to Reside (Student)
BHS.purpose: Authorizes non-Bahamian nationals to reside in the Bahamas for the purpose of attending school, college, or university, or as dependents of persons legally authorized to reside in the country.
BHS.notes: Annual permit fee BSD $300 for full-time students/trainees per the Immigration Fee Scale. Processing fee BSD $200 non-refundable. Processing time 8-12 weeks after complete submission. Applicants should not be in the Bahamas during processing. Requirements include: letter of request to Director of Immigration, completed notarized Form 1, medical certificate (within 30 days), police certificate (within 6 months covering 5 years), two passport photos, valid passport copy, sponsor passport copy, two character references, financial reference, annual permit questionnaire, and school enrollment documentation. Renewal available.

BHS.name: Resident Spouse Permit
BHS.purpose: Allows non-Bahamian nationals married to Bahamian citizens to legally reside and work in the Bahamas.
BHS.notes: Annual permit fee BSD $300 (or BSD $1,500 for a 5-year spouse permit option). Non-refundable processing fee BSD $200. For marriages of less than 5 years at application. After 5 years of marriage, the non-Bahamian spouse may apply for renewal, permanent residence, or citizenship. Applicants should not be in the Bahamas during initial processing. Requirements: completed notarized Form 1A, medical certificate (within 30 days), police certificate (within 6 months), passport photos, valid passports for both spouses, certified marriage certificate, birth certificates for children under 18. All foreign documents must be apostille-certified or legalized. Renewal available.

BHS.name: Permit to Reside (Dependent)
BHS.purpose: Authorizes dependent children (under 18) of persons legally authorized to reside in the Bahamas to reside in the country.
BHS.notes: Annual dependent permit fee BSD $300 per the Immigration Fee Scale. Processing fee BSD $200 non-refundable. Same application as Permit to Reside (Student). Applies to spouses or children under 18 of persons legally authorized to reside. Processing time 8-12 weeks.

BHS.name: Permit to Reside (Retired Person)
BHS.purpose: Allows retired foreign nationals with at least 20 years of work history to reside in the Bahamas without engaging in gainful employment.
BHS.notes: Annual permit fee BSD $250 for retired persons with 20 years work history per the Immigration Fee Scale. Non-refundable processing fee BSD $200. Requirements include financial reference or CPA statement demonstrating ability to self-sustain. Not authorized for gainful employment.

BHS.name: Economic Permanent Residence Certificate
BHS.purpose: Grants lifelong permanent resident status to foreign nationals making a qualifying investment of at least USD $1 million in Bahamian real estate or Zero Coupon Bonds, allowing the holder to reside and work.
BHS.notes: Minimum investment of USD $1.0 million in real estate OR purchase of Zero Coupon Bonds from the Central Bank of the Bahamas, with mandatory 10-year holding period. Certificate fee: BSD $25,000 with gainful occupation rights; BSD $20,000 without. Certificate is issued for the lifetime of the holder unless revoked. Processing fee BSD $200 non-refundable. Requirements include medical certificate (within 30 days), police certificate (within 6 months, covering 5 years), two passport photos, passport copies, birth certificate, two character references. Path to citizenship requires 10 years as permanent resident (including 12 months immediately before application) plus 6 years of prior residency.

BHS.name: General Permanent Residence Certificate
BHS.purpose: Grants lifelong permanent resident status to foreign nationals with long-term qualifying residence or professional service in the Bahamas, allowing the holder to reside and work.
BHS.notes: Standard applicant fee BSD $15,000. Reduced fees apply for: persons with 10-20 years residence on a work permit (scales 4-7) at BSD $10,000; 10-20 years as teacher/nurse/healthcare/government worker at BSD $3,000; 20+ years on higher professional work permits at BSD $1,000-$2,000; previously endorsed spouses (widowed) or children on parent certificate at BSD $3,000; spouses of permanent residents at BSD $1,000-$5,000; ministerial/religious workers with 20+ years at BSD $1,000. Certificate is for the lifetime of the holder unless revoked. Eligibility categories include spouses of Bahamians (after 5 years of marriage), children born abroad to Bahamian mothers, long-serving teachers/nurses/police/prison officers, ministers of religion, doctors, and legal work permit holders of 20+ consecutive years.

BHS.name: Home Owner Identification Card
BHS.purpose: Provides a residence identification card for foreign nationals who own a habitable residence in the Bahamas and maintain a primary residence in their home country, issued under the International Persons Land Holding Act.
BHS.notes: Non-refundable processing fee BSD $200. Applicants must own a habitable residence in the Bahamas AND maintain a primary residence outside the Bahamas. Issued under International Persons Land Holding Act – Chapter 140. Requirements: completed notarized application form with BSD $10 postage stamp, letter of request to Director, medical certificate (within 30 days), police certificate (within 6 months), two passport photos, valid passport copy (minimum 2 months validity), current real property tax payment proof, registered deed of conveyance for Bahamian home, International Landholding Certificate, marriage/birth certificates if applicable, Good Standing certificate, evidence of primary home outside Bahamas (insurance, mortgage, or tax documents). Applicants should not be in the Bahamas during processing. Same form applies for renewals.

BHS.name: Resident Belonger Permit
BHS.purpose: Authorizes persons born in the Bahamas to non-Bahamian parents, or persons born abroad to a Bahamian mother or father, who have not automatically acquired Bahamian citizenship to reside in the Bahamas.
BHS.notes: Annual permit fee BSD $300 for all Resident Belonger categories per the Immigration Fee Scale. Applies to persons with ancestral ties to the Bahamas who have not acquired Bahamian citizenship. Applications via online portal at epermits.immigration.gov.bs.

BHS.name: Diplomat Identification Card
BHS.purpose: Provides identification and status documentation for accredited diplomatic personnel and their recognized dependents residing in the Bahamas.
BHS.notes: Issued to accredited diplomatic personnel. Specific fees and requirements not published on the immigration website. Contact: (242) 225-5337 or (242) 322-7530-5.

BHS.name: Special Permit
BHS.purpose: Allows foreign nationals whose names appear on the Bahamas Restricted List (previously deported or removed) to enter the Bahamas for a limited period, subject to approval by the Director of Immigration.
BHS.notes: Non-refundable fee BSD $200. Maximum 28 days at the Director's discretion. Exclusively for persons on the Restricted List - NOT a general travel or nomad visa. Requirements: cover letter to Director of Immigration, police certificate (within 6 months, covering 5 years) for applicants aged 14+, two passport photos (white background, within 6 months), valid passport copy with 6+ months remaining validity, two written references (one from employer). Permit must be carried at all times while in the Bahamas and surrendered upon departure.

BHS.name: Re-Entry Permit
BHS.purpose: Allows non-Bahamian permanent residents or authorized residents to re-enter the Bahamas after travel abroad.
BHS.notes: Specific fees and requirements not published on the immigration website. Applications via online portal at epermits.immigration.gov.bs. Contact: (242) 225-5337 or (242) 322-7530-5.

BHS.name: Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS)
BHS.purpose: Annual residence permit allowing remote-working professionals employed or contracted by companies/clients outside the Bahamas, and students enrolled at overseas institutions, to live in the Bahamas while working or studying remotely.
BHS.notes: Official Government of the Bahamas remote-work programme launched October 2020 and administered by the Ministry responsible for Immigration. Total cost for a professional is USD $1,025 (USD $25 application fee + USD $1,000 permit fee); for a college student USD $525 (USD $25 + USD $500); each accompanying dependent USD $500. Permit is valid up to 12 months and renewals are considered for a maximum period of up to three years. Estimated 5 business days processing. Fully online application via the immigration portal at portal.immigration.gov.bs. Applicants must earn their income from employers or clients based outside the Bahamas; local employment is not permitted. Enquiries: immigrationbeats@bahamas.gov.bs.

BHS.name: Seaman's Visa
BHS.purpose: Entry visa for merchant seafarers and vessel crew members who need to enter the Bahamas to join, sign off, or otherwise attend a vessel.
BHS.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs eVISA portal (evisa.mofa.gov.bs) alongside self-sponsored and sponsored visitor visas. Official fee USD $160.00 (single journey). Standard eVISA processing 7-10 business days. Applicable to seafarers/crew of visa-required nationalities; issued for the purpose of joining or leaving a vessel rather than tourism or residence.

BHS.name: Trusted Traveller Programme
BHS.purpose: Allows senior management and professional personnel of companies operating in the Bahamas (or their affiliates) to visit for business meetings, research, audits, trade shows, conferences and seminars for under 14 days without obtaining a Work Permit.
BHS.notes: Non-refundable processing fee USD $200.00 (payable by credit/debit card, postal money order, or bank certified cheque). Permits visits of under fourteen (14) days without a Work Permit provided no gainful employment occurs. Eligible roles include Chairman, Director, CEO, CFO, COO, consultants, legal counsel, compliance officers, accountants, auditors, actuaries, medical professionals, analysts and other managerial titles of an organisation operating in the Bahamas or its affiliates. Does NOT cover persons organising such events for profit, who must obtain a Work Permit. Apply by submitting a letter of request, the fee, a passport bio-page copy, passport photos, and the completed application form to the Director of Immigration.

BIH.name: Aerodromska Tranzitna Viza (Visa A) - Airport Transit Visa
BIH.purpose: Permits transit through the international transit zone of an airport in Bosnia and Herzegovina without entering the country proper. Issued for single, dual, or multiple airport transits.
BIH.notes: Only required for nationals of certain countries who must transit through the airport international zone. The visa does not permit entry into BiH territory. Fee of 100 BAM applies if exceptionally issued at the border/airport. Applications made in advance at BiH embassies/consulates.

BIH.name: Viza za Kratkoročni Boravak (Visa C) - Short-Stay Visa (Tourist/Business/Private)
BIH.purpose: Covers short-term stays for tourism, business, private visits, education, cultural or sports events, and transit through Bosnia and Herzegovina territory. Allows up to 90 days within any 6-month period.
BIH.notes: This is Bosnia and Herzegovina's primary short-stay visa category, equivalent to a Schengen C visa. Issued as single or multiple entry. Validity up to 1 year (extendable in exceptional circumstances). If issued exceptionally at a land border crossing or airport, a 100 BAM fee applies. Applications must be submitted at a BiH embassy or consulate at least one month before travel. Applicants must show minimum BAM 150 per day financial means. Foreign nationals must register their residence address within 48 hours of entry. Bosnia and Herzegovina does not operate an e-visa system - all applications are in-person.

BIH.name: Viza za Kratkoročni Boravak (Visa C) - Short-Stay Business Visa
BIH.purpose: Short-stay business variant of Visa C covering business meetings, negotiations, conferences, and other commercial activities in Bosnia and Herzegovina for up to 90 days within a 6-month period.
BIH.notes: Sub-purpose of Visa C. Requires an employer/sponsor letter and an invitation letter from a BiH-registered company verified by the BiH Ministry of Security. Same visa document as tourist Visa C; the purpose is distinguished by supporting documents. Bosnia and Herzegovina does not issue a separate business visa document.

BIH.name: Viza za Kratkoročni Boravak (Visa C) - Short-Stay Family/Private Visit Visa
BIH.purpose: Short-stay variant of Visa C for visiting family members or friends residing in Bosnia and Herzegovina, valid for up to 90 days within a 6-month period.
BIH.notes: Sub-purpose of Visa C. Requires an invitation letter from the resident host in BiH, verified by relevant authorities, including a sponsor declaration of financial responsibility. The same Visa C document is issued; purpose is determined by supporting documents.

BIH.name: Viza za Dugoročni Boravak (Visa D) - Long-Stay/National Visa
BIH.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to stay in Bosnia and Herzegovina for more than 90 days within a 6-month period, typically as a precursor to obtaining a temporary residence permit.
BIH.notes: Bosnia and Herzegovina's long-stay national visa (Visa D) is required by those seeking temporary residence and must be obtained at a BiH embassy or consulate abroad before arriving. Issued for stays up to 6 months, validity up to 1 year. After entry on a D visa, applicants apply for a formal temporary residence permit (privremeni boravak) at the Service for Foreigners Affairs. The D visa covers purposes including employment, family reunification, education, humanitarian reasons, and real estate ownership. Bosnia and Herzegovina does not operate an e-visa system.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak - Temporary Residence (Employment/Work)
BIH.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to legally reside and work in Bosnia and Herzegovina for employment purposes, requiring both a temporary residence permit and a work permit in most cases.
BIH.notes: First-time applicants must enter on a Visa D. Temporary residence for employment is issued for up to 1 year and is renewable. Requires a valid passport (3+ months validity beyond the requested period), proof of employment or work permit, accommodation proof, health insurance, and a medical certificate (within 3 months). Extensions must be filed at least 15 days before expiration. After 5 consecutive years of temporary residence, applicants may apply for permanent residence. Administrative fees apply (amounts referenced in official fee schedule). Company founders/owners may qualify for work without a formal work permit under a separate business owner category.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak - Temporary Residence (Education/Study)
BIH.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to reside in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the duration of an accredited educational programme at a BiH institution.
BIH.notes: Issued as a category of Temporary Residence (privremeni boravak) on educational grounds. Entry via Visa D. Issued up to 1 year, renewable for the duration of study. Requires proof of enrolment, accommodation, financial means, and health insurance. After 5 years of uninterrupted temporary residence, permanent residence may be sought. Bosnia and Herzegovina has no separate dedicated student visa document - it is a purpose category within temporary residence.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak - Temporary Residence (Family Reunification)
BIH.purpose: Enables foreign nationals to reside in Bosnia and Herzegovina to join a family member who holds legal residence status in the country.
BIH.notes: Category of Temporary Residence for family reunification. Entry via Visa D. Requires proof of family relationship, sponsor's valid residence in BiH, accommodation, and financial means. Issued up to 1 year, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 5 years continuous temporary residence.

BIH.name: Stalni Boravak - Permanent Residence Permit
BIH.purpose: Grants foreign nationals an indefinite right to reside in Bosnia and Herzegovina after meeting the required continuous residence period and integration conditions.
BIH.notes: Requires minimum 5 years of continuous legal temporary residence in BiH immediately preceding the application. Additional requirements: valid passport, stable and regular income, adequate housing, health insurance, proficiency in at least one official BiH language (Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian), and criminal clearance from home country and BiH (certificates no older than 6 months). Upon approval, a unique identification number is assigned and the holder must apply for a resident ID card within 8 days. Administrative fee: 200 BAM referenced in SPS documentation. Permanent residence is not citizenship.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak na osnovu vlasništva nekretnina - Temporary Residence Based on Real Estate Ownership
BIH.purpose: Allows foreign nationals who own real estate in Bosnia and Herzegovina to obtain temporary residence, provided they demonstrate a real and lasting connection to the country.
BIH.notes: No minimum property value is specified in law. Applicant must demonstrate a 'real and lasting connection' to BiH (e.g., origin, children's education in BiH, pension receipt, or investment in economic activities). Issued for up to 1 year, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 5 consecutive years of continuous temporary residence. Administrative fee: 150 BAM for issuance.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak - Temporary Residence Based on Business/Company Establishment
BIH.purpose: Permits founders or owners of a company registered in Bosnia and Herzegovina to reside in the country and conduct business activities without a separate work permit.
BIH.notes: Classified as 'work without a work permit' for company founders/owners. No minimum investment threshold set for this residence category specifically; minimum registered share capital for a d.o.o. (LLC) in FBiH entity is 1,000 BAM (approx. EUR 511). Issued up to 1 year, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 5 consecutive years. Entry typically via Visa D.

BIH.name: Diplomatska / Službena Viza - Diplomatic and Official Visa
BIH.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic or official/service passports from countries that do not have a full visa-free agreement with Bosnia and Herzegovina, permitting official travel and residence.
BIH.notes: Diplomatic and official/service passport holders from select countries (including Algeria, Armenia, China, Cuba, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Morocco, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, Ukraine, and Russia) are exempt from visa requirements. Diplomatic visa fee is generally waived based on reciprocity. Duration determined by mission length or bilateral agreement terms.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak radi Liječenja ili Rehabilitacije - Temporary Residence for Medical Treatment or Rehabilitation
BIH.purpose: Allows a foreign national to reside in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the duration of medical treatment, rehabilitation, or placement in a care/nursing institution.
BIH.notes: One of the enumerated grounds for temporary residence under Article 52 of the Law on Movement and Stay of Aliens and Asylum: treatment or rehabilitation (Article 87 of the Rulebook on Entry and Stay of Aliens) and stay in a nursing home (Article 88). Requires proof of admission to a BiH institution for treatment/rehabilitation, accommodation, health insurance, and sufficient funds. Duration is tied to the treatment period, issued for up to one year, may be shorter, and is renewable. First-time applicants subject to the visa regime enter on a Visa D. Time spent on the treatment/rehabilitation basis does not count toward permanent residence. An administrative fee for approval/extension of temporary residence applies per the SPS fee schedule.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak na Osnovu Braka sa Državljaninom BiH - Temporary Residence Based on Marriage to a BiH Citizen
BIH.purpose: Enables the foreign spouse or extramarital (common-law) partner of a Bosnia and Herzegovina citizen to reside in the country.
BIH.notes: A ground distinct from family reunification (which is for joining a resident alien): this applies to spouses of BiH citizens (Article 59 of the Rulebook on Entry and Stay of Aliens) and to extramarital/common-law partners of BiH citizens (Article 60). Requires proof of the marriage or relationship, accommodation, health insurance, and financial means. Issued for up to one year, renewable, and provides a path to permanent residence after five continuous years and to facilitated naturalisation as the spouse of a citizen. First-time applicants subject to the visa regime enter on a Visa D. An administrative fee for approval/extension of temporary residence applies per the SPS fee schedule.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak iz Humanitarnih Razloga - Temporary Residence on Humanitarian Grounds
BIH.purpose: Discretionary residence for foreign nationals in humanitarian situations, such as victims of human trafficking, unaccompanied minors, or persons cooperating with authorities in criminal proceedings.
BIH.notes: Granted on humanitarian grounds under Article 54 of the Law on Movement and Stay of Aliens and Asylum (Article 89 of the Rulebook on Entry and Stay of Aliens). Covers victims of human trafficking, unaccompanied foreign minors, persons whose removal would be unreasonable for serious humanitarian reasons, and those cooperating with authorities in criminal proceedings. Discretionary and granted by the Service for Foreigners' Affairs; may be issued for periods shorter than one year and is renewable. Several of these sub-categories do not lead to permanent residence.

BIH.name: Privremeni Boravak - Rad bez Radne Dozvole (Profesori i Naučnici) - Temporary Residence for University Professors, Scientists and Researchers (Work Without a Work Permit)
BIH.purpose: Allows university professors, scientists, researchers, and members of international scientific missions to reside and work in Bosnia and Herzegovina without a separate work permit.
BIH.notes: One of the 'work without a work permit' categories under Article 84 of the Law on Movement and Stay of Aliens and Asylum: university professors and scientists (Article 68 of the Rulebook on Entry and Stay of Aliens) and members of international scientific missions conducting research approved by the Council of Ministers (Article 71). No labour-market test or separate work permit is required, but a temporary residence permit must still be obtained. Issued for up to one year, renewable. First-time applicants subject to the visa regime enter on a Visa D. An administrative fee for approval/extension of temporary residence applies per the SPS fee schedule.

BLR.name: Type B - Transit Visa
BLR.purpose: Allows passage through Belarus territory en route to a third country. Covers single, double, or multiple transit crossings.
BLR.notes: Max 2 days per crossing (including entry day). Valid up to 1 year. Can be single, double, or multiple-entry. Fee is EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU citizens under facilitation agreement). Expedited processing within 2 working days doubles the fee. Also issuable at Minsk National Airport 24/7 with advance document submission.

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Tourist Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry for tourism purposes. Allows single or double entry.
BLR.notes: Tourism variant of Type C: max 30 days, single or double-entry. Fee EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU citizens). Expedited processing in 2 working days doubles fee. Also available via e-visa (single-entry, 30 days, processed in 7 calendar days, EUR 60 or EUR 35 for EU). On-arrival available at Minsk National Airport with advance visa support document submission.

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Business Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry for business trips, negotiations, signing contracts, and commercial activities not amounting to employment.
BLR.notes: Part of the Type C short-term visa category covering business, private visits, cultural/scientific events, humanitarian work, religious ties, and journalism. Max validity 90 days; can be single, double, or multiple-entry. Supporting documents include invitation letters or employer letters. Fee EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU citizens under facilitation agreement). E-visa available for eligible 67 nationalities (single-entry, 30-day stay, 7-day processing).

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Student/Study Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry for study, educational internships, or participation in cultural and scientific programs.
BLR.notes: Type C category for study/educational purposes. Requires invitation or confirmation from educational institution. For on-arrival at Minsk National Airport, an institutional representative must be present. For long-term study (over 90 days), a Type D long-term visa is required.

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Private/Humanitarian/Religious/Press Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry for private visits, humanitarian activities, religious ties, or journalism purposes.
BLR.notes: Sub-category of Type C short-term visa for private, humanitarian, religious, and press purposes. Supporting documents vary by sub-purpose. Fee EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU). Expedited 2-working-day processing available at double fee.

BLR.name: Type D - Long-term Business Visa
BLR.purpose: Long-term multiple-entry visa for extended business activities, cultural/scientific participation, humanitarian programs, religious ties, journalism, private purposes, or employment in Belarus.
BLR.notes: Type D long-term visa covers all purposes (business, employment, cultural/scientific, humanitarian, religious, press, private). Validity exceeds 90 days up to 5 years; multiple-entry. 2-year visas require prior long-term visa use within 3 years. 3–5 year visas require prior 2-year visa within 5 years. Max stay per visit is 90 days. Must apply at Belarusian diplomatic mission; not available on arrival or online.

BLR.name: Type D - Long-term Employment/Work Visa
BLR.purpose: Long-term visa for foreign nationals intending to work in Belarus under an employment contract with a Belarusian employer.
BLR.notes: Employment is one of the purposes explicitly covered under the Type D long-term visa. Requires employment contract or work permit documentation. Hi-Tech Park (HTP) resident company employees and founders enjoy simplified immigration: visa-free entry with stays up to 180 days, simplified temporary residence, and no special work permits needed. See park.by/en/membership/benefits/.

BLR.name: Type D - Long-term Student Visa
BLR.purpose: Long-term visa for foreign nationals enrolled in accredited Belarusian educational institutions for programs exceeding 90 days.
BLR.notes: Educational purposes fall under the cultural/scientific/educational sub-category of Type D. Requires official enrollment confirmation from a Belarusian institution. After entry, foreign students must register with migration authorities if staying beyond 10 working days.

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Employment (Work) Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry to take up employment in Belarus under a special employment permit, for engagements not exceeding 90 days.
BLR.notes: Employment is a purpose available under the Type C short-term visa. The visa support document is a notarised copy of a special employment permit issued by the local unit of the Citizenship and Migration Department, or an original application from a commercial organization with foreign investment. For employment exceeding 90 days a Type D long-term employment visa is required. Fee EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU citizens under the facilitation agreement).

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Medical Treatment Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry for medical treatment or health improvement (sanatorium/rehabilitation) at a Belarusian healthcare institution, including for an accompanying attendant.
BLR.notes: Requires a letter of visa support from a Belarusian healthcare institution or a contract for medical services with a Belarusian healthcare institution (also covers a foreign attendant accompanying the patient). A short-term visa issued on the application of a treatment center or health-improvement (sanatorium) organization is limited to a maximum of 30 days; longer courses of treatment use a standard Type C (up to 90 days) or a Type D long-term visa. Compulsory medical insurance with minimum EUR 10,000 coverage required. Fee EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU citizens).

BLR.name: Type C - Short-term Private Visit (Family/Relatives) Visa
BLR.purpose: Short-term entry to visit close relatives or family members who are citizens or residents of Belarus, or for other private purposes.
BLR.notes: For a private visit to family/relatives the visa support document is a document proving family ties or marital relations with a citizen of the Republic of Belarus (birth certificate, marriage certificate, or certificate of name change), or an invitation approved by the Citizenship and Migration Department. Other private-purpose grounds accepted include property ownership in Belarus, serious illness or death of a relative, or a court summons. Fee EUR 60 standard (EUR 35 for EU citizens). For extended family reunification a Type D long-term visa is issued.

BLR.name: Type D - Long-term Permanent Residence Visa
BLR.purpose: Long-term entry visa for foreign nationals approved for permanent residence in Belarus (e.g. family reunification, ethnic Belarusians, or approved investors) to enter and obtain their residence permit.
BLR.notes: 'Permanent residence' is an official Type D long-term visa purpose. The visa support document is a decision of the regional branch of the Citizenship and Migration Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Grounds for permanent residence include family reunification with Belarusian citizens/residents, ethnic Belarusian origin, and investment (the residence-by-investment threshold is tracked separately under this country's RBI record). Max stay 90 days per visit; validity up to 5 years, multiple-entry. Applied for at a Belarusian diplomatic mission; not available online or on arrival.
