BLR.name: Belarus E-Visa (Single-entry Short-term)
BLR.purpose: Electronic visa for tourism, business, private affairs, sports, cultural, scientific, and educational events. Applied for online without visiting a diplomatic mission.
BLR.notes: Available to citizens of 67 eligible countries (including USA, Canada, EU states, UK, Australia, NZ, Japan). Fees: EUR 35 for EU citizens; EUR 60 for others; free for Japanese citizens and children under 12 (EU)/14 (others). Additional service fee EUR 6 for all. Processing: 7 calendar days. No visa support documents required. Valid for up to 30 days, single-entry. Entry via all international checkpoints including all 6 airports and road/rail borders. Program launched March 20, 2025. Apply at e-pasluga.by (service code 3.04.01).

BLR.name: Visa on Arrival - Minsk National Airport
BLR.purpose: Visa issued upon arrival at Minsk National Airport for travelers who could not obtain a visa in advance, subject to advance visa support document submission.
BLR.notes: Available 24/7 at Minsk National Airport's Division for the Admission of Foreigners (DAF). Citizens arriving from Russia CANNOT apply; they must obtain a visa in advance. Visa support documents (original invitation + copy) must be submitted at least 2 business days before arrival (delivered to DAF weekdays 11am–1pm or mailed). Short-term student and group visas require institutional representative present. Fee: EUR 60 standard; doubles if Belarus has no diplomatic representation in applicant's country; triples if Belarus has a mission there. Exceptional same-day submission allowed for death/critical illness of close relative. Contact: +375 17 279 20 58 / +375 17 279 28 72.

BLR.name: Brest-Grodno Visa-Free Tourist Zone (15 days)
BLR.purpose: Visa-free access to designated tourist zones in the Brest and Grodno regions for organized tour groups booked through licensed Belarusian travel agencies.
BLR.notes: Covers Brest city and Brest/Zhabinka/Kamenets/Pruzhany districts in Brest region, plus Grodno city and Grodno/Berestovitsa/Volkovysk/Voronovo/Lida/Svisloch/Shchuchin districts in Grodno region. Entry only at Brest (Terespol) international border crossing. Travelers must book tourism services through a licensed Belarusian travel agency which issues the required authorization document. Eligible nationalities not enumerated on official page. Health insurance for duration of stay required.

BLZ.name: Tourist Visa (Single Entry)
BLZ.purpose: For foreign nationals wishing to visit Belize for holiday, leisure, or exploration of settlement possibilities, who are not visa-exempt.
BLZ.notes: Belize visa fees are published in Belize Dollars (BZD). Single-entry visa for all nationalities (except China and specified Asian nationals): BZD $200 (~USD $100). For China nationals: BZD $3,000 (~USD $1,500). For India, Nepal, Thailand, Burma, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka nationals: BZD $750 (~USD $375). Valid for 6 months from issue; allows 30-day stay. Applications submitted at nearest Belizean diplomatic/consular mission or at Belmopan HQ for applicants already in Belize. US PR card, US multi-entry visa, Schengen multi-entry visa, or Canadian visa/PR card holders are exempt from needing a visa (max 30-day stay). Fees effective May 1, 2020.

BLZ.name: Tourist Visa (Multiple Entry)
BLZ.purpose: For foreign nationals requiring multiple entries into Belize for tourism or temporary business purposes within a 12-month period.
BLZ.notes: Multiple-entry visa valid for 12 months. Fees in BZD: all other nationalities BZD $300 (~USD $150); China nationals BZD $4,000 (~USD $2,000); India, Nepal, Thailand, Burma, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka nationals BZD $1,000 (~USD $500). Available to temporary permit holders and regular business/tourism visitors. Fees effective May 1, 2020.

BLZ.name: Visitor's Permit Extension
BLZ.purpose: Extends a visitor's legal stay in Belize by an additional 30 days beyond initial entry allowance.
BLZ.notes: Fee: BZD $200 (~USD $100) for all nationals. Grants an additional 30 days of legal stay. Cannot be used to engage in employment (paid or unpaid) or conduct business without Director of Immigration consent. Applicants requiring a visa must first obtain one before being granted a visitor's permit extension. Available at any Immigration Office in Belize.

BLZ.name: Employment Visa
BLZ.purpose: For foreign nationals officially hired locally, conducting consultations, representing overseas companies, working as foreign media personnel, or performing technical work assignments in Belize.
BLZ.notes: Entry visa required prior to taking up employment. Separate Work Permit must be obtained after entry. Visa fee structure same as tourist visa (nationality-based: BZD $200 / $750 / $3,000 for single entry). Applicant must be residing in Belize and hold a valid Belize visa before a Work Permit can be issued.

BLZ.name: Temporary Employment Permit (Work Permit)
BLZ.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals to engage in paid employment in Belize across professional, technical, agricultural, entertainment, or self-employed categories.
BLZ.notes: Fees in BZD vary by category: professional/technical workers BZD $3,000/year (~USD $1,500); general agricultural workers BZD $1,500/year (~USD $750); seasonal agricultural workers BZD $150/season; religious workers BZD $200/year; entertainers BZD $600–$1,500/week. Applicant must already be residing in Belize with valid visa. Process: employer submits to Labour Department; within 30 days applicant is notified; then visits Immigration Office for issuance. Categories include: professional (university degree), technical, general laborer, seasonal agricultural, self-employed, entertainer, religious/cultural volunteer, trader, peddler, domestic staff.

BLZ.name: Student Permit
BLZ.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled at primary, secondary, or tertiary educational institutions in Belize.
BLZ.notes: Fees in BZD: all nationalities (except below) BZD $200 (~USD $100) per school year/semester; India, Nepal, Thailand, Burma, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka nationals BZD $750; China nationals BZD $3,000. Validity: one school year for primary/secondary students; one semester for tertiary students. Processed on submission - Student Permit sticker placed in passport at time of application. Requires institutional letter, financial support letter, two passport photos, birth certificate, parent/guardian authority letter, sponsor's bank statement, and return ticket (tertiary extra-regional students only). Fees effective May 1, 2020.

BLZ.name: Student Visa
BLZ.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals who require a visa to enter Belize and plan to study at a Belizean educational institution.
BLZ.notes: Entry visa to be obtained before traveling; upon arrival applicant applies for Student Permit. Visa fee same structure as tourist/employment visa (BZD $200 / $750 / $3,000 depending on nationality). Must be at primary, secondary, or tertiary level institution in Belize.

BLZ.name: Work Where You Vacation Programme (Long Stay Permit)
BLZ.purpose: Allows remote workers employed outside Belize to live and work remotely in Belize for up to 6 months per calendar year.
BLZ.notes: Fee: BZD $500 (~USD $250) per adult; BZD $200 (~USD $100) per child under 18. Paid upon airport arrival. Eligibility: citizens or permanent residents of EU, UK, USA, or Canada; employed outside Belize; minimum annual income USD $75,000 (individual) or USD $100,000 (with dependents); clear police record (within 6 months); travel insurance minimum USD $50,000 coverage; notarized banking reference and account statement. Work restrictions: no employment in Belize permitted. Not extendable - must not exceed 6 months in calendar year. Waives work permit requirement for participant and student permits for dependent children. Also administered via travelbelize.org as 'Work Where You Vacation Programme'. Apply via email to visas@immigration.gov.bz or secretary@immigration.gov.bz prior to travel. Confirmed active as of June 2026.

BLZ.name: Qualified Retired Persons (QRP) Programme
BLZ.purpose: Residency program for retirees aged 40+ with foreign income who wish to live in Belize on a long-term basis with special tax and import privileges.
BLZ.notes: Administered by the Belize Tourism Board (BTB). Minimum age: 40 (official BTB retirement-program page states 'any person 40 years or older'; confirmed July 2026). Minimum annual income: USD $24,000 (USD $2,000/month) from sources outside Belize. Eligible income: pensions, annuities, Social Security, investments, inheritance, savings, retirement plans. Application fees: USD $150 (program application) + USD $1,000 per applicant + USD $750 per dependent + USD $200 QRP ID card. Annual renewal: USD $25. Grants Belize Residency (QRP Resident Card). Minimum 30 consecutive days per year in Belize required. Duty/tax exemptions on household effects, vehicle (max 5 years old), light aircraft, and motor boats in first year. Tax exemptions on foreign-sourced income. Option to operate a business with minimum BZD $1,000,000 investment employing 5 Belizean citizens. Qualifying nationalities: Commonwealth nations (excluding Belize), USA, EU member states, select Asia-Pacific and South American nations. Confirmed active as of June 2026.

BLZ.name: Temporary Residence by Investment
BLZ.purpose: Grants temporary residence status to foreign nationals who have made or are making substantial commercial investment in Belize.
BLZ.notes: Minimum investment threshold: BZD $500,000 in commercial investment. Required documentation includes: real estate title or lease agreement, bank statements, company registration documents, trade license. Renewable annually. No explicit path to permanent residence or citizenship stated on official page. Duration and specific fees not published on official page - verify at Belmopan Immigration Headquarters.

BLZ.name: Permanent Residence
BLZ.purpose: For foreign nationals who have legally resided in Belize for at least one continuous year and wish to obtain indefinite residence status with the right to live and remain in Belize.
BLZ.notes: Applicant must hold a passport with a Belize arrival stamp dated at least one (1) year prior to submission of application (i.e. at least one year of continuous legal residence in Belize). Required documents (originals plus copies): valid passport with arrival stamp, medical certificate with HIV/VDRL/TB tests, police record (valid within 6 months of issue), proof of financial stability, and two 2x2 inch photographs on white background taken within 6 months; spouse and children may be included on the application. The official Residence overview page states a minimum of 3 months (~90 days) for approval. Fees vary by nationality and type of residence and are not published on the official page. Grants indefinite residence status; path to citizenship not stated on the official page. Confirmed active as of July 2026.

BLZ.name: Dependent Permit
BLZ.purpose: For immediate family members (spouse, child, parent, or sibling) of Belize residents who are of retired age (55+), disabled, or children under 5 years of age.
BLZ.notes: Fees in BZD: all nationalities (except below) BZD $200 (~USD $100); India, Nepal, Thailand, Burma, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka nationals BZD $750; China nationals BZD $3,000. Applicant must be sponsored by a Belize resident who can provide housing. Qualifying dependents: persons of retired age (55+), disabled persons, or children under 5. Required documents: financial support letter, photographs, birth/marriage certificate, passport, proof of Belizean identity of sponsor, bank statement, 1-year return ticket. Processed on submission with permit sticker placed in passport. Fees effective May 1, 2020.

BLZ.name: Diplomatic/Official Visa Exemption
BLZ.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic or official passports under bilateral agreements between Belize and various countries.
BLZ.notes: Diplomatic and Official Passport holders are generally admitted for up to 30 days. Specific bilateral agreements extend exemptions to service and official passports of Hungary (90 days), Pakistan (90 days), Ecuador, Dominican Republic, and Venezuela (diplomatic/official only, ordinary passports require visas). Benelux states (Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg) diplomatic passport holders exempt under May 2025 agreement. Benin holders of diplomatic, official, service, and ordinary passports exempt under November 2024 agreement.

BOL.name: Visa de Turismo o Visita
BOL.purpose: Tourism, rest, recreation or visiting for nationals of Group II and Group III countries that require a visa (Group I nationals are visa-exempt).
BOL.notes: Fee US$30 for most nationalities (Resolucion Ministerial 081/2015 consular tariff). A US$160 sticker fee historically applied to US/Puerto Rico passports, now moot since the US moved to visa-free Group I on 1 Dec 2025. Maximum stay is 90 days per calendar year (DS 1923 Art. 9); initial 30-day stamp extendable twice. Visa-on-arrival for Group II nationals ended 25 July 2025 - the visa must be obtained in advance at a consulate. Group II apply ~20 calendar days ahead; Group III ~50-60 days with prior DIGEMIG consultation.

BOL.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Trabajo)
BOL.purpose: Foreign nationals entering to work/be employed in Bolivia; entry visa that must be converted to temporary residence (permanencia temporal) at DIGEMIG.
BOL.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular). Validity varies by purpose. Requires an invitation/employment letter from the Bolivian entity or company, a criminal-record certificate and proof of economic solvency. The holder has 30 days after entry to apply for temporary residence (permanencia temporal) before DIGEMIG.

BOL.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Trabajo Temporal)
BOL.purpose: Foreign nationals entering for temporary or seasonal work in Bolivia.
BOL.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular); free of charge when issued under an inter-state agreement/convenio (trabajo temporal con convenio estatal). Distinct consular line item from the standard Objeto Determinado work visa.

BOL.name: Visa de Estudiante
BOL.purpose: Foreign nationals enrolling in primary, secondary, institute or university studies (including academic exchanges) in Bolivia.
BOL.notes: Fee US$50 for regular students and exchange without a state agreement; free under a state exchange agreement (arancel consular). Valid up to 60 days, which enables the student to apply for a 1-year temporary residence (permanencia temporal) at DIGEMIG, renewable until studies are completed.

BOL.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Salud)
BOL.purpose: Foreign nationals entering Bolivia to receive medical treatment / for health reasons.
BOL.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular; 'objeto determinado - salud'). Health is an explicitly listed purpose of the Visa de Objeto Determinado. Unlike work/multiple visas, no invitation letter or proof of economic solvency is required for the health sub-purpose.

BOL.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Motivos Familiares)
BOL.purpose: Foreign nationals entering to join or reunite with family members resident in Bolivia.
BOL.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular; 'objeto determinado - familia'). Family is an explicitly listed purpose of the Visa de Objeto Determinado; no invitation letter or proof of economic solvency is required for the family sub-purpose. Typically converted to a family-based temporary residence at DIGEMIG.

BOL.name: Visa Multiple
BOL.purpose: Foreign investors and representatives of foreign companies carrying out investment and business activities in Bolivia; authorises repeated entry and exit.
BOL.notes: Fee US$200 (arancel consular). Valid 1 year with multiple entries; each stay must not exceed 90 consecutive days. Requires legalised company incorporation documents, the company's tax ID (NIT) if constituted in Bolivia, and an INTERPOL criminal-record certificate. This is Bolivia's investor/business entry visa.

BOL.name: Visa de Transito
BOL.purpose: Foreign nationals transiting through Bolivian territory to a third-country final destination, including vessel and aircraft crew.
BOL.notes: Free of charge (arancel consular). Maximum stay up to 15 days. Requires onward tickets proving the final destination is a third country.

BRA.name: e-Visa / Visitor Visa (VIVIS)
BRA.notes: Available to nationals of USA, Canada, and Australia under permanent e-visa regime (effective April 10, 2025 for US/Canada/Australia; permanent from January 1, 2026). Multiple-entry, up to 90 days per visit within 10-year validity (5-year for Australia/Canada). Fee approximately BRL 257 / USD 80.90. Applied via VFS Global portal. This is the Visitor Visa (VIVIS), the visit visa for tourism, business and transit (note: VITEM II is a separate health-treatment visa, not the visitor visa). France was briefly on e-visa then restored to visa-free (Feb 24, 2026). Argentina and Mexico remain visa-free as of June 2026 - not currently in e-visa regime.

BRA.name: Work Visa (VITEM V - Temporary Employment)
BRA.purpose: Employment in Brazil with Brazilian employer
BRA.notes: Employer-sponsored. Brazilian employer must obtain prior work authorization from Ministry of Justice (via MigranteWeb / temporary-residence authorization) before the visa is issued at a consulate. Valid up to 2 years, renewable. VITEM V code. Holders may apply for permanent residence after meeting residence requirements. After 4 years residence, may naturalize.

BRA.name: Student Visa (VITEM IV)
BRA.purpose: Full-time study at Brazilian educational institutions
BRA.notes: For enrollment in Brazilian public or private educational institution (courses lasting more than 90 days; shorter study uses the VIVIS visitor visa). Valid for course duration. Requires enrollment confirmation letter. VITEM IV code. Applied at Brazilian embassy/consulate. After completing study, must leave or obtain different authorization to remain.

BRA.name: Digital Nomad Visa (VITEM XIV - Nômade Digital)
BRA.purpose: Remote work for foreign employers while residing in Brazil
BRA.notes: For remote workers employed by or providing services to foreign companies/clients outside Brazil. Minimum income: USD 1,500/month or savings of USD 18,000. Requires health insurance (min USD 30,000 coverage), criminal background check (apostilled), employment contract or proof of freelance income from foreign sources. Initial 1-year validity, extendable 1 year (max 2 years). VITEM XIV code. Based on Normative Resolution RN 45/2021. In-country extension via MigranteWeb (BRL 168 fee). Also covers retirees and pensioners.

BRA.name: Business Visa (VIVIS - Visitor Visa)
BRA.purpose: Business meetings, events, fairs, contract signing, audit and consulting (no paid employment in Brazil)
BRA.notes: Brazil has no separate business visa: business travel uses the Visitor Visa (VIVIS), the same category as tourism, for stays up to 90 days. Paid employment in Brazil is prohibited, though reimbursement of expenses and allowances are permitted. Nationals of the US, Canada and Australia must instead obtain the electronic Visitor Visa (e-Visa) via VFS Global; most other nationals who require a visa apply at a Brazilian consulate. Consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity). Usually multiple-entry, at the discretion of the Brazilian government.

BRA.name: Medical Treatment Visa (VITEM II)
BRA.purpose: Foreigners undergoing health/medical treatment in Brazil expected to last more than 90 days
BRA.notes: Temporary visa for foreigners travelling to Brazil for health treatment expected to exceed 90 days (for treatment under 90 days the Visitor Visa/VIVIS is used). May be extended to an accompanying companion. Organ-transplant cases require a specific medical report accepted by the Brazilian Ministry of Health. Applied at a Brazilian consulate; consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity).

BRA.name: Research, Teaching & Academic Extension Visa (VITEM I)
BRA.purpose: Scientists, professors and researchers without a Brazilian employment contract staying over 90 days
BRA.notes: For scientists, professors, researchers or other professionals with no employment contract with a Brazilian institution who will stay more than 90 days - e.g. holders of research scholarships/grants or those working under an international cooperation agreement recognised by the Brazilian MFA. Distinct from the VITEM V employment work visa. Applied at a Brazilian consulate; consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity).

BRA.name: Artistic or Sports Activity Visa (VITEM XII)
BRA.purpose: Artists, performers and athletes coming to Brazil under contract for paid activity over 90 days
BRA.notes: For professional artists (musicians, performers, fashion models and their crew) and athletes coming to Brazil under contract to carry out paid artistic or sporting activity for more than 90 days. The Brazilian contractor must first obtain temporary-residence authorisation from the Ministry of Justice before the visa is issued at a consulate (exception: amateur athletes aged 14-18). Consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity).

BRA.name: Investor Visa (VITEM IX)
BRA.purpose: Foreign investors and company executives investing in a Brazilian company, startup or real estate
BRA.notes: Temporary-residence visa for investors. Official minimum investment thresholds: R$500,000 in a Brazilian company; R$150,000 in a Brazilian startup; or R$700,000 in real estate in the North/Northeast regions of Brazil. Also covers administrators/managers/directors of a foreign corporation supervising investment in a Brazilian counterpart. Process starts in Brazil: the Brazilian company must obtain temporary-residence authorisation from the Ministry of Justice before the visa is issued at a consulate. Consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity).

BRA.name: Working Holiday Visa (VITEM VI - Ferias-Trabalho)
BRA.purpose: Young travellers from partner countries working during a holiday in Brazil
BRA.notes: Vacation-work (ferias-trabalho) visa granted under bilateral working-holiday agreements. As of this update, only citizens of France and New Zealand may apply. Typically valid for 12 months. Applied at a Brazilian consulate; consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity).

BRA.name: Family Reunion Visa (VITEM XI)
BRA.purpose: Family members of Brazilian nationals or of foreigners legally resident in Brazil
BRA.notes: Allows family members (spouse/partner, children, parents, siblings, grandparents or grandchildren) of Brazilian nationals or of foreigners with legal residency in Brazil (RNM/RNE card or temporary-visa holders) to establish residence. May be requested concurrently with the sponsoring family member's own temporary visa, its issuance conditioned on the sponsor's temporary visa being granted first. Applied at a Brazilian consulate; consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity).

BRA.name: Retirement Visa (VITEM XIV - Aposentado)
BRA.purpose: Retirees and pensioners with stable income wishing to reside in Brazil
BRA.notes: Temporary-residence visa (VITEM XIV) for retirees/pensioners who can demonstrate stable, regular retirement or pension income transferred to Brazil. VITEM XIV is the same visa category that also covers digital nomads (tracked as a separate entry above). Applied at a Brazilian consulate; consular fee varies by nationality (reciprocity). Detailed income requirements are set by Brazilian immigration (CNIg) normative resolutions.

BRB.name: Barbados Entry Visa – Single Entry
BRB.purpose: Permits one entry into Barbados for tourism, visiting family, or other short-stay purposes. Required only for nationals of countries not covered by a visa waiver or abolition agreement.
BRB.notes: Single entry allows one visit within a three-month period from date of issue. Application is fully online via apps.immigration.gov.bb. Applicants submit Form J with supporting documents (passport copy, photograph, cover letter, employment/school letter, proof of funds, banker's draft payment). An entry visa is a pre-requisite but does not guarantee entry - immigration officers make final determination at the port of entry. Diplomatic corps members (whose countries require a visa) are exempt from payment of the fee but must still complete Form J.

BRB.name: Barbados Entry Visa – Multiple Entry
BRB.purpose: Permits multiple entries into Barbados within a six-month validity period for tourism, business visits, or family purposes.
BRB.notes: Multiple entry visa permits numerous entries within a six-month period from date of issue. Application is fully online via apps.immigration.gov.bb (formerly paper Form J). Processing takes approximately three weeks. Cruise ship passengers in transit or arriving/departing on cruise vessels, crew members transiting within 12 hours, and direct transit passengers staying under 12 hours may be exempt from standard visa requirements.

BRB.name: Barbados Entry Visa (Business Purpose)
BRB.purpose: Permits entry into Barbados for business meetings, conferences, or other commercial activities. Barbados does not issue a separate business visa category - the same single or multiple entry visa is used with business supporting documentation.
BRB.notes: Barbados does not operate a distinct business visa category. Applicants visiting for business purposes apply for the standard multiple-entry visa and must include a business-purpose cover letter and, if applicable, an employment letter from their sponsoring company. The visa category (single or multiple entry) is selected based on travel needs.

BRB.name: Work Permit
BRB.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to undertake paid employment in Barbados for a specified employer and occupation. This is the umbrella work-permit framework; it is issued as either a short-term or long-term permit.
BRB.notes: Issued under Section 17 of the Immigration Act CAP 190. Work permits are employer-sponsored and occupation-specific - the employer or 'sponsor' makes the application on behalf of the employee. Application fee is BDS $300 (~USD 150); the final fee for long-term permits varies with the category of work and length of time requested per the International Standard Code Fee Regulations. Permits are issued in two forms: short-term (up to 11 months) and long-term (up to 3 years). SERP Category 1 holders (investors of at least USD $2 million) are also entitled to a work permit. Foreign nationals wishing to work in Barbados typically need both an entry visa (if their nationality requires one) and a work permit issued by the Chief Immigration Officer.

BRB.name: Short-Term Work Permit
BRB.purpose: Authorises a non-national to work for a specified employer in Barbados for a short engagement of up to eleven months.
BRB.notes: Issued under Section 17 of the Immigration Act CAP 190 for a period of up to eleven (11) months. The employer or 'sponsor' applies on the employee's behalf. Application fee BDS $300 (~USD 150). Short-term work permit appointments can be booked via the dedicated system at immigration.gov.bb/pages/STWP.aspx. Unlike long-term permits, short-term permits do not require the employer to demonstrate that no Barbadian or resident could fill the position.

BRB.name: Long-Term Work Permit
BRB.purpose: Authorises a non-national to work for a specified employer in Barbados for an extended engagement of up to three years.
BRB.notes: Issued under Section 17 of the Immigration Act CAP 190 for a period of up to three (3) years. Application fee BDS $300 (~USD 150); the final fee varies depending on the category of work and the length of time requested, in accordance with the International Standard Code Fee Regulations. The employer must demonstrate that no resident or Barbadian national is capable and willing to fill the position. The employer or 'sponsor' applies on the employee's behalf.

BRB.name: Training Attachment Permit
BRB.purpose: Permits a non-national to undertake a short-term training or skills-transfer placement with a Barbadian employer.
BRB.notes: A short-term work-permit sub-category under Section 17 of the Immigration Act CAP 190 for training and skills-transfer placements. Requires the same documents as a short-term work permit and carries the BDS $300 (~USD 150) application fee, but does NOT carry a final/approval fee - making it an economical option for skills-transfer placements. The employer or sponsor applies on the trainee's behalf.

BRB.name: Student Visa
BRB.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to reside in Barbados for the purpose of full-time study at a recognised educational institution.
BRB.notes: Student visas are listed as a distinct category on the Barbados Immigration Department's services page. Applicants must provide a letter of enrollment from the educational institution. Entry visa applicants studying in Barbados must submit their school enrollment letter with their Form J application. Specific fee schedule is managed through the immigration portal at apps.immigration.gov.bb.

BRB.name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
BRB.purpose: Permits remote workers, freelancers, and location-independent entrepreneurs to live and work in Barbados for up to 12 months while employed by or serving clients outside Barbados.
BRB.notes: Introduced June 30, 2020 under the Immigration Act (Form C-5). Renewable for additional 12-month periods. Individual fee: USD $2,000; Family fee: USD $3,000 (non-refundable, due within 28 days of approval). Minimum annual income requirement: USD $50,000. Participants may not accept employment from or offer services to persons or entities conducting business in Barbados. Welcome Stamp holders are not subject to Barbados income tax during the 12-month period (17.5% VAT on goods and services still applies). Cabinet approved renewal of the programme until December 31, 2026 at its meeting of October 26, 2023. Application via barbadoswelcomestamp.bb/applynow. Processing approximately 7 business days.

BRB.name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) – Category 1 (Investor)
BRB.purpose: Grants long-term residence and work authorisation to foreign nationals who invest at least USD $2 million in Barbados from funds sourced outside the country.
BRB.notes: Requires investment of at least USD $2 million sourced from outside Barbados, plus demonstrated net worth exceeding USD $5 million. Category 1 SERP holders are entitled to a work permit. Official immigration.gov.bb lists a BDS $300 application fee; secondary sources cite USD $3,500 (under 60) and USD $5,000 (over 60) but these could not be confirmed from the official government page.

BRB.name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) – Category 2 (Real Estate)
BRB.purpose: Grants long-term residence rights to foreign nationals who own property in Barbados valued at a minimum of USD $300,000.
BRB.notes: Requires ownership of Barbados property valued at minimum USD $300,000. Renewable 5-year permit. Category 2 SERP holders are not eligible for a work permit. Official immigration.gov.bb lists application fee of BDS $300.

BRB.name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) – Category 3 (Special Skills)
BRB.purpose: Grants long-term residence rights to foreign nationals who possess special skills deemed critical to the growth and development of Barbados.
BRB.notes: No investment threshold required. Eligibility determined by the Chief Immigration Officer based on assessment of the applicant's skills and their value to Barbados's development. No specific fee, processing time or validity period was available from the official immigration.gov.bb page.

BRB.name: Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) – Category 4 (Parents/Grandparents of Citizens)
BRB.purpose: Grants long-term residence rights to parents or grandparents of Barbadian citizens who are over 60 years of age.
BRB.notes: Available to parents or grandparents of Barbadian citizens who are aged 60 or over. No investment threshold. Applicant must demonstrate the family relationship to a Barbadian citizen. No specific fee or processing timeline was available from the official immigration.gov.bb page.

BRB.name: Permanent Resident Status
BRB.purpose: Grants indefinite residence in Barbados to qualifying long-term residents, spouses of Barbadians, and other applicants who meet the statutory criteria.
BRB.notes: Governed by Section 5 of the Immigration Act CAP 190. Applicants file 'Application for Registration as a Permanent Resident - Form A1' with a birth certificate, police character certificates for each country lived in for 6+ months over the past three years, a medical certificate, four passport photographs, an employment letter and proof of qualifications. Fees: BDS $300 (~USD 150) initial submission fee plus a BDS $1,200 (~USD 600) approval fee. All fees are payable on submission of the application.

BRB.name: Immigrant Status
BRB.purpose: Confers settled immigrant status on qualifying non-nationals, including spouses of Barbadian citizens and long-term residents.
BRB.notes: Granted under Section 6 / sub-section 13(7) of the Immigration Act CAP 190. Applicants file 'Application for Immigrant Status and Non-National Registration - Form A' (three certified copies for adults) with a birth certificate, medical report, police character certificates, passport bio-data page, employment letter and proof of qualifications. Application fee BDS $300 (~USD 150) plus a BDS $1,200 (~USD 600) approval fee if granted. A distinct settlement category from Permanent Resident Status (which falls under Section 5).

BRB.name: Extension of Stay
BRB.purpose: Allows a visitor already in Barbados to apply to extend the length of stay granted to them at the port of entry.
BRB.notes: Listed as a distinct service ('Extensions of Stay') by the Barbados Immigration Department. Visitors whose initial permitted stay is coming to an end apply to the Immigration Department to extend their stay in Barbados. The fee and maximum extension are set under the Immigration (Forms and Fees) Regulations, Cap 190 and were not published on the online services page.

BRB.name: Transit Exemption (Cruise/Air)
BRB.purpose: Exempts certain transit passengers from requiring a Barbados entry visa when transiting the country for less than 12 hours or arriving as cruise passengers in transit.
BRB.notes: The following categories are exempt from the standard entry visa requirement: (1) cruise ship passengers in transit or arriving/departing on vessels; (2) crew members transiting within 12 hours; (3) direct transit passengers staying under 12 hours. Diplomatic corps members whose countries require a visa are exempt from the visa fee but must still complete Form J. These exemptions are stated on the official Barbados Immigration Department visa requirements page.

BRB.name: Diplomatic/Official Passport Entry
BRB.purpose: Allows holders of diplomatic or official passports to enter Barbados with reduced formalities, including fee waivers and, in some cases, full visa exemptions regardless of nationality.
BRB.notes: All members of the Diplomatic Corps (of countries that require a visa to enter Barbados) are exempt from payment of the entry visa fee, but must still complete Form J. Some nationalities are visa-free for diplomatic/official passport holders but not for ordinary passport holders (e.g., Haiti: no visa required for Official and Diplomatic passport holders, but visa required for regular passport holders). The full diplomatic-passport nationality list is detailed in the official MFA PDF at foreign.gov.bb.

BRN.name: Social Visit Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued for the purpose of social visits or tourism to Brunei Darussalam. Requires advance application through the nearest Brunei mission abroad for Category A/B nationals.
BRN.notes: Processing is 3 working days at HQ/Kuala Belait, 5 working days at Temburong. Must be applied through Brunei missions abroad. Terms and conditions apply.

BRN.name: Visa on Arrival – Category C1 (30 days)
BRN.purpose: Short-stay visa issued on arrival at Brunei International Airport for nationals of eligible Category C1 countries (e.g. Australia, Kuwait ordinary/diplomatic/special passport).
BRN.notes: Fee: BND 20.00 (single entry) or BND 30.00 (multiple entry). Applicants fill in Visa Form and arrival card available on incoming flights. Business/professional visits require separate sponsored application even for C1 nationals.

BRN.name: Visa on Arrival – Category C2 (14 days, single entry)
BRN.purpose: Short-stay single-entry visa issued on arrival for nationals of eligible Category C2 countries (e.g. Saudi Arabia).
BRN.notes: Fee: BND 20.00. Single entry only. Applicants fill in Visa Form and arrival card available on incoming flights.

BRN.name: Visa on Arrival – Category C3 (14 days)
BRN.purpose: Short-stay visa issued on arrival for nationals of eligible Category C3 countries (e.g. Qatar). Single or multiple entry options available.
BRN.notes: Fee: BND 20.00. Single or multiple entry available. Business/professional visits require sponsored application processed in 3–5 working days.

BRN.name: Visa on Arrival – Category C4 (14 days)
BRN.purpose: Short-stay visa issued on arrival for nationals of eligible Category C4 countries (e.g. Bahrain). Single or multiple entry options available.
BRN.notes: Fee: BND 20.00 (single entry) or BND 30.00 (multiple entry).

BRN.name: Business Visit Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued for the purpose of investment or business-related activities in Brunei Darussalam. Must be sponsored by a registered company or government entity in Brunei.
BRN.notes: Processing: 3 working days at HQ/Kuala Belait, 5 working days at Temburong. Requires sponsorship from a registered Brunei company or government agency. Even nationals who qualify for visa-free/VoA general entry must apply separately for Business Visit status. Applications submitted to Department of Immigration and National Registration; visa stamp collected at nearest Brunei mission abroad.

BRN.name: Employment Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued for the purpose of taking up employment in Brunei Darussalam.
BRN.notes: Must be applied through Brunei missions abroad. Typically requires a sponsor/employer in Brunei. Terms and conditions apply. Separate from the work permit (Pas Kerja) which is processed by the Department of Immigration and National Registration after entry.

BRN.name: Professional Visit Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued for the purpose of professional work or expertise required for a particular project in Brunei Darussalam.
BRN.notes: Processing: 3 working days at HQ/Kuala Belait, 5 working days at Temburong. Must be sponsored by a government agency or registered company in Brunei. Even nationals qualifying for visa-free/VoA general entry must apply separately for Professional Visit status.

BRN.name: Work Pass (Pas Kerja)
BRN.purpose: Mandatory work authorization issued by the Department of Immigration and National Registration to foreign nationals taking up employment in Brunei. Must be held in addition to a valid Employment Visa.
BRN.notes: Official requirement per the Work Pass Division: foreign nationals working in Brunei must hold BOTH a valid visa AND a valid work pass. The employer's representative first obtains a work visa approval letter; the employee then attends a Brunei mission abroad for the work visa endorsement (with medical check and travel document) before the work pass is issued. Companion document to the Employment Visa, not a substitute for it.

BRN.name: Student Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued for the purpose of studying in Brunei Darussalam at a recognized institution.
BRN.notes: Must be applied through Brunei missions abroad. Requires enrollment confirmation from an institution in Brunei. Terms and conditions apply.

BRN.name: Transit Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued to any person who is in transit and en route to a third country via Brunei Darussalam.
BRN.notes: Maximum stay 72 hours (3 days), per the official MFA Types of Visa page. Transit visas are only issued at Brunei International Airport (granted at the point of transit). Terms and conditions apply.

BRN.name: Dependent Visa
BRN.purpose: Issued to spouses and children (under 18 years old) of foreign nationals residing in Brunei Darussalam.
BRN.notes: Dependent visas cover spouses and children under 18. Must be applied through Brunei missions abroad. Terms and conditions apply.

BRN.name: Diplomatic Visa
BRN.purpose: Visa issued to foreign nationals holding a diplomatic passport travelling on official business.
BRN.notes: Many countries with diplomatic passport holders are granted visa-free access (Category D2/D3) under bilateral agreements. The Diplomatic Visa applies to those not covered by waiver arrangements. See also Forms for Diplomats on the MFA website.

BRN.name: Long-Term Business Visit Pass
BRN.purpose: Long-term multiple-entry pass for company owners and foreign investors who meet Brunei's economic contribution criteria, including local job creation and tax compliance.
BRN.notes: Valid up to 5 years with multiple-entry. Excludes convenience stores, restaurants, laundries, salons, and non-registered companies. No minimum investment amount stated officially. Pass may be revoked for law violations or failure to provide economic benefits. Effective from 31 December 2024. Does not explicitly lead to permanent residence.

BRN.name: Long-Term Professional Visit Pass
BRN.purpose: Long-term multiple-entry pass for foreign experts and professionals whose expertise is determined to be beneficial and needed for Brunei's national development.
BRN.notes: Valid up to 5 years. Granted based on national needs as determined by relevant government bodies. No minimum salary or investment amount stated officially. Effective from 31 December 2024.

BRN.name: Long-Term Social Visit Pass
BRN.purpose: Long-term pass for foreign nationals with family ties to Brunei citizens or permanent residents who do not yet meet criteria for permanent residency.
BRN.notes: Valid up to 5 years. For those with family ties to Brunei citizens or permanent residents. Effective from 31 December 2024.

BTN.name: Tourist Visa / Entry Permit (e-Visa)
BTN.purpose: Tourism and leisure visits to Bhutan for nationals of all countries except India, Bangladesh, and Maldives. Must be arranged through a licensed Bhutanese tour operator.
BTN.notes: Non-refundable visa application fee of USD 40. Additionally, a Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of USD 100 per person per day is mandatory. Application submitted online at immi.gov.bt through a licensed tour operator or hotel. Visa is electronic (stamp-less); e-Gates operational at Paro International Airport and Phuntsholing Pedestrian Terminal. Passport must have minimum 6 months validity from departure date. Travel insurance is mandatory.

BTN.name: Tourist Entry Permit (India)
BTN.purpose: Entry permit for Indian nationals visiting Bhutan for tourism or personal purposes, under the 1949 India-Bhutan Treaty of Friendship.
BTN.notes: Indian nationals receive an Entry Permit (not a visa) on arrival at port of entry or via advance online application at immi.gov.bt. Indian Voter Identity Card accepted in lieu of passport. OCI/PIO card holders do NOT qualify and must obtain a standard visa. No SDF applies to Indian nationals.

BTN.name: Visa on Arrival (Bangladesh & Maldives)
BTN.purpose: Visa stamped on passport at the port of entry for Bangladeshi and Maldivian nationals visiting Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Bangladeshi and Maldivian nationals do not require advance visa clearance. Visa is issued at the port of entry. Valid passport with minimum 6 months validity required. A recommendation letter from a local host or counterpart may be required.

BTN.name: Business Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Bhutan to establish or conduct business activities with prior government approval.
BTN.notes: Requires documentary evidence of government approval for the business activity. Applied through the Department of Immigration. Specific fees and validity periods are not published on official sources.

BTN.name: Investor / Promoter Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign investors and promoters engaged in approved investment projects in Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Requires prior approval from the Director, Department of Industry, Ministry of Industry Commerce and Employment (MoICE). Valid passport with minimum 6 months validity and a detailed day-wise program required. Does not confer permanent residency or path to citizenship. Minimum investment amount not published.

BTN.name: Employment Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals authorized to work in Bhutan under an approved employment arrangement.
BTN.notes: Maximum period of one year (renewable). Requires employer approval from the Department of Labour. Associated Work Permit must also be obtained through the Department of Immigration. Specific fees not published on official sources.

BTN.name: Student Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in an approved academic institution or course of study in Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Duration corresponds to the length of the approved course. Requires institutional approval from the relevant Bhutanese educational authority. Specific fees not published on official sources.

BTN.name: Dependent Visa
BTN.purpose: For immediate family members of foreign nationals holding a valid work permit or employment visa in Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Tied to the validity of the principal visa holder's work permit. Specific fees and detailed eligibility criteria not published on official sources reviewed.

BTN.name: Personal Guest Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Bhutan as personal guests at the invitation of a Bhutanese citizen or resident.
BTN.notes: Maximum stay of 30 days or the actual duration of stay, whichever is less. Each Bhutanese host is limited to inviting a maximum of two personal guests per year. A formal invitation letter from the Bhutanese host is required.

BTN.name: Diplomatic Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals holding diplomatic passports visiting Bhutan for official diplomatic purposes or postings/assignments.
BTN.notes: Gratis (no fee) for eligible diplomatic passport holders. UN passport holders also receive gratis visas. Holders of diplomatic/official passports from Thailand and Switzerland receive Visa on Arrival under bilateral agreements. Other diplomatic passport holders must apply through the Department of Immigration.

BTN.name: Official Visa
BTN.purpose: For foreign government representatives, official delegations, and official passport holders visiting Bhutan on official government business.
BTN.notes: Gratis (no fee) for eligible official passport holders. Requires documentation of official purpose and government delegation status.

BTN.name: Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) Digital Nomad Residence
BTN.purpose: Residence programme for remote workers, freelancers, entrepreneurs, and professionals employed by entities outside Bhutan, based in the Gelephu Mindfulness City special administrative zone.
BTN.notes: Launched February 2026 by the Gelephu Mindfulness City Authority (GMCA). Annual fee of USD 2,800 (non-refundable). Mandatory refundable deposit of USD 10,000 in TER tokens (Solana blockchain gold-backed digital token by DK Bank), fully refundable on exit. Valid 12 months, renewable for up to 24 months total. Residents may travel throughout Bhutan but must pay USD 100/day SDF outside GMC. Application portal operated by private partner NomadClub (digitalgmc.com), not a .gov.bt domain.

BTN.name: Work Permit
BTN.purpose: Labour authorization for foreign nationals aged 18 or over employed in Bhutan; issued by the Department of Immigration after Department of Labour approval. Separate from and in addition to the Employment Visa/Entry Permit.
BTN.notes: Requires prior approval from the Department of Labour (MoICE), a completed Work Permit application form, Employer and Employee Undertakings, and a Medical Fitness Certificate (general health and drug test) from a Bhutan government-certified medical officer. Applicant must be at least 18 years old. As of 7 May 2026, a Bhutanese bank account is mandatory for any foreign worker staying more than 30 days. Day workers and process workers in border towns are processed under this category.

BTN.name: Student Permit
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals (including monks and nuns) enrolled in a regular academic, monastic, or exchange study program at a government-approved institution in Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Governed by the Visa/Entry Permit Guideline for International Students, 2026 (effective 01 May 2026). Not renewed beyond the length of the course of study. Vetting agency depends on the institution: RUB, KGUMSB, Ministry of Education and Skills Development (schools), Dratshang Lhentshog (monastic institutions), or RIM/JSW Law School/Druk Gyalpoi Institute. Distinct from and issued alongside the Student Visa/Entry Permit.

BTN.name: Route Permit
BTN.purpose: Mandatory internal-movement permit allowing valid immigration permit/visa holders (including all non-tourist categories) to travel to restricted or protected areas within Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Issued only upon arrival in Bhutan, valid for a period not exceeding thirty days at a time. Mandatory for all non-tourist categories for movement within the country. This is not an international transit visa - it governs travel through restricted internal areas of Bhutan.

BTN.name: Trader Permit
BTN.purpose: For expatriate traders (primarily Indian nationals in the southern border towns) holding a valid business licence and trader card, and their direct dependents, engaged in cross-border commerce.
BTN.notes: Requires a valid business licence and trader card. Renewal is based on recommendations from the Ministry of Economic Affairs / Department of Trade. Vetted jointly by the Department of Immigration, Department of Trade, and MoFAET.

BTN.name: Spouse of a Bhutanese National (Visa/Entry Permit)
BTN.purpose: For foreign nationals married to a Bhutanese citizen, and their legitimate children, to reside in Bhutan on the basis of the family relationship.
BTN.notes: Classified as non-tourist category 1. Requires an application from the Bhutanese spouse/parent, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates, and the Bhutanese spouse's/parent's CID. If the spouse is entering to seek immigrant status, the marriage certificate must be issued by the Royal Court of Justice, Bhutan. Application is submitted directly to the Department of Immigration.

BTN.name: Journalist / Media Visa
BTN.purpose: For journalists and media personnel visiting Bhutan for professional media work, including coverage of state or national events.
BTN.notes: Classified as non-tourist category 22. Requires approval from MoFAET, plus accreditation from BICMA when covering state or national events such as elections or summit meetings. Passport must be valid for at least six months.

BTN.name: Sports Professional Visa (incl. International Professional Football Player)
BTN.purpose: For sports professionals - athletes, players on contract with licensed clubs, and trainers - taking part in sporting events or engaged by clubs in Bhutan.
BTN.notes: Classified as non-tourist category 24. Requires approval from the General Secretary, Bhutan Olympic Committee (BOC) and political clearance from MoFAET. International professional football players engaged by Bhutanese clubs are processed under the Visa/Entry Permit Guidelines for International Professional Football Player, 2019 of the Department of Immigration.

BWA.name: Tourist Visa - Single Entry
BWA.purpose: Tourism activities in Botswana for up to one month. Requires a tour plan, hotel confirmations, proof of employment or business, and bank statement.
BWA.notes: Processing is stated as 21 working days. Apply via evisa.gov.bw or at a Botswana embassy/consulate. Passport must have at least 6 months validity and 3 unused pages.

BWA.name: Tourist Visa - Multiple Entry
BWA.purpose: Multiple-entry tourism visa for Botswana valid for up to three months. Requires tour plan, hotel confirmations, proof of employment or business, and bank statement.
BWA.notes: Processing is stated as 21 working days. Apply via evisa.gov.bw or at a Botswana embassy/consulate.

BWA.name: Visitor Visa - Single Entry
BWA.purpose: For visiting friends, family, or general visitation purposes for up to three months. Requires invitation letter from host, hotel bookings or residential address, host's affidavit, and financial documentation.
BWA.notes: Processing is stated as 21 working days. Separate from tourist visa; intended for visiting hosts rather than general tourism.

BWA.name: Visitor Visa - Multiple Entry (up to 3 months)
BWA.purpose: Multiple-entry visitor visa for visiting friends or family in Botswana for up to three months. Requires invitation letter from host, hotel bookings or residential address, host's affidavit, and financial documentation.
BWA.notes: Processing is stated as 21 working days.

BWA.name: Visitor Visa - Multiple Entry (Dependents, up to 2 years)
BWA.purpose: Long-validity multiple-entry visitor visa for dependents visiting a resident in Botswana for over three months and up to two years.
BWA.notes: Validity covers over 3 months up to 2 years. Intended for dependents of residents. Processing is stated as 21 working days.

BWA.name: Business Visa - Single Entry
BWA.purpose: For business meetings, establishing enterprises, or professional engagement in Botswana for up to three months. Requires business profile, meeting schedule, and host invitation.
BWA.notes: Labour clearance required if staying 30 or more days. Processing is stated as 21 working days.

BWA.name: Business Visa - Multiple Entry (up to 3 months)
BWA.purpose: Multiple-entry business visa for conducting business meetings, enterprise activities, or professional engagements in Botswana for up to three months.
BWA.notes: Labour clearance required if staying 30 or more days. Processing is stated as 21 working days.

BWA.name: Business Visa - Multiple Entry (6 months to 1 year)
BWA.purpose: Long-validity multiple-entry business visa for ongoing business activities in Botswana for up to one year.
BWA.notes: Validity covers 6 months to 1 year. Labour clearance required if staying 30 or more days. Processing is stated as 21 working days.

BWA.name: Employment Visa
BWA.purpose: Authorizes non-citizens to travel to Botswana for employment, internship, research, work, or voluntary services. A valid work permit and residence permit must already be held.
BWA.notes: The Employment Visa is the entry visa; a separate Work Permit and Residence Permit are prerequisites. The dedicated gov.bw Employment Visa page states processing of 7-14 working days and does not publish a fee. (official_url updated July 2026 from the generic Embassy guidelines page to the dedicated gov.bw Employment Visa application page; the Embassy fee schedule does not list a separate employment-visa fee.)

BWA.name: Investor Visa - Multiple Entry (up to 6 months)
BWA.purpose: For foreign nationals investing in Botswana, allowing multiple entries for up to six months. Requires certificate of incorporation, trade license, and financial documentation.
BWA.notes: Processing is stated as 21 working days. Investors may separately apply for Permanent Residence - Investor Category via gov.bw.

BWA.name: Investor Visa - Multiple Entry (up to 5 years)
BWA.purpose: Long-validity multiple-entry visa for established foreign investors in Botswana, valid for up to five years. Requires certificate of incorporation, trade license, share valuations, and financial documentation.
BWA.notes: Processing is stated as 21 working days. The 5-year investor visa is the longest validity category listed on the Embassy fee schedule.

BWA.name: Transit Visa
BWA.purpose: For travellers passing through Botswana to reach an onward destination, permitting a short stay while in transit.
BWA.notes: No visa is required if departing on the same aircraft from the same airport. Maximum stay is 7 days; the visa does not permit work or formal study/training and cannot be extended. Transporters and tour operators (holding a cross-border tour operating licence) may transit for up to 7 days per entry. Requires proof of a confirmed onward booking / continuing journey within 3 days (14 days for transporters). Fee not published on the gov.bw page; processing 7-14 working days.

BWA.name: Study Visa
BWA.purpose: For non-citizens who have been accepted by an educational institution in Botswana and require a visa to enter to study.
BWA.notes: The Study Visa is the entry visa; a separate Study/Research Permit is a prerequisite to study. Required documents include a letter of acceptance from the educational institution, the study/research permit, and proof of sponsorship. Fee not published on the gov.bw page; processing 7-14 working days.

BWA.name: Botswana Blue Card
BWA.purpose: Grants former Botswana citizens who have renounced their citizenship the right to unlimited stay in Botswana, including visitation, residency, and work privileges.
BWA.notes: Eligibility is restricted to former Botswana citizens (those who renounced citizenship after being born in or descended from Botswana). Spouses and children born after renunciation are not eligible unless they independently qualify. Blue Card holders cannot obtain an Omang (national ID) or Botswana passport. The $300 fee is non-refundable. Required documents: completed application form, certified passport copy, renunciation certificate, acquired citizenship proof, two passport photos.

CAF.name: Visa Court Séjour - Tourisme (Short-Stay Tourist Visa)
CAF.purpose: Short-term entry for tourism and leisure purposes. Applied at a CAR embassy or consulate abroad.
CAF.notes: Fee schedule from CAR Embassy Washington: 0–1 month $150, express processing +$50. Application requires passport, 2 ID photos, and supporting documents. Postal return requires stamped envelope with CHRONOPOST insurance. E-visa option (evisa-centrafrique.com) exists but operational status unconfirmed.

CAF.name: Visa Court Séjour 45 Jours (Short-Stay 45-Day Visa)
CAF.purpose: Short-term entry visa valid for up to 45 days, for tourism or short business visits.
CAF.notes: Fee schedule from CAR Embassy Washington: 45 days $175, express processing +$50. Applied at CAR embassies/consulates abroad.

CAF.name: Visa Court Séjour - Affaires (Short-Stay Business Visa, 2–3 Months)
CAF.purpose: Entry visa for business purposes valid for two to three months.
CAF.notes: Fee schedule from CAR Embassy Washington: 2–3 months $250, express processing +$50. Applied at CAR embassies/consulates abroad.

CAF.name: Visa Court Séjour - Long Duration (Short-Stay Visa 3+ Months)
CAF.purpose: Short-stay visa for stays exceeding three months, for purposes such as extended visits, research, or short-term professional assignments.
CAF.notes: Fee schedule from CAR Embassy Washington: 3+ months $300, express processing +$50. Exact maximum stay not specified in official sources; long-stay visa (visa long séjour) is the formal category for extended residence.

CAF.name: Visa Long Séjour (Long-Stay Visa)
CAF.purpose: Long-term entry visa for work, study, family reunification, or extended residence in the Central African Republic. Issued by CAR embassies and consulates abroad.
CAF.notes: Official category listed by the CAR Embassy in Paris. Application accepts online form (with account creation) or paper PDF form. Payment by bank transfer or cash at embassy. Specific fee, validity, and stay duration not published on accessible official pages. Covers work, study, and residence purposes.

CAF.name: E-Visa (Visa Électronique Touristique)
CAF.purpose: Electronic tourist visa for individual or group tourism, available via the CAR Ministry of Foreign Affairs-referenced e-visa portal. Entry only permitted at Bangui M'Poko International Airport.
CAF.notes: Operated by DigitalGate SARL (third-party referencing CAR MFA); portal's explicit 'testing mode' notice was absent on 2026-06-29 re-fetch but e-visa processing operational status is unconfirmed from any official .gouv.cf source. Stay duration 1–180 days. Cannot be extended inside or outside CAR. Entry only at Bangui city airport. Visa-exempt nationalities and VoA holders are excluded from this requirement. Not a .gouv.cf official government domain.

CAF.name: Visa Diplomatique / Officiel (Diplomatic/Official Visa)
CAF.purpose: Visa for holders of diplomatic or official passports travelling to the Central African Republic on official business. Despite diplomatic passport status, a visa is still required.
CAF.notes: CAR Embassy Washington confirmed in prior verification: 'No change. Visa applications will be processed by the Embassy' for diplomatic/official passport holders - no exemption exists. Effective February 12, 2024, embassy staff, UN, EU, NGO personnel, and international organization contractors must obtain prior MFA authorization before entering CAR.

CAN.name: Temporary Resident Visa (Visitor Visa)
CAN.purpose: Tourism, visiting family, short business trips
CAN.notes: Apply online via IRCC. Most nationalities require a TRV; some require only an eTA. Fee is CAD 100.

CAN.name: Study Permit
CAN.purpose: Studying at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) for programs longer than 6 months
CAN.notes: Requires acceptance letter from a DLI. Fee is CAD 150. Students can work up to 20 hours/week off-campus.

CAN.name: Work Permit (Employer-Specific)
CAN.purpose: Working for a specific Canadian employer
CAN.notes: Tied to one employer, job and location. Most require a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) from the employer; CUSMA/USMCA and CETA provide LMIA-exempt streamlined pathways for US, Mexican, and EU nationals. Fee is CAD 155.

CAN.name: International Experience Canada (IEC) – Working Holiday
CAN.purpose: Living and working in Canada for up to 1–2 years (youth, select nationalities)
CAN.notes: Available for youth 18–35 from over 30 countries via bilateral agreements. Apply through IEC portal. Total fee is CAD 284.75 (CAD 184.75 IEC participation fee + CAD 100 open work permit holder fee), per the IRCC fee list updated 2026-07-02.

CAN.name: Business Visitor
CAN.purpose: Short business trips: attend meetings, conferences and events, buy Canadian goods, or receive/give after-sales service — without entering the Canadian labour market
CAN.notes: Not a separate visa: a business visitor travels on a visitor visa (TRV, CAD 100) or an eTA (CAD 7) depending on nationality. No work permit needed. Main source of income and principal place of business must remain outside Canada. Stay up to 6 months.

CAN.name: Transit Visa
CAN.purpose: Visa-required nationals passing through a Canadian airport en route to another country, transiting in 48 hours or less
CAN.notes: Free of charge (no processing fee). Required for visa-required nationals connecting through a Canadian airport for 48 hours or less. Not needed if you already hold a valid Canadian visitor visa or are eTA-eligible and flying. Separate from the Transit Without Visa (TWOV) and China Transit programs.

CAN.name: Open Work Permit
CAN.purpose: Work for almost any employer in Canada with no job offer or LMIA required (e.g., spouses of skilled workers/students, PGWP holders, IEC, PR applicants, vulnerable workers)
CAN.notes: Not job-specific — no LMIA, job offer or employer compliance fee needed. Available only in specific situations (spouses/common-law partners of skilled workers or students, PGWP holders, IEC Working Holiday, PR applicants, protected persons, vulnerable workers). Fee CAD 255 (CAD 155 work permit + CAD 100 open work permit holder fee).

CAN.name: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)
CAN.purpose: Graduates of eligible Canadian designated learning institutions (DLIs) to gain Canadian work experience after finishing their studies
CAN.notes: Open work permit for graduates of eligible DLIs. Length matches the study program (minimum 8 months) up to a maximum of 3 years; issued once per person. Fee CAD 255 (CAD 155 work permit + CAD 100 open work permit holder fee). Field-of-study and language eligibility criteria apply following the 2024–2025 reforms.

CAN.name: Super Visa (Parents and Grandparents)
CAN.purpose: Parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens or permanent residents to visit for extended periods
CAN.notes: Multiple-entry visa valid up to 10 years; each stay up to 5 years per entry (extendable by up to 2 more years from inside Canada). Requires qualifying medical insurance and proof the host child/grandchild meets the minimum income (LICO). Dependants cannot be included. Fee CAD 100 (same as a visitor visa).

CAN.name: Spouse or Common-Law Partner Sponsorship (Family Class)
CAN.purpose: A Canadian citizen or permanent resident sponsoring a spouse, common-law/conjugal partner or dependent child for permanent residence
CAN.notes: Family-class permanent residence pathway (not a temporary visa). Sponsor must be 18+ and a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Total fee CAD 1,260 (includes sponsorship, processing and right of permanent residence fees). A spouse/partner being sponsored from inside Canada may also apply for an open work permit while the application is processed.

CHE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Category C) – Tourism/Visit
CHE.purpose: Covers tourism, visiting family or friends, and cultural or sports events in Switzerland and the Schengen Area for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
CHE.notes: Fee is EUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for children aged 6–12; free for EU/EFTA family members. Multiple-entry visas valid up to 5 years may be issued to frequent compliant travelers. Apply at swiss-visa.ch or directly at a Swiss representation. Valid across all Schengen member states.

CHE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Category C) – Business
CHE.purpose: Permits short-term business activities such as meetings, conferences, and negotiations in Switzerland for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Does not authorize gainful employment.
CHE.notes: Same Category C fee structure as tourist visa (EUR 90 adults). Gainful employment requires an additional work permit. Business activities in sectors such as construction, catering, cleaning, security require a separate work authorization even for short stays.

CHE.name: Airport Transit Visa
CHE.purpose: Required for certain nationalities transiting through a Swiss international airport without entering Schengen territory, remaining in the international transit zone.
CHE.notes: Fee EUR 90 (standard Schengen visa fee). Required only for nationalities listed on the common Schengen Airport Transit Visa list. Travelers with a valid Schengen visa, residence permit, or valid visa from specific countries (USA, Canada, Japan, etc.) may be exempt.

CHE.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Category D) – Employment
CHE.purpose: Issued to non-EU/EFTA nationals approved for gainful employment in Switzerland, covering stays exceeding 90 days. Accompanies a B permit (residence permit) issued by cantonal authorities.
CHE.notes: Strictly restricted to managers, specialists, and highly qualified workers (university degree + experience). Employer must prove no suitable Swiss or EU/EFTA candidate available. Annual federal quotas apply. Canton processes the permit application; SEM approves. Fee EUR 90 base plus up to 50% surcharge for urgent processing. EU/EFTA nationals are not subject to these restrictions under the Agreement on Free Movement of Persons.

CHE.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Category D) – Education/Vocational Training
CHE.purpose: Issued to non-EU/EFTA nationals accepted for study or vocational training programs in Switzerland for stays exceeding 90 days.
CHE.notes: Requires enrollment confirmation from a Swiss educational institution recognized by cantonal authorities. Canton processes application; SEM approves. Limited part-time work may be permitted alongside studies. Processing takes one to several months depending on canton.

CHE.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Category D) – Family Reunification
CHE.purpose: Issued to non-EU/EFTA family members joining a Swiss citizen or lawful resident in Switzerland for stays exceeding 90 days.
CHE.notes: Cantonal authorities process family reunification permits. Sponsor must demonstrate sufficient financial means and adequate housing. Processing time is one to several months. Family members of EU/EFTA citizens benefit from faster processing under free movement rules; visa issued free of charge to EU/EFTA family members.

CHE.name: Working Holiday Permit / Youth Mobility Visa
CHE.purpose: Allows young nationals from partner countries to live and work in Switzerland temporarily, combining travel with work experience.
CHE.notes: Switzerland maintains bilateral youth mobility / working holiday agreements with a limited number of countries including Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan, South Korea, and others. Age limits (typically 18–30 or 18–35), once-per-lifetime, and additional conditions apply and vary by agreement. Annual quotas may apply. Applications processed via Swiss embassies/consulates in the applicant's country.

CHE.name: Residence Permit via Expenditure-Based Taxation (Lump-Sum Tax – B Permit)
CHE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals who do not engage in gainful employment in Switzerland to establish residence based on their cost of living, with tax calculated as a lump sum rather than on worldwide income.
CHE.notes: Available only to foreign nationals establishing Swiss domicile for the first time (or after 10+ years abroad) who do not engage in gainful employment in Switzerland. Available in 21 of 26 cantons (not in Zurich, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Schaffhausen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden). Federal minimum tax base is CHF 434,700; cantonal minimums vary. Results in a standard B permit (5-year renewable). After 10 years total residence and C permit, may apply for ordinary naturalization.

CHE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Category C) – Medical Treatment
CHE.purpose: Permits travel to Switzerland to receive medical treatment at a Swiss clinic or hospital for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
CHE.notes: Standard Schengen Category C visa issued for the purpose of medical treatment. Same fee structure as other C visas (EUR 90 adults, EUR 45 children aged 6–12). Applicants typically must present confirmation from the Swiss medical institution, proof of advance payment or sufficient funds to cover treatment and stay, and travel medical insurance. Treatment expected to exceed 90 days requires a national Category D visa authorised by the cantonal migration authority.

CHE.name: Residence Permit for Persons Not in Gainful Employment (Retirees) – Category B
CHE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EFTA nationals aged 55 or over who are no longer working to establish residence in Switzerland if they are financially self-sufficient and have close ties to the country.
CHE.notes: Legal basis Art. 28 Foreign Nationals and Integration Act (FNIA). Non-EU/EFTA applicants must be at least 55, no longer gainfully employed anywhere, financially independent (no recourse to social welfare), hold adequate accident and health insurance, and demonstrate special personal ties to Switzerland. Grant is discretionary, assessed first by the canton then federally. Requires a national Category D entry visa and results in a cantonal B residence permit. Distinct from the expenditure-based (lump-sum) taxation route. EU/EFTA nationals obtain an equivalent non-working B permit under the free movement agreement without the age condition.

CHE.name: Cross-Border Commuter Permit (Permit G)
CHE.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals resident in a neighbouring country's border zone who are gainfully employed within the adjacent Swiss border zone, commuting rather than taking up residence in Switzerland.
CHE.notes: Permit G for non-EU/EFTA nationals: the applicant must already hold a permanent residence permit in a neighbouring country (Germany, France, Italy, Austria, Liechtenstein), have lived in its border zone for at least six months, and the employment must satisfy labour-market conditions. Usually valid for one year and limited to the border zone of the issuing canton; the holder must return to their main residence abroad at least once a week. EU/EFTA cross-border commuters instead receive a G EU/EFTA permit valid up to five years without the border-zone residence restriction.

CHE.name: Au Pair Permit (Short-Term Residence Permit L)
CHE.purpose: Allows young non-EU/EFTA nationals aged 18–25 to live with a Swiss host family for up to one year to learn a national language while helping with light housework and childcare in exchange for board, lodging and pocket money.
CHE.notes: Legal basis Art. 30 para. 1(j) FNIA and Art. 48 ASEO. Third-country au pairs (aged 18–25) may only be placed through an agency recognised and authorised by SECO, and placements are subject to cantonal quotas – several cantons issue none. Maximum stay 12 months, non-renewable. The host family's household language must differ from the au pair's mother tongue and they may not share nationality or be related. Issued as a short-term Category L residence permit. EU/EFTA au pairs are admitted more freely (ages 17–30, up to two years).

CHE.name: Diplomatic/Official/Service Passport Visa Exemption
CHE.purpose: Holders of diplomatic, official, service, or special passports from countries with bilateral visa exemption agreements with Switzerland may enter and stay without a visa for up to 90 days.
CHE.notes: Switzerland has bilateral visa exemption agreements with 50+ countries for diplomatic/service/official passport holders. Countries include Algeria, Angola, Armenia, Benin, Bhutan, Brazil, Cameroon, Chile, China, Colombia, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Grenada, Guyana, India, Indonesia, Iran (official only), Jamaica, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Lebanon, Mauritius, Mexico, Moldova, Mongolia, Morocco, Namibia, North Macedonia, Oman, Palau, Peru, Philippines, Qatar, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent, South Africa, Thailand, Trinidad and Tobago, Tunisia, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, UAE, Venezuela, Vietnam. Exact passport types vary by agreement.

CHE.name: Return Visa
CHE.purpose: Issued to holders of expired Swiss residence permits who need to re-enter Switzerland after travel abroad.
CHE.notes: Issued to former residence permit holders who left Switzerland and whose permit has since expired but who need to return (e.g. to finalize affairs). Not a standard immigration visa category. Standard Schengen fee (EUR 90) typically applies.

CHL.name: Permiso de Permanencia Transitoria - Turismo
CHL.purpose: Grants temporary entry to Chile for tourism, sports, or similar non-remunerative purposes with no intention of settling. Holders may not engage in paid work.
CHL.notes: Extendable once for an additional 90 days (maximum 180 days total). Holders must demonstrate minimum USD 46/day of funds (Resolución Exenta Nº 3.464 de 2023). Nationals of 104 countries (listed in Decreto Supremo N°359) require prior consulate authorization. Cannot convert to residency permit except via specific family/humanitarian routes.

CHL.name: Permiso de Permanencia Transitoria - Tránsito
CHL.purpose: Permits international passenger and cargo transport crew members and others in transit to stay in Chile temporarily.
CHL.notes: Covers crew members of international passenger and cargo transport and individuals covered by international treaties. Part of the broader Permanencia Transitoria framework under Ley N°21.325.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Actividades Remuneradas (Remunerated Activities)
CHL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Chile and engage in lawful paid employment under an employment contract, service contract, or formal job offer.
CHL.notes: Standard grant is up to 2 years, extendable for two successive 2-year periods. Job-offer pathway grants initial 90 days then 1-year extension upon presenting employment contract within 45 days of entry. Application must be submitted from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal. All foreign documents require apostille or legalization.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Trabajadores de Temporada (Seasonal Workers)
CHL.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to reside in Chile for seasonal employment directly related to the employer's main line of business.
CHL.notes: Permit valid for up to 5 years (extendable for 2 more years) but actual stay limited to no more than 6 months per calendar year. Requires employment contract signed before a Chilean notary. Applicants have 45 days after entry to present employment contract. Nationals of bilateral-agreement countries may apply with a formal job offer instead.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Estudiantes (Students)
CHL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals enrolled in state-recognized Chilean educational institutions to reside in Chile for the duration of their studies.
CHL.notes: Holders may engage in lawful paid activities for up to 30 hours per week without additional authorization. Requires proof of enrollment and financial means. Extension requires proof of continued enrollment and financial capacity. Application must be made from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Inversores y Personal Relacionado (Investors and Related Personnel)
CHL.purpose: Allows foreign investors making a minimum USD 500,000 investment in productive goods or services in Chile, and their key personnel, to reside in Chile.
CHL.notes: Minimum investment of USD 500,000 or equivalent. Residential real estate for personal use does not qualify. Eligible applicants include legal representatives, executives, and specialized technical/management personnel of qualifying foreign companies. Requires sponsorship letter from INVESTCHILE per Interior Ministry Supreme Decree No. 177 of 2022 (Arts. 62-64). Must apply from outside Chile. Eligible family members may apply as dependents.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Rentistas y Pensionados (Retired Persons and Income Earners)
CHL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals with sufficient regular passive income (pensions, rental income, dividends) to reside in Chile without engaging in employment.
CHL.notes: Official SERMIG page states income sufficiency is assessed 'according to the parameters estimated by the Ministry of Social Development and Family' rather than a fixed published figure; third-party sources cite approximately USD 1,500-2,000/month but this exact amount is not published officially. Retirees submit a recent pension receipt; leasers (rentistas) submit lease contracts or asset-ownership certificates with income verification. Valid for up to 2 years, renewable. Path to permanent residency (Residencia Definitiva) after 24 months.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Reunificación Familiar (Family Reunification)
CHL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals with qualifying family bonds to Chilean citizens or permanent residents to reside in Chile.
CHL.notes: Eligible relationships: spouses/civil union partners, parents, children under 18, children with disabilities (any age), unmarried students under 24, and minors under guardianship. Applications processed via SERMIG's Portal de Trámites Digitales with separate processes for applicants inside vs. outside Chile.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Tratamiento Médico (Medical Treatment)
CHL.purpose: Permits foreign nationals requiring medical treatment at Chilean health providers registered with the Superintendencia de Salud to reside in Chile for the duration of treatment.
CHL.notes: Requires medical certificate detailing condition, treatment type, duration, and costs. Proof of economic means for subsistence and treatment financing required (health insurance acceptable). Extensions available with proof of ongoing treatment. Dependents may qualify. Must apply from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal.
