CHL.name: Working Holiday - Australia
CHL.purpose: Bilateral working holiday agreement allowing young Australian nationals to live and work temporarily in Chile.
CHL.notes: Age limit: up to 31 years. Based on bilateral Working Holiday Agreement between Chile and Australia. Australia was also removed from DS 359 visa-required list effective Sep 2025, so Australians may now also enter visa-free as tourists for up to 90 days separately.

CHL.name: Working Holiday - New Zealand
CHL.purpose: Bilateral working holiday agreement allowing young New Zealand nationals to live and work temporarily in Chile.
CHL.notes: Age limit: up to 30 years. Based on bilateral Working Holiday Agreement between Chile and New Zealand.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Acuerdos Internacionales / Mercosur (International Reciprocity)
CHL.purpose: Temporary residence based on bilateral or multilateral international treaties, including the Mercosur Residence Agreement for nationals of member and associate states.
CHL.notes: Covers nationals of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay under the Mercosur Residence Agreement (signed 6 Dec 2002, in force 28 Jul 2009). Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru ratified as of January 2024. Bolivia-Chile bilateral agreement eliminates application fees for Bolivian nationals. Holders may engage in lawful remunerated activities. Valid up to 2 years.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Personas Religiosas (Religious Persons)
CHL.purpose: Allows members of recognized faiths and denominations to reside in Chile for religious activities.
CHL.notes: Valid for up to 2 years, renewable. Applicant must belong to a religious entity legally constituted in Chile under Law N°19.638. Requires an approval report from the National Office of Religious Affairs and a legal-personality certificate. Apply from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal. One of the 15 Residencia Temporal subcategories under Ley N°21.325.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Razones Humanitarias (Humanitarian Reasons)
CHL.purpose: Grants temporary residence to foreign nationals who are victims of violence or in vulnerable situations, including human trafficking victims, domestic violence victims, pregnant individuals, and children.
CHL.notes: Five subcategories: children and adolescents, pregnant individuals, human trafficking victims, smuggling of migrant persons victims, and victims of domestic or gender-based violence. Duration and specific requirements vary by subcategory.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Gestión de Negocios (Multi-Entry Business Management)
CHL.purpose: For foreign business executives and managers who must regularly enter Chile to handle management or executive duties for companies and investments operating in the country.
CHL.notes: Distinct from the investor subcategory; covers executives conducting commercial operations that require regular multi-entry presence. Presence in Chile may not exceed six months per calendar year (Art. 72 of Ley N°21.325); permit term set by supreme decree. Requires an employer letter specifying role and income (apostilled/legalized) plus documentation of business interests. Apply from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Personas Amparadas por Acuerdos Internacionales (Persons Covered by International Agreements)
CHL.purpose: Temporary residence for foreign nationals covered by a bilateral or multilateral treaty in force with Chile, including Working Holiday participants and Free Trade Agreement business persons.
CHL.notes: Umbrella subcategory distinct from the Mercosur international-reciprocity route. Covers Working Holiday agreements (~20 partner countries incl. Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand) and the temporary-entry-for-business-persons chapters of Free Trade Agreements (Australia, Brazil, Canada, Central America, Colombia, South Korea, USA, Japan, Mexico, Peru, CPTPP). Validity, stay length, and fees are those established in the specific agreement/treaty. Working Holiday details at consulado.gob.cl/workingholiday. Apply from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Ex Titulares de Residencia Definitiva (Former Holders of Permanent Residency)
CHL.purpose: Allows foreign nationals whose Residencia Definitiva (or former Permanencia Definitiva) was revoked to regain temporary residence status.
CHL.notes: For those whose permanent residency was tacitly revoked under Art. 43 of Decreto Ley N°1.094 (1975) or Art. 83 of Ley N°21.325 (e.g. prolonged absence from Chile). Requires passport valid at least 1 year, criminal-record certificate, and proof of sufficient economic means. Family members may apply as dependents (Art. 74). Apply from outside Chile via SERMIG digital portal using ClaveÚnica.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Personas bajo Custodia de Gendarmería de Chile (Persons under Custody of Gendarmería)
CHL.purpose: Regularizes the residence status of foreign nationals under the authority and control of Chile's prison service.
CHL.notes: Covers foreigners serving a custodial sentence (including prison furlough), under pretrial detention, on probation, or serving alternative sentences under Law N°18.216. Applications for detained/sentenced persons are filed by Gendarmería de Chile; those on parole or alternative sentences apply via SERMIG's portal with prison-official guidance. Not a traveler-facing visa - included for completeness of the statutory subcategory list.

CHL.name: Residencia Temporal - Extranjeros por Orden de Tribunales de Justicia (Persons Required by Order of Courts)
CHL.purpose: Permits a foreign national to remain in Chile when a Chilean court orders their presence for the proper development of judicial proceedings in which they are a party.
CHL.notes: Granted for as long as the court deems necessary for the judicial process (e.g. under a travel ban or transfer order). The application is filed by the court official issuing the order through SERMIG's digital platform, accompanied by a court certificate of proceedings. Not a traveler-facing visa - included for completeness of the statutory subcategory list.

CHL.name: Permiso de Permanencia Transitoria - Residentes Oficiales que Terminan Misión (Official Residents Completing Mission)
CHL.purpose: Covers foreign diplomatic and official residents completing their official mission in Chile, allowing continued temporary stay.
CHL.notes: Part of the Permanencia Transitoria framework. Approximately 73 bilateral agreements exempt diplomatic/official/service passport holders from requiring a visa for stays up to 90 days per the MINREL VIDO Manual (May 2025).

CHL.name: Residencia Definitiva (Permanent Residency)
CHL.purpose: Grants the right to reside indefinitely in Chile and engage in any lawful activity without restrictions.
CHL.notes: Standard eligibility: minimum 24 months of Residencia Temporal. Reduced to 12 months for those with family ties to Chilean nationals/permanent residents, prior official missions, sufficient income/pensions, active business investments, or international agreement qualifications. ID card renewed every 5 years. Absence for more than 2 continuous years voids the permit. Path to citizenship by naturalization after 5 total years of legal residence.

CHN.name: L Visa (Tourist)
CHN.purpose: Tourism, family visits, transit with sightseeing
CHN.notes: Standard tourist visa. Single-entry most common; double/multiple entry available at embassy discretion. 30-day stay per entry typical. Applied at Chinese embassy/consulate or CVASC (China Visa Application Service Center). Fee varies by nationality (reciprocity-based).

CHN.name: M Visa (Business/Trade)
CHN.notes: For commercial/trade activities. Multiple-entry common for business travelers. Invitation letter from Chinese business partner typically required.

CHN.name: X1/X2 Visa (Student)
CHN.notes: X1 for study programs 180+ days (must convert to residence permit in China); X2 for programs under 180 days. Requires JW201/JW202 form and admission letter from recognized Chinese educational institution.

CHN.name: Z Visa (Work)
CHN.notes: Single-entry; must be converted to a work-type Residence Permit within 30 days of arrival. Requires work permit notification letter issued by Chinese authorities and employment contract. Sponsored by Chinese employer.

CHN.name: G Visa (Transit)
CHN.notes: For travelers transiting China who do not qualify for visa-free transit. Note: nationals of 55 countries qualify for 240-hour (10-day) Visa-Free Transit at 65 designated ports across 24 provinces/regions/municipalities without a G visa (policy expanded from 72/144 hours to 240 hours effective 2024-12-17; designated ports increased to 65 effective 2025-11-05; official source: https://us.china-embassy.gov.cn/eng/lsfw/zj/qz2021/202412/t20241217_11495647.htm) - check the official list. A G visa is required for those who do not qualify for visa-free transit, exceed the free-transit window, or leave the permitted transit area.

CHN.name: F Visa (Non-Commercial Exchange/Visit)
CHN.purpose: Non-commercial exchanges, visits, study tours, cultural/scientific/academic exchange, lectures, short-term research
CHN.notes: Official category: 'Issued to those who intend to go to China for exchanges, visits, study tours and other activities.' Distinct from the M (commercial/trade) visa - F covers non-commercial exchange, academic visits, lectures, cultural/scientific programs and volunteering. Stay length, validity and entries vary by grant; long-term F holders (intended stay over 180 days) must convert to a residence permit within 30 days of arrival. Fee varies by nationality (reciprocity-based). Applied at Chinese embassy/consulate or CVASC.

CHN.name: Q1/Q2 Visa (Family Reunion with Chinese Citizens/Permanent Residents)
CHN.purpose: Family reunion or short visits with Chinese citizens or holders of Chinese permanent residence; foster care
CHN.notes: Q1: long-term family reunion (intended stay over 180 days) for family members of Chinese citizens or of foreigners holding Chinese permanent residence, or for foster-care purposes - single entry; holder must apply for a residence permit within 30 days of arrival. Q2: short-term visits to relatives (stay no more than 180 days per entry); can be multiple-entry and valid up to 10 years for US/Canadian citizens. Invitation letter from the relative in China required. Fee varies by nationality (reciprocity-based).

CHN.name: S1/S2 Visa (Family of Foreigners Working/Studying in China)
CHN.purpose: Relatives visiting foreigners who are working or studying in China, and other private affairs
CHN.notes: S1: long-term (intended stay over 180 days) for spouses, parents, children under 18 or parents-in-law of foreigners residing in China for work/study - single entry; must apply for a residence permit within 30 days of arrival. S2: short-term family visits or private matters (stay no more than 180 days). Equivalent of the Q visa but for relatives of FOREIGN (not Chinese) residents. Invitation letter from the foreign resident in China required. Fee varies by nationality (reciprocity-based).

CHN.name: R Visa (High-Level Talent / Urgently Needed Skills)
CHN.purpose: High-level foreign talents and foreigners whose skills are urgently needed in China
CHN.notes: Official category: 'Issued to those who are high-level talents or whose skills are urgently needed in China.' China's premium talent visa - more favorable terms (multiple entry, longer validity, commonly up to 5-10 years) than a standard Z work visa. Requires a talent-qualification certification from competent Chinese authorities and/or a Confirmation Letter for High-level Foreign Talents from the inviting organization. Long-term holders convert to a residence permit after arrival. Fee varies by nationality. Fast-track processing (about 5 working days) is available for qualifying talent.

CHN.name: K Visa (Young Science and Technology Talent)
CHN.purpose: Young foreign STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) graduates and researchers - education, research, entrepreneurship and business exchange
CHN.notes: New ordinary visa category effective October 1, 2025 (State Council decision amending the Regulations on Exit-Entry Administration of Foreign Nationals). For young science-and-technology talent (STEM bachelor's degree or higher from a recognized university/research institution, or engaged in related teaching/research). No domestic employer, job offer or invitation letter required - self-sponsored. Offers greater flexibility in number of entries, validity and duration of stay than the 12 other ordinary visa types; permits education, cultural and science/technology exchange plus entrepreneurial and business activities. Official announcement: https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202508/14/content_WS689dd0d3c6d0868f4e8f4d1e.html. Detailed conditions and fees are published by individual Chinese embassies/consulates and not yet uniformly listed.

CHN.name: J1/J2 Visa (Journalist)
CHN.notes: J1: resident foreign journalists posted to China (intended stay over 180 days) - convert to a residence permit within 30 days of arrival. J2: foreign journalists on short-term news coverage (stay no more than 180 days). Requires prior clearance/authorization from China's competent foreign-affairs and press authorities. Fee varies by nationality (reciprocity-based).

CIV.name: Visa Biométrique (E-Visa / Visa Aéroport)
CIV.purpose: Short-stay entry for tourism, family visits, and general travel to Côte d'Ivoire. The applicant pre-enrolls online and completes biometric enrollment at Félix Houphouët-Boigny International Airport (Abidjan) upon arrival.
CIV.notes: Fee is 73 EUR (including bank fees). Processing up to 48 working hours (Monday–Friday). Requires ordinary passport with minimum 6 months validity, return air ticket, invitation letter or accommodation certificate (typed, printed, signed, stamped, and legalized), and yellow fever vaccination certificate at the airport. Biometric enrollment completed at 'Visa aéroport' desk (open 24/7) at Abidjan airport. Only snedai.com is officially state-recognized and accredited for this process. No separate tourist vs. business designation - one general-purpose short-stay visa category.

CIV.name: Visa Biométrique (E-Visa / Visa Aéroport)
CIV.purpose: Short-stay entry for business activities, meetings, and commercial purposes in Côte d'Ivoire. Same visa product as the tourist channel - Côte d'Ivoire does not issue a distinct business visa type; purpose is declared in the application.
CIV.notes: Fee is 73 EUR (including bank fees). For business travel, an invitation letter from the host company in Côte d'Ivoire is required (typed, printed, signed, stamped, and legalized). The visa system does not distinguish a separate business visa category - all short-stay applicants apply through the same biometric visa process.

CIV.name: Visa Biométrique à l'Ambassade (Embassy Biometric Visa)
CIV.purpose: Short-stay entry visa issued by Côte d'Ivoire embassies and consulates abroad for travel to Côte d'Ivoire. Covers all purposes including tourism, business, and family visits.
CIV.notes: Fee is 58 EUR total (50 EUR dossier fee + 5 EUR appointment/RDV fee + 3 EUR online processing fee). Application must be submitted through snedai.com/visaenambassade/ (officially accredited portal). Holders of diplomatic or service passports are exempt from the visa fee but must still apply. This is the in-person embassy channel distinct from the airport e-visa channel.

CIV.name: Visa Ordinaire 3 Mois à l'Ambassade (Ordinary 3-Month Visa)
CIV.purpose: Standard 3-month ordinary visa issued at Côte d'Ivoire embassies and consulates for short-stay travel purposes including tourism and business.
CIV.notes: Listed as a distinct service at the Côte d'Ivoire Embassy in the UK ('VISA ORDINAIRE 3 MOIS A L AMBASSADE'). Fee, entries, and processing details not published on official pages accessed. This appears to be a legacy or alternative in-person embassy visa channel. Applicants should contact the relevant embassy directly for current fee and document requirements.

CIV.name: Exemption de Visa - Passeport Diplomatique ou de Service
CIV.purpose: Visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and service passports from select countries, based on bilateral agreements with Côte d'Ivoire.
CIV.notes: Covers holders of diplomatic or service passports from: France (diplomatic only, per 2025 agreement in force June 2025), Austria, Brazil, China, Gabon, Israel, South Africa, Turkey, Uganda, Venezuela, Vietnam (per 2013 MFA document), and Switzerland (diplomatic and service, per 2022 Council of Ministers ratification). Must be accompanied by official diplomatic note or mission order. No employment permitted. French agreement: max 90 days within any 180-day period. Diplomatic fee exemption also applies to ordinary applicants holding diplomatic/service passports who must still obtain a visa - they are exempt from the visa fee only.

CIV.name: Visa de Transit (Transit Visa)
CIV.purpose: Short transit through Côte d'Ivoire for travellers continuing to a third country.
CIV.notes: One of the three official biometric-visa duration classes. Per the Ivorian entry-visa regulation, a transit visa (visa de transit) may not exceed three (3) days; the short-stay visa (court séjour) may not exceed three (3) months and the long-stay visa (long séjour) may not exceed one (1) year. Issued as a biometric visa via the same pre-enrollment process as the short-stay visa, with biometric enrollment at Abidjan airport or a Côte d'Ivoire embassy. Standard short-stay biometric visa fee applies (about 70 EUR e-visa / 50 EUR embassy dossier). Confirmed on snedai.com e-visa framework and diplomatie.gouv.ci embassy pages.

CIV.name: Visa d'Études et de Recherches (Study / Research Visa)
CIV.purpose: Foreign students and researchers enrolling at an educational or research institution in Côte d'Ivoire.
CIV.notes: Listed as a distinct purpose ('Visa d'études ou de recherches') on Côte d'Ivoire embassy visa pages. Requires a certificate of enrolment (certificat de scolarité/inscription), academic records, proof of accommodation, proof of financial means and health insurance. Biometric visa fee 50 EUR dossier (about 58 EUR total). Short-stay biometric visa validity is 1–3 months; for a long stay (long séjour, up to 1 year) students apply through a Côte d'Ivoire embassy/consulate or the competent ministry, then obtain a Carte de Résident (student category) from ONECI in-country.

CIV.name: Visa de Visite Privée (Private Visit Visa)
CIV.purpose: Private and family visits to relatives or hosts residing in Côte d'Ivoire.
CIV.notes: Listed as a distinct purpose ('Visa pour visite privée') on Côte d'Ivoire embassy visa pages. Requires an invitation letter from the host (or a hotel reservation). Biometric short-stay visa, valid 1–3 months. Fee 50 EUR dossier (about 58 EUR total) at an embassy, or about 70–73 EUR via the snedai e-visa airport channel. Same biometric visa product as tourism/business, differentiated by the declared purpose.

CIV.name: Visa Santé et Affaires Sociales (Health & Social Affairs Visa)
CIV.purpose: Foreign nationals travelling to Côte d'Ivoire for medical treatment or health/social-affairs reasons.
CIV.notes: 'Santé et affaires sociales' (health and social affairs) is one of the four official purpose categories of the biometric entry visa, alongside business (affaires), study (études) and tourism/leisure (tourisme), per the snedai e-visa framework and diplomatie.gouv.ci embassy guidance. Issued as a biometric short-stay visa (1–3 months); a long-stay visa (up to 1 year) is available for extended treatment via a Côte d'Ivoire embassy or the competent ministry. Standard biometric visa fee applies (about 70 EUR e-visa / 50 EUR embassy dossier).

CIV.name: Carte de Résident – Travailleur (Worker Resident Card)
CIV.purpose: Foreign nationals (non-UEMOA) employed in Côte d'Ivoire who take up residence to work.
CIV.notes: In-country residence/work permit issued by ONECI (Office National de l'État Civil et de l'Identification), the sole authority for resident cards for non-UEMOA nationals. Foreign workers must also hold a work authorization from AGEPE and provide a work attestation (attestation de travail) / employment contract. Fee 300,000 FCFA for non-ECOWAS nationals (150,000 FCFA for French nationals; 35,000 FCFA for French religious personnel/cooperants) — about 490 USD. Mandatory online pre-enrollment at pre-enregistrement-carte-resident.oneci.ci; processing about 15 working days (07 for renewals). Workers first obtain a long-stay entry visa via a Côte d'Ivoire embassy/consulate or the competent ministry, then this resident card. Renewable.

CIV.name: Carte de Résident – Retraité (Retiree Resident Card)
CIV.purpose: Retired foreign nationals (non-UEMOA) taking up residence in Côte d'Ivoire.
CIV.notes: The ONECI carte de résident is issued by category of applicant; retirees (retraités) are an explicitly eligible category, alongside workers, students, merchants, religious personnel and artisans. Issued by ONECI to non-UEMOA foreign residents. Fee 300,000 FCFA for non-ECOWAS nationals (about 490 USD; 150,000 FCFA for French nationals). Mandatory online pre-enrollment at pre-enregistrement-carte-resident.oneci.ci; processing about 15 working days. Not a separate 'retirement visa' product but the resident-card pathway available to retirees. Renewable.

CMR.name: Short-Stay Visa (Ordinary)
CMR.purpose: Temporary visits for tourism, family visits, or other short-term purposes. Covers stays up to 6 months.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal. Fee XAF 100,000 / approx. EUR 152 (diplocam.cm confirmed 2026-06-29). Multiple entry available. Passport must be valid at least 6 months. Yellow fever vaccination certificate required. Biometric procedures completed at embassy or at Cameroon border entry point.

CMR.name: Short-Stay Express Visa
CMR.purpose: Expedited temporary entry visa for tourism or short-term visits with 24-hour processing.
CMR.notes: Express processing option available through evisacam.cm portal. Fee XAF 150,000 / approx. EUR 229 (diplocam.cm confirmed 2026-06-29). Same eligibility and documentation as ordinary short-stay visa. Multiple entry available.

CMR.name: Short-Stay Visa (Business)
CMR.purpose: Short-term entry for business meetings, conferences, trade negotiations, or commercial activities up to 6 months.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal. The short-stay visa category covers business purposes. Fee XAF 100,000 / approx. EUR 152 per diplocam.cm. Express option at XAF 150,000 / approx. EUR 229 / 24 hours available.

CMR.name: Long-Stay Visa (Contract Worker)
CMR.purpose: For foreign nationals coming to Cameroon to take up salaried employment under a contract of employment, valid 6-12 months.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal (MINREX). Salaried/contract workers must present a contract of employment signed by the Minister in charge of employment, per Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023 implementing Law No. 97/012 of 10 January 1997. Fee XAF 150,000 normal / XAF 200,000 express per diplocam.cm (confirmed 2026-06-29). Cameroon High Commission UK cites EUR 305 for long-stay normal which does not match diplocam.cm; diplocam.cm is the MINREX primary source. Independent/self-employed workers and trainees/interns are covered by separate long-stay entries.

CMR.name: Long-Stay Visa (Student)
CMR.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in Cameroon educational institutions for studies longer than 6 months.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal (MINREX). Fee XAF 150,000 normal per diplocam.cm (confirmed 2026-06-29). Long-term trainees and students are listed as a category under the long-stay visa scheme per Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023.

CMR.name: Long-Stay Visa (Family Reunification)
CMR.purpose: For family members of foreign nationals lawfully residing in Cameroon who wish to join them for an extended period.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal (MINREX). Family members of aliens staying in Cameroon are an explicit long-stay visa sub-category per Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023. Fee XAF 150,000 normal per diplocam.cm (confirmed 2026-06-29).

CMR.name: Long-Stay Visa (Independent Worker / Self-Employed)
CMR.purpose: For foreign nationals establishing in Cameroon to pursue a liberal profession or to run an agricultural, pastoral, industrial, commercial, artistic or similar activity, valid 6-12 months.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal (MINREX). Distinct long-stay category under Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023: independent/self-employed workers must present an authorization to carry out a liberal profession or to promote an agricultural, pastoral, industrial, commercial, artistic or other activity, issued by the relevant authority. Confirmed on the official Cameroon Embassy Japan page (cameroonemb-jp.org). This is the closest Cameroon equivalent to a self-employed/investor residence pathway; no separate investor 'golden visa' with a defined investment threshold exists on official sources. Fee XAF 150,000 normal / XAF 200,000 express per diplocam.cm.

CMR.name: Long-Stay Visa (Trainee / Internship)
CMR.purpose: For foreign nationals coming to Cameroon for a training programme or internship (stage) lasting more than 6 months.
CMR.notes: Applied online via evisacam.cm portal (MINREX). Long-term trainees/interns are an explicit long-stay category under Decree No. 2023/147 of 02 March 2023, requiring an internship certificate signed by the relevant authority (confirmed on the official Cameroon Embassy Japan page, cameroonemb-jp.org). 'Internship' and 'Training' are listed among the recognized long-stay purposes on the evisacam.cm portal. Fee XAF 150,000 normal / XAF 200,000 express per diplocam.cm.

CMR.name: Transit Visa (up to 5 days, free)
CMR.purpose: For travellers transiting through Cameroon for up to 5 days en route to another destination.
CMR.notes: Free of charge. Applied online via evisacam.cm. Diplocam.cm (MINREX official, re-confirmed 2026-06-29) specifies 5-day maximum for the free transit visa. Cameroon High Commission UK (cameroonhighcommission.co.uk) separately lists a paid transit visa at EUR 153 for 4-30 days - this appears to be a different (paid) transit product or an inconsistency; diplocam.cm (MINREX) is authoritative for the free 5-day transit. Passport must be valid at least 6 months.

CMR.name: Diplomatic / Courtesy / Official Visa
CMR.purpose: Entry visa for holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports on official duty from countries that do not have a bilateral visa waiver agreement with Cameroon.
CMR.notes: No visa fees charged for diplomatic, service, and special passports on official duty. Bilateral visa waiver agreements exist (full exemption) for: Equatorial Guinea, Egypt, Mali, Brazil, Vietnam, Turkey, China, UAE, Switzerland, Italy, Russia, Tunisia, Algeria (Decree No. 2026/034, Jan 2026), Republic of Korea (Decree No. 2025/176, May 2025). Countries not covered by such agreements still require a visa but pay no fee.

COD.name: Visa Volant Ordinaire (Ordinary Flying Visa / e-Visa for Tourism)
COD.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit the DRC for tourism purposes. Issued online via the official e-visa portal operated by the Direction Générale de Migration.
COD.notes: Total cost is USD 300 (USD 50 non-refundable admin fee + USD 250 visa fee). Upon arrival at the border, the holder receives a VAP (Visa Aéroportuaire / airport visa) valid for 7 days, at an additional cost of USD 90 payable at the border post. The e-visa itself is valid for 3 months from issuance. Eligible for nationals of countries without DRC diplomatic representation, and any foreigner wishing to visit for tourism.

COD.name: Visa Volant Spécifique (Specific Flying Visa / e-Visa for Business)
COD.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit the DRC for business purposes. Issued online via the official e-visa portal.
COD.notes: Total cost is USD 300 (USD 50 non-refundable admin fee + USD 250 visa fee). VAP (airport visa) of USD 90 payable at border upon arrival; VAP valid for 7 days. E-visa valid for 3 months from issuance. Eligible for nationals of countries without DRC diplomatic representation, and any foreigner wishing to visit for business.

COD.name: Visa Volant pour Visite de Famille (Family Visit Flying Visa / e-Visa)
COD.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit family members residing in the DRC. Issued online via the official e-visa portal.
COD.notes: One of the three officially listed e-visa (visa volant) categories on the official DRC e-visa portal FAQ. Same fee structure as other e-visa types: USD 300 total + USD 90 VAP at border. VAP valid for 7 days.

COD.name: Single-Entry Short-Stay Visa (Embassy Issued - 1 Month)
COD.purpose: Standard short-stay visa for entry into the DRC for tourism or general purposes, issued at DRC embassies and consulates abroad.
COD.notes: Fee at DRC Embassy Paris: €85 for single entry, 1 month. Express processing available for additional €50. Applications must be submitted at least 7 days before planned departure. Fees vary by embassy; ambadrcusa.org lists USD 100–400 for single entry depending on validity. Consular fees are non-refundable. Visa approval subject to National Provisional Commission for Visa Granting.

COD.name: Multiple-Entry Short-Stay Visa (Embassy Issued - 1 to 6 Months)
COD.purpose: Allows multiple entries into the DRC during the validity period. Issued at DRC embassies and consulates for tourism or general purposes.
COD.notes: Fee at DRC Embassy Paris: €115–€310 depending on validity (1–6 months). Express processing available for additional €50. DRC Embassy in Washington DC (ambadrcusa.org) lists multiple-entry at USD 120–450. Double-entry variant also available at intermediate pricing. Visa approved by National Provisional Commission for Visa Granting.

COD.name: Airport Transit Visa
COD.purpose: Permits transit through a DRC airport without entering the country proper, for passengers connecting to onward flights.
COD.notes: USD 45 for one-way transit; USD 75 for roundtrip transit, per DRC Embassy Washington DC (ambadrcusa.org). Issued at DRC embassies and consulates abroad.

COD.name: Visa de Travail (Work Visa / Temporary Work Authorization)
COD.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to enter the DRC for employment purposes. Initial temporary work authorisation is limited to 6 consecutive months.
COD.notes: After the initial temporary work visa period (up to 6 months), the foreign worker may qualify for an Establishment Visa (Visa d'Établissement) with a minimum 1-year validity. Facilitation for initial investments over USD 200,000 is available via ANAPI (National Agency for Investment Promotion). Specific fee not published on official sources consulted.

COD.name: Visa d'Établissement - Régulier (Regular Establishment Visa)
COD.purpose: Long-stay residence visa for foreign nationals wishing to settle in the DRC without a specific professional or matrimonial basis.
COD.notes: One of five subtypes of the Establishment Visa (Visa d'Établissement): Regular, Professional, Studies, Matrimonial, and Permanent. Minimum validity of 1 year. Grants resident status and authorises activities under conditions set by law.

COD.name: Visa d'Établissement - Professionnel (Professional Establishment Visa)
COD.purpose: Long-stay residence visa for foreign nationals establishing themselves in the DRC for professional or economic activities.
COD.notes: Professional subtype of the Establishment Visa. Typically follows an initial temporary work visa (up to 6 months). Authorises professional or economic activities.

COD.name: Visa d'Établissement - Études (Studies Establishment Visa)
COD.purpose: Long-stay residence visa for foreign nationals pursuing academic studies in the DRC.
COD.notes: Studies subtype of the Establishment Visa (Visa d'Établissement). One of five official subtypes noted on the DRC Embassy USA website.

COD.name: Visa d'Établissement - Matrimonial (Matrimonial Establishment Visa)
COD.purpose: Long-stay residence visa for foreign nationals married to a DRC national or resident, allowing family reunification in the DRC.
COD.notes: Matrimonial subtype of the Establishment Visa. One of five official subtypes. Authorises residence based on marital ties.

COD.name: Visa d'Établissement - Permanent (Permanent Establishment Visa)
COD.purpose: Permanent residence authorisation for foreign nationals who have met the requirements for long-term settlement in the DRC.
COD.notes: Permanent subtype of the Establishment Visa (Visa d'Établissement Permanent). One of five official subtypes noted on the DRC Embassy USA website. Specific eligibility criteria and fees not published on official sources consulted.

COD.name: Visa Diplomatique / de Service (Diplomatic and Service Visa)
COD.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, and United Nations travel documents, in accordance with bilateral agreements and international protocols.
COD.notes: Per DRC Embassy Paris: special passports such as Diplomatic, Service, and United Nations travel documents are issued visas free of charge. Russia-DRC bilateral agreement (signed 27 July 2023) grants 90-day visa-free stay for diplomatic and service passport holders of both countries. Wikipedia also confirms diplomatic/official passport exemptions for Angola (on duty), Iran, South Africa, Turkey, and UAE (diplomatic only). Similar bilateral agreements exist with other states. DRC embassies issue diplomatic visas under diplomatic conventions.

COD.name: Visa de Courtoisie (Courtesy Visa)
COD.purpose: Short-stay courtesy visa issued by DRC embassies and consulates to invited guests and visitors on non-commercial courtesy visits. Not valid for any professional or remunerated activity in the DRC.
COD.notes: Confirmed as a distinct DRC visa category by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (France Diplomatie). Explicitly NOT intended for professional activities in the DRC, even short-term: travellers who will carry out any professional activity are advised to refuse a courtesy visa and instead obtain an ordinary visa with a mission letter (stays up to one week) or a work establishment visa (Visa d'Etablissement de Travail, stays over one week). Fee and stay duration are not published on an official DRC source; issued at embassy discretion. Processing typically at least one week.

COD.name: Visa pour Titre de Voyage de Refugie (Refugee Travel Document Visa)
COD.purpose: Entry visa for holders of a refugee travel document (rather than an ordinary national passport) travelling to the DRC for short stays, for tourism, business or family purposes.
COD.notes: Distinct visa product with its own fee schedule published on the official DRC Embassy Paris consular page for holders of refugee travel documents. Single entry: EUR 108 (1 month) / EUR 140 (2 months) / EUR 195 (3 months) / EUR 260 (6 months). Multiple entry: EUR 125 / EUR 160 / EUR 240 / EUR 340 respectively. Express processing surcharge +EUR 50. Validity up to 6 months, renewable within the DRC for a longer duration. Applications submitted at least 7 days before departure (two weeks for first-time travellers). Fee left null here as amounts are in EUR and vary by validity/entries; see notes for the full schedule.

COG.name: Tourist Visa (Visa de Tourisme)
COG.purpose: Short-stay entry for tourism and leisure travel to the Republic of the Congo.
COG.notes: Must be obtained prior to arrival at a Congolese embassy or consulate; no visa is issued at any port of entry. Per the official Embassy of the Republic of Congo to the USA (ambacongo-us.org), the tourist visa is issued for 90 days with multiple entries for non-US citizens, and 180 days multiple entries for US citizens; fee USD 200, processing 7-10 business days (fee and exact stay vary by issuing consulate). API-Congo and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs describe a shorter 15-day initial visitor stay that is extended in-country via a resident's card. Required documents: valid passport, two photos, notarised invitation letter or hotel reservation, and airline itinerary.

COG.name: Business Visa (Visa d'Affaires)
COG.purpose: Entry for business activities, meetings, feasibility studies, and commercial or investment arrangements in the Republic of the Congo.
COG.notes: Must be obtained prior to arrival at a Congolese embassy or consulate. Per the official Embassy of the Republic of Congo to the USA (ambacongo-us.org), the business visa is issued for 30 days with multiple entries for non-US citizens (cannot exceed 30 days; extend at the nearest Office of Immigration in Congo) and 180 days multiple entries for US citizens; fee USD 200, processing 7-10 business days (fee varies by consulate). Requires a notarised business letter on company letterhead stating the nature of business.

COG.name: Student Visa / Student Residence Permit (Carte de Séjour Étudiant)
COG.purpose: Foreign students and researchers enrolled at a Congolese educational or research institution.
COG.notes: No separate student entry visa is issued abroad. Per the official Congolese embassy (ambacongo-us.org), students on exchange programs and researchers enter on a tourist visa and then change their status at the nearest Office of Immigration in Congo, obtaining an ordinary resident's card (carte de séjour) on the basis of a school/university enrollment certificate. Resident's card fees: 1 year 106,000 FCFA (~USD 176), 3 years 206,000 FCFA (~USD 343), 5 years 106,000 FCFA (~USD 176), issued by the Direction Départementale de la Surveillance du Territoire. Sources: API-Congo (.cg) and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (diplobrazza.net).

COG.name: Family Reunion Visa / Spouse Residence (Regroupement Familial)
COG.purpose: Family members joining relatives resident in the Republic of the Congo, and foreign spouses of Congolese nationals.
COG.notes: For family reunification (regroupement familial), the official embassy (ambacongo-us.org) requires proof of family affiliation (birth certificate, adoption papers, or legal marriage certificate) submitted with the visa application; applicants then regularise status in-country. A foreign national married for at least 2 years to a Congolese national is automatically granted a resident's card (carte de séjour) per API-Congo (.cg). Sources: Embassy of the Republic of Congo (ambacongo-us.org) and API-Congo / Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

COG.name: Work Visa / Foreign Worker Authorization (Autorisation de Travail pour Étranger)
COG.purpose: Entry and authorization to work in the Republic of the Congo as a foreign employee.
COG.notes: Foreign worker visa fee is 100,000 FCFA (~USD 165); work card fee is 10,000 FCFA (~USD 16). Categories include national staff, subordinate agents, and foreign personnel. Temporary employment and provisional work authorizations are also available. Must be obtained through the relevant Congolese authorities.

COG.name: Temporary / Provisional Work Authorization (Autorisation Provisoire de Travail)
COG.purpose: Short-term or provisional employment authorization for foreign workers, arranged through the Congolese employment agency (ACPE).
COG.notes: Distinct from the standard foreign-worker contract visa. Temporary employment authorizations are obtained through the ACPE (Agence Congolaise Pour l'Emploi) application process, and provisional work authorizations are also available for foreign personnel. Source: API-Congo (official .cg investment-promotion agency).

COG.name: Residence Visa / Residence Permit (Carte de Séjour)
COG.purpose: Long-term residence authorization for foreign nationals staying beyond the initial visa period, covering employees, students, religious ministers, professionals, and academics.
COG.notes: Initial visa may allow up to 15 days; extended through the Direction Départementale de la Surveillance du Territoire. Permit durations: 1 year (106,000 FCFA / ~EUR 161.60), 3 years (206,000 FCFA / ~EUR 314.04), 5 years (106,000 FCFA / ~EUR 161.60). Express Visa option available at additional cost for same-day processing. Categories include employees, students, religious ministers, initiates, professionals, and academics/researchers. A Privileged Resident Card (Carte de Résident Privilégié) is available after 10 years of uninterrupted residence, and automatically granted to foreign spouses of Congolese nationals (married 2+ years), economic investors, and recognised religious leaders.

COG.name: Diplomatic / Service Passport Visa Exemption
COG.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, or special passports from countries with bilateral agreements with the Republic of the Congo.
COG.notes: Holders of diplomatic and service passports from Brazil, China, and Russia are exempt from visa requirements. Holders of diplomatic passports (only) from Portugal and Turkey are exempt. Chinese nationals with 'Public Affairs' passports (公务护照) are also exempt. These arrangements are based on bilateral agreements. Source for these specific exemptions is Wikipedia citing bilateral agreements; not independently confirmed on a directly accessible official Congo government page during this research.

COG.name: Official / Diplomatic Visa
COG.purpose: Holders of diplomatic or official passports, or UN Laissez-Passer, traveling to the Republic of the Congo on official government or international-organization business.
COG.notes: Issued to diplomatic/official passport bearers and UN Laissez-Passer holders traveling on official business. A 12-month (one-year) multiple-entry visa is granted when the application is accompanied by a diplomatic note, and diplomatic visa applications are exempt from visa fees. This is an issued visa and is distinct from the separate bilateral visa-free exemptions granted to certain nationalities' diplomatic/service passport holders. Source: official Embassy of the Republic of Congo to the USA (ambacongo-us.org).

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Tourism (V-Tourism)
COL.purpose: Short-stay entry for leisure, cultural activities, and sightseeing in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) visa category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Nationals from ~100+ countries are visa-exempt for up to 90 days (180 days per calendar year) and do not need this visa. Required by nationalities not on the visa-free list. Valid up to 2 years; cannot exceed 180 days total per calendar year inside Colombia. All visas are electronic (no passport stamp).

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Business (V-Business)
COL.purpose: Short-term entry for commercial negotiations, investment planning, business meetings, or attending conferences in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. For visa-exempt nationalities, no visa is needed for business visits under 90 days. For longer business presence with capital investment (100× SMMLV in a company), the M (Migrant) Business Visa applies instead.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Worker (M-Worker)
COL.purpose: Long-term visa for foreigners with a fixed-term or indefinite employment contract with a Colombian company or entity.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Valid up to 3 years, multiple entry. Automatically loses validity if holder remains outside Colombia for more than 6 consecutive months. After 2-5 years on M visa (depending on subcategory), holder may qualify for R (Resident) visa.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Technical Assistance (V-Technical)
COL.purpose: Short-term visa for foreigners providing professional technical assistance or specialized services to Colombian entities.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. For temporary technical work. For long-term professional work, the M-Worker or M-Expertise visa applies.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Expertise/Professional (M-Expertise)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners practicing an independent profession or providing specialized expertise services in Colombia on a long-term basis.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Valid up to 3 years. Requires demonstration of professional expertise. Loses validity if absent from Colombia more than 6 consecutive months.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Student (V-Student)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners enrolled in an educational institution in Colombia, including academic programs and language training.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Valid up to 2 years or for the duration of the academic program. Must maintain enrollment at a Colombian institution. Electronic visa with no passport stamp.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Digital Nomad (V-Nómada Digital)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners who work remotely for foreign companies or clients, or who develop digital content or IT ventures of interest to Colombia, while living in Colombia.
COL.notes: Created under Resolución 5477 de 2022. For visa-exempt nationalities, no visa is needed for digital nomad activities under 90 days. Requires minimum monthly income of 3× Colombia's SMMLV (~USD 1,400/month at 2026 rates). Must have health insurance covering Colombia. Income requirement indexed annually to SMMLV. Cannot earn income from Colombian sources.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Retirement/Pensioner (M-Pensionado)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners receiving a stable pension or retirement income from a foreign source who wish to reside in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Minimum pension income requirement: 3× Colombia's SMMLV (~COP 5,252,715/month, ~USD 1,400/month at 2026 rates). Pension must be periodic and from a foreign source. After 5 continuous years, holder may apply for R (Resident) visa. Considered one of the more accessible retirement visas in Latin America. FBI background check may be required for US citizens.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Real Estate Investment (M-Real Estate)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners making direct foreign investment in Colombian real estate.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Minimum investment: 350× SMMLV (~COP 612,816,750 / ~USD 161,300 at 2026 rates). After 3 continuous years on M visa, may qualify for R (Resident) visa. Automatically loses validity if holder remains outside Colombia more than 6 consecutive months.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Business/Company Investment (M-Business)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners investing in or owning a share of a Colombian commercial company.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Minimum investment: 100× SMMLV in the company. For large-scale direct foreign investment, minimum is 650× SMMLV. After 3 continuous years on M visa, may qualify for R (Resident) visa.

COL.name: Resident Visa - Direct Foreign Investment (R-Investor)
COL.purpose: Permanent residency visa granted directly to foreigners making a substantial direct foreign investment in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of R (Resident) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Minimum investment: USD 100,000 (or equivalent in COP) in one's own name per the International Investments Statute. Grants immediate permanent residency - no need to first hold an M visa. R Visa must be renewed every 5 years. Expires if absent from Colombia for more than 2 consecutive years. Official total visa cost is USD 425 (includes ~USD 50 study fee) per the Cancilleria Resident Investor's Visa page; real-estate route requires min USD 200,000 while non-real-estate direct investment requires min USD 100,000.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Working Holiday (V-Working Holiday)
COL.purpose: Visa for young foreigners from countries with reciprocal working holiday agreements who wish to travel and work temporarily in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Available only to nationals of countries with bilateral working holiday agreements with Colombia. Age restrictions typically apply (18-30 years). Allows temporary employment to fund travel.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Airport Transit (V-Transit)
COL.purpose: Visa for passengers transiting through Colombian international airports without entering Colombian territory.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Most passengers may transit without a visa for up to 24 hours. Certain nationalities require a transit visa. Must not leave the international zone of the airport.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Medical Treatment (V-Medical)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners entering Colombia to receive medical treatment, healthcare consultations, or medical procedures.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Required documentation includes proof of medical appointment/treatment in Colombia. Visa-exempt nationalities may enter for medical purposes without a visa for stays under 90 days.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Spouse/Partner of Colombian National (M-Marriage)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreign spouses or permanent partners of Colombian citizens or Colombian residents.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Includes both legally married spouses and permanent/common-law partners. Open work permit included. After 3 continuous years on M-Marriage visa, holder may apply for R (Resident) visa. Automatically loses validity if absent from Colombia more than 6 consecutive months.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Parent/Child of Colombian National (M-Family)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreign parents of Colombian nationals (by birth or adoption) or foreign children adopted by Colombian nationals.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Covers: foreign parent by birth of a Colombian national, and parent/child by adoption relationships. After 3 continuous years, may apply for R (Resident) visa.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - CAN/Andean Migrant (M-Andean)
COL.purpose: Visa for nationals of Andean Community (CAN) member states (Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru) seeking to reside long-term in Colombia under the Andean Migratory Statute.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Facilitated pathway for CAN nationals under Decision 545 of the Andean Community on Free Mobility and Residence. Provides simplified documentation requirements and path to residency.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - MERCOSUR Migrant (M-MERCOSUR)
COL.purpose: Visa for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associate states seeking to reside long-term in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Facilitated pathway for nationals of Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, Chile under MERCOSUR free movement agreements. Colombia is a MERCOSUR associated state.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Income Recipient/Rentista (M-Rentista)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners with a stable periodic income from foreign sources (rental income, dividends, royalties, etc.) who wish to reside in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. For foreigners with passive income from creditable sources (different from retirement pensions which have M-Pensionado). Income must be provably periodic. After 5 continuous years, may qualify for R (Resident) visa.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Refugee (M-Refugee)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners who have been granted refugee status by Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Issued after formal recognition of refugee status by Colombian authorities per Law 1997 of 2019 and international refugee conventions. Fee may be waived for humanitarian cases.

COL.name: Resident Visa - Accumulated Residency (R-Accumulated)
COL.purpose: Permanent residency visa for foreigners who have held a Colombian temporary/migrant visa and lived in Colombia continuously for the required number of years.
COL.notes: Part of R (Resident) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Residency accumulation periods vary by M-visa type: 2 years (CAN/MERCOSUR), 3 years (marriage, investment), 5 years (retirement, rentista, expertise). Application must be made at least 30 calendar days before visa expiration. R Visa renewed every 5 years. Expires if absent from Colombia more than 2 consecutive years. Official visa cost is USD 300 per the Cancilleria Qualified Resident's Visa page.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Courtesy Visa (V-Courtesy)
COL.purpose: Visa granted to foreign officials, government representatives, and special categories as a diplomatic courtesy.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Granted at the discretion of the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs to accredited foreign officials and special diplomatic categories. Fee typically waived.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Internship (V-Internship)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners undertaking professional training or internship positions in Colombian organizations.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. For formal internship and professional training programs. Must have a sponsoring organization in Colombia.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Social Cooperation/Volunteering (V-Volunteer)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners participating in development, human rights, or humanitarian projects in Colombia on a volunteer basis.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Requires sponsorship by a registered Colombian NGO or international organization. No salary may be received from Colombian sources.

COL.name: Migrant Visa - Internationalization Promotion (M-Internationalization)
COL.purpose: Visa for advanced degree holders (master's or doctorate) in fields of national interest who contribute to Colombia's economic and technological development.
COL.notes: Part of M (Migrant) category under Resolución 5477 de 2022. Created to attract highly skilled foreigners in priority sectors. Holder must have at least a master's degree. After 3 continuous years, may qualify for R (Resident) visa.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Events (V-Eventos)
COL.purpose: Short-stay entry to attend or take part in business, cultural, academic, sporting, or artistic events, conventions, and congresses in Colombia.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022 ('Eventos'). For attendees, speakers, performers, or athletes at conventions and business/cultural/academic events. Any work permit is limited to the specific event. Visa-exempt nationalities may attend short events without a visa.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Crew Member (V-Tripulante)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreign crew of vessels or aircraft working in Colombian jurisdictional waters or airspace.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022 ('Tripulante'). Grants a work permit limited to the crew activity. Crew of fishing vessels in the San Andres, Providencia and Santa Catalina archipelago are fee-exempt per the official cost schedule.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Seasonal Agricultural Worker (V-Trabajador Agricola de Temporada)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners performing seasonal agricultural work under programs established by Colombia's Ministry of Labour.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022 ('Trabajador agricola de temporada'). Grants a work permit limited to seasonal agricultural labour under Ministry of Labour programs.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Religious Worker/Missionary (V-Religioso)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners coming to Colombia to exercise a religious ministry or to serve as missionaries.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022 ('Religioso'). Grants a work permit limited to religious ministry or missionary activity for a specific religious entity. A related V subcategory covers religious students and religious volunteers ('Estudiante o voluntario religioso').

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Journalist/Press Correspondent (V-Corresponsal/Periodista)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreign journalists providing short-term news coverage in Colombia, or serving as a permanent correspondent of a foreign news outlet.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022. Covers two official subcategories: short-term journalistic coverage ('Cubrimiento periodistico') and permanent foreign press correspondent ('Corresponsal permanente'). Work permit limited to the accredited journalistic activity.

COL.name: Visitor Visa - Service Provider (V-Prestador de Servicios)
COL.purpose: Visa for foreigners temporarily providing services in Colombia under a service or works-and-labour contract with a Colombian entity.
COL.notes: Part of V (Visitor) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022 ('Prestador de servicios - obra o labor'). Work permit limited to the contracted service. Distinct from the M-Worker visa (fixed-term or indefinite employment contract) and the V-Technical Assistance visa.

COL.name: Resident Visa - Former Colombian National / Renunciation (R-Renuncia)
COL.purpose: Residency visa for foreigners who were formerly Colombian nationals by birth or adoption and who renounced Colombian nationality.
COL.notes: Part of R (Resident) category under Resolucion 5477 de 2022 ('Residente - Renuncia a nacionalidad'). Grants permanent residency and an open work permit. R Visa is renewed every 5 years; expires if the holder is absent from Colombia for more than 2 continuous years.

COL.name: Beneficiary Visa (Visa de Beneficiario)
COL.purpose: Dependent visa issued to the economically dependent immediate family of a principal V, M, or R visa holder.
COL.notes: Official standalone category on the Cancilleria visa catalogue ('Visa de beneficiario') under Resolucion 5477 de 2022. Beneficiaries are the spouse or permanent partner, children, and dependent parents of the principal visa holder. Validity mirrors the principal's visa; work authorization depends on the principal visa type (R and some M principals grant open work permits to beneficiaries).

COM.name: Transit Visa
COM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to transit through Comoros en route to another destination. Issued at the airport or port of entry.
COM.notes: Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 2 as 'un visa de transit permettant un séjour d'une durée maximum de cinq jours'. Issued at the point of entry. No paid work permitted during stay.

COM.name: Tourist Visa (45-day)
COM.purpose: Permits short-term tourism and leisure visits to Comoros for up to 45 days. Available on arrival at the airport or port.
COM.notes: Fee listed as 60 EUR by the official UN Mission of Comoros page (approximately USD 65 at typical rates). IATA Timatic cites 30 EUR; US State Department cites 30–50 EUR - discrepancy unresolved; 60 EUR is retained from the official UN Mission source. Holder may not engage in any paid work (Loi n°88-025, Art. 8). Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 2.

COM.name: Short-Stay Visa
COM.purpose: Permits stays of up to 3 months for tourism or short-term purposes. Renewable once.
COM.notes: Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 2 as a short-stay visa valid for a maximum of 3 months, renewable once. No paid work permitted. Fee determined by Finance Law - not specified in the law text itself.

COM.name: Long-Stay Visa (1-Year)
COM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Comoros for up to one year. Issued to those intending stays exceeding 3 months.
COM.notes: Fee listed as 250 EUR by the official UN Mission of Comoros page (approximately USD 272). Application must be made through diplomatic channels; decision is by Council of Ministers (Loi n°88-025, Art. 5). A residence card is issued within 10 days of entry and is renewable annually.

COM.name: Long-Stay Visa (10-Year)
COM.purpose: Allows long-term residence in Comoros for up to 10 years. Intended for foreign nationals with established ties or professional presence.
COM.notes: Fee listed as 500 EUR by the official UN Mission of Comoros page (approximately USD 543). The 10-year residence card for professional workers is defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 10, renewable. Holder requires special authorization for professional economic activity.

COM.name: Residence Card (Professional/Work)
COM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to engage in professional or salaried economic activities in Comoros. Required for any paid employment.
COM.notes: Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 10. Issued for 10 years and renewable. Ordinary tourist and short-stay visa holders are strictly prohibited from any paid work (Art. 8). Brief business transactions and temporary commerce may be authorized by special permission. Fee set by Finance Law (not specified in law text).

COM.name: Diplomatic Visa
COM.purpose: Issued to members of diplomatic missions, consular representations, and their families. Exempt from visa fees.
COM.notes: Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 3. Covers heads of diplomatic missions, consular representatives, and their household family members. Exempt from visa fees per Art. 15. Duration tied to accreditation period.

COM.name: Service Visa
COM.purpose: Issued to non-diplomatic foreign government personnel and public servants on official assignment in Comoros.
COM.notes: Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 3. Covers non-diplomatic administrative and technical personnel at foreign missions and foreign public servants on official duty. Duration tied to the period of official assignment.

COM.name: Courtesy Visa
COM.purpose: Issued to official visitors and dignitaries visiting Comoros at the invitation of the government.
COM.notes: Defined under Loi n°88-025, Art. 3. Issued at government discretion for official visitors. Fee exemption applies per Art. 15 alongside diplomatic visas.

COM.name: Business / Short-Stay Visa with Commercial Authorization
COM.purpose: Permits brief business transactions and temporary commercial activity in Comoros for foreign nationals, subject to special authorization.
COM.notes: Loi n°88-025, Art. 8 prohibits all paid work on a standard tourist or short-stay visa. Brief commercial transactions and temporary commerce are permitted only with specific governmental authorization. This is not a separate named visa category in the law but a conditional permission layer applied to the short-stay visa. No standalone business visa category found in official sources.

CPV.name: Visto de Trânsito (Transit Visa)
CPV.purpose: For travellers transiting through Cabo Verde to another country who disembark and remain in the country briefly before continuing their journey.
CPV.notes: Stay limited to 4 days; extendable once. Available via the consular portal at portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv. Transit passengers remaining airside (without clearing immigration) do not need a transit visa.

CPV.name: Visto Diplomático, Oficial ou de Cortesia (Diplomatic / Official / Courtesy Visa)
CPV.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports, and to persons traveling at the invitation of Cabo Verdean authorities.
CPV.notes: Must be used within 90 days of issuance. Allows stays of up to 30 days per entry with multiple entries possible during the 90-day validity window. Holders of diplomatic and service passports of any country are generally exempt from prior visa requirements per Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2025.

CPV.name: Visto de Turismo (Tourist Visa)
CPV.purpose: For recreational activities, leisure, and cruise travel to Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Must be used within 60 days of issuance. Allows a stay of up to 90 days, extendable once for an additional 90 days. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv. All travellers must also pre-register via ease.gov.cv and pay the Airport Security Fee (TSA: approx CVE 3,400 / EUR 30.83 for international arrivals).

CPV.name: Visto Temporário - Missão Empresarial (Temporary Visa: Business Mission)
CPV.purpose: For business missions, short-term commercial activities, and professional engagements in Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto Temporário. Single-entry variant permits stays up to 180 days. Multiple-entry variant allows a total of 90 days within one year. Also covers short-term professional/technical activities. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto Temporário - Cultural (Temporary Visa: Cultural)
CPV.purpose: For cultural trips, artistic residencies, and participation in cultural events in Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto Temporário. Must be used within 180 days of issuance. Multiple-entry variant allows 90 days total over one year. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto Temporário - Tratamento Médico (Temporary Visa: Medical Treatment)
CPV.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Cabo Verde to receive medical treatment.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto Temporário. Must be used within 180 days of issuance. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto Temporário - Visita Familiar (Temporary Visa: Family Visit)
CPV.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting family members residing in Cabo Verde on a short-term basis.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto Temporário. Multiple-entry variant allows 90 days total within one year. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto Temporário - Trabalho Qualificado / Atividade Profissional (Temporary Visa: Short-term Work / Professional Activity)
CPV.purpose: For short-term qualified or professional work not exceeding one year - including artistic and sporting activities, technical assignments and teaching roles - that does not require establishing permanent residence.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto Temporário, distinct from the permanent-employment Visto de Residência - Trabalho. Per the Alta Autoridade para a Imigração (AAI) official page, the Temporary Visa covers cultural trips, business missions, professional activities, artistic/sports work, technical positions, teaching roles and qualified work not exceeding one year. Single-entry variant permits stays up to 180 days; multiple-entry variant allows 90 days total within one year. Must be used within 180 days of issuance. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv; also described at aai.gov.cv/imigrantes/entrada-permanencia-e-saida-de-cabo-verde/vistos.

CPV.name: Visto de Residência - Trabalho (Residence Visa: Employment)
CPV.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to take up professional employment and establish permanent residence in Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto de Residência. Allows the holder to remain for 6 months, extendable until a final decision is made on the residence permit application. Must obtain a full Autorização de Residência after arrival. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto de Residência - Investimento (Residence Visa: Investment)
CPV.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to carry out investment or economically relevant activities and establish residence in Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto de Residência. Grants 6-month stay extendable pending residence permit decision. Related to the Green Card (real estate investment, min EUR 80,000–120,000) and Autorização de Residência for investment activity. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv and e-portaldef.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto de Residência - Estudante (Residence Visa: Studies)
CPV.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolling in higher education or courses lasting more than one year in Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto de Residência. Applies to study programs lasting over one year. Grants a 6-month stay extendable pending residence permit decision. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto de Residência - Reagrupamento Familiar (Residence Visa: Family Reunification)
CPV.purpose: For foreign nationals joining family members who are legally resident in Cabo Verde.
CPV.notes: Sub-category of the Visto de Residência for permanent family reunification. Grants a 6-month stay extendable pending residence permit decision. Application via portalconsular.mnec.gov.cv.

CPV.name: Visto Nómadas Digitais (Digital Nomad Visa)
CPV.purpose: For persons who work remotely for a company or entity located outside Cabo Verde and wish to reside in the country.
CPV.notes: Listed on the official National Police / e-Residência portal (e-portaldef.gov.cv). Required documents include: passport, criminal record from country of origin, proof of remote employment/contract with employer outside Cabo Verde, proof of income, proof of accommodation in Cabo Verde, and a medical certificate. The application portal was listed as 'Em manutenção' (under maintenance) as of June 2026. No income threshold, duration of stay, or fee stated on the official page.

CRI.name: Visa-Free Entry – Group 1
CRI.purpose: Tourism, business, family visits, and other short-stay purposes for nationals of approximately 60 privileged countries including USA, Canada, EU/Schengen, UK, Australia, Japan, South Korea, and select Latin American nations.
CRI.notes: No visa required. Passport must be valid for at least 1 natural day from the intended entry date (per DGME Alcance N° 148, La Gaceta N° 216, 17 November 2025). Stay of up to 180 calendar days. Proof of onward travel and sufficient funds may be requested at entry.

CRI.name: Visa-Free Entry – Group 2
CRI.purpose: Tourism, business, and short-stay visits for nationals of Group 2 countries including most Pacific island states, certain CARICOM members, Central American countries, Russia, Turkey, Malaysia, Philippines, and others.
CRI.notes: No visa required. Passport must be valid for at least 3 months (90 natural days) from the intended entry date. Stay of up to 30 calendar days; may be extendable to 90 days. Honduran nationals aged 18 and over must present a non-apostilled national police clearance certificate upon entry (unless they hold a qualifying US/Canada/Schengen/EU/UK/Iceland/Norway/Switzerland credential).

CRI.name: Visa Consular – Group 3 (Consular Visa)
CRI.purpose: General entry for nationals of countries classified in Group 3 who require a prior consular visa to enter Costa Rica for tourism, business, family visits, or other short-stay purposes.
CRI.notes: Must be obtained in advance from a Costa Rican consulate. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the intended entry date. Processing time: 30–60 calendar days after receipt of all required documents. Stay of up to 30 calendar days. Group 3 covers approximately 80+ countries including India, China, Colombia, Kenya, and most African, Asian, and Middle Eastern nations. Nationals holding a valid US, Canadian, or Schengen multiple-entry visa (or qualifying residence permit) may be exempt.

CRI.name: Visa Restringida – Group 4 (Restricted Visa)
CRI.purpose: General entry for nationals of approximately 23 high-risk countries (including Afghanistan, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria) who are subject to the most restrictive visa category.
CRI.notes: Must be obtained in advance from a Costa Rican consulate. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the intended entry date. Processing time: up to 90 calendar days. Stay of up to 30 calendar days, extendable to a maximum of 90 days. Fee is USD 52. Application subject to additional security review.

CRI.name: Visa de Tránsito (Transit Visa)
CRI.purpose: Airport transit through Costa Rica for nationals of Group 4 and specified African and Asian countries who do not have a qualifying onward visa to an exempt destination.
CRI.notes: Required for Group 4 nationals and certain other nationalities transiting through Costa Rican airports. Visa is issued with a 3-month (90-day) validity from the stamp date; the holder may remain in transit for up to 60 calendar days post-stamping. Stay is non-extendable. Applicant must hold an air ticket reservation and, if applicable, a valid visa for the final destination country.

CRI.name: Residencia Provisional por Motivos Religiosos (Religious Provisional Temporary Residency)
CRI.purpose: Temporary residency permit for foreign nationals engaged in religious work or activities through a legally registered Costa Rican religious congregation.
CRI.notes: Classified as a 'Temporary Residency Provisional' category. Available to nationals of Group 1 through Group 3 countries (Group 4 nationals are excluded from this path). Requires a sponsoring letter from a recognized Costa Rican religious congregation. Duration is determined by the needs of the religious congregation. Application processed through the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME).

CRI.name: Nómadas Digitales – Permiso de Permanencia Temporal (Digital Nomad Temporary Stay Permit)
CRI.purpose: Permits foreign nationals who work remotely for clients or employers located outside Costa Rica to reside in the country for up to one year while performing their professional activities using digital or telecommunication technologies.
CRI.notes: Established under General Law of Migration and Foreigners Article 256 and Law 10008 (Item 11 bis). Minimum income requirement: USD 3,000/month (USD 4,000/month if including dependents), documented over the prior 12 months from sources outside Costa Rica. Government fee: USD 100 (or equivalent in colones, payable to Bank of Costa Rica account 001-0242480-0). Health insurance covering the full stay with a minimum coverage of USD 50,000 is required. Applications submitted via the online TramiteYa platform or in person at DGME offices. Duration: 1 year, renewable once for an additional year (maximum 2 years total). Permit holders are exempt from paying Costa Rican income taxes and customs duties on electronic devices used professionally.

CRI.name: Residencia Temporal – Categoría Pensionado (Pensionado/Retiree Temporary Residency)
CRI.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign retirees who receive a permanent lifetime pension from a recognized authority (Social Security, military, retirement fund, or annuity) of at least USD 1,000 per month.
CRI.notes: Governed by Ley General de Migración y Extranjería No. 8764 and Law 9996. Minimum pension requirement: USD 1,000 per month from a permanent, certified foreign authority. Temporary residence is issued for 2 years and is renewable. Provides a path to citizenship via naturalization after 7 years of legal residency (5 years for Central Americans, Spaniards, and Latin Americans). Application requires notarized proof of pension, apostilled documents, criminal background check, medical certificate, and proof of accommodation. No work authorization is included; pensionados may not engage in paid employment in Costa Rica.

CRI.name: Residencia Temporal – Categoría Inversionista (Investor Temporary Residency)
CRI.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals who make a qualifying investment of at least USD 150,000 in Costa Rica in approved categories such as real estate, company shares, SUGEVAL-authorized securities, venture capital funds, tourism infrastructure, or national interest projects.
CRI.notes: Governed by Law No. 9996 (Official Gazette La Gaceta No. 135, July 14, 2021). Minimum qualifying investment: USD 150,000 (reduced from USD 200,000 under a sunset clause provision in Article 4). Investment must be maintained continuously. Temporary residence issued for 2 years, renewable. Permits path to citizenship after 7 years of residency (5 years for Central Americans, Spaniards, and Latin Americans). Approved investment categories include: real estate, active business shares, SUGEVAL-regulated securities, venture capital funds, tourism infrastructure, or projects declared in the national interest.

CRI.name: Residencia Temporal – Categoría Rentista (Rentista/Fixed-Income Temporary Residency)
CRI.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals who can demonstrate stable monthly income of at least USD 2,500 per month from foreign sources, without a requirement to hold a government pension.
CRI.notes: Governed by Law No. 9996 and Executive Decree No. 37112. Minimum income: USD 2,500 per month from stable foreign-source revenue (e.g., dividends, rental income, royalties, investment returns). Income must originate outside Costa Rica, demonstrated via certified bank statements. Temporary residence issued for 2 years, renewable. Path to citizenship via naturalization after 7 years (5 years for Central Americans, Spaniards, and Latin Americans). Rentistas may not work in Costa Rica.

CRI.name: Residencia Temporal por Vínculo con Costarricense (Spouse/Family of a Costa Rican)
CRI.purpose: Temporary residence for the foreign spouse of a Costa Rican citizen, and, as a special category, for the parents of a Costa Rican child and other first-degree family members of a Costa Rican national.
CRI.notes: Governed by Ley General de Migración y Extranjería No. 8764. Marriage to a Costa Rican is processed as a temporary residence ('Por Cónyuge costarricense'); the parent of a Costa Rican minor or other first-degree relative of a Costa Rican is processed as a special category ('Vínculo con ciudadano costarricense'). Requires a certified marriage/birth link with the Costa Rican, apostilled/legalized foreign documents, and a criminal record certificate. As a first-degree relative of a Costa Rican, the holder is generally authorized to work. After three consecutive years the holder may request a change to permanent residence. Filed through the DGME Trámite Ya online platform or in person.

CRI.name: Categoría Especial por Vínculo con Residente (Family Dependent of a Resident)
CRI.purpose: Special category for the spouse and first-degree dependents (children, and where applicable a guardian/curator link) of a foreign national who already holds permanent or temporary residence in Costa Rica.
CRI.notes: Special migratory category under Ley 8764 ('Vínculo con Residente Permanente' / 'Vínculo con Curador o tutor'). The dependent's legal permanence is tied to, and cannot exceed, the principal resident's status. Requires proof of the family link and of the principal's valid residence. Filed via the DGME Trámite Ya platform or in person at DGME.

CRI.name: Residencia Temporal como Empleado(a) Especializado(a) / Trabajador de Empresa (Company Worker)
CRI.purpose: Temporary residence for a foreign national hired in a dependent employment relationship by a Costa Rican company or institution, including specialized employees, scientists, professionals, specialized technicians, executives, managers, and representatives.
CRI.notes: Governed by Ley 8764 and the Reglamento de Extranjería (Decreto No. 37112). The sponsoring employer must be registered with the DGME and current on CCSS (social security) obligations, and a work contract per Articles 23-24 of the Labor Code is required; registered employers are classified into tiers that affect processing. Companies operating under the foreign-trade regime apply through a dedicated COMEX regulation. Work authorization is limited to the sponsoring employer. Filed via the DGME Trámite Ya platform or through the accredited employer.

CRI.name: Categoría Especial de Trabajador de Ocupación Específica (Specific-Occupation Worker)
CRI.purpose: Special-category work permit for foreign nationals performing a defined specific occupation, including domestic workers, self-employed specific-occupation workers, intra-company transferred personnel, business-visitor personnel, and after-sales technical personnel.
CRI.notes: Special migratory category under Article 94 of Ley 8764. Subcategories listed by the DGME include: specific-occupation worker for a physical employer (e.g. domestic worker), for a natural person, for a legal person, self-employed (por cuenta propia), intra-company transferred personnel, business-visitor personnel, and after-sales personnel.
