Applicant must document funds of ~DKK 15,000 plus ~DKK 5,000 for a return ticket, and full health/hospital/repatriation insurance. Processing time approximately 3 months. Applied online (or paper form) via SIRI/nyidanmark.dk.

DNK.name: Au Pair Residence Permit
DNK.purpose: Cultural-exchange residence permit for a young person aged 18-29 to live with a Danish host family, help with light housework and childcare in exchange for board, lodging and monthly pocket money.
DNK.notes: SIRI case-processing fee DKK 4,305 (~USD 633). Applicant must be at least 18 and must not have turned 30 at the time of application (exception when changing host family). Permit granted for a maximum of 2 years, limited to the au pair contract period or until the youngest child in the family turns 18. Host family must pay pocket money of at least DKK 5,250/month (2026 level) and, for first-time applicants, a one-off DKK 20,900 (2026 level) to cover the au pair's Danish lessons. Processing time normally 3 months (up to 4 if further information is needed). Online or paper application (form AU1).

DNK.name: Graduate Job-Seeking Residence Permit (3 years)
DNK.purpose: Residence permit allowing non-EU/EEA graduates of a Danish professional bachelor, bachelor, master or PhD programme to stay in Denmark for up to 3 years after completing their studies to look for and take up work.
DNK.notes: Fee DKK 3,060 (~USD 450). Open to holders of a Danish student residence permit who have completed a state-approved professional bachelor, bachelor, master or PhD programme. Valid for up to 3 years (cannot extend to beyond 3 months before passport expiry). Grants the same work rights held as a student: up to 90 hours/month September-May and full time June-August; a job requiring more hours needs a separate work permit. Replaced the Establishment Card scheme, which was abolished on 1 April 2023 (only extensions of existing establishment cards remain possible). Permit lapses if the holder gives up their Danish address or stays abroad for more than 6 consecutive months (exceptions for PhD and certain Erasmus programmes). Processing time approximately 3 months.

DNK.name: Religious Worker Residence Permit
DNK.purpose: Residence and work permit for missionaries, preachers and other religious workers affiliated with an officially recognised religious denomination or order in Denmark.
DNK.notes: Fee DKK 10,760 (~USD 1,582). Initial permit granted for seven months (~210 days); extendable one year at a time up to a maximum of 3 years total (longer if the holder is authorised to perform weddings). Applicant must document work as a missionary or religious worker for an officially acknowledged/sanctioned denomination in Denmark. Within 6 months the holder must pass an extension test (Danish language and knowledge of Danish society) and complete a course in Danish family law, individual rights and democracy. A national sanction list bans certain named religious preachers from entering Denmark. Application form RF1, available online. Expected maximum processing time 6 months.

DNK.name: Diplomatic/Official Entry (Passport-Based Exemption)
DNK.purpose: Visa-free entry to Denmark for holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports from countries that have bilateral visa-exemption agreements with Denmark, allowing official and non-official visits without a Schengen visa.
DNK.notes: No visa required. Applies to holders of diplomatic/service/official passports from countries with bilateral agreements with Denmark, including (but not limited to): Bolivia (diplomatic + service), China (diplomatic only), Egypt (diplomatic + service), India (diplomatic + service + official), Indonesia (biometric diplomatic + biometric service), Morocco (diplomatic + service), Pakistan (diplomatic + service + official), Philippines (diplomatic + service), Thailand (diplomatic + service + official), Turkey (diplomatic + service). Albania, Armenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Tunisia, Ukraine (diplomatic only for most). Full list in the official PDF overview document.

DNK.name: Visa-Free Short Stay (Schengen 90/180 Rule)
DNK.purpose: Allows nationals of visa-exempt countries to enter and stay in Denmark (and the Schengen Area) for up to 90 days in any 180-day period for tourism, business, family visits, or other short-term purposes without obtaining a visa.
DNK.notes: No visa required. Valid travel document must be valid for at least 3 months beyond intended departure and issued within the last 10 years. Must show sufficient financial means (approx. DKK 350/day private or DKK 500/day hotel), documentation of visit purpose, and must not be registered in the Schengen Information System or listed on UN/EU sanctions. Special bilateral arrangements for nationals of Australia, Canada, Chile, Israel, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea, and the USA allow 90 days/3 months calculated from first Nordic entry. ETIAS authorization will be required once launched (expected Q4 2026; EUR 20 fee).

DOM.name: Simple Tourism Visa (TS)
DOM.purpose: Single-entry tourist visa for short-term tourism and leisure visits to the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Required only for nationals not on the visa-free list. Applications submitted in-person or by email at Dominican consulates. Processing 10–20 business days. Most travelers from US, EU, Canada, UK and many other countries do not need this visa.

DOM.name: Multiple Tourism Visa (TM)
DOM.purpose: Multiple-entry tourist visa allowing repeated short-stay tourism visits to the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Multiple-entry version of the tourist visa. Each stay up to 60 days. Applications via Dominican consulates in-person or by email.

DOM.name: Simple Business Visa (NS)
DOM.purpose: Single-entry visa for foreign nationals traveling for business purposes such as meetings, conferences, or negotiations.
DOM.notes: For business activities not involving local employment. Applications via Dominican consulates.

DOM.name: Multiple Business Visa (NM)
DOM.purpose: Multiple-entry visa valid for one year for frequent business travelers visiting the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: One-year multiple-entry business visa. Each stay up to 60 days. Applications via Dominican consulates.

DOM.name: Business Visa with Labor Purposes (NM1)
DOM.purpose: Multiple-entry work visa for foreign nationals employed by private companies, multinationals, free trade zone companies, or international organizations operating in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Covers employment in private companies, multinational/transnational companies, free trade zones, and international organizations or public institutions. Valid 1 year, multiple entries. Labor contract and employer sponsorship required.

DOM.name: Temporary Worker Visa (VTT)
DOM.purpose: Visa for temporary foreign workers performing short-term labor in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Temporary Worker Visa (código VTT), US$95 per the MIREX consular fee schedule (tasas consulares). Lower-cost work visa category for temporary/short-term labor, distinct from the NM1 business-with-labor-purposes visa. Applications via Dominican consulates.

DOM.name: Artists, Athletes & Exchange Students Permit (PADEI)
DOM.purpose: Non-resident permit for foreigners entering the Dominican Republic to temporarily perform an artistic or sporting activity, undertake an exchange study, or provide voluntary service.
DOM.notes: Permiso para Artistas, Deportistas y Estudiantes de Intercambio (PADEI), issued by the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) rather than as a consular visa. Valid 1 year, renewable annually up to a maximum of 4 years. Requires the applicant to already hold a valid Multiple Business (NM) or Student (E) visa, plus a sponsoring institution/company certification (notarized and legalized), a medical certificate, and DGM-approved medical insurance. Covers performing artists, athletes, exchange students, and volunteers.

DOM.name: Student Visa (E)
DOM.purpose: Multiple-entry visa for foreign nationals enrolled in educational programs including university studies, religious studies, or internships in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Valid 1 year with multiple entries. Covers university enrollment, religious studies, and internships. Proof of enrollment from an accredited Dominican institution required.

DOM.name: Family Reunification Residency Visa (RS)
DOM.purpose: Single-entry visa issued to family members of Dominican residents or citizens seeking to reunite with their family in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Entry visa to initiate the family reunification residency process. After arrival, holders apply for temporary or permanent residence through DGM (migracion.gob.do).

DOM.name: Pensioner/Retiree Residency Visa (RS – Pensionado)
DOM.purpose: Entry visa for foreign retirees seeking residency in the Dominican Republic based on a qualifying pension income.
DOM.notes: Requires proof of a minimum monthly pension of US$1,500 from a government or private entity, plus US$250 per dependent. Grants entry to then apply for permanent residency. Under Law 285-04 / Regulation 631-11.

DOM.name: Rentista Residency Visa (RS – Rentista)
DOM.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals with passive income sources seeking residency in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Requires proof of at least US$2,000/month in passive income (investments, dividends, rental income - not active employment), plus US$250 per dependent. Leads to permanent residency. Under Law 285-04 / Regulation 631-11.

DOM.name: Investor Residency Visa (RS – Inversionista)
DOM.purpose: Entry visa for foreign investors making a qualifying capital investment in a Dominican company, leading to immediate permanent residency.
DOM.notes: Minimum capital contribution of US$200,000 in a Dominican company registered with ProDominicana. Investment may be in currency, in-kind, financial instruments, or technology. Grants immediate permanent residency (no prior temporary residency required). After 2 years of permanent residence, eligible for naturalisation. Under Law 285-04 / Regulation 631-11.

DOM.name: Residence Visa (RS – Residencia)
DOM.purpose: General residence entry visa for foreign nationals approved to establish residence in the Dominican Republic (outside the pensioner, rentista, and investor tracks), leading to Temporary Residence (Residencia Temporal RT-9).
DOM.notes: Base residence visa (US$200 per the MIREX consular fee schedule), issued by a Dominican consulate to foreigners approved to reside in the country - e.g. for employment, marriage to a Dominican, or general settlement. After arrival the holder applies at the Dirección General de Migración (migracion.gob.do) for Residencia Temporal (RT-9), valid 1 year and renewable, which is the pathway to permanent residence and the cédula. Requires an apostilled birth certificate translated to Spanish, a police clearance certificate, a medical certificate, and proof of financial solvency (minimum RD$300,000).

DOM.name: Multiple Dependency Visa (DPM)
DOM.purpose: Multiple-entry visa for dependents (spouse, minor children) of foreign nationals legally residing or working in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries. Issued to dependents of visa/residency holders. Proof of relationship and primary holder's legal status required.

DOM.name: Diplomatic Visa (DM – Multiple)
DOM.purpose: Multiple-entry visa for accredited diplomatic personnel and their families assigned to official missions in the Dominican Republic.
DOM.notes: Issued free of charge to holders of diplomatic passports on assignment. A Diplomatic Note from the relevant mission specifying diplomatic rank or position is required. Many countries' diplomatic passport holders are fully visa-exempt per bilateral agreements. Simple (DS) and multiple (DM) categories exist.

DOM.name: Official Visa (OS/OM)
DOM.purpose: Single or multiple-entry visa for government officials and service passport holders traveling on official business.
DOM.notes: Issued free of charge. OS = Official Simple, OM = Official Multiple. For official/service passport holders on government business. Diplomatic Note from issuing government required.

DOM.name: Courtesy Visa (CS/CM)
DOM.purpose: Complimentary visa issued as a courtesy to certain foreign officials, dignitaries, or persons of note not qualifying for full diplomatic status.
DOM.notes: Issued free of charge. CS = Courtesy Simple (60 days), CM = Courtesy Multiple (1 year). Granted at the discretion of MIREX.

DOM.name: Emergency Entry Facility (7-day)
DOM.purpose: Exceptional short-term entry authorization for special humanitarian or emergency cases not covered by standard visa categories.
DOM.notes: Emergency entry without a standard visa for a maximum of 7 days granted in special humanitarian or exceptional cases. Issued at DGM (Dirección General de Migración) discretion.

DZA.name: Tourist Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for holiday and leisure travel to Algeria. Also available as a regularization visa on arrival for organized tours exclusively to southern provinces.
DZA.notes: Must apply at Algerian embassy/consulate before travel. No e-visa system exists. Visa on arrival (regularization visa) available only for organized tours to specific southern provinces (Adrar, Tamanrasset, etc.) for all nationalities when booked through an Algerian-accredited travel agency. Validity periods available: 90 days, 180 days, 1 year, or 2 years. Max stay per entry: 90 days; cumulative: 180 days per year.

DZA.name: Business Visa
DZA.purpose: Short-term entry for commercial activities, meetings, and business negotiations in Algeria.
DZA.notes: Must apply at Algerian embassy/consulate before travel. Supports single or multiple entry. Validity can range from 90 days to 2 years.

DZA.name: Work Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for long-term employment in Algeria under a contract with an Algerian employer.
DZA.notes: Higher fee than tourist/business. Requires a work permit issued by Algerian authorities prior to visa application. Single or multiple entry supported.

DZA.name: Temporary Work Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for contract-based or temporary employment in Algeria for a period not exceeding 90 days.
DZA.notes: For short-term contract work of up to 90 days. Same fee category as the long-term work visa.

DZA.name: Family Reunion Visa (Spouse)
DZA.purpose: Entry for spouses of Algerian citizens or residents to join their family in Algeria.
DZA.notes: Requires proof of marriage and Algerian spouse's documentation. Single or multiple entry supported.

DZA.name: Family Reunion Visa (Children)
DZA.purpose: Entry for minor children of Algerian citizens or residents to join their family in Algeria.
DZA.notes: Requires proof of parentage and Algerian parent's documentation.

DZA.name: Cultural / Scientific / Sports Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals invited to participate in cultural, scientific, social, or sporting events in Algeria.
DZA.notes: Requires official invitation from an Algerian institution or event organizer. Covers cultural, scientific, social, and sports event participants.

DZA.name: Medical Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals seeking medical treatment in Algeria.
DZA.notes: Distinct official category - the Algerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists 'medical' and 'study' as separate visa types. Requires supporting documentation such as a hospital/clinic admission or invitation. Must apply at an Algerian embassy/consulate before travel; no e-visa. Chancery fee varies by nationality under the principle of reciprocity; the £85 shown is the UK consulate rate. Max stay 90 days per entry.

DZA.name: Study Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals enrolled at an Algerian-approved educational establishment or holding a scholarship, to pursue studies in Algeria.
DZA.notes: Distinct official category per the Algerian MFA (previously merged with 'medical' in this dataset). Requires a certificate of registration in a public or private educational establishment approved by the Algerian State, a scholarship certificate issued by Algerian or home-country authorities, or proof of the means to pay for studies and stay. Must apply at an Algerian embassy/consulate before travel; no e-visa. Chancery fee varies by nationality under the principle of reciprocity. General framework: validity 90/180 days, 1 year or 2 years; max stay 90 days per entry; longer study stays are continued in-country via a residence permit.

DZA.name: Press Visa
DZA.purpose: Entry for journalists and media professionals traveling to Algeria for professional reporting or to cover events.
DZA.notes: Distinct official category for members of the media. Applicants must submit a letter from their employer requesting a press visa (accreditation) on their behalf; foreign-press accreditation is coordinated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (mfa.gov.dz/services-for-foreigners/accreditation-of-journalists). Must apply at an Algerian embassy/consulate before travel; no e-visa. Chancery fee varies by nationality under the principle of reciprocity.

DZA.name: Transit Visa
DZA.purpose: Short-stay passage through Algeria en route to a third country.
DZA.notes: Lower fee than other visa types. Requires proof of onward travel and valid visa for destination country if required. Airport transit visa may also be required depending on nationality.

DZA.name: Visa Exemption (Diplomatic / Official Passport)
DZA.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic or official/service passports from eligible countries under bilateral agreements.
DZA.notes: Diplomatic-only exemptions: Argentina, Croatia, France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Romania. Diplomatic or service/official passport exemptions: Albania, Belarus, Benin, Brazil, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, Greece, Guinea, Italy, Malaysia, Mali, Malta, Mexico, Niger, Peru, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Senegal, Slovakia, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, Tanzania, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, Venezuela, Vietnam. Confirmed across Oslo and Dublin embassy pages.

ECU.name: Visa de Visitante Temporal – Turista (90 días)
ECU.purpose: Allows nationals from countries on Ecuador's special-regime (visa-required) list to enter Ecuador for tourism. Citizens of the approximately 150+ other nationalities enter visa-free without needing this visa.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 30 issuance. Available exclusively online via eVISAS portal at serviciosdigitales.cancilleria.gob.ec. Requires valid passport (6+ months), color photo, criminal background certificate (max 180-day-old, for applicants 18+), proof of lawful income, and round-trip itinerary. Stay is extendable once for an additional 90 days upon request and payment. Only required for nationals of the 45 special-regime countries; other nationalities enter visa-free for 90 days.

ECU.name: Visa de Visitante Temporal de Transeúnte
ECU.purpose: Required for nationals of the 45 visa-required countries who are transiting through Ecuadorian airports, including those remaining in the international transit zone.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 30 issuance. Effective September 1, 2025 for all 45 visa-required nationalities. Required even for airside transit (international transit area) without entering Ecuador. Applied online via eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal Rentista para Trabajo Remoto (Visa Nómada)
ECU.purpose: Allows foreign nationals who work remotely for employers or clients based outside Ecuador to reside in Ecuador while conducting their work digitally.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 400 grant. Valid for 2 years, renewable for an additional 2 years. Minimum income requirement: 3x the Unified Basic Salary (SBU) per month (~USD 1,446/month in 2026, SBU = USD 482). Additional USD 250/month income required per accompanying dependent. Applicant must work for foreign employers/clients only; valid health insurance covering Ecuador required. No Ecuador income tax on foreign-sourced income. Available to approximately 183 nationalities.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal Inversionista
ECU.purpose: Grants temporary residence to foreign nationals who make a qualifying investment in Ecuador through bank time deposits, real estate, or equity shares in an Ecuadorian company.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 270 grant. Minimum investment is 100 times the Unified Basic Salary (SBU): USD 48,200 in 2026 (SBU = USD 482/month); this amount changes annually. Three qualifying investment types: (1) bank time deposit for minimum 730 days; (2) real estate registered in cantonal Property Registry; (3) equity shares in Ecuadorian company registered with Superintendency of Companies. Visa valid 2 years; after 21 months of continuous residence, permanent residency can be requested. Path to citizenship after approximately 4 years.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal Rentista (Passive Income / Jubilado)
ECU.purpose: Allows foreign nationals with passive income from pensions, rents, or investments to reside in Ecuador. Suitable for retirees and those living off investment returns.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 200 grant. Minimum income: 3x the Unified Basic Salary (SBU) per month (~USD 1,446/month in 2026). Income must come from national or foreign sources (pensions, rents, dividends, etc.). Documentation for 3 months prior to application required. Visa duration 2 years, renewable. After 21 months continuous residence, permanent residency can be requested. Path to citizenship after approximately 4 years.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal – Trabajo Autónomo / Servicios Profesionales / Consultoría
ECU.purpose: Grants temporary residence to foreign professionals providing independent services, consulting, or autonomous professional activities in Ecuador.
ECU.notes: For independent professionals, consultants, and those providing professional services in Ecuador. Requires work authorization from Ministry of Labor or relevant authority. Specific income or qualification thresholds apply per ministerial requirements. Duration typically 2 years. Fee details not confirmed from accessible official sources at time of research.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Trabajo por Actividades Laborales bajo Relación de Dependencia
ECU.purpose: For foreign nationals employed under a dependent-employment relationship with an Ecuadorian employer.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 270 issuance (USD 320 total; 50% discount for applicants 65+, 100% exemption for persons with 30%+ disability). Valid 2 years, renewable. This is the main dependent-employment (relación de dependencia) work visa, distinct from the autonomous-work/professional-services visa above. Requires an employment contract and proof of lawful means of support. Applied online via the eVISAS portal. (Replaces a prior generic 'Residencia Temporal Profesional' placeholder that pointed only at the portal homepage.)

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Permanente por Matrimonio o Unión de Hecho
ECU.purpose: Grants permanent (indefinite) residence to foreign nationals married to, or in a registered common-law union with, an Ecuadorian citizen or a foreign national holding an indefinite/permanent Ecuadorian visa.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 175 issuance (USD 225 total). Grants indefinite (permanent) residence. Requires a marriage/union certificate registered in Ecuador, apostilled criminal-background certificate, proof of lawful means of subsistence (Acuerdo Ministerial No. 70, 2024), and an in-person interview at the Zonal Directorate or Consulate. Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: MERCOSUR Residence Agreement Visa (Visa MERCOSUR)
ECU.purpose: Grants temporary residence to nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay) based solely on nationality under the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 200 grant. Ecuador ratified the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement formally in January 2024. Grants 2-year temporary residence, renewable for an additional 2 years (change effective July 1, 2022). After two full years with proof of economic income, permanent residency can be requested. Eligible nationalities: ARG, BOL, BRA, CHL, COL, PRY, PER, URY.

ECU.name: Andean Migration Statute Residence (Estatuto Migratorio Andino / CAN)
ECU.purpose: Grants temporary residence and work authorization rights to nationals of Andean Community (CAN) member states based on the Andean Migration Statute (Decision 878).
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 200 grant. Entered into effect April 2023 under Decision 878. Eligible nationalities: BOL, COL, PER (Andean Community members). Grants 2-year temporary residence with multiple entries and includes work authorization rights. After 21 months continuous residence, permanent residency can be requested.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Estudiante
ECU.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled at an accredited Ecuadorian educational institution for basic, secondary, undergraduate or graduate study, or pre-professional/professional internships.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 80 issuance (USD 130 total; 50% discount for applicants 65+, 100% exemption for persons with 30%+ disability). Valid up to 2 years, matching the study/internship duration, renewable. Requires an enrollment/admission certificate from an officially accredited Ecuadorian institution, apostilled criminal-background certificate, and proof of lawful means of subsistence (Acuerdo Ministerial No. 70, 2024). Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Científico, Investigador o Académico
ECU.purpose: For foreign nationals contracted by recognized Ecuadorian public or private entities to carry out scientific, research or academic activities.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 270 issuance (USD 320 total; 50% discount for 65+, 100% exemption for 30%+ disability). Valid 2 years, renewable. Requires an employment contract with the sponsoring entity, professional credentials, apostilled criminal-background certificate, and proof of lawful means of support (Acuerdo Ministerial No. 70). Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal para Deportista, Artista o Gestor Cultural
ECU.purpose: For foreign athletes, artists or cultural managers contracted by a club, production company, NGO or other legally established Ecuadorian entity to perform sporting, artistic or cultural activities.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 270 issuance (USD 320 total; 50% discount for 65+, 100% exemption for 30%+ disability). Valid 2 years, renewable. Requires a contract or agreement with a sports club, production company, NGO or similar entity legally established in Ecuador, plus that entity's incorporation documents. Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal Religioso o Voluntario Religioso
ECU.purpose: For foreign nationals coming to Ecuador to carry out religious activities or religious volunteer work for an organization with legal status recognized by Ecuador.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 200 issuance (USD 250 total; 50% discount for 65+, 100% exemption for 30%+ disability). Valid 2 years, renewable once under the LOMH. Requires sponsorship by a religious organization with legal personhood recognized by Ecuador. Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Amparo (todas las categorías)
ECU.purpose: For dependents — spouse or common-law partner and children — of a foreign national who holds an Ecuadorian temporary residence visa.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 200 issuance (USD 250 total; 50% discount for 65+, 100% exemption for 30%+ disability). Validity is tied to (and cannot exceed) the validity of the principal holder's temporary residence visa. Covers the spouse/partner and children of the temporary resident. Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal por Convenio Vacaciones y Trabajo (Ecuador–Hungría)
ECU.purpose: Working-holiday visa for young Hungarian citizens (ages 18–31) coming to Ecuador for up to one year to holiday and work under the Ecuador–Hungary Working Holiday agreement.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 30 issuance (USD 80 total). Valid one year, multiple entries; granted only once and not extendable. Eligible: Hungarian citizens aged 18–31. Ecuador also operates Working Holiday agreements with Australia (concesion-visa-residencia-temporal-convenio-vacaciones-trabajo-ecuador-australia) and France, each with its own gob.ec tramite page and annual quota. Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

ECU.name: Visa de Residencia Permanente por Tiempo de Permanencia Mayor a 21 Meses
ECU.purpose: For foreign nationals who have held Ecuadorian temporary residence for more than 21 continuous months and wish to obtain permanent (indefinite) residency.
ECU.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 225 issuance (USD 275 total). Grants indefinite (permanent) residence. Main general pathway to permanent residency after 21 months of continuous temporary residence, and a prerequisite step toward naturalization. Applied online via the eVISAS portal.

EGY.name: Tourist Visa (Consular Sticker)
EGY.purpose: Tourism, leisure and short visits, applied at an Egyptian embassy or consulate
EGY.notes: Applied in person or by post at Egyptian embassies/consulates by nationalities not eligible for visa on arrival or e-Visa. Fee varies by nationality (approx US$32 single / US$67 multiple for US applicants; UK £33/£68). Visa valid 6 months from issue; max stay 30 days per entry; multiple-entry available. Extendable inside Egypt at Passport & Immigration offices. Corrected 2026-07: prior fee ($25) and official_url (visa.egov.eg, now unresolvable) were stale.

EGY.name: Visa on Arrival
EGY.purpose: Tourism - short stay, obtained at Egyptian ports of entry
EGY.notes: Single-entry sticker sold at Egyptian international airports/ports to eligible nationalities (UK, EU, USA, Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, Norway and others). US$30 paid on arrival in USD cash (fee increased from $25 effective 1 March 2026). Valid 6 months from issue, max stay 30 days; extendable inside Egypt. Free 'Sinai-only' entry permit available for South Sinai resorts. Corrected 2026-07: fee updated $25->$30; official_url moved from an airline page to the Egyptian Embassy.

EGY.name: Tourist e-Visa
EGY.purpose: Tourism and short visits - applied online before travel
EGY.notes: Official Egypt e-Visa portal operated by the Ministry of Interior. Tourism purpose only (business visits allowed if the traveller carries a company/invitation letter). Single entry US$30 (valid 90 days from issue), multiple entry US$65 (valid 180 days); max stay 30 days per entry. Apply at least 7 days before departure; pay online by card. Corrected 2026-07: fee updated $35->$30 and the dead official_url (visa.egov.eg) replaced with the live portal.

EGY.name: Business / Entry Visa (Non-Touristic)
EGY.purpose: Business meetings, conferences, seminars, training and other non-tourism visits
EGY.notes: Applied at an Egyptian embassy/consulate; requires a letter from the applicant's own company plus an invitation letter from an Egyptian company. Fee varies by nationality (approx US$67 single / US$92 multiple for US applicants; UK £108/£158). Visa valid 6 months; single-entry stay 30 days, multiple-entry up to a collective 90 days. Also called an 'Entry Visa for non-touristic purposes'.

EGY.name: Transit Visa
EGY.purpose: Short transit through Egypt while en route to another destination
EGY.notes: Issued by Egyptian embassies/consulates for travellers passing through Egypt en route elsewhere. Fee varies by nationality (e.g. £108 for Nigerian nationals via the Egyptian Consulate UK). Travellers with confirmed onward tickets can often transit airside without a visa; a transit visa is required to leave the airport.

EGY.name: 5-Year Multiple-Entry Visa
EGY.purpose: Frequent visitors for tourism or business needing long-validity multiple entry
EGY.notes: Long-validity multiple-entry entry visa for tourism or business, valid 5 years with a maximum stay of 3 months (90 days) per visit. Fee approx US$707 for US applicants (varies by nationality). Applied at an Egyptian embassy/consulate.

EGY.name: Student Visa / Study Residence Permit
EGY.purpose: Foreign students enrolled at a recognised Egyptian university or educational institution
EGY.notes: Study entry visa obtained from an Egyptian embassy/consulate on the basis of an official admission/enrolment letter, then converted to a Study Residence Permit (Iqama) at the Passport & Immigration Administration within 30 days of arrival. Permit is granted for the duration of study and renewed annually with an updated enrolment letter. Study in Egypt (study-in-egypt.gov.eg) is the official government admissions portal under the Ministry of Higher Education.

EGY.name: Work Permit (Foreign Worker)
EGY.purpose: Foreign nationals employed in Egypt, sponsored by a licensed Egyptian employer
EGY.notes: Issued inside Egypt by the Ministry of Labour (General Administration for Work Permits for Foreigners) under Labour Law No. 14 of 2025; the employer obtains the work permit first, after which the Passport Administration grants a matching work residence permit (a two-track authorisation). Valid 1 year, renewable annually (renew at least 30 days before expiry). Government/mandatory fees roughly EGP 6,000-15,000. Foreign workers are capped at 10% of a company's workforce; an HIV/AIDS test at the Ministry of Health Central Laboratory is required.

ERI.name: Tourist Visa
ERI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Eritrea for tourism purposes. Valid for one month from arrival; may be extended in Asmara.
ERI.notes: Fee is USD 50 per US Embassy (Washington D.C.) plus $23 in additional fees ($13 photo printing + $10 service fee). Australian consulate charges AUD 90 (adult) / AUD 45 (under 18). Validity 90 days from issue; upon arrival, permitted stay is one month. Urgent processing available (+AUD 20 surcharge at Melbourne consulate). Minors under 17 require birth certificate copies.

ERI.name: Business Visa
ERI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Eritrea for business activities. Available in durations of up to 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year.
ERI.notes: Fee tiers at US Embassy: $100 (single/1 month), $150 (3 months), $200 (6 months), $300 (1 year) plus $23 additional fees. Australian consulate charges AUD 170 (up to 1 month), AUD 240 (up to 3 months). Requires employment/business letter and proof of funds.

ERI.name: Employment Visa
ERI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Eritrea for employment purposes under a specific Eritrean employer sponsorship.
ERI.notes: Requires sponsorship letter from Eritrean employer detailing role and duration. Australian consulate charges AUD 170. Additional $23 in fees ($13 photo printing + $10 service fee) at US embassy.

ERI.name: Student Visa
ERI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Eritrea to undertake study at an Eritrean educational institution.
ERI.notes: Requires acceptance/enrollment letter from Eritrean school and proof of financial support. Additional $23 in fees ($13 photo printing + $10 service fee) at US embassy.

ERI.name: Family Visit Visa
ERI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals (or Eritreans without valid national ID) to visit family members resident in Eritrea.
ERI.notes: Requires details of Eritrean reference/host resident in Eritrea. Australian consulate charges AUD 120 (adult) / AUD 60 (under 18). Minors under 24 born to Eritrean parents must include copies of birth certificates. Additional $23 in fees at US embassy.

ERI.name: Transit Visa
ERI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to transit through Eritrea en route to a final destination.
ERI.notes: Requires air ticket and proof of valid visa for final destination country. Additional $23 in fees ($13 photo printing + $10 service fee) at US embassy.

ERI.name: Official Visa
ERI.purpose: Issued to holders of G4 visas, diplomats, or those invited by Eritrean government ministries or organizations for official purposes.
ERI.notes: Gratis (no fee). Requires diplomatic note from sponsoring ministry or organization. At US Embassy, available only to G4 visa holders. At Australian consulate, available to government/organizational invitees.

ERI.name: Other Visa
ERI.purpose: Miscellaneous visa category for purposes not covered by the named categories above.
ERI.notes: Listed as a separate fee category on the US Embassy visa page at $70. No further description provided by the embassy. Additional $23 in fees apply.

ESP.name: Schengen Short-Stay Tourist Visa (Type C)
ESP.purpose: Permits leisure travel within the Schengen area for tourism, family visits, medical treatment, or other non-gainful activities for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
ESP.notes: Fee is $106 for most nationals age 12+; $53 for ages 6-11; free for under 5. Reduced rates apply for select Eastern European countries (e.g. $41 for Albania, Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine). BLS service charge of $20 additional. Financial proof required: €122/day (under 9 days) or €1,099 minimum. Travel insurance mandatory (min €30,000). Single or multiple entries available. Apply 15-180 days before travel.

ESP.name: Schengen Short-Stay Business Visa (Type C)
ESP.purpose: For business travelers and self-employed individuals conducting business activities, attending conferences, or visiting trade fairs in Spain for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
ESP.notes: Same fee structure as tourist Schengen visa ($106 general; $53 ages 6-11; free under 6). BLS service fee $20 additional. Requires employer letter or Spanish company invitation, travel insurance, and proof of financial means. Apply at least 15 days before travel.

ESP.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
ESP.purpose: Allows travelers from certain nationalities to transit through the international transit zone of Spanish airports without exiting into Schengen territory.
ESP.notes: Only required for certain nationalities; many are exempt. Maximum validity 6 months. Single, double or multiple entries. Fee: $106 for most nationals age 12+; $53 for ages 6-11; free under 5. BLS service charge $20 additional. Not required if traveler holds a valid Schengen visa, residence permit, or certain other visas.

ESP.name: Transit Visa for Seamen
ESP.purpose: Permits maritime crew members to transit through Spain for the purpose of joining a ship or in transit after leaving a ship.
ESP.notes: Short-term visa category for maritime workers in transit. Same general fee structure as other short-stay visas.

ESP.name: Short-Stay Visa for Family Members of EU/EEA/Swiss Citizens (Type C)
ESP.purpose: Allows non-EU family members of EU/EEA/Swiss citizens to accompany or join them in Spain for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
ESP.notes: Free of charge. Eligible family members include spouse, registered partner, dependent children under 21, parents, and other qualifying relatives. For stays exceeding 90 days, a Residence Card as Union Citizen Family Member is required instead.

ESP.name: Residence Visa for Family Members of Spanish Citizens
ESP.purpose: Long-stay national visa enabling non-EU family members of Spanish nationals to relocate to Spain for residence exceeding 90 days.
ESP.notes: Free of charge. Visa valid 1 year; upon arrival in Spain applicant must apply for Foreigner Identity Card (TIE) within one month. Processing may take up to 2 months due to inter-authority consultations. Eligible relatives include spouses, partners, children under 26, parents, legal guardians, and caregivers.

ESP.name: Family Reunification Visa (General Scheme)
ESP.purpose: Long-stay national visa allowing close family members of a non-EU foreign national who holds legal residence in Spain to join them (general immigration regime, not the EU/Spanish-citizen regime).
ESP.notes: For family members of non-EU legal residents in Spain only (NOT family of EU/EEA/Swiss or Spanish citizens, who use the community regime visas). Sponsor must first obtain an 'Authorization of Initial Residence for family reunification' from the Government Delegation in Spain, then the relative applies for the D visa abroad. Eligible: spouse or registered/unregistered partner (only one), children under 18 or disabled adult children unable to support themselves, and parents over 65 in the applicant's care. Visa valid 1 year; Foreigner Identity Card (TIE) must be applied for within 1 month of arrival. Legal decision period 2 months. Fee (from 1 January 2026): US citizens $140; most others $106; Australia/Canada/UK/Ethiopia/Mauritania consult consulate. Financial requirement: 150% of IPREM for first relative plus 50% per additional member; adequate housing report required. Under Royal Decree 1155/2024 (effective 20 May 2025), reunified family members aged 16+ receive automatic work authorization.

ESP.name: Study Visa (National Long-Stay Visa for Studies)
ESP.purpose: National long-stay visa for higher education, post-secondary studies, student mobility programs, volunteering, and training activities in Spain for stays exceeding 90 days.
ESP.notes: Fee for US citizens $160; most other nationalities $106; UK citizens $106 (under 180 days) or $462 (over 180 days); Australian citizens $472. BLS service fee $20 additional. Visa valid 1 month before program start and 15 days after program end. For stays exceeding 180 days, TIE must be obtained within 30 days of arrival. Financial requirement: €600/month solo student. Apply 2-6 months before program start. Medical certificate required. New RD 1155/2024 effective May 20, 2025.

ESP.name: NALCAP Visa (North American Language and Culture Assistants Program)
ESP.purpose: Study visa for participants in Spain's Ministry of Education Language and Culture Assistant program, enabling language teaching assistants to reside in Spain for the program duration.
ESP.notes: Fee for US citizens $160; most nationalities $106; UK citizens $106 (under 180 days) or $462 (over 180 days); Australian citizens $472. Apply at least 2 months before program start. Processing takes minimum 5 weeks. For stays over 180 days, TIE required within 30 days of arrival.

ESP.name: Au Pair Visa
ESP.purpose: Allows young adults aged 17-30 to live with a Spanish host family for cultural and language exchange, providing household assistance in return for accommodation and stipend.
ESP.notes: Age requirement: 17-30 years. Must be enrolled in accredited Spanish language program. Services capped at 5 hours daily; one full day off per week. Financial proof: €600/month minimum. Fee: US citizens $160; Australian citizens $472; UK citizens $462; most others $106. BLS service fee $20. Processing approximately 1 month.

ESP.name: Working Holiday Visa (Youth Mobility)
ESP.purpose: Allows young people aged 18-30 from countries with a bilateral Working Holiday / Youth Mobility agreement with Spain to spend up to 12 months in Spain for a holiday, with the right to take incidental work to help fund the stay.
ESP.notes: Available only to nationals of countries with which Spain has a bilateral Working Holiday / Youth Mobility agreement: Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan, and South Korea. Age 18-30 at time of application; must not have previously held this visa. Purpose is primarily tourism, with work secondary: cannot work for the same employer for more than 6 months during the 12-month stay; study limited to about 4 months. Return ticket or sufficient funds to buy one required. Australia has an annual quota of 3,400 places. Applications are made in person at the competent Spanish consulate (not online) and no earlier than 3 months before intended entry; fee varies by consulate/nationality (confirm with the consulate). Some consulates require proof of DELE A1 Spanish language level.

ESP.name: Residence and Work Authorization - Employee (Cuenta Ajena)
ESP.purpose: Authorizes non-EU nationals to reside and work in Spain as an employee for a Spanish employer, subject to the national employment situation assessment.
ESP.notes: Employer must apply for the authorization; applicant then applies for the national work and residence visa at a Spanish consulate. Initial authorization valid 1 year. Seasonal work and cross-border worker variants also exist. Governed by Organic Law 4/2000 (Foreigners Law) and implementing Royal Decree 557/2011.

ESP.name: Highly Qualified Worker Visa (TAC) / EU Blue Card
ESP.purpose: Enables highly qualified non-EU professionals or senior managers to work in Spain, including the EU Blue Card for high-salary positions requiring tertiary education.
ESP.notes: Requires prior authorization from UGECE (Large Companies and Strategic Groups Unit). Fee: US citizens $190; most others $106; Canadian $992; UK $963; Australian $3,086. BLS service fee $20. Visa valid 1 year or matching residence authorization. Must hold higher education degree or 3+ years equivalent professional experience. EU Blue Card minimum salary threshold approx. €38,844/year (shortage occupations lower). Residence authorization processed by UGECE.

ESP.name: Intra-Company Transfer Visa (TTI)
ESP.purpose: Permits employees of multinational companies to be transferred to their company's Spanish entity as senior management, specialists, or trainees.
ESP.notes: Requires prior residence authorization from UGECE. Fee: US citizens $190; most others $106; Canadian $992; UK $963; Australian $3,086. BLS service fee $20. Visa valid 1 year or duration of residence authorization. Established under Law 14/2013. Family members may apply concurrently.

ESP.name: Researcher Visa
ESP.purpose: Allows non-EU nationals to conduct research, development, and innovation activities at authorized Spanish public or private entities.
ESP.notes: Requires Authorization of Initial Residence for Research from UGECE. Fee: US citizens $190; most others $106; BLS service fee $20. Visa valid 1 year or matching authorization. Covers research staff, scientific/technical personnel, teaching staff at R&D centers and universities. EU researcher mobility provisions apply (Sheet 69 for mobility between EU member states).

ESP.name: Internship Visa
ESP.purpose: For university graduates or current university students to participate in approved internship programs at Spanish entities to improve professional skills and experience.
ESP.notes: Must have obtained university degree within 2 years or be pursuing degree. Requires Authorization of Initial Residence for Internship from provincial government. Fee: US citizens $190; most others $106; Canadian $992; Australian $3,086; BLS $20. Maximum duration: 6 months (hosting agreement) or 1 year (trainee contract).

ESP.name: Residence Visa with Work Permit Exemption
ESP.purpose: Authorizes specific categories of professionals (academics, researchers, cultural staff, foreign correspondents, religious ministers, etc.) to work in Spain without a standard work permit.
ESP.notes: Covers: technical specialists at Spanish government/university/research organizations, educators at Spanish universities, cultural/educational staff from recognized foreign institutions, foreign officials under bilateral cooperation agreements, foreign media correspondents, scientific mission members, religious ministers, international trade union representatives, and foreign minors in protective services. Three durations: up to 90 days (Schengen code EET), 90-180 days (national code TEE), over 180 days (TRE). Fee: US citizens $190; most $106; Canadian $1,050; Australian $3,235; UK $414; residence fee $13 all. Processing 3 months. Authority: Article 117 of Royal Decree 557/2011.

ESP.name: Telework Visa (Digital Nomad Visa)
ESP.purpose: Allows non-EU nationals to reside in Spain while working remotely for companies or clients located exclusively outside Spain, using digital and telecommunications means.
ESP.notes: Established under Law 28/2022 (Startup Law), amending Law 14/2013, Article 74 bis. Income requirement: 200% of monthly SMI = €2,368/month (approx. $2,500) for solo applicant; add €888/month per first family member, €196/month per additional. Must hold university degree from recognized institution or 3+ years professional experience. Employees must work for non-Spanish companies only; self-employed may work up to 20% for Spanish entities. Work must be for companies (not individuals, NGOs, or government bodies). Fee: US citizens $190; Canadian $1,566; UK $963; Australian $3,020; most others $106. Can convert to 3-year residence permit via UGECE without leaving Spain. Processing 10 days.

ESP.name: Entrepreneur Visa
ESP.purpose: Visa for non-EU nationals relocating to Spain to undertake an innovative entrepreneurial activity of particular economic interest to Spain.
ESP.notes: Established under Law 14/2013 as amended by Law 28/2022 (Startup Law). Requires prior Authorization of Initial Residence from UGECE evaluating innovativeness and economic interest. Financial requirement: $8,000/year for solo applicant plus $4,000/year per dependent (2025 figures = 100% IPREM). Health insurance with 100% coverage required. FBI background check required. Fee: US citizens $270; Canadian $789; most others $106. Visa valid 1 year; convertible to entrepreneur residence authorization. Must apply within 1 year of capital investment (excluding real estate).

ESP.name: Non-Lucrative Residence Visa
ESP.purpose: Permits non-EU nationals with sufficient passive income or savings to reside in Spain without engaging in any gainful employment or professional activities.
ESP.notes: Income requirement: 400% of Spain's IPREM = €28,800/year (~$32,000) for solo applicant; add 100% IPREM (~$8,000) per dependent (2026 figures). Visa itself valid 90 days from issuance (must enter Spain within this window). Initial residence permit valid 1 year upon arrival. Renewable; after 5 years of continuous legal residence, may apply for long-term/permanent residence permit. Path to citizenship: 10 years (2 years for nationals of Latin American countries, Philippines, Andorra, Equatorial Guinea, Portugal). Visa fee varies by nationality: $106-$789; residence permit fee $13; BLS $20. Processing up to 3 months. No work authorization; any income must be passive. Governed by Article 37 of Royal Decree 557/2011.

ESP.name: Self-Employment / Entrepreneur Residence Authorization (Cuenta Propia)
ESP.purpose: Authorizes non-EU non-residents to establish themselves as self-employed workers in Spain or initiate a business project.
ESP.notes: Initial temporary residence and self-employment work authorization (Sheet 14). Also includes job search or business project initiation authorization (Sheet 20). Must not already be a legal resident in Spain. Requires viable business plan or self-employment documentation. Governed by Organic Law 4/2000 and Royal Decree 557/2011.

EST.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (C Visa) – Tourism
EST.purpose: Permits tourism, leisure, and family visits to Estonia and the wider Schengen Area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
EST.notes: Standard adult fee EUR 90 (approx USD 97). Children 6–11 pay EUR 45; under 6 are free. Facilitation agreement countries pay EUR 35–EUR 67.50. Multiple-entry variants valid up to 5 years. Application must be submitted 15 days before travel and no earlier than 6 months ahead. Financial means required: EUR 70/day. Processing standard 15 days; complex cases up to 45 days.

EST.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (C Visa) – Business
EST.purpose: Permits business-related activities such as meetings, conferences, and negotiations in Estonia and the Schengen Area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
EST.notes: Same fee and processing as tourist C visa. Researchers, pupils, and students may be exempt from the fee. Multi-entry variants available for frequent business travellers.

EST.name: Airport Transit Visa (A Visa)
EST.purpose: Permits passage through the international transit zone of an Estonian (Schengen) airport between connecting flights, without entering the Schengen Area.
EST.notes: Required for certain nationalities transiting through Schengen airports. Holders remain in the international area and do not enter the Schengen territory. Fee EUR 90. Many nationalities are exempt from the airport transit visa requirement.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Short-Term Employment
EST.purpose: Allows a third-country national to enter Estonia to take up short-term paid employment with an Estonian employer for a period exceeding 90 days but not more than 365 days.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120 (approx USD 130); children 6–11 EUR 60. Financial means requirement: EUR 1,320 one-time for short-term employment. Two consecutive D-visas cannot exceed 548 days within 730 consecutive days. Also allows up to 90 days travel in other Schengen states. Foreign documents require apostille/legalization and translation.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Seasonal Work
EST.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to undertake seasonal agricultural or other seasonal work in Estonia for up to 365 days within a 12-month period.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Financial means requirement: EUR 880 one-time for applicant; EUR 704 one-time for accompanying spouse. Separate from the standard work D-visa sub-category.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Studies
EST.purpose: Enables third-country nationals to enter Estonia for study at an accredited institution (university, college, or other recognised programme) for periods exceeding 90 days.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Financial means: EUR 880/month for student; accompanying spouse requires EUR 2,100/month. PhD students have reduced spouse requirement of EUR 704/month. Schengen travel allowed up to 90 days per 180 days.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Digital Nomad (Remote Work)
EST.purpose: Allows remote workers employed by companies or clients outside Estonia to live and work in Estonia for up to one year.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Financial means threshold: EUR 132/day (approximately EUR 3,960/month) per vm.ee D-visa table; program income benchmark is EUR 4,500/month (EUR 150/day) per e-resident.gov.ee. Applicant must be employed by or own a company registered outside Estonia, or freelance primarily for foreign clients. Application submitted at nearest Estonian Embassy. Processing up to 30 days.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Start-up Business
EST.purpose: Permits founders of start-up companies with international growth potential to enter Estonia to establish and operate their business.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Financial means: EUR 880/month for applicant; EUR 704/month for spouse. Typically a precursor to applying for Residence Permit for Start-up Entrepreneur. Expert committee evaluation required via Startup Estonia.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Working Holiday
EST.purpose: Allows young adults from partner countries to stay in Estonia for up to 12 months, combining tourism with incidental employment.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Available to citizens of Australia and New Zealand (ages 18–35) and Canada (ages 18–35) and Japan (ages 18–30). Bilateral working holiday agreements underpin eligibility. Primary purpose is holiday/travel; work is permitted incidentally.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Family Reunification / Other Purposes
EST.purpose: Permits third-country nationals joining family members legally residing in Estonia, or other long-stay purposes not covered by other D-visa sub-categories.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Financial means for 'other purposes': EUR 70/day for applicant and accompanying spouse; EUR 70/day per child. Covers family members of Estonian residents and other lawful long-stay purposes. Schengen travel up to 90/180 days also permitted.

EST.name: Schengen Visa – Diplomatic / Official Passport Holders
EST.purpose: Visa issued (or exemption granted) for holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports of countries with bilateral agreements with Estonia/EU, for official travel.
EST.notes: Approximately 25 countries' diplomatic/service/official passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days per 180-day period under bilateral agreements. Includes Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus (biometric), Belize, Bolivia, Cabo Verde, Egypt, India, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kuwait, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia (biometric), Morocco, China, Philippines, Suriname, Tajikistan, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Turkey, Uzbekistan, Vietnam. Russia's diplomatic exemption is suspended per EU Council Decision (EU) 2022/333 of 25 February 2022. Georgia's diplomatic/service exemption also suspended as of 8 May 2025.

EST.name: Long-Stay D Visa – Start-up Employment
EST.purpose: Allows a non-EU national to enter Estonia to take up employment at an officially recognised Estonian start-up company.
EST.notes: Fee EUR 120. Financial means: EUR 880 one-time for applicant; EUR 704 one-time for accompanying spouse. Intended for employees of start-up companies that have received a positive evaluation from the Ministry of Interior expert committee. Distinct from the start-up business D-visa (for founders).

EST.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Employment
EST.purpose: Enables a non-EU/EEA national with a job offer from an Estonian employer to live and work in Estonia long-term, beyond the 12-month limit of the long-stay D visa.
EST.notes: State fee EUR 250 when applied for at a service point in Estonia, EUR 280 at a foreign representation (Estonian embassy). Issued for up to 5 years and extendable up to 10 years at a time. Covers many employment sub-categories (skilled workers, top specialists, experts, ICT, scientists, teachers, athletes, creative workers, posted/company employees, etc.). Most employment requires prior authorisation from the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund and, unless exempt (e.g. ICT, start-up, top specialists), counts against the annual immigration quota. Decision within 90 days; residence-permit card issued within 30 days after approval.

EST.name: EU Blue Card (Estonia)
EST.purpose: Residence-and-work permit for highly qualified non-EU/EEA professionals with a higher-education qualification (or equivalent experience) and a qualifying salary who take up skilled employment in Estonia.
EST.notes: Highly-qualified employment residence permit issued under the (recast) EU Blue Card Directive and the Estonian Aliens Act. Requires a completed higher-education programme of at least 3 years (or at least 5 years of relevant professional experience) and a gross monthly salary of at least 1.5x the Estonian average (1.24x for shortage occupations such as ICT). Minimum employment contract 6 months; issued for the contract duration plus 3 months. Excluded from the annual immigration quota. State fee EUR 250 (in Estonia) / EUR 280 (abroad). Decision within 90 days. Also documented on the EU immigration portal: https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/eu-immigration-portal/eu-blue-card/eu-blue-card-estonia_en

EST.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Study
EST.purpose: Allows a non-EU/EEA national admitted to an accredited Estonian school, vocational institution or university (bachelor's, master's or doctoral level) to reside in Estonia for the duration of study.
EST.notes: Issued for up to 5 years depending on the nominal duration of study. Decision within 90 days; residence-permit card issued within 30 days after approval. Standard temporary-residence-permit state fee applies (the study category is not separately priced on the official fee schedule). Students may work in Estonia without a separate work permit provided it does not interfere with their studies. The long-stay D visa for studies is used to enter Estonia while this residence permit covers the full study period.

EST.name: Temporary Residence Permit to Settle with a Spouse or Family Member
EST.purpose: Family-reunification permit for the spouse, minor child or dependent close relative of an Estonian citizen or a foreigner residing in Estonia on the basis of a residence permit.
EST.notes: State fee EUR 115 when applied for at a service point in Estonia, EUR 145 at a foreign representation, when settling with a spouse or close relative. Issued for up to 5 years but not longer than the validity of the sponsor's residence permit; extendable up to 10 years at a time. The applicant must have legal income of at least twice the subsistence level and register their place of residence in the Population Register; the sponsoring family member submits a signed invitation. Decision within 90 days.

ETH.name: Tourist eVisa (VT) - 30-Day Single Entry
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Ethiopia for tourism, sightseeing, and leisure. Available online to citizens of all countries worldwide.
ETH.notes: Passport must be valid for at least 6 months from intended entry date. Validity runs from intended entry date. Extensions available online (up to 15 days past expiry) or in person at ICS Head Office Addis Ababa. Extension fee: USD 102 for a 30-day extension.

ETH.name: Tourist eVisa (VT) - 90-Day Single Entry
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Ethiopia for tourism, sightseeing, and leisure for an extended period. Available online to citizens of all countries worldwide.
ETH.notes: Passport must be valid for at least 6 months from intended entry date. Extension fee: USD 302 for a 90-day extension.

ETH.name: Tourist Visa on Arrival
ETH.purpose: Tourist visa issued at the port of entry (Bole International Airport, Addis Ababa) for eligible nationalities. Allows tourism and leisure visits.
ETH.notes: Available to approximately 119 eligible nationalities listed on evisa.gov.et. Fee payable in USD, EUR, GBP, or CAD on arrival. Max stay days not explicitly stated on the official site. Diplomatic and Service visas are processed by appointment at embassies, not on arrival.

ETH.name: Business Visa Application
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting business activities in Ethiopia, including attending meetings, conferences, or negotiating contracts with Ethiopian business partners.
ETH.notes: Requires valid passport (6+ months), invitation letter from an Ethiopian business partner or organization, proof of business activities, and two passport photos. Specific fee amounts not published on the official page - contact info@ics.gov.et or call 8133. Applications can be submitted online or in person at immigration offices.

ETH.name: Investment Visa (IV) - Single Entry 30-Day
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals engaged in or wishing to invest in Ethiopia. Facilitates investment activities and initial setup.
ETH.notes: Requires support letter from nearest Ethiopian Embassy, official application letter from inviting organization, business license, and support letter from Investment Commission of Ethiopia.

ETH.name: Investment Visa (IV) - Multiple Entry 90-Day
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals engaged in or wishing to invest in Ethiopia with multiple entry access over 90 days.
ETH.notes: Requires support letter from nearest Ethiopian Embassy, official application letter from inviting organization, business license, and support letter from Investment Commission of Ethiopia.

ETH.name: Investment Visa (IV) - Multiple Entry 6-Month
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals engaged in or wishing to invest in Ethiopia with extended multiple entry access over 6 months.
ETH.notes: Requires support letter from nearest Ethiopian Embassy, official application letter from inviting organization, business license, and support letter from Investment Commission of Ethiopia.

ETH.name: Investment Visa (IV) - Multiple Entry 12-Month
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals engaged in or wishing to invest in Ethiopia with long-term multiple entry access over 12 months.
ETH.notes: Requires support letter from nearest Ethiopian Embassy, official application letter from inviting organization, business license, and support letter from Investment Commission of Ethiopia.

ETH.name: Residence Visa (IMV) - Single Entry 30-Day
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia with intent to stay for a fixed duration, eventually leading to permanent residency.
ETH.notes: Extensions available at ICS Head Office in Addis Ababa. This visa is a pathway toward permanent residency status.

ETH.name: Residence Visa (IMV) - Multiple Entry 90-Day
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia with intent to stay for an extended fixed duration, eventually leading to permanent residency.
ETH.notes: Extensions available at ICS Head Office in Addis Ababa. This visa is a pathway toward permanent residency status.

ETH.name: Student Visa Application
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted to accredited educational institutions in Ethiopia to pursue academic study.
ETH.notes: Requires acceptance letter from an accredited Ethiopian educational institution, proof of tuition payment or scholarship, and proof of sufficient financial means. Specific fee not published - contact info@ics.gov.et or call 8133. Apply well in advance of intended travel.

ETH.name: NGO Work Permit
ETH.purpose: Employment authorization for foreign nationals working with non-governmental organizations registered and authorized to operate in Ethiopia.
ETH.notes: Requires employment contract or appointment letter from the NGO, proof of NGO registration and authorization in Ethiopia, police clearance certificate from home country, and professional qualifications documentation. Specific fee not published - contact info@ics.gov.et or call 8133.

ETH.name: Temporary Residence Permit Through Marriage
ETH.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals married to Ethiopian citizens, granting lawful residency in Ethiopia.
ETH.notes: Requires marriage certificate authenticated if from abroad, Ethiopian spouse's kebele ID or passport, and bank statement with 500,000 ETB or more (or property/vehicle documentation as alternative). Renewable and subject to conditions set by Ethiopian immigration authorities. Specific fee not published - contact info@ics.gov.et or call 8133.

ETH.name: Temporary ID (Temporary Residency)
ETH.purpose: Short-term residency identification for foreign nationals in Ethiopia on a temporary basis, covering employees, students, shareholders, and journalists.
ETH.notes: Requires employer letter with valid trade certificate, company trade certificate, valid visa and visa stamp. For students: Ministry of Education letter; for journalists: Ministry of Communication letter; for employees: Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs letter. Specific fee not published - contact info@ics.gov.et or call 8133.

ETH.name: Permanent Residence ID (Five-Year Renewable)
ETH.purpose: Long-term residency status for foreign nationals employed by a company with a valid trade certificate in Ethiopia.
ETH.notes: Valid for 5 years (1825 days), renewable upon expiration. Requires employer letter with valid trade certificate, company trade certificate, valid passport copy, and valid working visa or tourist visa with visa stamp. Specific fee not published - contact info@ics.gov.et or call 8133.

ETH.name: Diplomatic and Service Visa
ETH.purpose: Visa for holders of diplomatic and service passports, processed by appointment at Ethiopian embassies and consulates abroad.
ETH.notes: Processed by appointment only at Ethiopian embassies. Not available online or on arrival. Contact the nearest Ethiopian Embassy for requirements and processing times.

ETH.name: Business and Related Studies Visa (BRV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia to conduct business and market research.
ETH.notes: Two options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 152) and 90-day (USD 202). Requires passport valid 6+ months, bank statement, company profile, and application letter. Extendable before expiry at the ICS Head Office in Addis Ababa (extension fees USD 152 / USD 252).

ETH.name: Workshop/Conference Visa (CV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals attending an international conference, seminar, or workshop in Ethiopia on invitation.
ETH.notes: Single entry, 30-day only. Cannot be extended. Requires an invitation letter from the organizing government body, private company, registered NGO, or international organization. Processing time 3 business days.

ETH.name: Foreign Business Firm Employment Visa (WV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia to be employed by business firms owned or operated by foreigners.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 402) and multiple entry 90-day (USD 1002). Extendable before expiry; overstays incur fines. Processing time 3 business days.

ETH.name: Ethiopian Government Institutions Short Task Visa (GIV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia to carry out short-term tasks for Ethiopian government institutions.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 102), multiple entry 90-day (USD 152), and multiple entry 180-day (USD 402). Extensions of 1-15 days done online; over 15 days in person at the ICS Head Office. Processing time 3 business days.

ETH.name: Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) Work Visa (NV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals invited by NGOs operating in Ethiopia for employment or short-term assignments.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 202) and multiple entry 90-day (USD 602). Requires a support letter from the inviting organization and the inviting company's TIN certificate. This is the e-visa entry visa, distinct from the ICS in-country NGO work permit. Processing time 3 business days.

ETH.name: Student Visa (SV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia temporarily to undertake a course of study in the country.
ETH.notes: Single entry, 30-day. Cannot be extended. This is the online e-visa student visa issued via evisa.gov.et (distinct from the ICS student-visa application service). Passport must be valid 6+ months from the intended entry date.

ETH.name: Religion Visa (RV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia to take part in religious activities on invitation from a religious entity.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 152) and 90-day (USD 302). Requires an invitation letter from the inviting religious entity. Extendable before expiry at the ICS Head Office in Addis Ababa (extension fees USD 252 / USD 352).

ETH.name: Medical Treatment Visa (MDV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia to receive treatment for a medical condition.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 102), multiple entry 90-day (USD 202), multiple entry 180-day (USD 352), and multiple entry 365-day (USD 502). Extendable before expiry at the ICS Head Office in Addis Ababa.

ETH.name: Entertainment Industry Visa (EIV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Ethiopia to work in the entertainment industry (film, television, or live productions) as performers or production/support staff.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 102) and 90-day (USD 302). Extendable before expiry at the ICS Head Office in Addis Ababa (extension fees USD 202 / USD 302).

ETH.name: Sports Competition and Training Visa (SPV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign national athletes entering Ethiopia to participate in sports events and/or training.
ETH.notes: Options on evisa.gov.et: single entry 30-day (USD 82) and single entry 90-day (USD 202). Cannot be extended.

ETH.name: Journalist Visa (JV)
ETH.purpose: For foreign journalists, media professionals, and filmmakers entering Ethiopia to cover events, report for media organizations, or produce media.
ETH.notes: Single entry, 30-day only. Cannot be extended. Requires a support letter (issued within the past week) from the inviting media institution. Processing time 3 business days.

FIN.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourist/Visit
FIN.purpose: Short-term visits for tourism, recreation, or private purposes to Finland and the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
FIN.notes: Standard Schengen visa fee EUR 80 (adults) as of 2019 amendment to Visa Code (Regulation EU 2019/1155). Children aged 6–17 are exempt. Multiple, double, or single entry possible depending on travel history. Applications must be submitted in person at Finnish diplomatic mission or authorized visa centre. Processing normally 15 calendar days, up to 30–60 days in complex cases. Single-entry visa validity fixed; multiple-entry visas can be valid up to 5 years. No e-visa or visa-on-arrival for Finland.

FIN.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
FIN.purpose: Short-term business activities in Finland including meetings, conferences, and negotiations for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Does not permit employment.
FIN.notes: Same Schengen Type C visa as tourist; purpose declared as business on application. Fee EUR 80 (adults). Cannot be used for paid employment in Finland. Applications must be submitted in person at Finnish diplomatic mission.

FIN.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
FIN.purpose: Authorises transit through the international transit area of Finnish airports (no entry into Finland) for nationals of countries required to hold such a visa.
FIN.notes: Required for nationals of: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, and Sri Lanka - even when only transiting through a Finnish airport without entering Finland. Fee is same as standard Schengen visa (EUR 80). Does not permit entry into Finnish territory.

FIN.name: Residence Permit for an Employed Person (Työntekijän oleskelulupa)
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA nationals coming to Finland to work in occupations not covered by sector-specific permits (e.g. cooks, cleaners, nursing assistants). Requires employer sponsorship and may require a labour market test.
FIN.notes: Applied via Enter Finland online portal (application TTOL); identity verified in person at Finnish diplomatic mission within 3 months. Employer submits employment terms via Enter Finland for Employers. May require an availability (labour market) assessment to verify no available EU/EEA worker. Electronic application fee EUR 750 (EUR 950 on paper), confirmed on migri.fi 2026-07. D visa valid 100 days can be applied simultaneously for early travel. Permit valid typically up to 2 years, renewable.

FIN.name: Specialist Residence Permit (Fast Track)
FIN.purpose: For highly qualified non-EU/EEA specialists with special expertise, including IT specialists and higher education graduates, coming to work in Finland on employment requiring special skills.
FIN.notes: Salary requirement minimum EUR 3,937/month (2026). First permit only; must apply from outside Finland. Online application fee EUR 530. Fast-track processing maximum 2 weeks from identity verification at Finnish mission (within 5 working days). Spouse and children may apply simultaneously. D visa valid 100 days granted simultaneously.

FIN.name: EU Blue Card (Fast Track)
FIN.purpose: For highly qualified non-EU/EEA professionals with a higher education degree (minimum 3 years) or 5 years equivalent professional experience, employed in Finland under a qualifying employment contract.
FIN.notes: Salary requirement minimum EUR 3,937/month (2026). Employment contract must be at least 6 months. First permit only. No labour market test. Fee approximately EUR 380 online (per EC immigration portal). Valid up to 2 years or employment duration + 3 months, whichever shorter. EU Blue Card enables mobility to other EU states after 18 months.

FIN.name: Intra-Corporate Transferee (ICT) Residence Permit - Specialist/Manager
FIN.purpose: For specialists and managers transferred within a multinational company to work at a Finnish entity of the same corporate group.
FIN.notes: Fast-track processing available (2 weeks). Governed by EU Directive 2014/66/EU (ICT Directive). First permit only. Specific fee not confirmed during research (migri.fi returned 403).

FIN.name: Seasonal Worker's Permit/Visa
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA nationals coming to Finland for seasonal agricultural or tourism work (e.g. plant growing, forestry, festival work) for up to 9 months.
FIN.notes: Stays under 90 days: apply for seasonal work visa at Finnish embassy/consulate. Stays 90–270 days: apply to Finnish Immigration Service (Migri) via Enter Finland. Maximum permitted stay is 9 months (270 days). Employer must apply for a seasonal work notification first via TE Services.

FIN.name: Job Seeker / Post-Graduation Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: Allows foreign graduates who completed a degree in Finland to remain for up to 2 years to seek employment. Also available for those who have graduated from a Finnish institution within the last 5 years.
FIN.notes: Must have completed a degree program in Finland. Can be applied within 5 years of student permit expiration. Valid up to 2 years. Does not require a job offer at the time of application. Once employment is obtained, must switch to a work-based residence permit.

FIN.name: Researcher Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA researchers coming to Finland to conduct scientific research at a Finnish research organisation under a hosting agreement.
FIN.notes: Based on EU Directive 2016/801. Requires a hosting agreement with an approved Finnish research institution. Family members eligible for simultaneous permit. Specific fee not confirmed during research.

FIN.name: Student Residence Permit (A - Continuous)
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA students enrolled in a higher education degree programme at an approved Finnish institution. Granted for the full duration of the degree programme.
FIN.notes: Requires acceptance letter from approved Finnish educational institution, proof of funds (min EUR 800/month, approx EUR 9,600/year), health insurance (deductible max EUR 300), and paid tuition or scholarship proof. Applied via Enter Finland; identity verified in person at Finnish mission within 3 months. Type A permit (continuous). D visa valid 100 days may be issued simultaneously. Extensions require transcript showing adequate academic progress.

FIN.name: Student Residence Permit (B - Temporary)
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA students on exchange programmes, supplementary training, or other non-degree study at an approved Finnish institution.
FIN.notes: Type B permit (temporary) for exchange or short-programme students. Same financial and documentation requirements as degree-programme permit. Validity matched to study duration.

FIN.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA family members (spouse, minor children, and in limited cases other dependants) to join a family member residing legally in Finland.
FIN.notes: Eligible family members: spouses (including registered partners and cohabitants of 2+ years), unmarried minor children (under 18), parents of minors in Finland. Sponsor in Finland and/or applicant often required to demonstrate sufficient income. Children whose guardian(s) hold permanent permits (P) or long-term EU resident permits (P-EU) may receive permanent permits directly. Must apply from abroad before first entry for first permit.

FIN.name: Entrepreneur's Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA nationals establishing or operating a business in Finland as a sole proprietor, partner in a general or limited partnership, or active owner-operator of a company.
FIN.notes: Applicant must actively work in the company in Finland (not merely own it). Business must be profitable with income sufficient for livelihood (min approx EUR 1,030–1,210/month net, 2026).
