ELY Centre/elinvoimakeskus.fi assesses profitability before Migri decides on the permit. Must register business in Trade Register before applying. Cannot hold permit solely for investment/ownership.

FIN.name: Start-up Entrepreneur's Residence Permit (Fast Track)
FIN.purpose: For founders of growth-oriented startup companies in Finland. Requires a positive eligibility statement from Business Finland confirming the startup's growth potential.
FIN.notes: Two-phase process: obtain positive Eligibility Statement from Business Finland (processing ~1 month; statement valid 4 months at time of application), then apply to Migri. Fast-track option: maximum 2 weeks. First permit only; cannot already be in Finland. Valid 2 years. Monthly net income requirement min EUR 1,030–1,210 (2026). D visa valid 100 days granted simultaneously.

FIN.name: Permanent Residence Permit (P)
FIN.purpose: Grants indefinite right of residence in Finland to non-EU/EEA nationals who have resided in Finland legally and continuously for the required period.
FIN.notes: UPDATED 8 January 2026 (Aliens Act amendment): General requirement is now 6 years of continuous legal residence in Finland, with at least 2 years of work history in Finland and satisfactory Finnish or Swedish language skills (level B1). Alternative paths: (a) 4 years continuous residence with annual income over EUR 40,000; or (b) 4 years continuous residence with at least 3 years of work history in Finland and particularly good Finnish or Swedish language skills (level C1). Applications submitted before 8 January 2026 were assessed under the prior 4-year rule. Continuous permit (A) must have been held. Permanent permit card renewed every 5 years but permit itself does not expire. Source: migri.fi/en/amendments-to-aliens-act-regarding-permanent-residence-permits-2026 (confirmed via web search; direct migri.fi access returned 403 during this validation pass).

FIN.name: Long-Term EU Resident Permit (P-EU)
FIN.purpose: EU-harmonised long-term residence status for non-EU/EEA nationals who have resided legally in Finland for 5 consecutive years. Facilitates mobility to other EU member states.
FIN.notes: Based on EU Directive 2003/109/EC (Long-Term Residents Directive). Requires 5 continuous years of legal residence. Holder may move to and work in other EU member states under simplified procedures. Card renewed every 5 years but status is permanent.

FIN.name: Temporary Protection Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: Grants temporary protection to displaced persons who have fled a country in a mass displacement situation (e.g. war) and cannot return safely - currently applied to Ukrainian nationals.
FIN.notes: Based on EU Temporary Protection Directive 2001/55/EC. Activated by EU Council decision. Currently in effect for Ukrainian nationals displaced since 24 February 2022. Fee-free. Granted for 1 year initially, renewable while protection is in force. Holder is entitled to accommodation, healthcare, schooling, and work in Finland.

FIN.name: D Visa (National Long-Stay Visa)
FIN.purpose: Allows entry into Finland while awaiting the physical residence permit card. Valid for travel to Finland so the permit card can be collected; does not in itself grant residence.
FIN.notes: Issued simultaneously with the main residence permit application. Valid 100 days. Enables holder to travel to Finland before the residence permit card is issued and mailed. Also valid for transit in other Schengen states to reach Finland (Schengen Borders Code Art. 6). Cannot be used for extended Schengen travel - only for entry into Finland.

FIN.name: Working Holiday Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: For young citizens of Australia, New Zealand, Japan, and Canada coming to Finland primarily for a holiday, with the option to work as a secondary purpose of the stay.
FIN.notes: Available ONLY to citizens of the four countries with which Finland has a reciprocal agreement: Australia, New Zealand, Japan, and Canada. Age limits: 18-30 for Australia and Japan; 18-35 for New Zealand and Canada. Applicant must not have held a Finnish Working Holiday permit before, must have a departure ticket or funds to buy one, sufficient funds (about EUR 2,450 for the first 3 months), and (for NZ/Japan/Canada citizens) valid insurance for the whole stay. Family members/dependants cannot accompany on this basis. Granted for a maximum of 12 months; first permit applied for abroad, extension only from within Finland. Holiday must be the primary purpose. Work restrictions: Australian citizens may work max 9 months per 12-month trip and max 3 months per employer; New Zealand, Japan, and Canada citizens have unrestricted right to work. Online (Enter Finland) application fee EUR 530 (EUR 630 on paper); New Zealand citizens pay NO processing fee under the 1973 Finland-New Zealand visa-abolition agreement.

FIN.name: Au Pair Residence Permit
FIN.purpose: For young people coming to live with a Finnish host family to learn Finnish/Swedish language and culture in exchange for light housework and childcare.
FIN.notes: Applicant must be 17-30 years old. Purpose is cultural and language exchange; au pair duties (light housework) must be arranged so the au pair can attend Finnish or Swedish language classes. Requires basic knowledge of, or intention to study, Finnish/Swedish language or culture. Maximum stay one year (not extendable beyond one year in au pair status). Requires a written host-family agreement, a medical certificate (under 3 months old) confirming no infectious disease, a criminal-record document, and health/accident insurance for the whole stay. First permit applied for abroad via Enter Finland. Online application fee EUR 530 (EUR 630 on paper).

FIN.name: Residence Permit for an Athlete, Coach or Referee
FIN.purpose: For professional athletes, coaches, and referees coming to Finland to work in sport on the basis of an offer of employment or engagement with a Finnish sports organisation.
FIN.notes: Must have a job/engagement before applying. Salary from sport must be at least approximately EUR 1,149/month (migri.fi, 2026) and income must come mainly from the sport work covered by the permit. Coaches and referees additionally need relevant work experience or education, and the employer must confirm the applicant has the required professional skills. Athletes, coaches, and referees may work WITHOUT a residence permit if the work lasts a maximum of 90 days. Applied online via Enter Finland (application OLE_TY4); online fee EUR 530 (EUR 630 on paper).

FIN.name: Residence Permit for Internship / Traineeship
FIN.purpose: For non-EU/EEA nationals coming to Finland for a paid or unpaid internship, traineeship (e.g. Erasmus+), or apprenticeship training.
FIN.notes: Covers internships, traineeships through a training programme such as Erasmus+, and apprenticeship training (education taking place mainly at a workplace). Granted for a maximum of 18 months. A paid internship always requires this residence permit and a signed employment contract stating the salary, plus employer assurance that the internship does not replace a regular job. An unpaid intern may work without a residence permit for a maximum of 90 days if residing in Finland visa-free, on a visa, or on another EU member state's residence permit. Applied via Enter Finland (application OLE_TY3); online fee EUR 530 (EUR 630 on paper).

FJI.name: Visitors Permit (Visa-Exempt Entry)
FJI.purpose: Allows nationals of visa-exempt countries to enter Fiji for tourism, visiting friends/family, attending events, conferences, or transiting. Issued on arrival without prior application.
FJI.notes: Only available to nationals of visa-exempt countries listed at immigration.gov.fj/visa-exempted-countries/. Valid for up to 4 months (approx. 120 days). Extendable once by 2 months (FJD 93 fee) for a total maximum stay of 6 months. Business visitors on 30-day permits cannot extend. Cannot be used for employment.

FJI.name: Single Entry Visa (SEV)
FJI.purpose: Allows nationals of non-visa-exempt countries to enter Fiji once for tourism, business visits, training, transit, crew travel, or government duties. Must be obtained before travel.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 93.00 (approx. USD 42 at current rates; exact USD equivalent varies). Valid for 3 months from issue date. Processing takes approximately 14 working days. Applications lodged at any Fijian Immigration office in Suva, Nadi, Lautoka, Savusavu, Levuka, Labasa, and Rotuma, or through nearest Fiji High Commission/Embassy abroad. Online portal (ImmiHub) also available.

FJI.name: Multiple Entry Visa (MEV)
FJI.purpose: Allows nationals of non-visa-exempt countries to make repeated visits to Fiji over a 12-month period for tourism, business, training, transit, crew travel, or government duties.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 185.00 (approx. USD 84 at current rates; exact USD equivalent varies). Valid for 12 months from issue date; maximum stay per entry is 4 months (approx. 120 days). Processing takes approximately 14 working days. Applications lodged at Fijian Immigration offices or nearest Fiji High Commission/Embassy abroad.

FJI.name: Business Visitors Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to undertake short-term business, consultancy, research or work-related activities in Fiji such as meetings, conferences and negotiations, without taking up local employment.
FJI.notes: Granted on arrival for up to 21 days to nationals of Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and the USA; up to 14 days for other visa-exempt nationals. Nationals of visa-required countries must arrange it through a Fiji mission before travel. Cannot be extended and no paid local employment is permitted. Corrected 2026-07: the dedicated business-visitors-permit page specifies 21/14 days (previously recorded as a flat 30 days); URL updated from the generic visitors-permit page.

FJI.name: Long-Term Work Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens employed by an overseas employer or holding a local job offer to work in Fiji for periods exceeding one year.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 (general) or FJD 475.35 (religious purposes). Standard processing is 21 working days; may vary based on application completeness and background checks. Applicants must be over 18, hold a valid passport with 3+ years remaining, and have a signed employment contract. Spouse and children under 18 may be included. Extension applications must be lodged 1 month prior to expiry. Apply via ImmiHub portal at immihub.immigration.gov.fj.

FJI.name: Short-Term Work Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens to work in Fiji for one year or less under a specific employment contract with an overseas or local employer.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05. Work period is one year or less; permit cannot be extended as short-term - only upgradeable to long-term permit. No dependents permitted. Employment changes require immigration approval. Applicants must be over 18. Apply via ImmiHub portal.

FJI.name: Maritime and Fishing Work Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens to work aboard fishing vessels operating in Fijian waters, covering positions such as captain, engineer, deckhand, cook, seaman, and shore-based management staff.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 for new and extension applications; FJD 664.50 for processing/renewal. Applicants must be over 18. A Contract of Employment is mandatory. Extension applications must be lodged 1 month prior to expiry. Contact: fidpermits@gmail.com. URL updated 2026-07 to the dedicated maritime/fishing crew work-permit page.

FJI.name: NGO Work Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens to work in Fiji for registered international or regional non-governmental organisations.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 for new and extension applications. Applicants must be over 18 and hold a signed Contract of Employment with the NGO. Standard processing 21 working days. Apply via ImmiHub portal or contact fidpermits@gmail.com. URL and fee updated 2026-07 from the dedicated NGO work-permit page (previously pointed to the site homepage).

FJI.name: Secondment Work Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows employees of overseas-based employers to be seconded to a Fijian company or organisation for a defined period.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 for new and extension applications. Applicant must be over 18, hold a passport valid for 3+ years, and provide a secondment letter from the parent company. Standard processing 21 working days. Apply via ImmiHub portal. URL and fee updated 2026-07 from the dedicated secondments work-permit page (previously pointed to the site homepage).

FJI.name: Student Permit
FJI.purpose: Authorises non-citizens to study at secondary, tertiary, vocational institutions, or universities in Fiji. Not available for primary school enrolment.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 321.00 for both new and extension applications; additional bond fees apply after approval. Standard processing is 21 working days. Requires acceptance letter for current academic year, proof of financial support or scholarship documentation, medical report (under 3 months old), and local guardian/sponsor letter. Local police report required if applicant is over 18 and has studied 12+ months in Fiji. Extensions must be lodged 1 month before expiry. Apply via ImmiHub portal. URL updated 2026-07 to the dedicated student-permit-application page.

FJI.name: Internship or Training Attachment Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens to undertake internships or training attachments at Fijian organisations or institutions.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 321.00 for both new and extension applications. Standard processing 21 working days. Apply via ImmiHub portal. URL and fee updated 2026-07 from the dedicated internship/training-attachment page (previously pointed to the site homepage).

FJI.name: Research Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens to conduct academic or scientific research in Fiji.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 for both new and extension applications. Standard processing 21 working days. Apply via ImmiHub portal. URL and fee updated 2026-07 from the dedicated research-permit page (previously pointed to the site homepage).

FJI.name: Three-Year Investor Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens who have an approved business investment project (under FJD 500,000) approved by the Fiji Trade and Investment Bureau (FTIB) to reside in Fiji as investors.
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 for new and extension applications. Valid for 3 years. Requires Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) from FTIB, company registration, tax ID, proof of funds, police report, and medical report. Spouse and dependent children can be included. Path to citizenship only through naturalisation. Exact minimum investment threshold not stated on official site; FTIB approval required. URL updated 2026-07 to the current investor-permit-application page, which processes all investor permits (the page no longer separates 3-year and 7-year tiers by name).

FJI.name: Seven-Year Investor Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens investing FJD 500,000 or more in an approved business in Fiji to reside in Fiji as long-term investors.
FJI.notes: For investments of FJD 500,000 or more. Investor must introduce and maintain capital/assets of at least FJD 500,000 as personal capital (not unsecured loans), own or hold a lease/purchase option on required land or buildings, and demonstrate funds transferred from overseas. Valid for 7 years. Application fee FJD 650.05. Path to citizenship through naturalisation only. URL updated 2026-07 to the current investor-permit-application page (the FJD 500,000 threshold derives from FTIB/embassy guidance and is not stated verbatim on the current immigration page).

FJI.name: Residence Permit on Assured Income
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens aged 45 and over with a guaranteed foreign income or sufficient offshore assets to reside in Fiji long-term without taking up local employment (Fiji's de facto retirement permit).
FJI.notes: Fee is FJD 650.05 for new and extension applications. For non-citizens aged 45+ with offshore assets sufficient to avoid becoming a public charge; the principal applicant may not seek local employment. Ministry of Foreign Affairs guidance describes a bank-deposit requirement (historically F$100,000, waivable if Fiji property is purchased, plus roughly F$30,000-F$40,000 per year for accompanying family), but the current immigration application page states only the offshore-asset requirement, not a fixed amount. Spouse and dependent children may be included. Standard processing 21 working days. URL, fee and age requirement updated 2026-07 from the dedicated assured-income page (previously pointed to the site homepage).

FJI.name: Co-Extensive Residence Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows dependents (spouse and children) of a principal permit holder to enter and reside in Fiji for the same duration as the primary permit holder.
FJI.notes: Issued to dependents co-extensive with the primary permit holder's permit (work, investor, student, etc.); validity mirrors the primary permit. Fee is FJD 650.05 (international) or FJD 185.00 (regional). Standard processing 21 working days. URL and fee updated 2026-07 from the dedicated co-extensive residence-permit page (previously pointed to the site homepage).

FJI.name: Special Purpose Permit (Yacht Owners and Crew)
FJI.purpose: Allows non-citizens who are yacht owners or crew to reside aboard their yacht while in Fijian waters.
FJI.notes: Permit becomes null and void once the yacht exits Fiji. Yacht must be legally registered in Fiji. Requires an approved cruising permit from the Ministry of I-Taukei Affairs. Co-extensive permits available for spouses and dependents. Specific fee details not published.

FJI.name: Transit Visitors Permit
FJI.purpose: Allows travellers to transit through Fiji for more than three hours while in transit to another destination.
FJI.notes: Transit exceeding three hours requires a visitors permit. For visa-exempt nationals this is granted on arrival. Non-visa-exempt nationals transiting must hold a valid SEV or MEV. Specific transit-only visa category is not separately defined; transit is listed as one of the eligible purposes under the standard visitors permit/visa framework.

FJI.name: Exemption Status for Spouse of a Fiji Citizen
FJI.purpose: Allows a foreign national legally married to a Fiji citizen to enter, reside and study in Fiji without a separate visitor, student or residence permit.
FJI.notes: Granted to foreign spouses of Fiji citizens. Initially valid for one year (or the passport's remaining validity if shorter), extendable at the Director of Immigration's discretion, and remains valid only while the marriage subsists. Permits residence and tertiary study, but a work permit is still required to take up employment. Requires marriage certificate, police clearance, medical report and a request letter from the Fiji-citizen spouse. Apply via the ImmiHub portal.

FJI.name: Residence Permit on Special Purpose
FJI.purpose: Issued to non-citizens who need to reside in Fiji for a specific limited purpose not covered by work or study - most commonly medical treatment, but also residing with family and other special circumstances.
FJI.notes: Broad special-purpose residence permit covering medical grounds, residing with family, and similar unique circumstances (the yacht owners/crew special-purpose permit is tracked as a separate category). Fee is FJD 650.05. Standard processing 21 working days. Apply via the ImmiHub portal.

FRA.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourism / Private Visit
FRA.purpose: Allows foreign nationals not exempt from Schengen visa requirements to visit France and the Schengen Area for tourism, private visits, or family stays for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
FRA.notes: Fee is EUR 80 for adults, EUR 40 for children aged 6-11, free for children under 6. Applied for at the French consulate or VFS/TLS Contact centre in applicant's country of residence. Schengen-wide visa; allows travel to all Schengen states. An attestation d'accueil (host certificate, cost EUR 30) is required for private/family visits. Processing begins no earlier than 3 months before departure. Single-entry variants also exist.

FRA.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
FRA.purpose: Required for nationals of certain countries to transit through the international zone of a French airport without entering French territory, between two legs of an international journey.
FRA.notes: Fee is EUR 80. Only required for nationals of countries listed in the common EU airport transit visa list (e.g. Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Congo DR, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Ghana, India, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Sri Lanka, Turkey). Holders of valid Schengen, US, Canadian, or UK visas/residence permits are often exempt. Applied for at the French consulate.

FRA.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
FRA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals requiring a Schengen visa to travel to France for business meetings, conferences, trade fairs, or commercial activities for up to 90 days.
FRA.notes: Same Type C Schengen visa as tourist; purpose is distinguished by supporting documentation (e.g. invitation letter from French company, registration at trade fair). Fee EUR 80. Multiple-entry visas for frequent business travellers may be issued for up to 5 years. Applicants must not carry out paid work in France under this visa.

FRA.name: Long-Stay Student Visa (VLS-TS Etudiant)
FRA.purpose: Allows non-EU nationals to reside in France for the duration of their studies (above 3 months) at a French higher education institution or language school. Serves as both a visa and residence permit (VLS-TS) for the first year.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). For higher education: application must be made via the Campus France / Etudes en France procedure in applicable countries. VLS-TS Student visa validates within 3 months of arrival via ANEF online platform. Fee variable (EUR 99 standard long-stay fee; some nationalities exempt including scholarship holders). Must be validated within 3 months of arrival. After first year, apply for student residence card at prefecture. Part-time work (up to 964 hours/year) is permitted.

FRA.name: Long-Stay Minor Student Visa (VLS-TS Etudiant Mineur)
FRA.purpose: Authorises foreign minors under 18 to attend a French school or educational programme lasting more than 3 months, while their parents reside abroad.
FRA.notes: Maximum duration 11 months. Must not require a separate residence card (no prefecture registration required). Applicable to minors attending school in France whose parents live abroad. Applied for at the French consulate in the country of residence.

FRA.name: Long-Stay Work Visa - Salaried Employee (Salarié / Travailleur Temporaire)
FRA.purpose: Permits non-EU nationals to work in France under an employment contract, either as a permanent employee (salarié) or temporary worker (travailleur temporaire).
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). Employer must obtain work authorisation from DREETS (regional labour authority) before the visa can be issued, unless the occupation is on the shortage list. Visa fee EUR 99; some nationalities exempt (seasonal workers, etc.). After arrival, must apply for salarié or travailleur temporaire residence card at prefecture. Salarié card valid up to 1 year, renewable. Occupation-in-tension list allows simplified procedure.

FRA.name: Talent Passport Visa (Passeport Talent - multiple subcategories)
FRA.purpose: Multi-year long-stay visa for highly skilled workers, researchers, senior executives, artists of international renown, innovative company founders, and investors. The Passeport Talent consolidates multiple former permit types into a single framework.
FRA.notes: Valid up to 4 years. Subcategories include: Salarié qualifié (qualified employee, min salary EUR 39,582/yr + Master's or equivalent); EU Blue Card (min salary EUR 59,373/yr + 3 years higher education); Chercheur (researcher, hosting agreement + min EUR 2,200/month); Projet innovant (startup founder); Investisseur économique (EUR 300,000+ investment + job creation); Professions médicales/pharmaceutiques; Personne de renommée internationale. No separate work permit required. Administrative fee EUR 350 (EUR 300 tax + EUR 50 stamp duty). Online application via ANEF. Family members eligible for Passeport Talent Famille permit.

FRA.name: ICT (Intra-Company Transferee) Visa (Salarié détaché ICT)
FRA.purpose: Allows managers, specialists, or trainees employed by a multinational company to be transferred to the company's French affiliate, subsidiary, or branch for a temporary assignment.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D), implemented under EU Directive 2014/66/EU. Maximum 3 years for managers/specialists, 1 year for trainees. Requires minimum 3 months seniority with the sending company. Salary must equal at least what a French employee in equivalent position earns. Intra-EU mobility: holders of ICT permit from another EU state may move to France for up to 90 days without a new visa.

FRA.name: Seasonal Worker Visa (Travailleur Saisonnier)
FRA.purpose: Authorises non-EU nationals to undertake seasonal agricultural or tourist-sector work in France for a maximum of 6 months per year without requiring a full residence permit.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D) with multiple-entry for repeated seasonal stays. Maximum 6 months in any 12-month period. Visa fee may be waived for seasonal workers. Employer must have a seasonal work contract pre-approved by DREETS. Card may be renewed annually for recurring seasonal workers.

FRA.name: Working Holiday Visa (Visa Vacances-Travail / Programme Vacances-Travail)
FRA.purpose: Enables young adults from partner countries to stay in France for up to 12 months (or 24 months for certain nationalities) for leisure and incidental work, to supplement their travel funds.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). Available under bilateral agreements with: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada (up to 24 months), Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Hong Kong SAR, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Russia, South Korea, Taiwan, Uruguay. Age limits typically 18-30 or 18-35 depending on the bilateral agreement. Applicant must have sufficient funds (proof of at least EUR 2,500 typically required), valid health insurance, and no dependent children accompanying. Work must be secondary to travel. No residence card required on arrival for most nationalities.

FRA.name: Family Reunification Long-Stay Visa (Regroupement Familial)
FRA.purpose: Enables non-EU family members (spouse, minor children) of foreign nationals legally residing in France to join them through the official family reunification procedure.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). The sponsoring family member in France must have been legally resident for at least 18 months, have adequate housing and stable income. Application submitted to OFII (French Office of Immigration and Integration). After arrival, family members must apply for a 'Vie privée et familiale' residence card at the prefecture within 2 months. Sponsor must also demonstrate receipt of OFII medical examination.

FRA.name: Spouse of French National Visa (Conjoint de Français)
FRA.purpose: Allows a non-EU national who is the legally recognised spouse of a French citizen to enter and reside in France, with the visa serving as a temporary residence permit.
FRA.notes: Long-stay VLS-TS visa (Type D) valid 1 year, exempted from visa fee. Must be validated through ANEF within 3 months of arrival. After 1 year the holder may obtain a multi-year residence card. Marriage must be legally recognised. PACS (civil partnership) partners of French nationals may also be eligible for a long-stay visa but through the general family category.

FRA.name: Visitor Long-Stay Visa (Visa Visiteur / Retraité)
FRA.purpose: Allows non-EU nationals wishing to reside in France without working - including retirees and persons of independent means - to stay long-term provided they have sufficient financial resources and health insurance.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). Applicant must prove sufficient stable income or savings to support themselves without working (typically at least EUR 1,200-1,500/month recommended by consulates). Private health insurance covering France is required for the first year. After arrival must apply for 'Visiteur' residence card at prefecture. Work of any kind is strictly prohibited under this status. Temporary long-stay variant available for 4-6 month stays without need for prefecture registration.

FRA.name: Temporary Long-Stay Visa - Short Studies / Cultural Activities
FRA.purpose: Covers stays of 4 to 6 months for short educational programmes (language courses, professional training), artistic activities, or visits by persons with sufficient independent means who do not need a full long-stay permit.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D) valid 4-6 months. No prefecture registration or residence card required. The holder cannot extend this visa or convert it to a residence card while in France; a new application must be made from abroad if a longer stay is needed. Suitable for courses under 6 months, internships of limited duration, and other temporary activities.

FRA.name: Talent Passport - Economic Investor Visa (Passeport Talent Investisseur Economique)
FRA.purpose: Grants residency rights to non-EU nationals making a direct economic investment of at least EUR 300,000 in tangible or intangible fixed assets in a French company, with a commitment to create or maintain employment.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa under the Talent Passport framework. Minimum EUR 300,000 direct investment in tangible or intangible fixed assets. Must create or maintain jobs within 4 years. Pure financial investments excluded. Administrative fee EUR 349 (EUR 300 tax + EUR 50 stamp duty - EUR 1 discount via online). After 5 years of continuous regular residence eligible for 10-year permanent residence card. French Tech Visa fast-track variant available for investors in the startup ecosystem.

FRA.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
FRA.purpose: Issued to foreign diplomatic personnel, government officials, and their dependants for official missions and postings in France. Also covers diplomatic passport holders from countries with bilateral exemption agreements for short stays.
FRA.notes: Fee is waived for diplomatic and official visas. Issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs diplomatic missions. Duration corresponds to the duration of the official posting. Many diplomatic and service passport holders from countries listed in Annexe B of the Arrêté du 10 mai 2010 (as amended, in force 19 June 2025) are exempt from any visa requirement for stays up to 3 months.

FRA.name: Au Pair Visa (Jeune au pair)
FRA.purpose: Allows young foreigners to live with a French host family, participate in family life, and perform light childcare duties, while attending French language classes.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). Governed by the Strasbourg Agreement on au pair placement (1969). Requires a formal au pair placement contract (agreement) approved by the French labour authorities. Applicant must be aged 18-30, have adequate knowledge of French, and be enrolled in or commit to French language courses. Host family provides board, lodging, and pocket money. Duration usually up to 1 year, renewable once.

FRA.name: Intern / Trainee Visa (Stagiaire / Stagiaire ICT)
FRA.purpose: Permits non-EU nationals to undertake professional internships (conventions de stage) or intracompany training assignments in France for periods exceeding 3 months.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa (Type D). The trainee/intern category requires a signed training convention (agreement). The ICT (Intracompany Transferee) Trainee subtype is for trainees within multinationals, governed by EU Directive 2014/66/EU, maximum 1 year. Standard intern visa (stagiaire) is for academic internships. Minimum training allowance applies per French labour law.

FRA.name: Long-Stay Self-Employed / Liberal Profession Visa (Entrepreneur / Profession Liberale)
FRA.purpose: Allows non-EU nationals to create or take part in a commercial, industrial, artisanal or agricultural activity, or to practise a liberal (self-employed) profession in France.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa equivalent to a residence permit (VLS-TS) bearing the mention 'entrepreneur/profession liberale', valid 1 year. Must be validated within 15 days of arrival in France (via ANEF). Applicant must demonstrate the economic viability of a new business project, or (for an existing activity / liberal profession) prove financial resources at least equal to the French full-time minimum wage (SMIC). Regulated professions must meet qualification/diploma requirements. Private medical practitioners follow a separate regime tied to nationality and registration with the Ordre des medecins. Standard long-stay visa fee EUR 99. Projects contributing to France's economic attractiveness may instead qualify for the Passeport Talent.

FRA.name: Job Search / Business Creation Visa (Recherche d'Emploi ou Creation d'Entreprise)
FRA.purpose: Allows non-EU graduates of French higher-education institutions to remain in France after their studies to look for a job or start a business related to their qualification.
FRA.notes: Long-stay visa equivalent to a residence permit (VLS-TS) or residence card marked 'recherche d'emploi ou creation d'entreprise', valid 1 year and NOT renewable. For holders of a professional licence, Master's, or equivalent French degree; graduates may apply within 4 years of obtaining the qualifying French degree. Permits salaried work related to the training with a gross monthly salary above EUR 2,800.53. Does not apply to Algerian students (governed by the Franco-Algerian agreement). Cost when applied for in France EUR 150 (EUR 50 stamp duty + EUR 100 tax); when issued abroad as a VLS-TS, the visa fee plus EUR 100 validation tax on arrival.

FRA.name: Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Medical Treatment (Soins Medicaux)
FRA.purpose: Enables foreign nationals subject to visa requirements to travel to France to consult a doctor or specialised clinic, receive hospital treatment, or undergo aftercare.
FRA.notes: Short-stay Schengen visa (Type C) issued for medical-care reasons; it does not exclude a private or tourism stay. Standard short-stay fee EUR 80. In addition to the general short-stay documentation, applicants must provide medical certificates, the agreement of the host hospital/clinic in France, proof of accommodation and proof of sufficient funds; supporting documents are examined under strict medical confidentiality. Medical care received is NOT covered by the French health insurance system. Urgent cases may be expedited and extensions are possible where medical necessity requires. For longer treatment, a long-stay visa may apply.

FSM.name: Visa-Free Entry (30-Day)
FSM.purpose: Short-term tourism and leisure visits by all nationalities. No visa or entry permit required for stays of 30 days or less.
FSM.notes: Valid passport, sufficient funds, and proof of onward travel required. No visa or permit needed for stays of 30 days or less. US citizens need only a valid passport. All nationalities are eligible.

FSM.name: Entry Permit – General Nationalities
FSM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals (excluding US, Palau, and Marshall Islands citizens) to extend their stay in FSM beyond the initial 30-day visa-free period, up to a maximum of 90 days total.
FSM.notes: Entry permit required for stays exceeding 30 days. Maximum permitted stay via entry permit is 90 days for general nationalities. Application form (FSM_Entry_Permit_Application.pdf) available from the FSM Embassy. No e-visa or online portal exists. Contact: Division of Immigration & Labor, FSM Department of Justice (passport@doj.gov.fm / +619-320-5844).

FSM.name: Entry Permit – US, Palau, Marshall Islands Citizens
FSM.purpose: Allows US citizens and nationals of Palau and the Marshall Islands to stay in FSM for extended periods, with entry permits valid for the duration of the visit up to one year at a time.
FSM.notes: US citizens have an unlimited right to live, work, and study in FSM under the Compact of Free Association (Section 142(a)); entry permits are renewable with no statutory cap on total stay. Palau and Marshall Islands nationals are entitled to entry permits for up to one year (vs. 90-day cap for other nationalities). Confirmed by FSM Embassy entry permit application page. US passport must be valid for at least 180 days from date of entry per travel.state.gov guidance.

FSM.name: EU Short-Stay Visa Waiver (90-Day)
FSM.purpose: Allows citizens of EU member states (excluding Ireland) to visit FSM for up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa, under the bilateral EU-FSM visa waiver agreement.
FSM.notes: Covers holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official, and special passports issued by EU member states. Ireland and the UK are excluded and fall under the general 30-day visa-free regime. Does not apply to travel for paid activity. Agreement signed and entered provisional application 20 September 2016. Confirmed in effect as of 2026 per EEAS. Re-confirmed against EUR-Lex CELEX:22016A1025(01) on 2026-06-29.

FSM.name: Diplomatic/Service Passport Visa Exemption – Israel
FSM.purpose: Allows Israeli nationals holding diplomatic or service passports to enter FSM without a visa for visits not exceeding 90 days within any six-month period.
FSM.notes: Applies only to diplomatic and service passport holders. Ordinary passport holders from Israel fall under the general 30-day visa-free regime. Diplomatic/consular staff and household family members do not need a visa within 30 days of entry; full-term visas required thereafter. Agreement signed 21 January 2010.

FSM.name: Alien Worker's Permit
FSM.purpose: Foreign nationals entering FSM to take up authorized private or government employment; the main FSM work-authorization category for noncitizens.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(6): issued to a noncitizen entering FSM for employment upon compliance with all national laws relating to private or governmental employment. The employer must first obtain nonresident-worker employment authorization from the Division of Immigration & Labor (FSM Department of Justice, passport@doj.gov.fm). All entry permits are capped at one year with provision for renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee is set by presidential executive order (sec. 112) and is not published online. Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Foreign Investor's Permit
FSM.purpose: Foreign nationals investing in or operating a business in FSM; tied to an underlying Foreign Investment Permit (foreign investor's business permit).
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(7): issued for a specified duration and renewable upon renewal or extension of the holder's foreign investor's business permit. Requires a Foreign Investment Permit under the Foreign Investment Act 1997, administered by the state government / FSM Department of Economic Affairs (regulations: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/regulations/forinvreg.htm). This is an immigration entry permit, not a citizenship- or residency-by-investment programme. One-year max per entry permit with renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by executive order (sec. 112).

FSM.name: Student's Permit
FSM.purpose: Foreign nationals enrolled in a school or educational program in FSM.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(3): issued for a specified duration reflecting the student's enrollment in a school or educational program. Capped at one year with provision for renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by presidential executive order (sec. 112). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Salesperson's Permit
FSM.purpose: Foreign nationals engaging in wholesale or retail sales, or taking orders, without establishing a local business presence in FSM.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(5): for a noncitizen engaging in wholesale/retail sales or taking orders without establishing a local business presence. Short business visits of 30 days or less need no permit under the general visitor regime. One-year max with renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by executive order (sec. 112). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Foreign Government Official's Permit
FSM.purpose: Officials and employees of foreign governments or international organizations entering FSM to conduct official business.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(4): for officials/employees of foreign governments or international organizations on official business. Distinct from bilateral visa exemptions (e.g. the Israel diplomatic/service-passport waiver already listed). One-year max with renewal (sec. 104(1)). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Researcher's Permit
FSM.purpose: Foreign nationals conducting research in fields deemed beneficial to FSM citizens.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(8): issued for research in fields deemed beneficial to FSM citizens, subject to conditions set by the President. One-year max with renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by executive order (sec. 112). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Missionary's Permit
FSM.purpose: Duly ordained, licensed, and certified ministers or clergy entering FSM for religious or missionary work.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(9): issued to a duly ordained, licensed, and certified minister or clergyman. One-year max with renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by executive order (sec. 112). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Spouse's Permit
FSM.purpose: Foreign nationals who are the lawful spouse of an FSM citizen.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(10): issued to the lawful spouse of an FSM citizen; may be granted for an indefinite period upon a finding of hardship. Otherwise one-year max with renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by executive order (sec. 112). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Dependent's Permit
FSM.purpose: Unmarried children under 18 of FSM citizens or of noncitizen entry-permit holders.
FSM.notes: Established under FSM Code Title 50 sec. 103(11): issued to unmarried children under 18 of FSM citizens or of noncitizen permit holders. One-year max with renewal (sec. 104(1)); fee by executive order (sec. 112). Legal basis: https://www.fsmlaw.org/fsm/code/title50/T50_Ch01.htm

FSM.name: Vessel Entry Permit
FSM.purpose: Required for vessels (ships) entering FSM waters. Covers crew and passengers aboard private or commercial vessels.
FSM.notes: Application form available from the FSM Embassy. Required for vessels entering FSM waters.

FSM.name: Aircraft Entry Permit
FSM.purpose: Required for aircraft entering FSM airspace/airports, covering crew and passengers on private or chartered aircraft.
FSM.notes: Application form available from the FSM Embassy. Required for aircraft entering FSM.

GAB.name: Visa Court-séjour Tourisme (Short-Stay Tourist Visa)
GAB.purpose: For leisure travel and tourism to Gabon. Applicable to nationals who require a visa and are not eligible for visa-free entry.
GAB.notes: Issued by Gabonese diplomatic missions and consulates abroad. E-visa version available at evisa.dgdi.ga for approximately 70 EUR + 15 EUR processing fee for single-entry up to 3 months. Valid for air entry via Léon Mba International Airport, Libreville. A visa does not guarantee entry - immigration authorities make final admission decisions. Processing at embassy up to 2 weeks.

GAB.name: Visa Court-séjour Tourisme - Entrées Multiples (Short-Stay Tourist Visa, Multiple Entry)
GAB.purpose: For multiple short visits to Gabon for tourism or family visits within the validity period.
GAB.notes: Multiple-entry e-visa available via evisa.dgdi.ga for approximately 185 EUR + 15 EUR processing fee for 6-month validity. Processing time ~72 hours for e-visa route.

GAB.name: Visa Court-séjour Affaires (Short-Stay Business Visa)
GAB.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Gabon for business purposes including meetings, negotiations, and commercial activities.
GAB.notes: Requires a letter of invitation from an individual or company in Gabon explaining the reason for the trip (per UK FCDO guidance). E-visa option available via evisa.dgdi.ga at approximately 70 EUR + 15 EUR processing fee. Valid only for air entry at Libreville (Léon Mba International Airport) for e-visa route.

GAB.name: Visa de Courtoisie (Courtesy Visa)
GAB.purpose: For government officials and employees of international organizations travelling to Gabon on an official mission.
GAB.notes: Issued to government officials and international organization staff with official mission orders. Not available via e-visa portal; must apply through diplomatic missions.

GAB.name: Visa Diplomatique (Diplomatic Visa)
GAB.purpose: For holders of diplomatic passports and their accredited embassy/consulate staff and dependents.
GAB.notes: Issued to diplomatic passport holders and their embassy/consulate staff with dependents. Many nationalities with bilateral agreements are visa-free on diplomatic passports. Duration and conditions set by bilateral agreements.

GAB.name: Visa Long-séjour / Permis de Séjour (Long-Stay Visa / Residence Permit)
GAB.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to reside in Gabon for more than 90 days for work, study, or family reunification.
GAB.notes: Long-stay visas are NOT issued by Gabonese diplomatic missions or consular posts abroad. Applicants must enter on a short-stay visa and then apply within one month of arrival to the Direction Générale de la Documentation et de l'Immigration (DGDI) for a residence card (carte de séjour). Governed by Law N°5/86 of 18 June 1986.

GAB.name: Autorisation de Travail / Carte de Séjour (Work Permit / Residence Card for Workers)
GAB.purpose: For foreign nationals employed or seconded in Gabon requiring legal authorisation to work and reside in the country.
GAB.notes: Work authorisation is processed through the DGDI after entry on a short-stay visa. No separate work visa is issued abroad; the long-stay residence card pathway applies. Employer sponsorship typically required.

GAB.name: Visa Études / Carte de Séjour Étudiant (Student Visa / Student Residence Card)
GAB.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in Gabonese educational institutions for studies exceeding 90 days.
GAB.notes: Students enter on a short-stay visa with proof of enrolment and must apply to DGDI within one month of arrival for a student residence card. No dedicated student e-visa category exists on the evisa.dgdi.ga portal. The MFA short-stay visa page lists 'études' as a supported purpose under the short-stay visa application.

GAB.name: Visa Court-séjour Visite Familiale (Short-Stay Family/Friendly Visit Visa)
GAB.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Gabon to visit family members or friends resident in the country.
GAB.notes: 'Family Visit' (Visite familiale) and 'Friendly Visit' are official 'Purpose of visit' options on the DGDI e-visa application form at evisa.dgdi.ga, alongside Tourism and Business (verified against the live portal form, 2026-07). Issued as the standard short-stay e-visa: single-entry 1-3 months for approximately 70 EUR (45,000 XAF) + 15 EUR processing fee, ~72h processing; a 6-month multiple-entry option (185 EUR / 120,000 XAF + 15 EUR) is also available. The application requires a named contact/host in Gabon (name, address, phone). Valid only for air entry via Léon Mba International Airport, Libreville.

GAB.name: Visa Court-séjour Raison Médicale (Short-Stay Medical Visa)
GAB.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Gabon to receive medical treatment.
GAB.notes: 'Medical reason' (Raison médicale) is an official 'Purpose of visit' option on the DGDI e-visa application form at evisa.dgdi.ga (verified against the live portal form, 2026-07). Issued as the standard short-stay e-visa: single-entry 1-3 months for approximately 70 EUR (45,000 XAF) + 15 EUR processing fee, ~72h processing; a 6-month multiple-entry option (185 EUR / 120,000 XAF + 15 EUR) is available for longer treatment. Treatment exceeding 90 days requires applying to the DGDI in Libreville for a residence card. Valid only for air entry via Léon Mba International Airport, Libreville.

GBR.name: Standard Visitor Visa
GBR.purpose: Tourism, visiting family/friends, business meetings, short courses
GBR.notes: Apply online at gov.uk. Most applicants will be asked to attend a visa application centre. Fee is £135 (as of June 2026). Also covers business visits, so the UK has no separate short-term business visa. Long-term Standard Visitor visas (2, 5 or 10 years) are also available at higher fees.

GBR.name: Student Visa
GBR.purpose: Studying a course at a licensed UK student sponsor for longer than 6 months
GBR.notes: Requires a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from a UK Visas and Immigration-licensed sponsor. Application fee £558 when applying from outside the UK (June 2026). Degree-level students aged 18+ can usually stay up to 5 years; below degree level up to 2 years.

GBR.name: Child Student Visa
GBR.purpose: Studying at an independent (fee-paying) school in the UK, for children aged 4 to 17
GBR.notes: For children aged 4-17 attending a licensed independent school. Requires a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS). Application fee £558 from outside the UK (June 2026). Children aged 4-15 must be sponsored by an independent fee-paying school. Decision usually within 3 weeks.

GBR.name: Short-term study visa (English language)
GBR.purpose: Studying an accredited English language course lasting longer than 6 and up to 11 months
GBR.notes: Only for accredited English language courses lasting 6-11 months (shorter courses use the Standard Visitor route). Fee £228 (June 2026). Stay is the length of the course plus 30 days, up to 11 months. Cannot be extended, switched, or used for other subjects.

GBR.name: Skilled Worker Visa
GBR.purpose: Working in an eligible skilled job with a UK employer
GBR.notes: Requires a job offer from a UK licensed sponsor paying at least the required salary threshold. Standard fee from outside the UK is £819 for up to 3 years or £1,618 for more than 3 years (June 2026); lower fees apply if the job is on the immigration salary list.

GBR.name: Health and Care Worker Visa
GBR.purpose: Qualified doctors, nurses, health professionals and adult social care workers with a job offer from an approved UK health or care employer
GBR.notes: A subset of the Skilled Worker route with reduced fees and exemption from the immigration health surcharge. Fee £324 (up to 3 years) or £628 (more than 3 years) as of June 2026. Requires a certificate of sponsorship from a Home Office-approved health or care employer. Decision usually within 3 weeks.

GBR.name: Global Talent Visa
GBR.purpose: Recognised or emerging leaders in academia/research, arts and culture, or digital technology
GBR.notes: No employer sponsorship required, but most applicants need endorsement from an approved body (or an eligible prestigious prize). Fee £766 total (£561 endorsement + £205 visa) as of June 2026. Grant up to 5 years at a time; leads to settlement after 3-5 years. Decision usually within 3 weeks from outside the UK.

GBR.name: High Potential Individual (HPI) Visa
GBR.purpose: Recent graduates of a top global university who want to work or look for work in the UK without a job offer
GBR.notes: For those who obtained an eligible qualification from a top-ranked university in the last 5 years. No sponsorship needed. Application fee £880 (June 2026). Grants 2 years (3 years for PhD holders); cannot be extended and does not lead directly to settlement.

GBR.name: Graduate Visa
GBR.purpose: Post-study work for those who have completed an eligible UK degree on a Student visa
GBR.notes: Unsponsored work route for recent UK graduates; applied for from inside the UK. Fee £937 (June 2026). Grants 2 years (18 months if applied on/after 1 January 2027), or 3 years for PhD holders. Cannot be extended and does not lead directly to settlement.

GBR.name: UK Ancestry Visa
GBR.purpose: Commonwealth citizens with a grandparent born in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man who want to work in the UK
GBR.notes: For Commonwealth citizens (also British overseas citizens/nationals and Zimbabwean citizens) able to prove a UK-born grandparent. Fee £726 (June 2026). Grants 5 years; holders can work without sponsorship and apply for settlement after 5 years. Decision usually within 3 weeks.

GBR.name: Youth Mobility Scheme (Working Holiday)
GBR.purpose: Living and working in the UK for up to 2 years (age 18–30/35, select nationalities)
GBR.notes: Available to nationals of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Uruguay, Andorra, Iceland, India (ballot) and others via bilateral agreements. Fee £340 (June 2026). Base stay 2 years; Australian, Canadian and New Zealand nationals can extend by 1 further year.

GBR.name: Family Visa (spouse/partner/parent/child)
GBR.purpose: Joining a spouse, partner, fiancé(e), child, parent or relative who is British or settled in the UK, for longer than 6 months
GBR.notes: For partners, fiancé(e)s, children, parents and adult dependent relatives of British citizens or settled persons. Application fee £2,064 per person from outside the UK (£1,407 inside) as of June 2026. Partner route initial grant is typically 33 months from outside the UK; leads to settlement after 5 years. Decisions usually within 12 weeks from outside the UK.

GBR.name: Marriage Visitor Visa
GBR.purpose: Coming to the UK to marry or register a civil partnership without intending to stay or settle
GBR.notes: For those who will marry or form a civil partnership in the UK but do not plan to settle afterwards. Fee £135 (June 2026). Stay up to 6 months. Those intending to settle after marriage should use the Family visa (fiancé(e)) route instead.

GBR.name: Standard Visitor Visa (private medical treatment)
GBR.purpose: Receiving private medical treatment in the UK for longer than 6 and up to 11 months
GBR.notes: An extended Standard Visitor route for private medical treatment lasting up to 11 months. Fee £234 (June 2026). Requires evidence from a UK doctor/consultant, treatment details and ability to pay. Private treatment of up to 6 months uses the ordinary Standard Visitor visa (£135).

GBR.name: Innovator Founder Visa
GBR.purpose: Setting up or running a business in the UK that is innovative, viable, and scalable
GBR.notes: Requires endorsement from a UKVI-approved endorsing body. No minimum investment amount specified. Application fee £1,357 per person when applying from outside the UK (June 2026), plus endorsement fees. Valid 3 years, renewable; leads to settlement after 3 years.

GBR.name: Transit Visa (Direct Airside / Visitor in Transit)
GBR.purpose: Passing through the UK en route to another country
GBR.notes: Two types: Direct Airside Transit visa (£41.50, remain airside without passing border control) and Visitor in Transit visa (£74.50, pass through border control and leave within 48 hours). Required for visa nationals changing flights in the UK, unless exempt under the Transit Without Visa (TWOV) scheme.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Tourism - Short Stay)
GEO.purpose: Short-stay tourism visits to Georgia for leisure and sightseeing. Applied for online through the official e-visa portal.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee (non-refundable). Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Stay duration and validity vary by nationality - standard configurations are 30 days stay within 120-day validity (multiple entry), or 90 days stay within 180-day validity (multiple entry). Applicants must check the online calculator for their specific entitlement. Requires: biometric photo, passport scan, accommodation proof, flight ticket, travel insurance, proof of financial means. Passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond visa validity, with at least 2 blank pages, issued within 10 years.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Tourism up to 1 Year)
GEO.purpose: Extended tourism stay in Georgia for up to one year, available through the e-visa portal for eligible nationalities.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee. This is an extended tourism category distinct from the standard short-stay tourism e-visa. Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Actual availability depends on applicant's nationality. Same documentation requirements as standard tourism e-visa.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Business/Professional)
GEO.purpose: Short-stay visits to Georgia for business activities, professional meetings, conferences, and commercial purposes.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee. Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Stay duration and validity vary by nationality (typically 30/120 or 90/180 configurations). Requires: biometric photo, passport scan, proof of travel purpose/business purpose, accommodation proof, flight ticket, travel insurance. The e-visa portal is for short-stay visits (under 90 days); long-term business or work authorization requires separate permits.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Visiting Friends and Relatives)
GEO.purpose: Short-stay visits to Georgia for the purpose of visiting friends or family members residing in Georgia.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee. Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Requires: biometric photo, passport scan, supporting documentation, accommodation proof, flight ticket, travel insurance, proof of financial means. Duration and validity vary by nationality.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Study and Training - Short Stay)
GEO.purpose: Short-stay visits to Georgia for study, training, or educational programs lasting less than 90 days.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee. Explicitly for study/training durations under 90 days only. For longer-term study, a separate long-stay national visa (D3 Study Visa) is required, obtained through a Georgian embassy/consulate abroad. Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Requires supporting documentation from educational institution.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Health and Medical Care)
GEO.purpose: Short-stay visits to Georgia for medical treatment, health consultations, or recuperation at Georgian medical facilities.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee. Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Requires proof of medical appointment or treatment documentation in Georgia. Duration and validity may vary by nationality.

GEO.name: e-Visa (Religion/Pilgrimages)
GEO.purpose: Short-stay visits to Georgia for religious purposes, pilgrimages, or participation in religious events and ceremonies.
GEO.notes: Fee is USD 20 + 2% service fee. Georgia has significant Orthodox Christian religious sites making it a destination for pilgrimages. Processing is 'not less than 5 working days'. Requires supporting documentation related to religious purpose.

GEO.name: Remotely from Georgia Program
GEO.purpose: Allows remote workers, freelancers, and employees of foreign companies to live and work remotely from Georgia for up to 360 days.
GEO.notes: Launched in 2020. Open to citizens of visa-free countries (98+ nationalities). Requires: remote worker/freelancer/employee of foreign employer status, minimum income of USD 2,000/month or USD 24,000 in savings, health insurance. As of June 2025, Georgia passed amendments requiring mandatory work permits for foreign nationals (including remote workers) starting March 1, 2026, which may significantly affect or effectively end this program. Current status as of 2026 is uncertain. This is not a separate visa category but a formalization scheme for visa-free nationals staying long-term.

GEO.name: D1 Immigration Visa (Labour and Entrepreneurial Activity)
GEO.purpose: Foreign nationals coming to Georgia to conduct labour/employment activity, to work under a concluded contract, to act as representatives or consultants of companies and firms performing official duties, or to carry out entrepreneurial (business) activity.
GEO.notes: Long-stay national (immigration) visa applied for at a Georgian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad - NOT available through the e-visa portal. Issued with the right of multiple entries and with either 90-day or 1-year validity and duration of stay. Normally the gateway to a work residence permit for stays beyond the visa period. Decision made within 30 calendar days of application (Government Ordinance No. 280). From 1 March 2026, mandatory work permit rules for foreign nationals also apply.

GEO.name: D2 Immigration Visa (Professional, Freelance, Scientific/Cultural/Sports Missions, Internship and Volunteering)
GEO.purpose: Foreign nationals arriving for a scientific, sports, cultural or educational mission; freelancers; persons taking an internship or serving as volunteers; and mass-media workers performing official duties in Georgia.
GEO.notes: Long-stay national (immigration) visa applied for at a Georgian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad. Issued with multiple entries and 90-day or 1-year validity/stay. Covers freelancers and professional/cultural/sports/educational missions that are not standard employment (D1). Decision made within 30 calendar days of application (Government Ordinance No. 280).

GEO.name: D3 Immigration Visa (Study and Research)
GEO.purpose: Foreign nationals coming to study or conduct research at authorised educational institutions in Georgia, or to study under international programmes.
GEO.notes: Long-stay study visa applied for at a Georgian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad. This is distinct from the under-90-day 'Study and Training' e-visa: D3 is required for degree programmes and other studies lasting longer than 90 days. Issued with multiple entries and 90-day or 1-year validity/stay; gateway to a study residence permit. Decision made within 30 calendar days (Government Ordinance No. 280).

GEO.name: D4 Immigration Visa (Family Reunification)
GEO.purpose: Foreign nationals coming to Georgia for family reunification with a family member lawfully residing in Georgia.
GEO.notes: Long-stay national (immigration) visa for family reunification, applied for at a Georgian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad. Issued with multiple entries and 90-day or 1-year validity/stay; gateway to a family residence permit. Decision made within 30 calendar days of application (Government Ordinance No. 280).

GEO.name: D5 Immigration Visa (Real Property Owners)
GEO.purpose: Foreign nationals who, under the procedure established by Georgian law, hold the right of ownership of real property (real estate) within the territory of Georgia.
GEO.notes: Long-stay national (immigration) visa for owners of real property in Georgia, applied for at a Georgian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad. Distinct from the separately-tracked residence-permit-by-investment (RBI) programme - this is the entry visa tied to property ownership. Issued with multiple entries and 90-day or 1-year validity/stay. Decision made within 10 calendar days of application - faster than other D categories (Government Ordinance No. 280).

GEO.name: Transit Visa (Category B)
GEO.purpose: Foreign nationals transiting through Georgia en route to a third country.
GEO.notes: Short transit stay (up to about 5 days) for passing through Georgia to another destination. One of Georgia's five statutory visa categories (diplomatic, special, ordinary, immigration, transit). Issued by Georgian diplomatic missions and consular offices. Nationals who are visa-free or eligible for the e-visa generally do not need a separate transit visa.

GHA.name: Tourist e-Visa
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Ghana for tourism, leisure, or recreation. Applied for online through the official Ghana e-Visa portal.
GHA.notes: Applied for online at evisa.immigration.gov.gh. Standard processing $260 (72 hrs), priority $338 (48 hrs), express $442 (5 hrs). Multiple-entry: standard $468, priority $608, express $796. Visa delivered to email inbox for presentation at port of entry. Max stay of 30 days cited in portal sample.

GHA.name: Business e-Visa
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Ghana for business meetings, negotiations, conferences, or commercial activities. Applied for online through the official Ghana e-Visa portal.
GHA.notes: Standard single-entry $260 (72 hrs), priority $338, express $442. Multiple-entry: $468/$608/$796. Requires business commencement certificate, certificate of incorporation, company code, tax clearance certificate, host's passport biodata page, and flight itinerary.

GHA.name: Student e-Visa / Residence Permit
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted to a Ghanaian educational institution who need to reside in Ghana throughout the duration of their studies.
GHA.notes: Requires letter from educational institution, admission letter, school fees payment receipts, two passport-sized photos, and passport. Resident fee range GH¢129–259 (approx USD 12–24 at GH¢11=$1 rate per GIS fees page). Duration matches length of study. Application lodged with Ghana Immigration Service.

GHA.name: Transit Visa
GHA.purpose: For indirect transit passengers who must collect and recheck their luggage while transiting through Ghana to another destination.
GHA.notes: Valid for 48 hours. Direct airside transit passengers (no luggage collection) are exempt. Fee listed as $50 on GIS fees page (Transit Permit). Requires travel itinerary, proof of visa to final destination (if applicable), two passport-sized photographs, and completed disembarkation card. Also available via e-Visa portal.

GHA.name: Emergency Entry Visa (EEV) / Visa on Arrival
GHA.purpose: Granted at an immigration officer's discretion to persons who arrive at a Ghanaian port of entry without a pre-obtained visa, subject to conditions prescribed in regulations.
GHA.notes: Fee: $200 per GIS fees and charges page (effective May 15, 2025). Requires letter to the Comptroller-General stating country of origin, arrival date, stay duration, visit purpose, travel itinerary, and lodging information. Not guaranteed - granted at immigration officer discretion. For business visits: also requires certificate of incorporation, tax clearance, and host's passport biodata.

GHA.name: Re-Entry Visa (Single)
GHA.purpose: Issued to visitors who are already in Ghana on a valid permit and wish to leave the country temporarily and return without obtaining a new visa.
GHA.notes: Fee: $65–$100 (single) per GIS fees page. Requires completed Re-Entry Form, application letter, two passport-sized photographs, non-citizen identification card, and valid passport. Must already hold a valid Ghana residence status.

GHA.name: Re-Entry Visa (Multiple)
GHA.purpose: Multiple-entry re-entry permit for visitors in Ghana on a valid permit who need to make repeated temporary departures and returns.
GHA.notes: Fee: $129–$194 (multiple) per GIS fees page. Same requirements as single re-entry visa. Must already hold a valid Ghana residence status.

GHA.name: Work and Residence Permit (Companies)
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals who are lawfully admitted to Ghana and wish to work and reside in the country under employment by a registered company.
GHA.notes: Fee: $194–$1,293 per GIS fees page (range by company type/quota). Requires letter to Comptroller-General, GIPC registration, tax clearance, audited accounts, medical report from Ghana Immigration Clinic, police report from home country, employment contract, professional/educational certificates, CV, and passport biodata. Application submitted to Ghana Immigration Service.

GHA.name: Work and Residence Permit (Missionaries/NGOs/GIPC/Free Zones)
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals working with NGOs, missions, or businesses registered with the Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) or Ghana Free Zones Board.
GHA.notes: Fee: $194–$388 (Missionaries/NGOs); $194–$500 (GIPC Automatic Quota); $194–$647 (Immigrant Quota) per GIS fees page. Requires GIPC Registration Certificate, Ghana Free Zones Board approval (if applicable), ministerial support letter, and standard company/professional documents.

GHA.name: Work and Residence Permit - Shareholders
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals who hold shares in Ghanaian-registered companies and wish to reside in Ghana in connection with their business interests.
GHA.notes: Fee: GH¢2,000 (approx USD 182 at GH¢11=$1) per GIS fees page. Requires share certificate, company incorporation documents, GIPC registration, and standard GIS documentation.

GHA.name: Residence Permit (Dependent)
GHA.purpose: For dependants of expatriates working in Ghana and for Ghanaian nationals with foreign passports seeking to reside with their Ghanaian-citizen family members.
GHA.notes: Fee: GH¢194–388 (approx USD 18–35) per GIS fees page. Requires proof of relationship to principal permit holder or Ghanaian national. Specific requirements listed on GIS service page.

GHA.name: Indefinite Residence Status
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals wishing to reside permanently in Ghana, granting the right to live indefinitely, enter without a visa, and work without a work permit.
GHA.notes: Requires attestation by two Ghanaians of repute, evidence of immovable properties (where applicable), 6 years tax clearance, 3 years audited accounts, SSNIT returns, police report from Ghana, and medical report. Also available for foreign spouses of Ghanaian nationals. No minimum investment amount stated on GIS page. Fee (general Indefinite Resident Permit): GH¢10,000–$18,000 per GIS fees and charges page (effective May 15, 2025); GH¢5,000 (approx USD 455) for spouse of a Ghanaian national.

GHA.name: Right of Abode
GHA.purpose: Granted to Ghanaians who lost citizenship by acquiring foreign nationality and to persons of African descent in the diaspora, conferring the right to reside and work permanently in Ghana.
GHA.notes: Fee: GH¢1,940–3,879 (approx USD 176–353) per GIS fees page. Approved by the Minister with the President's approval. For Africans in the Diaspora: requires evidence of economic contribution to Ghana (shares, bank statements, audited accounts, employment records for Ghanaians). Grants entry without visa and work without work permit.

GHA.name: Concessionary Visa
GHA.purpose: A reduced-fee or special-arrangement visa for eligible diplomatic, official, or service passport holders from specific bilateral partner countries.
GHA.notes: Fee: $97–$100 per GIS fees and charges page. Specific eligibility criteria and issuing conditions are managed through bilateral agreements. Apply through Ghana Immigration Service or Ghanaian embassy/consulate.

GHA.name: Rotators Permit
GHA.purpose: For foreign workers who rotate in and out of Ghana on a scheduled basis, typically in extractive industries such as oil, gas, or mining.
GHA.notes: Fee: $647 for up to 6 months; $1,000 for 6–12 months per GIS fees page. Designed for workers in rotation schedules. Requires employer sponsorship and standard GIS documentation.

GHA.name: Free Zone Resident Permit
GHA.purpose: For foreign nationals employed by businesses operating within Ghana's designated Free Zone enclaves under the Ghana Free Zones Board.
GHA.notes: Fee: $240 (first year) per GIS fees page. Requires Ghana Free Zones Board approval letter and standard work permit documentation. Subsequent years may have different fee schedule.

GHA.name: Visa/Permit Extension (Extension of Visitor's Permit)
GHA.purpose: For visitors already in Ghana on a visitor's visa or permit who wish to extend their authorised stay beyond the original duration. Employment is not permitted while on a visitor's permit.
GHA.notes: Extensions granted for a minimum of 3 months initially, up to a maximum of 6 months. Fee: GH¢26–65 per month ('Visitor Permit Extension') per GIS fees and charges page (effective May 15, 2025); fee_usd left null as the charge is a per-month range (approx USD 2–6/month at GH¢11=$1). Requires completed Extension Form, application letter, two passport-sized photographs, photocopy of return ticket, letter of support from local host/institution (where applicable), copy of non-citizen identification card, and passport. Employment restricted while on visitor's permit. Lodged with Ghana Immigration Service.

GIN.name: Tourist Visa
GIN.purpose: Short-stay visits for tourism and leisure purposes. Requires a valid passport, return ticket, and Yellow Fever certificate.
GIN.notes: Applied online via paf.gov.gn; Entry Visa Letter received after approval (processing ~72 hours); physical visa collected at border arrival counter with biometric capture. Valid for stays not exceeding 90 days.

GIN.name: Transit Visa (Visa de Transit)
GIN.purpose: For travelers passing through Guinea in transit to a third country. Permits brief stay not exceeding three days.
GIN.notes: Applied online via paf.gov.gn; collected at border arrival counter with biometric registration. Requires valid passport, onward ticket, and Yellow Fever certificate.

GIN.name: Transbordement Visa (Visa de Transbordement / VTB)
GIN.purpose: For travelers transiting or transshipping through Guinea to a third country; issued on presentation of an onward ticket and, where applicable, a visa for the country of final destination.
GIN.notes: Corrected 2026-07-04: the prior record incorrectly listed this as a 5-year, USD 150 multiple-entry visa (it had been conflated with the VESRM Multiple Entry Visa). Per the official paf.gov.gn e-visa portal, the Transbordement/Transit visa (VTB) fee is USD 50 with a maximum stay not exceeding three days (DCPAF states validity of 3 to 5 days, beyond which a short-stay visa is required). Distinct from the general Transit Visa, this is the transshipment visa for travelers transferring between carriers/vessels; both are USD 50 for a maximum 3-day stay on the official portal. Requires valid passport, onward ticket, and Yellow Fever certificate. Applied online via paf.gov.gn; collected at border arrival counter.

GIN.name: Long Term Visa (Visa de Long Séjour / VLS)
GIN.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to reside in Guinea for an extended period, typically for employment. Valid for one year from date of issuance.
GIN.notes: Applied online via paf.gov.gn; collected at border arrival counter. Requires valid passport, copy of any prior visa, employment contract or equivalent supporting documentation, and Yellow Fever certificate. Non-ECOWAS foreign employers hiring foreign nationals must also obtain prior authorization from AGUIPE (Guinea's Employment Promotion Agency). Per the official PAF/DCPAF visa framework, the VLS is the long-stay category used to settle in Guinea for employment, business, family reunion, or study - Guinea does not issue separate business, student, or family visas; those purposes are documented within the VLS (employment contract, professional authorization, marriage deed, or student certificate of registration).

GIN.name: Multiple Entry Visa (Visa de Séjour à Entrées Multiples / VESRM)
GIN.purpose: For nationals of special treaty countries holding a bilateral visa agreement with Guinea; permits repeated entries over a multi-year period.
GIN.notes: Per Guinea's Police aux Frontières / DCPAF official visa framework (paf.gov.gn DNPAF visa page), the VESRM is issued only to nationals of countries holding a special bilateral treaty with Guinea; its validity varies between 3 and 5 years depending on the specific agreement (validity_days shown is the 5-year upper bound). Not a standard selectable option on the e-visa application form; arranged under the terms of the bilateral commitment. Fee not published on the official portal.

GIN.name: Diplomatic, Service and Courtesy Visa (VDSC)
GIN.purpose: For holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports and invited government guests. Issued upon prior official approval.
GIN.notes: Requires a security code authorization from the relevant Guinea authority before online application can proceed. Duration and fee are governed by the official approval documentation. Requires valid passport, appointment letter, and Yellow Fever certificate.

GMB.name: Tourist Visa (Single Entry)
GMB.purpose: Short-term leisure or holiday visits to The Gambia. Allows tourism and informal business visits not exceeding the permitted stay.
GMB.notes: Visa obtainable at embassies/consulates abroad or on arrival at Banjul International Airport. US State Dept notes on-arrival cost is $100–105 (cash only, USD or dalasi). Embassy fee quoted as $0 for single-entry tourist visa when processed via consulate for some nationalities. An airport security fee of $20 USD is additionally required on both entry and departure. Countries needing clearance must obtain pre-arrival clearance before travelling. 90-day maximum stay per gid.gov.gm and gambia.gov.gm.

GMB.name: Tourist Visa (Multiple Entry)
GMB.purpose: Multiple-entry leisure or holiday visits to The Gambia, valid for repeated entry over a longer period.
GMB.notes: Per gid.gov.gm/visa/, a Multiple Journey Visa is valid for any number of journeys for a validity period NOT exceeding 12 months (corrected from a previously recorded 5-year/1825-day figure that the official page contradicts). Applied for at a Gambian embassy or consulate abroad. Maximum single stay 90 days per entry. A Securiport airport fee of D1000 (~$20 USD) applies on both entry and departure, except diplomats and minors under 2. The ~$139 fee is an approximate agency figure; GID does not publish visa fees on its official site.

GMB.name: Business Visa
GMB.purpose: Visits for business meetings, conferences, trade, and exploration of business opportunities in The Gambia.
GMB.notes: Business travellers use the Short Visit Visa (bona-fide businessman, up to 90 days, subject to local security clearance) or a Multiple Journey Visa. Per gid.gov.gm/visa/, a Multiple Journey Visa's validity does NOT exceed 12 months (corrected from a previously recorded 5-year figure). Also obtainable on arrival at Banjul International Airport. Applicants must present business documentation and a passport valid 6+ months. gambia.gov.gm confirms business visits up to 90 days are covered under the visa-exemption framework for exempt nationalities. The ~$139 fee is an approximate agency figure; GID does not publish visa fees officially.

GMB.name: Transit Visa
GMB.purpose: Short-stay transit through The Gambia for travellers en route to a third country.
GMB.notes: Embassy fee is $0 for transit visa (consular processing). Transit passengers are exempt from the $20 airport security fee. Applicants must hold onward ticket to a third country, valid visa for final destination if required, and proof of sufficient funds for the layover period. Single entry only.

GMB.name: Missionary Visa
GMB.purpose: Visits for religious or faith-based missionary work in The Gambia.
GMB.notes: gid.gov.gm/visa/ does not enumerate a distinct 'missionary visa'; religious/mission visits are handled as a Multiple Journey Visa (validity NOT exceeding 12 months - corrected from a previously recorded 5-year figure) or, for longer stays, a Resident Permit A (issued to those on mission). Applied for at a Gambian embassy or consulate abroad. Applicants must submit a letter of invitation from their Gambian sponsor or host organisation detailing purpose, length of stay, accommodation, and contact information.

GMB.name: Official/Diplomatic Visa
GMB.purpose: Entry for government officials and diplomatic personnel travelling to The Gambia on official business.
