GMB.notes: Per gid.gov.gm/visa/, the Diplomatic Visa is issued only to Heads of Missions, is granted only by Gambian Missions abroad, and NO fee is charged for its issuance. Separately, the Feb 2026 New Visa Policy (HC Senegal) lists 'Diplomats and Consular Corps' as visa-exempt; holders of diplomatic, official/service, or ordinary passports from EU states (incl. UK and Switzerland) are visa-free per Section IV. The Securiport airport fee is waived for diplomats.

GMB.name: Resident Permit B (Work & Residence Permit)
GMB.purpose: For non-Gambians taking up gainful employment or self-employment in The Gambia - expatriates, businesspersons, professionals, and unskilled workers who earn a livelihood. This is the country's combined work-and-residence permit.
GMB.notes: gid.gov.gm/residential-permit/: Resident Permit B is issued to those who intend to live, reside AND work in The Gambia. It is an offence for a non-citizen to take up gainful employment without it. Official fee: D7,700 for non-ECOWAS nationals (~$105 USD, includes the D2,500 Alien Card) or D3,600 for ECOWAS nationals (~$49). Non-ECOWAS applicants must reside 56 days after admission before issuance; Permit B requires a GRA payroll tax receipt. Biometric card, renewed annually. Valid holders may re-enter The Gambia without a fresh visa; children/dependents are covered under the holder's permit.

GMB.name: Resident Permit A (Student Residence)
GMB.purpose: For foreign students residing in The Gambia to study, without engaging in gainful employment. Resident Permit A is the non-working residence permit the GID issues to foreign students.
GMB.notes: gid.gov.gm/residential-permit/ states Resident Permit A is issued to applicants who intend to reside without gainful employment, 'usually issued to foreign student residing in the Gambia, retirees, individuals on short business visit or mission.' The Gambia has no separate 'student visa' - foreign students reside under Permit A. Official fee: D5,700 for non-ECOWAS (~$78 USD, includes the D2,500 Alien Card) or D3,100 for ECOWAS (~$42). Non-ECOWAS applicants must reside 56 days after admission before issuance. Biometric card, renewed annually.

GMB.name: Resident Permit A (Retiree Residence)
GMB.purpose: For foreign retirees residing in The Gambia without engaging in gainful employment.
GMB.notes: gid.gov.gm/residential-permit/ explicitly lists retirees among those issued Resident Permit A (the non-working residence permit). The Gambia has no dedicated 'retirement visa' scheme; retirees reside under Permit A. Official fee: D5,700 for non-ECOWAS (~$78 USD, includes the D2,500 Alien Card) or D3,100 for ECOWAS (~$42). Non-ECOWAS applicants must reside 56 days after admission before issuance. Biometric card, renewed annually.

GMB.name: Non-Gambian ID Card
GMB.purpose: A residence-and-work identity document issued under bilateral agreements to nationals of Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Sierra Leone, and Ivory Coast, allowing them to legally reside and work in The Gambia.
GMB.notes: Per gid.gov.gm/residential-permit/, the Non-Gambian ID Card is issued to nationals of Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Sierra Leone and Ivory Coast under bilateral cooperation, letting them legally reside and work in The Gambia on payment of prescribed fees. Official fee: D750 (~$10 USD). Issued to holders aged 18 and above.

GNB.name: Short Stay Single-Entry Visa (Court Séjour - Entrée Unique)
GNB.purpose: Tourism and short visits to Guinea-Bissau for non-exempt nationalities.
GNB.notes: Available on arrival at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport or via pre-enrollment through the rgb-visa.com e-visa system (private domain, fee approx EUR 61.45 + EUR 2.50 processing). Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival required. Yellow fever vaccination certificate mandatory. US State Dept and UK FCDO both confirm visa on arrival is available. For longer stays, a multiple-entry visa must be obtained in advance.

GNB.name: Short Stay Multiple-Entry Visa - 3 Months
GNB.purpose: Tourism or short visits allowing multiple entries over a 3-month validity period.
GNB.notes: Must be obtained in advance via Guinea-Bissau embassy or e-visa pre-enrollment system (rgb-visa.com, fee approx EUR 70.45 + processing). Not available on arrival. Yellow fever certificate mandatory.

GNB.name: Long Stay Multiple-Entry Visa - 6 Months
GNB.purpose: Extended stays and multiple entries to Guinea-Bissau over a 6-month validity period.
GNB.notes: Must be obtained in advance via Guinea-Bissau embassy or e-visa pre-enrollment system (rgb-visa.com, fee approx EUR 88.32 + processing). Not available on arrival.

GNB.name: Long Stay Multiple-Entry Visa - 1 Year
GNB.purpose: Multiple entries to Guinea-Bissau over a 1-year validity period.
GNB.notes: Must be obtained in advance via Guinea-Bissau embassy or e-visa pre-enrollment system (rgb-visa.com, fee approx EUR 100.00 + processing). Not available on arrival.

GNB.name: Business Visa (Visto de Negócios)
GNB.purpose: Entry for business meetings, negotiations, and commercial activities in Guinea-Bissau.
GNB.notes: Business visa is confirmed as a required category by the Government of Canada travel advisory. Specific fee and processing details not published on an accessible official Guinea-Bissau government source. Apply via Guinea-Bissau embassy (nearest operational ones in Paris, Dakar, Lisbon) or via the rgb-visa.com e-visa pre-enrollment system. Yellow fever certificate mandatory.

GNB.name: Transit / Stopover Visa (Visto de Trânsito)
GNB.purpose: Short transit stop through Guinea-Bissau territory for travellers continuing to a third country.
GNB.notes: Single-entry transit/stopover visa valid for 1 day. Fee approx EUR 55.00 + EUR 2.50 processing per rgb-visa.com fee schedule. Also available on arrival at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport. Yellow fever certificate mandatory for all arrivals.

GNB.name: Diplomatic / Courtesy Visa (Visto de Cortesia)
GNB.purpose: Entry for diplomatic personnel, officials, or courtesy visits under formal invitation from the Guinea-Bissau government.
GNB.notes: Courtesy single-entry visa valid 1 month. Fee approx EUR 61.45 + EUR 2.50 processing per rgb-visa.com fee schedule. Holders of diplomatic or service passports from CPLP member states (Angola, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Mozambique, Portugal, São Tomé and Príncipe, Vietnam) are fully visa-exempt - they do not need this visa category.

GNB.name: Student Visa (Visto de Estudante)
GNB.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals enrolling in accredited educational institutions in Guinea-Bissau.
GNB.notes: Confirmed as a required visa category by the Government of Canada travel advisory. Specific fee, validity, and processing details not found on any accessible official Guinea-Bissau government source. Must be obtained via a Guinea-Bissau embassy before travel (nearest operational missions: Paris, Dakar, Lisbon). Yellow fever certificate mandatory.

GNB.name: Work / Employment Visa (Visto de Trabalho)
GNB.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals taking up employment or professional activities in Guinea-Bissau.
GNB.notes: Work visas exist as a formal immigration category under Guinea-Bissau law but no official government portal with fees, forms, or procedures was accessible (gov.gw does not resolve). Must be arranged via a Guinea-Bissau embassy. Employer sponsorship typically required. Yellow fever certificate mandatory.

GNB.name: Family Reunification / Family Visa (Visto Familiar)
GNB.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals joining family members who are resident or citizen in Guinea-Bissau.
GNB.notes: Family visa category inferred from standard West African immigration practice and CPLP Mobility Agreement provisions. No official Guinea-Bissau government page with procedures was accessible. Apply at a Guinea-Bissau embassy. Specific fees and processing times unknown.

GNQ.name: Tourist Visa (Embassy)
GNQ.purpose: Short-stay tourism and leisure visits to Equatorial Guinea, applied through an embassy or consulate.
GNQ.notes: Visa must be used within 60 days of issuance. Requires invitation letter from a government entity, registered business, or Equatorial Guinean citizen. Proof of at least USD 1,000 in available funds per month of stay required. Criminal record clearance (under 3 months old), vaccination booklet, flight itinerary, and accommodation proof required. Expedited processing (1-3 days) available for additional USD 50 (total USD 250). Max stay not explicitly stated on the embassy page. Cash no longer accepted as of February 7, 2025; payment by online or money order only.

GNQ.name: Tourist eVisa
GNQ.purpose: Online tourist visa for short-stay leisure visits to Equatorial Guinea, applied via the official e-visa portal without visiting an embassy.
GNQ.notes: Launched July 1, 2023 under Presidential Decree No. 49/2019. Operated by VFS Global as government technical partner. Processing is approximately 72 hours after payment. Fee EUR 105 (Spanish MFA re-confirmed June 2026; approximately USD 113 at current rates). Approval letter must be printed and presented on arrival. Entry via Malabo International Airport. Available to all eligible nationalities. The EG embassy in Washington DC notes the online system is completely separate and independent from embassy services.

GNQ.name: Business Visa (Embassy)
GNQ.purpose: Short-stay visa for business travel including meetings, negotiations, and official commercial activities in Equatorial Guinea.
GNQ.notes: Same fee and processing structure as the tourist visa. Requires an employer letter stating the purpose of travel and confirmation of expense coverage. Expedition available for additional USD 50 (total USD 250, 1-3 days). Invitation letter from a government entity or registered business in Equatorial Guinea required. Visa must be used within 60 days of issuance. Cash no longer accepted as of February 7, 2025; payment by online or money order only.

GNQ.name: Business eVisa
GNQ.purpose: Online business visa for short-stay commercial visits to Equatorial Guinea, covering meetings, congresses, and seminars.
GNQ.notes: One of the e-visa modalities under Presidential Decree No. 49/2019, covering commercial and professional visits. Launched July 1, 2023. Processing approximately 72 hours. Fee EUR 105 (Spanish MFA re-confirmed June 2026; approximately USD 113 at current rates). Entry via Malabo International Airport. Approval letter must be printed and presented on arrival. The Congresses/Meetings/Seminars modality is captured as its own separate entry.

GNQ.name: Congresses, Meetings and Seminars eVisa
GNQ.purpose: Online visa for attending congresses, official meetings, conferences, and seminars in Equatorial Guinea.
GNQ.notes: One of the four e-visa modalities established by Presidential Decree No. 49/2019 (the others being Tourism, Business, and Humanitarian Emergency), explicitly enumerated by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs (re-confirmed June 2026). Used for attending congresses, meetings and seminars. Fee EUR 105 for stays under 90 days (approximately USD 113). Processing approximately 72 hours after payment. Approval letter must be printed and presented on arrival via Malabo International Airport.

GNQ.name: Emergency Humanitarian eVisa
GNQ.purpose: Online visa for emergency humanitarian purposes, allowing urgent travel to Equatorial Guinea in humanitarian circumstances.
GNQ.notes: Listed as one of the e-visa categories under Decree No. 49/2019. Specific fee, validity, and max stay not disclosed on publicly accessible pages of the portal. Processing approximately 72 hours.

GNQ.name: Official/Diplomatic Visa
GNQ.purpose: Visa for holders of official or diplomatic passports traveling on government business or official missions to Equatorial Guinea.
GNQ.notes: Free of charge per the Embassy of Equatorial Guinea in Washington DC consular services page (re-confirmed June 2026). Diplomatic and official passport holders from countries with bilateral visa exemption agreements (e.g. Gabon, Cameroon, Serbia, Bolivia, India, Ghana, Qatar, Burundi, Guinea-Bissau, Gambia, Mauritania, Mozambique, Belarus) may enter without any visa under those agreements. For all other diplomatic passport holders a visa is still required but issued at no charge.

GNQ.name: Residence Permit (Permiso de Residencia)
GNQ.purpose: Long-stay authorization for foreign nationals remaining in Equatorial Guinea longer than 90 days, including for employment or family residence.
GNQ.notes: Required for stays longer than 90 days. Issued in-country by the Ministry of National Security; typically valid for one year and lets the holder exit and re-enter Equatorial Guinea without a separate visa (UK FCDO, re-confirmed June 2026). No online portal - the application is made in person after arriving on a short-term visa, and renewals through the National Security office can be slow (Spanish MFA). Foreign workers are sponsored via an employer-filed work authorisation / temporary residence permit. No official fee published on an accessible government source.

GRC.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourist/Visit
GRC.purpose: Authorizes entry into the Schengen Area, including Greece, for tourism, visiting family or friends, or other short-stay purposes not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.
GRC.notes: Standard fee €90 (approx $99 USD). Children aged 6–12 pay €45. Children under 6 are free. Multiple-entry visas may be valid up to 5 years for repeat applicants with good track record. Applied for at the Greek consulate of the applicant's country of residence. Governed by EU Visa Code (Regulation (EC) 810/2009). Applications must be submitted at least 15 days before travel.

GRC.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
GRC.purpose: Permits entry for business meetings, conferences, trade fairs, negotiations, or other commercial activities for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
GRC.notes: Same Type C Schengen visa as tourist; purpose is distinguished by supporting documents (invitation letters from Greek companies, trade fair registrations, etc.). Fee €90. Governed by EU Visa Code (Regulation (EC) 810/2009).

GRC.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
GRC.purpose: Required for certain nationalities to pass through the international transit zone of Greek airports without entering the Schengen Area.
GRC.notes: Fee €80 (approx $88 USD); children 6–12 pay €40. Maximum validity 6 months for multiple airport transit visas. Only required for nationals of countries listed in Annex IV of the EU Visa Code. Issued by Greek consulates. Does not permit entry into Greek territory outside the airport international zone.

GRC.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Studies
GRC.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Greece to pursue full-time studies at a recognized educational institution. Required prior to arriving to apply for a Student Residence Permit.
GRC.notes: Issued by Greek embassies/consulates abroad. After arrival, the holder must apply for a Student Residence Permit (Άδεια Διαμονής λόγω Σπουδών), renewable annually for the duration of studies. Governed by Law 4251/2014. Applicants must show proof of enrollment, sufficient funds, and health insurance.

GRC.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Employment
GRC.purpose: Grants entry for third-country nationals intending to take up employment in Greece under a contract with a Greek employer.
GRC.notes: Requires employer sponsorship and labor market test approval. After entry, the worker must convert to a Residence Permit for Employment. Seasonal workers (e.g., agriculture, tourism) may be covered under the Seasonal Worker permit category (Art. 13a, Law 4251/2014). EU nationals are exempt (freedom of movement). Governed by Law 4251/2014 as amended.

GRC.name: EU Blue Card (Highly Qualified Worker)
GRC.purpose: Residence and work permit for third-country nationals who are highly qualified workers employed in Greece, providing preferential treatment and path to long-term residence.
GRC.notes: Valid 2 years (or employment contract duration + 3 months if shorter). Renewable. Requires employment contract of at least 1 year and salary of at least 1.5x the average gross annual salary in Greece. Blue Card holders enjoy equal treatment with Greek nationals in employment, social security, and education. After 5 years of continuous legal residence, may apply for long-term residence. Governed by EU Blue Card Directive 2009/50/EC transposed into Greek law via Law 4251/2014.

GRC.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Type D) - Remote Work
GRC.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals who work remotely for employers or clients based entirely outside Greece to reside in Greece while conducting their work.
GRC.notes: Introduced under Law 4825/2021, updated by Law 5038/2023. Minimum monthly income of €3,500 net (€4,200 with a dependent spouse; €4,830 with additional dependents). Application fee approximately €1,000 (visa) plus ~€150 per family member. Initial visa valid 12 months (Type D). After arrival, applicants may apply for a 2-year Digital Nomad Residence Permit, renewable every 2 years. Eligible holders may receive a 50% income tax reduction for up to 7 years. Employer/clients must be based entirely outside Greece.

GRC.name: Golden Visa - Investor Residence Permit
GRC.purpose: Grants a renewable 5-year residence permit to non-EU nationals who make qualifying investments in Greece, including real estate, government bonds, bank deposits, or startup investments.
GRC.notes: Minimum investment thresholds (per Law 5100/2024, effective 31 August 2024): €800,000 for residential/commercial real estate in high-demand zones (Attica, Thessaloniki, islands with 3,100+ inhabitants); €400,000 in all other regions; €250,000 for commercial-to-residential conversion or heritage building restoration; €500,000 in Greek government bonds (3-year minimum maturity); €500,000 in fixed-term Greek bank deposit (1-year minimum); €350,000 in Greek-focused investment fund units; €250,000 in an Elevate Greece-registered startup. Fees: €16 for permit issuance; €2,000 electronic fee for renewals. No minimum stay requirement. Path to citizenship after 7 years of legal residence. Family members included. Short-term (Airbnb-type) rentals prohibited for real estate route.

GRC.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Family Reunification
GRC.purpose: Enables family members of legally resident third-country nationals in Greece to join and reside with them under the family reunification framework.
GRC.notes: Governed by EU Family Reunification Directive (2003/86/EC) transposed into Greek law. The sponsor must hold a valid Greek residence permit of at least 1 year validity and have reasonable prospects of obtaining permanent residence. Covers spouse, minor children, and in certain cases dependent parents. After entry, family members must apply for their own residence permit at the Aliens and Immigration service.

GRC.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Economically Independent Persons
GRC.purpose: Allows financially self-sufficient third-country nationals who do not intend to work in Greece to reside in the country, provided they can demonstrate sufficient regular income from abroad.
GRC.notes: Applicants must demonstrate regular income from abroad (pensions, investments, property income, etc.) sufficient to support themselves and dependents without working in Greece. Similar to a 'retirement/passive income' visa category. Governed by Law 4251/2014. Work is prohibited under this permit. Residence permit initially issued for 2 years and renewable.

GRC.name: Humanitarian Residence Permit
GRC.purpose: Granted to third-country nationals who face exceptional humanitarian circumstances that prevent their return to their country of origin, outside the formal asylum process.
GRC.notes: Issued on humanitarian grounds (e.g., serious illness, protection from violence, other compelling circumstances). Renewable annually. Governed by Law 4251/2014, Art. 19A. Applicants must be residing in Greece and apply through the local Aliens and Immigration Service. Does not require departure and re-entry.

GRC.name: Long-Term Resident Permit (EU)
GRC.purpose: Grants permanent or long-term residence status to third-country nationals who have legally resided in Greece continuously for at least 5 years, conferring near-equal rights to Greek nationals.
GRC.notes: Based on EU Long-Term Residents Directive (2003/109/EC). Requires 5 years of continuous legal residence in Greece. Holders have the right to work, access social benefits, and move to other EU member states for work or study. Valid for 5 years and renewable. Processing decision should arrive within 6 months (extendable by 3 months) per EU directive requirements.

GRC.name: Tech Visa
GRC.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Greece to work for a registered Greek tech startup, providing fast-track immigration for the technology sector.
GRC.notes: Introduced by Greek immigration reforms effective 6 February 2026. Salary must be at least 1.6x the national average gross salary. The Tech Visa cannot be transferred to another employer; immigration status lapses if employment ends. May be converted to an EU Blue Card if eligibility is met. Valid 12 months initially.

GRC.name: Talent Visa
GRC.purpose: Permits entry for highly educated third-country nationals with at minimum a Master's degree from a globally-ranked university to seek employment in Greece.
GRC.notes: Introduced by Greek immigration reforms effective 6 February 2026. Requires at minimum a Master's degree (or PhD/Postdoc) from an institution ranked on at least two international university ranking lists. No job offer required at entry. Does not grant immediate work authorization; upon securing employment in Greece, holder can transition to work/residence permits or EU Blue Card. Valid 12 months.

GRC.name: Seasonal Worker Permit
GRC.purpose: Authorizes third-country nationals to enter Greece for temporary seasonal employment, primarily in agriculture and tourism sectors.
GRC.notes: Governed by Article 13a of Law 4251/2014 and the EU Seasonal Workers Directive (2014/36/EU). Covers seasonal work in agriculture, tourism, and related sectors. Maximum stay varies by sector. Employer must obtain prior authorization from Greek labor authorities before the visa can be issued. Bilateral agreements may govern admission quotas for certain nationalities.

GRC.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Scientific Research
GRC.purpose: Allows non-EU researchers to enter Greece to carry out research at an approved research organisation under a hosting agreement.
GRC.notes: For third-country nationals conducting research under a hosting agreement with a research organisation approved by the General Secretariat for Research and Technology. Governed by the EU Researchers Directive (2016/801/EU) as transposed into the Greek Immigration Code (Law 5038/2023). The residence permit duration matches that of the hosting agreement and is renewable on the same basis. Holders enjoy equal treatment in working conditions, social security, and recognition of qualifications, plus intra-EU researcher mobility. Applicant obtains a national (Type D) visa at a Greek consulate, then a residence permit after arrival.

GRC.name: Intra-Corporate Transfer (ICT) Residence Permit
GRC.purpose: Enables managers, specialists, and trainee employees of a multinational company to be transferred from a non-EU branch to the company's Greek entity.
GRC.notes: Governed by the EU Intra-Corporate Transfer Directive (2014/66/EU) transposed into Greek law. Requires prior employment with the company of at least 12 months for managers and specialists, and 6 months for trainees. The Greek host entity applies for approval from the Ministry of Migration and Asylum; after approval the transferee obtains a national (Type D) visa and then the ICT residence permit. Maximum stay is up to 3 years for managers and specialists and up to 1 year for trainees. Permits intra-EU mobility to same-group entities in other member states.

GRC.name: Residence Permit for Independent Economic Activity / Self-Employment
GRC.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Greece to carry out independent (self-employed) economic activity or an approved investment activity.
GRC.notes: Two routes: (1) Independent economic activity - requires at least €250,000 in capital and a business plan showing benefit to the Greek economy; residence permit valid 2 years, renewable for identical periods. (2) Investment activity - requires a business investment (minimum €500,000) with positive effects on the national economy; residence permit valid 3 years, renewable. Applicant obtains an initial national (Type D) visa, then applies for the residence permit after arrival before the visa expires. Requires proof of financial resources, health insurance, and a medical certificate. Governed by the Greek Immigration Code (Law 5038/2023).

GRC.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Medical Treatment
GRC.purpose: Permits entry to Greece to receive planned medical treatment or hospitalization at a Greek healthcare facility for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
GRC.notes: Same Type C Schengen visa as tourist/business; the medical purpose is evidenced by supporting documents (e.g., a confirmed appointment or admission letter from the Greek medical institution and proof of sufficient funds to cover treatment). Standard fee €90 (approx $99 USD); children aged 6-12 pay €45. Governed by the EU Visa Code (Regulation (EC) 810/2009). For treatment expected to exceed 90 days, a national (Type D) visa route applies instead.

GRD.name: Grenada Visitor Visa (Single-Entry)
GRD.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who require a visa to visit Grenada for tourism, recreation, or visiting family/friends. Grants a single entry for the period specified by the immigration officer.
GRD.notes: Can be obtained prior-to-arrival at a Grenada Embassy/Mission or at the Port of Entry on arrival. Holders are not authorized to work in Grenada without permission from the Ministry of Labour. Processing time approximately 10 business days when obtained prior to arrival. Fee is USD 100 per the official Embassy of Grenada Beijing (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page. Max stay is at the discretion of the immigration officer (typically 14, 30, 60, or 90 days).

GRD.name: Grenada Visitor Visa (Single-Entry) - Business
GRD.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals requiring a visa who wish to enter Grenada for business meetings, conferences, or commercial activities. Uses the same single-entry visitor visa category as tourist visits.
GRD.notes: Grenada does not maintain a separate business visa category; business visitors use the standard Visitor Visa (Single-Entry) at USD 100. Holders are not authorized to work or receive remuneration from within Grenada. Prior-to-arrival or port-of-entry issuance available.

GRD.name: Grenada Visitor Visa (Multiple-Entry)
GRD.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who require a visa to make multiple visits to Grenada for tourism, business, or other short-stay purposes within the validity period of the visa.
GRD.notes: Fee is USD 250 per the official Embassy of Grenada Beijing (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page. Must be obtained prior to arrival (not available at port of entry). Holders are not authorized to work in Grenada without permission from the Ministry of Labour. Validity period is specified on the visa; each entry stay duration is at the discretion of the immigration officer.

GRD.name: Grenada Work Permit
GRD.purpose: Required for all non-nationals (excluding CARICOM Protocol free-movement beneficiaries) who wish to take up employment with a Grenadian employer. Applied for by the employer on behalf of the prospective employee.
GRD.notes: Fee structure varies by nationality: CARICOM nationals (Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Guyana, Jamaica, Montserrat, Suriname, Trinidad & Tobago, Cuba) XCD 1,000 (approx. USD 370); Commonwealth, North America, UK, EU nationals XCD 3,000 (approx. USD 1,110); all other nationalities XCD 5,000 (approx. USD 1,850). Application fee: XCD 100 (approx. USD 37). Late submission penalty: XCD 100. Renewals must be filed 3 months before expiry. Documents must be in English. Processing time not specified on official source. Employer bears responsibility for ensuring compliance with all labour obligations.

GRD.name: Grenada Remote Employment Permit
GRD.purpose: Allows non-nationals earning at least EC$100,000 per year (approx. USD 37,000) from employment or business activities outside Grenada to reside in Grenada while working remotely. Holders may not work for or offer services to any person or business within Grenada.
GRD.notes: Established under the Remote Employment Act, Act No. 3 of 2021. Application fee: USD 1,500 (individual); USD 2,000 (individual + up to 3 dependants); USD 200 per additional dependant beyond 3. Annual renewal fee: USD 1,400 (individual); USD 1,900 (individual + up to 3 dependants). Permit holders are exempt from Grenada income tax on income earned outside Grenada. Conditional duty exemptions apply to household effects (up to EC$75,000 c.i.f.) and one motor vehicle. Dependants cannot enrol in public educational institutions. Permit holders are deemed non-residents for citizenship and voting purposes. Not available to OECS Protocol Member State citizens (who have free movement rights). Minimum income threshold: EC$100,000/year (approx. USD 37,000). Renewable annually.

GRD.name: Grenada Citizenship by Investment - National Transformation Fund
GRD.purpose: Grants Grenadian citizenship through a non-refundable financial contribution to the National Transformation Fund (NTF), which finances projects in tourism, agriculture, and alternative energy. No prior residency in Grenada is required.
GRD.notes: Minimum contribution USD 235,000 (effective July 1, 2024 per SR&O 15 of 2024 / Caribbean MOA price standardization). Note: the cbi.gov.gd homepage still displayed USD 150,000 (old figure) as of June 2026 - the website has not been updated. Established under the Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013. All applications must be submitted through an Authorised Agent to the Citizenship by Investment Committee (CBIC). Processing time: approximately 3–4 months. Citizenship can be extended to spouse, dependent children under 18, dependent parents, and dependent grandchildren. Applicants must be at least 18, have no criminal record, and be in good health. No residency required before or after citizenship. Key benefit: Grenada citizenship provides E-2 Treaty Investor Visa eligibility for the United States, and visa-free/on-arrival access to 140+ countries including UK, Schengen Area, China, Singapore.

GRD.name: Grenada Citizenship by Investment - Approved Real Estate
GRD.purpose: Grants Grenadian citizenship through investment in a government-approved real estate project. The applicant must hold the qualifying real estate for at least 5 years after citizenship is granted.
GRD.notes: Minimum investment USD 270,000 (effective July 1, 2024 per SR&O 15 of 2024 / Caribbean MOA price standardization). Some approved projects may have different minimums (e.g., USD 220,000 for shared/fractional units vs. USD 350,000 for sole-ownership units). Applicant must hold the real estate for at least 5 years following the grant of citizenship. Approved projects include luxury hotels, resorts, and villas listed on the official CBI website. All applications through Authorised Agents. Processing time: approximately 3–4 months. Same eligibility and family extension rules as NTF route apply.

GRD.name: Grenada Diplomatic/Official Visa
GRD.purpose: Issued to diplomatic and government officials traveling to Grenada on official business. Separate application track available at Grenada Embassies and Missions.
GRD.notes: The Embassy of Grenada USA references a separate 'Instructions for Diplomats/Government Officials' document and a separate application pathway. Many diplomatic/official/service passport holders from countries that ordinarily require visas receive more favourable treatment (e.g., extended stay durations or visa exemptions). Fee information not published on official source. Details vary by nationality and bilateral agreement.

GRD.name: Grenadian Citizenship by Registration (Spouse of a Grenadian Citizen)
GRD.purpose: Allows a foreign national legally married to a citizen of Grenada to apply to be registered as a citizen of Grenada. Administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs / Immigration and Passport Department.
GRD.notes: Citizenship-by-registration route (not a temporary visa). The official 'Application - Married to a Grenadian' form is published on the Government of Grenada Home Affairs portal. Requires marriage certificate, proof of the spouse's Grenadian citizenship, police certificate of character, and supporting documents; foreign-language documents must be translated into English. Fee and processing time are not published on the official portal. Distinct Home Affairs registration routes also exist for children and grandchildren of Grenadian citizens and for Commonwealth citizens.

GRD.name: Grenadian Citizenship by Naturalisation
GRD.purpose: Route for foreign nationals who have lawfully resided in Grenada for the qualifying period to apply to become naturalised citizens of Grenada. Administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs / Immigration and Passport Department.
GRD.notes: Citizenship-acquisition route (not a temporary visa), distinct from the Citizenship by Investment programme. The official 'Application - Naturalization' form is published on the Government of Grenada Home Affairs portal. Applicants must normally hold permanent residence and have accumulated the required period of lawful residence in Grenada. Fee and processing time are not published on the official portal.

GTM.name: Visa de Turismo / Visitante (Category B - Consular Visa)
GTM.purpose: Short-stay tourism, leisure, or visiting family/friends. Issued at Guatemalan consulates abroad to nationals of Category B countries who do not hold a qualifying US/Canada/Schengen/Mexico visa.
GTM.notes: Single-entry fee is USD 50; multiple-entry is USD 150 (valid 1–5 years). Category B nationals holding a valid US, Canadian, Schengen, or Mexican visa are exempt from obtaining this visa. Processing is stated as 48 hours (2 business days) and requires in-person application. Passport must have at least 6 months validity. No online or visa-on-arrival option exists. Governed by Acuerdo IGM-015-2025 (Reglamento de Visas Guatemaltecas). Source: Guatemala Embassy in India (official MINEX domain consindia@minex.gob.gt).

GTM.name: Visa de Turismo / Visitante - Multiple Entry (Category B)
GTM.purpose: Multiple-entry short-stay tourism or visitor permit for Category B country nationals, allowing repeated entries within the validity period.
GTM.notes: Multiple-entry fee is USD 150; validity is 1–5 years (stated as 1–5 años in Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-015-2025; recorded here as up to 5 years / 1825 days maximum). Each stay limited to 90 days. Requires in-person application at a Guatemalan consulate. Category B nationals with valid US/Canada/Schengen/Mexico visa are exempt. Source: Guatemala Embassy in India (official MINEX domain) and Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-015-2025.

GTM.name: Visa de Turismo / Visitante (Category C - Consulted Visa)
GTM.purpose: Short-stay tourism for nationals of Category C countries, which require prior authorization from the Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración (IGM) before a consulate may issue the visa.
GTM.notes: Category C nationals must first obtain IGM authorization before the consulate can issue a visa - this is an additional step not required for Category B. Category C nationals are NOT exempt from the visa requirement even if they hold a US/Canada/Schengen/Mexico visa. Category C country list is published at igm.gob.gt/clasificacion-de-paises/ but embedded as a static image. Fees and processing times for Category C are not officially published in extractable text. Governed by Acuerdo IGM-015-2025.

GTM.name: Visa de Negocios (Business Visa)
GTM.purpose: Short-stay entry for business meetings, conferences, trade activities, or professional consultations that do not constitute employment in Guatemala.
GTM.notes: Business visas fall under the general consular visa framework of Guatemala's Reglamento de Visas (Acuerdo IGM-015-2025). Guatemala's Código de Migración (Decreto 44-2016) identifies business as a permitted visitor purpose. Fees and validity periods follow the same Category B/C consular visa structure as tourist visas. An employment letter or business invitation is required. Category B nationals with valid US/Canada/Schengen/Mexico visas are exempt. No online application.

GTM.name: Visa de Tránsito (Transit Visa)
GTM.purpose: Allows passage through Guatemala en route to a third country, without a stay for tourism or business purposes.
GTM.notes: Transit visas are recognized under Guatemala's Código de Migración (Decreto 44-2016). The specific fee and processing time for transit visas is not published in extractable official text. Category A nationals do not require a transit visa. Category B/C nationals transiting by air and not clearing immigration typically do not need a transit visa if airside only; land transit requires checking current requirements. Max stay of 3 days is approximate based on standard regional practice - official figure not confirmed from extractable text.

GTM.name: Visa de Estudiante / Residencia Temporal como Estudiante
GTM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Guatemala for the duration of an educational program at a recognized institution.
GTM.notes: Student residency falls under the temporary residency framework of Acuerdo IGM-016-2025 (Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas), Article 75(c) of Código de Migración (Decreto 44-2016). Requires enrollment proof from a recognized Guatemalan educational institution, valid passport, police clearance, and economic solvency. Annual renewal required. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): residencia temporal para estudiantes USD 100 per year, plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal como Trabajador Migrante con Empleador Guatemalteco (Migrant Worker - Guatemalan Employer)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency permit for foreign nationals employed by a Guatemalan-based employer.
GTM.notes: Governed by Acuerdo IGM-016-2025 (Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas, effective October 8, 2025). Requires a valid employment contract with a Guatemalan employer, valid passport, police clearance, and proof of economic solvency. The requirement for a Guatemalan guarantor certificate was eliminated by IGM-016-2025 as of October 8, 2025. Annual renewal required; after 5 years may apply for permanent residency. Field checks are now mandatory. Source: Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-016-2025 (official regulation, image-based PDF). Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): temporary residence USD 200 for 1 year (USD 300 for 2 years; USD 500 for 3-5 years), plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal como Trabajador Migrante con Empleador Extranjero (Migrant Worker - Foreign Employer / Remote Worker)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals employed by a foreign employer outside Guatemala, working remotely from within Guatemala.
GTM.notes: New category introduced by Acuerdo IGM-016-2025 (Article 11), effective October 8, 2025. Minimum monthly income from abroad: USD 2,000 (individual); USD 3,000 if accompanied by dependents. No Guatemalan employer or local guarantor required. Requires bank statements proving foreign-sourced income, valid passport, police clearance. Annual renewal; after 5 years may apply for permanent residency. This is Guatemala's functional equivalent of a 'digital nomad' visa - there is no separate formal 'digital nomad visa' branding in the official regulation. Source: Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-016-2025. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): temporary residence USD 200 for 1 year (USD 300 for 2 years; USD 500 for 3-5 years), plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal como Trabajador Independiente (Self-Employed / Independent Worker)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals operating as self-employed or independent workers in Guatemala.
GTM.notes: Third modality under the migrant worker residence framework of Acuerdo IGM-016-2025. Requires proof of self-employed status or independent professional work. Specific income requirements and documentation not confirmed in extractable text. Annual renewal; after 5 years may apply for permanent residency. Source: Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-016-2025. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): temporary residence USD 200 for 1 year (USD 300 for 2 years; USD 500 for 3-5 years), plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal como Inversionista (Investor Temporary Residency)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals who invest at least USD 100,000 in Guatemala through commercial entities or acquisition of assets.
GTM.notes: Article 17 of Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas (Acuerdo IGM-016-2025). Minimum investment: USD 100,000 in commercial entities and/or movable or immovable assets. Evidence required: property registrations, securities title certificates, fixed asset invoices, proof of fund origin. Annual renewal; after 5 years of temporary residency may apply for permanent residency. Source: Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-016-2025 (confirms USD 100,000 minimum). Processing fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): temporary residence USD 200 for 1 year (USD 300 for 2 years; USD 500 for 3-5 years), plus USD 25 application-intake fee - separate from the USD 100,000 investment requirement.

GTM.name: Residencia Permanente como Rentista o Pensionado (Permanent Residency for Retirees / Passive Income Holders)
GTM.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals subsisting on stable foreign-generated income (rentistas) or receiving regular pension payments from foreign sources (pensionados).
GTM.notes: Article 31 of Acuerdo IGM-016-2025. Minimum monthly income: USD 1,250 (individual); each dependent adds USD 300/month. Income must be generated outside Guatemala - from bank deposits, foreign company investments, real estate remittances, or pensions from foreign governments/organizations/companies. Granted directly as permanent residency (no temporary stage required). Income proof must be renewed every 5 years. Path to citizenship: standard naturalization after 5 continuous years residency (2 years for qualifying nationalities). Source: IGM official requirements form and Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-016-2025. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): residencia permanente para rentistas o pensionados USD 400, plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal para Intelectuales, Investigadores y Científicos (Intellectual, Researcher, and Scientist Residency)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals with documented qualifications to practice as intellectuals, researchers, or scientists in Guatemala.
GTM.notes: Article 19 of Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas (Acuerdo IGM-016-2025); based on Article 75(e) of Guatemala's Código de Migración (Decreto 44-2016). Requires documentation certifying qualifications, updated Guatemalan guarantor certification, and valid contract. Residency is temporary and tied to the contract. Extensions require proof of continued contract. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): temporary residence USD 200 for 1 year (USD 300 for 2 years; USD 500 for 3-5 years), plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Visa para Eventos Especiales (Special Events Visa)
GTM.purpose: Short-stay visa issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MINEX) for foreign nationals attending special events - transmission of presidential mandate, diplomatic and consular meetings, international summits, and official government meetings organized by ministries of state.
GTM.notes: Issued by the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MINEX) through the Direccion de Protocolo y Ceremonial Diplomatico, regulated under the Reglamento de Visas Guatemaltecas (articles 16-18). No cost; 30-day validity. Applies to events organized by MINEX (transmission of presidential mandate, diplomatic and consular meetings, summits) and official government meetings organized by other ministries of state. Source: IGM 'Consultas Frecuentes para Tramite de Visas Guatemaltecas' (igm.gob.gt/consultas-frecuentes-para-tramite-de-visas-guatemaltecas). Corrected 2026-07: the official IGM/MINEX name for this protocol/government-events category is 'Visa para Eventos Especiales' (the prior 'Academic/Professional Events' label was inaccurate).

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal como Dependiente (Dependent Family Residency)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency for economic dependents (spouses, minor children, dependents) of foreign nationals already holding a qualifying temporary or permanent residency in Guatemala.
GTM.notes: Governed by Acuerdo IGM-016-2025. Dependents may apply simultaneously with the primary residency holder. Qualifying relationships include spouses and minor children of primary residency holders. Category B/C nationals who are married to a Guatemalan national (minimum 6 months of marriage registered in RENAP) or have Guatemalan children are upgraded to Category A status for entry purposes under Acuerdo IGM-015-2025. Source: Consortium Legal analysis of IGM-015-2025 and IGM-016-2025. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjería, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): temporary residence USD 200 for 1 year (USD 300 for 2 years; USD 500 for 3-5 years), plus USD 25 application-intake fee.

GTM.name: Visa Diplomática / Visa Oficial (Diplomatic and Official Visa)
GTM.purpose: Entry documents for foreign diplomatic and official passport holders traveling on official government missions to Guatemala.
GTM.notes: Diplomatic and official passport holders are governed by bilateral agreements and the Vienna Convention. Guatemala has bilateral diplomatic/official passport visa waiver agreements with numerous countries. The exact list of countries exempt from diplomatic/official visa requirements is not available in extractable text from official sources; aggregator sources (not used here) suggest a wide range of bilateral agreements. Fee is conventionally zero for diplomatic visas. Duration corresponds to the length of the official mission.

GTM.name: Prorroga de Visa de Turista o Viajero (Tourist / Visitor Visa Extension)
GTM.purpose: Extends the legal stay of a tourist or visitor already in Guatemala beyond the period granted on entry, for up to 90 additional days.
GTM.notes: Applied for in person at the Subdireccion de Extranjeria of the Instituto Guatemalteco de Migracion (IGM) before the current authorized stay expires; the initial 90-day tourist stay is extendable once for up to 90 more days (180 days total). Requirements: application form, valid passport, onward travel ticket / international credit card / Guatemalan guarantor certificate, and proof of payment. Official application form: Prorroga-de-Visa-de-Turista-o-Viajero (PVT-IGM-01-2022). Fee (Tarifario de Extranjeria, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): 'ingreso de solicitud de prorroga de visa de turista' USD 25. Governed by the Reglamento de Visas Guatemaltecas. Source: IGM 'Consultas Frecuentes para Tramite de Visas Guatemaltecas'.

GTM.name: Visa por Expediente de Residencia en Tramite (Visa for Pending Residence Application)
GTM.purpose: Allows a foreign national whose Guatemalan residence application is still in process to legally exit and re-enter the country while the residence file is being resolved.
GTM.notes: Issued by the Subdireccion de Extranjeria of the IGM to applicants with a residence file in progress who need to travel abroad and return. Requirements: application form, valid passport, transport ticket, and (for land departures) a written request to the IGM with supporting documentation, plus proof of payment. Official application form: Visa-por-expediente-de-residencia-en-tramite (VET-IGM-01-2022). Fee (Tarifario de Extranjeria, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): 'visa multiple por expediente de residencia en tramite' USD 100. Multiple-entry validity is tied to the pending residence process. Source: IGM 'Consultas Frecuentes para Tramite de Visas Guatemaltecas'.

GTM.name: Visa Consultada por Actividad de Consulta o Asesoria Remunerada (Paid Consulting / Advisory Activity Visa)
GTM.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Guatemala to provide remunerated professional consulting or advisory services requested by a Guatemalan public or private entity.
GTM.notes: Distinct from the (non-remunerated) business/visitor visa: this covers paid consulting or advisory work and additionally requires an original letter of service requirement issued by the requesting Guatemalan public or private institution. Issued within the consular visa framework (Categoria B nationals apply at consulates; Categoria C nationals require prior IGM authorization). Official application form for Categoria C: Visa-de-Actividad-de-Consulta-o-Asesoria-Remunerada (VTV-IGM-01-2024). Fee approximated from the Tarifario de Extranjeria (Acuerdo IGM-029-2023) 'visa simple' USD 25 (plus USD 25 application intake). Governed by the Reglamento de Visas Guatemaltecas (Acuerdo IGM-015-2025). Source: IGM 'Conozca los Tipos de Visa que emite el IGM' (June 2025).

GTM.name: Residencia Temporal para Ministros de Culto o Religiosos (Religious Worker / Minister of Religion Residence)
GTM.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign ministers of religion, clergy, and religious workers affiliated with a religious organization recognized in Guatemala.
GTM.notes: Temporary residence modality for religious ministers under the Reglamento de Residencias Guatemaltecas (Acuerdo IGM-016-2025) and Article 75 of the Codigo de Migracion (Decreto 44-2016). Annual renewal; after 5 years may apply for permanent residency. Fee (Tarifario de Extranjeria, Acuerdo IGM-029-2023): 'residencia temporal para ministros de culto o religiosos' USD 50, plus USD 25 application-intake fee - a reduced rate versus the standard temporary-residence tariff. Source: IGM Tarifario de Extranjeria (igm.gob.gt/tarifario-de-extranjeria).

GTM.name: Solicitud de Reconocimiento del Estatuto de Refugiado (Refugee Status / Asylum)
GTM.purpose: Humanitarian protection for foreign nationals in Guatemala who fear persecution in their country of origin; grants the right to remain while the claim is assessed and, if recognized, refugee status and residence.
GTM.notes: Administered by the IGM Departamento de Reconocimiento del Estatuto de Refugiado under the Codigo de Migracion (Decreto 44-2016) and the 1951 Refugee Convention. Free of charge - the Tarifario de Extranjeria (Acuerdo IGM-029-2023) expressly exempts constancias and certificaciones issued by the refugee-status department from fees. Official guidance: 'Guia para solicitar refugio en Guatemala' (2025), published in the IGM Refugio section (igm.gob.gt/category/atencion-y-proteccion-a-los-migrantes). This is an in-country protection-status application, not a consular visa.

GUY.name: Visitor Visa (Tourist)
GUY.purpose: For tourism, vacation, meetings, workshops, seminars, events, religious functions, site visits, and short-term training.
GUY.notes: Single-entry valid 3 months (EUR 45 at Belgian embassy). Multiple-entry also available (valid 6 months, EUR 75). Embassy in Belgium does not accept electronic visa - physical submission required for that mission. Online pre-approval application available via eservices.iss.gov.gy for applicants in countries without a Guyana embassy. Processing approx. 5 working days at embassy; 10-14 working days via online portal. Guyana does not issue traditional e-visas - online portal issues a pre-approval letter. Fee shown is EUR 45 converted approximately to USD.

GUY.name: Visitor Visa (Multiple Entry)
GUY.purpose: For repeated short-term visits for tourism, vacation, meetings, and similar purposes.
GUY.notes: Multiple-entry, valid 6 months (EUR 75 at Belgian embassy). Same requirements as single-entry visitor visa. Online pre-approval available via eservices.iss.gov.gy for countries without Guyana diplomatic presence.

GUY.name: Transit Visa / Landing Permit
GUY.purpose: For travelers passing through Guyana en route to a third country, or for short transit stays.
GUY.notes: The Embassy of Guyana in Belgium does not issue transit visas - these are issued by Guyana immigration authorities upon arrival. Whether a transit visa or landing permit is granted depends on the length of stay. Requirements: passport valid 6+ months, valid Yellow Fever certificate (if applicable), proof of onward travel, proof of accommodation and funds if staying overnight. Fee not published on official sources.

GUY.name: Business Visa
GUY.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting business activities in Guyana, including meetings, negotiations, and commercial visits.
GUY.notes: Multiple-entry, valid 1 year (EUR 150 at Belgian embassy). Requires letter of support from sponsoring company/organization and invitation letter from host company if applicable. Also requires business registration and tax ID certificate from host entity if applicable. Online pre-approval also available via eservices.iss.gov.gy.

GUY.name: Employment Visa
GUY.purpose: For foreign nationals who have secured employment in Guyana and wish to reside and work in the country.
GUY.notes: Requires a signed contract or letter of employment, police clearance, and medical report. Applications accepted online via eservices.iss.gov.gy. Extensions also available through the same portal. Work permit (landing permit for employment) valid up to 3 years, renewable. Specific fee not published on official government pages.

GUY.name: Student Visa
GUY.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted to an accredited school or educational institution in Guyana.
GUY.notes: Multiple-entry, valid 3 years (EUR 130 at Belgian embassy). Requires Student Acceptance Letter from an accredited institution. Online applications also accepted via eservices.iss.gov.gy. Extensions available through the ISS eServices portal.

GUY.name: Visa on Arrival (Pre-Approval Letter)
GUY.purpose: For nationals of countries that require a visa but have no access to a Guyana embassy or consulate - allows obtaining a pre-approval letter online, which is converted to a visa upon arrival at the airport.
GUY.notes: Applicants must obtain a pre-approval letter through the online portal before travel - travelers cannot board without this letter. Upon arrival at the airport, the visa is affixed to the passport. Processing time is 10-14 working days. Applicants should confirm receipt with the Department of Immigration and Citizenship at (592) 223-5210. Fee not specified on official sources.

GUY.name: Landing Permit for Employment (Work Permit)
GUY.purpose: The work authorization a foreign national needs, in addition to an Employment Visa, to take up employment and reside in Guyana.
GUY.notes: Guyana's employment pathway requires both an Employment Visa and this Landing Permit for Employment (the work permit). Applied for online via the ISS eServices portal (Ministry of Home Affairs) - page verified live 2026-07. The vacancy must be advertised in the newspapers for three consecutive months. Required documents: letter requesting landing permission for employment, employment contract, sponsor/employer business registration, GRA compliance and NIS receipts, police clearance, and a medical report. Work permit reported valid up to 3 years, renewable; specific fee not published on the official portal.

GUY.name: Landing Permit for Business
GUY.purpose: In-country permit authorizing a foreign national to reside in Guyana to establish or operate a business.
GUY.notes: Applied for online via the ISS eServices portal (Ministry of Home Affairs) - page verified live 2026-07. Complements the Business Visa. Required documents: letter requesting landing permit for business, passport bio-data page, business registration/incorporation, GRA tax compliance certificate and NIS receipts, certificate of character, police clearance, and medical report. Fee and validity not published on the official portal.

GUY.name: Landing Permit for Student
GUY.purpose: In-country permit allowing a foreign national admitted to an accredited Guyanese institution to reside in Guyana for the duration of study.
GUY.notes: Applied for online via the ISS eServices portal (Ministry of Home Affairs) - page verified live 2026-07. Complements the Student Visa. Required documents: letter requesting landing permit for student status, passport bio-data page, birth certificate, evidence of financial support for studies, certificate of character, police clearance, and medical report. Fee and validity not published on the official portal.

GUY.name: CARICOM Free Movement Certificate
GUY.purpose: Allows qualified skilled nationals of CARICOM member states to live and work in Guyana without a work permit under the CARICOM Single Market and Economy (CSME) framework.
GUY.notes: Available to CARICOM nationals who qualify as skilled workers: university graduates (bachelor's or equivalent including ACCA), musicians and artistes, sports persons, media workers, registered nurses, trained teachers, artisans with Caribbean Vocational Qualifications, associate degree holders, self-employed and service providers. Fee in Guyana: G$1,500. Processing 3-6 weeks. Participating states: Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, St. Lucia, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago. Bahamas, Montserrat, and Haiti are excluded.

HKG.name: Visitor Visa / Entry Permit
HKG.purpose: Short-term tourism, leisure, or social visits to Hong Kong. Visitors may not work, study, or establish businesses.
HKG.notes: Required for nationalities not on the visa-free list. Can be applied for online, by post, or through Chinese diplomatic missions. Max stay varies by approval. Nationalities on the visa-free list do not need to apply.

HKG.name: Pre-Arrival Registration (PAR) for Indian Nationals
HKG.purpose: Mandatory free online pre-registration allowing Indian ordinary passport holders to visit Hong Kong visa-free for up to 14 days per stay.
HKG.notes: Free, instant approval. Valid 6 months with multiple visits, each stay up to 14 days. Printed notification slip and same passport must be carried. Diplomatic passport holders are exempt from PAR requirement.

HKG.name: Transit Visa
HKG.purpose: Permits passage through Hong Kong for travelers continuing to another destination who require a visa and do not hold a visa-free nationality.
HKG.notes: Must hold onward ticket unless destination is Mainland China or Macau. Cannot work, study or establish businesses. Approval is entirely discretionary. Airside transit (not leaving the airport) for most nationalities does not require a transit visa.

HKG.name: General Employment Policy (GEP) Visa
HKG.purpose: Allows skilled professionals with a confirmed job offer to work in Hong Kong where their skills are not readily available locally.
HKG.notes: Initial stay up to 36 months (or contract duration). Extensions follow a 3-2 year pattern. Requires confirmed job offer, first degree or equivalent, and market-rate compensation. Excludes Afghanistan, Cuba, North Korea, and Mainland Chinese (who use ASMTP). After 7 years continuous residence, eligible for right of abode.

HKG.name: Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (ASMTP)
HKG.purpose: Allows Mainland Chinese skilled professionals to work in Hong Kong where their skills are not readily available locally.
HKG.notes: Mainland Chinese equivalent of GEP. Requires confirmed job offer and relevant qualifications. Extensions follow similar patterns to GEP.

HKG.name: Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS)
HKG.purpose: Attracts high-earning global talent and graduates of top universities to live and work in Hong Kong without requiring a pre-arranged job offer.
HKG.notes: Category A: annual income HK$2.5M+, granted 36 months. Categories B & C: top university graduates, granted 24 months. Category C subject to annual quota. Extensions up to 3 years; top-tier earners (HK$2M+ salaries tax after 2 years) may receive 6-year extension. Excludes Afghanistan, Cuba, North Korea.

HKG.name: Technology Talent Admission Scheme (TechTAS)
HKG.purpose: Fast-track admission for technology talent to work in Hong Kong's innovation and technology sector.
HKG.notes: Streamlined procedures since December 2025. Parallel quota and visa applications now allowed. R&D activity requirement in designated tech areas removed. Aimed at tech companies in designated sectors.

HKG.name: Technical Professionals Stream (GEP(TP) & ASMTP(TP))
HKG.purpose: Admission channel under GEP and ASMTP for skilled tradespeople in eight designated trades, targeting applicants aged 18-40.
HKG.notes: Pilot program launched June 2025. Total quota of 10,000. Entry visas valid 24-36 months depending on qualifications. Targets eight specified skilled trades.

HKG.name: Vocational Professionals Admission Scheme (VPAS)
HKG.purpose: Allows admission of vocational professionals with technical qualifications to work in Hong Kong.
HKG.notes: Targets holders of vocational qualifications. Separate scheme from the professional degree-based GEP.

HKG.name: Foreign Domestic Helper Visa
HKG.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals employed as live-in domestic helpers in Hong Kong households.
HKG.notes: Subject to standard employment contract conditions. Helper must be employed by an approved employer, live in the employer's residence, and leave Hong Kong at contract end. Not a pathway to permanent residence.

HKG.name: Student Visa / Entry Permit
HKG.purpose: Permits non-local students to study at approved educational institutions in Hong Kong for the duration of their program.
HKG.notes: Processing takes approximately 6 weeks. Stay duration matches program length, max 6 years. Undergraduate+ students may take curriculum-related internships, part-time on-campus work (20 hrs/week max), and unrestricted summer employment (Jun 1-Aug 31). Certain nationalities (Afghanistan, Cuba, DPRK, some others) face restrictions. Forms ID 995A and ID 995B required.

HKG.name: Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates (IANG)
HKG.purpose: Allows graduates of Hong Kong's locally-accredited full-time degree programs or GBA campus programs to remain or return to Hong Kong to seek employment.
HKG.notes: Recent graduates (within 6 months): processed in ~2 weeks, no job offer required. Non-recent graduates (after 6 months): ~4 weeks, job offer required. Initial stay 24 months. Extension pattern typically 3-3 years. Top-tier earners (HK$2M+ annually) receive 6-year extension. Quota-free. Recipients can freely change employer.

HKG.name: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES)
HKG.purpose: Allows high-net-worth individuals who invest at least HK$30 million in permissible Hong Kong assets to obtain residency.
HKG.notes: Minimum net assets and investment of HK$30 million (approximately USD 3.8M). Initial permission to stay up to 24 months. Extensions of up to 3 years each. Must maintain portfolio requirements continuously. Applicants must be 18+. Cannot rely on employment or investment returns within HK to support themselves during initial period.

HKG.name: Investment as Entrepreneurs
HKG.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to establish or join a business in Hong Kong that makes a substantial contribution to the local economy.
HKG.notes: No fixed minimum investment threshold; assessed on business plan quality, financial resources, local job creation, and technology/skills contribution. Initial stay up to 36 months. Extensions follow 3-2 year pattern. Local sponsor required. Excludes Mainland Chinese, Afghanistan, Cuba, North Korea.

HKG.name: Quality Migrant Admission Scheme (QMAS)
HKG.purpose: Attracts highly skilled or talented persons to settle in Hong Kong to enhance economic competitiveness; no pre-arranged job required.
HKG.notes: Two routes: General Points Test (initial 36 months) or Achievement-based Points Test (initial 8 years). Applicants must be 18+, financially self-sufficient, clean record, and hold a first degree or equivalent. Extensions require proof of settlement. Top-tier earners (HK$2M+ assessable salaries income) receive 5-year extension. Excludes Afghanistan, Cuba, North Korea.

HKG.name: Working Holiday Scheme
HKG.purpose: Allows young adults from participating countries to take an extended working holiday in Hong Kong, combining travel with temporary employment.
HKG.notes: Eligible countries: Australia, Austria, Canada, France, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Japan, Korea (Republic of), Netherlands, New Zealand, Sweden, United Kingdom. Age limit 18-30. Stay up to 12 months. Maintenance funds required (HK$14,000-HK$25,000 depending on nationality). Annual quotas per country (100-5,000 slots). Employment with same employer limited to 3-12 months depending on nationality. Extensions not normally considered. Irish, Japanese, and Korean citizens receive free visas.

HKG.name: Dependant Visa / Entry Permit
HKG.purpose: Allows spouses, unmarried children under 18, and parents (aged 60+, for permanent residents only) to join approved residents or permanent residents in Hong Kong.
HKG.notes: Extensions for initial applications take 6 weeks; renewals 2-3 weeks. Stay follows sponsor's permission: spouses/children on 3-3 year pattern; parents on 2-2-3 year pattern. Dependants of employed or permanent resident sponsors may work freely; dependants of student sponsors require prior permission to work. Same-sex spouses recognized.

HKG.name: Second Generation of Chinese Hong Kong Permanent Residents Scheme (ASSG)
HKG.purpose: Allows overseas-born children of Hong Kong permanent residents to settle in Hong Kong even without having been born or raised there.
HKG.notes: Targets second generation of Chinese Hong Kong permanent residents who were born and raised overseas. Quota-free scheme.

HKG.name: Training Visa
HKG.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to come to Hong Kong for training purposes with an approved employer for a limited period.
HKG.notes: For structured training programs with a local employer. Not for general study or employment purposes.

HKG.name: Special Scheme to Import Care Workers for Residential Care Homes
HKG.purpose: Allows residential care homes for the elderly or persons with disabilities that have genuine local recruitment difficulties to employ imported care workers.
HKG.notes: Jointly administered by the Immigration Department and Social Welfare Department. e-Visa granted for up to 24 months or the employment contract term, whichever is shorter, under Standard Employment Contract SWD-ICW-16. Workers cannot change employer, post or workplace. Nationals of Afghanistan, Cuba, Laos, DPRK, Nepal and Vietnam are excluded. No right of abode acquired.

HKG.name: Enhanced Supplementary Labour Scheme (ESLS)
HKG.purpose: Allows employers with genuine difficulties recruiting locally to import workers at technician level and below for jobs that cannot be filled by the local workforce.
HKG.notes: Renamed from the Supplementary Labour Scheme effective 4 September 2023; operates under the Employees Retraining Ordinance. e-Visa normally granted for up to 24 months or the contract term, whichever is shorter, under Standard Employment Contract LD 294. Employer must pay a levy to the Employees Retraining Board. Workers cannot change employer, post or workplace, cannot bring dependants, and acquire no right of abode.

HKG.name: Sector-specific Labour Importation Schemes (SLIS)
HKG.purpose: Allows employers in designated sectors (e.g. construction and transport) facing genuine local recruitment difficulties to import labour from outside Hong Kong.
HKG.notes: Sectors administered by designated bureaux/departments and statutory bodies. e-Visa normally granted for up to 24 months or the employment contract term, whichever is shorter. Workers cannot change employer, post or workplace, cannot bring dependants, and acquire no right of abode. Nationals of Afghanistan, Cuba, Laos, DPRK, Nepal and Vietnam are excluded.

HKG.name: Pre-arrival Registration for Taiwan Residents
HKG.purpose: Free online registration allowing eligible Chinese residents of Taiwan to visit Hong Kong as visitors without a separate visa or entry permit.
HKG.notes: Free of charge. Valid for two months and good for two entries, with a stay of up to 30 days as a visitor on each landing. For Chinese residents of Taiwan born in Taiwan or previously admitted as Taiwan residents who do not hold other travel documents. Applicant must hold a Taiwan re-entry travel document valid for at least six months. Those unable to obtain PAR may apply for an entry permit instead.

HKG.name: Immigration Facilitation Scheme for Visitors Participating in Short-term Activities in Designated Sectors (STV Scheme)
HKG.purpose: Lets professionals and talent invited by government-endorsed organisations undertake specified short-term work activities in Hong Kong as visitors without applying for an employment visa.
HKG.notes: Launched 1 June 2024; scope expanded to 17 designated sectors (including healthcare, higher education, arts, sports, innovation and technology, aviation, finance and construction) from 1 November 2025. Eligible visitors may undertake the specified activities for up to 14 consecutive calendar days per period of permitted stay as a visitor, without an employment visa. Participation must be arranged through a government-endorsed organisation.

HND.name: Visa de Turismo / Tourist and Business Visa (Single Entry)
HND.purpose: Issued to foreigners wishing to travel to Honduras for recreational, tourism, business, or family purposes. Covers short-term stays for non-remunerative activities.
HND.notes: Required only for nationalities that do not enjoy a bilateral visa exemption with Honduras. Many nationalities (USA, Canada, EU/Schengen, etc.) do not need a visa for stays up to 90 days under the CA-4 agreement or bilateral exemptions. For those who do require a visa, the single-entry tourist/business visa is valid for 60 days. Payment must be via money order in USD. Cruise ship passengers in Roatán with limited stays are exempt. Canadian passport holders are visa-exempt for stays up to 90 days.

HND.name: Visa de Turismo / Tourist and Business Visa (Multiple Entry)
HND.purpose: Issued to foreigners for recurring tourism, business, or family visits to Honduras over a one-year period.
HND.notes: Multiple-entry version of the tourist/business (consular) visa, valid 360 days (USD $60). Per the official Honduran consulate, the multiple-entry visa can only be obtained after the applicant has previously held a simple (single-entry) visa. Individual stays subject to standard immigration discretion at point of entry. Payment via money order in USD only. Processing may take approximately 4–8 weeks when prior authorization is required.

HND.name: Visa de Turismo y/o Negocios (Business)
HND.purpose: Covers short-term business activities such as meetings, negotiations, conferences, and commercial visits to Honduras without engaging in local employment.
HND.notes: Business visits are covered under the same tourist/business visa category per the Honduras Embassy in Canada. Nationals of countries with visa exemptions (USA, Canada, EU/Schengen, etc.) do not require a visa for business stays up to 90 days. The Canadian government confirms business visits up to 90 days are visa-exempt for Canadian citizens.

HND.name: Visa de Tránsito (Transit Visa)
HND.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals transiting through Honduras en route to a third country.
HND.notes: Transit visa fee is USD $30.00 per the official consular fee schedule (Decree 263-2011 / VUCA Regulation). Required for nationalities that need a visa to enter Honduras and are transiting through Honduran airports or land borders.

HND.name: Residencia por Trabajo (Work Residency)
HND.purpose: Granted to foreign nationals employed in Honduras under a valid employment contract or with an employer commitment letter, allowing them to reside and work legally in the country.
HND.notes: Applicants must present an employment contract or employer commitment letter (notarized if not drafted in Honduras). Required documents include passport valid at least 1 year, 2 passport photos, authenticated birth certificate, criminal background check (with fingerprints), and health certificate. Application fee is USD $150. Per the Colombia embassy page, work visa applications must be processed directly in Honduras through the Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM). All documents require Spanish translation with originals plus two copies.

HND.name: Permiso/Residencia de Estudios (Student Permit)
HND.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to pursue formal education at an accredited institution in Honduras.
HND.notes: Issued as an INM 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia' under the category 'Extranjeros Estudiantes' (foreign students). Required for any foreign national studying at an accredited institution in Honduras. Per the Colombia embassy page, student permit (visa de estudios) applications must be processed directly in Honduras through the Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM). General requirements include a legal representative/power of attorney, migratory-movement certification, criminal-record and medical certificates. Specific fees must be confirmed with INM directly (inm.gob.hn, callcenter@inm.gob.hn).

HND.name: Residencia de Pensionado (Pensioner/Retiree Residency)
HND.purpose: Grants long-term residency to foreign retirees who can demonstrate a permanent pension income from abroad of at least USD $1,500 per month.
HND.notes: Minimum monthly pension income of USD $1,500 (or equivalent in local currency) from abroad, received via a Honduran financial institution. Requires bank reference and pension provider verification (both notarized and authenticated). Application fee is USD $150. After obtaining residency, naturalization may be pursued after continuous qualifying residency. Documents must be submitted with Spanish translations and originals plus two copies.

HND.name: Residencia de Inversionista (Investor Residency)
HND.purpose: Grants long-term residency to foreign nationals who make a qualifying investment of at least USD $50,000 in a lawful economic activity in Honduras.
HND.notes: Minimum investment of USD $50,000 in any lawful economic activity in Honduras (including certificates, securities, or State bonds). Also requires a certificate of deposit of not less than USD $5,000 from the Central Bank of Honduras as guarantee. A technical feasibility study and investment schedule must be submitted. Application processed through a Honduran lawyer registered with the National Bar Association. Covers the principal investor and immediate family. After 3 years of continuous residency, naturalization may be pursued.

HND.name: Residencia Rentista (Rentier/Passive Income Residency)
HND.purpose: Grants long-term residency to foreign nationals who demonstrate stable passive or rental income of at least USD $2,500 per month from domestic or foreign sources.
HND.notes: Minimum passive/rental income of USD $2,500 per month (or equivalent in national currency), received via a Honduran financial institution. Income can originate abroad or within Honduras. Requires notarized income documentation authenticated by a provincial notary chamber. Application fee is USD $150. Documents must be submitted with Spanish translations and originals plus two copies.

HND.name: Residencia por Matrimonio / Vínculo Familiar (Family Reunification Residency)
HND.purpose: Grants residency to foreign nationals who are married to or have close family ties with Honduran citizens or permanent residents.
HND.notes: Category covers spouses and close family relations (matrimonio/vínculo familiar). Per the Colombia embassy page, family relationship visas (vínculo familiar) must be processed directly in Honduras through the INM. Application fee is USD $150. Required documents include authenticated marriage or family relationship certificates, criminal background check, health certificate, and valid passport. All documents require Spanish translation.

HND.name: Visa Diplomática (Diplomatic Visa)
HND.purpose: Issued to diplomatic and consular officials, government representatives, and international organization officials holding valid diplomatic passports, for official missions to Honduras.
HND.notes: Issued free of charge to holders of diplomatic passports on official missions. Covers diplomatic and consular officials and government representatives accredited to Honduras. Members assigned as members of a diplomatic/consular mission must obtain the appropriate diplomatic or consular visa even if their nationality otherwise benefits from a visa exemption.

HND.name: Visa de Cortesía (Courtesy Visa)
HND.purpose: Issued to holders of special or service passports traveling on official missions, including cultural and sports delegations and certain international organization personnel.
HND.notes: Issued free of charge to special/service passport holders on official missions. Also covers official cultural and sports delegations and certain international organization personnel who do not qualify for a full diplomatic visa.

HND.name: Visa Oficial (Official Visa)
HND.purpose: Issued to consular officials, public officials, and international organization representatives holding official passports, UN Laissez-passer, or OAS passports.
HND.notes: Issued free of charge to consular officials and international organization representatives with official documents (official passports, UN Laissez-passer, or OAS passports). Distinct from the diplomatic visa category.

HND.name: Visa Consultada (Consulted Visa – Category C)
HND.purpose: Entry visa for nationals classified as 'consulted' (Category C) who must obtain prior authorization from the Instituto Nacional de Migración (INM) before a Honduran consulate can issue the visa.
HND.notes: Required for nationalities in Honduras's Category C (visa consultada) classification. The INM Secretaría General must first validate the request and issue written authorization; only then may the applicant apply at any Honduran consulate. Fee USD $100 per Article 127 numeral 12 of the Reglamento de la Ley de Migración y Extranjería. Requires a responsible sponsor in Honduras (with power of attorney and letter of responsibility), apostilled/authenticated passport copies, medical certificate and police/criminal-record certificate from the country of origin, and supporting family or employment documents as applicable. Tourist stay up to 90 days, extendable at INM. Distinct from the Category B 'Visa Consular' (single USD $30 / multiple USD $60) which consulates issue without prior INM authorization.

HND.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia – Servicios Religiosos (Religious Worker / Missionary Permit)
HND.purpose: Special stay permit for foreign clergy, missionaries, and religious workers serving with a church or religious organization in Honduras.
HND.notes: Issued by the INM as a 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia' under the category 'Extranjeros en servicios religiosos'. General requirements include a legal representative/power of attorney, migratory-movement certification from INM, criminal-record and medical certificates, and authenticated/apostilled passport copies.
