Requirement checklist published on the INM residencias/permits page.

HND.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia – Empresarios (Entrepreneur / Self-Employed Permit)
HND.purpose: Special stay permit for foreign nationals establishing or operating their own business or enterprise in Honduras (distinct from the USD $50,000 investor residency).
HND.notes: Issued by the INM as a 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia' under the category 'Extranjeros Empresarios'. For foreign business owners/entrepreneurs. General requirements include a legal representative/power of attorney, migratory-movement certification, criminal-record and medical certificates, plus company/business documentation. Requirement checklist published on the INM residencias/permits page.

HND.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia – Ejercicio de una Profesión Universitaria (Independent Professional Permit)
HND.purpose: Special stay permit for foreign nationals authorized to independently practice a university-level profession (e.g., medicine, engineering, law) in Honduras.
HND.notes: Issued by the INM as a 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia' under the category 'Ejercicio de una profesión universitaria'. For foreign professionals practising a regulated university profession. Requires authenticated/apostilled academic titles in addition to the general permit requirements (legal representative, migratory-movement certification, criminal-record and medical certificates). Requirement checklist published on the INM residencias/permits page.

HND.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia – Voluntarios (Volunteer Permit)
HND.purpose: Special stay permit for foreign volunteers serving with NGOs, humanitarian, development, or faith-based organizations in Honduras.
HND.notes: Issued by the INM as a 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia' under the category 'Extranjeros Voluntarios'. A related 'Servicio Social' permit covers foreign nationals performing social service. General requirements include a legal representative/power of attorney, migratory-movement certification, criminal-record and medical certificates. Requirement checklist published on the INM residencias/permits page.

HND.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia – Razones Humanitarias (Humanitarian Stay Permit)
HND.purpose: Special stay permit granted on humanitarian grounds to foreign nationals who do not qualify for another migratory status.
HND.notes: Issued by the INM as a 'Permiso Especial de Permanencia' under the category 'Razones Humanitarias'. Discretionary permit for foreign nationals in humanitarian situations. General requirements include a legal representative/power of attorney, migratory-movement certification, criminal-record and medical certificates. Requirement checklist published on the INM residencias/permits page.

HRV.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to transit through the international transit area of a Croatian airport without entering Croatian territory.
HRV.notes: Schengen Type A visa issued by Croatian diplomatic missions and consular offices since Croatia joined Schengen on 1 January 2023. Required only for nationals of certain countries that do not qualify for visa-free transit.

HRV.name: Short-Stay Schengen Visa (Type C)
HRV.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter and stay in Croatia (and the broader Schengen Area) for purposes including tourism, business visits, family visits, or cultural/sporting events for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
HRV.notes: Schengen uniform Type C visa valid across all Schengen member states. Issued by Croatian diplomatic missions for nationals of Schengen Annex I countries. May be single or multiple entry. Visa fee set by EU Schengen Visa Code (currently EUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for children 6-12). Short-stay extensions possible at police stations for force majeure/serious personal reasons (EUR 30 fee). Cannot exceed 90 days in any 180-day period.

HRV.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D)
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who have been granted a temporary stay or work permit in Croatia to enter the country for stays exceeding 90 days, bridging until the residence permit is issued.
HRV.notes: Croatian national Type D visa issued by Croatian diplomatic missions and consular offices since 1 January 2023. Valid only for Croatia; does not grant access to other Schengen states for more than 90 days. Typically issued to those who have already been granted a residence or work permit in Croatia. Max stay is up to 30 days on the visa itself; the underlying permit governs long-term stay.

HRV.name: Stay and Work Permit (Single Permit)
HRV.purpose: A unified authorisation allowing third-country nationals to temporarily reside and work in Croatia under a specific employer and occupation.
HRV.notes: Single permit combining residence and work authorisation. Application submitted to competent police administration at employer's location. Fee: EUR 74.32 for permit + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 9.29 administrative fee. Labour market test required unless position is on deficit occupations list. Permit holder may work only for the specified employer and occupation. Employer fines EUR 6,630-19,900 per violation.

HRV.name: Work Registration Certificate (Short-Term Work)
HRV.purpose: Short-term authorisation for third-country nationals to work in Croatia for up to 90 days or 30 days per calendar year without a full residence permit.
HRV.notes: Available in two durations: up to 90 days or up to 30 days annually. Fee: EUR 39.82. Applicants must hold valid travel document and employment contract. Does not confer residence rights beyond existing visa/visa-free entitlement.

HRV.name: Seasonal Worker Permit
HRV.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to work in seasonal industries (agriculture, forestry, hospitality, tourism) in Croatia for limited periods each calendar year.
HRV.notes: Two sub-types: up to 90 days annually (no labour market test required) and up to 9 months (requires labour market test unless deficit occupation). Applications submitted via Croatian Employment Service (HZZ) platform. Covers agriculture, forestry, hospitality, and tourism sectors.

HRV.name: EU Blue Card (Highly Qualified Worker Permit)
HRV.purpose: Residence and work permit for highly qualified third-country nationals with higher education qualifications working under a minimum one-year employment contract in Croatia.
HRV.notes: Requires higher education diploma or equivalent, employment contract for minimum 1 year, salary at least 1.5x average gross annual salary in Croatia. Valid for the duration of the employment contract; as of 2025 amendments, can be up to 48 months. No labour market test required. Fee: EUR 74.32 permit + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 9.29 administrative. Path to long-term residence after 5 years (may aggregate time across EU states with minimum 2 years in Croatia). Statutory processing deadline: 60 days.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay for Digital Nomads
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who work remotely via digital technology for a foreign employer or their own foreign-registered company to reside in Croatia for an extended period.
HRV.notes: Available to non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens only. Cannot work for Croatian employers or clients. Initial stay up to 18 months; extendable by 6 months if applied 60 days before expiry. New application possible 6 months after previous stay ends. Income requirement: minimum EUR 3,622.50/month (2.5x average Croatian monthly net salary), or lump sum EUR 43,470 for 12 months / EUR 65,205 for 18 months. Required documents: valid passport, health insurance, employment/business proof, bank statements, criminal record clearance, Croatian address. Fees: EUR 46.45 (temporary stay) + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 9.29 administrative. Visa-required nationals apply via embassy (additional Type D visa EUR 93). Online application available for visa-exempt nationals. Does not count toward permanent residence.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay for Education (Student Permit)
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Croatia for the purpose of secondary school education or university studies.
HRV.notes: Granted for up to 1 year, renewable. Applicants must provide proof of enrolment, valid travel document with 3+ months validity beyond permit expiry, proof of financial self-sufficiency, health insurance, and clean criminal record. Fees: EUR 46.45 (temporary stay approval) + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay for Family Reunification
HRV.purpose: Allows close family members (spouses, common-law partners, minor children, parents of minor Croatian citizens) of Croatian nationals or lawfully residing third-country nationals to join them in Croatia.
HRV.notes: Eligible family members: spouses and common-law partners, minor children (biological, adopted, step), parents of minor Croatian citizens. Family members of seasonal workers generally ineligible. Documents required: marriage/birth/partnership certificates; common-law partnership can be proved by shared child's birth certificate, 3 years cohabitation proof, or witness statements. Family members of Croatian nationals exempt from providing certain documents (obtained ex officio). Fees: EUR 46.45 + EUR 31.85 biometric card + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay for Scientific Research
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country national researchers with a hosting agreement with a Croatian research institution to reside in Croatia to conduct scientific research.
HRV.notes: Requires hosting agreement with a Croatian research institution. Fees: EUR 46.45 + EUR 31.85 biometric card + EUR 9.29 administrative. Renewable annually.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay for Humanitarian Grounds
HRV.purpose: Grants residence to third-country nationals who cannot return to their home country due to health crises, age-related issues, or as victims of domestic violence.
HRV.notes: Covers health crises, age-related inability to leave, and domestic violence victims. Applied for at police administration. Fees: EUR 46.45 + EUR 31.85 biometric card + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HRV.name: Self-Employment Residence and Work Permit (Business Owner)
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who own at least 51% of a Croatian-registered company or trade to reside and conduct business in Croatia.
HRV.notes: Requires minimum 51% ownership stake in a Croatian company or trade. No minimum investment threshold specified in official sources. Exempt from labour market test under Article 110 of the Aliens Act. Renewable annually. After 5 years of uninterrupted lawful residence, may qualify for long-term residence. Fee: EUR 74.32 permit + EUR 31.85 biometric card + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HRV.name: Long-Term Residence Permit (EU)
HRV.purpose: Grants stable, long-term EU residence status to third-country nationals who have legally resided in Croatia for at least 5 uninterrupted years.
HRV.notes: Requires 5 years uninterrupted lawful temporary stay. Absences up to 10 months total over 5 years (single absence max 6 months) permitted. Also requires: valid travel document, financial self-sufficiency, health insurance, knowledge of Croatian language and Latin script. Language exemptions for children under school age, those educated in Croatia, and persons over 65. Fee: EUR 83.62 decision + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 13.94 certified copy.

HRV.name: Permanent Stay Permit
HRV.purpose: Grants permanent residence rights in Croatia to qualifying third-country nationals including family members of Croatian citizens, diaspora members, long-term refugees, and others.
HRV.notes: Eligible categories: (1) family members/life partners of Croatian citizens after 4 years uninterrupted temporary stay; (2) Croatian diaspora members or stateless persons after 3 years; (3) refugees with 10+ years status; (4) minor children of permanent/long-term residents after 3 years; (5) returnees in housing programs; (6) children born in Croatia without regulated status. Requires valid travel document, no security or public health threat. Fee: EUR 83.62 + EUR 31.85 biometric card.

HRV.name: Intra-Corporate Transfer (ICT) Permit
HRV.purpose: Allows a manager, specialist, or trainee employee of a company established outside the EU to be transferred to a Croatian branch, subsidiary, or group company of the same undertaking.
HRV.notes: Croatia's implementation of EU Directive 2014/66/EU on intra-corporate transfers, listed as a distinct 'stay and work permit for intra-corporate transfer' on the official Work of third-country nationals page. Managers and specialists may be transferred for up to 3 years; trainees for up to 1 year. Requires prior employment within the group and an assignment letter/work contract. No labour market test required. Permits intra-EU mobility to group entities in other EU member states. Fee: EUR 74.32 permit + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay and Work of Posted Workers
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals employed by a foreign company to be posted to Croatia to provide a service or perform work under a contract between the foreign employer and a Croatian entity.
HRV.notes: Listed as a distinct work category ('temporary stay as a posted worker') alongside the single permit and EU Blue Card on the official Work of third-country nationals page. For workers posted to Croatia under a cross-border service contract; the foreign employer remains the employer. Duration is tied to the service contract/posting. No labour market test required in defined cases. Governed by the Croatian Aliens Act and EU posted-worker rules.

HRV.name: Working Holiday Visa (Youth Mobility Scheme)
HRV.purpose: Allows young citizens of partner countries (New Zealand, Canada) to travel to Croatia for up to 12 months and take up incidental employment to supplement their travel funds.
HRV.notes: Croatia operates reciprocal youth-mobility/working-holiday schemes with two countries. New Zealand scheme (in force 11 August 2014): citizens aged 18-30, stay up to 12 months, may work but not more than 3 months for a single employer, may enrol in study/training up to 6 months, annual quota approx. 100. Canada Youth Mobility MoU (in force 2010, implemented 2011): citizens aged 18-35, stay up to 12 months, usable up to twice with a pause between stays. Applicants need a valid passport, return ticket or sufficient funds, proof of financial means, and health insurance; consular fee approx. USD 100. Temporary stay decision issued by Croatian police; processing up to 2 months. Not available to third-country nationals without such a bilateral agreement.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay for Life Partnership
HRV.purpose: Allows a life partner or informal life partner of a Croatian citizen or of a third-country national lawfully residing in Croatia to reside in Croatia.
HRV.notes: Distinct temporary stay ground (Croatian: zivotno partnerstvo) separate from family reunification. Croatia recognises same-sex registered life partnerships. Proof of an informal life partnership may include a shared child's birth certificate, evidence of at least 3 years' cohabitation in a shared household, or witness statements. Granted for up to 1 year, renewable. Fees: EUR 46.45 temporary stay + EUR 31.85 biometric card (EUR 59.73 expedited) + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HRV.name: Temporary Stay of Long-Term Residents of Another EEA Member State
HRV.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who hold EU long-term resident (permanent stay) status in another EEA Member State to reside and work in Croatia.
HRV.notes: For third-country nationals granted EU long-term resident status in another EEA Member State under EU Directive 2003/109/EC. They may stay in Croatia up to 3 months without a permit; for stays exceeding 3 months they must apply for temporary stay at a police administration. Once granted, they may work in Croatia without a separate stay and work permit. Family members may also qualify. Renewable; can lead to Croatian long-term residence. Fees: EUR 46.45 temporary stay + EUR 31.85 biometric card + EUR 9.29 administrative.

HTI.name: Tourist Visa
HTI.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting Haiti for tourism or leisure. Most nationalities do not require this visa (default visa-free policy); only nationals of 9 specific countries must apply in advance.
HTI.notes: Only required for nationals of: Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam, and Yemen. All other nationalities enter visa-free and pay a US$10 tourist fee on arrival. Application must be submitted at least 1 month before departure to the Embassy of Haiti in Washington DC. Required documents: completed visa application form, two recent color passport photos, letter explaining purpose/duration of visit (including accommodation details), valid passport (6+ months validity), airline confirmation/round-trip ticket copy, employer letter. Payment by money order, certified check, or cashier's check payable to 'Embassy of Haiti in Washington'. A 6-month multiple-entry tourist visa is available for US$200.

HTI.name: Tourist Visa (Multiple Entry, 6 months)
HTI.purpose: Multiple-entry tourist visa valid for 6 months, for nationals who require a visa to enter Haiti.
HTI.notes: Available to nationals of the 9 countries that require a visa to enter Haiti. Same application process as the single-entry tourist visa. Payment by certified check or cashier's check payable to 'Embassy of Haiti in Washington'.

HTI.name: Diplomatic Visa
HTI.purpose: Issued on diplomatic passports and UN laissez-passer at the request of the institution for which the applicant works.
HTI.notes: Required documents: visa application letter from the relevant institution, valid diplomatic passport, two color passport photos. Issued on diplomatic passports or UN laissez-passer. Fee details not published on official page - contact Embassy of Haiti (+1 202-332-4090).

HTI.name: Official Visa
HTI.purpose: Issued on official passports at the request of the institution for which the applicant works.
HTI.notes: Issued on official passports. Required documents: visa application letter from the relevant institution, valid official passport, two color passport photos. Fee details not published on official page - contact Embassy of Haiti (+1 202-332-4090).

HTI.name: Work Permit (Permis de Travail)
HTI.purpose: Required for any foreign national travelling on a non-Haitian travel document who intends to work in Haiti - including missionaries, teachers, business people, retirees and students who take up employment.
HTI.notes: Issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour (Ministere des Affaires Sociales et du Travail - MAST), Avenue Charles Sumner, Port-au-Prince (tel +509 2519-0042 / +509 2940-0928). Every person travelling on a non-Haitian travel document who intends to work in Haiti must obtain a work permit, independently of the visa-free entry policy. Applied for in person in Haiti; no online application exists. Most nationalities still enter Haiti visa-free and then obtain the work permit plus a residence permit for stays beyond 90 days. Fee not published on an official source.

HTI.name: Residence Permit (Permis de Sejour)
HTI.purpose: Long-stay permit for foreign nationals (non-Haitian citizens) who wish to reside in Haiti beyond the 90-day visa-free entry period.
HTI.notes: Issued by the Direction de l'Immigration et de l'Emigration (DIE), 171 Avenue John Brown, Lalue, Port-au-Prince. Fee is 5,000 gourdes (approx. US$38) payable by cheque to the public treasury. Required documents include a passport bio-page copy, an employer/sponsor letter guaranteeing support and repatriation, a medical certificate issued within 30 days, two colour photos, a copy of the entry card from last arrival, a birth certificate (French translation), a Haitian bank attestation (minimum 7,500 gourdes / US$200), and a police record from the country of origin. Applied for in person; a written request explaining the reasons for the stay and an interview are required. No online application.

HUN.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
HUN.purpose: Permits short-term tourism, family visits, or business activity in Hungary and the Schengen Area for nationals not eligible for visa-free entry.
HUN.notes: Hungary is a Schengen member. Type C visas are issued by Hungarian consulates abroad. Allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the entire Schengen Area. Visa-free nationals do not need this visa. Fee: EUR 90 for adults (EUR 45 for children 6-12; under 6 free), per the official MFA consular page. Decision normally within 15 calendar days, extendable up to 45. Applied for at the Hungarian embassy/consulate in the applicant's country of residence.

HUN.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
HUN.purpose: Covers short-term business activities in Hungary such as meetings, negotiations, and conferences for nationals of countries not on the Schengen visa-free list.
HUN.notes: Business is a permitted purpose under the Schengen short-stay visa. Fee: EUR 90 for adults, per the official MFA consular page; decision normally within 15 calendar days (extendable up to 45). For longer-term employment or self-employment a national long-stay (Type D) visa is required. Applied for at the Hungarian embassy/consulate.

HUN.name: Airport Transit Visa (ATV)
HUN.purpose: Permits transit through the international zone of a Hungarian airport without entering the Schengen Area, required for certain nationalities.
HUN.notes: Required only for nationals of countries listed on the EU airport transit visa list. Fee: EUR 90 (standard Schengen visa fee). Does not permit entry into Hungary or other Schengen states. Applied for at the Hungarian consulate.

HUN.name: EU Blue Card (Kék Kártya)
HUN.purpose: Residence permit for highly qualified third-country nationals employed in Hungary in a job requiring tertiary education or equivalent professional experience.
HUN.notes: Valid up to 4 years, renewable. Minimum salary threshold: HUF 1,001,048/month (2026). Healthcare roles: HUF 800,838/month (2026). Employment restricted to sponsoring employer during first year. Must be applied for via Enter Hungary platform or Hungarian consulate. Grants access to EU-wide long-term mobility after 18 months.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Intra-Corporate Transfer
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals employed by a multinational group to be temporarily posted to a Hungarian entity within the same group for employment or training.
HUN.notes: Executive/specialist permits valid up to 3 years. Trainee permits valid up to 1 year. Requires proof of at least 3 months continuous employment at the sending company. Not available to private entrepreneurs, agency workers, full-time students, or researchers. Long-term mobility (for ICT permit holders from other EU states) must be applied for 20 days before posting starts.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Posted Work
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals holding an EU employment residence permit to work in Hungary on a temporary posting from their EU-based employer.
HUN.notes: Valid for up to 2 years, aligned with posting duration. Requires a valid EU employment residence permit from another Member State. Cannot exceed the original EU permit's validity. Does not lead to permanent residence. Extendable via Enter Hungary platform only.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Seasonal Employment
HUN.purpose: Covers third-country nationals employed in plant production, forest management, animal breeding, or fishery sectors in Hungary on a seasonal basis.
HUN.notes: Initial permit up to 6 months; extendable for up to 6 months within a 12-month period. Expedited 15-day processing for applicants with prior lawful stay in Hungary within last 5 years. Workers may only work for the designated employer listed on the permit. Employment termination invalidates permit after 6 days notice.

HUN.name: Hungarian Card (Magyar Kártya)
HUN.purpose: Work and residence permit for third-country nationals employed by a Hungarian employer, covering general employment not requiring the EU Blue Card level of qualification.
HUN.notes: Standard employment-based residence permit; distinct from the EU Blue Card. Valid up to 3 years, extendable for a further 3 years. Covers employees, business owners performing actual work, professional athletes/coaches, performers, and film-industry workers. Standard examination 21 days; final decision within 70 days. Applied for via the Enter Hungary platform or a Hungarian consulate.

HUN.name: White Card - Residency for Digital Nomads
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals working remotely for a foreign employer or managing their own foreign company to reside in Hungary for up to 2 years.
HUN.notes: Initial validity up to 1 year, extendable once for another year (maximum 2 years total). Requires minimum net monthly income of EUR 3,000 for at least 6 months prior to application. Applicant must not work for any Hungarian employer or hold shares in Hungarian companies. Family reunification not permitted (except children born during the permit's validity). Cannot transition to other permit types or obtain permanent residence. Must be applied for via Enter Hungary platform or at the NDGAP directorate.

HUN.name: Guest Investor Visa
HUN.purpose: Entry visa for third-country nationals committing to a qualifying investment in Hungary before applying for the Guest Investor Residence Permit.
HUN.notes: Valid up to 6 months; becomes void upon issuance of Guest Investor Residence Permit. Two qualifying investment routes: (1) EUR 250,000 minimum in Hungarian National Bank-registered real estate investment fund shares (5-year holding required); (2) EUR 1,000,000 donation to a public higher education institution. Applied for at a Hungarian consulate in the applicant's country of residence, nationality, or legal stay. Residence permit application must be filed within 30 days of first entry into Hungary.

HUN.name: Guest Investor Residence Permit
HUN.purpose: Long-term residence permit for third-country nationals who make a qualifying investment of national economic interest in Hungary.
HUN.notes: Valid up to 10 years, renewable for additional 10-year periods indefinitely. Two investment routes: EUR 250,000 in real estate fund shares (5-year hold), or EUR 1,000,000 educational/cultural donation to a public higher education institution. Work permitted without restrictions including employment, self-employment, and chief executive roles. Guest investors cannot obtain a National Residence Card (permanent residence). Not a citizenship pathway. Processing time: 21 days. Applied for via Enter Hungary platform or regional NDGAP directorate.

HUN.name: Guest Self-Employment Residence Permit
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to pursue self-employed activities or act as chief executive of a business organization registered in Hungary.
HUN.notes: Initial permit up to 1 year, extendable up to 3 years total. Self-employed must demonstrate annual income exceeding 24 times the minimum wage (via tax authority certification). Business executives: organization must employ at least 5 Hungarian/EEA nationals full-time for 6 consecutive months, or demonstrate sufficient income. Family reunification restricted for the first year after issuance. Cannot obtain National Residence Card (permanent residence). Cannot hold Hungarian Card or EU Blue Card simultaneously.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Traineeship
HUN.purpose: Permits third-country nationals who recently obtained a higher education degree or are currently studying to undertake a traineeship with a Hungarian host organization.
HUN.notes: Valid for up to 6 months; not renewable. Applicant must have obtained a higher education degree within 2 years prior, or be currently pursuing relevant studies. Requires a traineeship contract with an approved Hungarian host organization, language proficiency documentation, proof of financial resources, and health insurance. Host organization must commit to covering expulsion costs if needed.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Seeking a Job or Starting a Business
HUN.purpose: Grants third-country nationals who held a research or study permit additional time to find employment or set up a business in Hungary.
HUN.notes: Valid for maximum 9 months; not extendable. Only available to those transitioning from a research or study residence permit. Must apply via Enter Hungary platform at least 15 days before current permit expires. Holders may subsequently apply for a Hungarian Card, EU Blue Card, or Guest Self-Employment Residence Permit. Must register with employment services or provide employer certification of job commencement within 3 months.

HUN.name: Researcher Residence Permit
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country national researchers to reside in Hungary while conducting research under a hosting agreement with an accredited Hungarian research organization.
HUN.notes: Valid 1–2 years depending on hosting agreement duration. Long-term mobility permit for researchers from other EU Member States valid up to 365 days. Host organizations can submit applications on behalf of researchers via Enter Hungary. Family members of researchers may apply for their own permits. Initial examination within 15 days; final decision within 60 days.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Family Reunification
HUN.purpose: Allows family members of Hungarian citizens, residence permit holders, refugees, or qualifying EEA nationals to reside in Hungary.
HUN.notes: Valid up to 3 years (extendable); 4 years if sponsor holds EU Blue Card or Corporate Card; 5 years if sponsor is Hungarian citizen with permanent residence; 10 years if sponsor is guest investor. Eligible family members: spouses, minor children (including adopted/foster), and dependent minors with parental custody. Processing time: 21 days standard, 70 days when combined with employment. Cannot exceed the validity of the applicant's travel document or sponsor's permit.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Medical Treatment
HUN.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to reside in Hungary to receive medical treatment at a Hungarian medical facility, or to accompany a family member receiving treatment.
HUN.notes: Valid up to 2 years; potentially extended for an additional 2 years based on treatment duration. Requires formal statement from the host medical facility. Processing time: 21 days standard, 8 days for minor applicants. Must enter Hungary within 3 months of approval or permit becomes invalid. Cannot apply for other permit types while holding this permit; does not lead to permanent residence. Family members cannot use family reunification provisions.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Voluntary Activities
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Hungary to perform public interest voluntary activities under contract with an approved host organization or participate in European Voluntary Service.
HUN.notes: Valid for the duration of the hosting contract, capped at 2 years. Not available to those with refugee status, subsidiary protection, tolerated status, or EU residence permits. Family members cannot obtain permits through family reunification. Does not lead to permanent residence eligibility. Cannot apply for other permit types while holding or after holding this permit.

HUN.name: National Residence Card
HUN.purpose: Permanent residence card for third-country nationals who have legally and continuously resided in Hungary for at least 3 years, granting the right to stay indefinitely.
HUN.notes: Card valid up to 10 years, renewable for additional 10-year periods. Eligibility: 3 years continuous lawful residence, OR spouse of Hungarian citizen (married 2+ years), OR previously held Hungarian citizenship, OR minor children of long-term residents/recognized refugees, OR dependent ancestors residing with sponsor for 1+ years. Not available to those holding temporary work or study permits or to guest investors. Processing time 70 days standard; 5 days for children born in Hungary to eligible parents. Applications submitted via Enter Hungary platform only.

HUN.name: EU Long-Term Residence Card (EU Residence Card)
HUN.purpose: EU-standard permanent residence status for third-country nationals who have resided legally in Hungary for at least 5 years, conferring rights comparable to EU citizens within Hungary.
HUN.notes: Card valid up to 10 years, renewable. Requires 5 years continuous lawful residence, or 2 years in Hungary plus 5 years total holding EU Blue Card, research, or study permits across EU Member States. Not available to students, seasonal workers, those under diplomatic immunity, asylum applicants, refugees, or those with tolerated status. Requires Hungarian cultural knowledge exam certificate. Applications via Enter Hungary platform only. Administrative fee: confirmed applicable, amount not extracted.

HUN.name: Permanent Residence Card (EEA Nationals)
HUN.purpose: Grants EEA nationals the right to permanent residence in Hungary after 5 years of continuous legal residence.
HUN.notes: Available to EEA nationals who have resided continuously and legally in Hungary for 5 years, with accelerated pathways for workers reaching retirement age (3+ years residence), those forced to stop work due to illness (2+ years residence), accident-related incapacity, or workers commuting to another EEA state. Administrative fee: HUF 1,500 (paid electronically). Processing time: 70 days. Card remains valid indefinitely when paired with a valid travel/ID document. Application requires both in-person and electronic submission.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for the Purpose of Studies (Student/Pupil)
HUN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Hungary to pursue full-time studies at an accredited Hungarian higher education institution, public education institution, or preparatory course.
HUN.notes: Issued for the duration of studies: minimum 1 year (or shorter if the training lasts under 1 year), maximum 3 years; extendable for a further 1-3 years. First entry uses a single-entry Type D visa (valid 3 months, up to 30-day stay) to collect the permit. Students may undertake limited employment. Initial assessment 15 days; final decision within 60 days. Applied for via the Enter Hungary platform or a Hungarian consulate.

HUN.name: Working Holiday Residence Permit
HUN.purpose: Allows young nationals of partner countries with a working holiday agreement with Hungary to stay primarily for tourism while working temporarily to help fund their trip.
HUN.notes: Available only to nationals of the 10 partner countries with bilateral working holiday agreements: Australia (annual quota 500), Argentina (200), Chile (200), Hong Kong (200), Japan (200), South Korea (100), Ecuador (100), Colombia (100), Taiwan (100), and New Zealand (100). The number of permits issued per year cannot exceed the treaty quota; once exhausted, further applications are rejected. Exact age limits and stay duration are set by each individual bilateral agreement (typically for young adults, up to about 1 year).

HUN.name: National Card (Nemzeti Kártya)
HUN.purpose: Preferential work-and-residence permit for citizens of Serbia and Ukraine (and other nationals designated by government decree) employed by, or running a business in, Hungary.
HUN.notes: Introduced in 2024 for Serbian and Ukrainian citizens; scope later extended by government decree to certain additional third-country nationals. Valid up to 2 years, extendable for the same purpose up to 3 years at a time. Covers employees (including temporary-agency workers) and owners/chief executives performing actual work; permits family reunification. Standard examination 21 days; final decision within 70 days. Applied for via the Enter Hungary platform or a regional directorate; approval authorises a single-entry D visa to enter and collect the card.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Official Purposes
HUN.purpose: For third-country nationals residing in Hungary for official functions: diplomats and their family members, members of official state delegations, foreign press correspondents, and participants or staff of international educational, scientific, or cultural programs.
HUN.notes: Valid up to 3 years, extendable for a further period not exceeding 3 years. Covers persons enjoying diplomatic or other privileges/immunities under international law and their family members, official delegation members, accredited press correspondents, and participants in international educational/scientific/cultural cooperation. Standard processing 21 days. Applied for via the Enter Hungary platform or a Hungarian consulate.

HUN.name: Residence Permit for Reasons of Hungarian National Interest
HUN.purpose: Discretionary residence permit granted by the minister responsible for immigration when a third-country national's stay serves Hungary's economic, national-policy, scientific, cultural, or sporting interests.
HUN.notes: Discretionary permit with no fixed nationality list. Valid up to 3 years, renewable for additional 3-year periods. Applicant must generally perform actual work in Hungary or demonstrate an economic, national-policy, scientific, cultural, or sporting interest to Hungary. Standard processing 21 days. Extension requires having resided in Hungary at least 90 days in any 180-day period. Applied for via the Enter Hungary platform (for visa-free nationals already in Hungary) or a Hungarian consulate.

IDN.name: Visa on Arrival (e-VOA, Index B1)
IDN.purpose: Tourism, business meetings, or transit for eligible nationalities
IDN.notes: Available to nationals of ~97 eligible countries. IDR 500,000 (approx. USD 35). Single-entry, 30-day stay, extendable once for 30 more days at an immigration office. Can be paid on arrival at designated airports/seaports or online in advance as e-VOA. Index B1 (arrival visa); the legacy 'B211A' label actually referred to the old single-entry visit visa, now index C1.

IDN.name: Tourist Visit Visa (C1, single entry)
IDN.purpose: Tourism, family visits, attending meetings/conventions/exhibitions, transit
IDN.notes: Single-entry e-Visa applied in advance (successor to the legacy B211A tourist visa). 60-day initial stay, extendable up to a total of 180 days in-country. Official fee USD 65 at Indonesian missions (approx. IDR 1,500,000 via the e-Visa portal). Requires an Indonesian guarantor (penjamin). Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index C1.

IDN.name: Tourism Multiple-Entry Visit Visa (D1)
IDN.purpose: Frequent tourism/family visits over 1, 2 or 5 years
IDN.notes: Multiple-entry visit visa for tourism; issued with 1-, 2- or 5-year validity. Each entry allows a 60-day stay (extendable). Government fee approx. IDR 3,000,000 per year of validity (~USD 190 for 1 year). Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index D1.

IDN.name: Social/Cultural Visit Visa (C6, single entry)
IDN.purpose: Social, cultural, humanitarian, volunteer activities and family visits
IDN.notes: Single-entry visit visa for social/cultural and family-visit purposes; requires an Indonesian guarantor (penjamin). 60-day initial stay, extendable up to a total of 180 days in-country. Replaces the legacy 'B211/Sosial Budaya' index under the 2024-2025 visa reform. Short study/language courses now use index C9. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index C6.

IDN.name: Business Visit Visa (C2, single entry)
IDN.purpose: Business meetings, negotiations, purchasing goods; non-work business activities
IDN.notes: Single-entry business visit visa; no employment or paid work permitted. 60-day stay, extendable up to 180 days total. Official fee USD 125 at Indonesian missions. Requires an Indonesian company/individual guarantor. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index C2.

IDN.name: Business Multiple-Entry Visit Visa (D2)
IDN.purpose: Recurring business trips - meetings, negotiations, site/production inspections
IDN.notes: Multiple-entry business visit visa issued with 1-, 2- or 5-year validity; each entry allows a 60-day stay, extendable up to two times (up to 180 days per visit). No paid employment. Government fee approx. IDR 3,000,000 per year of validity (~USD 190 for 1 year). Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index D2.

IDN.name: Medical Treatment Visit Visa (C3, single entry)
IDN.notes: Single-entry visit visa for medical treatment. 60-day stay, extendable. Official fee USD 65 at Indonesian missions. A longer-stay medical option exists as limited-stay index E34. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index C3.

IDN.name: Student / Education Visa (E30)
IDN.purpose: Foreign students enrolled in Indonesian schools and universities
IDN.notes: Limited-stay permit (KITAS) for study. Sub-codes: E30A primary/secondary school, E30B higher education, E30F student exchange. Requires sponsorship by the accredited Indonesian educational institution; stay/validity tied to the study programme duration, renewable. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index E30.

IDN.name: Work Visa / KITAS (E23)
IDN.purpose: Foreign nationals employed by an Indonesian entity
IDN.notes: Limited-stay work permit (KITAS), index E23 (formerly TA-01/312). Employer must obtain an approved RPTKA (foreign worker utilisation plan) and NOTIFIKASI from the Ministry of Manpower (Kemnaker, tka-online.kemnaker.go.id) and pay the USD 100/month DKPTKA expatriate levy. Valid up to 2 years, renewable; holder may sponsor spouse/children (E31). Sub-codes cover special economic zones (E23A), trade offices (E23V), government experts (E23X) and digital-sector experts (E23Y). Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

IDN.name: Remote Worker Visa (E33G, Digital Nomad)
IDN.purpose: Foreign remote workers employed/contracted by companies outside Indonesia
IDN.notes: Limited-stay permit (KITAS) for remote workers employed/contracted by an overseas company, launched April 2024. 1-year stay, renewable once. Requirements: minimum annual income of USD 60,000 and savings of at least USD 2,000; holder may not work for or earn income from an Indonesian entity. Multiple entry; must enter within 90 days of issuance. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index E33G (distinct from the E33 Second Home Golden Visa).

IDN.name: Investor KITAS / Golden Visa (E28)
IDN.purpose: Foreign investors, shareholders and directors of Indonesian companies
IDN.notes: Limited-stay investor permit. The standard investor KITAS (E28A) is typically 2 years, renewable, for shareholders/directors of a PT PMA. The Golden Visa sub-codes grant longer stays: E28C (capital-market route) gives 5 years for USD 350,000 or 10 years for USD 700,000 invested in government bonds/IDX shares/mutual funds; corporate and IKN routes (E28B/E28D/E28F) require larger investments. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index E28.

IDN.name: Second Home Golden Visa (E33)
IDN.purpose: High-net-worth individuals settling long-term without local employment
IDN.notes: Second Home limited-stay permit (KITAS), 5- or 10-year validity. Requires proof of funds of at least IDR 2 billion (approx. USD 130,000) held in a state-owned Indonesian bank, or ownership of qualifying Indonesian property. No local employment permitted. Part of the E33 Golden Visa family (which also covers global-talent E33A/E33B and the Silver Hair retirement codes E33E/E33F). Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index E33.

IDN.name: Retirement / Silver Hair Visa (E33E / E33F)
IDN.notes: Under the 2024-2025 reform the retirement route sits within the E33 Second Home family: E33F is the 1-year elderly stay permit and E33E is the 5-year 'Silver Hair' Golden Visa for wealthy retirees (requires a substantial deposit/funds in an Indonesian state bank). Renewable and convertible toward KITAP (permanent residence). No local work authorization. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Replaces the legacy retirement KITAS (min ~USD 1,500/month pension, age 55+).

IDN.name: Family / Spouse Visa (E31)
IDN.purpose: Spouses and children joining an Indonesian citizen or a KITAS/KITAP holder
IDN.notes: Family-reunification limited-stay permit (KITAS). Sub-codes include E31A spouse of an Indonesian citizen, E31B spouse of a KITAS/KITAP holder, E31C-F children, and E31G/E31H parents. Requires a sponsor (Indonesian spouse/relative or the primary permit holder). Typically 1-2 years, renewable, convertible toward KITAP. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index E31.

IDN.name: Work and Holiday Visa (E35A, Australian nationals)
IDN.purpose: Young Australians combining a holiday with short-term work
IDN.notes: Bilateral Work and Holiday scheme; E35A is the operative sub-code for Australian citizens aged 18-30. 12-month multiple-entry stay; must enter within 90 days of issuance. Requires ~USD 2,000 savings, proof of tertiary study/degree, and a government letter of support (subject to annual quota). Work limited to 3 months per employer. Applied online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Index E35/E35A.

IND.name: e-Tourist Visa (eTV)
IND.purpose: Tourism, short-term recreation, casual visit to meet friends/family
IND.notes: Available to nationals of 156+ countries. Fee varies by nationality (USD 10, USD 25, or USD 80). Double-entry within 1-year validity. 30-day max stay per entry. 30-day eTV also available. Cannot be extended or converted in India. Only for approved airports and seaports.

IND.name: Paper Tourist Visa (Type T)
IND.purpose: Tourism, family/friend visits, yoga, short courses
IND.notes: Issued by Indian embassies/high commissions/consulates for stays up to 6 months. Multiple-entry 6-month visa most common. Longer durations (1/5/10 years) available for select nationalities. Requires in-person appointment or drop-off at VFS/BLS center.

IND.name: e-Business Visa
IND.purpose: Business meetings, trade fairs, establishing industrial/business ventures, purchase/sale of goods
IND.notes: Available for eligible nationalities. Multiple-entry, up to 180 days per visit within 1-year validity. For business activities only; paid employment in India is not permitted.

IND.name: e-Medical Visa
IND.purpose: Medical treatment at recognized Indian hospitals
IND.notes: Triple-entry visa valid 60 days from date of arrival. Requires letter from a recognized Indian hospital confirming treatment. Up to 2 attendants may apply for e-Medical Attendant Visa simultaneously. Available to nationals of eligible countries.

IND.name: Student Visa (Type S)
IND.purpose: Full-time study at Indian educational institutions
IND.notes: Duration of course + 1 month typically. Issued for the period of the course. Requires bonafide admission letter from a recognized Indian institution. Applied at Indian embassy/consulate or VFS/BLS center.

IND.name: Employment Visa (Type E)
IND.notes: Issued for the term of the employment contract (max 5 years). Requires employer invitation/appointment letter. Salary must meet minimum threshold (generally USD 25,000/year). Applicant must not be taking up a job that can be filled by an Indian national. Applied at Indian embassy/consulate.

IND.name: Conference Visa (B-5 / e-Conference)
IND.purpose: Attending international conferences, seminars or workshops organised by Indian government bodies or accredited organisations
IND.notes: Bureau of Immigration business sub-category B-5. Issued as an e-Conference Visa (single entry, valid 30 days from arrival) or as a regular B-5 Conference Visa at Indian missions. Requires an invitation from the event organiser plus political clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs and event clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs. Fee is nationality-specific.

IND.name: Transit Visa (TR)
IND.purpose: Travelling through India in direct transit to a destination outside India
IND.notes: Granted solely to transit India to an onward destination. Ordinarily valid for a single journey with entry within 15 days of issue; stay must not exceed 3 days per visit, and validity cannot exceed that of the visa for the country of ultimate destination. Not required for direct air transit if the traveller stays within the airport precincts for up to 24 hours. Fee is nationality-specific (reciprocity based).

IND.name: Research Visa (S-4)
IND.purpose: Research scholars, visiting research faculty, and members of scientific, anthropological or botanical expeditions
IND.notes: Bureau of Immigration Student Visa sub-category S-4, for research scholars, visiting research faculty, research on bilateral exchange programmes, members of scientific/anthropological/botanical expeditions and the G-20 Talent Visa. Requires clearance from the concerned Indian ministry/department and institutional affiliation. Applied at an Indian mission; fee is nationality-specific and processing can be long due to prior clearance requirements.

IND.name: Intern Visa (S-5)
IND.purpose: Foreign nationals undertaking an internship with an Indian company, firm, educational institution or NGO
IND.notes: Listed by the Bureau of Immigration under the Student Visa main category as sub-category S-5, for interns with companies, firms, educational institutions or NGOs. Granted for the duration of the internship or one year, whichever is earlier, and the internship must commence within a stipulated period after completion of the qualifying course. Applied at an Indian mission; fee is nationality-specific.

IND.name: e-Medical Attendant Visa (M-2)
IND.purpose: Family members or attendants accompanying a patient travelling to India for medical treatment
IND.notes: Companion visa to the (e-)Medical Visa; a maximum of two attendants per patient may hold it, and it is co-terminus with the same patient's medical visa. Triple entry, valid 60 days from arrival on the e-Visa route. Also issued as a regular M-2 attendant visa (M-4 for Ayush treatment) at Indian missions. Fee is nationality-specific.

IND.name: Entry Visa (X / X-1)
IND.purpose: Persons of Indian origin and foreign spouses/children of Indian citizens, PIO or OCI cardholders
IND.notes: Bureau of Immigration Miscellaneous Visa (X) main category, sub-category X-1: for persons of Indian origin and the foreign spouse and foreign children of an Indian citizen/PIO/OCI cardholder who are not themselves registered as OCI. Commonly granted multiple-entry for up to five years and extendable in India through the FRRO. Applied at an Indian mission; fee is nationality-specific.

IND.name: Family Visa (F)
IND.purpose: Dependents (spouse and children) of foreign nationals holding a long-term Indian visa
IND.notes: Bureau of Immigration Family Visa (F) main category, for dependents of foreign nationals holding a long-term Indian visa (Employment, Business, Student, etc.), other than dependents of Diplomatic/Official visa holders. Co-terminus with the principal visa holder's visa. Applied at an Indian mission; fee is nationality-specific.

IND.name: Film Visa (B-6)
IND.purpose: Foreign nationals shooting feature films, reality TV or web shows/series, or doing location recce in India
IND.notes: Bureau of Immigration business sub-category B-6, for the shooting of feature films, reality TV and web shows/series and for location recce. Requires prior clearance from the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting and the Ministry of External Affairs. Valid up to one year, multiple entry. Fee is nationality-specific.

IND.name: Production Investment Business Visa (B-4)
IND.purpose: Foreign nationals making production-related investments in India
IND.notes: Bureau of Immigration business sub-category B-4 (Production Investment Business Visa), granted only on the e-Visa platform. Distinct from the Permanent Residency Status (PRS) scheme for large FDI investors, which is tracked separately under the RBI programmes. Fee is nationality-specific.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Visit/Tourist Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals wishing to visit Ireland for tourism, sightseeing, or general visiting purposes for up to 90 days.
IRL.notes: Single entry fee is approximately €60 (~$65 USD); multiple entry fee is approximately €100 (~$108 USD). Applied for online via AVATS system. Valid for countries whose nationals require a visa per the official ISD list. Processing times vary by location and period. A multiple-entry C visa may be granted to frequent travellers.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Visit Family/Friend Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals visiting family members or friends residing lawfully in Ireland for up to 90 days.
IRL.notes: Sub-category of the short-stay C visit visa. Applicant must demonstrate genuine family or friendship ties. Host in Ireland must provide an invitation letter and proof of lawful residence.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Business Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals attending business meetings, conferences, or commercial activities in Ireland for up to 90 days without taking up employment.
IRL.notes: Covers short-term business activities only - no remuneration from an Irish source permitted. Separate from the employment visa. Conference/event visas and training visas are related sub-categories.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Conference/Event Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals attending a specific conference, seminar, exhibition, or event in Ireland for less than 90 days.
IRL.notes: Must provide conference/event invitation, registration, and itinerary. No remuneration from an Irish source permitted.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Training Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals coming to Ireland for a short training programme (under 90 days) with an Irish employer or organisation.
IRL.notes: Training must be short-term and not constitute employment in Ireland. Training letter from the host organisation required.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Performance/Tournament Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals coming to Ireland to participate in a sporting event, musical performance, or similar tournament for less than 90 days.
IRL.notes: Covers sportspeople and performers visiting for a specific event. Evidence of the event or tournament invitation required.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Join Ship Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required non-EEA seafarers joining a ship docked in an Irish port for less than 90 days.
IRL.notes: Applicant must have evidence of employment on the vessel and the vessel's docking details.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Exam Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals coming to Ireland solely to sit a specific professional or academic examination.
IRL.notes: Applicant must provide confirmation of examination registration, date, and location in Ireland.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Medical Treatment Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals seeking medical treatment at an Irish hospital or medical facility for a period of up to 90 days.
IRL.notes: Must provide a letter from an Irish medical professional confirming treatment, estimated duration, and costs. Proof of sufficient funds to cover treatment and repatriation required.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Marriage Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals coming to Ireland to marry or enter a civil partnership, for a stay of up to 90 days.
IRL.notes: Applicant must provide evidence of the planned marriage/civil partnership in Ireland including civil notification to the Registrar. Note: UK BIVS visa does NOT cover visitor in transit or visitor for marriage/civil partnership.

IRL.name: Short Stay 'C' Study Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals enrolling in a short course of study in Ireland lasting less than 90 days.
IRL.notes: For short courses only (under 90 days). Applicants must provide a letter of acceptance from a recognised Irish educational institution.

IRL.name: Long Stay 'D' Study Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals intending to study full-time at a recognised Irish educational institution for more than 90 days.
IRL.notes: Long-stay D visa fee is approximately €100 (~$108 USD). The D visa is a national long-stay visa valid for the duration of studies. After arrival, student must register with Immigration Service Delivery to obtain an Irish Residence Permit (Stamp 2). Must be enrolled in an approved full-time course. English language requirements and financial sufficiency proofs required.

IRL.name: Long Stay 'D' Employment Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals who have been granted an Irish employment permit and need entry authorisation to take up employment in Ireland.
IRL.notes: Applicant must first obtain an employment permit from the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment (enterprise.gov.ie). The D employment visa is required only by visa-required nationals; non-visa-required nationals with an employment permit can enter directly. After entry, holder must register for an Irish Residence Permit (IRP).

IRL.name: Long Stay 'D' Join Family Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals seeking to join a family member who is an Irish citizen or has long-term immigration permission in Ireland.
IRL.notes: Covers joining an Irish national or a non-EEA national with long-term permission. Applicant must demonstrate genuine family relationship. Processing can take several months. After arrival must register for an IRP (Stamp 3 or Stamp 4 depending on circumstances). Joining EU/EEA/Swiss nationals is handled under EU Treaty Rights pathway.

IRL.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For highly skilled non-EEA workers in occupations on the Critical Skills Occupations List or earning above €68,911 annually, allowing them to work in Ireland for up to 2 years initially.
IRL.notes: Fee is €1,000 (~$1,080 USD); 90% refunded if unsuccessful. No Labour Market Needs Test required. Minimum annual salary €40,904 (or €36,848 for recent graduates), or any occupation at €68,911+. Job offer must be for minimum 2 years. After permit expires, holder may apply directly for Stamp 4 (permission to work without permit). Pathway to citizenship after 5 years residence. Governed by Employment Permits Act 2024.

IRL.name: General Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA workers in occupations not on the excluded list, subject to a Labour Market Needs Test showing no suitable EEA workers were available.
IRL.notes: Fee: €500 for ≤6 months, €1,000 for 6–24 months; renewal €750/€1,500. 90% refund if unsuccessful. Minimum salary €36,605/year (lower for healthcare roles at €32,691). Labour Market Needs Test required for most occupations (EURES ad for at least 28 days). Initial permit up to 24 months; renewable for further 3 years. 50:50 rule requires 50% of employer workforce to be EEA nationals (exceptions for startups).

IRL.name: Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For senior management, key personnel, or trainees transferring from a foreign branch to an Irish branch of a multinational company.
IRL.notes: Fee: €500 (≤6 months) or €1,000 (6–24 months); renewal €500–€1,500. Senior/key personnel minimum salary €49,523; trainees minimum €36,605. Prior employment with foreign employer: 6 months for senior/key, 1 month for trainees. Maximum 5 years total stay. Does not accrue rights toward long-term residency. No Labour Market Needs Test required.

IRL.name: Dependant/Partner/Spouse Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: Allows family members (dependants, partners, spouses) of Critical Skills Employment Permit holders or researchers to work in Ireland.
IRL.notes: No fee for this permit. Applicant must already reside continuously in Ireland and have been determined a dependant by the Department of Justice. Cannot be used to apply from outside Ireland. Employment as a domestic operative is not permitted. Tied to primary permit holder's permission duration. Minimum wage applies.

IRL.name: Contract for Services Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA employees of foreign contractors being transferred to Ireland to fulfil a specific service contract with an Irish business.
IRL.notes: Fee: €500 (≤6 months) or €1,000 (6–24 months); renewal €750–€1,500. The foreign contractor must have a valid service contract with an Irish-registered company. Employee remains employed by and paid by the foreign contractor. No Labour Market Needs Test required.

IRL.name: Reactivation Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: Allows non-EEA nationals who previously held a valid employment permit but fell out of the employment permit system through no fault of their own to re-enter the legal work system.
IRL.notes: Fee: €500 (≤6 months) or €1,000 (6–24 months); renewal €750–€1,500. Designed to address situations where workers became undocumented due to employer failures or exploitation. Must demonstrate previous valid status and involuntary loss of status.

IRL.name: Internship Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For full-time international students studying outside Ireland who wish to complete a work placement/internship in a critical skills occupation with an Irish employer.
IRL.notes: Fee: €500 (≤6 months) or €1,000 (up to 12 months). 90% refunded if unsuccessful. Maximum duration 12 months, non-renewable. Must be enrolled full-time at a third-level institution outside Ireland pursuing a degree or higher. Role must align with Critical Skills Occupations List. No Labour Market Needs Test. Does not accrue rights toward long-term residency.

IRL.name: Sport and Cultural Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA nationals working in the sports or entertainment sectors in Ireland, including athletes, coaches, performers, and related roles.
IRL.notes: Fee: €500 (≤6 months) or €1,000 (up to 24 months); renewal €750–€1,500. Full-time employment maximum 2 years initially, extendable up to 3 additional years. Seasonal employment also available. No Labour Market Needs Test required. Holder must remain with initial employer for 12 months (except in cases of redundancy).

IRL.name: Exchange Agreement Employment Permit
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA nationals working in Ireland under an international bilateral reciprocal exchange agreement between Ireland and another country.
IRL.notes: No fee for this permit. Covers non-EEA nationals participating in formal government-to-government exchange schemes. Duration and conditions depend on the specific bilateral agreement. No Labour Market Needs Test required.

IRL.name: Working Holiday Authorisation
IRL.purpose: For young nationals of countries with a bilateral working holiday agreement with Ireland to live and work in Ireland for up to 12 months.
IRL.notes: Available to nationals of countries with bilateral working holiday agreements with Ireland (includes Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Argentina, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, USA, and others). Typically for ages 18–35. Holder can take casual or temporary employment. No employment permit required under this scheme. Must be applied for from home country. Eligible nationalities and exact terms vary by bilateral agreement.

IRL.name: Transit Visa
IRL.purpose: For visa-required nationals transiting through Irish airports or seaports en route to another country.
IRL.notes: Ireland is not part of the Schengen Area so Schengen transit rules do not apply. Transit visa may be required by nationals of certain countries even for airside (sterile transit) transit. Specific transit visa requirements depend on nationality and whether the transit involves passing through Irish immigration control (landside) or remaining airside. Applicants should check the ISD transit page for their specific nationality.

IRL.name: Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (STEP)
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA entrepreneurs with an innovative business proposal who wish to establish and develop a start-up business in Ireland.
IRL.notes: Requires minimum €50,000 in funding (from personal resources, loan, business angel, VC, or Irish state agency grant). Business must not be retail, catering, or personal services. Must have potential to create 10 jobs and €1 million in sales within 3–4 years. Additional €30,000 per additional co-founder. Applications evaluated quarterly. Successful applicants receive 2-year residence permission. Visa-required nationals also receive a multiple-entry visa. Established 2012; guidelines updated September 2023.

IRL.name: Atypical Working Scheme (AWS)
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA nationals undertaking specialised, highly-skilled short-term work (generally under 90 days) not supported by employment permit legislation - e.g. skill-shortage roles, specialist ICT/engineering, short paid internships, locum doctors, and nurses undertaking clinical adaptation.
IRL.notes: Administered by ISD (Department of Justice), separate from the DETE employment-permit system. Fee €250 (~$270 USD) non-refundable, paid by card via the INIS online portal. Must be applied for from OUTSIDE Ireland. General category: max 90 days over a 6-month period with a 1-month cooling-off; exceptions extend to 6 months (locum hospital doctors, nurses seeking NMBI registration) or up to 12 months (paid internships integral to a degree). Minimum 20 working days processing (stated on page last updated 30 April 2026); letter of approval valid 90 days. Salary must meet the General Employment Permit threshold. Visa-required nationals must additionally obtain a C multi-entry or D long-stay visa. Family members may not accompany. Not reckonable toward Stamp 4.

IRL.name: Van der Elst Visa (Employment)
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA nationals lawfully resident and employed by a company in another EU member state who are posted to Ireland to provide services on behalf of that employer, without needing an Irish employment permit.
IRL.notes: Derives from the 1994 Van der Elst ruling of the European Court of Justice. Applicant must be lawfully resident, employed and on the payroll of the employer in the sending EU member state, and coming on a temporary/short-term contract up to a maximum of 12 consecutive months. Applied online via AVATS up to 3 months before travel; decision generally within 8 weeks. Visa fee €60 single / €100 multiple entry per the ISD page (~$65/$108 USD). May not take up any other employment in the State; must return to the sending EU country when the contract ends.

IRL.name: Long Stay 'D' Minister of Religion Visa / Preclearance
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA nationals coming to work with an eligible religious body or faith community in Ireland as a minister of religion or in a related religious role.
IRL.notes: Permission granted for up to 3 years, with a possible further 3-year extension. Preclearance approval is required before travel for ALL non-EEA nationals (visa-required and non-visa-required). Visa-required nationals apply for both preclearance and a long stay D visa (D-visa fee approx €100 / ~$108 USD) via AVATS, up to 3 months before travel. After arrival, holder registers for an Irish Residence Permit.

IRL.name: Long Stay 'D' Volunteer Visa / Preclearance
IRL.purpose: For non-EEA nationals coming to Ireland to volunteer on an unpaid basis with an eligible charitable or non-profit organisation.
IRL.notes: Permission granted for up to 2 years, with the possibility of a third year. Preclearance approval required before travel for ALL non-EEA nationals; visa-required nationals also apply for a long stay D visa (approx €100 / ~$108 USD) via AVATS up to 3 months before travel. Holder cannot engage in paid work, rely on state benefits/public services, or bring family members, and cannot spend more than two years volunteering.

IRL.name: De Facto Partner of an Irish National Visa / Preclearance
IRL.purpose: For a non-EEA national in a committed durable relationship (akin to marriage/civil partnership) with an Irish citizen, seeking to live and work in Ireland with that partner.
IRL.notes: For unmarried partners of Irish citizens; generally requires evidence of a durable relationship (typically around 2 years' cohabitation). Preclearance approval (valid 6 months) must be obtained before travel regardless of whether the applicant is visa-required; visa-required nationals also apply for a long stay D visa via AVATS. Initial permission granted for 1 year and normally leads to Stamp 4 (live and work without an employment permit). Distinct routes exist for de facto partners of Critical Skills Employment Permit / Hosting Agreement holders.

IRL.name: Stamp 0 - Retiree / Person of Independent Means
IRL.purpose: For financially self-sufficient non-EEA nationals who wish to retire to or reside in Ireland as a person of independent means without accessing the labour market or public funds.
IRL.notes: Stamp 0 is a low-level, temporary residence permission for persons of independent means / retirees. Applicant (or an Irish sponsor) should have an individual income of at least €50,000 per year plus access to a lump sum to cover a major unexpected expense (roughly the price of a dwelling in the State). Private medical insurance is required; the holder may NOT work or run a business (unless specifically permitted in writing) and may not access public funds/benefits. Granted for 1 year at a time and renewable annually while criteria continue to be met. Visa-required nationals apply for a long stay D visa first. Ireland has no dedicated digital nomad / remote-work visa - Stamp 0 is the nearest equivalent for self-funded residents but does not authorise remote work for an Irish employer.

IRN.name: Type A - Entry Visa (Business/Commercial)
IRN.purpose: For business visits including negotiations, contract signing, machinery installation, and commercial activities. Also covers UN employees, faculty, and official business travelers.
IRN.notes: Covers merchants, academics, carrier personnel, and officials. Fee paid in EUR at airport banking terminals for on-arrival equivalent. Must apply via evisa.mfa.ir or at Iranian consulate. US, UK, Canada, Colombia nationals must apply at embassy only.

IRN.name: Type B - Tourist Visa
IRN.purpose: For leisure tourism and recreational travel within Iran. Issued to foreign nationals wishing to visit Iran as tourists.
IRN.notes: Visa on arrival (45-day stay) available at major international airports for eligible nationalities who apply electronically at least 2 days before travel. Fee paid in EUR at airport. US, UK, Canada, Colombia, Afghanistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Jordan, Pakistan, Somalia, Sri Lanka, and Israel nationals excluded from VOA. E-visa (30-day stay) available via evisatraveller.mfa.ir for ~48 eligible nationalities. As of August 2025, EU/AU/NZ nationals subject to mandatory guided-tour requirement (partially relaxed October 2025). US/UK/CA nationals must use pre-arranged tour packages.

IRN.name: Type C - Pilgrimage Visa
IRN.purpose: For Muslim tourists visiting holy and religious sites in Iran, primarily Mashhad (Imam Reza shrine) and Shiraz (Shah Cheragh).
IRN.notes: Restricted to Muslim travelers. Applicant typically requires documentation from an approved Islamic travel organization. Apply at Iranian consulate or embassy.

IRN.name: Type D - Diplomatic/Service Visa
IRN.purpose: For official government representatives, diplomats, consular officers, and holders of diplomatic or service passports traveling on official duties.
IRN.notes: Issued through diplomatic channels. Holders of diplomatic passports from most countries benefit from additional visa suppression agreements. Duration varies by bilateral agreement. Typically exempt from standard fees.

IRN.name: Type E - Education Visa
IRN.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking academic study, research, or scholarly activities at recognized Iranian universities and educational institutions.
IRN.notes: Requires acceptance letter from an approved Iranian university or research institute. Must be applied for at an Iranian embassy or consulate. Renewable annually. Students must register with the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology.

IRN.name: Type F - Temporary Work Visa
IRN.purpose: For skilled foreign workers, specialists, engineers, and technicians employed temporarily in Iran by Iranian or international companies.
IRN.notes: Requires work permit (issued by Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs) and employment contract with an Iranian entity. Applied at Iranian embassy or consulate. Renewable. Foreign executives and technicians employed by overseas firms operating in Iran may also qualify.

IRN.name: Type G - Transit Visa
IRN.purpose: For travelers passing through Iran en route to a third country, including truck drivers, overland travelers, and merchants in transit.
IRN.notes: Issued for transit purposes only. Duration typically 5 days but may vary. Travelers must have valid onward documentation for the destination country. Apply at Iranian embassy or consulate prior to travel.

IRN.name: Type H - Media Visa
IRN.purpose: For journalists, reporters, film crews, producers, cameramen, and other media professionals working in Iran.
IRN.notes: Requires prior accreditation and approval from the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) or the Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance. Apply at Iranian embassy or consulate. Processing time may be lengthy due to ministry approval requirements.

IRN.name: Type I - Investment Visa / Residence Permit
IRN.purpose: For foreign nationals making qualifying investments in Iran, enabling residency through the 5-year renewable investor residence permit.
IRN.notes: Minimum qualifying investment approximately USD 90,000 (reduced from EUR 250,000 in April 2022). Eligible investment forms: long-term bank deposits in Iranian banks, investment bonds and securities, housing/real estate. Administered by the Organization for Investment, Economic and Technical Assistance of Iran (OIETA). Provides 5-year renewable residency only - not a path to citizenship. Iran does not permit dual citizenship.

IRN.name: Type M - Marital/Family Visa
IRN.purpose: For foreign nationals married to Iranian citizens (particularly foreign men married to Iranian women) and their dependent children, for family unification.
IRN.notes: Requires proof of legal marriage recognized under Iranian law and documentation of family relationship. Must apply at an Iranian embassy or consulate. Iranian law governing family reunification applies asymmetrically by gender. Renewable.

IRN.name: Type T - Medical Visa
IRN.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Iran to receive medical treatment at approved Iranian hospitals and healthcare facilities.
IRN.notes: Requires prior authorization from an approved Iranian medical center. Applicant must submit documentation of the required treatment, including confirmation from the Iranian hospital or medical institution. Apply at Iranian embassy or consulate.

IRQ.name: Tourist/Visit Visa
IRQ.purpose: Visiting tourist sites, religious landmarks, and holy sites in Iraq. Also granted to tourist groups arriving through licensed tourism companies.
IRQ.notes: Single entry valid within 3 months of issuance; 1-month permitted stay. Available at Iraqi embassies/consulates and (for eligible nationalities) at ports of entry. The e-visa portal (eservice.evisa.iq) appears to offer an electronic version for eligible nationalities. Mandatory health insurance and registration with Directorate of Residence within 10 days of arrival required.

IRQ.name: Normal Visa
IRQ.purpose: General purpose entry into Iraq for visits not classified under tourism. Covers a broader range of visit reasons.
IRQ.notes: Single entry valid within 3 months; up to 3-month stay. Applicant must register with the Directorate of Residence within 10 days of arrival. Requires proof of financial means, full Iraqi address, and contact number.

IRQ.name: Transit Visa
IRQ.purpose: Passing through Iraqi territory en route to another destination.
IRQ.notes: Single entry valid within 3 months of issuance; maximum 7-day stay permitted. Issued by Iraqi embassies/consulates abroad.

IRQ.name: Non-Stop Transit Visa
IRQ.purpose: Transiting through Iraq without stopping - for travelers passing through Iraqi airspace or territory without entering the country.
IRQ.notes: Single entry valid within 3 months. Fee not specified on official source. For transit without stopping in Iraq; different from standard transit visa.

IRQ.name: Multi-Entry Visa
IRQ.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Iraq multiple times over an extended validity period without obtaining a new visa for each trip.
IRQ.notes: Available in 3-month, 6-month, or 12-month validity options. Fee is $100 USD. Issued by Iraqi embassies/consulates abroad. Maximum stay per visit not specified on the official source.

IRQ.name: Political Visa
IRQ.purpose: Issued to official government representatives, diplomatic mission staff and their families, and those traveling on official government business.
IRQ.notes: Issued to diplomatic personnel and their families. Special residency granted per official Ministry memorandum. Duration and fee vary by official approval and diplomatic protocol.

IRQ.name: Service Visa
IRQ.purpose: Issued to holders of official service passports traveling for government-related purposes.
IRQ.notes: Granted on a reciprocity basis per official Ministry memorandum. Fee and duration not specified in official sources.

IRQ.name: Urgent Visa
IRQ.purpose: Emergency entry visa for foreign nationals who arrive without a prior visa in exceptional or urgent circumstances.
IRQ.notes: Issued at border crossings by residency officers if the case is justified. Not a standard category - granted at officer discretion for emergency situations only. Duration and fee not specified.

IRQ.name: Electronic Entry Visa (E-Visa)
IRQ.purpose: Pre-travel electronic entry visa for nationals of designated countries who are no longer eligible for visa on arrival. Required before departure.
IRQ.notes: Mandatory since March 1, 2025 for 37 countries: all 27 EU member states plus USA, UK, Russia, China, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, and Norway. Apply at eservice.evisa.iq before travel. Fee of approximately $158 USD (206,000 IQD) includes mandatory health insurance. Valid for 60 days from date of arrival per official mofa.gov.iq Texas consulate page (some secondary sources cite 30 days - official source taken as authoritative). Processing 24-48 hours.

IRQ.name: Student Visa (Study in Iraq Program)
IRQ.purpose: Foreign nationals admitted to an Iraqi university or higher-education institution for undergraduate or postgraduate study under the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research's official 'Study in Iraq' program.
IRQ.notes: Official 'Study in Iraq' program run by Iraq's Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (launched 2024; 2025-2026 intake is the third round), announced via mofa.gov.iq embassy pages (e.g. mofa.gov.iq/kualalumpur/2025/06/11/study-in-iraq-program/). Offers fully-funded, partially-funded and self-funded places at Iraqi universities, including accommodation and health insurance for accepted international students. Applicants apply online at the official portal, receive admission, then obtain the student entry visa from an Iraqi embassy before travel and complete residency (student residence permit) at the General Directorate of Residency within 30 days of arrival. Visa fee not published on the official portal. Portal is a live .gov.iq government site (blocks automated fetchers with HTTP 403 but is reachable in a browser).

IRQ.name: Work Permit & Work Residence Permit (Foreign Worker)
IRQ.purpose: Employer-sponsored foreign nationals taking up employment in Iraq. Requires a work permit from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs before an entry visa and residence permit are issued.
IRQ.notes: Iraq does not issue a standalone MFA 'work visa'.
