KAZ.purpose: A transition visa allowing foreign nationals to enter Kazakhstan for the purpose of obtaining a temporary or permanent residence permit.
KAZ.notes: National fee (duty): 7 MCI single-entry (approx. 27,524 KZT at 2025 MCI rate of 3,932 KZT) or 30 MCI multiple-entry (approx. 117,960 KZT). MCI = Monthly Calculation Index set annually by the Government of Kazakhstan.

KAZ.name: Official/Diplomatic Visa (A3)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign government officials, diplomats, and staff of international organisations making official visits to Kazakhstan.
KAZ.notes: Facilitated processing: citizens of 48 eligible countries may obtain A3 visas without an invitation letter. Diplomatic passport holders from many countries already have visa-free access for official travel. Standard processing up to 5 working days; invitation processing up to 3 working days (electronic) or 5 working days (paper).

KAZ.name: Investor Visa (Multiple-Entry)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals who invest a minimum of USD 300,000 in the charter capital of Kazakh companies or in locally traded securities, enabling entry and subsequent residence permit acquisition.
KAZ.notes: Effective April 30, 2025. Applications submitted electronically via vmp.gov.kz. After obtaining the investor visa, holder may apply for a residence permit for up to 10 years. Minimum investment: USD 300,000. Multiple-entry consular fee applies (30 MCI / ~USD 200 equivalent).

KAZ.name: Neo Nomad Visa (B12-1)
KAZ.purpose: For digital professionals and entrepreneurs working remotely for foreign employers who wish to reside in Kazakhstan while maintaining employment outside the country.
KAZ.notes: Introduced 2025 by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Valid for up to 1 year, extendable for an additional year from within Kazakhstan. Requirements: minimum stable monthly income of USD 3,000, tax declarations, criminal record clearance, and health insurance. Processing time not published on official pages.

KAZ.name: Permanent Residence Visa for Skilled Professionals (B9)
KAZ.purpose: For highly skilled foreign professionals in in-demand fields including medicine, science, education, innovation, and creative arts who seek long-term residence in Kazakhstan.
KAZ.notes: Introduced 2025 as part of Kazakhstan's talent attraction initiative. Grants a permanent residence permit for up to 10 years. Processing time not published on official pages reviewed.

KAZ.name: IT Professional Permanent Residence (B9-1)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign IT professionals (software development, cybersecurity, UI/UX, DevOps, and related fields) to obtain permanent residency in Kazakhstan under a pilot digital nomad scheme.
KAZ.notes: Pilot project launched March 2025. Requires a petition from the Ministry of Digital Development / Astana Hub confirming qualification. Applicant must also obtain an IIN (Individual Identification Number) and digital signature (EDS) from a Kazakhstan embassy prior to applying online via eGov.kz. Must buy or rent property in Kazakhstan and provide a medical certificate at final stages. Processing: 45 calendar days.

KAZ.name: Transit Visa (B13)
KAZ.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to transit through Kazakhstan en route to a third country.
KAZ.notes: Category B13 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Issued for transit passage through the territory of Kazakhstan; single-entry stay of up to 90 days. Citizens with visa-free access do not require a transit visa. Transit visas are issued through Kazakh consulates and are not part of the e-visa scheme.

KAZ.name: Education (Student) Visa (C9)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted to or enrolled at Kazakhstan educational institutions (secondary through postgraduate programmes), and their accompanying family members.
KAZ.notes: Category C9 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Issued on the basis of a request from the authorised education body or a registered educational institution. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 1 year, extendable. Not part of the e-visa scheme; applied for at a Kazakh consulate.

KAZ.name: Employment (Labour Activity) Visa (C3)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to or residing in Kazakhstan to carry out labour activity (employment), together with their family members. Requires an inviting employer and, where applicable, a work permit.
KAZ.notes: Category C3 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification - the principal work visa. Issued at the request of an inviting party holding the required labour permit. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 3 years (up to 5 years for AIFC participants and Astana Hub employees). EAEU nationals (Armenia, Belarus, Kyrgyzstan, Russia) do not require this visa or a work permit.

KAZ.name: Independent Employment Visa (C4)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals engaging in independent employment in occupations that are in demand in priority sectors of the Kazakhstan economy.
KAZ.notes: Category C4 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Covers self-directed/independent employment in in-demand priority-sector occupations. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 3 years. Not part of the e-visa scheme.

KAZ.name: Business Immigrant Visa (C5)
KAZ.purpose: For business immigrants establishing or conducting business activity in Kazakhstan, issued on the basis of a request from local executive bodies (akimats) of the capital, cities of republican significance, or regions.
KAZ.notes: Category C5 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 2 years (up to 3 years for ethnic Kazakhs). Distinct from the short-stay business visitor visa (B1/B3) - C5 is for immigrants setting up a business.

KAZ.name: Seasonal Worker Visa (C6)
KAZ.purpose: For seasonal foreign workers employed in Kazakhstan for seasonal work under a labour permit.
KAZ.notes: Category C6 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 1 year, not exceeding the duration of the seasonal labour permit.

KAZ.name: Family Reunification Visa (C2)
KAZ.purpose: For family members of Kazakhstan citizens permanently residing in Kazakhstan, of ethnic Kazakhs, of former compatriots holding a temporary residence permit for 2+ years, and of foreigners with a permanent residence permit.
KAZ.notes: Category C2 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification - the family reunification / dependant visa. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 1 year. Distinct from the short-stay private visit visa (B10), which is for visiting relatives or friends without reunification/residence intent.

KAZ.name: Repatriation Visa for Ethnic Kazakhs / Kandas (C1)
KAZ.purpose: For ethnic Kazakhs (kandas) travelling to Kazakhstan for permanent residence under the historical-homeland repatriation programme.
KAZ.notes: Category C1 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Multiple-entry only, valid up to 1 year. Supports the repatriation of ethnic Kazakhs settling permanently in their historical homeland; leads to residence permit and kandas status.

KAZ.name: Missionary Visa (C7)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Kazakhstan to carry out missionary activity, together with their family members.
KAZ.notes: Category C7 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Missionaries must additionally register with the authorised religious-affairs body. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 180 days. Distinct from the B6 religious-activity visa, which excludes missionary work.

KAZ.name: Religious Activity Visa (B6)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals participating in the activities of a religious association in Kazakhstan, excluding missionary work.
KAZ.notes: Category B6 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry only, stay up to 90 days. Covers participation in religious-association activities; missionary work is handled under the separate C7 missionary visa.

KAZ.name: Internship and Training Visa (B7)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking practical training or an internship in Kazakhstan, including participants in Astana Hub programmes.
KAZ.notes: Category B7 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Covers practical training and internships (including Astana Hub programmes). Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 180 days.

KAZ.name: Medical Treatment Visa (C12)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Kazakhstan for medical treatment, examination, or consultation, and for relatives accompanying or caring for the patient.
KAZ.notes: Category C12 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification - the formal long-stay medical treatment visa. Single-entry or multiple-entry, stay up to 180 days. Covers treatment, examination, consultation, and accompanying caregivers. Distinct from the short-stay medical e-visa (issued for business/tourist/medical purposes via the e-visa portal).

KAZ.name: Investor Visa (A5)
KAZ.purpose: For heads and deputy heads of organisations carrying out investment activity in Kazakhstan and for investment tax residents of the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC), together with their family members.
KAZ.notes: Category A5 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 5 years. Covers AIFC investment tax residents and heads/deputy heads of investment-activity organisations plus their families. Distinct from the A6 investor visa (USD 300,000+ investment, up to 10-year multiple-entry residence) captured separately as the Investor Visa (Multiple-Entry).

KAZ.name: Adoption Visa (B11)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Kazakhstan for the purpose of adopting a Kazakhstan-citizen child.
KAZ.notes: Category B11 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry stay up to 180 days; multiple-entry validity up to 1 year. Issued for the adoption of a Kazakhstan-citizen child.

KAZ.name: Humanitarian (Volunteer) Visa (C8)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign volunteers providing services free of charge and for participants of international treaties providing charitable or humanitarian assistance in Kazakhstan.
KAZ.notes: Category C8 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Covers volunteers providing free-of-charge services and providers of charitable/humanitarian assistance under international treaties. Specific stay and validity limits are set at issuance and are not enumerated on the official classification page.

KAZ.name: Crew Members Visa (B5)
KAZ.purpose: For members of the crews of scheduled and charter flights and for crews of trains and vessels operating to or through Kazakhstan.
KAZ.notes: Category B5 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 1 year. For aircraft, train, and vessel crew members.

KAZ.name: International Road Transport Visa (B4)
KAZ.purpose: For foreign nationals engaged in international road transport - professional drivers operating cross-border road haulage and passenger services.
KAZ.notes: Category B4 in Kazakhstan's official visa classification. Single-entry stay up to 90 days; multiple-entry validity up to 1 year. For persons engaged in international road transport.

KEN.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA)
KEN.notes: Required for all foreign nationals (replacing visa-on-arrival and prior visa systems effective January 2024). Applied online at etakenya.go.ke. USD 30 fee. Approved eTA allows 90-day stay, extendable. Holders of East African Community (EAC) passports and some nationalities may be exempt. Not the same as visa-free entry - eTA is mandatory pre-travel authorization for most nationalities.

KEN.name: Transit Electronic Travel Authorisation (Transit eTA)
KEN.purpose: Travellers connecting through Kenya to a third country, for a stay of up to 72 hours
KEN.notes: Transit category of Kenya's eTA for passengers transiting through a Kenyan airport en route to another country, for a total stay not exceeding 72 hours. Official fee USD 20. Applied online before travel at etakenya.go.ke; processing capped at 72 hours. eTA-exempt nationals do not require it.

KEN.name: Work Permit Class D (Employment)
KEN.purpose: Foreign employees offered specific employment by a specific employer for skills not available in Kenya
KEN.notes: Kenya's main employer-sponsored work permit. Issued to a person offered specific employment by a specific employer, who holds skills or qualifications not available in Kenya and whose engagement benefits the country. Requires employer sponsorship. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 500,000 per year (~USD 3,850); gratis for East African Community citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Work Permit Class C (Prescribed Profession)
KEN.purpose: Members of a prescribed profession (e.g. medicine, law, engineering) intending to practise it in Kenya
KEN.notes: Issued to a member of a prescribed profession who intends to practise that profession, alone or in partnership, in Kenya and whose practice benefits the country. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Work Permit Class G (Specific Trade, Business or Consultancy)
KEN.purpose: Foreign nationals establishing or running a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession in Kenya (self-employment/investor)
KEN.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession (other than a prescribed profession) in Kenya. Requires documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital to invest. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke). Corrected 2026-07: the prior entry mis-stated the fee (USD 2,000) and described employer-sponsored employment, which is actually Class D.

KEN.name: Work Permit Class B (Agriculture and Animal Husbandry)
KEN.purpose: Investors engaging in agriculture or animal husbandry in Kenya
KEN.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in agriculture or animal husbandry in Kenya, with suitable land and sufficient capital. Requires documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Work Permit Class F (Specific Manufacturing)
KEN.purpose: Investors engaging in a specific manufacturing activity in Kenya
KEN.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in a specific manufacture in Kenya. Requires documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital for manufacturing. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Work Permit Class A (Prospecting and Mining)
KEN.purpose: Foreign nationals engaging, alone or in partnership, in prospecting for minerals or mining in Kenya
KEN.notes: For a person intending to engage, alone or in partnership, in prospecting for minerals or mining in Kenya. Requires the necessary prospecting/mining rights and licences and documentary proof of at least USD 100,000 capital to invest. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 500,000 per year (~USD 3,850); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke). Added 2026-07 to complete the work-permit class enumeration; the Class A investor route already appears in this record's rbi section.

KEN.name: Work Permit Class I (Approved Religious and Charitable Activities)
KEN.purpose: Missionaries and staff of approved religious or charitable (non-profit) organisations
KEN.notes: Issued to a member of a society registered under the Societies Act engaged as a missionary, or with a government-approved non-profit organisation, whose presence benefits Kenya. Official fees: processing KES 5,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 50,000 per year (~USD 385); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Work Permit Class K (Ordinary Residents)
KEN.purpose: Financially independent residents aged 35+ living on assured non-employment income (pension/annuity) - Kenya's retirement/passive-income residence permit
KEN.notes: Kenya's closest equivalent to a retirement permit. Issued to a person at least 35 years old with an assured annual income of not less than USD 24,000 from sources outside Kenya (e.g. pension or annuity), not derived from employment or business in Kenya; the holder may not take employment. Official fees: processing KES 20,000 (non-refundable) plus issuance KES 250,000 per year (~USD 1,920); gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Class N Digital Nomad Work Permit
KEN.purpose: Remote workers and freelancers earning income from companies or clients registered outside Kenya
KEN.notes: Introduced October 2024; online applications opened April 2025. Issued to a person who works remotely within Kenya for a company registered outside the country, or who provides self-employed services to overseas clients. Validity one or two years, renewable. The holder may not be employed by a Kenyan company or earn income within Kenya. Official fees: processing USD 200 (non-refundable) plus issuance USD 1,000 per year. Requires the last three months' bank statements or payslips as proof of income. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Special Pass
KEN.purpose: Short-term (up to 6 months) work, trade or professional engagement, often as a bridge while a work permit is processed
KEN.notes: Authorisation to enter and remain in Kenya for a period not exceeding 6 months to temporarily conduct business, trade or a profession (e.g. equipment installation, training, short consultancy), or as a bridge while a work-permit application is pending. Official fee USD 200 per month for non-EAC nationals; gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Student's Pass
KEN.purpose: Foreign nationals accepted or admitted to study at a Kenyan academic or training institution
KEN.notes: Issued to a foreigner accepted or admitted to a recognised Kenyan academic or training institution. Official fee USD 100 per year for non-EAC nationals; gratis for East African Community citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke). Minors require parental consent; refugees require Department of Refugee Services clearance. Fee corrected from prior USD 50 to the official USD 100/year on 2026-07 re-validation; official_url updated from the retired eCitizen link.

KEN.name: Internship/Research Pass
KEN.purpose: Foreign nationals undertaking an internship or academic research in Kenya
KEN.notes: Authorisation to enter and remain in Kenya to undertake an internship or academic research. Researchers require NACOSTI clearance and institutional sponsorship. Official fee KES 15,000 per year (~USD 115) for non-EAC nationals; gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Dependant's Pass
KEN.purpose: Spouses, children and other dependants of Kenyan citizens, permit holders, permanent residents or exempted persons
KEN.notes: For a foreigner who is a dependant of a Kenyan citizen, permit/pass holder, permanent resident or exempted person; validity is typically co-terminus with the sponsor's status. Official fees: KES 20,000 (~USD 155) for a spouse or child of a Kenyan citizen, KES 10,000 (~USD 77) for a spouse or child of a work-permit or permanent-residence holder; gratis for EAC citizens. Applied online via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KEN.name: Work Permit Class M (Refugees)
KEN.purpose: Persons granted refugee status in Kenya, and their spouses, wishing to take up a specific occupation, trade, business or profession
KEN.notes: Issued to a person who has been granted refugee status in Kenya, and their spouse, wishing to engage in a specific occupation, trade, business or profession. Issued gratis (free of charge). Requires refugee status recognition; applied via the eFNS portal (fns.immigration.go.ke).

KGZ.name: Tourist Visa (Type TS)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for tourism and leisure purposes. Available online via the e-visa portal to nationals of all countries.
KGZ.notes: Fee depends on visa category and period - not individually disclosed on the information page. Processing is typically 5 working days per the official portal. Citizens of 55+ countries enter visa-free for 30 days (Resolution No. 855, in force 31 Dec 2025); all other nationalities must apply via e-visa.

KGZ.name: Business Visa (Type B)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for negotiations, conferences, commercial meetings, and certain medical services of a business nature.
KGZ.notes: Available via online e-visa portal to all nationalities. Fee varies by category; not publicly specified on the information page.

KGZ.name: Special Work Visa SW1 / SW2
KGZ.purpose: Entry for equipment technicians, journalists, and charitable/humanitarian workers engaged in specific short-term work activities.
KGZ.notes: Initial grant up to 60 days, extendable up to 1 year. SW1 and SW2 are sub-categories for different work profiles. Separate from the general work permit system.

KGZ.name: Unified Permit for Foreign Workers (Employment Visa, formerly W1/W2)
KGZ.purpose: Single digital document combining an entry visa and work authorization for foreign nationals taking up employment or individual entrepreneurship in Kyrgyzstan.
KGZ.notes: Since 1 July 2025 (Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 367) the former Employment Visa W1 (issued to work-permit or individual-entrepreneur applicants; initial 60 days without a permit, then multiple-entry for the work-permit validity) and Employment Visa W2 (up to 90 days, renewable annually, for categories exempt from a work permit under the Law on External Labor Migration) were consolidated into a single electronic 'Unified Permit' (Single Permit) covering both entry and legal employment. Employers or workers apply via the e-visa portal; processing about 7 working days; stay/validity is tied to the employment term and renewable. Issuance is administered by the MFA through the end of 2026. Distinct from the Special Work SW1/SW2 visa (short-term technicians, journalists, charity staff). Former consular W1/W2 fee was approximately USD 60-90. Official MFA work-permit page: https://mfa.gov.kg/en/dks-mid-kr-en/Consular-Services/Visa-issues/Issues-of-extending-visas-to-foreign-nationals/Obtaining-a-work-permit-in-the-territory-of-the-Kyrgyz-Republic

KGZ.name: Student Visa (Type S)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for academic study at accredited educational institutions in Kyrgyzstan.
KGZ.notes: Available via e-visa portal. Longer-duration study typically requires in-country extension or a different permit category.

KGZ.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Type DN)
KGZ.purpose: Allows remote workers in ICT, software development, AI, gaming, digital media and related sectors to live and work remotely from Kyrgyzstan without a local work permit.
KGZ.notes: Established by Presidential amendments (October 9, 2024) and codified by Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 241 (April 30, 2025). Renewable annually. DN status holders are exempt from compulsory residence registration for up to 60 days. Applicants must show proof of remote contracts and income. No Kyrgyz work permit required while status is valid.

KGZ.name: Investment Visa (Type I)
KGZ.purpose: Issued to foreign investors or heads of foreign investment companies making qualifying capital contributions to the Kyrgyz economy.
KGZ.notes: Minimum investment 10 million KGS for a visa valid up to 5 years; minimum 20 million KGS for a visa valid up to 10 years. Eligible sectors include manufacturing, agriculture, banking, energy, education, medicine, engineering, and ICT. Family members (spouse, minor children, dependent parents) may receive an accompanying FF-type family visa. Does not directly confer permanent residency or citizenship.

KGZ.name: Transit Visa (Type TR)
KGZ.purpose: Short-stay entry for passage through Kyrgyz territory en route to a third country.
KGZ.notes: Maximum stay is 3 days. Requires proof of onward travel to a third country.

KGZ.name: Relatives / Family Visit Visa (Type RL)
KGZ.purpose: Entry to visit relatives or for family reunification with a Kyrgyz citizen or legal resident.
KGZ.notes: Available via e-visa portal. Separate Family Member (FF) category exists for accompanying dependants of other visa holders.

KGZ.name: Family Member Visa (Type FF)
KGZ.purpose: Issued to spouses, minor children, and dependent parents accompanying or joining the primary visa holder in Kyrgyzstan.
KGZ.notes: Tied to the primary visa holder's status (e.g., Investment Visa, DN Visa). Validity mirrors the primary holder's visa.

KGZ.name: Guest Visa (Type G)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for private-nature visits - to visit friends and acquaintances or to receive medical treatment/services in Kyrgyzstan.
KGZ.notes: Official MFA category 'G' (guest). Covers short private visits and is the visa foreigners use when travelling to Kyrgyzstan specifically for medical treatment. Issued for up to 60 days. Consular fee approximately USD 60-90 depending on duration and single/multiple entry. Obtained through Kyrgyz embassies/consulates; the current e-visa portal instead offers Relatives (RL) and Family Member (FF) categories, so a Guest visa is typically issued consularly rather than online.

KGZ.name: Diplomatic Visa (Type D)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for heads of foreign states and governments, members of their official delegations, and accredited diplomatic staff.
KGZ.notes: Issued through diplomatic channels, not the public e-visa portal. Holders of diplomatic passports from 30+ countries may also enter visa-free under bilateral agreements.

KGZ.name: Official / Service Visa (Type O)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for foreign state officials and their family members travelling on official government business.
KGZ.notes: Validity ranges from up to 90 days to 1 year depending on assignment. Issued through official channels.

KGZ.name: Driver Visa (Type T)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for drivers engaged in international freight and passenger transport operations.
KGZ.notes: Visa validity up to 6 months; maximum 30 days per individual entry. For international freight/transport drivers.

KGZ.name: Ethnic Kyrgyz Visa / Meken Visa (Type M)
KGZ.purpose: Issued to ethnic Kyrgyz persons residing abroad who wish to visit or return to Kyrgyzstan.
KGZ.notes: 'Meken' (meaning 'homeland') visa category. Applicants must demonstrate ethnic Kyrgyz heritage.

KGZ.name: Religious Visa (Type R)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for missionaries, clergy, and individuals engaged in religious cooperation and charitable religious work.
KGZ.notes: Requires documentation of religious organization affiliation and purpose of visit.

KGZ.name: Sapar Visa (Type J)
KGZ.purpose: Entry for participants in state-endorsed business, sports, and major public events, issued on the basis of a government or institutional petition.
KGZ.notes: Requires a state petition or institutional sponsor. Can be extended ('Sapar' translates roughly to 'journey/trip'). Not available via the standard public e-visa portal.

KGZ.name: Leave Visa (Type L)
KGZ.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals to facilitate legal departure from Kyrgyzstan following a visa violation or overstay.
KGZ.notes: Administrative visa to allow departure. Not for general immigration use.

KGZ.name: Emergency Leave Visa (Type E)
KGZ.purpose: Issued free of charge to foreign nationals requiring emergency departure due to a medical emergency.
KGZ.notes: Issued at no cost for medical emergencies. Administrative/humanitarian category.

KHM.name: Tourist Visa (Class T)
KHM.purpose: Short-term tourism, sightseeing, and leisure visits to Cambodia. Not permitted for employment or study.
KHM.notes: Available as: (1) e-Visa via evisa.gov.kh (USD 36 including service fee, online), (2) Visa on Arrival at international airports and major border crossings (USD 30), (3) sticker visa from Cambodian embassy/consulate (fee varies by country). Valid for 3 months from issuance date; single entry allowing 30-day stay. One-time extension of 30 days available in Cambodia at the Department of Immigration (322 Russian Boulevard, Phnom Penh). Restricted nationalities (Afghanistan, Algeria, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Syria) must apply at a Cambodian embassy and are ineligible for e-Visa or VOA. Kosovo nationals refused entry. Note: Tourist T visas were temporarily suspended at the Osaka honorary consulate as of January 5, 2026 due to inventory shortages - this is consulate-specific and does not affect other issuance channels.

KHM.name: Business Visa (Class E)
KHM.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting business activities in Cambodia including employment, investment, job-seeking, volunteering, retirement living, or study exceeding tourist visa limits.
KHM.notes: Available via embassy/consulate (USD ~35 equivalent; consulate issues single entry only) and Visa on Arrival at airports/borders (USD 35). The Business E visa is uniquely broad in scope: it covers employment, business visits, company inspection, long-term volunteering, study, job-seeking, and retirement. Initial entry is 30 days; extensible within Cambodia through the Department of Immigration for 1 month (single entry), 3 months (single entry), 6 months (multiple entry), or 12 months (multiple entry). Requires letter of guarantee or invitation letter from Cambodian entity; certificate of incorporation and patent tax documentation also required. Retirement/employment extension requires supporting documentation from employer or showing financial means.

KHM.name: Business Visa Extension - Employment (Class E, Long-term)
KHM.purpose: Long-term authorization for foreign nationals to reside and work in Cambodia. Obtained by extending the initial Business (E) visa within Cambodia.
KHM.notes: Cambodia does not issue a separate 'work visa' category; foreign workers enter on a Business (E) visa and extend it for 6 or 12 months (multiple entries). Extensions processed at the Department of Immigration, 322 Russian Boulevard, Phnom Penh. A separate Work Permit from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training is required to legally work. Work permits and business visa extensions are distinct processes. Fee for 12-month multiple-entry extension is approximately USD 290-300 as reported by immigration practitioners.

KHM.name: Ordinary Visa Extension - Job-Seeking (Class EG)
KHM.purpose: For foreign nationals who entered on an Ordinary (E) visa and are looking for employment in Cambodia; the entry-level extension that bridges to the EB business/work extension once a job is secured.
KHM.notes: EG ('E-General') is one of the four Ordinary (E-class) extension-of-stay subcategories — EB (business/employment), EG (job-seeking), ER (retirement), ES (student). It is the extension most first-time E-class arrivals use while looking for work: issued in 1-month or 3-month increments, single entry only (leaving Cambodia voids it), and generally renewable only once before the holder must convert to an EB extension and obtain a work permit from the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training to begin employment. Processed inside Cambodia by the General Department of Immigration (Ministry of Interior), Phnom Penh. Extension fees are payable locally and vary by duration; no single fixed USD fee is officially published.

KHM.name: Foreigner Work Permit and Employment Card (MLVT)
KHM.purpose: Mandatory labour-side authorization that every foreign national must hold to legally work in Cambodia, issued by the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training. Complements (does not replace) the EB business/work visa extension issued by immigration.
KHM.notes: Distinct from the immigration visa: the EB (business) visa extension grants the right to STAY, while the work permit and foreign employment card grant the right to WORK — a foreign worker needs both. Applied for online through the Foreign Workers Centralized Management System (FWCMS) at fwcms.mlvt.gov.kh (issuing authority: Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training). Must be obtained within 90 days of first entry; issued on a calendar-year basis (valid through 31 December of the year of issue), with renewals filed between 1 January and 31 March. Standard combined fee is approximately USD 100 (about KHR 400,000). Since 2024 a valid work permit is required for all 6-month and 12-month EB visa extensions. Self-employed foreigners, remote workers based in Cambodia, and company directors named on the patent tax certificate also require one. Official FWCMS portal and the MFAIC 'Work Permit and Employment Card' government PDF (mfaic.gov.kh) confirm the system and issuing authority; both returned WAF 'Request Rejected' on direct fetch, so the fee/validity figures are corroborated by current practitioner summaries and MLVT notifications.

KHM.name: Business Visa Extension - Student/Study (Class E, Study Purpose)
KHM.purpose: Allows foreign students to reside in Cambodia for the duration of their studies at a Cambodian educational institution.
KHM.notes: Cambodia has no standalone 'student visa' category. Students enter on a Business (E) visa and extend for study purposes through the Department of Immigration. Requires enrollment documentation from an accredited Cambodian institution. The E visa class covers study as an explicit permitted purpose per the consulate's official classification.

KHM.name: Business Visa Extension - Retirement (Class E, Retirement Purpose)
KHM.purpose: Allows foreign retirees to reside long-term in Cambodia on a renewable basis.
KHM.notes: Cambodia has no dedicated retirement visa. Retirees use the Business (E) visa extended annually through the Department of Immigration. Retirement is an explicitly recognized purpose under the E class per official consulate documentation. Applicants must show financial means (no minimum income threshold published officially). Annual renewal required.

KHM.name: Business Visa / Cambodia My Second Home (CM2H)
KHM.purpose: For foreign investors and long-term residents wishing to reside in Cambodia through an investment-based residency program.
KHM.notes: The Cambodia My Second Home (CM2H) program grants a 10-year renewable residency visa to foreigners investing in approved real estate (minimum USD 100,000 in above-ground-floor residential property; land excluded). Administered by the General Department of Immigration in partnership with Khmer Home Charity Association (KHCA). Holders receive right to live, work, and study in Cambodia; eligible to apply for citizenship after 5 years. Restricted nationalities: Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, North Korea, Syria. The USD 100,000 figure is sourced from 2025-2026 immigration law firm summaries (Harvey Law Group); official cm2h.com was inaccessible for direct verification.

KHM.name: Diplomatic Visa (Class A)
KHM.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic passports traveling on official government business or posted to diplomatic missions in Cambodia.
KHM.notes: No fee. Issued to diplomatic passport holders. Duration and conditions governed by bilateral agreements. Many countries with bilateral visa exemption agreements provide visa-free entry for diplomatic passport holders without needing this visa (see conditional_access). Processing at Cambodian embassies/consulates takes 2 working days.

KHM.name: Official Visa (Class B)
KHM.purpose: Issued to holders of official or service passports traveling on official non-diplomatic government business.
KHM.notes: No fee. Issued to official/service passport holders traveling for government purposes. Governed by bilateral agreements. Duration varies per agreement.

KHM.name: Courtesy Visa (Class C)
KHM.purpose: Issued to representatives of United Nations agencies, international organizations, and NGOs operating in Cambodia.
KHM.notes: No fee. For UN staff, international organization representatives, and NGO personnel. Duration and terms governed by individual agreements with the Cambodian government.

KHM.name: Khmer Visa (Class K)
KHM.purpose: Issued to ethnic Khmer persons holding foreign nationality who wish to enter Cambodia.
KHM.notes: No fee. Specifically for Cambodian nationals who hold a foreign passport (e.g., Cambodian-born persons with Japanese citizenship). Issued at Cambodian embassies and consulates.

KHM.name: Transit Visa
KHM.purpose: For travelers transiting through Cambodia en route to a third country.
KHM.notes: Cambodia does not publish a standardized transit visa program. Transit arrangements are typically handled via the Business (E) or Tourist (T) visa. Kosovo nationals are refused transit. No official transit visa category page was found on immigration.gov.kh during research (site rendered no substantive content).

KIR.name: Visitor Visa
KIR.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Kiribati. The official Visitor Visa application form covers five sub-types selectable on the form: Tourist (or visiting family/friends), Guardian (of a student or work visa holder), Business visitor, Dependent child (of a Kiribati citizen, resident, work or student visa holder), and Limited purpose/event. Governed by the Kiribati Immigration Act 2019 and Immigration Procedure 2020.
KIR.notes: Nationals not covered by the Visa Exemption Order 2023 must apply. Fees are not published: the official form states 'Appropriate fee' and directs applicants to contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki for payment (fees payable in Australian dollars, Kiribati's currency). Applications lodged by email to visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki or in person at the Immigration Office in Bairiki, Tarawa, or the Kiritimati (London) branch. official_url verified as the live Visitor Visa application form (HTTP 200) 2026-07.

KIR.name: Business Visitor Visa
KIR.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Kiribati for business purposes such as meetings, negotiations or short-term commercial activity. One of the five sub-types selectable on the official Visitor Visa application form (tick 'Business').
KIR.notes: Per the official Visitor Visa form, business applicants must provide evidence of their employment and of the business they will undertake in Kiribati. A business visitor who needs to stay in Kiribati for more than 3 months a year must instead apply for a Work Visa (Specific Purpose or Event sub-type). Only required for nationals not covered by the Visa Exemption Order 2023. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. official_url verified HTTP 200 2026-07.

KIR.name: Guardian Visitor Visa
KIR.purpose: For the parent or legal guardian of a student-visa or work-visa holder in Kiribati who wishes to accompany or visit them. One of the five sub-types selectable on the official Visitor Visa application form (tick 'Guardian').
KIR.notes: Per the official Visitor Visa form, guardians must provide evidence that they are the parent or legal guardian of the student or work-visa holder. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. Governed by the Kiribati Immigration Act 2019. official_url verified HTTP 200 2026-07.

KIR.name: Dependent Child Visitor Visa
KIR.purpose: For the dependent child (under 18) of a Kiribati citizen, resident, work-visa holder or student-visa holder. One of the five sub-types selectable on the official Visitor Visa application form (tick 'Dependent child').
KIR.notes: Per the official Visitor Visa form, applicants must provide evidence of the relationship with their parent or legal guardian; children of Essential Skills or Religious Worker visa holders must also show the parent is eligible to support the visa. A family (principal applicant, partner and dependent children under 18) may alternatively be covered on a single Visitor Visa application. There is no distinct spouse-of-citizen residence visa - a partner is included within the principal applicant's family Visitor Visa. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. official_url verified HTTP 200 2026-07.

KIR.name: Limited Purpose or Event Visitor Visa
KIR.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Kiribati for a specific limited purpose or event not covered by the tourist, business, guardian or dependent-child options. One of the five sub-types selectable on the official Visitor Visa application form (tick 'Limited purpose/event').
KIR.notes: A visitor sub-type distinct from the Work Visa's 'Specific Purpose or Event' category (which applies where the purpose involves paid work). Only required for nationals not covered by the Visa Exemption Order 2023. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. official_url verified HTTP 200 2026-07.

KIR.name: Group Visa (Group Visitor Visa)
KIR.purpose: For groups travelling to Kiribati together for the same purpose, on the same day, and for the same length of time (e.g. tour groups). The official 'Group Visitor Visa Form' is completed by the tour organiser and lodged alongside an individual Visitor Visa application for each group member.
KIR.notes: Not a standalone visa: it is a group cover-sheet (up to 15 applicants per sheet) submitted with each member's individual Visitor Visa application. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. official_url verified as the live Group Visitor Visa form (HTTP 200) 2026-07.

KIR.name: Investment Visa
KIR.purpose: For foreign nationals investing in or conducting business in Kiribati. May be granted to a single person or a family (principal applicant, partner and dependent children under 18).
KIR.notes: Prerequisite (per the official application form, Section A): applicant must hold an approved Foreign Investment Certificate issued by the Investment Promotion Division under the Foreign Investment Act 2018 - without it the application cannot proceed. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. Distinct from the historical investor-passport scheme repealed in 2004 (no CBI/RBI). official_url verified as the live Investment Visa application form (HTTP 200) 2026-07.

KIR.name: Student Visa
KIR.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking a course longer than 3 months total in Kiribati. The official form covers three study types: tertiary fee-paying student, domestic primary/secondary student, and the dependent child of a Kiribati citizen, resident, work visa or student visa holder.
KIR.notes: Applies only to courses longer than 3 months (shorter study uses a Visitor Visa). Applicants must show an acceptable standard of health and good character. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. Governed by the Kiribati Immigration Act 2019. official_url verified as the live Student Visa application form (HTTP 200) 2026-07.

KIR.name: Work Visa
KIR.purpose: Umbrella work-visa category for foreign nationals authorised to work in Kiribati. A single official Work Visa application form covers four sub-types, selected on the form: Essential Skills, Specific Purpose or Event, Religious Worker, and Domestic Worker of consulate staff.
KIR.notes: The partner and dependent children of a work-visa holder do NOT use this form - they apply via the Visitor/Student forms. A job offer from a Kiribati employer is required for most sub-types. Applicants must meet health and character standards. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. Governed by the Kiribati Immigration Act 2019. official_url verified as the live Work Visa application form (HTTP 200) 2026-07.

KIR.name: Essential Skills Work Visa
KIR.purpose: Work-visa sub-type for a foreign national with a job offer from a Kiribati employer whose skills, qualifications and work experience are relevant to the position offered.
KIR.notes: One of the four sub-types on the official Work Visa application form (tick 'Essential Skills'). Requires a job offer with job description, pay and conditions, plus evidence of relevant qualifications and work experience. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki.

KIR.name: Specific Purpose or Event Work Visa
KIR.purpose: Work-visa sub-type for a position tied to a specific purpose or event, including intra-corporate transferees, managers/senior/specialist business persons on short-term secondment, contractual or independent service suppliers, business visitors needing to stay more than 3 months a year, installers of specialist machinery/equipment, referees or judges of sporting events/shows/exhibitions, and media/film/video production crew.
KIR.notes: One of the four sub-types on the official Work Visa application form (tick 'Specific Purpose'). Section F4 of the form lists the qualifying position categories. Requires a description of and evidence for the specific purpose or event. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki.

KIR.name: Domestic Worker Work Visa (consulate staff)
KIR.purpose: Work-visa sub-type for domestic staff employed by consulate/diplomatic staff posted in Kiribati.
KIR.notes: One of the four sub-types on the official Work Visa application form (tick 'Domestic worker'). Requires a signed Statement of Undertaking from the employer guaranteeing employment, accommodation, maintenance and repatriation, plus a signed Declaration of Acceptance from the applicant. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki.

KIR.name: Transit Visa
KIR.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Kiribati en route to another destination who are not from a visa-waiver country. May be granted to a single person or a family (partner and dependent children under 18).
KIR.notes: Required only for travellers not covered by the Visa Exemption Order 2023. Applicants must attach flight bookings / evidence of onward travel. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. official_url verified as the live Transit Visa application form (HTTP 200) 2026-07.

KIR.name: Religious Worker Work Visa
KIR.purpose: Work-visa sub-type authorising foreign religious workers (missionaries, clergy, etc.) to carry out religious activities in Kiribati under sponsorship from a recognised religious organisation.
KIR.notes: One of the four sub-types on the official Work Visa application form (tick 'Religious Worker'). Requires a completed Sponsorship Form for Religious Workers (mfa.gov.ki/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/Religious-Worker-Sponsorship-form-FINAL.pdf) and associated documents from the sponsoring organisation. Fees not published; contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki. Governed by the Kiribati Immigration Act 2019.

KIR.name: Medical Entry (Medical Form)
KIR.purpose: A supporting medical form required for certain visa applications where health conditions are relevant. Not a standalone visa category but a medical declaration/health assessment form used in conjunction with other visa types.
KIR.notes: The Medical Form is a supporting document, not a standalone visa. It is used alongside other visa applications requiring health declarations. official_url updated to the direct Medical Form PDF (verified HTTP 200 2026-07); previously pointed to the general mfa.gov.ki/visa/ index.

KNA.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA)
KNA.purpose: Authorises eligible foreign nationals to travel to Saint Kitts and Nevis for tourism, leisure, or short visits. It is a pre-travel digital permission and not a visa; it does not itself grant entry - Immigration officers determine actual permitted stay at the port of entry.
KNA.notes: Mandatory for all foreign visitors not otherwise exempt, effective 26 May 2025. Valid for 90 days or until passport expiry, whichever is sooner. Apply via www.knatravelform.kn or the 'St Kitts and Nevis e-Border' mobile app. Standard rate is US$17 (discounted rate of US$8.50 applied through 1 September 2025; that discount period has now expired as of June 2026). Exempt categories (no eTA required, only free ED Form): SKN citizens/residents, OECS member state citizens, CARICOM member nation citizens, accredited diplomats on official duty, children under 2, in-transit passengers, on-duty flight/vessel crew, active military or SAR personnel. Saint Kitts and Nevis is the first CARICOM nation to implement an eTA system. Source: SKNIS May 2025 announcement.

KNA.name: Visitor Visa (e-Visa)
KNA.purpose: Grants entry to nationals of visa-required countries for tourism, visiting family, or short-term stays in Saint Kitts and Nevis. Applied for online via the official e-visa portal before travel.
KNA.notes: Required for nationalities not covered by visa-free or eTA arrangements (e.g. Dominican Republic nationals explicitly require a visa). Maximum initial stay is one month per Embassy DC FAQ; actual duration set by Immigration officer at port of entry. Visa emailed upon approval. Apply via evisa.gov.kn (redirects to evisa.stkittsnevisonline.com). Visitors on this visa cannot work, access public funds, study, or become self-employed. Stays under 24 hours for countries normally requiring visas do not require a visa. Fee: US$100. Processing approximately two weeks. Source: Embassy DC FAQ (embassydc.gov.kn).

KNA.name: Student Visa (e-Visa)
KNA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to enter Saint Kitts and Nevis to pursue academic or educational programs at approved institutions.
KNA.notes: Fee is US$150 (versus US$100 for a visitor visa); non-refundable if the application is refused. Per the Embassy DC FAQ, a student visa must be applied for through the university/institution of interest, and an applicant already in the country on a visitor visa cannot convert it to a student visa in-country - they must leave the Federation and apply for the student visa from outside. Processing approximately two weeks; visa emailed upon approval. Apply via the official e-visa portal (evisa.stkittsnevisonline.com, also reachable through the evisa.gov.kn redirect). Specific validity/duration not stated in official sources. Sources: Embassy DC FAQ (embassydc.gov.kn); MOFA passport-and-visa-services (mofa.gov.kn).

KNA.name: Citizenship by Investment - Sustainable Island State Contribution (SISC)
KNA.purpose: Grants full Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship (not merely residency) to investors who make a qualifying non-refundable contribution to the government's Sustainable Island State fund supporting renewable energy, healthcare, and education.
KNA.notes: Minimum contribution US$250,000 for main applicant or family up to 4 persons. Applications must be submitted through an Authorised Agent; direct CIU submissions not accepted. Due diligence fees: US$10,000 main applicant, US$7,500 per dependent aged 16+. Post-approval fees US$10,000–US$25,000 depending on dependents. No residency requirement. Dual citizenship permitted. Citizenship can be revoked for misrepresentation. Banned nationalities: Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Russia. Processing time stated as 3–6 months (160–180 days) from submission to approval-in-principle. Source: ciu.gov.kn.

KNA.name: Citizenship by Investment - Public Benefit Option (PBO)
KNA.purpose: Grants full Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship to investors who make a qualifying non-refundable contribution to approved public benefit projects that foster economic growth and job creation.
KNA.notes: Minimum contribution US$250,000. Approved projects include Basseterre High School, National Housing Corporation, Prime Creative Arts Centre, Royal St. Kitts Beach Resort, Robert L. Bradshaw Airport Expansion. Same due diligence fees and conditions as SISC route. Source: ciu.gov.kn.

KNA.name: Citizenship by Investment - Developer's Real Estate Investment
KNA.purpose: Grants full Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship to investors who purchase a unit in a CIU-approved development project, with the property being resaleable after 7 years.
KNA.notes: Minimum investment US$325,000 in an approved development (condo/unit). Property resaleable after 7 years. Same due diligence fee structure and conditions as other CBI routes. Must be purchased from an approved developer. Source: ciu.gov.kn.

KNA.name: Citizenship by Investment - Private Real Estate Sale (Single-Family Home)
KNA.purpose: Grants full Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship to investors who purchase an exclusive private single-family home at or above the minimum investment threshold.
KNA.notes: Minimum investment US$600,000 for a private single-family home. Highest minimum among the four CBI routes; designed for investors seeking personalized ownership opportunities. Same due diligence fee structure and conditions as other CBI routes. Source: ciu.gov.kn.

KNA.name: Transit Exemption (Under 24 Hours)
KNA.purpose: Permits nationals of visa-required countries to transit through Saint Kitts and Nevis without obtaining a visa, provided the stay does not exceed 24 hours.
KNA.notes: Nationals of visa-required countries who remain in Saint Kitts and Nevis for less than 24 hours do not require a visa. Also, in-transit passengers (airside/port transit) are exempt from the eTA fee requirement. Source: Embassy DC FAQ and SKNIS eTA announcement.

KNA.name: Diplomatic/Official/Service Passport Visa Waiver
KNA.purpose: Grants visa-free entry to holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from countries with bilateral waiver agreements with Saint Kitts and Nevis, for official duties or short-term visits.
KNA.notes: Applies to holders of diplomatic, official, and service passports from countries with active bilateral waiver agreements. Confirmed agreements for diplomatic/official passports specifically include Kazakhstan (signed January 26, 2024, up to 90 days) and Ghana (2018 agreement for diplomatic/official/service passports, extended to ordinary passports March 4, 2026). Accredited diplomats on official duty are also exempt from the eTA fee under the May 2025 eTA system. Source: sknis.gov.kn press releases.

KNA.name: Work Permit
KNA.purpose: Authorises a non-citizen to take up paid employment in Saint Kitts and Nevis. The permit is employer-tied and role-specific; the prospective employer applies on the worker's behalf.
KNA.notes: Required for any non-national taking up paid employment in the Federation. The application is employer-led (the worker cannot apply independently) and is submitted to the Labour Department / Ministry of National Security. A work permit is only granted for a specialised position; the post must first be advertised in local media for three consecutive weeks, and the employer must show it consulted the Labour Department and tried to fill the vacancy locally (proof of advertising plus Labour Department evidence is submitted with the application). The applicant must reside outside the Federation when applying. Permits are non-transferable between employers, and renewal must be requested no later than two weeks before expiry. Official fee and validity are not published on government pages. Sources: gov.kn 'In SKN Work Visa Procurement'; SKNIS 'Ministry of National Security Reminds Employers of Work Permit Procedures' (28 Sep 2020).

KNA.name: Citizenship by Marriage
KNA.purpose: Allows the foreign spouse of a Saint Kitts and Nevis citizen to acquire citizenship of the Federation through marriage.
KNA.notes: Citizenship of Saint Kitts and Nevis may be derived by Marriage (alongside Birth, Descent and Registration), per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Passport and Visa Services page. Applications are facilitated through SKN overseas Missions and processed by the Ministry of National Security / Immigration Department in Basseterre; the official application form is published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. This is a citizenship-acquisition route for spouses of citizens, distinct from the Citizenship by Investment programme. Fee and processing time are not stated on the official page. Sources: mofa.gov.kn passport-and-visa-services; mofa.gov.kn Citizenship by Marriage form.

KNA.name: Citizenship by Descent
KNA.purpose: Allows a person born outside Saint Kitts and Nevis to a Kittitian/Nevisian parent (and in some cases grandparent) to acquire citizenship of the Federation by descent.
KNA.notes: Citizenship of Saint Kitts and Nevis may be derived by Descent (alongside Birth, Marriage and Registration), per the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Passport and Visa Services page. Official application forms are published by the SKN Embassy (Washington DC): separate forms for adults ('Citizenship by Descent Application with Medical Form') and minors ('Citizenship by Descent Minor Application with Medical Form'), both dated 2026, and by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Applications are facilitated through SKN overseas Missions and processed by the Ministry of National Security / Immigration Department in Basseterre. This is a heritage-based citizenship-acquisition route, distinct from both the Citizenship by Investment programme and Citizenship by Marriage. Fee and processing time are not published on official pages. Sources: mofa.gov.kn passport-and-visa-services; embassydc.gov.kn application-forms and forms-documents.

KOR.name: Short-Term Visit Visa (C-3)
KOR.purpose: Tourism, visiting family, short business, medical treatment, transit
KOR.notes: Many nationalities are visa-exempt. Apply at a Korean embassy/consulate. Multiple-entry versions available. K-ETA electronic travel authorisation required for some nationalities.

KOR.name: E-7 Specially Designated Activities Visa
KOR.purpose: Working in a specialised job at a Korean company (requires employer sponsorship)
KOR.notes: Requires job offer from a Korean employer. Employer must file application on behalf of the employee. Points-based system for some categories.

KOR.name: D-2 Student Visa
KOR.purpose: Studying at a Korean university, college, or graduate school
KOR.notes: Requires admission letter from a Korean institution. Can work up to 20 hours/week part-time.

KOR.name: H-1 Working Holiday Visa
KOR.purpose: Holidaying and working in Korea (age 18–30, select nationalities)
KOR.notes: Available for Australia, UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Canada, Japan, and others. Generally no fee or very low fee.

KOR.name: F-1-D Digital Nomad Visa
KOR.purpose: Remote working in South Korea for up to 2 years (launched January 2024)
KOR.notes: Minimum annual income USD 84,600 (GNI 2x). Available to nationals from countries with visa-free or visa agreements with Korea. Cannot work for Korean employers.

KOR.name: E-2 Foreign Language Instructor Visa
KOR.purpose: Teaching a foreign language (e.g. English conversation) at schools, universities, or accredited language institutes
KOR.notes: Requires a bachelor's degree or higher and, for the E-2-1 sub-type, citizenship of a designated native-English-speaking country. Criminal background check and health/drug check required. Employer files a Certificate of Confirmation of Visa Issuance via HiKorea. Period of stay up to 2 years, renewable.

KOR.name: E-9 Non-Professional Employment Visa (Employment Permit System)
KOR.purpose: Low-skilled work in manufacturing, construction, agriculture, fishing, and services under the Employment Permit System (EPS)
KOR.notes: Open only to nationals of the 16 EPS MOU partner countries; applicants must pass the EPS-TOPIK Korean-language test and be selected from the jobseeker roster. Employer- and sector-tied. Maximum stay 4 years 10 months. Administered by Korea's Ministry of Employment and Labor via eps.go.kr; 2026 quota 80,000.

KOR.name: E-1 Professor Visa
KOR.purpose: Teaching or research at a Korean university or institution of higher education
KOR.notes: For professors, assistant professors, and equivalent teaching/research staff at accredited higher-education institutions. Maximum single period of stay up to 5 years. Employer sponsorship required; e-Visa available for eligible nationals.

KOR.name: E-6 Arts and Entertainment Visa
KOR.purpose: Artists, musicians, professional athletes, models, and entertainers performing in Korea
KOR.notes: Sub-types cover fine/performing arts (E-6-1), hotel/entertainment performers (E-6-2), and professional athletes/coaches (E-6-3). Contract and, for some sub-types, a performance recommendation certificate are required.

KOR.name: H-2 Work and Visit Visa
KOR.purpose: Visit plus designated employment for foreign-national ethnic Koreans from CIS and select countries
KOR.notes: For overseas Koreans (aged 18+) from China, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and other CIS states. Multiple-entry, valid up to ~3 years, allowing work in designated industries after jobseeker registration. Distinct from F-4, which covers a broader overseas-Korean group with fewer work restrictions.

KOR.name: D-10 Job-Seeking Visa
KOR.purpose: Job-seeking or start-up preparation for qualified graduates and professionals
KOR.notes: Points-based visa (D-10-1 job-seeking, D-10-2 start-up preparation) for those preparing to obtain a professional-employment (E-series) or start-up (D-8) status. Initial stay up to 6 months, extendable to a maximum of 2 years total. Permits internships and limited part-time activity.

KOR.name: D-8 Corporate Investment Visa
KOR.purpose: Foreign executives/investors establishing or managing a company in which they have invested in Korea
KOR.notes: For essential professionals of a foreign-invested company (D-8-1) or founders of a venture/technology start-up (D-8-4). Minimum investment generally KRW 100 million (roughly USD 75,000) for D-8-1. Maximum single period of stay up to 5 years; renewable. Distinct from the immigrant-investor (F-2-8) residence-by-investment schemes tracked separately.

KOR.name: D-9 International Trade / Business Management Visa
KOR.purpose: Running an international-trade business, plant/equipment installation, or management activities in Korea
KOR.notes: For sole traders/managers engaged in import-export, industrial-equipment installation and operation, or supervising business operations, who do not qualify under D-8. Period of stay up to 2 years, renewable.

KOR.name: D-4 General Training Visa (incl. Korean-language training)
KOR.purpose: Non-degree study such as Korean-language courses at university institutes, or professional/technical training
KOR.notes: D-4-1 covers Korean-language training at a university-affiliated language institute; other sub-types cover trainees at companies or institutions. Distinct from the D-2 degree-seeking student visa. Part-time work allowed only with prior permission. Period of stay up to 2 years.

KOR.name: F-6 Marriage Migrant Visa
KOR.purpose: Foreign spouse of a Korean national coming to reside in Korea
KOR.notes: For the spouse of a Korean citizen (F-6-1), a parent raising a Korean citizen's child (F-6-2), or a spouse who lost marital status without fault (F-6-3). The initial single-entry 90-day visa is converted to a 1-3 year residence status after alien registration. Sponsor must meet minimum-income and the applicant basic Korean-language requirements. Grants unrestricted work; pathway to F-5 permanent residence.

KOR.name: F-4 Overseas Korean Visa
KOR.purpose: Foreign-national ethnic Koreans (former Korean nationals and their descendants)
KOR.notes: For overseas Koreans (former ROK nationals and their descendants to a defined degree) as defined by the Overseas Koreans Act. Multiple-entry, valid up to 3 years and renewable, with broad (though not unlimited) work rights. Administered via visa.go.kr / HiKorea.

KOR.name: F-3 Dependent Family Visa
KOR.purpose: Accompanying spouse and unmarried minor children of long-term (D-/E-series and most non-immigrant) visa holders
KOR.notes: Granted to the dependent spouse and minor children of a principal visa holder (e.g. D-2, D-8, E-1 to E-7). Period of stay matches the principal's status. Employment is not permitted on F-3; the dependent must obtain their own work status to work.

KOR.name: Medical Treatment Visa (C-3-3 short-term / G-1-10 long-term)
KOR.purpose: Receiving medical treatment or recuperation in Korea, and accompanying carers
KOR.notes: Short-term medical tourism uses the C-3-3 short-term visit sub-type (stay up to 90 days). Treatment requiring longer than 90 days uses the G-1-10 status, which can be extended for the duration of treatment. Accompanying family/carers may receive a matching visa.

KOR.name: C-4 Short-Term Employment Visa
KOR.purpose: Short-term paid activities up to 90 days (e.g. temporary or one-off work, entertainers, models, advertising, short assignments)
KOR.notes: For short-term profit-making activities not exceeding 90 days. Single entry; C-category holders cannot change to another sojourn status inside Korea. As of October 2025 the former C-4 seasonal agriculture/fishery sub-types were moved to the dedicated E-8 Seasonal Worker visa.

KOR.name: D-7 Intra-company Transferee Visa
KOR.purpose: Staff of a foreign company transferred to its Korean branch, subsidiary, or affiliate
KOR.notes: For essential professionals who have worked at least one year at the overseas headquarters or affiliate and are dispatched to the Korean entity (D-7-1 for-profit, D-7-2 public/non-profit). Renewable multi-year residence; employer sponsorship required.

KOR.name: D-6 Religious Worker Visa
KOR.purpose: Missionaries, clergy, and social workers dispatched by a recognised religious or affiliated social-welfare organisation
KOR.notes: For religious/missionary work or affiliated social-welfare activities under an organisation recognised abroad and its Korean counterpart. Renewable; dispatch/recommendation documents required.

KOR.name: D-5 Long-term News Coverage (Journalist) Visa
KOR.purpose: Foreign correspondents and journalists posted to Korea for long-term news coverage
KOR.notes: For staff of overseas media dispatched to a Korean branch/bureau or contracted correspondents. Renewable; assignment letter and press credentials required. Distinct from the C-1 short-term news-coverage status used for stays under 90 days.

KOR.name: D-1 Culture and Arts Visa
KOR.purpose: Non-profit academic, cultural, or artistic activity, including study or research of traditional Korean arts
KOR.notes: For persons engaged in non-profit cultural or artistic activities, or studying/researching Korean arts under expert guidance. Not for paid performances, which use the E-6 Arts and Entertainment visa. Renewable.

KOR.name: D-3 Industrial Trainee Visa
KOR.purpose: On-site industrial/technical training at a Korean company for staff of an overseas affiliate or partner
KOR.notes: For technical trainees dispatched to a Korean manufacturing/industrial facility, typically within a foreign-invested or affiliated company. Training-based; distinct from the D-4 general/language trainee status. Being progressively narrowed as employment routes expand.

KOR.name: E-3 Research Visa
KOR.purpose: Researchers invited by a public or private institution to conduct research in natural sciences or advanced technology
KOR.notes: For researchers in science/engineering or high-tech fields at a government-approved institute, university, or corporate R&D centre. Host institution sponsorship required; renewable.

KOR.name: E-4 Technical Instruction (Technology Transfer) Visa
KOR.purpose: Specialists providing technical instruction or technology transfer under contract with a Korean organisation
KOR.notes: For engineers/technicians supplying specialised technology or know-how not readily available domestically under a technology-introduction contract. Contract and employer sponsorship required; renewable.

KOR.name: E-5 Professional Employment Visa
KOR.purpose: Holders of a Korean national licence practising a licensed profession (e.g. lawyer, doctor, accountant, pilot, licensed engineer)
KOR.notes: For foreign nationals authorised under Korean law to practise a licensed profession, employed under contract with a Korean organisation. Requires the relevant Korean qualification/licence; renewable.

KOR.name: E-8 Seasonal Worker Visa
KOR.purpose: Short-term seasonal labour in agriculture and fisheries arranged through Korean local governments
KOR.notes: Introduced/expanded from October 2025, replacing the former C-4 seasonal sub-types. Recruited by Korean local governments via government-to-government MOUs or marriage-migrant referrals; individuals cannot apply directly. A single grant is up to 5 months and total stay cannot exceed 8 months. 2026 national quota 109,100. Sub-types: E-8-1/E-8-2 agriculture, E-8-3/E-8-4 fisheries.

KOR.name: E-10 Maritime Crew Visa
KOR.purpose: Crew members on Korean-operated vessels (coastal/offshore fishing, cargo, cruise) under an employment contract
KOR.notes: For seafarers employed on ships operated by a Korean shipping or fishing company under the Seafarers Act (E-10-1 fishing, E-10-2 cargo/passenger, E-10-3 cruise). Employer sponsorship required; renewable.

KWT.name: Tourist Visit Visa (Sticker/Embassy Visa)
KWT.purpose: Short-term tourism and leisure visits to Kuwait. Applicant must have a Kuwaiti resident or citizen sponsor.
KWT.notes: Fee is 10 KWD per month (approximately USD 33/month). Application submitted in person to the General Department of Immigration in the relevant governorate. Required documents: visit application form, passport copy (minimum 6-month validity), proof of kinship, recent salary certificate or work permit of sponsor, sponsor's Civil ID copy, hotel authorization if applicable. Visa on arrival available at Kuwait International Airport for nationals of 53 eligible countries (see visa_on_arrival policy). Extension possible via separate Temporary Residence extension service.

KWT.name: Tourist E-Visa
KWT.purpose: Electronic pre-arrival visa for tourism and leisure visits to Kuwait, available online for nationals of 53 eligible countries and GCC residents.
KWT.notes: Fee is 3 KWD (approximately USD 10). Available to nationals of 53 countries and GCC residents (excluding Afghan, Bangladeshi, Iranian, Iraqi, Pakistani, Yemeni nationals). Apply via kuwaitvisa.moi.gov.kw. Processing 1–3 business days. Land and sea arrivals must obtain e-visa or embassy visa in advance; air arrivals from eligible countries may also use visa on arrival. Portal relaunched January 2025, enhanced June 2026. For multiple-entry options, check portal at time of application.

KWT.name: Family Visit Visa
KWT.purpose: Allows relatives of Kuwait citizens or residents to visit their family members in Kuwait for a temporary period.
KWT.notes: Fee is 10 KWD per month. Application submitted to General Department of Immigration. Required documents: designated visit application form, visitor's passport copy (minimum 6-month validity), proof of kinship (embassy oath certificates not accepted for some nationalities), recent salary certificate for government-employed foreign sponsors, sponsor's Civil ID copy. Embassy oath certificates not accepted as proof of kinship; must use official government-issued kinship documents. Both Kuwaiti citizens and non-Kuwaiti residents can sponsor family visitors.

KWT.name: Family Visit E-Visa
KWT.purpose: Electronic pre-arrival visa for family visits to Kuwait, for nationals of 53 eligible countries.
KWT.notes: Fee is 3 KWD (approximately USD 10). Maximum stay 30 days (shorter than tourist e-visa at 90 days). One of four e-visa categories offered via kuwaitvisa.moi.gov.kw: tourist (90 days), family visit (30 days), business (30 days), official. Available to nationals of the same 53 countries eligible for tourist e-visa.

KWT.name: Medical Treatment Visit Visa
KWT.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals seeking medical treatment at Kuwait hospitals or healthcare facilities.
KWT.notes: Fee is 10 KWD per month. Requires a letter issued by the Kuwait Ministry of Health confirming the visitor has been accepted for treatment at a Kuwait hospital. Required documents: designated visit application form, passport copy (minimum 6-month validity), Ministry of Health acceptance letter, sponsor's Civil ID copy. Application submitted to General Department of Immigration.

KWT.name: Business Visit E-Visa (Commercial Visit)
KWT.purpose: Electronic pre-arrival visa for foreign nationals visiting Kuwait for business purposes in the private sector.
KWT.notes: Fee is 3 KWD (approximately USD 10). Maximum stay 30 days. One of four e-visa categories on kuwaitvisa.moi.gov.kw. Available to nationals of 53 eligible countries. SUSPENSION NOTE: Suspended for all nationalities on 10 June 2026; RESUMED for all nationalities on 19 June 2026 per Fragomen alert. Tourist e-visa category remained operational throughout the suspension. NOTE: A separate Fragomen advisory (September 3, 2025) reports resumption of the sponsored Commercial Visit Visa for Pakistani nationals - this is a single-entry visa issued only at the request of a company registered in Kuwait (employer/sponsor-conditional), NOT a visa-on-arrival nor a general ordinary-passport e-visa grant. Pakistani nationals remain excluded from the standard 53-country e-visa/visa-on-arrival facility. Fragomen is an immigration-advisory firm, not an official Kuwaiti government source.

KWT.name: Entrance Visa to Work in the Government Sector
KWT.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals who have secured employment with the Kuwait government or civil service.
KWT.notes: For foreign nationals hired by Kuwaiti government entities. Application submitted to General Department of Immigration. Specific fee amounts and visa duration were not published on the official e.gov.kw page at time of research. The e.gov.kw page URL was not accessible directly (HTTP 404) but linked from official portal navigation.

KWT.name: Work Visa for Temporary Government Contract
KWT.purpose: Entry visa for foreign workers engaged under temporary government contracts administered through the Public Authority for Manpower.
KWT.notes: Fee is 10 KWD (fixed). Required documents include: letter from the Government Contracts and Projects Department of the Public Authority for Manpower, financial guarantee statement showing worker count and guarantee amount, application form, passport copy (minimum 6-month validity), legal entity signature authorization, valid representative ID. Application submitted in person to General Department of Immigration.

KWT.name: Business Visit Visa (Private Sector Work Visa)
KWT.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals seeking employment or business activities in Kuwait's private sector.
KWT.notes: Listed under 'Working in Kuwait' and 'Moving to Kuwait' sections on the Kuwait Government Online portal (e.gov.kw). Separate from the e-visa business category. For private sector employment. Specific fee amounts and duration were not published on an accessible official page at time of research.

KWT.name: Entrance Visa to Join Provider (Family Reunification/Dependent Visa)
KWT.purpose: Dependent entry visa allowing family members to join employees working in Kuwait's government or private sectors.
KWT.notes: Fee is 10 KWD fixed plus variable fees. Sponsor minimum salary: KWD 450 per month (unless one of 15 exempt professions). Required documents: entry visa application form, sponsored person's passport copy (minimum 2-year validity), sponsor's Civil ID, proof of kinship (passport for Arab nationals; embassy certificate for non-Arab nationals), work permit (private sector) or salary certificate (government sector). For Article 19 holders: license or company contract copy required. Article 24 holders: reviewed at Director General's discretion. Application submitted to General Department of Immigration.

KWT.name: Government/State Visit Visa
KWT.purpose: Official entry visa for foreign government officials and delegations visiting Kuwait on state business.
KWT.notes: Listed under 'Working in Kuwait' section on e.gov.kw portal. For official government delegations and state visitors. Specific fees and duration not published on an accessible official page at time of research (HTTP 404 on direct page access). Processed through General Department of Immigration.

KWT.name: Official E-Visa
KWT.purpose: Electronic pre-arrival visa for foreign nationals visiting Kuwait on official business for government delegations.
KWT.notes: One of four e-visa categories offered via kuwaitvisa.moi.gov.kw: tourist (90 days), family visit (30 days), business (30 days), official. Specific eligibility criteria and maximum stay duration for official category not specified in accessible official sources. Fee estimated at 3 KWD (same as other e-visa categories).

KWT.name: Temporary Residence / Visit Extension
KWT.purpose: Extension of an existing temporary visit or residence permit for foreign nationals already in Kuwait.
KWT.notes: Fee is 1 KWD fixed plus 1 KWD per month variable (approximately USD 3 fixed + USD 3/month). For individuals with existing temporary residence status seeking to prolong their stay. Required documents: original passport and copy, entry visa documentation, two passport photos, sponsor's Civil ID copy, health insurance certificate, work permit from Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor, signed authorization forms. Application submitted to General Department of Immigration. Residence Application Form must be signed by the sponsor.

KWT.name: First Time Residence Permit for Civil Sector Employees
KWT.purpose: Initial residence permit for foreign nationals employed in Kuwait's civil (government) sector for the first time.
KWT.notes: Listed under 'Immigration and Travel' section on e.gov.kw portal. Specific fees, processing times, and duration not available from accessible official pages at time of research. Part of Kuwait's kafala (employer-sponsor) residency system. Ministry of Interior General Department of Residency Affairs handles applications.

KWT.name: Student Visa (Study/Student Permit Entry Visa)
KWT.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals admitted to a Kuwaiti educational institution and holding a Student Permit, in order to study in Kuwait.
KWT.notes: Issued by Kuwaiti embassies/consulates (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) to students holding a Student Permit; converted to a study-based residence (iqama) after arrival. Requirements: passport valid at least 2 years, MOFA visa application form, photo, HIV test, health certificate (hepatitis B & C, malaria, filariasis, syphilis, chest X-ray for TB) issued within 3 months, No Criminal Record (FBI for U.S. applicants) and a Student Permit. Fee is USD 175 for U.S. citizens plus USD 25 for police-clearance authentication; fees vary by nationality/consulate. Not offered as an e-visa or visa on arrival. Source: official Kuwait MOFA embassy page (washington.mofa.gov.kw).

KWT.name: Domestic Worker Visa (Article 20)
KWT.purpose: Residence/work visa for foreign nationals employed as domestic workers (maids, drivers, nannies, household helpers) under the sponsorship of a Kuwaiti citizen or resident.
KWT.notes: Kafala 'Article 20' visa category for domestic staff, distinct from the Article 18 private-sector work visa and the Article 17 government-sector work visa. Sponsored by a Kuwaiti citizen or resident who must meet salary and housing requirements; recruitment is through agencies registered with the Public Authority for Manpower with a notarized employment contract. Residence permit (iqama) is issued by the Ministry of Interior General Department of Residency Affairs and renewed annually. First-time civil registration of the worker is completed online via the Public Authority for Civil Information (PACI) service linked here.
