Commonly issued to nationals of the Philippines, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bangladesh.

KWT.name: Private Sector Work Permit (Article 18)
KWT.purpose: The principal work authorization for foreign nationals employed by a private-sector company in Kuwait, sponsored by the employer under Article 18 of the residency (kafala) system.
KWT.notes: Article 18 is the standard private-sector work permit, distinct from the Article 17 government-sector permit and the Article 20 domestic-worker permit. The employer must hold a valid commercial registration and available work-permit quota and submits the application through the Public Authority for Manpower (PAM) 'Ashal' e-portal (e-portal.manpower.gov.kw). Work-permit fee is KWD 150 (approximately USD 490) under Ministerial Resolution No. 4 of 2025, effective June 2025. The related Ministry of Interior entry visa is captured separately in this list as the 'Business Visit Visa (Private Sector Work Visa)'; after entry the worker receives a residence permit (iqama), typically valid 1-3 years and renewable annually. End-to-end work-permit plus iqama processing is roughly 4-8 weeks. Requirements published officially by the Kuwait Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Requirements for a Work Visa - Private and Government Sectors); permit administered by the Public Authority for Manpower (manpower.gov.kw).

LAO.name: Tourist e-Visa (Travel Visa)
LAO.purpose: Single-entry tourist visa issued electronically by the Lao Ministry of Foreign Affairs for leisure travel and tourism.
LAO.notes: Available to approximately 162 nationalities. Validity 60 days from issuance; maximum stay 30 days from first entry. Processing is typically 3 working days; same-day processing for morning submissions (Laos time, GMT+7). Entry via 9 designated checkpoints including Vientiane and Luang Prabang international airports, Friendship Bridges, and railway stations. Passport must have at least 180 days validity. Non-refundable fee. eVisa Approval Letter must be presented at port of entry.

LAO.name: Visit e-Visa
LAO.purpose: Single-entry visa issued electronically for visiting hosts, organizations, or attending meetings and conferences in Laos.
LAO.notes: Second e-visa category issued through laoevisa.gov.la alongside the Travel Visa (tourist). Same fee, validity, processing, and entry restrictions as the tourist e-visa. Intended for visiting family, organizations, meetings. Available to the same ~162 eligible nationalities.

LAO.name: Visa on Arrival (VOA)
LAO.purpose: Sticker visa issued at designated international border checkpoints for short-stay tourism and general visits for most nationalities.
LAO.notes: Available to most nationalities at designated international airports and border crossings. Stay up to 30 days; extension possible twice for a maximum total stay of 90 days. Nationals of 32 restricted countries (including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Syria, and others) must obtain a visa at a Lao embassy/consulate before travel. Requires valid passport with sufficient validity, passport photo, and visa fee (amount varies; typically USD 30–42 depending on nationality and checkpoint, but official USD amount not confirmed from official source).

LAO.name: Embassy/Consulate Sticker Visa (Tourist - Type T-B3)
LAO.purpose: Traditional sticker visa for tourism obtained from a Lao embassy or consulate before travel, used by nationalities ineligible for e-visa or VOA.
LAO.notes: Official tourist category is T-B3 per the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR (an earlier entry mislabelled this as 'TR', which is the transit code). Required for the 32 VOA-restricted nationalities (e.g., Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Syria, Sudan, Zimbabwe, and others). Also an option for any nationality preferring an embassy visa. Multiple-entry variants may be available at embassies. Fees and processing times vary by embassy/consulate.

LAO.name: Business Visa (Type NI-B2)
LAO.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals conducting business activities, attending meetings, or engaging in commercial activities in Laos.
LAO.notes: Official category NI-B2 (Business Visa) per the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to foreign business people (including family members) coming for investment or economic data collection. Issued at Lao embassies and consulates abroad. Extension and conversion to longer-term stay permit may be available through the Department of Immigration in Laos. Exact fee and validity vary by embassy. VOA can sometimes be used for initial business visits followed by status adjustment in-country.

LAO.name: Labour Visa (Type LA-B2)
LAO.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals employed by companies or organizations registered in Laos, allowing residence and employment.
LAO.notes: Official category LA-B2 (Labour Visa) per the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to foreigners and stateless persons who come to work as laborers in Laos, including their family members. Requires sponsorship from a Laos-registered employer. Work permits (bai anuyat tham ngan) issued separately by the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare. Stay permit cards issued by Department of Immigration in 3-month, 6-month, or 12-month increments (fees: 300,000 / 600,000 / 1,200,000 LAK respectively). Managed through the One Stop Service for investors/companies via investlaos.gov.la.

LAO.name: Investor Visa (Type NI-B2) / Business Visa for Investors
LAO.purpose: Long-term visa and stay permit for foreign investors legally approved by the Government of Lao PDR, covering investors, shareholders, directors, technical officers, and their family members.
LAO.notes: Requires investment license, concession registration, or enterprise registration issued by IPMC (Investment Promotion and Management Committee). Stay permit cards issued in 3-month (300,000 LAK), 6-month (600,000 LAK), or 12-month (1,200,000 LAK) increments. Long-term stay permits of 3–5 years available only for concession holders with 10+ year government agreements. Managed through One Stop Service at investlaos.gov.la. Family members of eligible investors also covered.

LAO.name: Student Visa (Type ST-B2)
LAO.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals enrolled in educational institutions in Laos for study purposes.
LAO.notes: Official category ST-B2 (Student Visa) per the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to students who come to study, research, collect data or undertake a technical internship in Laos. Requires acceptance letter from a recognized Lao educational institution. Renewable annually through the Department of Immigration. Specific fee and processing details not confirmed from accessible official sources.

LAO.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa Exemption
LAO.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports under bilateral agreements between Laos and partner countries.
LAO.notes: Laos has bilateral diplomatic/service passport exemption agreements with 40+ countries. Stay durations vary: 14 days (Indonesia diplomatic/service), 30 days (most bilateral agreements), 90 days (Japan, South Korea, Czech Republic, Slovak Republic, Poland, Cuba, Brazil, Mexico, Peru, Hungary, Georgia, Norway diplomatic only). Ordinary passport holders under these agreements may or may not be visa-free depending on the specific bilateral treaty.

LAO.name: Transit Visa (Type TR-B3)
LAO.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals transiting through Laos en route to a third country.
LAO.notes: Official category TR-B3 (Transit Visa) per the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to foreigners and stateless persons whose travel is to transit through Laos to another country. Specific stay limit and fee are not published on the official page; contact the nearest Lao embassy for current requirements.

LAO.name: Spouse Visa (Type SP-B3)
LAO.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreigners and stateless persons who have legally registered their marriage with a Lao citizen.
LAO.notes: Official category SP-B3 (Spouse Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to foreigners and stateless persons who have legally registered their marriage with a Lao citizen under Lao law. Applied for and renewed in-country through the Department of Immigration; a stay permit card is issued in 3-, 6-, or 12-month increments (300,000 / 600,000 / 1,200,000 LAK). Exact fee and validity are not published on the official page.

LAO.name: Short-Term Visa (Type NI-B3)
LAO.purpose: Short-stay non-immigrant visa for foreign technical officers attending meetings, trainings or study tours, and for visiting relatives/friends, collecting investment information or coordinating commerce.
LAO.notes: Official category NI-B3 (Short-Term Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR. Issued to foreign technical officers approved to temporarily come for meetings, trainings or study tours, and to foreigners/stateless persons visiting parents, relatives or friends, collecting investment information, coordinating commerce or other lawful short-stay purposes. The e-Visa 'Visit Visa' is the online equivalent for eligible nationalities. Fee, validity and stay length are not published on the official page.

LAO.name: Expert Visa (Type E-B2)
LAO.purpose: Visa for foreign experts, technicians and NGO staff employed or contracted by government, private or international organizations, including their family members.
LAO.notes: Official category E-B2 (Expert Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR. Issued to experts and staff of Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) approved to perform their duties in Laos, and to experts and technicians employed or contracted by government, private or other international organizations, including their family members. Requires a work permit from the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and a stay permit card from the Department of Immigration (300,000 / 600,000 / 1,200,000 LAK for 3/6/12 months). Distinct from the LA-B2 Labour Visa used for general laborers.

LAO.name: Long-Term Visa (Type I-B3)
LAO.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign laborers and their family members, and for long-stay foreigners contributing to national development or with sufficient financial means.
LAO.notes: Official category I-B3 (Long-Term Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR. Issued to foreigners/stateless persons working as laborers (with family members), those whose contributions benefit national protection and development, and general long-stay foreigners. General long-stay applicants must hold at least USD 20,000 in a Lao bank account for a six-month stay, or USD 40,000 for a one-year stay (a bank-balance requirement, not a visa fee). Stay permit card fees are 300,000 / 600,000 / 1,200,000 LAK for 3/6/12 months.

LAO.name: Courtesy Visa (Type C-B1)
LAO.purpose: Visa for staff of bilateral cooperation offices, UN/international organization personnel, foreign experts on inter-government cooperation or grant-aid projects, invited seminar/training speakers, and certain embassy household staff and VIPs.
LAO.notes: Official category C-B1 (Courtesy Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR. Covers staff of bilateral cooperation offices and of UN/international organizations posted in Laos, foreign experts/technical officers on inter-governmental cooperation or foreign voluntary grant-assistance projects, loan-collection/monitoring officers, foreign experts invited to run seminars or trainings, non-Lao household staff of embassies/consulates/diplomats' residences, honorary VIPs on movement plans, and the family members of these persons. Requires a letter of proposal from the relevant organization.

LAO.name: Media Visa (Type M-B2)
LAO.purpose: Visa for foreign journalists who come to collect news in the Lao PDR.
LAO.notes: Official category M-B2 (Media Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to foreign journalists and media personnel who come to collect news in Laos. Typically requires prior approval/accreditation from the Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism and/or Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Fee and validity are not published on the official page.

LAO.name: Permanent Visa (Type P-B3)
LAO.purpose: Long-term visa for foreigners and stateless persons approved to reside permanently in the Lao PDR.
LAO.notes: Official category P-B3 (Permanent Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR, issued to foreigners and stateless persons who are approved to permanently reside in Laos. Subject to government approval; conditions, validity and fees are not published on the official page.

LAO.name: Diplomatic Visa (Type D-A1)
LAO.purpose: Visa for foreign diplomats, consular officers, high-level government delegations and representatives of the United Nations and international organizations, and their dependents, on official duty in the Lao PDR.
LAO.notes: Class 'A' visa category (D-A1, Diplomatic Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR. Issued to diplomats, consuls and representatives of international organizations and their dependents authorized for short- or long-term duty in Laos, and to high-level government delegations. Distinct from the separate visa-exemption agreements that already cover many diplomatic/service passport holders. Applied for through Lao embassies/consulates and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; normally fee-exempt on a reciprocal basis. Stay length and validity are set per posting and are not published on the official page.

LAO.name: Official Visa (Type S-A2)
LAO.purpose: Visa for administrative and technical staff of foreign embassies, consulates and governmental/international organizations, members of official delegations, and their dependents.
LAO.notes: Class 'A' visa category (S-A2, Official/Service Visa) listed by the Department of Immigration of Lao PDR. Issued to international diplomats and members of governmental organizations, and to administrative/technical staff of embassies and consulates and their dependents. Distinct from the separate visa-exemption agreements that already cover many service passport holders. Applied for through Lao embassies/consulates and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Stay length, validity and fee are set per posting and are not published on the official page.

LBN.name: Tourist / Visit Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Lebanon for tourism, leisure, or personal visits. Issued at airport/border for eligible nationalities or through Lebanese embassies abroad.
LBN.notes: Free for Section One countries (USA, UK, EU, Australia, Japan, Canada, etc.) and certain Arab nationals; extendable to 3 months at no cost. Arab nationals from Algeria, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia, Libya, etc. require round-trip ticket, hotel reservation, and USD 2,000 equivalent. Standard fee of 2,000,000 LBP applies where charged. Israel passport holders and those with Israeli stamps are refused entry.

LBN.name: Collective Tourist Group Visa
LBN.purpose: For organized tourist groups of 8 or more members travelling together to Lebanon.
LBN.notes: Groups from visa-exempt countries pay no fee. Nationals from Nigeria, Ghana, and Ivory Coast in tourist groups are charged 2,450,000 LBP per group member. Group must travel together and depart together. Prior authorization from General Security required for nationalities that need pre-clearance.

LBN.name: Transit Visa
LBN.purpose: For travelers passing through Lebanon en route to a third country without intending to stay.
LBN.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category (single or double entry) at a fee of 2,000,000 LBP. Issued through Lebanese embassies or at border for eligible nationalities. Israel passport holders and those with Israeli stamps refused. Entry/transit conditions mirror tourist visa nationality tiers.

LBN.name: Business / Commercial Visa
LBN.purpose: For investors, businessmen, traders, and professionals entering Lebanon for commercial consultations, training, or business activities.
LBN.notes: Investors and businessmen with accreditation from IDAL (Investment Development Authority of Lebanon) or an official invitation from a Lebanese business entity may receive a 6-month visa. Traders from certain Arab countries (Iraq, Yemen, etc.) with chamber of commerce registration, and doctors/engineers with professional board certification, may be auto-issued a visa on arrival. Fee: 2,000,000 LBP where applicable.

LBN.name: Work Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals authorized to work in Lebanon under a contract approved by the Ministry of Labor.
LBN.notes: Requires prior authorization from General Security and Ministry of Labor before entry. Valid for 3 months, renewable once (total maximum 1 month per renewal per official source). Nationalities from worker-exporting countries (Bangladesh, India, Philippines, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, etc.) must obtain pre-authorization. Work visa category listed at fee of 2,000,000 LBP. Domestic workers have a separate category with specific conditions.

LBN.name: Domestic Worker / Household Staff Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals employed as domestic workers (maids, caregivers, cleaners) in Lebanese households.
LBN.notes: Subject to specific conditions and prior authorization. Nationalities include workers from South/Southeast Asia (Philippines, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, etc.) and parts of Africa. Employee must leave Lebanon with their employer or following end of contract. Tied to employer sponsorship.

LBN.name: Foreign Technical Expert / Port Entry Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign technical or administrative specialists brought in for short-term expert work at Lebanese ports, and for foreign sailors and maritime inspectors boarding vessels.
LBN.notes: One-month non-renewable entry visa for foreign experts performing technical or administrative work at ports; stays beyond one month must qualify under first-class worker (work permit) requirements. Requires certified passport copy (6+ months validity), certified enterprise registration documents, documentation of the foreigner's profession, and employer-provided insurance. Foreign sailors and maritime specialists (superintendents, inspectors, marine surveyors) boarding foreign ships are issued a transit visa. Applied for through the enterprise's public relations bureau.

LBN.name: Artist / Performer Visa
LBN.purpose: For entertainers, artists, models, nightclub performers, and spa/massage workers performing or contracted in Lebanon.
LBN.notes: Issued by the Department of Artists at General Security under special conditions. Requires prior General Security authorization regardless of nationality. Female citizens ages 17-45 classified as artists or masseuses from certain countries (Eastern Europe, Central Asia, some East Asian nations) face additional scrutiny and mandatory pre-authorization even if their nationality is otherwise visa-on-arrival eligible. Specific categories include nightclub performers, models, and spa/massage workers.

LBN.name: Student Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in or accepted to educational institutions in Lebanon.
LBN.notes: Arab students receive a free 3-month student visa upon presenting a valid student card or admission certificate from an accredited Lebanese institution. Non-Arab students follow their nationality's standard tourist/entry visa process then convert to a residency permit. Visa listed as a distinct sub-category under visit visas (post/159). Religious students, volunteers, missionaries, and clergy have a separate sub-category.

LBN.name: Religious / Missionary / Volunteer Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign clergy, religious students, volunteers, and missionaries serving or studying in Lebanon.
LBN.notes: Explicitly listed as a separate visa sub-category on the General Security site. Foreigners affiliated with the Vatican have a specific track. Requires documentation of affiliation with a recognized religious or humanitarian organization registered in Lebanon.

LBN.name: Medical / Sanitary Services Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Lebanon to receive medical treatment or access sanitary services.
LBN.notes: Explicitly listed as a visit visa sub-category on general-security.gov.lb/en/posts/159. Applicant must present documentation from a Lebanese medical facility confirming appointment or treatment plan. Conditions (duration, fee) follow standard visit visa rules for the applicant's nationality.

LBN.name: Family Visit / Reunion Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Lebanon to visit family members or for family reunification purposes.
LBN.notes: Listed as a distinct sub-category under visit visas (friendship/relationship visits and family reasons). Marriage certificates must conform to current Lebanese regulations for spousal applications. Spouse of a Lebanese national may qualify for extended stay. GCC nationals' domestic workers (maids, drivers, bodyguards) accompanying their employer-family are covered under employer's GCC entry.

LBN.name: Engagement / Fiance(e) Visit Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Lebanon to join a fiance(e) or for engagement purposes, with the option to marry during the same stay.
LBN.notes: Explicitly listed as a distinct visit-visa sub-category ('engagement visit') on general-security.gov.lb/en/posts/159, separate from the general family visit. Requires standard visit-visa documents plus proof of engagement; the same visit may be used to complete the marriage without submitting a second application. Non-renewable and cannot be converted to a work visa without a decision of the General Director of General Security. Standard visit-visa fee of 2,000,000 LBP applies where charged.

LBN.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
LBN.purpose: For holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports accredited to Lebanon or transiting on official duty.
LBN.notes: Free multiple-entry 6-month visa issued at airport/border to all countries' diplomats, UN personnel, and DCAF workers. Many bilateral diplomatic passport waiver agreements exist (Armenia, Brazil, Colombia, Cyprus, Greece, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Liechtenstein, Malta, Switzerland, Venezuela) granting full visa-free entry. Domestic workers of accredited diplomats are also covered.

LBN.name: Investor Residence Permit
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals making a qualifying investment in Lebanon seeking annual residence.
LBN.notes: Requires a blocked bank account of at least 150,000,000 LBP at a Lebanese bank (3-month statement, bank-signed), lease contract or title deed, investment contracts, commercial register extract, and professional license. Annual renewal required. Mandatory health insurance for foreigners. Path to permanent residence or citizenship is not officially documented.

LBN.name: Annual Residence Permit (Foreign Worker)
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals holding an approved annual work permit who reside in Lebanon, together with their accompanying spouse and children.
LBN.notes: Renewable annual residency granted to foreign workers and tied to a valid Ministry of Labor work permit; validity follows the passport's remaining validity (must exceed 6 months, capped at one year). Spouse and children may obtain dependent annual residence with a marriage certificate, a notarized non-working attestation, and a passport valid at least one year (fee same as the sponsoring worker). Renewal requires a signed request from the employer, guarantor, or representative. Minors are exempt from fees; applicants over 64 are exempt from the work attestation.

LBN.name: Residence Permit for Spouse / Family of a Lebanese National
LBN.purpose: For foreign spouses and close family members of Lebanese citizens seeking to reside in Lebanon.
LBN.notes: Free (0 LBP) renewable annual residency for foreign wives of Lebanese men, foreign mothers of Lebanese children (divorced or widowed and not remarried), widows of Lebanese or Palestinian citizens, and dependent parents or single sisters of Lebanese citizens. Requires the relevant marriage, birth, or death certificate and a notarized non-working attestation (applicants over 64 are exempt from the work attestation). Distinct from the short-stay Family Visit visa - this is a residence permit. Validity follows the passport's remaining validity (6 months to one year).

LBN.name: Annual Residence for Persons of Means (Independent Income)
LBN.purpose: For financially self-sufficient foreigners - including retirees and those living on foreign income - who reside in Lebanon without taking local employment.
LBN.notes: Annual residency for 'persons of means' evidenced by a blocked Lebanese bank account of at least 1,000,000,000 LBP or a monthly income of at least 50,000,000 LBP. Fee 0 LBP. Family members receive automatic dependent permits (except adult males). This is Lebanon's de facto retirement / independent-means residency - there is no separately named retirement or digital-nomad visa. Validity follows the passport's remaining validity (6 months to one year).

LBN.name: Converting Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals already in Lebanon seeking to change their visa/entry status to a different category (e.g., tourist to work).
LBN.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category on general-security.gov.lb/en/posts/37 with a standard fee of 2,000,000 LBP. Allows change of status within Lebanon without exiting. Specific eligible conversions and conditions are not detailed on the publicly available official page.

LBN.name: Renewing Visa
LBN.purpose: For foreign nationals extending their current visa or stay authorization while already in Lebanon.
LBN.notes: Listed as a distinct category on general-security.gov.lb/en/posts/37 with a fee of 2,000,000 LBP. Tourist/visit visas (initially 1 month) are typically extended free of charge up to 3 months at General Security offices. Extensions beyond 3 months are subject to approval and may require additional documentation. Visa validity cannot exceed the holder's passport validity.

LBN.name: Courtesy Visa
LBN.purpose: For VIPs and dignitaries entering Lebanon on a complimentary basis at the discretion of Lebanese authorities.
LBN.notes: Granted at the discretion of the General Director of General Security or through Lebanese embassies/delegations abroad. Reserved for VIPs. No publicly published criteria or application process.

LBR.name: Electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VoA) - Tourism
LBR.purpose: Permits entry to Liberia for tourism purposes for nationals whose country lacks a Liberian embassy.
LBR.notes: Must apply online before travel at visaonarrival.lis.gov.lr. Available only at Roberts International Airport (ROB), Monrovia. Stay of 30 or 90 days is determined by immigration officer at arrival. Approval valid for 3 months from issuance date. If a Liberian embassy exists in the traveler's country, they must apply there instead. Covers tourism, business, and transit purposes. ECOWAS citizens are exempt (visa-free). Fee is non-refundable. Launched March 11, 2025. Re-confirmed operational June 2026.

LBR.name: Electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VoA) - Business
LBR.purpose: Permits entry to Liberia for business purposes for nationals whose country lacks a Liberian embassy.
LBR.notes: Same e-VoA system covers tourism, business, and transit. Must apply online before travel. Available only at Roberts International Airport (ROB), Monrovia. Stay determined by immigration officer (30 or 90 days). If a Liberian embassy exists in the traveler's country, they must apply there instead. ECOWAS citizens are exempt.

LBR.name: Electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VoA) - Transit
LBR.purpose: Permits transit through Liberia for travelers whose country lacks a Liberian embassy.
LBR.notes: Transit is one of the stated eligible purposes for the e-VoA. Must apply online before travel at visaonarrival.lis.gov.lr. Available only at Roberts International Airport (ROB), Monrovia. ECOWAS citizens are exempt.

LBR.name: Resident Permit
LBR.purpose: Required for all foreign nationals wishing to remain in Liberia beyond 90 days, covering long-term residence including work, study, or family.
LBR.notes: Apply via rp.lis.gov.lr. Fees vary by nationality: Non-African USD 750, Non-ECOWAS African USD 600, ECOWAS Citizen USD 150. Renewal fees: Non-African USD 350, Non-ECOWAS African USD 300, ECOWAS Citizen USD 100. Replacement (lost/stolen): USD 50-100. Status adjustment (employer/address change): USD 100-400. Processing takes approximately 2 weeks after biometric appointment. In-person biometric appointment required. Each dependent must apply separately. Fees are non-refundable. Appointment can be rescheduled maximum twice.

LBR.name: Re-entry Permit Card
LBR.purpose: Permits foreign nationals already in Liberia to leave and re-enter multiple times during their approved stay without applying for a new Visa on Arrival each trip.
LBR.notes: Applied for via the dedicated LIS portal reentryvisa.lis.gov.lr (biometric enrolment done in person in Monrovia). The card is valid for 6 months or 1 year and allows multiple entries; holders must still exit after 90 days and re-enter to continue their stay. Two types: RESIDENCE (for holders of a valid Liberian residence permit) and SPECIAL (for other foreigners without a residence permit). A Visa on Arrival must be obtained first. Fee not published on the official portal. Requires a passport valid 6+ months. Corrected 2026-07: official_url updated from lis.gov.lr homepage to the dedicated reentryvisa.lis.gov.lr portal (listed on lis.gov.lr/index.php/visa-passes/); added validity and RESIDENCE/SPECIAL type detail.

LBR.name: Tourist Visa (Consular / Embassy-Issued)
LBR.purpose: Tourism/leisure travel for nationals of countries where a Liberian embassy or consulate exists, who must apply at the mission rather than use the e-VoA.
LBR.notes: Issued as a 'Regular' visa by Liberian embassies/consulates for nationals of the ~23 countries that have a Liberian mission (who are NOT eligible for the e-VoA and must apply at the embassy). Validity-tiered fees per the Embassy in Washington DC and the Consulate General in New York: single-entry 1-3 months USD 70; multiple-entry 1 year USD 150; 2 years USD 250; 3 years USD 350 (US citizens: USD 180 for a 3-year multiple-entry visa). Requirements: passport valid 6+ months, passport photo(s), yellow fever vaccination certificate, round-trip itinerary, prepaid return envelope. Standard processing ~12 working days; expedite +USD 75 (same-day) or +USD 50 (next-day). Fees non-refundable, paid by money order/cashier's check. ECOWAS citizens are visa-exempt.

LBR.name: Business Visa (Consular / Embassy-Issued)
LBR.purpose: Business travel for nationals of countries where a Liberian embassy or consulate exists.
LBR.notes: Same 'Regular' visa channel and validity-tiered fees as the consular tourist visa (single-entry 1-3 months USD 70; 1 year USD 150; 2 years USD 250; 3 years USD 350; US citizens USD 180 for a 3-year multiple-entry visa). Additional requirement: a letter on company letterhead assuming financial responsibility for the traveler. Issued by Liberian embassies/consulates to nationals of countries with a Liberian mission (not eligible for e-VoA). Yellow fever certificate required. ECOWAS citizens are visa-exempt.

LBR.name: Employment Permit - Category A (Formal Sector)
LBR.purpose: Mandatory work authorization for foreign nationals (aliens) employed in the formal sector - institutions, corporations, partnerships, other entities and self-employed aliens.
LBR.notes: Issued by the Ministry of Labour (MoL) under Regulation No. 17 (Labour Employment Permit Regulation, 2025). All foreigners must hold a valid work permit before starting work. Category A (formal-sector employment) fee: USD 1,000 per the 2025 regulation; note the MoL announced a fee increase for ordinary/regular work permits to USD 3,000 in September 2025 (other categories to be revised later). Valid one calendar year from issuance, reviewed/renewed annually. A work permit does not by itself confer residence - workers must also obtain a Resident Permit (rp.lis.gov.lr) and register with LIS Alien Registration. Applications are handled via the MoL work-permit portal (workpermit-liberia.com, contractor-operated).

LBR.name: Employment Permit - Categories B/C/D (Informal Sector & Special)
LBR.purpose: Work authorization for foreign nationals in the informal sector and special cases: ECOWAS and other African nationals, government-contract workers, humanitarian/religious workers, and spouses of resident Liberian citizens.
LBR.notes: Reduced-fee Ministry of Labour permit categories under Regulation No. 17 (2025): Category B - ECOWAS citizens in the informal sector, USD 100; Category C - non-ECOWAS Africans in the informal sector, USD 200; Category D - aliens under written contract with the Government of Liberia, employed by religious/humanitarian/not-for-profit organizations, OR married to resident Liberian citizens, USD 200. Valid one calendar year, renewed annually. Category D is the pathway used by spouses of Liberian citizens who wish to work. A separate Resident Permit and LIS alien registration are also required for stays beyond 90 days. fee_usd shown is the USD 200 tier (Categories C/D); Category B is USD 100.

LBR.name: Border Crossing Pass
LBR.purpose: Allows residents living near Liberia's land borders to conduct routine daily cross-border activities without a full visa, under regional free-movement agreements.
LBR.notes: Issued by the Liberia Immigration Service to individuals living close to a land border who conduct daily cross-border activities, per ECOWAS/Mano River Union regional agreements. Fee, validity, and detailed eligibility are not published on the official LIS portal. Distinct from the e-VoA (airport) and resident-permit categories.

LBR.name: Family Visit Visa (Consular / Embassy-Issued)
LBR.purpose: Visiting family or relatives in Liberia, for nationals of countries where a Liberian embassy or consulate exists and who must apply at the mission rather than use the e-VoA.
LBR.notes: 'Family visit' is one of the official Purpose-of-Trip categories on the Liberian visa application form (revised 2025-04-15) and is issued through the standard 'Regular' consular visa channel (Liberian missions issue only Diplomatic, Official, or Regular visas). Same validity-tiered fees as the consular tourist/business visa: single-entry 1-3 months USD 70; multiple-entry 1 year USD 150; 2 years USD 250; 3 years USD 350 (US citizens USD 180 for a 3-year multiple-entry visa). Typically supported by an invitation letter from the host/relative in Liberia; passport valid 6+ months and yellow fever vaccination certificate required. Standard processing ~12 working days; expedite +USD 75 (same-day) or +USD 50 (next-day). Issued to nationals of the ~23 countries with a Liberian mission (not eligible for e-VoA). ECOWAS citizens are visa-exempt. Note: foreign spouses of resident Liberian citizens who wish to WORK use Ministry of Labour Employment Permit Category D, and residence beyond 90 days requires a Resident Permit (rp.lis.gov.lr).

LBR.name: Diplomatic and Official Visa (Consular / Embassy-Issued)
LBR.purpose: For accredited diplomats and foreign government officials (and their immediate family and personal/household staff) travelling to Liberia solely on official duties.
LBR.notes: One of the three visa types Liberian missions issue ('Visas issued are one of the following types: Diplomatic, Official, or Regular'). Intended for diplomats and other foreign government officials travelling to Liberia 'solely to engage in official duties or activities on behalf of their national government'; immediate family members and personal employees/attendants/domestic workers of eligible officials also qualify. Requires a diplomatic (verbal) note from the sending government stating name, date of birth, position, assignment location, purpose, travel dates and anticipated length of stay, plus a passport valid 6+ months and a completed application form with photo. Holders of diplomatic and official passports presenting a verbal note are exempt from visa fees (fee_usd 0). Interviews are generally waived for diplomats (may be required for personal employees/domestic workers). Distinct from Liberia's bilateral diplomatic/official-passport visa-waiver agreements with the UAE, South Africa and China (recorded under conditional_access).

LBY.name: Libya Electronic Tourist Visa (E-Visa)
LBY.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals for tourism purposes via the official Libya e-visa portal. All tourists must be accompanied by a licensed Libyan tourism officer for the duration of their stay; independent travel is not permitted.
LBY.notes: Available to most nationalities (can_apply_online: true) via evisa.gov.ly portal. Visa is delivered by email. Not available to nationals of Iran, Pakistan, Yemen, Egypt, Morocco, Iraq, Syria, Sudan, Afghanistan, Nigeria, Chad, Bangladesh, South Sudan, and Zaire (historical) - those must apply at a Libyan embassy. Visa-free nationals (Algeria, Tunisia, Mauritania, Malaysia, Benin) do not require this visa. The USD 63 fee and 30-day stay/90-day validity parameters are confirmed by the evisa.gov.ly portal but not directly stated in the API countries endpoint.

LBY.name: Libya Work Visa
LBY.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to work in Libya, requiring a work contract or sponsorship from a Libyan employer.
LBY.notes: Work Visa is listed in the Libya e-visa portal API (integration key: 3) but has status 'currently unavailable' as of March 2024. Applications must be made through Libyan diplomatic missions. Exact fees, duration, and requirements are not published on official sources.

LBY.name: Libya Business Visa
LBY.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals for conducting business activities in Libya, including meetings, conferences, and commercial negotiations. Requires sponsorship from a Libyan company.
LBY.notes: Applied for through Libyan embassies and consulates. Fee structure per Embassy of Libya in Washington DC: US citizens - $160/year (multiple entry, 1 year); Non-US citizens - $150 (single entry, 30 days), $200 (multiple entry, 90 days), $350 (multiple entry, 180 days). Requires sponsorship letter from a Libyan company. Final approval comes from Libyan authorities in Tripoli and typically takes 'a couple of days' plus postal transit time.

LBY.name: Libya Diplomatic and Official Visa
LBY.purpose: Issued to accredited government officials, diplomats, and their dependents traveling on official government business to Libya.
LBY.notes: Applied for through Libyan embassies. In the United States, requires a diplomatic note from the U.S. Department of State. Specific fees, validity, and stay duration are not published on official sources.

LBY.name: Non-Libyan Spouse Visa
LBY.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who are married to Libyan citizens, allowing them to reside in or visit Libya.
LBY.notes: Fee of $25 per Embassy of Libya in Washington DC. Requires documentation of marriage to a Libyan national. Additional requirements include valid passport, completed application form, passport photo, and prepaid return envelope. Stay duration and validity not specified on official source.

LBY.name: Libya Journalist Visa
LBY.purpose: Issued to accredited journalists and media personnel intending to travel to Libya for reportage, documentary work, or media coverage.
LBY.notes: Applied for through Libyan embassies. Requires a support letter from the applicant's publication or broadcaster and valid media credentials. Fees, validity, and stay duration are not specified on official sources. Final approval must come from Libyan authorities.

LBY.name: Investor Residence Visa (Investment Promotion Law No. 9, 2010)
LBY.purpose: Granted to approved foreign investors with active investment projects in Libya under Investment Promotion Law No. 9 of 2010, providing renewable residence and multiple entry/exit rights.
LBY.notes: Authorized under Article 12(7) of Investment Promotion Law No. 9 of 2010 published by the Economic Development Authority. Grants approved foreign investors residence visas renewable for 5 years (duration of the investment project) and multiple exit/re-entry visas. No minimum investment amount is specified in the law for this visa benefit. Does not apply to oil and gas sector projects (Article 27). This is a residence benefit tied to an active, approved investment project - not a standalone golden visa or formal RBI program.

LBY.name: Libya Entry Visa (Consular / Embassy-Issued)
LBY.purpose: General short-stay entry visa for tourism, visiting, and short business trips, issued in person through Libyan embassies and consulates for nationals who apply via a diplomatic mission rather than the online e-visa portal.
LBY.notes: Consular entry-visa fee tiers published by the Embassy of Libya in Ottawa (Canada): 1-month single entry CAD 102.50 (approx USD 75), 3-month CAD 205 (approx USD 150), 6-month CAD 410 (approx USD 300). Requires an original passport valid at least 6 months, completed visa form, two 50mm x 70mm photos, payment by certified cheque/money order, and a prepaid return envelope. All applications are vetted and finally approved by Libyan authorities in Tripoli. Entry to Libya is generally required within 45 days of visa issuance. Distinct from the online tourist e-visa (evisa.gov.ly); this is the embassy-issued sticker visa for applicants who cannot or do not use the e-visa portal. Passports showing prior travel to Israel are not accepted.

LBY.name: Entry Visa for Libyan Nationals Holding Foreign Passports
LBY.purpose: Issued to persons of Libyan nationality or origin who travel on a foreign passport, granting them the right to enter Libya.
LBY.notes: Per the Embassy of Libya in Washington DC: USD 25 for a 90-day validity single-entry visa, or USD 160 for a 365-day validity multiple-entry visa. Requires a valid passport (6+ months), a copy of the applicant's Libyan passport, a copy of a national ID or driver's license, an electronic birth certificate, and two passport photos. This is a distinct category for Libyan-origin dual nationals; it is not a residence or citizenship document. Final approval comes from authorities in Libya.

LCA.name: Non-Immigrant Visa (Vacation) - Single Entry
LCA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Saint Lucia for tourism and leisure purposes. Covers visits for pleasure or holiday stays.
LCA.notes: Fee varies by application location: US$30 (USA), CD$30 (Canada), £35 (UK), US$50 (rest of world or applied in Saint Lucia). Valid for 3 months (single entry). EC$125 if applied within Saint Lucia. Expedited 1-day processing available for additional fee. Application submitted to the Royal Saint Lucia Police Force Immigration Department; apply at least 2 weeks before travel. Airport application possible but may be denied. Required documents: 2 certified passport-size photographs, valid passport (min. 6-month validity), return ticket, travel itinerary copy, proof of accommodation, letter of invitation (if applicable).

LCA.name: Non-Immigrant Visa (Business) - Single Entry
LCA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Saint Lucia for business activities such as meetings, negotiations, or professional engagements. Does not permit local employment.
LCA.notes: Fee varies by application location: US$35 (USA), CD$35 (Canada), £40 (UK), US$50 (rest of world or applied in Saint Lucia). EC$125 if applied within Saint Lucia. Expedited 1-day processing available for additional fee. Apply at least 2 weeks before travel to Royal Saint Lucia Police Force Immigration Department (email: visaoffice@police.govt.lc). Required documents: 2 certified passport-size photographs, valid passport (min. 6-month validity), return ticket, travel itinerary, proof of accommodation, letter of invitation or business purpose documentation.

LCA.name: Non-Immigrant Visa (Business) - Multiple Entry
LCA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals from visa-required countries multiple entries to Saint Lucia for business purposes over a one-year period. Suited for frequent business travelers who require repeated access.
LCA.notes: US$75 for multiple-entry business visa valid up to 1 year (when applied in Saint Lucia). EC$190 if applied locally. Fee for other application locations not separately specified in official source; the US$75 rate is referenced specifically for the Saint Lucia application office. Expedited processing available. Apply to Royal Saint Lucia Police Force Immigration Department.

LCA.name: Non-Immigrant Visa (Student) - Single Entry
LCA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Saint Lucia for the purpose of study or enrollment at an educational institution. Covers formal academic programs.
LCA.notes: Fee varies by application location: US$25 (USA), CD$25 (Canada), £30 (UK), US$40 (rest of world or applied in Saint Lucia). EC$125 if applied within Saint Lucia. Expedited 1-day processing available for additional fee. Apply at least 2 weeks before travel. Required documents: 2 certified passport-size photographs, valid passport (min. 6-month validity), proof of enrollment or acceptance letter from Saint Lucia educational institution, accommodation proof.

LCA.name: Non-Immigrant Visa - Multiple Entry
LCA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Saint Lucia for tourism or general non-immigrant purposes on multiple occasions within the validity period.
LCA.notes: EC$190 for multiple-entry visa valid for one year. USD equivalent approximately US$70 at current XCD/USD exchange rate (XCD is pegged at 2.7 to 1 USD). The govt.lc service page lists single entry (EC$125, 3-month validity) and multiple entry (EC$190, 1-year validity) as the two standard options under the Non-Immigrant Visa service. Apply to Royal Saint Lucia Police Force Immigration Department; office hours 8:30 a.m.–12:00 p.m. Email: visaoffice@police.govt.lc.

LCA.name: Don't Just Visit, Live It - Remote Work / Digital Nomad Visa
LCA.purpose: Permits remote workers, freelancers, and students in remote learning programs to live and work from Saint Lucia for up to one year, provided their employer or clients are based outside Saint Lucia.
LCA.notes: Launched March 2021. Routed through the standard Non-Immigrant Visa (Multiple Entry, EC$190 / approx. US$70). No minimum income requirement stated on official source. No local income tax on foreign-sourced income. All nationalities eligible (visa-required nationals must apply; visa-exempt nationals may enter without a visa). No dedicated *.govt.lc landing page found under the 'Don't Just Visit, Live It' branding; the program is referenced in government press releases but applications are processed through the standard immigration channel at visaoffice@police.govt.lc. Administered by Royal Saint Lucia Police Force Immigration Department.

LCA.name: Work Permit (Annual Employment)
LCA.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals to engage in employment or paid work within Saint Lucia for each desired year of employment. Required for any non-CARICOM/OECS national seeking to work in the country.
LCA.notes: Ministry of Legal Affairs, Home Affairs and Labour (Work Permit Officer; the Minister for Labour grants final approval). Annual fees per Statutory Rules & Orders No. 73 of 1997, charged for each year of employment by nationality: Caribbean Commonwealth nationals EC$2,000/yr (approx. US$741); other Commonwealth nationals EC$4,000/yr (approx. US$1,481); other foreign nationals EC$5,000/yr (approx. US$1,852 - the fee_usd shown). A separate non-refundable EC$100 (approx. US$37) application fee is paid to the Treasury before the application form is issued. Renewed annually until the holder becomes a citizen; persons who hold residential status are NOT exempt and must still obtain a work permit. Submit to the Work Permit Officer at least two months before the intended start date; do not begin work while the application is pending. Additional statutory fee tiers: EC$400 for a period not exceeding one month, EC$200 per 12-month period for unskilled workers, EC$300 per entry for commercial sales personnel/professionals. Required documents: police record from country last resided, certified proof of qualifications, trade licence (where applicable), copies of job advertisements for the post, evidence income tax has been paid, one passport photo. Tel: (758) 468-2202. CARICOM nationals with a CSME skills certificate and OECS Protocol Member nationals may work without a separate work permit.

LCA.name: Diplomatic / Official Passport Visa Exemption
LCA.purpose: Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from all countries are exempt from Saint Lucia visa requirements and visa fees, regardless of the traveler's nationality.
LCA.notes: The official visa fee table lists 'Exempt' for both 'Diplomatic Passports' and 'Official/Service Passports' at all places of issue (UK, USA, Canada, rest of world, Saint Lucia). The DEA Visa Requirements by Country document confirms this with per-country entries (e.g., Armenia, Azerbaijan, Haiti, Moldova, Ukraine show 'YES(pta) NO(DIPLOMATIC/OFFICIAL)' - meaning ordinary passport requires visa but diplomatic/official passport does not). Cruise ship passengers visiting for one day are also exempt from visa requirements.

LCA.name: Non-Immigrant Visa on Arrival (Port of Entry)
LCA.purpose: Allows nationals of designated visa-required countries to obtain their non-immigrant (visitor/business/study) visa at the Saint Lucia port of entry rather than applying in advance. Applies only to nationalities the Department of External Affairs marks '(poe)' - port of entry.
LCA.notes: The official Department of External Affairs 'Saint Lucia Visa Requirements by Country' list marks each nationality as either '(pta) = prior to arrival' or '(poe) = port of entry'. Nationalities marked '(poe)' - e.g. Benin, Bhutan, Bolivia, Sudan, Thailand, Uganda, Vietnam - may obtain the visa on arrival at the port of entry; those marked '(pta)' must apply beforehand. The govt.lc non-immigrant visa page confirms that 'in some circumstances, application for a visa can be made at the airport on entry to Saint Lucia,' though approval is not guaranteed. Fee is the standard non-immigrant visa fee (US$50 rest of world / applied in Saint Lucia). Requirements match the standard non-immigrant visa. Country-by-country classification list: https://stluciaconsulate.ca/wp-content/uploads/forms/Saint-Lucia-Visa-Requirements-by-Country-of-Citizenship.pdf

LCA.name: Cruise Ship Passenger / Day Visitor Visa Exemption
LCA.purpose: Waives the visa requirement for cruise ship passengers and other travellers visiting Saint Lucia for a single day, regardless of nationality.
LCA.notes: The official visa FAQ states: 'Cruise ship passengers visiting Saint Lucia for one day are exempted from obtaining visas.' Applies to day visitors arriving by cruise; no visa or fee is required for the one-day visit. Travellers remaining beyond the day visit, or entering for other purposes, must obtain the applicable non-immigrant visa (or enter under a visa exemption if their nationality qualifies).

LCA.name: Short-Term Work Permit (up to one month)
LCA.purpose: Authorizes a foreign national to work in Saint Lucia for a single period not exceeding one month - suited to short assignments, performers, technicians, and temporary engagements.
LCA.notes: Statutory Rules & Orders No. 73 of 1997 sets a work permit fee of EC$400 (approx. US$148) for a person of any nationality for a period not exceeding one month for which the permit is valid. A separate non-refundable EC$100 (approx. US$37) application fee is paid to the Treasury before the application form is issued. A related tier of EC$300 per entry applies to commercial sales personnel/professionals. Administered by the Work Permit Officer, Ministry of Legal Affairs, Home Affairs and Labour; the Minister for Labour grants final approval. Submit at least two months before the intended start of work; do not begin work while the application is pending. Required documents: police record from country last resided, certified proof of qualifications, trade licence (where applicable), copies of job advertisements, evidence income tax has been paid, one passport photo.

LCA.name: Visitors Extension of Stay
LCA.purpose: Allows visitors already in Saint Lucia to extend their authorised stay beyond the period granted on entry, in 30-day increments, for continued tourism, family visits, medical care, property owners, or yacht crew.
LCA.notes: Apply to the Immigration Department before the entry stamp expires. Fee EC$200 (approx. US$74) per 30-day extension, plus an EC$2 application form fee; the fee is waived where the applicant is a foreign female spouse of a Saint Lucian national. Visitors are generally admitted for up to six weeks on arrival and may extend in 30-day increments. Processing about five working days; Extension of Stay counter hours 8:30 a.m.-12:00 p.m. First-time applicants provide a passport photo, valid passport, and return ticket (waived for property owners and persons of Saint Lucian parentage), plus a local host with ID and rental/accommodation documentation. Special categories (Saint Lucian parentage, married to a Saint Lucian, property owners, yacht crew) submit birth/marriage certificates, property deeds, or yacht registration papers. Source: Consulate General of Saint Lucia (Toronto).

LIE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Category C)
LIE.purpose: Allows entry for tourism, visiting family or friends, business meetings, cultural or sports events, and short-term studies. Valid across all Schengen member states including Liechtenstein.
LIE.notes: Liechtenstein does not issue its own visas. Schengen C visas are issued by Swiss representations abroad on behalf of Liechtenstein. Fee is EUR 90 (approx. USD 98) for adults, EUR 45 for children aged 6–12. Processing is generally within 15 days; may extend to 30–60 days in exceptional cases. Maximum stay is 90 days in any 180-day period. Requires valid travel document, EUR 30,000 minimum medical insurance, and proof of sufficient financial means (min. CHF 100/day). Apply via swiss-visa.ch.

LIE.name: Schengen Airport Transit Visa (Category A)
LIE.purpose: Required for nationals of certain third countries to pass through the international transit zone of a Schengen airport without entering the Schengen area. Liechtenstein has no international airport, but Category A visas issued for Swiss airports apply in this framework.
LIE.notes: Category A transit visa issued by Swiss representations abroad. Liechtenstein has no international airport of its own; travelers transit through Swiss airports. The same Swiss Schengen visa requirements apply to Liechtenstein without exception per official Liechtenstein Embassy (liechtensteinusa.org). Fee follows standard Schengen rate (EUR 90 adults).

LIE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Category C) - Business
LIE.purpose: Permits short-term business activities such as attending meetings, conferences, trade fairs, and negotiations in Liechtenstein and across the Schengen area, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
LIE.notes: Business is a permitted purpose under the standard Schengen C Visa. Gainful employment or income-generating work in Liechtenstein is not permitted under this category. Issued by Swiss representations abroad. Fee EUR 90 (approx. USD 98) for adults.

LIE.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Category D) - Gainful Employment
LIE.purpose: Grants entry to Liechtenstein for the purpose of taking up gainful employment for periods exceeding 90 days. This is a national (not Schengen-wide) visa, valid only for Liechtenstein and Switzerland.
LIE.notes: Category D visa for stays exceeding 90 days for the purpose of gainful employment. Processing time 'one to several months must be expected' per SEM. Non-EEA/non-Swiss nationals must be managers, specialists, or otherwise qualified employees sponsored by a Liechtenstein employer. Applications processed through cantonal migration offices in coordination with the Liechtenstein Migration and Passport Office (APA). EEA nationals instead participate in the B permit draw. A national visa premium of up to 50% surcharge may apply for urgent processing.

LIE.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Category D) - Education
LIE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Liechtenstein for the purpose of studying or vocational training for periods exceeding 90 days.
LIE.notes: Education is a permitted purpose under the Swiss/Liechtenstein Category D national visa framework. Students must demonstrate financial means (minimum CHF 30/day per SEM). Processed through Swiss representations abroad in coordination with Liechtenstein APA. Processing time generally one to several months.

LIE.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Category D) - Family Reunification
LIE.purpose: Permits entry and stay in Liechtenstein for the purpose of joining a family member who is lawfully resident, for periods exceeding 90 days.
LIE.notes: Family reunification is a recognised purpose under the Category D national visa. Issued by Swiss representations abroad. Processing one to several months. The family member residing in Liechtenstein must hold a valid B or C residence permit. Liechtenstein's strict residence quota system makes approval for family reunification subject to available quota.

LIE.name: Residence Permit B (Draw) - With Gainful Employment (EEA Nationals)
LIE.purpose: Annual lottery-based residence permit allowing EEA nationals to live and work in Liechtenstein for more than 12 months. Quota of 56 permits per year, allocated 50% by lottery and 50% by government decision.
LIE.notes: EEA nationals only (Swiss nationals excluded). Draws held twice yearly (spring and autumn). B permit is renewable annually. After 5 years of lawful residence, permanent residence (C permit) may be obtained. Citizenship requires 30 years continuous residence. No monetary investment requirement. Non-EEA nationals are not eligible for this draw.

LIE.name: Residence Permit B (Draw) - Without Gainful Employment (EEA Nationals)
LIE.purpose: Annual lottery-based residence permit for EEA nationals wishing to reside in Liechtenstein without working, subject to demonstrating sufficient financial means. Quota of 16 permits per year.
LIE.notes: EEA nationals only (Swiss and UK nationals excluded post-Brexit). Draws held twice yearly. Applicants must prove sufficient financial means to sustain themselves without social assistance. B permit renewable. After 5 years, permanent residence (C permit) may be obtained. Citizenship requires 30 years residence.

LIE.name: Short-term Residence Permit L - Qualified Specialists (Non-EEA Nationals)
LIE.purpose: Allows non-EEA and non-Swiss qualified specialists sponsored by a Liechtenstein employer to reside and work in Liechtenstein for up to 12 months.
LIE.notes: For managers, specialists, or other qualified employees who have completed an apprenticeship or have many years of professional experience. Must be sponsored by a Liechtenstein company. L permit valid for up to 12 months, extendable once for up to 6 months upon proof of extraordinary need. Application filed by the Liechtenstein employer through the Migration and Passport Office (APA). No digital nomad or startup visa exists.

LIE.name: Diplomatic/Service/Official Passport Visa Exemption
LIE.purpose: Bilateral visa exemption agreements allow holders of diplomatic, service, special, or official passports from specific countries to enter Liechtenstein (via Schengen/Switzerland) without a visa for stays up to 90 days.
LIE.notes: Liechtenstein applies Switzerland's bilateral diplomatic passport visa exemption agreements. As of June 2026, over 50 bilateral agreements exist covering countries including Albania (diplomatic), Angola (diplomatic/service), Brazil (diplomatic/official/service), China (diplomatic), India (diplomatic), and others. Stays are non-working and limited to 90 days in any 180-day period. See conditional_access array for full country-by-country breakdown.

LIE.name: Cross-Border Commuter Permit (G) - Third-Country Nationals
LIE.purpose: Allows non-EEA/non-Swiss nationals already lawfully resident in the EEA or Switzerland to take up employment with a Liechtenstein employer while returning to their foreign place of residence, without taking up residence in Liechtenstein.
LIE.notes: For third-country nationals already resident in the EEA or Switzerland who commute to a job in Liechtenstein. Only granted if the employer proves no suitable worker is available on the permit-free (EEA/Swiss) labour market. The complete application is filed by the Liechtenstein employer with the Migration and Passport Office (APA) at least 14 days before the intended start of employment; work may only begin once the permit is issued. Limited to one year and renewable. The holder does not reside in Liechtenstein and returns to their foreign residence.

LIE.name: Cross-Border Commuter Registration (GMB) - EEA Nationals
LIE.purpose: Registration confirmation for employed or self-employed EEA nationals whose employer and place of work are in Liechtenstein but who return to a place of residence abroad, without taking up residence in Liechtenstein.
LIE.notes: For EEA nationals (employed or self-employed) whose employer and workplace are in Liechtenstein and who commute from a residence abroad. Under EEA free-movement rules this is a declaratory registration confirmation, not a quota-restricted permit. The complete notification must be filed with the Migration and Passport Office (APA) no later than 10 days after taking up employment. All GMB holders also receive the digital eGMB free of charge in the eID.li app. Swiss cross-border commuters are covered under separate Swiss-Liechtenstein arrangements.

LIE.name: Settlement Permit C (Permanent Residence / Niederlassungsbewilligung)
LIE.purpose: Grants foreign nationals an indefinite right to reside in Liechtenstein without annual renewal, after a qualifying period of continuous lawful residence.
LIE.notes: Granted after continuous lawful residence: Swiss and Austrian nationals after 5 years; other EEA nationals and third-country nationals generally after 10 years, subject to integration and good-conduct criteria. Confers an indefinite right of residence with no annual renewal, though it can lapse on prolonged absence or serious grounds. Issued by the Migration and Passport Office (APA). Not a route of first entry - it follows prior residence on a B permit. Ordinary naturalisation as a Liechtenstein citizen requires 30 years of residence.

LIE.name: Residence Permit B - Gainful Employment (Long-Term Work Permit)
LIE.purpose: Long-term residence permit for foreign nationals taking up salaried employment or self-employment in Liechtenstein for more than 12 months, for managers, specialists and qualified employees sponsored by a Liechtenstein employer.
LIE.notes: The B permit for gainful employment is granted very restrictively and is quota-limited. Initial permits are typically valid for 12 months and renewable, up to 5 years overall; managers and specialists employed by internationally active companies may be granted up to 3 years. EEA nationals normally reach the B permit via the residence-permit draw; third-country (non-EEA) nationals can obtain it only exceptionally by government decision, and must be managers, specialists or qualified employees for whom no suitable worker is available on the permit-free (EEA/Swiss) labour market. The complete application is filed by the Liechtenstein employer with the Migration and Passport Office (APA); work may begin only once the permit is issued. This is distinct from the short-term L permit (max 12 months) and from the EEA-only B permit draw.

LIE.name: Au Pair Permit (Short-term Residence Permit L)
LIE.purpose: Short-term residence permit allowing young foreign nationals aged 18 to 25 to live with a host family in Liechtenstein, help with childcare and light housework, and improve their language skills as a cultural exchange.
LIE.notes: Open to nationals of any country aged 18 to 25 who join a host family; issued as a short-term L permit for up to 12 months. The au pair must receive board, lodging and a minimum cash allowance (the host family pays a minimum gross wage of about CHF 1,835 for a 30-hour week, with a net minimum of about CHF 700 per month). The application is filed by the host family with the Migration and Passport Office (APA). Quota-restricted like other L permits.

LKA.name: Tourist ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) – Free
LKA.purpose: Short-term tourism, sightseeing, visiting friends/relatives, medical treatment, participating in arts, music, dance and sport events.
LKA.notes: Free for nationals of 40 designated countries effective 25 May 2026. Double-entry facility permitted within validity. Maldivian nationals receive 90 days instead of 30. Seychelles and Singapore nationals also eligible for free ETA under bilateral arrangements. Children under 12 from any nationality receive free tourist ETA. Apply via eta.gov.lk.

LKA.name: Tourist ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) – Paid
LKA.purpose: Short-term tourism, sightseeing, visiting friends/relatives, medical treatment, participating in arts, music, dance and sport events.
LKA.notes: For nationalities not in the 40-country free ETA list. Fee: USD 20 (SAARC, applied online/at mission) or USD 25 (SAARC, on arrival); USD 50 (all others, applied online/at mission) or USD 60 (all others, on arrival). Double-entry facility permitted. Extensions possible for up to 6 months total. Some nationalities (e.g. Cameroon, Nigeria, Afghanistan, Syria) require a Sri Lankan sponsor and additional documents such as police clearance.

LKA.name: Business ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization)
LKA.purpose: Attending business meetings, negotiations, seminars, and conferences in Sri Lanka for a limited duration.
LKA.notes: Fee: USD 30 for SAARC nationalities; USD 55 for all other nationalities. No on-arrival option for business ETA. Single, double, or multiple entry available. Apply via eta.gov.lk.

LKA.name: Transit Visa
LKA.purpose: Allows travelers to transit through Sri Lanka ports and airports while continuing to their final destination.
LKA.notes: Valid for 48 hours only. Free of charge. Requires proof of onward air ticket or sea passage. Employment, self-employment, and business activities prohibited. Apply via eta.gov.lk.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Employment Category
LKA.purpose: For foreign professionals and expatriates employed in Sri Lanka, including BOI project personnel, bank employees, private company employees, and Colombo Port City workers.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Mandatory health protection plan required. Subcategories: government project professionals, BOI personnel, bank employees, private sector employees, Colombo Port City Commission workers. Dependents may accompany the primary visa holder. Appointment at Department of Immigration and Emigration required.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Investor Category
LKA.purpose: For foreign nationals investing capital in Sri Lanka or conducting business activities under approved investment schemes.
LKA.notes: Minimum investment USD 100,000 (5-year visa) or USD 200,000 (10-year visa) in approved sectors such as IT and tourism. Separate guideline document available from the Department. No pathway to permanent residence or citizenship officially stated.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Educational Category
LKA.purpose: For foreign nationals studying at Sri Lankan universities or approved educational institutions, as well as volunteers and interns.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Non-university students must show bank encashment receipts of at least USD 1,500 per year per person to prove sufficient funds. Subcategories: university students, approved institution students, volunteers, interns.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Medical Category
LKA.purpose: For foreign nationals undergoing medical treatment in Sri Lanka, along with one accompanying medical assistant.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Requires bank encashment receipts to the value of USD 1,500 per year per person to demonstrate ability to cover medical expenses. One medical assistant is permitted to accompany the patient.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Family Members (Spouse & Dependents)
LKA.purpose: For non-Sri Lankan spouses of Sri Lankan citizens and dependent children of Sri Lankan citizens residing in Sri Lanka.
LKA.notes: First issuance: 1 year free. Subsequent extensions: 2-year increments until 5 years total, then 5-year extensions. Dependent children aged 16 and over: USD 100 per year until age 22. Dependent children below 16 are free.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Religious Category
LKA.purpose: For members of the clergy and foreign nationals participating in religious activities with the recommendation of the relevant ministry.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Requires organization request letter, ministry recommendation, passport biodata page, and a health protection plan.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – NGO/INGO Personnel
LKA.purpose: For staff of non-governmental and international organizations operating in Sri Lanka with endorsement from the relevant ministry.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Relevant ministry endorsement required. Dependents may be included.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Ex-Sri Lankans & Dependents
LKA.purpose: For former Sri Lankan citizens and their dependents wishing to reside in Sri Lanka.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Security clearance reports generally not required for this category. Dependents are eligible.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Court Visa
LKA.purpose: For foreign nationals who have pending court cases in Sri Lanka and are required to appear before Sri Lankan courts.
LKA.notes: Renewable; each extension is valid for 14 days from the date of the next court hearing.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Diplomatic & Official Category
LKA.purpose: For diplomats, embassy staff, and government officials at accredited diplomatic missions in Sri Lanka and their dependents.
LKA.notes: Duration as recommended by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Gratis (no fee). Health protection plan exemption applies to this category.

LKA.name: My Dream Home Visa Programme
LKA.purpose: Residence visa for senior foreign nationals (retirees and those with independent income) wishing to reside long-term in Sri Lanka.
LKA.notes: Currently open for extensions only; not accepting new applicants. Requires USD 15,000 fixed deposit in a Sri Lankan bank plus monthly remittances of USD 1,500 (principal applicant) and USD 750 per spouse/dependent child. Visa valid for 2 years, renewable. Fee: USD 200 per year per person (including dependents over 16). No paid or unpaid employment permitted.

LKA.name: Resident Guest Scheme (RGS) Visa Programme
LKA.purpose: Long-term residence visa for high-net-worth foreign investors and skilled professionals wishing to reside in Sri Lanka.
LKA.notes: Currently open for extensions only; not accepting new applicants. Investor category: minimum USD 250,000 in a Foreign Currency Account (USD 35,000 per dependent). Professional category: monthly remittance of USD 2,000 (applicant) and USD 1,000 per dependent. Visa valid for 5 years from issuance. Fee: USD 200 per person per year. No employment permitted. No pathway to permanent residence or citizenship officially stated.

LKA.name: Golden Paradise Residence Visa
LKA.purpose: 10-year residence visa for foreign investors making a qualifying deposit in a Sri Lankan bank under the Golden Paradise Foreign Currency Account scheme.
LKA.notes: Minimum deposit of USD 200,000 in a Golden Paradise Foreign Currency Account (GPFCA) at a Central Bank of Sri Lanka-licensed bank. Up to 50% of the minimum investment may be withdrawn after the first year. Permitted investments include condominium property, land and building leases, Sri Lanka Development Bonds, and other government-approved investments. Fee: USD 2,000 for 10 years. Includes spouse and dependents. No official pathway to permanent residence or citizenship stated.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Digital Nomad Category
LKA.purpose: For foreign nationals who earn income remotely from clients or employers outside Sri Lanka and wish to reside in Sri Lanka.
LKA.notes: Annual visa, renewable. Requires recommendation from Ministry of Digital Economy. Must have international health insurance covering Sri Lanka. All income must be earned remotely from outside Sri Lanka; local employment prohibited. Exact minimum income/remittance requirement listed in official PDF (immigration.gov.lk/content/files/visa/digital_nomad/Digital%20Nomad%20Visa%20Category.pdf). Application submitted to Residence Visa Division, Department of Immigration and Emigration.

LKA.name: Residence Visa – Registered Indians (1954 Indo-Lanka Agreement)
LKA.purpose: For Indian nationals / persons of Indian origin statutorily registered under the 1954 Indo-Ceylon (Indo-Lanka) Agreement who reside in Sri Lanka.
LKA.notes: Statutory residence category listed on the Department of Immigration and Emigration residence-visa page. Annual visa, renewable. Health protection plan and standard residence-visa documentation apply. Niche category limited to the defined 1954-agreement population, not a general immigration route; specific fee not published on the accessible fees page.

LKA.name: Colombo Port City Special Economic Zone Visa
LKA.purpose: For foreign investors, business owners, employees and residents operating within the Colombo Port City Special Economic Zone, administered by the Colombo Port City Economic Commission (CPCEC) rather than the general residence-visa route.
LKA.notes: Distinct SEZ visa scheme under the Colombo Port City Economic Commission Act No. 11 of 2021, separate from the standard residence visa. Sub-categories: Business Visa (directors, shareholders and partners of an Authorised Person), Employment Visa, Investor Visa, and Residential Property Lessee Visa. Fee USD 200 per annum; annual renewal. Spouses and dependents eligible; spouses may work only within Port City. Applicants first obtain a Landing Endorsement and submit documents (police clearance, health plan from a recognised Sri Lankan hospital, TB/malaria/HIV/filariasis screening) to applications@portcity.gov.lk. Residents must obtain the visa within 30 days of arrival.

LSO.name: Single Entry Visa
LSO.purpose: Permits a single journey to Lesotho for tourism, family visits, or other short-term purposes. Issued to ordinary passport holders from countries not exempt from visa requirements.
LSO.notes: Fee is M1,000 (Lesotho Maloti). e-Visa system is currently suspended; applications submitted by email to VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls. Processing maximum 10 working days. Upon approval, a 72-hour visa-on-arrival authorization letter is emailed; traveller must enter via Maseru Port of Entry or Moshoeshoe I International Airport only. USD equivalent not stated in official source.

LSO.name: Multiple Entry Visa
LSO.purpose: Permits multiple journeys to Lesotho within the validity period for tourism, business visits, or other short-term purposes. Issued to ordinary passport holders requiring a visa.
LSO.notes: Fee is M2,000 (Lesotho Maloti). Valid for 6 months with multiple entries. e-Visa system suspended; applications by email to VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls. Maximum 10 working days processing. Approval results in a 72-hour visa-on-arrival letter for entry at Maseru Port of Entry or Moshoeshoe I International Airport only. Per-stay duration not specified in official source.

LSO.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
LSO.purpose: Issued free of charge to holders of diplomatic, official/service, UN, or Laissez Passer travel documents visiting Lesotho.
LSO.notes: UN Passport holders, Laissez Passer holders, Diplomatic Passport holders, and Official/Service Passport holders are issued visas free of charge. UN Passport and Laissez Passer holders do not need a visa at all according to official source. Application process same as ordinary visa (email to VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls).

LSO.name: Business Residence Permit
LSO.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to reside and conduct business activities in Lesotho. Available as a two-year or indefinite permit.
LSO.notes: Two-year or indefinite duration available. Applications processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru. Minimum investment not specified on official pages. After 5+ years of lawful residence, may qualify for citizenship. Fee schedule referenced in Aliens Control (Amendment of Schedule) Regulations 2018 but amounts not published online.

LSO.name: Teacher's Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit allowing qualified foreign teachers to reside and teach in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Available as a two-year or indefinite permit. Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru. Specific eligibility requirements and fees not published on official pages.

LSO.name: Doctor's and Nurses Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit allowing foreign medical professionals (doctors and nurses) to reside and practice in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Available as a two-year or indefinite permit. Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru. Specific eligibility requirements and fees not published on official pages.

LSO.name: Study Permit
LSO.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to reside in Lesotho for the purpose of studying at an accredited institution.
LSO.notes: Valid for up to 4 years per official immigration page. Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru. Specific eligibility requirements, supporting documents, and fees not published on official pages.

LSO.name: Joining Relative Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit allowing a foreign national to join a relative who is lawfully resident in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Available as a two-year or indefinite permit. Also referred to as 'Joining Relative Permit' and 'Spouse Joining Spouse Permit' (separate sub-categories). Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru.

LSO.name: Spouse Joining Spouse Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit allowing a foreign spouse to join a partner lawfully resident or working in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Available as a two-year or indefinite permit. Distinct from the 'Married Women Permit' category, which the official Home Affairs portal lists separately (a foreign woman married to a Mosotho male). Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru.

LSO.name: Married Women Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit issued to a foreign woman married to a Mosotho (Lesotho citizen) man who wishes to reside with her husband in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Distinct residence-permit category listed on the official VFS-operated Home Affairs portal (homeaffairslesotho.com), separate from the Spouse Joining Spouse permit. Issued to a woman married to a Basotho male to reside with him; available as a two-year or indefinite permit (Married-women-permit-Indefinite.html). Requires marriage certificate, medical certificate, police clearance from Lesotho and country of origin, sponsor (husband) national ID/passport copy, and proof of payment. M2,800 service/handling charge applies via the portal; statutory permit fees payable at the Ministry of Home Affairs per the Government Gazette.

LSO.name: Missionary Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals engaged in missionary or religious work in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Available as a two-year or indefinite permit. Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru. Specific requirements and fees not published on official pages.

LSO.name: Temporary Permit
