LSO.purpose: Short-term permit for foreign nationals who require an authorised stay in Lesotho beyond a visa or for purposes not covered by standard visa categories.
LSO.notes: 90-day temporary permit listed as a distinct permit category on the official immigration page. Specific eligibility, requirements, and fees not published on official pages.

LSO.name: Indefinite Residence Permit
LSO.purpose: Permanent residence authorisation for foreign nationals who have met the long-term residence requirements in Lesotho.
LSO.notes: Indefinite permit categories mirror the two-year permit categories: missionaries, business, joining relative, spouse joining spouse, returning former citizens, doctors/nurses, teachers. Minimum residence period and eligibility criteria not specified on official pages. Processed at the Residence Permit Facilitation Centre in Maseru.

LSO.name: Work Permit
LSO.purpose: Authorises a foreign national to take up general employment in Lesotho. The Lesotho-based employer sponsors the application and must demonstrate the position cannot be filled by a suitably qualified Mosotho national.
LSO.notes: General employment work permit, distinct from the profession-specific residence permits (teachers, doctors/nurses). The sponsoring employer must supply a Business Permit, valid Trader's Licence, Tax Clearance Certificate and Letter of Invitation, and complete the general visa requirements. Issued via the Ministry of Home Affairs Department of Immigration with Ministry of Labour and Employment (Labour Commissioner) involvement. Fee and validity period not published on the official page.

LSO.name: Returning Citizens Permit
LSO.purpose: Residence permit for a person who was previously a citizen of the Kingdom of Lesotho and wishes to return and reside in the country once again.
LSO.notes: Listed as 'Returning former citizens' on the official Ministry of Home Affairs immigration page; available as a two-year or indefinite residence permit. Applications submitted online via the VFS-operated Home Affairs services portal (homeaffairslesotho.com/Returning-Citizens-permit.html), which cites a standard residence-permit application fee of M2,800. Requires proof of previous Lesotho citizenship, medical certificate, police clearance and passport photos. Dependants under 21 are exempt from the fee; police clearance is not required for applicants under age 16.

LTU.name: Schengen Type C Visa (Uniform Short-Stay Visa)
LTU.purpose: Short stays for tourism, family visits, business trips, cultural events, or any other purpose not involving paid employment; valid across the entire Schengen Area including Lithuania.
LTU.notes: Fee is EUR 90 (approx USD 99) for adults; EUR 45 for children aged 6-11; free for children under 6. Valid for up to 90 days in any 180-day rolling period across the Schengen Area. Single, double, or multiple entry. Maximum validity 5 years for multiple-entry visas (graduated based on travel history). Standard processing 15 calendar days; up to 45 days for complex cases. Applications submitted via Lithuanian consulates or VFS Global centres. Lithuania has no national e-visa portal - Schengen visa applications are filed through MIGRIS (visa.vrm.lt/epm) or in-person at the consulate. The 'tourist' and 'business' purposes are both covered by the same Type C Schengen visa instrument.

LTU.name: Schengen Type C Visa (Uniform Short-Stay Visa - Business Purpose)
LTU.purpose: Short-term business activities in Lithuania or the Schengen Area including meetings, negotiations, conferences, and training, but not paid employment; uses the same Type C visa as tourist visits.
LTU.notes: Same instrument as tourist Schengen C visa. Business purpose declared in application. Fee EUR 90 adult. Processing 15-45 calendar days. For paid employment or long-term business activity a national D visa is required.

LTU.name: Schengen Type A Visa (Airport Transit Visa)
LTU.purpose: Transit through the international transit areas of Lithuanian airports (primarily Vilnius) without entering Schengen territory; required only for nationals of countries listed on the Airport Transit Visa list.
LTU.notes: Type A visa covers airside transit only; holder does not enter Schengen territory. Multiple airport transit visas may be issued with a maximum validity of 6 months. Fee EUR 90. Required only for nationals of countries on the EU airport transit visa list (e.g. Afghanistan, Ghana, India, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Sri Lanka, and others). Processing 15-45 calendar days.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - Work
LTU.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who have been granted a work permit or temporary residence permit for employment purposes in Lithuania, allowing them to enter and reside while working.
LTU.notes: Lithuania's national D visa is issued for stays exceeding 90 days. A work D visa is linked to a work permit or a temporary residence permit for employment. Valid for up to 1 year. Applications submitted via MIGRIS portal (www.migracija.lt) or Lithuanian consulate. Holders must obtain a temporary residence permit if staying beyond the D visa period. National visa (D) state fee is EUR 140 (approx USD 153) per the Migration Department state-fee schedule (migracija.lrv.lt) and the EU Immigration Portal. EU Blue Card holders also receive a D visa if entering from outside Lithuania.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - Study
LTU.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals accepted for full-time studies at a Lithuanian higher education institution, language school, or other accredited educational establishment.
LTU.notes: Requires acceptance letter from a Lithuanian educational institution and proof of sufficient funds. Valid up to 1 year; students in programmes longer than 1 year must obtain a temporary residence permit. Students may work part-time (up to 20 hours/week during term time) under Lithuanian labour law. National visa (D) state fee EUR 140 (approx USD 153). Applications via MIGRIS portal or Lithuanian consulate.

LTU.name: EU Blue Card (Highly Qualified Worker)
LTU.purpose: Residence and work permit for highly qualified non-EU nationals employed in Lithuania under a contract for at least 6 months, meeting minimum salary thresholds.
LTU.notes: Fee EUR 160 (approx USD 175); expedited EUR 320 (approx USD 350). Minimum salary: EUR 3,165/month for standard occupations (1.5x average wage); EUR 2,532/month for shortage/high-value-added occupations (1.2x average wage). Based on 2023 average monthly gross wage of EUR 2,110. Duration: 3 years or employment contract duration + 3 months (whichever shorter). Eligible for EU mobility after 18 months. Applied for via MIGRIS portal. Standard processing: 1 month; expedited: 15 days.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - Startup / Self-Employment
LTU.purpose: Issued to non-EU founders or key personnel of innovative startups confirmed by the Lithuanian Innovation Agency, or to qualified self-employed persons establishing a business in Lithuania.
LTU.notes: Startup applicants must first obtain confirmation from the Lithuanian Innovation Agency (Inovacijų agentūra) that the planned activity is innovative. Temporary residence permit issued for 2 years, renewable for up to 3 additional years upon Innovation Agency confirmation. Enterprise must be established and operations commenced within 120 days of permit issuance. National visa (D) state fee EUR 140 (approx USD 153); the linked temporary residence permit fee is EUR 160. Applications via MIGRIS.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - Family Reunification
LTU.purpose: Issued to family members (spouse, minor children, dependent relatives) of Lithuanian citizens, EU/EEA nationals residing in Lithuania, or third-country nationals holding a valid temporary or permanent residence permit.
LTU.notes: Requires proof of family relationship with the sponsor, sponsor's valid residence status, proof of adequate accommodation and financial means. Sponsor must have held a temporary residence permit for at least 1 year and have the right to reside for at least another year before applying. National visa (D) state fee EUR 140 (approx USD 153). Applications via MIGRIS portal or Lithuanian consulate.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - Scientific Research
LTU.purpose: Issued to researchers and scientists from non-EU countries who have signed a hosting agreement with a Lithuanian research institution accredited by the relevant ministry.
LTU.notes: Requires a signed hosting agreement with an accredited Lithuanian research or higher education institution. Holders may apply for a temporary residence permit if staying longer than the D visa period. National visa (D) state fee EUR 140 (approx USD 153). Implementing EU Directive 2016/801 on students and researchers. Applications via MIGRIS.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - Voluntary Activity / Traineeship
LTU.purpose: Issued to non-EU nationals participating in voluntary service programmes (e.g. European Solidarity Corps) or unpaid traineeships at Lithuanian organisations.
LTU.notes: Requires hosting agreement with a Lithuanian organisation. National visa (D) state fee EUR 140 (approx USD 153). Implementing EU Directive 2016/801. Applications via MIGRIS portal or Lithuanian consulate.

LTU.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
LTU.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals holding diplomatic, official, or service passports traveling to Lithuania on official government business, including accredited diplomats and their dependents.
LTU.notes: Diplomatic passport holders from many countries are exempt from Schengen visa requirements under bilateral agreements (see conditional_access entries). Where a visa is required, diplomatic visas are issued free of charge. Procedures coordinated via Lithuanian embassies and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (urm.lt).

LTU.name: Schengen Type C Visa (Medical Treatment Purpose)
LTU.purpose: Short-stay Schengen C visa issued for the purpose of receiving medical treatment in Lithuania; uses the same instrument as tourist/business visits.
LTU.notes: Same legal instrument as Schengen C visa. Requires documentation from a Lithuanian medical institution confirming appointment/treatment. Fee EUR 90. For treatments exceeding 90 days a national D visa and temporary residence permit based on medical grounds may be required.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D / Schengen C - Seasonal Work
LTU.purpose: Non-EU nationals coming to Lithuania for temporary seasonal employment (e.g. agriculture, food processing, hospitality) tied to a seasonal work permit issued by the Employment Service.
LTU.notes: Seasonal work permits are granted for a maximum of 6 months in any 12-month period. A Schengen C visa is used for seasonal stays up to 90 days; a national long-stay D visa for longer seasonal stays. The prospective employer notifies the local Employment Service (uzt.lt) of the vacancy and applies for the permit, which is issued within 7 working days; the corresponding national long-stay visa is issued within about 15 days. Implements EU Directive 2014/36/EU on seasonal workers. Applications via MIGRIS / Lithuanian consulate.

LTU.name: Intra-Corporate Transferee (ICT) Permit
LTU.purpose: Managers, specialists, or trainee employees of a company established outside the EU who are transferred to a group branch, subsidiary, or parent company in Lithuania.
LTU.notes: Requires prior employment with the sending company of at least 6 months (managers/specialists) or 3 months (trainees). Permit valid for the duration of the transfer up to a maximum of 3 years for managers and specialists and 1 year for trainees. Standard processing up to 2 months (managers/specialists) or 3 months (trainees); expedited decision in 1 month / 45 days for an additional fee. Allows intra-EU mobility within the same corporate group. Implements EU Directive 2014/66/EU. Applied for via MIGRIS or a Lithuanian consulate.

LTU.name: Working Holiday / Youth Mobility Visa (National Visa Type D)
LTU.purpose: Young citizens (typically aged 18-30, up to 35 for Canada) of countries holding a bilateral youth-mobility agreement with Lithuania, to travel and take up temporary employment for up to 12 months.
LTU.notes: Issued under bilateral youth-exchange / work-holiday agreements as a national (D) visa valid for up to 12 months with the right to work. National visa (D) state fee EUR 140 (approx USD 153). Confirmed partner countries: Canada (agreement signed 19 Nov 2009, in force 1 Oct 2010, ages 18-35), New Zealand (signed 1 Oct 2015, in force 1 Jan 2017, ages 18-30), Japan, and South Korea. Applicants must show sufficient funds, a return ticket or means to buy one, and health insurance. Issued by the Migration Department / Lithuanian consulates. Bilateral agreements confirmed via EACEA National Policies (European Commission youth wiki) and Government of Canada International Experience Canada.

LTU.name: National Long-Stay Visa Type D - International Service Provider / Posted Worker
LTU.purpose: Non-EU nationals posted to Lithuania to temporarily provide services under a contract, including contractual service suppliers (CSSs), business visitors for establishment purposes (BVEPs), and short-term business visitors (STBVs) sent by a foreign service-providing company.
LTU.notes: Officially recognised EU immigration category (EU Immigration Portal) covering Contractual Service Suppliers (CSSs), Business Visitors for Establishment Purposes (BVEPs) and Short-Term Business Visitors (STBVs). Stays up to 90 days may use a Schengen C visa; stays over 90 days require a national long-stay D visa (EUR 140, approx USD 153) or a temporary residence permit (EUR 160 standard / EUR 320 expedited). Standard processing about 3 months; expedited 45 days. Requires health insurance with minimum EUR 30,000 coverage. Applications via MIGRIS or a Lithuanian consulate / external service provider.

LUX.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Single Entry
LUX.purpose: Allows one entry into the Schengen Area for tourism, family visits, cultural or sporting events, or business travel. Does not permit paid employment.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 90 (approx. USD 98). Reduced fee of EUR 35 for nationals of Moldova, Ukraine, Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Albania, Georgia, North Macedonia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan. Children aged 6–12 pay EUR 45; children under 6, students on school trips, and researchers are exempt. Submit application at least 15 days before travel but no more than 6 months in advance. Maximum 90 days within any 180-day period.

LUX.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Multiple Entry
LUX.purpose: Permits multiple entries into the Schengen Area for tourism, business, family visits, or other permitted short-stay purposes as long as the visa remains valid and the 90/180-day rule is respected.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 90 (approx. USD 98). Same reduced-fee nationalities as single-entry Type C. Validity period and number of entries determined at consulate's discretion. Maximum 90 days within any 180-day period across all Schengen member states.

LUX.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
LUX.purpose: Enables transit through the international zone of a Luxembourg airport without entering the Schengen Area or leaving the international transit zone.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 90 (approx. USD 98). Only required for certain nationalities listed in the EU's common list; many nationalities do not require a Type A visa for airport transit. Holder does not enter Schengen territory.

LUX.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) + Salaried Worker Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Authorises third-country nationals to enter Luxembourg to take up paid employment under a contract compliant with Luxembourg labour law, requiring prior authorisation from the National Employment Agency (ADEM).
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87) for residence permit. Type D visa obtained from Luxembourg or Belgian diplomatic post before entry; valid 90 days to allow entry. First residence permit valid maximum 1 year, restricted to one profession and sector. Renewal valid up to 3 years, granting access to any sector. Processing for initial temporary authorisation normally up to 4 months. Employer must first obtain ADEM certificate confirming no suitable EU candidate is available.

LUX.name: EU Blue Card (Carte Bleue Européenne)
LUX.purpose: Residence and work permit for highly qualified third-country nationals who hold an employment contract for highly skilled work in Luxembourg meeting the minimum salary threshold.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Annual gross salary threshold: EUR 65,652. Employment contract must be for at least 6 months. Permit valid for 4 years (or contract duration + 3 months if shorter). No mandatory labour market test (unlike standard salaried worker permit). Path to long-term residence after 5 years of regular EU residence as Blue Card holder, with last 2 years in Luxembourg.

LUX.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) + Student Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Luxembourg for the purpose of pursuing higher education studies at an approved educational institution.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Applicant must be enrolled in an approved Luxembourg higher education institution. Ministry of Home Affairs normally responds within 60 days. Permit valid annually and renewable as long as enrolment and conditions are met. Renewal application must be submitted 2 months before expiry. Post-study job-search permit available after completing studies.

LUX.name: Investor Residence Permit - Existing Business
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who invest at least EUR 500,000 in an existing Luxembourg-registered company to reside in Luxembourg, provided they commit to maintaining the investment and employment levels for 5 years.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Minimum investment EUR 500,000. Ministerial opinion from Ministry of Economy required before submitting immigration application. Initial temporary authorisation processing: normally within 3 months. Permit valid up to 3 years, renewable. Long-term residence available after 5 years of lawful continuous stay.

LUX.name: Investor Residence Permit - New Business Creation
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who invest at least EUR 500,000 in a new Luxembourg-registered business creating at least 5 jobs within 3 years to reside in Luxembourg.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Minimum investment EUR 500,000. Must create at least 5 positions within 3 years, coordinated with ADEM. Ministerial opinion from Ministry of Economy required. Permit valid up to 3 years, renewable.

LUX.name: Investor Residence Permit - Management and Investment Structure
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who invest at least EUR 3,000,000 in a Luxembourg-based management or investment structure with real substance to reside in Luxembourg.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Minimum investment EUR 3,000,000. Ministerial opinion from Ministry of Finance required. Permit valid up to 3 years, renewable.

LUX.name: Investor Residence Permit - Financial Deposit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals who deposit at least EUR 20,000,000 with a Luxembourg-established financial institution for a minimum of 5 years to reside in Luxembourg.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Minimum deposit EUR 20,000,000, held for at least 5 years. Ministerial opinion from Ministry of Finance required. Real estate investments do not qualify for any investor permit. Permit valid up to 3 years, renewable.

LUX.name: Family Reunification - Temporary Authorisation + Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows spouses, registered partners, and unmarried children under 18 of lawfully resident third-country nationals to join them in Luxembourg.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Sponsor must demonstrate stable/regular/sufficient resources (at least minimum wage level for 12 months), suitable accommodation, and health insurance. Processing for temporary authorisation to stay normally up to 9 months. Temporary authorisation valid 90 days; residence permit must be applied for within 3 months of arrival. Family members may take employment once permit is obtained.

LUX.name: Working Holiday (Work & Travel) Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows young nationals from partner countries to live, work temporarily, and travel in Luxembourg for up to 12 months to experience cultural exchange and international mobility.
LUX.notes: Available to nationals of Australia, New Zealand, Taiwan, Canada, Chile, Japan, and South Korea. Age limit: 18–30 years (up to 35 for nationals of Taiwan, Chile, Canada, and South Korea). Participants must have sufficient financial resources, valid passport, medical certification, and clean criminal record. Cannot travel with dependants. Specific fees depend on the destination country's diplomatic mission. Does not provide social welfare or unemployment benefits. Japan requires a re-entry permit for multiple entries.

LUX.name: Researcher Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Luxembourg for the purpose of conducting research at a recognised research organisation under a hosting agreement.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Researcher must have a hosting agreement with a Luxembourg-approved research organisation. Also available for EU-mobility researchers already holding a permit in another EU Member State. Post-research job-search permit available after completing research.

LUX.name: Trainee Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Luxembourg for the purpose of completing a traineeship or internship with a Luxembourg employer.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Part of the broader third-country national long-stay category. Specific requirements and duration depend on the traineeship agreement.

LUX.name: Au Pair Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows young third-country nationals to live with a host family in Luxembourg as an au pair, performing limited household duties in exchange for accommodation, meals, and pocket money.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Listed under 'Young au pairs' category on the guichet.public.lu immigration portal. Age and duration conditions apply per au pair agreement.

LUX.name: Volunteer Worker Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Luxembourg for the purpose of carrying out voluntary work with an approved organisation under a volunteer agreement.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Listed under the third-country national long-stay categories on guichet.public.lu. Must have a formal volunteer agreement with an approved Luxembourg organisation.

LUX.name: Self-Employed Person Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Luxembourg for the purpose of conducting self-employed or entrepreneurial activity.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Listed as a separate category from salaried worker on guichet.public.lu. Must obtain appropriate business authorisation from the relevant Luxembourg authority. Specific conditions depend on the sector and nature of the self-employed activity.

LUX.name: Intra-Corporate Transferee (Transferred Salaried Worker) Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals transferred within a multinational company to work temporarily in the Luxembourg entity of that company.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Covers managers, specialists, and trainee employees transferred within a multinational group. Aligned with EU ICT Directive. Separate category from standard salaried worker on guichet.public.lu portal.

LUX.name: Seasonal Worker Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to work in Luxembourg for seasonal employment in sectors with cyclical demand, such as agriculture or hospitality.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Listed as a distinct category on guichet.public.lu. Duration tied to the seasonal employment contract. Specific sectors and conditions set by Grand-Ducal regulation.

LUX.name: Long-Term Resident Status (Statut de Résident de Longue Durée)
LUX.purpose: Grants stable long-term residence rights to third-country nationals who have lawfully and continuously resided in Luxembourg for at least 5 years.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Requires 5 years of lawful, uninterrupted residence in Luxembourg. Provides enhanced protection against expulsion and broader access to employment and social rights. Permit is of unlimited duration, subject to renewal. Pathway to citizenship by naturalisation after total 5 years of legal residence (with final year uninterrupted) plus language and civics requirements.

LUX.name: Residence Permit for Private Reasons (Personal Reasons)
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Luxembourg for more than 3 months without taking up employment - principally people living on their own resources such as an EU/Schengen old-age, invalidity or survivor's pension, or income from activity in another EU/Schengen state, as well as applicants with stable personal or family ties to Luxembourg.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Luxembourg's closest equivalent to a retirement / person-of-independent-means visa: applicants living on their own resources must show income at least equal to the social minimum wage for unskilled workers, sourced from an EU/Schengen professional activity or from an old-age, invalidity or survivor's pension paid by an EU/Schengen social security institution. Since 12 May 2023 applicants must prove a link with Luxembourg or another EU/Schengen country. Residence permit valid up to 3 years, renewable. Type D visa required beforehand for visa-obligated nationalities. Ministry normally responds within 3 months (no reply = refusal).

LUX.name: Posted Worker (Detache) Residence Permit - Business Established Outside the EU
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country nationals posted to Luxembourg by a service-provider business established outside the EU to stay and work for the duration of the service posting.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Distinct from the intra-corporate transfer (ICT) permit. The posting employer must first obtain an authorisation for collective posting; the worker must hold a permanent contract active for at least 6 months and obtain a temporary authorisation to stay from the General Department of Immigration. Residence permit valid for the duration of the posting at most and tied to the sponsoring employer. Type D visa required beforehand for visa-obligated nationalities.

LUX.name: Athlete or Coach (Sportsperson) Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country national professional athletes and their coaches/instructors to reside in Luxembourg to practise or coach a sport for an approved federation or club for more than 3 months.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). For athletes/instructors hired by an approved Luxembourg sports federation or club. Requires an employment contract paying at least the social minimum wage, health insurance, and a medical examination (including tuberculosis screening). Residence permit valid for maximum 1 year, renewable. Type D visa required beforehand for visa-obligated nationalities. Ministry normally responds within 3 months (no reply = refusal).

LUX.name: Pupil Residence Permit (School Exchange Programme)
LUX.purpose: Allows third-country national pupils (roughly aged 14-21) admitted to a Luxembourg secondary school under a school-exchange or European education programme to reside in Luxembourg for their studies.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). Distinct from the higher-education student permit. For pupils admitted to a secondary education establishment via an exchange programme, hosted by a selected family or host structure that vouches for living and return costs. Residence permit valid for 1 year and NOT renewable (holder cannot switch to another category afterwards). Type D visa required beforehand for visa-obligated nationalities. Ministry normally responds within 3 months (no reply = refusal).

LUX.name: Post-Study Job-Search / Business-Creation Residence Permit
LUX.purpose: Allows a third-country national who has completed a Master's-level higher education diploma or defended a research PhD in Luxembourg to stay in order to look for employment or start a business.
LUX.notes: Fee is EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). For graduates of a Luxembourg higher-education Master's diploma or a defended research PhD. Residence permit valid 12 months and non-renewable. Application must be filed at least 30 days before the student residence permit or mobility scheme expires. The General Department of Immigration decides within 90 days; if the diploma is not yet available a receipt authorises a further 3-month stay to obtain proof.

LVA.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourist/Visit
LVA.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Latvia and the Schengen Area for tourism, visiting family/friends, or other short stays not involving paid employment.
LVA.notes: Fee is EUR 90 (approx USD 97) for adults 12+; EUR 45 for ages 6–11; free for children under 6. Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period across Schengen. Applied for at Latvian embassies/consulates abroad or via VFS Global. Single or multiple entry issued at consular discretion. Other Schengen states may represent Latvia for short-stay visas where Latvia has no mission. Fee reduced to EUR 35 for nationals of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Moldova (facilitation agreements). Ukraine: EUR 35 standard (10 calendar days) or EUR 70 expedited (3 days).

LVA.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
LVA.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to travel to Latvia for business meetings, conferences, trade fairs, and other commercial activities not constituting paid employment in Latvia.
LVA.notes: Same Type C Schengen visa as tourist; purpose noted on visa sticker as 'BUSINESS'. Fee EUR 90 for adults. Applied at Latvian embassies/consulates or VFS Global. Work/employment requires a separate work visa. Subsistence requirement: EUR 14/day for stays under 30 days; EUR 780 for stays exceeding 30 days.

LVA.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
LVA.purpose: Required for nationals of certain countries transiting through Latvian international airports without entering the Schengen Area.
LVA.notes: Required for nationals of: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iraq, Iran, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Sri Lanka. Exemptions include holders of valid Latvian/Schengen visas or residence permits, and holders of residence permits from Andorra, USA, Japan, Canada, Liechtenstein, Monaco, San Marino, Switzerland, or Vatican. Also exempt: ICAO member state aircraft crew. Applied at Latvian embassies/consulates. Fee amounts not published on official page.

LVA.name: Long-Stay Visa with Right to Employment (Type D)
LVA.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside and work in Latvia for a specific employer, subject to a State Employment Agency opinion.
LVA.notes: Visa sticker endorsed with one of: 'THE RIGHT TO WORK WITH A SPECIFIC EMPLOYER', 'THE RIGHT TO WORK 20 H PER WEEK', 'VOLUNTARY WORK', or 'THE RIGHT TO WORK WITH NO RESTRICTIONS'. Employer must obtain State Employment Agency opinion before submitting invitation. Minimum subsistence: EUR 1,815/month (general employment). Application in-person at Latvian embassy/consulate abroad. Also possible as short-stay Type C visa for employment not exceeding 90 days in 180.

LVA.name: Seasonal Work Visa (Type D - Seasonal)
LVA.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to engage in temporary employment during peak seasons in specific sectors of the Latvian economy, primarily agriculture, forestry, and fishing.
LVA.notes: Visa sticker marked 'SEASONAL WORK'. Maximum 180 days within a 12-month period (seasonal worker provision). Minimum financial resources: EUR 1,815/month (general employment); EUR 1,516–EUR 1,990/month for agriculture/forestry/fishing depending on subsector. Application via paper form downloadable from pmlp.gov.lv; submitted at Latvian embassy/consulate.

LVA.name: Long-Stay Visa for Remote Work (Type D)
LVA.purpose: Enables third-country nationals employed by an OECD-registered employer or self-employed in an OECD country to reside in Latvia while working remotely.
LVA.notes: Minimum gross monthly income EUR 4,213 (2.5x Latvia's average monthly gross salary). Employees must show minimum 6 months employment with current employer. Health insurance required with minimum EUR 42,600 liability coverage valid in Latvia and all Schengen states. No right to local employment in Latvia. Application via e-form at epak.pmlp.gov.lv. Page last updated 11 February 2026.

LVA.name: Long-Stay Visa for Study (Type D)
LVA.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Latvia for the purpose of studying at an accredited Latvian educational institution.
LVA.notes: Long-stay national visa (Type D) issued for study purposes. Students attending short programs under 90 days may use a Schengen short-stay Type C visa (with fee exemptions for students/pupils on educational visits). Fee EUR 90 for long-stay visa (children under 12 exempt). Required documents include enrollment confirmation. Students staying longer than 1 year typically require a residence permit rather than a visa. EU Directive 2016/801 applies to researchers; fee exemptions apply for scientific research visits.

LVA.name: Long-Stay Visa for Family Reunion (Type D)
LVA.purpose: Allows family members of Latvian citizens or legal residents to enter and reside in Latvia pending a long-term residence permit.
LVA.notes: Type D national long-stay visa issued for family reunification purpose. Applicants typically transition to a residence permit after entry. Fee EUR 90. Application submitted at Latvian embassy/consulate with supporting family relationship documentation.

LVA.name: Diplomatic/Official/Service Visa
LVA.purpose: Issued to foreign diplomatic and official passport holders visiting Latvia on official government or diplomatic business.
LVA.notes: Many diplomatic/service passport holders are visa-exempt under bilateral agreements (see conditional_access). Where not exempt, diplomatic visas are issued fee-free through diplomatic channels (Ministry of Foreign Affairs to Ministry of Foreign Affairs) for official visits. Standard Schengen short-stay limits apply unless a longer-term arrangement is in place.

LVA.name: Long-Stay Visa - Other Purposes (Type D)
LVA.purpose: Covers any lawful long-stay purpose not falling under employment, study, remote work, or family reunification - including medical treatment, voluntary work, and cultural activities.
LVA.notes: Catch-all Type D national visa category. Includes voluntary work (visa sticker endorsed 'VOLUNTARY WORK'). Medical stays, cultural exchange, and other long-stay purposes handled under this category. Fee EUR 90 standard; children under 12 exempt. Subsistence minimum EUR 780 for stays over 30 days. Applied at Latvian embassy/consulate. Latvia does not issue a specific medical or retirement visa - these purposes are covered by the general long-stay Type D visa.

LVA.name: EU Blue Card (Residence Permit for Highly Qualified Employment)
LVA.purpose: Enables third-country nationals with higher-education qualifications (or equivalent professional experience) and a qualifying Latvian employment contract to live and work in a highly qualified job in Latvia.
LVA.notes: Residence permit issued for up to 5 years to attract highly qualified employees. Requires a higher-education qualification from a programme of 3+ years (or, in some fields, at least 5 years of relevant professional experience) plus an employment contract meeting the salary/subsistence threshold - officially published as EUR 1,916/month, reduced to EUR 1,532/month for professions in short supply under Cabinet Regulation No. 108. State fee EUR 100 (approx USD 108) for a 10-working-day review or EUR 200 for a 4-working-day expedited review. Blue Card is not annulled if unemployment does not exceed 3 consecutive months. Salary thresholds are updated periodically by Cabinet regulation. Official pmlp.gov.lv page last updated 22 April 2022.

LVA.name: Residence Permit for Creation or Development of an Innovative Product (Startup Visa)
LVA.purpose: Allows third-country founders and entrepreneurs to reside in Latvia to create or develop an innovative product and build a startup business.
LVA.notes: Temporary residence permit for startup founders developing an innovative product in Latvia. No minimum investment amount is required (distinct from the RBI/investor residence permits tracked separately). Applicant must submit a free-form description of the innovative product to be created or developed together with a business plan covering the next three years, and demonstrate subsistence of at least EUR 500/month (plus EUR 500/month per accompanying adult and EUR 150/month per minor). A stamp duty (state fee) applies; exact amount, validity period, and processing time are not published on the official page - applicants are directed to PMLP. Official pmlp.gov.lv page last updated 22 April 2022.

LVA.name: Working Holiday Visa (New Zealand Working Holiday Scheme)
LVA.purpose: For New Zealand citizens aged 18-30 to spend a working holiday in Latvia, holding a residence and work permit while employment remains casual and secondary to the holiday purpose.
LVA.notes: Based on the bilateral 'Treaty of the Government of the Republic of Latvia and the Government of New Zealand regarding the Working Holiday Scheme'. Open only to New Zealand citizens aged 18 to 30 inclusive; does not apply to dependants. Annual quota of 100 New Zealand citizens. Grants a residence permit and work permit for up to one year; employment must be casual/incidental, not the main purpose of the visit. State fee EUR 160 (approx USD 173). Applicant must show sufficient funds for the initial stay (approx EUR 780) plus the cost of return travel (or hold a return ticket). Application filed at an Embassy of Latvia with passport copy, completed questionnaire, photo and proof of fee payment; on arrival the holder must present a valid New Zealand passport and health insurance covering hospitalisation and repatriation for the whole stay. OCMA (PMLP) decides within 30 days. This is Latvia's only working holiday agreement currently in force.

LVA.name: Long-Stay Visa / Residence Permit for Researchers (Scientific Research)
LVA.purpose: For scientists and researchers carrying out research work in Latvia, either under EU researcher mobility from another Member State or under a hosting/scientific cooperation agreement with a Latvian scientific institution.
LVA.notes: Implements EU Directive 2016/801 on the entry and residence of researchers. A scientist who holds a long-term visa or temporary residence permit for research issued by another EU Member State and who plans research work in Latvia for more than 180 days (together with accompanying family members) can obtain a long-stay Type D visa, issued for up to one year (standard D-visa processing 15 days, up to 60 days if further checks are needed). For longer stays a temporary residence permit is issued to researchers invited by a Latvian scientific institution listed in the register of scientific institutions under a research cooperation agreement, granted for the duration of the cooperation plan up to a maximum of 5 years. The fee may be reduced or waived for scientific research visits under Directive 2016/801; otherwise the standard EUR 90 (approx USD 97) D-visa fee applies. See also the EU Immigration Portal 'Researcher in Latvia' page (home-affairs.ec.europa.eu).

MAC.name: Ordinary Visitor Visa
MAC.purpose: Issued through PRC diplomatic missions to nationals of countries not on the visa-free list (excluding the 6 advance-visa-required nationalities who must use this route) for tourism, family visits, and general travel to Macau.
MAC.notes: Applied through PRC Chinese embassies or consulates abroad. Validity options: single-entry 3 months/14 days stay, dual-entry 3 months/14 days stay, multiple-entry 6 months/30 days stay, 1 year/30 days stay, or 2 years/30 days stay. Standard fee USD 30 per adult plus USD 15 per child; relay communication fee USD 20 applies if consulate must relay to Macau PSP. Express (3 working days) and Urgent (2 working days) services available. Passport must be valid 90+ days beyond intended stay.

MAC.name: Entry Permit (Authorization to Enter and Stay - Visa on Arrival)
MAC.purpose: Allows nationals not on the 88-country visa-free exemption list to apply for permission to enter and stay in Macau for up to 30 days upon arrival at a border checkpoint.
MAC.notes: Fee in MOP: individual single MOP200, individual multiple MOP300; family passport single MOP400, multiple MOP600; children under 12 single MOP100, multiple MOP150; groups of 10+ with collective travel document single MOP100, multiple MOP150. Not available to nationals of Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Vietnam - those nationalities must obtain an advance visa through a PRC diplomatic mission. Diplomatic/consular identification holders from those 6 nationalities may still use visa-on-arrival.

MAC.name: Transit Stay
MAC.purpose: Allows travellers transiting through Macau with a confirmed onward journey to remain in Macau for up to 7 days without a visa.
MAC.notes: Applicant must hold a valid onward/return ticket. Transit stay is granted at the border checkpoint. Passport must be valid for the period of stay.

MAC.name: Ordinary Visitor Visa (Business/Group Tour Purpose)
MAC.purpose: Issued through PRC diplomatic missions for business visits or group tours to Macau, requiring a travel agency guarantee letter and member roster for group applications.
MAC.notes: Group tours require a travel agency guarantee letter, member roster, and proof of accommodation and transportation for all members, plus collective financial statements. Business visitors must provide documentation of the business purpose. Same fee schedule as ordinary visitor visa.

MAC.name: Ordinary Visitor Visa (Employment Purpose) / Non-Resident Worker Authorization
MAC.purpose: Required for foreign nationals who intend to work in Macau as non-resident workers; the visa is obtained through a PRC diplomatic mission and is tied to an employment authorization issued by Macau authorities.
MAC.notes: Required documents: completed application form, passport copy, and copy of employment authorization issued by Macau authorities. The employment authorization must be obtained from the competent Macau department before the visa is applied for. Non-resident workers are issued a Non-resident Worker's Identification Card upon entry. Stay duration determined by the employment authorization period.

MAC.name: Ordinary Visitor Visa (Study Purpose)
MAC.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals enrolling at higher education institutions in Macau, requiring an admission letter from the institution and proof of financial means and accommodation.
MAC.notes: Required documents: completed application form, passport bio page copy, financial proof (bank statements), admission letter from a recognized Macau institution, and proof of accommodation. Students are granted Special Authorization to Stay upon arrival and registration with the institution. Stay duration aligned to the academic program.

MAC.name: Ordinary Visitor Visa (Family of Non-Resident Worker)
MAC.purpose: Allows family members of authorized non-resident workers in Macau to obtain a visa to join or visit the worker.
MAC.notes: Required documents: completed application form, passport copy, and copy of the special authorization notification issued to the non-resident worker in Macau. Relationship documentation (marriage certificate, birth certificate) is also required. Stay is subject to Special Authorization to Stay for family dependents.

MAC.name: Diplomatic Visa
MAC.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic passports travelling to Macau in an official diplomatic capacity, granting unlimited length of stay.
MAC.notes: Diplomatic passport holders of any nationality (except US diplomatic passport holders, who are explicitly excluded) may enter without restriction on stay duration. Holders of a Laissez Passer issued by the United Nations or a diplomatic/consular identity card issued by the Macau SAR are also covered. US diplomatic passport holders must obtain an advance visa through a PRC diplomatic mission.

MAC.name: Official Visa
MAC.purpose: Issued to holders of official/service passports travelling to Macau on government business under applicable bilateral mutual visa-suppression agreements.
MAC.notes: Macau has bilateral agreements with certain countries covering official/service passport holders. The official Macau government source references 'countries and regions which have reached a mutual visa-free agreement with the Macao Special Administrative Region' but does not publish a full list of covered countries for service/official passports on the public-facing pages. Conditions and stay duration depend on the specific bilateral agreement.

MAC.name: Temporary Residence Permit by Investment (IPIM)
MAC.purpose: Allows non-local individuals holding major investments beneficial to the Macao SAR - major investors, fixed-deposit/real-estate investors, and management or technical personnel with special qualifications - to obtain a Macau temporary residence permit, renewable and leading to eligibility for permanent residence after 7 years.
MAC.notes: Administered by the Commerce and Investment Promotion Institute (IPIM, https://www.ipim.gov.mo). Three application pathways: (1) major investment beneficial to the Macao SAR under assessment/approved; (2) management or technical personnel with special qualifications; (3) fixed-deposit or local real-estate investment. Covers family dependents (spouse, children, parents) who must maintain the principal applicant's qualifying legal status. After 7 continuous years of temporary residence the holder may request a Confirmation Declaration toward permanent residence (not granted automatically). The approved residence authorization certificate is exchanged for a Macao Non-permanent Resident Identity Card via the Public Security Police Force (https://www.gov.mo/en/services/ps-1480/). Official fee and permit validity not published in English on the government portal.

MAC.name: Talent Recruitment Residency (Qualified Personnel Scheme, Law No. 7/2023)
MAC.purpose: Residency scheme to attract qualified personnel to Macao under three programmes - High-end Talents, Outstanding Talents, and Advanced Professionals - in support of the SAR's economic diversification.
MAC.notes: Enacted by Law No. 7/2023 and Administrative Regulation No. 19/2023 (in force 1 July 2023); administered by the Talent Development Committee (人才發展委員會). Three programmes: High-end Talents and Outstanding Talents (no local employment or habitual residence in Macao required to maintain status) and Advanced Professionals (must be locally employed, meet salary thresholds, and maintain habitual residence in Macao). Approval grants a residence authorization / temporary residence in Macau. Applications are filed online via the Talent Introduction Plan Electronic Application Platform (https://trplatform.cdqq.gov.mo). Qualifying applicants may receive tax benefits. Official fee and permit validity not published in English on the committee portal.

MAC.name: Residence Authorization by Family Reunion
MAC.purpose: For a foreign national who is the spouse (or eligible family member) of a Macao resident, granting the right to reside in Macao by family reunion.
MAC.notes: Distinct from the 'family of non-resident worker' visitor visa: this is a residence authorization for the family of a Macao RESIDENT. Per the official PSP Residence Authorization FAQ, any person who marries a Macao resident may apply for Residence Authorization at the Residence and Stay Affairs Department, provided the application meets Law No. 16/2021 and Administrative Regulation No. 38/2021. Holders must make Macao their centre of living and reside at least 183 days/year from the effective date, and not be away for more than half a year per departure, or the authorization may be revoked / renewal refused. The approved residence authorization is exchanged for a Macao Non-permanent Resident Identity Card. Official fee not published in English on the government portal.

MAC.name: Non-resident Worker's Identification Card (Blue Card)
MAC.purpose: The in-Macao work-stay permit held by a foreign national employed by a Macao employer that holds a valid employment authorization (informally the 'Blue Card').
MAC.notes: Represents a 'Non-resident Worker's Authorization to Stay' granted by the PSP Residence and Stay Affairs Department (Non-resident Workers Subdivision). Applied for through the employer, who must first hold employment authorization (quota) issued by the Labour Affairs Bureau (DSAL) under the non-resident workers regime (Law No. 21/2009). Card validity is tied to the employment authorization and the worker's travel document; it must be renewed/updated when either changes. Distinct from the ordinary employment-purpose entry visa obtained abroad through a PRC diplomatic mission. Official fee not published in English on the government portal.

MAC.name: Special Authorization to Stay for Non-resident Students
MAC.purpose: In-Macao stay authorization for enrolled non-resident students whose initial authorization to stay is shorter than their higher-education program, covering the program duration.
MAC.notes: Governed by Law No. 16/2021 and Administrative Regulation No. 38/2021; administered by the PSP Stay Subdivision. For students admitted to an accredited Macao higher-education institution on programs lasting one scholastic year or longer, applied for when the limit of stay in the original 'Authorization to Stay' granted on entry is not long enough to remain legally until the program ends. Applies to both Mainland and international (other country/region) students. Distinct from the ordinary visitor visa (study purpose) obtained abroad. Official fee and required documents not published in English on the government portal.

MAR.name: Short-Stay Visa (Visa de Court Séjour)
MAR.purpose: Tourism, leisure, and short visits to Morocco for nationals not exempt from visa requirements. Required for stays up to 90 days for visa-obligated nationalities.
MAR.notes: Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate. Most Western nationals receive visa-free access instead. Processing times are approximately 5-10 business days per unofficial sources. Official fees and processing times not available from official sources due to WAF access restrictions on consulat.ma.

MAR.name: Business Short-Stay Visa
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Morocco for business meetings, commercial activities, or professional visits of short duration not requiring work authorization.
MAR.notes: Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate. Many nationalities receive visa-free entry for business purposes (e.g., German, UK, US, Canadian nationals for up to 90 days). This visa is for visa-obligated nationals conducting business activities. Official fees not published on accessible official sources.

MAR.name: Work/Employment Long-Stay Visa
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to take up paid employment in Morocco. Applicants require a work contract from a Moroccan employer and approval from the National Agency for the Promotion of Employment and Skills (ANAPEC).
MAR.notes: Long-stay visa (visa de long séjour). After arrival, holders must obtain a Certificat d'Immatriculation (residence permit) from the Bureau des Etrangers of the local police prefecture or Commissariat Central within 90 days. Requires an employer-signed work contract and ANAPEC endorsement for most nationalities.

MAR.name: Student Long-Stay Visa
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted to a Moroccan educational institution for studies of more than 90 days duration. Requires proof of enrollment in a recognized Moroccan institution.
MAR.notes: Long-stay visa (visa de long séjour - étudiant). Requires university or school acceptance letter, proof of financial means for the duration of study, and accommodation proof. After arrival, holders must register for a residence permit (Certificat d'Immatriculation).

MAR.name: Investor Long-Stay Visa
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to invest in Morocco, requiring a recommendation from official investment authorities including Regional Centers of Investment (C.R.I.) or the Management of External Investments.
MAR.notes: Requires recommendation from the Management of External Investments, a professional federation, a proper authority for supervision, Regional Centers of Investment (C.R.I.), or a Moroccan partner or foreign investor branch in Morocco. No formal minimum investment threshold is published on official sources. This is a long-stay visa within the ordinary visa framework, not a golden visa or CBI program.

MAR.name: Family Reunification Long-Stay Visa
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals joining a spouse, parent, or other close family member who is legally residing in Morocco. Enables long-term family reunification stays.
MAR.notes: Long-stay visa (visa de long séjour - regroupement familial). Requires proof of family relationship, proof that the sponsor is legally resident in Morocco with a valid residence permit (Certificat d'Immatriculation), and proof of adequate housing and financial means.

MAR.name: Transit Visa (Visa de Transit)
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to a third State who need to cross Moroccan territory en route. Not for entry/stay in Morocco itself.
MAR.notes: Official definition (consulat.ma): the transit visa authorises a foreigner travelling to a third State to cross the territory of Morocco; it may be issued for one or two transits, with the duration of each transit not exceeding 72 hours. Required only for nationals of countries that require a transit visa for Morocco; most nationals who are visa-exempt for Morocco do not need one. Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate. In exceptional cases the security services may issue short-stay and transit visas at border posts.

MAR.name: eVisa (Visa Electronique - Category A: Nationality-Based)
MAR.purpose: Electronic visa for tourism and short stays, available to nationals of specific countries who are otherwise subject to standard visa requirements. Applied for online prior to travel via the official acces-maroc.ma portal.
MAR.notes: Launched 10 July 2022 via the official acces-maroc.ma portal. Valid for 30 days, extendable up to 6 months, with multiple entries. Processing time 24-72 Moroccan working hours. Category A nationalities (nationality-based): Thailand, Israel, India (effective 10 Jan 2023), Jordan (effective 10 Jan 2023), Guatemala (effective 10 Jan 2023), and others including Benin, Brunei, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam per secondary sources. Eligible nationals apply online without visiting an embassy.

MAR.name: eVisa (Visa Electronique - Category B: Credential-Based)
MAR.purpose: Electronic visa for tourism and short stays available to any nationality that holds a valid residence permit or multiple-entry visa issued by an eligible country (EU states, US, UK, Canada, Japan, Norway, Switzerland, New Zealand, Australia, Israel, UAE).
MAR.notes: Credential-based eVisa eligibility: (1) valid residence permit of an EU member state, US, UK, Canada, Japan, Norway, Switzerland, New Zealand, Australia, Israel, or UAE - valid minimum 180 days from application date; OR (2) valid non-electronic multiple-entry visa of the US, Australia, Canada, UK, Ireland, New Zealand, or Schengen area - valid minimum 90 days from application date. Apply via www.acces-maroc.ma. Visa valid 30 days, extendable up to 6 months with multiple entries. Processing 24-72 Moroccan working hours.

MAR.name: Electronic Travel Authorization (AEVM - Autorisation Electronique de Voyage au Maroc)
MAR.purpose: Required prior travel authorization for visa-free nationals of certain countries (Congo Brazzaville, Guinea Conakry, Ecuador, Ghana). Not a visa but a mandatory pre-registration for otherwise visa-free nationals.
MAR.notes: Required permanently for Congo (Brazzaville), Guinea (Conakry), Ecuador, and Ghana nationals despite their visa-free status. Applied for online via www.acces-maroc.ma before departure. This is not a visa - it is an electronic pre-authorization for entry. Several other African nations had temporary AEVM requirements for AFCON 2025 (25 September 2025 to 25 January 2026) which have since been lifted.

MAR.name: Conference/Seminar Short-Stay Visa (Visa Conferences)
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals attending a conference, seminar, workshop, or professional meeting in Morocco.
MAR.notes: One of the ordinary visa purposes officially listed by the Moroccan consular services (Tourism, Work, Business, Investor, Conferences, Student, Intern, Researcher, Family reunification, Journalist). Short-term visa (1-90 days per stay). Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate; typically requires an official invitation letter from the organising body. Not available online. Official fees not published on accessible official sources (consulat.ma is WAF-protected).

MAR.name: Intern/Trainee Visa (Visa Stagiaire)
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking an internship or professional training placement with a host organisation in Morocco.
MAR.notes: One of the ordinary visa purposes officially listed by the Moroccan consular services. Requires an original copy of the internship/training agreement signed by the host organisation. Issued as a short-stay visa (up to 90 days) or, for placements exceeding three months, as a long-stay visa after which the holder must obtain a registration card (Certificat d'Immatriculation) from the DGSN. Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate. Official fees not published on accessible official sources.

MAR.name: Researcher Visa (Visa Chercheur)
MAR.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting research hosted by an approved Moroccan research organisation.
MAR.notes: One of the ordinary visa purposes officially listed by the Moroccan consular services. Requires a hosting agreement signed with an approved Moroccan research organisation. Issued as a short-stay visa (up to 90 days) or, for stays exceeding three months, as a long-stay visa after which the holder must obtain a registration card (Certificat d'Immatriculation) from the DGSN. Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate. Official fees not published on accessible official sources.

MAR.name: Journalist Visa (Visa Journaliste)
MAR.purpose: For foreign media professionals travelling to Morocco to carry out press, reporting, or media activities.
MAR.notes: One of the ordinary visa purposes officially listed by the Moroccan consular services. Issued for professional journalism/media activity; typically requires accreditation or authorisation from the relevant Moroccan authorities (Ministry of Communication/press accreditation) in addition to the standard visa file. Applied for at a Moroccan embassy or consulate; not available online. Official fees not published on accessible official sources.

MAR.name: Visa Issued at the Border (Border Visa)
MAR.purpose: Short-stay or transit visa granted, in exceptional cases, at Moroccan border posts (airports/land crossings) by the security services to travellers who could not obtain a visa in advance - typically those whose country of residence has no Moroccan diplomatic mission.
MAR.notes: One of the four official entry-visa types listed by the Moroccan consular services (short-term visa, long-term visa, transit visa, and visa issued at the border). Per the official wording, 'in some exceptional cases the Security Services may issue short-stay and transit visas at the Border Posts.' This is not a guaranteed visa on arrival - it is issued only in exceptional circumstances and does not confer an irrevocable right of entry. A traveller whose country of residence has no Moroccan diplomatic mission may request a border/airport visa in advance from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Directorate of Consular and Social Affairs in Rabat (visa@maec.gov.ma). Official fees not published on accessible official sources (consulat.ma is WAF-protected).

MCO.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourist
MCO.purpose: Allows non-EEA, non-Schengen-exempt nationals to visit Monaco and the Schengen Area for tourism for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Monaco does not issue its own visas; this visa must be obtained from the embassy of the Schengen country serving as the primary European entry point.
MCO.notes: Monaco has no independent visa issuance system. Non-EEA nationals who are not Schengen-visa-exempt must apply for a Schengen Type C short-stay visa at the embassy/consulate of the Schengen country that is their primary destination or first point of entry into Europe. Once a valid Schengen visa is held, entry to Monaco requires no additional formalities. EEA nationals and Monaco-designated 'associated states' (UK, Andorra, San Marino, Vatican City, Switzerland) are visa-free for stays up to 90 days.

MCO.name: Visa-Free Entry (EEA and Associated States)
MCO.purpose: Nationals of EEA member states and countries Monaco treats equivalently (UK, Andorra, San Marino, Vatican City, Switzerland) may enter and stay for up to 90 days with only a valid passport or national identity card. No visa is required.
MCO.notes: Confirmed visa-free countries include: Germany, Andorra, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Denmark, Spain, Estonia, Vatican City, France, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Iceland, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Norway, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Czech Republic, Romania, United Kingdom, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Sweden, and Switzerland. Passport or valid national identity card required. Confirmed across multiple Monaco official embassy pages in June 2026 (re-confirmed 2026-06-29).

MCO.name: Visa-Free Entry (Schengen-exempt third-country nationals)
MCO.purpose: Nationals of non-EEA countries that are exempt from the Schengen short-stay visa requirement may enter Monaco without a separate visa for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period, in accordance with the Schengen external border rules Monaco follows.
MCO.notes: Monaco official pages direct visitors to France's Service-Public.fr for the authoritative list of Schengen-visa-exempt nationalities. ETIAS (expected Q4 2026, fee €20 for ages 18–70, 3-year validity) will add a pre-travel authorisation requirement for these nationals transiting Schengen territory to reach Monaco. EES became fully operational 10 April 2026. A transitional period of at least 6 months applies after ETIAS launch.

MCO.name: Monaco Residence Permit (Carte de Séjour) - Long Stay
MCO.purpose: Any person aged 16 or over wishing to stay in Monaco for more than 3 months must obtain a Monaco residence permit. Non-EEA nationals must first obtain a French long-stay Type D visa before applying. Covers all long-stay purposes including work, study, and family.
MCO.notes: First residence permit fee is €80. Non-EEA nationals must first obtain a French long-stay (Type D) Schengen visa or transfer from French residency of over one year. The permit requires proof of sufficient funds (amount at discretion of Monaco bank providing reference), accommodation in Monaco, and police background check (criminal records extract less than 3 months old from last country of residence within the past 5 years). After 10 years of ordinary residence from age 18, holders may apply for Monegasque naturalisation. A valid Monaco residence permit allows non-Schengen nationals to travel within the Schengen Area without a short-stay visa. No fixed minimum deposit amount is stated on official pages - the widely cited €500,000 figure appears only in third-party sources. A personal interview is mandatory once the application file is complete.

MCO.name: Monaco Work Authorisation (Work Permit)
MCO.purpose: Required for any foreign national taking up salaried employment in Monaco. The employer applies to the Monaco Employment Service (Direction du Travail) for authorisation to hire; the employee also needs a residence permit (and, if non-EEA, a French long-stay Type D visa first).
MCO.notes: All employment in Monaco requires a work permit regardless of nationality. The employer submits the hiring/renewal authorisation application to the Employment Service (Service de l'Emploi / Direction du Travail) with a €5 stamp duty; appointments are booked via MonGuichet.mc. Recruitment follows a statutory priority order (Monegasque nationals first, then residents) under Act No. 629. Non-EEA workers must hold a valid residence permit authorising employment, obtained after a French long-stay Type D visa. This is a distinct authorisation from the residence permit itself.

MCO.name: Monaco Business Permit (Authorisation to Carry Out a Professional Activity)
MCO.purpose: Required for foreign nationals wishing to set up and run a business or carry out a self-employed / professional activity in Monaco (sole trader or company). Issued by the Minister of State.
MCO.notes: Foreign nationals must obtain a business permit (autorisation d'exercice) from the Minister of State, examined by the Business Development Agency, before operating as a sole trader or setting up a company. The statutory review period is 45 days from notification that the application is admissible. Since September 2025 sole-trader applications can be filed fully online via MonGuichet.mc. Authorised operators must register with the self-employed social-security schemes CAMTI/CARTI. A business permit underpins the self-employed route to a Monaco residence permit.

MCO.name: Residence Permit – Spouse of a Monegasque National
MCO.purpose: Residence permit for a foreign national married to a Monegasque citizen. (Family members joining a non-Monegasque foreign resident instead apply under the general residence permit.)
MCO.notes: Distinct residence-permit category issued to the foreign spouse of a Monegasque national (minimum 1 year of residence). Valid 5 years; first-issue fee €80, renewal €40. Non-EEA spouses must first obtain a French long-stay Type D visa via the French consulate before applying. Family members joining a non-Monegasque foreign resident apply under the general 'temporary' or 'ordinary' residence permit rather than this specific category.

MCO.name: Residence Permit for Retired / Financially Self-Sufficient Persons
MCO.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals who do not intend to work in Monaco and support themselves through a pension or sufficient savings.
MCO.notes: The official first-permit application explicitly defines a non-working applicant category: retirees provide proof of pension, and self-funded applicants provide a reference letter (less than 1 month old) from a Monaco banking establishment confirming sufficient funds to live in Monaco. Issued as a 'temporary' residence permit valid 1 year (renewable), first-issue fee €80. Non-EEA applicants must first obtain a French long-stay Type D visa. Monaco publishes no fixed minimum deposit; the widely cited €500,000 figure appears only in third-party sources. This self-sufficiency route is Monaco's de facto residence-by-means path — there is no citizenship- or investment-by-investment visa program.

MCO.name: Residence Permit - Student
MCO.purpose: Residence permit route for foreign nationals coming to Monaco to study (e.g. at the private International University of Monaco). Study is one of the recognised applicant categories for the Monaco first residence permit; there is no standalone Monaco student visa.
MCO.notes: Study is an official applicant category for the Monaco first (temporary) residence permit - applicants must submit proof of student status. Issued as a temporary permit valid 1 year (renewable), first-issue fee €80. Non-EEA students must first obtain a French long-stay (Type D) visa for Monaco via the French Consulate before applying; EEA and Swiss nationals need no visa. Applicants must be at least 16 years old.

MCO.name: Ordinary Resident Permit (Carte de Séjour Ordinaire)
MCO.purpose: Second-tier Monaco residence permit for foreign residents who have completed at least 3 years of continuous residence in the Principality, extending the right to reside for a longer period than the initial temporary permit.
MCO.notes: Available after 3 years of residence in Monaco. Valid 3 years. First-issue fee €100, renewal €50. This is a progression tier of the same carte de séjour, not a separately-chosen visa. Ten years of ordinary residence from age 18 is the precondition for eligibility to apply for Monegasque naturalisation. Non-EEA holders retain Schengen travel rights via the Monegasque permit.

MCO.name: Privileged Resident Permit (Carte de Séjour Privilégié)
MCO.purpose: Highest-tier, longest-validity Monaco residence permit for foreign nationals who have genuinely resided in the Principality for at least 10 years (reducible to 1 year in special cases at the government's discretion). Nearest equivalent to permanent residence in Monaco.
MCO.notes: Requires at least 10 years of genuine residence in Monaco (reducible to 1 year in special cases). Valid 10 years - the longest Monegasque residence permit and the nearest thing to permanent residence; Monaco issues no separate settlement/permanent-residence permit. First-issue fee €160, renewal €80. Non-EEA holders retain Schengen travel rights via the permit.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/T (Tourism)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Moldova for tourist purposes, including visits to tourist attractions, recreation, and leisure activities.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires confirmed reservation at tourist accommodation, medical insurance of at least €30,000. Apply at Moldovan embassy/consulate or via e-visa portal at evisa.gov.md. 90 days within any 180-day period.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/A (Business)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Moldova for commercial or economic purposes, including negotiations, meetings, conferences, and trade activities.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires business invitation, proof of accommodation, and subsistence funds (minimum €30/day). Medical insurance required. 90 days within any 180-day period.

MDA.name: Airport Transit Visa Type A
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through a Moldovan international airport without entering the country's territory.
MDA.notes: Fee is €20 (approx USD 22). Requires onward air ticket for destination country and evidence of admission to the third country of destination. Only for international transit zone at airport.

MDA.name: Transit Visa Type B
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Moldova by land, sea, or air en route to a third country.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires valid travel ticket to destination country, proof of entry permission in destination country, and medical insurance of at least €30,000. Transit duration typically up to 5 days.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/MI (Official Mission)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Moldova on official government or public administration missions.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires verbal note from the sending government or public administration body. Valid passport issued within 10 years.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/V (Private Visit)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting family members or friends who are residents of Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires invitation from host resident, copy of host's identity document, and medical insurance. 90 days within any 180-day period.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/TS (Transport)
MDA.purpose: For professional drivers and transport workers engaged in freight or passenger transport through or to Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires transport license, vehicle registration documents, and proof of employment as transport professional.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/S (Sports)
MDA.purpose: For athletes, coaches, and sports officials participating in official sports competitions or events in Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires official sports delegation list, proof of accommodation, and medical insurance.

MDA.name: Short-Stay Visa Type C/AD (Cultural/Scientific/Humanitarian/Medical)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals participating in short-term cultural, scientific, humanitarian, religious, or health/medical-treatment activities in Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Official MFA catalogue lists C/AD scope as cultural, scientific, humanitarian, religious and medical-treatment (health) activities for short stays; long-term medical treatment uses the separate D/TR visa. Requires justification of the activity's purpose, proof of accommodation, and medical insurance.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/AI (Entrepreneurship/Investment)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to establish or invest in a business in Moldova, including shareholders and company founders.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires proof of investments or business activity in Moldova, criminal record certificate, and medical insurance. Entry visa that precedes application for temporary residence permit based on investment/entrepreneurship.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/AM (Employment)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals who have received authorization to work in Moldova, including seasonal workers.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires work authorization decision from Moldova's General Inspectorate for Migration (IGM), proof of subsistence, and criminal record certificate. Covers both permanent and seasonal employment.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/AS (Study)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals accepted to study at an educational institution in Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires confirmation of enrollment/approval to study from the educational institution and proof of financial capacity to support studies and stay.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/VF (Family Reunification)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals joining a spouse, children, or parents who hold a residence permit or are citizens of Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires acceptance for family reunification from Moldova's authorities and proof of family ties (marriage certificate, birth certificates, etc.).

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/RU (Religious/Humanitarian)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting religious, charitable, or humanitarian volunteer work in Moldova.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires registration of the religious or charitable organization in Moldova, a volunteer/employment contract, and proof of accommodation.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/DS (Diplomatic/Service)
MDA.purpose: For diplomatic staff, consular officers, and accredited international organization personnel and their family members.
MDA.notes: No consular fee. Requires diplomatic passport and verbal note from the sending state. Issued to diplomatic mission staff and accredited international organization personnel posted to Moldova.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/TR (Medical Treatment)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Moldova for long-term medical treatment at a medical institution.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires acceptance letter from the medical institution in Moldova, and proof of financial capacity to cover treatment costs.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/IT (IT Activities)
MDA.purpose: For technology specialists intending to carry out IT activities, particularly within Moldova's IT Park system.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires employer declaration from an IT Park registered company and an employment decision. Entry visa preceding temporary residence permit application for IT activities in Moldova's IT Park.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/TP (Intra-Company Transfer)
MDA.purpose: For foreign employees temporarily transferred to a branch, subsidiary, or affiliated entity in Moldova within the same company.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires confirmation of the intra-company transfer, copy of the legal entity's registration certificate in Moldova.

MDA.name: Long-Stay Visa Type D/FT (Internship/Professional Training)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals participating in professional development programs, internships, or vocational training at a Moldovan organization.
MDA.notes: Fee is €40 (approx USD 43). Requires confirmation from the legal entity in Moldova of the internship/training purpose and program details.

MDA.name: Digital Nomad Residence Permit (Remote Work)
MDA.purpose: For foreign nationals who work remotely for foreign companies or clients while residing in Moldova.
MDA.notes: Introduced via Law 144/2025, in force 20 September 2025. This is a residence permit (not a visa). Applicants must demonstrate minimum income of 18 times Moldova's forecasted average salary per year for the preceding 6 months (approx €2,700-2,800/month as of 2026). Income must derive exclusively from remote work for foreign entities - as employee, independent contractor, or shareholder/partner. Valid health insurance and proof of accommodation required. Apply in person at General Inspectorate for Migration (IGM) in Chisinau. Duration up to 2 years, renewable. Fee governed by Law on state fees no. 213 of 31.07.2023 (exact amount not published on official source).

MDG.name: Tourist eVisa (Electronic Travel Authorization)
MDG.purpose: Short-stay tourism visits to Madagascar. Covers leisure, sightseeing, and non-business activities.
MDG.notes: Available to all nationalities except Burundi and Palestine. Four fee tiers based on stay duration (eVisa only - effective 16 February 2026): 1–15 days = US$35/€30 (tripled from US$10/€10); 16–30 days = US$41/€35; 31–60 days = US$47/€40; 61–90 days = US$59/€50. The fee increase applies exclusively to the eVisa system; VoA fees at airports/consulates were not confirmed as changed (may retain pre-increase 15-day rate of US$10/€10). Apply 1 week to 6 months before departure; ETA issued within 72 hours. Diplomats and employees of certain international organizations are exempt from fees.

MDG.name: Tourist Visa on Arrival
MDG.purpose: Short-stay tourism visits granted at the port of entry for travelers who did not apply online in advance.
MDG.notes: Available at international airports and ports for all nationalities except Burundi and Palestine. Allows up to 90 days (eVisa is capped at 60 days). The official eVisa portal (evisamada-mg.com) states 'the prices of the online visa are the same as those paid on arrival,' indicating the February 2026 fee schedule applies on arrival as well: 1–15 days = US$35/€30; 16–30 days = US$41/€35; 31–60 days = US$47/€40; 61–90 days = US$59/€50 (portal currently displays placeholder amounts while the service is being upgraded). Can be extended to a maximum total stay of 90 days within Madagascar. Diplomats and employees of certain international organizations are exempt from fees.

MDG.name: Short-Stay Business Visa (Non-Immigrant)
MDG.purpose: Short-term business visits including meetings, trade missions, internships, and short business assignments without paid employment in Madagascar.
