MDG.notes: Classified under the short-stay non-immigrant visa category by Madagascar Embassy Paris. Covers business visits, short missions, internships, and journalism. Maximum stay up to 90 days with up to 3 entries. Work authorization is not included. Can be issued by diplomatic missions or at airport immigration offices. No paid work permitted.

MDG.name: Long-Stay Work/Expatriate Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term stay for expatriate workers and employees of companies operating in Madagascar; intended to be converted into a long-stay residence permit at the Ministry of Interior.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival - cannot be issued on arrival. Once in Madagascar, the holder must apply for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior (Department of Immigration) within 1 month of arrival. Categories include expatriate workers, NGO members, and religious missionaries. Source: Madagascar Embassy Paris visa categories page.

MDG.name: Long-Stay Student Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term stay for foreign nationals enrolled in an educational institution in Madagascar; intended to be converted into a long-stay residence permit.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival - cannot be issued on arrival. Once in Madagascar, the holder must apply for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior within 1 month of arrival. Listed explicitly as a long-stay transformable visa category by Madagascar Embassy Paris.

MDG.name: Long-Stay Retirement/Rentier Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term residence for retirees and those making a definitive move to Madagascar; intended to be converted into a permanent residence permit.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival. Holder must apply for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior within 1 month of arrival. Listed as 'rentiers' (retirees/those living on investment income) in the long-stay transformable category by Madagascar Embassy Paris. Vocation to obtain permanent residence permit.

MDG.name: Investor/Business Long-Stay Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term residence for foreign investors, business creators, or those transferring businesses to Madagascar; intended to be converted into a long-stay residence permit.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival - cannot be issued on arrival or via eVisa. Once in Madagascar, the holder applies for a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior (Department of Immigration) within 1 month. Managed by EDBM (Economic Development Board of Madagascar). No minimum investment amount specified on accessible official pages. Categories include investors, business creators, and business transferees.

MDG.name: Long-Stay Family Reunification Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term stay for foreign nationals joining family members residing in Madagascar; intended to be converted into a long-stay residence permit.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival. Once in Madagascar, the holder must apply for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior within 1 month. Listed as a specific long-stay transformable category ('family reunification') by Madagascar Embassy Paris.

MDG.name: Special/Diplomatic Visa (Visa Spécial)
MDG.purpose: Entry for diplomats, international organization staff, development agency personnel, and their eligible family members on official assignment.
MDG.notes: Issued to holders of diplomatic passports, international organization staff, development agency personnel, and their family members. Fee-exempt. Issued by diplomatic missions or the Madagascar Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Duration up to 1 month per the Madagascar Embassy Paris page. Bilateral agreements (with India, China, Morocco) additionally grant full visa-free entry for diplomatic/service passport holders of those countries.

MDG.name: Long-Stay Journalist & Internship Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term stay for foreign journalists on assignment and for trainees/interns (stagiaires); intended to be converted into a long-stay residence permit.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival. Once in Madagascar, the holder must apply for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior within 1 month. Madagascar Embassy Paris lists journalist long-term missions (journalistes) and long-term internships (stagiaires) as distinct transformable categories. Short-stay non-transformable variants also exist for journalist missions and internships under 3 months (court séjour, max 90 days, up to 3 entries).

MDG.name: Long-Stay Missionary & NGO/Volunteer Visa (Transformable)
MDG.purpose: Long-term stay for religious missionaries and members of foreign or local NGOs/associations working in Madagascar; intended to be converted into a long-stay residence permit.
MDG.notes: Initial visa validity is 1 month. Must be obtained from a consulate before arrival - cannot be issued on arrival or via eVisa. Once in Madagascar, the holder applies for conversion to a Long Stay Visa at the Ministry of Interior (Department of Immigration) within 1 month. Madagascar Embassy Paris lists 'membres des ONG étrangères' (foreign NGO members), 'membres des associations/ONG locales' (local associations/NGOs) and religious missionaries (missionnaires) as distinct long-stay transformable categories. A common pathway for foreign missionaries and NGO/humanitarian volunteers in Madagascar. No official fee published on accessible government pages.

MDV.name: Tourist Visa on Arrival
MDV.purpose: Leisure travel and tourism to the Maldives. No business activities or paid/unpaid work permitted.
MDV.notes: Granted free of charge on arrival to all nationalities except Israeli passport holders (ban effective 15 April 2025). Requires: MRZ-compliant passport with minimum 1 month validity, return/onward ticket within 30 days of arrival, confirmed accommodation or proof of funds (min USD 100 + USD 50/day), completed IMUGA Traveller Declaration (via imuga.immigration.gov.mv, up to 96 hours before arrival). Yellow Fever vaccination certificate required if travelling from endemic countries (children under 1 exempt). Extendable in-country up to 60 additional days (total 90 days) by applying to Maldives Immigration before expiry. Extension process streamlined effective April 23, 2026 under Maldives 2.0 Initiative. Azerbaijan ordinary passport holders receive 90 days visa-free under bilateral agreement (signed Sept 2025).

MDV.name: Work e-Visa
MDV.purpose: For foreign nationals holding an approved Work Permit to reside and work in the Maldives.
MDV.notes: Validity mirrors the associated Work Permit; renewed visas have a maximum validity of 1 year. Must be obtained within 15 days of arrival in the Maldives on a valid Work Permit. As of 23 November 2025, physical visa stickers are no longer valid - only the digital e-Visa via the Xpat Online System (xpat.egov.mv) is recognized. Employer or authorized representative submits the application. Requires valid Work Permit from Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology.

MDV.name: Business Visa
MDV.purpose: Temporary multiple-entry visa for foreign nationals visiting the Maldives for business-related purposes.
MDV.notes: Temporary multiple-entry visa granted for 30 to 90 days at a time, not to exceed a total of 180 days per calendar year. Applied online only via the Business Portal (business.egov.mv); not issued on arrival. Applications are first reviewed by the Ministry of Economic Development, then verified and processed by Maldives Immigration. Requires a passport with minimum 6 months validity and a recent photograph (within 3 months); applicant must not hold a visa type under Article 9 of Law No. 1/2007 nor fall under the entry prohibitions in Article 8. Fees and processing times not published on the official page. Distinct from the tourist visa, which prohibits business engagements.

MDV.name: Dependent Visa
MDV.purpose: For immediate family members (dependents) of expatriates in professional categories working in the Maldives.
MDV.notes: Issued to immediate family members of expatriates employed in professional categories in the Maldives. Fee MVR 750 plus MVR 50 card fee (approx. USD 52 total). Applied online via the IMUGA portal. First-time entrants must arrive under a Sponsorship Declaration (filed at least 5 working days before arrival), then apply for the Dependent Visa after arrival. Requires application form IM23, passport copy and photo, proof of relationship, a medical report, health insurance, and the sponsorship declaration. Duration, entries, and processing times not published on the official page.

MDV.name: Student Visa
MDV.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled at a recognised educational institution in the Maldives.
MDV.notes: Issued by Maldives Immigration to enrolled international students. Two-stage process: (1) before travel, the sponsoring institution files a Sponsorship Declaration (form IM21) that must be approved before entry; (2) after arrival, the student applies for the Student Visa (form IM23) within 30 days. Approved health and travel insurance (e.g., MVR 800 / approx. USD 52 annually) is mandatory for the visa duration. Applied via the IMUGA portal (imuga.immigration.gov.mv). There is no dedicated public Student Visa page on immigration.gov.mv; the process is documented by The Maldives National University (public university, mnu.edu.mv/international-students). Application fee not published on official pages.

MDV.name: Marriage Visa (Resident Visa - Marriage-based)
MDV.purpose: For foreign nationals married to Maldivian citizens, allowing long-term residence in the Maldives.
MDV.notes: Issued for 1 year on a new application; extensions issued for up to 5 years per renewal (extension requires a minimum of 3 months remaining before expiry). MVR 50 card fee (approx. USD 3). Applied exclusively online via the IMUGA portal (imuga.immigration.gov.mv). Those marrying in the Maldives must first obtain Sponsorship Declaration approval before arrival, then register the marriage legally, then apply for the visa. Requires passport copy, marriage certificate, a Family Court-stamped form, and (first-time only) medical screening and health insurance. Confirmed on the official Maldives Immigration Marriage Visa page (re-verified 2026-07).

MDV.name: Sponsorship (Sponsorship Declaration)
MDV.purpose: Pre-arrival permit requested by a Maldivian citizen or a professional-category visa holder to bring a foreign national into the Maldives (for visiting, dependency, or other approved purposes); prerequisite step for Dependent, Student and Marriage visas.
MDV.notes: Not a stay-granting visa itself but the pre-arrival sponsorship approval required before a foreign national travels under a non-tourist category. Applied online via the IMUGA portal (form IM21); the applicant must not be in the Maldives when applying. The sponsored person must arrive within 30 days of approval; a pre-arrival sponsorship approval slip is issued on the portal. A company seal is required if the sponsor is an employer. Fees, duration, and processing times not published on the official page. Verified on the official Maldives Immigration Sponsorship Declaration page (2026-07).

MDV.name: Meeting Visa
MDV.purpose: On-arrival short-stay visa for foreign nationals whose primary purpose is attending a meeting, conference or convention held in the Maldives.
MDV.notes: Effective 14 May 2023: a 14-day on-arrival short-stay visa granted to foreign nationals attending a meeting, conference or convention in the Maldives, provided general entry requirements are met. Non-extendable; the holder cannot obtain a Business Visa while in the country. A Traveller Declaration must be submitted electronically via IMUGA (imuga.immigration.gov.mv) within 96 hours before flight departure. Fee not published on the official page. Verified on the official Maldives Immigration Meeting Visa page (2026-07).

MDV.name: Resident Visa
MDV.purpose: Long-term residence in the Maldives; per the official Resident Visa page, granted to a foreign national married to a Maldivian citizen.
MDV.notes: The official immigration.gov.mv/visa/resident page describes the Resident Visa as granted to a foreign national married to a Maldivian citizen: initial validity 1 year, renewable up to 5 years, MVR 50 (approx. USD 3) card fee, applied online via the IMUGA portal, requiring pre-arrival sponsorship and completed legal marriage registration before applying. This is the same marriage-to-Maldivian residence route also captured in the Marriage Visa entry. The Corporate Resident Maldives program (permanent-residency card for qualifying foreign investors) and the Pearl Residence by-investment program are tracked separately under rbi. Verified on the official Maldives Immigration Resident Visa page (2026-07).

MEX.name: Visitor Visa - Non-Lucrative (Visa de Visitante sin Permiso para Realizar Actividades Remuneradas)
MEX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Mexico for tourism, transit, business meetings, studies, or medical treatment without engaging in paid activities. Covers activities that do not generate income within Mexico.
MEX.notes: Citizens of 50+ nationalities are visa-exempt and may enter without a visa for up to 180 days. Those requiring a visa must apply at a Mexican consulate. Immigration officer determines the exact authorized stay up to 180 days. FMM card issued at land borders must be retained for departure. UK temporary residents (students, workers) who are not permanent residents must apply for this visa even if their nationality is on the visa-free list.

MEX.name: Visitor Visa - Business (Visa de Visitante con Permiso para Realizar Actividades Remuneradas)
MEX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Mexico to carry out paid or lucrative activities on a temporary basis, such as short-term contracts, conferences, or professional services paid from abroad.
MEX.notes: This category authorizes remunerated activities during the visitor stay. Applicants must demonstrate the purpose of the visit and source of remuneration. Issued at Mexican consulates abroad. For stays intended to exceed 180 days or for full employment in Mexico, a Temporary Resident Visa with work authorization is required instead.

MEX.name: Transit Visitor Visa (Visa de Visitante en Tránsito)
MEX.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to transit through Mexico en route to a third country, covering layovers or brief stops that require passing through Mexican immigration.
MEX.notes: Visa-exempt nationals do not require a transit visa. Citizens of nationalities that require a visa must obtain one prior to transit. Transit visas are covered under the Visitor Visa framework in Mexico's Ley de Migración. The standard non-lucrative visitor visa also covers transit purposes for those who require a visa.

MEX.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Studies (Residente Temporal - Estudiante)
MEX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Mexico for the purpose of studying at an accredited educational institution for a period exceeding 180 days.
MEX.notes: Issued for stays exceeding 180 days and up to 4 years (annual renewals). Requires acceptance letter from a Mexican educational institution. Holder must apply for a Temporary Resident Card (Tarjeta de Residente Temporal) at INM within 30 days of arrival. Short-term study programs of up to 180 days may use the non-lucrative visitor visa instead.

MEX.name: Temporary Resident Visa with Authorization for Paid Activities (Residente Temporal con Permiso para Realizar Actividades Remuneradas)
MEX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Mexico and engage in paid employment or professional activities under a Mexican employer or contract for stays exceeding 180 days.
MEX.notes: Requires an offer of employment or contract from a Mexican company. The employer typically initiates the process with INM to obtain a work authorization (oficio de autorización) before the applicant applies at the consulate. Issued for up to 1 year, renewable annually up to 4 years total. Holder must register at INM within 30 days of arrival for Temporary Resident Card.

MEX.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Remote Worker / Digital Nomad (Residente Temporal - Solvencia Económica)
MEX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals with income from outside Mexico to reside in the country for more than 180 days without taking local employment, serving as the de facto digital nomad pathway.
MEX.notes: Mexico has no separately named digital nomad visa. Remote workers apply for the standard Temporary Resident Visa under economic solvency. Requirements: minimum monthly income of approximately $3,738 USD (equivalent to ~400 UMA days/month based on UMA $117.31/day as of February 2026) evidenced for 6 months, OR savings of approximately $73,258 USD. Income must originate from outside Mexico. Valid for 1 year, renewable annually up to 4 years. No minimum presence requirement.

MEX.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Rentista / Economic Solvency (Residente Temporal - Solvencia Económica / Rentista)
MEX.purpose: Allows retirees and persons with passive income or sufficient assets to reside in Mexico on a temporary basis without working locally.
MEX.notes: Financial requirements (based on UMA $117.31/day as of February 2026): average monthly income equivalent to ~400 UMA days (~MXN $46,924/month) for 6 months; OR average monthly bank balance of ~20,000 UMA days (~MXN $2,346,200) for 12 months; OR real property in Mexico exceeding ~40,000 UMA days (~MXN $4,692,400) in assessed value. Grants up to 4 years temporary residency, renewable. After 4 years can apply for Permanent Residency.

MEX.name: Temporary Resident Visa for Investors (Residente Temporal - Inversión)
MEX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals who have made qualifying investments in Mexico to reside there on a temporary basis for up to 4 years.
MEX.notes: Investment threshold: equity stake, assets, or business activity exceeding approximately MXN $5,378,663 (45,850 UMA days at $117.31/day as of February 2026; approximately EUR 256,127 per Belgium embassy page). Can also qualify by employing at least 3 Mexican workers. Visa must be used within 180 days of issuance. Does not authorize paid employment in Mexico. Must apply for Temporary Resident Card at INM within 30 days of arrival. After 4 years of temporary residency can apply for Permanent Residency.

MEX.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Family Unity (Residente Temporal - Unidad Familiar / Vínculo Familiar)
MEX.purpose: Allows immediate family members (spouse, children, dependent parents) of Mexican citizens, permanent residents, or temporary residents to live in Mexico under family reunification.
MEX.notes: Issued to spouses, children, and dependent parents of Mexican nationals or of foreigners holding temporary or permanent resident status. Duration mirrors the principal holder's residency or up to 4 years. Holder must apply for Temporary Resident Card at INM within 30 days of arrival. Can lead to Permanent Residency after required period.

MEX.name: Permanent Resident Visa (Visa de Residente Permanente)
MEX.purpose: Grants indefinite authorization to reside in Mexico without the need for periodic renewal, available to those who have completed 4 years as a Temporary Resident, qualify through marriage to a Mexican national, or meet the economic solvency threshold for permanent residency.
MEX.notes: Pathways to permanent residency include: (1) completing 4 consecutive years as a Temporary Resident; (2) being the spouse or dependent child of a Mexican citizen; (3) economic solvency - requires average monthly bank balance exceeding approximately $292,859 USD (12-month period). Grants indefinite right of residence. Work authorization included. After the required period of actual physical residence, permanent residents may apply for Mexican nationality by naturalization.

MEX.name: Diplomatic and Official Visa (Visa Diplomática / Visa Oficial)
MEX.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic, official, service, or consular passports traveling to Mexico on official missions or private visits, under bilateral agreements between Mexico and the issuing country.
MEX.notes: No consular fee applies. Many countries' diplomatic/official/service passport holders are visa-exempt under bilateral agreements (see conditional_access entries). Where a visa is required, it is issued within 1 working day of submitting complete documentation. A verbal note from the applicant's diplomatic representation is required. US diplomatic/official passport holders receive 180 days (not 90). Pakistan diplomatic passport holders receive 3 months. Passport must remain valid from entry date onward.

MEX.name: Visa Electrónica / SAE (Sistema de Autorización Electrónica)
MEX.purpose: An electronic visa (officially called 'Visa Electrónica' by the SRE) required for certain nationalities traveling to Mexico by air. Applied for online before travel; classified as e_visa not ETA because the SRE itself calls it a visa.
MEX.notes: Currently covers: Brazil (air travel only, effective February 5, 2026; 180 days max stay); Russia, Turkey, Ukraine (air travel only; stay duration determined by immigration officer at port of entry, not fixed by the document). Authorization valid 30 days from issuance. Single entry. Land and sea entry by these nationalities still requires a traditional consular visa. Apply online at visaelectronica.sre.gob.mx. The SRE program page at gob.mx/sre/acciones-y-programas/visa-electronica-sae confirms this is officially called 'Visa Electrónica'.

MEX.name: Working Holiday Visa (Visa de Trabajo y Vacaciones) - Mexico-New Zealand
MEX.purpose: Allows young New Zealand nationals (aged 18-30) to travel in Mexico for up to one year while undertaking incidental short-term work or study to help fund the holiday, under the reciprocal Mexico-New Zealand Working Holiday agreement.
MEX.notes: Reciprocal bilateral scheme. New Zealand citizens aged 18-30 inclusive at time of application, no accompanying dependents. Holder must not work for the same employer for more than 3 months and may take one training/study course of up to 3 months. Apply at the Embassy of Mexico in Wellington. On arrival the holder must register with INM within 30 days to obtain a one-year Temporary Resident Card. New Zealand was Mexico's first working-holiday partner; Mexico also has an in-force Vacaciones y Trabajo (Working Holiday) agreement with France (see separate entry).

MEX.name: Regional Visitor Card (Tarjeta de Visitante Regional, TVR)
MEX.purpose: Allows nationals and permanent residents of Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador and Honduras to make short, repeated visa-free visits to Mexico's southern border states.
MEX.notes: Free of charge; valid 5 years with multiple entries. Each entry permits transit/visit of up to 7 calendar days limited to five southern border states: Campeche, Chiapas, Tabasco, Quintana Roo and Yucatan. Does NOT authorize paid/remunerated activities. Issued on the spot at one of seven designated southern-border internation points after biometric capture; no online application. Eligible: nationals of Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador and Honduras (and permanent residents of those countries).

MEX.name: Border Worker Visitor Card (Tarjeta de Visitante Trabajador Fronterizo, TVTF)
MEX.purpose: Allows Guatemalan and Belizean nationals holding a job offer to work legally in Mexico's southern border states.
MEX.notes: For nationals of Guatemala and Belize with a written job offer. Authorizes paid/remunerated work with multiple entries and exits, limited to four southern border states: Campeche, Chiapas, Tabasco and Quintana Roo. Valid 1 year, renewable. Fee approximately MXN $581 (2026 rate, ~31 USD); applicants earning the regional minimum wage are exempt from the fee. Issued at designated southern-border internation points; not available online.

MEX.name: Humanitarian Visitor Visa (Visa / Condicion de Estancia de Visitante por Razones Humanitarias)
MEX.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who need to enter or remain in Mexico for humanitarian reasons - e.g. victims or witnesses of crime, unaccompanied minors, asylum seekers, persons whose life or integrity is at risk, or those providing disaster relief.
MEX.notes: Statutory condicion de estancia under Article 52(V) of the Ley de Migracion. May be requested at a Mexican consulate (consular authorization valid 30 business days to enter) or applied for / regularized inside Mexico at INM. Grounds include family ties where a relative is a victim of disaster or violence or is in a serious state of health, and members of relief/rescue organizations on temporary non-remunerated missions; applicants are also advised of the right to request refugee status on entry. The resulting card is valid up to 1 year and is renewable while the humanitarian cause subsists; the humanitarian-visitor condition permits paid work in Mexico.

MEX.name: Adoption Visitor Visa (Visa de Visitante para Realizar Trámites de Adopción / Visitante con Fines de Adopción)
MEX.purpose: Issued to a foreign national carrying out the adoption of a Mexican minor, authorizing them to remain in Mexico until the adoption is finalized and the child can lawfully leave the country with the adoptive parent(s).
MEX.notes: Statutory condicion de estancia 'Visitante con fines de adopción' under the Ley de Migración (Art. 52). Applicable to foreign nationals who are nationals or habitual residents of a country party to the Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption, or of a country with which Mexico has a bilateral adoption agreement. Requires the adoptability/pre-assignment report issued by the DIF (Sistema Nacional para el Desarrollo Integral de la Familia) and acceptance of the assignment by the receiving State's Central Authority. No fixed stay length: the holder may remain until the adoption resolution is executed, the child's birth certificate is registered, the Mexican passport is issued and documents guaranteeing the child's admission to the adoptive parent's country of residence are obtained. Apply by appointment via the MiConsulado portal at a Mexican embassy/consulate; within 30 calendar days of entry the holder must obtain the tarjeta de visitante con fines de adopción from INM.

MEX.name: Working Holiday Visa (Visa de Vacaciones y Trabajo / Trabajo y Vacaciones) - Mexico-France
MEX.purpose: Allows young French nationals (aged 18-30) to holiday in Mexico for up to one year while undertaking incidental paid work to help fund the stay, under the reciprocal Mexico-France Vacaciones y Trabajo agreement.
MEX.notes: Reciprocal bilateral scheme, in force since 1 September 2016. Reserved for French citizens (not third-country nationals resident in France), aged 18-30 inclusive at time of application; may be obtained only once in a lifetime. Requires proof of funds of approximately EUR 2,500 and health/medical insurance covering the full stay. Apply at the Embassy/Consulate of Mexico in France by appointment via the MiConsulado portal. On arrival the holder registers with INM within 30 days to obtain a one-year Temporary Resident Card. Both states may set an annual cap on beneficiaries.

MHL.name: V1 Visitor Visa
MHL.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting the Marshall Islands for tourism or personal travel. Covers short-term non-immigrant stays for leisure, sightseeing, or visiting family and friends.
MHL.notes: V1 is the visitor visa category listed on the official RMI Division of Immigration applications page. Applicants not eligible for visa-on-arrival or visa-free entry must apply in advance. Fee of approximately $100 referenced in Embassy notes. Requires 6+ months passport validity, confirmed return/onward ticket, applicable visas for onward destinations, and proof of sufficient funds.

MHL.name: B1 Business Visa
MHL.purpose: For foreign nationals entering the Marshall Islands for business activities such as meetings, negotiations, or conferences. Does not authorize employment.
MHL.notes: B1 is the business visa category listed on the official RMI Division of Immigration applications page for 'establishing, seeking to establish, or conducting trade with a business'. The official enrollment page states the Business VISA (B-1) is valid for up to 2 years (validity_days=730); the 90-day figure is the typical initial admitted-stay per entry. Fee of approximately $300 referenced in Embassy notes. Does not permit change of status to employment. Application form and checklist available from rmiimmigration.org.

MHL.name: E1 Employment Visa
MHL.purpose: For foreign nationals who have secured employment in the Marshall Islands. Authorizes the holder to reside and work in the Republic for the duration specified.
MHL.notes: Corrected 2026-07-04: E1 is the employment visa category listed on the official RMI Division of Immigration applications and enrollment pages. The enrollment page's regulatory section (Work VISAs, §136) states the work visa is 'valid for the same duration as the work permit or not more than 21 calendar days longer than the duration of the permit' - i.e. validity is tied to the underlying work permit, not a fixed 2-year term (prior validity_days=730 removed). Specific fees and processing times are not published online; applicants should contact the Division directly at majuro.doi@gmail.com or (692) 625-8633. A work permit, job offer, and employer sponsorship are required.

MHL.name: S1 Student Visa
MHL.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in or accepted to an educational institution in the Marshall Islands. Authorizes study for the duration of the academic program.
MHL.notes: S1 is the student visa category listed on the official RMI Division of Immigration applications and enrollment pages for 'studying at a school or academic institution'. The enrollment page states the Student VISA (S-1) is valid for up to 1 year (validity_days=365). Specific fees and processing timelines are not published online. Requires acceptance letter from a recognised institution in the Marshall Islands. Extensions, change of status, and employment are subject to separate approval.

MHL.name: G-1 General Visa
MHL.purpose: For the legal spouse or dependent child of a person who is legally working in or stationed in the Marshall Islands. A dependant/family visa tied to a principal status holder (e.g. an E-1 employment or D-1 diplomatic visa holder).
MHL.notes: Corrected: the official RMI Division of Immigration enrollment page defines the General VISA (G-1) as for the 'legal spouse or dependent child of a person who is legally working or stationed' in the Republic - i.e. a family/dependant visa, not a generic catch-all category. Validity up to 2 years. Fees and processing times are not published online; contact the Division at majuro.doi@gmail.com or (692) 625-8633.

MHL.name: T-1 Transit Visa
MHL.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through the Marshall Islands en route to another country. Covers short stopovers, not entry for tourism, business, work, or study.
MHL.notes: The official RMI Division of Immigration enrollment page defines the Transit VISA (T-1) as for travellers in 'transit to another country', valid for up to 3 days. Onward travel documentation is expected. Fees and processing times are not published online; contact the Division at majuro.doi@gmail.com or (692) 625-8633.

MHL.name: R-1 Residence Visa
MHL.purpose: For non-citizens seeking to reside in the Marshall Islands for longer than six months. The long-term residence permit for foreign nationals settling in the Republic.
MHL.notes: The official RMI Division of Immigration enrollment page defines the Residence VISA (R-1) for non-citizens registering to reside in the Republic beyond six months, valid for up to 5 years. Fees and processing times are not published online; contact the Division at majuro.doi@gmail.com or (692) 625-8633.

MHL.name: C-1 Cruising Visa
MHL.purpose: For foreign nationals cruising in Marshall Islands waters, typically owners and crew of private or recreational vessels/yachts calling at the Republic's atolls.
MHL.notes: The Cruising VISA (C-1) is listed as a distinct visa category on the official RMI Division of Immigration enrollment page. Detailed stay length, validity, and fee are not published online; contact the Division at majuro.doi@gmail.com or (692) 625-8633. Distinct from the visa-free exemption for cruise-ship passengers staying under 7 days.

MHL.name: D-1 Diplomatic Visa
MHL.purpose: For serving diplomats visiting or stationed in the Marshall Islands who require an issued visa (as opposed to entering on a diplomatic-passport waiver).
MHL.notes: The official RMI Division of Immigration enrollment page defines the Diplomatic VISA (D-1) as for serving diplomats visiting or stationed in the Republic, valid for up to 2 years. This is the issued diplomatic visa category, distinct from the diplomatic/official-passport visa waiver (no visa required) available to diplomatic passport holders under the VOA summary.

MHL.name: Visa on Arrival (Visitor)
MHL.purpose: Allows nationals of eligible countries to obtain entry permission upon arrival at a Marshall Islands port of entry for short-term tourism or business visits without needing to obtain a visa in advance.
MHL.notes: Available to nationals of countries listed in the official 'Summary of Countries Entitled for Visa Exemption/Waiver or Visa On Arrival' (March 2024 update). Fee is waived for all listed VOA-eligible countries. Stay is 90 days from date of arrival. Extensions, change of status, and employment are not permitted. Requires: 6+ months passport validity from date of departure, confirmed return/onward ticket, and applicable visas for onward destinations. Countries on the VOA list include Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Japan, India, South Korea, South Africa, Brazil, and many others. Pacific Island Forum members and countries with diplomatic relations with RMI are generally included.

MHL.name: Diplomatic/Official Passport Visa Waiver
MHL.purpose: Allows holders of diplomatic passports or UN Laissez-Passer travelling on official or diplomatic missions to enter the Marshall Islands without a visa for an unrestricted period.
MHL.notes: Listed under the 'ALL OTHERS – VISA WAIVERS' section of the official RMI immigration summary (March 2024). Diplomatic passport holders of any nationality entering on a diplomatic mission, and Laissez-Passer holders on official missions, are exempt from visa requirements with no period restriction. Japanese and Indian diplomatic/official passport holders receive a specific 90-day waiver under the same section.

MKD.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
MKD.purpose: Permits transit through an international airport in North Macedonia without passing through border control. Required for certain nationalities transiting through Macedonian airports.
MKD.notes: Airport transit only; does not permit entry into North Macedonia territory. Must be obtained at a North Macedonian embassy or consulate abroad.

MKD.name: Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourism/Business/Transit
MKD.purpose: Permits short-term entry for tourism, business, or transit through North Macedonia. Valid for stays up to 90 days for tourism/business, or up to 5 days for transit purposes.
MKD.notes: Fee is 60 EUR (approximately 65 USD); reduced fee of 35 EUR for children aged 6–12. Transit sub-category allows up to 5 days stay. Applicant's travel document must be valid for at least 3 months beyond the intended stay. Required documents: valid passport, travel insurance, invitation letter (if applicable), proof of sufficient funds, and a recent photograph (3.5×4.5 cm). Covers tourism, business visits, and transit through the country.

MKD.name: Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
MKD.purpose: Permits short-term entry for business visits, meetings, negotiations, conferences, and similar commercial activities in North Macedonia. Issued as a Type C short-stay visa for a business purpose.
MKD.notes: Business is one of the purposes covered by the Type C short-stay visa; North Macedonia has no separate business-visa letter. Maximum stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Fee is 60 EUR (approximately 65 USD). Required documents: valid passport (valid at least 3 months beyond the intended stay), travel insurance, invitation letter from the host company/organisation, proof of sufficient funds, and a recent photograph (3.5x4.5 cm). Must be applied for at a North Macedonian embassy or consulate abroad.

MKD.name: Short-Stay Transit Visa (Type C - Transit)
MKD.purpose: Specifically for transit through North Macedonia territory (not airport-only), permitting a short stay of up to 5 days while transiting between countries.
MKD.notes: This is a sub-category of the Type C visa specifically issued for transit. Maximum stay is 5 days. Fee is 60 EUR. Must be applied for at a North Macedonian embassy or consulate abroad.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Work
MKD.purpose: Permits entry into North Macedonia for the purpose of taking up employment. Requires prior approval of a temporary residence permit from the Ministry of Interior.
MKD.notes: Long-stay D visa sub-category for work purposes. Must have prior approval of temporary residence permit from the Ministry of Interior before applying. Also covers vocational training and practical training. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); 35 EUR for children aged 6-12, per the MFA visa application procedure page. A separate work permit from the Employment Service Agency is required before employment.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Study / Student Exchange
MKD.purpose: Permits entry for the purpose of studying, enrolling in educational institutions, or participating in international student exchange programmes in North Macedonia.
MKD.notes: Long-stay D visa sub-category for study. Covers study, participation in international student exchange programmes, and specialisation, vocational and practical training. Requires prior approval of temporary residence permit from the Ministry of Interior. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); 35 EUR for children aged 6-12, per the MFA visa application procedure page.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Medical Treatment
MKD.purpose: Permits entry into North Macedonia for the purpose of receiving medical treatment or accommodation in nursing homes.
MKD.notes: Long-stay D visa sub-category for medical purposes. Covers medical treatment and accommodation in nursing/care homes. Requires prior approval of temporary residence permit from the Ministry of Interior. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); 35 EUR for children aged 6-12, per the MFA visa application procedure page.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Family Reunion
MKD.purpose: Permits entry into North Macedonia for family reunification with a North Macedonian citizen or a foreign national legally residing in the country.
MKD.notes: Long-stay D visa sub-category for family reunion. Also extends to close family members of North Macedonian citizens. Requires prior approval of temporary residence permit from the Ministry of Interior. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); 35 EUR for children aged 6-12, per the MFA visa application procedure page.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Scientific Research / Volunteering / Humanitarian
MKD.purpose: Permits entry for scientific-research activities, volunteering, or humanitarian reasons in North Macedonia.
MKD.notes: Long-stay D visa covering scientific-research activities, volunteering, and humanitarian reasons. Requires prior approval of temporary residence permit from the Ministry of Interior. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); 35 EUR for children aged 6-12, per the MFA visa application procedure page.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Persons of Macedonian Origin
MKD.purpose: Permits foreign nationals of Macedonian origin (ethnic Macedonian descent) to enter North Macedonia to obtain temporary residence on a facilitated basis.
MKD.notes: Long-stay D visa sub-category. The MFA 'Types of entry visas' page lists 'persons of Macedonian origin' as a distinct ground for temporary residence, separate from ordinary family reunion (also listed alongside close family members of Macedonian citizens and children born in the country to foreign parents). Requires prior approval of temporary residence from the Ministry of Interior. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); 35 EUR for children aged 6-12, per the MFA visa application procedure page.

MKD.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Property Owner (EU/OECD nationals)
MKD.purpose: Permits EU and OECD nationals who own property in North Macedonia (valued at minimum EUR 40,000) to apply for a long-stay visa leading to temporary residence.
MKD.notes: Restricted to EU and OECD nationals. Property must be an apartment, residential building, or house valued at a minimum of EUR 40,000. Temporary residence issued for up to 1 year and can be renewed annually. Long-stay (D) visa fee is 70 EUR (approximately 76 USD); the EUR 40,000 is the qualifying property value, not a fee. Path to permanent residence/citizenship not specified in official sources reviewed.

MLI.name: Mali Short-Stay Entry Visa (Tourism)
MLI.purpose: General short-stay entry visa for tourism, family visits, and leisure travel for foreign nationals holding ordinary passports who are not visa-exempt.
MLI.notes: Mali issues a single general entry visa for all short-stay purposes (tourism, business, family), priced by duration and number of entries rather than by purpose. Official tariff per the Permanent Mission of Mali to the UN (un.int/mali): 3-month single entry USD 80, 3-month multiple entry USD 110, 6-month multiple entry USD 200, 1-year multiple entry USD 370. Separately, the Mali Embassy in Washington DC charges US citizens a flat USD 185 for a visa valid up to 5 years, multiple entry. Applications are submitted online via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs portal at diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml/vitrine/. Visas are NOT issued on arrival at Malian airports. Yellow fever vaccination certificate mandatory. US citizens are currently subject to a reciprocal entry ban effective January 1, 2026 (with limited exceptions).

MLI.name: Mali Entry Visa (Business)
MLI.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals travelling to Mali for meetings, conferences, commercial negotiations, or other professional activities.
MLI.notes: Mali does not publish a separately named business visa instrument; business travel uses the same general entry visa as tourism, priced by duration and number of entries. Business trips are commonly issued a 3-to-6-month multiple-entry visa. Official tariff (Permanent Mission of Mali to the UN, un.int/mali): 3-month multiple entry USD 110, 6-month multiple entry USD 200, 1-year multiple entry USD 370. US citizens are charged a flat USD 185 (up to 5 years, multiple entry) by the Mali Embassy in Washington DC. Apply online via diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml/vitrine/. Yellow fever certificate mandatory. US citizens currently subject to a reciprocal entry ban (effective January 1, 2026).

MLI.name: Mali Diplomatic / Official Visa
MLI.purpose: Visa for holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports travelling to Mali on behalf of their government or an international organization.
MLI.notes: Free of charge; 3-year validity, multiple entry per maliembassy.us. Covers diplomatic passport holders and holders of laissez-passer for international organizations. A note verbale from the sending government may be required (noted by ambamali.ca). Some nationalities holding diplomatic/service passports are exempt from visa requirements entirely.

MLI.name: Mali Long-Stay Visa (Visa de Long Sejour - Employment)
MLI.purpose: Long-stay entry visa for foreign nationals taking up employment or residing in Mali for more than six months; followed by an in-country residence card and work permit.
MLI.notes: Mali issues a long-stay visa (visa de long sejour) for stays over six months, used by expatriate workers, employees, and long-term residents. The official 1-year multiple-entry entry-visa fee is USD 370 (Permanent Mission of Mali to the UN, un.int/mali). After arrival, foreign employees must obtain a residence card (carte de sejour) from the Direction Nationale de la Police and a work permit (permis de travail) from the Ministere du Travail; the employer initiates the work-permit application. The carte de sejour is valid up to one year, renewable, and costs roughly 50,000-100,000 XOF locally. There is no separately named work visa instrument - this is the general long-stay entry visa. Apply online via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs portal.

MLI.name: Mali Long-Stay Visa (Visa de Long Sejour - Studies)
MLI.purpose: Long-stay entry visa for foreign nationals enrolling at an accredited Malian university or training institution for a course of study exceeding six months.
MLI.notes: Foreign students are admitted on the general long-stay visa (visa de long sejour); Mali does not publish a separately named student visa instrument. An admission/enrolment letter from an accredited Malian institution (e.g. University of Bamako, Ecole Polytechnique) is the central supporting document. The long-stay visa tariff applies (see un.int/mali: up to USD 370 for a 1-year multiple-entry visa); a distinct student fee is not separately published. After arrival, students obtain a residence card (carte de sejour) from the Direction Nationale de la Police. Apply online via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs portal.

MLI.name: Mali Transit Visa
MLI.purpose: Entry authorization for foreign nationals transiting through Mali en route to a third country.
MLI.notes: Transit visa is referenced as a passport type/purpose category in the Mali Ministry of Foreign Affairs online portal (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml/vitrine/), which accepts applications by nationality and passport type. Specific fee and duration not published on accessible official pages. Syrian nationals are refused even airside transit. Apply online via the MFA portal.

MLT.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
MLT.purpose: Authorises third-country nationals to visit Malta (and other Schengen states) for tourism, leisure or family visits. Does not permit employment or academic study.
MLT.notes: Valid for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Covers travel throughout the entire Schengen Zone. Standard Schengen visa fee is €90 for adults (approx. USD 100), increased from €80 effective 11 June 2024; reduced or waived for certain categories (children 6-11: €45; children under 6: free). Single-entry or multiple-entry issued based on applicant's travel history and need. Applications submitted through External Service Provider (VFS) or at a Maltese diplomatic mission. Fee Ordinance L.N.287 of 2020 applies. Malta is a full Schengen member state.

MLT.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business Purpose
MLT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Malta for business meetings, conferences, negotiations or commercial activities for up to 90 days. Does not permit taking up employment.
MLT.notes: Same Schengen Type C visa as the tourist visa; purpose declared at application as 'business'. Standard fee €90 for adults (~USD 100), increased from €80 effective 11 June 2024. Applications via VFS or Maltese diplomatic mission. Must demonstrate ties to home country and intention to leave within 90 days.

MLT.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Student
MLT.purpose: Issued to third-country nationals (including visa-exempt nationals) wishing to enrol in courses in Malta exceeding 90 calendar days.
MLT.notes: A National D-Visa (long-stay) valid for up to 365 days. Required for any course exceeding 90 calendar days even for visa-exempt nationals. Educational institutions must maintain attendance records and report non-arrivals to Identità. Applications submitted through External Service Provider (VFS). Fee Ordinance L.N.287 of 2020 applies; specific fees not published on official page - contact Central Visa Unit at visa.identita@gov.mt or +356 2590 4550.

MLT.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Employment
MLT.purpose: Issued to third-country nationals who have obtained an employment permit to work in Malta for a period exceeding 90 days.
MLT.notes: National D-Visa (long-stay) valid up to 365 days, issued alongside or after obtaining a single permit or employment licence from Identità's Expatriates Unit. Typically issued for the period of the employment permit. Fee Ordinance L.N.287 of 2020 applies. Applications submitted through Central Visa Unit or Maltese diplomatic mission. Separate from the fast-track Key Employee Initiative (KEI) or Specialist Employee Initiative (SEI) single permit processes.

MLT.name: Nomad Residence Permit
MLT.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals who work remotely using telecommunications technologies - for a foreign employer or as a freelancer/consultant with foreign clients - to reside in Malta for up to one year, renewable.
MLT.notes: Initial permit: 1 year, renewable up to 3 times (maximum 4 years total in Malta). Minimum gross annual income: €42,000 (threshold effective 1 April 2024). Applicant must work for a foreign-registered employer under contract, or be a partner/shareholder of a foreign-registered company, or provide freelance/consulting services to foreign-based clients. Requires: valid travel document, health insurance covering EU risks, property rental/purchase agreement in Malta, police clearance certificate. Applications submitted online at portal.residencymalta.gov.mt. Administered by Residency Malta Agency. Not available to EU/EEA/Swiss nationals who have right of free movement.

MLT.name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
MLT.purpose: Grants non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals permanent residency status in Malta in exchange for a qualifying financial investment in real estate and a government contribution.
MLT.notes: Grants permanent residency (not citizenship). UPDATED via Legal Notice 146 of 2025 (effective for applications from 1 January 2025). Key requirements: (1) Administration fee: €60,000 (€15,000 non-refundable upfront + €45,000 after Letter of Approval in Principle). (2) Government contribution: €37,000 (unified regardless of purchase or lease; replaces previous dual structure of €28,000 purchase / €58,000 rental). Spouse and minor children no longer attract a separate contribution fee. (3) Property: purchase min €375,000; OR lease min €14,000/year for at least 5 years. (4) NGO donation: €2,000. (5) Proof of capital: Option A - €500,000 total assets (min €150,000 financial); Option B - €650,000 total assets (min €75,000 financial). Assets monitored annually for first 5 years. (6) Adult dependant fee: €7,500 each. Residence certificate does not expire if obligations are maintained. Certain nationalities ineligible (Afghanistan, North Korea, Iran, DRC, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Yemen, Venezuela, Russia, Belarus). Regulated by S.L. 217.26.

MLT.name: Malta Residence and Visa Programme (MRVP)
MLT.purpose: Grants eligible non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals and their families Maltese residency with Schengen travel rights through a qualifying property investment.
MLT.notes: Regulated under S.L. 217.18. Grants Schengen travel rights with Maltese residency. Covers up to four generations of family members. Investment must be maintained for minimum 5 years. Full fee/investment schedule not publicly available on official pages - consult licensed agents or official MRVP FAQs PDF. Administered by Residency Malta Agency.

MLT.name: Global Residence Programme (GRP)
MLT.purpose: Tax-residency programme for non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals providing a flat 15% tax rate on foreign-sourced income remitted to Malta, with a qualifying property purchase or lease requirement.
MLT.notes: Administrative fee: €5,500 if qualifying property is in South Malta; €6,000 otherwise. Flat 15% tax on foreign-sourced income remitted to Malta; 35% on locally-sourced income. Applicants must purchase or lease qualifying property in Malta. Not available to those already long-term residents. Regulated by Malta Tax & Customs Administration (MTCA, formerly CFR). Commonly used as a retirement/passive-income residency route.

MLT.name: Malta Retirement Programme (MRP)
MLT.purpose: Special tax-residency status for EU/EEA/Swiss and non-EU nationals who are not in employment and receive a pension as their regular source of income, wishing to retire in Malta.
MLT.notes: Distinct from the Global Residence Programme (GRP): the MRP is specifically for pensioners. Grants a flat 15% tax rate on foreign pension income remitted to Malta, with a minimum annual tax of €7,500 plus €500 per dependant/household staff member. The pension must be remitted to Malta and represent at least 75% of the beneficiary's chargeable income; the applicant must not be in an employment relationship. Property requirement: purchase a qualifying property of at least €275,000 (€220,000 in Gozo or South Malta), OR rent at least €9,600/year (€8,750 in Gozo or South Malta). Beneficiary must reside in Malta for an average of at least 90 days per calendar year over any 5-year period and not reside in any other single jurisdiction for more than 183 days in a year. Non-refundable administrative fee: €2,500 (approx. USD 2,700). Applications must be submitted through an Authorised Registered Mandatary. Administered by the Malta Tax & Customs Administration (MTCA, formerly CFR). Open to both EU/EEA/Swiss and third-country national pensioners.

MLT.name: Working Holiday Visa - Australia
MLT.purpose: Allows Australian citizens aged 18–30 to live and work in Malta on a working holiday basis for up to one year.
MLT.notes: Exclusively for Australian biometric passport holders. Age: 18–30 at time of application. Visa issued free of charge by Maltese authorities; applicant pays VFS service fee (amount not published on official page). Non-renewable and one-time use only. Requires: valid biometric passport (90+ days beyond stay), comprehensive medical insurance (hospitalisation, liability, medical repatriation), proof of reasonable funds for initial stay, return ticket or funds to purchase one, no criminal record, no dependents, no prior Working Holiday Visa for Malta. Applications via VFS (Identità's External Service Provider).

MLT.name: Working Holiday Visa - Andorra
MLT.purpose: Allows Andorran citizens aged 18–30 to live and work in Malta on a working holiday basis for up to one year.
MLT.notes: Exclusively for Andorran biometric passport holders. Age: 18–30. Visa issued free of charge by Maltese authorities; applicant pays VFS service fee. Requires: valid biometric passport (90+ days beyond stay), comprehensive medical insurance, proof of funds, return ticket or funds, no criminal record, no dependents, no prior Malta working holiday visa. Applications via VFS.

MLT.name: Working Holiday Visa - Japan
MLT.purpose: Allows Japanese citizens aged 18–30 to live and work in Malta on a working holiday basis for up to one year.
MLT.notes: Exclusively for Japanese biometric passport holders. Age: 18–30. Visa issued free of charge by Maltese authorities; applicant pays VFS service fee. Requires: valid biometric passport (90+ days beyond stay), comprehensive medical insurance, proof of funds, return ticket or funds, no criminal record, no dependents, no prior Malta working holiday visa. Applications via VFS. Interviews may be conducted.

MLT.name: Working Holiday Visa - New Zealand
MLT.purpose: Allows New Zealand citizens aged 18–30 to live and work in Malta on a working holiday basis for up to one year.
MLT.notes: Exclusively for New Zealand biometric passport holders. Age: 18–30. Visa issued free of charge by Maltese authorities; applicant pays VFS service fee. Requires: valid biometric passport (90+ days beyond stay), comprehensive medical insurance (hospitalisation, liability, medical repatriation), proof of funds, return ticket or funds, no criminal record, no dependents, no prior Malta working holiday visa. Applications via VFS.

MLT.name: Working Holiday Visa - Youth of Maltese Descent
MLT.purpose: Allows young people aged 18–30 who can demonstrate Maltese descent to live and work in Malta on a working holiday basis for up to one year.
MLT.notes: For applicants aged 18–30 who can demonstrate Maltese descent through documentation (ancestor birth certificates, passports or citizenship certificates), regardless of current nationality. Visa issued free of charge by Maltese authorities; applicant pays VFS service fee. Single entry, with the arrival date specified in the application (flight itinerary must show arrival 3+ months after the expression of interest). Processing approximately 6–8 weeks. Requires: valid passport (12+ months validity), police clearance (issued within 6 months), proof of funds equal to the Median National Equivalised Income OR a hosting letter from a Maltese citizen, private health insurance. Cannot be accompanied by dependents. Extensions require applying for a residence permit in-country. Applications via VFS (Identità's External Service Provider).

MLT.name: Airport Transit Visa (ATV)
MLT.purpose: Required for nationals of certain third countries to transit through the international zone of a Schengen airport without entering Schengen territory.
MLT.notes: Airport Transit Visa (ATV) is a Schengen category for transit through the international transit area only (does not permit entry into Schengen territory). Required for nationals listed in Annex IV of EU Regulation 2018/1806 and national lists. Standard fee same as Schengen short-stay visa (€90 / ~USD 100 for adults, increased from €80 effective 11 June 2024). Not applicable to Schengen-area connecting flights without exit from international zone. Applications via VFS or Maltese diplomatic mission.

MLT.name: Malta Startup Residence Programme
MLT.purpose: Grants non-EU/EEA/Swiss startup founders, co-founders, and core employees residency in Malta to build and operate their startup business.
MLT.notes: Founders/co-founders: 3-year permit renewable for up to 5 further years. Core employees: 3-year permit renewable for 3 further years. Startup must be registered no longer than 7 years globally and operate in eligible sectors (manufacturing, software, health/biotech, eco, or other innovative activities). Minimum paid-up share capital: €25,000 (plus €10,000 per additional co-founder beyond 4; max 6 co-founders). Core employees must earn min €30,000 gross annually. Business plan must be approved by Malta Enterprise. Application fee: €750/adult applicant for 3-year permit + €300 residence card issuance + €690 Jobsplus employment licence. Jointly administered by Residency Malta Agency and Malta Enterprise. Certain nationalities ineligible.

MLT.name: Single Permit (Residence and Employment)
MLT.purpose: The primary combined residence-and-work permit authorising a third-country national to legally reside and take up employment in Malta for a period exceeding six months.
MLT.notes: Regulated by Subsidiary Legislation 217.17. A single application procedure combining an employment licence and a residence permit for third-country nationals employed in Malta for over 6 months; renewable. Applications must be submitted by the employer through the Single Permit Online Portal (live-in carers may apply directly if endorsed by the employer). Requires health insurance with minimum €100,000 coverage for the entire period of stay. On approval an Approval in Principle letter is issued; the applicant then applies for an entry visa (National Type D) as applicable and attends the Expatriates Unit in Msida for biometric capture. The Key Employee Initiative, Specialist Employee Initiative and EU Blue Card are fast-track or specialised variants of this permit. Managed by Identità's Expatriates Unit.

MLT.name: Key Employee Initiative (KEI) Single Permit
MLT.purpose: Fast-track single permit for non-EU nationals accepting managerial or highly technical positions in Malta, or roles in endorsed startups, with a minimum annual gross salary of €45,000.
MLT.notes: Processing time: 5 working days from complete application submission. Initial permit valid 1 year; renewable up to 3 years. Fee: €600 for first application; €150/year for renewal. Minimum annual gross salary: €45,000. Employer must advertise the role for at least 2 weeks within 2 months prior to application. Managed by Identità's Expatriates Unit.

MLT.name: Specialist Employee Initiative (SEI) Single Permit
MLT.purpose: Single permit for non-EU nationals in skilled roles meeting minimum qualification and salary criteria (MQF Level 6+ or equivalent experience, minimum €30,000 gross annually).
MLT.notes: For non-EU nationals not meeting KEI criteria. Minimum annual gross salary: €30,000. Requires MQF Level 6+ qualification OR lower-level qualification plus 3+ years relevant experience proven via contracts/references. Standard Single Permit process applies (processing time not specified). Managed by Identità's Expatriates Unit.

MLT.name: EU Blue Card
MLT.purpose: Residence and work permit for non-EU nationals with advanced professional qualifications and a high-salary job offer in Malta, issued under the EU Blue Card Directive.
MLT.notes: Issued under the EU Blue Card Directive. Holders may move between EU member states after 18 months of legal residence. Managed by Identità's Expatriates Unit. Full eligibility requirements and fee schedule available from Identità.

MLT.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit (Family Member)
MLT.purpose: Allows a third-country national legally residing in Malta (the sponsor) to be joined by eligible family members - spouse and minor children - from abroad.
MLT.notes: Regulated by Subsidiary Legislation 217.06 (Family Reunification Regulations). The sponsor must hold a valid Malta residence permit and have resided legally and continuously in Malta; an application may be submitted only after a minimum of 12 months from issuance of the sponsor's initial residence permit. Eligible family members: spouse (minimum age 21, monogamous marriage) and unmarried minor children under 18 (including legally adopted children). The sponsor must show stable and regular income (at least the national median annual wage plus 20% for each dependent), adequate accommodation, and health insurance with minimum €100,000 coverage per family member. Travel document must have at least 8 months' validity at submission. Applicants who do not meet the SL 217.06 criteria may still qualify under a separate Family Members Policy. Applications submitted online through the Expatriates Unit Portal. Managed by Identità's Expatriates Unit.

MLT.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa Exemption (Bilateral Treaties)
MLT.purpose: Visa-free access for holders of diplomatic, official, service or special passports of qualifying countries under bilateral agreements or national derogations communicated to the EU Commission.
MLT.notes: Malta has bilateral visa-waiver agreements for diplomatic/official/special passports with China (diplomatic: up to 30 days), Qatar (diplomatic/special), Pakistan (diplomatic/official). National derogations from the Schengen visa requirement also cover diplomatic/service/special passport holders from: Algeria (diplomatic), Bolivia (diplomatic/service), Egypt (diplomatic/service/special), India (diplomatic), Indonesia (diplomatic/service), Jordan (diplomatic), Kazakhstan (diplomatic), Morocco (diplomatic/service), Oman (diplomatic/service/special), Philippines (diplomatic/service), Thailand (diplomatic/service), Tunisia (diplomatic/service), Turkey (diplomatic/service). Source: EU OJ national derogations notice CELEX:52023XC0927(01) and individual bilateral treaty pages on foreign.gov.mt.

MMR.name: Tourist Visa
MMR.purpose: Short-term leisure and tourism visits to Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Available as e-Visa (USD 50, 28 days, valid 90 days from issuance) for approximately 100 nationalities. Also available via Visa on Arrival at Yangon, Mandalay, and Naypyidaw International Airports for China, India, Japan, South Korea, Macau SAR, and Hong Kong SAR nationals (pilot programs). Embassy/consulate tourist visa fee is USD 40. Entry at designated international airports and Kawthaung land border.

MMR.name: Business Visa
MMR.purpose: Visits for business meetings, negotiations, and commercial activities in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Available as e-Visa (USD 70) for 54 nationalities; requires invitation from registered Myanmar company or Chamber of Commerce. Also available as Visa on Arrival (USD 50, 70 days) at Yangon, Mandalay, and Naypyidaw International Airports for eligible nationalities. Multiple-entry options available at embassy (3 months USD 200, 6 months USD 400, 1 year USD 600).

MMR.name: ASEAN-China / Lancang-Mekong Multiple-Entry Business Visa
MMR.purpose: Long-validity multiple-entry visa for eligible business personnel (and accompanying spouse/children) travelling under the ASEAN-China and Lancang-Mekong Cooperation frameworks.
MMR.notes: Special multiple-entry business visa issued under the ASEAN-China and Lancang-Mekong Cooperation frameworks: USD 600, up to 180 days stay per visit, valid 5 years. Restricted to eligible business personnel and accompanying spouse/children. Embassy/consulate-issued (not e-Visa or visa on arrival). Fee and terms per the official Myanmar Consulate General (Los Angeles) visa fee schedule; this is a reciprocal regional-cooperation facilitation category (member states of the ASEAN-China Free Trade Area and the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation issue equivalent visas to each other's business travellers). Distinct from the standard Business Visa, whose multiple-entry option maxes out at 1 year validity.

MMR.name: Transit Visa
MMR.purpose: Short-term transit through Myanmar en route to another destination.
MMR.notes: Allows 24-hour transit. Available on arrival at Yangon, Mandalay, and Naypyidaw International Airports for eligible nationalities including most Western countries, ASEAN, and major Asian nations.

MMR.name: Employment Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals taking up employment in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Initial single-entry Employment Visa (USD 50, 70 days) is obtained from Myanmar embassy abroad. After arrival, a Stay Permit must be obtained from the Ministry of Immigration. Multiple-entry versions available for extended validity. Work permit from Ministry of Labour is required separately.

MMR.name: Education Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals enrolled in educational or training programs in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Single-entry Education Visa (USD 50, 90 days). Multiple-entry: 1 year for USD 160 (per official Myanmar Consulate General Los Angeles and Embassy of Myanmar Riyadh fee schedules). Requires acceptance letter from an accredited Myanmar educational institution. Extensions possible with appropriate documentation.

MMR.name: Social Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals visiting family members or for social/humanitarian purposes in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Single-entry Social Visa (USD 50, 70 days). Multiple-entry options: 3 months USD 150, 6 months USD 300, 1 year USD 450 (per official Myanmar Consulate General Los Angeles fee schedule). Covers family visits and social activities.

MMR.name: Religious Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals engaging in religious activities, missionary work, or pilgrimages in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Single-entry Religious Visa (USD 50, 70 days). Multiple-entry options: 3 months USD 150, 6 months USD 300, 1 year USD 450. Requires documentation from a recognized religious organization (missionary/clergy work).

MMR.name: Meditation Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals attending meditation retreats or undertaking monastic/religious training at a Myanmar meditation centre, monastery, or under a Sayadaw.
MMR.notes: Myanmar is the only country that issues a dedicated Meditation Visa. Single-entry USD 50, 70 days stay, valid 3 months from issue; multiple-entry options USD 150 (3 months), USD 300 (6 months), USD 450 (1 year). Requires a sponsorship/invitation letter from a recognized Myanmar meditation centre, monastery, or Sayadaw plus approval from the Ministry of Religious Affairs (approval can take 2-4 months); embassy processing thereafter is roughly 5-7 business days. Extendable in-country at the Immigration Department (up to 1 year per extension). Distinct from the Religious Visa, which covers missionary/clergy work. Confirmed as a separate category by Myanmar Consulate Hong Kong and the Embassy of Myanmar, Ottawa.

MMR.name: Journalist Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign journalists and media personnel covering events in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Single-entry Journalist Visa (USD 40, 28 days). Requires press credentials and assignment documentation. Must apply at Myanmar embassy abroad. Note: Myanmar has heavily restricted press access since the February 2021 coup; approvals are rare in practice.

MMR.name: Workshop / Seminar / Meeting / Research Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals attending or presenting at official workshops, seminars, conferences, or conducting research in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Single-entry, 28 days, USD 40. Available via embassy and also as Visa on Arrival at Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyidaw International Airports for eligible nationalities. Research visa holders may apply for extensions. Invitation/approval letter from Myanmar institution or government agency required.

MMR.name: Crew Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for air crew and maritime crew members transiting or working in Myanmar.
MMR.notes: Visa on Arrival Crew Visa: USD 40, 28 days (Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyidaw International Airports for eligible nationalities). Embassy/consulate Crew Visa: single-entry USD 50 (90 days), multiple-entry USD 160 valid 2 years (per official Myanmar Consulate General Los Angeles and Embassy of Myanmar Riyadh fee schedules). Requires crew member documentation.

MMR.name: Official / Diplomatic Visa
MMR.purpose: Entry for holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports traveling on government business.
MMR.notes: Diplomatic/Courtesy Visa is issued free of charge. Official Visa for non-diplomatic government travelers: single-entry USD 50, multiple-entry options USD 200-600. Separate from bilateral diplomatic visa exemption agreements. Duration determined case-by-case.

MNE.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
MNE.purpose: Allows transit through the international transit area of a Montenegrin airport without entering Montenegrin territory. Required for certain nationalities changing flights at Podgorica airport.
MNE.notes: Issued for one or several entries. Validity up to 3 months. Holder does not enter Montenegrin territory; stays within airport international transit zone. Processing time is 10 days from submission, extendable to 30–60 days in complex cases.

MNE.name: Transit Visa (Type B)
MNE.purpose: Allows transit through Montenegrin territory when travelling to a third destination country. Intended for travellers passing through Montenegro en route to another country.
MNE.notes: Issued for one, two, or exceptionally multiple entries. Validity up to 6 months. Stay per journey up to 5 days. Applicant must hold confirmed entry authorisation to destination country. Can be issued as a collective (group) visa. Processing time 10 days, extendable to 30–60 days.

MNE.name: Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
MNE.purpose: Allows entry and stay in Montenegro for tourism, business, personal, or other short-term purposes not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period. Also covers family visits, cultural, scientific, and other short-term activities.
MNE.notes: Issued for single, double, or multiple entries. Validity up to 1 year for multiple-entry; exceptionally up to 5 years for frequent travellers with demonstrated need and no misuse history. A collective (group) visa may be issued for organised groups with maximum 30-day validity. Financial proof required: minimum €50 per day of stay. Passport must be valid at least 3 months beyond visa. Processing 10 days, extendable to 30–60 days.

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Business/Work (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows stays exceeding 90 days but not longer than 180 days in a 12-month period for business activities or employment. Issued to foreign nationals with employment contracts or business engagements in Montenegro.
MNE.notes: One of several subcategories of the Type D long-stay visa. Requires employment contract or other proof of business activity, and financial documentation. Processing time 10 days from submission, extendable to 30–60 days. Issued for single, double, or multiple entries. Intended as a precursor to a temporary residence permit for longer-term stays.

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Diplomatic/Official (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows stays exceeding 90 days for diplomatic or consular staff and representatives of international organisations accredited to or operating in Montenegro.
MNE.notes: Subcategory of Type D long-stay visa. Requires a verbal note from the applicant's foreign ministry or an international organisation. Exempt from standard consular fees. Processing time 10 days, extendable to 30–60 days.

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Digital Nomad (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows remote workers employed by or owning a company not registered in Montenegro to reside in Montenegro for up to 180 days as a bridging status before obtaining a digital nomad temporary residence permit.
MNE.notes: Subcategory of Type D long-stay visa specifically for digital nomads. Requires proof of remote employment or ownership of a foreign-registered company, financial means, accommodation, and health insurance. For stays beyond 180 days, applicants must apply for the Digital Nomad Temporary Residence Permit (up to 2 years, renewable once for 2 more years) at the Ministry of Internal Affairs. See also: https://digitalnomads.gov.me/article/legal-status-for-nomads

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Studies (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals admitted to an educational institution in Montenegro to reside for the duration of their studies, up to 180 days initially before transitioning to a temporary residence permit.
MNE.notes: Subcategory of Type D long-stay visa. Issued for purposes of studies at accredited Montenegrin educational institutions. Proof of enrolment required. Longer-term students apply for a temporary residence permit for studies after entry.

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Medical Treatment (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals requiring medical treatment in Montenegro to stay beyond 90 days, up to a maximum of 180 days within a 12-month period.
MNE.notes: Subcategory of Type D long-stay visa. Requires documentation confirming the medical treatment to be received in Montenegro, from a recognised Montenegrin medical facility.

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Family Reunification (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows close family members of Montenegrin citizens or foreign nationals holding a valid Montenegrin temporary or permanent residence permit to stay beyond 90 days for family reunification purposes.
MNE.notes: Subcategory of Type D long-stay visa. Eligible family members include spouses and minor children (under 18). Documentation proving family relationship and sponsor's status required.

MNE.name: Long-Stay Visa – Scientific Research / Humanitarian (Type D)
MNE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals engaged in scientific research projects or humanitarian activities in Montenegro to reside for more than 90 days, up to 180 days.
MNE.notes: Subcategory of Type D long-stay visa. Covers both scientific research conducted in collaboration with Montenegrin institutions and humanitarian missions. Proof of research/humanitarian engagement required. Processing time 10 days, extendable to 30–60 days.

MNE.name: Temporary Residence and Work Permit – Employment
MNE.purpose: Main work authorisation for a foreign national employed by a Montenegrin employer; a single (unified) permit combining the right of temporary residence and the right to work.
MNE.notes: Issued for a validity period of one year and may be extended up to two years. Requirements include a written offer of employment, proof of education and professional qualifications, and a health certificate. Application submitted in person to the ministry responsible in the foreigner's area of residence. After entry a Type D long-stay visa or visa-free entry precedes application; the permit itself is issued by the Ministry of Interior / labour authority.

MNE.name: Temporary Residence and Work Permit – Seasonal Employment
MNE.purpose: Work authorisation for foreign nationals performing seasonal work (e.g. tourism, hospitality, agriculture) for a Montenegrin employer.
MNE.notes: Issued for a validity period of up to six months within a period of one year. Requirements mirror the standard employment permit (written job offer, proof of qualifications, health certificate). Submitted in person at the responsible ministry.

MNE.name: Temporary Residence and Work Permit – Contracted Services Provision
MNE.purpose: Work authorisation for an employee of a foreign company providing services in Montenegro under a service contract concluded with a Montenegrin entity.
MNE.notes: Issued for one year and may be extended until the end of the service or up to two years. Requires the service contract, proof of employment with the foreign company, and confirmation of social insurance coverage. Submitted in person at the responsible ministry.

MNE.name: Temporary Residence and Work Permit – Intra-Corporate Transfer (Secondment)
MNE.purpose: Work authorisation for a manager or specialist seconded from a foreign company to a related entity in Montenegro (intra-corporate transfer).
MNE.notes: Issued for one year and may be extended until completion of the works or up to two years. Applicant must have been employed by the foreign company for at least one year and hold manager or specialist status; confirmation of social insurance is required. Submitted in person at the responsible ministry.

MNE.name: Work Registration Certificate (Confirmation of Work Registration)
MNE.purpose: Short-term work authorisation, without a full temporary residence and work permit, for enumerated categories such as business visitors, consultants, researchers, athletes, and artists/cultural workers.
MNE.notes: Allows work for up to 90 days within a period of one year for specific categories of foreigners (e.g. persons performing business activities, researchers, athletes, cultural and artistic workers). Registered in person at the responsible ministry before work begins; it is a work registration rather than a residence permit.

MNG.name: K2 Tourist Visa
MNG.purpose: Short-term leisure and tourism travel to Mongolia. Available as an e-visa via evisa.mn.
MNG.notes: E-visa is non-extendable and non-convertible. Passport must be valid for at least 180 days. Multiple-entry temporary tourist visa (G category) also available for long-term tourists with 30-day max stay per entry and 183–365 day validity.

MNG.name: G Tourist Visa (Long-term/Multiple Entry)
MNG.purpose: Long-stay or multiple-entry tourism for foreign nationals who intend to visit Mongolia repeatedly or for extended tourism purposes.
MNG.notes: Multiple-entry temporary visa. Stay per entry is up to 30 days; validity ranges 183–365 days. Applied at Mongolian embassy/consulate.

MNG.name: K6 Transit Visa
