MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Mongolia en route to a third country. Available as an e-visa.
MNG.notes: E-visa available via evisa.mn. Non-extendable and non-convertible.

MNG.name: K3 Border Region Day Pass
MNG.purpose: For tourists making brief cross-border day trips to Mongolian border regions.
MNG.notes: Border region tourism only; issued by border immigration authority.

MNG.name: K1 Business Visa
MNG.purpose: Short-term business travel including meetings, negotiations, conferences, and commercial activities. Available without an inviting entity for 10-day stays.
MNG.notes: Single or double entry up to 90 days; validity 150 days. A 10-day business visa is available without an inviting entity per immigration.gov.mn.

MNG.name: B2 Business/Company Representative Visa
MNG.purpose: For company representatives, executives, and senior managers of foreign entities operating in Mongolia.
MNG.notes: B2-1 variant available for accompanying family members. Multiple-entry; validity up to 365 days.

MNG.name: B1 Investor Visa
MNG.purpose: For foreign investors establishing or operating business entities with foreign investment in Mongolia.
MNG.notes: B1-1 variant for family members. Minimum investment threshold for residence permit pathway is USD 100,000 (25% equity). Visa renewable; residence permit pathway available after qualifying investment.

MNG.name: B3 Foreign Legal Entity Branch Manager Visa
MNG.purpose: For managers of registered branch offices of foreign legal entities operating in Mongolia.
MNG.notes: B3-1 variant for family members.

MNG.name: C Visa (Employment Visa - Multiple Sectors)
MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals employed in Mongolia across various sectors including construction, science, mining, finance, culture, production, agriculture, healthcare, humanitarian services, and transportation.
MNG.notes: 11 sub-categories (C1–C11) covering different employment sectors. Each sub-category has a family member variant (e.g., C1-1). Requires valid employment contract and sponsoring employer.

MNG.name: E Visa (Education/Student Visa - Multiple Types)
MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals studying, conducting research, participating in language/culture/vocational training, or doing internships at Mongolian institutions.
MNG.notes: Five sub-categories: E1 (general education), E2 (higher education), E3 (language/culture/vocational), E4 (research/internship at state institutions), E5 (innovation and research). E2-1 and E5-1 variants for family members. Requires acceptance letter from accredited Mongolian institution.

MNG.name: F Visa (Family/Personal Connection Visa)
MNG.purpose: For spouses of Mongolian citizens, former Mongolian nationals, and their close relatives seeking to reside in or visit Mongolia based on family ties.
MNG.notes: Three sub-categories: F1 (spouses of Mongolian citizens), F2 (former Mongolian nationals), F3 (close relatives of former nationals). Requires supporting documentation of family relationship.

MNG.name: H Visa (Personal Purpose Visa)
MNG.purpose: For distinguished professionals, scholars, and persons with a recognized personal connection to Mongolia, including dual citizenship holders and others with personal purposes.
MNG.notes: Three sub-categories: H1 (distinguished professionals/scholars), H2 (dual citizenship holders), H3 (other personal purposes).

MNG.name: J Religious Visa
MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Mongolia for religious purposes, including missionaries, clergy, and religious organization representatives.
MNG.notes: Requires documentation from recognized religious organization.

MNG.name: K4 Cultural and Sports Visa
MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals participating in cultural events, arts competitions, or sports competitions held in Mongolia. Available as an e-visa.
MNG.notes: E-visa available via evisa.mn. Non-extendable and non-convertible. Requires official invitation from organizing body.

MNG.name: K5 Cargo/Passenger Transport Visa
MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals engaged in international cargo or passenger transport operations passing through or operating within Mongolia.
MNG.notes: For transport crew and operators in international cargo or passenger transit.

MNG.name: K8 Medical Treatment Visa
MNG.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Mongolia specifically for medical treatment at Mongolian healthcare facilities.
MNG.notes: Requires confirmation or invitation from a Mongolian medical institution.

MNG.name: K7 Work and Holiday Visa
MNG.purpose: Allows eligible Australian nationals to work and travel in Mongolia under a bilateral working holiday arrangement.
MNG.notes: Available only to Australian citizens. Applicant must be at least 18 and under 31 years of age at time of application. Cannot have previously participated in the program. Applied via the e-visa portal (evisa.mn). Introduced under Government Resolution No. 107 of 2024.

MNG.name: A1 Official/Diplomatic Visa
MNG.purpose: For foreign government officials travelling to Mongolia on official state business, requiring an invitation from Mongolia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
MNG.notes: Requires official invitation from Mongolia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. A1-1 variant for family members. A2 sub-category for accredited foreign media and international news organization staff, with A2-1 for their family members.

MNG.name: A2 Foreign Media/Journalist Visa
MNG.purpose: For accredited foreign and international media and news-organization professionals travelling to Mongolia to report or produce news content.
MNG.notes: Distinct sub-category of the A official/diplomatic visa class for foreign and international media professionals. A2-1 variant for accompanying family members. Requires media accreditation/invitation coordinated through Mongolia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

MOZ.name: Tourist eVisa (Single Entry)
MOZ.purpose: Short-stay tourism and leisure visits to Mozambique for eligible nationalities applying online through the official eVisa portal.
MOZ.notes: Duration options of 30, 60, or 90 days. Visa must be used within 60 days of issuance. Restricted nationalities (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal, Somalia) must apply at nearest embassy and cannot use the eVisa portal. Standard processing approximately 5 business days.

MOZ.name: Tourist Visa (Consular / Single Entry)
MOZ.purpose: Tourism visits obtained at a Mozambican embassy or consulate for applicants not eligible for the eVisa portal, or those applying in person.
MOZ.notes: Normal processing: 10 business days, $220 USD. Expedited processing (3 business days): $280 USD. Requires confirmed flight and hotel reservations. Visa must be used within 60 days from issuance date.

MOZ.name: Tourist Visa (Consular / Multiple Entry)
MOZ.purpose: Multi-entry tourism visits obtained at a Mozambican embassy or consulate, permitting multiple entries over the validity period.
MOZ.notes: Normal processing: 10 business days, $240 USD. Expedited processing (3 business days): $310 USD. Requires confirmed flight and hotel reservations. Visa must be used within 60 days from issuance date.

MOZ.name: Business eVisa
MOZ.purpose: Business activities in Mozambique for eligible nationalities applying online through the official eVisa portal.
MOZ.notes: Duration options of 30, 60, or 90 days. Visa must be used within 60 days of issuance. Restricted nationalities must apply at nearest embassy.

MOZ.name: Business Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Business activities in Mozambique obtained at a Mozambican embassy or consulate.
MOZ.notes: Normal processing: 10 business days, $220 USD. Expedited processing (3 business days): $280 USD. Requires letter from applicant's or inviting company, hotel and flight reservations.

MOZ.name: Visit Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Visiting family or friends in Mozambique with a signed invitation from the inviting party in Mozambique.
MOZ.notes: Normal processing: 10 business days, $220 USD. Expedited processing (3 business days): $280 USD. Requires signed invitation letter from the inviting party in Mozambique plus flight itinerary and identification documentation.

MOZ.name: Work Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Employment in Mozambique; single-entry visa obtained at a Mozambican embassy or consulate for those with authorized employment.
MOZ.notes: Single entry only. Requires authorization from Ministry of Labor, health certificate, work contract, authenticated police clearance, business letter, and business permit (ALVARA).

MOZ.name: Student Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Foreign nationals admitted to study at a Mozambican school or university; single-entry visa obtained at a Mozambican embassy or consulate.
MOZ.notes: Single entry only; issued at a Mozambican embassy/consulate - Student is not offered as an eVisa category on the evisa.gov.mz portal. Requirements: letter of acceptance from the Mozambican school/university certified by the Ministry of Education, medical certificate, police clearance record, and proof of funds and accommodation. Entry visa is intended to be converted to a longer study/residence authorization after arrival for the course duration. Fee varies by mission (Embassy of Mozambique in Japan lists JPY 10,420, approximately USD 70, for single entry); other missions charge from approximately USD 220 for single-entry consular visas. Urgent processing available at higher fees.

MOZ.name: Work eVisa (Oil & Gas Business/Work)
MOZ.purpose: Work or business activities in Mozambique's oil and gas sector via the official eVisa portal.
MOZ.notes: Listed as a distinct eVisa category on the official portal separate from standard Business eVisa. Processing approximately 5 business days.

MOZ.name: Sports & Culture eVisa
MOZ.purpose: Participation in sports events or cultural activities in Mozambique for eligible nationalities applying online.
MOZ.notes: Listed as a distinct eVisa category on the official portal.

MOZ.name: Crew eVisa
MOZ.purpose: Entry for crew members of vessels or aircraft operating in or through Mozambique.
MOZ.notes: Listed as a distinct eVisa category on the official portal.

MOZ.name: Humanitarian eVisa
MOZ.purpose: Entry for humanitarian workers and aid personnel conducting relief or development activities in Mozambique.
MOZ.notes: Listed as a distinct eVisa category on the official portal.

MOZ.name: Investment Visa (eVisa)
MOZ.purpose: Entry for foreign investors undertaking a qualifying investment project in Mozambique worth USD 500,000 or more.
MOZ.notes: Duration options: 90, 180, 365 or 730 days (multiple-entry). Minimum investment threshold: USD 500,000. Governed by Law No. 23/2022 of December 29. Processing time: 3 to 5 business days. This is an entry/investment visa; it is not a formal long-term residency-by-investment or golden visa program.

MOZ.name: Transit Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Short stay in Mozambique for passengers transiting to another destination.
MOZ.notes: Requires valid visa for the final destination unless the final destination is the applicant's country of origin or residence. Normal processing: 10 business days, $220 USD. Expedited processing (3 business days): $280 USD.

MOZ.name: Residence Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Long-stay residence in Mozambique for individuals with authorized employment or family ties, obtained at a Mozambican embassy or consulate.
MOZ.notes: Single entry only. Requires authorization letter from Ministry of Labor, work contract, authenticated police clearance, and business documentation. Fee: $240 USD (normal processing, 10 business days); expedited 3 business days: $310 USD.

MOZ.name: Diplomatic / Official / UN Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Entry for foreign government officials, diplomats, and staff of international organizations (UN, World Bank, IMF) on official business in Mozambique.
MOZ.notes: Reserved for government officials and UN/World Bank/IMF staff on official business. Separate requirements apply. Many bilateral agreements grant diplomatic/service passport holders visa-free entry - see conditional_access.

MOZ.name: Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA)
MOZ.purpose: Pre-travel electronic authorization for selected nationalities allowing short-stay tourist and business visits without a full visa.
MOZ.notes: Available to exactly 29 nationalities (Belgium, Canada, China, Côte d'Ivoire, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ghana, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Senegal, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Ukraine, UAE, UK, USA) via the evisa.gov.mz portal (relaunched February 11, 2026 with VFS Global). Processing: at least 48 hours before departure. Permits stay up to 30 days for tourist/business purposes. Fee: approximately USD 48 (increased from approximately USD 10/650 MZN under the previous portal). ETA was briefly suspended May 16–early 2026 due to technical issues; fully reinstated on the new portal.

MOZ.name: Border Visa (Visa on Arrival)
MOZ.purpose: Short tourist visits for nationals of countries that have no Mozambican embassy or consulate, issued on arrival at designated border posts and international airports.
MOZ.notes: Officially confirmed by the Embassy of Mozambique in Japan: 'Arrival tourist visas are now available at border posts, including international airports in Mozambique, for those who originate from countries where there is no Embassy/Consulate of Mozambique.' Eligibility is limited to nationals of countries lacking a Mozambican diplomatic mission; travellers from countries that have a mission must obtain a visa in advance. Widely reported as an approximately USD 50, 30-day, dual-entry visa (not extendable). Availability at the border can be unreliable, so the ETA or eVisa is recommended for travellers who are eligible for those.

MOZ.name: Journalist / Press Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Foreign journalists and press or media personnel travelling to Mozambique to report on or cover events.
MOZ.notes: Visto de Jornalista - a distinct consular visa category listed by Mozambican embassies. Single entry; issued at a Mozambican embassy/consulate and not offered on the evisa.gov.mz portal. Fee varies by mission (Embassy of Mozambique in Japan lists JPY 10,420, approximately USD 70, single entry, ordinary processing 4-5 business days). Press accreditation and supporting documentation from the sponsoring media organisation are generally required.

MOZ.name: Temporary Permanence Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Foreign spouse and minor or incapacitated children of a foreign national holding a Mozambican work visa, allowing them to accompany and reside with the work-visa holder.
MOZ.notes: Visto de Permanência Temporária. Granted to the spouse and minor/incapacitated children of a foreign citizen who holds a Mozambican work visa. Multiple-entry and renewable in step with the sponsor's work visa/employment contract. Requires a term of responsibility from the work-visa holder, criminal record certificate, round-trip ticket and a passport valid for at least 6 months. The initial 30-day entry is extended/renewed after arrival. Processing minimum approximately 15 days. Confirmed by the Embassy of Mozambique in Japan and the Mozambique High Commission (Rwanda).

MOZ.name: Courtesy Visa (Consular)
MOZ.purpose: Persons deserving special consideration - such as guests of the Mozambican government and family members of diplomatic or official visa holders - who do not qualify for a diplomatic or official visa.
MOZ.notes: Visto de Cortesia. Issued free of charge, single or multiple entry with 30- or 90-day validity. Ordinary processing 4-5 business days; urgent 2-3 business days. Reserved for persons granted courtesy status by the Mozambican authorities and is not a general-purpose travel visa.

MRT.name: E-Visa (30 days) - Tourist/Visit
MRT.purpose: Short-term visit for tourism or personal travel to Mauritania. No separate tourist visa category exists; the single e-visa covers all visit purposes.
MRT.notes: Mauritania operates a single e-visa system with no separate visa categories by purpose (tourist, business, etc.). The 30-day duration is the shortest option. Fee: Arab/African nationals ~€40/$45; Rest of World €55/$60. Application at anrpts.gov.mr; fees paid in cash on arrival (exact change required). Biometric data collected at the border entry point. Launched 5 January 2025, replacing visa-on-arrival.

MRT.name: E-Visa (30 days) - Business
MRT.purpose: Short-term business travel to Mauritania including meetings, conferences, and negotiations. No separate business visa category - the single e-visa covers all visit purposes.
MRT.notes: No distinct business visa category. The e-visa system uses the same fee structure regardless of visit purpose. Fee: Arab/African nationals ~€40/$45; Rest of World €55/$60. Longer durations (90 days, 3–12 months) are available under the same single e-visa system if needed.

MRT.name: E-Visa - Transit
MRT.purpose: Transiting through Mauritania en route to a third country. No dedicated transit visa category is published; transit travelers requiring a visa must obtain the standard e-visa.
MRT.notes: No separate transit visa category is published on any official Mauritanian government source. Transit travelers from visa-required nationalities must apply for the standard e-visa at anrpts.gov.mr. Fee and duration details not separately specified for transit purposes.

MRT.name: E-Visa (90 days)
MRT.purpose: Medium-term stay in Mauritania for any purpose including extended visits, business, or research.
MRT.notes: 90-day duration e-visa. Fee: Arab/African nationals €70/$75; Rest of World €95/$100. Same application process via anrpts.gov.mr; fees paid in cash on arrival.

MRT.name: E-Visa (3–12 months)
MRT.purpose: Long-term stay in Mauritania for any purpose including work, study, or extended residence. No separate work or student visa category is published on official sources.
MRT.notes: 3-month to 1-year (up to 360-day) duration e-visa covering purposes including work and study. The 360-day tier supports multiple entries and is aimed at business/frequent travelers. Fee: Arab/African nationals €135/$145; Rest of World €190/$200. No official distinction between work visa, student visa, or other long-stay categories is published on Mauritanian government sources.

MRT.name: E-Visa (720 days / 2 years)
MRT.purpose: Longest standard e-visa duration for extended or repeat travel to Mauritania, typically frequent business travel or extended residence with multiple entries.
MRT.notes: Longest standard duration tier in Mauritania's single e-visa system. The ANRPTS portal (anrpts.gov.mr) offers selectable durations of 30, 90, 360 and 720 days; the 360- and 720-day options support multiple entries and are aimed at frequent/business travelers. Confirmed as an available duration by the official ANRPTS-based application flow. Exact fee for the 720-day tier is not published on an authoritative source; fees scale by duration and by region (Arab/Africa vs Rest of World) and are paid in cash on arrival. No purpose-based category exists - reason for travel is a free-text field on the application.

MRT.name: E-Visa (Long-Stay) - Work
MRT.purpose: Stay in Mauritania for employment or professional activity. No dedicated work visa is published; long-stay e-visa durations (3 months to 3+ years) serve this purpose.
MRT.notes: No separate work visa category is published on any official Mauritanian government source. Workers must obtain the general e-visa for the required duration (3–12 months: €135–190; 1–2 years: €190–270; 2–3 years: €270–405; 3+ years: €540–810 depending on region). Work permit requirements from the Ministry of Labor are separate from the visa and not documented on the official visa portal.

MRT.name: E-Visa (Long-Stay) - Student
MRT.purpose: Study at a Mauritanian educational institution. No dedicated student visa is published; long-stay e-visa durations serve this purpose.
MRT.notes: No separate student visa category is published on any official Mauritanian government source. Students must apply for the general long-stay e-visa at anrpts.gov.mr. No student-specific fee reduction or processing distinction is documented.

MRT.name: Visa Exemption - Diplomatic/Service Passport
MRT.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports from countries with bilateral visa suppression agreements with Mauritania.
MRT.notes: Mauritania has bilateral visa suppression agreements with approximately 20+ countries. Most cover only diplomatic and service passports. Countries with diplomatic/service exemptions include Morocco, Syria, Yemen, UAE, Romania, Spain (diplomatic only), Turkey, Brazil (diplomatic/service/official), China, Iran, India, Guinea-Bissau, Egypt, and Russia among others. Full visa abolition for all passport types (ordinary) applies to: Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Mali, Senegal, Gambia, Niger, Côte d'Ivoire, Chad, and Burkina Faso - all for up to 90 days.

MUS.name: Standard Tourist Visa
MUS.purpose: Short-term leisure visits to Mauritius for tourism purposes.
MUS.notes: Maximum stay of 6 months per calendar year. Visa is free of cost. Processing is 12 working days; applicants should apply at least one month before travel. Applied for through Mauritius diplomatic/consulate representatives. A visa does not guarantee admission - the final decision rests with the Immigration Officer.

MUS.name: Business Visa
MUS.purpose: For visits to establish or conduct business or investment activities in Mauritius. Applicant must not receive any payment within Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Maximum 120 days per calendar year; individual trip stays capped at 90 days. A Multiple Entry Business Visa exists for repeated business visits under the same 120-day annual cap. Requires a letter from a local sponsor or company. Applicant must not receive payment within Mauritius. Free of charge.

MUS.name: Transit Visa
MUS.purpose: Passage through Mauritius to a third country without leaving the transit area, valid for within a 24-hour period.
MUS.notes: Valid for a 24-hour transit period only. Free of charge.

MUS.name: Medical Visa
MUS.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking medical treatment at registered private healthcare institutions in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Duration is for the treatment period, not exceeding 6 months. Treatment must occur at facilities registered with the Ministry of Health. Free of charge.

MUS.name: Social Visa
MUS.purpose: For socio-cultural, community, or religious activities in Mauritius, sponsored by recognized socio-cultural or religious organizations.
MUS.notes: Maximum stay of 45 days. Requires a letter from the sponsoring socio-cultural or religious institution in Mauritius. Free of charge.

MUS.name: Wedding Visa
MUS.purpose: Allows a foreign national to enter Mauritius for the purpose of civil marriage to a Mauritian citizen.
MUS.notes: Applicant must be a national of a country listed in the 9th, 10th, or 11th schedules of the Passport Regulations. Requires proof of financial capacity (USD 50 per day), confirmed letter from Mauritian fiancé/fiancée, character/criminal record certificate, full birth certificate, and return ticket. Mauritian partner must show minimum monthly income of MUR 45,000. An extension of the Wedding Visa is also available (page_id=635). Free of charge.

MUS.name: Student Visa
MUS.purpose: Permits non-citizens to pursue full-time or part-time education at recognized tertiary institutions or TVET centers in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Eligible for certificate/diploma (minimum 1 academic year), undergraduate, postgraduate, postdoctoral, and exchange program students (up to 1 year). Application must be submitted by the educational institution, not the student directly. Requires letter of admission, proof of financial capacity, accommodation proof, and medical certificate (including HIV/Hepatitis B tests and chest X-ray). Tourists cannot convert their status to student. Duration varies by program. Renewal requires attendance records and continued enrollment proof. Free of charge.

MUS.name: Workshop, Events and Conference Visa
MUS.purpose: For foreign nationals attending workshops, events, or conferences hosted by recognized institutions or ministries in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Requires a covering letter from the relevant Mauritius Ministry or Institution confirming the event. Free of charge.

MUS.name: Premium Visa
MUS.purpose: Allows foreign nationals including tourists, retirees, and remote workers to relocate to Mauritius for an extended stay of up to one year, working or conducting business remotely from outside Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Valid for stays exceeding 6 months up to 1 year, renewable. Targeted at remote professionals, retirees, and long-stay tourists. Applicant's main place of business and source of income must be outside Mauritius; must not enter the Mauritius labour market. Requires proof of travel and health insurance. Application is through the Economic Development Board (EDB) online portal at residency.mu. Available to nationals of 180+ eligible countries. Free of charge. Administered by EDB Mauritius.

MUS.name: Retired Non-Citizen Residence Permit
MUS.purpose: Long-stay residence permit for foreign nationals aged 50 and above who wish to retire in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Valid for up to 5 years (effective August 2025; previously 10 years). Requires transfer of at least USD 2,000 per month (USD 24,000 per year) to a Mauritian bank account and minimum 180 days per year residency. Non-refundable application fee of USD 50. Eligible for 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after 5 years with total transfers of at least USD 200,000 over the 5-year period. Applied for through the NELS (National Electronic Licensing System) portal. Must be aged 50+.

MUS.name: Occupation Permit – Professional Category
MUS.purpose: Allows foreign professionals employed by a company in Mauritius to work and reside in the country.
MUS.notes: Minimum salary MUR 30,000/month. Valid for up to 3 years or duration of employment contract. Eligible for 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after at least 5 years with a basic monthly salary of at least MUR 400,000 for 5 consecutive years. Applied for via NELS. USD 50 non-refundable application fee.

MUS.name: Expert Pass
MUS.purpose: A residence and work permit for highly skilled foreign professionals earning above a senior salary threshold, introduced August 2025.
MUS.notes: New category effective August 2025. Minimum salary of MUR 250,000/month. Administered through NELS. Full eligibility criteria and PRP pathway details not yet fully published on official pages as of June 2026.

MUS.name: Occupation Permit – Investor Category
MUS.purpose: Allows foreign investors who invest in a business in Mauritius to reside and manage that investment.
MUS.notes: Two investment options: Option 1 requires minimum USD 50,000 with cumulative turnover target of MUR 20 million over 5 years; Option 2 requires USD 100,000 with MUR 15 million cumulative over 5 years. Occupation Permit valid for 10 years, renewable. Eligible for 20-year Permanent Residence Permit after 5 years. Application fee USD 1,000 upon approval; USD 50 non-refundable application fee. Applied for through NELS.

MUS.name: Occupation Permit – Self-Employed Category
MUS.purpose: Allows self-employed foreign entrepreneurs in the services sector to reside and operate their business in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Restricted to the services sector (effective August 2025). Minimum investment of USD 50,000. Must provide letters of intent from at least 3 clients (2 local). Annual income target: MUR 750,000 in year 1, scaling to MUR 6 million cumulative over 5 years. Valid for up to 10 years. Eligible for 20-year PRP after 5 years with annual income of at least MUR 3 million per year. Applied for via NELS.

MUS.name: Young Professional Occupation Permit (YPOP)
MUS.purpose: Allows foreign graduates of recognized Mauritius tertiary institutions to work in designated high-tech sectors after completing their studies.
MUS.notes: Available to foreign students who completed at least an undergraduate degree at a TEC-recognized Mauritius institution. Must apply within 6 months of publication of results. Valid for maximum 2 years (reduced from 3 years effective August 2025). Minimum salary MUR 25,000/month. Permitted sectors: Artificial Intelligence, Biotechnology, Fintech, Robotics, Financial Services, Information Technology. Must transition to a standard Occupation Permit after 2 years. Established under Section 13 of the Economic Development Board Act 2017 and Section 9A of the Immigration Act 1970.

MUS.name: Family Occupation Permit
MUS.purpose: Allows a dependent family member or person employed exclusively for the family unit of an Occupation Permit holder to reside in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Established under section 14 of the Immigration Act 2022 and section 13(1)(b) of the Economic Development Board Act 2017. Covers spouse, dependent children, parent, other dependents, or a person working exclusively for the family unit. Valid for 10 years.

MUS.name: Residence Permit for Employment
MUS.purpose: For non-citizens employed by a Mauritian employer, typically below the Occupation Permit salary threshold; held together with a Work Permit issued by the Ministry of Labour.
MUS.notes: This is the standard employment route (distinct from the EDB-administered Occupation Permit). A foreign worker requires BOTH a Residence Permit from the Passport and Immigration Office AND a Work Permit from the Ministry of Labour, Industrial Relations, Employment and Training. Applications are made simultaneously by the employer through the e-Work Permit portal (workpermit.mu) using the Common Application Form for Work Permit / Certificate of Exemption. Residence Permit fee is RS 500 (approx. USD 11) per year per non-citizen worker, payable before issuance. Persons on tourist or business visas cannot switch to employment status. Applied for at the Residence Permit Counter, Sterling House, Port Louis. Validity is tied to the Work Permit / employment contract period.

MUS.name: Residence Permit as Spouse of a Mauritius Citizen
MUS.purpose: For non-citizens civilly married to a citizen of Mauritius who wish to reside in the country with their spouse.
MUS.notes: Granted under Section 5(1)(c) of the Immigration Act to non-citizens civilly married to a Mauritius citizen (who must not have lost or renounced citizenship). Distinct from the Wedding Visa, which is for entering Mauritius in order to marry; this permit is for those already married. Both spouses must call personally at the Passport and Immigration Office to submit the application and collect the permit. Requires marriage certificate, police clearance under 6 months old, supporting letter from the citizen spouse, and financial evidence. Residence Permit is free of cost.

MUS.name: Residence Permit for Internship
MUS.purpose: For non-citizens undertaking a full-time practical training, industrial placement, or internship with a local firm or company in Mauritius.
MUS.notes: Maximum duration of six (6) months, extendable once for an additional three (3) months. The placement/training must be full-time and confirmed by the accepting local firm or company. Governed by the official Guidelines for Application of Residence Permit for Internship/Placement of Non-Citizens in Mauritius (PDF linked from the PIO page). Applied for using the 'Application to Enter Mauritius' form.

MWI.name: Single Entry Visa (Tourism)
MWI.purpose: Issued to persons intending to enter Malawi for tourism, visits, or short-stay purposes. Covers the 'Tourism' and 'Family Visit' purposes of travel as listed on the e-visa portal.
MWI.notes: Applicable to Category 1 (advance visa required) and Category 2 (visa on arrival eligible) nationals. The immigration.gov.mw visa types page states a tourist visa is 'Issued to persons intending to enter Malawi for visits or residence or business.' Actual stay duration granted at port of entry by an Immigration Officer. Fee reduced from USD 75 to USD 50 under the 2026 regulations. Apply online at evisa.gov.mw. Payment by Visa/Mastercard only; non-refundable if rejected. Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Single Entry Visa (Business)
MWI.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to enter Malawi for business activities such as meetings, conferences, negotiations, or short-term commercial visits.
MWI.notes: Business is one of the stated purposes of travel on evisa.gov.mw. The immigration.gov.mw types page notes the tourist/visitor visa covers 'visits or residence or business.' For longer-term work or employment, a separate Employment Permit via epermit.gov.mw is required. Fee USD 50 (single entry). Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Single Entry Visa (Study)
MWI.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to enter Malawi to undertake a course of study at an approved institution.
MWI.notes: Study is listed as a purpose of travel on evisa.gov.mw. The initial entry visa allows 90 days; students intending to stay longer must obtain a Temporary Residence Permit or Student Permit via epermit.gov.mw. Fee USD 50 (single entry). Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Single Entry Visa (Medical)
MWI.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals entering Malawi to receive medical treatment at a healthcare facility.
MWI.notes: Medical is listed as a purpose of travel on evisa.gov.mw. Uses the standard single-entry visa fee of USD 50. Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Single Entry Visa (Religious)
MWI.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals entering Malawi for religious activities such as missionary work, religious conferences, or worship-related visits.
MWI.notes: Religious is listed as a purpose of travel on evisa.gov.mw. Uses the standard single-entry visa fee of USD 50. Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Single Entry Visa (Family Visit)
MWI.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting family members resident in Malawi.
MWI.notes: Family Visit is listed as a purpose of travel on evisa.gov.mw. Uses the standard single-entry visa fee of USD 50. Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Transit Visa
MWI.purpose: Issued to persons intending to transit through Malawi for a period not exceeding seven days.
MWI.notes: Defined on immigration.gov.mw as 'Issued to persons intending to transit through Malawi for a period of seven days.' Fee: USD 50. Apply online at evisa.gov.mw or obtain on arrival at designated ports of entry. Processing within 3 working days.

MWI.name: Multiple Entry Visa (6 months)
MWI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to make multiple entries into Malawi within a six-month validity period, suitable for frequent business or personal travel.
MWI.notes: Explicit fee of USD 150 listed on immigration.gov.mw/visa/visa-fees/. Apply online via evisa.gov.mw. Max stay per visit determined by immigration officer at port of entry. Must be applied for in advance online.

MWI.name: Multiple Entry Visa (12 months)
MWI.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to make multiple entries into Malawi within a twelve-month validity period, suitable for frequent business or personal travel.
MWI.notes: Explicit fee of USD 250 listed on immigration.gov.mw/visa/visa-fees/. Apply online via evisa.gov.mw. Max stay per visit determined by immigration officer at port of entry. Must be applied for in advance online.

MWI.name: Temporary Employment Permit (TEP)
MWI.purpose: Malawi's principal employment/work permit, issued to a foreign national before entering Malawi for the purpose of taking up specified employment with a Malawi-based employer.
MWI.notes: Official Department of Immigration permit (also listed simply as 'Employment Permit' on the epermit.gov.mw portal): 'issued to persons before they enter Malawi for the purpose of taking up specified employment in Malawi.' This is the main long-term work authorisation, separate from the short-stay business/single-entry visa. Apply online via epermit.gov.mw. Information page: immigration.gov.mw/permits/temporary-employee-permit/. Validity period and fee amounts are not published on the official portal.

MWI.name: Technical Assistance Permit
MWI.purpose: Work permit for foreign nationals engaged in development activities in Malawi under a sponsoring country or agency (e.g. donor-funded technical assistance and development projects).
MWI.notes: Official Department of Immigration permit listed on the epermit.gov.mw portal: 'allows foreign nationals working on development activities in Malawi from the sponsors (country/agency).' A distinct work category from the Temporary Employment Permit, used for personnel on development/technical-assistance projects. Apply online via epermit.gov.mw. Validity period and fee amounts are not published on the official portal.

MWI.name: Student Permit
MWI.purpose: Long-stay permit allowing a foreign national to enter Malawi to study at an approved educational institution or to conduct educational research.
MWI.notes: Official Department of Immigration permit, distinct from the short-stay single-entry Study visa: 'a permit which allows person to enter Malawi and study at an approved Educational Institution.' Eligibility: any foreign national who intends to study in Malawi or conduct educational research. Renewal applications must be submitted 3 months before expiry. Apply online via epermit.gov.mw. Validity period and fee amounts are not published on the official page.

MWI.name: Diplomatic Visa
MWI.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic passports travelling to Malawi on official diplomatic missions.
MWI.notes: Defined on immigration.gov.mw as issued to diplomatic passport holders on official missions. Validity 3 months, single entry as stated on source. Issued gratis (free) per immigration regulations. Subject to reciprocity: exempted 'except where reciprocal visa requirements apply to Malawian diplomatic passport holders.'

MWI.name: Official/Service Visa
MWI.purpose: Issued to holders of official or service passports travelling to Malawi on state business on behalf of their government.
MWI.notes: Referred to as 'Official Visa' on immigration.gov.mw - 'For government officials with official/service passports on state business.' Validity 3 months, single entry. Issued gratis per immigration regulations. Subject to reciprocity conditions.

MWI.name: Courtesy Visa
MWI.purpose: Issued to persons holding official/service or ordinary passports who are invited guests of the Government of Malawi or deemed desirable for diplomatic or goodwill reasons.
MWI.notes: Defined on immigration.gov.mw as 'Issued to persons holding either official/service or ordinary passport' for government-invited guests or those deemed desirable for diplomatic reasons. Validity 3 months, single entry. Issued gratis.

MYS.name: Single Entry Visa (Social Visit)
MYS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who require a visa to enter Malaysia for a social/tourist visit. One entry only.
MYS.notes: Valid 3 months from issue date. Applicants must apply via MyVISA (malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my) or through a Malaysian embassy abroad. Not available to nationals of Israel or North Korea via standard channels. Applicable to all nationalities that require a visa for Malaysia.

MYS.name: Multiple Entry Visa (Social Visit) - Indian Nationals
MYS.purpose: Allows Indian nationals to make multiple visits to Malaysia for social/tourist purposes within the visa validity period.
MYS.notes: Fee: MYR 100. Valid 1 year from issue date; maximum 30 days per entry. For Indian citizens only. Tour groups are not eligible. Requires proof of sufficient funds and valid confirmed return ticket. Note: Indian nationals currently enjoy visa-free access until 31 December 2026, so this MEV is an alternative for those needing multi-entry documentation.

MYS.name: Multiple Entry Visa (Social Visit) - Chinese (PRC) Nationals
MYS.purpose: Allows Chinese (PRC) nationals to make multiple visits to Malaysia for social/tourist purposes within the visa validity period.
MYS.notes: Fee: MYR 30. Valid 1 year from issue date; maximum 30 days per entry. For PRC citizens only. Tour groups not eligible. Requires proof of sufficient funds and valid confirmed return ticket. Note: Chinese nationals enjoy mutual visa exemption (30 days per entry, max 90 days per 180-day period) in force since 17 July 2025.

MYS.name: Multiple Entry Visa (Business/Government Affairs)
MYS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals requiring multiple visits to Malaysia for business, trade, or official government matters.
MYS.notes: Valid 3–12 months from issue date (up to 1 year). Issued via MyVISA portal or Malaysian embassy abroad. Maximum stay per entry determined by immigration officer on arrival. Tour groups not eligible.

MYS.name: Transit Visa
MYS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals passing through Malaysia en route to another destination who need to clear immigration.
MYS.notes: Not required if traveller remains airside (does not clear immigration) and continues on the same flight. Transit visa needed only if entering Malaysia between connecting flights. Apply via MyVISA portal or Malaysian embassy abroad.

MYS.name: Visa With Reference (VDR) - Social Visit
MYS.purpose: A visa requiring pre-approval from Immigration Department headquarters before issuance by a Malaysian Representative Office abroad; typically for nationals of restricted countries or spouses of Malaysian citizens seeking entry.
MYS.notes: Applies to: spouses of Malaysian citizens, and citizens from Afghanistan, India (when visa exemption not in force), China, Vietnam, North Korea, Cuba, and other restricted countries. Application submitted through Malaysian embassy/high commission abroad; forwarded to IMI HQ for approval before visa is issued. Spouses of Malaysians must show sponsor income of at least MYR 2,000/month.

MYS.name: Employment Pass (EP) - Category I
MYS.purpose: Issued to highly-skilled foreign professionals employed by Malaysian companies in senior/specialist positions with high salary thresholds.
MYS.notes: Managed by Expatriate Services Division (ESD). Issued via Xpats Gateway (MDEC-registered companies) or ESD portal. Requires prior approval from Expatriate Committee (EC) or relevant regulatory agency. Fee: MYR 800 + 6% SST = MYR 848. Three EP categories based on salary level; salary thresholds revised effective June 2026. EP holders may bring Dependant Pass holders. Valid up to 5 years.

MYS.name: Employment Pass (EP) - Category II
MYS.purpose: Issued to skilled foreign professionals employed by Malaysian companies at mid-level salary thresholds.
MYS.notes: Same application process as Category I via ESD. Salary thresholds revised June 2026. Valid up to 2 years. Succession plan mandate to facilitate knowledge transfer to local staff introduced from June 2026.

MYS.name: Employment Pass (EP) - Category III
MYS.purpose: Issued to foreign workers employed by Malaysian companies at entry-level professional salary thresholds.
MYS.notes: Valid up to 1 year (renewable). Same ESD application process. Salary thresholds revised June 2026. Holder may bring dependants on Dependant Pass.

MYS.name: Visitor's Pass (Temporary Employment)
MYS.purpose: Temporary work authorization for foreign nationals engaged in short-term employment or contract work in Malaysia.
MYS.notes: Also covers foreign domestic helpers (maids). Short-term in nature; specific validity and fees depend on the category and employer type. Managed by Immigration Department.

MYS.name: Professional Visit Pass (PVP)
MYS.purpose: Issued to foreign professionals conducting temporary professional or technical activities in Malaysia, including training, installation, or consultancy work.
MYS.notes: This is also the pass type used for the DE Rantau Digital Nomad programme. Maximum 12 months per grant; renewable. Applicants are sponsored by a Malaysian company or organisation. Applied through ESD or IMI.

MYS.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass
MYS.purpose: Allows qualified foreign digital nomads (tech and non-tech professionals) to live and work remotely in Malaysia for non-Malaysian employers.
MYS.notes: Issued as a Professional Visit Pass (Pas Lawatan Ikhtisas). Duration: 3–12 months initial stay, renewable once for up to additional 12 months (max 24 months total). Fee: MYR 1,000 for main applicant, MYR 500 per dependent. Tech roles minimum USD 24,000/year income; non-tech roles minimum USD 60,000/year income. Open to all nationalities except Israel. Applicants can bring spouse, children (under 18), and parents. Programme operated by Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC). Apply at malaysiadigital.mdec.my.

MYS.name: Student Pass
MYS.purpose: Issued to non-citizen students (aged 3 and above) enrolled in approved Malaysian educational institutions from pre-school to higher education.
MYS.notes: Fee: MYR 60. Higher education applicants must apply via EMGS (Education Malaysia Global Services) STARS system or EMGS portal, and must be outside Malaysia when applying. Valid for duration of studies. Post-arrival medical exam required within 7 days for higher education students. University students may work up to 20 hours/week at approved venues (restaurants, petrol stations, hotels, universities) only. Dependants at Master's/PhD level may accompany on Social Visit Pass (MYR 90) but cannot work. Valid passport must have at least 18 months validity and health insurance of at least 12 months coverage is required.

MYS.name: Dependant Pass
MYS.purpose: Issued to immediate family members (spouse and children) of Employment Pass or Professional Visit Pass holders to allow them to reside in Malaysia during the primary pass holder's tenure.
MYS.notes: Validity tied to primary Employment Pass holder's pass. Dependant Pass holders generally cannot work without converting to an appropriate work pass. Children and spouses of EP holders are the primary eligible group. Applied through ESD together with or after the main EP application.

MYS.name: Long Term Social Visit Pass (LTSVP)
MYS.purpose: Issued to family members of Malaysian citizens or permanent residents for extended residence in Malaysia, including spouses, step-children, elderly parents, and dependants of foreign students.
MYS.notes: Minimum 6-month stay authorisation. Spouses of Malaysian citizens may receive up to 5 years validity and are permitted to work, conduct business, or engage in professional employment without converting to an Employment Pass. Categories include: spouses of citizens, children/stepchildren of citizens under 7 years, elderly without home-country family but with local family support, immediate family of foreign students, medical patients, spouses of permanent residents, and widows/widowers of deceased citizens. Application submitted at state Visa, Pass and Permit Division with original documents. Applications submitted at a Malaysian embassy abroad are not typically accepted for this pass type.

MYS.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Silver Category
MYS.purpose: Long-term social visit pass allowing eligible foreign nationals to reside in Malaysia for an extended period under the entry-tier MM2H programme.
MYS.notes: One of four MM2H tiers managed by Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC). Programme does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship. Financial requirements (fixed deposit amounts, liquid asset thresholds) apply per the January 2026 Terms and Regulations but specific amounts not publicly accessible from official web pages (mm2h.gov.my returns HTTP 403 on category pages). Non-official sources indicate approximately MYR 675,000 fixed deposit for Silver but this is unverified from official source. Pass is typically valid 5 years (renewable). Spouses and children may be included as dependants.

MYS.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Gold Category
MYS.purpose: Long-term social visit pass for the mid-tier MM2H programme, allowing foreign nationals to reside in Malaysia with higher financial requirements than Silver.
MYS.notes: Second of four MM2H tiers under MOTAC. Programme does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship. Financial requirements not text-extractable from official pages (403 errors). Pass typically valid 5 years renewable. Dependants (spouse and children) may be included.

MYS.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - Platinum Category
MYS.purpose: Long-term social visit pass for the highest-tier MM2H programme, targeting high-net-worth individuals seeking extended residence in Malaysia.
MYS.notes: Highest MM2H tier under MOTAC. Programme does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship. Financial requirements (highest among tiers) not text-extractable from official pages (403 errors). Pass typically valid 5 years renewable. Holders may be eligible for additional benefits vs lower tiers.

MYS.name: Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) - SEZ/SFZ Category
MYS.purpose: Long-term social visit pass for investors in Malaysia's Special Economic Zones or Special Financial Zones under the MM2H framework.
MYS.notes: SEZ/SFZ-specific MM2H category for investors in designated economic zones. Specific financial requirements not accessible from official web pages. Programme under MOTAC and does not lead to PR or citizenship.

MYS.name: Malaysia Premium Visa Programme (PVIP)
MYS.purpose: A premium 20-year renewable long-term visa for high-net-worth individuals who wish to live, work, and study in Malaysia, requiring a significant fixed deposit and offshore income.
MYS.notes: Requires: MYR 1,000,000 fixed deposit in a Malaysian licensed bank (up to 50% may be withdrawn after 1 year for approved purposes); minimum offshore income of MYR 40,000/month; government participation fee MYR 200,000 for main applicant, MYR 100,000 per dependant. Pass valid 20 years, renewed every 5 years. Holders may work and study in Malaysia. Processing time: 30 working days. Managed by Immigration Department (IMI). Does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship. Excludes Israeli nationals.

MYS.name: Residence Pass - Talent (RP-T)
MYS.purpose: A long-term residence pass for highly-skilled foreign professionals and talent who have been working in Malaysia, providing greater flexibility and longer-term stay rights.
MYS.notes: Valid 10 years. Issued to highly-skilled foreign professionals meeting talent criteria set by Immigration Department. Holder may work for any employer in Malaysia without changing pass. Full eligibility criteria and financial requirements not detailed on accessible official pages during research. Applied through IMI.

MYS.name: Long Term Social Visit Pass (Medical Treatment)
MYS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who need to remain in Malaysia for extended medical treatment at approved healthcare facilities.
MYS.notes: Sub-category of the Long Term Social Visit Pass specifically for medical patients. Duration tied to treatment period. Application typically requires medical documentation from a Malaysian licensed hospital or clinic. Applied at state Visa, Pass and Permit Division.

MYS.name: Border Pass (Malaysia-Indonesia / Malaysia-Thailand)
MYS.purpose: Allows residents of border areas between Malaysia and Indonesia or Malaysia and Thailand to cross the border for short-term visits without a standard visa.
MYS.notes: Bilateral arrangement for border communities. Specific eligibility (residence within a defined km of border), validity, and fees are governed by bilateral agreements. Only valid for use at designated border crossing points and for travel within a specified border zone. Not available to general public.

MYS.name: APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC)
MYS.purpose: Allows pre-cleared business travellers from APEC economies to enter Malaysia (and other participating ABTC economies) for short business visits without requiring individual visas.
MYS.notes: ABTC holders can enter Malaysia via dedicated ABTC lanes at international entry points. Card valid 5 years. Must be a citizen of an ABTC-participating economy and meet business traveller criteria. Applications submitted through the home economy's ABTC administrator. Malaysia is a full ABTC participant.

MYS.name: Work and Holiday Visa (Malaysia-Australia Programme)
MYS.purpose: Allows young Australian citizens to holiday in Malaysia for up to 12 months while undertaking incidental short-term work to help fund their travel.
MYS.notes: Bilateral 'Work and Holiday' arrangement; Malaysia's inbound programme currently applies to Australian citizens only (reciprocal for Malaysians travelling to Australia). Applicants must be aged 18-30 at time of application, hold tertiary qualifications or have completed at least 2 years of undergraduate study, be proficient in English, have no dependent children, and not have previously joined the programme. Fee RM90 for Australian applicants. Work is incidental to the holiday: holders cannot work for any single employer longer than 6 months and cannot undertake study/training exceeding 4 months; Australian participants also barred from work in professional firms, entertainment, spa, or front-office roles. Australian applicants apply through the Malaysian High Commission in Canberra or the Malaysian Consulate General in Perth. Forms IM.12 and KDN required.

NAM.name: Visitors' Entry Permit (Holiday/Tourism Visa)
NAM.purpose: Short-term entry for holiday, vacation, visiting friends/relatives, or tourism purposes. Issued to nationals who are not visa-exempt.
NAM.notes: Fee NAD 1,200 per visa; maximum 90 days per calendar year. Handling fee NAD 80 (non-refundable) payable on submission. Can be applied online via eservices.mhaiss.gov.na or on arrival (VOA). Applying online avoids an additional NAD 400 manual service fee charged at port of entry. Requires valid passport (6+ months), return ticket, and proof of sufficient funds.

NAM.name: Transit Visa
NAM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to transit through Namibia en route to another destination.
NAM.notes: Maximum validity 3 days (72 hours). Must be applied for in advance. Applicants must show proof of onward travel and valid visa for destination country if required.

NAM.name: Visitors' Entry Permit (Business/Commercial Visit)
NAM.purpose: Entry for business exploration, attending meetings, conferences, or workshops as a non-facilitator. Does not permit actual employment.
NAM.notes: Falls under the Visitors' Entry Permit category alongside holiday/medical/family visit purposes. Fee NAD 1,200. Does not permit taking up employment; for work see Employment Visa or Employment Permit. Handling fee NAD 80 non-refundable.

NAM.name: Visitors' Entry Permit (Medical Treatment)
NAM.purpose: Entry for foreign nationals seeking medical treatment in Namibia.
NAM.notes: Issued as a Visitors' Entry Permit for medical purposes. Requires documentation from a Namibian medical institution. Fee NAD 1,200; handling fee NAD 80.

NAM.name: Employment Visa / Short Term Employment Permit
NAM.purpose: Authorizes a foreign national to enter and work in Namibia on a short-term basis for up to 90 days.
NAM.notes: Fee NAD 1,100. For employment beyond 90 days or 6 months, a full Employment Permit must be obtained instead. Requires employer sponsorship. Handling fee NAD 80 non-refundable. All applications for work authorization beyond 6 months must follow Employment Permit requirements (see Employment Permit below).

NAM.name: Employment Permit
NAM.purpose: Grants a foreign national the right to work in Namibia for a defined employer for up to one year, renewable annually.
NAM.notes: Fee NAD 2,600 per year (for first application and extensions). Requires employer sponsorship, deed of surety, police clearance (Namibia and country of origin), proof that vacancy was advertised locally, medical and radiological reports, registration with applicable professional board, certified copies of qualifications, and two passport photographs. Processed by the Immigration Selection Board (ISB). Renewable annually.

NAM.name: Student Permit (Study Permit)
NAM.purpose: Authorizes a foreign national to reside in Namibia for the purpose of full-time study at an accredited institution.
NAM.notes: Fee: NAD 1,600/year for primary/secondary school; NAD 2,200/year for tertiary education. Renewable per academic year. Requires proof of acceptance/registration with a Namibian institution, sponsor undertaking, proof of financial support, police clearance (for applicants 18+), medical and radiological reports, and two passport photographs.

NAM.name: Permanent Residence Permit
NAM.purpose: Grants a foreign national indefinite leave to remain in Namibia on a permanent basis.
NAM.notes: Fee NAD 20,000. Requires police clearances from country of origin and Namibia, proof of financial resources, employment references, detailed CV, medical and radiological reports, and two passport photographs. Eligibility typically requires several years of prior lawful residence or qualifying investment. PRP holders may obtain a re-entry visa (NAD 800, valid 2 years) when travelling abroad.

NAM.name: PRP Re-Entry Visa
NAM.purpose: Allows holders of a Namibian Permanent Residence Permit who travel abroad to re-enter Namibia.
NAM.notes: Available to Permanent Residence Permit holders only. Fee NAD 800; validity 2 years. Issued alongside or in conjunction with the PRP.

NAM.name: Temporary Residence Permit (Spouse/Dependent Children)
NAM.purpose: Issued to the spouse and dependent children of a Namibian citizen or lawful permit holder to reside in Namibia temporarily.
NAM.notes: Fee NAD 1,600 per year. Renewable annually. Issued to qualifying dependants (spouse and minor children) of Namibian nationals or permit holders. Full requirements must be confirmed with MHAISS directly.

NAM.name: Digital Nomad Visa
NAM.purpose: Allows remote workers, freelancers, and self-employed professionals to live and work remotely for their overseas employer or own business while residing in Namibia.
NAM.notes: Introduced October 2022. Administered by the Namibia Investment Promotion and Development Board (NIPDB). Minimum income requirement: USD 2,000/month for primary applicant; USD 1,000/month for accompanying spouse; USD 500/month per child. Fee NAD 3,300 payable upon approval. Non-renewable - must wait at least 12 months before reapplying. Cannot take up local employment. Applications submitted online via the Ministry of Home Affairs portal.

NAM.name: Multiple Entry Visa
NAM.purpose: For travelers (tourism or frequent business) who need to enter Namibia more than once during the visa's validity, e.g. re-entering after a regional trip such as Victoria Falls. Granted on the basis of reasonable grounds.
NAM.notes: Multiple entry visas are granted on the basis of reasonable grounds. Adult fee NAD 1,200 for African Union nationals and NAD 1,600 for non-AU nationals; children aged 6-11 pay NAD 600 (AU) / NAD 800 (non-AU); children under 6 are exempt. Maximum stay 90 days per calendar year (may be taken once-off or in parts). E-visas issued via eservices.mhaiss.gov.na are typically multiple-entry, allowing re-entry after excursions to neighbouring countries. Embassy processing usually about 3 working days.

NER.name: Visa de Tourisme (Tourist Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Niger for tourism, leisure, or sightseeing purposes. Available both via the official Niger e-visa portal online and through Embassy of Niger in person.
NER.notes: Fee of USD 155 applies to Embassy in-person applications (money order payable to Embassy of Niger). E-visa fee amount is not explicitly published on the portal (shown as placeholder). E-visa processing is 3-5 working days per FAQ. Max stay of 30 days per aggregator sources; not explicitly stated on the official portal. Requires valid passport with minimum 6 months validity, recent color photo, and flight itinerary. Must have contract with tourism agency or invitation letter for Embassy applications. US nationals are banned from entry since January 2026.

NER.name: Visa d'Affaires (Business Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Niger for professional activities, commercial meetings, or business negotiations. Requires a work or business invitation letter and proof of occupation.
NER.notes: Available through Embassy of Niger in Washington DC (and other Niger embassies). Fee is USD 155 via money order payable to Embassy of Niger. Requires work or business invitation letter and proof of occupation. Specific duration of stay and validity not published. Not available through the e-visa portal (portal only offers Tourist Visa). US nationals are banned from entry since January 2026.

NER.name: Visa de Famille (Family/Private Visit Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting family members or personal contacts in Niger. Requires invitation letter, proof of relationship, and parental consent for minors.
NER.notes: Available through Embassy of Niger. Fee is USD 155 via money order. Requires invitation letter from host in Niger, proof of family relationship, and parental consent documents for minors. Duration of stay not specified. Not available through the e-visa portal.

NER.name: Visa Etudiant (Student Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled or seeking enrollment in an educational institution in Niger. Requires proof of admission from a Niger educational institution.
NER.notes: Available through Embassy of Niger. Fee is USD 155 via money order. Requires proof of admission issued by a Niger educational institution. Duration of stay and validity not specified by the Embassy. Not available through the e-visa portal.

NER.name: Visa pour Soins Médicaux (Medical Care Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Niger to seek medical treatment or healthcare services. Requires medical documentation and proof of treatment arrangements.
NER.notes: Available through Embassy of Niger. Fee is USD 155 via money order. Requires medical file, cost estimates for treatment, and travel insurance. Duration of stay not specified. Not available through the e-visa portal.

NER.name: Visa de Transit (Transit Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals passing through Niger in transit to another country. Requires a round-trip itinerary showing Niger as a transit point to a final destination.
NER.notes: Available through Embassy of Niger. Fee is USD 155 via money order. Requires round-trip itinerary showing final destination beyond Niger. Transit is not permitted for US nationals (full ban since January 2026) or Afghan nationals. Duration of transit stay not specified.

NER.name: Visa de Long Sejour (Long-Stay / Settlement Visa)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals relocating to settle and reside long-term in Niger (including for employment, assignment, family reunification, or residence). This is the entry visa that authorizes installation ('s'installer') in Niger.
NER.notes: Described by the Embassy of Niger in France: a 'visa de long sejour' authorizes a foreign national to settle ('s'installer') in Niger, as distinct from a short-stay tourist/business visa. Applicants should allow about 1 month between filing and departure; processing can extend to roughly 4 months where additional verification is required. Taking up employment additionally requires a work authorization (autorisation de travail) and a residence card (carte de sejour) obtained locally. Chancellery fees are set by each Niger diplomatic mission and are not published on a single fixed grid. Not available through the e-visa portal.

NER.name: Visa de Long Sejour Temporaire (Temporary Long-Stay Visa - Short Studies / Internship)
NER.purpose: For foreign nationals coming to Niger for short-term studies (etudes courtes) or an internship (stage), for a stay of three to six months. Distinct from the standard full-enrollment student visa.
NER.notes: Per the Embassy of Niger in France: a 'visa de long sejour temporaire' valid for three to six months, issued for short studies or an internship (stage). Allow about 1 month between application and departure. Chancellery fees are set by each Niger diplomatic mission. Not available through the e-visa portal.

NER.name: Visa de Presse / Journaliste (Journalist Visa)
NER.purpose: For accredited journalists and media professionals conducting reporting or filming activities in Niger. Requires filming authorization from the Niger Ministry of Communication.
NER.notes: Available through Embassy of Niger. Fee is USD 155 via money order. Requires filming authorization from Niger Ministry of Communication. Duration of stay not specified.

NER.name: Visa Diplomatique / Officiel (Diplomatic/Official Visa)
NER.purpose: For government officials, diplomats, and representatives traveling to Niger on official government business. Granted on the basis of diplomatic notes or official appointment letters.
NER.notes: Fees vary or are waived for diplomatic/official visas. Requires a diplomatic note from the sending government or an official appointment letter. Holders of diplomatic and service passports of China, Turkey, and Indonesia are fully exempt from visa requirements per bilateral agreements. Visa details not publicly enumerated.

NGA.name: Transit Without Visa (F3A)
NGA.purpose: Allows airside transfer/transit passengers to connect to onward flights without entering Nigerian territory. Travelers must remain in the airport transit zone throughout.
NGA.notes: No formal visa is issued. Maximum 48 hours in transit zone only. Requires confirmed onward ticket. Cannot be extended. Not applicable for those requiring entry into Nigeria.

NGA.name: Transit Visa (F3B)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay transit visa for travelers passing through Nigeria who need to enter the country briefly before departing for a third destination.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng). Duration 1–7 days. Distinct from the airside Transit Without Visa (F3A).

NGA.name: Tourism Visa (F5A)
NGA.purpose: Single-entry short-stay visa granted to persons who wish to visit Nigeria for the purpose of tourism. Employment is not permitted.
NGA.notes: Applies to non-ECOWAS nationals and citizens from countries without a Nigeria visa abolition/waiver agreement. Valid 90 days from issuance; maximum 30-day stay per visit; non-extendable. Group/family applications accepted (up to 10 persons). Requires valid passport (6+ months), return flight proof, hotel reservation or host address, and 180-day bank statement.

NGA.name: Religious Tourism Visa (F7J)
NGA.purpose: Single-entry visa for foreign nationals visiting Nigeria for religious tourism purposes such as pilgrimages or religious study tours.
NGA.notes: Short-stay e-visa category. Employment not permitted.

NGA.name: Medical Tourism Visa
NGA.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals seeking medical treatment in Nigeria. Allows for an extended stay relative to standard short-stay visas.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa. Entry validity up to 90 days; potential stay up to 180 days for ongoing medical treatment. Employment not permitted.

NGA.name: Business Visa – Single Entry (F4A)
NGA.purpose: Single-entry visa for foreign nationals visiting Nigeria for business purposes such as meetings, negotiations, or short-term commercial activities.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal. Employment not permitted. Requires invitation from a Nigerian-registered company.

NGA.name: Business Visa – Multiple Entry (F4B)
NGA.purpose: Multiple-entry short-stay visa for frequent business travelers visiting Nigeria on a reciprocal basis.
NGA.notes: Issued on a reciprocal basis. Each visit capped at 30 days. Available via e-Visa portal.

NGA.name: Business Visa – Frequently Travelled Executives (F4C)
NGA.purpose: Multiple-entry business visa for high-profile executives who have invested at least USD 250,000 in Nigeria, allowing repeated short stays over 1 year.
NGA.notes: Embassy visa. Requires proof of at least USD 250,000 invested in Nigeria (verified by a recognized agency), CAC documentation for host company, and invitation letter. Each stay capped at 30 days. This visa is also a prerequisite for applying for the Investor Permanent Residence Visa categories (N3A/N3B).

NGA.name: Visiting Visa – Single Entry (F6A)
NGA.purpose: Single-entry visa for foreign nationals visiting family or friends in Nigeria for personal/social purposes.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal. Employment not permitted.

NGA.name: Visiting Visa – Multiple Entry
NGA.purpose: Multiple-entry visa for foreign nationals making repeated visits to Nigeria for personal or family purposes, valid for up to 5 years.
NGA.notes: Embassy visa. Validity up to 5 years; 180 days stay per visit. Employment not permitted.

NGA.name: Sports Visa (F7E)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals visiting Nigeria to participate in sporting events, competitions, or sports-related activities.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal. Employment not permitted beyond the sporting event.

NGA.name: Creative Arts Visa (F7F)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals visiting Nigeria for creative arts activities such as film, music, or cultural performances.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal.

NGA.name: Study Tour Visa (F7G)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals visiting Nigeria for a structured educational study tour, not constituting full enrollment in an academic program.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal. Distinct from the full Student Visa (R7A/R7B).

NGA.name: Academic Exchange Programme Visa – Short Stay (F7H)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign academics or researchers participating in a specific academic exchange programme in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal. Duration up to 90 days single entry. Distinct from the long-stay Temporary Residence Academic Exchange visa (R8A/R8B).

NGA.name: International Cultural Exchange Visa (F7I)
NGA.purpose: Single-entry visa for foreign nationals participating in an officially recognized international cultural exchange programme in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal.

NGA.name: Emergency/Relief Work Visa (F7K)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign humanitarian or emergency relief workers deployed to Nigeria for disaster response or relief operations.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal.

NGA.name: Journalist Visa
NGA.purpose: Visa for foreign journalists and media professionals visiting Nigeria for newsgathering, reporting, or media production purposes.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa. Duration up to 90 days.

NGA.name: Cleric Visa – Short Stay
NGA.purpose: Visa for foreign religious clerics visiting Nigeria for short-term pastoral, religious, or missionary activities.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa. Entry validity up to 90 days; maximum stay once admitted is 30 days. Distinct from the long-stay Employment (Cleric) Visa (R6A–R6E).

NGA.name: Humanitarian Services Visa
NGA.purpose: Single-entry visa for foreign nationals providing humanitarian services in Nigeria through recognized non-governmental or international organizations.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa.

NGA.name: Staff of INGO Visa – Short Stay
NGA.purpose: Visa for foreign staff of International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs) visiting Nigeria for short-term programme activities.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa. Duration up to 90 days single entry. Distinct from the long-stay Employment (INGO) Visa (R5A–R5E).

NGA.name: Staff of NGO Visa – Short Stay
NGA.purpose: Visa for foreign staff of domestic Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) registered in Nigeria visiting for short-term engagements.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa.

NGA.name: Returning Holders of Foreign Passports – Nigerian by Birth (F7L)
NGA.purpose: Short-stay e-visa for persons born in Nigeria who now hold a foreign passport and wish to return for visits.
NGA.notes: Available via e-Visa portal.

NGA.name: Diplomatic Visa – Non-Accredited (Embassy)
NGA.purpose: Visa for diplomatic passport holders of countries that do not have an accreditation-based agreement with Nigeria, covering non-resident diplomatic travel.
NGA.notes: Embassy/consulate visa. Duration up to 90 days. Distinct from the Accredited Diplomat Visa (R1A–R1E) for formally accredited diplomats.

NGA.name: Accredited Diplomat Visa (R1A–R1E)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for formally accredited diplomatic and consular officers and their dependants posted to Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV). Valid for 2 years, renewable. Issued in conjunction with accreditation through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

NGA.name: Employment (Expatriate) Visa (R2A–R2E)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for skilled foreign nationals employed by a company registered and operating in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Initial entry via a 90-day visa; holder then applies for the Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Aliens Card (CERPAC) for a 2-year renewable residence/work permit. Employer must obtain a quota approval. Multiple sub-categories (R2A–R2E) based on position/seniority.

NGA.name: Employment (Expatriate Free Zone) Visa (R3A–R3E)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for skilled foreign nationals employed within Nigeria's Export Processing Zones or Free Trade Zones.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV). Valid for 2 years, renewable. Sponsored by a Free Zone enterprise.

NGA.name: Employment – Government Official (R4A–R4E)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for foreign nationals officially employed or seconded to a Nigerian government ministry, department, or agency.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV). Valid for 2 years, renewable.

NGA.name: Employment (INGO) Visa (R5A–R5E)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for foreign nationals employed by an International Non-Governmental Organization registered and operating in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV). Valid for 2 years, renewable.

NGA.name: Employment (Cleric) Visa (R6A–R6E)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for foreign religious clerics (pastors, imams, priests, etc.) taking up long-term pastoral positions in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV). Valid for 2 years, renewable. Distinct from the short-stay Cleric Visa.

NGA.name: Temporary Work Permit – 90 Days (R10)
NGA.purpose: Short-term work authorization for foreign nationals undertaking specific, time-limited work assignments in Nigeria not exceeding 90 days.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV) sub-category. Not renewable. Applied for via twp.immigration.gov.ng portal.

NGA.name: Temporary Work Permit – 6 Months (R11)
NGA.purpose: Medium-term work authorization for foreign nationals undertaking specific assignments in Nigeria for up to 6 months.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV) sub-category. Multiple entries; non-renewable. Applied for via twp.immigration.gov.ng portal.

NGA.name: Combined Expatriate Residence Permit and Aliens Card (e-CERPAC)
NGA.purpose: Combined residence-and-work permit plus alien identity card issued to expatriates (and their dependants) taking up long-term employment, business, study, or investment in Nigeria. It is the residence permit that accompanies an Employment (Expatriate) R2 or Free Zone R3 visa.
NGA.notes: Serves as both a residence permit and an identification card, granting expatriates the legal right to live, work, study, or invest in Nigeria. The e-CERPAC is now processed and issued before the expatriate enters the country, eliminating the former post-arrival regularization (STR) step. Tied to the Employment (Expatriate) R2A or Free Zone R3A visa and the employer's expatriate quota; commonly issued for an initial 1–2 year term and renewable. Applied for online via the NIS e-CERPAC portal (cerpac.immigration.gov.ng); biometrics captured at a designated NIS office. Exact validity period and fee are not stated verbatim on the official e-CERPAC page.

NGA.name: Student Visa (R7A/R7B)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for foreign nationals enrolled full-time in an accredited educational institution in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV). Initially issued for 1 year; renewable annually for the duration of the academic program. Requires acceptance letter from a recognized Nigerian institution.

NGA.name: Academic Exchange Programme Visa – Long Stay (R8A/R8B)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for foreign academics, researchers, or professors participating in a long-term academic exchange programme at a Nigerian institution.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV) sub-category. Duration aligned with the exchange programme.

NGA.name: Intern Visa (R9A)
NGA.purpose: Temporary Residence Visa for foreign nationals undertaking internships or supervised training placements at Nigerian organizations.
NGA.notes: Temporary Residence Visa (TRV) sub-category. Duration several months to 1 year; possible renewal depending on programme.

NGA.name: Spouse of Nigerian Citizen Permanent Residence Visa (N1A)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for foreign spouses of Nigerian citizens who wish to reside permanently in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Requires evidence of valid marriage to a Nigerian citizen and spousal relationship documentation.

NGA.name: Nigerian by Birth (Renounced Citizenship) Permanent Residence Visa (N2A/N2B)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for persons who were born Nigerian but have renounced their Nigerian citizenship, and their foreign spouses, wishing to reside in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). N2A for the person themselves; N2B for their foreign spouse.

NGA.name: Investor Visa – Small Scale Enterprise (N3A)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for foreign investors who have imported and retained USD 250,000–500,000 as capital in a Nigerian small-scale enterprise.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Residence permit duration 3 years (multiple entry), subject to renewal. Requires prior holding of F4B or F4C visa, security clearance, proof of enterprise investment, and business plan.

NGA.name: Investor Visa – Medium Scale Enterprise (N3B)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for foreign investors who have imported and retained USD 500,000–1,000,000 as capital in a Nigerian medium-scale enterprise.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Residence permit duration 4 years (multiple entry), subject to renewal. Requires prior F4B or F4C visa holding and security clearance.

NGA.name: Investor Visa – Large Scale Corporations (N3C)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for senior executives of large corporations with significant capital and business presence in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Specific minimum capital threshold not stated verbatim on official page. Requires corporate registration and audited financial statements.

NGA.name: Investor Visa – Ultra Large Scale Corporations (N3D)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for key executives of major multinational or ultra-large corporations with the highest levels of capital, assets, or turnover in Nigeria.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Specific minimum thresholds not stated verbatim on official page.

NGA.name: Investor Visa – Oil, Gas & Power Sector (N3E)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for investors with significant ventures in Nigeria's oil, gas, or power sectors requiring specialized technical expertise and substantial capital.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Specific minimum capital not stated verbatim on official page. Requires industry licenses or partnerships.

NGA.name: Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa (N4A)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for foreign nationals with specialized knowledge and technical expertise highly relevant to the current and future needs of the Nigerian economy.
