NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Residence permit duration 5 years (multiple entry), extendable. Holder may work and reside in Nigeria. Requires recommendation letter from the Nigerian Skills Gap Assessment (under the Industrial Training Fund, ITF), vetted credentials, and police report.

NGA.name: Retirement Visa – Retired in Nigeria (N5A)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for foreign nationals who have retired while residing in Nigeria and wish to continue residing there in retirement.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Employment not permitted. Specific financial threshold not stated verbatim on official page.

NGA.name: Retirement Visa – Retiree from Abroad (N5B)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for foreign retirees wishing to relocate to Nigeria from overseas, demonstrating sufficient financial resources to support themselves.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources (pensions, annuities, savings) and secure local accommodation. Health insurance strongly recommended. Employment not permitted. Specific minimum income/savings threshold not stated verbatim on official page.

NGA.name: Spouse/Dependant of Permanent Resident Visa (N6A–N6D)
NGA.purpose: Permanent Residence Visa for spouses and dependants of existing Nigerian Permanent Residence Visa holders.
NGA.notes: Permanent Residence Visa (PRV). Sub-categories N6A–N6D cover different classes of dependants. Employment restrictions may apply depending on sub-category.

NIC.name: Tarjeta de Turista / Tourist Entry Stamp
NIC.purpose: Short-term tourism and leisure visits to Nicaragua. Issued as an entry stamp upon arrival.
NIC.notes: Paid on arrival in cash (USD). Eligible for nationals of 69 visa-exempt countries under Disposición N° 002-2026 (effective Feb 16, 2026). Extendable up to 90 additional days at $25 USD per 30-day period before expiry. CA-4 regional agreement means 90 days counts across all four member states (Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua). Passport must be valid for at least 6 months. Onward/return ticket and proof of funds may be required at border. $42 USD departure tax applies (usually included in airfare). Yellow fever vaccination proof required if arriving from endemic countries.

NIC.name: Visa Consultada (Categoría C) - Electronic Visa
NIC.purpose: Pre-authorized electronic entry visa for nationals of approximately 128 countries not on the visa-free list, for short-term tourist or business visits.
NIC.notes: Required for nationals of approximately 128 countries including Cuba, Venezuela, China (ordinary passport), Iran, India, Mexico, Peru, UAE, Colombia, and most of Africa, Middle East and Central Asia. UPDATED 2026-06-29: The Category C visa is fully electronic — no consulate visit or physical stamp is required. Applications submitted via official portal tramitesconsulares.mint.gob.ni. Steps: register with valid email, complete form with personal/travel details, upload passport-style photo (front-facing, plain background, no glasses/hats) and passport biodata scan, Migration reviews and sends payment link by email, complete payment, receive electronic authorization notification, download and print. Official fee: nil (Ministry announcement: 'el tramite no tendra ningun costo'). Authorization valid for 30 days from notification date. Visa verifiable at evisa-verifica.mint.gob.ni via reference code or QR code. Sources: Consortium Legal (2026-02-19), Dentons (2026-03-10), Wikipedia Visa policy of Nicaragua. Category B (visa on arrival) was eliminated under Disposición N 002-2026.

NIC.name: Visa de Negocios / Business Visa
NIC.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting business activities, attending meetings, negotiations, or trade events in Nicaragua.
NIC.notes: Nationals from visa-exempt countries may enter for business purposes under the standard 90-day tourist entry stamp (no separate business visa category). Nationals requiring a Visa Consultada (Category C) must obtain pre-authorization specifying business purpose. Nicaragua's Law 761 does not define a standalone business visa separate from the general entry visa framework - business stays within 90 days fall under the tourist/general entry category.

NIC.name: Visa de Trabajador / Work Visa (Residencia Temporal - Trabajador)
NIC.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside and work legally in Nicaragua under an employment contract with a Nicaraguan employer.
NIC.notes: Under Ley General de Migración y Extranjería No. 761 (Articles 30–32), foreign workers may obtain temporary residency. The employer in Nicaragua typically sponsors the application. Required documents include employment contract, police clearance certificate (apostilled), medical certificate, birth certificate (apostilled), and passport photos. Application filed at the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME). Total immigration law work quota: foreign workers generally limited to 10–15% of a company's total workforce per Nicaraguan labor law. Residency card valid 1 year, renewable. Processing 6–8 months approximately.

NIC.name: Visa de Estudiante / Student Visa (Residencia Temporal - Estudiante)
NIC.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to study at accredited Nicaraguan educational institutions for the duration of their studies.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761, students enrolled in accredited Nicaraguan universities or schools may apply for temporary residency. Required documents include: acceptance letter from recognized Nicaraguan educational institution, proof of financial support, police clearance (apostilled), medical certificate, birth certificate (apostilled). Application submitted to DGME. Renewable annually for duration of studies. Work is generally not permitted on student status.

NIC.name: Residencia de Pensionado / Retiree Residency
NIC.purpose: Permanent residency category for foreign retirees receiving a guaranteed monthly pension or retirement income who wish to reside in Nicaragua.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761 Article 30(3), 'Inmigrante Pensionado' category. Minimum requirement: USD 600/month guaranteed pension income (Social Security, retirement fund, annuity, etc.). Age requirement: generally over 40 years old per common practice. Must spend minimum 6 months per year in Nicaragua. Residency card valid 5 years, renewable. Tax exemption on foreign-source income. Path to citizenship after 2 years of legal residency (180+ days/year). Required documents: police clearance (apostilled), medical certificate, birth certificate (apostilled), proof of pension income (bank statements, pension award letter), passport. Administrative costs approximately USD 150–300 plus government fees (residency card: approximately C$18,312 / ~USD 500 for 5 years). Processing approximately 6–8 months. Fee data from expat.com summary of Law 761; official mint.gob.ni/migob.gob.ni currently return 403.

NIC.name: Residencia de Rentista / Passive Income Residency
NIC.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals receiving regular passive income (dividends, rental income, investment returns) who wish to reside in Nicaragua.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761 Article 30(4), 'Inmigrante Rentista' category. Minimum income requirement: approximately USD 750–1,250/month from dividends, rental income, or investment returns (figure from expat.com summary; official minimum not confirmed on accessible government pages). No minimum age requirement. Must spend minimum 6 months per year in Nicaragua. Residency card valid 5 years, renewable. Path to citizenship after 2 years legal residency. Required documents same as Pensionado category. Administrative costs approximately USD 150–300 plus government fees.

NIC.name: Residencia de Inversionista / Investor Residency (Inmigrante con Capital)
NIC.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals who invest capital in lawful economic activities in Nicaragua.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761 Article 30 'Inmigrante con Capital o Inversionista'. A minimum of USD 30,000 investment is widely cited in third-party sources including PRONicaragua, but this figure is NOT confirmed on accessible official government pages (DGME page returns 403). Eligible sectors include tourism, agribusiness, and services. Requires: MIFIC Certificate of Investment Registration (RUIE), company registration, municipal trading licence, tax clearance (DGI), notarised declaration of income sources, police clearance (apostilled), medical certificate, birth certificate (apostilled). Must make minimum 2 visits per year for ID renewal. Residency card valid 5 years at approximately C$18,312 (~USD 500). Path to citizenship after 2 years legal residency. Processing 6–8 months.

NIC.name: Visa Diplomática / Diplomatic Visa
NIC.purpose: Entry and residency for accredited diplomats, embassy staff, and holders of diplomatic or official passports from countries with bilateral agreements with Nicaragua.
NIC.notes: Disposición N° 002-2026 (Article 2) maintains visa exemption for holders of diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs (asuntos públicos) and special passports from any nationality with which Nicaragua has signed bilateral migration-facilitation agreements. Duration of stay governed by individual bilateral instrument. Confirmed bilateral agreements include: Nicaragua–Peru (signed Lima, June 4, 2004; ratified Decree A.N. 4965, Dec 12, 2006); Nicaragua–Taiwan/ROC; Nicaragua–Sweden (visa suppression convention); UK (La Gaceta No. 54, March 5, 1969). Many additional bilateral instruments likely in force. Accredited resident diplomats hold separate status under Vienna Convention. No maximum stay specified; governed by terms of assignment and bilateral treaty.

NIC.name: Residencia por Vínculo Familiar / Family Reunification Residency
NIC.purpose: Temporary or permanent residency for foreign nationals who are immediate family members (spouse, children) of Nicaraguan citizens or legal permanent residents.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761, spouses and minor children of Nicaraguan citizens or permanent residents may apply for residency. Required documents include: marriage certificate or birth certificate proving family relationship (apostilled), Nicaraguan sponsor's identity documents, police clearance (apostilled), medical certificate. Application filed at DGME. Leads to permanent residency and path to naturalization. Administrative costs approximately USD 150–300 plus government fees.

NIC.name: Tránsito Migratorio / Transit
NIC.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to pass through Nicaragua in transit to a third country without remaining as tourists or immigrants.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761, transit (tránsito) is a recognized non-immigrant status for travelers passing through Nicaragua. Nationals who are visa-free may transit without separate authorization. Nationals requiring Category C must obtain electronic pre-authorization via tramitesconsulares.mint.gob.ni in advance even for transit. Proof of onward travel to final destination required. Maximum authorized transit stay is 5 days per Ley 761 Article 21 ('La estadía máxima autorizada para las personas extranjeras en tránsito en el territorio nacional será de cinco días') — corrected from the previously stated 72 hours. No dedicated e-transit authorization system.

NIC.name: Residencia Permanente General / General Permanent Residency
NIC.purpose: Long-term permanent residency for foreign nationals who have resided legally in Nicaragua for the required period or qualify under other categories defined in Law 761.
NIC.notes: Under Ley 761 Articles 30–32, various 'Inmigrante' subcategories exist including: Inmigrante Pensionado (retiree), Inmigrante Rentista (passive income), Inmigrante con Capital/Inversionista (investor), Inmigrante Trabajador (worker), Inmigrante por Vínculo Familiar (family ties), and Inmigrante Científico, Técnico o Profesional (skilled professional). Residency card valid 5 years, approximately C$18,312.15 (~USD 500); reduced rate C$9,156.07 for certain subcategories under numerals 1 and 4 of Art. 30, Law 761. After 2 years of legal residency (minimum 180 days/year), applicants may apply for Nicaraguan citizenship. Dual citizenship permitted under Nicaraguan law.

NIC.name: Ingreso por Salud / Medical (Health) Visitor Entry
NIC.purpose: Short-term entry for foreign nationals travelling to Nicaragua to receive medical treatment or for other health-related visits.
NIC.notes: Recognized non-resident entry motive under Ley General de Migración y Extranjería No. 761, Article 15(4), which lists 'viajeros en vías de ... salud' (travellers for health/medical purposes) among the No Residente subcategories. There is no separate medical-visa document: visa-exempt nationals enter on the standard 90-day tourist entry stamp (US$10 tourist card) declaring a health purpose, while nationals requiring a Category C Visa Consultada must obtain it in advance. Under Art. 22, stays for health, business, sports, conventions and similar motives may be extended according to the category of entry. Travellers should carry supporting documentation from the treating Nicaraguan hospital or clinic. Legal basis: Ley 761 Arts. 15 and 22.

NIC.name: Residencia Temporal - Científicos, Profesionales y Técnicos / Skilled Professional & Specialist Residency
NIC.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign scientists, professionals, technicians and specialized personnel coming to Nicaragua to perform qualified work.
NIC.notes: Distinct temporary-residency subcategory under Ley 761 Article 25(1) — 'Científicos, profesionales, técnicos y personal especializado' — separate from the general dependent-employment work visa. Granted for 1 to 3 years, renewable (Art. 25). Application filed at the Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería (DGME); work authorization is coordinated with the Ministerio del Trabajo (MITRAB). Typical documents: professional/technical credentials, employment or service contract, apostilled police clearance, medical certificate, apostilled birth certificate, passport photos. After 3 years of legal temporary residency the holder may apply for permanent residency (Ley 761 Art. 30.7). Fees not published on accessible official pages.

NIC.name: Residencia Temporal - Religiosos / Religious Worker (Missionary) Residency
NIC.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign clergy, missionaries and religious workers assigned to a recognized religious organization in Nicaragua.
NIC.notes: Temporary-residency subcategory under Ley 761 Article 25(5) — 'Religiosos'. For clergy, missionaries and religious workers sponsored by a recognized church or religious association operating in Nicaragua. Granted for 1 to 3 years, renewable. Application filed at the DGME; the sponsoring organization provides a letter of assignment. Typical documents: letter from the religious organization, apostilled police clearance, medical certificate, apostilled birth certificate, passport photos. Legal basis: Ley 761 Arts. 24–25.

NIC.name: Residencia Temporal - Periodistas / Journalist (Press Correspondent) Residency
NIC.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign journalists and press correspondents based in Nicaragua to report for a media organization.
NIC.notes: Temporary-residency subcategory under Ley 761 Article 25(3) — 'Periodistas'. For foreign correspondents and media workers based in Nicaragua for their assignment (1 to 3 years, renewable). Application filed at the DGME; media accreditation may also be required. Short-term news coverage by non-resident reporters instead falls under the No Residente motive of Art. 15(4) ('convenciones, conferencias o eventos especiales'). Legal basis: Ley 761 Arts. 15, 24–25.

NIC.name: Permiso Especial de Trabajador Migrante Temporal / Temporary Migrant Worker Permit
NIC.purpose: Special permit allowing a foreign national to stay and work in Nicaragua for a limited period of seasonal or temporary activity.
NIC.notes: Special stay-with-work permit for temporary migrant workers under Ley 761 Articles 16–17, issued by the DGME for a period of up to one year (Art. 10.27: 'Emitir permisos especiales de permanencia con derecho a laborar por un periodo hasta de un año'). Covers foreigners entering to perform economic, social, cultural, academic, scientific or religious activities for a defined period; the authorization is granted in consultation with the Ministerio del Trabajo. Distinct from the multi-year temporary-residency worker category. Fees not published on accessible official pages.

NIC.name: Residencia Temporal - Artistas y Deportistas / Artist, Entertainer & Athlete Residency
NIC.purpose: Temporary residency (or special entry) for foreign performing artists, public-performance entertainers and athletes coming to Nicaragua to perform or compete.
NIC.notes: Temporary-residency subcategories under Ley 761 Article 25(7) 'Artistas' and 25(8) 'Deportistas'. For foreign performing artists, entertainers and professional athletes residing in Nicaragua for their engagement (1 to 3 years, renewable). Short public-performance engagements by non-residents instead use the No Residente motives of Art. 15(5) 'Artistas de espectáculos públicos' and Art. 15(4) 'deportes', authorized by the Ministerio de Gobernación and typically coordinated with the Ministerio del Trabajo. Legal basis: Ley 761 Arts. 15, 25.

NLD.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
NLD.purpose: Allows foreign nationals from visa-required countries to visit the Netherlands for tourism, family visits, or short business trips for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
NLD.notes: Fee is €80 for adults, €40 for children 6–12, free for children under 6. Applied for at the Dutch embassy or consulate. For nationals of countries in Annex I of EU Regulation 2018/1806. The Netherlands does not offer a national e-visa or visa-on-arrival for short stays. Extensions cost €30. Applications must be submitted at a Dutch embassy, consulate, or authorized visa application centre.

NLD.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
NLD.purpose: Required for certain nationalities transiting through an international zone at a Dutch airport (e.g., Amsterdam Schiphol) without entering the Schengen area.
NLD.notes: Fee is €80 for adults, €40 for children 6–12, free for children under 6. Required for nationals of specific high-risk countries when transiting through Schengen international zones. Separate from the Type C short-stay visa. Applied for at the Dutch embassy or consulate.

NLD.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) – Business
NLD.purpose: Allows foreign nationals from visa-required countries to visit the Netherlands for business meetings, conferences, or short-term commercial activities for up to 90 days.
NLD.notes: Same visa category as tourist (Type C Schengen visa). Purpose declared at application. Applied for at Dutch embassy or consulate. Visa-free nationals (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806) do not need a visa for short business stays.

NLD.name: Highly Skilled Migrant Residence Permit (Kennismigrant)
NLD.purpose: Long-stay residence permit for highly skilled foreign nationals employed by an IND-recognised sponsor in the Netherlands, allowing them to live and work in the country.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Permit validity matches contract duration, max 5 years. Requires employment with IND-recognised sponsor. Salary thresholds (gross/month, from 1 Jan 2026): reduced criterion €3,122; under 30 years €4,357; 30+ years €5,942. If job is lost, 3–6 months to find new employment. Path to permanent residence after 5 years.

NLD.name: European Blue Card Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: EU-level work permit for highly qualified non-EU nationals with a university degree or equivalent experience, employed in a high-skilled role in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Requires higher education diploma (min 3 years) or 5 years professional experience at higher level. Salary thresholds (gross/month, from 1 Jan 2026): standard €5,942; recent graduates (within 3 years) €4,754. Contract minimum 6 months. Processing: 30 days for recognised sponsors, 45 days for certain existing holders, 90 days for others. Valid up to 5 years.

NLD.name: Single Permit (GVVA – Gecombineerde Vergunning voor Verblijf en Arbeid)
NLD.purpose: Combined residence and work permit for non-EU nationals taking up paid employment in the Netherlands that does not fall under the highly skilled migrant or Blue Card schemes.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Valid up to 3 years (or 5 years if applicant has worked legally for 5 years in the Netherlands). Employer must apply on behalf of the employee. Employer must be registered in the Dutch Chamber of Commerce, advertise the vacancy through UWV, and pay salary per applicable collective labour agreement. Covers various roles including spiritual counselors, artists, intra-corporate transferees, and international non-profit employees.

NLD.name: Intra-Corporate Transferee Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Residence permit for managers, specialists, or trainees being transferred from a non-EU company to a branch or subsidiary in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Governed by EU Directive 2014/66/EU. Transferee must have worked for the company group for at least 3 months. Valid for managers/specialists up to 3 years; trainees up to 1 year. Eligible for EU intra-corporate transferee mobility to other EU member states.

NLD.name: Self-Employed Person Residence Permit (Zelfstandige)
NLD.purpose: Residence permit for non-EU nationals who wish to establish and run their own business or work as a freelancer in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Applicant's work must be of 'essential interest to the Dutch economy,' assessed by RVO (Netherlands Enterprise Agency) via a points system (minimum 30 points per category). No minimum investment amount for general route; Dutch-American and Dutch-Japanese trade treaties require 'substantial capital' (typically at least €4,500). Permit valid up to 2 years; renewable. Path to permanent residence after 5 years.

NLD.name: Start-Up Founder Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Temporary residence permit for non-EU entrepreneurs who want to develop an innovative business in the Netherlands with the guidance of an approved facilitator.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Valid for 1 year, not extendable. Applicant must work with an approved facilitator under a signed contract. Business must be innovative (new to the Netherlands or using new technology). After 1 year, can apply for self-employed person permit. RVO provides advisory assessment and positive assessment is required. Requires registration in Chamber of Commerce Trade Register.

NLD.name: Seasonal Work Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Temporary work permit for non-EU nationals performing seasonal agricultural or horticultural work in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €254. Maximum stay 24 weeks (168 days). Primarily for agricultural sector. Employer must apply on behalf of the worker. Worker must be paid at least minimum wage.

NLD.name: Researcher Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Residence permit for non-EU nationals conducting scientific research in the Netherlands under a hosting agreement with a recognised research institution.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Governed by EU Directive 2016/801. Eligible for EU long-term mobility to other member states after at least 6 months in the Netherlands. Recognised research organisations must host the researcher under a formal hosting agreement.

NLD.name: Student Residence Permit (University / Higher Professional Education)
NLD.purpose: Long-stay residence permit for non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled in an accredited bachelor's, master's, or doctoral programme at a Dutch university or higher professional education institution.
NLD.notes: Fee is €254 for first application and extensions. Typically applied for by the educational institution on the student's behalf. Valid for 1 year; renewable for duration of study. Institution must be IND-recognised. Work is permitted up to 16 hours/week or full-time during summer months.

NLD.name: Student Residence Permit (Secondary / Vocational Education)
NLD.purpose: Long-stay residence permit for non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled in secondary school (VMBO/HAVO/VWO) or vocational education (MBO) in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €254. For students studying below university level. Educational institution typically applies on behalf of the student. Renewable for duration of study.

NLD.name: Orientation Year Residence Permit (Zoekjaar – Highly Educated Migrants)
NLD.purpose: One-year residence permit for recent graduates or researchers who completed their studies/research in the Netherlands or at a top-ranked institution abroad, allowing them to seek employment or start a business.
NLD.notes: Fee is €254 (exempt for Turkish, San Marinese, and Israeli nationals). Valid for 1 year; not extendable. Must have completed accredited bachelor's/master's/doctoral degree at Dutch institution, or Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, or master's/doctoral from top-200 ranked institution (THE, QS, Shanghai) within 3 years before application. Permits free work during validity. Not available if orientation year permit was previously held.

NLD.name: Working Holiday Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Residence permit for young nationals of specific countries allowing them to live and work in the Netherlands on a temporary basis, primarily to experience Dutch culture while financing their stay through employment.
NLD.notes: Available to nationals of: Australia (no quota), Canada (no quota), New Zealand (no quota), Japan (200/year), South Korea (200/year), Argentina (100/year), Uruguay (100/year), Hong Kong (100/year), Taiwan (100/year). Applicants must be aged 18–30. Must have return ticket or funds to purchase one, and sufficient funds for the stay. Australia, Canada, and New Zealand nationals do not need an MVV; they apply upon arrival. Quota countries must apply before quota is exhausted. Not extendable. From 1 April 2026, pre-registration is no longer required.

NLD.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit (Partner)
NLD.purpose: Long-stay residence permit allowing the foreign partner or spouse of a Dutch or lawfully resident non-EU national to live in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €254 for adults; €85 for children under 18; €44–€85 for Turkish nationals (reduced rates under EU-Turkey Association Agreement). Sponsor must meet income requirement (generally 100% of applicable social assistance norm). Sponsor must have a valid residence permit of at least 1 year. Relationship must be genuine. Permit valid 1 year; renewable.

NLD.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit (Minor Child)
NLD.purpose: Long-stay residence permit for non-EU minor children (under 18) to join a parent lawfully residing in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €85 for children under 18. Parent sponsor must meet income requirements and have a valid residence permit. Permit valid 1 year; renewable.

NLD.name: Medical Treatment Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Residence permit for non-EU nationals who need to receive medical treatment in the Netherlands that is not available in their home country.
NLD.notes: Fee is €1,337 for first application; €466 for extension. High fee reflects the specialised nature of this permit. Treatment must be unavailable in applicant's country of origin. Applicant must demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover treatment and living expenses. Permit tied to the duration of treatment.

NLD.name: Return Visa (Terugkeervisum)
NLD.purpose: A national visa for non-EU nationals who hold a Dutch residence permit that has expired or is being renewed, allowing them to return to the Netherlands after travelling abroad.
NLD.notes: Fee is €197 standard; €57 for EC-Turkey Agreement holders; free for Moluccans. Issued by the Dutch embassy or consulate abroad when a permit holder has left the Netherlands and their permit has been renewed or is pending. Allows re-entry to the Netherlands.

NLD.name: Au Pair Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Temporary residence permit for young foreign nationals to live with a Dutch host family, providing childcare and light household tasks in exchange for board and pocket money, as part of a cultural exchange.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423 (first application and change in purpose). Host family must be approved; au pair must be aged 18–30 (some exceptions). Duration typically 1 year. Applicant must have adequate health insurance. Not a work permit; income is limited to pocket money. Cultural exchange focus. Note: fee updated from €254 to €423 as of 2026 IND fee schedule (confirmed from ind.nl/en/fees).

NLD.name: Long-Term Resident EU Status (Duurzame Verblijfsvergunning EU)
NLD.purpose: Permanent long-term resident status within the EU for non-EU nationals who have legally resided in the Netherlands for at least 5 continuous years.
NLD.notes: Fee is €254 for first application; €85 for 5-year renewal. Requires 5 years legal continuous residence. Provides near-equal rights to Dutch nationals and facilitates mobility to other EU member states. Renewable every 5 years for €85. Governed by EU Directive 2003/109/EC.

NLD.name: Essential Start-Up Personnel Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Residence permit for foreign employees whose specialised expertise is essential to an innovative, scalable start-up in the Netherlands.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Pilot scheme running 1 June 2021 to 1 June 2028. The start-up must be innovative, have at most 15 employees, and may sponsor up to 5 foreign employees. The employee must be an expert in a specialised field and receive mandatory participation of at least a 1% equity stake OR shares/options worth €65,000+ (granted within 3 years). RVO provides an advisory assessment. Permit valid up to 3 years, tied to the employment contract; extendable. Distinct from the Start-Up (founder) permit. Path to permanent residence after 5 years.

NLD.name: Intern or Apprentice Residence Permit (Traineeship)
NLD.purpose: Combined residence and work permit for non-EU nationals coming to the Netherlands for more than 90 days to complete an internship, traineeship, or apprenticeship.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Issued as a Single Permit (GVVA - combined residence and work permit) for internships/traineeships exceeding 90 days. Maximum duration depends on the placement: MBO vocational internships max 6 months; university-level traineeships max 1 year; apprenticeships max 24 weeks. Canadian nationals aged 18–30 may qualify under the Young Workers Exchange Program (max 1 year). The employer usually applies on the applicant's behalf by post. IND decides within 60 days (target 7 weeks) once the application is complete.

NLD.name: Cultural Exchange Residence Permit
NLD.purpose: Temporary residence permit for young people to experience Dutch culture and society through a programme run by a recognised exchange organisation.
NLD.notes: Fee is €423. Applicant must be aged 18–30 (or 15–18 if the exchange programme allows) and must not have previously held a Dutch exchange permit. Only a recognised exchange organisation may apply on the applicant's behalf, and it may submit the application online (or by post using form 7503). Applicant must live with a registered host family and have adequate means and health insurance. Valid up to 1 year; IND aims to decide within about 2 weeks (legal maximum 90 days). Also covers European Solidarity Corps volunteers. Distinct from the Au Pair and Working Holiday permits.

NOR.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) – Visitor Visa
NOR.purpose: Allows non-visa-exempt nationals to visit Norway for tourism, visiting family/friends, or other short stays. Norway is a Schengen member state, so this is a standard Schengen C visa.
NOR.notes: Norway processes Schengen visas through Norwegian embassies and consulates abroad. Fee is the standard Schengen short-stay fee (€90 / approx. USD 97), raised from €80 to €90 on 11 June 2024; children aged 6–11 pay €45. Must apply at Norwegian embassy/consulate or VFS Global service centres. Applicants must have valid travel insurance for minimum €30,000 cover. Must show proof of accommodation, sufficient funds, and intent to leave before visa expiry. 90 days is within any 180-day period. Citizens of visa-exempt countries do not need this visa.

NOR.name: Schengen Short-Stay Business Visa (Type C)
NOR.purpose: Permits business travellers from non-visa-exempt countries to attend meetings, conferences, negotiations, or business visits in Norway for up to 90 days.
NOR.notes: Same Schengen C visa category as tourist; standard short-stay fee €90 / approx. USD 97 (raised from €80 on 11 June 2024). Applicant must provide an invitation letter from a Norwegian company, proof of business purpose, and sufficient financial means. Does not permit gainful employment in Norway.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Skilled Workers
NOR.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals with higher education or vocational training to live and work in Norway with a confirmed job offer from a Norwegian employer.
NOR.notes: Requires a job offer paying at minimum NOK 341,373/year pre-tax. Vocational-level permits granted up to 1 year; university-level up to 3 years; assignment-based up to 2 years (max 6 years total). Must have employer confirmation code before applying (introduced February 2026). Pay and working conditions must meet Norwegian standards. Eligible for permanent residence after 3 years. Processing times vary; extended delays possible for vocational qualifications from Bangladesh, China, India, Iran, Kosovo, Nepal, Pakistan, Turkey, Vietnam. Does NOT allow self-employment.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Seasonal Workers
NOR.purpose: Permits non-EU/EEA nationals aged 18+ to work in Norway in seasonal industries (e.g. agriculture, tourism, fishing) for up to 6 months per 12-month period.
NOR.notes: Must secure full-time employment before applying. Employer must confirm NAV approval that local/EEA workers cannot fill the role (exceptions: agriculture and forestry). Must leave Norway for 6 months after each seasonal period. Time does not count toward permanent residence. Family members cannot join. Minimum age 18. Stays under 3 months may not require a permit.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Self-Employed Persons
NOR.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals with completed higher education or vocational training to establish and run a sole proprietorship (enkeltpersonforetak) in Norway.
NOR.notes: Business must be a sole proprietorship (not a limited company). Must generate profit of at least NOK 341,373/year pre-tax. Active participation in the business is required. Eligible for permanent residence after 3 years. Not a passive investment visa.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Employees in Humanitarian, Non-Profit or Religious Organisations
NOR.purpose: Grants non-EU/EEA nationals the right to reside in Norway to work for Norwegian humanitarian, non-profit, or religious organisations.
NOR.notes: Specific documentation from the employing organisation required. Employment terms must meet Norwegian standards. Part of the broader work immigration category on UDI.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Studies
NOR.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to reside in Norway to attend accredited educational institutions including universities, vocational schools, upper secondary schools, folk high schools, or language courses.
NOR.notes: Must have an acceptance letter from a Norwegian educational institution. Must demonstrate sufficient financial means. Permit duration tied to the duration of the study programme. EU/EEA citizens do not need this permit. Also covers traineeships, research, and supplementary education for skilled workers seeking credential recognition.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Family Immigration
NOR.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to reunite with family members (spouses, cohabitants, children, parents, fiancés) who are legally residing in Norway.
NOR.notes: Eligible family members include spouses, cohabitants, children, parents of children in Norway, fiancés, foster children, and full siblings. The sponsor (reference person) in Norway must usually meet income requirements (changed January 2025). EU/EEA family members apply under EU/EEA regulations instead.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Victims of Abuse
NOR.purpose: Grants an independent residence permit to non-EU/EEA nationals who entered Norway on a family immigration basis and have experienced abuse in the relationship.
NOR.notes: Applicant must have held a family immigration permit. The permit allows continued residence in Norway independent of the abusive relationship. Documented evidence of abuse is required.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Victims of Human Trafficking
NOR.purpose: Provides a temporary residence permit to victims of human trafficking and their children to allow recovery, cooperation with authorities, and access to support services in Norway.
NOR.notes: For non-EU/EEA victims of human trafficking. The permit may be extended if the victim cooperates with police investigations or faces risks upon return. Covers the victim and their dependent children.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Medical Treatment
NOR.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals requiring medical treatment in Norway lasting longer than 90 days to reside in Norway for the duration of their treatment.
NOR.notes: Maximum permit duration is one year. Must have a confirmed offer of medical treatment from a Norwegian medical institution. Treatment must be funded personally or through the applicant's home country public funds (Norway's public healthcare is not available). The hospital must confirm treatment will not negatively impact Norwegian healthcare services. An accompanying person may also receive a permit if necessary. Applicant must intend to leave after treatment.

NOR.name: Job Seeker Residence Permit
NOR.purpose: Allows recently graduated skilled workers from Norwegian institutions or researchers to reside in Norway for up to one year while seeking skilled employment.
NOR.notes: Must have sufficient financial support of at least NOK 28,448/month. Must hold a higher education degree or vocational training. Duration: maximum 1 year. Time does NOT count toward permanent residence. Can work in any job (including part-time) while seeking skilled employment. If a job offer is received during processing, application can be converted to skilled worker permit at no extra cost.

NOR.name: EU/EEA Registration / Residence Card
NOR.purpose: EU/EEA nationals (and their non-EU/EEA family members) exercise their free movement rights in Norway. EU/EEA nationals register with local police; their non-EU/EEA family members apply for a residence card.
NOR.notes: EU/EEA nationals have a right of residence in Norway under EEA freedom of movement - not a visa in the traditional sense. Registration is required for stays over 3 months. Non-EU/EEA family members of EU/EEA nationals must apply for a residence card. The residence card is required for travel outside Norway. Nordic nationals (Swedish, Danish, Icelandic, Finnish citizens) have an even simpler registration scheme.

NOR.name: Permanent Residence Permit
NOR.purpose: Grants non-EU/EEA nationals the right to live and work in Norway indefinitely, without needing to renew or maintain a time-limited permit.
NOR.notes: Generally requires 3 years of qualifying residence on a time-limited permit (e.g. skilled worker permit). Additional requirements include language proficiency and financial self-sufficiency. Permanent residents may travel outside Norway but cannot remain abroad for extended periods without risk of losing permanent residence status.

NOR.name: Diplomatic / Official Passport Visa Exemptions
NOR.purpose: Holders of diplomatic, service, official, or special passports from select non-visa-exempt countries may enter Norway without a Schengen visa under bilateral agreements.
NOR.notes: Countries whose diplomatic/service/official/special passport holders are visa-exempt include: Albania (diplomatic – accredited ambassadors only), Armenia (diplomatic), Azerbaijan (diplomatic), Bolivia (diplomatic + service), China (diplomatic), India (diplomatic), Indonesia (diplomatic + service), Jordan (diplomatic), Kazakhstan (diplomatic), Laos (diplomatic), Moldova (diplomatic), Morocco (diplomatic + service + special), North Macedonia (diplomatic + service), Pakistan (diplomatic + official), Philippines (diplomatic + service + special), South Africa (diplomatic + official), Thailand (diplomatic + official), Tunisia (diplomatic), Turkey (diplomatic + service + special), Ukraine (diplomatic), UAE (diplomatic + special). Conditions vary by country. Diplomatic passport holder must usually not be working at an embassy in Norway.

NOR.name: Airport Transit Visa (Schengen Visa Type A)
NOR.purpose: Required for certain nationals changing planes at a Norwegian airport (e.g. Oslo Gardermoen) when travelling from one non-Schengen country to another non-Schengen country, without entering the Schengen area.
NOR.notes: Only nationals of specified countries need an Airport Transit Visa (Type A); most transit passengers who remain airside do not need a visa. UDI instructs applicants to submit the application through the visa portal as a Schengen Type C application with an attached explanation letter stating it is for a Type A airport transit visa. Fee is the standard Schengen short-stay fee (€90 / approx. USD 97). Does not permit leaving the international transit zone or entering Norway.

NOR.name: Working Holiday Residence Permit (Young Adults)
NOR.purpose: Lets young adults from partner countries take an extended holiday in Norway and work part-time to help fund their stay.
NOR.notes: Available to citizens of Argentina, Australia, Canada, Japan and New Zealand; Norway maintains separate per-nationality working-holiday pages under the Exchange Programmes section (Andorra also listed). Applicants must generally be aged 18 and not yet have turned 31 at the time of application (Canadians up to age 35). Granted for one year at a time, for a maximum of two years in total. Work is permitted but not for more than six months with the same employer. Must document at least NOK 15,488 per month (NOK 46,464 for the first three months) and take out medical/hospital insurance before entry.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Researchers with Own Funds
NOR.purpose: For researchers holding a master's degree who will carry out PhD-level research at a Norwegian university, college or institute without being employed by a Norwegian employer.
NOR.notes: Funding may come from a foreign employer, a grant (from Norway or abroad) or own funds; requires at least NOK 15,488 per month (NOK 170,368 per year). The permit also allows part-time work of up to 20 hours per week (including remote work) plus full-time during holidays. Time on this permit does NOT count toward permanent residence. UDI lists case processing as up to about 4 months (as of 2026). Researchers who are employed by a Norwegian institution instead apply under the skilled worker route.

NOR.name: Residence Permit for Artists, Musicians and Performers
NOR.purpose: For performers, artists, musicians and their support staff who have a concrete engagement to work in Norway for more than 14 days.
NOR.notes: Engagements of up to 14 days do not require a permit (only notification to the police). For longer engagements a permit is granted for a maximum of one year at a time. Requires a concrete offer of employment for a specific, continuous period, with pay meeting the collective agreement/minimum for the industry. After a permit, the holder must generally stay outside Norway for three months before a new permit can be granted.

NPL.name: Tourist Visa
NPL.purpose: Short-term leisure, recreation, and sightseeing visits to Nepal. Employment is strictly prohibited.
NPL.notes: Available in three durations: 15 days (USD 30), 30 days (USD 50), 90 days (USD 125), all multiple-entry. Maximum cumulative stay per calendar year is 150 days. Obtainable on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport and 11 border immigration offices, or via online pre-arrival application at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np. Gratis (free) for SAARC nationals (first 30 days of first visit annually, excl. Afghanistan), Chinese nationals (any duration), NRN card holders, and children under 10 (except US citizens). Nationals of 13 restricted countries must apply at a Nepal embassy/consulate in advance. Diplomatic/official passport holders issued a 30-day tourist/diplomatic visa.

NPL.name: Transit Visa
NPL.purpose: Allows travelers transiting through Nepal to enter and spend a night (up to 24 hours) between connecting international journeys.
NPL.notes: Issued for 24 hours (overnight) to foreign nationals in transit, on production of proof of onward transit (a confirmed air ticket). Visa fee is USD 5. Cannot be extended. Obtained at the Tribhuvan International Airport immigration counter. Fee and 24-hour duration confirmed on the Department of Immigration Transit Visa page.

NPL.name: Business Visa
NPL.purpose: Long-term business visa for foreign nationals who invest in and operate a business or industry in Nepal (short business meetings/visits use a tourist visa).
NPL.notes: Issued for periods from 1 month up to 1 year, or for 5 years at a time (multiple-entry), by the Department of Immigration. Fees are tiered by investment size: investment under NRS 10 million = USD 35/month, USD 400/year, USD 1,000 for 5 years; investment over NRS 10 million = USD 20/month, USD 200/year, USD 500 for 5 years; investment over NRS 100 million = no charge. Applicants investing over NRS 10 million must submit share details. The fee_usd shown (USD 400) is the standard annual fee for the under-NRS-10-million tier. Short business meetings/visits do not require this visa - a tourist visa suffices.

NPL.name: Study Visa
NPL.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals pursuing academic/non-academic degrees, courses, or research at institutions in Nepal, on the recommendation of the Ministry of Education.
NPL.notes: A non-tourist visa issued by the Department of Immigration on the recommendation of the Ministry of Education, for a maximum of 1 year at a time (renewable for the length of study). Fee: USD 20 for stays up to 15 days, USD 40 per month beyond 15 days; teaching/research applicants and their dependents pay USD 50/month. Dependents' visas: children under 10 free, other dependents USD 15/month (for fee-waived students under university MoUs). A minimum bank balance of USD 3,000 per six months (plus USD 2,000 per dependent) is required for academic programs. Applicants typically enter on a tourist visa and convert to a study visa after enrollment.

NPL.name: Working Visa
NPL.purpose: Required for foreign nationals to accept employment and work in Nepal for a company, industry, or organization.
NPL.notes: Officially the 'Working Visa' (a non-tourist visa). Only holders of a working visa may take up jobs in Nepal. Issued by the Department of Immigration on the basis of a recommendation from the concerned Ministry of the Government of Nepal, a Labour Permit from the Department of Labour, and a Work Agreement approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs. Validity is set to the period of the work/labour permit. Not available on arrival - foreigners typically enter on a tourist visa and convert after obtaining the labour permit. Specific fees not published on the official page.

NPL.name: Residential Visa (Investment Category)
NPL.purpose: Grants long-term residency in Nepal to foreign nationals who make a minimum qualifying investment in an industrial enterprise registered in Nepal.
NPL.notes: Minimum investment of USD 100,000 (or equivalent in convertible foreign currency) in a registered industrial enterprise in Nepal. Requires a recommendation letter from the Department of Industry. Annual fee: Nepalese currency equivalent to USD 700. Renewal fee: Nepalese currency equivalent to USD 1,200. Does not provide a direct path to permanent residence or citizenship. For non-investors wishing to reside in Nepal, proof of annual income of at least USD 20,000 is required instead.

NPL.name: Non-Residential Nepali (NRN) Visa
NPL.purpose: Grants foreign nationals of Nepali origin (holding non-SAARC citizenship) the right to visit and reside in Nepal under the Non-Resident Nepali scheme.
NPL.notes: Available to foreign nationals of Nepali origin holding citizenship of a non-SAARC country, provided they hold a valid NRN card issued by Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs or a Nepali diplomatic mission abroad. Issued gratis (free of charge) for 30 days on arrival. Extendable up to 1 year at the Department of Immigration at no charge while the NRN card remains valid. NRN card holders must maintain an active NRN visa during their stay - the card alone does not substitute for the visa.

NPL.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
NPL.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic or official passports traveling to Nepal on official government business or diplomatic assignments.
NPL.notes: Issued for 30 days. Extendable through Nepal's Department of Consular Services in Kathmandu. Requires a diplomatic note (note verbale) from the relevant foreign ministry or diplomatic mission. Diplomatic/official/service passport holders from 14 countries (Thailand, Russia, China, Brazil, Myanmar, Vietnam, Cambodia, Mongolia, Jordan, Israel, Georgia, Qatar, Oman, Indonesia) are fully visa-exempt under bilateral agreements for 30–90 days depending on the agreement.

NPL.name: Marriage Visa
NPL.purpose: For foreign nationals married to a Nepali citizen (spouse of a Nepali passport holder).
NPL.notes: A non-tourist visa for the foreign spouse of a Nepali citizen. Issued for a maximum of 6 months on first application, extendable for up to 1 year at a time thereafter. Requires a Marriage Registration Certificate from the District Administration Office/District Court (or, if married abroad, the foreign certificate plus an embassy verification letter) and the Nepali spouse's citizenship certificate. The Nepali spouse must be physically present at every application and renewal (no proxy). Applied for at the Department of Immigration, Kathmandu after entering Nepal on a tourist visa. Does not itself authorize employment - a separate work permit is required to work.

NPL.name: Relationship (Relation) Visa
NPL.purpose: For foreign nationals who are blood relatives (within three generations) of a Nepali citizen.
NPL.notes: A non-tourist visa for foreign nationals who can establish a blood relationship (within three generations) with a Nepali citizen, evidenced by a Relationship Certificate issued by the concerned local government body. Issued for a minimum of one month and renewable. Applied for at the Department of Immigration (Non-Tourist Visa Section). Distinct from the Marriage Visa, which is specifically for the spouse of a Nepali citizen.

NPL.name: Press Visa
NPL.purpose: For foreign journalists and press representatives working in or reporting from Nepal.
NPL.notes: A non-tourist visa for accredited foreign journalists/press representatives. Issued for a maximum of 4 months at a time. Fee: USD 15 per month. Requires a recommendation letter from the Department of Information, an identity card issued by the Nepal Press Council, an online application form, and copies of the passport and current Nepalese visa. Obtained at the Department of Immigration.

NRU.name: Visitor Visa (up to 1 month)
NRU.purpose: Short-term tourism and personal visits to Nauru for up to one month.
NRU.notes: Application submitted by email to the Immigration Division (visa@naurugov.nr or darlenenauruimmi@gmail.com). Schedule 3 countries (16 Pacific/regional nations) are exempt from the visitor visa fee. Schedule 4 countries (~66 nations) qualify for a Simplified Visitor's Visa Application process. No e-visa portal exists.

NRU.name: Visitor Visa (up to 2 months)
NRU.purpose: Short-term tourism and personal visits to Nauru for stays of up to two months.
NRU.notes: Application submitted by email to the Immigration Division. This 2-month tier confirmed by justice.gov.nr/immigration-division/ fee schedule. Schedule 3 countries are fee-exempt. Schedule 4 countries qualify for simplified application process.

NRU.name: Visitor Visa (up to 3 months)
NRU.purpose: Short-term tourism and personal visits to Nauru for stays of up to three months.
NRU.notes: Application submitted by email to the Immigration Division. Schedule 3 countries are fee-exempt but still require an advance visa. Schedule 4 countries qualify for simplified application process.

NRU.name: Business Visa (General)
NRU.purpose: Permits a foreign national to conduct general business or a profession in Nauru; a local sponsor is required.
NRU.notes: General 12-month, multiple-entry Business Visa: fee AUD 6,000 plus an AUD 50 application/processing fee (justice.gov.nr fee schedule). A local sponsor is required (Wikipedia 'Visa policy of Nauru' and official page). The Business Visa class also has distinct sub-categories captured as separate entries here (Media, Research, Religious Vocation, Employment, Education) plus a fee-exempt Diplomatic/Consular sub-category. Application by email to the Immigration Division (visa@naurugov.nr).

NRU.name: Employment Visa
NRU.purpose: Permits a foreign national to take up private-sector employment in Nauru under a local sponsoring employer.
NRU.notes: Employment sub-category of the Business Visa. Fee AUD 1,000 for most employment (a higher AUD 8,000 multiple-entry rate applies to certain categories), plus an AUD 50 processing fee (justice.gov.nr fee schedule). Distinct from the Local Business (Employment) Visa (restricted to work with 100% Nauruan-owned businesses) and the Public Service Employment Visa (government sector). Requires a local sponsoring employer. Application by email to the Immigration Division.

NRU.name: Media Visa
NRU.purpose: For visiting media, journalists, and film crews reporting on or filming in Nauru.
NRU.notes: Media sub-category of the Business Visa. Fee AUD 8,000 (approx. USD 5,200), single entry, 3 months; non-refundable if the application is unsuccessful. Applicants submit a completed application form, passport bio-page, and an employer letter stating the reason for the trip, by email to the Immigration Division. Confirmed on the official Government of Nauru visa-requirements page and the justice.gov.nr fee schedule.

NRU.name: Research Visa
NRU.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting research in Nauru.
NRU.notes: Research sub-category of the Business Visa. Fee AUD 200 (multiple entry) or AUD 100 (single entry), plus an AUD 50 processing fee (justice.gov.nr fee schedule). Application by email to the Immigration Division.

NRU.name: Religious Vocation Visa
NRU.purpose: For clergy, missionaries, and persons entering Nauru for a religious vocation.
NRU.notes: Religious Vocation sub-category of the Business Visa. No visa fee, multiple entry (an AUD 50 processing fee applies to Business Visa applications; justice.gov.nr fee schedule). Application by email to the Immigration Division.

NRU.name: Education Visa
NRU.purpose: Education sub-category of the Business Visa, for persons entering Nauru in connection with education.
NRU.notes: Education sub-category of the Business Visa. No visa fee, multiple entry (an AUD 50 processing fee applies to Business Visa applications; justice.gov.nr fee schedule). The official fee schedule does not state whether this covers enrolled students or persons employed in Nauru's education sector; Nauru publishes no separate student-visa category. Application by email to the Immigration Division.

NRU.name: Local Business (Employment) Visa
NRU.purpose: Permits employment with Nauruan businesses or 100% Nauruan-owned companies operating in Nauru.
NRU.notes: Fee is AUD 300–400 depending on duration. Restricted to work with Nauruan nationals or 100% Nauruan-owned businesses. Introduced by Immigration (Amendment) Regulations 2023 (SL No. 8 of 2023), Gazette No. 47, 6 March 2023.

NRU.name: Residence Visa
NRU.purpose: Grants long-term or permanent settlement rights in Nauru for eligible foreign nationals.
NRU.notes: No application fee. Specific eligibility criteria and processing times not published officially online. Application by email to the Immigration Division.

NRU.name: Regional Processing Centre Visa
NRU.purpose: Issued to asylum seekers undergoing refugee processing at the Nauru Regional Processing Centre established under bilateral arrangements with Australia.
NRU.notes: Fee is AUD 1,000/month. This is not a standard immigration pathway for ordinary foreign nationals. Issued under bilateral arrangements between Nauru and Australia.

NRU.name: Special Purpose Visa
NRU.purpose: Covers various specialized entry purposes as defined in the Immigration Regulations 2014 that do not fall under other visa classes.
NRU.notes: Specific fee, duration, and eligibility depend on the specific purpose authorized under the regulations. Application by email to the Immigration Division.

NRU.name: Long Term Stay Visa
NRU.purpose: A special long-term visa class for persons from states with bilateral arrangements with Nauru, introduced in 2025.
NRU.notes: Established by Immigration (Long Term Stay Visa) Regulations 2025 (SL No. 3 of 2025), Gazette No. 58, 12 February 2025. The Regulations set the visa fee at AUD 1,000 per year ('or any other sum that may be prescribed'). Primarily for individuals from states holding bilateral arrangements with Nauru (context includes Australia's NZYQ cohort). Not a standard tourist or work pathway.

NRU.name: Temporary Settlement Visa
NRU.purpose: Issued to recognized refugees for temporary settlement in Nauru.
NRU.notes: Fee is AUD 2,000/month. Not a standard immigration pathway for ordinary foreign nationals. Applicable only to persons granted refugee status in Nauru.

NRU.name: Dependant Visa
NRU.purpose: Permits family members (dependants) of valid Nauru visa holders to accompany or join them in Nauru.
NRU.notes: Fee is AUD 1,000. Issued to dependants of holders of other valid Nauru visas. Application by email to the Immigration Division. Specific eligibility (relationship types, age limits) not published in detail online.

NRU.name: Public Service Employment Visa
NRU.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to take up employment in the Nauru public service sector.
NRU.notes: Established by Immigration (Public Service Employment Visa) Regulations 2025, Gazette No. 256, 2025. Full fee and duration details not extractable from binary PDF. Specifically for employment within Nauru government/public sector.

NZL.name: Visitor Visa
NZL.purpose: Holiday/tourism, visiting family and friends, or study of up to 3 months
NZL.notes: Apply online via Immigration New Zealand. Stay up to 9 months in an 18-month period. Fee from NZD 441; processing 80% within 2 weeks. Since 27 January 2025 visitors may also work remotely for an overseas employer while in New Zealand on this visa.

NZL.name: Business Visitor Visa
NZL.purpose: Business meetings, negotiations, exploring opportunities (no local employment)
NZL.notes: For business visits of up to 3 months in a 12-month period. Cannot be used to work for a New Zealand employer. Fee from NZD 341; processing 80% within 1 week.

NZL.name: Transit Visa
NZL.purpose: Passing through Auckland International Airport en route to another country
NZL.notes: Required for nationals of transit-visa countries transiting through Auckland Airport (max 24 hours in the transit area). Fee from NZD 235; processing 80% within 4 days. Not needed if you hold a valid NZeTA or NZ visa.

NZL.name: Medical Treatment Visitor Visa
NZL.purpose: Receiving pre-approved medical treatment or consultation in New Zealand
NZL.notes: For pre-approved treatment at a specified hospital/institution. Must show ability to pay for treatment. Up to 6 months; can reapply for longer stays. Fee from NZD 341; processing 80% within 4 weeks.

NZL.name: Fee Paying Student Visa
NZL.purpose: Full-time study with an approved New Zealand education provider
NZL.notes: Requires an offer of place from an approved provider; student pays international tuition. Valid up to 4 years. Fee from NZD 850; processing 80% within 9.5 weeks. Paper applications no longer accepted.

NZL.name: Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV)
NZL.purpose: Working for an accredited New Zealand employer with a job offer
NZL.notes: Employer must be AEWV-accredited. Valid up to 5 years (3 years for skill level 4-5 roles). Fee from NZD 1,540; processing 80% within 7 weeks. Pathway to residence via Skilled Migrant Category.

NZL.name: Specific Purpose Work Visa
NZL.purpose: Working in New Zealand for a specific purpose or event
NZL.notes: For a defined purpose or event (e.g. seconded staff, contract, specialist work). Length granted as needed to complete the work; must arrive within 12 months of issue. Fee from NZD 1,455; processing 80% within 3 weeks.

NZL.name: Post Study Work Visa
NZL.purpose: Graduates of eligible NZ qualifications working for any employer after study
NZL.notes: Open work rights for up to 3 years depending on qualification level and where you studied. Fee from NZD 1,670; processing 80% within 5 weeks.

NZL.name: Working Holiday Visa
NZL.purpose: Holidaying and working in New Zealand (typically age 18–30, 18–35 for some countries)
NZL.notes: Available to citizens of countries with a working holiday agreement with New Zealand (normally up to 12 months). All applications must be made online and only while the relevant scheme is open.

NZL.name: Partner of a New Zealander Work Visa
NZL.purpose: Partners of New Zealand citizens/residents to live and work in New Zealand
NZL.notes: For partners of NZ citizens or residents in a genuine and stable relationship. Open work rights; up to 3 years (initially up to 1 year if living together less than 12 months). Fee from NZD 1,630; processing 80% within 5 weeks.

NZL.name: Temporary Retirement Visitor Visa
NZL.purpose: Retirees aged 66+ who invest in New Zealand and can support themselves
NZL.notes: For applicants aged 66 or older with NZD 750,000 to invest for 2 years, plus NZD 500,000 to live on and annual income of NZD 60,000. Valid 2 years; can reapply if conditions maintained. Fee from NZD 7,891.

OMN.name: Tourist Visit Visa (Unsponsored)
OMN.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Oman for tourism without a local sponsor. The standard tourist visa applied for online through the ROP eVisa portal.
OMN.notes: Falls under the 'Visit Unsponsored' visa class on the ROP eVisa platform. Issued as a 10-day single-entry (OMR 5, approx. USD 13) or 30-day single-entry (OMR 20, approx. USD 52) visa; the 30-day fee is shown here. The fm.gov.om entry-visas page describes this as 'usually appropriate' for tourists. Applied for at evisa.rop.gov.om. Eligibility depends on nationality; check evisa.rop.gov.om/visa-eligibility.

OMN.name: Tourist Visit Visa (Sponsored)
OMN.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Oman for tourism where a licensed tourism company or local sponsor in Oman acts as sponsor.
OMN.notes: Falls under the 'Visit Sponsored' visa class on the ROP eVisa platform. Enables tourists of all nationalities to obtain a tourism visa valid 30 days, extendable for a similar period, sponsored by a company licensed to practice tourism activities. Issued as 10-day (OMR 5, approx. USD 13) or 30-day (OMR 20, approx. USD 52); the 30-day fee is shown here. Applied for via gov.om / evisa.rop.gov.om.

OMN.name: GCC Resident Tourist Visa (Type 29A)
OMN.purpose: Allows any foreign national holding a valid GCC country residence permit with an approved profession to visit Oman for tourism.
OMN.notes: Fee is OMR 5 (approximately USD 13). Available at Oman airports and land borders (on arrival) or via evisa.rop.gov.om. Requires valid GCC residence permit with approved profession and minimum 3 months validity. Companion visa (Type 29B) also available. GCC resident must hold one of 139 approved professions.

OMN.name: Work Visa
OMN.purpose: Granted to foreign nationals coming to Oman for employment at the request and responsibility of an Omani employer (sponsor).
OMN.notes: Fee is OMR 20 (approximately USD 52). Valid for 2 years from date of passport stamping. Multi-entry. Applicant must be at least 21 years old. Sponsor must be a locally registered entity with full legal competence. Requires Ministry of Manpower labor permit, valid passport (6+ months), two photographs, and medical certificate for nationals of India, Pakistan, Philippines, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Egypt, Sudan, Ethiopia, Syria, Nepal. Monthly fine of OMR 50 for delay in renewal. PRO accreditation required on the eVisa system for work visa applications.

OMN.name: Employment Contracting Visa
OMN.purpose: A visa category for foreign nationals entering Oman under an employment contracting arrangement.
OMN.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category by the Royal Oman Police alongside Work Visa, Temporary Work Visa, Family Joining Visa, and Student Visa. Specific fee, duration, and detailed eligibility requirements were not publicly available on official pages at time of research. Managed via the ROP eVisa portal with PRO accreditation.

OMN.name: Temporary Work Visa
OMN.purpose: A short-term work visa for foreign nationals coming to Oman for temporary employment or project-based work.
OMN.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category by the Royal Oman Police. Specific fee, duration, and detailed eligibility requirements were not publicly available on official pages at time of research. Managed via the ROP eVisa portal with PRO accreditation.

OMN.name: Family Joining Visa
OMN.purpose: Allows family members of foreign nationals legally residing in Oman to join their resident sponsor.
OMN.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category by the Royal Oman Police. Falls under the 'Resident Sponsored' visa class. Specific fee, duration, and detailed eligibility requirements were not publicly available on official pages at time of research. Managed via the ROP eVisa portal.

OMN.name: Student Visa
OMN.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolling in educational institutions in Oman, requiring a local sponsor (typically the educational institution).
OMN.notes: Listed as a distinct visa category by the Royal Oman Police. Falls under the 'Resident Sponsored' visa class. Specific fee, duration, and detailed eligibility requirements were not publicly available on official pages at time of research. Managed via the ROP eVisa portal.

OMN.name: Oman Golden Residency (10-Year Residency)
OMN.purpose: Long-term renewable residency for international investors, entrepreneurs, and high-net-worth individuals investing in Oman through one of seven qualifying routes.
OMN.notes: Renewable 10-year residency. Minimum investment approximately OMR 200,000 (approx. USD 520,000). Seven qualifying routes: (1) Real estate in Integrated Tourism Complexes; (2) Company formation in Oman; (3) Government Development Bonds; (4) Muscat Stock Exchange shares; (5) Fixed-term bank deposit (min. 5 years); (6) Owning a company employing 50+ Omani nationals; (7) Nomination under Foreign Capital Investment Law. Benefits include full foreign ownership rights, up to 3 domestic workers, sponsorship of spouse and children, fast-track immigration lanes. No pathway to citizenship.

OMN.name: One Year Tourist Visit Visa (Multiple Entry)
OMN.purpose: Multiple-entry tourist visa allowing repeated visits to Oman over one year for tourism and leisure.
OMN.notes: Fee is OMR 50 (approx. USD 130). Valid one year from issuance with multiple entries; each stay in Oman must not exceed one month (30 days). Applicant must be outside Oman when applying and hold no other valid Oman visa. Passport valid 6+ months required. Applied via the ROP eVisa portal / gov.om.

OMN.name: Qatar-Oman Joint Tourist Visa
OMN.purpose: Allows foreign tourists holding a valid Qatar tourist visa to enter Oman when arriving directly from Qatar, at no additional fee.
OMN.notes: No fee (0 OMR). Applicant must be a national of a country eligible for the Qatar-Oman Joint Tourist Visa, hold a valid Qatar entry visa, and arrive in Oman directly from Qatar (no intervening country). Only a valid passport is required. Applied via the ROP eVisa portal / gov.om.

OMN.name: Land Transit Visa
OMN.purpose: Permits the holder to travel through Oman to and from neighboring countries via designated land ports.
OMN.notes: Fee is OMR 5 (approx. USD 13). Requires a passport copy, personal photograph, an entry visa for the neighboring country or valid residency, and a request letter. Applied via the ROP eVisa portal / gov.om.

OMN.name: Airport Transit Visa
OMN.purpose: For passengers transiting through Oman's airports on flights passing through the Sultanate; obtained by the airline on the passenger's behalf.
OMN.notes: Fee is OMR 5 (approx. USD 13). Maximum stay up to 72 hours. The application must be submitted by the airline company; all passengers' passports must be valid at least 6 months. Applied via the ROP eVisa portal / gov.om.

OMN.name: Emergency Visa
OMN.purpose: For foreign nationals needing to enter Oman for a short period due to medical reasons or other urgent situations; submitted by a local employer.
OMN.notes: Fee is OMR 15 (approx. USD 39). Covers entry for medical reasons or other urgent situations. The visa must be applied for by a local employer in Oman, not the individual directly. Requires passport valid 6+ months, passport copy, and a digital photo. Administered by the Royal Oman Police via gov.om.

PAK.name: Tourist Visa
PAK.purpose: For leisure, sightseeing, and recreational travel to Pakistan. Issued to foreign nationals who intend to visit Pakistan for tourism purposes.
PAK.notes: Applied for via Pakistan Online Visa System (POVS) at visa.nadra.gov.pk. Available to nationals of approximately 175 countries (List A). The Visa on Arrival (VOA) and Visa Prior to Arrival (VPA) programs were suspended effective 1 January 2026 - only standard online e-visa route is available. Nationals of Afghanistan, China, Japan, Iceland, North Korea, Slovakia, Malaysia, UAE, and Saudi Arabia reportedly pay no visa fee. Processing time ~7 business days at missions abroad or up to 20 business days per Fragomen (March 2026).

PAK.name: Business Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Pakistan for commercial, trade, or business meetings. Also covers the Business Visa List (BVL) countries with facilitated access.
PAK.notes: Applied for via POVS portal. Fee is approximately 150% of the tourist/visit visa fee for most nationalities (per Consulate General LA). Business Visa List (BVL) countries may have facilitated processing. Requires documentation of business purpose, invitation letters, or company correspondence.

PAK.name: SIFC Business Visa
PAK.purpose: Issued under the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) framework for foreign investors and business persons targeting Pakistan's priority investment sectors including mining, gold, and IT.
PAK.notes: Short-term: single-entry up to 6 months; long-term: multiple-entry up to 5 years (extendable by 2 additional years). SIFC recommendation letter may be required. Available to citizens of all countries, including both BVL and non-BVL countries. Priority sectors: mining, gold, IT/technology, energy.

PAK.name: SIFC Investor Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign investors making significant investments in Pakistan under the Special Investment Facilitation Council framework, particularly in priority sectors such as technology, energy, and manufacturing.
PAK.notes: Short-term: up to 3 years; long-term: up to 5 years (extendable by 2 additional years). SIFC recommendation letter required for visas over 1 year. For non-SIFC investor visas: investment in SECP-registered companies of not less than USD 50,000 or real estate investment exceeding USD 100,000. After 5 years legal residence and mastering an official language, foreigners can apply for citizenship per visa.nadra.gov.pk.

PAK.name: Work/Employment Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking to take up employment with a Pakistani organization or company. Requires sponsorship from a Pakistani employer.
PAK.notes: Requires approval from employer and relevant government ministry. Fee approximately 150% of tourist visa rate (per Consulate General LA fee structure). Separate fee structure applies for US nationals. All visa applications must be submitted through the POVS online portal; manual processing discontinued.

PAK.name: Student Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted to an educational institution in Pakistan to pursue academic studies.
PAK.notes: Requires prior approval from the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Interior, Government of Pakistan. Must have confirmed admission to a recognized Pakistani institution. Applied through POVS portal. Details page at Consulate General LA was marked 'under construction' as of June 2026.

PAK.name: Family Visit Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting family members residing in Pakistan. Covers spouse, children, parents, and other close relatives.
PAK.notes: Requires invitation letter from the family member in Pakistan detailing purpose, duration, and cities of visit. Bank statements (3 months) and proof of family relationship required. Applied via POVS portal. For Indian nationals, fee is USD 192 per Consulate General LA. Afghan nationals have visa fee waived.

PAK.name: Transit Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Pakistan en route to a third country without leaving the airport or for a short stopover.
PAK.notes: Transit without a visa permitted for up to 24 hours in some cases (per Pakistan Embassy Russia). Standard transit visa allows short stopover of up to 72 hours. Applied via POVS portal. Requires confirmed onward ticket and valid visa/residence permit for destination country.

PAK.name: Medical Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Pakistan to receive medical treatment at a recognized Pakistani healthcare facility.
PAK.notes: Requires letter from a recognized Pakistani medical institution confirming admission for treatment. Applied via POVS portal. May be extended in-country if treatment continues longer than anticipated.

PAK.name: NGO Representatives Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals representing non-governmental organizations working in Pakistan on approved development, humanitarian, or charitable projects.
PAK.notes: Requires prior approval of Ministry of Interior, Government of Pakistan. NGO must be registered and approved to operate in Pakistan. Applied via POVS portal. Separate NOC (No Objection Certificate) may be required from relevant federal ministries.

PAK.name: Journalist / Film / TV / Documentary Team Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign journalists, filmmakers, television crews, and documentary teams seeking to work in Pakistan on media projects.
PAK.notes: Requires prior approval of Ministry of Information, Government of Pakistan. Press accreditation and project documentation required. Applied via POVS portal. Separate NOC from PEMRA or Ministry of Information may be required for filming activities.

PAK.name: Missionary Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Pakistan for religious missionary activities under an officially recognized and approved religious organization.
PAK.notes: Requires prior approval of Ministry of Interior, Government of Pakistan. Religious organization must be officially recognized in Pakistan. Applied via POVS portal. Strict scrutiny applies; approval is discretionary.

PAK.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
PAK.purpose: For holders of diplomatic or official passports traveling to Pakistan on government business, including members of diplomatic missions, consular posts, and international organizations.
PAK.notes: 49 countries have bilateral visa abolition agreements with Pakistan covering diplomatic and/or official passport holders (per dgip.gov.pk as of 21-02-2024). Visa-free duration ranges from 30 to 90 days depending on the country. Members of diplomatic/consular missions and their families are exempt for the full duration of assignment. Processed through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, not the standard POVS portal.

PAK.name: Pilgrimage / Religious Tourism Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Pakistan for religious pilgrimage and religious tourism - e.g. Sikh pilgrims (Kartarpur Sahib, Nankana Sahib), Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims visiting sites of religious importance.
PAK.notes: Applied via POVS portal under the Pilgrim Tourism category. Business, Tourist and Sikh Pilgrimage visas are issued with 'No Visa Fee' for eligible nationalities. Sikh pilgrims may apply through sub-categories including residents of a third country other than India and their spouses/children (letter from the Jatha/group leader required for organized groups from India). The separate Visa Prior to Arrival (Sikh Pilgrims) fast-track route was suspended effective 1 January 2026, leaving the standard online pilgrim visa as the operative route.

PAK.name: Tabligh Visa
PAK.purpose: For Muslim citizens of foreign countries who wish to enter Pakistan to participate in Tabligh (Islamic preaching / religious outreach) activities.
PAK.notes: Applied via POVS portal. Requires an invitation letter from an authorized Tableeghi Centre in Pakistan, plus passport and photograph. Granted for up to 45 days; processing approximately 4-6 weeks. Distinct from the Missionary Visa, which covers non-Muslim religious workers under Ministry of Interior approval. The Tabligh Visa on Arrival / ETA fast-track route was suspended effective 1 January 2026.

PAK.name: Work - Domestic Aide Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals employed in Pakistan as domestic aides (housemaids, personal/household staff) under the sponsorship of their employer.
PAK.notes: A separate work sub-category from the standard Work/Employment Visa. Applied via POVS portal as a new visa (Entry) if the applicant holds no valid Pakistan visa, or as an Extension if already residing in Pakistan on a valid visa. Requires sponsorship and supporting documentation from the employer.

PAK.name: Conference / Seminar / Sports / Cultural Events Visa
PAK.purpose: For foreign nationals attending conferences, seminars, workshops, sports fixtures, and cultural events taking place in Pakistan.
PAK.notes: Listed under the POVS 'Other Visa' category. Applicants must apply at least 6 weeks in advance of the event. Requires an invitation letter from the host organization (with a separate invitation letter for any accompanying family members); applicants applying from a third country must provide proof of legal residence. Processing typically around 4 weeks.

PAN.name: Tourist Entry (Visa-Free / Visa Exemption)
PAN.purpose: Short-term tourism and leisure for nationals of exempt countries. Entry is granted at the border without prior application.
PAN.notes: USA and Canada nationals receive up to 180 days; other exempt nationalities (100+ countries) receive up to 90 days under Resolution 22706. Minimum passport validity 3 months. Must show proof of economic solvency (B/.500 / USD 500) and a return ticket. Nationals of non-exempt countries must obtain a stamped or authorized visa from a consulate before travel.

PAN.name: Visa Estampada (Stamped Visa)
PAN.purpose: Tourist/visitor visa for nationals of countries not covered by visa-free exemptions. Obtained at a Panamanian consulate before travel.
PAN.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 90 (Western Union); total ~USD 140. Processing up to 30 business days. Requires: visa application form, passport copies, flight reservation, government-issued ID, 3 passport photos, proof of funds (USD 500 minimum), hotel reservation. Must apply in person at nearest Panamanian consulate.

PAN.name: Visa Autorizada (Authorized Visa)
