PAN.purpose: Tourist/visitor visa for nationals requiring prior SNM (National Migration Service) authorization, typically where no local consulate is available.
PAN.notes: Fee is USD 50 application + USD 90 (Western Union); total ~USD 140. Processing up to 60 business days. Same documentation as stamped visa. Authorization is granted by SNM headquarters; applicant must then present authorization at port of entry.

PAN.name: Visa de Tránsito (Transit Visa)
PAN.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to transit through Panama en route to another destination without entering the country proper.
PAN.notes: Required for nationals of countries that do not qualify for visa-free transit. Exemptions exist for holders of valid Panamanian visas or qualifying third-country visas (US, Canada, UK, EU, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Singapore). Must hold onward travel documentation. As of 2025 Decrees 21 and 22 (August 2025), transit visa requirements were amended for Haitian and Cuban nationals.

PAN.name: Visa de Corta Estancia - Negocios (Short-Stay Business Visa)
PAN.purpose: Permits short-term business activities in Panama such as meetings, negotiations, and conferences without taking up local employment.
PAN.notes: Listed as a non-resident short-stay visa category on the SNM Permisos Migratorios page. Specific fee and processing time not published on official web pages; requirements are available as downloadable PDFs from migracion.gob.pa.

PAN.name: Visa de Corta Estancia como Trabajador Remoto (Short-Stay Remote Worker Visa)
PAN.purpose: Allows foreign remote workers employed by or contracted with foreign transnational companies to live and work remotely from Panama for up to 18 months.
PAN.notes: Created by Executive Decree 198 of May 7, 2021. Initial stay 9 months, renewable once for a further 9 months (total maximum 18 months). Minimum annual income requirement: B/.36,000 (USD 36,000) from foreign sources. Applicant must be physically present in Panama to apply at SNM Special Processing Window. Must not work for Panamanian companies or local clients. Foreign-source income is not subject to Panamanian income tax under Panama's territorial tax system. Also referenced on ProPanama official site.

PAN.name: Permiso de Trabajo Temporal - Trabajador Técnico/Temporal (V-TET) (Temporary/Technical Worker Permit)
PAN.purpose: Non-resident permit for foreign technical or temporary workers engaged by Panamanian employers for a defined project or term.
PAN.notes: Listed as a non-resident work-related permit on the SNM Permisos Migratorios page. Specific fees and processing times are in downloadable requirement PDFs on migracion.gob.pa. Other non-resident work permits include those for sailors, entertainment workers, domestic workers, transient/event workers, banking professionals, and special commercial/investor categories.

PAN.name: Permiso de Trabajo - Representante de Empresa Multinacional (Multinational Company Representative Permit)
PAN.purpose: Temporary residency permit for executives and specialists working for multinational companies headquartered or operating in Panama's Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime.
PAN.notes: Temporary resident category under Panama's SEM (Sedes de Empresas Multinacionales) law. Companies must be registered under Law 41 of 2007. Includes accompanying dependents. Processing handled by SNM.

PAN.name: Permiso de Residente Temporal por Contrato con el Estado (Temporary Residence - Government Contract Worker)
PAN.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals contracted to work on specific government-awarded projects in Panama.
PAN.notes: Tied to the duration of the government contract. Permit lapses when the contract ends.

PAN.name: Visa de Estudiante (Student Visa / Temporary Resident Student Permit)
PAN.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Panama for the duration of an accredited academic program at a recognized Panamanian institution.
PAN.notes: Official SNM temporary-resident student permit checklist ('Temporal por Razones de Educación'). Covers standard students as well as exchange program participants and Fulbright scholarship recipients. Permit is tied to enrollment in the educational institution. Specific fees and processing times available via downloadable PDFs on migracion.gob.pa. Executive Decree 3 of February 6, 2026 created a permanent residency pathway for students after completing their studies.

PAN.name: Pensionado / Jubilado (Retiree / Pensioner Permanent Residency)
PAN.purpose: Grants immediate permanent residency to foreign retirees who can demonstrate a lifetime monthly pension income from an official or private pension source.
PAN.notes: Grants immediate permanent residency (not a temporary visa). Requires proof of lifetime monthly income of at least USD 1,000 from a government pension, social security, military pension, or private pension plan. Income threshold reduces to USD 750/month if applicant purchases Panamanian real estate worth at least USD 100,000. Available to anyone 18 years or older regardless of nationality. Path to citizenship after 5 years of permanent residency. Widely considered one of Panama's most popular residency programs. Accompanied by significant discount benefits (Pensionado card) on healthcare, transport, hotels, and entertainment.

PAN.name: Visa de Inversionista Calificado (Qualified Investor Visa)
PAN.purpose: Grants immediate permanent residency to foreign nationals making a qualifying investment in Panama via real estate, securities, or fixed-term bank deposit.
PAN.notes: Established by Decreto Ejecutivo 722 (amended by Decrees 109 and 193 of 2024). Grants immediate permanent residency upon approval. Three investment modalities: (1) Real estate: USD 300,000 minimum (valid until October 15, 2026, then increases to USD 500,000); (2) Securities/stocks on Panama Stock Exchange: USD 500,000 minimum for at least 5 years; (3) Fixed-term bank deposit: USD 750,000 minimum for at least 5 years. Investment must originate from abroad and be maintained for at least 5 years. Processing approximately 30 business days. After 5 years of permanent residency, eligible for naturalization. Administered by SNM and MICI.

PAN.name: Residencia por Solvencia Económica (Economic Solvency Residence)
PAN.purpose: Temporary then permanent residency for foreign nationals who demonstrate economic solvency through investment in Panamanian real estate or fixed-term bank deposits.
PAN.notes: Requires investment of at least USD 300,000 in real estate and/or a Panamanian bank fixed-term deposit (or mixed investment). Grants 2-year temporary residency first, then permanent residency after 2 years. Three sub-options: fixed-term deposit, real estate investment, or mixed investment. Available to all nationalities. Citizenship pathway after 5 years of permanent residency.

PAN.name: Naciones Amigas / Países Específicos (Friendly Nations Visa)
PAN.purpose: Permanent residency for nationals of approximately 50 'friendly nations' who can demonstrate economic ties to Panama.
PAN.notes: Established by Executive Decree 226 of July 20, 2021. Open to nationals of approximately 50 'friendly' nations. Requires proof of economic ties to Panama (employment with a Panamanian company, ownership of a Panamanian business, or real estate purchase) and a bank balance of at least USD 5,000 in a Panamanian bank. Grants permanent residency. After 5 years continuous permanent residency, eligible for naturalization. Eligible nationalities include: Germany, Andorra, Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Cyprus, South Korea, Costa Rica, Croatia, Denmark, Slovakia, Spain, USA, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Ireland, Israel, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, San Marino, Mexico, Monaco, Montenegro, Norway, New Zealand, Netherlands, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, UK, Czech Republic, Serbia, Singapore, South Africa, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Uruguay (approx. 50 nations per Decree 226 of 2021).

PAN.name: Permiso de Residente Permanente por Matrimonio con Panameño/a (Permanent Residency - Spouse of Panamanian National)
PAN.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals legally married to a Panamanian citizen.
PAN.notes: Official SNM permanent-resident checklist 'Casado con Panameño'. Also covers parents of Panamanian children and dependents of permanent residents under the family reunification categories listed by SNM. Processing handled by SNM. Specific fees and required documents available via downloadable PDFs on migracion.gob.pa.

PAN.name: Reunificación Familiar (Family Regrouping Permit)
PAN.purpose: Temporary residency permit that allows qualifying family members (dependents) of legally resident foreign nationals to join them in Panama.
PAN.notes: Official SNM temporary-resident checklist 'Permiso de Residente Temporal por Reagrupación Familiar'. Covers dependents (spouse, children) of foreign nationals who already hold a valid temporary or permanent residency in Panama.

PAN.name: Visa de Corta Estancia - Tratamiento Médico (Short-Stay Medical Treatment Visa)
PAN.purpose: Short-stay visa for foreign nationals traveling to Panama specifically to receive medical treatment at a Panamanian healthcare facility.
PAN.notes: Listed as a short-stay non-resident visa category on the SNM Permisos Migratorios page. Specific fees and documentation requirements available in downloadable PDFs from migracion.gob.pa. Typically requires a letter from the treating Panamanian medical institution.

PAN.name: Visa Diplomática / Exención para Pasaporte Diplomático (Diplomatic Visa / Diplomatic Passport Exemption)
PAN.purpose: Visa-free or facilitated entry for holders of diplomatic passports under bilateral agreements, and visas for diplomatic personnel not covered by exemptions.
PAN.notes: Diplomatic passport holders of Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, Indonesia, Philippines, Republic of China (Taiwan), and Venezuela receive visa-free entry despite those nationalities' ordinary passports requiring visas. Diplomatic personnel accredited to Panama receive MIRE-coordinated courtesy visas. Special commercial/investor visas and former diplomat categories also exist under SNM permit system.

PAN.name: Permiso de Residente Permanente - Regularización Migratoria 'Crisol de Razas' (General Migration Regularization)
PAN.purpose: Permanent residency pathway for foreign nationals already residing in Panama who do not meet standard permit requirements, provided they meet humanitarian or demographic criteria.
PAN.notes: Official SNM permanent-resident checklist for General Migration Regularization (PRP-RMG, Decree 235). Periodic amnesty/regularization programs. The 'Crisol de Razas' category represents Panama's historical immigration policy welcoming migrants of diverse backgrounds. Activated periodically by executive decree. Not a continuously available visa type.

PAN.name: Protección Humanitaria (Humanitarian Protection / Asylum)
PAN.purpose: Temporary humanitarian protection for foreign nationals who cannot safely return to their home country, including asylum seekers and refugees.
PAN.notes: Official SNM checklist for the Humanitarian Protection Permit (Permiso de Protección de Seguridad Humanitaria, 2026 decree). Panama is a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention. Refugee/asylum applications are processed by the National Office for Refugees (ONPAR) under MIRE. Short-stay humanitarian assistance visa is also listed as a non-resident category on the SNM page.

PAN.name: Permiso Especial de Permanencia - Zona Franca de Colón / Panama Pacífico (Special Economic Zone Permit)
PAN.purpose: Permanent or temporary residency for investors, executives, and workers operating within Panama's special economic zones including the Colón Free Zone and Panama Pacífico.
PAN.notes: Separate permit regimes exist for the Colón Free Zone, Panama Pacífico Special Economic Area, export processing zones, and film/audiovisual industry investors. Panama Pacífico is governed by Law 41 of 2004. Specific investment and employment thresholds apply per zone.

PAN.name: Inversionista Forestal / Inversión Forestal (Forest / Reforestation Investor Residency)
PAN.purpose: Residency for foreign nationals who invest in a government-certified reforestation or forestry-plantation project in Panama.
PAN.notes: SNM 'Por Razones Económicas' investor category under the immigration regulations (Decreto Ejecutivo 320 of 2008). The investment must be in a reforestation / forestry-plantation project certified by the Ministry of Environment (MiAmbiente). Offered in tiers: a temporary-resident forest-investor permit at a lower threshold (commonly cited around USD 80,000; see separate checklist https://www.migracion.gob.pa/wp-content/uploads/PERMISO-TEMPORAL-INVERSIONISTAS-FORESTAL.pdf) and a permanent-resident forest-investor permit (from about USD 100,000, with immediate permanent residency around USD 350,000). Investment must be maintained for at least 5 years or the residency is cancelled. Verify current exact amounts against the official checklist PDF.

PAN.name: Inversionista Macro Empresa (Business / Macro-Enterprise Investor Permanent Residency)
PAN.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals who invest their own capital in a Panamanian company that employs Panamanian workers.
PAN.notes: Permanent-resident 'Por Razones Económicas' category under Decreto Ejecutivo 320 of 2008. Requires a personal investment in a Panamanian business (commonly cited minimum around USD 160,000) plus employment of at least five (5) Panamanian workers registered with social security and paid at least the minimum wage. Investment capital must originate from abroad. Path to naturalization after 5 years of permanent residency. Verify current exact amounts against the official checklist PDF.

PAN.name: Rentista Retirado (Retired Person of Independent Means Residency)
PAN.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals who fund a Panamanian fixed-term bank deposit generating a guaranteed monthly interest income, without a lifetime pension.
PAN.notes: Permanent-resident 'Políticas Especiales' category under Decreto Ejecutivo 320 of 2008. Distinct from the Pensionado/Jubilado program: instead of a lifetime pension, the applicant places a 5-year fixed-term deposit (CD) with the Banco Nacional de Panamá (or an authorized Panamanian bank) whose interest yields a guaranteed monthly income (commonly cited minimum around USD 850/month). Grants permanent residency; renews with the deposit term. Verify current exact amounts against the official checklist PDF.

PAN.name: Extranjero Profesional (Foreign Professional Permanent Residency)
PAN.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign university-educated professionals who will practise a profession in Panama that is not constitutionally reserved for Panamanian nationals.
PAN.notes: Permanent-resident 'Por Leyes Especiales' category under Decreto Ejecutivo 320 of 2008. Requires a university degree recognised/revalidated in Panama, registration with the relevant professional board where applicable, and proof of economic solvency (Panamanian bank account). The profession must not be one reserved exclusively for Panamanian citizens by the Constitution or law. Does not require an employer sponsor. Path to naturalization after 5 years of permanent residency.

PER.name: Visa de Turista / Calidad Migratoria de Turista
PER.purpose: Short-stay visits for tourism, recreation, sport, health, study trips of up to 30 days, family visits, or transit. No lucrative activities permitted.
PER.notes: Nationals of visa-exempt countries enter without a visa for up to 90 or 183 days (depending on nationality) under the tourist/negocios category. Nationals requiring a visa must apply at a Peruvian consulate abroad. Stay granted at port of entry by immigration officer; typically up to 90 days, extendable to a maximum of 183 days total within a 365-day period. Peru does not offer a tourist e-visa or visa-on-arrival for ordinary passport holders requiring a visa - consulate application only. Governed by Decreto Legislativo N° 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Negocios
PER.purpose: Short-stay visits for business activities such as meetings, negotiations, contract signings, conferences, and market research. No employment or income-generating work permitted.
PER.notes: Visa-exempt nationals may enter for business purposes under the Negocios category (same exemption as tourist). Max stay up to 183 days in a 12-month period. Nationals requiring a visa must apply at a Peruvian consulate. Japan's business exemption (DS 020-2025-RE, effective July 1, 2025) explicitly names the Calidad Migratoria de Negocios category for up to 183 days.

PER.name: Visa de Tránsito / Calidad Migratoria de Transeúnte
PER.purpose: Permits transit through Peru's territory or international airport areas for passengers continuing to a third country.
PER.notes: Since January 22, 2025 (DS 004-2025-RE), a transit visa is required for third-country nationals transiting Peru who are not already exempt from the tourist/business visa. Nationals who are visa-exempt for tourist/business entry are also exempt from the transit visa requirement. Must be applied for at a Peruvian consulate abroad. Transit without visa (TWOV) is not available for those who require a visa.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Trabajador
PER.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals to reside in Peru and work for a Peruvian employer or under a Peruvian labor contract.
PER.notes: Work authorization must be obtained before the visa can be issued; the employer typically sponsors the application and must obtain prior labor authorization from Peru's Ministry of Labor (MTPE) in most cases. Renewable annually. Path to permanent residency after 2 consecutive years. Governed by DL 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN. Application at Peruvian consulate abroad or via change of status in-country at Migraciones.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Estudiante
PER.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to reside in Peru to pursue full-time studies at an officially recognized educational institution.
PER.notes: Applicant must have an acceptance letter from a Peruvian educational institution recognized by the Ministry of Education (MINEDU) or equivalent. Cannot be used for tourist-style language courses under 30 days (those fall under tourist category). Renewable annually for the duration of studies. Path to permanent residency after 2 consecutive years of continuous residence. Governed by DL 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Residente para Inversionista
PER.purpose: Grants temporary residency to foreign nationals who make a qualifying investment in a Peruvian company and commit to creating local employment.
PER.notes: Minimum investment of PEN 500,000 (approximately USD 130,000) in a new or existing Peruvian company via international bank transfer through a Peruvian SBS-supervised institution. Applicant must commit to create at least 5 jobs for Peruvian nationals within 1 year of obtaining residency. Application fee: S/ 57.60 (code 07567 at Banco de la Nación). Renewable annually. After 2 years, permanent residency may be applied for. Governed by DL 1350, DS 007-2017-IN, and DS 002-2021-IN.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Rentista
PER.purpose: Grants permanent residency to foreign nationals who demonstrate a stable, permanent passive income from qualifying sources such as pensions, annuities, royalties, or dividends.
PER.notes: Requires proof of permanent monthly passive income of at least USD 1,000 from qualifying sources (pension, lifetime annuity, royalties guaranteed for life, or dividends). An additional USD 500/month per dependent is required. Income must be deposited through a Peruvian financial institution. Qualifying income does NOT include remote/freelance work, rental income, capital gains, or interest. Grants permanent residency (indefinite validity). Governed by DS 002-2021-IN.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Nómada Digital
PER.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals who work remotely for companies or clients domiciled outside Peru to reside and work in Peru without engaging in local employment.
PER.notes: Created by Decreto Legislativo N° 1582 (November 2023), which amended DL 1350 to add the Nómada Digital migration category. Would allow up to 365 days stay with renewal. However, as of June 2026, implementing regulations and TUPA procedures have not been published and this category is NOT yet operational - applications cannot be accepted. Status: legislated but unimplemented.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Familiar de Residente / Reagrupación Familiar
PER.purpose: Permits family members of legally resident foreign nationals or Peruvian citizens to join them and reside in Peru.
PER.notes: Eligible family members include spouses/partners, minor children, and economically dependent parents of the principal resident or Peruvian national. Documents required include proof of relationship (marriage certificate, birth certificate) and proof of the principal's legal status. Renewable annually. Governed by DL 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN. Also available under Andean Community (CAN) Decision 878 for nationals of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Religioso
PER.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals who are members of officially recognized religious organizations to reside in Peru to carry out religious activities.
PER.notes: Must be a member of a religious organization formally registered in Peru. Requires a letter of support from the religious organization. Renewable annually. Governed by DL 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria Diplomática / Oficial Temporal
PER.purpose: Admits foreign diplomats, consular officers, and official government representatives and their families to Peru for diplomatic or official duties.
PER.notes: Diplomatic and official passport holders from countries with visa suppression agreements with Peru (covering diplomatic/official/service passports) enter visa-free. These include a large list of countries per the official RREE May 2015 table and subsequent updates. The UK specifically was granted a unilateral exemption for diplomatic/official/service passport holders for up to 183 days by DS 003-2024-RE (published January 23, 2024). Indonesia was added by bilateral agreement ratified by DS 006-2025-RE. Accredited diplomatic staff receive the 'Calidad Migratoria Diplomática' status through the Ministry of Foreign Relations, not through standard Migraciones channels.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria Humanitaria
PER.purpose: Provides temporary protection and legal residency to foreign nationals who require humanitarian protection, including asylum seekers, refugees, stateless persons, and victims of trafficking.
PER.notes: Established under DL 1350. Covers refugees (under 1951 Refugee Convention), asylum seekers with pending applications, stateless persons, and victims of human trafficking. Administered jointly by Migraciones and the Comisión Especial para los Refugiados (CEPAR). Renewable annually while humanitarian need persists. Governed by DL 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN.

PER.name: Residencia de Comunidad Andina (CAN) / Estatuto Migratorio Andino
PER.purpose: Grants two-year temporary residency with path to permanent residency for nationals of Andean Community member states (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador) based on reciprocal regional free movement agreement.
PER.notes: Available to nationals of Bolivia, Colombia, and Ecuador under Andean Community Decision 878 (Andean Migration Statute, in force August 2021). Implemented in Peru by decree effective October 23, 2023. Two-year temporary residence. After 2 years, permanent residence may be applied for. Applicant must have clean criminal record and demonstrate means of support. Can enter with national ID card (cedula/DNI) - no passport required.

PER.name: Residencia MERCOSUR / Acuerdo de Residencia MERCOSUR
PER.purpose: Grants two-year temporary residency with path to permanent residency for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states based on bilateral regional agreement.
PER.notes: Available to nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Uruguay). Peru ratified the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement effective January 1, 2024. Can be applied for at a Peruvian consulate abroad or in-country at Migraciones. Two-year temporary residence, path to permanent residence after 2 years. MERCOSUR members may also enter with national ID card - no passport required.

PER.name: Calidad Migratoria de Designado (Trabajador Designado / Designado Residente)
PER.purpose: Foreign nationals sent by a foreign company or international corporation to carry out a specific task, project, or highly specialized technical/professional assignment in Peru (e.g. installing or maintaining complex machinery, international audits or certifications) without being on a Peruvian payroll.
PER.notes: Distinct from the standard Trabajador category: the worker is posted/seconded by a foreign employer for a defined assignment and is not hired under a local Peruvian labour contract. Requires a service-provision or technical-cooperation contract between the foreign corporation and the Peruvian receiving entity, plus a designation letter naming the worker. Fee S/ 58.80 (code 07567 via Pagalo.pe or Banco de la Nacion). Applied for online through Migraciones' Agencia Virtual while the applicant is outside Peru; decision within 30 business days. Renewable (prorroga). A temporary Designado variant (up to 183 days) also exists. Governed by DL 1350 and DS 007-2017-IN.

PER.name: Visa de Vacaciones y Trabajo / Calidad Migratoria de Intercambio (Working Holiday)
PER.purpose: Young foreign nationals (aged 18-30) from partner countries to spend up to one year in Peru combining tourism with incidental temporary work, under reciprocal 'Vacaciones y Trabajo' / Working Holiday agreements.
PER.notes: Issued under the Pacific Alliance 'Vacaciones y Trabajo' program (nationals of Mexico, Chile and Colombia, aged 18-30) and reciprocal bilateral Working Holiday agreements Peru maintains with France, Australia, New Zealand and Portugal (Czech Republic added from February 1, 2026). Multiple entries, one calendar year; work is permitted provided it is not the main purpose of the stay, and study/training is capped at roughly two months. Annual quota applies (about 300 permits per country per year under the Pacific Alliance scheme). Applicant must not have previously used the program. Applied for at a Peruvian consulate abroad; corresponds to the 'Intercambio' calidad migratoria under DL 1350.

PHL.name: 9(a-2) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Tourism/Leisure
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting the Philippines temporarily for pleasure, tourism, leisure, religious, recreational, or amusement purposes, or to visit family, relatives, or friends.
PHL.notes: Issued as Philippine e-Visa via evisa.gov.ph. Single entry: 7-12 working days processing; multiple entry: 15-21 working days. Cannot be extended or converted locally. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond departure. Most nationalities under EO 408 are visa-free for 30 days; e-Visa grants up to 59 days. Fee varies by nationality (dynamic pricing on site).

PHL.name: 9(a-1) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Business
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting temporary business or commercial activities in the Philippines without receiving Philippine-sourced compensation.
PHL.notes: Sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa. Issued as Philippine e-Visa via evisa.gov.ph. Covers business meetings, conferences, training, and seminars. Cannot be extended or converted locally. Processing: 7-12 working days (single), 15-21 working days (multiple).

PHL.name: 9(a-3) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Medical Treatment
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking medical treatment or health care in the Philippines, including their escorts.
PHL.notes: Sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa. Issued as Philippine e-Visa. Cannot be extended or converted locally. Escorts of medical patients are included under this category.

PHL.name: 9(a-4) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Private Yachtsmen/Sailors
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals making a temporary visit to the Philippines on board a private yacht or sailboat without any employment relationship in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa. Covers private maritime visits only; no local employment permitted.

PHL.name: 9(a-5) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Filmmaking
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting the Philippines for movie or documentary filming purposes as an independent activity.
PHL.notes: Sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa. No local compensation permitted.

PHL.name: 9(a-6) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Journalism
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting the Philippines for news and journalism purposes without local employment arrangements.
PHL.notes: Sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa. No Philippine-sourced compensation permitted.

PHL.name: 9(a-7) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Athletic and Performing Arts
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting the Philippines for athletic competitions or performing arts engagements without receiving Philippine compensation.
PHL.notes: Sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa. Covers athletes, performers, and entertainers for temporary visits without local employment.

PHL.name: 9(a-8) Temporary Visitor's Visa – Other Purposes
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting the Philippines temporarily for purposes not covered by other 9(a) sub-categories.
PHL.notes: Catch-all sub-category of the 9(a) Temporary Visitor's Visa with appropriate supporting documentation required.

PHL.name: 9(f) Student Visa
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals aged 18 or older who will take up a course of study higher than high school at a Philippine university, seminary, or college.
PHL.notes: Conversion fee: PHP 9,720 (approximately USD 170 as of 2014 rates) plus USD 50 for ACR I-Card. Extension fee: PHP 4,020 plus USD 50 for ACR I-Card. Applicant must be enrolled at a Philippine Commission on Higher Education (CHED)-accredited institution. Apply at BI Main Office or authorized regional immigration offices. Duration of stay tied to program enrollment.

PHL.name: 9(g) Pre-arranged Employment Visa
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals who have a pre-arranged employment offer in the Philippines and will engage in lawful occupation for wages, salary, or other compensation.
PHL.notes: Two categories: Commercial (for regular company employment) and Non-Commercial (for missionary, social, or rehabilitation work). Validity options: 1, 2, or 3 years. Fees (as of 2014): PHP 10,130 principal (commercial, non-Top 1,000 corp, 1-year) plus USD 50 ACR I-Card fee. Top 1,000 Corporation and non-commercial rates vary. Employer must provide notarized certification of foreign and Filipino employee count. Process involves pre-screening, fee payment, hearing, biometric capture, and passport submission.

PHL.name: 9(d) Treaty Trader or Treaty Investor Visa
PHL.purpose: For nationals of the USA, Japan, and Germany to carry on trade or commerce pursuant to an existing bilateral treaty or to develop and direct operations of a business enterprise in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Available only to nationals of USA, Japan, and Germany under existing treaties of commerce and navigation. Validity options: 1 year (PHP 9,620 principal) or 2 years (PHP 13,650 principal) plus ACR I-Card fee of USD 50/year. No minimum investment amount specified. Renewable. Dependents (spouse, children) may be included with separate fees.

PHL.name: 9(e) Accredited Official of Foreign Government Visa
PHL.purpose: For accredited officials of foreign governments and international organizations on assignment to the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Issued to diplomats, consular officers, and officials of accredited international organizations. Granted in coordination with the Department of Foreign Affairs. Specific fee structure and duration tied to assignment term.

PHL.name: Special Resident Retiree's Visa (SRRV)
PHL.purpose: A special non-immigrant visa for foreign retirees allowing indefinite stay in the Philippines as long as the required time deposit or investment is maintained.
PHL.notes: Issued by Bureau of Immigration through the Philippine Retirement Authority (PRA). Multiple sub-types: SRRV Classic (age 50+, pensioner: USD 15,000 deposit; non-pensioner: USD 30,000; age 40-49: higher thresholds), SRRV Courtesy (age 50+, pensioner: USD 1,500; lower thresholds for former Filipinos). Minimum age: 40 years. Multiple-entry, indefinite stay while investment maintained. Holders may retain original citizenship. No documented path to Philippine citizenship through SRRV. Contact: Philippine Retirement Authority, +632 8848 1412.

PHL.name: Special Investor's Resident Visa (SIRV)
PHL.purpose: For qualified foreign investors remitting funds to establish or participate in a business enterprise in the Philippines under Board of Investments priority areas.
PHL.notes: Requires remittance of at least USD 75,000 into a Peso Time Deposit at Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) or Development Bank of the Philippines (DBP). Funds must remain on deposit minimum 30 days, maximum 180 days. Investment must be made within 180 days of probationary visa issuance. Probationary SIRV valid 6 months; Indefinite SIRV valid indefinitely while investment maintained. Minimum age: 21 years. Apply at BOI One-Stop SIRV Center, 2nd Floor, BOI, #385 Senator Gil J. Puyat Avenue, Makati City.

PHL.name: Temporary Resident Visa (TRV)
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals married to Filipino citizens or under specific bilateral arrangements, allowing temporary residence in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Primarily for foreign spouses of Filipino citizens from countries without reciprocity agreements, and Indian nationals under a special arrangement. Conversion fee: PHP 8,620 per person (general), PHP 37,060 for Indian nationals. Extension fee: PHP 13,100 per person. Indian nationals may receive 5-year validity extensions. ACR I-Card required at additional USD 50/year. Passport surrendered during processing.

PHL.name: Immigrant Visa by Marriage (13A)
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals married to Filipino citizens to obtain permanent immigrant residence in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Grants permanent resident status to foreign spouses of Filipino citizens. Requires valid marriage to a Filipino citizen. Apply at Bureau of Immigration Main Office. Initial probationary period typically required before indefinite status granted.

PHL.name: Permanent Resident Visa (PRV) / Returning Resident (13E/13G)
PHL.purpose: For returning former residents and former natural-born Filipino citizens who wish to re-establish permanent residence in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: 13E: Returning Resident for those who previously held Philippine permanent residency. 13G: Returning former natural-born Filipino citizens who have been naturalized abroad. Apply at Bureau of Immigration.

PHL.name: Special Visa for Employment Generation (SVEG)
PHL.purpose: For qualified foreign nationals who will establish and operate a business enterprise in the Philippines that creates employment for at least 10 Filipino workers.
PHL.notes: Requires applicant to employ at least 10 Filipinos in a lawful and sustainable enterprise. Fee: PHP 29,330 per person (principal, spouse, and each dependent child) plus USD 250 ACR I-Card fee. Fees last updated March 2014; verify current rates with BI. Apply at Bureau of Immigration Main Office. Process involves pre-screening, payment, hearing, biometric capture, and visa implementation.

PHL.name: Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals who work remotely via digital technologies exclusively for overseas clients or employers and wish to reside temporarily in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Authorized by Executive Order No. 86, s. 2025 (signed April 24, 2025). Allows stay up to 1 year, renewable for another year. Eligibility: age 18+, works remotely for overseas clients/employers, from countries offering reciprocal digital nomad visas to Filipinos, minimum income USD 24,000/year, valid health insurance, clean criminal record. Foreign-sourced income not subject to Philippine taxation. Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) by Bureau of Immigration were pending as of mid-2025; check immigration.gov.ph for current status.

PHL.name: Special Visa Upon Arrival (SEVUA)
PHL.purpose: For endorsed foreign investors, athletes, conference delegates, World Bank/ADB officials, and other special categories requiring expedited visa processing on arrival.
PHL.notes: Not nationality-based; requires prior endorsement from relevant Philippine government agency (BOI, PRA, PCCI) or event organizer. Single-entry typically grants 30 days. Multiple-entry SEVUA available for multinational executives at Commissioner's discretion. Must be arranged before arrival through the endorsing government agency.

PHL.name: 9(b) Transit Visa
PHL.purpose: For visa-required foreign nationals transiting through the Philippines en route to a third-country destination who will leave the airport during the stopover.
PHL.notes: Issued by Philippine embassies/consulates (DFA Foreign Service Posts) abroad to visa-required nationals transiting the Philippines. Transit limited to 72 hours (3 days), single entry. Not required if the traveler remains airside and does not leave the airport during the layover. Requires a confirmed onward/return ticket. Fee varies by post.

PHL.name: 9(c) Seaman's Visa
PHL.purpose: For foreign crew members who have signed on the articles of a vessel arriving at a Philippine port and seek to enter solely in pursuit of their calling as a seaman.
PHL.notes: Non-immigrant visa for bona fide foreign seafarers/crew joining or leaving a vessel at a Philippine port, intending to depart with the vessel. Issued by DFA Foreign Service Posts abroad. Not for local employment ashore.

PHL.name: 47(a)(2) Special Non-Immigrant Visa
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals employed by or assigned to enterprises registered with government investment agencies (BOI, PEZA, CEZA, SBMA) or to regional/area headquarters, admitted for a temporary period under Section 47(a)(2) of the Philippine Immigration Act.
PHL.notes: Granted under Section 47(a)(2) of Commonwealth Act No. 613 (Philippine Immigration Act of 1940, as amended), with authority delegated to the Department of Justice. Employer/enterprise-sponsored and company-specific; valid for the term of the contract/appointment or one year, whichever is shorter, and renewable. Commonly used by BOI/PEZA/CEZA/SBMA-registered firms and regional headquarters (RHQ/ROHQ) as an alternative to the 9(g) visa.

PHL.name: Special Work Permit (SWP) – Commercial
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals holding a 9(a) visa who will engage in short-term gainful employment or a commercial assignment in the Philippines not exceeding six months.
PHL.notes: Issued by the Bureau of Immigration to 9(a) visa holders for short-term employment/assignments of 3-6 months; renewable once. Fee approximately PHP 6,440 (about USD 115) plus USD 50 for ACR I-Card if applicable. BI fee schedule last updated 2014; verify current rates. A separate Special Work Permit exists for artists and athletes.

PHL.name: Provisional Work Permit (PWP)
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals awaiting approval of a 9(g) pre-arranged employment visa who wish to begin working legally while the application is pending.
PHL.notes: Issued by the Bureau of Immigration during the pendency of a 9(g) pre-arranged employment visa application, allowing lawful work in the interim. Requires a valid Alien Employment Permit (AEP) from DOLE. Fee approximately PHP 4,040 (about USD 72); BI fee schedule last updated 2014, verify current rates.

PHL.name: Special Study Permit (SSP)
PHL.purpose: For foreign nationals who do not qualify for a 9(f) Student Visa (including minors and those taking short courses) but wish to study in the Philippines.
PHL.notes: Issued by the Bureau of Immigration to foreign students ineligible for the 9(f) Student Visa (e.g., minors below 18, and short-course or non-degree students). Fee approximately PHP 5,240 (about USD 94) plus USD 50 for ACR I-Card; BI fee schedule last updated 2014, verify current rates.

PHL.name: Quota Immigrant Visa (13)
PHL.purpose: For qualified foreign nationals of countries that grant reciprocal immigration privileges to Filipinos who wish to become permanent residents of the Philippines under the annual quota.
PHL.notes: Immigrant (permanent resident) visa limited to a maximum of 50 nationals of any one nationality per calendar year, available only to nationals of countries that extend reciprocal immigration privileges to Filipinos. Fee approximately PHP 18,830 (about USD 336) plus USD 50 ACR I-Card; BI fee schedule last updated 2014, verify current rates. Apply at BI Main Office.

PLW.name: Tourist Visa
PLW.purpose: Tourism, leisure, and social visits to Palau. Employment, commercial activity, and studying are strictly prohibited.
PLW.notes: Granted on arrival for eligible nationalities. Extendable for two additional 30-day periods at $50 USD per extension, applied for at the Division of Immigration in Koror. Requires valid passport (6+ months validity), return/onward ticket, proof of sufficient funds, and signing of the Palau Pledge. $100 PPEF environmental fee applies. Pre-clearance required for 12 designated nationalities per EO 499. Bangladesh and Myanmar must obtain advance visa before travel.

PLW.name: Business Visa
PLW.purpose: Business meetings, conferences, and contract negotiations in Palau. Employment and commercial activity are not permitted.
PLW.notes: Granted on arrival for eligible nationalities. Extendable for two additional 30-day periods at $50 USD per extension. Same entry requirements as Tourist Visa. Strictly prohibits employment or paid activity.

PLW.name: Transit Visa
PLW.purpose: Short-duration transit through Palau with confirmed onward travel within 24 hours.
PLW.notes: No fee. Requires confirmed airline ticket for departure within 24 hours. $100 PPEF environmental fee is exempt for transit passengers.

PLW.name: Digital Resident Tourist Visa
PLW.purpose: Allows remote workers and digital nomads to live in Palau for extended periods while working for employers or clients outside Palau.
PLW.notes: Allows two consecutive 90-day extensions per calendar year (total up to 180 days per year). Extension fee is $50 per month. Applied for at the Division of Immigration. Working for Palauan employers or engaging in local commerce is not permitted.

PLW.name: Temporary Visa
PLW.purpose: Humanitarian or discretionary short-term visa issued at the Director of Immigration's discretion for exceptional circumstances.
PLW.notes: No fee. Issued at the discretion of the Director of Bureau of Customs and Border Protection for humanitarian or other exceptional reasons. Maximum stay 30 days.

PLW.name: Crew Member Entry
PLW.purpose: Allows ship or aircraft crew members short-duration shore leave or layover in Palau.
PLW.notes: No fee for stays up to 48 hours. Stays beyond 48 hours require a Tourist or Business Visa at $50 extension fee. $100 PPEF environmental fee is exempt for crew on duty.

PLW.name: Resident Visa
PLW.purpose: Long-term residency visa for foreign nationals seeking extended stay in Palau outside specific investor or employment categories.
PLW.notes: Up to 2-year validity. Fee is $200 USD. Advance application required at the Division of Immigration, MOJ Building, Koror. Processing time 5-10 working days. Does not confer permanent residency or citizenship.

PLW.name: Elite Resident Visa
PLW.purpose: Premium long-term residency visa for high-net-worth individuals who purchase or lease qualifying property in Palau.
PLW.notes: 10-year validity, unlimited multiple entries. Initial fee $20,000 USD (non-refundable); renewal fee $10,000 USD. Requires purchase or lease of dwelling for at least $250,000 USD (cash only) from a Palauan citizen, clan, family, NGO, or corporation. Maximum 1,000 non-citizen holders at any time. Applicant must have major medical health insurance and no felony convictions. Does NOT confer permanent residency or citizenship.

PLW.name: Investor Visa
PLW.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals who have made a qualifying investment in a Palau business, certified by the Foreign Investment Board.
PLW.notes: Up to 5-year validity. Fee is $50 USD. Requires at least 25% equity interest in a Palauan business and certification from the Foreign Investment Board. Advance application required. Minimum investment amount not specified on official page.

PLW.name: Government Employee Visa
PLW.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals employed by the national government, state governments, or public corporations of Palau.
PLW.notes: Up to 5-year validity. Fee exempt for the primary holder. Dependents (spouse and children under 21) eligible for Dependent Visa with no fee. Requires proof of government employment in Palau.

PLW.name: FG/IOR Visa (Foreign Government / International Organization Representative)
PLW.purpose: Visa for representatives of foreign governments or international organizations (such as the UN) conducting official business in Palau.
PLW.notes: Up to 5-year validity. Fee exempt. Issued to accredited foreign government officials and international organization representatives on official duty. Accredited diplomatic mission members may also enter without a visa.

PLW.name: Missionary Visa
PLW.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals affiliated with recognized religious organizations conducting missionary or religious work in Palau.
PLW.notes: Up to 5-year validity. Fee exempt for primary missionary holder; $10 USD fee for dependents. Requires affiliation with a recognized religious organization.

PLW.name: Student Visa
PLW.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals enrolled full-time at an accredited educational institution in Palau.
PLW.notes: Maximum 1-year validity. No fee. Requires full-time enrollment at an accredited school and school-maintained (on-campus) housing. Advance application required at the Division of Immigration.

PLW.name: Dependent Visa
PLW.purpose: Visa for spouses and dependent children of foreign nationals holding a qualifying long-term visa in Palau.
PLW.notes: Up to 5-year validity (expires with or when sponsor's primary visa expires). No fee for dependents of government employees. $10 USD fee for dependents of missionary visa holders. Eligible dependents: spouses and children under 21 years of age.

PLW.name: Work Permit
PLW.purpose: Employment in Palau for foreign nationals working for private-sector employers who hold a valid labor permit issued by the Bureau of Labor & Human Resources.
PLW.notes: Two-step process: the foreign national must first obtain a labor permit from the Bureau of Labor & Human Resources, after which the Division of Immigration issues the corresponding Work Permit visa. Validity matches the term of the underlying labor permit. Immigration does not publish a set visa fee - the official page directs applicants to contact the Bureau of Labor & Human Resources regarding fees. Distinct from the Government Employee Visa (which covers national/state government and public-corporation employment). Foreign nationals may work only in accordance with Palau's labor, foreign investment, tax, and other applicable laws; holders of Tourist, Business, Student, or Temporary visas may not work.

PNG.name: Tourist Visa – Own Itinerary
PNG.purpose: For individuals who wish to sightsee independently, travel, or visit friends in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50. Initial application fee is Nil; extension fee USD 150; late extension USD 700. Apply at www.ica.gov.pg. Requires request letter, passport bio page copy, and travel itinerary with onward/return ticket.

PNG.name: Tourist Visa – Tour Package
PNG.purpose: For group tours, student excursion groups, and other organised tour parties visiting Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50. Sponsor/tour agent must be registered with PNG Tourism Promotion Authority (TPA) and Investment Promotion Authority (IPA). Requires letter of request from registered tour agent, passport bio page, and travel itinerary.

PNG.name: Visiting Relative Visa
PNG.purpose: For individuals visiting husbands, wives, or other family members residing in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50. Extension fee USD 150; late extension USD 700. Requires request letter, passport bio page, onward/return ticket, and financial guarantee.

PNG.name: Easy Visitor Permit (EVP) – 30 Days
PNG.purpose: For eligible nationality holders wishing to visit PNG for holidays, sightseeing, social or recreational activities, or to visit relatives and friends, for up to 30 days.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. Available to passport holders from VOA-eligible countries. Single entry, valid 30 days from date of arrival. Not extendable. eVisa fee USD 50. Also obtainable on arrival at Jacksons International Airport. Check eligibility at www.ica.gov.pg.

PNG.name: Easy Visitor Permit (EVP) – 60 Days
PNG.purpose: For eligible nationality holders wishing to visit PNG for holidays, sightseeing, social or recreational activities, or to visit relatives and friends, for up to 60 days.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. Available to passport holders from VOA-eligible countries. Single entry, valid 60 days from date of arrival. Extension fee USD 150; late extension USD 700. eVisa fee USD 50. Also obtainable on arrival at Jacksons International Airport. Check eligibility at www.ica.gov.pg.

PNG.name: Yachtperson Visa (Owner/Captain/Crew)
PNG.purpose: For the owner and/or captain of a yacht, as well as any accompanying spouse and/or children, arriving by sea.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50. Extension fee USD 150 (owner/captain), USD 200 (crew); late extension USD 700. Requires request letter from owner/captain, passport bio page, and yacht particulars (optional).

PNG.name: Sportsperson Visa
PNG.purpose: For individuals taking part in representative sporting events or codes in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires letter from PNG-based sponsor, passport bio page, onward/return ticket, and prescribed migration fee.

PNG.name: Journalist/Reporter Visa
PNG.purpose: For journalists, reporters, TV presenters, announcers, camerapersons, photographers, and media correspondents visiting Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Visitor Visa class. Extension fee USD 500; late extension USD 1,050. eVisa fee USD 50. Requires prior clearance letter from the Prime Minister's Media Unit before applying. Not available online without pre-clearance. Passport bio page, travel itinerary with onward/return ticket required.

PNG.name: Business Visa – Short-Term Multiple Entry
PNG.purpose: For persons making multiple business visits during a single 12-month period, including for meetings, conferences, exploratory visits, or business negotiations.
PNG.notes: Business Visa class. Open to all nationalities. eVisa fee USD 50. Extension fee USD 500; late extension USD 1,000. Requires letter from PNG-based sponsor, passport bio page, prescribed migration fee, and return/ongoing ticket.

PNG.name: Business Visa – Short-Term Single Entry
PNG.purpose: For persons entering PNG for a single business visit of up to 30 days for meetings, conferences, exploratory visits, or business negotiations.
PNG.notes: Business Visa class. Not extendable. eVisa (eVisa) available for nationals from eligible countries. eVisa fee USD 50. Requires letter from PNG-based sponsor, passport bio page, prescribed migration fee, and return/ongoing ticket. Check eligibility at www.ica.gov.pg.

PNG.name: Restricted Employment Visa (REV)
PNG.purpose: Allows businesses to sponsor foreign workers with recognised qualifications and experience in fields not available locally, primarily in Oil & Gas, Mining, and major corporate or agricultural companies.
PNG.notes: Business Visa class. 30-day single entry per use; not extendable; maximum 4 uses per year. Available online (eVisa) for nationals from eligible countries. eVisa fee USD 50. Requires cover letter from PNG-based sponsor, passport bio page, prescribed migration fee, and proof of return ticket.

PNG.name: Work Visa
PNG.purpose: For foreign nationals employed in the private sector in Papua New Guinea requiring formal work authorisation.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment Visa. Application must be submitted by the employer through the Sponsor Portal at www.ica.gov.pg. Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Requires: employee passport bio page, CV, job description, certified qualifications, signed employment contract, two colour passport photos, right thumb print, professional registration evidence, IPA Certificate of Incorporation, police clearance, medical report including X-ray, and Maintenance Guarantee Bond signed by employer. HIV test required for applicants over 16 years of age for long-term stays.

PNG.name: Working Resident – Consultant/Specialist
PNG.purpose: For consultants and specialists providing services in large corporate, Oil & Gas, and Mining companies for short stays of up to 90 days.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50 (eVisa available). Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Requires letter from PNG-based company/sponsor, passport bio page, prescribed fee, proof of onward/return ticket, Maintenance Guarantee Bond completed by sponsor, and copy of Contract/Service Agreement.

PNG.name: Working Resident – Short-Term Employment
PNG.purpose: For organisations wishing to employ a foreign national for a term of 6 months or less.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment Visa class. Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter signed at managerial level, IPA Company Form 4 and 5, completed and signed application form, Maintenance Guarantee Bond, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Business Person/Investor Visa
PNG.purpose: For business persons or investors who want to do business and invest in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment Visa class. Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, completed application form, Maintenance Guarantee Bond, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Working Dependent Visa
PNG.purpose: Extension visa for dependents previously under Working Resident Dependent status who wish to seek employment in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment Visa class (Change of Status). Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Applicable when: legally dependent spouse with teaching/medical/other essential qualification decides to obtain employment; person has changed marital status while in PNG; person completed employment obligations and seeking new employer; or company name change. Requirements differ by COS category - see www.ica.gov.pg.

PNG.name: Dependent Visa (Working Resident)
PNG.purpose: For non-citizens who are biological family members (including spouses, children, and aged/de facto partners) of a principal Working Resident visa holder.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment Visa class. Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, completed application form, passport bio page, certified principal visa page, birth certificate, and marriage certificate (for spouse). De facto relationships require statutory declarations from both parties.

PNG.name: Entertainer Visa – Film Maker (Commercial)
PNG.purpose: For non-citizens intending to make a commercial film or documentary in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Entertainer Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50 (eVisa available). Extension fee USD 700; late extension USD 1,350. Requires approval from PNG National Film Institute (NFI), clearance letters from PNG Department of Foreign Affairs and the relevant Provincial Administration, and clearance from PNG Prime Minister's Office Media Unit.

PNG.name: Entertainer Visa – Film Maker (Non-Commercial)
PNG.purpose: For individuals who wish to make not-for-profit or public release films in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Entertainer Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50 (eVisa available). Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires clearance from PNG National Film Institute and PNG Prime Minister's Office Media Unit.

PNG.name: Entertainer Visa – Comedian (Commercial)
PNG.purpose: For persons providing entertainment or advertisements as comedians for commercial purposes in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Entertainer Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50 (eVisa available). Extension fee USD 500; late extension USD 1,050. Requires sponsor letter from event organiser, passport bio page, prescribed fee, and return/ongoing ticket.

PNG.name: Entertainer Visa – Musician (Commercial)
PNG.purpose: For individuals who wish to tour Papua New Guinea to perform live music or for recording purposes, commercially.
PNG.notes: Entertainer Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50 (eVisa available). Extension fee USD 500; late extension USD 1,050. Requires sponsor letter from event organiser, passport bio page, prescribed fee, and return/ongoing ticket.

PNG.name: Entertainer Visa – Gospel Group (Charity)
PNG.purpose: For gospel groups doing performances and shows for charity purposes in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Entertainer Visa class. Not available online - manual application required. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires sponsor letter from event organiser, duly completed application form, passport bio page, prescribed fee, and return/ongoing ticket.

PNG.name: Entertainer Visa – Cultural Group (Charity)
PNG.purpose: For cultural groups wishing to travel to Papua New Guinea to do charity work or showcase their country of origin.
PNG.notes: Entertainer Visa class. Not available online - manual application required. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires sponsor letter from sponsoring organisation, duly completed and signed application form, passport bio page, prescribed fee, and return/ongoing ticket.

PNG.name: Student Visa – Formal Education
PNG.purpose: For foreign nationals who wish to study in Papua New Guinea on exchange programmes or by self-invitation at registered educational institutions.
PNG.notes: Student Visa class. Applications are submitted manually (not online). Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, acceptance letter from school Registrar, duly completed and signed application form, passport bio page, and prescribed fee.

PNG.name: Student Visa – Occupational Trainee
PNG.purpose: For students sponsored by institutions to undertake training with government organisations, companies, or under individual training/programme circumstances in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Student Visa class. Applications are submitted manually (not online). Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Visa consideration: non-extendable, valid 6 months to 1 year. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, completed and signed application form, passport bio page, and prescribed fee.

PNG.name: Student Dependent Visa
PNG.purpose: For family members (children, spouse, de facto partner) who wish to accompany the principal student visa applicant during their stay in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Student Visa class. Applications are submitted manually (not online). Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires sponsor letter, completed and signed application form, passport bio page, prescribed fee. If lodged separately from principal applicant, must provide certified copies of principal's passport bio page and valid visa.

PNG.name: Special Exemption Visa – Foreign Officials (Long Term)
PNG.purpose: For foreign government and international organisation employees without diplomatic or official status who are conducting business on behalf of their government or international organisations, on a long-term basis.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Fee: Nil. Extension fee: Nil. Requires sponsor letter from foreign government or international organisation (Diplomatic Note), clearance letter from PNG Department of Foreign Affairs (Diplomatic Note), completed and signed application form, and copy of valid Official Passport bio page.

PNG.name: Special Exemption Visa – Foreign Officials (Short Term)
PNG.purpose: For foreign national employees without diplomatic or official status conducting short-term business on behalf of their government.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Fee: Nil. eVisa fee USD 50. eVisa application available online. Requires sponsoring letter from foreign government/international organisation (Diplomatic Note), clearance letter from PNG Department of Foreign Affairs (Diplomatic Note), and copy of valid Official Passport bio page.

PNG.name: Diplomat Visa
PNG.purpose: For Diplomatic Passport holders of foreign governments who conduct official negotiations and maintain political, economic, and social relations with Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Fee: Nil. Extension: Nil. Requires sponsor letter from Foreign Mission (Diplomatic Note), clearance letter from PNG Department of Foreign Affairs, completed and signed application form, and copy of Diplomatic Passport bio page.

PNG.name: Aid Worker/Volunteer Visa
PNG.purpose: For foreign nationals who work for an international organisation providing humanitarian or development assistance to the citizens of Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. eVisa fee USD 50 (YWAM Aid Worker variant also available online). Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter signed at managerial level, work permit (if applicable), completed application form, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Research Academic Visa
PNG.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking educational, medical, or scientific research in Papua New Guinea, or teaching in a PNG institution.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, approval from PNG National Research Institute, Institute of Medical Research, or educational institution stating purpose and duration, completed application form, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Religious Worker Visa
PNG.purpose: For foreign religious workers who are members of a national religious denomination in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, completed application form, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Emergency Relief Worker Visa
PNG.purpose: For humanitarian aid workers intending to assist in humanitarian crises caused by natural or man-made disasters in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires clearance letter from PNG National Disaster Office, completed application form, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Medical Workers Visa
PNG.purpose: For doctors or trainees entering Papua New Guinea for short-term placements in hospitals, valid for periods up to six months.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires clearance letter from the PNG Medical Board, letter from sponsor, completed application form, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Visa
PNG.purpose: For passport holders of Melanesian Spearhead Group member countries visiting Papua New Guinea for up to 30 days.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Fee: Nil. Extension: Nil. Only applicable to passport holders of MSG member countries (Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu - PNG is a founding member). Valid for stays of 30 days or less. Obtained on arrival. Requires incoming Passenger Arrival Card, valid passport bio page, and travel itinerary with onward/return ticket.

PNG.name: Domestic Worker Visa (Accredited Diplomats)
PNG.purpose: For domestic workers of foreign nationals approved by their government to conduct official negotiations and maintain relations with Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires sponsor letter from Foreign Mission, clearance letter from PNG Department of Foreign Affairs, completed application form, and passport bio page.

PNG.name: Dependent Visa (Diplomat/International Organisation)
PNG.purpose: For spouses and aged parents (non-working) of a Diplomat or non-citizen employee of an international organisation posted in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Fee: Nil. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter, completed application form, and passport bio page. If lodged without principal applicant, must provide certified copies of principal's valid passport page and valid visa.

PNG.name: Dependent of Citizen (Non-Working)
PNG.purpose: For children of Papua New Guinea citizens who are foreign nationals and wish to reside non-working in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Extension fee USD 75; late extension USD 380. Requires undertaking/sponsor letter signed at managerial level, completed application form, passport bio pages for applicant and both parents, prescribed fee, birth certificate of child, marriage certificate for spouse, and statutory declarations for de facto relationships.

PNG.name: Dependent of Citizen (Working)
PNG.purpose: For non-citizen family members (spouse/children) of a Papua New Guinea citizen who wish to take up employment while residing in Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Working Resident Employment class. Listed in the 2025 ICA Immigration & Entry Permit Handbook visa fee schedule as 'Dependent of Citizen (Working)': fee USD 380, extension USD 500, late extension USD 1,050. This is the working counterpart to the 'Dependent of Citizen (Non-Working)' class - it permits an eligible dependent of a PNG citizen to seek employment. Manual (paper) application via www.ica.gov.pg.

PNG.name: Permanent Residence – Long-Term Resident
PNG.purpose: For foreign nationals who have lawfully resided in Papua New Guinea for a minimum of 5 years and meet eligibility criteria including CEOs, investors, skilled professionals, missionaries, or retirees.
PNG.notes: Permanent Residence class. Eligibility: Minimum 5 years lawful residency in PNG; must hold a current PNG entry permit; working knowledge of English or a PNG language. Eligible categories: (1) CEOs of companies with 250+ employees and K10M+ annual turnover operating 5+ years; (2) Majority owners of a registered business with net assets/turnover >K2M or property investment >K10M in PNG for 5+ years; (3) Skilled professionals (medical doctors, specialists, educationists) with tertiary qualifications and 5+ years in PNG; (4) Missionaries/religious workers with 5+ years in PNG and K25,000+/year income or written guarantee; (5) Retirees over age 55 with K50,000+/year income who worked in PNG 5+ years; (6) Legally married spouse of PNG citizen for 5+ years. After 8+ years, can apply for citizenship by naturalization. Dependent PR fee covered by principal.

PNG.name: Transit (No Visa Required – Under 7 Hours)
PNG.purpose: Airside transit through Papua New Guinea for passengers with a total waiting time of less than 7 hours.
PNG.notes: No visa required for transit passengers with less than 7 hours waiting time. Transit for over 7 hours requires a visitor visa. Confirmed in 2025 ICA handbook general information section.

PNG.name: Transit Visitor Visa (Over 7 Hours)
PNG.purpose: For passengers transiting through Papua New Guinea with a waiting time exceeding 7 hours who must leave the international zone.
PNG.notes: ICA handbook recommends applying for a visitor visa online if transit time exceeds 7 hours. Standard Visitor Visa application fees apply (Nil base fee; eVisa USD 50). Apply at www.ica.gov.pg in advance.

PNG.name: Designated Events Visa
PNG.purpose: For foreign nationals attending designated events approved by the Government of Papua New Guinea.
PNG.notes: Special Exemption Visa class. Listed as one of the 21 eVisa classes available online. Specific fee not separately itemised in the 2025 handbook fee schedule under Special Exemption (likely Nil or standard Special Exemption fee applies). For government-approved events only.

POL.name: Schengen Visa (C-Type) – Tourist/Visit
POL.purpose: Short-stay visa for tourism, leisure, and social visits to Poland and the Schengen Area. Permits stays of up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
POL.notes: Standard Schengen C-type visa. Fee is EUR 90 for adults (approx. USD 98), EUR 45 for children 6–12 years, free for under 6. Single or multiple-entry options available. Applications must be submitted in person at a Polish consulate via the e-Konsulat booking system no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before travel. Standard processing 15 calendar days; may extend to 30–45 days in exceptional cases.

POL.name: Schengen Visa (C-Type) – Business
POL.purpose: Short-stay visa for business purposes including commercial meetings, conferences, and negotiations with Polish partners. Permits stays up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
POL.notes: Subcategory of C-type Schengen visa for business purposes. Same fee structure and processing as tourist C-type (EUR 90 adults). Multiple-entry versions commonly issued for frequent business travelers.

POL.name: Schengen Visa (C-Type) – Transit
POL.purpose: Short-stay visa for travelers passing through Polish or Schengen territory en route to a third country. Permits transit through the Schengen Area.
POL.notes: C-type transit subcategory for passage through Schengen territory. Standard Schengen visa fees and processing apply. Not to be confused with the A-type airport transit visa.

POL.name: Airport Transit Visa (A-Type)
POL.purpose: Visa for transit through the international transit area of a Polish (Schengen) airport without entering the Schengen Area. Required for nationals of certain countries even when not leaving the transit zone.
POL.notes: Required only for nationals of (13 nationalities): Afghanistan, Armenia (from 1 August 2022), Bangladesh, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, Sri Lanka. Exemptions exist for diplomatic passport holders, EU family members, holders of valid C/D-type Schengen visas, and holders of valid residence permits or visas from Canada, Japan, San Marino, the US, or EEA countries. Fee USD 106 (US consulate); appeal/reconsideration fee USD 84. Processing 15 calendar days; may extend to 30–60 days. Does not authorise entry into the Schengen Area.

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Study
POL.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreign nationals pursuing full-time education at Polish higher education institutions, including degree programs, PhD studies, exchange programs (Erasmus, NAWA), and language courses.
POL.notes: Subcategories include: Study I year (beginning students), Study II year and above, and Study – Others (PhD, exchange, Erasmus, NAWA). Fee is EUR 100 in most jurisdictions (USD ~109); USD 235 at US consulates; GBP 175 in UK; free for Ukrainian nationals. Valid up to 1 year; holders may also stay in other Schengen states up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Processing 15 calendar days; up to 30 days for complex cases. Applications via e-Konsulat system in person at Polish consulate.

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Work
POL.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreign nationals taking up employment in Poland, requiring a valid work permit or declaration of intent to entrust work from a Polish employer.
POL.notes: Requires prior work permit (Zezwolenie na pracę) or employer declaration (oświadczenie o powierzeniu wykonywania pracy). Fee USD 235 at US consulate; EUR 100 (~USD 109) at most European consulates. Valid for up to 1 year. Processing 15 working days standard; expedited in 3 working days for urgent cases. Does not include EU Blue Card (fast-track highly-qualified worker stream, processed separately via MOS portal).

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Family Member of Polish National
POL.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreign family members of Polish citizens who wish to join or visit their Polish relative in Poland for a period exceeding 90 days.
POL.notes: Fee GBP 175 at UK consulate; varies by consulate elsewhere. Fee may be waived in certain circumstances. Applicants must demonstrate family relationship with a Polish citizen. Valid up to 1 year. For longer stays, a temporary residence permit application may be required in Poland.

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Pole's Card (Karta Polaka)
POL.purpose: Long-stay visa issued to holders of the Pole's Card (Karta Polaka), a document confirming Polish heritage or membership in the Polish nation for persons from former Soviet Union countries.
POL.notes: Available to Karta Polaka holders from countries of the former Soviet Union (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan). Fee may be reduced or waived for Karta Polaka holders. Provides certain privileges including reduced visa fees and right to work without a separate work permit.

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Medical Professional
POL.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreign-qualified doctors, dentists, nurses, obstetricians, and paramedics seeking to practice their profession in Poland following recognition of their qualifications by the Minister of Health.
POL.notes: Requires prior approval from the Minister of Health for recognition of non-EU qualifications. Expedited processing of approximately 4 working days. Eligible professions: doctor, dentist, nurse, obstetrician, paramedic. Applicants from Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, and Armenia may submit applications by post; others must appear in person. Full consular fee schedule applies (same D-type fee structure).

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – NATO/SOFA
POL.purpose: National visa issued to NATO military and civilian personnel and their dependants stationed in or transiting through Poland under the NATO Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA).
POL.notes: Issued to NATO/SOFA personnel and dependants. Fee exemptions may apply under SOFA provisions. Applicants must present NATO orders or equivalent official documentation.

POL.name: Schengen Visa (C-Type) / National Visa (D-Type) – Diplomatic/Service
POL.purpose: Visas issued to holders of diplomatic or service passports for official missions, including diplomatic representatives, consular officers, and accredited international organization staff.
POL.notes: Fee exempt under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. Diplomatic passport holders from most countries are also exempt from standard Schengen visa requirements. Issued via the Protocol Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for accredited diplomats; consulates for service passport holders. Bilateral diplomatic visa waiver agreements may apply.

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Seasonal Work (D/05a)
POL.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreign nationals performing seasonal work in Poland (e.g. agriculture, horticulture, tourism, and gastronomy) on the basis of a seasonal work permit issued by the starosta (district labour office).
POL.notes: Seasonal work is permitted for a maximum of 9 months within a calendar year. Requires a prior seasonal work permit (zezwolenie na pracę sezonową, type S) obtained by the employer from the powiat (district) labour office, or an entry in the register of seasonal-work applications. After entering on a D/05a visa or under the visa-free regime, the foreigner may apply for a temporary residence permit for seasonal work. National visa fee EUR 80 (approx. USD 87); some consulates charge a different local-currency amount. Visa applied for in person at a Polish consulate via e-Konsulat.

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Scientific Research (Researcher, D/13)
POL.purpose: Long-stay national visa for non-EU researchers conducting scientific research or development work at an approved Polish research institution under a hosting agreement, for stays exceeding 3 months.
POL.notes: Annotated 'D/13'. Requires a hosting agreement (umowa o przyjęciu w celu realizacji projektu badawczego) with a research institution on the Ministry of the Interior's approved list, specifying the research project, duration, remuneration, and working conditions. Applicant must hold qualifications giving access to doctoral studies (Polish Master's-equivalent). Holders may perform research work without a separate work permit. Fee EUR 80 (approx. USD 87). A national visa or refusal is issued within 30 days of submission. Valid up to 1 year; also permits travel in other Schengen states up to 90 days within any 180-day period.

POL.name: Working Holiday Visa (National D-Type)
POL.purpose: Long-stay visa for young citizens (aged 18 to under 31) of partner countries to spend up to a year in Poland discovering its culture and language, with the right to take up supplementary employment.
POL.notes: Poland operates working-holiday / youth-mobility agreements with New Zealand, Australia, Taiwan, Japan, Chile, Republic of Korea, Argentina, and Peru; a parallel Youth Mobility Program covers Canada (ages 18–35). Applicants must be at least 18 and not yet 31 at the time of applying (Canada up to 35). Issued as a national D-type visa valid for up to 1 year; no separate work permit is required. The main purpose must be leisure/travel, with employment being supplementary. Administered by the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy; visas issued by Polish consulates. Fee varies by partner country (e.g. Poland–Canada Youth Mobility Program: 202 CAD).

POL.name: National Visa (D-Type) – Other (General/Miscellaneous)
POL.purpose: Catch-all category of the Polish national D-type visa covering purposes not listed separately, such as cultural activities, sports competitions, volunteering, internships, and other justified long-stay purposes.
POL.notes: Used for purposes such as cultural, sports, scientific, religious, and humanitarian activities. Same fee structure and processing times as other D-type categories. Applicants must provide documents proving their specific purpose of stay.

PRK.name: Tourist Visa
PRK.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to North Korea for tourism purposes as part of an organised tour arranged by a state-authorised tour operator. Independent tourist travel is not permitted.
PRK.notes: Must be obtained before arrival from a DPRK diplomatic mission in a third country (commonly Beijing or the relevant country's capital) after prior approval from Pyongyang. Cannot be obtained at the border or on arrival. Journalists may not enter on a tourist visa even for personal travel - they must apply for special permission separately. North Korea's borders have been effectively closed to general foreign entry since early 2020 (COVID-19 restrictions); tourist visa availability as of June 2026 is effectively suspended - only Russian nationals are permitted limited entry.

PRK.name: Business Visa
PRK.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting North Korea for commercial or business-related purposes, including meetings with state-affiliated enterprises.
