PRK.notes: Must be obtained before arrival from a DPRK diplomatic mission abroad after approval from Pyongyang. The process is described by the Canadian government as 'extremely slow and arduous.' Serbian MFA (mfa.gov.rs) notes that ordinary/national Serbian passport holders are visa-exempt for business travel specifically; this is recorded as conditional_access (purpose-based), not unconditional visa_free. All commercial activity must be conducted through state-sanctioned channels.

PRK.name: Work Permit / Work Visa
PRK.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals authorised to undertake employment or long-term professional assignments in North Korea, typically within state-designated special economic zones or diplomatic contexts.
PRK.notes: Requires formal employment authorisation from North Korean authorities in addition to the visa. Must be arranged prior to arrival through the receiving institution in the DPRK. Specific conditions and fees are not published by any accessible official source.

PRK.name: Student Visa
PRK.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals accepted for study at a North Korean educational institution, such as Kim Il-sung University or the Pyongyang University of Science and Technology.
PRK.notes: Requires acceptance by a state-approved institution before a visa application can be submitted. Must be obtained from a DPRK embassy or consulate abroad after Pyongyang approval. Specific duration, fees, and processing times are not published on any accessible official DPRK government source.

PRK.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
PRK.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic or official passports from countries that do not have a bilateral visa-exemption agreement with the DPRK, allowing entry for official government duties.
PRK.notes: Holders of Chinese diplomatic, official, and official-ordinary passports are visa-exempt for up to 30 days with invitation and hosting unit (confirmed via kp.china-embassy.gov.cn, June 2026). Holders of Serbian diplomatic and official passports are visa-exempt for up to 90 days (confirmed via mfa.gov.rs, June 2026). All other diplomatic/official passport holders who do not benefit from a confirmed bilateral exemption require a visa obtained before entry. DPRK does not publish a list of bilateral diplomatic exemptions on any accessible official website.

PRK.name: Transit Visa
PRK.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to transit through North Korean territory (primarily overland via rail or by air through Pyongyang Sunan International Airport) without entering the country proper.
PRK.notes: Serbian MFA notes that holders of emergency travel documents are visa-exempt for transit only if departing the international zone within 24 hours. General transit visa requirements for ordinary passport holders are not detailed on any accessible DPRK official source. The Beijing–Pyongyang passenger train service resumed on 2026-03-12 after a six-year hiatus, initially restricted to diplomats and business visa holders; Air China also resumed weekly Beijing–Pyongyang flights around the same period. Overland transit through the DPRK historically required a transit visa arranged in advance. Transit via Pyongyang Sunan airport is subject to DPRK immigration control.

PRK.name: Special Permission / Journalist Visa
PRK.purpose: Required for professional journalists and media personnel wishing to enter North Korea, including those travelling for personal reasons. Cannot be substituted by a tourist visa.
PRK.notes: Explicitly cited by the Canadian government travel advisory: professional journalists 'must apply for special permission to visit North Korea and may not enter the country on a tourist visa, even if they are travelling for personal reasons.' Requirements, fees, and processing times are not published by any accessible DPRK official source. Access is tightly controlled and rarely granted.

PRT.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourism/Family/Business
PRT.purpose: Allows entry for tourism, family visits, business meetings, and other short-stay purposes in the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
PRT.notes: Standard Schengen short-stay visa fee is EUR 90 for adults; EUR 45 for children aged 6–12; free for children under 6. Reduced fee of EUR 35 applies to nationals of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Belarus, Georgia, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, and Ukraine under EU visa facilitation agreements. Reduced fee of EUR 67.75 applies to Cape Verde nationals. Visa does not guarantee entry - border control may still refuse. ETIAS authorisation expected to replace the visa-free regime for exempt nationals from Q4 2026.

PRT.name: Airport Transit Visa (ATV) - Schengen
PRT.purpose: Permits transit through the international zone of Portuguese airports without entering the Schengen Area, applicable to nationals of countries subject to ATV requirements.
PRT.notes: Required for nationals of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, and Somalia at all Schengen airports. Additionally required at Portuguese airports specifically for nationals of Guinea, Senegal, and Uzbekistan. Exemptions apply to holders of valid Schengen visas/permits, US/Canada/Japan visas or residence permits, and diplomatic passport holders.

PRT.name: Schengen Seasonal Work Visa
PRT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to engage in subordinate seasonal employment in Portugal for a period of up to 90 days.
PRT.notes: This is a Schengen-category visa for short-term seasonal work (90 days or less). For seasonal work exceeding 90 days, a national Temporary Stay Visa for seasonal work is required instead.

PRT.name: National Visa - Subordinate Work (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter and remain in Portugal for subordinate (employed) work for stays of more than 90 days and up to one year.
PRT.notes: Temporary Stay Visa valid for up to 1 year with multiple entries. Standard national visa fee EUR 110. Processing deadline 30 days. A separate Residency Visa for subordinate work (valid 4 months, 2 entries) is available for those seeking to obtain a full residence permit through AIMA.

PRT.name: National Residency Visa - Subordinate Work
PRT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Portugal and apply for a residence permit for subordinate employment through AIMA.
PRT.notes: Residency visa valid 4 months (approximately 120 days) with 2 entries. Holder must apply for a residence permit with AIMA (Agência para a Integração, Migrações e Asilo) within Portugal during validity. Processing deadline 60 days. Fee EUR 110.

PRT.name: National Visa - Independent Work / Self-Employment (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to enter Portugal to carry out independent professional work or self-employed activity for up to one year.
PRT.notes: Covers freelancers and independent contractors. Also available as a Residency Visa (4 months, 2 entries) for applicants intending to obtain a full residence permit.

PRT.name: National Visa - Highly Qualified Activity (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows highly qualified third-country nationals to enter Portugal for scientific research, higher education, or highly qualified professional activity for up to one year.
PRT.notes: Fee waived for highly qualified researchers. Covers university professors, researchers, and senior professionals. Also available as Residency Visa (4 months, 2 entries). Tech Visa program (IAPMEI-certified companies) provides fast-track access to this category.

PRT.name: D8 Digital Nomad / Remote Work Visa (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows remote workers and digital nomads who earn income from sources outside Portugal to reside in Portugal and work remotely for up to one year.
PRT.notes: Established under Article 60(2)(c) of the Foreigners Law. Minimum income approximately EUR 3,480/month (4x national minimum wage as of 2025) for the preceding 3 months. Applies to both salaried employees working remotely and self-employed/freelancers. Also available as Residency Visa D8 (valid 4 months, 2 entries) for those seeking a 2-year residence permit from AIMA. Minimum stay for maintaining D8 residence permit: 183 days/year.

PRT.name: D8 Digital Nomad / Remote Work Residency Visa
PRT.purpose: Allows remote workers to enter Portugal and apply for a 2-year residence permit through AIMA, establishing long-term residency as a digital nomad.
PRT.notes: Residency visa valid 4 months with 2 entries. Holder must apply to AIMA for a 2-year residence permit within Portugal. Renewable; leads to permanent residency after 5 years. Processing deadline 60 days. Fee EUR 110.

PRT.name: National Visa - Study (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to enter Portugal for secondary education, bachelor's, master's, PhD, or post-doctoral study programs for more than 3 months.
PRT.notes: Fee waived for holders of Portuguese government study scholarships. Covers all levels of formal education. Also available as a Residency Visa (4 months, 2 entries) for students intending to apply for a student residence permit through AIMA.

PRT.name: National Visa - Professional Training / Internship / Volunteer Work (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Portugal for professional training programs, formal internships, or volunteer work for more than 3 months.
PRT.notes: Covers structured training programs, accredited internships, and recognised volunteer schemes. Also available as a Residency Visa (4 months, 2 entries).

PRT.name: D7 Passive Income / Retirement Visa (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows retirees and persons living from passive income (pensions, property income, dividends, or financial assets) to reside in Portugal for up to one year.
PRT.notes: Applicant must demonstrate sufficient regular passive income. No statutory minimum income amount is specified on the official page - documentary evidence of income/assets required. Also available as a Residency Visa D7 (4 months, 2 entries) for those intending to obtain a long-term residence permit. Leads to permanent residency after 5 years.

PRT.name: D7 Passive Income / Retirement Residency Visa
PRT.purpose: Allows retirees and passive income holders to enter Portugal and apply for a long-term residence permit through AIMA.
PRT.notes: Residency visa valid 4 months with 2 entries. Holder must apply for a residence permit with AIMA within Portugal. Renewable; leads to permanent residency after 5 years of legal residence. Processing deadline 60 days. Fee EUR 110.

PRT.name: ARI - Autorização de Residência para Investimento (Golden Visa)
PRT.purpose: Grants residency to third-country nationals making qualifying investments in Portugal, including capital transfers, job creation, cultural heritage, or scientific research.
PRT.notes: Regulated under Article 90-A of the Aliens Act (Law 23/2007), as amended by Law 56/2023 ('Mais Habitação', in force from 7 October 2023). Real estate purchase routes were eliminated by Law 56/2023. Current qualifying routes: (1) EUR 500,000 capital transfer into qualifying non-real estate investment funds; (2) EUR 500,000 to establish or reinforce a Portuguese company with job creation; (3) EUR 500,000 for scientific research; (4) EUR 250,000 for artistic production or national cultural heritage; (5) Creation of at least 10 job positions. Minimum physical presence: 7 days in year 1, 14 days per subsequent 2-year renewal. Path to permanent residency and citizenship after 5 years. Applications managed by AIMA.

PRT.name: National Residency Visa - Family Reunification
PRT.purpose: Allows family members of residents legally residing in Portugal to join them and apply for a residence permit through AIMA.
PRT.notes: Fee waived for family reunification descendants of residency permit holders and family members exempt under EU legislation. Residency visa valid 4 months with 2 entries; holder must apply to AIMA for a residence permit within Portugal. Processing deadline 60 days.

PRT.name: National Visa - Medical Treatment (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Portugal for medical treatment and permits accompanying family members of patients undergoing treatment.
PRT.notes: Covers both the patient and accompanying family members. Fee waived for patients and companions under health cooperation agreements. Temporary Stay Visa valid up to 1 year with multiple entries. Processing deadline 30 days.

PRT.name: National Visa - Amateur Sports (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Portugal for amateur sporting activities and competitions for stays of more than 90 days and up to one year.
PRT.notes: Specifically for amateur athletes; professional sporting activities would fall under work visa categories. Temporary Stay Visa valid up to 1 year with multiple entries. Processing deadline 30 days. Fee EUR 110.

PRT.name: National Visa - Religious Purposes (Temporary Stay)
PRT.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to enter Portugal for religious activities or ministry for more than 3 months in exceptional cases.
PRT.notes: Available in exceptional cases only. Temporary Stay Visa valid up to 1 year with multiple entries. Processing deadline 30 days. Fee EUR 110.

PRT.name: Skilled Job Seeker Visa
PRT.purpose: Allows specialised technical professionals to enter Portugal to seek qualified employment, permitting highly qualified work until visa expiration or residence permit issuance.
PRT.notes: Exists in Portuguese legislation under Article 57-A of the Foreigners Law but was not yet operational at consular posts as of the last official page update. Not currently accepting applications - awaiting regulatory implementation. Processing deadline would be 60 days once operational.

PRT.name: Youth Mobility (Work and Holiday) Visa - Temporary Stay
PRT.purpose: Allows young people from partner countries to spend an extended holiday in Portugal of up to 12 months with authorisation to work on a secondary basis.
PRT.notes: Temporary stay visa issued under bilateral Youth Mobility / Work and Holiday Memoranda of Understanding. Eligible nationalities: Argentina, Australia, Canada, Chile, Japan, New Zealand, Peru, Republic of Korea, United States, and Uruguay. Age range varies by country (18-30 Argentina/Chile/Japan/New Zealand; 18-31 Australia/Peru; 18-34 Republic of Korea; 18-35 Canada/Uruguay; 18+ USA). Stay of up to 12 months with no possibility of extension (Uruguay: up to 6 months). Purpose must be primarily holiday; paid work is allowed but the holder may not hold a permanent contract or work more than 3 months for the same employer, and may attend training/study of up to 6 months. Annual quotas apply per country (e.g. Australia 500, Canada 600, USA 400).

PRT.name: EU Blue Card (Cartão Azul UE) - Highly Qualified Employment Residence Permit
PRT.purpose: Residence permit allowing highly qualified third-country nationals with a qualifying job offer and salary to live and work in Portugal, with intra-EU mobility rights.
PRT.notes: Granted under Articles 121-A et seq. of the Foreigners Law (Law 23/2007), transposing EU Directive 2021/1883, and administered by AIMA. Requires a work contract of at least one year offering a gross annual salary of at least 1.5x the national average (approximately EUR 35,000+ as of 2026) plus higher-education qualifications or equivalent professional experience. Initially valid for 2 years and renewable for 3-year periods; no labour-market test is applied. During the first 12 months of residence the holder is restricted to the employer/activity that justified the card, after which they may change employer freely. Maximum processing time 60 days. Entry to Portugal is obtained via the National Visa for Highly Qualified Activity; this permit is distinct from the Article 90 national highly-qualified residence permit.

PRT.name: Diplomatic / Service / Official Visa
PRT.purpose: Issued to diplomatic personnel, official government representatives, and their dependants travelling to Portugal on official duty.
PRT.notes: Holders of diplomatic passports are exempt from airport transit visa requirements under Article 3(5)(e) of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009. Bilateral diplomatic and service passport waiver agreements exist with numerous countries (Turkey confirmed: service and special passports exempt from Schengen short-stay requirement under agreement signed 14 July 2010). Diplomatic visas are issued outside standard procedures and fees are typically waived.

PRY.name: Visa de No Residente – Turista
PRY.purpose: For foreign nationals whose nationality requires a visa to enter Paraguay for tourism purposes. Allows stays of up to 90 days.
PRY.notes: Application submitted via MRE online pre-application portal (mre.gov.py/visasenlinea), then completed in person at a Paraguayan embassy or consulate. Processing recommended at least 30 days before travel. Applicant must be a resident or legal visitor in the country of the consulate applied to. Not a fully electronic e-visa.

PRY.name: Visa de No Residente – Técnico
PRY.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Paraguay for technical, business, or professional activities requiring a visa.
PRY.notes: Listed alongside the tourist category as 'Turista o Técnico' (Tourist or Technical) in the MRE online visa portal. Same application process via the online portal followed by consular appearance.

PRY.name: Residencia Temporaria (Temporary Residency)
PRY.purpose: For foreign nationals who intend to reside and work in Paraguay temporarily, under an employment contract or similar arrangement.
PRY.notes: Governed by Migration Law N°6984/2022. Valid for up to 2 years (730 days), renewable for equal periods, and is a prerequisite for later permanent residency. Requires employment promise with salary details, employer credentials, and technical/educational certification (or other proof of lawful activity/solvency). Processed through the immigration authority (migraciones.gov.py); the MRE consular residency page (www2.mre.gov.py/index.php/tramites/residencia-en-paraguay) describes the same category.

PRY.name: Residencia Permanente – Solvencia Económica
PRY.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign nationals who can demonstrate economic solvency, suitable for retirees or those with passive income.
PRY.notes: Requires minimum USD 5,000 in a Paraguayan bank or cooperative account as proof of economic solvency. Alternatively accepted: university degree with employment contract, property ownership (minimum 10 hectares), or company incorporation with USD 5,000 capital. Permanent residency granted directly; no separate rentista/retiree category is defined - economic solvency serves this function. Path to citizenship after 3 years of permanent residency.

PRY.name: Paraguay Investor Pass
PRY.purpose: Permanent residency for foreign investors who make qualifying investments in Paraguay across multiple sectors.
PRY.notes: Launched April 17, 2026 via MIC Resolution No. 0283/2026. Four investment modalities: (1) Productive investments from USD 70,000 with at least 5 formal jobs created; (2) Financial instruments (stock market) from USD 200,000; (3) Real estate from USD 200,000 for economic activity; (4) Tourism sector from USD 150,000. Grants permanent residency directly without prior temporary residency. Process is mostly electronic; physical presence required only for national ID card issuance. Dividend tax rate reduced to 8% for residents. Path to citizenship via naturalization after 3 years.

PRY.name: Residencia Permanente para Inversionistas – SUACE
PRY.purpose: Special permanent residency for foreign investors using Paraguay's Unified System for Business Opening and Closure (SUACE).
PRY.notes: Available under Migration Law No. 6984/2022. Grants direct permanent residency without requiring prior temporary residency. Minimum investment amount not published in official sources. Processed through the SUACE business registration platform.

PRY.name: Residencia por Vínculo Familiar
PRY.purpose: Residency for spouses, children, or dependents of Paraguayan nationals or foreign residents.
PRY.notes: Available for spouses of Paraguayan nationals, children of Paraguayan nationals, and minors (with parental authorization). Specific documentary requirements apply per relationship type. Processed through Paraguayan consulates or migraciones.gov.py.

PRY.name: Residencia Precaria
PRY.purpose: A temporary provisional residency status for foreign nationals while their main residency application is being processed.
PRY.notes: Renewable 6-month periods. Requires origin documents and criminal background clearance. Acts as an interim status while permanent or temporary residency is adjudicated.

PRY.name: Prórroga de Turista (Tourist Extension)
PRY.purpose: Extension of tourist status for visitors who have already entered Paraguay and need additional time beyond their initial authorized stay.
PRY.notes: Available through the Department of Investigations' Foreign Registry Office. Duration of extension and fees not specified in available official sources.

PRY.name: Visa Diplomática / Oficial
PRY.purpose: For holders of diplomatic and official passports traveling to Paraguay on official government business.
PRY.notes: Listed as a distinct category in the MRE online visa portal ('Diplomática, Oficial'). Many nationalities that require a visa for ordinary passport holders have visa-free access for diplomatic/official/service passports under bilateral agreements (e.g., Cuba, Saudi Arabia, Azerbaijan, India, Indonesia, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Lebanon, Qatar, Vietnam, Egypt, Morocco, Serbia).

PRY.name: Visa de Llegada Excepcional (Arrival Visa)
PRY.purpose: An exceptional visa-on-arrival issued at Silvio Pettirossi International Airport in Asunción for specific nationalities under special circumstances.
PRY.notes: Listed as 'excepcional' (exceptional) in the MRE online visa portal under arrival visas. Available exclusively at Asunción's Silvio Pettirossi International Airport. Only applicable to certain nationalities; the January 2026 official migraciones.gov.py document does not confirm specific countries for visa-on-arrival - previously cited countries (Qatar, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia) are not confirmed by the 2026 official PDF. MRE consulate sub-pages list Qatar and Oman as VOA - this discrepancy is tracked in data_quality.gaps.

PRY.name: Residencia Temporal – Estudiante
PRY.purpose: Temporary-residence pathway for foreign nationals who come to Paraguay to study (university or other regular studies).
PRY.notes: Paraguay has no separate stand-alone 'student visa'; students regularise their stay through Temporary Residency under Migration Law N°6984/2022, valid up to 2 years and renewable. Students demonstrate their basis by presenting a study certificate stating they are a regular student, issued by the faculty, plus proof of payment of tuition/monthly fees (per official migraciones.gov.py requirements). Documents in foreign languages must be translated to Spanish by a certified public translator.

PRY.name: Residencia Temporaria MERCOSUR
PRY.purpose: Temporary residency for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associate states wishing to settle in Paraguay to carry out lawful activities.
PRY.notes: Under the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement (implemented via Migration Law N°6984/2022), citizens of Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Peru, Colombia and Ecuador may obtain temporary residency valid for 2 years (not renewable), which can then be converted to MERCOSUR permanent residency. Nationality-based category requiring proof of nationality, criminal-record clearances and the standard documentary set; no employment contract required.

PRY.name: Residencia Permanente MERCOSUR
PRY.purpose: Permanent residency for nationals of MERCOSUR member and associate states who wish to establish themselves permanently in Paraguay.
PRY.notes: Authorization granted to citizens of countries subscribed to the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement (Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Bolivia, Chile, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador) who wish to reside permanently in Paraguay to carry out lawful activities. The applicant submits the permanent-residency application starting 90 days before the expiration of their MERCOSUR Temporary Admission card. Governed by Migration Law N°6984/2022; path to naturalization after 3 years of permanent residency.

QAT.name: Hayya Tourist E-Visa (A1)
QAT.purpose: Short-term tourism and leisure visits to Qatar applied for online via the Hayya platform before travel.
QAT.notes: Fee is QAR 100 (approx. USD 27). Extendable by an additional 30 days from inside Qatar. Passport must be valid for at least 3 months from arrival. Return/onward ticket required. Mandatory health insurance from MOH-registered providers required. Available via Hayya portal or mobile app.

QAT.name: Visa on Arrival
QAT.purpose: Entry permit issued at Qatar's ports of entry for eligible nationalities for tourism, transit, or short visits without prior application.
QAT.notes: Paid visa on arrival (QAR 100 / approx. USD 27) available to nationals of Belarus, Iran, Macau, Mauritius, Montenegro, and Taiwan. Stay 30 days extendable by another 30 days. Iran requires hotel reservation or invitation letter. Belarus requires credit/debit card with USD 1,000+ balance. Separately, over 100 nationalities receive a FREE on-arrival entry permit (no QAR 100 fee) - see visa_policy.visa_free entries.

QAT.name: Joint Tourist Visa - Qatar & Oman
QAT.purpose: Combined tourist visa allowing holders to visit both Qatar and Oman on a single visa, issued through consular channels.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27) per MOFA fee schedule. Applied for through Qatari embassies/consulates or Omani equivalents. Exact stay duration and validity not published on official source consulted.

QAT.name: Businessmen Visa
QAT.purpose: Visa for foreign nationals travelling to Qatar for business meetings, conferences, or commercial activities.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 200 (approx. USD 55) per MOFA official fee schedule - the highest published fee among visitor visa categories. Applied for through Qatari embassies/consulates or via the Hayya e-platform. Exact stay duration and validity not published on official source consulted.

QAT.name: Visit Visa
QAT.purpose: General-purpose short-stay visitor visa for foreign nationals visiting Qatar for personal, family, or social reasons.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27) per MOFA official fee schedule. Can be applied for through Qatari embassies/consulates or the MOI e-services portal. Extendable inside Qatar. The Consular Affairs Department handles cases not eligible for electronic visa system.

QAT.name: GCC Residents Visit Visa (Hayya A2)
QAT.purpose: Entry visa for foreign nationals holding a valid GCC country (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia, or UAE) residence permit who wish to visit Qatar.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27). GCC resident permit must be valid for at least 3 months from date of arrival. Passport must also be valid for at least 3 months from arrival. Applicant must be travelling from their country of GCC residency. Job title on application must match permit. Extendable. Also available on arrival at ports of entry. Hayya A2 category.

QAT.name: Companion of GCC National Visa (Hayya A4)
QAT.purpose: Entry visa for individuals accompanying GCC citizens travelling to Qatar.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27) per MOFA fee schedule. Issued to companions (family members or associates) of GCC national travellers. Also described as 'Entry visa for companions of GCC Nationals' in MOFA fee table. Hayya A4 category.

QAT.name: Transit Visa
QAT.purpose: Short-stay transit visa for passengers transiting through Qatar's Hamad International Airport without leaving the transit zone or during a stopover.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27) per MOFA official fee schedule. Applied for through Qatari embassies/consulates. Qatar Airways passengers may be eligible for complimentary Doha stopover packages. Exact stay duration not published on MOFA page consulted - 4 days is commonly referenced for Qatar transit but not confirmed on official source fetched.

QAT.name: Electronic Travel Authorization / ETA-Backed E-Visa (Hayya A3)
QAT.purpose: Online e-visa for nationals of countries not otherwise eligible for visa-free entry, if they hold a valid visa or residency permit from the US, UK, Canada, Schengen area, Australia, or New Zealand.
QAT.notes: Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27). Credential (third-country visa or residency) must be valid at time of Hayya e-visa issuance, not merely at travel date. Qualifying credentials: valid US, UK, Canadian, Schengen, Australian, or New Zealand visa or permanent residency. Passport valid 3+ months from arrival required. Return ticket required. Hayya A3 category.

QAT.name: Official / Diplomatic Visa
QAT.purpose: Visa issued to foreign officials, diplomats, and government representatives travelling to Qatar on official business.
QAT.notes: Fee exempted per MOFA official fee schedule. Issued through diplomatic channels to holders of diplomatic, official, or special passports. Many nationalities have bilateral agreements with Qatar exempting diplomatic/official/special passport holders entirely (e.g., Thailand per March 2025 agreement).

QAT.name: Work Visa / Employment Entry Permit
QAT.purpose: Entry permit for foreign nationals sponsored by a Qatari employer, allowing the holder to enter Qatar to take up employment.
QAT.notes: Qatar operates a kafala-derived sponsorship system. A Qatari employer (sponsor) must apply on the worker's behalf through the MOI e-services portal. Fee and processing time not published on accessible official pages. Upon arrival, worker obtains a Qatar ID (QID). Work visa tracking available at portal.moi.gov.qa visa inquiry service. Fees and processing times not confirmed from official pages fetched.

QAT.name: Family Visa / Family Reunification (Host Family & Friends)
QAT.purpose: Visa enabling Qatar residents to sponsor visits by family members or friends to Qatar for short stays.
QAT.notes: Hayya platform offers a 'Host Family & Friends' feature allowing Qatar residents to sponsor short-stay visit visas for their family and friends. Fee QAR 100 (approx. USD 27). Duration and validity follow standard visit visa conditions (30 days, extendable). Full details require login to Hayya portal.

QAT.name: Student Residence Visa (Educational Residence Visa)
QAT.purpose: Residence visa for international students admitted to an accredited Qatari university or educational institution, allowing them to live in Qatar for the duration of their studies.
QAT.notes: Sponsored by the accredited educational institution, not an employer. Typically issued for one academic year and renewable annually for the duration of the study program. Requires an official admission/enrolment letter, valid passport, medical examination by the Medical Commission, and issuance of a Qatar ID (QID). Applied for online via the Hukoomi e-government portal / MOI e-services. Exact fee not published on the official service page consulted.

QAT.name: Family Residence Permit (Family Residence Visa)
QAT.purpose: Long-term residence visa allowing an expatriate resident of Qatar to sponsor immediate family members (spouse, sons, unmarried daughters) to reside in Qatar with them.
QAT.notes: Distinct from the short 'Host Family & Friends' visit visa: this is a long-term residence permit for dependents. Sponsor must hold a valid Qatar Residence Permit in a technical/specialized (non-labour) profession and meet a minimum salary (approx. QAR 10,000, or QAR 6,000-7,000 with employer housing). Each family member receives an individual Family Residence Visa stamped in their passport, typically issued for 1-5 years and renewable while tied to the sponsor's residence permit. Dependents must complete a Medical Commission examination within 30 days of arrival and obtain a QID. Applied for via MOI e-services, the Metrash app, or Hukoomi. Reported fee components (~QAR 200 family visa + QAR 500 residence permit + QAR 100 medical per dependent) not confirmed from the official page consulted.

QAT.name: Real Estate Owner Residence Permit
QAT.purpose: Residence permit granted to foreign nationals who own qualifying real estate in Qatar, without the need for an employer sponsor.
QAT.notes: Administered by Qatar's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Aqarat) with the Ministry of Interior. Two tiers per the official Aqarat page: (1) property valued at not less than QAR 730,000 (approx. USD 200,000) grants a renewable residence permit (holder plus family), with roughly 90 days per year of presence in Qatar expected; (2) property valued at not less than QAR 3,650,000 (approx. USD 1,000,000) grants permanent-residency-class benefits including health, education, and investment privileges. No employer sponsor required. Applications submitted online via MOI / Hukoomi (Hukoomi 'apply for investor residence visa' service) subject to background and medical checks and valid health insurance. This is the closest program Qatar offers to a real-estate golden visa; Qatar has no citizenship-by-investment program.

QAT.name: Permanent Residency Card (Law No. 10 of 2018)
QAT.purpose: Indefinite permanent residence granted by a dedicated Ministry of Interior committee to eligible non-Qataris, giving near-citizen access to health, education, and investment/ownership rights.
QAT.notes: Established under Law No. 10 of 2018; issued by the MOI 'Permanent Residence Card Granting Committee'. Eligible categories include children of Qatari women, persons who have rendered valuable services to Qatar or hold special competencies/talent, and long-term residents (reportedly 20 years' residence for those born abroad, 10 years for those born in Qatar) with a stable income. Grants indefinite residence with benefits in health, education, and property ownership/investment. Annual approvals are capped. Applied for online via MOI e-services using a smart card / Qatar ID; a committee reviews each case. Reported application fee (~QAR 3,000) and eligibility salary thresholds not published on the official committee page consulted.

ROU.name: Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Tourism/Visit/Business
ROU.purpose: Allows foreign nationals requiring a visa to enter Romania for short-term purposes including tourism, visiting family or friends, and business meetings. Romania is a full Schengen member since 1 January 2025.
ROU.notes: Maximum 90 days within any 180-day period (Schengen rule). Both single and multiple entry options available. IGI approves invitations within 45 days (extendable 15 days); organized tourist groups (20+ people) processed within 30 days. Financial requirement: €50/day but not less than €500 total. Extension fee €30 (personal reasons) or free (humanitarian/force majeure). Visa application via eVisa portal at evisa.mae.ro; in-person finalisation at Romanian diplomatic mission required. Holders of valid Schengen visas/permits may enter without a separate Romanian visa.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Commercial Activities (Category D/CA)
ROU.purpose: Enables non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to establish and operate a business in Romania, including founding or acquiring a company and conducting commercial activities.
ROU.notes: Visa fee is €300 (approximately USD 330), paid in the country where application is made. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Requires approval from Ministry of Energy/SMEs, technical business plan opinion from Romanian Agency for Investments, travel medical insurance (min €30,000 coverage), criminal record certificate, accommodation proof. Subsequent residence permit: annual renewal; 3-year permit available for investments ≥€500,000 or ≥50 full-time jobs created. Financial minimums: €500/month (associates), €700/month (shareholders), waivable with ≥€200,000 investment or ≥50 jobs.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Employment (Category D/AM)
ROU.purpose: Grants non-EU/EEA foreign workers the right to work in Romania, required before taking up employment with a Romanian employer.
ROU.notes: Two subtypes: D/AM1 (applied for by employers through WorkinRomania.gov.ro) and D/AM2 (applied for by foreign employment agencies or authorized employers). Eligible categories include highly qualified workers, central government appointees on infrastructure projects, academic/research personnel at state universities, professional athletes, and citizens of Moldova, Ukraine, and Serbia with full-time contracts. Requires individual employment contract registered in REGES-ONLINE, travel medical insurance (min €30,000), criminal record certificate, and proof of subsistence funds (minimum gross salary for 90 days). Visa fee €120 (approximately USD 130), per the official IGI long-stay employment visa page. Followed by Single Permit or EU Blue Card for long-term stay.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Studies (Category D/SD)
ROU.purpose: Enables non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to pursue full-time education in Romania at accredited institutions, including undergraduate, master's, and doctoral programs.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €300 (scholarship recipients exempt from consular fees). Visa granted for 90 days with one or more entries. National Visa Center approves within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Requires proof of institutional acceptance, tuition payment for at least one year, financial means equal to minimum monthly salary, medical insurance (min €30,000 coverage), and criminal record certificate. Minors require parental consent. Residence permit can be extended for the total study duration, with additional extensions up to one year for incomplete studies. Exchange program participants must be 13-19 years old. Ethnic Romanians and scholarship holders exempt from financial means requirement.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Scientific Research (Category D/CS)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to conduct research activities in Romania through an approved research institution under a hosting agreement.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €300. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Residence permit can be extended for periods specified in hosting agreements, up to maximum 5 consecutive years. Requires hosting agreement approved by the National Authority for Scientific Research, criminal record certificate, travel medical insurance (min €30,000), proof of financial means (minimum gross salary for 6+ months), social health insurance, medical certificate, and proof of legal housing. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Applicants must submit residence permit request at least 30 days before visa expiration.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Family Reunification - Sponsors with Long-Stay Permits (Category D/VF)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA family members of foreign nationals legally residing in Romania on long-stay permits to join their family member sponsor in Romania.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €300. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Requires communication to the General Inspectorate for Immigration, travel medical insurance (min €30,000 coverage, valid across EU Member States), and criminal record certificate from country of domicile/residence.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Family Reunification - Romanian Citizens (Category D/VF)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA family members of Romanian citizens to join their Romanian citizen sponsor for purposes of family reunification.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €300. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Requires marriage certificate issued/transcribed by Romanian authorities, or kinship/partnership evidence.

ROU.name: Entry Visa for Non-EU/EEA Family Members of EU/EEA Citizens (Free Movement)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals who are family members of EU/EEA/Swiss citizens exercising free movement rights in Romania to accompany or join their EU family member.
ROU.notes: Issued free of charge under EU free movement law (Directive 2004/38/EC). Issued as soon as possible and under an accelerated procedure (approximately 48 hours per National Visa Centre). Non-EU family members may be exempt from visa requirements if they hold valid residence documentation from another EU Member State showing family member status. Requires valid passport, application form, and documentation proving family relationship.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Company Administrator (Category D)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to legally reside in Romania for the purpose of managing a Romanian company as an administrator.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Residence permit extended annually; 3-year permit available for investments ≥€500,000 or ≥50 full-time jobs. Part of the RBI pathway for long-term residence.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Branch or Subsidiary Manager (Category D)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to reside in Romania to manage operations of a foreign company's branch or subsidiary registered in Romania.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days).

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Unpaid Training (Category D)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to undertake professional qualification or vocational training programs with accredited providers in Romania without remuneration.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Maximum validity 1 year, non-extendable. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). No remuneration permitted.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Volunteering (Category D)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to carry out voluntary work with non-profit organizations operating in Romania.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Duration corresponds to the voluntary contract, maximum 1 year total. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Activity must be with a non-profit organization.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Au-Pair (Category D)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to reside with a Romanian host family and perform household assistance and childcare activities as an au pair.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Maximum 1 year. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Requires au pair placement agreement with host family.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Medical Treatment (Category D)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA foreign nationals to enter and reside in Romania for the purpose of receiving long-term medical treatment in public or private medical institutions.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Visa valid for 90 days with one or more entries. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Intended for ongoing/long-term medical care; short medical visits may fall under the short-stay (Type C) visa.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa - Other Lawful Activities (Category D)
ROU.purpose: A catch-all long-stay visa category for non-EU/EEA foreign nationals wishing to reside in Romania for purposes not covered by other specific visa categories, provided the activity does not contravene Romanian law.
ROU.notes: Fee €300. Validity up to 1 year, renewable. Processing within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Activity must not contravene Romanian law. Requires travel medical insurance (min €30,000 coverage) and proof of accommodation.

ROU.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
ROU.purpose: Allows nationals of certain third countries to pass through the international transit zone of a Romanian (Schengen) airport during a stopover or connection between two international flights, without entering Romanian/Schengen territory.
ROU.notes: Required only for nationals of a specific list of third countries when transiting airside; it does NOT authorise entry into Romania or the Schengen area. Issued for a single or two transits; multiple-entry airport transit visas may be granted for a maximum validity of six months. Holders of valid Schengen/EU visas or residence permits are generally exempt. Romania became a full Schengen member on 1 January 2025 and issues the uniform (Type A) airport transit visa. Romania no longer issues the former Type B transit visa (discontinued on full Schengen implementation). Applications via the eVisa portal (eviza.mae.ro) with in-person finalisation at a Romanian diplomatic mission.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Posting/Secondment - Detached Workers (Category D/DT)
ROU.purpose: Enables non-EU/EEA workers who are posted (seconded) to Romania by a foreign service provider or employer to carry out work on a temporary basis under a posting arrangement.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €120 (approximately USD 130) per the official IGI page. Visa granted for 90 days with one or more entries. Requires a copy of the posting/secondment permit issued under Romanian labour legislation, proof of financial means at the minimum guaranteed gross salary for the whole period, criminal record certificate, and valid travel medical insurance. Certain workers (e.g. EU/EEA employees posted by their employer, or those on temporary educational, scientific or diplomatic assignments under bilateral agreements) may be posted without a prior posting permit. Followed by a residence permit for the posting duration.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Professional Activities (Category D/AP)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to enter Romania to independently practise a regulated profession for which they are qualified and authorised under Romanian special laws.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €300 (approximately USD 330). Visa granted for 90 days with one or more entries. Applicant must prove their profession is recognised under Romanian special laws, that they practised a similar profession in their country of origin, and hold travel medical insurance (min €30,000) plus a criminal record certificate. IGI issues its favourable opinion within 30 days (extendable 15 days). A residence permit must be requested at the county immigration office at least 30 days before the visa expires.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Religious Activities (Category D/AR)
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to carry out religious activities in Romania as representatives of legally recognised religious denominations or organisations.
ROU.notes: Visa fee €300 (approximately USD 330). Visa granted for 90 days with one or more entries. Requires prior approval from the State Secretariat for Religious Affairs (Cults), proof of accommodation, financial means (three national average salaries), travel medical insurance (min €30,000) and a criminal record certificate. IGI issues its favourable opinion within 30 days (extendable 15 days). Residence permit extended for the period matching the State Secretariat for Cults approval.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Digital Nomads
ROU.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals who work remotely via information and communication technology for a company registered outside Romania (as an employee, or as owner/manager of a foreign company) to live in Romania while continuing that remote work.
ROU.notes: Introduced by Law 22/2022 (amending GEO 194/2002); administratively issued under the D/AS 'other purposes' long-stay category (also referred to as the D/NV nomad visa). Visa fee €120 (approximately USD 130). Applicant must earn at least three times the Romanian average gross monthly salary (approximately RON 26,700/month in 2025) for each of the last 6 months, prove remote work for (or ownership/management of) a company registered abroad — company managers need at least 3 years of activity — and hold travel medical insurance. Visa granted for 90 days; a digital-nomad residence permit is then issued for up to 12 months, renewable for a further 12 months (up to 24 months total). Foreign-sourced income may be exempt from Romanian income tax if the holder stays under 183 days in a 12-month period.

ROU.name: Long-Stay Visa for Holiday and Work (Category D/VM)
ROU.purpose: Allows young nationals of countries that have a bilateral working-holiday agreement with Romania to spend an extended holiday in Romania while taking up incidental employment to help fund their stay.
ROU.notes: Granted only under the conditions of the bilateral holiday-and-work treaties Romania has concluded with third countries. Romania operates a working-holiday programme with the Republic of Korea: South Korean nationals aged 18-30 may obtain a one-year Romanian working-holiday visa. Fee is the standard long-stay consular fee (paid in the state where the application is made). Visa granted for 90 days; residence permit issued for up to one year. Eligibility, quotas and age limits depend on the specific bilateral agreement.

RUS.name: Unified Electronic Visa (Tourist/Private/Business)
RUS.purpose: Permits entry for tourism, private visits, business meetings, and participation in scientific, cultural, socio-political, economic, or sporting events. Does not permit employment, study, or permanent residency.
RUS.notes: Available to citizens of 76 countries approved by the Russian Government. Valid 120 days from date of issue; stay must not exceed 30 days from entry. Children under 6 are exempt from the consular fee. Must enter via designated border crossing points. Application window: no earlier than 86 days and no later than 4 days before intended entry. Medical insurance valid in Russia is required for the entire stay. Extensions permitted only for emergency medical treatment, force majeure, or natural disasters.

RUS.name: Business Visa (Standard Consular)
RUS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Russia for business meetings, negotiations, conferences, exhibitions, and commercial activities. Requires an official invitation from a Russian legal entity or registered through the Chamber of Commerce.
RUS.notes: Applied for at a Russian embassy or consulate abroad. Invitation (vyzov) required from a Russian host organization registered with the Ministry of Internal Affairs or through the Chamber of Commerce and Industry. Single-entry and multiple-entry variants available; validity and entries depend on bilateral agreement and host organization's application. Fee varies by nationality and processing speed. Business visa does not permit employment - a work permit and work visa are required for that.

RUS.name: Work Visa
RUS.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to undertake paid employment in Russia under a labour contract. Must be sponsored by a Russian employer who has obtained a work permit (razresheniye na rabotu) on behalf of the foreign national.
RUS.notes: Employer must first obtain a quota slot (or use quota-exempt Highly Qualified Specialist pathway, HQS, with minimum quarterly salary of RUB 750,000 effective March 1, 2024). Initial work visa valid up to 1 year; extendable in-country. HQS pathway allows work permits valid up to 3 years. EAEU citizens (Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan) do not need a work visa or permit. Citizens of CIS countries with visa-free regimes may also work under simplified rules.

RUS.name: Student Visa
RUS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals accepted for full-time study at an accredited Russian educational institution (university, college, or language school). Requires an official invitation from the institution.
RUS.notes: Requires an official invitation (vyzov) issued by the educational institution through the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Issued at Russian embassies/consulates abroad. Must be renewed annually in-country via the university's foreign student office. Student visa does not automatically confer work rights; separate permission required to work part-time.

RUS.name: Transit Visa
RUS.purpose: Permits passage through Russian territory en route to a third country. Required for most non-visa-free nationals transiting through Russian airports or overland.
RUS.notes: Transit visa typically allows up to 72 hours (3 days) in transit. Airside transit (remaining in the international zone of an airport) may not require a visa for some nationalities, depending on passport. Overland transit always requires a transit visa or valid Russian visa. Issued at Russian consulates with confirmed onward documentation.

RUS.name: Humanitarian/Medical Visa
RUS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Russia for medical treatment at a licensed Russian medical facility. Requires an invitation from the treating medical institution.
RUS.notes: Falls under the humanitarian visa category in Russian immigration law. Requires a formal invitation from the Russian medical institution and documentation confirming planned treatment. Accompanying family members may apply for a separate private/guest visa. Extensions possible in-country if treatment is ongoing.

RUS.name: Private/Guest Visa (Family Reunion)
RUS.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to visit immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, siblings) who are Russian citizens or registered foreign residents in Russia.
RUS.notes: The Russian host (citizen or permanent resident) submits an invitation through the local MVD office (GUVM). Alternatively, a notarised private invitation is accepted. The consulate may request proof of family relationship. Spouses of Russian citizens may subsequently apply for a temporary residence permit and follow the path to permanent residency.

RUS.name: Diplomatic/Official Visa
RUS.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic, service, official, or special passports travelling to Russia on official government business or assigned to diplomatic missions.
RUS.notes: Holders of diplomatic, official, service, and/or special passports of 100+ countries may enter Russia without a visa under bilateral agreements (typically 90 days per 180-day period). For countries without such agreements, diplomatic/official visas are issued gratis. Exemptions for EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland diplomatic passport holders have been suspended. Exact terms governed by individual bilateral treaties listed on the Russian MFA portal.

RUS.name: Golden Visa (Investor Permanent Residence Permit)
RUS.purpose: Grants direct permanent residence to foreign investors who meet prescribed investment thresholds in Russia, without requiring a prior temporary residence permit stage.
RUS.notes: Established by Government Decree No. 2573 (Dec 31, 2022), effective Jan 11, 2023. Investment options include: (1) RUB 15 million in socially significant regional projects within 3 years; (2) RUB 30 million in a Russian company with RUB 6 million/year in taxes; (3) Russian commercial entity with RUB 4 million/year taxes, operating 2+ years; (4) Real estate with cadastral value RUB 50 million (Moscow), RUB 20 million (Far East), RUB 25 million (elsewhere). Annual quota: 3,802 permits for 2026. Path to citizenship after 5 years of permanent residence. Requirement to stay 6 months/year was removed in late 2025/early 2026.

RUS.name: Shared Values Temporary Residence Permit
RUS.purpose: Grants temporary residence to foreign nationals from designated countries who demonstrate alignment with traditional Russian values, without requiring a standard quota slot.
RUS.notes: Established by Presidential Decree No. 702 (Aug 19, 2024). Available to citizens of 47 countries (including US, UK, Canada, most EU states; list approved Sep 17, 2024). No Russian language test or history exam required. Quota-exempt. Leads to standard permanent residency and citizenship pathway after meeting residency requirements.

RUS.name: Highly Qualified Specialist (HQS) Work Permit + Visa
RUS.purpose: Fast-track work authorisation for highly skilled foreign specialists sponsored by a Russian employer, offering expedited processing and longer validity than the standard work permit.
RUS.notes: Minimum quarterly salary of RUB 750,000 required (effective March 1, 2024). Employer files with Ministry of Internal Affairs. Work permit valid up to 3 years (matching contract duration); extendable without leaving Russia. Exempt from standard labour quotas. Family members receive derivative visas. HQS status also facilitates accelerated temporary and permanent residence.

RUS.name: Ordinary Tourist Visa (Consular)
RUS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Russia for tourism and sightseeing who are not eligible for, or prefer not to use, the unified e-visa. Requires confirmation of tourist services from an authorised Russian tour operator.
RUS.notes: Single- and double-entry consular tourist visas are valid for a stay not exceeding 30 days. Requires a tourist confirmation (voucher plus confirmation of acceptance) from a Russian tour operator listed in the Federal Register of Tour Operators. Multiple-entry tourist visas are issued only to nationals of countries specified by Russian Government decree. Distinct from the unified e-visa (which is single-entry, online, and limited to approved nationalities). Fee varies by nationality and reciprocity. Application form is completed at visa.kdmid.ru; documents are submitted to a Russian embassy, consulate, or visa centre.

RUS.name: Ordinary Humanitarian Visa
RUS.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Russia to establish or strengthen scientific, cultural, or socio-political ties, to participate in sporting events or religious activities, or to provide humanitarian assistance.
RUS.notes: Covers scientific, cultural, and socio-political ties, sporting events, religious activities, and the provision of humanitarian assistance. Single- and double-entry variants are valid up to 90 days; a multiple-entry humanitarian visa may be issued for up to 1 year. Requires an invitation issued by a Russian host organisation through the Ministry of Internal Affairs (or a decision of the MFA). Broader than, and distinct from, the medical-treatment humanitarian sub-category. Application form completed at visa.kdmid.ru; submitted to a Russian embassy or consulate.

RUS.name: Ordinary Private Visa for Temporary Residence Permit (RVP)
RUS.purpose: Single-entry private visa issued to foreign nationals who intend to enter Russia in order to apply for a temporary residence permit (RVP) at the territorial migration office of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
RUS.notes: A single-entry ordinary private visa valid for up to 90 days, issued specifically for entry to submit an RVP application to the MVD. The standard route is subject to the annual RVP regional quota and normally requires proof of Russian language, history, and legislation; some applicants (e.g. spouses of Russian citizens, persons born in the RSFSR/USSR) are quota-exempt. A separate quota- and exam-exempt variant exists for persons who share traditional Russian spiritual and moral values under Presidential Decree No. 702 (see the Shared Values entry). Complete the form at visa.kdmid.ru selecting the private visa category; a consular interview may be required.

RWA.name: Holiday/Tourism Visa (V1) – Single Entry
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals wishing to visit Rwanda for tourism, leisure or holiday purposes. Work is not permitted.
RWA.notes: Fee is waived (free) for nationals of countries with bilateral visa waiver arrangements (AU, Commonwealth, La Francophonie members and specific 90-day free-visa countries). Status change permitted. Applications via irembo.gov.rw, diplomatic missions, or border entry points.

RWA.name: Holiday/Tourism Visa (V1) – Multiple Entry
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals wishing to visit Rwanda for tourism, leisure or holiday purposes on multiple trips. Work is not permitted.
RWA.notes: Fee is waived for eligible nationals (AU/Commonwealth/La Francophonie/bilateral waiver countries). Status change permitted.

RWA.name: Group Tourist Visa (V8)
RWA.purpose: For organized tourist groups of 4 to 10 persons visiting Rwanda together for leisure or tourism.
RWA.notes: Fee of USD 150 covers the entire group of 4–10 tourists. Work not permitted.

RWA.name: East African Tourist Visa (V11 / EATV)
RWA.purpose: Regional multi-country tourist visa covering Rwanda, Kenya and Uganda with multiple entries for tourism across all three countries.
RWA.notes: Valid for travel within Rwanda, Kenya, and Uganda. Governed by EAC regional agreement. Available at Rwandan diplomatic missions, border entry points, or via irembo.gov.rw.

RWA.name: Transit Visa (VT)
RWA.purpose: For travelers transiting through Rwanda en route to a third destination.
RWA.notes: Valid for 72 hours maximum. Work not permitted. Status change not allowed. Free for nationals of countries with visa waiver arrangements. Available at entry points and via irembo.gov.rw.

RWA.name: Transit Visa – Unforeseen Circumstances (VE-2)
RWA.purpose: For travelers stranded in Rwanda due to unforeseen circumstances such as flight cancellation, schedule changes, or bad weather.
RWA.notes: Free of charge. Issued at the border/airport when traveler is inconvenienced due to circumstances beyond their control. Valid for up to 72 hours. Work not permitted. Status change not allowed.

RWA.name: Business Survey Visa (V6) – Single Entry
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Rwanda to survey business opportunities, conduct market research, or explore investment prospects.
RWA.notes: Renewable once. Status change prohibited. Work not permitted during visit.

RWA.name: Business Survey Visa (V6) – Multiple Entry
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals making multiple visits to Rwanda to survey business opportunities, conduct market research, or explore investment prospects.
RWA.notes: Renewable once. Status change prohibited. Work not permitted during visit.

RWA.name: Itinerant Business Visa (V9)
RWA.purpose: For frequent business visitors including foreign investors, board members, and representatives of multinational companies with significant ongoing business activities in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Valid for 2 to 10 years, renewable. Intended for persons who do not reside in Rwanda but have significant regular business activity in the country. Multiple entries permitted.

RWA.name: Reciprocity Visa (V12)
RWA.purpose: Long-stay multiple-entry visa issued based on bilateral reciprocal arrangements between Rwanda and the applicant's home country.
RWA.notes: Valid up to 10 years, renewable. Granted on the basis of reciprocal bilateral agreements. Conditions depend on the specific bilateral arrangement.

RWA.name: Job Search Visa (V4)
RWA.purpose: For skilled foreign workers whose occupation appears on Rwanda's official Occupations on Demand List (ODL) to visit Rwanda and seek employment.
RWA.notes: Available only to skilled workers on the official Occupations on Demand List (ODL). Multiple entries. Status change to work permit (H1) is allowed after finding employment. Work prohibited during the job-search period.

RWA.name: Conference/Meetings Visa (V5)
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals attending official conferences, seminars, meetings, or similar events in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Free for nationals of countries with visa waiver arrangements. Work is prohibited beyond the conference scope. Status change is allowed.

RWA.name: Medical Treatment Visa (V7)
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals traveling to Rwanda to receive medical treatment, and their care attendants.
RWA.notes: Covers the patient and their care attendants. Renewable in cases where continued treatment requires an extended stay. Status change permitted.

RWA.name: Family Visit Visa (V2)
RWA.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting family members residing in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Single entry at USD 50; multiple entry (90 days) at USD 70. Fee waived for eligible nationals. Status change permitted. Specifications mirror the Holiday/Tourism V1 visa.

RWA.name: Official Visit Visa (V3-1)
RWA.purpose: For non-accredited foreign government officials making an official visit to Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Free of charge. Issued to non-accredited government officials on an official mission. Status change prohibited. Work not permitted beyond the scope of the official visit.

RWA.name: Accredited Diplomat Visa (V3-2)
RWA.purpose: For foreign diplomatic officials formally accredited to Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Free of charge. Valid for 2 years, renewable. Issued to officially accredited diplomatic personnel assigned to Rwanda. Multiple entries permitted.

RWA.name: Visa Waiver – Free Entry (VE-1)
RWA.purpose: Entry pass issued to nationals of countries with a bilateral visa waiver arrangement with Rwanda, allowing visa-free or free-of-charge entry.
RWA.notes: 90-day waiver for bilateral agreement nations; 30-day free visa for AU/Commonwealth/La Francophonie members. Issued at border/entry points or diplomatic missions. EAC citizens receive a separate Visitor's Pass (VP-1) rather than this waiver entry.

RWA.name: EAC Visitor's Pass (VP-1)
RWA.purpose: Free entry pass for citizens of East African Community (EAC) member states, allowing stays of up to six months without a visa.
RWA.notes: For citizens of EAC Partner States (Burundi, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, South Sudan). Issued free upon arrival. Citizens of Uganda and Kenya may enter on a national ID card. This is a genuine visitor's pass under EAC free-movement obligations, not a standard visa.

RWA.name: Crew Member Visa (VC)
RWA.purpose: For aircraft or boat crew members entering Rwanda at official entry points in the course of their duties.
RWA.notes: Free of charge. Valid for 72 hours. Issued at the entry point. Work beyond crew duties not permitted.

RWA.name: Bridging Visa (V10)
RWA.purpose: Temporary visa issued to persons whose existing immigration status has lapsed while they regularize their situation in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Maximum 90 days. Intended for status-lapsed visitors pending permit renewal or change of status. Applied for in-country at the Directorate General of Immigration.

RWA.name: Remote Worker Visa (2-year)
RWA.purpose: Allows qualifying remote workers in priority professional fields to live and legally work in Rwanda for a foreign employer or their own offshore company.
RWA.notes: Established under Investment Promotion and Facilitation Law No. 006/2021 of 8 February 2021. Detailed in RRA Investment Incentives document (August 2023), Section XVII (Talent Attraction Incentives). Fee and application portal not published on migration.gov.rw or irembo.gov.rw as of June 2026.

RWA.name: Entrepreneurship Visa (2-year)
RWA.purpose: Allows foreign startup founders and innovative entrepreneurs and their dependents to reside in Rwanda and establish a business.
RWA.notes: Established under Investment Promotion and Facilitation Law No. 006/2021. Detailed in RRA Investment Incentives document (August 2023), Section XVII. No dedicated application portal found on migration.gov.rw or irembo.gov.rw as of June 2026.

RWA.name: Talent Visa (2-year) – International Graduates
RWA.purpose: Allows qualifying international graduates from recognized higher institutions to remain in Rwanda for up to two years after completing their studies.
RWA.notes: Commences from the date of study completion. Established under Investment Promotion and Facilitation Law No. 006/2021. Detailed in RRA Investment Incentives document (August 2023), Section XVII. No dedicated application portal found on migration.gov.rw or irembo.gov.rw as of June 2026.

RWA.name: Person with Assured Income Permit (K Permit)
RWA.purpose: Residence permit for retired persons and others with a guaranteed passive income who do not intend to be employed in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Minimum age: 55 years. Minimum income requirement: USD 5,000 per month. This is a resident permit, not a visa; applicants must apply in-country after entering Rwanda. Work in Rwanda not permitted.

RWA.name: Business Investor Resident Permit (Temporary)
RWA.purpose: Resident permits for foreign nationals certified as investors by the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), covering multiple economic sectors.
RWA.notes: Multiple category codes depending on sector: mining (A1/A3-1), agriculture (B1/B3-1), manufacturing (F1/F3-1), hospitality (O1/O3-1), IT (W1/W3-1), transport/logistics (X1/X3-1), other (Z1/Z3-1). New permit fee: 150,000 RWF (up to 2 years). Recurring permit fee: 250,000 RWF (up to 5 years). No minimum investment threshold published. Path to citizenship after 15 consecutive years of residence.

RWA.name: Skilled Worker Permit – Occupations on Demand (H1)
RWA.purpose: Temporary resident work permit for skilled foreign workers whose occupation appears on Rwanda's Occupations on Demand List (ODL) and who hold the required qualifications and relevant work experience.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 3 years, renewable. No labour-market test required (unlike the H2 sponsored category). Requires an employment contract, certified academic certificates, employer recommendation, CV and police clearance. A 90-day Job Search Visa (V4) is available to ODL workers before securing employment.

RWA.name: Sponsored Skilled Worker Permit (H2)
RWA.purpose: Temporary resident work permit for skilled foreign workers sponsored by a specific Rwandan employer who hold the required qualifications and relevant work experience.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Tied to a specific sponsoring employer. Requires certified academic certificates, an employment contract, employer recommendation, CV and police clearance.

RWA.name: Government/Public Institution Employment Permit (E1)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for foreign nationals contracted by the Government of Rwanda, tertiary institutions or parastatals.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires a government/institution contract, application letter, certified academic certificates, police clearance (last 6 months) and a detailed CV.

RWA.name: Technical Assistance Employment Permit (E2)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for foreign nationals providing technical expertise or assistance under a bilateral or cooperation agreement.
RWA.notes: Fee: 100,000 RWF (approx USD 70). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires a MINAFFET recommendation, Note Verbale, police clearance, certified academic certificates and CV.

RWA.name: Journalist/Media Permit (H3)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for foreign journalists and media representatives accredited by the competent Rwandan authority.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires media accreditation, an employment contract, recommendation letter, police clearance and CV.

RWA.name: Semi-Skilled Regional Worker Permit (H4)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for semi-skilled workers or artisans who are nationals of a country within the region (EAC/regional bloc).
RWA.notes: Fee: 50,000 RWF (approx USD 35) - reduced fee for regional nationals. Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires an employment contract, police clearance, CV and employer recommendation.

RWA.name: International/Regional Organisation Staff Permit (H5)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for foreign staff employed by an international or regional organization operating in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires a MINAFFET recommendation, Note Verbale, police clearance, academic certificates, CV and employment contract.

RWA.name: Special Agreement/Reciprocity Employment Permit (H6)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for foreign employees admitted under a special agreement or reciprocity arrangement between Rwanda and their home country.
RWA.notes: Fee and validity are set on a reciprocal basis per the underlying bilateral agreement. Requires an employment contract, certified academic certificates, police clearance, CV and recommendation letter.

RWA.name: NGO Employee Permit (N2)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for foreign nationals employed by a Non-Governmental Organization registered in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires an employment contract, RGB (Rwanda Governance Board) registration certificate, employer recommendation, certified academic certificates, police clearance and CV.

RWA.name: Professional Player/Artist Permit (C2)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for professional foreign athletes, players and entertainers/artists engaged in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 100,000 RWF (approx USD 70). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires an employment/engagement contract, CV, recommendation letter and police clearance.

RWA.name: Multinational/Regional Company Employee Permit (Q1)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for a foreign employee of a multinational or regional company that maintains its international or regional office in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid 1 year, renewable only under exceptional circumstances. Requires proof of company affiliation, the foreign employment contract, police clearance, CV and recommendation letter.

RWA.name: Refugee Worker Permit (J)
RWA.purpose: Work permit for a foreign worker holding refugee status in another country who has secured employment in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires an employment contract, certified academic certificates, CV, police clearance and recommendation letter.

RWA.name: Student Permit (U1)
RWA.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals enrolled to study at a school or institution of learning in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 20,000 RWF (approx USD 14). Valid 1 year, renewable. Requires a travel document valid 6+ months, a school recommendation/admission letter, a sponsorship letter and police clearance (applicants aged 18+).

RWA.name: Occupational Trainee Permit (U2)
RWA.purpose: Residence permit for foreign nationals undertaking training, an internship or academic research in Rwanda to enhance professional skills.
RWA.notes: Fee: 50,000 RWF (approx USD 35). Valid 1 year, renewable. Requires a university recommendation, internship/training agreement, CV, academic transcript and police clearance (18+).

RWA.name: Professional Research Permit (H7)
RWA.purpose: Residence permit for foreign professional researchers who are not accredited to or affiliated with a Rwandan school, vocational or research institution.
RWA.notes: Fee: 150,000 RWF (approx USD 105). Valid up to 2 years, renewable. Requires certified academic certificates, a research permit from the competent Rwandan authority, police clearance (last 6 months), CV and a recommendation.

RWA.name: Student Holiday/Graduate Work Permit (P2)
RWA.purpose: Work permit allowing higher-education students to work during holidays and recent graduates to take up employment in Rwanda.
RWA.notes: Fee: 20,000 RWF (approx USD 14). Valid 1 year. Requires an employment contract, CV, academic certificate, employer recommendation and police clearance (last 6 months).

RWA.name: Dependent Pass (M1/M2/M3)
RWA.purpose: Residence pass for the spouse, children and dependent family members of a Rwandan citizen (M1), a temporary resident permit holder (M2) or a permanent resident permit holder (M3).
RWA.notes: M1 (dependent of a Rwandan) and M3 (close relative of a permanent resident) are valid 3 years; M2 (dependent of a temporary resident) matches the principal's validity. Fee is 50% (half) of the fee paid by the principal applicant. Requires an application letter, marriage/birth/adoption certificate and police clearance (18+). M2 dependents also submit a copy of the principal's identity card.

SAU.name: Tourist e-Visa
SAU.notes: Available to nationals of 50+ eligible countries. Multiple-entry, up to 90 days per visit within 1-year validity. Applied online at visitsaudi.com or through Absher platform. Mandatory travel insurance included in fee. Alcohol prohibited; dress code modesty rules apply.

SAU.name: Visa on Arrival
SAU.notes: Available to nationals of eligible countries at Saudi international airports. Same fee and conditions as the e-Visa: SAR 300 base visa fee under Tourist Visa Regulations Article 9, around SAR 480-500 (~USD 134) all-in including the mandatory travel insurance. Available to same 50+ nationalities eligible for e-Visa. Effectively the same product issued on arrival rather than pre-travel.

SAU.name: Work Visa / Iqama (Residence Permit)
SAU.notes: Employer-sponsored. Work visa issued by Saudi embassy abroad; upon arrival, converted to Iqama (residence permit) within 90 days. Iqama valid 1-2 years, renewable. Kafala (sponsorship) system - employer is legal sponsor. Annual Iqama fees: SAR 2,400-4,800 depending on category. Fee listed is approximate combined cost. Employees under kafala require employer permission to change jobs (partially reformed via Saudi Vision 2030 labor reforms).

SAU.name: Premium Residency (Saudi Green Card)
SAU.notes: Two tracks: (1) Permanent Premium Residency: SAR 800,000 (approx. USD 213,000) one-time fee, lifetime residence without sponsor; (2) Temporary Premium Residency: SAR 100,000/year (approx. USD 26,667/year), annual renewable. No kafala sponsor required. Holders may work, invest, own property, sponsor family. Applied via pr.gov.sa. Available to select eligible foreigners. Fee shown is for permanent track.

SAU.name: Business Visit Visa
SAU.purpose: Business meetings, negotiations, and managerial visits with a Saudi company or institution
SAU.notes: Sponsored by a Saudi company or institution inviting one or more persons in managerial positions with an existing business relationship. Applied online through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa platform (ksavisa.sa / Enjaz), initiated by the inviting Saudi entity. Commonly issued as a single- or multiple-entry visit visa; validity and per-visit stay are set per invitation. Does not permit employment - a Work Visa is required to take up a job.

SAU.name: Family Visit Visa
SAU.purpose: Visiting first-degree relatives who are residents (Iqama holders) or citizens of Saudi Arabia
SAU.notes: Initiated by a Saudi resident or citizen sponsor for first-degree relatives (spouse, parents, children). Applied online via the MOFA visa platform (ksavisa.sa) by the inviting sponsor, who submits an invitation request. Often issued for up to one year; per-visit stay and number of entries depend on the invitation and the sponsor's status.

SAU.name: Study Visa (Educational Visa)
SAU.purpose: Full-time study at a licensed Saudi university or educational institution
SAU.notes: Sponsored by the admitting Saudi educational institution. Jointly launched by the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the 'Study in Saudi Arabia' platform. On arrival the student is issued a student Iqama (residence permit) valid for the duration of the study programme. Government scholarship students receive full sponsorship (tuition, housing, monthly stipend, medical care and travel allowance).

SAU.name: Medical Treatment Visa
SAU.purpose: Receiving medical treatment at a licensed hospital or medical organization in Saudi Arabia
SAU.notes: Requested by a licensed Saudi medical organization on behalf of the foreign patient, permitting a visit to the Kingdom for treatment. Applied via the MOFA visa platform (ksavisa.sa). Private hospitals must attach a support letter from Health Affairs. Typically processed in about 3 business days (longer in exceptional cases).

SAU.name: Transit Visa (Stopover Visa)
SAU.purpose: Short stopover or passing through Saudi Arabia en route to a third country
SAU.notes: Free of charge (subject to applicable taxes and insurance). Valid 90 days from issuance; maximum stay 96 hours (4 days), non-extendable. Available to applicants of any nationality. A free stopover transit visa is granted automatically when flying Saudia or flynas; passengers on other carriers apply through the Enjaz e-service platform (enjazit.com.sa). Travellers transiting under 12 hours without leaving the airport do not need a transit visa.

SAU.name: Temporary Work Visa
