SAU.purpose: Short-term employment or project work (contracts of 3 months or less) without residency or Iqama
SAU.notes: Employer-sponsored short-term work permit for contracts of up to 3 months; the holder's status remains 'visitor' with no Iqama or residency required. Issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (Qiwa platform) together with the MOFA visa platform. Valid up to one year from issuance; the 90-day stay can be extended once for a further 3 months via the Ministry of Interior. Used for consultants, technicians, engineers and specialists, and for seasonal (Hajj/Umrah) assignments.

SAU.name: Umrah Visa
SAU.purpose: Performing Umrah pilgrimage - for Muslim travellers
SAU.notes: Issued under the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah via the official Nusuk platform. Open to Muslim travellers of any nationality; applicants from the roughly 66 e-visa-eligible countries apply directly online, others through an agent licensed by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. Under 2026 rules the pilgrim must enter within 30 days of issuance and may then stay up to 90 days. Every application must be linked to confirmed Nusuk accommodation and transport bookings. Not available during the Hajj season blackout. Tourist e-Visa holders may also perform Umrah without a separate Umrah visa.

SAU.name: Hajj Visa
SAU.purpose: Performing the Hajj pilgrimage during the Hajj season - for Muslim travellers
SAU.notes: Issued under the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah exclusively via the official Nusuk Hajj platform for pilgrims from serviced countries, and bundled with an approved Hajj package (housing, transport, catering, Mashair and guidance services). Single-entry and valid only for the Hajj season, whose dates are set by the Islamic calendar. Cannot be obtained through third-party agents outside Nusuk. The visa itself carries no fee, but package costs apply.

SDN.name: Entry Visa - Business/Official
SDN.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals traveling to Sudan for business, official, or work purposes. Requires a sponsorship letter from a Sudanese organization detailing the nature of work, duration, and financial responsibility.
SDN.notes: Requires sponsorship letter from a recognized Sudanese organization. Non-US passport holders applying at Washington D.C. embassy must include a valid US residence permit copy. Processing time is 'up to 10 working days'. Fee is $154 USD (Washington D.C. embassy) or £100 (London embassy). Payment by money order, company check, cashier's check, or cash (walk-in); no personal checks or credit cards. Entry permit from Sudan's Aliens Department (Ministry of Interior) must be obtained by the sponsor in Khartoum before a visa can be issued by London embassy.

SDN.name: Entry Visa - Work
SDN.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals entering Sudan for employment purposes, sponsored by a Sudanese employer or organization.
SDN.notes: Listed alongside business/official visas under the same application category. Requires sponsorship letter from employer specifying type of work and duration. Same fee and processing as business visa ($154, up to 10 working days).

SDN.name: Entry Visa - Humanitarian
SDN.purpose: Issued to humanitarian workers and NGO personnel traveling to Sudan for relief and aid operations.
SDN.notes: Requires a certificate from Sudan's Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC) in addition to standard sponsorship letter. Same fee ($154) and processing time (up to 10 working days) as business visa.

SDN.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa (Note Verbale)
SDN.purpose: Issued to diplomatic and UN personnel, State Department officials, and other government representatives requiring entry to Sudan on official missions.
SDN.notes: Requires a note verbale from the U.S. Department of State or the applicant's international organization. Actual passport is submitted only after Ministry of Foreign Affairs approval. Fee not specified on official page. Processing up to 10 working days.

SDN.name: Entry Visa - Sudanese National (Foreign Passport Holder)
SDN.purpose: Issued to individuals of Sudanese nationality who hold a foreign passport, allowing them to enter Sudan.
SDN.notes: Requires a valid Sudanese identification document (passport or national number) plus a copy of the Sudanese sponsor's ID. For minors under 18: paternal written consent and father's ID copy required. Minors traveling without parents require a notarized paternal no-objection letter. Fee £50 (London embassy) or $154 (Washington D.C. embassy).

SDN.name: Entry Visa - Tourism / Visit
SDN.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Sudan for tourism or a short personal visit. The Sudan Embassy (Ottawa) issues this under two tiers: a Visit/Tourist visa for stays of one to seven days, and a Business/Tourism visa for stays of eight days up to three months.
SDN.notes: Per the Embassy of Sudan (Ottawa) Entry Visa page: 'Visit/Tourist Visa - issued to persons going to Sudan for the purpose of transit, tourism or whose stay would be one (1) to seven (7) days'; 'Business/Tourism Visa - issued to persons going to Sudan for the purpose of tourism or business whose stay would be from eight (8) days to three (3) months.' Passport must be valid at least 6 months; processing takes at least three weeks; yellow fever and cholera vaccination recommended. No self-service e-visa portal exists for Sudan (evisa.gov.ss belongs to South Sudan). Fee not published on the Ottawa fee schedule online; the Washington D.C. mission charges a general $154 processing fee. All visitors must complete police registration within days of arrival. Tourism to Sudan is heavily disrupted by the civil conflict ongoing since April 2023.

SDN.name: Transit Visa
SDN.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals passing through Sudan en route to an onward destination.
SDN.notes: Per the Embassy of Sudan (Ottawa) Entry Visa page, the applicant's passport should be duly endorsed with permission to enter the next country of destination after Sudan before a transit visa is applied for; the onward country of destination must be indicated on the application form together with the anticipated dates of arrival in and departure from Sudan. Transit falls within the short-stay one-to-seven-day band. Passport must be valid at least 6 months; processing takes at least three weeks. Fee not published on the Ottawa fee schedule online.

SEN.name: Visa on Arrival (Court Séjour)
SEN.purpose: Short-stay visit for tourism, family visits, or general purposes for Category B nationals. Issued by an immigration officer upon landing at Blaise Diagne International Airport (DSS).
SEN.notes: Available only at Dakar Blaise Diagne International Airport (DSS). Requires valid passport, return air ticket, proof of accommodation (tourism) or Letter of Intent (business), and yellow fever vaccination card. Free of charge. Applies to Category B nationals only; Category A nationals are visa-exempt and do not need this.

SEN.name: Special Business Authorisation (SBA)
SEN.purpose: Formal authorisation for business activities in Senegal for nationals who do not qualify for standard Category A or B entry. Required for certain business visitors from restricted-access countries.
SEN.notes: Downloadable SBA application form available from the Embassy of Senegal in London. Must be submitted to the relevant Senegalese embassy or consulate before travel. The embassy states all visa applications are free of charge.

SEN.name: Prior Authorisation Visa (Visa avec autorisation préalable)
SEN.purpose: Pre-travel visa authorisation required for Category C (restricted) nationals and holders of refugee travel documents (1951 Convention). Approval is granted by Dakar Central Visa Office or Ministry of Interior; the actual visa stamp is issued on arrival at DSS airport.
SEN.notes: Two application routes: (1) Apply via a Senegalese embassy abroad - minimum 4 months processing. (2) Have a Senegal-resident contact apply at Dakar Central Visa Office on your behalf - 1 to 2 weeks minimum; requires phone interview with Ministry of Interior. Required documents: copy of travel document, letter of invitation with full contact details of inviter, passport photo. Upon approval, a short-stay visa is stamped in the passport at DSS airport. Applies to Category C nationals and refugee travel document holders. Free of charge.

SEN.name: Diplomatic / Official Passport Visa Exemption
SEN.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, or official passports from countries with bilateral visa-abolition agreements with Senegal, even where the country's ordinary passport holders fall under Category B or C.
SEN.notes: Countries with split treatment (ordinary = Category B or C, diplomatic/service = Category A visa-free) include: Algeria (diplomatic/service), China (diplomatic/service/official), Gabon (diplomatic/service), Iran (diplomatic - 30-day limit), Kenya (diplomatic/service), Libya (diplomatic/service), Pakistan (diplomatic/official/service), South Africa (diplomatic/service), Tanzania (diplomatic/service), Turkey (diplomatic), Uganda (diplomatic/service). Entry is granted directly without a stamp or prior application for diplomatic passport holders.

SEN.name: Carte d'Identité d'Étranger (Foreigner Residence Permit)
SEN.purpose: Mandatory residence/identity card for any foreign national residing in Senegal for more than three months (long-stay residents, employees, students, and family members). Issued by the Foreign Police (DPETV) under the Ministry of the Interior.
SEN.notes: Card is valid 5 years and renewable. A foreigner must apply within 3 months of settling in Senegal. Required documents: handwritten application to the Minister of the Interior, copy of the first 5 passport pages, criminal-record extract (<3 months), birth certificate (<6 months), medical certificate, 3 photos, a 15,000 FCFA fiscal stamp (timbre fiscal), and a refundable repatriation bond (caution de rapatriement, amount varies by nationality). Issuing timeline exceeds 1 year; in the meantime a récépissé de dépôt valid 6 months is issued as a temporary permit. Purpose-specific documents are added on top of this common file (employment contract for workers, enrollment certificate for students). Processed via DPETV, DGPN, and final ministerial decision.

SEN.name: Carte d'Identité d'Étranger - Étudiant (Student Residence Permit)
SEN.purpose: Residence permit variant for foreign students enrolled at a Senegalese school or university who reside in the country for more than three months.
SEN.notes: Same carte d'identité d'étranger issued by the Ministry of the Interior (DPETV), granted on the basis of study. In addition to the common residence-permit file it requires a school/university enrollment certificate (certificat d'inscription) and, for sponsored students, a sponsorship/scholarship confirmation from the student's embassy. Same 15,000 FCFA fiscal stamp and repatriation bond apply. Card valid 5 years, renewable; a 6-month récépissé is issued while the card is produced.

SEN.name: Visa d'Approbation du Contrat de Travail d'Expatrié (Expatriate Work Contract Approval)
SEN.purpose: Mandatory government approval (endorsement) of a foreign/expatriate worker's employment contract before the worker may lawfully start work in Senegal. This is the core work authorisation, obtained by the employer in addition to the foreigner's residence permit.
SEN.notes: Issued by the Direction Générale du Travail et de la Sécurité Sociale (DGTSS, Ministry of Labour). Employer-initiated: the employer must submit the contract for approval before it takes effect, and an unapproved contract is null and void. An expatriate contract must be a fixed-term contract (CDD). The DGTSS approves with a stamp (visa d'approbation) or rejects with justification within 15 days; the approval must be renewed every 2 years. Contract filing/processing is dematerialised via the teledac.sec.gouv.sn portal. A separate carte d'identité d'étranger (residence permit) is also required to reside in Senegal.

SGP.name: Social Visit Visa
SGP.notes: Required only for visa-required nationalities; most nationalities are visa-exempt and receive a 30- or 90-day Visit Pass on arrival. The same entry visa covers both social and business visits. Single-journey visa fee is S$30 (about US$22). Apply online via the ICA e-Service or through a local contact/authorised visa agent.

SGP.name: Employment Pass (EP)
SGP.purpose: Working in Singapore as a professional, manager, or executive
SGP.notes: Minimum fixed monthly salary of SGD 5,600/month (general sectors, age 23 base), higher for older candidates (up to SGD 10,700/month at age 45+) and for financial services (SGD 6,200/month base, up to SGD 11,800/month at age 45+). Employer applies on behalf of candidate via EP Online. Fee SGD 105.

SGP.name: S Pass
SGP.purpose: Mid-level skilled workers earning at least SGD 3,300/month (SGD 3,800 in financial services)
SGP.notes: Minimum qualifying salary from 1 September 2025: SGD 3,300/month (general sectors) and SGD 3,800/month (financial services), rising with age up to SGD 4,800 / SGD 5,650 at age 45+. Increases again to SGD 3,600 / SGD 4,000 base for new applications from 1 January 2027. Quota- and levy-based (companies capped at a sector dependency ceiling). Employer applies via EP Online.

SGP.name: Student's Pass
SGP.purpose: Full-time study at a Singapore government school or approved institution
SGP.notes: Apply via SOLAR (Student's Pass Online Application & Registration) system. Fee SGD 30 for in-principle approval + SGD 60 for issuance.

SGP.name: Tech.Pass
SGP.purpose: Established tech entrepreneurs, leaders, and technical experts (salary at least SGD 22,500/month or equivalent track record)
SGP.notes: Requires last drawn fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 22,500 in the last year, AND 5+ cumulative years in a leading role at a technology company valued US$500M+ or with US$30M+ funding, or at a VC firm with US$500M+ assets under management. Valid 2 years, renewable once (max 4 years); 500 places on a first-come basis. Not tied to an employer. Singapore does not offer a dedicated digital-nomad/remote-work visa; Tech.Pass is a tech-talent work pass. Fee not published on the EDB page. To be superseded by a new ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track from January 2027.

SGP.name: Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass (ONE Pass)
SGP.purpose: Top talent across all sectors — fixed salary of at least SGD 30,000/month, or outstanding achievements in arts, sports, science or academia; not tied to an employer
SGP.notes: Personalised 5-year pass, renewable. No employer sponsorship required; holder may concurrently start, operate and work for multiple Singapore companies. From January 2027 a new ONE Pass (AI and Tech) track is expected to be introduced.

SGP.name: Personalised Employment Pass (PEP)
SGP.purpose: High-earning professionals not tied to any single employer
SGP.notes: To apply, fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 22,500; to keep the pass, at least SGD 270,000 in fixed annual salary per calendar year. Valid up to 3 years, issued once and non-renewable. Holder must not be unemployed for more than 6 months and cannot start a business or freelance.

SGP.name: EntrePass
SGP.purpose: Foreign entrepreneurs starting and operating a venture-backed or innovative company in Singapore
SGP.notes: New pass and first renewal valid up to 1 year; subsequent renewals up to 2 years. No minimum salary or levy/quota, but the company must be ACRA-registered with the applicant holding at least 30% and must meet innovation/funding criteria (e.g. raised at least SGD 100,000). Administered by MOM.

SGP.name: Work Permit (for migrant workers)
SGP.purpose: Semi-skilled migrant workers in the construction, manufacturing, marine shipyard, process and services sectors
SGP.notes: Valid up to 2 years, tied to the worker's passport validity, security bond and employment period. Applicant must be aged 18 to below 62. Employer or appointed agent applies; sector-based quotas (dependency ceilings) and monthly levies apply, and workers come only from approved source countries/regions.

SGP.name: Training Employment Pass (TEP)
SGP.purpose: Foreign professionals or students undergoing practical training in professional, managerial, executive or specialist jobs
SGP.notes: For trainees earning a fixed monthly salary of at least SGD 3,000, or foreign students whose training attachment is part of their course at an acceptable institution. Valid up to 3 months and not renewable. Employer applies.

SGP.name: Work Holiday Pass (Work Holiday Programme)
SGP.purpose: Students and young graduates who want to work and holiday in Singapore for up to 6 months
SGP.notes: Open to undergraduates and graduates aged 18 to 25 from recognised universities in Australia, France, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States. Valid up to 6 months, non-renewable; capped at 2,000 pass holders at any one time.

SGP.name: Work Holiday Pass (Work and Holiday Visa Programme)
SGP.purpose: Australian and New Zealander students and graduates who want to work and holiday in Singapore for up to 12 months
SGP.notes: Separate from the 6-month Work Holiday Programme; issued under bilateral Work and Holiday visa arrangements. Valid for 12 months.

SGP.name: Dependant's Pass (DP)
SGP.purpose: Legally married spouse and unmarried children under 21 of eligible Employment Pass, ONE Pass, Personalised Employment Pass or S Pass holders
SGP.notes: Validity is tied to the principal pass holder's pass (up to 2 years). The sponsor must earn a qualifying minimum salary. DP holders who wish to work need a Letter of Consent.

SGP.name: Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP)
SGP.purpose: Common-law spouse, step-children, handicapped children, or parents of an eligible work pass holder who cannot get a Dependant's Pass
SGP.notes: Validity tied to the principal pass holder (up to 2 years). Parents can be sponsored only if the pass holder earns over SGD 12,000/month. Note: ICA separately issues an LTVP/LTVP+ for foreign spouses of Singapore citizens and permanent residents.

SGP.name: Visa-Free Transit Facility (VFTF)
SGP.purpose: 96-hour visa-free transit through Singapore for certain visa-required nationals travelling to/from a third country
SGP.notes: Free 96-hour transit granted at the checkpoint. India nationals and selected PRC travel-document holders must hold a valid visa or long-term pass for Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the UK or the USA; nationals of CIS countries, Georgia, Turkmenistan and Ukraine need only a confirmed onward air ticket. No extension allowed.

SLB.name: Visitor Visa - Tourist
SLB.purpose: Allows a single entry for tourism, sightseeing, and leisure activities. Not for business or paid work.
SLB.notes: On arrival grant is 30 days. Online application fee is $50 USD (discounted); in-person fee is $100 USD. Extendable up to 150 days total for $100 USD per extension. No work permitted. Online payment described as 'coming soon' - applications submitted in-person at Immigration Services Office in Honiara.

SLB.name: Extended Stay Visitor Visa
SLB.purpose: Short-term visa for eligible visitors who wish to remain in Solomon Islands beyond the period permitted under a standard Visitor Visa, for continued tourism-related or visiting purposes.
SLB.notes: Allows a minimum stay of 6 months and a maximum stay of up to 12 months. Application fee is SBD $1,000 (approx. USD $120), paid to the Ministry of Finance. Processed by the Immigration Division's Border Control Unit on behalf of the Director of Immigration. Application made on Form 2 (Regulation 17). Also listed as a short-term visa on the Ministry of Commerce, Industries, Labour and Immigration site (commerce.gov.sb/visas_imm/). Not shown in the main immigration.gov.sb/visas/ fee table.

SLB.name: Visitor Visa - Visiting Relatives
SLB.purpose: Allows MSG passport holders to visit relatives resident in Solomon Islands for extended stays.
SLB.notes: Eligibility restricted to MSG (Melanesian Spearhead Group) passport holders - citizens of Fiji, Papua New Guinea, and Vanuatu. Extendable up to 1 year.

SLB.name: Visitor Visa - Yacht Person (Master & Crew)
SLB.purpose: Covers masters and crew of private yachts entering Solomon Islands waters for tourism or transit purposes.
SLB.notes: 60-day initial grant, non-extendable. Maximum aggregate stay of 180 days. Separate from the standard tourist visa.

SLB.name: Visitor Visa - Journalist/Reporter
SLB.purpose: Permits journalists and reporters to enter Solomon Islands for media and reporting activities.
SLB.notes: Renewable. Requires media organisation details. 30-day initial grant.

SLB.name: MSG (Melanesian Spearhead Group) Visitor Visa
SLB.purpose: Complimentary visitor visa for citizens of MSG member states (Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu) for tourism and visits.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. No extension permitted. No supporting documents required beyond valid passport.

SLB.name: Business Visa - Short-Term
SLB.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to conduct short-term business activities such as meetings, negotiations, and conferences in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Not extendable. Single or multiple entry options listed. Work/employment not permitted - business activities only.

SLB.name: Emergency Employment Visa
SLB.purpose: Allows emergency short-term employment in Solomon Islands where a local worker is not immediately available.
SLB.notes: Limited to 4 entries per year. Requires Labour Department support letter.

SLB.name: Foreign Official/Diplomat Visa - Long-Term
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign officials and diplomats for long-term postings in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Renewable. Work rights permitted within diplomatic capacity.

SLB.name: Foreign Official/Diplomat Visa - Short-Term
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign officials and diplomats for short-term visits to Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. No extension permitted. Requires third-party diplomatic note.

SLB.name: Dependent of Diplomat Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to dependents (family members) of accredited foreign diplomats resident in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Work rights not permitted.

SLB.name: Ministerial Special Exemption Visa
SLB.purpose: A special visa granted at the discretion of the Minister for exceptional cases not covered by standard visa categories.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Renewable. Requires Ministerial support/approval.

SLB.name: Dependent of Ministerial Special Exemption Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to dependents of holders of a Ministerial Special Exemption Visa.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Renewable. Requires Ministerial support.

SLB.name: Emergency Visa - 30 Days
SLB.purpose: Issued for emergency short-stay situations requiring urgent entry into Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. Non-extendable. Requires Ministerial support.

SLB.name: Emergency Visa - 3 Months
SLB.purpose: Issued for emergency situations requiring a longer short-term stay in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. Non-extendable. Requires Ministerial support.

SLB.name: Aid Worker/Volunteer Visa (Non-Commercial)
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign aid workers and volunteers working for non-commercial organisations in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Work rights permitted for volunteer/non-commercial activities only.

SLB.name: Research Academic Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to researchers and academics conducting academic or scientific research in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Requires Ministerial support.

SLB.name: Sportsperson Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to professional sportspersons competing or training in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Requires Ministerial support.

SLB.name: Religious Worker Visa (Non-Commercial)
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign religious workers and missionaries engaged in non-commercial religious activities in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Requires Ministerial support.

SLB.name: Mutual Reciprocal Visa - China
SLB.purpose: Pre-approval visa arrangement allowing Chinese nationals to visit Solomon Islands under a mutual reciprocal agreement.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. 90 days accumulative, non-extendable. Work prohibited. Must apply via eVisa portal before arrival and present grant letter on entry. Note: Chinese ordinary passport holders are also entitled to visa-free on-arrival access (30 days/visit, 90 days/180-day period) under the December 28, 2024 agreement - this pathway is an alternative pre-approval route.

SLB.name: Mutual Reciprocal Visa - EU Official Passport Holders
SLB.purpose: Pre-approval reciprocal visa for EU official passport holders visiting Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Non-extendable. Work prohibited. Ordinary EU passport holders are visa-free under the 2016 EU-Solomon Islands agreement; this pathway specifically covers official passport holders applying via the mutual reciprocal arrangement.

SLB.name: Mutual Reciprocal Visa - UAE
SLB.purpose: Pre-approval visa arrangement for UAE nationals to visit Solomon Islands under a mutual reciprocal agreement.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Non-extendable. Work prohibited. Must apply via eVisa portal before arrival and present grant letter on entry.

SLB.name: Mutual Reciprocal Visa - India
SLB.purpose: Pre-approval visa arrangement for Indian nationals to visit Solomon Islands under a mutual reciprocal agreement.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Non-extendable. Work prohibited. Must apply via eVisa portal before arrival and present grant letter on entry.

SLB.name: Mutual Reciprocal Visa - Indonesia
SLB.purpose: Pre-approval visa arrangement for Indonesian nationals to visit Solomon Islands under a mutual reciprocal agreement.
SLB.notes: Fee exempted. Non-extendable. Work prohibited. Must apply via eVisa portal before arrival and present grant letter on entry.

SLB.name: Long-Term Employment Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals taking up long-term employment positions with registered businesses in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Unlimited entries. Requires business name, type, and address details. Work rights permitted.

SLB.name: Short-Term Employment Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals for short-term employment engagements in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Requires Labour Department support letter.

SLB.name: Dependent of Resident Visa (Short or Long-Term)
SLB.purpose: Issued to dependents (spouses, children) of foreign residents holding a valid short or long-term employment visa.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Linked to and co-expires with the primary applicant's visa.

SLB.name: Family Relationship Visa - Solomon Islands Citizen Dependent
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who are dependents of Solomon Islands citizens, allowing long-term family residence.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Work rights not automatically permitted - requires separate work authorisation.

SLB.name: Permanent Resident Visa - Long-Term
SLB.purpose: Grants permanent resident status to long-term foreign residents who have continuously resided in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable (5-year grant). Requires minimum 5 years of continuous prior residence. Work rights not automatic - requires separate authorisation.

SLB.name: Permanent Resident Visa - Dependent
SLB.purpose: Issued to dependents of approved Permanent Resident Visa holders in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. Linked to primary permanent resident holder. Re-evaluation required after 5 years.

SLB.name: Film-maker Visa - Commercial
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign film-makers conducting commercial film production in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Work rights permitted for project-specific commercial film production.

SLB.name: Film-maker Visa - Non-Commercial
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign film-makers conducting non-commercial documentary or personal film projects in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Non-extendable. Work rights permitted within non-commercial scope only.

SLB.name: Comedian Visa - Commercial
SLB.purpose: Issued to professional comedians performing commercially in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Non-extendable. Requires Ministry/PM's Office support.

SLB.name: Musician Visa - Commercial
SLB.purpose: Issued to professional musicians performing commercially in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Non-extendable. Requires Ministry/PM's Office support.

SLB.name: Church or Cultural Entertainer Visa (Non-Commercial)
SLB.purpose: Issued to church groups and cultural entertainers for non-commercial performances and events in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Non-extendable. Requires Ministry/PM's Office support.

SLB.name: Student Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals enrolled in accredited educational institutions in Solomon Islands.
SLB.notes: Extendable. Requires confirmation letter from accredited institution. Dependents of students may be issued a separate student dependent visa under the same category at the same fee.

SLB.name: Transit Visa - Commercial Maritime
SLB.purpose: Issued to crew and passengers of commercial maritime vessels transiting Solomon Islands ports.
SLB.notes: 7-day single entry granted on arrival. Maximum 14-day stay permitted. Extension possible only if a substantive visa application is lodged.

SLB.name: Asylum Seeker Protection Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to persons who have lodged a formal asylum claim in Solomon Islands pending assessment of their refugee status.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. Not extendable as a standalone grant - status depends on outcome of Ministerial assessment. Duration tied to assessment proceedings.

SLB.name: Refugee Protection Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to persons formally recognised as refugees under international protection obligations.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. Granted under specific international protection obligations. Not extendable.

SLB.name: Human Trafficking and Smuggling Victim Visa
SLB.purpose: Issued to identified victims of human trafficking and people smuggling to provide temporary protected status.
SLB.notes: Free of charge. Protected status subject to formal assessment. Not extendable.

SLE.name: Landing Visa / Visa on Arrival (Tourist/Visitor)
SLE.purpose: Short-stay entry for tourism, family visits, religious travel, or academic purposes. Issued at designated ports of entry.

fee_local.note: Le800,000 single entry / Le1,200,000 multiple re-entry for non-AU nationals. Le250,000 single / Le375,000 multiple for non-ECOWAS AU nationals. Free for ECOWAS member nationals, diplomats, and UN Laissez-Passer holders. Fee structure published by SLID (March 2023). Original 2019 NTB policy quoted USD 80 (non-AU) / USD 25 (non-ECOWAS AU) - these USD amounts may represent the pre-2023 structure.

SLE.notes: Now officially termed 'Landing Visa' on SLID website (slid.gov.sl/landing-visa/, published March 2023). VoA policy originally introduced 5 September 2019 per NTB. Available at Freetown International Airport, Jendema (Liberia border), and Gbalamuya (Guinea border). Extendable once in-country. Single or multiple re-entry options available.

SLE.name: E-Visa (Tourist/Visitor)
SLE.purpose: Advance online visa for tourism, family visits, or short-stay purposes for nationals not eligible for visa on arrival or ECOWAS free movement.
SLE.notes: Applied for through the official Sierra Leone eVisa portal (evisa.sl), operated by the Government of Sierra Leone, or at Sierra Leone embassies/high commissions. Required for nationals not covered by ECOWAS free movement or the Landing Visa (VoA) policy. Per official Sierra Leone diplomatic-mission fee schedules (kw.slembassy.gov.sl/visas, sa.slembassy.gov.sl/visa-services), the single-entry visa is valid 3 months (90 days) from issue for a stay not exceeding 30 days; multiple-entry variants (6-month and 1-year validity) are also offered (see separate multiple-entry entry). The exact fee is set per mission/nationality and is not published on evisa.sl without beginning an application. Missions state applications are usually processed within about 24 hours.

SLE.name: Multiple-Entry Visa (Tourist/Business)
SLE.purpose: Pre-arrival visa for travellers making repeat tourism or business trips to Sierra Leone.
SLE.notes: Advance multiple-entry visa issued through the official eVisa portal (evisa.sl) or at Sierra Leone embassies/high commissions. Per official Sierra Leone diplomatic-mission fee schedules (kw.slembassy.gov.sl/visas, sa.slembassy.gov.sl/visa-services), it is offered in a 6-month (180-day) and a 1-year (365-day) variant, each allowing a maximum stay of 30 days per entry, valid for tourism or business. Fees are set per mission/nationality and payable in the mission's local currency (for reference, the Kuwait mission lists KD 50 for the 6-month and KD 100 for the 1-year variant). The single-entry alternative is the Landing Visa/VoA or single-entry e-visa. Embassies state applications are usually processed within about 24 hours.

SLE.name: Business Landing Visa / Visa on Arrival
SLE.purpose: Short-stay entry for business meetings, negotiations, or commercial activities. Issued under the same VoA/landing visa framework as tourist visits.

fee_local.note: Same fee structure as tourist landing visa. Le800,000 single / Le1,200,000 multiple for non-AU nationals; Le250,000 single / Le375,000 multiple for non-ECOWAS AU nationals.

SLE.notes: Business visits are covered under the same landing visa framework as tourism. NTB official policy (effective September 5, 2019) confirms VoA covers tourism, business, religious, academic, and family visits. Same fee structure applies. Extendable once in-country.

SLE.name: Work Permit (Employment Permit)
SLE.purpose: Authorises a foreign national to undertake employment in Sierra Leone for a Sierra Leonean employer or organisation.
SLE.notes: Applied for through the Unified Permit portal (unifiedpermit.gov.sl). Mandatory as of January 1, 2026 - all applications and renewals must go through the online platform. Non-ECOWAS fee per SLIEPA FAQ: Employee 3,000,000 Leones; Self-Employed 3,600,000 Leones; renewal 855,000 Leones. ECOWAS nationals: Employee/Self-Employed 1,500,000 Leones. Also referred to as the Employment category under the Unified Permit system.

SLE.name: Business Immigration Quota (BIQ) Permit
SLE.purpose: Permits foreign investors and business owners to reside and operate businesses in Sierra Leone, with an allocated immigration quota for key personnel.
SLE.notes: One of the named categories under the Unified Permit system (unifiedpermit.gov.sl). BIQ allows companies to bring foreign workers up to a quota. Alongside this is the Company Quota (CQ) permit. Specific fees and validity periods are not published on the public-facing pages of unifiedpermit.gov.sl.

SLE.name: Company Quota (CQ) Permit
SLE.purpose: Allows an established company registered in Sierra Leone to employ foreign nationals against an approved quota of expatriate positions.
SLE.notes: One of the named resident-permit categories in Sierra Leone's Unified Permit system, alongside the Business Immigration Quota (BIQ), Employment, Student, and Dependant categories (per the SLIEPA immigration FAQ and unifiedpermit.gov.sl). CQ authorises a registered company to bring in expatriate staff up to an allocated immigration quota, whereas the separate work/employment permit covers an individual employee. Specific fee amounts and validity are not published on the public-facing pages of unifiedpermit.gov.sl. Applications and renewals are online-only as of 1 January 2026.

SLE.name: Student Permit
SLE.purpose: Authorises a foreign national to reside in Sierra Leone for the purpose of full-time study at an accredited institution.
SLE.notes: Named as one of the categories in Sierra Leone's Unified Permit system. Applications and renewals must be submitted online via unifiedpermit.gov.sl as of January 1, 2026. Specific fee amounts, duration, and eligibility requirements are not published on publicly accessible pages of the unified permit portal.

SLE.name: Dependant Permit
SLE.purpose: Allows family members (dependants) of foreign nationals holding a valid work, business, or resident permit to reside in Sierra Leone.
SLE.notes: Listed as a named category in Sierra Leone's Unified Permit system. Intended for spouses and dependent children of permit holders. Applications submitted online via unifiedpermit.gov.sl. Specific eligibility, fees, and durations are not published on publicly accessible portions of the portal.

SLE.name: GO-FOR-GOLD Permanent Residency Programme
SLE.purpose: Grants immediate Permanent Residency to high-net-worth foreign investors who deposit gold bullion in Sierra Leone government vaults.
SLE.notes: Officially announced by SLID in a January 2025 press release. No in-country residency requirement to acquire or retain PR. Includes an upgrade pathway to citizenship. Administered by SLID. Minimum investment amounts appear only on the private operator website (goforgold.center) and are not published on any official *.gov.sl domain. Programme status as of June 2026 is uncertain - SLID website does not actively feature current articles about this programme.

SLE.name: Diplomatic/Service Passport Visa Exemption (China)
SLE.purpose: Mutual visa exemption for holders of valid PRC diplomatic and service passports travelling to Sierra Leone on official duties.
SLE.notes: Based on the Agreement Between China and Sierra Leone on Mutual Visa Exemption for Holders of Diplomatic and Service Passports, entered into force December 24, 2018. Covers diplomatic and service passports (including public affairs passports) of the PRC. Stays exceeding 30 days require registration with competent authorities. Diplomatic/consular mission members and accredited families are exempt for the duration of their accreditation. Ordinary PRC passport holders are NOT exempt; they qualify for VoA/landing visa under the BRICS category.

SLE.name: Diplomatic/Service/Official Passport Visa Waiver (South Africa)
SLE.purpose: Mutual visa waiver for holders of South African diplomatic, service, and official passports travelling to Sierra Leone.
SLE.notes: Agreed effective November 30, 2023, announced during a courtesy call by South African High Commissioner H.E. Grace Jeanet Mason at MoFAIC Building, Freetown on November 2, 2023. Ordinary South African passport holders qualify for landing visa under the BRICS/AU category. Max stay duration for diplomatic/service/official holders not confirmed - mofaic.gov.sl was inaccessible (ECONNREFUSED) during June 2026 re-validation.

SLE.name: Transit (Visa-Free Airside Transit)
SLE.purpose: Short airport transit for passengers continuing to a third country without formally entering Sierra Leone.
SLE.notes: Per official Sierra Leone diplomatic-mission guidance (kw.slembassy.gov.sl/visas, sa.slembassy.gov.sl/visa-services), no transit visa is required for passengers holding a confirmed onward ticket to a third country within 24 hours who remain in the international transit area of Freetown (Lungi) International Airport and hold the documents required for their onward destination. Travellers who need to leave the transit area, or non-ECOWAS travellers transiting overland, require a standard landing visa or entry visa instead. There is no separate paid transit-visa product.

SLE.name: ECOWAS Free Movement Right of Entry
SLE.purpose: Visa-free entry and right of residence for up to 90 days for citizens of ECOWAS member states, per the 1979 ECOWAS free movement protocol.
SLE.notes: Under ECOWAS Protocol A/P.1/5/79 dated May 29, 1979. Citizens of the 14 other ECOWAS member states (Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Côte d'Ivoire, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Togo) may enter without a visa and reside up to 90 days. Free landing visa per SLID (slid.gov.sl/landing-visa/, March 2023). Right to reside is granted but does not confer right to employment - a work permit is still required for employment.

SLV.name: Admission for Category A Visa-Exempt Entry (formerly Tarjeta de Ingreso Migratorio)
SLV.purpose: Short-stay tourism, leisure, or family visits for nationals of visa-exempt (Category A) countries. Processed at the port of entry.
SLV.notes: Available to nationals of approximately 89 Category A (visa-exempt) jurisdictions. The USD 12 Tarjeta de Ingreso Migratorio (TIM) fee was eliminated by the Legislative Assembly of El Salvador in April/May 2025; as of 2026 entry is fee-free for Category A nationals. Standard stay is 180 days (confirmed by UK GOV.UK and Canada travel.gc.ca official government sources, June 2026). CA-4 nationals (Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua) enter under the CA-4 Agreement instead and share a 90-day regional quota. Note: the CA-4 shared 90-day quota applies to movement within the CA-4 bloc as a whole; El Salvador can grant up to 180 days as its own individual entry period.

SLV.name: Visa Consular – Category B (Tourism/Short Stay)
SLV.purpose: Entry visa for nationals of Category B countries who require a consular visa, obtainable at a Salvadoran embassy or consulate without prior DGME authorization.
SLV.notes: Category B countries require a consular visa (visa consular o sin consulta) obtained before travel from a Salvadoran embassy or consulate. The consular office grants the visa without needing prior approval from DGME. Approximately 65 countries fall into this category. Form F46 is the consulted visa form; Form F47 is the multiple non-resident visa (1–3 years).

SLV.name: Visa Consultada – Category C (Tourism/Short Stay)
SLV.purpose: Entry visa for nationals of Category C countries, which requires prior authorization from the General Directorate of Migration and Foreigners (DGME) before the consulate can issue the visa.
SLV.notes: Approximately 41 countries are Category C. Applicants must first obtain DGME authorization (consulted visa, Form F46 or F49) before the consulate will issue the visa. The PEI (Special Entry Permit) online process is an alternative pathway for Category C nationals when no local Salvadoran consulate is accessible. Form F49 covers consulted visas specifically for investors, business persons, and commercial representatives.

SLV.name: Permiso Especial de Ingreso/Tránsito/Salida para Marineros (Special Permit for Sailors)
SLV.purpose: Special entry, transit, or exit permit for foreign sailors arriving by sea or air for crew purposes.
SLV.notes: Form F50. Specific fees and duration not published on official page. Applied for through the DGME.

SLV.name: Permiso Especial de Ingreso para Eventos de Artistas (Special Entry Permit for Artists)
SLV.purpose: Allows foreign artists to enter El Salvador to perform at concerts, theater, dance, circus, or other cultural and commercial entertainment events.
SLV.notes: Form F51. Fee: USD 60 for Central American artists, USD 100 for non-Central American artists. Processing: 5 business days after payment and document verification. Application submitted by email to peiartistas@migracion.gob.sv. Requires authorization from the General Directorate of Public Spectacles, artist roster with passport details, and travel itineraries. The sponsoring entity must be a Salvadoran-based person or company.

SLV.name: Permiso Especial de Ingreso (PEI) – Special Entry Permit (Online)
SLV.purpose: Allows foreign nationals who require a visa but cannot access a Salvadoran consulate (due to lack of embassy, residency issues, or force majeure) to obtain entry authorization online.
SLV.notes: Applied online at https://elsalvadorpei.migracion.gob.sv/. Eligibility: any foreign national whose nationality requires a visa (Category B or C) but who cannot obtain one through a Salvadoran consulate. Fee: USD 100. Outcome (approval, conditional approval, denial, or cancellation) sent by email. Not a substitute for a standard visa when consular access exists.

SLV.name: Extensión de Estancia para No Residentes (Non-Resident Stay Extension)
SLV.purpose: Extends the permitted stay of a non-resident foreign visitor beyond their initial authorized period.
SLV.notes: Form F44 (adults) and F45 (children/adolescents). Extension up to 90 additional days. Specific fees not published on official page. Applied for at DGME offices.

SLV.name: Tarjeta de Viajero Frecuente / Visa Múltiple No Residente para Inversionista, Empresario o Representante Comercial
SLV.purpose: Multiple-entry non-resident visa or frequent traveler card for investors, business persons, and commercial representatives enabling repeated short-stay entries.
SLV.notes: Forms F47 (Multiple Non-Resident Visa, 1–3 years) and F48 (Frequent Traveler Card for investors, business persons, or commercial representatives). Also F49 for consulted visa in this category. Fees and specific per-entry stay limits not published on official page. Designed for those who need to travel to El Salvador regularly for investment or commercial purposes without residing there.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F3 – Trabajador con Autorización (Temporary Residency with Work Authorization)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency status for foreign nationals who have received a job offer or employment contract in El Salvador and require authorization to work.
SLV.notes: Form F3 for initial application; Form F20 for renewal. Issued as a residency card with a validity period specific to the category. Applicants submit to the DGME (General Directorate of Migration and Foreigners) with required employment documentation. Fees not published on official page. Renewable.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F5 – Empresario (Temporary Residency for Business)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals establishing or operating a business in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F5 for initial; Form F22 for renewal. Residency card issued with category-specific validity period. Fees not published on official page. Renewable.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F4 – Inversionista (Temporary Residency for Investors)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals making qualifying investments in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F4 for initial; Form F21 for renewal. Minimum investment amount not specified in any official document reviewed. Residency card issued with category-specific validity. Also available via Art. 152 reform (May 2025): investors in government-promoted programs may obtain definitive (permanent) residence directly, bypassing temporary residence, for a fee of USD 690.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F6 – Representante Comercial (Temporary Residency for Commercial Representatives)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals representing international commercial entities in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F6 for initial; Form F23 for renewal. Fees and specific duration not published on official page. Renewable.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F7 – Pensionado (Temporary Residency for Retirees)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign retirees receiving a pension who wish to reside in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F7 for initial; Form F24 for renewal. Minimum pension income requirement not specified in any official document reviewed. Fees and specific duration not published on official page. Renewable.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F8 – Rentista (Temporary Residency for Income-Based/Annuitant)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals who can demonstrate sufficient passive income or annuity to support themselves in El Salvador without employment.
SLV.notes: Form F8 for initial; Form F25 for renewal. Distinct from the pensioner category (F7) - covers private income, investment income, or annuities rather than formal pension. Minimum income requirement not specified in any official document. Fees and duration not published on official page. Renewable.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F9 – Para Acompañar (Temporary Residency for Accompanying Dependents)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for family members (spouse, children) accompanying a principal foreign resident in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F9 for initial; Form F26 for renewal. The principal holder must already hold or be applying for a qualifying residency category. Fees and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F10 – Estudiante (Temporary Residency for Students)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals enrolled in an accredited educational institution in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F10 for initial; Form F27 for renewal. Requires enrollment documentation from a Salvadoran educational institution. Fees and specific duration not published on official page. Renewable as long as studies continue.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F1 – Transitoria (Transitory Residency)
SLV.purpose: Short-term transitional residency status for foreign nationals in specific transitional circumstances prior to obtaining a substantive residency category.
SLV.notes: Form F1. Specific conditions, fees, and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F2 – Temporal (Standard Temporary Residency)
SLV.purpose: General temporary residency status for foreign nationals not falling into other specific categories.
SLV.notes: Form F2. A catch-all temporary residency category. Specific conditions, fees, and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F11 – Accionista (Temporary Residency for Shareholders)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals who are shareholders in Salvadoran companies.
SLV.notes: Form F11 for initial; Form F28 for renewal. Distinct from the investor category (F4). Fees and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F12 – Comerciante Individual (Temporary Residency for Individual Merchants)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals operating as sole traders or individual merchants in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F12 for initial; Form F29 for renewal. Fees and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F13 – Cooperante (Temporary Residency for Aid/Cooperation Workers)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign nationals working in El Salvador under international cooperation, development, or humanitarian aid agreements.
SLV.notes: Form F13 for initial; Form F30 for renewal. Typically requires sponsorship from a recognized international organization or NGO operating in El Salvador. Fees and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F14 – Víctima de Trata (Temporary Residency for Trafficking Victims)
SLV.purpose: Humanitarian temporary residency granted to foreign nationals identified as victims of human trafficking in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F14 for initial; Form F31 for renewal. Granted through official anti-trafficking identification processes. Fees waived or not applicable in humanitarian cases.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F15 – Razones Humanitarias (Temporary Residency for Humanitarian Reasons)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency granted to foreign nationals requiring protection on humanitarian grounds.
SLV.notes: Form F15. Specific conditions, fees, and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Temporal F16 – Personal Religioso (Temporary Residency for Religious Personnel)
SLV.purpose: Temporary residency for foreign religious workers, missionaries, clergy, and other religious personnel serving in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F16. Requires documentation from the sponsoring religious institution. Fees and duration not published on official page.

SLV.name: Diplomatic/Official Passport Visa Exemption
SLV.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from countries with bilateral agreements or arrangements with El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports from countries such as Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Egypt, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Indonesia, Jamaica, Jordan, Kenya, Montenegro, Morocco, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Peru, Philippines, Serbia, Suriname, Thailand, Venezuela, Vietnam, and others (full list at rree.gob.sv) are visa-exempt. India diplomatic/official passport holders are visa-exempt for 90 days under a bilateral agreement (signed 2008, in force 2009). The RREE table is paginated and the full list was not retrievable in a single scrape.

SLV.name: Residencia Definitiva para Categorías Varias (Definitive/Permanent Residence – Various Categories, F32)
SLV.purpose: Permanent (definitive) residence for foreign nationals qualifying under general categories, typically after holding temporary residence or meeting long-term regular-residence conditions.
SLV.notes: Form F32. Definitive (permanent) residence is a distinct legal status from the F1–F16 temporary residences, granted by the DGME after qualifying conditions are met (e.g., prior continuous temporary residence, or more than seven years of regular residence). Renewal/endorsement is via Form F37 (Refrenda de Residencia Definitiva). Fees and validity not published on the official page.

SLV.name: Residencia Definitiva para Pensionado (Definitive/Permanent Residence for Pensioners, F33)
SLV.purpose: Permanent residence for foreign retirees/pensioners who wish to settle permanently in El Salvador.
SLV.notes: Form F33. Permanent-residence counterpart to the temporary pensioner residence (F7). Minimum pension income, fees, and validity not published on the official page. Renewal/endorsement via Form F37.

SLV.name: Residencia Definitiva para Casado o Conviviente de Salvadoreño (Definitive/Permanent Residence for Spouse or Cohabiting Partner of a Salvadoran, F34)
SLV.purpose: Permanent residence for foreign nationals married to, or in a recognized domestic partnership (unión no matrimonial) with, a Salvadoran citizen.
SLV.notes: Form F34. Marriage/partnership-based permanent residence. Per DGME rules a foreigner married to or cohabiting with a Salvadoran who has continuously held temporary residence for one year may apply for definitive residence. Distinct from the temporary accompanying-dependent residence (F9). Fees and validity not published on the official page. Renewal/endorsement via Form F37.

SLV.name: Residencia Definitiva para Personas Refugiadas o Apátrida (Definitive/Permanent Residence for Refugees or Stateless Persons, F35)
SLV.purpose: Permanent residence granted to recognized refugees or stateless persons who have resided in El Salvador under protection.
SLV.notes: Form F35. Refugees and stateless persons may apply for definitive residence (generally two years after filing their protection request; one year for Central American refugees). Humanitarian category; fees typically waived or not applicable. Renewal/endorsement via Form F37.

SLV.name: Residencia Definitiva para Personas Víctimas de Trata (Definitive/Permanent Residence for Trafficking Victims, F36)
SLV.purpose: Permanent residence granted on humanitarian grounds to foreign nationals identified as victims of human trafficking.
SLV.notes: Form F36. Permanent-residence counterpart to the temporary trafficking-victim residence (F14). Granted through official anti-trafficking identification processes; fees waived or not applicable in humanitarian cases. Renewal/endorsement via Form F37.

SMR.name: Short-Stay Tourist Entry (De Facto Schengen Visa-Free)
SMR.purpose: Tourism and short visits to San Marino for nationals who are exempt from Schengen area visa requirements. San Marino has no independent border controls and entry is via Italy.
SMR.notes: San Marino does not issue its own entry visas. Entry is governed de facto by Schengen Area rules since San Marino is entirely surrounded by Italy. Nationals who may enter the Schengen Area without a visa may enter San Marino freely. The San Marino MFA states that stays up to 30 days do not require a permit; stays beyond 30 days require a Stay Permit from the Gendarmerie - Foreigners' Office. The effective outer ceiling under the Schengen framework is 90 days in any 180-day period. No passport control at the San Marino border; no entry stamps are issued.

SMR.name: Stay Permit – Tourism (Permesso di Soggiorno per Turismo)
SMR.purpose: Formal stay permit for tourists wishing to remain in San Marino for more than 30 days and up to 12 months.
SMR.notes: Must be applied for at the Gendarmerie - Foreigners' Office within the first 30 days of stay. Maximum validity 12 months, renewable. This is a temporary stay permit, not an entry visa. Exact fee and processing time not published on the official English page.

SMR.name: Stay Permit – Work (Permesso di Soggiorno per Lavoro)
SMR.purpose: Temporary stay permit for foreign nationals employed in San Marino. Required for stays exceeding 30 days for the purpose of work.
SMR.notes: Maximum validity 12 months, renewable upon request. Application submitted to the Gendarmerie - Foreigners' Office. Specific documentation requirements and fee not detailed on the official English page.

SMR.name: Stay Permit – Education (Permesso di Soggiorno per Studio)
SMR.purpose: Special stay permit for foreign nationals pursuing education in San Marino.
SMR.notes: Listed under 'special permits' category on the official MFA page, alongside sport, medical treatment, health assistance, rehabilitation, religion, humanitarian reasons, and international volunteering. Maximum validity 12 months, renewable.

SMR.name: Stay Permit – Family Reunification (Permesso di Soggiorno per Ricongiungimento Familiare)
SMR.purpose: Temporary stay permit for spouses and children of foreign nationals legally resident in San Marino.
SMR.notes: Available for spouse and children (family reunification) and cohabitation. Maximum validity 12 months, renewable. Application to the Gendarmerie - Foreigners' Office.

SMR.name: Stay Permit – Working Holiday Scheme
SMR.purpose: Special temporary stay permit for foreign nationals participating in a working holiday scheme in San Marino.
SMR.notes: Listed explicitly under the 'special permits' category on the official MFA page. Eligibility conditions, eligible nationalities, and quotas not detailed on the official English page. Maximum validity 12 months, renewable.

SMR.name: Stay Permit – Medical Treatment (Permesso di Soggiorno per Cure Mediche)
SMR.purpose: Special stay permit for foreign nationals undergoing medical treatment, health assistance, or rehabilitation in San Marino.
SMR.notes: Covers medical treatment, health assistance, and rehabilitation. Listed under the 'special permits' category on the official MFA page. Maximum validity 12 months, renewable.

SMR.name: Pensioners' Atypical Residence (Residenza Atipica per Pensionati)
SMR.purpose: Long-term residence for retirees from EU countries and Switzerland, based on pension income or movable assets, with a facilitated tax regime.
SMR.notes: Limited to citizens from EU countries, Switzerland, and additional nations specified by a Congress of State Regulation. Minimum annual pension/passive income of €50,000 OR movable assets of at least €300,000 required. Facilitated taxation at 6% on pension income. Private health insurance required. No public sector employment; no state benefits. Converts to registered residence after 10 years. Path to citizenship is 30 years total continuous registered residence.

SMR.name: Elective Residence Permit (Residenza Elettiva)
SMR.purpose: Long-term residence for foreign nationals who make and maintain a qualifying property or financial investment in San Marino.
SMR.notes: Under Law 94/2017, Article 19. Three investment options: (a) purchase of completed residential property for ≥€500,000; (b) purchase of unfinished building for ≥€350,000 plus completion costs (total capped at €500,000); (c) non-interest-bearing 10-year restricted deposit of ≥€600,000 in State bonds. Application fee €1,000; one-time tax of €10,000 (deposit option). Private health insurance required. No public sector employment; no state benefits. Converts to registered residence after 10 years. Family dependants can be added at €20,000 per person.

SMR.name: Atypical Residence – Facilitated Tax Regime (Residenza Atipica)
SMR.purpose: Long-term residence for foreign nationals generating income abroad who wish to establish residence in San Marino under a facilitated flat tax.
SMR.notes: For foreign citizens generating income abroad who have not previously resided in San Marino for tax purposes. Substitute facilitated tax rate of 7% on foreign-source income, with a minimum of €10,000 and maximum of €100,000 annually. Private health insurance required. Cannot work in public sector or receive state benefits. Converts to registered residence after 10 years.

SMR.name: Registered Residence for Foreign Nationals (Residenza per Stranieri)
SMR.purpose: Long-term or permanent residence for foreign nationals seeking family reunification with San Marino citizens, establishing businesses, or holding management positions in San Marino companies.
SMR.notes: Available for family reunification with San Marino citizens, business establishment, or management roles in local institutes or companies. This is the standard long-term registered residence status; atypical and elective residence types convert to registered residence after 10 years. Path to citizenship via naturalization is 30 years continuous registered residence (standard) or 15 years for spouses of San Marino citizens.

SMR.name: Special Stay Permit – Sport, Religion, Humanitarian, Volunteering
SMR.purpose: Special temporary stay permits for foreign nationals in San Marino for sport activities, religious purposes, humanitarian reasons, or international volunteering.
SMR.notes: Grouped under 'special permits' on the official MFA page alongside education, sport, medical treatment, health assistance, rehabilitation, religion, humanitarian reasons, and international volunteering. Each sub-category likely has distinct documentation requirements not detailed on the official English page. Maximum validity 12 months, renewable.

SMR.name: Business Purpose Residence Permit (Residenza per Motivi di Business)
SMR.purpose: Stay/residence permit for foreign nationals who hold an active role in a San Marino company - shareholders owning at least 25% of company capital, sole administrators, or board chairmen - in priority economic sectors.
SMR.notes: Administered by startup.sm, the official San Marino agency for economic development. Eligibility: shareholders holding at least 25% of company capital, sole administrators, or board chairmen, in eligible sectors (technology, green economy, arts/culture, development services, marketing, research, training, low emissions, health/pharmaceuticals). Requires private health insurance with a minimum of EUR 30,000 annual coverage per person and documentation of adequate housing. Duration: 12 months initial, renewable up to 5 years. No fixed minimum investment - residence is linked to an active company role rather than a passive investment. This is the primary business-purpose immigration route and is distinct from the passive-investment elective/atypical residences.

SOM.name: Transit Visa
SOM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to pass through Somalia en route to another destination.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Visa on arrival is available to citizens of all countries; pre-approved visa letter can be processed within 48 hours and is valid 14 days from issuance. Most travelers now apply via eTAS at etas.gov.so.

SOM.name: Business Visa
SOM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Somalia for business activities, meetings, or commercial purposes.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Pre-approval letter valid 14 days from issuance; applicants must provide passport, return ticket, two photos, and payment receipt at port of entry. Apply via eTAS at etas.gov.so or through a local representative.

SOM.name: Tourism Visa
SOM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting Somalia for tourism and leisure purposes.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Pre-approval letter valid 14 days from issuance. For most nationalities, apply via eTAS (etas.gov.so). Visa on arrival available to citizens of listed African/Arab nations. Rwanda and Malaysia nationals are visa-free.

SOM.name: Work Permit
SOM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who intend to take up employment or provide professional services in Somalia.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Specific conditions, fees, and processing times not published on official sources as of research date. Applied through the Immigration Directorate.

SOM.name: Education and Research Visa
SOM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Somalia for educational study or academic research purposes.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Specific conditions, fees, and processing times not published on official sources as of research date.

SOM.name: Temporary Residence
SOM.purpose: Grants foreign nationals the right to reside in Somalia on a temporary basis for an extended period.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Holders of valid temporary residence permits are exempt from the eTAS (Electronic Travel Authorisation) requirement per SCAA AIC A 10/2025. Specific conditions and fees not published on official sources as of research date.

SOM.name: Permanent Residence
SOM.purpose: Grants foreign nationals the right to reside in Somalia indefinitely on a permanent basis.
SOM.notes: One of seven visa categories issued by Somalia's Immigration Directorate. Holders of valid permanent residence permits are exempt from the eTAS (Electronic Travel Authorisation) requirement per SCAA AIC A 10/2025. Specific conditions and fees not published on official sources as of research date.

SOM.name: Multiple-Entry Visa
SOM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who need to enter Somalia more than once during the visa's validity period, rather than the standard single-entry eTAS/e-visa.
SOM.notes: Listed as a selectable visa type ('multiple') on the official Immigration and Naturalization Directorate (IND) visa application form (info@immigration.gov.so), alongside Entry/Transit, Tourist, Work, Resident, Permanent, Education and Special visa. Holders of a valid multiple-entry visa are exempt from the eTAS requirement per SCAA AIC A 10/2025. Specific fee, stay length, and validity not stated on the IND form or on a live official page as of research date. Note: the IND form also lists a 'Special visa' category, omitted here because no official source defines its purpose.

SRB.name: Visa C (Short-Stay Visa) - Tourist
SRB.purpose: Short-term tourism, leisure, or visiting family/friends. Permits entry, transit, and stay in Serbia.
SRB.notes: Visa C covers stays up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Available as single, double, or multiple-entry. Requires valid passport (90+ days beyond departure, 2 blank pages), photo, travel insurance, proof of accommodation, and proof of financial means. Fees and processing times not published centrally - contact nearest Serbian diplomatic mission. As of April 23, 2025, also available in electronic form (Digital Travel Authorization) for eligible nationalities via evisa.welcometoserbia.gov.rs.

SRB.name: Visa C (Short-Stay Visa) - Business
SRB.purpose: Short-term business visits including meetings, conferences, negotiations, and trade activities in Serbia.
SRB.notes: Visa C for business purposes. Requires invitation letter from a Serbian business entity, company registration documents, and proof of financial means. Same 90/180-day rule as tourist Visa C. Short-Term Visa shall not be grounds to apply for temporary residence unless otherwise specified by law.

SRB.name: Transit Visa (Visa C - Transit)
SRB.purpose: Permits transit through Serbia's territory when traveling to another destination country.
SRB.notes: Applicant must demonstrate entry authorization for the next destination country. Falls under Visa C category. Airport Transit Visa (ATV) is a separate category for transit through international zones of Serbian airports without entering Serbian territory - required for certain nationalities.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Employment
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to work in Serbia; serves as the entry document before obtaining a unified residence and work permit.
SRB.notes: Visa D issued for stays between 90 and 180 days. Requires employment contract or other proof of employment in Serbia (employer certificate of registration, invitation letter). Holders are expected to apply for a unified Single (Temporary Residence and Work) Permit after arrival, issued for up to 36 months. Applications may be submitted electronically via the eApplications Visa (eForeigner) portal or at a Serbian diplomatic-consular mission abroad.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Education
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals enrolled in accredited educational institutions in Serbia for study or training programs.
SRB.notes: Requires enrollment letter or acceptance letter from a Serbian educational institution. Covers studying, schooling, Serbian-language learning, international student/pupil exchange, and scientific research/training grounds. Holders must apply for a temporary residence permit based on education after arrival. Visa D covers stays from 90 to 180 days. Application available electronically via the eApplications Visa (eForeigner) portal.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Family Reunification
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals joining a family member who is a Serbian citizen or holds lawful residence in Serbia.
SRB.notes: Requires proof of family relationship (marriage or kinship) and proof that the family member in Serbia is a citizen or holds valid legal status. Holders must apply for temporary residence permit based on family reunification after entry. Visa D covers stays from 90 to 180 days. Application available electronically via the eApplications Visa (eForeigner) portal.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Medical Treatment / Care
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Serbia for medical treatment at a registered healthcare institution or long-term care at a registered social-protection institution.
SRB.notes: Visa D covers stays from 90 to 180 days. Requires a letter from the healthcare institution stating the place and expected duration of continuous treatment, the institution's registration decision, valid health insurance, and proof of funds to cover treatment/emergency medical costs (or a certified guarantee from a registered legal/natural person). A separate 'medical care' variant additionally requires a social-protection institution's accommodation letter and work license. Application available electronically via the eApplications Visa (eForeigner) portal. Holders may apply for a temporary residence permit (up to 3 years) on the same basis while the visa is valid.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Seasonal Work
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals hired for seasonal jobs in the agriculture, forestry and fishing sectors in Serbia.
SRB.notes: Seasonal employment is permitted only for jobs of a seasonal character in the agriculture, forestry and fishing sectors, for up to 120 working days in a calendar year. Requires an invitation letter, employer certificate of registration (active status, not older than 6 months), a job offer detailing work conditions and duration, and an employer accommodation certificate. Visa D stay window is 90 to 180 days. Application available electronically via the eApplications Visa (eForeigner) portal.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Religious Service
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign priests and religious officials coming to perform religious worship within a church or religious community registered in Serbia.
SRB.notes: The church or religious community must be registered in the Republic of Serbia. Requires the community's certificate of registration and an employment contract or letter confirming the applicant is employed as a priest/religious official, plus valid health insurance and proof of funds. Visa D stay window is 90 to 180 days. Application available electronically via the eApplications Visa (eForeigner) portal. Holders may apply for a temporary residence permit on the basis of religious service.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Digital Nomad / Remote Worker
SRB.purpose: Enables foreign nationals working remotely for foreign employers or clients to reside in Serbia while conducting remote work.
SRB.notes: Not a standalone branded 'digital nomad visa' - uses the standard Visa D or temporary residence framework under the 2023 Law on Foreigners (amendments effective February 2024). Applicants must demonstrate proof of remote employment or self-employment contracts with foreign companies, and sufficient funds. Serbia introduced tax incentives for digital nomads. After entry on Visa D, applicants apply for temporary residence permit. Average processing time for temporary residence permit: approximately 19 working days post-2024 digital reform.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Investor
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to invest in Serbia and establish or manage a business entity registered in Serbia.
SRB.notes: Entry visa before obtaining a Temporary Residence Permit for Investors. Investor permit requires certificate of at least EUR 50,000 in a Serbian-registered bank account and proof of invested assets in a registered Serbian company. For renewal, proof of paid cash capital contribution of at least EUR 5,000 into share capital is required. Permit issued for up to 3 years, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 3 years continuous temporary residence.

SRB.name: Visa D (Long-Stay Visa) - Real Estate Ownership
SRB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who own real estate in Serbia and wish to reside there based on property ownership.
SRB.notes: Residence basis available to foreign nationals who own real estate in Serbia. No government-mandated minimum investment threshold stated on official sources. Requires proof of real estate ownership. Permit issued for up to 3 years, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 3 years continuous temporary residence.

SRB.name: Visa C - Electronic (Digital Travel Authorization)
SRB.purpose: Online e-visa equivalent to Visa C for eligible nationalities that require a visa but lack convenient access to a Serbian diplomatic mission.
SRB.notes: Launched April 23, 2025. Available to citizens of 46 nationalities that require a visa to enter Serbia. First e-visa arrivals at Nikola Tesla Airport on 9 June 2025 (two travelers from Lesotho). Visa C valid for up to 90 days, single or multiple entries within 180 days. Primarily for citizens of countries without Serbian diplomatic or consular missions, particularly in South America, Africa, and Asia. Lesotho was specifically named as one eligible country. Processing as fast as 1 hour when complete documentation submitted. Applications submitted 24/7 at evisa.welcometoserbia.gov.rs. First e-visa arrivals at Nikola Tesla Airport recorded June 9, 2025 (two travelers from Lesotho). The list of eligible 46 nationalities is not publicly enumerated on official pages - portal requires login.

SRB.name: Visa C / Visa D - Diplomatic / Official
SRB.purpose: Entry visas for holders of diplomatic and official/service passports on official government business or diplomatic assignments in Serbia.
SRB.notes: Many countries have bilateral diplomatic/service passport visa exemption agreements with Serbia allowing visa-free entry for diplomatic and official passport holders. For instance, Russian diplomatic/official passport holders may enter visa-free for up to 90 days versus the 30-day limit for ordinary passport holders. Where no bilateral exemption exists, diplomatic/official passport holders apply through the same Visa C/D system. Serbia presented 12 new bilateral agreements for diplomatic passport exemptions to the National Assembly (Sao Tome and Principe, Togo, Maldives, Burundi, Guinea-Bissau, Uzbekistan, Ghana, Nepal, Republic of the Congo, Tajikistan, Eswatini, Saint Lucia) - these apply to diplomatic and official passports only, not ordinary passports.

SSD.name: Single Entry e-Visa (Tourist/Business)
SSD.purpose: For tourism or business visits to South Sudan for a single entry. Applied for online through the official e-visa portal.
SSD.notes: Standard fee is USD 100 for most nationalities. Reduced fee of USD 50 for nationals of neighboring/African countries (e.g., Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Sudan, DRC, CAF). USA nationals pay USD 160. Egypt and Tanzania are exempt (USD 0 - visa-free). Processing time is within 72 hours per official portal. Yellow fever vaccination certificate required.

SSD.name: 3-Month Multiple Entry e-Visa
SSD.purpose: Allows multiple entries into South Sudan within a 3-month validity period, for business or tourism purposes.
SSD.notes: Standard fee is USD 200. Reduced fee of USD 125 for eligible neighboring/African nationals. USA nationals pay USD 500. Applied online through the official e-visa portal at evisa.gov.ss. Yellow fever vaccination certificate required.

SSD.name: 6-Month Multiple Entry e-Visa
SSD.purpose: Allows multiple entries into South Sudan within a 6-month validity period, for tourism or business purposes.
SSD.notes: Standard fee is USD 350. Reduced fee of USD 250 for eligible neighboring/African nationals. Not available for USA nationals. Applied online through the official e-visa portal at evisa.gov.ss. Yellow fever vaccination certificate required.

SSD.name: Transit Visa
SSD.purpose: For travelers passing through South Sudan en route to other destinations. Issued by South Sudanese embassies or consulates.
SSD.notes: Generally issued for periods not exceeding 72 hours (3 days). Applied in person at South Sudanese embassies or consulates. Processing time is a minimum of 7 working days. Fee not specified on official source. Requires passport valid for at least 180 days, completed application form, passport photo, and relevant travel documentation.

SSD.name: Diplomatic / Official / Service Visa
SSD.purpose: Issued to diplomatic, official, and service passport holders traveling to South Sudan on official duty. Issued gratis (no fee).
SSD.notes: Complimentary (gratis) visa for holders of diplomatic, official, service, or special passports of any nationality traveling on official duty. Available on arrival. Must present an official Note Verbale from the appropriate authorities. Multiple-entry visas are only granted to diplomatic and official passport holders. Source: mofaic.gov.ss/visas/ and mofaic.gov.ss/types-of-visas/.

SSD.name: Single Entry Visa (Embassy/Consulate)
SSD.purpose: A standard single-entry visa issued by South Sudanese embassies or consulates abroad for business or tourism, when the online e-visa portal is unavailable or suspended.
SSD.notes: Issued in person at South Sudanese embassies and consulates when the e-visa service is temporarily suspended or unavailable. The Embassy of South Sudan in Washington D.C. states the online portal may be temporarily suspended. Fee varies by nationality: USD 50 for bordering African countries, USD 100 for most nationalities, USD 160 for US passport holders, free for EAC/Egyptian nationals and diplomatic passport holders. Requires passport valid for at least 180 days, invitation letter from a South Sudanese organization, passport photos, money order or certified check. Processing time is approximately 10 business days.

SSD.name: Work Permit (Alien Employment)
