SSD.purpose: Legal authorization for a foreign national to take up employment in South Sudan; applied for by the employer after the worker has entered on an entry/e-visa.
SSD.notes: Issued by the National Ministry of Labour, Department of Alien Employment. Valid for one year from the date of issuance and renewable. A USD 100 application-form fee applies, plus a separate work-permit fee whose amount is not published on the official page. Required documents include a valid passport, entry visa, employment contract, CV, academic certificates, and CID/Interpol clearance certificates. A foreign national must first hold an entry (e-)visa; the work permit is a separate labour document, not an entry visa. Applied online at the Ministry of Labour portal workpermit.eservices.gov.ss. Source: mol.gov.ss/page/work-permit-applications.

SSD.name: Special Residence Permit
SSD.purpose: Long-term residence for aliens who have resided continuously in South Sudan for at least 3 years, or lawfully for more than 5 years while carrying out scientific, technical or commercial activities deemed of value to South Sudan.
SSD.notes: Defined in the Passports and Immigration Act 2011, Chapter V, section 19. Valid and renewable for five-year periods. Granted by the Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration (Ministry of Interior). A residence permit extends to the holder's spouse(s), children and dependents (section 23). The holder forfeits the permit after continuous absence exceeding six months unless a return visa was obtained before departure (section 21). Fee not published on official sources. Applied via the immigration eServices portal (immigration.eservices.gov.ss). Source: Passports and Immigration Act 2011 (mojca.gov.ss).

SSD.name: Ordinary Residence Permit
SSD.purpose: Residence for aliens who have resided continuously in South Sudan for at least 5 years, or lawfully for more than 2 years while carrying out scientific, technical or commercial activities deemed of value to South Sudan.
SSD.notes: Defined in the Passports and Immigration Act 2011, Chapter V, section 20. Valid and renewable for two-year periods. Granted by the Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration (Ministry of Interior). A residence permit extends to the holder's spouse(s), children and dependents (section 23). Fee not published on official sources. Applied via the immigration eServices portal (immigration.eservices.gov.ss). Source: Passports and Immigration Act 2011 (mojca.gov.ss).

SSD.name: Temporary Residence Permit
SSD.purpose: Residence for aliens who are not eligible for a special or ordinary residence permit but need to reside in South Sudan (e.g. expatriate workers and their families in the early years of stay).
SSD.notes: Defined in the Passports and Immigration Act 2011, Chapter V, section 20(3)-(4). Valid and renewable for periods not exceeding twelve months. Granted by the Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration (Ministry of Interior). A residence permit extends to the holder's spouse(s), children and dependents (section 23). Tourists staying not more than three months are exempt from residence-permit/alien-registration requirements (section 24). Fee not published on official sources. Applied via the immigration eServices portal (immigration.eservices.gov.ss). Source: Passports and Immigration Act 2011 (mojca.gov.ss).

STP.name: Autorização de Entrada (e-Visa / Entry Authorization)
STP.purpose: Grants foreign nationals permission to enter São Tomé and Príncipe for tourism, leisure, or short visits. Applied for online via the official SMF e-Visa portal.
STP.notes: Processing is 7 business days (7 dias úteis). Payment is collected at the border upon arrival, not during the online application. Requires: scanned passport in PDF (valid 3+ months beyond intended stay), return ticket, proof of accommodation or contact in STP, and proof of financial means (€100/day minimum at border). Minors additionally require birth certificate and guardian declarations. No information changes allowed after submission. Legal basis: Decreto Lei 11/2009 and Lei 5/2008. The e-visa Autorização de Entrada implements the statutory Visto Temporário (Art. 32.º, Lei 5/2008): validity up to 180 days, one or more entries, uninterrupted stay not exceeding 3 months (90 days); must be used within 90 days of grant; profit-making activity is not permitted on this visa. The official portal does not differentiate tourist from other short-stay purposes - a single e-visa entry authorization covers all short-stay purposes.

STP.name: Autorização de Entrada (e-Visa / Entry Authorization) - Business
STP.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter São Tomé and Príncipe for business meetings, commercial activities, or investment-related visits. Applied via the same SMF e-Visa portal as tourist entry.
STP.notes: The SMF e-visa portal (smf.st/evisa) uses a single entry authorization form for all short-stay purposes. No separate business visa category is listed officially; business travelers use the same Autorização de Entrada, which implements the statutory Visto Temporário (Art. 32.º, Lei 5/2008): validity up to 180 days, uninterrupted stay up to 3 months (90 days). Suitable for business meetings and commercial visits only - paid/lucrative employment requires a residence visa for professional activity (Art. 35.º/36.º). Payment at border. Same documentation requirements as tourist entry authorization.

STP.name: Visto de Trânsito (Transit Visa)
STP.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to transit through São Tomé and Príncipe en route to a third country.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 30.º, Lei 5/2008. Grants entry to a traveller heading to a third country where admission is guaranteed. Granted for one or, exceptionally, two entries; each transit may not exceed 4 days. No transit visa is required for a traveller passing through in continuous transit (interrupted only for technical stopovers on the same means of transport). Transit is explicitly referenced on the SMF e-visa page as a separate use case and applied via the same e-visa portal; applicants must hold valid entry authorization for their destination country. Specific fee not published on the official portal.

STP.name: Visto de Residência (Residence Visa - general)
STP.purpose: Authorizes a foreign national to enter São Tomé and Príncipe in order to apply for a residence certificate (certificado de residência); the umbrella category covering all long-stay purposes.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 33.º, Lei 5/2008. The residence visa is valid for two entries and lets the holder remain 2 months (60 days) in order to request the residence certificate that governs the long-term stay. It may be granted for dependent work, independent work, family reunification, study, volunteering, professional training, research activity, or highly-qualified activity (specific sub-categories are covered by their own entries below). Applied online via the SMF eCidadão system (Autorização para Fixação de Residência). Documents: travel document valid 1+ year, criminal-record certificate, proof of adequate housing, means of subsistence (min. €100/day). Fees not published online; paid at border or by bank transfer to SMF's BISTP account. General enquiries: (+239) 2222098 or direccaosmf@gmail.com.

STP.name: Visto de Residência para Exercício de Actividade Profissional Subordinada (Residence Visa - Employed Work)
STP.purpose: For foreign nationals coming to work under an employment contract for an employer in São Tomé and Príncipe.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 35.º, Lei 5/2008; eCidadão residence category 'Actividade Profissional Subordinada'. Residence visa valid for two entries and 2 months' stay to obtain the residence certificate that then authorises the work stay. Requires an employment contract, criminal-record certificate, proof of housing and means of subsistence (min. €100/day). Fees not published online; paid at border or by bank transfer to SMF's BISTP account.

STP.name: Visto de Residência para Exercício de Actividade Profissional Independente (Residence Visa - Self-Employed / Investor)
STP.purpose: For foreign nationals establishing self-employment, a business, or an investment operation in São Tomé and Príncipe.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 36.º, Lei 5/2008; eCidadão residence category 'Actividade Profissional Independente'. Granted to a foreigner who has carried out an investment operation or will exercise an independent professional activity. Residence visa valid for two entries and 2 months' stay to obtain the residence certificate. Distinct from the citizenship-by-investment programme (tracked under cbi). Fees not published online; paid at border or by bank transfer to SMF's BISTP account.

STP.name: Visto de Residência para Actividade de Investigação ou Altamente Qualificada (Residence Visa - Research / Highly-Qualified Activity)
STP.purpose: For researchers and highly-qualified professionals coming to carry out scientific research or a highly-qualified activity in São Tomé and Príncipe.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 37.º, Lei 5/2008. Residence visa for foreigners engaged in scientific research or a highly-qualified activity. Statutory category defined in the Regime Jurídico; not separately listed in the eCidadão online category menu (apply under the residence-authorisation flow). Residence visa valid for two entries and 2 months' stay to obtain the residence certificate. Fees not published online.

STP.name: Visto de Residência para Estudo, Intercâmbio de Estudantes, Estágio Profissional ou Voluntariado (Residence Visa - Study / Exchange / Internship / Volunteering)
STP.purpose: For foreign nationals admitted for studies, a secondary-school student-exchange programme, a professional internship, or volunteering.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 38.º, Lei 5/2008; eCidadão residence category 'Estudo, Intercâmbio de Estudantes e Estágio Profissional' (also covers voluntariado/volunteering). Residence visa valid for two entries and 2 months' stay to obtain the residence certificate. Requires proof of enrolment/acceptance, criminal-record certificate, proof of housing and means of subsistence (min. €100/day). Fees not published online; paid at border or by bank transfer to SMF's BISTP account.

STP.name: Visto de Residência para Efeitos de Reagrupamento Familiar (Residence Visa - Family Reunification)
STP.purpose: For family members joining a foreign national or citizen legally resident in São Tomé and Príncipe.
STP.notes: Legal basis: Artigo 39.º, Lei 5/2008; eCidadão residence category 'Reagrupamento Familiar'. Granted where a resident's family member seeks to join them. Residence visa valid for two entries and 2 months' stay to obtain the residence certificate. Requires proof of family relationship, criminal-record certificate, proof of housing and means of subsistence (min. €100/day). Fees not published online; paid at border or by bank transfer to SMF's BISTP account.

STP.name: Isenção de Visto - Passaporte Diplomático/Serviço (Diplomatic/Service Passport Exemption)
STP.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic and service passports from CPLP member states and countries with bilateral diplomatic agreements.
STP.notes: Presidential Decree n. 21/2002 (20 December 2002) ratifies CPLP agreement suppressing visas for diplomatic and service passports among CPLP member states (Angola, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Equatorial Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, Portugal, Timor-Leste). China diplomatic, service, and public-affairs passport holders also receive 30-day visa-free entry under bilateral agreement (Decree n. 09/2017, in force 2018-02-03). South Africa diplomatic/service passport agreement was approved November 2024. Duration for CPLP diplomatic/service passports not specified in available official sources.

SUR.name: E-Tourist Card (Entry Fee - Single Entry)
SUR.purpose: Short-term tourism and family visits to Suriname. Applies to the majority of world passport holders not covered by CARICOM exemption or the 21-country full e-visa requirement.
SUR.notes: Fee is USD 50 (or EUR 50) plus USD 18 (EUR 17) VFS Global service fee (service fee increased from USD/EUR 8; confirmed via VFS portal as of 2025). Total single-entry cost is approximately USD 68 / EUR 67. Must be purchased online via suriname.vfsevisa.com at least 24 hours before departure. Physical payment is also available at Suriname's Consulate-General in Cayenne (French Guiana) and the office in Saint Laurent du Maroni per gov.sr MFA page. CARICOM passport holders and holders of diplomatic/service/official/special passports are exempt from this fee. Transit passengers are also exempt. A Multiple Entry Fee option (5 entries over 3 months, USD 75 / EUR 75 + service fee) was introduced from January 1, 2025 (initially for Brazil and France only) and expanded to all eligible nationalities from May 1, 2025 — see separate E-Tourist Card (Multiple Entry Fee) visa type.

SUR.name: E-Tourist Card (Entry Fee - Multiple Entry)
SUR.purpose: Short-term tourism and family visits to Suriname with up to 5 entries over a 3-month window. Introduced from 1 January 2025 (pilot for Brazilian and French Guiana nationals), expanded to all entry-fee-eligible nationalities from 1 May 2025.
SUR.notes: Voucher costs USD 75 (or EUR 75) plus USD 18 (EUR 17) VFS Global service fee; total approximately USD 93 / EUR 92. Valid for 3 months from first arrival, permitting up to 5 entries within that window. After 3 months, voucher expires regardless of remaining entries. Children aged 0-2 years are exempt from all entry fees. Children 3 years and older pay the standard entry fee. Pilot program launched 1 January 2025 for Brazilian citizens and French nationals residing in French Guiana; expanded to all eligible entry-fee nationalities from 1 May 2025 per Suriname Government announcement (gov.sr). Source: https://gov.sr/introductie-multiple-entry-fee/ (official gov.sr announcement).

SUR.name: E-Visa (Tourist/Visit)
SUR.purpose: Entry authorization for nationals of 21 countries that had their visa-free status reinstated as a full visa requirement from 1 May 2023. Covers tourism and family visits.
SUR.notes: Required for nationals of: Afghanistan, Angola, Bangladesh, Cameroon, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Egypt, Eritrea, Ghana, India, Kenya, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Syria, Tunisia, Venezuela, Zambia. Full adjudicated e-visa application required via suriname.vfsevisa.com; not merely a fee payment. Introduced/reimposed 1 May 2023.

SUR.name: Business E-Visa
SUR.purpose: Short-term entry for business purposes including attending conferences, training sessions, exploratory visits, and other commercial activities.
SUR.notes: Business visa applications are processed exclusively electronically via the VFS Global online portal (suriname.vfsvisa.com). Required for business visitors who cannot enter under the standard entry fee/e-tourist card category. Multiple-entry options are available for business purposes.

SUR.name: Short-Stay Work Authorization (MKV - Machtiging voor Kort Verblijf)
SUR.purpose: Authorizes foreign nationals to enter Suriname for short-term work or internship purposes of up to 3 months, or as a precursor authorization for longer work stays.
SUR.notes: Applied for at a Surinamese embassy or consulate in the applicant's home country. Required for visa-obligated foreigners intending stays longer than 3 months. Also required for work and internship stays. The OSU (One Stop Unit) fast-track program launched in 2024/2025 allows concurrent processing of MKV, Work Permit, and Residence Permit for an additional USD 1,500 government fee, reducing processing from 6+ months to approximately 3-4 weeks.

SUR.name: Work Permit (Werkvergunning)
SUR.purpose: Authorizes a foreign national to be employed by a Surinamese employer or work in Suriname on a longer-term basis.
SUR.notes: Typically applied for alongside or after obtaining MKV short-stay authorization. Under the OSU fast-track program, the Work Permit is processed concurrently with MKV and Residence Permit. Employer sponsorship required. Exact fee schedule not published on official government website.

SUR.name: Temporary Residence Permit (Verblijfsvergunning voor bepaalde tijd)
SUR.purpose: Grants a foreign national the right to reside in Suriname for a fixed period of up to 2 years, renewable before expiration.
SUR.notes: Maximum duration is 2 years per permit. Application fee is USD 150 or SRD equivalent at Central Bank daily rate, plus SRD 1.50 stamp duty. Application requires formal request letter to the Minister of Justice and Police, passport copy, proof of means of subsistence, and payment receipt. Renewal must be filed at least 3 months before expiration. Filed in person at the Main Department of Alien Affairs, Ministry of Public Works, mr. J. Lachmonstraat no. 166-168, Paramaribo. Persons of Surinamese origin receive preferential treatment.

SUR.name: Permanent Residence Permit (Verblijfsvergunning voor onbepaalde tijd)
SUR.purpose: Grants a foreign national the right to reside indefinitely in Suriname without need for periodic renewal.
SUR.notes: Application fee is USD 150 or SRD equivalent at Central Bank daily rate, plus SRD 1.50 stamp duty. Requires prior temporary residence history in Suriname. Filed in person at the Main Department of Alien Affairs. Persons of Surinamese origin are exempt from the short-stay MKV requirement and may apply directly for temporary or permanent residence.

SUR.name: Transit (Visa-Free Airside/Landside)
SUR.purpose: Allows passengers transiting through Suriname's Johan Adolf Pengel International Airport or land border crossings to proceed without a visa or entry fee.
SUR.notes: Transit passengers are explicitly exempt from the Entry Fee (E-Tourist Card). Haitian nationals are refused entry including transit - they are refused even if not disembarking and proceeding on the same flight. All other nationalities in transit are exempt from the USD 50 entry fee. No transit visa category formally named; transit exemption is from the general entry fee rule.

SUR.name: Diplomatic/Official/Service Passport Entry (Fee-Exempt)
SUR.purpose: Entry for holders of diplomatic, official, service, or special passports of any nationality, who are exempt from the Entry Fee requirement.
SUR.notes: Holders of Diplomatic, Service, Special and Official passports from any country are exempt from the Entry Fee. The general 90-day tourism stay limit applies. Indian holders of diplomatic, official, and service passports benefit from a bilateral visa exemption agreement (signed 28 April 2017, in force 23 February 2019) allowing stays of up to 30 days without visa.

SUR.name: Temporary Stay Visa (KV - Kort Verblijf)
SUR.purpose: Entry visa issued to visa-required foreigners who hold an approved MKV and intend to stay in Suriname longer than 90 days (for work, study, family reunification or residence).
SUR.notes: Second step of Suriname's long-stay process: after an Authorization for Temporary Stay (MKV) is approved, the applicant applies for a KV sticker visa at a Surinamese embassy/consulate to actually enter the country. Fee EUR 40 (approx. USD 43). The KV is issued for the first entry only; on arrival a short term of 30 days is granted, and the holder must register with the Aliens' Registration Department (Ministry of Justice and Police) within two weeks to formalise the longer residence permit. Distinct from the MKV (the pre-approval) and from the residence permit (issued after arrival). Persons of Surinamese origin may instead enter on a tourist/business visa and apply for a residence permit within two weeks of arrival.

SUR.name: Student Visa / Study Residence (via MKV)
SUR.purpose: Foreign nationals admitted to a recognised Surinamese educational institution (e.g. Anton de Kom University of Suriname) for full-time study exceeding 90 days.
SUR.notes: Study stays over 90 days require an Authorization for Temporary Stay (MKV) obtained from a Surinamese embassy/consulate before travel, followed by a study residence permit issued after arrival (registered at the Aliens' Affairs Department, Ministry of Justice and Police). Requires a letter of acceptance from a recognised institution, proof of sufficient funds, health insurance and a police certificate of good conduct. Typically issued for one year and renewable for the duration of the programme. Apply at least three months before the course start date. The residence permit fee is USD 150 or SRD equivalent (per gov.sr Justice: https://gov.sr/ministeries/ministerie-van-justitie-en-politie/verblijfsvergunningen/).

SUR.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit (via MKV)
SUR.purpose: Spouses, registered partners, dependent children and dependent parents of a Surinamese national or of a foreigner legally residing in Suriname, joining them for stays exceeding 90 days.
SUR.notes: Requires an Authorization for Temporary Stay (MKV) applied for at a Surinamese embassy/consulate before travel (except persons of Surinamese origin, who may apply for a residence permit within two weeks of arrival). Supporting documents include a legalised marriage/partnership or birth certificate proving the family relationship and proof of sufficient financial means. A temporary residence permit (maximum 2 years, fee USD 150 or SRD equivalent plus SRD 1.50 stamp duty) is then issued by the Aliens' Affairs Department, renewable, and forms a route to permanent residence after continuous legal residence (generally about 5 years).

SVK.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
SVK.purpose: Short-term tourism, visiting friends or family, cultural events, and other non-work purposes within the Schengen Area. Valid for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the entire Schengen Area.
SVK.notes: Applied for at Slovak diplomatic missions or consulates abroad. Processing within 15 calendar days from receipt of application. Emergency issuance at border crossing possible for humanitarian cases only (up to 15 days). Applicant must provide valid travel document, photo, proof of purpose, financial means, return transport, health insurance, and accommodation confirmation not older than 90 days. Fee set by EU Regulation (EUR 80 for adults, EUR 40 for children 6–12 years). Slovakia as Schengen member state applies the common Schengen visa. Single or multiple entry at consular discretion.

SVK.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
SVK.purpose: Authorises nationals of specific countries to transit through the international transit zone of a Slovak (or any Schengen) airport without entering the Schengen Area.
SVK.notes: Required only for nationals of countries listed in Annex IV of the EU Visa Code. Applied for at Slovak diplomatic missions abroad. The holder does not enter Slovak territory; transit is confined to the international zone of the airport. Governed by the EU Visa Code (Regulation EC 810/2009).

SVK.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) – Business
SVK.purpose: Short-term business activities such as meetings, negotiations, conferences, and trade fairs in Slovakia or the Schengen Area, not constituting employment.
SVK.notes: Same Type C Schengen visa; purpose declared as business. Applicant must provide employment letter or invitation from Slovak company. Does not authorise paid work. For longer-term business activity or self-employment, see Temporary Residence for Business (Type D / residence permit).

SVK.name: National Long-Stay Visa (Type D)
SVK.purpose: Authorises stays exceeding three months in Slovakia for specific purposes such as awaiting residence permit, language studies, national interest, or international treaty obligations. Serves as a bridge to a residence permit.
SVK.notes: Maximum validity one year. Eligible categories include: persons with approved residence permit awaiting card issuance; language students aged 15+ enrolled in minimum 25 weekly hours; persons serving Slovakia's national interest; persons fulfilling international treaty obligations; family members of asylum seekers or persons under supplementary protection. Applications at Slovak diplomatic missions abroad, or at Border and Foreign Police in specific circumstances. Governed by Act No. 404/2011 on Residence of Foreigners. Online appointment booking mandatory via the national booking system since December 2022.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Employment
SVK.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside and work in Slovakia under a specific employment contract. Includes regular employment, seasonal work, and intra-company transfers.
SVK.notes: Permit valid up to 3 years, renewable. Standard processing 90 days; expedited (30 days) for certain categories. Applicant must have an employment contract or binding job offer. Labour market test may apply unless employer holds a labour shortage exemption. Applications at Slovak diplomatic missions abroad (as of July 2025 for new applications). Governed by Act No. 404/2011. Digital application platform operational since December 2024. After 5 years continuous legal residence, permanent residence may be sought.

SVK.name: EU Blue Card (Modrá karta EÚ)
SVK.purpose: Temporary residence and work permit for highly qualified third-country nationals employed in a skilled occupation requiring at least a university degree, with a salary of at least 1.2x the average monthly wage in Slovakia.
SVK.notes: Valid up to 5 years (or contract duration + 90 days if shorter). Fee EUR 250 initial (~USD 272), EUR 140 renewal. 30-day processing from complete application. No labour market test required as of 15 July 2024. Employment contract minimum 6 months. Salary threshold approximately EUR 1,716/month (1.2x 2023 average; updated annually). Employer must notify Labour Office. Blue Card holders may apply for long-term/permanent residence after 5 consecutive years. Governed by Act No. 404/2011 as amended.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Study (Štúdium)
SVK.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Slovakia for the purpose of studying at an accredited Slovak educational institution, including universities, secondary schools, and language courses.
SVK.notes: Permit valid up to 6 years. Processing 30 days from complete application. Administrative fees may be waived for students. Applicant must provide proof of admission to accredited institution, financial means, and accommodation. Governed by Act No. 404/2011. Digital application platform available since December 2024. Language students (15+ years) enrolled in minimum 25 weekly instruction hours may qualify for a National Visa (Type D) rather than a residence permit for shorter stays.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Research and Development
SVK.purpose: Allows third-country national researchers and scientists to reside in Slovakia to conduct research or development activities at accredited research organisations.
SVK.notes: Permit valid up to 2 years. Processing 30 days. Applicant must hold a hosting agreement with an accredited research organisation in Slovakia. Governed by Act No. 404/2011. Implements EU Directive 2016/801 on students and researchers.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Business / Entrepreneurship (Podnikanie)
SVK.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Slovakia for the purpose of operating a business as a self-employed person (sole trader) or as a company director/owner managing a Slovak company.
SVK.notes: As of 1 July 2025, applications must be submitted exclusively at Slovak diplomatic missions abroad. Ministry of Economy issues opinion within 60 days; Border and Foreign Police issues final decision within 90 days (total up to 150 days). Permit valid up to 3 years, renewable. Feasibility and sustainability of the business plan is assessed, including job creation or activity in labour-shortage sectors. No fixed minimum investment in law but economic benefit must be demonstrated. After 5 years continuous legal residence, permanent residence may be applied for.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Family Reunification (Zlúčenie rodiny)
SVK.purpose: Allows family members of legally residing third-country nationals or Slovak citizens to join and reside with them in Slovakia.
SVK.notes: Permit valid up to 3 years, tied to sponsor's permit duration. Standard processing 90 days. Family members of EU Blue Card holders and highly qualified workers may benefit from expedited 30-day processing. Administrative fee exemptions apply for minor children. Sponsor must demonstrate stable income, health insurance, and adequate accommodation. Governed by Act No. 404/2011.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Special Activities (Špeciálna činnosť)
SVK.purpose: Covers third-country nationals engaged in specific temporary activities in Slovakia not falling under standard employment, such as artists, athletes, journalists, or trainees on structured programmes.
SVK.notes: Permit valid up to 3 years. Governed by Act No. 404/2011. Applicant must provide documentation of the specific activity and sponsor/organiser in Slovakia.

SVK.name: Tolerated Residence (Tolerovaný pobyt)
SVK.purpose: Granted to third-country nationals who cannot be removed from Slovakia due to legal or humanitarian obstacles, and to victims of trafficking in persons, pending regularisation or removal.
SVK.notes: Issued by the Border and Foreign Police as a protection status rather than a typical visa or permit application. Valid in 6-month increments. Not a pathway to regular immigration status. Governed by Act No. 404/2011.

SVK.name: Permanent Residence – 5-Year (Trvalý pobyt na 5 rokov)
SVK.purpose: Grants long-term settlement rights in Slovakia to third-country nationals who have resided legally in the country for a qualifying period (generally 5 years of continuous temporary residence).
SVK.notes: Valid for 5 years, renewable. Standard processing 90 days; 30 days for families of significant investors. Requires proof of 5 years continuous legal residence, stable income, health insurance, and accommodation. After holding the 5-year permit for 4 years (total 9+ years legal residence), unlimited permanent residence may be sought. Governed by Act No. 404/2011.

SVK.name: Permanent Residence – Unlimited (Trvalý pobyt na neurčitý čas)
SVK.purpose: Grants indefinite settlement rights in Slovakia to qualifying long-term residents.
SVK.notes: Eligible after 4 years of holding a 5-year permanent residence permit, or for minor children of permanent residents. Standard processing 90 days; 30 days for investor category. Permit becomes invalid if holder is outside Slovakia for 180+ consecutive days without authorisation. Governed by Act No. 404/2011. Pathway to citizenship after total 8 years continuous legal residence.

SVK.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
SVK.purpose: Issued to diplomatic and official passport holders of countries requiring visas for Slovakia, for the purpose of official government business, postings, or assignments.
SVK.notes: Diplomatic and service/official passport holders of many countries benefit from visa exemptions under bilateral agreements (separate from ordinary passport exemptions). NATO and Partnership for Peace military/civilian personnel are exempt from visa requirements on official assignment using military ID or movement orders. The full bilateral diplomatic passport table is published at www.minv.sk/?bezvizovy-rezim; the page was not fully machine-readable during June 2026 validation.

SVK.name: Working Holiday National Visa (Type D)
SVK.purpose: Young people from countries with a bilateral working holiday / youth mobility agreement to spend up to one year in Slovakia, funding an extended holiday through incidental temporary work.
SVK.notes: Issued as a Slovak national (Type D) long-stay visa under bilateral Working Holiday / Youth Mobility agreements. Slovakia has agreements with Australia (age 18-30), New Zealand (18-35), Canada (18-35, Youth Mobility Program), Japan and Taiwan. Valid up to 1 year; permits residence plus incidental/temporary work in Slovakia and travel in the rest of the Schengen Area up to 90 days per 180. Annual quotas and reciprocal age/eligibility conditions apply per country. Applied for at a Slovak embassy or consulate abroad. Governed by the respective bilateral agreement and Act No. 404/2011.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Seasonal Employment
SVK.purpose: Third-country nationals performing season-dependent work (e.g. agriculture, tourism, hospitality) in Slovakia for more than 90 days.
SVK.notes: Seasonal employment exceeding 90 days requires temporary residence for the purpose of seasonal employment; total seasonal work may not exceed 180 days in any 12 consecutive months. The employer must first report the vacancy to the Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family (at least 20 working days before). Decision within 90 days, reduced to 30 days if the applicant performed seasonal work or held this residence within the previous 5 years. Administrative fee EUR 33 (Foreign Police) or EUR 35 (Slovak embassy) plus EUR 4.50 for the residence card. Governed by Act No. 404/2011 implementing EU Directive 2014/36/EU on seasonal workers.

SVK.name: Temporary Residence for Employment - Intra-Corporate Transfer (ICT)
SVK.purpose: Managers, specialists, or trainee employees of a company established outside the EU temporarily seconded (more than 90 days) to a Slovak branch or group company.
SVK.notes: Implements EU Directive 2014/66/EU on intra-corporate transfers. The worker must have been employed by the non-EU company for at least 6 months (managers/specialists) or 3 months (trainees) before transfer. Valid a maximum of 3 years for managers and specialists, and a maximum of 1 year for trainee employees. No separate work permit is required; the employer reports the posting to the Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family. Application is made in person at a Slovak embassy abroad; the Foreign Police decide within 90 days (30 days for significant foreign investors or OECD nationals). Fee EUR 170 for the residence application plus EUR 4.50 for the residence card. Permits intra-EU mobility to other member states under the ICT scheme. Governed by Act No. 404/2011.

SVK.name: Long-term Residence (Dlhodoby pobyt) - EU Long-Term Resident Status
SVK.purpose: Third-country nationals who have resided legally and continuously in Slovakia for 5 years, granting EU long-term resident status with enhanced rights and intra-EU mobility.
SVK.notes: EU long-term resident status under Council Directive 2003/109/EC, legally distinct from national permanent residence (trvaly pobyt). Granted after 5 years of continuous lawful residence immediately preceding the application, with proof of stable and regular income, accommodation, and - since 15 July 2025 - Slovak language knowledge at A2 level verified by examination. Confers rights close to those of nationals and the possibility to relocate to other EU member states. Application submitted in person at the Border and Foreign Police Department. Governed by Act No. 404/2011.

SVN.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C)
SVN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter and stay in Slovenia (and the Schengen Area) for tourism, family visits, business meetings, or other short-term purposes. Valid for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
SVN.notes: Fee is EUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for children aged 6-12 (approx USD 98/49 at current rates). Applications must be submitted in person at a Slovenian diplomatic mission or consular post at least 15 days before intended travel. Required documents include valid passport, application form, photo, travel medical insurance (min EUR 30,000 coverage), proof of accommodation, and proof of financial means. Normal processing is 15 days; may be extended to 45 days if additional examination is needed. Single-entry variants also available. As a Schengen member, a Type C visa issued by Slovenia is valid across all Schengen states.

SVN.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
SVN.purpose: Required for certain nationalities to pass through the international transit zone of Slovenian airports without entering the Schengen Area.
SVN.notes: Only required for nationals of specific countries listed in EU Regulation 2018/1806 Annex I who are transiting through a Slovenian airport. Many nationalities are exempt. Fee follows standard Schengen visa fee schedule (EUR 90 for adults). Processing times align with standard Schengen procedures.

SVN.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) - Business
SVN.purpose: Permits third-country nationals to travel to Slovenia for business meetings, conferences, trade fairs, contract negotiations, or other commercial activities not constituting employment.
SVN.notes: No separate business visa category - business travel uses the standard Schengen Type C short-stay visa. An invitation letter from a Slovenian business entity may be required as supporting documentation. Fee EUR 90 adults, EUR 45 children 6-12. Must not involve remunerated employment in Slovenia.

SVN.name: Single Permit (Combined Residence and Work Permit)
SVN.purpose: Enables third-country nationals to enter, reside in, and work in Slovenia under a single unified administrative procedure, combining both the residence and work permit.
SVN.notes: Issued for the duration of the employment contract, up to 2 years initially; first extension granted for up to 3 years. Employer must demonstrate no suitable EU/EEA worker was available (labour market test applies). A change of employer or employment terms requires written approval from the relevant administrative unit. Application submitted at Slovenian diplomatic mission abroad or administrative unit in Slovenia. Covers employees, self-employed (after 1 year legal residence), seasonal workers, intra-company transferees, posted workers, and trainees.

SVN.name: EU Blue Card
SVN.purpose: Allows highly qualified non-EU nationals to live and work in Slovenia in a highly paid, skilled position, with a streamlined path to intra-EU mobility and long-term residence.
SVN.notes: Requires a valid employment contract or binding job offer for at least 6 months (amended 2025) with salary of at least 1.5x the average annual gross salary in Slovenia. Requires higher professional qualifications (university degree) or, for ICT professionals, demonstrated competence via certificates or expert opinion. Issued for the duration of the contract plus 3 months, max 2 years; renewable for up to 3 years. Initial application fee approximately EUR 70-102; residence permit card EUR 15.47. Grants enhanced intra-EU mobility rights after 12 months.

SVN.name: Work Permit for Foreign Company Representative / Director
SVN.purpose: Allows non-EU nationals who serve as directors, procurators, or authorised representatives of a Slovenian registered company to live and work in Slovenia.
SVN.notes: For companies registered for less than 6 months: proof of minimum EUR 30,000 investment in company start-up is required. Companies with 10 or fewer workers may have no more than one such permit. Valid for up to 2 years; renewable. Application fee approximately EUR 90.

SVN.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Digital Nomads
SVN.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals who work remotely for employers or clients registered outside Slovenia to reside in Slovenia for up to one year without entering the Slovenian labour market.
SVN.notes: Launched 21 November 2025. Applicant must have monthly funds of at least twice the average monthly net salary in Slovenia (approximately EUR 3,200/month as of early 2026). Must hold valid health insurance and have a clean criminal record. Work must be performed entirely via remote communication technologies for employers/clients outside Slovenia. Permit is not renewable; reapplication allowed 6 months after expiry. Family members may join immediately without duration restrictions. Applications submitted at Slovenian diplomatic missions abroad or any administrative unit in Slovenia.

SVN.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) - Study / Temporary Residence Permit for Study
SVN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to enter Slovenia to pursue studies, vocational training, or other educational programmes at accredited institutions.
SVN.notes: A Type D (national long-stay) visa authorises residence from 91 days up to 1 year and enables the holder to apply directly at an administrative unit in Slovenia for a temporary residence permit upon arrival. Students must provide proof of enrolment, financial means, accommodation, and health insurance. Fee EUR 90 adults (approx USD 98). After arriving, a formal temporary residence permit for study must be obtained from the administrative unit.

SVN.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification
SVN.purpose: Permits third-country nationals who are family members of a legally residing non-EU national (or Slovenian citizen) to join and reside with their family member in Slovenia.
SVN.notes: Eligible family members include spouses, registered partners, children under 21, dependent relatives, and long-term partners. Non-EU family members of EU/EEA citizens have a different and more favourable regime: they receive a residence permit for family members of EU citizens. Third-country national family members must apply at a Slovenian diplomatic mission abroad. Digital nomad permit holders may bring family members immediately without duration restrictions.

SVN.name: Long-Stay National Visa (Type D)
SVN.purpose: A national visa authorising third-country nationals to enter and reside in Slovenia for a period between 91 days and 1 year, issued for a specific purpose (work, study, family, etc.) before a full residence permit is granted.
SVN.notes: The Type D visa serves as the entry document that enables a foreigner to enter Slovenia and then apply directly at an administrative unit for a temporary residence permit. It is purpose-specific (work, study, family reunification, etc.) and not a standalone long-term status. Fee EUR 90 for adults (approx USD 98). Processing normally 15 days, up to 45 days if additional examination needed. Applied for at Slovenian diplomatic missions abroad.

SVN.name: Temporary Residence Permit via Business Investment (Company Director / Procurator)
SVN.purpose: Grants residence and work rights to non-EU nationals who establish or invest in a Slovenian company and act as its director or authorised representative.
SVN.notes: Slovenia has no standalone investor visa or golden visa program. Residence via investment flows from active business engagement (company director role). For companies registered less than 6 months: minimum investment of EUR 30,000 required as proof of company start-up capital. Permit valid up to 2 years, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 5 years continuous legal residence; citizenship available after 10 years total. Applications submitted at Slovenian diplomatic missions abroad or administrative units.

SVN.name: Work Permit for Seasonal Work in Agriculture
SVN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to perform seasonal work in agriculture (e.g. planting, harvesting) in Slovenia for a short period on the basis of a work permit obtained by the employer.
SVN.notes: For seasonal agricultural work of up to 90 days, the employer obtains a work permit for seasonal work from the Employment Service of Slovenia (ZRSZ); no separate residence permit is required for stays up to 90 days. If seasonal work exceeds 90 days within a year, the worker must obtain a single permit for residence and work issued with the Employment Service's consent for seasonal work. Governed by the Employment, Self-employment and Work of Foreigners Act (ZZSDT).

SVN.name: Single Permit for Intra-Corporate Transfer (ICT)
SVN.purpose: Allows managers, specialists, and trainee employees of a non-EU company to be transferred to a Slovenian host entity of the same corporate group to live and work in Slovenia.
SVN.notes: Applicant must have been employed within the corporate group for at least 9 months (managers and specialists) or 6 months (trainees) before the transfer. Initial permit issued for the duration of the transfer, up to 1 year; maximum total stay in the EU is 3 years for managers and specialists, and 1 year for trainees. Family members may reunite without a prior-residence time limit. Based on Articles 45b-45d of the Foreigners Act (ZTuj-2) transposing EU Directive 2014/66/EU on intra-corporate transfers.

SVN.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Research (Researcher)
SVN.purpose: Allows third-country researchers, higher-education lecturers, and scientific workers to reside in Slovenia to carry out research or educational work under a hosting agreement with a Slovenian research organisation or higher-education institution.
SVN.notes: Requires a signed hosting agreement with a research organisation or higher-education institution in Slovenia. The first permit is issued for the duration of the research work, up to 1 year, and is renewable for successive periods of up to 1 year while the research continues. The application may be lodged by the researcher or by the host institution. Slovenia has not transposed the Students and Researchers Directive (EU) 2016/801, so EU-wide researcher mobility provisions do not apply.

SVN.name: Single Permit for Self-Employed Work
SVN.purpose: Allows third-country nationals to reside in Slovenia and work independently as a self-employed person or registered professional (e.g. sole proprietor, freelancer, regulated professional).
SVN.notes: Generally requires at least one year of prior legal residence in Slovenia on a valid residence permit before engaging in self-employment, unless the applicant is already registered as a regulated professional (e.g. lawyer, doctor) in the business register. First permit issued for up to 1 year; extensions granted for up to 2 years. Fee EUR 102 if lodged at a diplomatic mission or EUR 70 at an administrative unit, plus EUR 12 for the permit card. Requires proof of sufficient means, health insurance, and a clean criminal record.

SVN.name: Working Holiday Visa (Type D National Visa)
SVN.purpose: Allows young citizens of countries with a bilateral youth mobility agreement (Australia, Canada, New Zealand) to holiday in Slovenia for up to one year and undertake incidental employment to help fund their stay.
SVN.notes: Issued as a Slovenian long-stay (Type D) national visa valid for up to 12 months; also permits travel elsewhere in the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Available only under bilateral youth-mobility agreements. Canada: Canada-Slovenia Youth Mobility Agreement (signed 22 October 2009), ages 18-35, up to two participations under different categories (working holiday, young professionals, student work placement). Australia: annual quota approx. 200 places, ages 18-30, applications lodged via the Slovenian Embassy in Canberra. New Zealand: annual quota approx. 100 places, ages 18-30. Work must be incidental to the holiday. Approx. national visa fee EUR 77.

SWE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) – Tourism
SWE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals from visa-required countries to visit Sweden and the Schengen area for tourism, family visits, or cultural events for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
SWE.notes: Fee is EUR 90 for adults (approx. USD 99), EUR 45 for children 6-11, free for children under 6. Standard processing is 15 days; may extend up to 30 days for complex cases. Multiple-entry visas valid up to 5 years may be issued to frequent travellers. Reduced fee (EUR 35) applies to citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Cape Verde, Georgia, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, and Ukraine. Must show proof of accommodation, return travel, and financial means of SEK 450 per day. Applied through Swedish embassies or VFS Global.

SWE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) – Business
SWE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Sweden for business meetings, conferences, negotiations, or trade activities for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
SWE.notes: Same fee structure and processing times as tourism Schengen visa. Requires an invitation letter from the Swedish company or organisation. Does not permit gainful employment; only business activities such as meetings and conferences.

SWE.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C) – Medical Treatment
SWE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Sweden to receive medical treatment for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
SWE.notes: Requires two medical certificates confirming diagnosis and treatment necessity, and proof of a deposit or payment guarantee for treatment costs. Same base fee as standard Schengen visa (EUR 90 adults). If medical stay exceeds 90 days, a visitor's residence permit must be applied for instead.

SWE.name: Airport Transit Visa (Type A)
SWE.purpose: Allows nationals of certain countries to transit through Swedish international airport zones without entering the Schengen area.
SWE.notes: Required for nationals of specific high-risk countries transiting through Schengen airports (e.g., Afghanistan, Iraq, Iran, Somalia, and others as listed in EU Regulation 2018/1806 Annex IV). Holders of valid Schengen visas, residence permits from Schengen states, or certain other countries' valid travel documents may be exempt. Fee is EUR 90 (same as Type C). Applied through Swedish embassies.

SWE.name: Visitor's Residence Permit (Long-Stay Tourist)
SWE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Sweden for tourism or to visit family/friends for stays exceeding 90 days, up to a maximum of 6 months (or 9 months in exceptional cases).
SWE.notes: Fee is SEK 1,500 for adults (approx. USD 165), SEK 750 for children. Standard tourist purpose: up to 6 months; exceptionally up to 9 months. Processing: 75% of cases decided within 3 months (outside Sweden) or 4 months (from within Sweden). Requires valid passport, medical travel insurance (EUR 30,000 minimum), and financial means of SEK 450/day. Must demonstrate genuine intent to leave after the visit.

SWE.name: Visitor's Residence Permit – Family/Relative Visit
SWE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit a relative, spouse, or close family member residing in Sweden for extended stays exceeding 90 days.
SWE.notes: Parents visiting their children in Sweden may be granted up to 1 year. Relatives visiting family members may receive up to 6 months. Fee SEK 1,500 adults / SEK 750 children. Requires invitation from the host in Sweden along with the host's ID and income documentation. Processing: 75% within 3-4 months.

SWE.name: Visitor's Residence Permit – Medical Treatment (Long-Stay)
SWE.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to stay in Sweden for medical treatment for extended periods exceeding 90 days, up to a maximum of 1 year.
SWE.notes: Maximum stay 1 year. Requires medical certificates and proof of treatment costs. Fee SEK 1,500 adults / SEK 750 children.

SWE.name: Work Permit (Employee)
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals with a job offer from a Swedish employer to live and work in Sweden.
SWE.notes: Fee is SEK 2,000 (approx. USD 220). As of 1 June 2026, minimum salary is SEK 34,470/month (90% of median salary). Comprehensive health insurance required from 1 June 2026. Permit typically issued for up to 2 years, renewable. Eligible for permanent residence after 4 years of work permit. Processing averages 18 days for fast-tracked complete applications. The employer must advertise the position in the EU/EEA before offering to a third-country national (new rule from June 2026).

SWE.name: Work Permit (Self-Employed)
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to reside in Sweden and run their own business.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 2,000. Must own and actively manage at least 51% of the business. Financial self-sufficiency requirement: SEK 200,000 for applicant plus SEK 100,000 per accompanying spouse and SEK 50,000 per child. Requires good industry experience, language skills, and a credible business plan with established customer contacts. Permit up to 2 years, renewable. Path to permanent residence after 4 years.

SWE.name: EU Blue Card
SWE.purpose: Allows highly qualified non-EU/EEA nationals with a high-salary job offer to live and work in Sweden with facilitated pathways to permanent residence.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 2,000. Minimum salary: SEK 52,000/month (1.25x average Swedish salary, effective 9 July 2025). Requires higher education (minimum 180 credits) or 5+ years relevant professional experience. Employment contract for minimum 6 months required. Comprehensive health insurance required. Permit duration: 9 months to 4 years. Processing: 75% of complete applications decided within 1 month. Path to permanent residence after 4 years.

SWE.name: Seasonal Work Permit
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to perform seasonal agricultural or horticultural work in Sweden for a limited period.
SWE.notes: Sweden implements the EU Seasonal Workers Directive. Seasonal work permits are issued for up to 90 days and cover sectors such as agriculture, horticulture, and tourism. Must have a job offer meeting Swedish collective agreement or industry-standard wages. Specific fee and processing times not published on the main Migrationsverket page.

SWE.name: ICT Permit (Intra-Company Transfer)
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to be temporarily posted to a Swedish entity of a multinational company as a manager, specialist, or trainee.
SWE.notes: Sweden implements the EU ICT Directive. Minimum salary thresholds apply and were updated from 1 June 2026. Managers and specialists may be granted up to 3 years; trainees up to 1 year. ICT permit holders may move between EU member states under the directive's mobility provisions. Specific fee not published on the main listing page.

SWE.name: Residence Permit to Look for Work or Start a Business
SWE.purpose: Allows highly-educated non-EU/EEA nationals to enter Sweden for up to 9 months to search for employment or explore business establishment, without a prior job offer.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 2,200 (approx. USD 242). Requires a second-cycle qualification (60+ credit Master's, professional degree, or PhD). Must show financial self-sufficiency of SEK 13,000/month and hold comprehensive health insurance. If employment or business is secured during the permit period, holder may apply for a work/self-employment residence permit from within Sweden. Processing: 75% decided within 7 months. Not a digital nomad visa per se, but functionally similar for job-seeking professionals.

SWE.name: Student Residence Permit – Higher Education
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to reside in Sweden to pursue bachelor's or master's degree studies at a Swedish higher education institution.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 1,500 adults / SEK 750 children under 18. Processing: 75% decided within 2 months. Maximum 1-2 years per permit depending on institution (designated universities can issue up to 2 years). Cannot exceed passport validity. Full-time enrollment required (30 credits/semester). Tuition fees must be paid before applying. Financial requirement: SEK 10,656/month (2026). Work limited to 15 hours/week for bachelor's/master's students from June 11, 2026. Permit renewable for duration of studies.

SWE.name: Student Residence Permit – Doctoral Studies
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to reside in Sweden to pursue doctoral research at a Swedish university.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 1,500. Doctoral students may be eligible to apply for permanent residence directly after completing doctoral studies. Accompanying family members can apply simultaneously. Processing similar to higher education student permit.

SWE.name: Student Residence Permit – Other Studies and Upper Secondary School
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to reside in Sweden to attend upper secondary school or other study programmes lasting more than 90 days.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 1,500 adults / SEK 750 children. Covers exchange programmes, upper secondary studies, contract or specialisation education. Full-time study required (minimum 20 teaching hours weekly). Health insurance required for studies under one year. Financial requirement SEK 10,656/month.

SWE.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit
SWE.purpose: Allows the partner, spouse, children, or other close relatives of a person with a Swedish residence permit or citizenship to join them and live in Sweden.
SWE.notes: Fee SEK 1,500 adults / SEK 750 children. Covers partners/spouses, children, parents visiting adult children, and other relatives. The sponsor (anchor person) in Sweden must generally have a permanent residence permit, Swedish citizenship, or a valid temporary residence permit of sufficient duration. Maintenance requirement: sponsor must demonstrate adequate housing and income. Processing times can be lengthy (12+ months for complex family cases).

SWE.name: Temporary Protection Permit (Ukraine/EU Directive)
SWE.purpose: Grants temporary residence in Sweden to displaced persons from Ukraine under the EU Temporary Protection Directive, allowing right to work and access to social services.
SWE.notes: No application fee. Granted to Ukrainian nationals and stateless persons who were residing in Ukraine before 24 February 2022. Provides access to employment, housing, social welfare, and healthcare. Duration aligned with EU Council decisions on temporary protection extension.

SWE.name: Diplomatic/Official Visa Exemption
SWE.purpose: Visa-free entry for holders of diplomatic, service, official, or special passports from designated countries under bilateral agreements or Sweden's national visa list.
SWE.notes: Countries whose nationals ordinarily require a Schengen visa but whose diplomatic/service/special passport holders are exempt include: Bolivia, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Turkey (including special passport holders), China (diplomatic only), India (diplomatic only), Morocco (diplomatic only), Tunisia (diplomatic only), Armenia (diplomatic only, per EC-Armenia agreement), Azerbaijan (diplomatic only, per EC-Azerbaijan agreement), Belarus (diplomatic only, per EC-Belarus agreement - NOTE: suspended in practice due to EU sanctions since 2021), Cape Verde (diplomatic only). Based on Swedish Government official visa list last updated 01 September 2023.

SWE.name: Working Holiday Residence Permit
SWE.purpose: Allows young people (18-30) from partner countries to holiday in Sweden for up to one year and work incidentally to fund their stay and experience Swedish life and culture.
SWE.notes: For citizens aged 18-30 of countries with a youth-exchange agreement with Sweden: Australia, Canada, Hong Kong, Japan, New Zealand, and South Korea. Fee SEK 1,500 (approx. USD 165); Japanese citizens are exempt from the fee. Applicant must have at least SEK 15,000 to support themselves on arrival. Work is permitted but must not be the main purpose of the stay. Maximum one year and cannot be extended. Comprehensive health insurance required (Australian citizens exempt). Processing: 75% of complete applications decided within 3 months.

SWE.name: Au Pair Residence Permit
SWE.purpose: Allows a young person (18-29) to live with a Swedish host family for up to one year, helping with childcare and light housework while studying Swedish and experiencing Swedish culture.
SWE.notes: For applicants aged 18-29 (must be under 30 at time of decision) with a written agreement with a host family. Childcare and light housework are limited to a maximum of 25 hours per week, and the applicant must spend most non-working time studying Swedish (combined work + study capped at 40 hours/week). Fee SEK 1,500 (approx. USD 165). Maximum one year; cannot be extended. Must apply from outside Sweden and family members cannot accompany. Host family must provide work-accident insurance; the applicant needs comprehensive health insurance.

SWE.name: Residence Permit for Research (Guest Researcher)
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals invited by an approved Swedish research principal to conduct research in Sweden under a hosting agreement.
SWE.notes: Requires a signed hosting agreement with a research principal approved by the Swedish Research Council; at least 50% of working hours must be devoted to research. Fee SEK 1,500 adults / SEK 750 children (approx. USD 165); Japanese citizens exempt. Financial requirement approximately SEK 9,700/month. Permit granted for up to 4 years at a time, not exceeding passport or hosting-agreement validity. Processing: 75% of complete applications decided within 1 month. From 11 June 2026, doctoral students who hold a hosting agreement receive this same research permit rather than a study permit.

SWE.name: Residence Permit for Traineeship/Internship
SWE.purpose: Allows non-EU/EEA nationals to come to Sweden for a traineeship or internship, either connected to their higher education or arranged via an international exchange programme.
SWE.notes: Two routes: a traineeship/internship related to the applicant's higher education, or one offered through an international exchange programme. Applied for from outside Sweden before entering. Specific fee and maximum duration depend on the route and are set out on the relevant Migration Agency sub-pages.

SWZ.name: Tourist Visa (Standard)
SWZ.purpose: For foreign nationals from visa-required countries visiting Eswatini for holiday or tourism purposes. Not for work-related intentions.
SWZ.notes: Applied for at the Ministry of Home Affairs Visa & Citizenship department or through Eswatini foreign missions. Fee: E80.00 (single entry, 3-month validity). Requires completed application form, cover letter, valid passport with at least 2 blank pages, proof of financial means, and return/onward ticket. Visa on arrival has been suspended; the eVisa (online) route is now the primary channel for pre-travel applications.

SWZ.name: Tourist eVisa
SWZ.purpose: Online tourist visa for foreign nationals from eligible countries visiting Eswatini for tourism, valid for a single entry within 90 days of issuance.
SWZ.notes: Must be obtained before travel; visa on arrival is not available. Extensions are not permitted - must exit and re-enter if longer stay is needed. Requires scanned passport copy, passport-sized photo, and proof of travel arrangements. Fee schedule not publicly published on official portal.

SWZ.name: Business Visa (Standard)
SWZ.purpose: For foreign nationals from visa-required countries visiting Eswatini for business purposes, including business meetings and related activities.
SWZ.notes: Multiple entry options available: E300 (3 months), E700 (6 months), E1000 (9 months), E1300 (12 months). Applied for at Ministry of Home Affairs or Eswatini foreign missions. Single entry business visa also available at E80 (3 months).

SWZ.name: Business eVisa
SWZ.purpose: Online business visa for foreign nationals from eligible countries traveling to Eswatini for business activities.
SWZ.notes: Must be obtained before travel. Fee schedule not publicly published on official portal.

SWZ.name: Transit Visa
SWZ.purpose: For foreign nationals passing through Eswatini en route to another destination, who require a visa to enter.
SWZ.notes: Applicants must clearly state transit purpose and explain why Eswatini is the transit point. Those who fail to indicate transit status risk being returned to their entry point. Also available as a transit eVisa via evisa.gov.sz.

SWZ.name: Transit eVisa
SWZ.purpose: Online transit visa for foreign nationals from eligible countries passing through Eswatini en route to another destination.
SWZ.notes: One of the four eVisa categories (tourist, business, student, transit) offered via the Ministry of Home Affairs portal evisa.gov.sz. Single entry, valid 90 days from issuance. Applicants must state the transit purpose. Must be obtained before travel; visa on arrival is suspended. Fee schedule not publicly published on the official portal.

SWZ.name: Work Permit / Temporary Residence Permit (Employees)
SWZ.purpose: Temporary residence permit for foreign nationals employed by an Eswatini-registered employer; required for stays exceeding 30 days or for working in the country.
SWZ.notes: Granted by committee on merit. Requires Application Form 3, employer's covering letter, proof of job advertisement, internationally recognized police clearance, qualification certificates, medical certificate, and Certificate of Incorporation documentation. Distinct from an entry visa - permits are for longer-term stay/residency.

SWZ.name: Business Person Permit / Temporary Residence Permit (Business)
SWZ.purpose: Temporary residence permit for foreign nationals establishing or operating a business in Eswatini, allowing longer-term residency beyond the 30-day visitor limit.
SWZ.notes: Requires Application Form 3, Memorandum of Association, two passport photos, covering letter, police clearance from country of origin, lease agreement, medical certificate, Certificate of Incorporation (Forms J and C), and passport copy. All copies must be certified.

SWZ.name: Student Pass / Temporary Residence Permit (Students)
SWZ.purpose: Temporary residence permit for foreign nationals studying at an accredited Eswatini educational institution.
SWZ.notes: Requires Application Form 10, two passport photos, letter from school/institution, Ministry of Education support letter, police clearance (for applicants aged 18 and over), medical certificate, and passport copy. A student eVisa may also be available via evisa.gov.sz (referenced in navigation but no further details found on the official portal).

SWZ.name: Student eVisa
SWZ.purpose: Online student entry visa for foreign nationals from eligible countries travelling to Eswatini to study at an accredited institution.
SWZ.notes: One of the four eVisa categories (tourist, business, student, transit) offered via the Ministry of Home Affairs portal evisa.gov.sz. Single entry, valid 90 days from issuance, stay up to 30 days. For study periods beyond the eVisa stay, a Student Pass / Temporary Residence Permit must be obtained from the Ministry of Home Affairs. Fee schedule not publicly published on the official portal.

SWZ.name: Dependants Pass / Temporary Residence Permit (Dependants)
SWZ.purpose: Temporary residence permit for dependants (spouse, children) of a foreign national holding a valid Eswatini residence permit.
SWZ.notes: Requires Application Form 6, copy of guardian's residence permit, two passport photos, guardian's covering letter, marriage certificate copy, police clearance for applicants over 18, medical certificate, and passport copy.

SWZ.name: Visitor's Pass / Temporary Residence Permit (Visitors)
SWZ.purpose: Temporary residence permit for foreign nationals visiting a host in Eswatini for stays exceeding the 30-day tourist visa limit.
SWZ.notes: Requires Application Form 10, two passport photos, host's application letter, host's copy of residence status, medical certificate, and passport copy. Different from a standard tourist visa in that it is a longer-term residence permit granted to guests of Eswatini residents.

SWZ.name: Special Pass
SWZ.purpose: A special temporary permit issued in cases such as pending appeals or exceptional circumstances not covered by standard permit categories.
SWZ.notes: Requires Application Form 10, a recent copy of the relevant appeal or application, application letter, two passport photos, and passport copy.

SYC.name: Visitor's Permit
SYC.purpose: Issued on arrival to visitors entering Seychelles for holiday, pleasure, visiting friends and family, or short-term business. Covers tourism and leisure activities.
SYC.notes: Initial 3-month (90-day) permit granted free of charge on arrival. Extendable in 3-month increments up to a maximum of 12 months total stay; each extension costs SCR 5,000. Extensions available online at permits.ics.gov.sc or in person at Independence House, Victoria, Mahé. Mandatory pre-travel ETA/TA required (EUR 10 standard / EUR 30 premium) via seychelles.govtas.com. Visitors must show proof of return/onward ticket, confirmed accommodation, and minimum funds of USD 150/day. Kosovo nationals excluded.

SYC.name: Visitor's Permit (Business Purpose)
SYC.purpose: Covers short-term business visits to Seychelles including meetings, negotiations, and commercial activities that do not constitute gainful occupation.
SYC.notes: Business visitors are covered under the same Visitor's Permit framework as tourists - no separate business visa exists. The permit does not authorise employment or self-employment; a Gainful Occupation Permit (GOP) is required for any work. Mandatory pre-travel ETA/TA required (EUR 10 standard / EUR 30 premium). Extendable up to 12 months total in 3-month increments at SCR 5,000 each.

SYC.name: Gainful Occupation Permit (GOP)
SYC.purpose: Authorises non-Seychellois nationals to reside and work in Seychelles either as an employee of a Seychellois organisation or as a self-employed person.
SYC.notes: All expatriate workers in Seychelles require a GOP. Two categories: employed (as an employee) and self-employed. Employer must first obtain approval from the Ministry of Employment and Social Affairs before applying. Application submitted at least 1 week before employment start. Fees: SCR 1,000 processing fee + SCR 500 per month or part thereof (permit fee, payable upfront for the full duration). Applied for in person at Independence House, Victoria. Holders of Permanent Residence by Investment are exempt from GOP fees. Extensions follow the same procedure as initial applications.

SYC.name: Student's Permit
SYC.purpose: Granted to non-Seychellois nationals accepted to follow a course of study at an approved educational institution in Seychelles. Does not authorise employment.
SYC.notes: Valid for one year or part thereof. Fees: SCR 1,000 processing fee + SCR 1,500 permit fee for one year. Required documents: completed application form, documentary proof of acceptance from the educational institution, evidence of financial means, passport bio-data copy, two recent passport photographs, full birth certificate (with translation if necessary), proof of accommodation (may be requested). Eligible for dependants of permit-holders in Seychelles who are aged 18+ and continuing studies. Employment not permitted under this permit.

SYC.name: Dependant's Permit
SYC.purpose: Issued to the non-Seychellois spouse and/or minor child(ren) of a Seychelles citizen so they may reside in Seychelles together with the citizen.
SYC.notes: Applied for by a Seychelles citizen on behalf of their non-citizen spouse and/or minor children who are to reside with them in Seychelles. Fees: SCR 1,000 processing fee + SCR 1,000 per year permit fee. Does NOT authorise employment - a separate Gainful Occupation Permit (GOP) is required to work. The applicant must not be a prohibited immigrant or already hold a Residence Permit or a GOP. The permit ceases to be valid if the holder fails to enter Seychelles within 12 months of issue, is absent for more than 12 months, breaches its conditions, is convicted of an offence against the Immigration Laws, or is deported. Distinct from the Residence Permit (which is for those with a family/domestic connection or special contribution but not necessarily a citizen's immediate dependant).

SYC.name: Residence Permit (Family/Special Contribution)
SYC.purpose: Granted to non-Seychellois with family or domestic connections to Seychelles, or those who have made or will make a special contribution to the economic, social or cultural life of Seychelles.
SYC.notes: Valid for 5 years (1,825 days). Does NOT authorise gainful occupation - a separate GOP is required for any work. Holder must reside in Seychelles for at least 5 days per 12-month period. Bank guarantee of SCR 20,000 required. Fees: SCR 1,000 processing fee + SCR 150,000 permit fee (main applicant, 5-year term) + SCR 75,000 for spouse (if applied simultaneously) + SCR 25,000 per child endorsement. No entitlement to free medical services or social security benefits. Contact: m.laporte@gov.sc / (+248) 4293636.

SYC.name: Permanent Residence Permit by Investment
SYC.purpose: Grants permanent residence to foreign nationals who have made a qualifying investment in Seychelles and meet residence requirements, exempting them from Gainful Occupation Permits.
SYC.notes: Requires: (1) direct investment of USD 1 million or more in a Seychelles business; (2) at least 5 years of business association from that investment; (3) residency in Seychelles for at least 5 years on a Dependent Permit or GOP; (4) not been absent continuously for 1+ year without ministerial consent; (5) not sentenced to imprisonment exceeding 1 year. Fees: SCR 1,000 processing fee (non-refundable, paid in cash upfront); SCR 350,000 permit fee if approved. Benefits: exempt from GOP fees; may purchase residential land from government at 50% sanction fee reduction; work authorisation without separate GOP.

SYC.name: Permanent Residence Permit (General)
SYC.purpose: Grants permanent residency to long-term residents of Seychelles who meet general eligibility criteria, providing the right to live and work without additional permits.
SYC.notes: Eligibility: must not be a prohibited immigrant; absence from Seychelles cannot exceed 1 year without ministerial consent; must not have been sentenced to imprisonment exceeding 1 year. Rights: authorises work without a separate GOP; exempt from other permits required for residency or employment; eligible to purchase land/property with government approval at 50% sanction fee reduction. Specific fees not published on the ICS page - contact Permanent Residence and Citizenship Section at (+248) 4293636.

SYC.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (TA/ETA)
SYC.purpose: Mandatory pre-travel authorisation required for ALL visitors to Seychelles before departure. Enhances border security and provides government visibility of incoming travellers. Not a visa - does not replace the Visitor's Permit issued on arrival.
SYC.notes: Required by ALL nationalities (except Kosovo who are refused entry). Fee: EUR 10 for standard processing (up to 24 hours); EUR 30 for premium processing (approximately 6 hours). The EUR 10.90 figure seen on some pages reflects a payment processing surcharge on top of the EUR 10 base fee. Apply at seychelles.govtas.com or via the Seychelles e-Border mobile app. Applications accepted up to 10 days before travel (up to 30 days before for sea arrivals). Required documents: valid passport, selfie photograph, contact information, trip details, airline booking confirmation (showing arrival/departure dates), accommodation confirmation. Failure to obtain the TA before departure may result in a penalty fee on arrival. Extended to sea arrivals (cruise ship/private yacht) effective December 1, 2024: all international passengers arriving by sea must apply online prior to arrival (Maritime Travel Authorisation); seafarers/crew disembarking and leaving by air the same day are exempt.

SYC.name: Workcation Retreat Program (Visitor Workcation Permit)
SYC.purpose: Allows remote workers, freelancers, and owners of businesses registered outside Seychelles to live in Seychelles while continuing to work remotely for foreign employers or clients.
SYC.notes: Official Government of Seychelles digital-nomad programme, launched 2021 and administered through the national e-Border System (seychelles.govtas.com) - the same government portal that issues the Travel Authorisation. Valid for up to 1 year. One-time fee of approximately EUR 45 (~USD 48) covering the Visitor Workcation Permit plus a Health Travel Authorisation. Eligibility: the applicant must work remotely for a foreign employer, be a freelancer, or own a business that is NOT registered in Seychelles; and must hold valid international medical/travel (health) insurance for the stay. Holders may NOT take up local employment or run a Seychelles-registered business. Required documents: passport valid 6+ months, proof of remote employment/business/freelance status (employment letter, business registration + bank statements, or certificate of good standing), proof of accommodation, proof of sufficient financial means (bank/investment statements), and a return/onward flight booking. Apply fully online via the e-Border portal; programme also described at seychelles.com/special_interest/workcation.

SYR.name: Single Entry Tourist Visa
SYR.purpose: Tourism and general visits to Syria for a single entry and exit. Issued as a stamp on a separate sheet of paper rather than in the passport.
SYR.notes: Available on arrival at Damascus and Aleppo airports and at land borders with Lebanon and Jordan. Fee varies by nationality: visa-free/fee-exempt nationalities pay $0; many nationalities $25–$400 (payable in USD cash). Restricted nationalities (India, China, Pakistan, Philippines, Vietnam, Afghanistan, Russia and others) require prior entry approval (OK to board) before departure — processing 3 days to 1 month. At airports, ALL nationalities require prior visa approval before boarding regardless of restricted status. Israeli nationals are barred from entry. Iranian nationals require an advance visa from a Syrian embassy and are not eligible for visa on arrival. Passports with Israeli stamps result in denial of entry.

SYR.name: Double Entry Tourist Visa
SYR.purpose: Tourism allowing two separate entries into Syria within the validity period.
SYR.notes: Permits two entries within the 3-month validity window. Fee varies by nationality. Must be arranged through a tour operator or Syrian embassy/consulate. Not documented on official Syrian government websites.

SYR.name: Multiple Entry Tourist Visa
SYR.purpose: Tourism allowing unlimited entries into Syria within the 6-month validity period.
SYR.notes: Permits multiple entries within the 6-month validity window. The official Ministry of Tourism entry-visa page describes a 'six months visa' valid for one or multiple trips that may exceptionally be extended to one year. Fee varies by nationality. Historically arranged through a tour operator or Syrian embassy/consulate; since 1 May 2024 the Ministry of Foreign Affairs directs foreigners to apply via the e-visa portal (evisa.sy), which remains non-operational.

SYR.name: Transit Visa
SYR.purpose: Brief passage through Syria for travelers entering from one border point and exiting from a different border point or airport.
SYR.notes: Designed for travelers passing through Syria and exiting from a different border/airport than entry. Fee varies by nationality (approximately $15–$250). Not documented in detail on official Syrian government websites.

SYR.name: Work Permit (Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor Authorization)
SYR.purpose: Foreign nationals taking up paid employment in Syria. A residence permit by itself does not authorize work; a separate work permit is required.
SYR.notes: Domestic work authorization rather than a consular visa. The official Ministry of Tourism entry-visa page states that granted residence permission is not a license to work and that those who wish to engage in employment in the Syrian Arab Republic must obtain permission from the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor. The work permit is employer-sponsored (the employer applies on the foreign worker's behalf) and must be held alongside a residence permit. Foreign hiring is legally restricted (permitted only where no suitably qualified Syrian is available; historically capped near 10% of an employer's workforce) under a Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor resolution.
