TWN.notes: Official page states visas for religious work shall in principle be single-entry. Requires supporting documentation from a recognized religious organization. Standard visitor visa fee applies (single-entry US$50). For longer stays a Resident Visa for Religious Work is issued separately. Stay duration and validity not stated verbatim on the official page.

TWN.name: Visitor Visa - Attending Training Courses
TWN.purpose: For foreign nationals attending training programs sponsored or approved by Taiwan government agencies.
TWN.notes: For training programs run by government agencies such as the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Health and Welfare, Sports Administration, or Ministry of Education. Requires an official permit or approval letter from the competent agency; interview may be required. Standard visitor visa fee applies (single-entry US$50). Stay duration and validity not stated verbatim on the official page.

TWN.name: Visitor Visa - Foreign Exchange Students (under 6 months)
TWN.purpose: For foreign exchange students studying full-time in Taiwan for a period of less than six months.
TWN.notes: For exchange stays of less than six months (longer study is handled by a Resident Visa). Applicant must be enrolled as a full-time exchange student; a school admission permit does not guarantee visa issuance. Standard visitor visa fee applies (single-entry US$50). Exact maximum stay in days not stated verbatim on the official page.

TWN.name: Resident Visa - Overseas Chinese Students
TWN.purpose: For overseas Chinese students assigned/admitted to educational institutions in Taiwan (universities, vocational schools, or high schools).
TWN.notes: Separate category for overseas Chinese (huaqiao) students, distinct from the general foreign-student resident visa. Resident visa validity 3 months; holder must apply for an Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) within 30 days of arrival, with stay tied to enrollment. Single-entry resident visa fee NT$2,200 / US$66; converting from a visitor visa inside Taiwan adds an NT$800 handling fee.

TZA.name: Ordinary Visa (Single Entry)
TZA.purpose: For tourism, visiting friends or relatives, attending meetings and workshops. Holders are not permitted to work or conduct business activities.
TZA.notes: Applied via e-visa portal at visa.immigration.go.tz (advance application) OR obtainable on arrival at official entry points. Both options confirmed operational as of June 2026 per Tanzania Immigration Department and US State Dept (updated Oct 2025). USA nationals are required to apply for a Multiple Entry Visa instead of the Ordinary Visa. Only passports with M or F sex marker accepted for entry.

TZA.name: Multiple Entry Visa
TZA.purpose: For tourism, family visits, and certain professional categories requiring repeated entry over a 12-month period. Max 3 consecutive months per visit.
TZA.notes: Eligible categories include: USA nationals (mandatory), company directors (requires BRELA registration documents), government consultants (requires ministry letter), NGO representatives, and family visitors (requires marriage/birth certificate). Valid for maximum 12 months with max 3 consecutive months (90 days) per stay.

TZA.name: Business Visa
TZA.purpose: For specific short-term professional assignments including machine repairs, training, feasibility studies, and other professional work not available locally.
TZA.notes: Issued on a single entry basis only - cannot be used to re-enter Tanzania. Requires proof of work contract or assignment documentation. Not for general business/commerce purposes; those would use the Ordinary or Multiple Entry Visa.

TZA.name: Transit Visa
TZA.purpose: For passing through Tanzania en route to a third country.
TZA.notes: Requires valid passport, onward/destination visa or ticket proving onward travel. Valid for up to 7 days.

TZA.name: Student Visa (Single Entry, up to 3 months)
TZA.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in educational programs or courses of up to 3 months in Tanzania.
TZA.notes: Requires letter from the institution detailing course name and duration, open return ticket. Fee confirmed from official immigration fee page.

TZA.name: Student Visa (Multiple Entry, up to 2 years)
TZA.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in longer educational programs up to 2 years.
TZA.notes: Multiple entry, up to 2 years validity. Fee confirmed from official immigration fee page.

TZA.name: Student Visa (Research, up to 6 months)
TZA.purpose: For foreign nationals conducting academic research programs up to 6 months in Tanzania.
TZA.notes: Research-specific student visa, 6-month cap. Fee confirmed from official immigration fee page.

TZA.name: Student Visa (PhD, up to 2 years)
TZA.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in PhD programs in Tanzania.
TZA.notes: PhD-level student visa, up to 2 years. Highest fee tier in the student visa category. Fee confirmed from official immigration fee page.

TZA.name: Referral Visa
TZA.purpose: Entry visa for nationals of specified countries (and stateless persons/refugees holding Vienna Convention travel documents) whose applications require prior special clearance from the Commissioner General of Immigration before a visa is issued.
TZA.notes: Required for nationals of approximately 25 countries (e.g. Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Burkina Faso, Chad, Eritrea, Guinea Bissau, Guinea Conakry, Iran, Iraq, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Pakistan, Palestine, Somalia, Sierra Leone, Syria, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Yemen) plus stateless persons and refugees. NOT eligible for visa on arrival - must apply online via the e-visa portal (visa.immigration.go.tz) at least 2 months before travel and should not book flights until approved. Requires a covering letter from a registered institution/company (official visits) or a host individual (personal visits), host's ID/permit, and a completed Security Bond form (T.I.F 12). Fee is the respective standard visa fee, which varies by nationality (e.g. Pakistan USD 200; USA and Ireland USD 100; most others USD 50) - no separate referral surcharge, hence fee_usd left null.

TZA.name: Gratis Visa
TZA.purpose: Complimentary visa issued to holders of diplomatic or official passports and representatives of international organizations.
TZA.notes: No fee. Issued to holders of diplomatic/official passports and international organization representatives. Must still apply through the e-visa portal or immigration channels.

UGA.name: Tourist Visa (Single Entry)
UGA.purpose: Short-term tourism, leisure, and visiting friends or family in Uganda. Must be applied for online before travel.
UGA.notes: Mandatory pre-travel e-visa via visas.immigration.go.ug. Applicant receives an email authorization letter with barcode; border officials complete visa issuance on arrival. Yellow fever vaccination certificate required. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond arrival date.

UGA.name: Multiple Entry Visa (6–12 months)
UGA.purpose: Allows multiple entries into Uganda for tourism and short visits over a 6 to 12-month validity period.
UGA.notes: Applied online through visas.immigration.go.ug. Valid for 6–12 months from approval date. USD 100 fee. Each stay duration within Uganda is governed by conditions set at entry.

UGA.name: Multiple Entry Visa (24 months)
UGA.purpose: Allows multiple entries into Uganda for tourism and short visits over a 24-month validity period.
UGA.notes: Applied online through visas.immigration.go.ug. Valid for 24 months from approval date. USD 200 fee.

UGA.name: East African Tourist Visa
UGA.purpose: Regional multi-country tourist visa allowing multiple entries into Uganda, Kenya, and Rwanda for tourism purposes.
UGA.notes: Joint visa issued by Uganda, Kenya, and Rwanda. Valid for 90 days with multiple entries across all three countries. Apply online. Confirmed by UK GOV travel advice at USD 100.

UGA.name: Transit Visa
UGA.purpose: For travelers passing through Uganda to a third country who require a visa and will remain in Uganda for a short transit period.
UGA.notes: Applied online via visas.immigration.go.ug before travel. Fee USD 50. Granted for a maximum of 7 days and is NOT extendable (per the official immigration.go.ug transit visa page). Fees are non-refundable and payments are subject to a bank charge.

UGA.name: Business Visa (Single Entry)
UGA.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Uganda for business meetings, conferences, trade negotiations, or commercial activities that do not constitute employment.
UGA.notes: Applied online via Uganda's Electronic Visa and Permit Application System. Business visitors engaging in any form of employment or paid work must obtain a work permit instead. Canada travel advisory confirms business visa as a distinct category.

UGA.name: Entry Permit – Class G (Employment / Work Permit)
UGA.purpose: For foreign nationals employed by a Ugandan company or organization. Required for any form of paid employment, including missionary and volunteer work.
UGA.notes: Class G is the standard employment entry permit. Subclass G3 covers rare-skilled expatriates in agro-processing, manufacturing, and mining. EAC nationals (Kenya, Rwanda) are exempt from work permit fees; Tanzanian nationals pay reduced fee of USD 1,550/year. Applied online via visas.immigration.go.ug. US State Dept advisory warns that missionary and volunteer work frequently require a work visa; operating without valid permit may result in fines or imprisonment.

UGA.name: Entry Permit – Investor Classes (B, C, D, E, F)
UGA.purpose: For foreign nationals who are shareholders or investors in Ugandan companies across sectors including agriculture, agro-processing, mining, manufacturing, general trade, and specific professions.
UGA.notes: Class B1: Agriculture shareholders. Class B2: Agro-processing (fees: 6 months USD 400; 12 months USD 400; 24 months available). Class C1/C2: Prospecting/mining of minerals. Class D: General trade. Class E: Manufacturing. Class F: Specific professions. No minimum investment threshold stated on official pages. Linked to active investment in Uganda companies.

UGA.name: Entry Permit – Class H (Independent Means / Ordinary Resident)
UGA.purpose: For foreign nationals who have assured income derived from sources outside Uganda and commit not to accept any employment in Uganda.
UGA.notes: Closest equivalent to a retirement/passive income residence permit. No minimum income threshold stated on official pages. Holder must not engage in any form of employment within Uganda.

UGA.name: Student Pass
UGA.purpose: For foreign nationals above the age of 4 years enrolled in a recognized learning institution in Uganda.
UGA.notes: Granted for 3, 6, or 12 months (validity varies by tier selected). Flat fee of USD 100 payable at the point of application regardless of the period granted; East African Community nationals are exempted from this fee. Holders of a valid Student Pass do not require a visa to re-enter Uganda while the pass is valid.

UGA.name: Dependant's Pass
UGA.purpose: For children (under 18 years), the spouse, and other relatives of a foreign resident who holds proof of legal stay in Uganda (Student Pass, Work Permit/Entry Permit, or Certificate of Residence).
UGA.notes: Granted to dependants of a foreign national who has a valid Uganda residence document. Holders do not require a visa to re-enter Uganda while their pass is valid. Specific fee not published on the official page.

UGA.name: Special Pass
UGA.purpose: A short-term pass for foreign nationals coming for short contract/temporary work assignments, medical treatment, tourism, or business opportunities, or awaiting processing of an Entry Permit.
UGA.notes: Issued for short-term work assignments and other temporary activities, typically for up to 90 days with the possibility of a limited extension. Also commonly used as a bridge document while an Entry Permit application is being processed. Holders do not require a visa to re-enter Uganda while the pass is valid.

UGA.name: Diplomatic / Official Passport Visa Exemption
UGA.purpose: Visa-free entry to Uganda for holders of diplomatic or official passports of certain countries under bilateral agreements.
UGA.notes: Countries whose diplomatic and official passport holders are exempt: Algeria, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Iran, Russia, Senegal, South Africa, Venezuela, Vietnam. Turkey: diplomatic passport only (not official). These exemptions are based on bilateral visa abolition agreements. Ordinary passport holders from these countries still require an e-visa.

UGA.name: Diplomatic and Official Visa
UGA.purpose: For holders of diplomatic, official, and service passports entering Uganda on official business or duties, and for ordinary passport holders who are exempted from immigration fees.
UGA.notes: Gratis visa: fee is Nil and there is no processing fee. Requires a copy of the diplomatic/official/service passport (bio-data and cover page, valid at least 6 months), a recent passport photo, and a Diplomatic Note (Note Verbale) or supporting document for the official visit. Applied online at visas.immigration.go.ug, with biometric capture at an immigration office after approval. Distinct from the nationality-based diplomatic/official passport visa EXEMPTION granted to citizens of specific treaty countries.

UGA.name: Certificate of Residence
UGA.purpose: Long-term / permanent residence document for foreign nationals qualifying by marriage to a Ugandan (married at least 3 years), by continuous long stay (10 years contributing to Uganda's socio-economic development), or as a former Ugandan who acquired another citizenship.
UGA.notes: Issued in durations of 5 years, 10 years, or Life. For the 'due to long stay' category the fees are USD 4,000 (5 years), USD 3,500 (10 years), and USD 3,000 (Life), each including a USD 200 processing fee. Other categories: 'due to marriage' (legally married to a Ugandan for at least 3 years) and former Ugandans. This is Uganda's closest equivalent to permanent-residence status. Applied online at visas.immigration.go.ug.

UGA.name: Inter-State Pass
UGA.purpose: Regional free-movement travel document allowing nationals (and lawful residents) of Uganda, Kenya, and Rwanda to travel between the three countries using only a National Identity Card instead of a passport.
UGA.notes: Issued FREE at the border at the point of exit; no visa required and no charge. Citizens of Kenya and Rwanda may enter Uganda using a valid National ID card or e-Passport. Foreign nationals holding valid resident permits issued by Kenya, Rwanda, or Uganda may also use the Inter-State Pass to move within the region without a visa.

UKR.name: Type C Short-Stay Visa (Tourist/Private Visit)
UKR.purpose: Issued for tourism, private visits, and short-term stays not exceeding 90 days. Required for nationals of countries that do not have a visa-free agreement with Ukraine.
UKR.notes: Issued at Ukrainian embassies and consulates abroad. Single-entry and multiple-entry variants exist. Ukraine does not issue visas at the border or airport. Fee varies by nationality based on reciprocity. Based on Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 567 (2001) on visa issuance rules.

UKR.name: Type C Short-Stay Visa (Business)
UKR.purpose: Issued for business purposes including negotiations, conferences, trade fairs, and short-term commercial activities not exceeding 90 days.
UKR.notes: A letter of invitation from a Ukrainian company or official invitation document is typically required. Single-entry and multiple-entry variants. Issued at Ukrainian embassies and consulates abroad.

UKR.name: Type A / Type B Transit Visa
UKR.purpose: Type A is an airport transit visa for passing through an international transit zone. Type B is a transit visa for transiting through Ukrainian territory to a third country.
UKR.notes: Transit visa (Type B) allows up to 5 days in Ukraine when transiting to a third country. Proof of onward ticket and valid visa for destination country is required. Airport transit visa (Type A) is for the international zone only.

UKR.name: E-Visa (Electronic Visa) - Tourist/Private
UKR.purpose: Electronic short-stay visa for tourism and private visits, available online for nationals of eligible countries (approximately 45 countries). Resumed 19 February 2025.
UKR.notes: Single-entry e-visa costs USD 20; double-entry costs USD 30. Standard processing: 3 working days; urgent processing: 1 working day. Maximum stay: 30 days. Available to nationals of approximately 45 eligible countries including India, China, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, and others. Application via evisa.mfa.gov.ua. E-visa program was suspended during active hostilities and resumed 19 February 2025.

UKR.name: E-Visa (Electronic Visa) - Business
UKR.purpose: Electronic short-stay visa for business purposes, available online for nationals of eligible countries. Resumed 19 February 2025.
UKR.notes: Single-entry e-visa costs USD 20; double-entry costs USD 30. Same processing times and eligibility as tourist e-visa. Double-entry variant available for USD 30.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (Employment)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreigners who have obtained a work permit in Ukraine, allowing entry for the purpose of employment under a labor contract.
UKR.notes: Requires a valid work permit (labor permission) issued by the State Employment Service of Ukraine. After entry, the foreigner must apply to the State Migration Service (DMSU) for a Temporary Residence Permit, which is issued for the duration of the employment contract. Processing of the residence permit: 15 working days.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (Study)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreigners admitted to accredited Ukrainian educational institutions, allowing entry for the purpose of study.
UKR.notes: Requires an official invitation (vyzov) from the Ukrainian educational institution. After entry, must apply for a Temporary Residence Permit for the duration of studies. Permit valid for the duration of studies.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (Family Reunification)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreign nationals joining a close family member (spouse, minor child, or dependent parent) who is a Ukrainian citizen or permanent resident.
UKR.notes: Requires proof of family relationship (marriage certificate, birth certificate, etc.) and that the Ukrainian-side family member is a citizen or permanent resident. After entry, must apply for a Temporary Residence Permit at DMSU.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (Foreign Investor)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreign nationals who are founders, participants, or beneficial owners of a Ukrainian legal entity with a minimum ownership share of EUR 100,000.
UKR.notes: After entry on Type D visa, investor must apply to DMSU for a Temporary Residence Permit valid for 2 years (renewable). Minimum investment threshold: EUR 100,000 (at NBU exchange rate). Investment may be in monetary form, property, or securities. Government fee approximately UAH 1,140 (combined). Processing: 15 working days.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (Religious Activity / NGO / Cultural / Scientific / Media)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay national visa for foreigners conducting religious activities, working for non-governmental organizations, engaged in cultural or scientific exchange, or accredited as foreign media correspondents.
UKR.notes: Category covers multiple sub-purposes: religious leaders/missionaries, foreign NGO staff, participants in technical assistance projects, cultural exchange programs, scientific research, and foreign media correspondents with accreditation. After entry, must apply for a Temporary Residence Permit for the relevant activity duration.

UKR.name: Diplomatic / Official / Service Visa (Type D)
UKR.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of countries that do not have a visa-free agreement covering such passport types with Ukraine.
UKR.notes: Diplomatic visas are typically fee-exempt. Many countries have bilateral agreements with Ukraine exempting diplomatic/official/service passport holders from visa requirements entirely. Duration and validity are determined by the diplomatic mission's accreditation period.

UKR.name: Type C Short-Stay Visa (Medical Treatment)
UKR.purpose: Issued for the purpose of receiving medical treatment in a Ukrainian healthcare institution for nationals of countries that require a visa.
UKR.notes: Requires an invitation/confirmation from a Ukrainian medical institution specifying the treatment and expected duration. If treatment exceeds 90 days, a Type D long-stay visa may be required instead.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (D-01 Immigration / Permanent Residence)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay entry visa for foreigners who have already obtained an immigration permit from the State Migration Service, allowing entry to Ukraine to obtain a Permanent Residence Permit. Immigration permits cover spouses and close family of Ukrainian citizens, persons of Ukrainian origin, immigrant investors, highly qualified specialists needed by Ukraine, and other quota/non-quota categories.
UKR.notes: The D-01 visa itself is a 90-day multiple-entry entry visa; it is issued only to holders of an immigration permit already granted by the State Migration Service (DMSU). After entry, the holder applies for a Permanent Residence Permit (indefinite). Immigration permits are quota-based, with separate non-quota categories for spouses/children of Ukrainian citizens, persons of Ukrainian origin, guardians, and foreign investors (USD 100,000+). This is the immigration / permanent-residence pathway, distinct from the 2-year temporary-residence investor route (D-12).

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (D-08/D-09 Representative Office Employee)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay work visa for foreign employees of a registered representative office of a foreign company (D-08) or a foreign bank (D-09) in Ukraine. Unlike the general employment visa, eligibility is based on a Service Card issued to accredited representative-office staff rather than a work permit from the State Employment Service.
UKR.notes: The D visa is a 90-day multiple-entry entry visa. Issued to foreign staff of representative offices of foreign business entities (D-08) or foreign banks (D-09) registered in Ukraine, based on a Service Card (sluzhbova kartka) issued by the Ministry of Economy rather than a State Employment Service work permit. After entry the holder obtains a Temporary Residence Permit valid for the accreditation period. Fee varies by nationality on a reciprocity basis.

UKR.name: Type D Long-Stay Visa (D-10 Volunteer / Cultural / Sports Activity)
UKR.purpose: Long-stay visa for foreigners coming to Ukraine for volunteer work, or for cultural, educational, scientific, or sports programs, on the invitation of a Ukrainian state body or of an organisation that engages volunteers.
UKR.notes: The D-10 visa is a 90-day multiple-entry entry visa. Requires a letter of invitation from a Ukrainian state body responsible for cultural, educational, scientific, sports or volunteer programs, or from a volunteer-engaging organisation listed on the Ministry of Social Policy website (accompanied by its state-registration certificate). After entry, a Temporary Residence Permit is obtained for the duration of the activity. Distinct legal ground from the religious/NGO/media/technical-assistance category above.

URY.name: Admisión Temporaria Sin Visa (ATSV) / Visa de Turismo
URY.purpose: Entry for recreation, rest, or leisure purposes without conducting paid work. For nationalities requiring a visa, a Tourism Visa (Visa de Turismo) is issued by Uruguayan consulates.
URY.notes: Visa-free nationals receive 90 days automatically on entry, extendable once for additional 90 days. Nationals requiring a consular visa must apply at a Uruguayan embassy or consulate; the visa must be used within 180 days of issuance. Multiple entries permitted per Decree 356/018 Article 3. Governed by Migration Law 18.250 and Decree 356/018.

URY.name: Visa de Negocios
URY.purpose: For investment and commercial exchange activities with Uruguayan companies or public organisms. Does not permit employment or residence.
URY.notes: Renewable for an additional 90 days. Multiple entries permitted per Decree 356/018 Article 3. Must be applied for at a Uruguayan embassy or consulate. Governed by Decree 356/018.

URY.name: Visa de Trabajo
URY.purpose: For foreign nationals who will develop labor activities in Uruguay. Requires initiating residency proceedings within 30 days of entry.
URY.notes: Duration depends on the migrant's residency subcategory (temporary: 6 months to 2 years; permanent: indefinite). Applicant must process legal residency within 30 days of entry. Applied for at Uruguayan consulates. Governed by Decree 356/018.

URY.name: Visa de Estudio
URY.purpose: For foreign nationals pursuing studies, scholarships, or internships at officially recognized Uruguayan educational institutions.
URY.notes: Duration regulated by temporary residency terms (minimum 6 months, maximum 2 years, renewable). Must process temporary residency within 30 days of entry. Proof of enrollment and financial support required. Applied for at Uruguayan consulates. Governed by Decree 356/018 and Migration Law 18.250 Art. 34.

URY.name: Visa de Reunificación Familiar
URY.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking to reunite with a family member who holds permanent legal residency in Uruguay.
URY.notes: Duration matches the sponsoring family member's residency period. Applicant must process residency within 30 days of entry. Applied for at Uruguayan consulates. Governed by Decree 356/018.

URY.name: Visa Humanitaria y de Urgencia
URY.purpose: For medical treatment, participation in judicial proceedings, or attendance due to family emergencies such as critical illness or death of a family member.
URY.notes: Duration tied to the specific humanitarian necessity. If the stay will exceed the visa period, applicant must apply for residency within 30 days. Applied for at Uruguayan consulates. Also covers judicial-related attendance. Governed by Decree 356/018.

URY.name: Visa de Congresos, Convenciones y Seminarios
URY.purpose: For attending national or international events of public interest such as congresses, conventions, seminars, and similar events.
URY.notes: Renewable for an additional 90 days. Multiple entries permitted per Decree 356/018 Article 3. Applied for at Uruguayan consulates. Governed by Decree 356/018.

URY.name: Visa Diplomática / Oficial / de Servicio
URY.purpose: For holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports representing their governments in Uruguay. Provides exemption from standard migration regulations.
URY.notes: Diplomatic personnel are exempt from standard entry/exit regulations under Migration Law 18.250 Art. 5; authorities merely verify documentation. Many nationalities that require visas on ordinary passports are visa-free on diplomatic/official/service passports via bilateral agreements. The Régimen de Visas de Admisión table lists specific exemptions by country and passport type.

URY.name: Residencia Legal Temporaria (Temporary Legal Residency)
URY.purpose: For foreign nationals settling in Uruguay for work, study, religious activities, or other legally recognized purposes for stays of more than 6 months and up to 2 years.
URY.notes: Fee: 557.30 UI (Unidades Indexadas, adjusted semiannually). Additional: 55.70 UI for identity card; 225.60 UI per re-entry permit. Renewable for equal periods. Requires criminal background certificate, health card, vaccination certificate, proof of activity (work letter, enrollment, or religious affiliation). Online initial submission then in-person at National Migration Directorate (Mercedes 1004, Montevideo). Path to citizenship after 3 years of accumulated legal residency.

URY.name: Residencia Legal Permanente (Permanent Legal Residency)
URY.purpose: For any foreign national intending to reside permanently in Uruguay, regardless of nationality.
URY.notes: Fee: 557.30 UI. Additional: 55.70 UI for identity card; 225.60 UI per re-entry permit. Brazilian and Paraguayan nationals exempt from fees. Requires valid ID/passport, criminal background certificate, health card, vaccination certificate, and proof of income. Foreign documents must be apostilled or legalized and translated to Spanish (Brazilian documents exempt). Path to citizenship after 3 years of legal residency.

URY.name: Residencia Permanente Mercosur
URY.purpose: Permanent residency for nationals of Mercosur member and associate states (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, Suriname, Guyana) and foreign family members of Uruguayan nationals.
URY.notes: Available to nationals born or naturalized in Mercosur member/associate countries and foreign family members of Uruguayan citizens (children, spouses, common-law partners, siblings). Path to citizenship after 3 years of legal residency. Fee structure similar to standard permanent residency.

URY.name: Residencia Temporaria Mercosur
URY.purpose: Temporary residency for Mercosur and associated country nationals with at least 5 years of citizenship, allowing a 2-year stay renewable once.
URY.notes: Duration: 2 years, renewable once for additional 2 years. Renewal must be requested at least 90 days before expiration. Available to nationals of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Venezuela, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Guyana, and Suriname with 5+ years of citizenship. Path to citizenship after 3 years of legal residency.

URY.name: Permiso TID-Nómades (Digital Nomad Permit)
URY.purpose: For self-employed foreign nationals or those employed by companies outside Uruguay who wish to live and work remotely from Uruguay.
URY.notes: Established under Decree 238/022. Duration: 6 months, renewable once for additional 6 months (12 months total). Must first enter Uruguay as a regular tourist. Requirements: online application form, affidavit of financial self-sufficiency, clean criminal record (for extension), Uruguayan vaccination certificate. No minimum income threshold specified on official page. Can transition to temporary or permanent residency. Contact: dnm-hip@minterior.gub.uy.

URY.name: Documento Especial Fronterizo (Special Border Document)
URY.purpose: For Brazilian nationals residing in designated Uruguayan-Brazilian border cities, enabling work, study, or retirement/pension activities in Uruguay.
URY.notes: Valid for up to 5 years, renewable. Exclusively for Brazilian nationals living in designated border cities. Includes coverage for retirees and pensioners. Applied for at the National Migration Directorate.

URY.name: Vacaciones y Trabajo (Working Holiday)
URY.purpose: For young nationals (aged 18-30, up to 35 under some agreements) of countries holding a bilateral Working Holiday agreement with Uruguay to visit primarily for tourism while working temporarily to help fund their stay.
URY.notes: Bilateral agreements in force with Germany, Australia, France, Japan, New Zealand, Netherlands, United Kingdom and Portugal. No cost ('no tiene costo'). Requirements: valid passport, comprehensive health insurance ('seguro de salud integral'), proof of sufficient initial funds, return-ticket capacity, apostilled/legalized criminal-record certificate; no accompanying dependents. Single entry; holder must enter Uruguay within 180 calendar days of notification. Official trámite page caps duration at 2 years; most bilateral programmes grant 12 months (UK up to 24 months). Applied for in person at a Uruguayan embassy or consulate.

URY.name: Residencia Permanente para Jubilados y Pensionistas (Beneficio Ley 16.340)
URY.purpose: Permanent residency pathway for retired or pensioned foreign nationals with foreign-sourced retirement/pension income who wish to settle permanently in Uruguay.
URY.notes: Governed by Ley 16.340, administered by the Dirección Nacional de Migración (Ministerio del Interior). Requires a minimum of USD 1,500/month in foreign pension or retirement income, plus either purchase of residential property worth at least USD 100,000 (non-transferable for 10 years) or holding Uruguayan government securities of equal value in a Central Bank custodial account for 10 years. Benefits: duty-free import of household goods and one vehicle (non-saleable for 4 years) and eligibility for a Uruguayan passport. The benefit procedure itself has no cost. Path to citizenship after 3 years of legal residency.

USA.name: B-1/B-2 Visitor Visa
USA.purpose: Tourism, business visits, transit, medical treatment
USA.notes: Admission period (typically up to 6 months) is set at port of entry by CBP. Must apply at a US embassy or consulate.

USA.name: F-1 Student Visa
USA.purpose: Full-time academic study at SEVP-approved institutions
USA.notes: Duration of Status (D/S) - valid for the duration of your academic program. Requires I-20 from school and SEVIS fee.

USA.name: H-1B Specialty Occupation Visa
USA.purpose: Working in specialty occupations requiring at least a bachelor's degree
USA.notes: Requires employer sponsorship. Annual cap of 65,000 (plus 20,000 for US master's). Initial period 3 years, extendable to 6.

USA.name: L-1 Intracompany Transferee Visa
USA.purpose: Transferring to a US office in a managerial, executive, or specialised knowledge role
USA.notes: Must have worked for the sponsoring company for at least 1 year in the past 3 years.

USA.name: J-1 Exchange Visitor Visa
USA.purpose: Au pairs, camp counsellors, interns, teachers, research scholars, professors
USA.notes: Duration of Status. Requires DS-2019 from a designated exchange program sponsor.

USA.name: EB-5 Investor Visa
USA.purpose: Immigrant visa through investment of at least USD 1.05M (or USD 800K in rural/high-unemployment areas) creating 10 US jobs
USA.notes: Leads to lawful permanent residence (Green Card). Can apply through a USCIS-designated Regional Center.

USA.name: M-1 Vocational Student Visa
USA.purpose: Full-time study at vocational or other recognised nonacademic institutions (other than language training)
USA.notes: Requires Form I-20 from an SEVP-approved school plus the SEVIS fee. Admitted for Duration of Status covering the vocational program, generally up to 1 year. Distinct from the academic F-1 visa.

USA.name: C-1 Transit Visa
USA.purpose: Immediate and continuous transit through the United States en route to another country
USA.notes: For travellers passing through the US to another destination. Not valid for layover tourism. Crew joining a vessel or aircraft typically use a combined C-1/D transit/crew visa.

USA.name: D Crewmember Visa
USA.purpose: Crew serving aboard sea vessels or aircraft operating in the United States
USA.notes: For pilots, flight attendants, ship crew and similar personnel. Frequently issued as a combined C-1/D transit/crew visa. Departure generally required within 29 days.

USA.name: K-1 Fiancé(e) Visa
USA.purpose: Foreign-citizen fiancé(e) of a US citizen, to enter and marry the sponsor within 90 days
USA.notes: US citizen sponsor first files Form I-129F with USCIS. Visa is single-entry, valid up to 6 months; marriage must occur within 90 days of entry, after which the spouse may apply to adjust status to permanent resident.

USA.name: O-1 Extraordinary Ability Visa
USA.purpose: Individuals with extraordinary ability in the sciences, arts, education, business or athletics, or extraordinary achievement in film/TV
USA.notes: Petition-based (US employer or agent files Form I-129). Initial stay up to 3 years, extendable in 1-year increments. No annual cap. Can be a stepping stone to EB-1A permanent residence.

USA.name: P-1 Athlete and Entertainer Visa
USA.purpose: Internationally recognised athletes and members of internationally recognised entertainment groups
USA.notes: Petition-based (Form I-129). P-1 individual athletes may be admitted up to 5 years (extendable to a total of 10); entertainment groups and P-2/P-3 performers are generally admitted up to 1 year.

USA.name: E-1 Treaty Trader Visa
USA.purpose: Nationals of treaty countries carrying on substantial trade principally between the US and their home country
USA.notes: Only for nationals of countries with a qualifying commerce and navigation treaty with the US. Admitted for up to 2 years per stay, renewable indefinitely while trade continues. Does not lead directly to permanent residence.

USA.name: E-2 Treaty Investor Visa
USA.purpose: Nationals of treaty countries investing a substantial amount of capital in a US business they direct
USA.notes: Only for nationals of qualifying treaty-investment countries. No fixed minimum investment (must be 'substantial' and proportional to the enterprise). Renewable indefinitely but does not directly lead to a green card. Also tracked under residency-by-investment programs.

USA.name: E-3 Australian Professional Specialty Visa
USA.purpose: Australian nationals coming to perform services in a specialty occupation
USA.notes: Only for Australian citizens. Requires a US job offer in a specialty occupation and a certified Labor Condition Application. Granted in up to 2-year increments, renewable indefinitely. Annual cap of 10,500.

USA.name: TN USMCA Professional Visa
USA.purpose: Canadian and Mexican professionals in qualifying occupations under the USMCA (formerly NAFTA)
USA.notes: Available only to Canadian and Mexican citizens in USMCA-listed professions with a US job offer. Canadians may apply directly at a port of entry (no visa foil required); Mexicans obtain a TN visa at a consulate. Admitted up to 3 years, indefinitely renewable.

USA.name: H-2A Temporary Agricultural Worker Visa
USA.purpose: Temporary or seasonal agricultural work for employers facing a shortage of domestic workers
USA.notes: Employer must obtain a temporary labor certification and file Form I-129. Generally limited to nationals of designated eligible countries. Initial stay tied to the certified period (typically up to 1 year); maximum 3 years before a required departure.

USA.name: H-2B Temporary Non-Agricultural Worker Visa
USA.purpose: Temporary or seasonal non-agricultural work (e.g. hospitality, landscaping, seafood processing)
USA.notes: Employer must obtain a temporary labor certification and file Form I-129. Subject to a statutory annual cap (66,000). Generally limited to nationals of designated eligible countries. Maximum 3 years.

USA.name: R-1 Religious Worker Visa
USA.purpose: Ministers and other religious workers employed by a bona fide non-profit religious organisation in the US
USA.notes: Requires a US petitioner (Form I-129) that is a bona fide non-profit religious organisation. Initial stay up to 30 months, extendable to a total of 5 years.

USA.name: I Media (Journalist) Visa
USA.purpose: Representatives of foreign media (press, radio, film, print) on assignment in the US
USA.notes: For employees of foreign-based media organisations engaged in informational/news activities. Admitted for Duration of Status. Media work is not permitted on a B visa or under the Visa Waiver Program.

USA.name: Family-Based Immigrant Visa (IR/CR/F)
USA.purpose: Spouses, children, parents and other qualifying relatives of US citizens and lawful permanent residents to immigrate permanently
USA.notes: Immigrant (green card) category. A US citizen or LPR sponsor files Form I-130. Immediate relatives (IR1/CR1 spouse, IR2 child, IR5 parent) have no annual cap; family-preference categories (F1-F4) are numerically limited with multi-year waits. Grants lawful permanent residence on entry.

UZB.name: Tourist Visa (T)
UZB.purpose: Issued for tourism and leisure travel to Uzbekistan. Covers sightseeing, cultural visits, and recreation.
UZB.notes: Standard single-entry tourist visa issued via Uzbekistan embassy or consulate. Fee is for up to 30-day stay. Longer validity options available at higher fees: 7 days $40, 15 days $50, 30 days $60, 3 months $80, 6 months $120, 1 year $160.

UZB.name: Group Tourist Visa (TG)
UZB.purpose: Tourist entry visa for organized groups of 5 or more foreign nationals visiting Uzbekistan for tourism purposes.
UZB.notes: Reduced per-person fee of $15–$25 for groups of 5 or more persons. Must be organized through a licensed Uzbekistan tour operator.

UZB.name: Electronic Visa - Single Entry (e-visa)
UZB.purpose: Online tourist/visit visa for eligible nationalities allowing a single entry stay in Uzbekistan for up to 30 days.
UZB.notes: Available for 76+ eligible countries via e-visa.gov.uz. E-visa is valid for 90 days from date of issue; single entry for up to 30 days stay. Available for tourist, business, and other purposes under one application type.

UZB.name: Electronic Visa - Double Entry (e-visa)
UZB.purpose: Online visa allowing two entries to Uzbekistan, each for up to 30 days, suitable for multi-leg itineraries.
UZB.notes: Double-entry e-visa for 30-day stays per entry. Valid for 90 days from issuance.

UZB.name: Electronic Visa - Multiple Entry (e-visa)
UZB.purpose: Online multiple-entry visa for eligible nationalities, allowing repeated entries into Uzbekistan within the validity period.
UZB.notes: Multiple-entry e-visa; each stay up to 30 days. Valid for 90 days from issuance.

UZB.name: Business Visa (B-2)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Uzbekistan for general business activities including meetings, negotiations, and commercial visits.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 1 year. Requires invitation from a registered Uzbekistan legal entity. Multiple-entry fee for 1 year is $250.

UZB.name: Accredited Business Representative Visa (B-1)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who are officially accredited as representatives of foreign banks, commercial offices, or trade companies in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid for the accreditation period. Requires formal accreditation with Uzbekistan authorities.

UZB.name: Work Visa (Is)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals authorized to work in Uzbekistan under a legal employment contract or labor agreement.
UZB.notes: Requires prior approval from the Agency for External Labor Migration. Employer must obtain a work permit before visa is issued.

UZB.name: Student Visa (A-1)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals enrolled full-time in an educational institution in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 1 year, renewable. Requires acceptance letter and enrollment confirmation from an accredited Uzbekistan educational institution.

UZB.name: Short-Term Student Exchange Visa (STD)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals participating in short-term student exchange programs with Uzbekistan educational institutions.
UZB.notes: For structured exchange programs. Validity aligned with program duration, up to 1 year.

UZB.name: Teaching / Educational Staff Visa (A-2)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals taking up teaching positions at educational institutions in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Requires contract with an accredited Uzbekistan educational institution. Valid up to 1 year.

UZB.name: Academic Research / Lecturer Visa (A-3)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign scientists, researchers, and lecturers conducting academic research or delivering lectures at Uzbekistan institutions.
UZB.notes: Validity ranges from 3 months to 2 years depending on the research or lecture program duration.

UZB.name: Transit Visa (TRAN)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals transiting through Uzbekistan territory en route to a third country.
UZB.notes: Allows transit passage of up to 3 days. Available at embassy/consulate and also at Tashkent International Airport for same-day transit. Uzbekistan Airways transit passengers may qualify for a 5-day visa-free transit procedure.

UZB.name: Medical Treatment Visa (WITH)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals travelling to Uzbekistan to receive medical treatment at a licensed healthcare facility.
UZB.notes: Requires confirmation letter from an accredited medical institution in Uzbekistan. Valid up to 3 months.

UZB.name: Private / Guest Visit Visa - Invited by Uzbek Citizen (PV-1)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting Uzbekistan at the invitation of a citizen or permanent resident of Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Inviting party must be a citizen or permanent resident of Uzbekistan. Valid up to 1 year.

UZB.name: Private / Guest Visit Visa - Invited by Foreign Resident (PV-2)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting Uzbekistan at the invitation of a foreign national legally residing in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Inviting party must be a foreign national holding a valid residence permit in Uzbekistan. Valid up to 1 year.

UZB.name: Compatriot Family Visit Visa (VTD)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who are relatives of Uzbek citizens residing abroad, visiting family members in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 2 years. Intended for relatives of Uzbek diaspora members or compatriots. Documentation of family relationship required.

UZB.name: Investment Visa (INV)
UZB.purpose: Multiple-entry visa issued to foreign investors who have made qualifying investments in Uzbekistan, facilitating repeated business travel related to their investment.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 3 years, multiple entry. Minimum investment threshold is approximately USD 8,500 or more to qualify. Different from the RBI golden visa/residence permit programs which require USD 100,000–$3,000,000+.

UZB.name: Pilgrimage / Religious-Cultural Heritage Visa (PLG)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals visiting Uzbekistan for religious pilgrimages or study of cultural and religious heritage sites.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 2 months. Intended for religious visitors to Uzbekistan's historic Islamic sites (Samarkand, Bukhara, etc.) and cultural heritage travel.

UZB.name: Diplomatic Entry Visa - Permanent Accreditation (D-1)
UZB.purpose: Entry visa for foreign diplomatic staff with permanent accreditation to Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid for the duration of the accreditation period. Issued to holders of diplomatic passports with full accreditation to Uzbekistan. No fee applies to diplomatic visas.

UZB.name: Temporary Diplomatic Stay Visa (D-2)
UZB.purpose: Temporary stay visa for diplomatic passport holders on short-term missions or visits to Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 3 months. For diplomatic passport holders on temporary assignment.

UZB.name: Diplomatic Tourist Visa (DT)
UZB.purpose: Issued to diplomatic passport holders travelling to Uzbekistan for personal tourism purposes.
UZB.notes: Up to 1 month. For private tourism by holders of diplomatic passports.

UZB.name: Service Entry Visa - Permanent Accreditation (S-1)
UZB.purpose: Entry visa for embassy support staff, NGO representatives, and service-category personnel with permanent accreditation.
UZB.notes: Valid for the accreditation period. For service passport holders with formal accreditation.

UZB.name: Temporary Service Stay Visa (S-2)
UZB.purpose: Temporary stay visa for service passport holders on short-term official missions in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 3 months.

UZB.name: Service Entry Visa - State Organization Invitation (S-3)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals invited by Uzbekistan state organizations for official business or project-related visits.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 1 year. Requires formal invitation from a recognized Uzbekistan state body.

UZB.name: Official / State Visit Visa
UZB.purpose: Issued to members of official state delegations visiting Uzbekistan for government-level meetings and state visits.
UZB.notes: Validity aligned with the duration of the official event. Restricted to official government delegations.

UZB.name: Journalist Visa - Permanent Accreditation (J-1)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign journalists and media representatives with permanent accreditation to work in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid for the accreditation period. Requires accreditation from the Uzbekistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs press service.

UZB.name: Journalist Visa - Temporary Accreditation (J-2)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign journalists on temporary assignment or event coverage in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid for the duration of the temporary accreditation or assignment.

UZB.name: Crew Member Visa (C-1)
UZB.purpose: Issued to crew members of international aircraft and railway services transiting or operating in Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 1 year, multiple entry. For international transport crew members on commercial routes.

UZB.name: Freight Driver Visa (C-2)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign commercial freight vehicle drivers operating on international routes through or into Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Valid up to 1 year, multiple entry. For international truck drivers on commercial freight routes.

UZB.name: Emergency Exit Visa (EXIT)
UZB.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who have overstayed their permitted period and require authorization to depart Uzbekistan.
UZB.notes: Up to 1 month. Issued to resolve overstay situations and allow lawful departure. Applied for at the relevant immigration authority.

UZB.name: Group Electronic Visa (e-visa group)
UZB.purpose: Online group visa application for organized tourist groups of 5 or more persons from eligible countries.
UZB.notes: Per-person fee of $20+ for group e-visa applications. Group must have a minimum of 5 persons from eligible e-visa nationalities. Applied via e-visa.gov.uz portal.

UZB.name: IT Visa
UZB.purpose: Long-term visa for foreign IT specialists, IT Park resident founders, and IT-sector investors to live and work in Uzbekistan without a separate work permit.
UZB.notes: Valid 3 years, renewable every 3 years. Allows work in Uzbekistan without a work permit and grants social rights equal to citizens; immediate family members may also obtain the visa. Eligibility (per rules updated 7 March 2026): IT specialists must confirm IT income of at least USD 30,000 over the prior 12 months; IT-sector investors qualify with financing of at least USD 10,000 to a resident IT legal entity; founders of IT Park resident companies are also eligible. Applied online via itvisa.uz; also enables IT Park resident status.

VAT.name: No separate Vatican tourist visa - entry via Italy/Schengen
VAT.purpose: Vatican City issues no national tourist visa. Foreign nationals who are lawfully admitted to Italy under Schengen rules may enter Vatican City freely through its five guarded entrances (St. Peter's Square, Arco delle Campane, Porta Sant'Anna, Porta Perugino, and the access via the Vatican Museums).
VAT.notes: Entry is governed by the Lateran Treaty open-border arrangement with Italy (1929). The vaticanstate.va population page confirms: 'Acquiring and losing citizenship, permits to reside within the State's territory and any other formality related to access are regulated by specific provisions, issued in line with the Lateran Treaty.' The Secretariat of State informazione_generale page references Law N. III of 7 June 1929 on citizenship and residence and Regulation N. XXXVI of 27 September 1932 as the governing instruments. A 2011 law (Law N. CXXXI of 22 February 2011) on citizenship, residence and access is referenced in Vatican population data but is NOT cited on the informazione_generale page; both references are retained pending clarification. Vatican City does not publish a separate tourist visa scheme. Visitors holding a valid Schengen visa or qualifying under Schengen visa-exempt rules for Italy may enter. Most public areas (St. Peter's Square, Basilica) are freely accessible during opening hours; the Vatican Museums require a ticketed entry but no visa. ETIAS - the EU travel authorisation - is expected in late 2026 and will apply to roughly 59 currently visa-exempt nationalities entering via Italy; Vatican City citizens and European microstates (Andorra, Monaco, San Marino) are ETIAS-exempt.

VAT.name: Authorisation to reside / access (non-citizens/non-residents)
VAT.purpose: Chapter Three of Law N. CXXXI of 22 February 2011 provides for individual authorisations for non-citizens and non-residents who need access to Vatican City beyond normal public visiting hours or to restricted areas (e.g. staff of accredited Holy See entities, researchers, accredited journalists). These authorisations are granted by Vatican authorities on a case-by-case basis.
VAT.notes: The full text of Chapter Three of Law N. CXXXI of 2011 is not publicly available in English on any official Vatican domain. Authorisations are not equivalent to visas and are not available to the general public through a publicly documented application process. Separate from, and in addition to, any required Italy/Schengen entry credentials.

VAT.name: Diplomatic / official access (accredited personnel)
VAT.purpose: Diplomatic, consular, and official personnel accredited to the Holy See, and staff of international organisations with agreements with the Holy See, are granted access to Vatican City through accreditation procedures administered by the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State and the Secretariat of State.
VAT.notes: The Holy See maintains diplomatic relations with over 180 states. Diplomatic personnel are accredited to the Holy See (not Vatican City State per se) through normal diplomatic channels. No online application portal is publicly available. Vatican City is not a Schengen member but operates an open border with Italy under the Lateran Treaty; diplomatic staff must still comply with Italy/Schengen entry requirements or hold a diplomatic visa for Italy.

VAT.name: Residence by reason of office / service
VAT.purpose: Vatican citizenship and the right to reside in Vatican City are granted to specific categories of persons holding qualifying ecclesiastical or administrative appointments: Cardinals resident in Vatican City, Holy See diplomats on active mission, Pontifical Swiss Guards, and other persons residing in Vatican City by reason of office. Citizenship - and thus residence - is automatically lost when the qualifying appointment ends.
VAT.notes: This is not a conventional work visa but a functional citizenship/residency tied to employment by the Holy See or Vatican City State. Governed by Law N. III of 7 June 1929 on citizenship and residence (per the informazione_generale page) and potentially also Law N. CXXXI of 22 February 2011 (referenced in population data). Only the Pope holds Vatican citizenship for life. No application process is publicly documented for external applicants; appointments are made by the Holy See through internal ecclesiastical and administrative procedures. As of December 31, 2024 (per vaticanstate.va population page re-verified 2026-06-29), 673 citizens and 882 residents (citizens + non-citizens) exist.

VCT.name: Transit Visa
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals transiting through Saint Vincent and the Grenadines to a destination outside the country. Required only for nationalities that cannot enter visa-free.
VCT.notes: Fee is EC$200 (approximately USD 74 at 2.7 EC per USD). Application submitted through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Consular Section) or Ministry of National Security. Only nationals of the 12 visa-required countries need this visa; all others transit visa-free. The official MFA page lists transit visa as a distinct category.

VCT.name: Short-stay Visa
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Saint Vincent and the Grenadines for tourism, holiday, or short-term stays. Applies to the 12 nationalities that cannot enter visa-free.
VCT.notes: Fee is EC$200 (approximately USD 74 at 2.7 EC per USD). Application submitted through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Section or via fax to the Ministry of National Security. Applicants must provide: passport bio-page copy, 2 passport photographs, sponsorship letter, police character certificate, proof of financial means, hotel/accommodation reservation (where applicable), travel itinerary. Interview with proposed sponsor may be arranged. The official MFA page lists short-stay visa as a distinct category. Most nationalities do not require this visa and are admitted visa-free on arrival.

VCT.name: Short-stay Visa (Business)
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Saint Vincent and the Grenadines for business meetings, negotiations, or commercial activities on a short-term basis.
VCT.notes: Fee is EC$200 (approximately USD 74 at 2.7 EC per USD). Business purposes are processed under the short-stay visa category. Only applicable to the 12 visa-required nationalities. Most nationals enter visa-free for business short stays. No separate business visa category is listed; business falls under short-stay.

VCT.name: Student Visa
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to study at an educational institution in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
VCT.notes: Fee is EC$200 (approximately USD 74 at 2.7 EC per USD). The official MFA visas page explicitly lists 'Student' as a distinct visa category. Specific processing times, duration, and additional requirements for student visas are not published on official online sources as of June 2026. Applicants should contact the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Section at (784) 456-2060 or office.foreignaffairs@mail.gov.vc.

VCT.name: Long-stay Visa
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to remain in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines for an extended period beyond the short-stay allowance, for purposes such as extended work, family, or residence.
VCT.notes: Fee is EC$200 (approximately USD 74 at 2.7 EC per USD). The official MFA visas page explicitly lists 'Long-stay Visa' as a distinct visa category. Specific duration, validity, conditions, and additional requirements are not published on official online sources as of June 2026. Applicants should contact the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Section at (784) 456-2060 or office.foreignaffairs@mail.gov.vc.

VCT.name: Humanitarian Visa
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals requiring entry into Saint Vincent and the Grenadines on humanitarian grounds, such as medical emergencies or family crises.
VCT.notes: The official MFA visas page explicitly lists 'Humanitarian' as a distinct visa category. Fee, duration, processing time, and specific requirements are not published on official online sources as of June 2026. Humanitarian visa fee may differ from the standard EC$200. Applicants should contact the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Section at (784) 456-2060 or office.foreignaffairs@mail.gov.vc.

VCT.name: Immigrant Visa
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals intending to immigrate and settle permanently in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
VCT.notes: The official MFA visas page explicitly lists 'Immigrant' as a distinct visa category. Fee, processing time, eligibility criteria, and specific requirements for immigrant visa are not published on official online sources as of June 2026. Applicants should contact the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Section at (784) 456-2060 or office.foreignaffairs@mail.gov.vc. Note: a Citizenship by Investment (CBI) program was announced in the February 2026 Budget Address with a mid-2026 launch target but has not yet been formally established.

VCT.name: Work Permit (Employment by an Employer)
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals taking up paid employment with an employer in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; must be approved before the foreign national may legally work.
VCT.notes: Administered by the Office of the Prime Minister (Residency Department), not the MFA. Official form: 'Work Permit Form to be Employed by an Employer' (pmoffice.gov.vc Forms page). A work permit is issued on a one-time basis for not more than six (6) months; applicants requiring more than six months must also apply for a residence permit. Application fee EC$150 (~USD 56, non-refundable) with additional fees due on approval per the official fees schedule. Processing averages six (6) to eight (8) weeks. Requirements: completed form, employer letter, certified passport bio-pages, proof the position was advertised, police record. Verified July 2026 from pmoffice.gov.vc, svgconsulate.vc, and svghighcom.co.uk.

VCT.name: Work Permit (Self-Employment)
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals engaging in self-employment for occupation, reward, or profit in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
VCT.notes: Administered by the Office of the Prime Minister (Residency Department). Official form: 'Self-employed Work Permit Form' (pmoffice.gov.vc Forms page). Covers self-employment for occupation, reward, or profit and is a distinct application from the employer-sponsored work permit. Issued one-time for not more than six (6) months; longer stays require a residence permit. Application fee EC$150 (~USD 56, non-refundable) plus additional fees on approval per the official fees schedule. Processing averages six (6) to eight (8) weeks. Medical students accepted for electives at Milton Cato Memorial Hospital are exempt from work permits. Verified July 2026.

VCT.name: Temporary Residence Permit
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals wishing to reside in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines for an extended period beyond the visitor-permit allowance.
VCT.notes: Administered by the Office of the Prime Minister (Residency Department). Official form: 'Temporary Residence Application Form' (pmoffice.gov.vc Forms page). Open to anyone wishing to reside in SVG for an extended period; also required (in addition to a work permit) where employment exceeds six months. Application fee EC$150 (~USD 56, non-refundable); non-CARICOM applicants with an interest in land pay an additional fee of EC$6,000 per the official fees schedule. Processing averages six (6) to eight (8) weeks. Verified July 2026.

VCT.name: Permanent Residence Permit
VCT.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking indefinite residence in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines after long-term temporary residence or land ownership.
VCT.notes: Administered by the Office of the Prime Minister (Residency Department). Eligibility per the official FAQ: the applicant must have held temporary residence for seven (7) or more consecutive years, or hold an Alien's Land-Holding Licence. Fee amounts are set out in the official fees schedule (pmoffice.gov.vc Forms page: 'Fees for Residence, Work Permits, Citizenship etc.') but are not itemised online; the standard non-refundable application fee is EC$150. Processing averages six (6) to eight (8) weeks. Verified July 2026.

VEN.name: Visa de Turista (T)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Venezuela for recreation, leisure, health purposes, or other non-remunerated activities. Applies to nationalities not on the visa-free list.
VEN.notes: Dedicated official MPPRE visa page: mppre.gob.ve/descripcion/30. Requires valid passport (6+ months), proof of residency, 2 photos, bank statement, employment letter, round-trip ticket, medical certificate, hotel reservation or invitation, and consular fee receipt. Fee amount must be confirmed at the relevant Venezuelan diplomatic or consular office. As of April 2026, Venezuela also offers an electronic visa option (TR-V tourist category) via cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Turista (TR-V) - Electronic
VEN.purpose: Electronic tourist visa for foreign nationals wishing to enter Venezuela for tourism; mandatory e-visa system for all nationalities requiring a visa to enter Venezuela.
VEN.notes: Introduced as part of Venezuela's mandatory electronic visa system as of April 2026. Applied online at cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve. Visa delivered electronically via email. Fee of USD 180 is reported by multiple aggregators but has NOT been confirmed from an official Venezuelan government page - verify at cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve. Processing approximately 10-15 days. A user manual (febrero 2026) for this category is published by MPPRE at mppre.gob.ve/cancilleria-digital.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Negocios (TR-N)
VEN.purpose: Issued to merchants, executives, company/industry representatives and micro-entrepreneurs (non-migrants) entering Venezuela for commercial, mercantile, financial or other lawful profit-related business activity, without taking up employment.
VEN.notes: The dedicated official MPPRE page (mppre.gob.ve/descripcion/28) specifies 1-year validity, multiple entries, and a maximum stay of 90 days per entry (non-extendable). Available via Venezuela's mandatory electronic visa system (cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve) as of April 2026, and also through Venezuelan embassies and consulates. Visa delivered electronically via email. Fee of USD 180 reported by aggregators but not confirmed from an official Venezuelan government page - verify at cancilleriadigital.mppre.gob.ve.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Laboral (TR-L)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals who have been offered employment in Venezuela and wish to enter the country to work for a Venezuelan employer.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with an equal permitted period of stay. Authorisation is issued by the Ministry of Interior, Justice and Peace with prior approval from the Ministry of Labour; the applicant or employer must file the request. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee must be confirmed at the relevant diplomatic mission.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Estudiante (TR-E)
VEN.purpose: For non-migrant foreign nationals entering Venezuela to pursue higher, technical or university education, specialization, or internships in their field at a recognized Venezuelan institution.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with an equal permitted period of stay. Extensions are requested from the Ministry of Interior, Justice and Peace at least two months in advance. Requires proof of enrollment at a Venezuelan educational institution. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee confirmed at the relevant mission.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Inversionista (TR-I)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals who make a productive investment in Venezuela, requiring at least 20% ownership in a registered Venezuelan company or equivalent capital contribution.
VEN.notes: Dedicated official MPPRE page (mppre.gob.ve/descripcion/27) confirms 3-year validity, multiple entries, and no limit on length of stay in the country. Extendable up to 2 additional years; afterwards can apply for Resident status (5-year validity). No minimum investment amount specified on official pages. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Rentista (TR-RE)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals who can demonstrate a stable passive income (rentier income) allowing them to support themselves in Venezuela without employment.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with an equal permitted period of stay; renewable through the Ministry of Interior, Justice and Peace if income sources remain valid. Official MPPRE page requires proof of monthly income of USD 1,200 from foreign sources, plus USD 500 per accompanying family member. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate. Suitable for retirees or others with independent income sources.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Rentista (TR-RE) - Retirement
VEN.purpose: The TR-RE (Rentista) visa category also covers retired foreign nationals who can demonstrate sufficient passive/pension income to reside in Venezuela without working.
VEN.notes: Venezuela does not have a dedicated retirement visa; retirees apply under the TR-RE (Rentista) category. Valid 1 year, multiple entries, equal permitted stay, renewable. Official MPPRE page requires proof of monthly income of USD 1,200 from foreign sources, plus USD 500 per accompanying family member. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Familiar Venezolano (TR-FV)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals who are family members of a Venezuelan citizen and wish to reside in or visit Venezuela based on that family relationship.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with no limit on length of stay in the country. Applies to spouses of Venezuelan citizens, unmarried children under 18, and parents of Venezuelan citizens, with documented family ties. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Familiar Migrante Permanente (TR-FMP)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals who are family members of a permanent resident (migrante permanente) in Venezuela, allowing them to join the resident family member.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with no limit on length of stay in the country. Applies to family members of Venezuelan permanent residents (not citizens). Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee confirmed at the relevant mission.

VEN.name: Visa de Tránsito (V-T)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals whose itinerary includes a stopover in Venezuelan territory en route to a third country.
VEN.notes: Official MPPRE page: 72 hours (3 days) per entry; single entry, or two entries if the return itinerary also requires transit through Venezuela. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee confirmed at the relevant mission.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Religioso (TR-REL)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Venezuela to carry out religious activities, missionary work, or ministry as part of a recognized religious organization.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with an equal permitted period of stay. Requires documentation from a recognized religious institution. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee confirmed at the relevant mission.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Empresario/Industrial (TR-EI)
VEN.purpose: For foreign entrepreneurs or industrial operators who wish to establish or operate a business or industrial enterprise in Venezuela.
VEN.notes: Official MPPRE page: valid 2 years, multiple entries, up to 4 months per entry (non-extendable per entry). Distinct from the TR-I Investor visa; intended for entrepreneurs and industrial operators. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee confirmed at the relevant mission.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Empleado Doméstico (TR-ED)
VEN.purpose: For foreign nationals employed as domestic workers in the household of a Venezuelan citizen or legal resident.
VEN.notes: Valid 1 year, multiple entries, with an equal permitted period of stay; may be extended for the same period through the Ministry of Interior on request by the sponsoring diplomat/household. Requires proof of domestic employment and sponsor details. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate.

VEN.name: Visa de Transeúnte Reingreso (TR-RI)
VEN.purpose: A re-entry visa for foreign nationals who held a previous Venezuelan visa or residence status and wish to return to Venezuela.
VEN.notes: Official MPPRE page: valid 6 months, single entry. Re-entry visa for former residents or visa holders returning to Venezuela. Must be applied for at a Venezuelan embassy or consulate; consular fee confirmed at the relevant mission.

VNM.name: E-Visa (Electronic Visa, symbol EV)
VNM.purpose: Tourism, business, and other short-term visits for nationals of all countries
VNM.notes: Symbol EV (Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13). Available to nationals of all countries and territories. Single-entry USD 25 or multiple-entry USD 50 (Circular 25/2021/TT-BTC). Up to 90 days stay and 90-day validity - extended from the original 30 days by Law 23/2023/QH15 (effective 15 Aug 2023). Applied online at the official Vietnam Immigration Department portal; accepted at all international airports, land borders, and seaports.

VNM.name: Visa on Arrival (with Pre-Approved Letter)
VNM.notes: Only valid at international airports (not land/sea borders). Requires pre-approved letter from Vietnamese Immigration Department (obtained through licensed travel agent or online service - not an official government portal for this specific service). USD 25 stamping fee paid on arrival + service fee for approval letter (varies, typically USD 20-30). Effectively replaced by the e-Visa system for most travelers.

VNM.name: Tourist Visa (symbol DL)
VNM.purpose: Foreign tourists entering Vietnam for leisure travel
VNM.notes: Symbol DL under Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13; valid up to 3 months per Article 9. Issued at Vietnamese diplomatic missions abroad (or delivered as an e-visa carrying the DL purpose). Fee USD 25 single-entry / USD 50 multiple-entry up to 3 months (Circular 25/2021/TT-BTC). Most tourists now use the EV e-visa instead.

VNM.name: Business Visa (symbols DN1, DN2)
VNM.purpose: Foreigners working with Vietnamese enterprises/organizations (DN1) or offering services / establishing commercial presence under treaty (DN2)
VNM.notes: Symbols DN1 (working with an enterprise/organization that has legal status under Vietnamese law) and DN2 (offering services, establishing commercial presence, or other activities under an international treaty), Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13. Valid up to 12 months (Article 9) and requires a sponsoring Vietnamese entity. Fee scales with validity/entries per Circular 25/2021/TT-BTC (multiple-entry up to 3 months USD 50; up to 6 months USD 95; up to 1 year USD 135). Short business visits are also possible on the EV e-visa.

VNM.name: Work Visa - Work Permit Required (symbol LĐ2)
VNM.purpose: Foreign nationals employed in Vietnam who must hold a work permit
VNM.notes: Symbol LĐ2 (Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13). Requires BOTH a work permit (Giấy phép lao động) issued by the competent provincial labour authority (DOLISA, formerly under MOLISA) - employer-sponsored, needing a criminal-record check, health certificate and qualification documents - AND the LĐ2 entry visa issued by the Immigration Department. Valid up to 2 years, renewable (Article 9). Visa fee USD 145 for a 1-2 year multiple-entry visa (Circular 25/2021/TT-BTC). Holders may then obtain a temporary residence card.

VNM.name: Work Visa - Work Permit Exempt (symbol LĐ1)
VNM.purpose: Foreign workers who hold a work-permit-exemption confirmation
VNM.notes: Symbol LĐ1 (Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13). For foreigners certified as exempt from a work permit - e.g. capital-contributing owners/members of an LLC, chairpersons/board members of a joint-stock company, intra-corporate transferees in the WTO service sectors, or others confirmed exempt by the labour authority. Valid up to 2 years (Article 9). A work-permit-exemption confirmation must be obtained before the LĐ1 visa is issued.

VNM.name: Student / Intern Visa (symbol DH)
VNM.purpose: Foreigners coming to Vietnam to study or undertake an internship
VNM.notes: Symbol DH under Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13. For students and interns at Vietnamese schools, universities, or organizations. Valid up to 12 months (Article 9). Requires an admission/invitation letter from the sponsoring educational institution. Fee per Circular 25/2021/TT-BTC (single-entry USD 25; longer multiple-entry visas cost more).

VNM.name: Family / Dependent Visa (symbol TT)
VNM.purpose: Spouse, parents, and children under 18 of certain visa holders or of Vietnamese citizens
VNM.notes: Symbol TT under Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13. Issued to the spouse, children under 18, and parents of foreigners holding an LV1, LV2, ĐT, NN1, NN2, DH, PV1 or LĐ visa, and to the spouse, children, or parents of Vietnamese citizens. Valid up to 12 months (Article 9). Requires proof of the family relationship and the sponsor's status.

VNM.name: Visiting Relatives Visa (symbol VR)
VNM.purpose: Foreigners visiting relatives or entering for other personal purposes
VNM.notes: Symbol VR under Article 8, Law 47/2014/QH13. For visiting relatives or other purposes not covered by another symbol. Valid up to 6 months (Article 9). Requires a Vietnamese sponsor/guarantor.

VUT.name: Tourist Visa (eVisa)
VUT.purpose: For non-exempt nationals wishing to visit Vanuatu for tourism, family visits, or short-stay purposes. Employment, commercial, or business activities are not permitted.
VUT.notes: Available via evisa.gov.vu for nationalities not on the visa-exempt list. Extension is not allowed. Fee is 5,150 VUV. Must be approved before travelling to Vanuatu.

VUT.name: Visitors Visa
VUT.purpose: For visitors intending to stay in Vanuatu for up to 30 days. Requires proof of intent to depart and financial capacity.
VUT.notes: Fee 3,600 VUV. Requires completed Visitor Application Form, valid passport, return ticket, proof of funds. Also available via evisa.gov.vu (fee 7,420 VUV on that portal). 30-day stay limit evidenced by requirement to depart within 30 days.

VUT.name: Extended Visitors Visa
VUT.purpose: Extension of a visitor's stay in Vanuatu for up to 4 months (from initial entry). For those who need to extend beyond their original visitor visa.
VUT.notes: Fee 6,000 VUV for a visa valid up to 4 months. Applied for in-country. Requires Extended Visa Application Form, valid passport, photographs, return ticket, evidence of reasons and funds. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 (Sections 42, 43, 46, 60) and Immigration Visa Regulation Order 2011.

VUT.name: Interim Visa
VUT.purpose: A transitional visa for applicants awaiting a decision on a longer-stay visa or whose status is otherwise pending. Requires undertaking from a Vanuatu citizen.
VUT.notes: Fee 10,000 VUV. Applied for in-country. Requires Extended Visa Application Form, passport copy, photographs, return ticket, evidence of reasons, funds, and undertaking from a Vanuatu citizen. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 (Sections 27(a), 31(a)).

VUT.name: Transit Visa
VUT.purpose: For travellers passing through Vanuatu in transit to a third destination.
VUT.notes: Fee 1,800 VUV. Requires Transit Visa Application Form, valid passport, travel itinerary. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 (Sections 34–37, 75–76) and Immigration Visa Regulation Order 2011.

VUT.name: Student Visa
VUT.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled in an educational institution in Vanuatu. Requires evidence of enrollment and medical examination.
VUT.notes: Fee 2,880 VUV (for applicants under 18; fees for adults not stated on portal page). Requires Student Visa Application Form, valid passport, evidence of enrollment, security deposit, evidence of funds, medical examination. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 (Sections 35(1), 37(a-e)).

VUT.name: Business Visa
VUT.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting Vanuatu for business-related activities, including meetings, conferences, and employer-sponsored visits.
VUT.notes: Fee 20,000 VUV for single entry. Requires Business Visa Application Form, valid passport, photographs, letter from employer, letter of acceptance from employer, employer's business registration or license, proof of relationship (if family), and government cashier receipt. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 (Section 44) and Immigration Visa Regulation Order 2011.

VUT.name: Employment Visa
VUT.purpose: For persons under acceptable sponsorship from an employer to undertake skilled work in Vanuatu for a period of more than two months. The applicant may include their spouse (married or de facto) and any children in the application.
VUT.notes: Fee 51,500 VUV. Valid 1 to 4 months, multiple entry. For employer-sponsored skilled work exceeding two months; spouse (married or de facto) and children may be included in the application. A separate Work Permit from the Department of Labour is also required to work legally in Vanuatu. Source: immigration.gov.vu/work/.

VUT.name: Specialist Skills Visa
VUT.purpose: For persons under acceptable sponsorship from an employer to undertake specialist skills work in Vanuatu for not more than two weeks.
