VUT.notes: Fee 30,900 VUV. Single entry. For employer-sponsored specialist skills work not exceeding two weeks. Requires terms of reference, a letter from the requesting Vanuatu-registered company, a valid passport, and a return ticket to country of origin. Source: immigration.gov.vu/specialist/.

VUT.name: Special Category Visa
VUT.purpose: For foreign nationals who do not fall under standard visa categories; for specific circumstances as defined by the immigration authority.
VUT.notes: Fee not specified on portal. Requires Special Category Visa Application Form, valid passport, photographs, certified birth certificate, police clearance, medical examination, marriage/death/divorce certificates as applicable, and letter of recommendation. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 (Sections 32, 44(a-e), 45(4)).

VUT.name: Residence Visa
VUT.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking to reside in Vanuatu for 1 year based on employment, land ownership, foreign investor status, or self-funding.
VUT.notes: Fee 57,600 VUV for applicants aged 18+ for a 1-year visa. Requires Residence Application Form, valid passport, photographs, police clearance, medical examination, certified birth/marriage/death/divorce certificates, supporting documents based on status (employment letter, land ownership proof, foreign investor documentation, or self-funding evidence), and security deposit. Governed by Immigration Visa Regulation Order 2011 (Articles 6, 12, 16).

VUT.name: Permanent Residence Visa
VUT.purpose: For foreign nationals seeking permanent residency in Vanuatu. Grants long-term right to reside in Vanuatu.
VUT.notes: Fee not specified on tradeportal page; evisa.gov.vu data indicates 206,000 VUV for individuals, 463,500 VUV for family of 4, 100,000 VUV per additional child. Requires Vanuatu Permanent Residence Application Form. Governed by Immigration Act 2010 and Immigration Visa Regulation Order No. 180 of 2011. Note: Cannot engage in employment, commercial, or business activities.

VUT.name: Diplomatic Visa
VUT.purpose: For non-citizens holding diplomatic passports on a diplomatic mission for a foreign government in Vanuatu, including their family members.
VUT.notes: Fee-exempt. Duration at Director's discretion. Multiple entry. Only for holders of diplomatic passports on official diplomatic missions.

VUT.name: Provisional Investor Visa
VUT.purpose: For non-citizens intending to invest in Vanuatu who are in the phase of setting up a business while communicating with VFIPA and VFSC.
VUT.notes: Fee 51,500 VUV. Duration 1 year, multiple entry. Extendable. Can change status to Business Investor Visa. Applicant must be in phase of setting up a business while communicating with VFIPA and VFSC.

VUT.name: Business Investor Visa
VUT.purpose: For individuals who have been granted a Foreign Investment Approval Certificate by VFIPA, a certificate of registration from VFSC, or a business license from relevant authorities.
VUT.notes: Fee 206,000 VUV. Duration 3 years, multiple entry, renewable. Can change status to Direct Investor Visa or Permanent Investor Visa. Requires VFIPA Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, VFSC registration, or business license.

VUT.name: Direct Investor Visa
VUT.purpose: For individuals who have deposited a bond into a nominated Government bank account for 8 years and provided proof of sufficient funds to cover ongoing living expenses.
VUT.notes: Fee 309,000 VUV. Duration 8 years, multiple entry. Can change to Investor Visa or Leasehold Owner Visa. Requires bond deposit into nominated Government bank account for 8-year term and proof of sufficient funds for living expenses.

VUT.name: Permanent Investor Visa
VUT.purpose: For foreign investors who have been residing lawfully and continuously in Vanuatu for at least 10 years and are maintaining ownership and management of their business.
VUT.notes: Fee 3,090,000 VUV. Duration indefinite, multiple entry. Requires 10 years of lawful continuous residence in Vanuatu and active ownership/management of business.

VUT.name: Retiree Visa
VUT.purpose: For non-citizens aged 50 or above proposing to retire in Vanuatu. Cannot engage in employment, commercial, or business activities.
VUT.notes: Fee 309,000 VUV. Duration 10 years, multiple entry. Extendable. Applicant must be aged 50 or above. Cannot engage in employment, commercial, or business activities.

VUT.name: Self-Funded / Leasehold Holder Visa
VUT.purpose: For non-citizens with leasehold ownership of property certified to be worth VT 10,000,000 or more, and monthly income of at least VT 250,000 per person. Must reside physically in Vanuatu.
VUT.notes: Fee 59,330 VUV. Duration 12 months, multiple entry. Requires leasehold ownership of property certified at VT 10,000,000 or more, and income of at least VT 250,000/month per person (max 1,000,000 VUV). Must reside physically in Vanuatu. Can change to investor visa.

WSM.name: Visitor's Permit (on arrival)
WSM.purpose: Grants all foreign nationals the right to enter Samoa for tourism, visiting family, or short-term business without a prior visa. Issued on arrival at the port of entry using the arrival card.
WSM.notes: Available to ALL nationalities without exception (except US Nationals of American Samoa who are exempt from the permit requirement). Visitors must: hold a passport valid for at least 6 months after intended departure date; have a return or onward ticket; hold a valid visa/permit for onward destination; have documented accommodation; provide evidence of sufficient funds; have no record of deportation; have no health problems posing a risk to Samoa; have no criminal convictions resulting in sentences of 1 year or more; not appear on any alert or warning list. Extensions beyond 90 days must be applied for at the Immigration Office in Apia before expiration. No e-visa or prior application required.

WSM.name: Extended Stay Permit
WSM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to stay in Samoa beyond the standard 90-day Visitor's Permit, for continued tourism or personal visits.
WSM.notes: For stays exceeding 90 days, a permit extension must be applied for at the Immigration Office in Apia before the Visitor's Permit expires. For stays exceeding 60 days obtained before arrival, a permit must also be obtained in advance from the nearest Samoa diplomatic mission (Consulate General, High Commission, or Embassy in New Zealand, Australia, New York, Tokyo, Beijing, or Belgium). Extensions while already in Samoa are handled by Samoa Immigration (MPMC - Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet).

WSM.name: Visitor's Permit (Business, on arrival)
WSM.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Samoa for short-term business activities such as meetings, negotiations, and conferences.
WSM.notes: Business visitors are covered under the same universal Visitor's Permit on arrival as tourists. No separate business visa category exists for short stays under 90 days. All nationalities are eligible. Longer-term business activity requiring employment requires a Foreign Employment Permit (FEEP).

WSM.name: Foreign Employment Employee Permit (FEEP)
WSM.purpose: Authorises a specific foreign national to work for a specific employer in a specific role in Samoa. Issued under Part IX of the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 (as amended 2023).
WSM.notes: The employer (not the employee) must apply before the employee commences work. MCIL reviews applications against local labour market conditions. The permit is non-transferable between employers or roles. Valid for up to 3 years, subject to conditions set by the MCIL CEO. The foreign employee must also hold a valid Residence Permit (issued separately by MPMC). Contact: employmentinfo@mcil.gov.ws or +685 20 442.

WSM.name: Residence Permit
WSM.purpose: Authorises a foreign national to reside in Samoa for an extended period, required in conjunction with a Foreign Employment Permit for workers.
WSM.notes: Administered by the Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (MPMC) - Immigration Division. Required alongside the FEEP for any foreigner working in Samoa. Also required as part of the Citizenship Investment Act 2015 pathway (Temporary Resident Permit stage). Detailed permit types, fees, and eligibility rules were not accessible from the MPMC website (returns HTTP 403) at time of research (June 2026). Applicants are advised to contact MPMC Immigration directly.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Investment Pathway)
WSM.purpose: First stage of the Citizenship Investment Act 2015 pathway, granted to qualifying foreign investors who invest WST 4 million or more in Samoa.
WSM.notes: Administered by MCIL under the Citizenship Investment Act 2015 (launched 31 January 2017). Qualifying investments include: leasing/developing government lands; processing/manufacturing of agricultural or fishery products; tourism hotel/resort development; ICT; renewable electricity generation; or other services not restricted under the Foreign Investment Act 2000. The pathway progresses from Temporary Resident Permit → Permanent Resident Permit (minimum 15 days per year physical presence required) → citizenship eligibility after 3 years. No investor has completed the process as of June 2026.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Study)
WSM.purpose: Foreign nationals enrolled in an academic programme at a recognised Samoan educational institution.
WSM.notes: One of the six Temporary Resident Permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020 (administered by MPMC Immigration Division). Requires the MPMC100 application form, a letter of acceptance from the local counterpart in Samoa, a confirmation-of-enrolment letter from the university/institution, and evidence of sufficient funds. Medical (MPMC102) and police (MPMC103) reports are required for stays exceeding one year. Students may work part-time if authorised on the permit. Applications should be lodged at least 4 weeks before travel; fees are set by the MPMC fee schedule.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Medical Elective / Treatment)
WSM.purpose: Foreign nationals coming to Samoa for medical electives, short-term clinical attachments, exchange programmes, or medical treatment.
WSM.notes: Issued as a Temporary Resident Permit for 'medical electives / short-term attachments / exchange programme', per the official Embassy of Samoa (Belgium). Stated fee EUR 470 (approx. USD 510). Medical students must provide a confirmation letter from the Samoa Ministry of Health plus evidence of funds. Requires the MPMC100 form, passport bio-data, acceptance letter from the local counterpart, university confirmation, accommodation confirmation, and medical/police reports. Submit at least 4 weeks before departure.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Business and Investment)
WSM.purpose: Foreign nationals establishing, operating, or holding an investment in a business in Samoa.
WSM.notes: One of the six Temporary Resident Permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020 (MPMC Immigration Division). Requires an Investment Certificate, Business License and Company Registration, plus the MPMC100 form and (for stays over one year) medical (MPMC102) and police (MPMC103) reports. Distinct from the Citizenship Investment Act 2015 investment-to-citizenship pathway: this is the general immigration permit for running a business or holding an investment in Samoa, not a citizenship route.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Family Support / Reunion)
WSM.purpose: Foreign nationals joining or being supported by family members resident in Samoa, including spouses and dependent children.
WSM.notes: One of the six Temporary Resident Permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020 (MPMC Immigration Division). Requires a host accommodation/support letter, the MPMC100 form, and (for stays over one year) medical (MPMC102) and police (MPMC103) reports. Used for family reunion and dependent support of residents/citizens.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Academic and Scientific Research)
WSM.purpose: Foreign researchers conducting academic or scientific research in Samoa.
WSM.notes: One of the six Temporary Resident Permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020 (MPMC Immigration Division). Requires a letter of support from the sponsoring institution, the MPMC100 form, and (for stays over one year) medical (MPMC102) and police (MPMC103) reports.

WSM.name: Temporary Resident Permit (Cultural and Religious)
WSM.purpose: Foreign nationals coming to Samoa for cultural or religious activities or events (e.g. missionaries, performers).
WSM.notes: One of the six Temporary Resident Permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020 (MPMC Immigration Division). Requires a confirmation letter from the event/activity organiser, the MPMC100 form, and (for stays over one year) medical (MPMC102) and police (MPMC103) reports.

WSM.name: Permanent Resident Permit
WSM.purpose: Long-term foreign residents, significant investors, and spouses or dependent children of Samoan citizens seeking permanent residence.
WSM.notes: One of the four entry-permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020 (MPMC Immigration Division). Typically granted after sustained lawful temporary residence (commonly cited as 10+ years), through significant economic contribution/investment, or via family ties to a Samoan citizen. Requires the MPMC100 form, medical (MPMC102) and police (MPMC103) reports, extensive supporting documentation, and background checks.

WSM.name: Ministerial Permit
WSM.purpose: Discretionary permit for exceptional or special cases falling outside the standard permit categories.
WSM.notes: One of the four entry-permit categories under the Immigration Act 2020. A discretionary permit issued at the discretion of the Minister responsible for immigration, used for special or exceptional cases not covered by the Visitor, Temporary Resident, or Permanent Resident permit categories.

XKX.name: Kosovo C Visa (Short-Stay Visa)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit or transit through Kosovo for tourism, leisure, or short-stay purposes. Applies to nationals of countries that are not on the visa-free list.
XKX.notes: Fee is 40 EUR (approx. 43 USD). Applications must be lodged in person at Kosovo's Embassy in Tirana, Albania or Consulate General in Istanbul, Turkey, no more than 3 months before intended travel. Requires completed application form, recent ICAO-compliant photo, valid travel document (expiry at least 3 months beyond departure, 2 blank pages), proof of accommodation, sufficient financial means, travel medical insurance valid in Kosovo, and documents indicating purpose of journey. Diplomatic/official passport holders are fee-exempt and need not apply in person. Children under 6, school children, students, and teachers on study/training visits are also fee-exempt. Visa refusals may be contested within 8 calendar days.

XKX.name: Kosovo C Visa (Transit Visa)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to transit through Kosovo. Covered under the same short-stay C visa category as tourist/visit visas.
XKX.notes: Transit is explicitly covered under the Kosovo C Visa. The same 40 EUR fee and application requirements apply. Nationals holding a valid biometric Schengen residence permit or valid multi-entry Schengen visa may transit without a visa for up to 15 days. Laissez-Passer holders from UN, NATO, OSCE, Council of Europe and EU are fully exempt from visa requirements.

XKX.name: Kosovo C Visa (Short-Stay Business Visa)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Kosovo for business meetings, negotiations, or short-term commercial activities. Falls under the general C visa (short-stay) framework.
XKX.notes: Kosovo does not publish a separately named 'business visa'; business visitors from visa-required countries use the same C visa application process with business purpose documentation. Same 40 EUR fee applies. Applicants must provide documents indicating the business purpose of the journey.

XKX.name: Kosovo D Visa - Family Reunification (Temporary Residence Permit)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to obtain a long-stay D visa as a precursor to a temporary residence permit for family reunification with Kosovo residents or citizens.
XKX.notes: The D visa is a long-stay entry visa used to apply for a temporary residence permit. The residence permit means any authorization by Kosovo authorities permitting lawful stay beyond a short-stay visa. The family reunification category is one of three officially documented D visa pathways. Applicants must submit standard visa documents plus additional category-specific PDF-documented requirements. The D (long-stay) visa fee is 80 EUR (approx. 86 USD), higher than the 40 EUR C visa fee. Applications must be lodged at Kosovo Embassy in Tirana or Consulate General in Istanbul.

XKX.name: Kosovo D Visa - Higher Education and Scientific Research (Temporary Residence Permit)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Kosovo for the purpose of higher education studies or scientific research, as a long-stay D visa leading to a temporary residence permit.
XKX.notes: One of three officially documented D visa categories for Kosovo. Covers temporary residence for higher education and scientific research. The D (long-stay) visa fee is 80 EUR (approx. 86 USD), though pupils, students and teachers travelling for studies or training may qualify for a fee exemption. Students on short study or training visits may alternatively use the C visa process. Detailed requirements are published in PDF form by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

XKX.name: Kosovo D Visa - Employment (Temporary Residence Permit within Annual Quota)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Kosovo for the purpose of employment within the annual employment quota, as a long-stay D visa leading to a temporary residence permit.
XKX.notes: One of three officially documented D visa categories for Kosovo. Covers temporary residence for the purpose of working within the annual employment quota. The D (long-stay) visa fee is 80 EUR (approx. 86 USD). Foreign nationals may also register and operate a business in Kosovo to obtain a temporary residence permit for employment/business purposes under Law 08/L-296 on Foreigners (5 years of continuous temporary residence leads to permanent residence eligibility). Detailed requirements are published in PDF form by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Applications are accepted at Kosovo Embassy in Tirana or Consulate General in Istanbul.

XKX.name: Diplomatic/Official Passport Visa Exemption
XKX.purpose: Holders of diplomatic and official passports are exempt from both the Kosovo visa fee and the in-person application requirement. Certain countries' diplomatic/service passport holders receive a short-stay visa-free exemption.
XKX.notes: Holders of diplomatic and official passports from all countries are exempted from the 40 EUR visa fee and need not apply in person (for C visa purposes). Additionally, holders of diplomatic and service passports from Russia, China, Egypt, Indonesia, and Ukraine receive a full 15-day visa-free entry without any visa application. No visa fee applies to diplomatic/official passport holders regardless of nationality.

XKX.name: Kosovo C Visa (Medical Treatment)
XKX.purpose: Allows foreign nationals from visa-required countries to enter Kosovo for short-term medical treatment. Covered under the general short-stay C visa framework.
XKX.notes: Kosovo does not issue a separately named 'medical visa'; medical treatment is a recognized purpose of the general short-stay C visa (max 90 days within 180). Applicants supply documents indicating the medical purpose of the journey (e.g. confirmation from the receiving medical institution) plus proof of sufficient financial means and travel medical insurance valid in Kosovo. Fee is 40 EUR (approx. 43 USD). Applications are lodged in person at Kosovo's Embassy in Tirana or Consulate General in Istanbul. Long-term medical care beyond 90 days requires a D visa and temporary residence permit.

XKX.name: Kosovo Blue Card (Temporary Residence for Highly Qualified Employment)
XKX.purpose: Temporary residence permit for highly qualified foreign nationals with recognized academic qualifications taking up highly skilled employment in Kosovo. Kosovo's EU-acquis-aligned equivalent of the EU Blue Card.
XKX.notes: Introduced by Law No. 08/L-296 on Foreigners (in force, replacing Law 04/L-219; full implementation completed 15 March 2026) as Kosovo's EU-acquis-aligned 'Blue Card' for highly qualified workers holding academic qualifications. Requires a prior long-stay D visa (80 EUR, approx. 86 USD) as the entry route, then a temporary residence permit issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MPB). Temporary residence permits are generally valid up to one year and renewable; 5 continuous years lead to permanent-residence eligibility. Distinct from the standard employment-quota D visa in that it targets highly skilled professionals.

XKX.name: Temporary Residence Permit on Humanitarian Grounds
XKX.purpose: Temporary residence for foreign nationals who qualify to stay in Kosovo on humanitarian grounds recognized under the Law on Foreigners.
XKX.notes: Humanitarian grounds are one of the temporary-residence purposes enumerated in Law No. 08/L-296 on Foreigners (alongside employment, secondment, family reunification and education). Permit is issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MPB) and is generally valid up to one year and renewable. Not a nationality-based waiver and not applied for at an embassy as a standard visa.

YEM.name: Group Tourism Visa
YEM.purpose: Allows organised group tourism to Yemen for sightseeing and leisure. Only accepted through accredited travel agencies with a minimum group size of 10 members.
YEM.notes: Only tourist group visas submitted by accredited travel agencies are currently accepted through the e-visa portal (launched June 24, 2025). The Yemen Embassy Washington DC states it is not issuing tourist visas at this time. The Yemen Permanent Mission to the UN also states it is not issuing tourist visas. Payment is cash-only in USD at the IPNA main centre in Aden or via embassies/consulates. Individual tourist visa applications are not accepted.

YEM.name: Visitor Visa
YEM.purpose: For foreign nationals visiting an inviting person or organisation in Yemen (e.g. relatives, friends, or a host entity). Requires the details of the inviting person or organisation.
YEM.notes: Distinct from the tourist visa: requires an invitation from a host person or organisation in Yemen rather than a travel-agency letter. Fee of $50 for a single-entry visa with 3-month (90-day) validity and approximately 2-week processing is per the Yemen Embassy in Poland (embassy-of-yemen.pl); fees and terms vary by mission and all entry visas require prior approval from Yemen's immigration authorities. Non-Yemenis must obtain entry-visa approval from inside Yemen.

YEM.name: Business Visa
YEM.purpose: Issued for business activities in Yemen including meetings, trade, and commercial activities. Requires an employer or sponsoring entity letter from Yemen.
YEM.notes: Requires an employer letter from a Yemeni company and MOFA Yemen approval. Fee of $65 (money order) is for embassy applications in the US; may vary at other missions. E-visa application also available via yemenevisa.org. Valid passport with at least 6 months validity required plus two passport photos and a doctor's letter confirming no contagious diseases.

YEM.name: Student Visa
YEM.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals accepted at Yemeni educational institutions for the purpose of study.
YEM.notes: Requires an acceptance letter from a Yemeni educational institution indicating the nature and duration of study. Application must include valid passport (6+ months), two passport photos, and a doctor's letter confirming no contagious diseases. Embassy in Washington DC handles applications for US-based applicants.

YEM.name: Work Visa
YEM.purpose: Authorises foreign nationals to reside and work in Yemen under a sponsor or employer.
YEM.notes: Listed as one of the five visa categories on the official e-visa portal (yemenevisa.org). Specific fee and stay duration not published in accessible static form on the portal (JavaScript SPA). Sponsor/employer in Yemen required.

YEM.name: Transit Visa
YEM.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to transit through Yemen en route to a third country.
YEM.notes: Listed as one of the five visa categories on the official e-visa portal. Onward ticket confirmation required. Specific fee and stay duration not published in accessible static form on the portal (JavaScript SPA).

YEM.name: Diplomatic / Official Visa
YEM.purpose: Issued to diplomats, government officials, and staff of international organisations on official missions to Yemen.
YEM.notes: Listed as one of the five categories on the e-visa portal. Embassy Washington DC requires two typed application forms, valid passport (6+ months), two passport photos, and an original letter from the concerned government agency. Must include sponsor/host information in Yemen. The Yemen Embassy Netherlands issues entry visas for diplomats at a fee of approximately EUR 50 with approximately 2-week processing.

YEM.name: Entry Visa (Yemeni Origin / International Organisation / Media)
YEM.purpose: Special entry visa issued to persons of Yemeni origin, workers at international organisations, and journalists or media delegates, as the only categories currently receiving general entry visas at certain Yemen missions.
YEM.notes: Yemen Embassy Netherlands (official source) states entry visas are issued only for those of Yemeni origin, workers at international organisations, journalists and media delegates, and diplomats. Fee approximately EUR 50 (~2-week processing). Proof of heritage or organisational affiliation required. This reflects practical operational policy under Yemen's ongoing armed conflict.

ZAF.name: Visitor's Visa (Tourist) - Up to 90 days
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to visit South Africa temporarily for tourism, family or friend visits, conferences, or sports events.
ZAF.notes: Visa-exempt nationalities do not need this visa for stays up to their permitted period. Non-exempt travelers may apply via eVisa (ehome.dha.gov.za) or ETA (eta.dha.gov.za). Visitors may not work on this visa. Fees updated annually and vary by nationality/currency.

ZAF.name: Visitor's Visa (Tourist) - More than 90 days
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to stay in South Africa for tourism or short-term non-work purposes beyond 90 days.
ZAF.notes: Application submitted at South African embassy/consulate abroad or via ePermit portal. Specific duration determined on a case-by-case basis.

ZAF.name: Visitor's Visa (Business) - Short-term
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreigners visiting South Africa for business purposes such as meetings, negotiations, or conferences for up to 90 days.
ZAF.notes: Short-term business visits; holder may not be employed by a South African entity. Separate from the long-term Business Visa (investment/establishment).

ZAF.name: Business Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who intend to establish or invest in a business in South Africa as contemplated in Section 15 of the Immigration Act.
ZAF.notes: Requires minimum capital investment as determined by the Minister; applicant's business must employ at least 60% South African citizens or permanent residents. Renewable. Governed by Section 15 of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: General Work Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who have a confirmed offer of employment in South Africa in an occupation where South African citizens or permanent residents are not available.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 5 years. Employer must demonstrate that no suitable South African candidate is available (labour market test). Governed by Section 19(2) of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Critical Skills Work Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals whose occupation appears on the South African Critical Skills List, allowing them to work for a South African employer.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 5 years. Requires confirmation from a professional body/council recognised by SAQA. Employment offer required. Critical Skills List is gazetted periodically. Governed by Section 19(4) of the Immigration Act. Requirements version effective 9 October 2024.

ZAF.name: Intra-Company Transfer Work Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to employees of multinational corporations being transferred to a South African branch, subsidiary, or affiliate within the same group.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 4 years. Non-renewable and non-extendable. Governed by Section 19(7) of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Corporate Visa
ZAF.purpose: Enables corporations to employ a predetermined number of foreign nationals in specific occupations where South African workers are unavailable.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 3 years. Issued to the corporation; employees named under the corporate visa are then authorised to work. Governed by Section 21 of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Section 11(2) Short-term Work Authorisation
ZAF.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to perform short-term work in South Africa as a sub-category of the Visitor's Visa framework.
ZAF.notes: Governed by Section 11(2) of the Immigration Act 2002. For short-term assignments, filming, performance, etc. not exceeding 90 days.

ZAF.name: Crew Visa (Section 16)
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals working as a crew member of a conveyance (ship or aircraft) calling at or operating within South Africa.
ZAF.notes: Governed by Section 16 of the Immigration Act 2002. Issued for a maximum of three months at a time, and only for the period the crew member's conveyance remains in South Africa. Holder may not conduct work other than duties as a crew member of the conveyance. Applies to crew of foreign private, chartered, or commercial ships and aircraft.

ZAF.name: Remote Work Visa (Port of Entry Visa)
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals employed by a foreign-based employer who wish to work remotely from South Africa for more than 90 days.
ZAF.notes: Minimum gross annual salary of R650,796.00 required. Applicant must hold a valid employment contract signed by both parties. Must be resident in a country with valid long-term residence status. B1/B2 US visa holders must apply from their country of origin. Requires FBI background check, medical report, and proof of accommodation. SARS registration required if present for more than 183 aggregate days. Fee listed is USD $36 from US applications. Added to Immigration Regulations effective 28 March 2024.

ZAF.name: Study Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals intending to undertake full-time study at an accredited educational institution in South Africa.
ZAF.notes: Valid for the duration of the course. Holder may work up to 20 hours per week. Must have medical cover with a registered South African medical scheme. Governed by Section 18 of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Exchange Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals under 25 years of age participating in cultural, economic, or social exchange programmes in South Africa.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 12 months. Non-renewable and non-extendable. Applicant must be under 25 years of age. Governed by Section 18 of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Retired Person's Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who wish to retire in South Africa on a temporary basis for limited or seasonal periods.
ZAF.notes: Requires proof of minimum monthly income of R37,000 or minimum net worth of R37,000 (note: official website states R37,000; actual threshold may be higher - verify current gazette). Holder may not work. Governed by Section 17 of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Transit Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals passing through South Africa en route to a third country, particularly those intending to obtain long-term residence in a neighboring country.
ZAF.notes: Required for certain nationalities transiting through South Africa even without leaving the international transit area. Pakistan and Bangladesh ordinary passport holders require a transit visa effective 1 August 2022. Governed by Section 11(1) of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Medical Treatment Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who need to travel to South Africa for life-saving or specialised medical treatment unavailable in their home country.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 6 months. Requires letter from a South African medical practitioner confirming treatment. Holder may not work. Governed by Section 11(4) of the Immigration Act 2002.

ZAF.name: Relative's Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to relatives of South African citizens or permanent residents wishing to live in South Africa for an extended period.
ZAF.notes: Valid for up to 2 years. The South African relative must provide a financial assurance of at least R8,500 per month per person. Governed by Section 18 of the Immigration Act 2002. Spouses of South African citizens/permanent residents may apply under Section 11(6) Spousal Visa.

ZAF.name: Spousal / Life Partner Visa - Section 11(6)
ZAF.purpose: Issued to the spouse or life partner of a South African citizen or permanent resident who intends to visit or reside in South Africa.
ZAF.notes: Governed by Section 11(6) of the Immigration Act 2002. Allows the holder to work in South Africa. Must demonstrate a bona fide spousal or life partnership relationship.

ZAF.name: Diplomatic Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to accredited diplomatic personnel and their dependents assigned to South Africa in an official diplomatic capacity.
ZAF.notes: Issued to diplomats accrediting to South Africa. Diplomatic passport holders from certain countries still require a port-of-entry accreditation visa (e.g., USA, Australia, Germany). Managed via DIRCO (Department of International Relations and Cooperation).

ZAF.name: Treaty Visa
ZAF.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals conducting activities in South Africa under the terms of an international treaty or agreement to which South Africa is a party.
ZAF.notes: Governed by international agreements to which South Africa is a signatory. Specific terms depend on the relevant treaty.

ZAF.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
ZAF.purpose: An online pre-travel authorisation for eligible visa-required nationalities visiting South Africa for tourism or short-term purposes, replacing the traditional paper visa for qualifying travellers.
ZAF.notes: Launched September/October 2025. Initial eligible nationalities: China, India, Indonesia, Mexico; expanding to all visa-required nationalities. Stay extendable once for additional 90 days (max 180 days total). Entry initially limited to OR Tambo and Cape Town International Airports, expanding to secondary airports. Work not permitted. Processing within 24 hours per Minister Schreiber. Not required for visa-exempt travellers.

ZAF.name: eVisa (ePermit)
ZAF.purpose: An online visa application system allowing visa-required foreign nationals to apply for South African visitor, study, business, and other visa categories digitally.
ZAF.notes: Available at ehome.dha.gov.za. Eligible applicants must enter through OR Tambo, Cape Town, or Lanseria International Airports. The eVisa is a digital form of the paper visa covering all visa categories available under the Immigration Act. Replaces traditional embassy paper applications for eligible nationalities.

ZAF.name: Permanent Residence Permit
ZAF.purpose: Grants foreign nationals the right to reside permanently in South Africa without time limitations, available under various categories including retirement, business, critical skills, family, and financial independence.
ZAF.notes: Governed by Section 27 of the Immigration Act 2002. Categories: (a) spouse/life partner of SA citizen, (b) critical skills, (c) business/investor, (d) refugee, (e) child of SA citizen, (f) financially independent. Applicants typically must hold a temporary residence visa for 5 years before qualifying (except certain categories). Does not automatically confer citizenship; naturalisation requires additional years of PR.

ZMB.name: Single Entry Visa
ZMB.purpose: Allows a foreign national one entry into Zambia for tourism or short-term visits.
ZMB.notes: Available via e-visa portal (eservices.zambiaimmigration.gov.zm) and on arrival at ports of entry. Persons under 16 cannot apply for an e-Visa independently and must be included in the travelling adult's application. Requires passport with at least 6 months validity and 3 blank pages.

ZMB.name: Double Entry Visa
ZMB.purpose: Permits two entries into Zambia during the validity period for tourism or short-term visits.
ZMB.notes: Allows two entries during the 90-day validity period. Available via e-visa portal and on arrival.

ZMB.name: Multiple Entry Visa
ZMB.purpose: Allows unlimited entries into Zambia during the validity period for tourism or short-term visits.
ZMB.notes: Issued by Headquarters through the e-visa facility. Unlimited entries during the 90-day validity period.

ZMB.name: Transit Visa
ZMB.purpose: For foreign nationals passing through Zambia overland who require a visa.
ZMB.notes: Maximum stay of 7 days. Intended for overland transit passengers who are visa-required nationals.

ZMB.name: Day Tripper Visa
ZMB.purpose: For short day visits of under 24 hours at the same port of entry, typically for Victoria Falls visitors.
ZMB.notes: Available only at Victoria Falls and Kazungula Border Controls. Currently only issued offline (not available via e-visa portal). For visits under 24 hours returning to same port.

ZMB.name: KAZA UNIVISA
ZMB.purpose: A regional visa covering Zambia and Zimbabwe, with permitted day trips to Botswana via Kazungula, for tourism in the Kavango-Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area.
ZMB.notes: Covers Zambia and Zimbabwe with multiple entries between the two countries. Includes day trips to Botswana via Kazungula border. Available at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport (KKIA), Harry Mwanga Nkumbula International Airport (HMNIA), Victoria Falls border, and Kazungula border. Valid up to 30 days within the regional area.

ZMB.name: Gratis Visa
ZMB.purpose: A complimentary visa issued free of charge to members of the diplomatic community entering Zambia on official or accredited business.
ZMB.notes: Issued at Zambia Missions Abroad or at ports of entry to members of the Diplomatic Community presenting letters of accreditation and/or diplomatic passports. Also issued to diplomats not accredited to Zambia but visiting on official business with letters of invitation. No fee charged.

ZMB.name: Employment Permit
ZMB.purpose: For foreign nationals entering Zambia for employment purposes for a period exceeding 6 months.
ZMB.notes: Valid for up to 10 years (extendable). Covers government employees, private sector workers, NGO staff, volunteers, religious organization employees, and spouses or adult children working in family businesses. Requires employment contract, police clearance, CV, qualifications, and a succession/training plan. Holder cannot purchase land or engage in studies. Issuance fee: 24,240 ZMW; Renewal: 28,280 ZMW. After 10 consecutive years, holder may apply for Residence Permit (permanent residence).

ZMB.name: Temporary Employment Permit
ZMB.purpose: For business visitors intending to remain in Zambia for more than 30 days but not exceeding 6 months.
ZMB.notes: Maximum validity of 6 months per 12-month period. Requires covering letter from the institution the applicant is doing business with, completed Form 25, passport, and photograph.

ZMB.name: Investor's Permit
ZMB.purpose: For foreign nationals aged 18 and above who wish to establish a new business or invest in an existing company in Zambia.
ZMB.notes: Requires proof of personal investment of USD 250,000 for a new business or USD 150,000 for joining an existing company. Requires Certificate of Incorporation, proof of investment, lease or ownership agreement, bank statements, and ZRA tax clearance for renewals. Issuance fee: 16,160 ZMW; Renewal: 20,200 ZMW. After holding an Investor's Permit for more than 3 years, holder may qualify for a Residence Permit (permanent residence).

ZMB.name: Study Permit
ZMB.purpose: For foreign nationals undertaking full-time or part-time studies at accredited Zambian educational institutions for longer than 3 months.
ZMB.notes: Renewable for the duration of studies. Requires letter of acceptance from institution, medical report from a Zambian government facility, sponsor letter, and proof of sponsor's financial status. Holders cannot engage in paid work. Issuance fee: 9,090 ZMW; Renewal: 12,120 ZMW.

ZMB.name: Spouse Permit
ZMB.purpose: For spouses of Zambian citizens, established residents, or Residence Permit holders to reside in Zambia.
ZMB.notes: Renewable. Requires marriage certificate, spouse's consent letter, proof of spouse's status, and proof of sustenance. After holding a Spouse Permit for at least 5 years, holder may apply for a Residence Permit (permanent residence).

ZMB.name: Residence Permit (Retiree)
ZMB.purpose: Grants permanent residence to qualifying retirees who can demonstrate sufficient funds to support themselves in Zambia.
ZMB.notes: Retirees qualify for Residence Permit by demonstrating proof of sufficient funds (pension, irrevocable annuity, or retirement account). This is one of several eligibility routes for the Residence Permit. Permit ceases to be valid if holder is absent from Zambia for any period exceeding 12 months. Issuance fee: 20,200 ZMW.

ZMB.name: Visiting Permit
ZMB.purpose: For visitors who wish to remain in Zambia beyond the standard 90-day visa-free or visa entitlement period.
ZMB.notes: Issued for 3 months; maximum 9 months within any 12-month period. Requires host consent letter, host's proof of immigration status, return ticket or proof of sufficient funds, and valid passport.

ZMB.name: Cross Border Permit
ZMB.purpose: For members of regional trade groupings and cross-border traders from neighboring countries engaging in trade across Zambia's borders.
ZMB.notes: Issued for 90 days, renewable for a further 90 days. Maximum 6 months per 12-month period. Requires proof of membership in a cross-border traders' association and a support letter from that association.

ZMB.name: Transit Permit
ZMB.purpose: For commercial truck drivers and crew members transiting through Zambia.
ZMB.notes: Issued for 1 year, renewable for a further 1 year. Distinct from the Transit Visa (which is for overland transit by air/land passengers). Intended for commercial transport operators and crew. Requires company or host letter, passport, and photograph.

ZMB.name: Diplomatic Permit
ZMB.purpose: For ambassadors, diplomats, consular officers, international organization representatives, and their immediate families residing in Zambia.
ZMB.notes: Requires Ministry of Foreign Affairs support letter, Note Verbale or accreditation letter, diplomatic passport, and diplomatic identity card. Covers immediate family members of the permit holder.

ZMB.name: Asylum Seeker's Permit
ZMB.purpose: Issued to individuals who have entered Zambia and are seeking asylum, allowing them to remain lawfully during refugee status determination.
ZMB.notes: Issued for 30 days for the purpose of refugee status determination. Requires national registration card or passport if available. No fee charged.

ZMB.name: Residence Permit
ZMB.purpose: Confers permanent residence on qualifying foreign nationals wishing to settle in Zambia.
ZMB.notes: Grants permanent residence. Eligibility routes include: holding an Employment Permit for 10+ continuous years, holding an Investor's Permit for 3+ years, holding a Spouse Permit for 5+ years, persons born to Zambian citizens, dependants of residence permit holders, and retirees with proof of sufficient funds. Ceases to be valid if the holder is absent from Zambia for more than 12 months or does not enter within 6 months of issuance. Issuance fee: approximately 20,000 ZMW (private sector) or 11,333 ZMW (government/NGO sector). The retiree eligibility route is captured separately as 'Residence Permit (Retiree)'.

ZMB.name: Temporary Permit
ZMB.purpose: Issued to prohibited immigrants directed to remain by the Minister, parents of employment or investor permit holders, and appellants awaiting determination of an appeal.
ZMB.notes: Granted at the direction of the Minister to prohibited immigrants permitted to remain, to parents of Employment or Investor's Permit holders, and to appellants pending determination of an appeal. Distinct from the Temporary Employment Permit. Issuance fee: approximately 24,000 ZMW / renewal 21,000 ZMW (private sector); 12,000 ZMW / renewal 10,667 ZMW (government/NGO sector).

ZWE.name: Single Entry Visa (Holiday)
ZWE.purpose: For visitors travelling to Zimbabwe for leisure, tourism, or holiday purposes. Valid for a single entry.
ZWE.notes: Available as e-visa (Category B and C countries) or visa on arrival (Category B countries only). Standard fee USD 30 (ordinary). Nationality-specific fees apply: UK/British nationals pay USD 55 online; Chinese nationals pay USD 60 online. Category A nationals do not require a visa. Fee schedule confirmed at zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6958; evisa.gov.zw/faq.html no longer publicly lists fees as of June 2026.

ZWE.name: Double Entry Visa (Holiday)
ZWE.purpose: For visitors wishing to make two entries into Zimbabwe within the validity period, e.g. for a trip that crosses into a neighbouring country and returns.
ZWE.notes: Two entries permitted within 3-month validity. Available as e-visa online or visa on arrival for Category B countries. Standard fee USD 45. Nationality-specific fee: UK/British nationals pay USD 70 online. Fee schedule confirmed at zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6958; evisa.gov.zw/faq.html no longer publicly lists fees as of June 2026.

ZWE.name: Multiple Entry Visa (Holiday)
ZWE.purpose: For visitors requiring multiple entries into Zimbabwe over the validity period.
ZWE.notes: Fee updated to USD 55 per zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6958 (re-verified June 2026). Previous record showed USD 160 - that figure was sourced from zimembassydc.org and evisa.gov.zw FAQ (when it still listed fees). evisa.gov.zw FAQ no longer publicly lists fees. validity_days set to null pending official re-confirmation; previous entries showed 6 months (evisa.gov.zw) or 12 months (zimembassydc.org); zimimmigration fees page does not state validity period.

ZWE.name: KAZA UNIVISA
ZWE.purpose: A joint visa permitting entry into both Zimbabwe and Zambia (and day visits to Botswana via the Kazungula border post) within the Kavango-Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area.
ZWE.notes: KAZA UNIVISA is jointly issued by Zimbabwe and Zambia. It allows multiple entries across the KAZA conservation area. Fee is USD 50 (not listed on the zimimmigration fees page; fee retained from previous evisa.gov.zw source). Available as e-visa via evisa.gov.zw or on arrival at designated border posts. Only available to eligible nationalities (not all nationalities qualify for KAZA).

ZWE.name: Emergency Visa (Online)
ZWE.purpose: For urgent travel to Zimbabwe where normal processing timelines cannot be met.
ZWE.notes: Emergency online visa at USD 100, confirmed on zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6958 fee schedule (re-verified June 2026). Eligibility criteria, max stay duration, and processing time not stated on the official fee page. Available only online via evisa.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Business Visa
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals travelling to Zimbabwe for business-related activities such as meetings, negotiations, and seminars, without entering the local workforce.
ZWE.notes: Business visa does not permit the holder to take up employment in Zimbabwe. Category B nationals may obtain on arrival; Category C nationals must apply via evisa.gov.zw in advance. Same fee structure as the holiday visa applies (USD 30 single, USD 45 double, USD 160 multiple entry).

ZWE.name: Conferencing Visa
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals attending conferences, seminars, workshops, or professional events in Zimbabwe.
ZWE.notes: Conferencing visa is specifically for attendance at official events. Holder may not take up employment. Available via e-visa portal or on arrival depending on nationality category.

ZWE.name: Transit Visa
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals passing through Zimbabwe to a third destination, without intending to remain in the country.
ZWE.notes: Transit visa allows passage through Zimbabwe only; the holder may not stay. Specific fee and maximum transit duration were not stated on the official zimimmigration.gov.zw page at time of research. Available via e-visa portal or on arrival depending on nationality.

ZWE.name: Temporary Employment Permit
ZWE.purpose: Allows skilled foreign nationals to work in Zimbabwe for a specific employer where no suitable local candidate is available.
ZWE.notes: Non-refundable application fee of USD 500; USD 300 per dependent. Requires 15 documents including IF5 form, employment contract, notarised academic and professional certificates, police clearance (max 6 months old), medical radiological certificate, company incorporation documents, and proof that the role was advertised locally. Renewals require a letter to the Chief Director of Immigration. Applied for via the e-permits portal at epermits.zimimmigration.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Student Permit
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals enrolled at an accredited educational institution in Zimbabwe for formal study.
ZWE.notes: For students accepted into a higher/tertiary programme at a Zimbabwean institution. Statutory non-refundable fee USD 200 plus USD 300 per dependant; extension same (confirmed on zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6980 Permits page and requirements page ?p=7277, re-verified July 2026). Requires completed I.F.5 form, acceptance letter from the institution, Ministry of Education clearance, passport bio-data page, police clearance, and radiological certificate. Applications via epermits.zimimmigration.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Scholars Permit
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals attending school (primary or secondary level) at an institution in Zimbabwe.
ZWE.notes: Covers pre-tertiary (primary/secondary) school attendance and is listed separately from the Student Permit. Statutory non-refundable fee USD 100; extension USD 100 (confirmed on zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6980 Permits page and requirements page ?p=7272, re-verified July 2026). Requires acceptance from the school, Ministry of Education clearance, and (for minors) a local guardian affidavit. Applications via epermits.zimimmigration.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Spouse Residence Permit
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals who are spouses of Zimbabwean citizens or permanent residents, allowing lawful residence in Zimbabwe.
ZWE.notes: For foreign spouses of Zimbabwean citizens or residents. Statutory non-refundable fee USD 500 plus USD 300 per dependant; extension USD 300 (+USD 300/dependant); permanent-residence track USD 500 (+USD 300/dependant) (confirmed on zimimmigration.gov.zw/?page_id=6980 Permits page and requirements page ?p=7343, re-verified July 2026). Requires an application letter to the Chief Director of Immigration, support letter from the local spouse, marriage certificate, guarantor's proof of accommodation and funds, police clearance (max 6 months old), and radiological certificate. Applications via epermits.zimimmigration.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Investor Residence Permit
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals who invest in Zimbabwe's economy, granting lawful residence tied to their ongoing investment.
ZWE.notes: Issued for 12 months, renewable annually. Non-refundable application fee of USD 500; USD 300 per dependent. Required documents include IF5 form, project proposal, police clearance (max 6 months old), medical radiological certificate, banking history, and proof of funds. The minimum investment threshold is not stated on the official page at time of research - previously cited figures (USD 100,000 or USD 1,000,000) could not be confirmed from the official source. Applications via epermits.zimimmigration.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Permanent Residence Permit
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals who have satisfied the residency requirements and wish to permanently reside in Zimbabwe.
ZWE.notes: Permanent Residence Permit is listed on the official Zimbabwe Department of Immigration website. Eligibility criteria, minimum residency period, and fees are not published on the accessible official pages at time of research. Applications via epermits.zimimmigration.gov.zw.

ZWE.name: Missionary Permit (Religious Worker Permit)
ZWE.purpose: For foreign nationals coming to work full-time as a Minister of Religion or church worker for a local congregation in Zimbabwe.
ZWE.notes: Religious-worker permit for foreign nationals employed full-time as a Minister of Religion or church worker at the request of the leadership of a local congregation. Applicant must have worked at least one year as a religious worker OR have been ordained as a Minister of Religion following ministerial training; the sponsoring church organisation must take full responsibility for the maintenance of the worker and dependants (and their return to country of domicile) without recourse to public funds. A dedicated requirements page existed on the former Department of Immigration site (zimimmigration.gov.zw/index.php/permits/missionary-permit) which now returns HTTP 404 following the site's migration to WordPress; the current Permits overview page (?page_id=6980) lists five permit types and does not separately itemise this one. The permit remains a recognised category applied for via the e-permits portal. Fee not confirmed on a current official page.
